title: Pretty & I love it!
text: Lovely ink. Writes well. The right amount of wet/dry. Currently using it in both a platinum curidas (f) & a pelican twist (m) & it writes well in both.  Beautiful color & flows nicely. It has not clogged up my nibs.

title: 2 excellent 1 extremely dry (blue)
text: Overall I’m pretty happy with this purchase bc the ink is good & I’ve purchased it before.  The green is gorgeous.  The purple didn’t really wow me, but it flows nicely. The blue however is a disappointment bc it’s extremely dry & keeps drying in my pen. I am using the inks in the same type of pen- platinum curidas & all have same size nib. So the only difference is the actual ink.  I’m gonna try to mix a little of the ink with a tiny bit of glycerin next time I refill it & see if that helps it to stay wetter & not dry out in my pen. Aside from that I love their ink. Think I just received a dud this time with the blue.

title: I don’t get the reviews. Mine are garbage.
text:
[[VIDEOID:63276c19932aa4f3687042b8b9f8613c]] Update: tried again to return them. I have prime. Amazon wants $7.99 to pick them up. Why? Bc I return garbage products & I don’t feel like I should be penalized when third party sellers & amazon send damaged/defective products & then expect me to be happy with them & keep them. Why should I bear the burden of a billion dollar plus corporation as a disabled veteran living on disability? These skip all over the place. The yellow won’t write no matter how much I shake the ball bearing. It and the black give a second of ink & stop. I even tried warming the ink up. The black finally became more viscous, but the yellow won’t lay down. If you have a fast hand & are used to taking fast notes these are useless. At least my set is. Garbage. Utter & complete garbage. Some work better if you write slow like a toddler, but I have never had to slow my hand with a zebra fountain pen nor any of the 200 others I own. And you don’t have to shake the zebra pen!

I purchased these bc of the reviews. Maybe I receive a bad batch. Idk. Mine are awful. I have fountain pens I purchased online for a dollar and less that works better & that write every single time I pick them up. Half of these did not even work after I attached the ink. I had to squeeze the cartridge repeatedly & even then I’m lucky if I get anything to come out. For $18 I was expecting to at least get something that would write every time I picked it up. These are a scratchy mess. I have tried them on cheap paper & expensive Tomoe River paper with the same results. I have hundreds of fountain pens, but I was looking for something that I could visually see at a moment’s glance what color was in the pen & I thought these would work. I will give them a few more days, but if the ink doesn’t settle in & lubricate the innards so that the writing experience is improved then I will definitely be sending these back bc they are garbage as-is.

title: Ordering Ink online: never a good idea I guess.
text: It’s a beautiful color, but even though it had been packed extremely well imo it still arrived & showed considerable loss of ink due to shipping/handling disturbances.  It also left a stain on my bathroom vanity that I am still working on & thankfully it’s just a small one as I placed paper towels down before I opened the mess.  Next time I receive a bottle like this I’m just going to rinse it off, pat it dry, & slip a non-latex glove over it to keep everything in the vicinity safe including my hands bc the ink stained the label & wont come off except if my hands happen to be wet/moist.  The ink works well on both Tomoe River paper & cheap notebook paper & dries quickly.  As for the ink itself: I love it!  I don’t understand why it stained my vanity tho bc to my knowledge it’s not supposed to be waterproof.  Luckily after much scrubbing there is only a tiny mark left & I know it’s there, but I am really hoping my LL does not notice it.  Gonna try a little bleach on it next.  Also, I was able to mix a bit of it with a J Herbin red ink (scented red rose I believe) that I had on hand to get another shade of purple & I am quite pleased with it.  It is currently in a Dryden pen rn & it’s working beautifully with zero issues. This ink R&K is in a Lamy  “Candy” purple pen & is also working beautifully.  I wish they offered the inks in glass bottles instead of the cheap plastic.  Tho I recently received a bottle of Pilot Iroshiziku ink with a cracked lid & zero ink as it had obviously been upside down at some point during transit so glass is no guarantee that ink doesn’t get damaged. I’m disabled so I generally order everything online as it’s easier for me, but it appears I am going to have to venture out of my cave at some point. Lol. The ink is lovely if you can get one that has not been damaged or lost too much of it’s contents en route as I have.  I did notice that the cap on mine was dented & I believe that’s probably what allowed the ink to escape as they always tell us not to buy dented cans at grocery stores!  Things are only as good as their weakest links.

title: Mine are iffy at best.
text: Idk if I just got a bad batch which is possible I suppose bc let’s face it sometimes companies have bad manufacturing runs, but all 4 of my pens are a total pain to use. They skip or the ink just does not flow at all no matter how hard I press on the Nov & then I get a puddle of ink.  Every once in a blue moon if I dip them in ink they seem to work a bit better, but it’s definitely not how they were meant to be used. I am not a newbie either. I own well over 200 fountain pens & calligraphy pens of versing widths & I have a large collection of inks as well. I also tried these out on every type of paper I have from Tomoe River to Mead & composition notebooks, but the pens I have are just useless for me as they will not write fluidly.  If I wanted to stop & start a hundred x I would just stick with my dip pens.  These are a huge let down as they have so many high reviews & I just wasn’t expecting them to be so awful.  Idk if I’m going to try the amazon replacement or not.  In my experience I tend to get another item from the same bad quality lot (or worse).  Decisions, decisions.

title: Quality not as pictured in advertising.
text:
[[VIDEOID:ffd2a834f42a38fd089e2bfa848e4b5d]] Idk what to say bc what I received looks nothing like the one advertised. What I received looks like someone poured motor oil on leather after they stamped it then went on a long lunch & came back & tried to fix the mess they left on the leather. It looks like they tried to distress or something which I hate to begin with as I’m not a fan of fake distressing. I find that seems to be the norm when the leather is not the best quality. When the leather is thinner or more scratched up as this is the sellers seem to think it’s best to distress it.

The stamping itself is well done. The only problem with it is that the leather is so thin & thinner even in some places that it has created humps in the cover front & back. I am not joking about the motor oil. It feels & smells like motor oil. Their is a slick substance on my hands after touching it & I am allergic to petroleum products so I’ve had to wash my hands several times & put on gloves. The distressing job was so uneven that if I decide to keep the journal I will definitely not keep it in this incarnation. I will definitely use leather cleaner to remove whatever I can sue to my allergies & then I will have to cover it with something else that I’m not allergic to, but that just adds time & money to this so idk what I’m going to do yet. I’ve even thought of painting it & sealing it. Fortunately the dye job on the front isn’t as bad as the one on the back & I’m the only one that will see it as it’s not a gift for anyone except myself.

I like the locking mechanism & feel they did a good job on thst tho it was covered in the oil too. That has made it easy to open tho. Lol. However, bc of the locking mechanism this is not a journal you will be able to paste or collage many things into. It’s a straight up writing journal imo bc it’s in no way expandable due to the locking device. Tho I suppose if your crafty/handy you can change out the rivets in the back & add a longer piece of leather there after you have filled it to ur heart’s desire.

As for the paper I don’t find it any better than any paper I’ve had in similar journals. It has flecks & bits of other papers which I personally don’t care for bc I use fountain pens & dip pens & my pens will skip on the uneven surfaces & that is literally on every page. There are also quite a few wrinkled pages in the journal which you can find with homemade journals.

So at this point I just don’t know. I need to think about it a bit more. If I had received a journal that looked as good as the advertised one & was not covered in oil & I would definitely keep it & just use different pens or use it for watercolor or bird sketches. This one requires more thought. I definitely would not give this as a gift to anyone unless I ordered it to be delivered to me & had a chance to clean it up & check it out first, but if you are a crafty person who likes a challenge or is willing to take a chance & hope for one like the pic then idk maybe take a chance?

title: Packing is awful will update pen review later
text: Literally one of the worst packing jobs I’ve seen.  It’s the lightest pen I have ever used & as I am post surgery on my dominant hand & am used to less than 5 minutes of writing even remotely comfortably I absolutely love that part.  I think it’s pricey for what it is though. The Pilot Petit are $3 on Jet pens. 8 x cheaper & imho write just as well. Where this has the advantage for me is tho I am a woman I am tall & have man hands so said two hubbies. Bloody mean things to say if you ask me. Lol.  I am in love with it even though I hate the price point & truly believe it to be massively overpriced for plastic, but being s fountain pen junkie with well over a hundred including Montblanc I fully intend to buy bc thst is what we fountain pen ppl do. We collect them in all shapes & sizes. I have 5 kids & I tend to collect them in both my & my children’s & my grandchildren’s favorite colors.  Some I gift while I am alive & others they will only inherit bc I use them daily for writing & art.  It is a little beauty & I love that the cap screws on.  This mint color is beautiful & just happens to match a cutting mat I picked up at Wally World recently. Lol. Yay me!

title: Defective hardware & workmanship
text: [[VIDEOID:c4ffdd909a55f78e5a83951e34c4528e]] Unfortunately I received a pen that has some very bad metal parts that has the actual gold finish missing in quite a few places & is scratched up in many others.  That means the metal parts actually test my skin & cut it because the metal is actual quite jagged in many places. I don’t know if the metal pieces were dropped or were caught in some machinery or what, but it makes for a very unpleasant feeling when you hold it & a very unsafe result when it cut my fingers in several places.  I liked the look of the ribbed design of the metal on the pen, but it made for a less than ideal experience when actually holding the pen as it was uncomfortable.  It’s a very pretty pen & I found it quite beautiful even though it honestly triggered issues with my vertigo. Something about the design where it looks almost holographic & like the design is actually moving kicked my vertigo into high gear which is unfortunate bc the design was the entire reason I purchased the pen in the first place. Lol.  The issue with the workmanship should be able to ne seen in the pics as there are quite a few globs of resin or acrylic down the side of the pen which are a darker yellow stain than the rest of the pen & there are globs of what must be wood pulp or shavings in the resin that end up sitting directly on top of the top layer & you can both see them & feel them when you run your hand over the pen. Which is extremely annoying to someone who likes to pet her fountain pens.  It would definitely be worth checking back in a couple of months as the crafter gets better at their trade and/or uses better materials.  However, right now with these damaged metal materials with nicks, scratches, & paint missing & with the flaws/damages to the wood I’m not in the mood for a replacement & I intend to go for a return/refund.  Though I do hope to try this seller again at a later date if I see an improvement in the issues bc I prefer hand made fountain pens.

title: My pen is utter garbage & leaks like a sieve.
text: [[VIDEOID:b5de3fbb67572893aa86f7052023b9ba]] I’m dumbfounded by the great reviews. Maybe I just received a dud? Idk.  My pen leaks like a sieve as you can see in the pics & by the ink collected on my fingers. The cap will not post which makes me crazy.  The clip is askew. It’s like a third grader put it together with left over fittings & tried to make it fit. The fittings are a hot mess too. The gold is all scratched, dinged, & dented & it came like that right out of the packaging.  I also can’t u deer and why they have 2 shades of teal making up the pen body. The very tip is one shader & it just looks like they ran out of resin imo.  The resin itself has some obvious impurities in it. Idk if it was dusty where these were made or what, but something definitely got into the mix that produced this pen.  I am a fountain pen freak & I have purchased pens off eBay for 99 cents or less that write 100x better than this pen. The nib is so scratchy it has actually torn paper & I have a very light hand & use pricey papers.  I love Jane Davenport stuff, but after seeing the cancer warnings no thx.  I’ll purchase from artists who care as much about my health as I do.

title: Damaged! Stamps don’t pick up the ink properly.
text: I’ve used Carter’s for 4 decades in a work environment & home environment for arts & crafts, but I have never in my life received one looking like this. Looks like some kid stick their fingers in it.  Lol. And the seal actually looked as tho it had been previously compromised when I went to open it. I wish I had thought to take a pic of that.  I’m less than thrilled bc I needed this asap for a current project.  The front of the pad is pretty beat up too.  It has a very obvious dent in it which I would assume is when the interior pad got messed up making it hard to get stamps to pick up the ink evenly without applying a lot of pressure & then you get parts of the stamp that aren’t part of the design. This seems like a scratch & dent sale ink pad to me which sucks bc I love Carter’s & have used them for decades as I stated before.  The pad appears to be inked well & is not dry. It even seems to close pretty well considering the huge dent in the lid, but it does not work for the purposes I purchased it for. I’m hoping I can return it or exchange it.

title: Excellent! Buy it. Buy lots in fact!
text: New to this brand & as a huge fan & collector of fountain pens I am now a huge fan of this brand.  I purchased the 5-1/2” x 8” size & a smaller one to throw in my purse.  I plan on purchasing more in the future as my fountain pens have finally found a home for their ink & words.  I am very excited about the two ribbons too.  The only issue I see that already annoys me immensely as these are brand spanking new right out of the plastic is that they are missing the green color in several places. Idk if it has flaked off or what, but these were sealed in plastic when I I received them. I have handled them exactly  one time since opening them so idk how that paint job on the cover is going to hold up to daily use.  I knocked of a star for that bc imo they should not be flaking off their color after one handling of extremely light use.  I’m disabled with a bad arm so I’m not able to be rough with it even if I wanted to. Lol. It’s lost the green color at the top & the bottom already.  That is concerning to me as it’s not even been placed on a book shelf yet, but just been lying on a table tray by itself.

title: Could have been wonderful.  Has execution flaws.
text:
Update: received replacement & the second is just like the first unfortunately. So I will assume this was made by the same crafter & from the same batch as the last. Again, the paper has been pulled too tightly & ripped through the backing. It has also been cut through the first 30% of the pages at one edge. There are paint pen marking all over the journal inside & out. This one has a cut down the front where maybe they had begun to make a scoring cut in the leather & realized it was going to be too short & then just put the design over it. They did a better job of getting a deeper embossing on this one tho. The finish is worse however. This one has a weird finish almost like pumice stones where it looks kind of crackled & porous Idk if it was done on purpose as a design or not. I wish this crafter would learn to not use paint pens to mark up leather bc it ruins the product. If you try to remove the paint pen you ruin the leather. I am double bummed for having given them a second chance.
Old review:
This could have been a beautiful little hotter notebook. Unfortunately it is not. The ppl that made it decided to use metallic paint pens & permanent markers to mark all their sewing lines ruining the aesthetic. There is not a spot on either side without a blemish. I had resolved myself that if only the inside was ugly I could live with that. Lol. Bc there’s a lot of that irl imo, but it turned out that both the inside & outside had imperfections behind what I was prepared to pay for & live with. As a disabled person I can generally live with a lot lol, but I spend my little bit of money on writing tools & I like them to be nice. This could have been a thing of true beauty as it reminds me of several Levenger notebooks I own. Sadly, while the idea was great the execution is lacking. I hope they will do it right next time bc it’s the perfect size to throw into a purse or backpack for a short trip or even a longer jaunt if you bring paper refills. The paper quality was not what I was hoping for either & as it arrived torn & already pulling away from its base I would not have used it anyways. As it is it is a hard no for me in its current state. I hope that either the seller or amazon will do right me. Someone should definitely be doing quality inspection checks bc this would not have passed even a rudimentary one. The metallic silver paint pen was a glaring no staring me right in the face the second I opened it up. The black permanent marker while it did match the journal better was still extremely obvious & still extremely annoying to see. It’s a well thought out design in my estimation just an extremely flawed execution. I hope the seller tweaks their issues & offers it in other colors bc I would totally try again.

title: Lovely, but front bent  corner & toner (?) splotches throughout.
text: It’s a nice heavy journal with thick pages.  The rose gold color is very pretty. Of course the first thing I noticed when I pulled it from the package was that the upper right hand corner had already been bent.  For some reason the quick reference page has been glued in weirdly imo so that there is no margin to the left & it makes it hard to write ur information there.  I haven’t written mine in there yet bc my entire book seems to have toner or printer ink or something on every single page like someone decided to just sprinkle some fairy dust on every page.  As I intend to use this partly as an art journal I would prefer one without the added splotches all over.  I believe there are 43 sheets of lined paper after the journal section & I am quite happy about that added bonus.  The envelope in the back is quite roomy & will hold a lot of receipts.  It’s a pretty journal & I suspect I will buy more from the manufacturer in the future albeit hopefully without these issues bc this one needs to be replaced & hopefully Amazon will do so.

title: Wrong pens!!!
text: My review is whacked bc I received the wrong pens & I am extremely unhappy about it. I have not had a very good week with Amazon in particular.  I love Amazon, but I keep receiving packages that are damaged containing items that are damaged.  Now this mess arrives. Argh!  The pens are excellent in every regard. They just aren’t the colors ordered. I wanted the purple & yellow pens & as you can see they are not in my order.  I ordered a journal earlier this week that came with some pens & stencils & the pens are too thick to fit in the stencils. These do an amazing job in them. The stencils have very tight corners & are very sharp & these handle them beautifully. I just did not want to waste ink filling them in. Lol. The first thing I noticed about these pens was the heft. I love a pen with some heft to it. Even tho I’ve had hand surgery & I can no longer write, paint, or draw as long as I used to I have always loved the feel of a well balanced writing instrument in my hand. These aren’t exactly balanced lol bc of the ink distribution & the plastic fatigue finger rest, but it feels nice in my hand.  I’m just thoroughly ticked off that these are not what I paid for & what I have been waiting for. Lol.  Back to my pen search.

title: Arrived dinged up. Not happy.
text: It’s pretty, but it’s not very sturdy. Mine arrived looking like it had been dropped on its edges either before or during transit tho I suppose it could have happened in a warehouse somewhere.  Even if I was willing to overlook that- which I am most definitely not- I opened it up to see that the tabbed monthly pages were all bent and folded too.  They are just regular paper pages with a little tan at the top that has a protective tape over it to make it sturdier i guess. Clearly it does not make it stuffy enough to survive the shipping.  I briefly thought that I would keep it & try to make it work bc returns are such a hassle for me bc I am disabled.  I get really annoyed with having to watch out for porch pirates trying to steal my returns if I put them on my porch to wait for UPS.  I am both physically disabled & hearing impaired so I have 2 service dogs, but I have found that if I try to keep my returns inside my home until UPS arrives they either don’t ring my doorbell to alert my service dogs who then alert me or they leave before I can physically get myself to the door. So yeah- returns are a big deal to me. Lol.  Bc if miss the window for UPS to pick it up (they only try once now) I then have to take it to a drop off center. Did I mention I am disabled? Lol. And I don’t drive?  Yeah. Big time fun at my house with returns.  So then I would have to pay more for a taxi there & back than what the products are worth. Lol. Not to mention my pain & suffering throughout all of it.  I just can’t help feeling that sometimes stuff gets shipped that has already been dropped or dinged bc I have received an awful lot lately  & it’s really ticking me off.  If I wanted dropped & dinged stuff I would buy used not new!  Hence the very long winded diatribe of venting here.  Let’s see if Amazon will post it. Lol.

title: Pretty Flipping Awesome!
text: I’m a book freak & I adore mine!  I use fountain pens. Cheap ones off eBay I paid anywhere from 5 cents to 99 cents for up to my Montblanc pens & Pilot pens & they all work fine. Sure you may have a little paper on the end of ur nib once in a while, but to me it’s nbd bc it homemade paper & I think they did a marvelous job on it. I’m not generally a fan of the “antiquing” of anything. I usually hate it, but I fell in love w the silver paper in this journal & decided why not?  The only thing I would change is the closure. I hate the tab thingy. I prefer the wrap around string method to close my journals or anything that does not leave me any type of uneven surface to write on later.  It’s a neat design feature to some ppl & it does look good & cute, but it’s not my personal preference.  I would not let that keep me from buying another one though. Lol. I do hope they make them with a different closing option in the future though bc I love the size of the book & the superior craftsmanship.  It’s well worth the price!

title: First one mis-delivered to??? Replacement A+!
text: It’s beautiful. I wasn’t sure if I would be happy with it given the price I paid which I felt was costly, but I’m happy enough with it. Bought it to record bird sightings in my backyard. I’m disabled & I am trying to find new ways to keep my mind off chronic pain which can consume a lot of brain cells.  Sadly, I took a disastrous fall shortly after buying it bc my neighbor blamed my bird feeders for injuring a local squirrel that likes to raid my bird feeders even though I left food for the squirrels too. The exact same food. I kid you not, but the evil little bigger decided to get on a light branch I was advised to place the feeder on by a bird conservancy place that “should keep the squirrels off of it”. Ha!  The squirrel was limping from a fall. I went out & stood on a 36” crate & took a nasty fall & I now have to have another back surgery. Proof that no good deed goes unpunished as the saying goes. Lol.  The fall lead to a concussion & repeated blackouts & exacerbated sciatica & massive swelling on my head, face, butt, elbows, hips, knees, etc. lol. Literally everywhere that hit the ground when I fell. So the irony is I have not even been able to use my beautiful bird journal to record any bird sightings since I bought it bc I am laid up awaiting back surgery. The last one left me disabled 15 years ago. Anyone reading this please keep me (Sherri) & my family in ur prayers bc if my past surgery is anything to go by i & we will need it.  So… now that you know my life story & I have saved $500 on therapy… buy the journal bc it’s simply lovely. Lol.

title: I love it!
text: It’s pretty. The color is gorgeous. It has nice paper. I can use my fountain pens in it even the cheapest 99 cent ones I buy on eBay. Lol. What’s not to love?  But it bc you will not regret it. And truth bomb: I bought this for my grandson - and kept it! Lol. Yeah- I’m that b*tch!,  but I gave him something better in his opinion as a kid. Win-win!

title: Best purchase ever!!!!
text: Where has this been since I became disabled & mostly bedridden?  I’ve been through so many subpar bed trays it’s ridiculous. This one is a gem!  I absolutely love it!  I am stunned that my art easel actually fits it & even better two of the plastic legs nicely fit into the book ledge groove to keep it nice & steady while I draw & paint.  I love the ski sled legs because it makes it so easy to move when I have to get up. One of the previous types I tried was so heavy I could barely lift it due to my disabilities, but this is sturdy & light.  The only thing I might do is add 2 pieces of small rubber to the ski sled legs at the ends by my body for added stability so that it doesn’t move when I don’t want it to because I suffer with vertigo & sleep apnea & I don’t want it to move if I fall over. Lol. So I would still be able to just lightly lift the legs w the rubber attached & still be able to push it forward easily enough. The only other thing I miss & need is a cup holder as I am on medications & need to stay hydrated & do lots of arts & crafts where I need to have water handy. I understand they probably didn’t add it bc most ppl buy it to use as a laptop table & electronics & fluids are never a hood idea, but I wish I had the option to choose for myself. I’ve thought about drilling a hole in the top & adding a cup holder or more likely just adding one to the side. As I will likely add some cup holders for my pens, pencils, & brushes, & craft supplies. I also wish that they offered an even larger size.  For those of us who are stuck in our beds & literally live in them there are very few options that are not homemade.  I would love one to go the full length of my queen bed & have designed several of them. Lol. As I live alone with 2 service dogs there’s nobody to complain about me dropping beads in the bed or spiking paint on the sheets. Lol.  To the manufacturers: bravo on a well-designed product & please for the love of God & this disabled woman please make a larger option!!!!  Mine never leaves my bed. I just push it to the end of the bed & go to sleep & wake up the next morning & pull it back towards me & resume my crafting or bills or whatever I was doing the night before. Lol.  Oh- and sometime- yeah SOMETIMES- I even use it as a food tray. Imagine that!! Lol.

title: Hard as a rock!  Lumpy. Gross. Ugly!
text: I expected to love this journal Bc I love the color & I absolutely love glitter. However, what arrived is a hot mess. It’s hard as a rock on one entire side. There is no fluid & there is absolutely no consistency in this product. All of the glitter is bunched up & melted/solidified to one side of the journal. It’s vile. This was supposed to be a gift. Thank heaven I had it delivered to me for wrapping Bc I would have been absolutely mortified for the recipient to have received this & equated it’s total lack of quality with my feelings for the recipient.  I do not even understand how a product in this condition is being shipped by the manufacturer or Amazon. Shame on both of them. It’s been a complete waste of my time & my $ (spent looking for the item, waiting for the item, paying for the item & now having to return the item)!  Unreal this is offered for sale in this condition. Not cool ppl.

title: I love this pen!
text: It writes beautifully!  Now I need it in more colors. I love the stub nib.

title: Obviously dropped while packing!
text: Aside from the fact that this was obviously dropped while being packed bc it has dirt on it & is so damaged I cannot believe it was even shipped I still cannot believe how lacking in quality these are.  I ordered two & while the second is in a little better shape I already know this will be a return for me. As a disabled person I tend to take falls & maybe the bad packaging person that dropped the book did me a favor by pointing out its obvious flaws.  The main reason I purchased these books to begin with was because the company donates a book for every book you buy and I always try to support companies that give back in this manner & to this degree, but for my personal needs these just won’t work. They just are not sturdy enough.  If they had arrived I damaged & I could have used them for a while & found that out for myself I probably would have given them a higher rating, but I think 3 stars is fair as they are usable for most oriole & priced okay currently. They are actually cheaper today than when I purchased them days ago.  Amazon always seems to lower prices after I purchase stuff. Lol. So much for Irish luck. Lol.  These will do for grocery lists or general to do lists, but you won’t want to trust your poetry or fine writing to these imo. The paper is very thin & see through & some of my pages are glued together weirdly. Idk why & it’s driving me crazy. Definitely a return.

title: Perfect!  Great size, refillable, & affordable! Trifecta!
text: Not the best pics, but I bought these to give to my kids & grandkids along with these pens I’m making for them with resin. I used temporary tattoos & then I sprayed a clear urethane over them so they the gold tattoos don’t run off & I make sure to place the tattoos above & below the rubber band thingy.  For less than $4 a kid my kids have a great planner that’s refillable & I can personalize each with animals they  like & I have since added their names using the creep $1 alphabet stickers you can buy most places. title: AT&T CL84107 phone set
text:
UPDATE BELOW...I purchased this set because my local phone service offers me TEN (that's one zero) "blocks" on unwanted calls. That fills up in about 2 days - so, I have to delete my 'log' and start over. OMG. I looked into purchasing a plug in blocker box but this was actually less expensive - so I dived in. It was easy to hook up, but... it is a rather complicated and not very intuitive install on pretty much all the settings. It's a LOT of reading.. a lot of doing. But I have it set up. We shall see how it goes. I have high hopes. I did purchase one additional handset because we needed 2, but not 3 and it was still cheaper than purchasing the plug in boxes (that didn't have super great recent reviews). I believe you can purchase up to 12 (?) additional receivers if you need them with this unit - but I am not certain. The base unit is a corded phone - and the screen is large and easy to read. You can sit on a desk, or hang on a wall. The two cordless units have fairly large screens too - pretty easy to use with nice large numbers - however, they do NOT like to stay in their charging units - a slight nudge and the fall over. Eh. I am really just hoping for less spam calls. We rarely use the landline -but where we live it is necessary to get the DSL we need - so any calls coming to the landline are 99.9% spam. Says you can block up to 1000 numbers. That seems like a miracle after just 10. Fingers crossed. Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
UPDATE: 4/6/2021... So after a few weeks...I have to say that all of sudden - it' s the sweet sound of silence. I have literally not had a single call of any kind, let alone SPAM (which is actually the only calls I get on my landline) I did activate the option to have callers "announced" (caller must say their name and be announced before call goes through) - maybe that's it.. but whatever it is - I am very much appreciating the huge reduction of spam calls. I haven't had to push the "call block" button once. In all honesty, we keep the landline only because it's the only way we can get the DSL we do - as crappy as it is. In a very small rural area, we sadly have little choice. So a system like this - stopping the long lists of SPAM calls is real relief. I do wish the system was a bit easier to use - it's a bit complicated - thus I still stand on the 4 star review. If you have reasonable ability to read a bit of lengthy and boring instructions, you can get through it. And if you're overwhelmed with SPAM calls, I would definitely recommend it. I will continue to update if new info would be helpful.

There are several different types of these - I have 'pretty' ones and these - which are very, how shall we say, very utilitarian - nothing fancy.  Brushed silver metal.  No sparkle or cute shape. This order contains 6 pieces, 3 in each bag. You can buy individually as well.  The new, updated style is a lot better designed and offers much, much stronger magnets.  I have worn these on a lot of different material tops, thick, thin, smooth, silky, thermal, sweatshirts.. and all with secure success.  I have tried the leash type of reader holders but I hate the string around my neck - plus your glasses dangle over what your working on - or become like a bib when eating.  I am a woman so placing the magnet holder in the right spot is a consideration but I have found the perfect spot for me.  If you haven't tried this version, I encourage you to try them.  This particular style has TWO strong magnets, one on each end.  They do offer this version with sparkly dots and in gold tones if you prefer.  I wanted just a simple, plain version (I already have some cutesy versions) and these are definitely plain and simple - great for every day use.  I have found the magnets are so strong you use them on scarves and other neck treatments if you'd like.  I have even used on a thin wool ruana - worked perfectly to hold the ruana in place all day.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and this is no exception.  I waited before reviewing these because I wanted to be certain I had tried in various ways.  Overall, 5 stars.  I can't think of a thing negative to say.

title: Sharpie gel pens
text:

title: coin counter
text:
UPDATE BELOW....I ordered this just to keep track of the loose change in my bowl. It is a fully plastic item and lightweight... but if it were any heavier you wouldn't be able to lift it when full of coins. The plastic bottle, while lightweight, appears to be pretty sturdy. Time will tell. The pics I have included show around $45.00 in change so I estimate the jar will hold around $200+ in change if I keep around the same mix of coins shown....It will obviously depend on what coins you are dropping in. There are two "pinches" on the side of jar, but they are pretty useless unless the jar is empty. When it has change in the jar, it's too heavy for the side pinches to be useful. The opening of the jar is about 2 1/2" . And adult cannot put a hand inside the jar, so you will have to pour the contents out. The jar is about 10 or so inches tall... eye balling it. The top (counter part) requires 2 AAA batteries (not included) AND a tiny screwdriver to open the battery compartment. Upon opening and inserting batteries, I put in a counted number of coins.. $1.67 for a test. The lid immediately failed after 3 coins and just stopped adding or reading denominations at all. I read the directions and inserted a pen into the "reset" hole on the underside of the lid (to the top right area of the battery compartment). It reset and I tried again. It worked. And continued working through the rest of the coin drops. The screen read stays on a few minutes (haven't timed it yet) and then blacks out. It re-awakens when you drop another coin in. With each coin dropped the screen flashed the denomination of the coin 3x and then shows the total. Normally I just throw my coins into a big bowl. When it gets full I load up into a ziplock and take it to my bank. Back in the day they wanted the coin rolled... now, no bank will take rolled coins. Thus the ziplock bag. The counter will take some of the guess work out of the total.. IF it continues to work... but I am ok with a "close" total. It's amazing how fast it adds up. I am disappointed it failed right out of the gate. PLUS. I HATE it when you have to use a tiny screwdriver to get into the battery compartment!! I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
UPDATE 2/14/2017.... the seller contacted me immediately and offered a replacement top, stating that the top should not have failed even with a restart. Currently the original top is still working. I will keep the second as a back up. It is rare to come in contact with such a responsible seller. I added one star to the rating for this response and hope the jar will keep working. It's not a high quality electronic instrument - I understand that - but I do really appreciate the effort by the seller.

title: Smooth writing; nice grip
text: I have used gel pens for years as they are so much nicer than other types of pens.  I never tried Sharpie Brand, but like all the other Sharpie products, these are good quality.  They write smoothly and have a comfortable grip.  The only thing that might keep you from buying these is the price.  All gel pens tend to be a little pricey.  You can probably find cheaper gel pens, but you get what you pay for and may be disappointed with cheaper versions.  If you have never used a gel pen, give yourself a treat and get some.  Just realize that gel pens are not ideal for filling out multi-part forms.  You need to press hard to do that type of forms and gel pens don't require much pressure to use them.  In fact they are probably ideal for people who have limited hand strength and can't easily use another type of pen.

title: Wi-Fi Setup is Tricky, Control Panel a little difficult to get used to; otherwise a great printer
text: Unpacking and doing the basic printer set up and filling with ink was pretty easy.  The instruction sheet is clear and easy to understand and follow.  This printer is different than any other I have had in that it doesn't use ink cartridges, but instead uses ink tanks.  You fill each tank with the appropriate color of ink from a bottle (bottles are included to fill each color tank fully).  You can actually see the ink levels from a semi-clear window on each tank; you also can view levels from software.  Print quality seems decent with good colors.  I liked the fact that the printer is not overly large or heavy.  It has a reasonable footprint for the capability it has.  Now the negatives.  First of all, since there are tanks with ink in them, if you tip up the printer much when moving it, you could potentially spill ink out.  The tanks have covers, but not sure how secure they are; there is an obvious warning on the box not to tilt the printer after the tanks are filled.  If you wanted to ship the printer, you would have to find a way to drain the tanks.  The control panel on the printer is a little confusing until you get used to it.  I kept wanting to press the LCD display, but it is not touch screen.  You use buttons to the right of the screen to navigate.  To make a photo copy is a number of presses on the panel.  Even turning the printer off is a three step process.  Another brand of printer I have is easier to operate.  Another gripe that I have when setting up is that when you are unable to connect from your computer, if you have to end the program, you have to start all over from the beginning with a complete reinstall of software.  The only real negative to this printer is the Wi-Fi setup.  I could not get it to set up properly, until I used a USB cable.  At first I thought the problem was that my router was running at 5GHZ and not broadcasting a 2.5GHZ signal and actually ended up setting up a separate SSID for dedicated 2.5GHZ.  That did not work at all.  Finally by using the original SSID of my router, was able to connect my computer to the printer with WiFi, but ONLY by using a USB connection for the setup (USB cable is not included).  After you connect, you can remove the USB cable and then print with WiFi.  This printer only works on 2.5 GHZ and I think it is time that manufacturers start supporting 5 GHZ on their devices.  If you want to use this with WiFi, you better know a lot about your router.  Fortunately you can use the printer on a network (Ethernet cable), a USB connection or wireless.  Scanning is a little hard to figure out because you have to download and install a separate utility from the Epson website and it is not quite clear what it is that you download and install; fortunately I guessed correctly, as I got scanning to work from my computer; however, I could not get scanning to work from the printer panel.  A label on the top of the printer mentions FAX capability, but the outside box does not and apparently a different model does faxing.  As far as how long the ink lasts, I am not optimistic as the black ink has already gone down quite a bit and I have only printed about a half dozen pages.  I think once you get over the oddities of setup, this is a good printer.  A little weak on setup.  Nothing included to set it up; you have to download from the Epson website.  That's probably a good thing as you always have the most up-to-date software that way.

title: Works good; cheaper than OEM toner
text: It has always been my policy to use only OEM toner and ink, but as much as it costs, I thought maybe it was time to try a non-OEM product.  The black toner just ran out in my printer soon after I got a set of these Arthur cartridges.  I had a little trouble installing because at first I didn't realize that the ink mechanism has both a toner cartridge and a drum.  I removed both together and then tried to insert a toner cartridge, which of course didn't fit.  Then I realized that it was a two part assembly and got the Arthur cartridge inserted and within just a few minutes it was printing perfectly.  I am assuming that the color cartridges will work just as well, but it will be some time before the colors run out.  I was confused by one reviewer who wrote about a cartridge drying up.  Since toner is a dry powder to begin with, I didn't understand this.  I didn't give these 5-stars because I don't know how long they will last.  Also I noticed that my ink monitor program, while it does show the black ink level at full capacity after replacement, it has a question mark over the top of the graphic showing the ink level.  This might indicate that the printer doesn't fully recognize the refill.

title: Seems to work about the same as the full sized BIC correction Tape

I tried these mini ones and after I stopped pressing too hard they seemed to work reasonably well and about the same as the full sized ones.  It did seem that the movement might have been a little less smooth than the full size tapes, but that could be just my perception, since I don't use correction tape a lot.  Sometimes the tape didn't seem to stick as well as I would hope, but just pressing down with a finger took care of that problem.  Was able to write on the tape without any difficulty.  I seem to recall using other brands in the past that were better overall; however, more expensive.  These are not that inexpensive either, but correction tape is generally a little pricey and these are competitively priced.  Next time I would opt for the full sized reels, rather than these mini reels.  BIC products generally work well and I like their pens a lot.

title: Does everything I need; very heavy, but not a large footprint; fast; quiet
text: I am giving this 5-stars with some reservations.  First of, the cons.  The printer is very heavy and I had a hard time getting it out of the box; almost pulled a muscle.  Also had a hard time lifting it up on the table where it will sit.  I am 70 and I can just barely handle 40 pounds of weight; this weighs in at approximately 50 pounds.  If you can't handle 50 pounds and don't have help to lift and place it, don't get this printer.  The other concern I have is how long the toner cartridges might last and I have seen some say they have had problems with the printer reporting toner out before it is, but apparently there are ways to get full use of the cartridges before they are truly out, so it may not be a big deal.  When toner does run out, you'll end up spending about $70 a cartridge, so a replacement of all 4 (3 color and 1 black) will cost you between $200 and $300 depending on where you get the cartridges from.  What I recommend is that if you don't do a lot of color printing, just by a monochrome laser printer and supplement it with a cheap color ink jet.  Of course you have to consider whether or not you have room for two printers and also the cost of ink jet cartridges, which are not cheap either.  Now lets cover the good stuff and why I rated this 5-stars.  The printer is very fast and quiet.  It shoots out black & white pages very rapidly.  Of course color pages take a little longer, which you would expect, but are still reasonably fast.  Color print quality doesn't seem quite as good as some printers from other top printer manufacturers (such as EPSON and Canon), but it is adequate if your color printing requirements are not too precise.  Another thing I really like about Brother printers is that they include a FAX function.  Fax is a feature not as much needed these days, but there are times when it is needed and convenient.  Try to find a non-Brother printer with fax capability; I doubt you will.  The software install went easily and it wasn't too difficult to set up for wireless use.  You can use either USB or wireless.  The software is easy to use, but I did have difficulty trying to configure the printer to scan from the printer panel instead of the computer.  The scanning software on the computer is easy to use and it is easy to figure out how to scan letter or legal (or other sizes) and also not difficult to print on legal size.  For legal printing you do have to open a door on the front and feed the sheets in.  There is no paper tray for legal size, so this is not the ideal printer for printing lots of legal sized pages.  My older monochrome Brother laser could also handle legal scans and printing, but very complicated and difficult to set up.  It is fairly easy with this printer.  Overall, so far, I find this printer to be a big improvement over previous laser printers I have owned.  If I run into any problems later, I will update this review.  Note: I did not try the duplex scan, which seems like a good feature to have.

title: LIFTING HANDLE ON THE SHREDDING HEAD IS A REAL PLUS
text: The best feature of this shredder is that it has a handle to lift off the shredding head so you can easily empty the bin.  I have always struggled removing the shredding heads and have nearly dropped one a few times.  The handle only requires one hand lets you get a good grip on it and makes it so easy.  Shredders are noisy in general, but this one is reasonably quiet.  It has the added feature of a slot for CD/DVD shredding and you can also shred plastic credit cards.  I didn't try shredding 12 sheets that it is supposed to handle.  I noticed that most shredders work a lot better if you don't try to use them at full capacity.  This does seem powerful enough to do 12 pages at once, if you want to do that.  Amazingly this comes with a complete 12 page manual, explaining the features of the shredder, maintenance, trouble shooting and warnings. There is also a separate one page troubleshooting guide.  These days manuals are a rarity, so I think that is a real plus.  Well designed machine.  So what's not to like?  Even though this is a crosscut shredder the pieces are a little bigger than with my prior shredder. It still does an adequate job of shredding, but would have liked to see smaller pieces.  Also, the waste bin is a little small and will require emptying more often than my previous shredder that has a much larger bin.  Overall, this is a great medium duty shredder and I like it a lot.

title: Decent printer, but can be difficult to set up.  Ink is too expensive.
text: Stylish and attractive with a somewhat small footprint and reasonably quiet operation.  It is not really fast printing, but adequate.  Printing starts right away, which was not the case with one printer that I own that takes forever to start printing.  Making a copy is very easy; just put your page face down on the glass and press the copy button.  Unfortunately, there is no sheet feeder for copying or scanning multiple pages, so it is a page at a time.  If you do a lot of page scanning or copying, you need a printer with a sheet feeder, but you will pay a lot more for that convenience.  There is no button on the printer panel to use to scan a document; you have to use software for that.  The driver for the printer, scanning software and manual must be downloaded from a website given in the instructions.  It makes some sense to me not to have the software included, as these things change over time and having it online ensures you get the latest version when you install but that does make a little more difficult for the novice.  Also until you download and check the user's guide, you really don't have a clue on how to scan.  The software installs a program simply called "scanning" on your Windows PC and you run that to scan.  One of the first things I did not like about this printer is that there are only two ink cartridges; one for black and one for color.  I have never liked that because if you run out of just one color, you have to replace the whole color cartridge.  The printer has an "ECO" button you can press that puts out less ink to help you save on ink when you don't need the very best quality, so that's something that can help save on ink.  The ink is a very pricey, so not sure this would be as economical as printers that have 4 or more ink cartridges  This only has color and black and the cartridges shipped with the printer did not last very long..  If you want to use this on USB, rather than wireless, a USB cable is not included, so if you don't have a spare around, you have to buy one.  After you download the software, you have to run it and apparently connect a USB cable initially, even if you are going to use it wireless.  You are given a choice in the install as to whether you want to go wireless or with USB.  On one computer I had trouble with either option; it kept telling me to attach a USB cable that was already attached.  I investigated and found out that the printer was showing up in Windows and I could use it with USB.  As far as wireless, there are two options; either with a WPS button or manual where you enter your router information.  On one computer, neither option worked, even after multiple attempts; I could not get wireless to work at all.  I tried connecting the printer to another computer and both the USB option and the manual setup for wireless worked perfectly on the first try.  I could not get the WPS option to work, even on the second computer.  Since the manual setup worked, I didn't need to.  (If you don't know, WPS is a button you press on your router and then you press a button on the printer within two minutes and it is supposed to connect automatically).  Was going to contact support about the wireless problem, but since I got it working with manual settings on one computer, I didn't call.  If you are not somewhat computer literate, this is not the best printer for you to try to set up; you might struggle with it for a while.  This printer also is supposed to be able to scan remotely with your smartphone with a free app that you can download from the app store, but I did not test that capability, as it seemed to me to be of limited value.

title: SOLID, WELL MADE; SEVERE LIMITATION ON HOW MUCH WEIGHT YOU CAN PUT ON IT; TOO SMALL; PRICEY
text: This is a nice looking desk, but the one I got is a little darker than what it looks like in the picture (more black than brown).  Also, the picture makes it look like one end is narrower than the other.  It's not; it is equal width on both ends.  Easy and fast to assemble.  Comes in three pieces; base, pedestal and top.  Just insert the pedestal into the base and push all the way down.  Then put the top on and push down until it locks in place.  Genius design.  It is ready to use in 10 minutes or less.  Seems quite sturdy and well made, but it supposedly only holds 15 pounds, which is not much.  Has a nice big easy to use lever underneath to raise or lower the desk to the exact height you want.  It goes up high enough to use as a standing desk or low enough to use as a work table.  It might not work quite as well as a computer desk if you are seated, as it is a couple inches too high at the lowest setting; at least for me it was.  It works good as a work table, which is probably how I am going to use it, with thoughts of maybe later using it as a standing desk.  The main problem with this "desk" is that it just isn't quite large enough.  It would be ideal for a laptop, but you couldn't put a desktop computer plus monitor, keyboard and mouse on it; it would be crowded.  Also with the weight limitation of 15 pounds, it probably is too much weight for it to hold.  It works well for a monitor, keyboard, mouse and a little space on the side for paperwork that you might be typing from and not much else.  Your desktop computer needs to be elsewhere on the floor below it, probably.  The desk is not easy to move, as there are no wheels on it.  I knocked off one star on my review for the weight limitation and the price.  This is not a $500 desk.  I think maybe $200-$300 would be a more appropriate price.  Of course you get what you pay for and the base and pedistal are all metal and the top does appear to be solid wood and not pressboard.  For the price though, locking wheels would have been nice, as well as a little larger size and ability to hold more weight.  If you know the limitations of this desk, I don't think you will be disappointed at all, as it is a quality product.

title: Definitely some pros and cons
text:
This envelope making board has its pros and cons. I had purchased the original gray design with white lettering about 4 years ago. Although the print is small, I could read it without any issue at all. Then when I spotted the new pretty blue and white punch board I thought why not. I
use my old one so much that I thought it would be nice to have a much prettier one, ong with a new punch blade to justify my senseless purchase. Big mistake! The pretty new design is extremely difficult to read the tiny print. The background color is blue with white font. I never struggle to read anything, but I do with this.
My suggestion is that if you are also having an issue reading yours, just print the measurements out on a piece of paper to store away with the board.
The other issue I have is that when making the larger envelopes, the board itself is not large enough to accommodate your paper. And I mean for envelopes only like 4x6 or larger. The paper hangs off the board so you can’t score the entire paper. I have made 100+ envelopes of all sizes so it can be done regardless, but sometimes my score lines are off a bit because of this and I end up with a crooked envelope that can’t be fixed. So I end up having to throw the wonky envelope one in my scrap pile for another project.
PROS: Despite all mentioned above, I still find this method far easier that cutting everything by hand, which I did for years before the board.
Initially I thought there was something wrong with the design because all my envelopes came out wrong. I watched a YouTube video and got the hang of it after making 3-4 envelopes and now it’s a breeze and the process is very fast.
My 3 star review is because the new color combination is hard to read for some. And another star dinged because this really needs to be on a larger board platform. Us crafters spend our $ like crazy on our hobby, so why not make a larger version for $10 more. I sure would buy it! Don’t take the reviews seriously that say it
doesn’t work. They just don’t have patience and the willingness to learn something new. Quitters never win :)

This is when your patience is a virtue lol. I hit it once, then waited...nothing happened...hit it again..still nothing, hmm then the on light began to flash ( the pic info was coming thru) and the picture began its printing cycle. It prints one color comes out and is sucked back in for another color. It does this 4times, then the picture comes out, drops on the tray and is done! Easy peasy! Until the second picture began to print because remb, I hit the button twice lol because I didnt wait...I didnt know then, but now I do. The second time I printed a picture I hit the print icon and waited..the picture began its cycle. After all this I can honestly say this is the easiest gadget to set up and use! Since it didnt come with much paper, I ordered more. I compared prices on 4 different sites/stores and they were exactly the same as Amazon, 34.99 for 80 picture papers and 2 ink cartridges...Im guessing 1 cartridge for every 40 pictures...makes each pic cost 43.73 cents per picture, which is a bit more than printing in stores but I think those machines are harder to use so to me, this is def. worth the money. I just started to check on some features on the app for adding to pictures. There are happy birthday banners you can add to the picture before it prints and a lace one, pumpkins etc. It also has holiday things to add too! I bet there are so many more features in the app to enhance the photos that I will find as I get better using it!  In closing as you might have guessed, I love this machine and find it was the easiest thing to learn about! Get one lol

title: A never ending sales pitch and mismanaged basic features, disguised as a printer
text:
I wish that useability was a feature that I could rate separately. Any printer can manage a quality piece of paper so I'm not sure that's a feature I need to rate separately in 2020. The fact is they never stop trying to force Instant Ink on you at every turn is something I'd like to rate. Where is the option to rate how often they shove their subscription service down your throat?

You also cannot actually start any features from the printer directly but you have to go back to where the app is. What this means is you cannot scan things to a location...even though it's connected to the computer via WI-FI. The scan button just tells you it will not work and you need to use the app (why include the button then??) So if you have multiple pages to scan on to your computer you must go to the printer, put the item in the scanner, go back to your computer and initiate the scan, wait for the scan to complete, return back to the printer to add another page. Or you can scan to your phone and then share the documents from your phone to your computer. There is no option to have the printer save a device or file location making this the most inconvenient scanning experience I've had in the past decade. There isn't a multi-page option either. You have to return the computer and let the app know there is another page to be scanned. Selecting scan on the printer using the touchscreen will not just send this next page to the correct place

There is an option to add the smart task app to your printer app (requires an email and password). Smart Task is for...I'm not sure. It allows you to create favorite save locations...provided they are attached to a company that paid to have them listed as storage locations like Dropbox, One Drive, and Evernote. There is no "Smart" option that leads back to your own computer. An option to email the files to a place automatically with the subject line prefilled with "You've got HP Smart app files" though. There was plenty of thought put into THAT during development. There also isn't an option to smartly scan multiple documents. So again, HP has found a way to try and profit multiple times from your purchase of this printer, this time through selling this space inside their Smart Task app to file storage companies rather than making a functional product. I guess I do know what Smart Task is for actually. Ha.

Also, while the touchscreen functions all operations must be handled through the apps HP makes you download sooo........1 star for a feature that is made redundant by their insistence that all functions ONLY initialize from the application.

title: Cute Lanyard
text: This is a cute lanyard. It's also a good quality. My husband and I are taking our niece to Disney. I thought she might like wearing this at the park and start collecting pins. It would also work well for your work ID.

title: Great Looking Poly Bags!
text: These are some great looking poly bags. The designs are fun. They also make your packages stand out. This set comes with 3 different sizes. Each size has a different design. They seem durable. I used one today and the seams didn't bulge or tear. The adhesive strip worked well and secured the flap down. I would recommend these.

title: Nice Bags
text: I do a lot of shipping and I love using poly bags when I can. These are cute! I really like the color scheme. These are smaller bags than I expected because I didn't read the measurements ahead of time, so I probably won't be using these as frequently as larger sizes. The adhesive strip works well. Overall, I am satisfied.

title: Labels
text: This is definitely a good value. You get a lot of labels for a good price. The labels are decent. I didn't have any problems with printing on them. The adhesion seems good. I did find them to be a little difficult to peel off the sheets. Other than that, no problems. This will probably last me a long while.

title: Great Planner!
text: I have been using Happy Planners for the last several years. After trying out different planners for years, I am happy to have found a brand that I like. I like the Big size the best, even though my schedule is pretty light! I used to do crafts such as stamping &  scrapbooking. The Happy Planners allow me to harness that creativity in a small but doable amount. I spend one day each week decorating the next week's layout. Of course I buy lots of their stickers for that job! This planner is gorgeous. It has a calming vibe to it. There's plenty of room for me to put my "to do" lists, activities, and more. I even print out pictures. In fact, sometimes it's more of a memory book than a planner. The planner is durable. One of my favorite features is that you can remove and add pages simply.

title: These Should Last a While!
text: My husband owns a small business that he runs out of the house. Usually once a month he asks me for an envelope. I decided he needed his own stash of them. These are good envelopes and are comparable to what I would get from the store. The adhesion is good. These should last us a while!

title: Excellent!
text: My daughter is in college and almost done. She hasn't been that good with managing her money, so I thought this might help her. I know it could be worse, but I believe that if she doesn't learn some budgeting skills, it will only get worse when she's older. I wish I had something like this when I was younger. Anyway.... this is an excellent kit. It comes with everything you need to help you take control of your spending. Plus, it's by Happy Planner so it's colorful and fun! The quality is very good as I would expect from the brand.

title: Gorgeous Planner!
text: I have been using the Happy Planner for the last few years. I really like the Dashboard layout a lot. This planner theme is gorgeous! I love the flowers. They're so pretty! I have been going back and forth between the Classic and the Big sizes. There are so many more options in the Classic. My favorite thing about these planners is that the pages are easy to remove and rearrange if needed.

title: There's a Learning Curve
text: There's definitely a learning curve to using these adhesive laminating sheets. I recommend doing a trial run before doing the real thing. My daughter had a few things she wanted to laminate. Her items were on cardstock which I think is easier to work with than regular paper because it's less likely to wrinkle during the process. She has been pleased with the results and is now looking for other things that would benefit from lamination.

title: Just as Described
text: I ordered these for business card holders for my husband's business. He goes to a few trade shows each year and has a booth. He's been putting a small stack of his business cards on the table, but they frequently need to be straightened up. These will keep his table looking neater. Since there are 4 of these, he can use one for his sales person, too. They are not much bigger than a standard business card so they won't take up a lot of room. I have no concerns about the quality. These are just as described.

title: A Good Start!
text: This vision board is a good start toward creating your own vision board. There are lots of color, glossy pictures and phrases to use. The board itself uses velcro to attach your items to the included board so you can swap out items as your goals change. The images themselves are attractive. There is some diversity, but the majority of the people are white. The quality of the kit is very good.

title: Sturdier Than Expected
text: My son lives in our basement. He just started his first real job. He was looking for a small file cabinet to keep some work papers in. I saw this and thought it might work. Not only is it perfect for what he needs, it also fills another need he has. He has been wanting a fireproof box for some of his valuable collectible trading cards. This is sturdier than I expected. It will easily accommodate all of his stuff. The top part will work well for the trading cards. It can be entirely separated from the rest of the box. There are a few pockets and storage slots too. He's very happy that it's fire and water proof. Plus, if there was an emergency, the handles make it easy to grab and go.

title: Great Color!
text: I do a lot of shipping. When I can get by with using a poly bag instead of a cardboard box, I do. This color is great! It's vibrant and just like the pictures. The adhesive strip works well. The bags seem sturdy enough for standard use.

title: Great Padded Envelopes!
text: These leopard print padded envelopes are great! The adhesive seal is good. The seams of the bags look fine. It's fun sending packages in printed packaging!

title: Worked Great!
text: These thermal labels worked great! My husband has a Zebra printer. We were able to print out labels with his company logo to use at an upcoming tradeshow. We are very pleased with how they turned out.

title: Just What I Needed
text: These are great bags for packing items. They would work well for handmade gifts. The size is good. The adhesive strip works fine. After ordering these, I was looking at the pictures again and thought maybe they were white on one side, clear on the other. I am happy to say that they are clear on all sides which is what I prefer.

title: Great Assortment!
text: I've been using The Happy Planner for the past few years. I love them! I buy a lot of their stickers. I was so excited to get these. It's a great assortment. They are perfect for my planner. The quality is good and as expected. The pictures and illustrations are lovely! I have had a lot of fun using them !

title: Nice Quality
text: My husband is a software developer and needed a bar code scanner for testing purposes that could scan US driver's licenses. This bar code reader can read that bar code, but that information is missing characters when it is sent back to the computer. He contacted the seller about this issue. The seller replied promptly, but in the end, they weren't able to do anything about this problem. As far as the actual bar code reader goes, it's a nice quality. It scans other bar codes without any difficulties. It's wireless and easy to use. It has a USB charger. The wireless feature can be used with Bluetooth or a keyboard dongle.

title: Family Organization!
text: This is a set of 3 magnetic chore charts. There are spaces for daily and weekly chores. If you want to assign points or money value, there's space for that, too. It also comes with a set of dry erase markers. It's an easy way to keep track of what the kids need to be doing to help out around the house.

title: Just What We Wanted!
text: We're getting ready to move my daughter into a new apartment. We're usually "mostly" careful when moving, but she's taking some nice furniture this time, so we wanted to step up our game. These rolls work well. Dispensing the plastic works as expected. We've been wrapping blankets around the furniture and wrapping the plastic around it to keep the blankets in place.

title: Nice Quality
text: I am a fan of Happy Planner. I have been using their regular planners for several years now. I thought this would be a regular planner, but for teachers. Unfortunately for me, it's a teacher planner - for lesson plans. I already have the larger lesson planner and thought it would be fun to have my personal planner coordinate. I do like the layout. It has horizontal and lined sections for Monday through Friday. It's a nice quality as expected from the brand.

title: Great Layout!
text: I am very happy with the layout of this teacher planner. It has a quick glance yearly calendar in the front. Then it breaks down into monthly sections. Each section starts with a 2 page full month's calendar. After that, there are weekly pages with 5 days per 2 page layout. The days are horizontal and go across both pages. There are 7 divided sections which you could use for each subject or class. The spaces are lined. In the very back are a few checklist pages where you can list the students and assignments or goals. The pages are not flimsy. No marker bleed through. I am very happy with it!!

title: Not the Cheap Kind
text: These plastic page protectors are NOT the cheap, thin kind that rip easily. They are very durable. I use these for my recipes. When I find a new recipe online and print it out, it goes into a page protector and then into a 3 inch binder. These are working great!

title: Nice Cards!
text: It's graduation season! These pop up cards by Hallmark are very nice. However, one out of the 4 cards I received fell apart the first time it was opened. I haven't been able to get the piece back in the right way yet.  These are heavy weight cards, not cheap thin ones. The envelopes are lined with gold paper.

title: Pretty!
text: I love shipping things in poly bags. I try to use them whenever I can. Of course, some items require a box. These are really pretty. They seal well. All the seams are sturdy.

title: Another Great Planner!
text: The Happy Planner planners are the best! This is another great one! I started using them about 4 years ago. They are fun to use. This one has the Dashboard layout. I think this layout is my favorite. The quality of the planner is as expected. The paper is a good thickness and most pen and markers don't bleed through. The illustrations are beautiful. I'm a fan!

title: Quality Stickers
text: These Happy Planner stickers are quality stickers. The theme is "modern wild". They're mostly decorative or accent stickers, but there are a few functional ones. I enjoy switching up my sticker themes every so often, so I have been using these for the past week.

title: Nice To Do Notebook
text: This is a nice to-do notebook. It incorporates your daily to-dos with some wellness trackers. The page thickness is very good. The colorful design is fun. Each day starts with a quote.

title: Works Great!
text: I do a lot of shipping from home and I have my own thermal printer for the labels. I recently ran out of labels, so I ordered these. They work great! I haven't had any problems with them getting stuck in the printer. They print well.

title: Beautiful Planner
text: I'm currently using a big planner by the happy planner company. I wasn't sure I would like the larger size, but I love it! This new planner starts in July, which is perfectly timed with when my current one ends. The quality is excellent and just as I would expect from the brand. I love the plant theme and pastel colors of this new planner. This is a vertical layout whereas the current one I'm using is a dashboard layout. I'm not too picky when it comes to the layout and I can adjust easily to the different ones. I'm very pleased with this planner and can't wait to start using it.

title: Fun Stickers!
text: I have been using the Happy Planner products for several years now. They are my favorite planner items. I just got my first Disney planner so I ordered these stickers to go with it. The sticker quality is excellent and what I expect from the Happy Planner brand. There's a good mix of actual functional stickers such as reminders, events, etc as well as fun illustrations and phrases. My Disney planner doesn't start until July so I am looking forward to getting started with these new stickers.

title: Beautiful planner
text: I've been using planners by the Happy Planner company for several years now. I like how flexible they are. You can easily remove or add pages as needed. This is my first Disney themed planner by them. It's a beautiful planner with lots of gorgeous illustrations and details. This is the vertical style layout. I would consider this to be an academic type of planner since it starts in July and goes through June the following year. I do realize that you pay a little extra for the official Disney licensing. The quality is as expected from the Happy Planner brand

title: Darling!
text: This is a darling edition to my desk. I am a new fan to Rae Dunn products. I can't seem to get enough. This is a unique piece that can hold a cell phone or a pad of post-its. My Google Pixel 4A fits nicely into it. The piece is sturdy and well made. I am very pleased with how this functions and looks in my home office.

title: A great new planner
text: I have been using planners by the happy planner company for several years now. They are definitely my favorite planners. This one is new to me. The twin loop bound is basically a nice fancy way of saying spiral bound. It's not the cheap spiral binding that you would find on a school notebook. It's definitely a nice quality. The planner itself is what I would expect from the company. The layout is a horizontal. There is plenty of room for notes stickers and all that. I was a little concerned because it had a new binding, but when I think about it I don't usually take my pages out and reinsert new ones and you can still insert new pages. Though if you take pages out they will have to be torn out.

title: Good labels
text: These are good labels. They work well in my thermal printer. The quality seems comparable to what I have used before. The adhesiveness is adequate. With 500 labels I should be set for a while.

title: Good Boxes
text: My husband owns a small business. He does have some shipping to do a few times a week. I ordered these boxes to give him another option when it comes to selecting the right size box. There's no sense using a larger box than needed. They are good boxes - nothing fancy. They do the job!

title: Nice Habit Tracker
text: This is a nice habit tracker. What I like about it is that there's only space for five habits at a time. I felt overwhelmed when I tried a habit tracker that had space for twice as much. I think less is best for sure. I also like the layout for this. The other habit tracker had a spiral circle thingy and it was difficult to keep track of which row went with which habit. This one is simple and easy to use. There are also some tips and guidelines which I found useful in the front. On the back of each week there is some pretty artwork. I think this will work much better for me.

title: Works Well!
text: I was using my husband's Zebra printer for shipping items, but he had to use it recently and it didn't make its way back to my office. I decided to see if I could find a thermal printer for my own use. Set up was easy. I was able to pair it with my phone. I did have to download an app, but that's okay. It works very well. It prints out my Poshmark labels easily. I tried to download the app for my Chromebook, but the app doesn't work with Chromebook (yet??). I am hoping that it gets updated soon.  A few labels are included. It even comes with stand to hold the labels. Overall, I am very pleased with it and how easy it is to use.

title: Great!
text: We have been installing hard flooring throughout our house. We didn't want to have to use those ugly mats under our computer chairs, so my husband found out about these types of wheels. They are super easy to put onto the chairs. They glide very easily. They're quite, too. We've been putting these on all of our rolling chairs.

title: Colorful Folders!
text: I don't use plain file folders. I like fun, colorful ones. These are perfect! They quality of the folders is great. They are sturdy and durable. It's much more fun using these than the old manila ones!

title: Nice File Box
text: I have been redoing my home office. I thought this pink file would hold my files well and keep them safe, but also go with my pink and gray color scheme. I was right! It looks great! It's easy to put together. There are handles on the side for carrying. I only wish there was a little window/pocket where I could label the contents. I have not tested the fireproof feature, so I am just going to take their word for it.

title: Rolls Smoothly
text: My husband recently discovered these types of chair wheels so we have been replacing all of our desk chairs with them. These are comparable to the other brands we have tried. They were very easy to install. They roll very smoothly. We love that they are protecting our hard floors!

title: Just What I Wanted!
