This SOUTHWORTH PLANNER (JAN.-DEC.2022) (7" x 9.25", Metallic Black Leopard, Premium Paper, (91458)) is a convenient size--smaller than a sheet of printer paper but larger than a standard notebook planner. When opened, the planner displays a full week at a time.

The planner has plastic tabs for the months. Each month begins with a double page for setting the month’s goals and evaluating the previous month’s achievements. Following each monthly tab is a double-page calendar for the month, which gives you an overview of the month’s appointments, etc.

The monthly calendar is followed by the week-by-week displays. Major holidays are printed on the calendar and weekly pages. There is a double pocket at the back for holding loose notes. The planner also has a convenient elastic band that holds it closed.

title: Attractive Rainbow-Colored Pockets; Durable Plastic Exterior
text:
This CHEPULA EXPANDING FILE FOLDER WITH HANDLE (13 Pockets) works exactly as I expected. I use it to organize medical “after visit summaries” and other medical reports that I print out for my husband and myself.

The exterior is made of hard plastic, so the file is more durable than the standard heavy cardboard expanding file. The interior pockets are rainbow-colored, with tabs that can be labeled as desired.

The interior pockets are made of lightweight, flexible plastic that may not be as durable as the exterior. However, the interior pockets can easily be patched with clear plastic tape if necessary.

title: Dissolvable Labels Won’t Clog Dishwasher
text: These DISSOLVABLE FREEZER LABELS (500 Per Roll; 1x2") are useful for labeling jam or jelly jars, or for labeling containers of food destined for the freezer.  I love that the labels dissolve in water.  (It’s no fun scraping labels off food containers to keep them from clogging the dishwasher.)

title: Superb Rolling Utility Cart
text:
This ORIETA 3 TIERED ROLLING UTILITY CART (Blue) is everything that I’d hoped it would be. It saves a huge amount of floor space in my garage, because a variety of jugs and bottles are now stacked (and organized).

First, the cart is simple to assemble. The box includes both a Phillips screwdriver and a wrench, which are the tools you need. Assembly took less than 30 minutes.

Second, the cart holds an amazing quantity of big laundry detergent bottles and miscellaneous spray cleaners.. The basket heights cannot be adjusted, but the extra tall bottles can go into the top.

Third, the cart is stable and rolls easily, even when fully loaded. I can leave the cart in front of the shelves in my garage, because it is so easy to move out of the way.

Finally, the frame is made of steel, and the baskets are made of a solid plastic-like material. The cart will stand up well to the temperature and humidity changes in my garage.

title: Everything You Want in Large Daily Planner
text:
This SOUTHWORTH 2021 MONTHLY & YEARLY PLANNER (January-December 2021, 8”x 11”, Rustic Floral Wreath, 28 lb Paper (91913)) has everything that you want in a large daily planner. There is (1) a double-page, plastic-tabbed, wall-calendar-style spread for each month; (2) a double-page spread for each week with plenty of room for entering daily appointments or notes; (3) a quick-reference, single-page yearly calendar; (4) a list of 2021 holidays; and (5) a double-sided pocket at the back for holding loose paper slips or notes.

The covers are made of heavy cardboard. This isn’t ideal, because the corners are easily bent. (For attractiveness and durability, I prefer planners that have hard plastic covers, but they are more expensive.) The paper is heavy 28 lb paper that doesn’t bleed through excessively.

The cover comes with an elastic band that holds the planner securely closed. This is NOT my favorite feature, because elastic bands stretch with use, and they are in the way when you want to open the planner quickly. The band can easily be cut off, and the planner will lose no functionality.

The interior design for the weekly spread shows the days in vertical columns, which is a bit unusual. However, the vertical arrangement is very good for showing appointments chronologically, if you have more than one during a single day.

title: Easy to Write With, Don’t Dry Out Quickly
text:
These AMAZONBASICS RETRACTABLE PERMANENT MARKERS (Red, 12 Count) are easy to write with. The hard plastic points aren’t as fine as ball point pen points, but they produce a far finer line than standard chisel point markers.

Surprisingly, the markers don’t dry out quickly, even though the retractable points are NOT capped in any way. The markers suit my needs, which mostly consist of making labels for garage storage boxes, marking dates on plastic freezer bags, and adding shipping instructions to package return boxes

title: Staples 210 Sheets of 20-Pound Printer Paper With Minimal Effort
text:
This AMAZONBASICS EFFORTLESS HEAVY-DUTY STAPLER (210 Sheets) really will staple a block of 210 sheets of 20-pound printer paper with minimal effort. However, it staples cleanly (without bending or distorting the staple) only about 25% of the time. (And of course it’s quite difficult to remove a bent staple that’s gone through 180-plus sheets of paper.)

To some extent, the staples are to blame. The stapler comes with a box of 5/16” staples (the maximum length). These may not be as sharp as they need to be, to staple big blocks of paper. Better quality staples will probably improve the stapler’s performance.

The stapler seems to give the best results when the handle is pressed down with a slow, steady pressure. The staples load through an opening at the rear. You pull on the black plastic that is located just below the screws on the handle--the black plastic is attached to a spring-loaded rod that pushes the staples forward as they’re used.

The staple-pusher mechanism seems a bit flimsy. It’s impossible to say whether this will stand up to regular use. The rest of the stapler is quite sturdy in its construction.

The stapler has a chart attached to the base that tells you which size staples you need for your stapling job, depending on how many sheets you need to staple. The stapler has a strike plate that rotates to properly bend the ends of the shorter staples used for fewer sheets of paper.

title: Close Second to “Pink Pearl” Pencil Eraser
text:
My all-time favorite pencil eraser is the [[ASIN:B004E2S0K2 “Pink Pearl”]], but this AMAZONBASICS PINK ERASER (12 Count) comes in as a close second. The soft pink rubber removes all pencil marks quickly and easily.

If the price is right, the 12-pack is a good deal. However, in my experience all rubber erasers dry out and get hard over time. Thus you don’t want to stock up on more erasers than you can expect to use in a year or so.

The AmazonBasics erasers are packed in a plain, unlined cardboard box.

title: Delightful Pop Up Birthday Card Shows Hogwarts Castle
text:
This HALLMARK SIGNATURE PAPER WONDER POP UP BIRTHDAY CARD (HARRY POTTER) will delight any Harry Potter fan. When you open the card, Hogwarts Castle pops up smoothly, and stays open for display.

The castle is gray, with gold accents on the rocks the castle stands on. The front of the card has a gold border, and the envelope has a gold lining. The moon over the castle shows Harry Potter flying on his broom; at the back of the castle, Hedwig is shown flying home.

title: Quality College-Ruled Notebook With Inspiring Quote, Colored Page Borders
text:
This attractive CHALKBOARD QUOTE NOTEBOOK (“The Future Belongs ...") is suitable for a journal, record-keeping, or personal notes. I love the inspiring cover quote from Eleanor Roosevelt. (“The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams.”) It is the sort of quote that one never tires of.

The pages are college-ruled, and they have colored borders (turquoise, pink, green, and orange). The borders are visible when the notebook is closed, so you can use the colors like section tabs. (You can keep four different types of notes, records, journal, or other entries in this one notebook by color-coding them.)

The notebook has sturdy cardboard covers, and contains 120 pages (30 pages of each color of border). The paper is good quality--when you write with a rollerball pen, there is only a slight bleed-through of ink from one side of the page to the other. The pages are perforated along the spiral binding, for easy and neat removal of single pages.

title: Overpriced, Overpackaged Planner With Decorative Stickers, Colored Pens
text:
This STMT DIY AGENDA SET (by Horizon Group USA; Planner/Organizer/Diary with Debossed & Regular Stickers, Sticky Notes & Glitter Tape. Gel Pens & Paper Clips) consists of a thin spiral notebook with cheap cardboard covers (floral-printed), and cheap filler paper (35 total filler pages). There are three types of filler paper--blank calendar pages (you fill in the dates), wide-ruled pages, and dotted sketch pages.

In addition, there is a small sheet of colored stickers for the months, two small sheets for the alphabet, and two sheets for events (e.g., party, birthday) and reminders (e.g., don’t forget). There are a few embossed lightweight cardboard stickers (star, diamond, flower, etc.). There is a small roll of fuchsia glitter tape. There are four fuchsia-colored paper clips. There are three ballpoint pens (neon orange, neon pink, blue). And there is a small pad of lavender sticky notes shaped like an arrow.

You get all this for a little less than $24 on Amazon! In my opinion, this “agenda set” is grossly overpriced for what it is. The box is a masterpiece of deceptive packaging--it is 2 inches deep, with the thickest item being the notebook (½ inch thick, including the spiral binding). Everything is laid out on a single layer atop a clear plastic insert, and the presentation makes it look like there are many more decorative items than there actually are.

The best thing about this set is that ballpoint pen ink doesn’t bleed through the filler paper pages.

title: Costly “Printer Stand” With Highly Misleading Ad Photos
text:
One star for this IPARTS EXPERT DESKTOP PRINTER STAND (with 4 Rolling Wheels), because of the highly misleading advertising photos on the Amazon product page. This is NOT a wheeled printer stand that you place on the floor next to a desk. Instead, it is a small DESKTOP ORGANIZER STAND with wheels. It is very expensive (about $46 on Amazon) for something you place atop a desk to hold a very small printer and make space underneath.

By adding wheels to this desktop organizer, the seller can photograph it in a way that makes it look like furniture--like a full-size printer stand. In the product page photo, the “plant” alongside the organizer is actually a bunch of flowers in a vase of water. It gives you no idea of the actual size of the organizer.

The price is also in line with the price of a budget-priced printer stand. (Yes, the product page text cautions you to measure your printer before ordering, but that doesn’t excuse the intentionally misleading photos.)

The wheels help create the deception in the photos. Why would anyone want wheels on a DESKTOP organizer? Few desktops have space for rolling anything around, let alone a heavy item like a printer. Should the wheels go past the edge of the desk, they will tip the printer onto the floor. (This is a real possibility, because the wheel locks do NOT prevent the stand from rolling on a smooth surface.)

ASSEMBLY. The organizer stand comes with an alternate set of pads that you can use instead of the wheels. It is easy to assemble, using the included Allen wrench, until you come to the wheels. (On my stand, the holes for the screws were drilled correctly and the screws went in straight.)

The wheels screw into the holes in the metal parts, but you need a slender wrench of the correct size (not included) to accomplish this. The pads can be screwed in by hand. My assembly instructions consisted of a single letter-sized page which said nothing about how to add either the pads or wheels. (I’d suggest putting the wheels with the locks at the front, where you can reach the locks.)

PRINTER SIZE. The organizer will hold an EPSON WF-2530 all-in-one printer, which is advertised as the Epson Workforce printer with the smallest footprint. The organizer is hopelessly too small for my larger Epson and Canon printers, which are the ones heavy enough to benefit from placement on a wheeled printer stand.

See my photos to get some idea of the size of the stand. The letter-sized assembly instructions are shown atop the wooden parts. The big Quaker Oats box (42 oz.) is included for scale. The large hardcover cookbook pretty much covers the lower shelf; the book only fits when laid on its side.

title: Quality “Book” Boxes Work for Stacking, Shelf Storage
text:
Moving goes much, much faster when you pack everything in uniform-sized moving boxes. If you’re paying movers by the hour, the savings can really add up. If you’re moving your stuff yourself, you’ll find it much easier to pack your car, truck, or van when your boxes are all the same size and shape.

These CARDBOARD MOVING BOXES (Medium Size - 16 x 12 x 12 inch Packing Boxes - 25 Boxes Per Pack) are good quality “book” boxes. Because books are heavy--especially hardcover books--you want relatively small boxes for books. The size of the box itself limits the contents to a weight that a strong man or woman can lift.

Even if you aren’t packing books, these medium-sized boxes are an extremely useful size. They hold a lot of stuff, and have a manageable footprint for stacking. I find that they work well when stacked against my garage walls. The boxes are also small enough to fit on the widely spaced steel shelves that I have in my garage.

The boxes are shipped flat, in a very big cardboard box. They do NOT come with tape for assembly. You will need heavy duty shipping tape (e.g., [[ASIN:B073XVQ3GD clear shipping tape]]) or adhesive-backed Kraft paper tape (e.g., [[ASIN:B07K7SYSXN reinforced paper shipping tape]]) to put the boxes together.

I like to use the cheap brown paper tape that comes in rolls--you cut the tape to size, and wet the adhesive with regular water (using a sponge in a saucer of water) to make it stick. You don’t need reinforced tape if you’re only packing items for storage.

title: Slow, But Good for Shredding Junk Mail; Has Tiny Footprint
text:
There are many different AmazonBasics shredders, but what distinguishes this AMAZONBASICS 12-SHEET CROSS-CUT JUNK MAIL, CD, AND CREDIT CARD SHREDDER (with Pullout Basket) is the tiny footprint. The shredder is only 12” wide and 9-1/2” deep, so it easily fits on top of a low bookshelf, credenza, or filing cabinet. It can even fit on a desktop, if you’re a “clean desk” type who doesn’t need much desktop workspace.

The small size comes at a cost, though. The junk-mail shredder is much slower than my wonderful [[ASIN:B00D7H8XB6 AmazonBasics 12-Sheet High-Security Micro-Cut Shredder]]; and the small pull-out basket fills up very, very quickly. The basket is fairly easy to empty into a large wastebasket; but if you overfill it, you’ll have lots of shredded paper bits to clean up.

The cross-cut blades cut the paper into strips that are 3/16” wide and 1” long, which offers pretty good protection from snoops. However, my micro-cut shredder makes strips that are 3/16” wide and 5/8” long, which offers much more security.

The manual doesn’t say how long you can run this junk-mail shredder before it will turn off and require a 45-minute cooldown. Probably it will run for several minutes. In my experience, if you pause frequently between batches of documents, you will never encounter the need for a long cooldown.

I ordered this shredder because I wanted a small shredder dedicated to junk mail, and it fills this need perfectly. However, I won’t be using it for large batches of documents, because it’s too slow. When I have a major shredding task--as when I’m cleaning out file cabinet drawers--I will be using the big micro-cut shredder.

title: Six Filing Surfaces in 2” Expansion File Folders
text:
These AMAZONBASICS CLASSIFICATION FOLDERS (100% Recycled, 2 Dividers, 2" Expansion, Letter, Light Blue, 10 per Box) have 2 dividers, so you get six separate filing surfaces. The front and back covers and each side of each divider has a firmly affixed metal fastener for securing 2-hole-punched documents. The fasteners are designed to work with standard 2-hole punches like this [[ASIN:B000J0B9N8 Swingline model]].

I use these folders for keeping printed-out correspondence and financial reports. The bindings and fasteners are durable enough for all but the heaviest use. Compare these AmazonBasics classification file folders to the slightly higher quality, single-divider [[ASIN:B00094A7YG Smead classification file folders]]. Just bear in mind that the pressboard covers and lighter weight dividers add bulk, if you’re keeping these in a filing cabinet.

title: Appear to Be Standard Tank-Style Permanent Markers
text:
These BIC INTENSITY PERMANENT MARKERS (Tank style, Chisel Tip; Box of 36 Black Markers) don’t seem “special” to me--they seem like standard tank-style permanent markers. When the markers are brand new, the lines drawn by the chisel tips aren’t particularly fine.The chisel tips are firm to begin with, but will soften with use, so the lines will eventually be even less fine.

The product page states that these markers will write on nearly every surface--I have no reason to think that the claim is untrue. In my experience, all tank-style permanent markers write on most surfaces (regardless of the brand). That’s why you have to be extra careful with permanent markers, so you don’t mark clothing, your desktop, or something else that you don’t intend to mark.

BIC is generally a brand that I trust when purchasing pens, dry-erase markers, and permanent markers. I definitely buy BIC products, regardless of price, rather than similar generic products that are offered by unknown manufacturers.

title: Great Stocking Stuffer for Person Who Loves Colorful Bulletin Boards
text:
This POST-IT NOTES LIMITED EDITION SUPER STICKY COLOR COLLECTION (3 in x 3 in, 15 Pads/Pack, 45 Sheets/Pad (654-15Ssall)) is a great stocking stuffer for any person who writes a lot of reminder notes or to-do lists for his/her personal bulletin board. It’s great fun to have colorful notes to brighten up the display!

I don’t think that the set is especially useful for color-coded reminders (e.g., lavender for Mom, red for Dad, orange for kids, etc.), because there aren’t a whole lot of individual notes in each pad. (You get 15 different-colored pads, with 45 notes in each pad.) When you finish with one pad, you’ll have to assign a new color for whatever the used-up pad was color-coded to.

The notes themselves are high-quality sticky notes—exactly what you would expect from the “Post-It” brand. I love these, because I’m an office-supply-store junkie, and generally a sucker for colored pencil/pen sets, and all rainbow-colored office supplies.

title: Beautiful “Frozen” Card for Truly Special Person
text:
If you love the movie “Frozen”, you may want to treat yourself to this HALLMARK SIGNATURE PAPER WONDER FROZEN POP UP CHRISTMAS CARD (Elsa, Feel The Magic). It’s almost too beautiful to give away! It’s a card for a truly special person, and the recipient is sure to treasure it.

The front of the card is covered in white glitter. When you open it, the display with Elsa pops up smoothly. Some of the snowflakes flutter gently with any slight air movement. The rear of the pop up display is also pretty, should you want to set the card atop a filing cabinet, bookcase, or similar room divider.

The non-religious messages--”Feel the magic”, and “May the holiday season warm your heart”--are appropriate for anyone. The card comes with a silver-lined envelope.

The whole card is pale blue, silver, and white. (In my photos, there appear to be some gold tones, but these are just the result of overhead fluorescent lighting.)

title: Bright Sticky Notes Add Color to Your Workspace
text:
These colorful STICKY NOTES (3x3in, Strong Adhesive, 70 Sheets/pad, Pack of 24 Pads) work every bit as well as the yellow name-brand sticky notes. The paper is a little thicker, and the stacked rainbow colors add a decorative touch to your desk, table, or countertop. As message notes, they’re hard for the intended recipient to miss!

Assuming the product is competitively priced (you should always shop around a little on Amazon), these are a good choice for sticky notes. You get 24 pads of 70 sheets each, or 1,680 notes; plus some bonus plastic sticky flags for marking places in books and documents. There are 4 pads of each super-bright color (purple, blue, green, yellow, orange, pink).

title: Really Good Call Blocker for Landlines--Love That Big Red Block Button!
text:
Do I love this PANASONIC CALL BLOCKER (for Landline Phones; with One-Touch Call Block,16,000 Number Block, Bilingual Talking Caller ID (KX-TGA710); Black)? Yes, yes, yes! It adds another arrow to my landline’s robocall-blocking quiver, which already includes the Do Not Call Registry, Nomorobo, and Comcast number blocking.

The three above mentioned services are helpful--especially Nomorobo--but some new unwanted robocalls always slip through the net. The beauty of this Panasonic Call Blocker, is that when you see an unrecognized number on the Caller ID screen, you can hit the big red BLOCK button to immediately disconnect the call and add the number to your blocked call list. This stops your phone’s ringing, and cuts off the caller’s ability to leave a text message or voicemail (which can happen if you simply don’t answer an obviously unwanted call).

With blocked calls, your phone will ring once (like Nomorobo), or even a few times, while the number is being processed. With incoming calls, the phone rings and the Panasonic Call Blocker shows a flashing red light for an unrecognized number, and a flashing green light for a number on the allowed list.

The easiest way to use this call blocker is (1) to hit the Block button when calls are coming in; and/or (2) to later copy numbers from the blocker’s own call list (a list of calls received after you first connect the device) to the Call Blocker’s Block or Allow lists. The program navigation is a bit confusing in places, so keep the instruction booklet nearby.

Nice optional blocking options are (1) block all anonymous calls, (2) block all international calls, and (3) block all 00 prefix calls. I use the latter two, but NOT the anonymous option, because doctors, delivery people, and the like may legitimately hide their numbers when they’re using a personal cell phone for work calls.

If you allow anonymous calls, the Call Blocker records the anonymous callers’ numbers--unlike Comcast, where the anonymous calls show up in call logs that as “private” (with no number, making them unblockable by Comcast). Thus I can add the numbers to my Block list if they’re repeat callers. The Call Blocker also expands the quantity of numbers that I can permanently block well beyond the 25 numbers allowed by Comcast.

Once you’ve blocked or allowed some numbers, your Call List will show a checkmark next to allowed numbers, and a circle with a slash mark next to blocked numbers. The Block list gives you a count of the calls from each number.

The Call Blocker also has a Talking ID option that will announce the number of each incoming call.

NOTE: In testing the device, I tried to block a number (using the Block button) that I’d added to the Allow list, and found that the blocking wouldn’t take effect until I’d manually erased the number from the allowed list. So you may encounter some unexpected behavior from this extremely useful but occasionally confusing device.

title: Low Height, Built-In Rollers Add Versatility to Fully Assembled Metal File Cabinet
text:
This PRO SERIES THREE DRAWER MOBILE PEDESTAL FILE CABINET (Black, 20 inches deep (22283)) is a good choice for a home office, because it stands just 27½” high, and is on rollers. It will fit alongside desks and worktables, and will fit underneath some of them. If placed alongside a desk, the top of the file cabinet can be used as a table or small credenza. The rollers make the cabinet fairly easy to shift for cleaning, or for rearranging the office furniture.

A big plus is that this file cabinet arrives fully assembled. I’ve put together all kinds of furniture (Ikea, Office Depot, Scandinavian Imports, etc.), and the only piece that ever really challenged me was a wooden file cabinet. File cabinets are difficult to assemble, because the hardware for the drawers must be placed exactly right; otherwise the drawers won’t open and close smoothly.

The file cabinet is heavy, but is well constructed. It is an all-metal cabinet.

title: Charming Birthday Card Is Treat for Pop Up Card Lover
text:
This HALLMARK PAPER WONDER POP UP BIRTHDAY CARD (GET CARRIED AWAY) is charming. I love pop up cards, so I really like the doggie’s hanging from the balloons at the center of the card when you open the card. Also, the doggie and the balloons are mounted on bits of foam on the front of the card, which provides another kind of interesting 3D effect.

The card comes wrapped in a cellophane envelope that keeps it pristine until you present it. The colorful card has a bright yellow envelope. It’s beautifully printed on quality paper, just as you would expect from the Hallmark greeting card company.

title: Pale Gold-Toned Ink Nearly Vanishes in Artificial Light
text:
I love the cover design and layout of this compact ASHLEY G FOR BLUE SKY 2019-2020 ACADEMIC YEAR WEEKLY & MONTHLY PLANNER (Flexible Cover, Twin-Wire Binding, 5" x 8", Painterly Stripe). However, I hate that the inside pages are printed with gold-toned ink that nearly disappears in indoor artificial light.

The pale ink makes it hard to quickly read the dates on the tabbed two-page calendar spreads. On the weekly pages, you have to look closely to see the date and day of the week, and the dotted lines that substitute for solid-ruled lines in the daily spaces practically vanish.

This design is impractical for a school-year diary of important dates, regardless of whether you are a student or a teacher/professor. It’s just too easy to write events down on the wrong calendar day or weekday. The elegant design is nice, but it’s inappropriate for an academic planner.

title: Too Wide to Fit Desk’s Hanging File Drawer, Lateral File Cabinet Drawers
text:
This C-LINE 13-POCKET EXPANDING FILE WITH HANGING TABS (Bright Blue, 8-1/2" x 11" (58215)) is a nice, durable, plastic expansion file. However, it is ⅜” wider than a standard Pendaflex hanging folder (the paper portion) so it doesn’t fit in my desk’s hanging file drawer, or in my lateral file cabinet drawers. (It is 12⅛” wide, which is wider than the space between the hanging file support rods.)

The idea is clever. The expanding file has four pull-out plastic tabs at the top, so that you can store it as a hanging file, but pull it out and use it (with the tabs pushed in, out of the way) at your desk like a regular expansion file. Unfortunately, the good idea is badly executed.

title: Fast, Portable Battery-Operated Sharpeners Don’t Tie Up Electrical Outlet
text:
These OFFICE1ST BATTERY OPERATED PENCIL SHARPENERS (2 Pack, Double Blade Design) don’t make as nice a point as my electric pencil sharpener, but they’re just as fast, and they don’t tie up a precious electrical outlet. (The electric pencil sharpener makes a longer, more tapered point.)

The pencil sharpeners are totally portable, and have a tiny footprint. They have a window compartment that holds a lot of shavings. The compartment is easy to empty, with just a twist. The compartment doesn’t jar loose and dump its contents unexpectedly.

The sharpeners run on two AA batteries; and four batteries are included with the two sharpeners. Each sharpener comes with an extra blade packed inside the shavings chamber.

title: Pretty, Well-Laid-Out Planner; No Plastic-Reinforced Monthly Tabs, No Plastic Pocket
text:
This AT-A-GLANCE 2019 WEEKLY & MONTHLY PLANNER (8-1/2" x 11", Large, Recycled, Watercolors, (791-905G)) has ALMOST everything that I want in a daily planner. It’s laid out and ruled perfectly--with unruled two-page, full-month calendars, and ruled daily entry spaces in the two-page weekly spreads.

However, it has printed tabs for the months, instead of the jutting-out, plastic-coated tabs that I’ve come to like in my large At-a-Glance desk planners. Also, it is missing the plastic pocket at the front that I’ve come to rely on to hold sheets of small custom-printed labels.

My printed adhesive labels have checkboxes for repeated tasks that I track--I add the labels as needed to the day spaces on the planner’s weekly spreads. (For a planner with plastic tabs and a plastic pocket, see, e.g., [[ASIN:B07DFT7MYV At-a-Glance Planner, Paige]]).

This planner costs a few dollars less than planners with the plastic features, so it’s a good choice if you don’t care about sturdy month tabs and a plastic pocket. It’s a very pretty planner, with its subdued butterfly theme.

title: Excellent Dry-Erase Calendar Board With Magnetic Marker Pen, Magnets, Self-Stick Mounts
text:
This QUARTET MAGNETIC DRY ERASE CALENDAR BOARD (16" x 20", Aluminum Frame (63537)) is lightweight, and easy to mount on any wall with the included self-stick mounts. The mounts hold the calendar very securely, and won’t damage the wall (no nail holes).

Magnetic dry erase boards are the best, because you can post extra notes anywhere on them with magnets. (This board includes two round magnets.) Also, a magnetic board holds your magnetic dry erase marker pens right on the board, so you always have something at hand to write with. (This board includes one black magnetic marker pen with a fine point and a felt eraser.)

Quartet magnetic marker pens are available in a variety of colors. The pens have narrow barrels, but they hold a LOT of dry-erase ink! Most dry erase markers will work with this calendar board, but in my experience Quartet markers are the best for all kinds of dry erase boards (magnetic or plain, all brands). Quartet markers write with bold ink that is easy to see and read, regardless of whether the writing is broad or fine.

The calendar board erases cleanly, use after use, with no more than the felt tip on the included pen. Occasionally, when normal erasing leaves ink bits behind, the board can be wiped off with a damp tissue or paper towel.

The calendar board is a very good size for use as an appointment calendar. There is plenty of room in the date boxes for noting important upcoming appointments or to-dos. I like the fact that the months are listed at the top of this calendar board, so that you can check or circle the month you’re tracking.

title: Versatile, Space-Saving Countertop Organizer
text:
This AMAZONBASICS PIVOTING TRAY ORGANIZER is a remarkable space saver, although it won’t win any home decor design awards. (When you pivot the trays outward, they hang slightly unevenly.) The organizer clears up a lot of clutter from my bathroom countertop, holding small tubes, nail scissors, dental floss, etc. within easy reach.

The organizer consists of three separate trays (5” interior diameter; 1½” deep) with conical posts that allow the trays to stack. If you want to pick up the whole organizer, you must grasp the lowest tray, because the trays don’t snap together in any way. However, the fact that the trays are loose means you can lift off a tray or rearrange the stack at any time.

The organizer has a footprint that is very similar to the footprint of a big round Quaker Oats box (42 oz.).

title: Excellent Large-Sized Weekly/Monthly Planner
text:
This BLUE SKY 2019 WEEKLY & MONTHLY PLANNER (Flexible Cover, Twin-Wire Binding, 8.5" x 11", Geometric Triangles) is an excellent large (business-letter-sized) planner. The spaces for daily entries are unlined, and stretch across the full width of the page, so you can enter a lot of appointments and/or notes! The missing lines actually make the spaces very flexible for practical use. You can even add diagrams or doodles.

The two-page monthly calendars and weekly spreads lie completely flat when opened. The paper is good quality--it doesn’t allow bleed-through from ballpoint or gel pen ink.

The months are separated by pages with plastic-reinforced tabs. The daily spaces on the weekly spreads have the specific dates (e.g., 5, 31) and days of the week (e.g., Friday). Holidays are entered on both the calendars and the daily spaces. The weekly spreads also have a small space for weekly to-dos and notes.

Extras include plastic-reinforced front and back pages. These have brief reference calendars for 2019 & 2020, charts of dates for holidays in 2019 thru 2022, and a map of the continental United States with state capitals and time zones. The pink/fuchsia/blue/gray/marble/metallic cover and page decoration is subtle and easy to live with for an entire year.

title: Ideal Handbook-Sized Weekly/Monthly Planner
text:
This BLUE SKY 2019 WEEKLY & MONTHLY PLANNER (Flexible Cover, Twin-Wire Binding, 5" x 8", Grenada) is an ideal small (handbook-sized) planner. The two-page monthly calendars and weekly spreads lie completely flat when opened, and the paper is good quality that doesn’t allow bleed-through from ballpoint or gel pen ink.

The months are separated by pages with plastic-reinforced tabs. The daily spaces on the weekly spreads have the specific dates (e.g., 1, 21) and days of the week (e.g., Tuesday), and have adequate lines of space for your diary entries. The weekly spreads also have a small space for weekly to-dos and notes.

Extras include plastic-reinforced front and back pages. These have brief reference calendars for 2019 & 2020, charts of dates for holidays in 2019 thru 2022, and a map of the continental United States with state capitals and time zones.

title: Easier to Use Than Electronic Tracker
text:
This BLUE SKY WEEKLY & MONTHLY FITNESS PLANNER (Flexible Cover, Twin Wire Binding, 5" x 8", Hustle Hard (110936)) is a well-designed, compact fitness planner that’s the right size to slip into a gym bag. It has a two-page calendar spread for each month; you can use the big calendar for keeping track of your most important appointments or events during the month. The monthly calendar spreads include small reference calendars for the previous and following months.

The calendar spread is followed by two-page spreads for each week. In the weekly spreads, the daily pages have spaces to record meals, to check off the glasses of water you’ve drunk, to check off the types of workouts you’ve completed each day, and to describe or note down things about your workouts. The weekly spreads also have space to enter your weekly goals: (1) things you need to do less often, (2) things you need to do more often, and (3) things you need to learn and test.

The months are separated by pages with plastic-reinforced tabs. The tabs have the abbreviated names of the months. The tab pages themselves have motivating phrases (e.g., for February, “Be stronger than your excuses”). At the end of each month there is a “Monthly Check-In” page for recording your measurements, and your progress towards achieving your goals. There is also at least one page for notes at the end of each month.

At the end, there is a page listing the dates of holidays for 2019-2022. There is also a map of the continental United States, with state capitals and time zones.

This book is easier to use than an electronic tracker, because it doesn’t require typing or locating correct display screens in order to record information.

title: Rounded-Tip Markers Write Smoothly, Effortlessly on Mirror, Metal Whiteboard
text:
These QUARTET GLASS WHITEBOARD DRY ERASE MARKERS (Bullet Tip, Premium, Assorted Colors, 12 Pack (79554)) write incredibly smoothly, thanks to the rounded bullet tips. The colors are intense, so that your writing can easily be read from several feet away. The points make fine lines so that your words are effortlessly legible.

I tested these on a mirror, where they wrote silently (no squeaking!). They also performed beautifully with my metal whiteboard wall calendar. The markers erased very easily from both surfaces.

title: Hard-to-See, Pale Colors; Clumsy to Write With
text:
These KINGART DRY ERASE MARKER PENS (945-36; 36 Chisel Tip Non-Toxic Pens in 12 Colors) were disappointing to me in three ways: (1) the colors are very pale when applied to my cheap metal whiteboard calendar, (2) the fine edge of the tip doesn’t apply color evenly and the wide edge is clumsy to write with, and (3) the package has 3 sets of the same 12 colors (as stated in the description, but I stupidly expected 36 colors).

These dry erase markers may work better with other whiteboards. From experience, I know that different marker brands work better or worse with specific whiteboards. (I own whiteboards from several different manufacturers.) However, I’m disinclined to use these dry erase markers on the wall calendar as intended, because the markings can’t be read clearly from a few feet away. (Unlike the markings from the black Quartet markers that I’ve been using for date numbers and appointments; in photo, see black numbers and "Darlene".)

The 36 markers come in a clear, flexible-plastic retail box that can be retained for storage. They erase very easily.

title: Blue Inserts Leave Fine Scratches on Whiteboard
text:
In my experience, Quartet makes the very best whiteboard markers and products, but it missed the mark with this QUARTET WHITEBOARD/DRY ERASE BOARD ERASER (6" x 2-3/8", (DFEB5)). The big eraser has a hard felt surface with two blue “scratchee” inserts that extend above the felt surface by about ¼”. Unfortunately, the inserts leave behind very fine scratches on the surface of my cheap magnetic whiteboard calendar.

I solved the problem by pulling the blue inserts out of the eraser. I can still use the eraser, and it stays handy in the excellent magnetic eraser holder that comes with it. The magnetic holder sticks very firmly to the wall calendar, and it doesn’t slide anywhere.

title: Elegant Spiral-Bound Journal With Good Paper, Golden Page Edges
text:
This HALLMARK SIGNATURE GOLD SPIRAL NOTEBOOK (Gold Diamonds) is a simple spiral bound notebook filled with college-ruled pages that have a place (at the top right) for writing in a date. What makes it special is the gold gilt applied to the page edges--when the notebook is closed, the diamond-design covers and the pages between them all shine with gold.

This elegant notebook is perfect for a personal journal, because its size (6” x 8”) makes it easy to slip into a large handbag. It’s also a good choice for a record book that keeps track of additions to a prized collection.

The paper is thick enough to keep ball point pen ink from bleeding through, so you can write on both sides of every page. (The pages even stand up fairly well to writing with a Sharpie permanent black marker, though of course this ink bleeds through to some extent.)

title: Permanent Markers Write in Beautiful But Muted Metallic Colors
text:
These SHARPIE METALLIC PERMANENT MARKERS (Fine Point, Assorted Colors, 4-Count (2029674)) write in beautiful metallic green, red, silver, and gold. They’re intended for writing on dark surfaces, such as the solid-colored envelopes that come with many Christmas or birthday cards. The markers work on white backgrounds, of course, but the metallic shine is harder to see against a light background.

The markers come in muted metallic colors that resemble the metallic colors of cell phone cases. These are permanent markers, with ink that lasts in the same way that the ink in other Sharpie permanent markers lasts--it’s permanent, but will fade over time, especially if applied to plastic or other nonporous surfaces.

title: Box of 50,000 Non-Jamming Staples
text:
These AMAZONBASICS STANDARD STAPLES (5000 per Pack,10-Pack) should keep a small office (10 persons) supplied with staples for at least a year (unless everyone does a LOT of stapling!). The staples are packed in 10 individual boxes, each box containing 24 full-length strips (5000 staples per box).

Stapling with these staples requires a little more force than stapling with my favorite [[ASIN:B00006IFM9 Swingline S.F.4 Speedpoint Staples]]. However, the AmazonBasics staples feed smoothly, without jamming the stapler. This 50,000-staple package will keep my household in staples for a long, long time.

title: Water Beads Up on Pages; Write on Wet Pages With Pencil
text:
This RITE IN THE RAIN ALL-WEATHER WEEKLY PLANNER (Undated, Side-Spiral 4-5/8" x 7" (No. P52)) performs as advertised. Water beads up on the pages, and the pages dry out quickly. You can write on wet pages with a pencil (but not with a ballpoint or permanent marker pen). You can also write on wet pages with a Rite in the Rain All-Weather Pen (not included with the planner).

The undated weekly planner is as “plain vanilla” as a planner can be. Each week has a 2-page spread with divided spaces for 7 days and notes. You indicate the months by checking boxes at the right-hand margin, and fill in the dates in boxes next to the days of the week. The first page has a form for filling in your name, address, etc. The last page has a list of major holidays.

If you really need a waterproof planner, you should probably invest in an all-weather pen to go with the planner. If you write in pencil on a wet page, it’s possible to erase the marks after the page dries.

title: Purple Background, Stylized Flowers Resemble Monet Painting
text:
This HALLMARK BIRTHDAY CARD (FLORAL DESIGN) is a simple, but very pretty, birthday card. I like the purple background and the stylized flowers, which make me think of a Monet painting. The front says “happy birthday”; the inside message is “and many, many more!”.

The price (about $5 on Amazon) is reasonable. Unfortunately, my card was slightly bent on arrival, because it was delivered in a padded envelope (no cardboard backing).

title: Elegant, Beautiful, Hand-Made Cards Have Applied  “Gems”
text:
These PAPYRUS GEM CHRISTMAS TREE CHRISTMAS CARDS (Boxed with Gold Foil-Lined Red Envelopes, Gold Foil Seals; 8-Count) are hand-made--you can tell because each card varies slightly in the placement of the tree decorations. The colorful plastic 3D “gems” gently glow, and the glitter areas (especially at the tree base) sparkle like gold. These cards are standouts.

The red envelopes are lined with gold foil, and there are 8 gold hummingbird seals to decorate the envelope flaps. The message inside is “Celebrate the season and have a very merry Christmas”. There is room on the back of the message insert to write a short note if desired. Every detail of these cards is so carefully thought out, to make it all "just so".

Papyrus products are more expensive than Hallmark or American Greetings products, but I really love the elegant Papyrus designs. I think they're worth the extra cost whenever you want a really special card or gift wrap for someone.

title: Fun Set of Permanent Marker Pens in Different Colors
text:
Who doesn’t love colored pen and pencil sets? These SHARPIE PERMANENT MARKERS, AARON JUDGE SPECIAL EDITION (Fine Point, Assorted Colors, 24 Count) are fun to look at, and fun to draw or mark with. Just remember that these are PERMANENT markers--if you get the ink on your clothing or a desktop, it won’t come out.

I use these for labeling file folders, storage tubs, and cardboard boxes. They aren’t good for coloring books, because the colors bleed through the thin paper. The colors often bleed through coated papers, too (as in Post-Its or file folders).

Happily, my set of “Aaron Judge” Sharpies didn’t have any dried out markers. (Markers do dry out, though, so don’t expect them to last forever--even if they’re unopened.) Unhappily, my set had only 23 different colors. There were two bright blue markers, instead of one bright blue and one bright green marker.

The Sharpie Uncap the Possibilities prize sweepstakes offer that comes with the “Aaron Judge” set appears to be open through March 31, 2019.

title: Powerful 45-Sheet Electric Stapler Is a Beast!
text:
This SWINGLINE SPEED PRO 45 ELECTRIC STAPLER (45 Sheets, Black (S7042155)) is a beast! It staples with so much force, it needs suction cups (on the bottom) to hold it down on a tabletop. Fortunately, there’s no way that I can see to staple a finger--the opening is 45 paper sheets high, and that’s it.

Because it’s so forceful, it’s noisy. However, it’s a godsend to a busy person who must staple big stacks of documents. The stapler has a sensor that tells it when paper is inserted for stapling, so there’s no need to press down on the stapler or to touch it to complete the stapling task. You insert the paper all the way, and Bang! the machine staples the papers.

The stapler works with both regular and high capacity staples. (A box of each type is included with the stapler.) A button at the back releases the stapler magazine, and then you pull it straight out to load the staples. (Pulling the magazine out takes a strong pull the first time you do it.)

I tested the stapler with 45 sheets of 20-lb. Hewlett-Packard multipurpose paper, and it performed beautifully.

SAFETY NOTE: Always follow the direction in the instructions, and unplug the stapler before reloading staples or clearing jams.

title: AmazonBasics Accordion-Style Sticky Notes Work Same as Similar Name Brand Sticky Notes
text:
These AMAZONBASICS STICKY NOTES FOR DISPENSERS (3" x 3", Yellow, 12-Pack) work exactly like the accordion-style Post-It notes. In both cases, the accordion-style 3” x 3” sticky notes perform exactly the same as regular sticky notes.

The advantage of using dispenser-style sticky notes is that the dispensers serve up the notes one at a time (just like pop-up facial tissue boxes). Dispensers are available in many styles, to either complement or jazz up your workspace.

title: Works as Standalone, or With Keynote, Powerpoint
text:
This CANON PR-500-R WIRELESS PRESENTER has a USB-port dongle that’s pre-programmed to work with Keynote or Powerpoint when plugged into a Mac or PC. With the dongle plugged in, the clicker buttons advance the slides, and the pointer button activates the bright red laser dot. The device allows the person doing the presentation to walk away from the podium. The dongle fits unobtrusively into a storage dock at the lower end of the device, so it isn’t easy to lose.

The presenter device also works as a standalone laser pointer (which is how I use it). After you insert the AAA alkaline batteries (included), you slide the power button to either Keynote or Powerpoint, and the pointer button will then activate the pointer.

A nice feature is the battery life indicator, which shows for only a few seconds—in green when the batteries are full, in orange when the batteries are partly discharged, and in flashing red when the batteries are almost empty. The device is very comfortable to hold in your hand. A black velveteen drawstring carrying case is also included.

title: Well-Designed Weekly Planner Starts With July 2018, Has Pinky-Beige Pages
text:
This AT-A-GLANCE 2018-2019 ACADEMIC YEAR WEEKLY & MONTHLY PLANNER (Large, 8-1/2 x 11, “Garden Party” (150-905A)) is strictly for the current academic year. It runs from July 2018 through June 2019, with NO bonus pages to take you to the end of 2019.

The planner has the mix of daily diary pages that really works for me. There are tabbed 2-page spreads in calendar format for every month, and 2-page spreads for every week with plenty of lines for writing down appointments, etc. There are small year-at-a-glance calendars (2018, 2019, 2020) printed at the front. Holidays are shown on the monthly spreads, but NOT on the weekly spreads.

Note that the pages of this planner are NOT white, but a sort of pinky-beige. This may be easier on the eyes, but makes the dates and days a little harder to read than I like. (There are many similar At-a-Glance planners available with white pages.)

I’ve used these big planners with letter-sized pages for a few years now. I note down tasks/appointments that I need to complete each day, and check them off when they’re done. That way I have a record of when I last fertilized the garden plants, serviced the car, etc.

At-a-Glance makes little improvements in these planners in most years. This one has a new plastic pocket (double-sided) for holding note slips, letters, clippings, etc. It also has new paper that resists ink bleed from ballpoints and gel pens.

title: “Printing” Is Limited to LCD Display; Manual Uses Miniscule Type
text:
This SHARP EL-1901 PAPERLESS PRINTING CALCULATOR (with Check and Correct, 12-Digit LCD) is a powerful, versatile desk calculator, but using it isn’t at all intuitive. For me, the learning curve was quite steep, because I needed a strong magnifying glass to comfortably read the accompanying Manual.

You must read the manual to understand the button sequences required for different types of calculations; yet the Manual is printed in positively miniscule type. (The online Manual available at Sharp’s website is exactly the same as the two-sheet, double-sided Manual that comes with the calculator. I will need to use a copier to enlarge sections of this Manual for regular reference.)

The key to using the calculator is the C/CE key, which gets you out of whatever special mode (e.g., Correct, GT) you may have landed in. It’s also good to know that the scroll buttons put you into Check mode, and the Correct button puts you into a submode of Check. Getting totals or performing computations may require use of both the = button and the * button.

In short, this is a calculator intended for a regular, heavy user—someone who won’t forget the correct button sequences. It’s very easy to get erroneous calculations if you don’t know exactly what you’re doing.

Probably the thing that I dislike most about this calculator is that it’s advertised as a “printing” calculator. The only “printing” that you get is the readout on the upper LCD screen. The readout is nice—you can check your list of entries, and correct any that have errors without having to re-enter the full list. However, there is no way to get a paper printout of the list. The calculator does NOT have a USB cable port or wireless capability that would enable printing from a computer’s printer, so the calculator doesn’t do traditional paper-and-ink printing.

title: THE Solution to Managing Printed Internet Recipes!
text:
Wow! These CHARLES LEONARD MAGNETIC POCKETS (9½”W x 11¾”H, 4 Assorted Colors, 4 Pack (26400)) are fabulous! They hold a fairly thick sheaf of 8½” x 11” papers, and they stay firmly attached to metal surfaces like filing cabinets or a refrigerator door.

These are the perfect solution to managing the recipes that my family likes that are printed from the Internet. I’ve been using a magnetic clip to hold the loose recipe sheets on the refrigerator door, but it’s hard to unclip a bundle of pages without dropping some on the floor.

These pockets hold the pages securely at the bottom and sides, so I can flip through the page titles at the top, and pull out just the single recipe that I want. Then I can shift the selected recipe to the front of the pocket, and read it through the clear plastic pocket front. The pocket even keeps the recipe page clean. How cool is that?

Being a sucker for “storage solutions” (and office supply store items of all kinds), I’ve tried magnet-backed plastic pockets before, and always found them wanting. You have to be careful not to overload them, or they will fall off. Or if you overload them just a little, they will cunningly take their time, and slide ever so slowly down to the floor.

But these magnetic pockets are different! The back of each pocket is an entire sheet of that flexible plastic magnet material frequently used for holding things on magnetic whiteboards or metal copy holders. The full sheet has a LOT of holding power, and attaches like a limpet to all magnetic or metal surfaces. I love these pockets, because they’re fairly inexpensive (about $14 for a pack of four on Amazon), and they really, really work!

title: Works to Re-Attach Air Fresheners to Garbage Cans
text:
This SAUNDERS UHU TAC HOME DECO REUSABLE PUTTY (2.1 oz (60g), 32 pads (48710)) is useful to have on hand for attaching lightweight items to all sorts of surfaces. It’s definitely reusable, and it comes off smooth surfaces without leaving marks. (I’d recommend testing it in an unobtrusive area before using it on a painted wall, but would expect it to come off without pulling off a layer of paint.)

My favorite use is for re-attaching [[ASIN:B00AN5L8FS Air Wick Stick-Ups]] to the inside of my garbage can. I have to remove the Stick-Ups when I roll the can to the curb for pickup, or they’ll fall out with the trash when the can is emptied. This reusable putty makes it easy to pull them off and stick them back on.

The main key to success is to use enough putty pads to handle the weight of your object. This UHU TAC product is intended to hold items up to 4.4 lbs. “under optimal conditions”. For slightly heavier objects, try [[ASIN:B0085T0G2K UHU TAC PROPOWER]].

title: Brilliant Colors Are Great for Shippers’ Warning Labels
text:
With these AVERY ASTROBRIGHTS COLOR EASY PEEL RECTANGLE LABELS (2" x 2-5/8" (4331)), you get bright-colored labels in five brilliant, eye-catching colors (2 sheets of each color). The colors are Pulsar Pink, Cosmic Orange, Solar Yellow, Terra Green, and Lunar Blue. You can print or write anything you want on them. You can also cut them into small, decorative shapes.

Scrapbooking and papercrafts projects are obvious uses, but I use mine for can’t-miss-seeing-it shipping warnings (e.g., “Fragile”, or “Heavy”). I also use them for labeling closet and garage storage boxes with their contents.

title: Stretchy Standard-Length Bands at Great Price
text:
These AMAZONBASICS RUBBER BANDS, SIZE 33 (3-1/2" x 1/8'') (600 Bands/1 lb. Pack, 3-Pack) are stretchier than my #33 rubber bands from Staples, so I often need to “double” them around the things that I’m banding together. This isn’t a problem, except for the extra motion involved if I’m banding up lots of stuff. The AmazonBasics price is great—about $11 for 3 lbs. (Staples price is about $8 for 1 lb.).

Size 33 is the standard size used for everyday office use. Just remember that all rubber bands deteriorate over time—they begin to dry out when the package is opened and they’re exposed to air—so you don’t want to stock up beyond your immediate regular needs. Also, if your banded items will be going into a filing cabinet or otherwise stored, it’s better to use metal clips.

title: Inktank Printer Was Dream to Set Up
text:
This EPSON WORKFORCE ET-4750 ECOTANK WIRELESS ALL-IN-ONE PRINTER was a dream to set up. Filling the huge ink tanks—which is simple but requires a 10-minute wait during ink-charging—was probably the hardest part.

The all-in-one ET-4750 was ready to send faxes once it was plugged into a telephone jack. It was ready to print from all my devices (desktop PC, iPad Air 2, Galaxy S8+) as soon as it was added to my home network. (The mobile devices already had Epson iPrint installed.)

The only fiddly thing was the scanner. For wireless scanning to a computer, you must set up your computer with either (1) the Epson Event Manager and Epson Scan2, or (2) the Windows WDS app. To scan to the Cloud, you must set up an Epson Connect account and then name a Cloud destination (e.g., Google Drive). Setting up Cloud scanning is very simple.

With my previous Epson Workforce 645 printer, I bypassed all the fiddly scanner stuff by scanning to an inserted memory card and then walking the memory card over to my desktop PC’s card reader. Unfortunately, the ET-4750 does NOT have a slot for inserting a memory card. This missing feature is the only thing I do NOT like about the ET-4750.

The ET-4750 has a sensitive touchscreen that you can use for everything from copier settings, to manual wireless connections, to creating fax headers, to fine-tuning the printer nozzle alignment. It has a very small footprint for a 250-sheet capacity printer with ADF. Like other wireless Epson printers, the ET-4750 can be assigned an email address, so that it prints from emails. It can also be set up with a wired Ethernet connection.

I really love this printer. It prints beautifully, and it won’t need more ink for 5-6 months or more. It also comes with a full second set of ink bottles, so I won’t be ordering ink for a good long time.

title: Cadillac of Printer Papers (Package Contains ½ Ream)
text:
This HP PREMIUM CHOICE LASERJET PRINTER PAPER (32lb, 8.5 x 11-inch Letter, 250 Sheets /1 Pack, (113500)) is truly the Cadillac of printer papers. It's heavy (32 lb., not the usual 20 lb.); takes ink beautifully (even with my plebian inkjet printers); provides an ultra-clear white ground; and feeds flawlessly.

As the wrapper says, this is the paper to use for a presentation that looks commercially printed. Note that this is a one-half ream package (250 sheets).

In my photo, the Premium Choice Laserjet paper is on the right. (The paper on the left is 20 lb. HP Multipurpose). The images are printed with an inkjet printer. With the HP Premium Choice paper, the colors are a little deeper, and the background is a clearer white.

title: Double-Sided Gelatinous Tape Bonds Permanently to Mounting Surface
text:
This T-REX STRONG AND CLEAR DOUBLE SIDED MOUNTING TAPE (All Weather, 1 Inch x 60 Inches, 1 Roll (285338)) is like glue dots on steroids! The double-sided, gelatinous tape is about ⅛” thick. It's clear, but looks red on the roll because one adhesive side is covered with a red plastic liner.

The tape is easy to use for wall-mounting objects that are no thicker than ¾”. You cut a length of tape; firmly press the tape horizontally to the back of the object; remove the liner from the tape; and press the object to the mounting surface, holding the object in place for 30 seconds. You should use 4” of tape to hold 2 lbs. of weight, so 30 lbs. requires 60” (a full roll) of tape.

This tape is NOT repositionable--the mounting is permanent. Removal of the tape will damage most mounting surfaces. This tape is NOT recommended for use on wallpaper or delicate, uneven surfaces.

title: 17-Month Planner Offers Good Value
text:
This ORANGE CIRCLE STUDIO 17-MONTH 2018 EXTRA LARGE FLEXI PLANNER (Bold Blossoms) offers good value for the money (about $18 on Amazon), because it covers a full 17 months (September 2017 through December 2018). I use planners like this to write down appointments and other time-consuming tasks completed each day. That way I don't have to wonder “Where did the day go?” when I’ve been busy all day, but don't seem to have anything to show for it.

At the front, this planner has seventeen 2-page, wall-calendar-like spreads for the months, so you can see your upcoming appointments and commitments at a glance. Following these are week-by-week, single-page spreads that have room for daily details. (These weekly pages are the ones I use for recording completed tasks.)

At the back is a page of stickers you can use to liven up your planner pages. There is a page of holidays included as well. The back cover has a handy pocket for notes, appointment cards, and the like. The front cover is clear heavy plastic that lets the “Bold Blossoms” cover show through while ensuring the durability of the planner over 17 months.

title: Count on Avery for Help With Designing Custom Labels (That Really Stick)
text:
You can always count on Avery labels to stick and stay stuck! This packet of AVERY GLOSSY CLEAR FULL-SHEET STICKER PROJECT PAPER (4397) contains 7 adhesive-backed sheets (8-½” x 11”) of clear plastic that is suitable for either laser or inkjet printing. You can print anything you want on the plastic--either a batch of small labels, or one big, letter-sized label. The clear labels look great on glass bottles, mirrors, or any backgrounds that contrast with the ink colors used for the printing.

The Avery web site has many, many free label design templates, along with copious tips for successful custom label design and printing. For example, if you're wondering whether you’ll need special printing inks to keep the labels from smearing--you won't. Avery’s tip explains: “To keep your printer's ink from smearing on your labels, be sure to always use inkjet products with an inkjet printer and laser products with a laser printer. Some of our glossy products take a minute to dry, so please wait before you touch the printing.”

title: Springy Mat Is Perfect Size for Single Standing Workstation
text:
This STARTECH ANTI-FATIGUE MAT FOR STANDING DESKS (20" x 30" - STSMAT) isn't the thickest anti-fatigue mat that I’ve ever tried, but it's very springy, and definitely thick enough to provide needed cushioning at a standing desk. The size is perfect for one person at a single standing workstation.

The beveled edges are a significant feature, worth paying for, because they (1) keep the edges from curling up with use, and (2) help prevent tripping over the edges when you step onto the mat. The underside has a nobbly surface that lightly grips the floor. That surface and the weight of the mat itself keep the mat in place so that it doesn't slide easily around the floor.

title: Mechanical Pencils With Strong Colored Leads, Amazing Erasers
text:
Who doesn't love colored pencils? These PAPER MATE CLEARPOINT COLOR LEAD MECHANICAL PENCILS (0.7mm, Assorted Colors, 6 Count) are an especially nice set. They’re mechanical, so they don't need sharpening, and they're nicely balanced for writing (or even for coloring, though the leads are thin for coloring).

The big erasers are amazing--they pick up all or nearly all of the color. The erasers twist up, and are long, so they’ll last (even if you do a lot of erasing).

The colors are bright and vibrant. The colored leads advance when you press a rocker button on the side of the barrel. (The leads do NOT roll back.) The leads are strong, and there are two of each color. (The eraser end of the pencil pulls straight off, to give access to the compartment where the pencil leads are stored and reloaded.)

When you use up the pencil leads, you can get refills (see [[ASIN:B01N5HCWFB Paper Mate Clearpoint Color Mechanical Pencil Lead and Eraser Refills]]).

title: Incredibly Compact, Versatile, Portable Scanner--Autofeeds Grocery Receipts; Scans Two Sides in One Pass
text:
Ever since I set up this EPSON WORKFORCE ES-200 PORTABLE DOCUMENT SCANNER, I haven't been able to stop smiling! It's incredibly compact, weighs only a couple of pounds, works on AC power or a computer's USB 3.0 power (including a powered USB 3.0 hub), and scans business cards, receipts, and documents incredibly fast!

Two things really amazed me: (1) it scans two-sided documents in a single pass, and (2) it will auto-feed long, thin grocery-store receipts of varying lengths. This little scanner is wonderferfully versatile, because it will scan (and auto-feed) documents of many widths and weights, and business and plastic cards of different weights (as long as the documents and cards fall within certain specified limits).

It takes a little practice to master the feeder, but document jams are easy to clear. (You turn the power off, pull up a horizontal guide, and lift the document out.) I have the ES-200, which is NOT wireless, but I see no advantage to having a wireless document scanner--after all, you have to feed the documents through it. It's also nice having a new device that doesn't require fiddling with a network connection.

This scanner comes with the same software as some bigger, non-portable Epson scanners (Epson Scan, Epson Document Capture Pro, ABBYY FineReader OCR, NewSoft Presto! BizCard). I would recommend familiarizing yourself with the full User Manual before trying to scan anything. The settings are a little confusing--there are so many choices!--and it took me quite a while to figure out how to set the destinations for my scanned files.

For your first scans, the Epson Scan 2 software is probably the easiest (most intuitive) to use. It also has the advantage that its settings screens are used in the fancier, fuller-featured Epson Document Capture Pro software. In setting this little scanner up, be sure to download and install the installation software BEFORE you plug in the scanner.

This scanner is going to help me clear a lot of space in my condo. I have quite a few boxes of old financial documents that I'm saving just in case of ... well, I don't really know what. I've had them for years and never needed to look at them, but I'm superstitious (certain that if I throw them out, I will need them 2 weeks later). Once I scan these docs, and back up the files, I can pitch the paper and sleep well.

title: Fancy Case for Standard Parker Ballpoint Pen Refill
text:

If you love the "Urban" pen's looks, or if you want to gift someone with an expensive (about $47 on Amazon) ballpoint pen, then this is a good choice. However, as a writing instrument, it performs exactly the same as any other ballpoint pen with the same Parker refill. The pen's weighted, black-lacquer-and-chrome barrel is nice, and it feels good in the hand, but the pen tip size and ink flow are determined by the refill you choose.

title: Big-Barrelled Dry-Erase Markers With Strong Magnets, Good Felt Erasers
text:
These QUARTET DRY-ERASE MARKERS WITH CAP-MOUNTED ERASER (Chisel Tip, Low Odor, Black, Magnetic, 6-Pack (14079)) are extra-large capacity (5-3/4" long, with barrels that measure 2" around). If you keep them capped and stored horizontally, per the instructions printed on the barrels, they should last a long time.

The markers are low odor, as advertised, and the big felt erasers are very effective. The magnets are stronger and hold better than the magnets you find on most magnetic dry-erase markers.

In my experience, Quartet dry-erase markers work well on a wide variety of whiteboard surfaces, so they're my preferred brand.

title: Great Dispenser, Great Concept; But No "Permanent Bond"
text:
This TOMBOW MONO ADHESIVE+ (62165) item consists of a well-designed glue-tape dispenser containing a replaceable "permanent bond" glue cartridge. The Tombow dispenser has made me a convert to glue tape. Glue tape is far superior to the inexpensive glue sticks I've been using for attaching labels to letters and filing folders. Glue tape goes on smoothly, in a thin layer, precisely where I want it, and presumably won't dry out like the clumsy glue sticks.

The dispenser has a plastic flap that flips down when you want to glue something; the flap flips up to protect the glue side of the tape when the dispenser is stored in a drawer, box, purse, or carryall. The used tape rolls up automatically inside the tape cartridge. A switch on the back of the dispenser opens and closes for cartridge replacement and secure, locked-in cartridge replacement.

The pre-installed Tombow cartridge seems to contain a substantial amount of tape, so the dispenser shouldn't need constant refilling. The replacement cartridges (Tombow Mono Permanent Adhesive Refills, 3 Pack (62207)), currently about $7 on Amazon) are fairly inexpensive.

However, the Tombow "permanent bond" adhesive does NOT provide a permanent bond. I tested the bond by gluing two standard Post-It notes together. The bond certainly was stronger than the weak, removable bond of a Post-It (and is probably much stronger than the bond of Tombow removable adhesive). However, the two Post-Its peeled apart easily, with no tearing of the paper, in multiple tests--even in a test where I pressed on the paper for a maximum bond, and waited 15 minutes. (The adhesive is not supposed to require drying time.)

The "permanent bond" is probably strong enough to hold photos and papers in albums and scrapbooks. Because the adhesive is advertised as "acid free", it's probably a good choice for those purposes.

However, the "permanent bond" is not nearly as strong as Elmer's glue. I really like this glue tape's non-messy, controlled application, but I don't trust the "permanent bond" for securing mailing labels (which I will continue to cover with clear shipping tape). I rate this product at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

title: Fabulous Adhesive--Great Labels for Items Stored in Unheated Areas
text:
The adhesive on these AVERY DURABLE MULTI-SURFACE ID LABELS, HANDWRITE (3/4" x 1-1/2", White, Pack of 120 (61521)) is absolutely fabulous. These labels pass my personal "acid test"--they stick to Rubbermaid Roughneck storage tubs. They also STAY stuck, even though the tubs are in an unheated garage, and subject to daily temperature changes. (I didn't test the Avery claim that these labels will stick to cement, but I believe it.)

In my experience, all Avery labels are hand-writeable, but these have a smooth, water-resistant surface that holds the ink from permanent markers. (The instructions warn that ballpoint pen and rollerball ink will wash off, so you do want to write with a permanent marker.)

These 3/4" x 1-3/4" labels have space for only a few words, so are good for things like labeling small tools with an owner's name, or labeling small utility cabinet drawers containing screws, nuts, fasteners, and other loose items. The larger 1-1/4" x 3-1/2" labels (61522) are a good all-purpose size for labeling boxes, tubs, buckets, larger tools, pipes, etc., because they're large enough for a few lines of hand printing.

title: Charming Christmas Card for Young "Crafty" Child
text:
This SNOWMAN CHRISTMAS CARD WITH STICKERS is a charming card to send to a young child who likes craft activities and playing with stickers. The accordion-fold card has a two-part Christmas tree for the child to punch out and assemble into a display tree that stands up on its own. The child can then decorate the tree with the included stickers (ornaments, stockings, etc.).

Added to a Christmas gift, the card is a little bonus play gift. The card could also be used as a stocking stuffer, or in a Christmas gift basket for a family with small children.

It's a big card (5-5/8" high by 8-1/2" long), but it falls within the size limits for machine-sorted mail. (It won't require an "oversized mail" surcharge.) However, it weighs 1.6 ounces, so it will require more than one first-class stamp for mailing. The card is "printed on sustainably sourced paper", and it comes with a red envelope.

title: Big, Impressive Card Needs Extra First-Class Postage
text:
