Maybe it's slightly better for women, because of the two "diamonds" that are glued onto the stylized flower design, near the top. The flower design itself, done in copper foil, is raised from the card surface. The copper foil contrasts nicely with the silver background.

This is a big, impressive card that you might want to keep on hand for an unexpected birthday. It comes with a plain white envelope, and is "printed on sustainably sourced paper". At 1.3 ounces, this card will take two stamps for mailing; however, the envelope (6-1/8" high by 9-1/4" wide) falls within the size limits for machine-sorted mail (and thus doesn't qualify for an "oversized mail" surcharge).

Because this card is heavy enough to require extra postage for mailing, I rate it at 4 stars ("I like it" on the official Amazon scale).

title: Big, Bargain-Priced Calendar With Magnets, Markers, Sticky Mounting Patches
text:
This QUARTET DRY ERASE MAGNETIC CORK CALENDAR BOARD (Combo Value Pack) gives terrific value for the price (about $7 on Amazon). It's big--about the size of a desk blotter--and there is plenty of room to write in your upcoming appointments and events. The included dry-erase markers have good felt "erasers"; and they attach to the board with magnets, so you will always have a marker available to write with. In addition, you get four rainbow-design magnets for sticking up paper reminders and notes.

The corkboard strip along the bottom is very thin, and is kind of an afterthought. It's no surprise that this Value Pack does NOT come with pushpins. To test the corkboard strip, I used T-pins (on hand for sewing and crafts projects), and they worked okay. However, if you want to pin your notes, you should get pushpins or use thumbtacks, because long pins will go right through the board and damage the wall behind it.

The board is magnetic--it holds lightweight markers and magnets--but it doesn't attach magnetically to metal surfaces. To hang the board, you use 3M double-sided sticky patches (included). You need to position the board carefully when you mount it, because the patches are more or less permanent. They won't produce nail holes, but they can pull paint off the wall when they're removed.

This dry erase board works with all of my markers (Quartet, [[ASIN:B005GPFWG6 Board Dudes]], Foray), which is a good thing. (In my experience, dry erase boards work best with the brand of markers they come with, and some boards won't accept any other marker brand. With this board, the black Foray markers write in gray, so I wouldn't recommend them for this product.) The included red and green Quartet markers produce rather pale writing, so I'll be using the black and blue markers most of the time.

Once the board is mounted on a wall, it's a little awkward to write on (you're writing on a vertical surface). Because you have to fill in the calendar date numbers, this board will require frequent erasing and rewriting. For this reason, you may want to hang the board in a way that will allow you to remove it easily from the wall (e.g., use a nail and an adhesive picture hanger), or you may want to skip the wall mounting entirely and just lean it up against a wall.

The black frame is not one solid piece of plastic--it is assembled from four pieces (a top piece, a bottom piece, and two side pieces with curved corners). At the places where the side pieces meet the top and bottom pieces, there are slight, barely noticeable gaps. These gaps may give the impression that the frame is cracked, even though the calendar board and frame are undamaged. However, in my opinion the tiny "cracks" do NOT detract from the overall appearance.

title: Perfect Solution for Organizing Stored Paper Products, Rolls of Trash Bags; Moderately Difficult to Assemble
text:
This wheeled KING SIZE WIRE BIN FILE (in white coated steel) is the perfect solution for organizing stockpiled paper products (food storage bags, trash bags, toilet paper, facial tissues, etc.) in my garage.

To save money, I usually purchase paper products by the case or in large-quantity packages. I have to store them in the garage. I've been storing them in [[ASIN:B002ORQ0QU Rubbermaid Storage Tubs]], but the tubs (1) don't let me see the stock on hand; (2) need unpacking whenever I need to remove something (a single roll of plastic food storage bags, for example); and (3) are heavy to move around when filled.

It makes perfect sense to store paper products--which are constantly being used up, and replaced--in a rolling wire cart like this one. The four divided sections are very tall and capacious, and the cart holds a lot of paper products. Best of all, when the cart is filled, it can be placed anywhere in the garage, because if it's blocking something it can be rolled out of the way.

This particular wire cart took me about 90 minutes to assemble. Snapping each clip onto a pair of steel wires required a fair amount of hand strength, and this was almost beyond my capacity. I did find that once the clips were attached to the wires, they were easy to remove with pliers, to correct the occasional mistake. The wire parts are easy to identify, and the assembly instructions are adequate. However, it would help if the drawings showed more clearly where the 42 clips should be positioned.

title: Great Idea; Would Be Better If Made With Heavier Plastic
text:
These flexible plastic AVERY TABBED SNAP-IN BOOKMARK DIVIDERS are a great idea. They easily snap onto the rings of a standard three-ring binder, so you can bookmark sections of, or specific pages in, a filled ring binder. The colorful designs incorporated in the bookmarks are cheerful, and the designs are sufficiently memorable that you can find a particular place without reading the labels on the bookmark tabs. (These come with a page of printable labels for the tabs.)

However, if your ring binder isn't very full, the bookmarks will snap OUT almost as easily as they snap IN. (Mine actually fell off the rings of an empty binder when I closed the binder.) I would like to see these snap-in bookmarks manufactured in heavier plastic, which I think would cure the snap-out problem, and make them just about perfect for my needs. Because the bookmarks snap out too easily, I rate them at only 4 stars ("I like it" on the official Amazon scale).

title: Just the Ticket for Students' Schoolwork Binders!
text:
These AVERY BIG TAB POCKET INSERTABLE PLASTIC DIVIDERS are just the ticket for loose-leaf binders used for schoolwork. Each divider consists of a pocket that will hold a very thick class handout--up to 35 sheets, anyway--and still turn smoothly along the binder rings. Once inserted, the loose pages stay in the pocket, because the pocket front slants upwards all the way to the top binder ring.

The dotted, striped, and diagonal decorations are cheerful. Each pocket has a different design or color, so you can identify your notebook sections at a glance. These pocketed loose-leaf-binder dividers have large tabs that extend beyond the cover of a standard binder. I'm not keen on things that stick out of a loose-leaf binder, but these tabs are more or less okay because they're made of flexible (and presumably durable) plastic. Also, there isn't room for the tabs inside the binder cover if the pockets are going to work for holding lots of loose papers.

These plastic dividers come with a paper sheet of blank tab inserts that is perforated for easy separation of individual inserts. The sheet is are suitable for printing, using MS Word or Avery's online templates. The tabs on the dividers have notches that make the printed tab inserts easy to slide in. The notched tabs are also designed hold the tab inserts securely.

title: Versatile Dolly for Moving Groceries, Shipping Boxes, Storage Tubs
text:
This SAFCO PRODUCTS STOW AWAY DOLLY is one of the best purchases I've ever made on Amazon. I have a bad back, so I use it for transporting moderately heavy grocery and hardware store purchases (e.g., cases of bottled water, bags of mulch or potting soil) from my car to my house. I also use it to move indoors the large boxes that FedEx, UPS, and USPS deliver to my front door. And I use it to shift loaded 14-gal. and 18-gal. [[ASIN:B0014CVDA4 Rubbermaid Roughneck]] tubs around my house and garage.

A feature I find particularly useful is the bright yellow, heavy-duty, nylon pull rope. It makes it possible to move boxes (carefully) without strapping them down. It's a bit tricky to control the loaded dolly with just the rope, but you learn quickly enough. A word of caution: the pull rope can be a trip hazard, if you don't pay attention to where you drop it--I learned the hard way!

The dolly is lightweight, and very easy to carry with the built-in handle. It stores standing upright on one end, and takes up little garage space. The 220-lb. capacity is more than adequate for me, because I try to keep shipping boxes and local store purchases under 50 lbs. total weight.

title: Cadillac of Spiral Notebooks!
text: Wow!  This 3-subject FIVE STAR ADVANCE SPIRAL NOTEBOOK is the Cadillac of spiral notebooks!  The spiral binding is covered to protect it from any distortion, and the interior of the notebook has moveable (!) tabbed subject dividers.  The dividers even have expandable pockets for holding handouts and other loose papers.  With this notebook, you can allocate the pages you need for each of your three subjects, and you should never have to mess with pages that are hard to turn because the spiral binding wire has been snagged and pulled out of shape.  It's expensive (about $16), but it's a great notebook for important course notes or for household records that you're planning to hold onto for a while.

title: Outperformed by AmazonBasics 12-Sheet Micro-Cut Shredder
text:
My neighborhood has scavengers who regularly rummage through garbage and recycle bins, looking for credit card bills or anything else they might use for identity theft. Being a little paranoid, I'm always looking for an affordable shredder that will cut household mail, credit cards, CDs, and documents into tinier pieces than I'm getting with my current shredders.

I ordered this SENTINEL PRO FMC120P MICRO-CUT SHREDDER in hopes that it would shred more finely than my excellent [[ASIN:B00D7H8XB6 AmazonBasics 12-Sheet High-Security Micro-Cut Shredder]] . Unfortunately, the two micro-cut shredders perform about the same with paper, and this Sentinel shredder does a much worse job with plastics like CDs (see my customer photos). It just cuts the CDs into big pieces.

The Sentinel shredder doesn't feel quite as sturdy as the AmazonBasics shredder. The two shredders make about the same amount of noise. The AmazonBasics shredder is a little faster. The Sentinel shredder has a larger bin (7.7 gallons as against 6.6 gallons). Both shredders have forward and reverse switches for clearing jams. The Sentinel shredder has a light that comes on when the bin is full. Both shredders handle a maximum 12 sheets at once; both can shred staples, although both user manuals recommend against shredding staples, paperclips, or anything with adhesive, if you want to prolong the shredder's life.

My true workhorse shredder is an old Fellowes PS-14C crosscut model (no longer sold) that handles 14 sheets at once. It has a powerful motor, and cuts through CDs, staples, paperclips, and folded mail with ease. Its only flaw is that it doesn't shred as finely as I would like it to.

Overall, this Sentinel Pro Micro-Cut Shredder is a decent machine, and worth purchasing if you can get a good deal on it. However, because it does such a poor job on plastics, and is generally outperformed by the AmazonBasics shredder, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale.)

title: You get what you pay for and it's worth every penny!!
text:
I had a learning experience before purchasing this item that relates to a couple of the reviews listed for this product.
BEFORE I purchased Desk York, I saw advertisements on social media for a product similar (not the same brand). After seeing the ads over a couple of weeks, I was presented a new ad for a quarter of the price ($10) so I decided to purchase. I waited for weeks for them to arrive but it turned into close to almost 3 months! The product that I received was thin aluminum bars that would hold an e-reader or a tablet. It was NOT this product - so to those who say "I could have gotten this for a fraction of the price" - beware - what you think you're ordering and what you receive are not always the same. My review is below, containing honest key points.
NOW The Desk York was available on Amazon so I ordered one because I want to stand more while working from home. While waiting the couple of days it took to arrive to me, I read the reviews for this product to see how others felt about it. I was really surprised that people reported being unable to figure out how to use it and complained about it. The product I received proved to me that the negative reviews are untrue.
THE DESK YORK IS AMAZING!!!!
I have had the Desk York for a few days and have put it to the test. I can stand with it on my desk, holding my keyboard or my laptop, the top panel is sturdy metal with a solid lip on the bottom edge of the platform that keeps my keyboard or laptop secure from slipping off. Great feature #1!
The legs are NOT completely plastic but are made from a mix of strong plastic and the same metal material that the desk platform is made of. The leg joints are not cheaply made (as shown in pictures) and the fans are a good size, secured in place underneath the platform. The joints have buttons that push in to adjust and then click securely into place when the next angle is found. Adjusting each leg is easy and the angles are marked clearly (see pictures) which is Great feature #2!
Overall: The platform of this desk is a great size. I have enough room for my laptop with a couple of inches on either side, or even to place a bigger laptop on it. The The fans are quiet, the desk is sturdy, the product comes with instructions to help you find the right angles. The angles are very easy to find and adjust due to the built in dials on the sides (see photos). It holds light keyboards to heavy laptops with ease. I will be purchasing another one via this seller for the holidays and upcoming birthdays after the New Year. I will definitely recommend this to anyone interested! THANK YOU DESK YORK!!

title: Wasn't able to achieve kiss cut on Cricut.
text: If you're going to print then do your own cutting with scissors, this paper is ok. The colors print adequately and dry quickly. But I wasted more than half the pack and an entire afternoon trying to achieve a kiss cut on planner stickers with my Cricut. No setting I tried worked - not printable vinyl, not regular vinyl, not sticky paper or washi tape (those had been suggested in some forums online), not even paper. Some settings cut all the way through - which, if that's what you're looking for, would work. (That didn't work well for me, since I was trying to cut about 60 small stickers, which was time consuming to then remove from the mat.) Some settings did a terrible in-between, which basically ripped up the paper and left a ton of stuff for me to peel off the mat. All I wanted was a nice sheet of stickers, kiss cut so I could peel them away from the sheet as needed. No settings I tried would work, and I figured my time was worth going out and buying an actual pack of Cricut printable vinyl to work like I wanted it to. ps: if you've been able to achieve a kiss cut on Cricut with a setting I haven't mentioned here, I'd love to know!

title: Great with 110 lb cardstock.
text: This printer has some quirks that keep me from giving it a 5-star review. First of all, the design is rather clunky - the way the paper tray comes out and the display screen panel lifts up does not feel very streamlined, and takes more space than expected on a desk. It was also very temperamental when trying to connect to wifi the first time. I'll need to go into my settings, but it also seems like the default is to shut off while not in use, then requiring that I "register" my paper type every single time I use the printer. Despite all this, I got this printer in the hopes it would do one thing that many other mid-level printers do not: seamlessly print on 110 lb cardstock. And I'm happy to say this printer is a CHAMP at doing that, using the rear paper feed. I use 110 lb cardstock often for my craft business, and economy & mid-level printers typically chew it up getting caught on the rollers. Larger, more expensive printers are better suited for it, but are just not affordable for me. The rear paper feed does the trick here, and the print quality is great.

title: Ink leaked all over the place
text: Once I cleaned off all the ink from my hands, dress, and the surrounding area, the cartridges did what they were expected to do.  Probably won't order remanufactured ink cartridges again.

title: Useful to keep all your passwords together
text:
This is a useful book for those who like to write down their passwords and other important information. There are a couple extra pages in the front for contacts (2 pages) and software licenses (1 page), and ISP/wifi info (1 page).

The cover feels nice and the elastic band is useful for keeping it closed. There is also a little "envelope" pocket on the back cover, but I'm not sure what to put in there. Maybe business cards? TBD. But a nice touch, I suppose.

title: Perfect for Valentine's Day!
text:
This is a nice card. It folds out and says "Love every little thing about you", which is cute. What I really like, however, is that there is room on the card to write a note. Overall, nice card, would recommend.

I will add that my card came in an envelope with some other items, so there was a little bit of bending. Make sure to leave time to reorder a card in case yours comes the same way.

title: Thick and High quality
text: This is nice thick paper. Double-sided lines with no bleeding. I'd recommend this.

title: Decent printer…if you can get it set up
text:
I had quite a bit of trouble getting this installed. It comes with a USB stick with drivers and an app, which is nice. Installing the drivers for this printer somehow messed with the drivers of my regular printer, which was frustrating. I had to uninstall and reinstall this printer first and then my regular printer. It sounds straightforward, but there was a bit of troubleshooting involved before I figured it all out.

All that said, once you get it set up and working, it's great. It prints really fast, which I wasn't expecting as this is my first thermal label printer. The printing is clear and high quality. I was between giving this 3 stars and 4 stars, but once I got it going, I didn't have any problems. So 4 stars it is.

**Importantly: this doesn't come with any label paper, so be sure to get your own.

title: Simple but nice
text:
As a tip: I got this card to give on Valentine's day, but unfortunately it came bent--so leave time to get another one just in case!

In terms of the card itself, it's good. A little simple. The design on the front and the inside leaves a little to be desired, but I do appreciate that there isn't a lot of text inside so that I can write my own note. The card itself is on the smaller size; approximately the size of a standard pen. Not my favorite, but also not the worst.

title: Works perfectly in Brother HL-L2325DW Printer
text: The ink came well-packaged and was in a sealed plastic bag with an orange cover to make sure the toner wouldn't come out. I installed the toner into my 2325DW printer, and it worked like a charm. No error messages or print issues. Everything came out great. Would recommend!

title: A joy to write with! And it hasn't leaked!
text:
This is a high quality fountain pen. I've tried some of the cheaper ones (Pilot Metropolitan, Pilot Varsity), and while they were good, this is leaps beyond. The pen is a little heavy, which I appreciate, but not so heavy that is interferes with writing.

The ink flow is constant, and maybe a little thick. I'd guess that it's around a 0.8 or 0.9. The pen also comes with 3 ink cartridges (2 black and 1 blue) and an ink converter. One I was a little confused on how to install the ink, but you just need to push the cartridge down (harder than I expected) into the feed.

On my particular pen, one of the 2 feed pieces broke off, but I was still able to get the ink cartridge installed. Fortunately I haven't had any leaks (a problem I've had in the past), but will keep an eye on it.

Everything comes packaged in a nice black storage box, which is a nice touch.

title: Nice paper, as expected
text:
This is good graph paper, perfect for school or work. It is not super heavy, but heavy enough to where my rollerball and gel pens do not bleed through.

The paper also appears to be well-manufactured, as the lines are clean and crisp on the pages with no visible smudging. I'd recommend this paper.

title: Works in my HP Photosmart B209A
text: These cartridges work in my B209A without issue. I haven't noticed any difference in ink quality vs. the Jarbo brand ink (another generic brand) I used before this. No complaints here.

title: Good Gel Pens! But doesn't dethrone the champ
text:
My go-to gel pen is the Sarasa Clip 0.7 Retractable. It's the gold standard for me. So naturally, I was excited to see how they compare. And they compare pretty well. Both pens write very smoothly and unless you are a very discerning user of pens, you probably wouldn't notice the difference in a blind test.

I'll discuss some of the differences between these and the Sarasa pens below. Overall, my critiques are minor.

First, it's the construction of the pen. These pens feel less polished--a little cheaper. The barrel is larger and not tapered anywhere, and the shirt clip feels like a solid block of plastic, whereas the Sarasa has a bit of a taper and is more molded. Next, it’s the smoothness of the pen. While both these and the Sarasa are very smooth, when you use them back-to-back (as I did to test these), the Sarasa is noticeably smoother. Also, the black ink in these pens fades a little and doesn't stay as black as the Sarasas.

title: A nice notebook that shows too many fingerprints….
text:
This is a good notebook. Quality construction, 100 gsm paper, a nice closing band and bookmark.

What bothers me about this notebook is that it is a fingerprint magnet. The pics don't quite capture the extent of it, but there are fingerprints all over. It's possible it wouldn't be as visible with another color, but on the blue, the fingerprints/oil are quite visible.

There is a name page at the front and the paper in the book is all uniform and clean (i.e., no smudged dots that I saw).

title: High quality notebook with thick paper!
text:
This notebook is great. The pages are thick, the spiral is clean (i.e., the pages turn without issue), and the dots on the pages are not too dark. So many notebooks have 100 gsm paper, so the 120 gsm is wonderful.

The only thing I dislike is that the front and back covers show fingerprints/oil from your skin (see pics). That said, I don't think that would stop me from getting this again.

title: It will staple what it says. The first one ...
text: It will staple what it says. The first one I ordered after a week of use the black guard that hooks to the front of the staple cradle fell off. Sent it back for a replacement and about 2 weeks the same thing happened!! So now when you have to fill it hopefully you have a small screwdriver to pry it out. Not going to bother returning it again because fear it will happen a 3rd time

title: Great product!
text:
Very impressed!!
Quality product, and the same cards would cost four to five times more in the store.

title: Nice set for price
text: This was a gift and when it arrived one of the pencils was broken.  Ordered the second set and it was delivered without any damage.  The person who received them was very pleased with the quality and usability.

title: Love my chair!
text: This chair was very easy for me to put together by myself. I love it, it helps me move around in my kitchen because I cannot walk or stand much.  It rolls around so nicely!

title: Cover color is not as vibrant a “Sky Blue” as I expected; pages are darker; binder is non-standard
text: The current price of $9.99 is competitive for a diary notebook like this. I like the design and the fact that the pages can be removed and replaced. I also like the cord closure with a leaf emblem. What I do not like is that the notebook cover is a lot less vibrant than pictured on the Amazon site. Also, I thought the pages were going to be lighter but they are darker than I expected. The paper is easy to write on though. This is a non-standard six-ring binder, so special paper will have to be purchased when a replacement is needed.  Had I known the color was not as pictured and the paper was darker than pictured, I would not have ordered this. Other than this, it is very functional and although the cover is not leather, it is attractive and sturdy.

title: Large footrest; can be used to rock back and forth
text:
This footrest is larger than I expected and actually works well to raise my feet under my desk during long bouts of sitting. As long as my chair is not low to the ground it works well. There are nubs on one side that feel great on bare feet or feet with socks on. If I put the round side down, I can use it as a rocking footrest.

The cover can be unzipped and washed.

Note if one has enough room, this can be used to prop the feet up when on the toilet. It can also be used to lean against the lumbar region, although it is a bit large for that.

The current price of $39.99 is a bit pricey but is still comparable to what is on the market today.

title: Works as designed & comes with touchless keychain tool
text:
There is one padded and nicely sewn shopping cart handle cover in this package along with a touchless keychain tool.

The handle cover will fit most shopping carts and is wide enough for protection. It is Velcroed in place as can be seen in my photos. The photos show this installed on a BJs cart. Note that it is easy to forget this on the cart, however. I like how it keeps an icy handle away from my hands in the winter.

The touchless keychain tool has a rubberized tip to punch numbers on a keypad, etc. and keep one's hands away from touching things. It also has an indentation that enables certain bathroom handles to be lifted without touching them.

In my opinion, this will contaminate their hands after using these items just by removing the handle cover or holding the keychain tool. However, if this gives one peace of mind, then it is worth it. I personally like it to cover cold shopping cart handles.

The current price of $7.99 is reasonable for this.

title: Scale not sensitive enough to register letters; 2 half-dead AAA batteries & Type C USB cable incl
text:
In the box is the scale with the reader attached via a cord, an instruction sheet, two half-dead AAA batteries, a USB Type C cable (if one does not want to use the batteries), a tape measure, two screws with plastic mollies, and a paper nail guide if securing this. Although this says it is a postal scale, it is really for packages because it does not register letters. I even tried weighing a full cup of coffee and the scale stayed at zero whether I had it on kg or lb and oz.

There is a TARE button to zero out the scale in case a container is used and I only want to weigh what's inside the container. There is also a hold button to hold the weight on the screen temporarily. There are also three units of measurement - kilogram, pounds, and pounds and ounces. I cannot attest to the accuracy of this scale but it seems to be correct because my cat is the 8+ pounds specified.

In summary, I think this is a good package weighing postal scale that is simple to operate and has all the features needed to weigh large items like boxes and luggage, supposedly up to 440 pounds. It could probably even weigh a human. Also, the current price of $44.99 ($49.99 minus $5) is competitively priced.

title: Roll organizer for foil, wax paper, & plastic wrap but awkward to thread; magnets weak
text:
This organizer holds three rolls and has three rods inside. I use it for my foil, plastic wrap, and wax paper. The design is nice and it has three holes on the back for hanging this on the wall. Three screws with plastic mollies are included. There are stickers provided if one wants to name their compartments but I find that is not needed. The cutters work well.

There are only two negatives with this. First, the magnets are not strong at all. If I accidently turn this the wrong way, the door opens up. Second, the rolls are initially difficult to feed through the holes--particularly the foil. I actually had to use a tweezer to pick the ends of the rolls through. This is going to be typical of all roll organizers like this. However, what is not typical is that this only has one door for all compartments and that means all three rolls have to be fed through every time one roll is changed. I have another organizer similar to this that does not have rods inside and it is easy to use because each compartment can be changed separately.

The current price of $25.19 is competitively priced.

title: Good protection for little fingers; versatile; pricey
text: This is one of those simple but nifty inventions that make me say to myself "Why didn't I think of that." There are four foam door stoppers in this package. Each one has a little wedge that can be used to stick the entire door stop to the wall to act as a foam bumper to prevent a door handle from hitting the wall. This is also great to keep spaces between the doors. All I had to do was remove the wedge and slip the foam around the door (see photo).  These are excellent for protection from closing little fingers in doors. However, the current price of $8.99 ($9.99 minus 10%) is a bit too pricey for this as it comes to $2.25 per stopper. I do not feel this should be priced at more than $6 as I doubt it takes more than $2 to make the entire set.

title: Huge, sturdy book stand but cannot hold super large books; plastic holders weakest point
text:
This book stand is huge compared to two others I purchased a while ago. I have a  plastic book stand [[ASIN:B005IV6U0U like this one]] and a decorative vintage-looking metal bookstand similar to [[ASIN:B07L4D3THG this one]]. However, none of them satisfy every book scenario and size, which is why I ordered this.

This stand is excellent and has a very large footprint but does not support large books that are large like this [[ASIN:0764557343 Professional Chef]] book or an unabridged dictionary. With these enormous books--books over 800 pages, the stand collapses even if tightened (see photo) and the book tilts the stand to the point that it is falling over while collapsed (see photo).

However, these do hold most books including small ones. They also hold small computers, like my 14" LG. The only negative I found is that the plastic holders in front feel like they can easily break. It is also hard to seat those arms into position. Nevertheless, this stand is excellent even though it is not perfect. Everything is well made except for the plastic holders which feel cheap.

It also comes with an instruction pamphlet and instructions on how to adjust the friction hinge with the supplied wrench to loosen or tighten the unit. The current price of $39.50 is expensive but competitively priced. Note that the "findthisbest" website rates this book stand in the 11th place out of 22 book stands they rated in their "Best Adjustable Desktop Book Stands" article.

title: These markers do not glide well and are too dry
text: I should have known better than to order these for the current low price of $2.99. There are six highlighters in six muted colors in this package. They work like regular highlighters similar to Sharpies in that they do not cover the text being highlighted. However, these do not glide on easily and they are very dry. To me, they are almost ready to throw out straight out of the box. These will only last a few uses before I have to get rid of them. I am disappointed in the quality.

title: Totally does not work & they shipped 3 of the same size
text:
[[VIDEOID:859525fbffa5aab65b86b6747e35198]] This seemed like a great idea so I ordered a set of three that are supposed to come in three different sizes of small, medium, and large. Instead, I received three of the same size. This is total garbage. These do not work. In the photo, they have this placed in the centerfold of the book. I should have known better than to order these. Buyer BEWARE. At the current price of $12.98, this is an expensive mistake. This is another item for the garbage.

Note that these can be used to slip one's finger through the hole (if it fits the thumb), to hold the book open while reading. However, that is not what this is advertised as. Also, I can hold a book with my hands and have no desire to have something on my thumb when reading as that will hurt after extended periods of reading.

title: Attractive COVID vaccination card protector with hole for lanyard or clip (NOT INCLUDED)
text: This card is designed specifically for a vaccination card. It fits my COVID vaccination card perfectly. The green holder is super attractive but is a bit large to fit in a wallet. I put this in my wallet but it is one that should be used with a lanyard or some sort of clip and hung around one's neck or clipped to one's outfit. Note that no lanyard or clip are included.

title: Not as good as Post-It flags but good enough; must be removed from flat end - 3.5 stars
text:
There are supposedly 1120 flags in this set in 8 separate packages of 140 each package and 20 flags of each of the 7 colors per package. Obviously, I did not count them.

These work similar to Post-It flags. I use flags all the time. They are great to mark a specific section in a book, point out a particular recipe, point out where to sign a document, etc. These are not as good as the Post-It because they do not come in a dispenser type format. Instead, I have to separate the flat end with my nails to remove a note. It is very easy to remove more than one. There is also no clear section as there is on a Post-it flag. See my photo for the comparison.

The current price of $6.29 ($6.99 minus 10%) comes to $.79 cents per pack of 140 and there are 8 of those in this set.

title: Two sizes in 80 labels each; love the design of these with its waterproofing
text:
There are 160 labels in this set. There are 80 small and 80 large labels. To use a label, I just removed it from the sheet and applied it to the bottle or surface I wanted. I then partially lifted the laminate tab that sits on top and wrote what I wanted on the label. When I was done, I removed the tab that keeps the laminate from sticking, so that I could now adhere it over the words I wrote.

The labels stick very well and they remove pretty easily as well. They are also waterproof as I ran the label under water without any bleeding. They can be used for canning jars and other projects as well as long as one does not mind the cute design. These are not only useful for baby bottles. I absolutely love these labels. I had tried them previously and could not get the laminate to stick but on this set, that is working well.

The current price of $12.99 for 160 labels comes to $.08 cents each.

title: Extremely delicate; works well for eyeglasses or masks with thin ear elastics
text:
This chain has three purposes. It can be worn as jewelry or to hold eyeglasses or a mask around one's neck. There are removable silicone loops inside the hooks that can be put around one's eyeglass ear arms. To use with a mask, the silicone loops need to be removed.

This chain is attractive and delicate or what I would call somewhat flimsy. I do feel it is easy to lose the silicone loops for the eyeglasses, so I have to be careful not to lose them.

The current price of $9.99 is competitively priced. Note, however, that my absolute favorite mask chain is [[ASIN:B08HQZ1D1Z the Luxure Store Chain]], which is almost four times the price but is incredibly well made.

title: A bit flimsy but works well for eyeglasses or masks with almost any type of ear elastic
text:
This chain has two purposes. It can either be worn to hold eyeglasses or a mask around one's neck. There are removable silicone loops inside the clips that are best to remove before putting around one's eyeglass ear arms. The silicone can be left in place when using the same clasp around a mask's ear elastic or it can be used without them.

Nevertheless, I like this chain as it is basic but stylish even though it is a bit flimsy. I do feel it is easy to lose the silicone loops for the eyeglasses, so I have to be careful not to lose them.

The current price of $9.99 is competitively priced. Note, however, that my absolute favorite mask chain is [[ASIN:B08HQZ1D1Z the Luxure Store Chain]], which is almost four times the price.

title: A bit flimsy but works well for eyeglasses or masks with a thin ear elastic
text:
This chain has three purposes. It can either be worn as chain jewelry, to hold eyeglasses, or to hook onto a mask that has a very thin elastic. The silicone loops have to be removed to use for a mask. The clasp is not easy to get around a mask's elastic as I had to be careful to make sure the elastic was inside the hook. At one point I got it caught at the end of the hook simply because there is not much "hook" room to play with.

Nevertheless, I like this chain as it is very stylish even though it is a bit flimsy. I ordered two of these (one in gold and this one in silver). The gold one arrived with the clasp broken so I am concerned a bit about the quality of this chain.

The current price of $9.99 is competitively priced. Note, however, that my absolute favorite mask chain is [[ASIN:B08HQZ1D1Z the Luxure Store Chain]], which is almost four times the price.

title: Fun set of mask lanyards
text:
There are four snap closure lanyards in this package in some fun designs. These are a reasonable solution to hold one's mask. Each lanyard is only 24 inches long and when closed at the end snap, it hangs above my chest area. Nevertheless, these are perfect to keep my masks around my neck so that I don't have to go fishing through my purse for it.

The current price of $11.99 ($19.99 minus 40%) it comes to $3 per lanyard, which is pricey but still competitive compared to some others like this that I have seen.

title: Heavy heavy-duty electric sharpener; excellent quality; simple operation but overpriced
text: This pencil sharpener is a very heavy, heavy-duty electric sharpener. It sharpens well, catches the shavings without going all over the place, and is simple to operate. As long as I gently held my pencils in the sharpening hole, the tips came out pointy. It has a large footprint and may be overkill for some. Even though this is well made, I still feel the current price of $49.99 is about $20 too much for this unit. That is the only reason I took off one star.

title: Easy access for a month’s worth of pills; case is good as long as I do not move it
text:
This is a nice set of 32 dual-compartment pill cases in a tray. What I like is that the compartments are very easy to remove and each cell is easy to open. Each day of the month is labeled. The dual compartments are labeled AM and PM. There are extra stickers supplied with this and I do not know why that is needed--perhaps if the numbers wear off the compartments or if someone wants to label the other side of the tabs.

The only negatives I see with this case is that the compartments want to pop out if I move the case. Second, the cells are large enough to hold a "horse pill" or two but not many more. The footprint is large as well but not as large as some monthly cases I tried before.

In summary, this is a nice monthly pill organizer for two times per day dosing. Each dual cell is mobile and can be taken in a purse. The biggest negative is that the compartments want to pop out of the organizer if I move the case because my fingers are pushing them out from underneath during the grab.

The current price of $16.98 is typical for this type case.

title: OVERKILL – Big, heavy sharpener; dial difficult to move; otherwise works fine
text:
For years I have been trying to find a good electric pencil sharpener that is suitable to my simple needs. Unfortunately, I still have not found one as this is not for me.

It is a huge sharpener and very heavy. There are six holes for various pencil diameters. I just used the regular hole. It sharpened my pencils well as can be seen in my photo. I did have to hold the pencil in the sharpener as it is strong. I love the large catch tray for the shavings and the tray empties easily. The biggest problem I see is turning the dial. I had to put in a marker into the hole and strongly use that as leverage to turn the dial. Otherwise it is impossible to turn. Had I wanted to sharpen another diameter pencil, this would annoy me. 

I wish this were a bit easier to use and took up less space. Otherwise, it works as designed and the current price of $29.99 ($32.99 minus $3) is reasonable for this. This heavy duty sharpener is best suited for those who have grade school children that need lots of pencils sharpened.

title: Not really invisible & requires a tape dispenser but it tapes – 3.5 stars
text: First of all, it was not easy to figure out how to open the box with the white label stuck around the entire box of tape. Second, I thought this was six rolls of tape with the typical plastic dispenser most tape comes with; however, this requires a tape dispenser. That is disappointment number 2. Third, the tape is not exactly invisible (see photo) but many invisible tapes can still be seen. It is more like regular tape and it tapes fine. If one is looking for an invisible tape that is less seen or does not have a dispenser, then pass on this set of six rolls.

title: Takes 2 pencil sizes; USB or battery power possible; sharpens well but... - 2.5 stars
text:
I wanted to love this but I do not. Yes it works but the design is so, so.

In the box is the sharpener, micro-USB cable, instructions, extra sharpening blades, and a screwdriver. This can be powered via 4 AAA batteries (not included) or the supplied USB cable (A/C connector not included). I plugged this directly into my laptop, and as long as I held the pencil tight, it sharpened well (see photo).

However, the canister for the shavings is not really a canister at all. It is just a plastic cover with a small lip that keeps the shavings from spilling out. Instead, once I pry it off, the pencil shavings go all over the place. That is a terrible design. In addition, the unit feels very cheap. I doubt it will last. Also, I personally would not want to fiddle with the sharpener to change the blades.

This is just an OK, cheap sharpener, with a poorly designed shaving canister. I consider a price more than $6 too much for this unit.

title: Excellent binder that displays my loose recipes over 120 pages
text:
This binder holds 120 viewable sheets inside over the 60 clear inserts.

It has a front pocket as well as a pocket opposite the regular sheets inside. There is also a small full length pocket on the binder.

These are excellent for presentations or just to store recipes like I did. It has so many uses.

The clear pockets are thin and they do get staticky. I really love this binder's versatility.

title: Displays 46 pages not 48 because there’s only 23 sheets inside; still very good
text:
This binder holds 46 viewable sheets inside and not 48. I only had 23 sheets and not 24 and I counted several times.

It has a front pocket as well as a pocket opposite the regular sheets inside. There is also a small full length pocket on the binder.

These are excellent for presentations or just to store recipes like I did. It has so many uses.

The clear pockets are thin and they do get staticky. Other than the one less sheet, I really love this binder.

title: Attractive 5" x 7.5" 6-ring binder; NO PAPER; feels cheap
text:
When I ordered this I had no idea this did not come with paper. It is only a 5" x 7.5" 6-ring binder. Either I would have to order 6-ring paper or order a 6-hole punch to create my own paper inserts. I have no intention of doing either, so this is a disappointment.

The binder itself feels cheap but the color is attractive. It has a magnetic snap closure. The binder rings open and close easily. There is a full length pocket on the right and left. There are also four credit card pockets on the left and a pen holder elastic. If this came with paper, it would have gotten four stars. There is not even a recommendation on Amazon as to which paper to buy as there is no guarantee the holes on the paper will line up with the binder rings in this planner. It is best if one has a six-hole punch to create their own paper inserts.

Currently there is no price on Amazon, but I do not feel this should be priced more than $7.

title: Good case if one wants portability for the days and large compartments
text:
I have this fetish for pill cases. When I started having to take medicine, I purchased several cases and was disappointed with all but one and that one was a case that is EXACTLY like this one with one difference. That difference is that my case also has the moon and sun written on the front.

There are seven colorful compartments for two pill doses per day. The lids open most of the way but it is best to bend them back to get full access to the pills. Each cell can hold many small pills or a few "horse" pills. I like that the days are written along the sides. I do wish the moon and sun were on the front of the case along with the AM and PM. The reason is that without the pictures, it is easy to mistake which side is which. This set of seven has its own plastic carrying case. It also comes with extra labels for days and the numbers 1 to 7.

This type of case is not for everyone. It is a bit bulky due to the fat cylindrical shape. However, I like that each day is portable and it does fit a sufficient amount of pills.

The current price of $9.99 is competitive.

title: Sizing is all wrong which reduces capacity; envelopes are still a useful at 3-1/2" x 7"
text:
First of all, I did not expect this to come in such a huge box large enough for a super large microwave. However, since this is a 480 pack, I should have expected this, so that is my fault. I only needed a few of these envelopes.

Second, the size on the Amazon site is totally incorrect. The useable sizing is only 3-1/2" x 7" - below is the sizing depending on how the envelope is being measured and none of the sizes match what is on the Amazon site.

4-3/4" x 8-1/4" - this is when envelope is fully opened (flap is unsealed) from end to end

4-3/4" x 7-1/4" - this is when envelope is fully closed and flap is sealed

4" x 7" - this is the area of padding as measured from the outside of the envelope

3-1/2" x 7" - THIS IS THE USEABLE SPACE INSIDE THE ENVELOPE and is what matters

Based on the sizing above, 4" x 6" print photos cannot even be mailed in these envelopes. I tried to get a 4" x 6" card in the envelope and could not. I had to fold it down to 3-1/2" in order to get it in this envelope.

The seals on the few envelopes I tried were great.

In summary, each envelope comes to about $.11 cents based on the current price of $49.99. However, unless one is mailing a few bulbs of garlic, a 100 pack set of stamps, a small perfume bottle, or a headband or foldable mask in this envelope, the usefulness is limited.

title: Well-thought out bookstand, laptop desk; eating or drawing desk
text:
This is a relatively well-designed bed desk. I can use it for my laptop, coloring, reading, eating, etc. It is also collapsible which is great when storing.

The desk comes with a plastic bookstand that can be used separately or placed in the top of the desk slot. It gets stored away underneath the desk. There is also a drawer on the left side for pencils or glasses. There is a laptop oval that fits in the front slot of the desk to prevent the laptop from sliding off when the desk is tilted.

The legs are foldable and adjustable up or down. The tray also tilts. The only reason I rated this well-designed desk 4 stars is because it is a bit tricky to collapse and expand the legs and to engage the tilt. Sometimes, I could not get it to adjust and had to play with the release mechanisms. The desk is also a bit heavy. Other than this, it is a great large desk and perfect for small spaces due to its ability to collapse.

title: Say “I love you” for Valentine’s day with an expensive and intricate card such as this
text:
This is a lovely card with a very intricate pop-up design made of thin wood. It is also expensive at the current price of $14.99 but it is beautiful and simple. The card front says "I LOVE YOU" (no quotes) with a heart substituted for the word LOVE. The card inside has the same pop-up message intricately designed in wood with hearts and a base that looks like an "ice-cube-divider" from those tin ice-cube trays of yesteryear. 

The inside message is a continuation of what is on the front of the card and says (without the quotes):

 "....WITH ALL OF MY HEART. HAPPY VALENTINE'S DAY"

The envelope is white with a deep red interior.

This is a wonderful card for the special someone or significant other. It is also well made and well executed.

title: Eight festive cards but there is no "Christmas" mentioned; write on back side only
text:
These cards are simple and festive. Its pop-up feature is a nice touch. To keep the cards standing, the two tabs in the back have to be pushed in.

The car's license plate says "Merry" and on the back of the card it says "Hope you'll enjoy every happy thing the season brings." (See second photo.) I am disappointed that there is no Christmas written on the plate or at least X-MAS.

The only space to write on this card is on the back of the card where the one sentence saying is located. Of course one can write on the one inch rim below the car tires, but there is not much room.

Besides the limited writing space and the lack of any Christmas in these cards, I do not like all the packaging it comes with. There is no need for such waste as the cards could have been shipped closed.

Also note that these cards are not very functional. It is a bit awkward to wedge money behind the driver's seat.

title: Cute blank cards with funny inscriptions on cover
text:
These cards have very cute sayings on the front. They are blank inside, so they are more versatile and can be used for any appropriate occasion.

There are 12 cards with envelopes spread over 4 card varieties.

- Three cards say "Cat Treadmills" on front and has two cats shredding toilet paper.

- Three cards say "Whoa, STRAIGHT FLUSH! Must not wag tail. MUST....NOT...WAG....TAIL! on front and has a cat and three dogs playing cards with the pug who is saying this.

- Three cards say "Oh, Crap! Was that today?" and has a picture of two unicorns looking hopelessly on as Noah's Ark sails away.

- Three cards say ""She Loves Me More!" with each saying over one glass of wine and one cup of coffee.

I really love the cat and Noah's Ark cards and I like the other two. These are great for friends or love ones who have a sense of humor, whether given on birthdays or just for some other "thinking of you" type of special occasion.

title: “Post-It” impostors with a larger sticky surface in six vibrant colors that make me smile
text:
Boy these fooled me. These are Post-It impostors from "vanpad," which I assume is one of the many Amazon businesses. 

There are a total of 24 pads in 6 vibrant colors (pink, orange, yellow, lime, blue, and purple) with 70 sheets each pad. There is also one tiny package of "Post-It-Like" flags which I use to bookmark pages in a cookbook and can be written on.

So far these are working well for me and are sticking. I love the electric colors and the larger sticky area on top of each sheet. The only negative I found so far is that when I write on the dark blue flag, it is hard to read the writing because of the dark color. I wish that blue were just a little lighter; however, this applies to the flag only as the blue pad is lighter and shows my writing much better with a blue ballpoint pen.

title: Finally, a journal I can rave about; it is handcrafted quality at its highest standard!
text:
Over the past year I ordered three vintage journals that ranged from not so great to good enough. However, this journal is pure perfection without being dirty vintage.

The craftsmanship of the leather binding is impeccable. The stitching is clean, the buckle closure (which is actually a snap closure) is stylish, and the feel of the leather is supple. The included dog bookmark is a sweet and useful touch, especially for animal lovers like me.

The journal itself is made of recycled cotton paper but still has a vintage look without being "dirty." I love that the journal is replaceable (meaning removable) in the sense that I can use this leather cover for any other appropriately sized notepad or book.

In summary, this removable vintage leather-bound journal with dog bookmark is exquisitely handcrafted to the finest detail. If I could give it 10 stars I would.

title: Binder-ready sheet protectors perfect for my recipe sheets; they are thin
text:
This review is for the 200-pack of AmazonBasics Sheet Protectors.

These sheet protectors are very thin but they protect my papers. I wanted them to cover some recipes I have (see second photo). I like that they are three-hole punched so that I can assemble the recipes in a binder if I wish to. I have no idea how much these will cost as no price is currently available. All I can say is that they are thin and the three-hole punch is not reinforced; however, they work perfectly to store one sheet of paper per protector. As long as the price is reasonable, like under $12 for the 200, then these are worth the purchase. If the price is over $12, then I would consider this a four-star product only because of the thinness.

title: Five simple, yet beautiful, friendship / young love cards
text:
There are five simple friendship and young love cards in this pack with teal envelopes. Three are friendship oriented, one is thinking of you, and my favorite is more of a younger lover card. It has a two dimensional image of peanut butter and jelly jars on the front and says "you and me" and on the inside it says "talk about a perfect pair." That card is so cute and sweet.

I attached a picture of the front of each card in photo one and the inside inscriptions in each card in photo two lined up in the same order as in photo one.

At the current price of $13.99, it comes to $2.80 a card. That is not much of a bargain but it is still better than can be purchased at a Hallmark Shop.

title: Great for storing and organizing recipes, creating flash cards, etc.
text:
This is a great set of four holders each with 100 index cards each, 5 colored indices, and 5 self-stick labels. I ordered this to write short recipes on each index card when I find the time. However, these can be used to create flash cards for school, to keep various lists, etc. I also like how the card holder has some style to it with the etched designs.

Each item comes pre-packaged for sale even with plastic tab for hanging in a store.

As per the Yoobi website, for every Yoobi item purchased, they donate a school supply item to a U.S. classroom in need.

title: Beautifully designed & colorful cover; tablet lays flat when opened
text: This journal is absolutely lovely. I love the vibrant colors and the design of the hard cardboard cover. I also am impressed how this journal stays flat if I open it. That is due to it being coptic-bound. I never encountered a coptic-bound book or tablet or journal before and this is wonderful. I am highly impressed. In addition, it is small enough to carry around but a little bigger than a 5" x7" photo.

title: Sturdy plastic folders for letter-sized paperwork
text:
I ordered these folders for storing my car paperwork and also recipes and other odds and ends. What I love is that they are plastic, so they hold up well and water runs right off them. Besides the two pockets, there is a centerfold with prong clips that allow three-hole-punched paper to be stored.

The current price of $6.99 is reasonable for these. I highly recommend them when storage for non-bulky paperwork is needed.

title: Small stunning bell perfect for door bell, dinner bell, etc.; hardware not included
text:
I ordered both this 2" bell and also the [[ASIN:B07QJ5RKJ9 3" version of this bell]] which is slightly different in the sense of the mounting arm and ring. The last photo shows a picture of the 2" bell on the left and 3" bell on the right for comparison purposes.

I did not realize how small this bell would be. It is tiny enough to fit in the palm of my hand. The inches are measured from the widest point on the bottom.

It does not come with mounting hardware. I wish it did because one has to find the right nails/screws to fit this. There are three screw holes in the mounting arm. The clang is tinny but yet loud enough and is made by rocking the cord back and forth which swings the bell ball against the bell.

This is gorgeous and perfect to affix on a door or somewhere near a hotel or sales reception area.

title: Large stunning bell perfect for door bell, dinner bell, etc.; hardware not included
text:
I ordered both this 3" bell and also the [[ASIN:B07QJ5MVC7 2" version of this bell]] which is slightly different in the sense of the mounting arm and ring. The last photo shows a picture of the 2" bell on the left and 3" bell on the right for comparison purposes. The first picture shows this bell against my salt and pepper shakers for a size comparison.

I did not realize how much bigger in size this bell would be. It looks almost two to three times the size. The inches are measured from the widest point on the bottom.

It does not come with mounting hardware. I wish it did because one has to find the right nails/screws to fit this. There are three screw holes in the mounting arm. The clang is loud enough and is made by rocking the cord back and forth which swings the bell ball against the bell.

This is gorgeous and perfect to affix on a post in front of a building, on a door, or somewhere near a hotel or sales reception area. When I say large, I mean comparatively larger than the 2" inch bell. It does fit fully in the palm of my hand.

title: Very nice 3D like housewarming card with a simple message
text:
I ordered this for a friend who plans to get a new home soon. This is a perfect card for that new chapter in life. On the outside is a 3D-like raised cutout three to four layers deep if counting the printed picture behind it. It is three layers at the roof but four layers with the door, fence, and chair.

The inside message reads "Congratulations on finding a new place to call your own." The envelope is red with white interior with a red and green flower-like pattern. A blank sheet is supplied to put over the front of the card so that the 3D-like image does not get destroyed during insertion into the envelope.

Overall, this is a very inviting and simple housewarming card for the person who has a new apartment, condo, townhouse, house, trailer / manufactured home, or any other place to call their own.

title: Perfect mini-monthly calendar for my purse; covers August 2019 to December 2020
text:
I only ever buy monthly calendars because I like to see my appointments for 30 days. Of course, I trade off writing space when the monthly comes in a mini-version like this. Note that because it is a mini, there is only a 1" square box for each day but it is enough for one to two appointments abbreviated.

This is a 17-month calendar going from August 2019 to December 2020. The cover is Leatheresque in that it feels like leather but it is not. It is sturdy, however. The cover is a glitzy gold and the inside calendar pages are various hues of purples, pinks, and greens. Unfortunately, with my camera and lighting, the pictures do not show how attractive these pages are. This is a perfect planner for me and I already put it into service and carry it around in my purse.

title: Vintage-looking journal with a few "dirty" pages and cheaply dyed leather; nice design
text:
I ordered their [[ASIN:B07PZVN2WN tree journal]] and was not happy with it. However, this journal is cleaner and the paper whiter. It is vintage-looking but not too dirty and worn that it offends my senses.

As is typical of a leather-bound journal, the paper is not replaceable. Writing on the paper with pen or pencil works well. A few pages have smudges on them and I did see some thread or lint between some pages. The underside of the leather is poorly dyed looking as if it is dirty and does appear to have fingerprints dyed in the back of the journal. I do not care for those fingerprints. The tie is just a string of leather and not set in a way that makes it intuitive to tie the book shut. The embossing on the outside is very attractive, however.

There are five sections that are "stitched" into the book. Each section has a centerfold string.

The six photos show the following in order:

1 - The attractive stitching on the binding and the outer leather embossing.

2 - The front of the journal.

3 - The back of the journal.

4 - The blotchy spots found on some pages pages.

5 - The front inside leather cover and blotchy dye work.

6 - The back inside leather cover and blotchy dye work with fingerprint stains.

In summary, they succeeded in making this look dirty vintage and handmade from scrap. The exterior embossing of a dragon design is super attractive and so is the binder stitching. The leather is cheap and the paper is sometimes blotchy with occasional pieces of lint. This is definitely better than the [[ASIN:B07PZVN2WN tree journal]] I ordered from them. Since the intention here is to look vintage, I would say they succeeded. I would not expect to pay more than $18 - $20 for this in its current condition. It has "found in the attic" sort of vibe to it.

title: This cart is extremely versatile but I wish it was 8-12" taller
text:
I absolutely love this cart in every way but the height. I'm 5'5" and this cart comes up to the top of my legs. This wheels easily on both low-pile carpet and a regular floor. Setting it up is less than a few seconds; just grab the sides and pull outward. It then locks in place. To close, just pull up on the levers on either side of the locking mechanism and it folds.

I ordered this for two purposes.

First, when I do canning, I want a work area to the left of my stove for holding my jars, cutting up ingredients, etc. Because this comes below my stove (see fourth picture) and below my waistline, it makes using this a bit more awkward and uncomfortable for this purpose. Since I am standing, my arms are stretched out more than they would be had this been taller.

Second, I also want to use this when I clean off my dining room table (which I use for storage). I need a place to put the items temporarily and this two-tier cart is perfect for that.

Nevertheless, this is an excellent choice as long as one is not going to work on this regularly in a standing position. Set-up and breakdown is a cinch and it is guaranteed for three years.

title: Contains 50 sheets of cardboard-stock-like note sheets that are gold embossed
text: I counted the sheets in this pad because I originally thought there were 100 sheets. However, the note sheets are so thick like cardboard that there are only 50 sheets. They are really high quality and the Micky emblem and the sides are gold embossed. This would make a great gift but, in my opinion, at $12.99 this is too expensive for everyday use.

title: Perfect organizer for a backpack or to store on a shelf
text:
I expected this in purple but it does say the color may vary. The color I got was green. I can organize my 8-1/2" x 11" size or less documents (taxes, papers, etc.) with this.

There are a total of the seven pockets but only six have tab dividers. There is one sheet of pre-printed tab inserts included that are labeled days of the week (like Sat/Sun) or months of the year (like May/Jun). There are two ID card slots with what looks like a miniature ruled index card in each slot.

This claims to hold 400 sheets but I am skeptical how well the folder would hold up under such a load. It has an elastic closure that provides for expansion. Overall, I am very pleased with this folder; I just wish I could choose my own color.

title: Excellent manual sharpener for my colored and lead pencils
text: This sharpens my colored and lead pencils exceptionally well. I bought this because my electric sharpener just chewed up my pencils. This will work on make-up pencils too. The only negative is that the pencil shavings get stuck in the well, especially when they are removed by the sharpener in one long pencil shaving.

title: Excellent manual sharpener for my colored and lead pencils
text: This sharpens my colored and lead pencils exceptionally well. I bought this because my electric sharpener just chewed up my pencils. This will work on make-up pencils too. The only negative is that the pencil shavings get stuck in the well, especially when they are removed by the sharpener in one long pencil shaving.

title: Good cushion for my car seat but not for my office chair
text:
I sit many hours per day for my job. I recently purchased the [[ASIN:B010TLSFA6 ComfiLife Premium Comfort Seat Cushion]] and find that to be good but not perfect. Therefore, I decided to order this. It felt very comfortable when I first tried it. However, after sitting on it for a couple of days, I feel as if I am sliding forward in my desk chair. Also, it is not as comfortable as it felt the first moment I sat on it. I decided to move it to my car and it works well there because my car seat in slanted back, so I do not feel like I am falling off the cushion.

Overall this is just okay. I have not found anything yet that is perfect but the [[ASIN:B010TLSFA6 ComfiLife Premium Comfort Seat Cushion]] is a tad more comfortable to me and thicker too. One thing I really like about this HNOS cushion is that it is a solid piece and does not have a hole in it like my ComfiLife.

title: This eraser does not fully erase my Rembrandt or #2 graphite pencil mistakes
text:
I have never used this type eraser before so I have nothing to compare it to. However, after reading online how good "plastic" (a.k.a. vinyl) erasers are supposed to be, I expected better than a fair job. The eraser shreds itself during use so there are tiny pieces left behind as there would be with a pencil (a.k.a. rubber) eraser. Those pieces have to be brushed aside.

This eraser is tiny and requires manual dexterity to use. Nevertheless, it only did a fair job. It is true that it did not damage the paper but it also did not do an exceptional removal job.

The first picture shows a purple flower with two purple colors. In the second photo, I erased the light color on the left but a haze of the old color remained no matter how I tried to get rid of it.

The third photo shows a quick outline made with a #2 graphite pencil. In the fourth photo, I erased the eyes. A haze was also left behind.

The last picture shows the Rembrandt pencils I was using as well as the # 2 graphite pencil.

title: Elegant yet plain THANK YOU cards to be reserved for the finer gifts
text: There are 10 blank cards with 10 interior gold-colored envelopes in the box. At the current price of $11.99, it comes to $1.20 per card.  These are elegant and feel like quality and should probably not be used for just any THANK YOU. The blue face with gold lines is okay but a silver / platinum hue would have screamed super elegant.

title: Excellent cushion that makes sitting a long time comfortable for me
text:
I sit many hours per day for my job. My boyfriend purchased one of these because he has some pain that he attributes to sciatica. He has all his packages delivered to my house and when it arrived, he said I could try it. I was previously sitting on two seat cushions and after I tried this, I am in love with the comfort even if it is a tad too big for my posterior. In addition to this I use a [[ASIN:B004V7P6MA travel pillow]] for my back. The combination allows me to sit for an extended period of time without aching. So far this is the best cushion I have tried and gets 4.3 stars from me. Another plus is that it has a carrying handle making it easily transportable.

I like this so much that I plan to order some of their other items including the one with the gel, the knee pillow, and the Cocyx & Posture Support Seat Cushion that is currently out of stock.

PS: By registering this cushion with the company, I was sent a 10% off for the next purchase on their site which is just a few cents better than the Amazon price. They also offer free shipping.

title: Eight beautiful individually wrapped birthday cards with mostly one-liners
text: There are eight cards in this package (see picture) and each one is individually packaged. The covers are dazzling and even though the sayings are simple, these cards are perfect for the right friend. I absolutely love them and feel that the current price of $14.99  is reasonable.

title: These clips are gorgeous and hefty and hold up to 20 sheets of paper but sometimes marks are left behind on the border
text:
My first impression of these clips was "WOW" these are really nice. There are twelve small clips in the package in three different colors. The colors to my eyes are eggplant purple, light bluish/gray, and slate gray. They look elegant and are hefty.

Each clip holds 20 pieces of paper together and they easily slide on and off but not so easy that they will fall off. I was able to get 21 pieces of paper under each clip but it was a tight squeeze.

I love these except for two issues. The colored coating that covers each clip is really only held on by an adhesive. A few of the coverings were pulling away until I pressed them back down on the metal part of the clip. Second, the act of clipping and unclipping pieces of paper sometimes leaves a light brown mark on the edge of the documents. This is my biggest disappointment. Despite this, they are very nice, feel good in the hands, and do the job they claim to do which is hold up to 20 sheets of paper together.

title: This notebook has four pockets, a TOC section, 100 ruled sheets but does not have the tabbed sections I prefer
text:
I am not as enamored with this notebook as I thought I would be.

The front cover is a plastic pocket with two sides. A full 8" x 11" sheet of paper can sit in the front of the notebook that can contain anything from a picture of what is inside, one's name, subject matter, or anything that fits on that paper size. It can also just be used to store any number of papers. The back of the front cover is a half pocket like one would find in a standard two subject paper folder. This can be used for more storage. In addition to this there are two half pockets that fit smaller pieces of paper and other items.

The first two ruled sheets are table of content (TOC) sheets where the date, topic/description, and page number can be hand written. The rest of the notebook is ruled with a sidebar for notes or a vertical subject and a section at the bottom for the page number. I would have preferred a pre-printed page number on each sheet. However, I guess the manufacturer made a decision to let the user to write in the numbers in case some sheets are ripped out of the notebook.

There's also an 8 x 17" folded "thick" sheet in the back of the notebook for reference notes. I personally do not like the checker-box rule on this sheet and would have preferred a blank un-ruled piece of paper.

Personally, I prefer notebooks with dividers in them and tabs that stick out so that I can easily see the subject of each section. If this notebook had tabs and the page numbers were preprinted, I would have rated this 4 stars. If they included tabbed sections and each section had pockets on either side, then I would have rated this 5 stars. As this is currently designed, it is just okay for my taste. However, this is a personal preference. On another note, I do like how the pages turn smoothly. Some notebooks I have used before are "sticky" with its page rotation and the one I received does not have that problem.

The video on the Amazon site gives a good idea of what this notebook is about and what is included.

title: I use this to store items on my fridge; LOVE the product; HATE the label on front
text:
These magnetic pockets are absolutely awesome. I use them on my refrigerator. Attached is a picture of one of those pockets. I love that I can label them with the tab included if desired. Also, the pockets hold at lot because they expand and the magnet is strong.

I would have rated this 5 stars except that I absolutely hate the company name on the clear plastic part of the pocket as it obstructs my view of the contents. I store my seasonality chart in the front of some other stuff and I cannot fully read it with that writing on the front. Instead I have to remove the chart and would prefer that I read it while it is inside the pocket. That is the only disappointment I have as it will hold up to 8.5" x 11" size items.

title: This paper worked fine in both my inkjets but it is thin, geared toward non-business documents, & a tad $$ than my regular paper
text: This paper is thinner than my regular ream of white paper I normally use. It is also best for flyers and non-business documents or just for artsy projects.  At the current price of $8.99, this is a few dollars more than I usually pay for the white thicker stock paper. I printed documents using this paper on both of my inkjet printers--an Epson XP-520 and an Epson ET-2700. It printed fine. The quality of the printout is good and the paper did not jam. Other than the slightly higher price for recycled paper that is colored, this works fine.  The green makes any document stand out among a sea of white paper.

title: Write nicely but are difficult for me to hold for extended writing
text:
These pens write well and are mostly smooth. However, because they are small (around four inches not including the press top), I find them a bit uncomfortable to hold for extended writing.

I love the 10 colors, which are:
- black
- blue
- light blue
- teal
- green
- light green
- orange
- pink
- red
- purple

If these felt more comfortable to write with, I would have rated this four stars. The small size, however, allows one to carry them around easily. So there is a bit and give and take here.

title: An excellent blank one-subject notebook that also supports a cause, so it's a tad expensive
text:
This spiral bound notebook has 100 double-sided college ruled pages. In the front is one double-sided blue folder compartment that can hold a limited number of paper on both sides. The cardboard backing is thick and the front cover is a bit thinner. What I like is that the pages do not get hung up on the binding as I have encountered with some other notebooks. There is also a loose note inside in the shape of a bookmark that says one notebook is given to a child for every notebook purchased. That is a nice touch. You can actually enter the unique code to see who received that notebook. I entered my code and attached a picture of who received the corresponding book.

According to their website, AUGUST BLANKS is a non-profit organization with a vision to give every child in the world access to a notebook every year for his (or her, I assume) education.

The only reason I rated this 4 stars is because $4.99 is a lot for a one subject notebook. Yes it has one double-sided folder compartment in the front and yes the cardboard backing can withstand a lot of abuse. However, this notebook is not that much different than others available for purchase for almost half the price at Walmart. Other than the price, it is an excellent blank one-subject notebook. If one does not have the money or does not want to support their vision, then one can find cheaper notebooks elsewhere.

title: These labels are almost too easy to remove; they are small and thin as well and almost half price on the Avery site
text:
The labels are super tiny, sort of thin and see-through, and easily come off. Attached is a picture of one item I labeled so that the size can be seen.

I do feel these are great for canning because the labels can be easily removed. However, they are almost too easy to remove. I was able to lift the corner of the label and remove it immediately. When I ran the label under water, the adhesive disintegrated as it should.

One other dislike I have besides the small size and thin texture, is that I found it almost impossible to see the label outline and as a result it was difficult for me to remove it from the paper backing it came on. I guess I can chalk that up to older eyes but the delineation between the label and the sheet it comes on needs to be clearer.

Nevertheless, these do work as designed and are easily removed from plastic, glass, and canning lids. The fact that a laser or inkjet printer can be used with the appropriate Avery template from their website is a plus. At the current price of $14.14 for 50 tiny labels ($.28 cents each), I think this is very expensive for what they are. However, when I looked on the Avery site, the list price for the same labels is $6.25 so I would order them there.

title: Good thin document-sized envelopes that have sufficient but not great adhesive lids
text: At the current price of $12.99, this 100-pack of self-adhesive envelopes comes to $.13 cents each and are perfect for mailing or storing unfolded 8-1/2" x 11" documents. The peel and stick lid makes these easy to seal. Each lid has just enough adhesive to hold the envelop closed. I do wish the adhesive surface was larger and closer to the outer edges of the lid, however. The paper stock is extremely lightweight yet still protective in the sense that the white envelopes are not see-through. Overall, I think these are a good buy if one needs a 100 pack of document-sized envelopes.
