They’re great for putting papers and that you’re gonna put in your bag that you don’t want bent and messed up.

title: Book Cart
text: This cart is very similar to the one at Michael’s. It assembles easily. It has three good sized baskets. I use it for books, but you could use it for anything. It is pretty sturdy, but I would overload it with too many books. These carts make things so much easier!

title: Cute Planner
text: This planner doesn’t hit all my planner hopes, but it is a good basic planner that doesn’t cost an arm and a leg. It definitely works and has lots of functional options. But it is fine.

title: Letterboard
text: If you want to be a cool kid, you’ve got to have a letterboard. This one works well. It takes a thousand years (or an hour) to get all the little letters popped out. But the board is really cute and it works well.

title: Nice Notebooks
text: These are great notebooks for school. I like the composition style. The paper has a slightly recycled feel to it. The covers are pretty heavy duty. Definitely a good quality notebook.

title: Story Books
text: I love these notebooks for younger kids. We use the “Draw, Write, Now” program for handwriting. These notebooks give them space for their drawing at the top of the page and then their handwriting practice at the bottom. They also work well for little ones writing stories as they have drawing space at the top.

title: They Work
text: These notebooks are pretty mediocre. They are, in no way, even close to comparable to the big brands of similar style. They just look cheap next to those notebooks. They're thinner than those, too. Not quite as many pages per book. They work. But they aren't the best quality.

title: Mail Box
text: This is a great box to use as a landing place for all your mail. Big enough for magazines, catalogues, and all sizes of mail. It really will hold quite a bit. It looks nice. And it gives the mail a place to live that isn't on the kitchen table.

title: 3-Pack
text: This is a cute little 3-pack of office supplies. Each color comes with tiny clips, small clips, paperclips, and pushpins. The pink and teal have silver metal. The clear have rose gold metal. I do kind of wish they were all rose gold metal, but that is just being picky.

title: Not Great
text: These pencil sharpeners are not great. They eat through batteries and don't give a smooth point. They also stop with slightly too much pressure, so they've been less than ideal for kids to use.

title: Works great!
text: It works great and feels good, and I appreciate the tear-off corners. Those along with the two place-marking ribbons are great features. The "vegan leather" cover, though, is a bit think and soft.

title: A Couple Weird Colors
text: This set looks exactly like the Zebra Mildliners. The pens are very similar, and I even like the design of these more than the Zebra pens. They'd be completely perfect, if a few of the colors weren't weird. The bright coral color was fine on the chisel tip end, but the fine point end was a dark gray color mixed with the bright coral. It has a cool effect, but definitely was not the color it should have been. If there weren't issues like that on a couple of the markers, this product would be better than the name brand, in my opinion. But with the inconsistency of color, I'd probably stick with the name brand.

title: Good Chair
text: This is a good office chair. It is comfortable to sit in for long periods of time. It feels like a zero gravity chair. It isn't plush, but more like sitting in a tightly stretched hammock. Super comfortable, I promise.

title: Good Cart
text: We use this cart weekly to haul things in and out of our church. (We're a nomadic church, so things have to be set up weekly.) We put a lot of heavy stuff in this cart and it is holding up really well. It pushes smoothly. It is easy to maneuver. I'm really happy with this cart.

title: Comfortable Chair
text: This is a comfortable desk chair. It looks pretty nice, too. Though you do have to be a little careful with the faux leather or it'll look awful pretty fast. It is comfortable to sit in. I like it.

title: Basic Mechanical Pencils
text: These are the basic mechanical pencils. They're decent quality. They write smoothly. I wish they each had more lead in them to make them last a bit longer before needing a refill. My kids like the colors. Good quality pencils that are the same every time you buy them.

title: Such Random Stickers
text: I love stickers. This set is just such a random assortment. I end up having to flip through all of them looking for that one sticker I knew came in this set. It is like you purchased someone else's leftover stickers or something. They're even random in the finish. Some are on clear paper, some are on standard white paper. I do like them. They are all pretty small so they tend to work well on calendars and planners.

title: Close
text: These notebooks are not quite a nice as the pricey name brand version. The paper is a little thinner and not quite as nice. But they are definitely a decent notebook. They’ve got all the bells and whistles and work well and look great.

title: Very Flimsy
text: This chore chart is cute and I love that it has all the little magnets with different colors for different kids. However, the chart itself is the same thickness as the other magnets. You can put it on a magnetic whiteboard for more stability. But if you just hang it by itself, it moves and bends and the magnets fall off of it. It really works better stuck to a whiteboard or fridge.

title: Beautiful Journal
text: This journal is not refillable. It is beautiful. It has nice paper inside. It is definitely an intimidating journal. It is so hard to begin marking up this beauty. But it is lovely. And the wrap closure is a nice touch.

title: Nice Journal
text: This journal isn’t refillable. However, it is super nice. The paper has hand pressed flowers in it. The paper is thick and soft. It just has a very handmade, vintage feel. It is one of those journals that can be intimidating to start because of how nice it is. With the beautiful flower paper, you almost feel bad having your ink mess up the beautiful page.

title: Monthly Calendar
text: This is a monthly calendar. Weeks start on Sunday (as they should) and end on Saturday. Paper is thicker than regular planner paper! It has a nice large box for each day. (2.25” square) There are some double days that only get half a square. There is a little note strip to the side of each month. Each month has a generic self-helpy quote. It has a couple vision pages at the beginning and a spending summary at the end. Very simple.

title: Pencil Sharpener
text: I’ve been trying to figure out why this pencil sharpener is so expensive. It does seem so significantly superior to all other electric pencil sharpeners. Does it work? Well, yes it does. Is it somehow magically so much better? Not that I can tell. It still has the problems of a mechanical pencil sharpener. The pencil sharpening mechanism is deeper, meaning shorter pencils become trash. It does have an automatic stop, but that never works with colored pencils. It does have a large shavings area, so you have to empty it less often. The sharpening hole isn’t big enough to accommodate more than a standard sized pencil. The point on the pencil isn’t better than other sharpeners. I still have issues with lead breaking with this one. It is as loud as electric pencil sharpeners usually are. It works. It is fine. I just can’t figure out why it would be any better than cheaper versions.

title: Why Did I Think This Was Small?
text: For some reason, I thought this was a post it sized pad of paper. It is very much not post it sized. It is a 1 ft.². That is quite far from post it sized. Has a lot of area to ride on. There are only 150 sheets, so you couldn’t really use a sheet per day. It has both the annual calendar on the bottom right and an hourly daily tracker on the bottom left. The paper is slightly thick. It doesn’t bleed through with regular pens, felt-tip pens, or even fine point fountain pens. It isn’t card stock, though. So it isn’t going to stand up against Sharpies. It is a nice organization tool. Just be aware of the size! Very, very big!

title: Fit Field Notes D&D Well
text: When I couldn’t find a traveler’s notebook to fit the Field Notes Dungeons and Dragons notebooks, I ordered this portfolio. The notebooks fit well it this portfolio. It isn’t regular notebook sized. It has lots of little pockets and places for pens and various rulers and things.

title: Okay Notebook
text: These travelers notebook inserts are blank. The paper isn’t particularly good. It is on the thin side. It feels about like regular printer paper. So, if you are just going to write in them with a pencil or ballpoint pen, they’re fine. If you are hoping to do art or write with a fountain pen or something fancy— these will likely make you mad. They ghost most pens. They bleed through most markers and paint instantly. These are definitely not for painting or markers! They’d be okay for collage style journaling or writing in (as long as it isn’t wetter ink products).

title: Support
text: I really like this pillow set. You can get great support while sitting in a non-ideal chair. For everyone shifting to working from home, you know the pain of sitting on your wooden dining room chair for way too long working on the laptop. This pillow set turns that dining room chair into an ergonomic office chair! It is comfortable to sit for long periods of time. You can even use it on a bench or in the car.

title: Not Very Sustained
text: These bells are hard to get a sustained “ding” on. We use them for quiz games, and if you smack it like a buzzer, it just “clinks” against the side. To get it to “ding” you have to gently tap the top, and then let go immediately. The little mechanism inside is more of a lever, than a bell I would say. So it doesn’t “ding” easily.

title: Poor Quality
text: My 9 year old always uses pencil grips. He has a hard time holding a pencil properly (ADHD). He loved having a variety of grips to choose from. Any of them work well for him. He just needs a physical reminder of how to hold the pencil. But these are much more cheaply made than other grips we have had. They work fine, but if you have a sensory seeking kid— they don’t last long!

title: Great Notebook
text: This is a really nice notebook. The only complaint I have is that it isn’t refillable. The pages are sewn in. But it is super nice. The paper is thick and soft like hand pressed paper. The paper has no bleed through, even with markers and paint! Great notebook.

title: Passport Size
text: These fit my passport sized travelers notebook perfectly. The paper is decent. The covers are quite thin, but since I use them inside a leather cover, they don’t really matter. I do wish they had a dot grid or blank option. But overall, good little notebook.

title: Field Note Sized
text: If you have a traveler’s notebook, these are Field Note or Pocket sized. They fit perfectly in my pocket sized traveler’s notebook. They are also the perfect size to fit in your actual pocket. These little books are great for keeping lists or reminders. They’re perfect for jotting quick notes. They have a sewn spine and they come in so many colors.

title: Plastic Folders
text: While I think I prefer paper folders, these plastic folders are fine. They work well. They’re a little more study than paper folders. They’re just a little noisy and slip off of each other when you stack them. These have prongs and pockets.

title: Plastic
text: The top of this is not wood. It is plastic molded to look like wood. The stuffing is also pretty low. I didn’t find it to be a good height or really able to adjust well because of how the filling is done and distributed. The cup holder is the size of a can. So it won’t hold a coffee cup, which is what I usually have at my side. All in all, this just isn’t the best lap desk. I have had others that are much better. It works okay. But the surface isn’t smooth, so it isn’t great for writing. It doesn’t adjust to fit you super well.

title: Fits Perfectly
text: These fit my passport size travelers notebook perfectly! They’re a little on the thin side, but inside a cover they work perfectly! I love them. I do wish there were options to have completely blank with no lines. But overall, great little notebook.

title: Not The Same as The Standard
text: These are quite nice. But they aren't quite the same as my gold standard. They do have a pen loop, which I loved. The paper is decent. Pages are not numbered. No table of contents page. There is a pocket inside the back cover. It does have two ribbon markers, but they are thinner than I usually have. They work fine, though. The front page sticks a bit. It comes close to lying flat. All in all, a decent notebook.

title: Black Ink
text: First, the sweet peach pens are black ink. I thought it would be dark peach. It isn't. It is black. They write really well. Nice and smooth with a fairly fine point. The black ink is deeply saturated and looks black on paper. Every pen is the same, there is no variety. The tips are sealed with wax. Really nice pen.

title: Circles
text: I don’t know what magic I thought was going to happen with this. You can draw circles with it. You can draw small circles and medium circles. It is just a little bit of a fancy circle stencil. I’d prefer a compass for accurate angles. But for circles, this does work well. The circles just can’t be very big.

title: English Typos
text: These notebooks are of mediocre quality. The paper is on the thin side. They do not compare to name brand notebooks of this size. They also have serious English issues. One notebook says, "You must take your place in the circle of lifr." (You can't see the typo in the photo because the elastic strap is covering the mistaken r. Even if they had managed to spell "life" correctly, that is a very grim saying to put on a notebook. Hardly inspirational. Maybe funny if you meant it to be inspirational. One notebooks reads like a fortune cookie and says, "Sometimes empty page presents more possibilities." Probably best to skip these. Unless, of course, you're looking for a gag gift.

title: Lightweight
text: This tray was lightweight and easy to assemble. I was a little terrified at point in assembly that I would break the plastic tray. However, those fears were not realized. You could use all three trays separately or only use two stacked if you like. It is easy enough to customize what you need. They stack completely vertically and it is easy to get papers in and out of the trays. Works exactly as I need it to.

title: Notebook
text: These small notebooks are really impressive. I usually use the name brand version that is bigger and these are very similar. They have a little pocket in the front and back, a pen loop, and the elastic strap to close the notebook. It only has one bookmark, which is fine since it is so small. Great little pocket sized books for quick notes and reminders.

title: Highlighters
text: These highlighters are very vivid. They apply easily. We do have some issues with them bleeding through as they do put down a lot of ink. The purple and blue are also a bit dark for highlighting purposes. They do lighten up a little as they dry, but they're still too dark for my liking.

title: Lots of Malfunctioning
text: These pencils look nice, however, there are a few problems with them. They don't come with much lead. They erasers bend and break when trying to erase with them. They're just not firm enough or too long or something. We also have had a lot of problems with them suddenly spitting out the lead or the lead not holding properly while writing. I won't be rebuying these.

title: Super Fine
text: These are very fine tip pens. They write very smoothly. They don't scratch the paper or make me feel like I'm writing with a needle. But the lines are so thin and crisp.

title: Came Broken
text: The back piece came broken. The instructions are very basic, but you can figure it out. Our confusion, I think, was because the back piece was broken so it looked like we had 5 shelves and 1 random plank. The shelves just slide in. The top tray holds with magnets. While that is clever, where mine is sitting, every time someone bumps it, the top bumps off because the magnets aren't very strong. It is also really big. The shelves are too narrow to label.  I'd be happier with it if it wasn't broken.

title: Fits Well
text: This fits my daughter’s hardback Journaling the Word Bible perfectly. It has nice interior pockets for pens and things. It also has a front pocket for extra pens or stickers or post-it notes. It works well and looks nice. It isn’t super durable feeling, but it isn’t cheap feeling either.

title: Big Lined Notes
text: I really like these sticky notes. They’re great for annotating books you don’t necessarily want to write directly on. They also make decent shopping lists. They’re a nice size.

title: Work Well
text: These sticky notes work really well. Each color has its own backing. The color selection is great. They adhere similarly to the name brand version. They are a little difficult to write on the top portion with a ball point pen because of the sticky stuff, but I find that true of most sticky notes.

title: Super Thin
text: I really like this paper for teaching handwriting to kids. I like loose paper more than the notebooks because kids tend to want to destroy mistakes. Really, my only complaint about this paper is the thickness. It is super thin, so it tears really easily. Since it is made for small children, this is clearly a problem. It doesn't erase well, either-- because of the thinness. The paper is also about 1/2" too tall for my three-hole punch.

title: What Happened?
text: These pens used to be so awesome. The pen itself still has the same weight and feel, but the ink is completely substandard. It isn’t very pigmented and doesn’t come out of the pen very smoothly. It makes you feel like you need to bear down more to get it to write better— but that doesn’t help. It just writes very faded and not smoothly at all.

title: Super Thin
text: This paper is so super thin. It is obnoxious. It is difficult to erase because the paper is so thin. I'm also not a fan of it coming glued into a pad. I really would have preferred it to be loose.

title: Not As Great
text: I usually buy the At-A-Glance desk calendar for our family calendar. Since 2020 made me scribble out practically everything on the 2020 calendar, I thought it was awesome to have a school year version so I could go ahead and start over. This is much smaller than the one I usually buy. It is large, but not the biggest available. The paper is on the thin side, so I can't write on it with a Sharpie. One of the corner holders was missing when it arrived. The back isn't very thick. It just overall felt much cheaper than others I have used in the past.

title: Index Cards
text: These are decent index cards. They're just a good as store-brand cards. They run a tiny bit thinner than the nicer name-brand cards. However, for the quantity and price, the slightly thinner card is acceptable to me. I find these work well for study and school purposes.

title: Gel Highlighter
text: I'm not a fan of gel highlighters. I want to like them. I try to like them. They don't show through thin Bible paper. I'm just not a fan of how it crumbles when you highlight with it. It isn't smooth and even when writing. It goes on with chunks like cheap crayons. I've tried various angles and pressure-- but it never goes on smooth.

title: Good Set
text: These are good dual-tipped markers. Every single marker in the pack worked perfectly. You also get a nice zippered cloth storage pouch, which I think is awesome. The markers don't come all neat and organized like the picture-- they look rather haphazard in the pouch. But I'm happy with their performance.

title: So Thin
text: These are amazing! The nib is so fine! The lines are so thin and crisp looking. It is just a fantastic pen. Perfect for writing in a planner! They write really smoothly. I haven’t had any trouble with the roller balls getting stuck like some fine too gel pens like to do.

title: Write Well
text: These pens write well. Much better than the cheapie pens you’d usually buy in bulk. They feel nice in your hand. They also come with a lazy Susan pen holder, which is pretty cool. They have a nib between medium and fine.

title: Decent Cards
text: These index cards are pretty equivalent to the standard store brand index cards. They aren’t super thick or anything. But they are decent cards. Great for buying in bulk.

title: Terrible Cards
text: These are terrible flash cards. They aren’t cards at all. They aren’t even as thick as cardstock. They feel like a cross between regular paper and construction paper. If you’re only going to write on them once and then put them away, sure they’ll work. If you actually use them to look through, they’re never going to hold up.

title: Gets Stuck
text: I like the idea of this clipboard. However, this one gets stuck when opening. It just seems to catch and rub in places. It isn’t super smooth in opening or using.

title: Packaging Is Weird
text: The packaging made it look like a makeup subscription box. However, the journal cover itself is super nice. It is soft and a bit fluffy feeling. It is floppy. The wrap closure is just a long leather strip through a loop on the back of the journal. It has an elastic pen loop. And the included journal is unlined with 3 ribbon bookmarks! The book it comes with isn’t the highest quality, but it is pretty nice compared to the usual filler notebooks. The size is shorter than a standard Leutchtturm notebook.

title: Good Planner
text: The cover of this planner is a little thinner and more flexible than I'd really like. However, the paper is really good quality. It holds up to any pen or highlighter I use. Why buy expensive planners when these work so well?

title: Print Your Own
text: I prefer the lanyard style name tags to these magnetic ones. The magnets do keep people from having to put a pin or adhesive on their clothing. However, some fabrics (like sweaters and sports coats) were a bit thick for the magnets. They held well on t-shirts and button-up shirts. Overall, though, I'd choose the lanyard style over these.

title: Print Your Own
text: These print-your-own name tags are of decent quality. For an event, they work really well. They are a nice, thoughtful touch. They wouldn't be sturdy enough for daily use over a long period of time. But for a week or weekend, they're great.

title: Planner
text: A pretty standard planner. The paper is good quality and thick enough pens and highlighters don't show through. It looks nice. Works well.

title: Giant Calendar
text: This calendar is excellent for long term planning sessions. When thinking through planning the whole year, especially in a meeting setting, this calendar is great. However, for everyday use, I'm just not a big fan. It would be good in a classroom, but it is really not the best for keeping track of things on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis. It is just awesome for long term planning sessions.

title: Pencils
text: These pencils are not sharpened. They are just basic pencils. These used to be nicer. The wood is a little tougher and more difficult to sharpen than they used to be. It just feels like they’ve gone down in quality. They’re usable. They’re fine. They work. They just don’t seem as high quality as they used to.

title: Not Durable
text: These pencils are a great price. I like the amount you get. The quality, well, these seem a little more prone to having issues than other mechanical pencils at their price point. They look higher end, but the break pretty easily. They also have tiny erasers. These aren’t the best for younger kids.

title: Great Set
text: I go through highlighters like crazy. I usually buy Mild Liners, but their price has been creeping up. I decided to give these a try. I really like them. They go on smooth. The chisel tip is nice and firm. There is a nice color assortment. They bleed and ghost about the same as Mild Liners, which is pretty minimal. They do pool a bit at the end of a line, but that is pretty standard. Overall, I’m impressed with these and happy with my purchase. Would definitely buy these again.

title: Love
text: I have tried other bullet journals and I just don’t like them. These are just the best. The page count is just right for a year’s worth of monthly and weekly spreads with several extra pages each month. They hold up really well to daily use.

title: Great Erasers
text: We go through so many erasers! I really like these. They are stiffer and sturdier than the multicolored ones you can buy. They hold up to heavy use a lot better and fit the pencil much tighter. These are now my favorite cap pencil erasers.

title: Massive Calendar
text: I use these huge desk calendars as a wall calendar for our large family. The paper on this is a little thinner than the At-A-Glance versions. All months are the same color. The paper is like regular printer paper thickness, so don’t write on it with a Sharpie or anything. But overall, lots of space to write.

title: Great Printer
text: This is a great printer. The print quality is awesome. The ink wells save you from wasting a ton of ink and a ton of money on ink.

title: Hexagon Panels
text: These stick really easily and well. They are really cute and a great way to jazz up a room a bit. The push pins are completely awful and you should just toss them and buy cute ones. They are on the small side, so your kid’s artwork will completely cover the hexagon. Small things, like business cards, don’t obscure the panels but give them purpose.

title: Cute
text: These stick really easily and well. They are really cute and a great way to jazz up a room a bit. The push pins are completely awful and you should just toss them and buy cute ones. They are on the small side, so your kid’s artwork will completely cover the hexagon. Small things, like business cards, don’t obscure the panels but give them purpose.

title: Smelly Pens
text: I bought these as stocking stuffers for my kids and hen gave a few away in gifts. The kids really like these. The scents re unique for each color. They aren’t super strong, but the kids can sniff and tell hem apart. The pens write well and we didn’t come across any that’s didn’t work.

title: Book Holder
text: These work really well. I purchased them for my children to use for their math books, so they could work on their own paper but have the book easily viewable. It worked well for textbook size and smaller paperback size, as well. Super thick textbooks wouldn’t fit as well. They don’t store super easily. They don’t stack together well. But they do fold up and they are easy to set up. These also work well to hold up an iPad.

title: Eco Tank
text: The eco tank is definitely the way to go! Seriously, this thing has ink that lasts quite a long time. In terms of print quality, it is good. I have used other printers with exceptional printing abilities. This one isn’t bad— it is actually good, but not exceptional.

title: My Favorite
text: These are my favorite highlighters. A couple of the bright colors aren’t very visible. A couple of the darker colors can be a bit much for highlighting. I use these in my Bible, planner, and books. Each marker has a chisel tip on one end and a regular marker tip on the other.

title: Cute Calendar
text: I love the size and look of this planner. The paper is really nice. The set up of this calendar is a bit weird. All of the monthly spreads are up front. All of the weekly spreads are in the back. I actually like that set up, so it isn’t a problem, but it is unusual. The weekly are two weeks per spread, one week per page. My real problem is layout. The weeks on the monthly spreads begin properly on Sundays. Then you turn to the weekly spreads and suddenly weeks begin on Monday. I’m a firmly Sunday week start person, so Monday week starts are a complete dealbreaker for me.

title: Love These
text: These come with the standard Bob books. They workbook is where this is different. The Versa Tiles set sits on top of the workbook opened. Each tile is moved to the answer spot. When you've answered all 8 questions, you close the Versa Tiles box and flip it over to see if the pattern on the bottom matches the answer key. My boys think it is so much fun! And because you're never writing in the workbook, you can use it over and over.

title: Report Covers
text: These are really basic report covers. They have the clear folded sleeve that goes around your paper and then the plastic bar on the edge that you slide over. Amazon Basics makes really nice office supplies-- better than most store brands I have tried.

title: Just As Good As The Name Brand
text: Amazon Basics makes some really nice office products. These binders are the same quality as the name brand and better than most store brands. They have a clear sleeve on the front and back. The rings are nice and smooth. Very satisfied with Amazon Basics.

title: Pretty
text: This glass dip pen is so lovely. I love the way it puts ink on paper. I mostly use it for drawing because you do have to dip it into the ink pretty often. The only thing I dislike is how difficult it is to clean the ink from the tiny grooves toward the tip.

title: Fabulous Pens
text: I'll admit, I'm a bit of a pen snob. I really like these. I love that the set has red, blue, and black pens. I like the variety. The pens write so well. No skipping. The nib is between a fine and medium size. I haven't had issues at all with the ink smearing.

title: Tape Strip
text: I love having this double-sided adhesive on hand. It makes it simple to add non-sticky things to my planner. The size is really great because it can fit in a pencil case easily without taking up much room. The Amazon brand has been as good as other brands I have used in the past.

title: Really Great
text: I’ve used Bob Books for years. They are early readers that kids can actually read and they progress on a sensical basis. The versa tiles aspecthad me skeptical. You have a workbook and you put the open tiles  notebook. The kids move the numbered tiles to answer the questions. When they are done, you close the case and compare the pattern on the back of the tiles to see if they are right or wrong. My five year old loves the tiles. They give a hands on aspect to traditional workbook material. And because you aren’t writing on the book, you can reuse it over and over.

title: Nice Notebook
text: This is a beautiful notebook. It feels nice in hand and the paper is good quality. You don’t get much bleed through or ghosting with the paper. I have had cheaper notebooks that were just as nice. But I cannot find any fault with this notebook.

title: Cute Board
text: This is a nice letterboard. The letters stick well into the felt lines. They are a bit cumbersome to get all the letters out. Cutting with scissors was definitely the fastest way to get them all out. The bag it came with to store the letters was too small to hold all the letters. It also came with an easel like stand that is really cute.

title: Thin Paper
text: This is a very basic calendar. It is full sized. The paper is really thin and my pens ghost and bleed pretty badly. The monthly view has weeks beginning on Sunday. Weekly views begin on Monday. I hate that. There are also half the space for Saturday and Sunday, which is unfortunate for me since those are the busiest days of my week. There are no notes sections for the week either.

title: Thin Paper
text: This is a pretty basic planner. Not a lot of bells and whistles. The paper is a little on the thin side. Also, the monthly calendar has weeks that begin on Sunday, but the weekly view begins the week on Monday. I hate it when calendars do that. There is also half the space available for Saturday and Sunday, which is unfortunate since those are my busiest days of the week.

title: Fun, But Not Fantastic
text: This pen has a very wide nib. It comes with a disposable ink cartridge with black ink. It is a little on the scratchy side, which makes the writing a little less smooth. This would be great to learn with, but it isn't going to give you nice, smooth results. Your lines will be a little bumpy and scratchy. It isn't a bad pen, it just has limitations. If you're just wanting a calligraphy pen to play around with, this pen is great. If you're more serious about your lettering, you'll likely be disappointed.

title: Invisible Mess
text: These do work. They have a glow in the dark ink that you can only see with the special light. However, one of the pens (who knows which one) busted while in shipping and everything was covered in invisible ink. You can feel it on you, but can only see it with the light. It is like an old episode of Room Raiders trying to figure out what you got invisible ink on before you realized you were smearing invisible fluorescent fluid on everything in sight. The kids do like them. I'm not liking having to check for invisible graffiti.

title: Good Sharpener
text: This old school pencil sharpener works really well. It is very solidly built. Three screws hold it into place. You can rotate the size of your pencil. It will accommodate those chubby pencils little kids use.

title: Excellent Planner
text: I'm a little bit of a planner fanatic. I was really surprised at how much I love this one. The cover has a slit at the top of the plastic so you can add in your own personalized cover. (It is standard paper sized, so it is really easy to print something out to put in.  The months are tabbed so you can find them easily. With the spiral binding, it lays completely flat when writing in it or you can even turn the pages back. My only complaint is that they did what many planner makers do and started the weekly weeks on Monday, when the full month week starts on Sunday. Sunday is the first day of the week and I like it to be the first day on the weekly pages. I know that is a personal preference, but I do wish they'd at least be consistent in their choice of when to start to week.

title: Basic Tape Dispenser
text: These are basic tape dispensers. They are weighted, so you can grab tape with one hand. They work well. I like them.

title: Not for Cardstock
text: Printer works well on standard paper. Card stock is another issue entirely- it isn’t good on card stock. But it prints very quickly on standard paper.

title: Little Notebooks
text: I love these smaller notebooks. They are set up on a grid. I’m not an engineer or a field scientist. I use these as small grade books for teaching. They work really well. I have no issues with bleeding or ghosting through the pages.

title: Leather Folder
text: This folder is really pretty. However, the leather is so stiff- it makes this a little bit difficult to use. Cards are a tight fit, so it is hard to get business cards to fit. I think it isn’t as useful as it could be because the pockets are tight with really stiff leather. But the folder looks super nice.

title: Binders
text: These are great binders. The quality is good. They are an everyday use, but not super durable quality. They are great. The rings work well. I have no complaints about these binders.

title: Minion Binder
text: A binder Minion fans will love! This is the quality of an Acery clear view binder, but with Minions! My kids love the fancy binders- so this doesn’t disappoint.

title: Troll Binder
text: A binder every little troll fan will love. It is the quality of an Avery clear view binder, only with trolls on it!

title: Not My Favorite
text: I think I am just not a fan of this style of correction tape. The white strips tend to run off the side of the applicator if you aren’t being super slow and super careful. They are also pretty thin, so I find for my “normal” sized writing, the strip doesn’t cover it. I’ve also had some issues with the white strip moving after I have applied it. Like, shifting around.

title: Hard To Use
text:
I'm a planner junky. This planner has some good parts, but some glaring flaws. The good first:
I like the amount of space in each day. You have two columns on a page. You can either plan for two people (or split your work and personal planning in a side by side manner) for 12 hours (beginning at 7). OR you could plan out the entire 24 hours, using one column for day hours and the other for night hours. Each daily page has a small calendar at a glance at the top of the page for the current month, previous month, and next month. The days are numbered with the current day of the year and how many days are left in the year (3/363, 151/214, 289/76, etc.) This does contain the entire year. The last pages is a three year at a glance calendar. It does list holidays on the pages. It does lay completely flat when open.
Now, the glaring problems. There are no tabs, so finding a given month to jot something on the calendar isn't quick. Sundays do not get a full day. The bottom of Saturday is cut short at 11 hours instead of 12 hour and you get 4 blank lines for Sunday. If you have busy weekends, this may not work at all. (Which is pretty much where I found myself.) There are no transitions between months. No monthly calendar at all. There is only a tiny space (2 lines) to write non- time specific items. You could put washi tape over all the times and just write in whatever you want. My other issue is the inconsistency in the start of the year and end of the year. The calendar starts on January 1st. Which is a Tuesday. No Sunday and Monday for that week is included. You just start your new calendar on Tuesday. But it doesn't end the same way. You would think if they chose to stick to only 2019, the calendar would also end on a Tuesday, December 31st, right? Nope. It ends on January 3rd, which is a Friday. It didn't even finish that week. Just added three extra days at random. That completely bothers me.

title: Big & Lined
text: I had the unlined version for 2018, and I think I prefer the unlined version. It gives me more freedom to write in all the things I need to write in. The lines kind of dictate how large I'll write and how much I can fit in. I hang mine on the wall. I love the plain paper that lets me write with any pen, pencil, or marker. It is very plain, so your plans and writing stand out. No frills. Just a big calendar with plenty of space to write down what you need to write down.

title: Flimsy
text: I’m a calendar junkie. I cannot resist a well made calendar. This one is not too impressive. The pages are thin and glossy. There is no cover or back to hold it more sturdily. It has a piece of cardboard in the package, but it is not attached to the calendar. The boxes are pretty small and the glossy paper limits your pen options. There is a pocket on each month, which I like, but due to the flimsiness of the entire calendar, you can’t put much in the pocket. The wall hanger portion like to move around and will fall out of the coil if you are not careful. The paper really needs to be thicker for this style to work. It really needs to be thicker to be a wall calendar. The colors are nice, but the flimsy paper makes it unusable for me.

title: Cute Set
text: This set has several Journaling items. You have some washi Tape, stickers, die cuts, paper clips, and book marks along with a journal and a pen. The supplies themselves are pretty sub par. You definitely get better quality buying each item individually at a craft store. But as a set, this is cute. Plus the box is a storage box for stationary items. As a gift, it is really cute. My 12 year old loved it. It is definitely more geared toward tweens and young teens.

title: Great Notebook
text: If you’re expecting a Leuchtturm, you’re going to be madly disappointed. That isn’t what this bullet notebook is. It is a standard size notebook. Glued edges. Soft cover. I love this notebook. I use a Leuchtturm for my daily bullet journal. But for my school planning, I like this notebook. For just random notes and thought, working things out on paper, really general use- I love this notebook. I don’t feel like my brain dumps have to be perfect or well thought out. For homeschooling planning, I like having the extra space. It also has fewer pages, so it does fill up faster. For the price, this is a great notebook. I’m not having any issues with bleed through using Micron pens, Stabilo 68s, Stabilo 88s, and Mild Liners. I’m seeing some ghosting, but not enough to bother me.

title: Poorly Planned
text:
I am a planner lover. This planner is such a let down. I’ll walk you through it, but this is not ever a planner I would recommend.
This is a premade planner that is undated. All the pages have a set function, but you fill in the dates for yourself. The cover is hardback with a leatherlike feel. It has three bookmarks sewn into the binding. It is bigger than a standard size bullet journal, but more narrow than an Erin Condren style planner.
The elastic band to hold the planner shut is far too tight. It is very difficult to get it around the planner brand new. As my planners fill up, they bulk up. This elastic has no hope of being at all useful for long. And it really is difficult to get it around the planner.
The cover of the planner is marked. It has a tree and says “productivity planner”. I would like the cover blank or with just the tree.
Each section of the planner (monthly, weekly, and daily) is in its own section. It is not lined up with the month, weeks, and days together for the month. You’ll have three separate places in the planner to flip. This isn’t a problem for me, I actually set my bullet journal up in a similar way.
There are twelve monthly spreads, 2 pages per month. A typical monthly calendar layout with weeks beginning on Sunday. There is a side bar for notes. Across the bottom of each month, you have 4 boxes with numbered entries. There are 5 numbered lines for : goals, priorities, accomplishments, and knowledge gained. You could put washi tape over the headers and make these fit your life better.
Then you reach the weekly section. Only 23 weekly spreads. Not sure how that math works out. The weekly spreads have specific boxes on a two page spread. You have room for 5 successes and 5 improvements each week. A small box with new skills to acquire. A small box to focus on. You have a very specific list of plans for your week: about me, work, family & friends, and relationship. Then you have five project boxes to fill in. And five goals for the week.
Then you get to your daily pages. No, there are not enough for the entire year. There are enough (plus a couple extra) for those 23 weeks if you only fill them out Monday to Friday. Each two page daily spread has a schedule for the day where you write in the time and task. There is a small space for a daily to-donlist and a small box where you write in why today is special. So specific. You also list your top five priorities of the day, your affirmations, and what you are grateful for.
At the end you have a few pages of mind maps and vision boards. This planner is so specific, while leaving you to fill in the dates. I feel like it is trying to be the Passion Planner, but it isn’t the Passion Planner. It is also poorly planned. Either give me 52 weekly spreads OR 365 daily spreads. Don’t give me an inadequate number of both.
The paper is fine. A little on the thin side for a planner, so ghosting and bleed through can definitely be a problem.

title: Field Notebook
text: This field notebook is not typical field book size. When I think field book, my brain says 3x5. This book is 5x8. The cover is nice and durable. Cardstock, but with a nice texture and finish that keeps it looking pretty good. It has math helps and notes inside the front covers. I don’t use my field books for actual engineering purposes, so all of that is a waste for me. The paper is a nice thickness. I had minimal ghosting and no bleed through, even when using a Sharpie. One side of the page is little rectangular boxes. The other side is larger. So, each two page spread, you get both. Really, my only complaint is that this book hates being open. It doesn’t lay flat. It takes a lot of bending and breaking the cover in to get it to open well enough to use the whole page well. And then once you get the cover broken in, it doesn’t like fully closing. The pages are sewn together, though the cover is glued on. So the pages don’t fall out with all the breaking in.

title: Guided Math Workshop
text: This book is intended for classroom use. I am a homeschool mom, not a teacher. This book is reproducible for classroom use. This is a system to model math in a classroom setting. You can adapt this for homeschool. There are worksheets that are used in conjunction with a rotation through math stations. The worksheets don't give very much practice. I don't find this to be meaty enough to be a math curriculum by itself. However, it is too much to be a supplement. In a classroom setting, I can see it working. But it the homeschool setting, it just doesn't have much of a use unless you do a "school at home" approach to your homeschool, which I do not.

title: Math Workshop 5
text:
I am a homeschool mom, so I am often on the lookout for educational helps. This workbook is allowed to be reproduced in the classroom setting. The “workshop” set up is intended for classroom group work done through stations.
Each section has a an essential question, a math warm-up, a mini-lesson, “math talk” (questions to ask about solving problems), and a journaling question. You then have guided math questions and worksheets- one worksheet is recommended, one is on level but branching out a bit, and one worksheet is enrichment. All answers are in the back of the workbook.
As a homeschooler, this could be used as enrichment. You could simply take the worksheets or hands on activities and use those to supplement curriculum you’re already using. You could also use the entire model as complete curriculum. The workshop model would work just fine for one kid just like it would for 20. It is going to be pretty teacher intensive and they aren’t going to be able to complete this as a curriculum completely independently. You would still need to give the mini-lessons. But some kids do better with having someone show them and walk through it with them. You can also fold the entire thing in with your current curriculum, using this to beef up a curriculum that has a few more holes.
This book covers:
Operations (PEMDAS) and Algebraic Thinking
Number Operations in Base Ten
Number and Operations of Fractions
Measurement and Data
Geometry
There are also a few extras in the back for games you could play for a number of different skills.

title: Good Quality
text: These are really good file jackets. I find them to be good quality. They work well and are just as well made as the name brand versions.

title: Big Calendar
text: I bought this desk pad to go on my wall. I hate the glossiness of standard wall calendars, so I opted for this one. It is really large. There is so much space to write in each day. It does have corner protectors on the bottom corners. It is very simple and plain, but works perfectly. The paper is thick and nice to write on.

title: Mediocre Set
text:
I have several hand lettering pens from various brands. This set is not my favorite. The instructional sheet is much less than helpful. I have taken a couple lettering classes and read quite a few lettering books, and these instructions sound like someone who never hand lettered anything wrote them. They tell you your paper options are wide ruled paper or grid dot paper, noting nothing about paper texture and if rough or smooth paper will work best with their markers. Just throw the instructions away.
The large black permanent marker isn’t quite black enough. One side of it has a massive chisel tip, the other side a very small marker tip. There is no normal size tip. You get jumbo or small. These all bleed through paper. Even with a light touch, the ghosting is really bad. The sides of the marker are also not labeled, so you just have to open both ends to find the tip you were looking for.
The chisel tip marker is more like a calligraphy marker. It also isn’t very black and bleeds through paper.
The 05 Fine Tip pen is similar to a micron, but the Prismacolor 05 is larger than my micron 05. It is closer to the micron 08 tip. It also bleeds through. The black on it, I think is the exact same, but looks a bit better because of the smaller size.
The brush tip is a small felt brush tip. It is not very firm at all. And it bleeds through.
The two pencils are fine, I guess. They come unsharpened. The eraser is good.
Overall the set isn’t bad, it just isn’t great. There are great products out there, these are just mediocre art supplies.

title: Nice To-Do Lists
text: I am really liking this weekly calendar. It has lots of space to put my daily to-do list and then hang it on the wall so it doesn’t get tucked away and forgotten. The wood trim is actually printed on the paper.

title: Love It
text: This chair looks fabulous. I love the way it looks. The cushion is really sturdy. It is pretty wide. Very sturdy. It was super simple to put together. I’m really digging it.

title: Good Oragnaized Pencil Case.
text: I really like this pencil case. Now, the slots to slide your pencils in are really narrow. My Stabilo pens fit, though I do have to kind of twist them into their spots. Micron pens are too big. Zebra mildliners are too big. You can get them in if you fight for it, but then getting them in and out is a very difficult task. So, if you’re actually needing to use your pens, that would be a problem.It has three pen holder “pages”. Two of those “pages” are removable. You can use one for your smaller pens or pencils and then just dump the rest of your pens into the bottom. It also has pockets in the front for other various items you might need. It wouldn’t fit a ton of stuff, but maybe a couple kinds of washi, some white out, some paper clips or page tabs, an eraser, a small pencil sharpener- that sort of thing. Standard sized pencils fit easily. It zips really easily and is very portable but also sits on it’s sides easily in storage. I’m really happy with it.

title: Brush Tip Highlighters
text:
I like these highlighters, I’ll say that first. I have no idea why they decided to put a brush tip on a highlighter. A standard chisel tip can do thick and thin lines, so I’m not understanding why they chose to make a brush tip highlighter. We’re not going to be doing hand lettering with a highlighter. If this was a box of colored highlighters, I’d understand. But basic yellow highlighters with a brush tip just doesn’t seem like a thing the world needs.
The brush tip is a felt brush tip. So, there are no little hairs to separate and go crazy. It is an easy brush tip to use. I like the amount of highlight it provides. It is a little more difficult to keep going in a straight line across words because of the brush tip. But it does seem to saturate more than a chisel tip. Despite it seeming to drop more ink, I don’t have any bleed through, even on Bible pages. There is some ghosting, but I find that you can’t avoid that with Bible paper unless you’re using gel highlighters, which have their own issues. You’re not going to get a tidy block of highlighting. The brush tip is going to leave it start and stop places a little thinner that the rest of the line it makes.
All in all, I like these. I don’t understand the market for them, but I do like them. They work well. These are comfortable in hand. The textured grip sits nicely against your finger. The actual pen itself is a kind of matte plastic finish, so it feels nice in your hand, as well.

title: Great Printer
text: This printer is awesome. I love the new eco tank concept. It works so much better than cartridges. They stay full for longer and you get to use all your ink. The print quality is great. The ink lasts a really long time. I’m very happy and impressed with this printer for a variety of uses. Plain black and white documents to full color graphic design on photo finish paper.

title: Good Pen
text: I really like the pen. It writes well. It is a great size point. The felt tip doesn’t feather or fall easily. My only complaint is the pen color and the ink color do not match. I would honestly rather then ink match the pen. The pen is a deep burgundy. The ink is a bright red.

title: Great Solution
text: I got so tired of my kids completely destroying pencils and leaving them all over the house. Inevitably, the pencil part would last longer than the eraser, then we were dealing with additional erasers. It just became a mess. So, I grabbed these golf pencils WITH erasers. Now the eraser lasts as long as the pencil. I’m still finding pencils all over my house, but at least they are intact now and not broken to bits. Plus, they all came presharpened, which meant I just had to dump them into the pencil bucket! No sharpening necessary.

title: Works Well
text: My boys love this desk. It really works well for fidgety kids who end up on the floor trying to do their school work. However, I have a couple issues with the desk. It is one solid piece. It does not fold up. It does not store in any simple or easy way. It is just there and big when not in use. Also, the table top isn't weight bearing. I'm always worrying they'll try to lay across it or sit on it in their wallowing. I'm just always reminding them not to sit or lay on the top.

title: Excellent
text: I love this new printer trend toward refillable ink tanks rather than cartridges. It is so much more economical, less wasteful, and the tanks stay full so much longer! Plus, when you are down to that teeny tiny bit in the bottom, you don’t have to waste it! Just refill the tank on top of it instead of throwing that tiny bit of ink away. This printer is great. I have no complaints about the quality of the printed pages. It is on the larger side, but that isn’t a problem for me.

title: Classic
text: I love this notebook. The paper is dreamy. It is smooth and pretty thick. I have not had any problem with ghosting or bleed through. I usually use Stabilo 88s and Zebra Mildliners in this notebook. There are plenty of pages. Double bookmarks, though I am wishing I had a third bookmark. Table of contents up front. Envelope in the back cover. And the handy elastic loop to keep it lol closed.

title: Love
text: I got these to refill my traveler’ Notebook. These fit perfectly. I like the feel of the paper. No ghosting, even when I use a fountain pen. The pages don’t hold up extremely well with watercolor or paint, but that is pretty standard. You can use watercolor if you make an effort to keep the pint as dry as possible or use it very minimally.

title: Love These
text: Print your own stickers! The actual stickers are white. They are similar size to oil label stickers. I got these for use in my planner and love that I can print whatever on my own stickers! They are matte, so you can write on them, as well. The template for making them is on Avery's website. I'm really happy with these! Easy to use.

title: Massive Index Cards
text: These are HUGE index cards. Lined on one side. Plain on the other. They are on the thin side, about like cardstock. They do run through a standard printer without issues. I really like these index cards.

title: Good Cards
text: I like these index cards. They are standard sized and come in 4 bright colors. One side is lined, one is blank. You get 75 of each of the four colors. The 300 cards are 3 packs of 100 cards wrapped and then all 300 are wrapped again. So, you're getting 3 individually wrapped 100 packs of cards. These, as I have found with all the Amazon Basics Index Cards, are a little on the thin side for index cards. That works fine for my uses. I can't find the exact paper weight on the cards, but it is a little thinner feeling than 110lb. Cardstock.

title: Monthly Planner
text: This is a MONTHLY calendar. Not the daily or weekly thing. It is much trimmer and fits in your bag much more easily. Each box is about 1.75 inches. The cover is leather-like and soft. The inner covers are gold marble paper. The paper on this is much thicker than standard planner paper. Each page has a light marble effect. This planner runs from August 2017- December 2018. The edges of the pages are rounded. Each month has space for notes in the side column. There are 7 lined pages for notes at the end of the planner. The planner is slightly larger than a standard size weekly planner, but slimmer. It is really pretty and really well done. I love the colors.

title: Good File Folders
text: Good, basic file folders. I go through a lot of file folder since I often use them for crafts and homeschooling reasons. These are great file folders. Just basic file folders. I'm happy with them.

title: Good Printer
text: This is a really nice printer. It prints well. It is not the quickest, it seems to prep a lot before it actually starts printing. Setting up the ink was simple. I also love that I can visibly see the ink levels on the outside of the printer. The ink comes in bottles and you open and pour the bottles of ink into the wells on the printer. This printer holds a lot of ink! The wireless set up was pretty complicated. It took about half an hour and multiple attempts to get it paired with our wireless router and ready to print. And as a homeschool mom, I love the ability to make copies without having to run to the office supply store to do so.

title: New Favorite Pen
text: These pens just changed my life. Why have I not heard about these before now? They are THE MOST amazing pens. My usual love is PaperMate Flair. These are even better! So many awesome colors. Super fine, strong tip. No bleeding through paper. Some ghosting with the darker colors, especially if you are really making some thick lines. Can letter, draw, or color with these bad boys. Super smooth. Awesomely saturated colors that don't bleed!  These have quickly become my new favorite pen!

title: Okay Tabs for Study or Temporary Marking
text:
I'm a school supplies fanatic. I buy and use way more stickers and tabs than a grown adult probably should. These tabs are just okay. First, the holes don't line up for my FiloFax style planner. They are 3 ring binder, mini 3 ring binder placement. So, the clip and go insn't really the case for me. The tabs themselves are really thick cardstock-like material. That makes them very easy to write on with no smearing and you can use any pen or pencil for the job. But that also means they aren't waterproof and they don't hold up extremely well for long term use. Short term, they are fine and good. The sticker part is clear, but more of a frosty matte clear. You can definitely still see it over the page, but you can read the words under it if you need to. They peel off easily and are repositionable up to a certain point. Putting them in is definitely not permanent. The sticker part of the tab is really thick and not very bendable.
You get 8 of each color of the large tabs. And 10 of each color of the small tabs.

title: Reliable Pens
text: While I like these pens, I'm not going to lie and say they are the best. They are reliable, like the Bib Crystal pen. This medium point is pretty big (1.0). The ink isn't as saturated in color as nicer pens. On paper it looks like a cheap ball point pen in color. But it is clickable, which I like. The entire outside is plastic. The grip is slightly textured, which is usually comfortable for me. (Unless I happen to quickly grab it wrong, then it isn't so comfortable.) The pens are really basic, but reliable pens.

title: Nice Pens
text: These pens are awesome! They don't smear at all. They write really smooth. I usually like a fine point, but these don't actually seem too thick. I usually like less than 0.5mm points, but these write so nice and smooth, the added mm's don't bother me at all. The distance from the grip to the point is a little shorter on these than other pens I use, so that took a little getting used to. Each pen comes sealed, with a little ball of wax on the tip to keep the ink from drying out. I'm really a fan of these.

title: Thin
text: These cards are good. They are lined on one side, blank on the other. I like the texture of the card surface, it is a little rough. The only real problem I have with the cards is that they are on the thin side. Certain pens and markers show right through because of the thinness. And they don't hold up extremely well. For my uses, they are okay, but for many, the flimsiness would be a deal breaker for these. They aren't as thick as standard cardstock, but a little heavier weight than regular paper.

title: So Adorable
text: These pens are so stinking cute! I absolutely love them. Mine came with 2 dark green, 2 bright green, and 1 sage green pen. They are all very fine tip gel pens and THEY ALL HAVE BLACK INK. I wasn't aware they would all be black ink, but that is fine with me. Just something that should be pointed out. The lids do not fit on the top of the pen while you are writing. You can place it on one of the cactus "arms" and it will stay, though it rattles around a bit and doesn't exactly "fit" there.

title: Dark, Muted Colors
text: These pens are beautiful! The colors are just amazing. I'm normally a fine tip or micro tip person. These are bold. The tips seem huge to me. But the colors are so amazing. And the writing is so smooth. A couple of them bleed on certain papers. They definitely show through paper on the thinner. But the colors are so beautiful, I don't even care. They smear on shiny paper. They take time to dry or they'll smear. I know all this makes them sound awful. But the colors. I give them 5 stars despite all of this. And I would absolutely buy them again.

title: Classic
text: I go through highlighters. I'm not even sure how. These are neon yellow. I read several reviews saying they weren't neon, but they are. They are the fat, chisel tip, neon yellow highlighters. I like these. Classic. Cheap enough that I don't have to feel bad about how many I end up going through.

title: LOVE
text: I love this pen. The fine nib is perfect. It isn't super fine. Ink flows smoothly and doesn't pool. The fill able ink cartridge works really well. I love it. I'm new to fountain pens and this one is the perfect introduction. It feels heavy in the hand. Writing is superb.

title: Great Ink
text: This ink is such a beautiful color. It is deep and pigmented. It is thin and easily usable in a fountain pen. (Pilot fine nib) The color is reddish orangish brown. Very beautiful and unique. Additionally, the jar is huge. 3 oz. of ink is a lot of ink!

title: Good Markers
text: These are great markers. I bought mine for Bible journaling, since these do not bleed through thin Bible pages. You get a 01, 02, 03, 05, 08, graphic 1, and brush pen in this set.

title: Great Pens
text: These pens are amazing. They write super smooth and fine. Sometimes fine point pens feel scratchy on the paper, not these. They are so smooth. The color is also very true black. No smearing. My only problem with these pens is that people keep stealing them. I can't say I really blame them. They are great.

title: Just Okay
text: I'm slightly obsessed with notebooks, but this one just did not meet my high expectations. The color is nice. The gold accent on the front is a nice touch. The paper is fine. It is slightly thicker than standard notebook paper, but pretty rough in feel. Not like the super nice buttery feel of nicer pressed paper. Grey lined front and back with no margin lines. The date oval only appears on the right hand pages (the front of each page). My main complaint is the finish on the cover. It looks nice and feels nice until it gets the slightest bit beat up. It just marks up way too easily. I would also like the notebook to be a bit longer and have a satin bookmark ribbon (which would be simple with the binding style). There is also nowhere to place any identification on the notebook. No place in the front cover for this book belongs to. That isn't the biggest deal. I just made a clear sticker with my name for the inside of the front cover. Honestly, I would just expect more from a notebook at this price point.

title: REALLY Good Printer
text:
**UPDATED**
I initially gave this printer 4 stars based on my use making color copies from my HP Desktop computer on Microsoft Word. My feelings on that are the same. However, after using it with my MacBook, I'm upping my review to five stars, simply because it does excel in some key areas for me. I don't have the settings issue with the Mac and this printer, which is funny since I have them going from HP to HP, but not from Mac to HP. Go figure. There is really no set up on the Mac. Your wifi finds the printer and you use it. Easy. This printer also is great with cardstock. My Brother laser printer slightly rolls my cardstock. It is an annoying issue I have just always dealt with. This printer, no rolling or curving my card stock. It is flat when it comes out of the printer! It also doesn't skip or have feed issues with cardstock like my previous Lexmark printer was prone to. So, it does a better job than some other very expensive printers that I own. The image quality stays crisp, even when doing all black and even when doing draft quality. That is pretty impressive. So, despite the small draw backs of settings issues with my HP, this is a REALLY good printer.
I like this printer. The only reason I wouldn't give it a full five stars is because of one issue I have with the settings. It connects easy enough. The printer walks you through setting it up. It doesn't hold much paper. Around 20 sheets seems to be about all it can hold. It has no tray, so be aware of that when it is spitting out copies. Ink was simple to install. It does work while it is charging. My other issue is the settings. It ignores whatever I put in on my computer end. Like, I say on Microsoft Word to print 5 copies, it ignores that. You have to open the printer settings every time the printer box pops up when you choose this printer and change the settings you need changed there. Also, the power saver mode turns the printer off. It doesn't reawaken when you click "print". You have to go to the printer and manually push the power button, wait about 30 seconds, then click "print" on the computer. You don't have to use the power saver mode. It does give you options on that.
If you need to print a lot of stuff very often, this is not the printer for you. If you need to print one or two things every now and then, this is the printer for you. It would work well for students. It does fold down to a pretty compact size.

The plastic is light and seems a little cheap, but the feel of the blade cutting through the paper is satisfying, clean and easy to use.  I love how easy it is to line up pages and cut squarely.  But again, I just don't think it has a the power to cut through many pages at once or over the years.  But for what it is, I'm impressed with its functionality.

title: Very Nice Mechanical Pencil
text:
I have to admit, I have a thing about mechanical pencils. For me, the Pentel Graphgear 1000 is the stand out mechanical pencil. It makes me feel rich just holding one because of its weight and feel in the hand. Very few other pencils rival them, but this one does. Both have retractable tips, although this pencils extension and retraction is the same action as the lead advance. It is just a difference of pressure that either toggles the point in and out or advances the lead. For the Graphgear, these are separate actions which made for a little adjusting for bringing more lead out.

Otherwise, the richness of weight and feel were very similar. I would be happy with either. Sadly, I took this pencil on a flight last weekend and set it on the empty seat next to me and it rocketed off under the seats ahead of me and disappeared. I will miss it.

This actually could become a go to mechanical pencil if the price is good. Currently the price is not listed, but a Graphgear is usually around $14-$20 and if this one falls $10 and below, this would be a great mechanical pencil for price and quality.

title: Great for Graphic Project Work
text: I use a lot of loose leaf graph paper for sketching out page designs for book and web sites and thought this would be nearly perfect for allowing me to have graph paper on one side and place for notes on the other.  And I was right.  I really like the idea of this design for my graphic layout.  The paper is decent, I'm only giving four stars because my pages looked a little beaten up despite being plastic wrapped and appearing to have come through shipping undamaged.  But when I unwrapped the paper, many of the pages had small bends. Otherwise, a lot to like here.

title: Wonderfully Intricate and Detailed
text: This Christmas card has a lot of Wow factor.  It opens up beautifully and dramatically and I cannot wait to send it out to someone special.  In fact, I think I'm ordering a few more.  The branches are delicate and detailed, the overall design, simple and elegant.  I don't know that I can say anything better than "Wow!"  Highly recommend.

title: Cute, Elegant and Good Wow factor
text: I really like this card.  For the size and price, the pop up is rather subdued which is nice and classy and still has a lot of visual punch.  I like the sentiment written in it and happily sent it off as soon as I got it.  It is a perfect, beautiful and classy card.  Keep coming up with more like these.

title: A Very Nice Little Journal
text:
Ok, I do not plan to use this journal as a fitness journal in anyway. It seems like the only fitness specific thing about this journal is the two sample pages that are scrawled with fitness references. But for me, the dotted notebook format is perfect. The dots allow a grid for printing on, sketching paintings in square frames, working website pages, making lists with perfectly formed check boxes. I could not think of a better format than this. I actually just wish they had left the sample pages out. I'm ok with the breath cover because for me it says relax, not work out.

The journal is good quality and it will stand up to the paces I will take it through. The paper is thick, although not sharpie thick, but definitely pen thick. There would be bleed through with markers. All in all, this is a great journal.

text:

The one criticism I have is that each pad is individually wrapped then overwrapped which seems like a waste of packaging. But perhaps that makes sense in warmer, humid climates. Here it just seems like a waste of plastic.

title: So Far So Good
text:
I received these Author replacement cartridges a while ago, but it turns out, it took a long time to finally use up the black cartridge. I simply replaced it with the black from this set and everything looks fine. I really can't tell the difference between the OEM and this cartridge as far as print quality goes. I wish I could try a color cartridge but we don't seem to print enough to be even close to replacing one of them.

I have had mixed performances with third party toners in the past, but so far these seem pretty good. The price is hard to beat for chipped cartridges so it is hard to go OEM for so much more. Will update if I see any issues.

title: Love It!!
text: We do a lot of coloring with colored pencils for different rendering and sketching.  We have only had a hand sharpener in the house and I cannot tell you wonderful this works.  I have used a number of electric sharpeners in the past and this one is quiet and effective.  It just chews through the pencils in no time and leaves a wonderfully sharp point.  The clear plastic is good for showing when it is getting full, but it also tends to look a little messy. Otherwise the design is very pleasant and elegant and looks good on the art table.  Love it!

title: Received Wrong Product, Perhaps for Best

I will have to order a cork board separately, but I think I'm going to be happier with two full sized boards.  We had it received and mounted on the wall in about 20 minutes and it works well.

title: Easy Setup and Use, Very Fast
text:
I am increasingly impressed by the speed of this printer, it is far faster than anything I have had at home before. I was equally impressed how quickly I had it out of the box and up and running. The copying feature is great and all in all, I am very happy with this printer. I am now inkjet free in the house and hopefully will keep it that way. (okay I have one for special print jobs on CD/DVD's but it is in the closet now.)

The prints are crisp, and toners are not cheap but hopefully will be on par with ink cartridges that it is replacing. Recommend this for a budget laserjet.

title: So Far So Good!
text:
Printers are love or hate relationships and so far I am still in the newly wed stage. The setup went well and easy. It has been holding WiFi so far with no networking issues. I'm in IT and I can vouch that that is a hard thing to say about a lot of wireless printers, so I'm feeling good about this printer.

I am also very happy to be off of inkjet printing for color. I can't tell you how many times I've realized that I haven't used my ink jet in months and it becomes an all day job to clean heads and get a decent print again. So happy to have a good color laserprinter with a decent feature set. The only thing I find myself wishing for is a document feeder, but at this price point I guess you can't have it all.

Print quality is definitely good. I can't say great, but definitely passable for all our needs from work to school projects and printing images for art references. I've seen better, but again, a step up from even my best inkjet printer so an improvement for our household.

If I had any criticisms, it would be that it is pretty darn big and since it is a new printer, there are not third party toner cartridges available when I looked and new toners are pricey at this time. But that is just part of the game.

All in all, still in love with this printer after a month.

title: A Very Good Staff Paper Notebook

title: A Decent, but not quite Sharpie quality marker set.
text:
This is a great selection of colors, although definitely a step below Sharpies for quality. The tips seem to break apart with too much force in a way that I don't see with Sharpies. They still work, but the fineness of the lines is affected. Otherwise I really do like these markers and I have used them several times with my kids for various art projects. I love that small box they come in despite the fact that it was plain cardboard. It is a wonderfully small packing size and has gone into our road trip bag.

A decent marker set for a reasonable price.

title: Nice Idea, wish the dry erase worked better
text:
We were looking to get these as gifts for our kids' coaches as a thank you gifts. Glad we got one before purchasing this one en masse. It concept it is great and we are still looking for a solution like this for thanking the coaches, but this one falls short in a couple areas. While it feels like it is constructed well enough this does not seem to be the same material that our white board is made out of. First, the dry erase pen does not erase well (or work particularly well.) We used both the included pen and some of our dry erase pens and it does not wipe off easily or cleanly. I almost want to put a plastic sheet on it to keep the surface clean. Second, some of the field outline is peeling or scraping off.

This board is fine, but I think there is a better manufactured product out there.

title: Nice Naturally Decorated 17 month Calendar
text:
I was looking for a calendar to schedule my "wasted time" or non money making/bucket list project and the cover sentiment fills the bill pretty well. Love that It starts with August 2017 but makes it kind of timely to get it sooner than later. The biggest failing I see in it is that the individual day boxes are small and they do not give much room for notes. The design is nice and matches my natural history project.

There are a couple of blank pages in the back, one page labeled birthdays/addresses one labeled notes and a dozen perforated strips labeled as notes. So there is room for notes, but not much. I like this very much visually but I could use a little more flexible notes space. All in all a nice calendar.

title: Good quality labels
text:
OK, first I have to admit, I did not pay for these, I got a reviewer box of these labels. This is important in this case because I was looking at getting some large labels for some time and kept balking at the price. Right now they are over 13 cents a piece and $67 for the box. I love the simplicity of using these labels, but I still have pretty bad sticker shock. But with shipping ebay sales etc, I guess it is just the cost of business these days.

What I do like about Avery labels in general is their easy to use templates you can download. (Well easy if you have admin rights to your computer as the template installer is a little more complicated than it needs to be.) The templates make printing fairly consistently successful and save on waste from trying to line things up through trial and error.

They labels are rather thick and high quality and work well both in my personal inkjet as well as my work laserjet and make clean sharp images. I have even used these to make cute little labels to relabel wine bottles for gifts and they stick rather well for the gift giving purposes as long as they stay dry.

All in all, these feel like high quality stickers. They have had no issues going through my printers. The printing is crisp and the adhesive backing is firm and easy to peel. Everything you would want in a label, but a little on the expensive side.

text: Great quality! I have shipped many many packages with these mailers some very fragile and they have held up well. I have not had any package arrive damaged. Very flexible and easy to fit objects inside that are odd shaped. Seals Very well!

title: Nice notebooks
text: Nice little, fat notebooks! Received just what I thought I would.

title: As close to a $100 Canon toner cartridge you can get!
text: This toner cartridge far exceeded my expectations.  I have tried other aftermarket toner cartridges and the black is always light. I think for the money I save over buying the $100 Canon cartridge, I can live with it.  The Arthur Imaging toner cartridge is just like a Canon toner cartridge with respect to the print quality.  I have recommended the Arthur Imaging toner cartridge to two other people and they were also extremely happy with the print quality.  The Arthur Imaging toner cartridge is a few dollars more than the other aftermarket toner cartridges but it is well worth the money.

title: Great but ….

title: Best printer I've ever owned

You may also want to search for Doors on Display - another set of note cards that includes this cover and several other shots of doors. This is my favorite of the Doors on Display set. title: Spiral on top allows me to easily use both sides of each page
text:
I've been using these notebooks for work projects for about a year. Professional looking but still functional. Spiral on top allows me to easily use both sides of each page.

April 2016 Update - Still my go-to notebook for work. Haven't found anything better. Every notebook I've purchased from Amazon has arrived in great shape. No bent covers as mentioned by another reviewer.

title: Five Stars

title: Just ok
