text: I needed coin wrappers and these fit the bill, but it seems to me like they are very flimsy compared to my older ones. Anyway, they worked, and that’s what mattered.

title: Highlighter Pencils
text:
The problem with regular highlighters is that they are too wet and bleed through when using them to highlight pages in a Bible. There are specialty highlighters that are made for Bible study and these are reminiscent of crayons. This is the first set I have seen that is more like colored pencils, and so far I am pleased with them. They work well.

These are basically fluorescent yellow colored pencils, when you step back and look at them with no context. That's not a complaint but an observation. Because they use a dry filament as does a pencil, these will not soak a page and bleed through. When the tips are sharper it takes a little more effort to highlight with these, but once the tip dulls a bit they give good, even coverage.

These are all wood pencils that are not made in China. That packaging claims these are made in Austria. They have a quality feel to them and are a bit larger than regular pencils so I think they will last longer than cheap pencils.

I like these highlighters, quite a bit. Being more like pencils than pens, these don't soak the page and bleed through and they won't dry out either.

title: Decent Small Dry Erase Surface
text:
I selected these dry erase cards for use in my office. My manager writes on every surface available and has on more than one occasions taken my personal clipboard-sized board to write on. Normally I need a small space for writing and I don’t like using up sticky notes or notebook pages unless it is for something at least semi-permanent. These seemed like a good solution to me, and so far they are working out well.

These are index-sized cards, and there are ruled cards as well as blank in the pack I received. It should be noted that packs with just one type or the other are available; I deliberately chose these to get both types.

These have the feel of plastic-coated playing cards, without the texture. They’re flexible and light, and while in most cases they should be fine be aware that they can be bent and ruined. Their intended use is probably more in line with classroom use, for teaching. They’re ideal for flash cards and even short answer games, though for something like flash cards I would expect a more permanent solution would be better unless there is limited supply.

These seem to erase fairly easily too. Be careful when trying to erase when wet, as the marker can smear off the card and onto the surface you’re working on. I have not let any writing stay on these for very long so I do not know yet how susceptible they are to staining.

Because of the small writing surface, I would recommend using a fine-point marker unless writing something large over multiple cards such as flash cards and alphabet letters.

So far these answer the need I have. They’re better suited for classroom use than office use, but in my case they’re a good solution.

title: Good Password Book
text:
I selected this book for storing all my passwords after realizing that should something happen to me, my family would have no access to several important accounts, spread across the Internet. I do not use a common password for everything so giving a single password isn't enough, and I have enough different log-ins out there that keeping track is tedious. A book like this is a good option.

This book is fairly straightforward and has spaces for website names, log-ins, passwords, and notes with sections based on alphabetically ordered tabs. That's probably all that's needed for most sites. Each page has enough room for four different sites and/or log-in combinations. There is also a section at the beginning for keeping track of a small number of contacts - not enough to be a replacement for an address book but enough for important contacts like family and legal.

I like the size of this book. It's just the right size to fit in a bag or briefcase. It also seems to be well-made with a leather-like cover to keep the cover water resistant and it is stiff enough to handle some time in a book bag without taking damage. It even has a couple of nice touches, including a loop for holding a pen, a pocket for holding papers or even a CD/DVD or two, and a ribbon marker to mark a page for later.

Overall, I am happy with this little password book. It's made well, seems to be well-thought-out and it has a nice feature set.

title: Very Nice Spiral Notebooks
text:
My wife uses notebooks for all manner of things around the house - tracking meals and spending, making lists, keeping track of when appointments are coming, and a lot more. I selected these notebooks with that thought in mind, that she would use these for keeping up with stuff in the house. These have proven to be decent notebooks so far.

Instead of a thin cardstock-type of cover, these have a poly cover that will not easily rip or tear easily, and that has a couple of benefits. First, it will provide longer protection for the pages in the notebook. Second, the color makes identifying the notebook easy (distinct from others in the pack due to color) without concern that the cover will go away.

The pages are perforated and make tearing out sheets easier. It's not difficult at all to get straight, clean edges on pages that are removed. I personally like that the pages are college ruled, so there is better use of room for writing more.

These are decent spiral notebooks and they will get used up over time in my house. They're made well and the colors make them easy to tell apart when using different notebooks for different purposes.

title: Better than Average Spiral Notebooks
text:
I have used my share of composition notebooks as well as spiral-bound notebooks over the years. I prefer the traditional composition notebooks over spiral-bound, but for spiral bound notebooks these are just fine and will serve well.

The main thing these have in common with traditional or standard composition notebooks is the cover. The cover has that distinctive black-and-white design and the cardboard is a little thicker than with normal spiral-bound notebooks so they'll wear better in a book bag. These are easy to identify and will last a bit longer than other notebooks.

The pages are perforated and are relatively easy to tear out. It's easy to get a clean, straight edge on these when they're torn out. They're also college-ruled too so there is more room for straight writing. There are some charts on the inside covers too, which may or may not be helpful depending on how these are to be used, though it's clear these are designed for students.

These have attributes of both composition notebooks and spiral-bound notebooks. They're superior to normal notebooks. If you need notebooks with removable pages and are made to stand up to some abuse in a book bag, these are a choice to consider.

title: Eye Catching and Well Made
text:
I selected this journal with the intent of using it in the office as a way to track "tribal lore" as well as keep project notes and important bits of data that I need to avoid misplacing. I wanted something a little more distinct than a plain notebook or scratch pad and this seemed like it had some potential. I have not used it for that stated purpose, but I am pleased with it and so far it has worked out for me.

This is a nice leather-bound journal with hand-made paper pages that is very distinct and artisanal. Unlike some other journals like this that I have seen, the pages are permanent and are not intended to be refilled when all used, so keep this in mind if you're looking for a journal that you can use repeatedly without buying again.

The closure is a little different than I have seen with other journals. It has the typical leather cover and strap that holds it closed, but the closure is an antique style key (almost steampunk) that slips through a loop to keep the strap from unraveling. It would be nice to have some options for that - an anchor for a nautical theme, a fish hook, or some other bauble.

There are five colors of paper in this journal and that has some advantages if you like to organize as you go. The colors can be used to differentiate sections of your writing if you are that regimented, or they can simply be a splash of color.

I have not tried using felt markers or a fountain pen on the pages but so far I have had no issues with gel and ink pens. The ink does not bleed through and does not seep in and blur either. I can't complain.

This is a nice journal and it will serve you well if you are looking for a distinctive book in which to write. It is made well and it quite striking in appearance.

title: Fine Notebook with Nice Features
text:
I use notebooks like these in my office to keep track of projects, record "tribal lore" about critical systems and otherwise track information that don't want to lose, so this notebook is a good fit for me. So far I am pleased with it.

This is at a glance a fairly basic notebook; however, there is a little more to this notebook than being a simple composition notebook. The cover itself is plain brown in color but it is quite thick and substantial, and the back cover has an inside pocket that is large enough to hold a CD or DVD and still close flat which is convenient (especially since it opens toward the spine instead of the edge so things in the pocket are a lot less likely to fall out). The notebook comes with a ribbon marker which is an unusual feature for a simple notebook like this. It also has an elastic closure band as well as a loop for securing a pen or pencil.

The pages are a nice off-white color instead of blistering white which makes them easier to look at. The ruling is tight, though for me this is not a problem.

It should be noted that the pages are not replaceable. When the notebook is full, it's time to buy a new one.

I like this notebook and anticipate replacing it after I fill it up. I like the feel of the cover, the inside pocket and the band for securing my pen.

title: Decent Pens; Writing is a Little Dry
text:
I selected this set of markers for a few different reasons. I have had good fortune with the brand, and I like the variety of colors. I also like the fact that they're retractable. I had high hopes for these and they mostly have met my expectations, though there's room for a little improvement.

There are 36 pens in the box I received and there's a good variety of colors. Each came with a little rubber plug over the tip to keep the pen from drying out, and that's a good thing. When using these, I put the plug right back in when I'm done, though I am not so sure how much that helps.

The clicker works as expected on each and this has one very specific benefit for me - I like that I can lay the pen down and not worry about it staining anything on which it sits. I have had other felt-tip pens stain textiles on multiple occasions from my carelessness, and these pens already help me with that.

I have one complaint with these pens. For felt pens, they seem to be quite dry. They do write, and they certainly are not dried out already, but they write like pens that have been 75% used already. Time will tell how long they'll last - I am hoping the drier writing means they will last longer from using less fluid?

These are decent art pens with a good variety of colors and thoughtful design. I am still deciding if I am happy with them but so far they're working for me. I just wish they wrote a little more boldly.

title: Good Highlighter Markers, Great Value
text:
We have a need for highlighters in my house and I selected this box with the thought of not needing to buy more for a long time. This is a substantial box of highlighters with multiple colors. I wish I had this when I was in school.

I received the 100-count box and it comes with six different color markers. There are 16 of each color, plus 4 extra yellow ones. Running out of markers in the next year seems very unlikely and I imagine I will lose a few to simply drying out over time. That said, they're all sealed nicely and none of them leaked in the box which is a good sign.

Colors are bold enough to work well. I would not use these on super-thin paper such as onion skin or Bible paper, but for normal books and for print-outs on 20 lb. paper stock these are fine. They do not bleed through or oversaturate (unless you hold them in place for a while).

As I write this, these go for slightly less than $0.25 each. That's really hard to beat.

I'm happy with these markers. I would say I would buy more when I use them up, but that's going to take a while...

title: Fine Entry-Level Parker Ballpoint Pen
text:
One of the best pens I own is a Parker fountain pen, and I was pleased to have the opportunity to use this Parker ballpoint pen as well. So far it has been a smooth operator for me and I like it.

I will start by saying the gift box was destroyed in the mail though the pen was unharmed. When I received my pen it looked like someone had tried to stab the package with a hollow pipe and it severely damaged the box, such that I had to destroy the box completely just to get the pen out. I believe this happened in transit. Not sure what happened. This pen is for me, not for a gift to someone else, so I don't really need the box.

This is a solid blue pen - no stripes or other embellishments. To look at it is quite pretty and I have been surprised that my wife hasn't tried to take it away from me yet. It scores well on the attractiveness scale, to be sure.

It's a smooth operator, too. The click mechanism is easy and I cannot feel any hitch in it, and it is well-balanced in my hand too. The writing is smooth and does not skip, either.

This is not Parker's top-of-the-line offering but it is far better than most ballpoint pens you will use. It's very attractive, it is well balanced, and it writes nicely.

title: Sturdy, Accurate, and Priced Well
text:
I have needed a straight-edge for my home office for a while and I have always needed to hunt one down when I need to use one. I have wanted one of these triangular rulers for a while, not just for the cool factor but more for the stability. So far I am pleased with this one.

One of the things that I have been burned by in the past was inaccurate scales. I had one tape measure that supposedly measured in inches but the measurement was off, such that it measured 6" where all other rulers and tape measures showed 5". As such, I always check these for accuracy as a result. This ruler is accurate - 1" is actually 1" and not something else.

For my typical use, though, the ability to measure is not as important is it is to get straight, clean lines. This straight edge does a fine job for me and right out of the package is clean and pristine. Being aluminum I expect it to hold an edge indefinitely, though it is susceptible to nicks and dents if not careful with it. The shape gives me more control over the ruler so it is less likely to slide.

I like with weight, too. It is a little more hefty than a plastic or wooden ruler but it is still very lightweight and easy to handle.

I am happy with this ruler. It meets my need and it is scaled accurately. It's very well-priced too which is an added bonus.

title: Good Pencils
text:
I usually use mechanical pencils, primarily because I need a finer point than I usually can get with a wooden pencil. However, I'm not totally opposed to using wooden pencils, especially around the house for things like family games and making lists. I selected these with that in mind and so far I am very pleased with them.

I was unaware Bostitch made pencils; I am familiar with the brand for staples, which are good quality. I was pleased to see that these are also good quality. Occasionally when I have bought pre-sharpened pencils (either writing or colored), I will receive a package with a broken tip or two. That was not the case with these - all are sharp and intact. Also, I have found none that have rough spots on the shaft.

These have a distinctive smell that takes me back to my school days.

These perform well - they write nice, appropriately dark lines and they erase decently, though I personally prefer using a block-style eraser most of the time.

As I write this, these work out to about $0.19/pencil and that is reasonable. Most name-brand pencils are more when pricing is broken out this way.

I'm happy with these and based on my experience with them I can recommend them. They're priced nicely and they seem to be of good quality.

title: These Work Well and are Reasonably Priced
text:
I use flags like these to mark pages in cookbooks, though these do get used for other things as well. I selected this large pack of flags because I know I will use them and they're reasonably priced when considering the quantity. They've proven to be about equal to other plastic flags that I have used.

There are 6 packs of 200 flags each in this package, which comes to 1,200 flags total (I didn't count individually, of course). Each pack is a little different and there's a wide assortment of colors. Most flags have 4-5 basic colors liike red, orange, yellow, green and blue; this pack has a broad array of pastels that are very different than any other set of flags I have worked with or seen.

These are plastic flags and they adhere like most other flags. There's enough adhesive to make them stick properly without sticking so hard that removing them strips print from a page or tears the paper to which it's stuck. These can be written on too, though some writing instruments work better than others.

These are fine tabs and there's a lot of them in the pack. The colors are more interesting that usual because they're not the typical colors most packs of flags use. They're priced reasonably too when considering the overall cost. It'll take me a long while to use all of these up, but I will buy more when/if I run out.

title: Better Fountain Pen Than Expected
text:
I love writing with fountain pens and I have a few of them that I use. I have used expensive ones and I have used cheaper ones, and this one by GC QUILL falls into the lower-end range price-wise. That said, it is a better pen than I expected and I really like it. This is a good daily-use pen.

First, I want to say something about the brand, GC QUILL. This is not the same company as the Quill pen company that made ballpoint pens in the 90's. That company seems to have faded away. This is a completely different company that produces more generalized gifts, and in particular it produces feather pens.

This is a striking pen in appearance - it has a gray barrel but an orange cap and butt, and a silver nib. While it doesn't look like a high end pen like a Parker, Cross or other fine writing instrument, it has a much more refined appearance than most fountain pens in the price range.

This pen has a little heft to it though it is certainly not heavy. It is heavier than it looks. The cap seems to be the weight that sets it slightly off-balance; with no cap in place the pen is very well-balanced in the middle of the barrel, but the cap moves the balance point by about an inch in either direction.

This is a fine nib pen and it writes like it. Writing is smooth and easy, with fine lines that suit me. So far it doesn't skip or glob. The pen does not come with any ink cartridges but comes with a refillable cartridge which is my preference anyway. It's easy to fill.

It comes in a nice little box that is suitable for gifting.

Considering the price I looked for things that would make this pen a less-than-desirable choice and found none of the earmarks of cheaper fountain pens. The nip it attached tightly and lays snugly against the plastic point. Another reviewer stated that the nib on his pen was misaligned; mine is straight. The cap clicks in place with a satisfying sound that lets you know it is secured. And, when unscrewing the barrel from the writing assembly it unscrews smoothly and does not feel (or sound) like it is grinding.

I like this pen and I expect to get several years' use from it. It writes very nicely and it has a nice feel in the hand. In its price range it is a better pen than expected. Based on my experience with it, it is easy to recommend.

title: Good Quality Gel Pens
text:
I have worked with uniball pens in the past and they have always been good quality disposable pens. I selected these with the same expectation, and they have not let me down. These are better than typical ball-point pens.

I favor gel pens to ink pens so these had an advantage right out of the gate. Gel pens typically write more smoothly and also are less odorous (typically) than regular ink pens, and I have found these to meet that expectation. These write very smooth, without skips or globs, and they do not have the weird smell that you get from ink pens.

These make bold and clear lines when writing which is great. I personally prefer finer-point pens than these (personal preference based on needing to write small and clearly for math classes in college), but for general writing and signatures these are very acceptable. These write in blue, so keep that in mind if you need black pens.

I like these pens and will use them in my office where I need to write frequently. They're good quality pens that are reasonably priced.

title: Difficult to Peel
text:
This is my second pass at this review. I originally wrote this one thinking that these weren’t stickers at all and that what I had received was just paper pictures that required a glue stick to adhere to anything. It turns out that this was incorrect - these are in fact stickers, but they’re difficult to peel. As such I have rewritten this review to be fair.

I received a pack of 100 individual stickers, packaged in two separate baggies. These are small and individually cut so they’re not like sheets of stickers you normally buy in a craft store that have a paper backing and are easy to peel. They’re colorful, and each sticker is unique. Most have a Christian message, some even with Scripture references, while some are more targeted toward Catholics in particular and a smaller number are just inspirational.

I have two issues with these. First, these are not at all easy to peel. I honestly did not think they were stickers at all because I was unable to peel any of them. My wife was able to peel one with some persistence. Once peeled, they adhere well and they should have no trouble with peeling at the edges, at least for a while. The second issue is the product description. These are listed as vinyl stickers, and I am not so sure that these are actually vinyl. They’re not paper as I originally thought, but I believe they’re very thin plastic. Either way, they’re waterproof.

My initial assessment of these was wrong. These are stickers as advertised, but they’re not easy to peel and I am not convinced they’re vinyl as advertised (though that’s a minor point). If you can get past the difficulty in removing the backing, these are decent stickers.

title: Nice-Sized Notebooks in a Variety of Colors
text:
We go through notebooks in my house at a surprising rate. The main user is my wife who makes lists for everything - menus, shopping lists, inventory needed for trips, etc. I selected these notebooks with the thought that the size and the color coding would make life a little easier for her. I was right.

These are nice-sized little notebooks, that fit well in a coat pocket, purse pocket, briefcase or other small area. They’re a little bigger than similar spiral-bound notebooks I have purchased in the past. The covers are a little more substantial too so they’re less likely to get crumpled when crammed in a book bag or other cramped space.

This pack comes with six notebooks with different colored covers. For some this may just prove to be a nice variety pack, but the colors can be used for organization as well.

Each notebook contains 80 sheets, college-ruled.

These are nice little notebooks. They’re a good size, they come in nice colors and they seem to be made decently well.

title: Far Better than the Price Suggests
text:
I like fountain pens and up to this point I have only used higher-end pens that cost a small fortune but are very fine instruments. After reading others' reviews on this one I decided to take a chance on it and bought two during the Prime Day event this year. This is one of the better pen purchases I have made.

This is a metal barrel pen and I like the feel of it in my hand. It reminds me of a tactical pen that I have, only a lot less bulky and lightweight. It is a balanced instrument and it is not hard to hold while writing.

I selected the extra-fine nib version because I need the finer point for detailed writing that is inappropriate for medium nib pens. It writes almost as finely as my favorite 0.5mm mechanical pencil - not quite, but close. The writing is very smooth and easy and I have had no issues with drips, globs or stutters.

This pen comes only with the converter and this is just fine with me. I prefer a pen I can refill versus using cartridges. The cartridge is easy to fill and does require a small amount of maneuvering if you're not used to this process but it's not hard at all. For those that prefer the convenience of pre-filled cartridges, there are cartridges available.

This is an inexpensive fountain pen (under $20 as I write this) but it is made well - better than could reasonably be expected at the price point. There's no gap in the tip between the nib and the plastic portion of the pen, the clip is very tight (almost too tight, to be fair), and when unscrewing the pen body to access the converter is unscrews smoothly without feeling like it's grinding or shaving itself.

I am very happy with this pen. I'll be buying a couple more.

title: Smudge-Free Writing
text:
I prefer gel pens to rollerball ink pens, though I have had troubles with smears and globs on occasion. I have used other Zebra writing instruments in the past (in particular, mechanical pencils) and have been mostly pleased with them. I was hopeful that these would work well for me, and so far they have.

This is a pack of 12 pens. I selected the X20 pack in blue. They have a 0.7mm point which is a little wider than I usually prefer (having a background in mathematics, I rely on fine point pens and pencils often), though for note taking and daily writing tasks they're just fine. They're relatively lightweight and they feel decent in my hand with the rubber grip on the barrel.

The gel coming out of these pens comes out looking like I wrote with a quality felt-tip marker, very bold and with no skips or globs. Most interesting and most important, it dries almost instantly and when I try to smudge it after a second or two, it simply doesn't smudge. I have never had pens where the ink/gel dries this quickly. These live up to the claims made in the listing - these dry so quickly that they produce smudge free writing.

One of the complaints other reviewers have brought up is that these pens are very lightweight and feel cheap. For many I suppose that is true; they are very light and aren't the kind of pen you'd want to put in your back pocket. For plastic pens, they don't feel luxurious but to me they don't feel all that cheap either. I do prefer a pen with more heft, but that's not a flaw in the pen design but more of a personal preference.

These pens are much better than most gel pens I have seen and used in the past and I do not intent to share with my family or coworkers. They can buy their own; this box is mine.

title: Good Size and Good Adhesion; Colorful
text:
Post-It notes are a hot commodity in my house. They get used for a lot of things from leaving reminders to scribbling down phone numbers to making short shopping lists. I selected this pack of Post-Its as much for the quantity as for the sticky aspect of them. I have not been disappointed.

This is a pack of 6 3"x3" notes. That's the "medium" sized note pad and in my experience is the most useful in most cases. There's enough room to write short messages and even short shopping lists without having to use multiple notes and without wasting too much space. It's a good size.

These are marketed as being "stickier" than most, and they have proven themselves in that regard. I have worked with some sticky notes that stick for a little while and then fall off, or aren't sticky enough to stick to anything in the first place. These stick well and so far I haven't had any drop off or not stick to a normal surface (the fridge, a computer screen or even the TV remote). So far, none have left residue either.

I like the colors too. These come in six flashy colors, not just pale lemon yellow. This could potentially be used for organization if desired, though that's useful mainly for people who are really retentive about being organized.

I like these notes and will put them to good use. They stick as advertised and they are colorful enough to be interesting.

title: Good Fit for My Camera Bag
text:
Little journals like these are ideal for stashing in my camera bag. I use a lot of manual lenses with my camera, and I need a small journal or note pad to keep track of the settings I use with those lenses. The different colors are a bonus.

This is an 8-pack of small ruled journals that are good for notes and light journaling. Each has just shy of 50 pages. These look like miniature composition notebooks with the stitched spine. They're sufficiently small that they can fit in a purse, coat pocket or in my case a pocket in my camera bag. They're nothing special in terms of waterproofing or anything like that; their appeal is in the size and handiness of them.

The different colors afford an opportunity to keep information organized and separated. For me that's not too useful, but others may find a functional use for the colors beyond them just being pretty.

I really like these mini journals. They're the right size for putting in my camera bag and I use them to keep track of camera settings. It will take a good bit of time for me to fill all of these, but when that times comes I will buy more.

title: Large Bible Cover with Good Features
text:
I selected this Bible cover with the intent of using it for a large-print Life Application Study Bible which is a huge volume that approaches 4 lbs. in weight. Other Bible covers I have are just too small for that volume. This one has proven to be almost a little too big, actually, though that's preferable than not being big enough.

The dimensions are clearly given in the product description. I do not have a Bible so large that this cover fits perfectly, and I am not sure I have ever seen one that it would fit. Then again, it is not so grossly oversided to be unwieldy or awkward. As mentioned above, having extra space is far and away better than not having enough. When opened, my Bible lies flat and spans the width of the flaps so that the fit is proper from spine to handle/zipper edge. There's a lot of room at the top and bottom of the pages, though (height), and it makes even a study Bible look a little small.

The very best feature of this Bible cover is the placement of the handles. Some covers have the handles on the spine side of the cover, which means when the whole is carried the spine is up and the weight of the volume pulls on it which can crumple pages and cause binding damage. Because the handles are along the page edge instead of the binding edge, the spine is down and supports the weight of the whole which is better. There's less chance of crumpled pages and separated binding.

Inside there are pockets and pen holders, enough room for a journal, a calculator if needed, and even a phone as well as several pens and pencils. Mine will hold index cards. What is especially interesting is the inclusion of an extra page ribbon marker. There have been so many times when a second marker would come in handy and I have not had one, and this cover provides one.

The outer shell feels like canvas though it isn't and it seems to be fairly water resistant. It's sufficient to protect anything inside from moisture as well as scuffs and cuts. The inner shell feels and looks like nylon though the product description says it's polyester.

When I selected this cover I thought the little wooden cross in the product pictures was part of the cover. It is not and is an extra that is not included. That was mildly disappointing.

This is a very large Bible cover that will accommodate a large study Bible with room to spare. Some thought went into the design and it has some great features. I expect this Bible cover to keep my Bible clean and protected for the foreseeable future.

title: Decent Pens; Expensive and Video Does Not Match Product
text:
I have used gel pens for several years and I prefer them because they don’t generally skip or smudge as easily as ink pens (though that’s a generality, not an absolute). I have also worked with Zebra mechanical pencils and have had very good success with them. So, I was pleased to get my hands on a set of these metallic gel pens, thinking they would be equally as good as some of the other gel pen brands I have used. They’re good but I have a couple of comments about them.

The pens themselves are fine-point pens which suits me just fine. I prefer fine-tip pens as I usually write small. The gel comes out smooth and less smudgy as expected which is a good thing. They feel decent in my hands though like with most pens I am not used to writing for extended periods of time so I have trouble with fatigue when using them. These are no better comfort-wise than other gel pens I have used but they’re no worse either.

The colors are not as vibrant as I had hoped, though the product packaging says these are best on dark paper. On white paper they wash out a bit.

The product page here shows a video of someone using highlighters and double-tipped pens, and these do not match the product attached to this listing. This is a posting issue, not a product issue, but it is sufficient to potentially cause some confusion. Be aware that what’s in the video is not what you’re getting.

Price-wise, these are mildly expensive. As I write this, the $18 price tag works out to $2/pen which is a little steep when considering unit pricing.

I do like these pens, though there are marketing issues that I think take away from an otherwise good product. These are good and I can recommend them based on experience; however, pay attention to the unit pricing and be aware that the video here does not match the product.

title: Beautiful, Well-Made Fountain Pen
text:
Years ago I had a very nice fountain pen that I loved. I haven't used it in years and I have missed it terribly. I was pleased to have the opportunity to use this one. I haven had relatively limited exposure to Parker pens in particular but what exposure I have had has left a positive impression. This pen is no different in that regard.

I received the violet version of this pen. It's an interesting color, to be sure, but it is not out of place and it does look very sophisticated. Of the three colors available I think it is the most appropriate for a business setting.

Included in the box is the pen, a refillable cartridge and two pre-filled cartridges. The pre-filled cartridges are quite a bit bigger than my older fountain pen's cartridges so I expect to get significantly longer run times from these.

As is typical with fountain pens, this one writes smoothly. The nib is a medium which is fine for my purposes, and so far I have had no trouble with skips, blobs or leaking. I have not tried swapping out the nib for a fine point, and the likelihood that I will (assuming I can get the right sized part for this pen from Parker) it is likely that I won't bother.

Everything about this pen suggests quality. I have looked it over and it has absolutely no obvious flaws in materials or assembly. It comes in a nice box that is suitable for gifting.

I am very pleased with this pen and expect to get years of service from it. It's a smooth operator and it seems to be made very well. I have missed writing with a fountain pen and am glad I have this one now.

title: Smooth Writing, Priced Very Well
text:
My wife goes through a lot of pens and has some very definite opinions of what makes a good pen. I handed off a box of these pens to her and she put them to work. So far, these have been very good.

At a glance these look a lot like many other basic pens I have used - seamless plastic barrel, simple cap with a tab to hold it in a pocket, capped on the open end to capture leaks, etc. However, these are advertised as being made out of recycled materials, and that's a positive thing. In use that affects nothing, but in the grand scheme of things recycling when practical is responsible.

My wife's criteria for a good pen are simple: it has to write smoothly, the ink shouldn't glob, and it must be hard to smear. We obviously have not tested every pen in this set, but the ones we have tried have met all of those criteria. That's really all that can be asked of these.

As I write this, the full retail on this set of pens is $25. That works out to just under $0.13 per pen, and that's an excellent price point.

These are good pens that are priced well. The fact that they're made from recycled materials makes them that much more worthwhile.

title: Nice Light Duty Cycle Shredder
text:
I have had a cross-cut shredder for years and it is finally starting to wear down. I selected this shredder as a replacement for it and so far I am happy with it. It works well and it is well-suited for home and small office use.

This is a straightforward shredder that can handle 6-8 pages at a time. Envelopes that have not been opened can pose a challenge as there can be plastic within as well as other items (like paper clips) that can cause issues. The shredder is smart enough to stop when it senses that it is being fed too much and it is easy enough to reverse and start again.

Though paper clips are an issue, small staples and credit cards are not and this shredder has no problem chewing up those items without difficulty.

One of the issues I had with my older shredder is that the basket would slide out from the front. There's nothing wrong with that, but if the basket was full it was easy to spill and get shreds all over the carpet. This shredder has the assembly on the top and it lifts off, which means a lot less spilling.

This is not a shredder that can be used continuously but is fine for occasional use. I would not recommend trying to feed a year's worth of old bill statements through in one sitting; the printer does have some built-in intelligence that prevents it from getting too hot and getting damaged. If you need a heavier duty cycle shredder, consider other models. For small jobs, though, this one is just fine.

I am satisfied with this shredder and based on my working with it I can recommend it. It's not the most powerful one out there, but it is just fine for small jobs and occasional tasks.

title: Handy and Well Made Small Journal
text:
I like to travel with my camera and I shoot a lot with third-party manual lenses. The problem with such is that the aperture setting does not get recorded in the image because of the lack of communication between the camera and lens. A field journal like this one is just the ticket for recording lens and exposure settings.

This is a small journal (roughly the size of a large smartphone) that will fit in the front pocket of a pair of jeans, or in a coat pocket, without any issues. I usually keep it in my camera bag and because of the size it can stash almost anywhere in that bag even though I have the bag stuffed.

While a small pocket-sized notebook would work just fine for my purposes, this journal has some distinct advantages. The outer shell is canvas and will hold up to some abuse (within reason), and to a point it can get wet without damaging the pages. The inner shell is nylon which also helps with water resistance. It is refillable which is always a plus. And, there are places to put a few extra things, like a pen, a little bit of paper money and more.

It seems to be well made, too. Looking it over it appears to be stitched evenly and tightly and I have found no defects in the material. I do expect it to wear over time, but out of the package it was pristine.

For my purposes this is a great little journal and I am happy with it. If you need a full journal this is not the right choice; if you need a field journal or something to jot down quick notes, this is not a bad choice. There are less expensive options out there, but this one is well made and does a good job of protecting its contents.

title: Lower-End Quality, Not Ideal for All Uses
text:
I selected these cards for labeling packing boxes, an ongoing task in my house. My wife was excited to work with these and so far she likes them though I see some issues with the quality.

I'll get right to the point on these - these are not the highest quality cards. If you are working with markers or pens that saturate the paper when you write, these will allow bleed-through. The card stock used is not the best quality and is not thick or sturdy so if you need cards that have some heft or are sturdy, these will definitely disappoint. For our purposes, these are just fine, but if you're thinking flash cards or small handwritten signs, these are not the best choice.

These are ok. For my particular case these work just fine, but many others will find them to be just too thin and flimsy for a lot of uses.

title: Fine Variety Pack of Adhesive Flags
text:
I selected this pack of flags for my wife who uses these to mark all kinds of things (usually recipes in cookbooks). We never seem to have these around when we need them. With this pack, we've solved the issue of running out and misplacing flags.

There's a huge variety of flags in this pack - narrow ones with arrows, thin squared ones, fat squared ones, and more. I like the assortment, not just of the sizes but also of the colors.

These are very typical Post-It flags in terms of how they're made and how they apply. The adhesive is sticky enough to make them stick together and to stick to pages, but it is not so sticky that it leaves a residue behind or miscolors paper to which these are fastened. I have actually worked with off-brand flags that stain the pages then they get damp and the adhesive comes off when they're removed.

This is a great assortment of flags that will last a household a long time and will cover the needs of a small office for a while. They're made like typical Post-It flags and have the same quality you'd expect from the brand.

title: Monthly Calendar Poorly Designed
text:
Organization is always a challenge in our house and figuring who is where, at what time, doing what, is a bit of a moving target. We’ve gotten by with writing on a wall calendar but this gets messy quickly, especially when the schedules change. This system of rewriteable boards has helped, but it there is some room for improvement.

The most interesting component of this set for us is the monthly planner. It allows for writing out appointments, dates, reminders and other tidbits of information that can be erased and rewritten when no longer relevant. However, there is an issue we found with this calendar right away. The planner has exactly 30 squares for days, the first being on a Sunday and the last being a Monday. So, as I write this, it is January 2022, and the first day of the month is Saturday. Unless we’re willing to erase that day and rewrite the calendar, we will run out of room on January 24. We can add lines to add 5 more days in the notes area, but the first added day is taken up with a big “NOTES:” label that takes away valuable writing space. This was not thought through too well.

The shopping list and to-do list are both handy for keeping track of things to pick up before the full grocery list is made and for errands to run/tasks to complete, respectively. They’re smaller than the main calendar and the chore chart, so they have a little more versatility at the expense of writing room.

The conversion chart is especially handy for the kitchen.

The chore chart is the same size as the calendar and it competes for room on the refrigerator, so a little planning of how to arrange these two is required. This particular chart would have been handy when my kids were younger...

This is not a bad set, but the calendar leaves something to be desired. It doesn’t have enough room for a whole month in some cases, and working around this can be a challenge though it is usable. It should have been planned out a little better.

title: Smooth Writing and Quick Drying
text:
Note: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am specifically writing this review for the 12-count box of blue 0.7mm gel pens.

My wife does a lot of writing and she is very fussy about her pens. Her favorite pens have slowly been drying out as she uses them up, so she has been looking for new pens to replace what she has been using. I selected these, hoping they would work out for her. So far she has been happy with them.

Normally, my wife doesn't care for gel pens in particular but she agreed to try these. Her first observation is that these dry quickly and don't smear as much as others she has tried. That's a huge plus right there. None of the ones we have tried have skipped or globbed either which is good. We also have seen no issues with bleeding through the paper. Some of the other reviewers here have complained of dried out pens and inconsistent writing, but so far we have not seen those issues with the box I have received.

Based on our using these pens, I am happy to recommend these. They write smoothly and they smear less than other gel pens we have tried.

title: Excellent Variety Pack
text:
My wife goes through sticky notes at a surprising rate so this variety pack is a good fit for her needs. There's a good variety of sizes in this pack and they're good quality.

I mention the quality for a reason. In the past I have gotten generic or off-brand sticky notes that have had bad adhesive. The adhesive would either hold too tightly and it would be difficult to get one note off the pad (or not tear it in the process), or it would come off the back too easily and the sticky note wouldn't be sticky enough. 3M's Post-Its have never given me that issue, and this pack is no exception. These peel off easily and still stick to other surfaces like they should, with no residue.

There's a good variety of sizes in this pack. There are three 4"x6" ruled pads which are great for making lists, three 4"x4" ruled pads which are nice for larger notes and six 2"x2" unruled pads (close enough) that are ideal for either leaving small notes or marking pages. They're packaged nicely in a small box that is good for storage.

This pack would make a nice gift for a teacher, too.

This is a great pack of sticky notes for those that use them a lot and need a variety of sizes. They're made well and the variety of sizes makes the whole more versatile.

title: Good Mechanical Pencil When You Need Bold Lines
text:
I have preferred mechanical pencils over wood pencils for many years, and I was curious about this one. My preference is 0.5mm lead pencils, mainly because they're well suited for graphing and mathematical writing. This is my first exposure to a pencil larger than 0.7mm. It's not well-suited for my tastes, and it is probably one I will not use very often, but it is a good pencil nonetheless. In the right hands and used for the right task, this pencil will serve very well.

This is a 1.3mm lead pencil which is huge compared to most typical mechanical pencils you can find elsewhere. If you need a pencil for writing fine lines such as in graphing or drafting, this is probably not the pencil you want. This is a more specialized pencil that writes bold lines. This is the kind of pencil you want if you are marking cut lines in a wood shop or similar. In that role, this pencil is fantastic.

The operation is typical of most mechanical pencils I have used, with a push-down clicker top and a concealed eraser under the cap. The grip is reasonably comfortable and there should be little trouble holding on to the pencil when hands get wet or sweaty.

The thicker lead is much less likely to break than that in a 0.5mm or 0.7mm pencil. It can be broken but it requires more angular force.

This is a decent pencil and I do like it. My personal use for pencils does not make this pencil a good fit for me in the large majority of situations but that's not a reflection of a bad product. When it is used in cases where bold, thick likes are desirable, this is a fine pencil that will serve well.

title: Decent Mechanical Pencils
text:
I have preferred mechanical pencils over wooden ones since I was in college, and I have several around the house that I use on a regular basis. I selected this box of pencils to take with me to the office. So far I am very pleased with them.

First, I have the 0.7mm pencils. I usually prefer 0.5mm pencils because of the finer writing tip (a result of a background in mathematics). That said, I have had no issue with these and have been able to write fairly fine lines with these without much difficulty.

These feel solid and sturdy enough to take some jostling and drops. These are not the most solid pencils I have ever used, of course, but they're better than disposable pencils and so far have held up to some light abuse.

I'm happy with these pencils and based on my working with them I am happy to recommend them. They write nicely, they're a bit more sturdy and well-made than cheap pencils and they're not outrageously priced.

title: Good Value Pack of Pens
text:
We go through a lot of pens in my house (my wife is a list-maker) so I look for economical packs of pens like these to keep us well stocked. I received the 18-pack of blue medium-point pens and so far they've been good pens. I wouldn't call them perfect, but they're a good value for what you get.

As I write this these pens are priced just below $0.60/pen, and that's a very good deal. That alone is a good enough reason to look at these as an option for bulk pens.

In use, there work reasonably well. I have had a couple of duds that have quit on us before the ink is gone, but most of them seem to be decent and work well. We have not run through the whole pack, of course, but we have had more work properly than haven't. Writing is smooth with no skips and relatively little globbing. We haven't had any of them leak, either.

Overall, these are good pens and they seem to work well. The best feature is the pricing for this pack which makes them very much worth a look if you are looking for bulk pens.

title: Tend to Skip
text:
I love gel pens and I use different color pens in the office for work. I did not select these for work, though; I have other projects that can benefit from colored pens. These seemed like a good fit for recipe labels as well as gift packages. So far, I have been right, though they have their issues.

These are not the typical gel pens you'll find between the check-out in the grocery store. Instead of colorful pens in red, green and blue, these write in gold, silver and white. These are fine colors for things with dark or black backgrounds like labels and some gift cards. I typically don't use these kinds of colors, but then again I have not had access to them.

These are fine-point pens, and I think this might be part of the problem that others have seen with them. These have a tendency to start writing and then stop. I don't know if the particulates in the tips jam the ball or if there's something about the gel itself that makes these skip, but it's a definite issue. I have been able to get them writing again, usually by carefully applying a little heat to the tips though this is risky.

When they write properly they write very smoothly.

These are hit-or-miss pens. The colors are fun and they definitely have their use when working on dark backgrounds. On the other hand, they have a tendency to skip which means either working a lot more slowly or putting up with spotty writing.

title: Fine Gel Pens
text:
I love colored gel pens and I use them daily in the office. I selected these because the pens I have been using for the last couple of years are finally drying out and need to be replaced. So far I am happy with these pans.

This pack of pens come with 8 colors. The colors are bold and these write smoothly without globbing or skipping which is all I could really ask of them. So far, smearing hasn’t been much of an issue; I can smear the writing immediately after I write if I deliberately try to do so, though I have yet to accidentally smear what I have written with them.

I like the feel of these pens as I write with them. The barrels are rubberized so they do not get slippery when my hands are wet or sweaty and there is just enough cushion to reduce fatigue and cramping when writing for more than a few minutes. The end of the barrel (towards the point end) has a textured grip that makes maintaining a steady hold on these even a little easier.

The price on these is reasonable too. I have seen less expensive pens but I have seen more expensive ones as well, and this pack falls somewhere in the middle. Comparing the price to the quality, I think they’re priced very nicely.

Overall I am pleased with these pens. They write very well, they have a pleasant feel to them and the price is very reasonable when considering the quality. These have replaced the pens I have been using in the office and are my go-to in the day-to-day.

title: Adorable Novelty Note Pads
text:
I selected these pads for my wife who is always looking for something to write on, and these are just about the perfect size for her. So far, we're both very pleased with them.

This is a four-pack of ruled writing pads, decorated with cat silhouettes and a cute comment next to each. Some thought went into the design, bending the lines around the cat pictures.

I like that these have adhesive on the back so they can be stuck on the refrigerator, mirror, window or other surface where they will most likely be seen. Basically, these are oversized sticky notes, and that works for us. We haven't had any trouble with them either leaving residue behind or falling from where they're stuck, and that's all we could really ask.

These are a novelty item and are slightly on the pricey side, so I wouldn't buy these in place of plain note pads if you take a lot of notes, unless you're really into cats and want to share that interest.

So far we're both happy with these note pads. They're cute, they're a good size and the adhesive makes then functional for leaving notes where they'll be seen.

title: Simple and Functional Cart; Good in its Price Range
text:
We have needed a rolling laptop cart for some time and this one seemed to be a good fit for our needs. It’s not especially expensive so I didn’t have high expectations, though I did figure it to be up to the task for which we needed it. Though this isn’t a high end cart and there are better choices out there, those choices cost quite a bit more; in it’s price range, this one is just fine.

The cart came disassembled as expected. It took about 15 minutes to put together after unboxing, and it required no tools beyond what was in the package. The exact number of parts were included – no more and no less. When finished, the cart looks exactly like it does in the product listing photos.

The cart is very balanced and has no trouble handling a laptop or even working as a small table while packing a suitcase on it (though I do not recommend this in most situations). It is lightweight and I can carry it around one-handed when I want to move it between floors of the house.

The downside of this cart is that it doesn’t pull close enough if there is no gap under where you’re seated when working with it. Our couch has maybe a one-inch gap between the floor and the upholstered wood, and as such the cart pulls up close but still far enough away that we have to sit on the edge of the couch seat to use it as a laptop cart.

The upshot is that this is a very affordable cart. It sells for $50 as I write this, which is quite reasonable.

The vertical adjustment is fairly easy and straightforward. It can be lowered enough to work for a child and tall enough to almost work as a standing desk, and the adjustment takes seconds..

I am not unhappy with this cart. It’s a good one and I am getting use out of it already. I do wish there was a way to get it to come closer to the couch, but to have that either as an adjustable sliding desk or have it on longer arms would change the cost as well as the balance and weight.

title: No Skipping or Clotting
text:
I selected this box of pens because good pens tend to wander away in our house, and a good supply of pens should keep us going for a little while. I wasn’t too sure about these simply because I had not used Amazon’s store-brand office products before this. So far I am very pleased with these pens, though there is a caveat.

The box came with 24 pens - six each of black, blue, red and green. For most households, the black and blue pens will see the most use, and we are no exception here, though the red is very useful for certain things. The green pens are a nice to have when you want lower-contrast writing, but they’re not as useful as the other colors for most things.

These pens write extremely fine lines are are perfect for delicate writing projects where a wider ink path is less than ideal. For me, the black ones fit well with a project I have been working on for several years - transcribing recipe cards. The ink comes out very smoothly and so far we have had no problems with skipping or clotting.

There is one catch with these pens, though. The ink comes out very wet and it stays wet for quite a while. As such, these are less than ideal for things like check writing and filling out certain forms of paperwork. Once dry the writing is just fine, but it does require a little patience if you’re always in a hurry.

I really like these pens and these will see some heavy use. Eventually these will wear out, get used up completely or slowly wander away like the other pens we’ve had. When that happens, I plan to buy more.

title: Jaws Grip Well. Magnets No So Much.
text:
My wife has complained for a while that we’ve used a large number of clothes pins in the kitchen for closing up bags of chips and popcorn. This collection of bag clips seemed like an ideal solution. It’s a good solution though not perfect, the main issue being the weak magnets.

These are brightly colored clips and there are 15 in the set – and every one of them has a unique color. Though this is a colorful set as such, the colors don’t serve too much purpose other than aesthetic appeal. That is, there’s no way to label these without adding a glob of tape. That’s not a criticism in the least, but using a specific color for a specific purpose will take an understanding among members of the household.

Even though these have a small area of contact between the jaws, these grip well and we’ve had no trouble with these keeping even larger bags closed (when we fold or roll the bag decently, of course). These are fine clips for the main purpose they serve.

Where these fail is in the magnets that are supposed to make them suitable for tacking things to a metal surface. The magnets are weak, enough so that much more than a sheet of paper makes these slide down a refrigerator door if there’s nothing in the way to stop them.

These are good bag clips and they work well as bag clips. For holding things to metal surfaces these are less useful because of the relatively weak magnets.

title: Novelty Meets Functionality
text:
I selected this unique paperclip holder for some fun in the office. It is a clever conversation piece but it also is practical and well made.

Do the clips hold papers together? Yes, they do. I was a little concerned that this was more novelty than function but I tried using the clips and they hold well. This comes with 20 cows...er, clips...and while it is difficult to find more of this exact shape to refill when these are gone, regular clips will work.

The top fits on snugly but is not hard to pop on or off. You can pick up the whole thing and flip it upside down, and the top will remain in place. The magnet is strong enough to pick up 3-4 clips and not drop them when popped off.

Of course, there’s the novelty aspect. This is a great conversation starter as well as an office gizmo that is sure to get a few chuckles from others. However, in some environments it might wander off when you’re not looking… And if you have access to a UV light, it gets even more interesting.

This silly thing makes me smile. It’s first a novelty item but it is very functional too. It’s a great gift idea for the office – or just for yourself.

title: Decent White Board, but Room for Improvement
text:
My wife is a teacher and has need of things like this whiteboard in the classroom so I selected this with her in mind. There are some really nice features about this board that make is a useful too, but there are also some things about it that could use some more thought.

The whole comes requiring assembly. Other than the tools included in the package there is no need for additional tools to assemble the board. Assembly took 15-20 minutes and the instructions were fairly clear and easy to follow. It’s easy enough to put together that I was able to do it without needing assistance.

The board has a nice, smooth writing surface without any scratches or damage which is a big plus. Included is a magnetic square that is also suitable for dry erase work, and this is handy when you need to either expand your writing a little or you need to cover up and keep writing. It’s not an expensive thing to add either so it’s a thoughtful inclusion. Also included is a paper flip chart which attaches to the front of the board.

All this is well and good but I found a few things that could use some improvement. First, the instructions are not complete. When I was done assembling the board, there was no information on how to attach the flip chart to the front of the board, and though the included clips made it semi-obvious what needed to happen there was no instruction on how to actually attach the clips. I assume I did it right, but I don’t know. Another issue is that the assembly is not completely stable and it does not roll smoothly, especially on carpet though not on hard flooring either. (To be clear, it feels a lot more stable on hard floors, but it is still somewhat top-heavy.) Whenever I move it I feel I have to steady it or it could topple.

The last issue I found is more of a design decision. When all put together, the board stands vertical, meaning the long edge is vertical and the short edge is horizontal. There’s no way to rotate the board. I understand that rotating it would mess up the flip chart, but it would be very useful to be able to use the board as wide and short rather than tall and narrow when the flip chart is not attached.

This is not a bad board at all and it has some very nice features, but there are some things that could be improved.

title: Very Nice Functional Journal
text:
I have kept a journal for several years though most of the time I do so on the computer. I do like having a paper journal. This one is a little different than some of the others I have seen in that the paper is replaceable. This journal amounts to a plain, unlined paper notebook with a fancy leather cover which is sufficient for my needs. However, how this journal is described in terms of size here is slightly confusing.

I will start with the sizing thing. This is listed as a 9”x6” refillable journal. That does not mean that the paper is 9”x6” - the cover is that size. The paper within is actually 8.25”x5.75”. So, if you want to refill this journal the closest size of paper I have found that is readily available is 8”x5” (which is A5). Bear that in mind. If you look online for 9”x6” paper you will find a definite lack of options.

With that out of the way, this is a nice every-day journal as delivered. While I like journals that have hand-made paper, they are more expensive and the paper is hard to write on. The paper included is smooth and unruled, making it easy to write on and without lines it is easy to do free-form expression.

The cover is embossed with the image of an old tree and there is a turquoise-like bead embedded in the middle of the cover. While the bead isn’t necessary it does add a splash of color and some character to the cover. I looked over the cover and was not able to find any real issues with the assembly – the stitching is straight and there are no loose threads, plus I did not find any cuts, stains or obvious blemishes in the leather itself

Other than the fact that the size description is slightly confusing (a listing issue, not a product issue), this is a very nice journal with smooth paper that is replaceable. The size is nice and compact and is easy to tuck in an oversized pocket or book bag. I like it.

title: Nice Hand-Made Journal
text:
I have been a journaler for years though most of my writing is done on the computer. I have used paper journals, though, and I prefer leather-bound ones to cardboard-covered. I was interested in this journal and I am mostly pleased with it though there is some room for improvement.

The cover is pressed leather and is very pretty, and the outside of the cover looks pristine. Inside, the leather looks hand-cut and is uneven. It isn’t a problem but it shows that the journal is hand-crafted.

The paper is interesting to me. I have made paper by hand, and it has a very rough feel to it and is speckled with imperfections. The paper in this journal has the same qualities of hand-made paper. While it does make this journal feel more “rustic”, it does mean the paper is harder to write on. It’s workable but it does mean that more care and effort is required when writing. There are things that can be done to smooth the paper out a bit, and this doesn’t appear to have been done in the production process.

This is a nice little journal but unless you’re willing to accept its imperfections and prefer a more “commercial” journal it will disappoint. The paper is slightly rough, and the cover shows signs of hand craftmanship, both of which are not necessarily bad things unless you’re more interested in the actual writing process.

title: It Works
text:
We get frequent bogus calls on our home line and I have considered getting a number blocker like this one to help with the call load. We have a phone that has a small bank of 30 numbers that can be blocked, but that block quickly filled up. I was hopeful that this device would help, and so far it has.

Instead of just 30 numbers, this unit has 2,000 user-programmable numbers as well as a large number of pre-programmed numbers that are used to block known junk calls. It also has a smaller bank for “white list” numbers for friends and family to ensure that such numbers are never blocked.

Installation is mindlessly simple. Plug in the power, connect the line into the unit, and then connect the unit to the land-line phone. That’s it.

When a call comes in, the unit blocks the call if the number is in the internal block lists. Otherwise it shows the caller ID and passes the call to the phone. If the call is junk, all you have to do is push the big red button to add the number to the user-defined block list. If you accidentally add a number to the block list, using the menu buttons to navigate the lists the number can be unblocked.

The built-in block lists include some of the number ranges that have been plaguing our land line, in particular numbers that start with “00”. We have seen an appreciable drop in junk calls since connecting the unit to our phone line.

So far, we’ve had a good experience with this unit. We have not been using it very long but so far we’re pleased with how it works. I will revisit after a more time has passed, but based on our experience up to this point I am happy to recommend this unit.

title: Not a Fan
text:
I selected these pencils for my wife who needs pencils for working with children. I will state up front that I have not worked regularly with wooden pencils in years and prefer metal mechanical pencils but I was willing to give them a try. Honestly, I am not a fan.

We do have other traditional pencils in the house and I use those only occasionally. Some of them are new, some old, but all feel the same in my hand. These new BIC pencils just feel “off”. I can’t really put my finger on it, but they seem almost slippery and I have to hold them funny to keep a firm grip. They look like regular wooden pencils, and they’re weighted about the same. They even seem to be the same size (width). But, the hand feel is different somehow.

I think the core is different too. They do write but I have to really bear down to get them to write dark enough to match that from a standard #2 pencil. I have no idea why. It may be that because I have a hard time gripping these pencils that I can’t hold them firmly enough to write properly?

One of the selling points of these pencils is that the leads are hard to break. When I received my pack of 24, all of the pencils in the pack were pre-sharpened, but one of the pencils had no tip. The tip on that one was broken off completely and had settled elsewhere in the package, meaning it probably was not broken when it was packaged. That’s not a good testament to being hard to break.

These pencils are all right, but I would not purchase these in favor of cheaper wooden pencils. They don’t feel right in my hand and if they can be broken in a sealed package it makes me question the claim of being harder to break.

title: Damaged Prior to Shipment?
text:
I bought a nice whiteboard when I was in college to get me through my math and physics classes, and that board served me well long after I graduated - until I got married and my school teacher wife needed it more than I did. I have been wanting a replacement for a while, and this looked like a good one. One very interesting negative about it though - the frame was damaged, though the packing box was not, evidence that the board was damaged before it shipped.

This is a big, sturdy board with a heavy aluminum frame and plastic bumpers. it’s a generous 3’x4’ which is larger than what is typically needed in a home environment, though it is approximately the same size as the one I bought in college. However, this one is much thicker and heavier than the old one I bought, and the frame will keep it from warping.

On two of the edges there are sliding hanging hooks so that the board can be hung either on a short edge or a long edge and because the hooks slide along the frame there is some versatility in how the board can be mounted on the wall. I like this configuration better than having the hooks attached permanently in the frame at fixed places.

The board comes with 12 colorful magnets, 2 magnetic erasers, a small set of markers and a mountable shelf for the markers and erasers. The magnets are bigger than they look in the product description’s pictures, roughly the size of quarters. To be honest, I will not need the magnets at all, though my wife always needs more so they will be used elsewhere.

My one complaint with this board - and it’s a serious one - is that the board came out of the box slightly damaged. One of the aluminum frame edges was bent, not in a way that impacts the usability (and not one of the edges with the hooks), but it is noticeable. The board’s frame is damaged, but the packing box was not. This means that the board was damaged when it went into the box. Does it really matter? In my specific case, no, it doesn’t affect me. But, does the severity of damage mitigate shipping anyway? Would you buy a brand-new car off the lot with a noticeably dented door?

My rating of this product would have been much higher had the frame not been damaged in such a way that was evident it went into the packing box already damaged. If you choose this particular whiteboard, inspect it carefully when it arrives.

title: Nicely Made, Attractive Pen
text:
Cross pens have been around for a while and I have a classic gold one that I received as a high school graduation gift. It still works. Every Cross pen I have seen and used over the years – including that one – has been a quality writing instrument. This particular Cross pen is the largest one I have seen and used and I am pleased with it for a number of reasons.

The size is a good fit for my hand, but what makes it really work for me is that it is very balanced. It has a good feel in the hand and when writing it is not top-heavy so I don’t feel like I’m fighting with it while trying to write.

The matte finish is also a plus for me. While a shiny pen is pretty, it promotes slipping in the hand. The matte finish is not as glassy smooth as a metallic shined pen and as such I am able to grip this pen and hold it with less fatigue as it doesn’t slip as much. The dark blue color is a bonus.

As with all Cross pens, it writes smoothly and cleanly, and it uses standard Cross refills.

This is a very nice pen and I am pleased with it. It’s well made, well balanced, and looks great.

title: Simple and Pretty; On the Small Side
text:
I selected this set of Christmas cards with the intent of using them, this season. They’re pretty and they have pretty designs. My main complaint with them is the size, which is a little on the small side for full Christmas cards.

The designs on these cards are simple and cheerful. They use winter colors – blue, gold, silver and white – and do not use a whole lot of words, letting the artwork be the star of each design. These cards have nothing written inside, leaving plenty of room for your own messages. They come with the envelopes necessary to send them off (expected but worth mentioning anyway).

Another reviewer here commented that these are more the size of thank-you notes, and that is very much true. These are quite small. I could see these in use as cards you’d leave at a place setting at a holiday dinner instead of sending out as to everyone at Christmas time.

These are nice Christmas cards, if a little small. Maybe note-card size is suitable to you, but they’re a bit smaller than the average Christmas card.

title: Solid and Easy to Assemble; Not a Suitable Desk Chair Replacement
text:
I have been looking for a new chair for working at my computer desk, as my old chair was falling apart. This chair looked like a good one and I decided to give it a chance. It’s poorly suited for my purposes - it’s a drafting chair, not a computer chair - but that does not take away from the fact that it is well made and seems to be a quality product.

Let me get this one point out of the way up front. This is not a computer desk chair at all. It’s a drafting and workbench chair, meaning it is a lot taller than the typical office chair and doesn’t fit right under a typical desk. If you are looking to use this chair at a typical desk, it’s the wrong chair for the job. I am 6’ tall and when the chair is lowered completely my feet do not sit flat on the floor, and when it is raised up as high as it will go my feet don’t touch the floor at all. I wasn’t expecting it to be quite that high of a chair, but that oversight is mine, not a problem with the chair.

The chair comes disassembled and you have to put it together. Assembly took maybe 15 minutes for me, and the instructions were easy to follow. The package had exactly the right number of screws and washers, and it also had the Allen wrench needed to tighten everything up. All parts were accounted for and there was nothing extra.

I like the ergonomics of this chair. It has a mesh back so it has some give to it but the back is contoured to give Lumbar support. When I sit all the way back in this chair it forces me to have good posture without being uncomfortable. The cushion itself has a reasonable amount of padding, though I use a contoured cushion to give me additional support (at the expense of additional height).

The one downside of this chair is the arm rests. they do fold out of the way, but it would have been nice if they were adjustable for height as well. This likely would have increased the overall price, though, and someone who is not quite as tall as I am will likely not have issues with the arm rests.

The mechanism for adjusting the height and recline is a single lever - pull up to raise and lower, and slide out to release the recline lock. This is fairly standard and the mechanism seems to work well. Considering the height of the chair, I tend to leave it locked upright. There is also a tension knob for adjusting the ease with which the seat reclines, and this also is a typical feature.

My issues with this chair are because it is not the best choice for my uses, not because it is a bad product. It’s actually a very good, solid chair with reasonable comfort and typical adjustment features. For working at a high table, workbench, drafting table or other higher work surface, this is a good and affordable chair that’s worth consideration.

title: Solid and Very Functional
text:
I spend a lot of time working on the computer and as such I spend a lot of time sitting. One problem with this is the lack of exercise I get during the day, but more of a concern to me is the poor circulation because of being seated for long periods of time. I looked to this standing desk to help me with that, and it works well. That said, I have found another use for it that makes it even more useful.

I have the medium-sized standing desk, and it is large enough to handle my laptop as well as my keyboard and mouse. This is all the space I need. With the standing desk raised, there is some room under it for things like speakers, art supplies and a few other things. Obviously, they have to move when the desk is collapsed.

This is a solid desk and it’s made very well. A latch mechanism on the side is used to lift the desk, and a piston as part of the lift mechanism assists in lifting. The piston also resists when collapsing the desk and I found it took some effort to push the desk back down. This is good from a stability point and is a necessary part of the design, but it should be kept in mind - it’s not effortless to open or close, it does require some exertion in both directions.

I found that this desk is a perfect size for a dinner tray, and when set on the floor it works very, very well as a tray table in front of the TV. It’s not an ideal solution, of course, but it does work.

This is a nice standing desk and I am very pleased with it. It’s a good size and it’s made well, and it can server as a tray table in a pinch.

title: Cheap Pens but They Do Write Nicely
text:
I like colorful and bright pens, and these definitely qualify. I took them to the office as they are very distinguishable from the other pens available (so I can definitely identify these as mine). I like the colors, but honestly these are very low-quality pens.

This pack of pens comes in a set of 8, and each is a different color. These are fine for drawing and marking, though the black, blue and red are the only ones really appropriate for the office in most cases. They write fairly smoothly though I have one that leaks and I end up with ink on my hands if I’m not careful.
