The real issue with these is that they’re cheap. They break easily (don’t put them in a back pocket) and when they do they’re just not useful at all anymore - especially if they leak too.

I wanted to like these and I gave them a fair shot. I’ve used pens that are cheaper and did not work as well, but then again I have used some that are a lot better too.

title: Unnecessary and Awkward to Use
text:
I have been a Wacom Intuos user for years and I have been very pleased with mine. I was excited about getting the opportunity to work with this digital notebook, based on my experience with other Wacom products. I will confess to being disappointed with this device. It seems like an interesting idea on the surface, but the reality is that it’s not all than convenient.

The concept is great - write on the pad, upload your drawing to the cloud, then pull it down to other devices so you can work with it everywhere. The potential is there to bridge between paper note taking and writing on a digital tablet like an iPad. However, the implementation is awkward and not at all ideal.

The folio needs to be charged and it comes with a pen that the folio recognizes. This is not at all unexpected. It comes with a pad of paper in it which is good. Tying the package together is an app that needs to be downloaded to an Android or iOS phone (so, if you are a Windows phone user or want to use it with your Windows desktop/laptop, you’re out of luck). I downloaded the app to my iPhone and had no problem tying to the device to the app.

My first discovery was a good one (I think). I tried writing on the pad without opening the pen and extending the ball and it would not work until I actually extended the pen so it would actually write. That’s great for use but it makes testing more difficult. It wasn’t made for the testers so there’s not really a reason to complain; this is just a data point.

The app tells you when the folio is ready to receive input. I found that I needed to fiddle with the app and the folio before it was ready to receive, and this is counter-intuitive. If the folio is on, it should start to receive as soon as it’s opened, though I understand that the app needs to be running (background should be fine in my opinion). I wasn’t able to get the folio to recognize that I was on a new sheet without twiddling some more and that’s not helpful. Forget to tell it that you’re starting another page and suddenly you have two pages one top of one another in the app.

My main complaint is that OCR is not automatic - you get to pay for it separately on a monthly basis. There might be a free trial, but if you have spent that much for a device it should have OCR either included or for a nominal one-time fee ($20-$30 seems reasonable to me). Without OCR - what distinguishes this unit from a phone camera and a regular pad of paper? Other than saving to PDF instead of JPG, not much.

This is an expensive unit for what you get and it doesn’t work as smoothly as it could or should. I am having difficulty recommending it when I can accomplish the same thing with a pad of paper and my cell phone without spending any more money.

title: Premium Paper at a Premium Price
text:
For years I have used 24-lb. paper with my inkjet printers. I prefer it to 20-lb. paper as it is a little stiffer and more durable, though it’s largely just personal preference. I wasn’t aware that 32-lb. paper even existed, so I was interested in trying it. It’s good paper and I like it, but the cost is guaranteed to keep me away from buying more.

32-lb. paper is somewhere between regular paper and card stock. It’s heavier and less flimsy which I like, and so far I have had no problem with it in the printer (meaning, so far no jams). On usability, I have no complaints. This is high quality paper, without question.

However, at the price point (just north of $20 for a pack of 250 sheets as I write this), it’s expensive. A pack of good 24-lb. paper costs between $7 and $10 locally, depending on brand. I have a very difficult time justifying spending double or more on a pack of printer paper when it comes to (in my case) a preference.

Now, that said, this is premium paper and there are reasons why you might want to spend the extra. What comes to mind is more business use, printed resumes and in some cases craft work, but not for the average home user. In my mind, it isn’t a practical solution for everyday printing. For the occasion when you want or need a higher quality paper, this is definitely a better choice than the average pack you’d get in most retail stores.

Based on the paper itself, this is an excellent product and it’s easy to recommend. That said, it’s premium paper at a premium price, and it’s a price that is hard to justify for just everyday use.

title: Solid Whiteboard, Right Size
text:
NOTE: There are two products attached to this listing. I am writing the review for the desktop easel product.

I have had a whiteboard since college, when I bought it to assist me with doing classwork. It’s a large and unwieldy thing and it is certainly not portable. My wife and I have a smaller one on the fridge, but a small, portable whiteboard would come in handy all over the house. I was very interested in this 9”x11” clipboard-size board as it is about the size I have had in mind for a while. It’s an excellent board and I am very pleased with it.

This is a glass board which is a positive and a negative at the same time. On the plus side, it does not scratch or stain like coated fiberboard which is a problem with “normal” whiteboards. On the flip side, glass is susceptible to cracking when dropped and it is heavier than fiberboard.

The glass surface is smooth and ideal for working with dry erase markers. It is basically just straight glass that is painted white on the back side. Writing goes on easy and wipes right off. I have not had this long, but so far there has been no staining and cleaning off residue is very easy.

Though I use this as a clipboard, it is set up with a fold-out back to make it stand on a flat surface. This is handy when I want to set the board up on the kitchen table or other central location in the house. What this board does not have is a hole in the back to make handing the board up on a hook or nail which would have been useful but it’s not necessary. When the board is laid flat, the easel forms a small drawer underneath which is large enough to hold a couple of markers.

I am very pleased with this whiteboard. It’s the size I need, it’s easy to write on and easy to clean off again. It works as a clipboard too.

title: Does One Thing, and Does It Well
text:
About two years ago I purchased a Brother all-in-one laser printer, to replace a failed inkjet printer of another brand. I was fed up with inkjets – I have had a series of them fail in spectacular fashion, and I wanted something more reliable. After I completed my research I settled on a Brother printer which has so far been an excellent investment. I was excited to try this Brother printer which is not an all-in-one but is a one-trick pony that does one thing – print – and it does it well.

As is typical with other Brother printers, this one is well packed and secure in the packing materials. It took a little effort to get it out of the box but I am willing to put up with that to ensure I have a printer that is not dead on arrival. Set-up once unpacked is not a big deal and takes minutes.

I recommend going to Brother’s website and downloading the latest driver package, versus using the included CD with drivers and software, unless there is a problem getting on the Internet. By getting the drivers from Brother’s site you’re guaranteed to get the latest drivers. The CD is a fine option and it works well if downloading the latest drivers is not an option.

I got the printer set up on the wi-fi network with minimal effort. I chose to set it up by hand, though the software is able to configure it without trouble when you follow the directions.

Printing is fast. The printer takes longer to warm up and start feeding the paper than it takes to print a single page, typical of most laser printers. It does slow down when printing duplex, though, which should be obvious but it’s not significant enough to cause concern. The print quality is excellent as well for text and graphics, though it is less than ideal for pictures; for photos I still have to rely on an inkjet to produce high-quality prints.

The one thing I have noticed about printing with this printer is that it has a tendency to really curl the pages. I have noticed this with other laser printers, but not to the same extent as with this one. The pages do relax and flatten after a little while, but it is noticeable enough to merit mention.

This printer does one thing and it does it well – it prints. It’s fast and it produces good quality output. If you do not need scanning and copying capabilities, this is a fine choice in printers that will serve you well.

title: Large Inkjet with Lots of Ink; Best Suited for a Small Office; Pricey
text:
I have worked with a large number of inkjet printers across several manufacturers and almost all of them have failed me in one way or another. I made the move to a color laser printer for generalized printing last year and the printer I chose was a Brother so I have some familiarity with the brand. I was interested in finding out how this printer would work and how it would integrate with my network. So far, I have had no complaints though admittedly I have not had it long.

First off, this is a large printer, the largest inkjet I have ever used. This is not a problem, but it means planning your desk space when finding a place to put this printer. I would recommend using a printer stand just for this printer, where it will not crowd other things on a desk or table. The box in which is ships is huge, and our cats have decided it is a perfect place to sit on top and survey the kingdom...

Setup is not hard and I was able to get it on my wifi network and connected within a few minutes. It does come with the software necessary to set it up, but I would recommend getting the drivers and applications directly from the Brother website to ensure having the latest versions unless there is some reason that connecting to the Internet is not feasible. This is not to say that the drivers on the CD are out of date, but the website is much more likely to have the absolute latest versions.

This is a multi-function printer that handles printing (in duplex), scanning, faxing and copying. I have not used the fax capability yet though I do occasionally have need to fax documents (it's rare but I do have to do it sometimes). The functions that I use regularly – printing, scanning and copying – all work as they should and the printer is fast and efficient.

The most important function is printing, and this printer is very efficient, producing good quality black and color images. The printer is fast and quiet, so much so that I had to check on it when I first printed, thinking that it had not printed anything and had only warmed up. I have not yet tried using photo paper in this printer so I have not yet tested the true potential of this printer's ability to produce color prints from high-resolution pictures, but I will shortly.

This printer comes with a BUNCH of ink, enough for about 2 years according the manufacturer's estimate. For the average household this is a lot, and likely is more than most need. This amount of ink is better suited for an office setting, though I can see it being useful in a small business or even in a college dorm. For home use, getting the MFCJ6535DW model (no XL on the end) may be more economical. The price difference between the two models (as of April 2017) is approximately $250, and that is a savings over buying the printer and ink separately. Consider which is a better fit for your needs and budget.

On the network I have had no issues at all with this printer. Connectivity is good and it seems to respond quickly to print requests. It does go into a sleep mode and when printing to it, it does wake up for printing without requiring intervention (I problem I have seen with some other printers).

So far, I have no complaints with this printer. It works very well and it has been stable and responsive on my network. For the home user it is probably a little heavy-handed on the budget though that depends on the need of the household; the model without all the included ink costs half as much and likely would fit a home's needs better. For a small office, though, this is a good printer with good value.

As I mentioned above, almost every inkjet I have had has failed me along the way. Time will tell if this one holds up better. I will revisit this review after I have used it more and have a better feel for its overall durability, though initial indicators are good.

title: Decent Entry Level B/W Laser Printer
text:
I have a kiddo in college and so far he has had access to a printer when he needs to print assignments so there has been no issue with getting things turned in on time. That said, I have been looking for an inexpensive unit for him, so that should he not otherwise have access he'll have some way to print his assignments when he needs to do so. I was hopeful this unit would be a good fit. It is not a color unit so it is not a perfect fit for the need, but it does work well for my own personal needs. It is a good, entry-level laser printer that handles the basics.

In the past I have had good success with HP printers, though it has been some time since I have used one in my home. This printer is another good one though it is not large and it is not as capable as some others I have seen and used. It does a good job of printing black and white pages, it does a nice job of copying and it is a capable scanner. It is not capable of faxing, which admittedly is not a feature I use often though I do have rare occasion to send faxes and on those rare occasions this unit will not help me.

Build quality is not particularly good and I am a little concerned that a good bump or a very short drop would result in enough damage to keep the printer from working properly anymore. This is the main concern I have. Unlike some other manufacturers, HP does offer some Linux support and the printer does work with Linux after a bit of fiddling with the CUPS system.

This is a surprisingly fast little printer and it works well enough to keep up with my [very] modest printing needs. It is rated to print up to 23 ppm, and so far I have not printed anything more than a dozen pages at a time and it has churned out the pages quickly enough to suit me.

Overall I have few complaints with this printer, beyond the build quality. It works well, it is fast and I can use either Windows or Linux to print. It is not a color laser (the price should be a good clue there) but it is fine for cranking out documents that do not require color at all. Take a look at this printer if you do not need color printing or fax capabilities.

title: Fast, Quiet, Produces Good Quality Output and It Works with Linux Too!
text:
I have worked with a good number of inkjet printers from several different manufacturers. Some inkjets are worth your money, and some aren't worth the box they are packaged in. After working with a series of inket printers that failed me in spectacular fashion, I bought a Brother color laser printer and so far it has proven to be a very good investment. I was curious to see if Brother's inkjet line was better than the last manufacturer's offerings and was pleased to have the opportunity to test this printer. I've not had it long so I cannot yet say how it will hold up over time, but so far it has worked out well for me and has given me no issues – initial indicators are good.

This is a multi-function inkjet, capable of printing, scanning/copying, and faxing. This is a fairly standard set of functions for all-in-wonder printers. I will state for the record that so far I have used only the printing capabilities of this printer as that is the main function I need. I will update this review as I use other aspects of it and learn more.

It comes very securely packaged in a well-padded box, so the chance of getting a printer damaged in shipping is relatively small. It does make getting the printer out of said box a slight chore but not a huge problem. One I had it out of the box, I had it set up and ready to go in just a few minutes.

Though it comes with a driver CD, I chose instead to go to Brother's website to download the latest driver package. This is not a necessary step but it does ensure I have the latest (at the time) drivers for my printer. I ran the installation, followed the steps and had a test page printed fairly quickly with no fuss or fanfare. I recommend getting the driver package from the manufacturer's website instead of using the CD if you have that option, though the CD will certainly suffice.

I connected it to my WiFi network, so that I can access it from anywhere in the house from any computer. Getting it on the network is simple and easy, though I did notice that it cannot see my 5GHz network, seeing only the 2.4GHz network I have configured. This is not a big deal to me, but if you live in an area where there are a lot of networks competing for channels, this could get interesting.

I decided to feed it a photograph to check the print speeds as well as print quality. Here is where the printer really surprised me. Using regular paper and using standard print quality, I fed a very colorful 8”x10” photograph to the printer. I sat and listened from the other room as the printer sounded like it was warming up, made a couple of diagnostic noises and then was silent. Thinking the printer had malfunctioned, I went to see if it had jammed or returned an error code. Instead, I found my print waiting for me. It never sounded like it actually printed, but it did, and it was quick about it too. The colors on my picture were bright and clear and not at all unsatisfactory. I thought about sending the same picture through again on photo paper and bumping up the quality but I did not. Text comes out clear and bold with fine edges. I really cannot find fault with this printer's output.

An important note for those using Linux – yes, it does work under Linux! I run CentOS 7.3 as I write this and the printer works just fine. It does require a driver from Brother but you can get that from the website.

One more point that is important, at least to me. It is fully capable of duplex printing, which saves paper. I have always liked automatic duplex print and I am pleased with how well this printer handles duplex printing.

I have not had this printer long enough to find a lot to criticize (though I will return to this review and update as I learn more). So far it has proven to be fast, quiet and it generates good-quality print. It's priced well too, making it a good choice if you cannot afford a color laser or if you need to print more pictures (laser printers are typically poor at this). Consider this printer if you are looking for a good inkjet, priced well and produces quick output of good quality. If you are a Linux user, this printer should be on your short list.

title: Very Good Mechanical Pencil
text:
I have for years preferred mechanical pencils to traditional wood pencils as mechanical pencils typically stay sharper and I can get finer lines with them. My instrument of choice is a Uni-Ball KuruToga which I have been using for almost 4 years now and even bought another for my wife. I was interested in trying this Zebra mechanical pencil and comparing it to my KuruToga. It compares well and is not particularly expensive.

This pencil has a nice hand feel to it and I can hold it and work with it without any more fatigue than when I use any other pencil. The barrel is ridged hard plastic so it is easy to grip, though I personally prefer a pencil that has a softer (rubberized) grip to make it even more comfortable.

The innovation with this pencil is the spring loaded barrel which is designed to absorb excess pressure and prevent the lead from breaking as easily. In use, it seems to work fairly well and I have had fewer breaks than with many other pencils I have used. When you bear down hard, you can actually see the spring in the tip of the pencil compress to absorb some of the pressure. I cannot say with certainty that this is the only reason that the leads break less – the leads themselves may be a contributor.

The main area for improvement with this pencil is the eraser, which is very small and is typical of a lot of the better mechanical pencils I have seen and used. If you plan to use this pencil a lot, plan to keep a larger eraser close by which is easier to use anyway.

The cost of this pencil is quite reasonable. As I write this it sells here for $7, which is not terribly expensive. While disposable mechanical pencils may cost less, they quality is usually not there and in the long run you end up paying a little more than you would for a good quality pencil in the first place.

My wife has confiscated this pencil from me and uses it now. She prefers it to the KuruToga, though I am still debating which I think is better. Regardless, this is a fine pencil and it will serve you well if you need a 0.5mm pencil that will not cost you a fortune.

title: Helps With Circulation When Sitting
text:
I will start by saying that a lot of cushions like this claim to be memory foam but are not, instead being softer foam that quickly returns to its normal shape. This is not the case with this cushion – this one really is memory foam and it holds it shape for a while after pressure from it is removed.

The memory foam comes with trade-offs. It does conform to your shape when you sit on it and it does get comfortable, but it also is a bit harder than some cushions and initially I find it a little uncomfortable when I first sit on this cushion. It takes a moment to make the adjustment, but once the adjustment is made it conforms very nicely and is quite comfortable.

It is shaped to basically conform to your posterior (unless you are a very small or very large individual, it is fairly close), providing good support for your tailbone as well as for your upper thigh. I have trouble with circulation in my legs after sitting for a long period of time, and this cushion has helped alleviate that. It's not a cure-all, but it does help.

The cushion itself is memory foam but the outer sleeve that covers it is a soft, almost fleece-like material that can be removed and washed when it gets dirty. It zips closed so it stays secure but is easy to remove.

This is a good cushion that does help with relieving discomfort when sitting. It does adjust shape to conform to you, it provides good support and it isn't cost prohibitive. Considering the relieve it gives when siting for any length of time, it is worth some consideration.

title: Interesting Concept, but Limited Usefulness
text:
I had never heard of the Justik but it sounded like a fascinating device - an electronic pinboard of sorts. I was curious to see how well it would work and for some things it works very well. For others things, no so much. I would consider it “somewhat useful”.

This is a clipboard-sized device that uses batteries to generate an electrostatic field that can be used to attract paper, CDs and other small items to it. The idea here is that it can work as an organizational tool to keep important items off the desk and out of piles, making them a lot easier to find. The concept is simple and straightforward, and it is in some ways better than an actual clipboard as it does not apply pressure on what it’s holding.

In service, though, it is limited. It cannot hold two sheets of paper that are on top of one another unless the top sheet is offset a bit and touches the Justik surface. Thicker items such as poster board, even when small, do not stick well and are more likely to slide off. It does hold CDs, but ONLY if they are on the label side and they simply slide off if you try to place them recording side down. My guess is that it needs a non-sheer surface, as smooth plastic (even very lightweight) does not stick.

I had trouble getting the battery compartments open to put in the 4 AA batteries. The covers simply slide off, but they are quite tight and are not easy to move until you have done them a couple of times. I suppose this is good in that the batteries will remain secure, but it also means frustration when changing the batteries.

There is some room for improvement with this device, though it does work to some degree. It will hold papers and CDs though the capacity is limited and it is a little fussy with certain materials. I have it in my office where it holds a checklist for me.

title: Affordable Set with Vibrant Colors and Good Coverage
text:
Coloring is something I loved as a child and I still find myself coloring on occasion though nowhere near as often as I once did. I always preferred colored pencils to crayons, even when I was very young, and I have a set of nice Prang pencils I have used for several years as my go-to set as they compare beautifully against more expensive brands. This set is a bit more than my Prang set and I was very interested in seeing how it compared, and so far I have been happy with them.

There are two sets of pencils available on this listing, a set of 36 and a set of 48. Both come in a nice, hard cylindrical tube which is nicer than a cardboard box for keeping the pencils organized and for keeping them well protected. The case is not crush-proof but it does survive drops and it protects the pencils from most things.

There is a fairly good variety of colors in the set that allow for getting the colors in your drawings more accurate without requiring as much blending. There is likely always going to be a situation where you need to blend to get the color exactly as you would want it, so do not expect absolute perfection. But, with more colors to choose from there is a good chance you can find a color that is close to what you need at the time.

In coloring I have found the pencils to provide fine coverage, though the cores are a little hard and as a result are a little more brittle than my Prang pencils. While this is a difference, the difference is not big enough to call this a huge detriment. It means using a lightly lighter grip when coloring and working just a little longer to get the same effect. It also means less smudging - even when I bear down hard in an effort to smear the color I have not had much success. When I have laid down thicker coverage, the coverage is creamy and the colors vibrant.

I have no complaints with these pencils. They are different than my main set though not in ways that make them unusable to me. I like the coverage and I like that they do not smudge easily. I really like the affordability too - these are quite inexpensive for what you get and they compete well. If you are looking for a nice set of colored pencils that is affordable and has a good variety of colors, this set is definitely worth a look.

title: No FIlling Instructions and Ships with Fine Nib Instead of Medium
text:
I will start by saying that I have not made the same observations as some of the other reviewers have made about this pen, and I will talk to those points in my review. This is not an ideal pen, though, and I found a couple of drawbacks with it that make it less than perfect. It is workable, but it lacks a few details that would make it a better product.

One of the critical comments that has been made about this pen is that it is counterfeit. I disagree. It is marketed as an eBoot pen, and it has the logo stamped right on the cap. That does not make it a genuine article, but this is a $20 pen from a company that makes a lot of different things, not like Cross or Parker that specialize in making fine writing instruments. To counterfeit would be a waste of time.

The pen, and the case, are definitely bamboo. This is easiest to tell by looking inside the case at the groove cut for the pen to fit inside, as well as the rounded tips on either end of the pen. There is definitely rough grain in these spots.

Fountain pens are usually shipped with a medium nib which is suitable for most people. This one does not and instead has a fine nib which is what is typically recommended for women. A fine nib writes thinner, more delicate lines, where a medium is more bold and is what is typically recommended for men. It is unclear why this pen ships with a fine nib and not a medium nib, especially since this is not mentioned in the product description.

The last fountain pen I used took ink cartridges. This one is refillable, but it takes the ink into a built-in ink well in the pen. It’s semi-intuitive when it comes to refilling it, but there are no instructions with the pen at all which is a major shortcoming for this type of pen. There needs to be some kind of instruction on how to fill it up, how to clean it and how to do general maintenance on it.

This pen comes with no ink at all, another minor disappointment. I would have liked to have had at least a small amount of ink come with it.

In writing, this pen works decently. I have been able to get fine, clean lines from it. It have not had problems with globbing or leaking.

This is not a bad pen. It does work well for me and I like the way it writes. There were some shortcuts taken in the final package though, such as not including instructions and including a non-medium nib, that make it less than ideal.

title: A Fine Travel Journal
text:
I have kept a journal for a while and I have used mostly a computer package for keeping my journal in one place. That said, sometimes I have needed to use a paper journal, and though a regular old notebook is acceptable it is not ideal; there are times when the lines on ruled paper are a hindrance to the entry and the paper is not always the best for working with different inks or pigments. I was interested in trying this small notebook/pad/journal, and it has proven to be a better fit for journaling than regular notebooks. It is also a nice portfolio notebook for keeping drawings, experimental art and other non-language creations.

I have the rabbit design notebook. The cover is a little on the disturbing side in terms of appearance, but it is a tastefully done pencil drawing of a rabbit and deer head. It is different than most notebooks and suggests a good place for artwork, not just prose. Out of the gate this is good.

The majority of pages are off-white and are smooth but not glossy. These are ideal for pencil drawings, but they also work well for gel pens, ink and other non-soaking wet writing utensils. I have not tried using heavy felt markers, but I suspect the pages would hold up acceptably to them unless they are allowed to saturate and bleed through by pinpointing.

There is a short section in the middle that is all black pages, and these have proven to be interesting in their own right. White colored pencils work well here, and the effect is striking. Many very light colors are ok on these pages (white and yellow being the best choices) but darker colors are not good on the black pages.

Though designed for artwork, this is also a good little travel journal. It stashes nicely in a book bag or a briefcase and is just the right size for a quick entry when on the go. I keep it in my daily bad so I can jot down thoughts and flesh out ideas when I am at the office.

This is a nice little notebook for drawing, writing and otherwise making art on paper. I use it for a journal; others will like it for drawing, sketching and other artwork.

title: Meets a Specific Need for Me
text:
Note: There are several products attached to this product listing. I am writing this review for the silver colored aluminum mouse pad.

I like to sit with my laptop on a lap desk in a comfortable chair but this poses a problem for me. Using the mouse on the arm of the chair is hit-or-miss at best and usually amounts to an exercise in frustration. I had been using a book as my platform for my mouse but I was given the opportunity to try this aluminum mouse pad instead. It is a fine solution for my situation.

This is a standard-sized mouse pad and it provides a good work area for a mouse – it's not small and it is not huge either. This is a positive out of the starting gate. Because it is metal and not pliable material it is rigid and provides a surface on which to use the mouse without having to make manual adjustments for the fabric on the arm of my chair.

The surface of the mouse pad is not perfectly smooth but it is somewhat like a matte finish – it has a very fine texture that is rough enough to feel but smooth enough to allow the mouse to glide across the surface unhindered. As a side note, if the surface was perfectly smooth and shiny, most mice would not work on the surface due to reflectivity.

Flipping the pad over, he entire underside is covered with a non-slip pad that will keep the mouse pad stationary on the work surface. Without this the pad would slide all over the surface on which it is being used. While it probably would have been sufficient to put four dots on the corners, I like having the entire surface covered.

This is a nice mouse pad. It serves the need I have – mousing on the arm of a plush chair – but I use it all the time now as my mouse pad everywhere. It's rigid, non-skid and the surface is the right balance of textured and smooth.

title: Excellent Dividers for the Obsessively Organized
text:
My wife maintains a complex filing and organization system and she is frequently looking for additional binders, folders and tabs to expand or change her system to suit her need. I looked to these erasable tabbed dividers as a possible help to her system; so far, so good.

These are similar to typical separators in that they are 3-hole punched with reinforced holes for dividing up a document or collection of papers in a binder and the tabs make it easy to find the sections. The tabs are different though - instead of a plastic sleeve either glued or pressed to the sheet where a small heavy paper tag gets inserted, the tabs themselves serve as the label and can be written on directly. Better, they can be erased and reused when the papers with which they are used are no longer needed.

Depending on what is used to write on then, erasing may be easy or may require a little effort. Pencil erases easily, though, and pen does come off but leaves some residue behind. One other reviewer mentioned that the Magic Eraser (Mr. Clean) does well for getting ink residue off the tabs; I have not tried that yet though it makes good sense.

These dividers do have pockets for storing additional sheets and that is handy for storing blank sheets or pages that need to be found a little more quickly (tax documents come to mind though we are not using them in that context). I especially like the fact that the upper corner has a small pocket in which to tuck the corner of a page so that the sheet does not get dog-eared and does not slip out as easily as with other pockets.

So far we have had no issues with these dividers. My wife is pleased with them. I intend to buy more when she needs more dividers.

All 10 were the exact same size when assembled. All Lids fit snugly, are perfectly flat and stay on when moving them. Because the sides of the lids are double folds, they are extremely sturdy.
2. STRONG & SECURE - I bought packing tape, which I did not need. The cardboard is thick and strong. The clever assembly creates a no-seam bottom, that is 3 layers of sturdy cardboard. Nothing is falling thru the bottom of this box. I filled one with a heavy set of cast iron pans and another with a full set of dishes. Neither required additional packing tape. I was truly shocked I did not need ANY tape.
3. HANDLING - Because you fold in the side grip-holes, it creates a smooth Handle that does not dig into your hand. These boxes were easy to carry, even when loaded down with heavy cast iron pans. This was probably my favorite feature - no more struggling to awkwardly try to pick up and carry taped moving boxes. No more trying to push taped moving boxes across the floor that I am unable to pick up. Hooray!
4. STACK-ABLE - The sturdy cardboard sides allowed me stack them 4 high, without any issue. There were no bent lids or crushed sides.
5. PRICE - So, at about $2 per box, these are a great bargain in my opinion. Superior quality compared to traditional packing boxes which dont cost much less than these.
6. REUSE - Not only do I not need any packing tape - if I use these for moving, I can easily un-assemble the Box and Lid then stack and store them flat, without damaging them. The thick cardboard makes them strong and stable.

text:
I’ll be honest, when I first saw this, I didn’t think much if it. I read, a lot, and have never thought about something like this as something I’d need, or even want. But, decided I should try it, especially after seeing others give it a good review. I got it around Christmas, and immediately gave it a try.

I must say, I was wrong, this little gadget is pretty amazing. It’s not so necessary when you first start a book, but about 1/4 - 1/2 way in, it is really helpful. I initially used it with a soft back book, and it worked great, but it was even greater with larger, hardback books.

The wood is sanded nicely, and the finger/thumb hole is a decent size. The holder itself is designed so that it doesn’t damage the book, or leave any markings on the pages. It appears to be stained, but doesn’t have any smell to it. The middle groove fits right into the center of the book, making it much easier to keep the pages open and keeps your hands from getting tired with larger books. And, it doesn’t damage the books binding.

My only regret is that I didn’t try this before, this is a great item to have and will make a great gift for any avid book reader.

title: Impressive printer and easy to set up
text:
I’m very happy with this printer. It was very easy to get up and running, taking about 20 min to physically set up out of the box and another 10 to connect the Wifi and update the firmware. The ecotank bottles were easy to use, and one set filled up the inkwells about halfway for each color. If the page estimates are correct, these bottles will save a lot of money over cartridges.

The printer is very fast, even when printing double sided. It also is very convenient printing from my phone. I’ve printed PDFs, word documents, and pictures. In addition to regular copy paper, it worked well with thick photo paper in the regular tray. It did not require feeding it from the back. The quality of the print on photo paper is pretty good considering the ink cost and the speed. As a point of comparison, I have a large format photo printer (the Canon Pixma pro 100 which has 8 color tanks), and the details are not as good on this Epson, especially in darker areas of a photo. I wouldn’t use this printer for pictures to be framed and hung on my wall, but it is good enough for making quick prints for the kids to have.

Also, I am impressed with the quality of the touchscreen because it is big and highly responsive. Don’t expect an iPad on here, but it is more than adequate for an all in one machine.

Scanning on both the glass and the autofeed worked well, so no complaints there.

This is for my home office, but I don’t have a landline so I can’t try the fax functionality. I have no doubts that it would work just fine, but this is 2020 and I’ll end this review with that. .

I think the shade would complement a wide range of skin tones, and it highlights the face in such a flattering way. Love this product!

title: I’m Thankful for These Cute Stickers!! 🌸
text: These THANK YOU stickers are super cute and handy! I’m an online reseller, and it’s always nice to have a pretty way to affordably accent my shipments as I send things out to buyers. I use these stickers (instead of Scotch tape) around my tissue papered garments, and I add them onto the address labels affixed to the front of my poly-mailer bags and boxes. They are reasonably sized, and they seem to provide good adhesion! The bohemian patterns on each of the 4 rolls are really feminine and classy, and I’d definitely order these again without hesitation.

title: Transparent, Flexible, Sturdy, and Secure! 🤍
text: This bulk set of plastic baggies comes packaged in three separate bags of 100. They offer loads of versatile storage possibilities, and I always love having a flexible, transparent option available for easy organization! These are great for separating pieces of jewelry, small cosmetics, complimentary gifts, potpourri, or home repair things like screws and nails. These bags seem sturdy, and the grip-seal closures feel secure and reliable. I’m really pleased with them!

title: Practical, Reliable, and Nicely Packaged! ⭐️
text: I love this combo pack of printer cartridges!! Since the black one always gets depleted twice as fast (I print soooo many shipping labels), this product provides a blend of exactly what I need! It’s a complete set that always arrives super fast.

title: Velvety Soft but I Found The Elastic Restrictive
text:
I’ll start by saying that I love the mossy green shade of this fabric! It’s velvety soft and has an “enchanted forest” vibe. Each little pillow measures approximately 2.25” wide by 2.75” long, and the elastic bands feel strong and secure. There were some loose white and orange thread ends visible that I had to carefully trim away, and the stitched seams became somewhat apparent when the elastic was stretched, so some of the finished details seemed slightly undone to me. From a functionality standpoint, I feel that this product may only suit a select segment of customers. When I placed these cushions on my wrists, I felt like they restricted my circulation somewhat.

Diminished blood flow to the hands can cause a tingling sensation, so rather than providing strain relief from typing, these actually have the propensity to create a temporarily new problem. I also don’t wear elastic hair bands around my wrists for the same reason, so these simply weren’t a good fit for me personally, but they might be a beneficial accessory for some! I’ll stick with the free-standing, flat-bottom wrist support pads from now on, but these tiny pillows possess conceptual potential.

title: You’ve Got (Well-Protected) Mail! 📦📬
text: I love these handy brown mailer bags! Made with water-resistant kraft paper, they do feel reliably durable but still lightweight. I love the peel and seal design, and the tear-off strip has the cutest little zipper design printed on it. I like that the far end of each bag has an expandable bottom that will unfold and sit flat, so these really just resemble heavy-duty paper lunch bags. I’m an online reseller and often ship smaller items that need something a bit sturdier than a flimsy plastic polymailer bag, so these are perfect containment vessels for books and single items of clothing that need a bit more protection! Hope this helps other potential buyers because I’d definitely order these again!

title: Marbleized Memory Foam Delights! ⌨️🖱
text: First of all, I love the marbleized swirl pattern of this Lycra fabric! It looks like metallic rivers of copper are intermixing with the waters of a luminous blue lagoon. The mouse pad and keyboard wrist support color-match each other perfectly, but the fabric on the *free* coaster is a completely different shade than the other two (more aqua instead of blue). The backs of the two main pieces have a black, rubberized, non-slip coating; the back of the coaster is a slick white plastic. The lumps are indeed filled with memory foam because you can watch them slowly rise back to their original shape once downward pressure has been removed. I do think that this is a quality set that’s been thoughtfully constructed, and the sizing seems efficiently tailored to the average working adult. The ergonomic design offers pleasing shapes with functionality, and these computer accessories help me alleviate some of the ulnar deviation wrist pain that comes from typing every week, so I’m pleased with the results overall. I just wish the coaster matched the others!

title: A Dependable Essential!
text: I’m always impressed by how fast one of these printer cartridges arrives after I place an order! I immediately put this one to work, and it provided me with the dependable and invaluable print quality I’ve come to know and love.

title: These Keep My World Brightly Colored! 🎨
text: I have a WF-2650 printer that I’ve happily used for years, and this combo package of replacement ink cartridges is always exactly what I need! My order always arrives quickly and safely, and this listing offers the most affordable pricing that I’ve found. I plan to be a repeat customer!

title: Ergonomic Elegance! 🖱🌿
text: I am so pleased with the pattern on this mouse pad! The floral petals and leafy fronds look exquisite against the smooth black background, and I adore the feather that’s hiding in the botanical mix. The gel wrist support offers an ideal hump of comfortable cushioning, and the non-slip bottom keeps this product firmly on my desk top. I think it’s the perfect size for my wireless mouse to move around with ease, and I’ve had no problems integrating it into my daily work-from-home activities. I would highly recommend this glamorously vibrant mouse pad to all of my family and friends!

title: Marbleized Magic! 🍥
text: The fluid art design of the marbleized effect on this mousepad really comes to life in varying shades of pink and violet, and the gold ripples make it a truly feminine chic office accessory! The Lycra surface really does ensure ultra-smooth mouse control, and it gives the material a delightful, satiny sheen. I didn’t think I’d like the look of the stitched edges at first, but I think they give the piece a tailored, finished look overall. The reverse side being non-slip rubber is an essential must, and I couldn’t be more pleased with this affordably priced product.

title: Beneficial Tech Accessory with the Perfect Amount of Squish
text: This affordably priced, packaged pair of keyboard wrist rests is exactly as pictured and described. The memory foam feature offers an appreciable degree of squish, and the non-skid bottom keeps each pad firmly in place. I use them in combination with my laptop, and I have noticed a beneficial degree of pressure relief and comfort. I have not noticed any issues with body temperature transference, so they don’t become undesirably warm with consistent use. Would gladly recommend these to others or give them as a thoughtful gift!

title: Polka Dot Perfection! 🟠
text: I adore the peachy gold pattern of polka dot happiness on these bags! I am an online reseller, and these mailers are perfect for shipping out single articles of clothing. Super lightweight, yet tough enough to withstand the (sometimes) rough transport they experience when moving through the US postal service distribution routes. The self-adhesive strips offer secure closure without concerns. Will definitely be back to purchase more bags when it comes time to restock my supply!

title: Will Satisfy All Your Shipment Needs!
text: As an online reseller, I depend on quality tape products for all of my packaging and shipment needs! I love that this set easily adapts to the refillable plastic dispensers I already have. Will buy again!

title: Technicolor Coils of Delight! 🍭
text:
Adore these dual-colored, spiral cuties!! They remind me of sno-cone syrup flavors 🍧
The wide range of colors gives you such a versatile set of options to coordinate your outfits with. They are adequately stretchy, lightweight, and super comfortable to wear. Would gladly give these out as gifts or recommend to friends! The colors are vibrant and the attached silver keyring makes them handy to have for toting single keys or little ID tags.

title: Coiled Versatility!
text:
This set of stretchy spirals offers coiled comfort and convertible versatility! The matte finish and darker color palette are a welcome shift away from all the bright and shiny options on the market. My group of 5 includes slightly different shades than the ones pictured in the listing though: (charcoal, forest green, dusty pink, chocolate brown, and royal blue) are the colors I received.

title: These Clips Are The Cat’s Meow!
text:
Adore this assortment of brightly colored and metallic cat-shaped paper clips! With a smooth coating, these felines are feeling fine. They come packaged in an adorable tin box that can also be used for storing a variety of other small keepsakes or office supplies.

They grip a single piece of paper without issue, but they could easily accommodate a slightly thicker stack as well. I think any family member or friend would enjoy these utilitarian meows!

I only deducted a star because the listing title and item description indicates a quantity of 60 paper clips, but my package only contained a total of 30 (with an equal distribution of 5 clips for each of the 6 colors available). I admittedly thought “you gotta be kitten me!” Other than the amount discrepancy, I’d highly recommend these cat cuties!

title: works with big ergonomic keyboard
text:
As advertised. Solid and strong. The answered questions above were accurate with regard to how much space there is between the underside of the table and the tray...etc.Only 4 stars because it was quite a pain to put together. Had to flip my desk upside down to make sure I could see that all the holes were lined up before I drilled...I'm handy, but it took me many sweaty hours to finish. But worth it because it FITS MY BIG OLD MICROSOFT ERGONOMIC KEYBOARD!
UPDATE:
Out of pity for others who are trying to figure out whether they can really install this thing, I have now added two photos. The first is a basic shot of the keyboard tray underneath my desk, with a focus on the depth of the product. The second is a really quick drawing I made of it, indicating measurements. The numbers (if you can't read them in the photo) are from top to bottom: 11 3/4 inches, 8 3/4 inches, 14 1/8 inches (when closed), and 22 3/4 inches (when fully extended). My tray was mounted so that the edge of the keyboard is flush with the edge of my desk...you need not make it flush, but it might look best if it is flush.
What I had to really pay attention to was where the screws needed to go in!!! I had a gap in the underpaneling of my desk, and I was forced to use a very long screw to secure the deepest brackets. Hard to explain, but trust me--not fun. The point is, the measurement that mattered to me most was NOT 'how deep is the tray' but 'how far apart are the screw brackets'...and that is why I added these photos.
Hope they help someone.
Edit:
I am adding 3 new photos to help someone. The three new photos are all taken with the keyboard tray fully closed (as far as it will slide in). The tape measure reads pretty clearly in the photos I think. The third photo is of the front of the tray. The fifth and last photo is taken from under the desk looking up at the back of the tray. Yes, when fully closed, the glide rails stick out a bit beyond the wood tray--again this in the back. My tape measure reads 2.5 inches there, give or take a millimeter or two.

title: I’m small and these made my chair too tall
text:
I’m petite, only 5 feet tall. Was looking to replace the factory wheels on my new desk chair because they were scratching up the vinyl flooring in my apartment. These wheels are great and I don’t think they would scratch the floor because they are made of a soft rubber-like material (not rubber). They look great on too for those wanting to consider aesthetics and are pretty quiet and smooth. They glide VERY EASILY. Almost too easily, especially since I now cannot reach the floor even at the chairs lowest setting, it’s a little hard to get the chair where I want it and stay there. Overall all I think this would be a great product/solution for those who are average height or taller.

Unfortunately for me though, I’ll need to return them. Also, I may have received a used product. The wheels had minor signs of wear and came in a plain, white box with no paperwork or stickers of any sort. Not a big deal since the installation is pretty self-explanatory but I really think Amazon should disclose when it is a “used” or “refurbished” product. You order and pay for a new product so that is the expectation.

title: My favorite notebooks for work!
text: These are my absolute favorite! Everything about them is well made and thought out. It is the perfect size in my opinion. It has a stretchy loop on the side to hold your pen and a stretchy loop to keep the journal closed. The paper is thick and my ballpoint pen writes easily on it. The covers are a matte finish and not hard, but a tiny bit cushioned. It even has a pocket on the back cover on the inside to hold other small papers. GREAT PRODUCT! Will continue to buy.

title: Great, inexpensive desk mat!
text: I love this desk mat! I hadn’t realized that the lights reflected off the tables surface which can be hard on the eyes. This desk mat eliminates that and makes my work area more comfortable. It came in perfect condition with nice packaging. I didn’t have any issues with wrinkles. As soon as I laid it out on my desk, it was flat. No weird odors either. All in all, I’m happy with my purchase!

title: Lovely calendar, but the paper quality can be improved.
text:
Very lovely calendar that looks handsome on our wall. The standard American holidays are on there, and there's enough space in each square to write a few short events.

The paper can be different, however. It has a matte feel but the print isn't clean. There's some pixelation, if slight, on the edges of some text. The month's page also curls at the bottom edges, so it can look a bit weird on the wall.

title: Fun, but difficult to fully clean.
text: Great cards that work as expected, save for one issue: difficulty in cleaning. Sure, they're very thin so I'm not expecting thick whiteboard material, but getting them perfectly white requires a few wipes, even with whiteboard-cleaning spray.

title: It is what it is!
text: And perfect at that. The organizer seems sturdy enough and that it'll last for years. I wish all the shelves had the same space; only the top carries more. Still, holds all our kids' markers, crayons, and colored pencils just perfectly.

title: Handy.
text: I'm no pen snob, though I love finer instruments. I have fountain pens, fancy pencils, and nib holders, but Bic pens are always in my arsenal too. They're great for having in places where I won't worry about it getting lost (backpack, car, etc.) and are reliable. These write just as well as they always have.

title: Lock isn't too bad.
text: Good stash bag to keep in the home. I read other reviews that indicated the lock can be fussy. For my purposes, the lock is fine. I'm the only person who uses it and it's for my stash. The dials can be a bit stiff, but rotate fine. I do think the way the zipper pulls lock can be too precise for some, but, again, it works fine for me. I wish there were 4 dials to keep it more secure, but for such a small pouch 3 is fine.

title: Staples.
text:
Staples in the essential sense. These are far from competing with the superior, technologically advanced pencils we have today, but I still use these frequently if for the comfort alone. I'm also glad I got this set because I discovered I really like writing with 0.9mm lead. Initially, I thought that lead would be too thick, which was my assumption for years. I stuck with 0.5mm most of my life, and only recently discovered the benefits of 07.mm. I much prefer 0.7mm and 0.9mm to 0.5mm.

The 0.5mm from this set is a different color from teh green available in most stores and has a different stamping, which makes this set easy to recommend on that alone. The display case is fine, but I have the pencils in my pen-and-pencil organizer.

I love the pencils because they're light and just the right girth and length. The lightness makes the lead glide on paper and fun to twirl. Even though they're light they can withstand normal wear and tear. I've had a 0.5mm for years.

title: Mostly fine, but wish it were thicker.
text:
Not bad for the price. I journal daily and have other notebooks for various reasons. I carry at least two in my backpack because my thoughts flow more naturally than if I were to type them. Stream of consciousness doesn't mean I have to go back and edit my own work; journaling, for me, is perfect for that.

Anyway, I wanted to get this to better store my notebook and other writing gear I use. Currently, I use a writing mat, blotter, a ruler, and several pens and pencils. I use a laptop sleeve that has an extra compartment for small tech gear; all my stuff fits nicely, but I'd prefer something tailored specifically for my stuff. This portfolio fits my Endless notebook perfectly, but not if the back were tucked into the pad. That extra slip in the inside back of the portfolio lets notebooks with no hardcover be tucked it, which makes it no wonder that my Endless notebook doesn't fit.

Unfortunately, I couldn't make the most of this portfolio. I got it also because it has pen loops. The pen loop slip is removable, but I wanted to keep it there to house my fountain pens. The widest pen I placed in the loop was my Pilot Custom 823 and there was no squeeze. But closing the portfolio showed that I can't keep the pens and notebook inside with the portfolio closed. When I opened it back up, I saw dents in my notebook from the pen clip, which makes me very worried how long-term use will be. The other compartments are tight so only a few slips of paper or a ruler will fit.

title: Works perfectly with The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game.
text:
I didn't get these for regular playing cards, but they work fine for that. What I wanted to use these for are my solo LotR: LCG games. That game requires a lot of table space and, while I consolidated some space using dice, there's still a lot of space to save.

Once the package arrived, I was surprised--though pleasantly so--to find how heavy the box was. The two stands come packaged in a box, which I keep to put these away in. The stands are solid. I have no concerns of their longevity. There are nice felt bottoms, but they stay in place when I need them. Each slot can fit two double-sleeved cards together, but no more. That's fine, since most of my setup doesn't require more than that. The slots are spaced far apart to allow only the very tops of the cards to be seen when behind another. That's fine for playing cards, but I wish they were spaced just a bit more. C'est la vie.

title: Daily affirmations to jumpstart my workday
text: I have enjoyed having these daily affirmations on my desk. There is a stack of affirmation cards that came in a bag (see photo) with a mini gold stand that holds one card at a time. I love having it for myself and would even recommend it as a gift for someone you love.

title: Great after all these years.
text: I used these notebooks a while back. They were some of my first notebooks to doodle in. I thought it'd be great to get them for my kids. They're always looking for paper for various activities. The covers aren't as rigid as they used to be, but the paper is great (a bit thin, but does the job). Having them spiral-bound is plus so that the notebook can be completely flipped.

title: Timer is awesome. Whiteboard? Not so much.
text:
My family loves TIME TIMERs. We're a family of ADHD'ers (thanks to me), so we have a handful at home, and I have one at work. We use them daily. I thought this whiteboard version would be great for work since I also use whiteboards to help me be on top of tasks.

It's a weird setup. The whiteboard is about the size of a B5 sheet of paper, but, as you can see from the photos, there's a chunk taken out for the timer. Because of the size of the whiteboard, this takes out quite a bit of writing space. In theory, it should work well for things like the pomodoro technique, where you can write a task and set a timer for it. But writing more than that is not possible. Also, as for the actual writing experience, it's quite uncomfortable. There's a nice tray in the back to keep markers and erasers, but it's non-removable. This makes writing on the whiteboard on a flat surface impossible. The angle of the whiteboard makes my wrist cramp.

The materials are top-notch. I wish more whiteboards came as sturdy as this one. Unfortunately, I removed the timer (thank goodness that's removable, at least) and put the whiteboard in my desk.

title: Not the most effective eraser.
text:
On first use, I realized this is not a good eraser. In theory, the reusable wipes are great, and the fact that the replacements go inside the holder is awesome, but the shape of the eraser and the reusable wipes is uneven. The reusable wipes are smaller than the holder, so when I'm erasing something I can't exactly see what I'm erasing. The actual surface area of the wipes is smaller than what I'm holding.

Now, for large areas, that wouldn't be an issue--if it erased well. The eraser needs a lot of force and multiple swipes before anything is erased. And even then the markings are never completely erased. Such a shame, too, because I loved the idea of having an eraser that used reusable wipes and stored the wipes inside the container.

title: A life saver.
text:
As someone diagnosed with ADHD not too long ago (but lived a lifetime of knowing I most likely had it), I've gathered lots of resources and advice to make my organization better. One was utilizing whiteboards. I had my eye on a similar whiteboard to this listing, but this one met my needs better.

For one, it comes with storage that I can make most use of. There's a deep groove at the top to hold a couple writing instruments; I store a couple dry-erase markers in there. And the little circle groove to the right of that holds another marker but only if it's standing. I currently use Pilot Board Master S (ultra fine); they're too narrow for the circle groove, so it tilts a bit, but they're perfect for the longer groove on top.

The board is very easy to clean and indeed glass. In fact, all it is is just clear glass over a white base. I wish I got a non-glass version because the glass creates a small shadow underneath the writing, but it's not that big a deal. I just like the cleaner look of marker on a non-glass whiteboard.

To the right there's a calculator. Admittedly, I put that thing out of site because (1) I already have a few calculators and (2) I wanted to use it for more storage. Thankfully, it's removable, revealing two storage compartments underneath (albeit uncovered without the calculator). I keep a Rubik's cube knock-off and dry eraser there.

Underneath the glass are three more storage compartments: one as wide as the glass and two half-size compartments. The half-size ones have thin, protruding grooves, which are prefect for keeping more markers without them rolling around. In the long one I keep a cleaning cloth that I use when it's time to deep clean the board.

It's been great using this. I write quick notes and it makes my daily tasks more manageable.

title: Perfect for our family.
text:
Got this to write down the weekly schedule for our kids. Since half our family has ADHD, we struggle with timing. I personally must have things written down at work or else it's completely forgotten. I have multiple whiteboards, stickies (which I'll replace with reusable notes), a TIME Timer, and my phone. At home, while we have a command center and another calendar in a different room, I thought the kids having their own schedule on their wall will help.

So far it has. This whiteboard is nicely built and sturdy. The weekly print is bold and I hope it'll last a while. One thing I wish is that it had more lines. The markers it comes with are shockingly good, but the tip is a bit wide, so some schedules run into multiple lines. Still, I appreciate it came with a lot of colors so we can color-coordinate the schedule. We use the magnets to mark days complete. We haven't used the blank side yet, but I'm sure it'll come in handy.

title: Pretty good.
text:
Along with another organizer, this is used to organize my stationery at work. It has enough compartments for me because I can separate the types of pens, pencils, and refills I have. The bottom drawer houses my wooden pencils, and is even long enough for Blackwings.

The metal construction is great. The only wish I have is that the pen trays had a mesh-type bottom rather than slits; because of the slits, sometimes my pens will roll over awkwardly, but this is more of an aesthetic desire rather than utilitarian.

title: Excellent!
text:
I use it to store my notebooks and random paper supplies at work. The top cubby for pens is a super-nice touch; I store taller instruments there, and the shorter ones in the drawers. Note that the drawers aren't the same length; because of that cubby for the taller instruments, the top two drawers are shorter than the bottom most.

It's very sturdy and I have no fear of it breaking here at work.

title: Super clear, seems sturdy, but a bit thin in the fingers.
text:
I used these to sort printed recipes. Sure, recipes are available digitally (and I even have an app that lets me read recipes from my cloud), but sometimes paper is nice to have around. Okay, a lot of times.

So I got a bunch of the printed recipes that had been stacked in a kitchen cabinet. It became so unwieldy that we had no idea how many recipes we had, or which ones. So away I organized.

Most of the pages opened right away; some took a bit more pulling apart. One even seemed to glued shut, but I got it open. When I was inserting the recipes, I felt that the pages were a bit thin. I'm not sure how they'll hold up in the long term, but I guess that's something future me will have to deal with when it happens.

Once everything was in the binder, though, it was awesome. The pages are super clear and, somehow, make some sheets more legible. Weird.

title: Nice visual supports
text: As a BCBA and the mother of a daughter with ADHD, these time timers are ESSENTIAL. They are the perfect visual support to aid my learners and daughter with understanding time and helping with transitions. These particular timers are heavy duty. Although they haven't been thrown or tossed across the room, they are fairly sturdy and I predict that they can survive it should it happen. I love the vibrant color options that are included in the pack. The only drawback to these timers is the price tag - they are extremely expensive.

title: Excellent organizer, though I wish it were a bit taller.
text:
Ordered this to replace our old crayon organizer, which was a solid piece made of wood. It certainly was sturdy, but there was very little modularity and the rotating wheel broke off. We opted for this plastic iteration as a replacement.

I was concerned about the "slices" being removable easily, but so far they've stayed in place. My main concern was them staying in place despite constant use, but so far so good. I like that they're removable so that my kids won't have to fight over who gets to have the organizer near them. While this has more room than our previous one, it's a bit short. Colored pencils stay in place, but I wish the organizer was a bit taller anyway.

title: Works great for gaming. Tabletop gaming, that is.
text:
After realizing I needed more space for an LCG I'm playing (Lord of the Rings), I browsed larger play mats. The largest I had was a 24x24 two-player play mat; it fit everything I wanted, but I realized I needed something that was shorter and wider rather than wide in all directions. There are some good play mats dedicated for card games, but the prices can vary. Then I realized I'd have better results when searching mouse pads with the dimensions I wanted.

This is the perfect size for my game. I can fit all the cards I need horizontally, and the shorter vertical height helps with having the enemy deck closer so I can read everything. I don't rotate my cards, but I did try on this mat to find out how it worked. Overall it was fine, but the mat did give some resistance. I don't fault the mouse pad though since it's not meant for my current use. The cushioning also helps me pick up cards more easily since I can dig my fingertips a bit into the mat.

title: Fine for single sheets or small books, but awkward.
text:
I use a plastic book stand at work that I love. It's able to fit nearly any sized book. The page holders even allow for frequent page turning because the arms end in small rollers. But I wanted one for home, so I ordered these.

The metal is nice and it feels sturdy--for the base, that is. The arms are a lot thinner and easy to bend (case in point: my daughter did so in the first five minutes). The stands are fine for smaller books with plenty of text, or single sheets. The angles are okay too. The arms are a disaster. They make page-turning more cumbersome because I have to flip the bottom arm down and finagle with the arms. They move easily when I'm trying to turn a page, so I just put them behind the stand. But there's no way to easily put them back there, so I bend them just a little.

The colors are perfect for spring if you're into that.

title: Comfy!
text:
So far, so good. I use these and another arm rest by the company. Seeing as I have an L-shaped desk, it's important to have my hands and arms as comfortable as possible. The keyboard rest is a bit short for my dual keyboard/num-pad setup, but the rest is made for a TKL anyway.

The mouse rest is nice too. It's a bit short for my liking, but does the job.

The texture on these are nice and supports my wrists comfortably.

title: Nice!
text:
Because I work at my desk all the time, and I have a corner desk, my elbow becomes sore after a long period of resting on the desk. This elbow pad comes to the rescue!

It works just great. My elbow rests comfortably, and the pattern is nice against my skin. There's no logo on mine, unlike in the producting listing, but I prefer it that way. And the bottom comes with a non-slip surface, so the pad stays in place.

title: Makes life more organized.
text:
I've used several label makers at work recently, but the last one I actually owned was from the 90s. You know, the ones that printed the raised, white letters on black (and later, colored) tapes? It's been a while since I labeled things at home, but with current technology I had a strong itch to do so.

This particular model is nearly perfect for home use. It's a bit bulkier than it needs to be, but the bulk does make it comfortable to hold. The screen is as clear as it needs to be, and finding the settings becomes second nature. I've used nearly all the fonts, frames, and sizes, and haven't had a complaint. This is for the actual maker itself.

My gripes come with the tape and dispenser. The tape this maker accepts is on the thin side, so big labels are out of the question. The fonts aren't crisp, so there is some fuzzing around the letters, etc. There is also a LOT of tape wasted because of the distance from the cutter to the ejection border. I feel they could make the cutter closer to save on tape. Even with the margins at the thinnest, the maker wastes more tape than I'd like; it certainly doesn't help that official cartridges are about $15 each.

Still, organizing things around the home is easy. Depending on the tapes you get, the labels are durable and last many washes. My daughters take water bottles to school and they're required to have their names on them. I slap on a label and it lasts about a month's worth of dish-washing.

title: Still don't get how to use these.
text: I've gone through two before, this is my third. This one is more difficult to use, but more comfortable to hold. I use official Scotch packing tape to seal packages. Since the packages vary in length, I thought these dispensers would make taping easier. My experience led me otherwise. The tape is difficult to place onto the box, and it's even more difficult to rip off. I go through two or three times before I get a good seal on the box, which is a waste of tape. I've resorted to using just the standard disposable dispensers.

title: Great if it didn't skip a lot.
text:
I've been into fountain pens for over a decade. My two first pens were a Pilot and a vintage Esterbrook. Since then, I've honed my tastes and know what I like.

Given the opportunity to try a Parker 51, I immediately jumped on the opportunity. Initial impressions were fine. The pen came with a cartridge which I used since, when the ink ran out, I was gonna re-use with a syringe. The cap is metal, while the body is plastic. It's a weird balance when capped or posted, so I leave the cap off. The body leading to the nib is a nice look, but the nib skips a *lot*. Every time I begin writing with this pen, there is some scribbling required to get the pen out, and if I pause for too long I have to rewrite a letter or so to get the ink pouring again.

It's very easy to take apart and clean, but the price isn't justified for the quality.

title: Great for us.
text: Great corkboard for the wall. There was no warping when it arrived, which is a problem we've had with other boards. This board also comes with some pins.

title: Nice pen, but skips a lot.
text:
Lovely pen that unfortunately skips a lot, and in my opinion is overpriced for what it is. The resin body is polished but scratches easily. The cap is awesome; it's metal and weighted. However, this gives an unbalanced feel when posted. Since the body is composed from a light resin material, there's an awkward dive toward the cap.

The pen skips every time I write with it. I've gone through a refill, and not matter how often I start the pen skips. Once it flows, it flows.

title: Very good paper.
text: Good paper that's great for all kinds of kids' paint. Whether finger painting or brush painting, the paper absorbs the colors well and helps it dry. The glue that holds the paper into the pad isn't strong, but that doesn't matter to us; we take the pages out when they're being used.

title: Overall good, but skipping can be annoying.
text:
Lovely pen that overall performs as I would expect a pen at this price range. The weight is nice, though a bit lighter than expected. It feels great in my hand. The nib width is pleasant; I opted for a Medium. I know western medium nibs are wider than eastern widths, but I wanted to try a wider than preferred nib this time. I'm not disappointed.

However, the pen does skip every time I start writing with it. Once I get the ink flowing, there's little to no skipping, though always at the beginning.

title: Fantastic upgrade.
text:
Previously, I had a similar (albeit slightly smaller) black mouse pad that cost about a third of this Razer. I'm no gamer, but I do like mechanical keyboards, and am very particular with mouse sensitivity. I use a gaming mouse, but I use it at work; I prefer the gaming mouse because I find it to be far more precise than others I've tried (including some that are double the cost).

The pad feels well-made. Usually, I'm not one to get Razer products because of the gaudy green branding, but this one masks the branding well. The logo is stitched on a very small cloth; otherwise, the entire pad is plain black.

There is a coarser feel to the mouse than my previous one, but it doesn't detract from the mouse's ability to glide easily. It's more of a rugged feel. After a couple of months of usage, the pad shows little to no wear.

title: Nice addition to the school year

It is one board with the front and back filled out. It comes with a pack of chalk. It would’ve been nice to have an eraser come with it too. Overall, nice addition to the school year.

They were extremely easy to use when creating them on the computer and editing them. We just used the template that Avery recommended. The labels went onto the envelopes easily and stayed in place. We had many compliments on how classy these labels were on the envelopes! I would definitely use these again.

title: Great starter set.

title: Great quality cards
text: Hallmark has always made great quality cards and these are no exception. They are the perfect addition to any Mother's Day gift. The designs are bright and vibrant. Highly recommend.

title: Nice addition to any home office
text: This is a nice addition to any home office or any busy parent trying to keep track of a crazy schedule. I used this for my family's schedule and had everyone a different colored marker depending on what needed to be done that particular day. This really helped me keep track of things. The only caveat is that I kept it in my bedroom where my little munchkins couldn't touch it (that tends to lead to them erasing things and writing over what I have). The only drawback I have, which I would run into with any dry erase product, is that you have to clean it regularly in order to ensure that the markers do not stain.

This is a great addition to a playroom or work space. I would, however, be mindful of how to hang it. This was not an easy task!

title: Beautiful cover; great planner
text: I don’t usually use planners. I need to organize my life but the thought of a planner has always overwhelmed me. I decided to give this planner a go. I love it! Super easy to use. Beautiful cover. When I’m done using this one I’ll definitely be getting another AT-A-GLANCE planner!

title: Amazing erasers. They saved me during finals.
text:
One of my finals was a handwritten coding course. I had to make sure each indent was precise and each character perfect. I decided to use these erasers during the final and they were my go-to. Naturally, during finals you don't want to risk it, so I had two others as backups just in case, but I turned to this one the whole way.
Not only was the size perfect, but the Tombow Mono erased better than all of my other erasers. The graphite markings were nearly obliterated, and I was free to correct some of my mistakes as though they were my initial writings.
