title: Lovely, but not sure how I'm going to clean this.
text:
Brought this thing to work to see how it would fare in an office environment, and whether it would enhance the sound of my mechanical keyboard. The lighting effect isn't too glaring; thankfully, there's a pulsing mode which makes the light "breath" in and out, so it's not always super bright. It even changes colors in the breathing mode!
The mat comes rolled up in a box with just a micro-USB cable. There are no instructions, but for this you don't really need any. Just plug in the cable and tap the button on the mat controller. The buttons cycle first through colors, then through a strobe mode (not recommended), then to a pulsing mode (which is what I have it on), then completely off. Very simple.
The mat feels really good. A soft, cloth texture on top, but seems pretty durable so as to withstand a long period of time. The keyboard I have it on now is made of solid aluminum, so we'll see how it holds up over time. The bottom is VERY grippy. I tried moving it and had to lift it up completely to do so.

I'm not sure how I'll be able to clean this because of the electronics. I was hoping to toss it in the wash but that doesn't seem possible. The listing states it's very easy to clean, so we'll see once it comes time to do so. If I remember I'll update this review.

A bonus is that, because this if my first cloth mat, the sound of my keyboard is actually a lot better. I have tactile switches which sound more deepened. Nice!

title: Works amazingly for my Hobonichi Cousin.
text:
After browsing the official covers for the Hobonichi cousin as well as handmade ones, I randomly landed on this Kokuyo cover on Amazon. As I use my Hobonich for school and need more than one ribbon, I thought it was perfect with three and had lots of additional features like a band to keep it closed, a pen loop, and plastic inside flaps to use for various things like marking additional pages, keeping things secure, or even as a writing board.
The Hobonichi Cousin contains different calendar views, and the extra ribbons come in handy for that. I use two for recent assignments, and another to keep tabs on a different calendar where I put important deadlines that I can see at a glance. The Kokuyo cover is A5 in size, so I imagine it would fit any A5 book no thicker than an inch. I believe the Cousin is just under an inch in thickness and it fits beautifully.

After about a year of use, the planner shows very little wear. I use it almost daily and keep it in my backpack, as well as sprawled on the table when it's study time. Extremely versatile cover and well worth the price if you want to use it to house your Cousin.

title: Colorful, well-made mat
text: My six year old daughter loves to roll around and wants to join gymnastics. This has been the perfect addition to our playroom. What I like most is that it is easy to clean. I usually just wipe it down with baby wipes and it's good to go! It also fold easily which makes storage a breeze. This is a great mat for home, the gym, or schools/daycares. The mat appears to be made from durable materials and I expect this mat to last a while.

title: Great resource for first graders!
text:
Being an educator and a mother, I love finding new resources to reinforce concepts that my kids will learn at school.
My daughter is six years old and started working on this book two months ago, right before starting first grade. Math is a subject that she usually struggles in so I was excited to use this book to provide her with extra practice with lessons that are difficult for her.

This book is perfect for children who are going into first grade or who have just started first grade. The lessons included in this book are: Operations and Algebraic Thinking, Number and Operations in Base Ten, Measurement and Data, Geometry, and Reproducibles. In the beginning of the book it outlines how to utilize the math workshop for each of the sections. This includes a warm-up consisting of 5 minutes, mini-lesson consisting of 10-15 minutes, rotations consisting 10-20 minutes each, and closure/reflection of 3-5 minutes. The math workshop outlined in the book is great for classrooms, but the worksheets within in the book work well for practice at home as well.

title: Great product, confusing set up.
text:
Reviewing the Epson Scanner. It was a bit confusing while setting up because the instructions stated that the scanner shouldn’t be connected to the laptop. Then it stated to download the software from the internet. So there was a delay trying to figure out if the scanner needed to be connected directly to the internet and but didn’t know how to do this. After a few minutes I realized the instructions meant the scanner shouldn’t be connected to the laptop via USB cord and the software needed to be downloaded to the laptop being used to set up the scanner.

Once I figured this out I was able to easily and quickly follow the 3 step set-up guide and "viola" I scanned a picture with the Epson DS-770 scanner. Now I have a beautiful picture of my daughter on my computer. It took me 15 minutes to scan the picture but would have taken me less than 10 minutes if the instructions where a bit more clear for those of us that are not as tech-y.

The Epson-DS770 is compact and makes scanning a breeze. Very cool!

title: Super fast printer. A few hiccups, but overall very, very pleased.
text:
The installation process was extremely easy. The touch screen guides you through the process step by step. It starts with a series of questions (date, time, etc). It then prompts you to install the ink cartridges that come with the printer. This is a great deal as these ink cartridges can cost a pretty penny. The cartridge installation takes approximately twenty minutes. While it is installing, you can complete the remaining steps. It then prompts you to place paper in the paper tray. You will need to place paper in the paper tray in order to complete the installation process, so make sure you have some handy.
I did notice that it didn't ask me to calibrate the color settings, etc., as my previous printers did, but there are options to do so once all the initializing has completed.

You are able to install the printer app on your smartphone in order to access information regarding the printer (printing, scanning, capture document, look at printer settings). By the time we arrived at this step, the installation process was about half-way done. We needed to wait another ten minutes or so until we could install the printer on our computers using the CDs that came with the printer, although I'm sure you can download the latest software from HP's website.
We downloaded the software on all our devices, and did our first printing from a phone--coupons. The image came out blurry, though I'm not sure if that's because it was the first print or because it was from a phone. The fine print on the coupon was unreadable, whereas it's easily readable from our previous printers (that cost a third of this!).

That said, we waited a while and did some additional printing from out computer, and the images came out as clear as crystal.
However, we did have some issues with printing from Safari and Chrome; Firefox printed without issue, so I'm not sure what the disconnect is here. May follow up once I've figured it out.

We are using this printer for personal use at home. We will mostly use it for small work projects, school assignments, and, mostly, coupon printing. It is a bit on the bigger side for a personal-use printer, but it is extremely user friendly and efficient. The ink cartridges are expected to last a while which makes their price fairly reasonable, compared to other printers. The look of the printer is extremely sleek and sophisticated. I was worried about the white as most of our previous printers had a glossy finish, but I was extremely pleased when it came and I saw the finish is a nice, textured matte finish. This way any dust and whatnot won't show as easily.

So far we like it, despite the minor gripes mentioned above. We did all the calibrating available, and the prints are super fast. The ink comes out a bit heavy on plain office paper, though there are settings to set the density. (Husband note: I plan on printing custom home video covers, so I'll be ordering special paper for that; I expect the print quality will be better.)

title: Same great Avery labels; receipts if necessary.
text:
I've been using Avery labels for years, and without many issues. At least, compared to the other brands out there, especially third-party offerings.
Does that mean that Avery has no issues? Absolutely no, but they are minimal compared to the competition. The only real issue I have, which is the same with these labels, is that, depending on the surface of the package/envelope, it needs to be spread hard for the label to stick properly. Otherwise, using these is *far* easier than printing labels on standard copy paper and taping the edges.

They are thick and able to cover the previous label if you re-use packages (Who doesn't these days?), although I tend to remove the previous labels anyway with box cutters. I prefer to use the two-label paper, but there are times when you need to print receipts. This number, 5127, is perfect for that, especially if you issue invoices and print the labels from those same invoices. They're indispensable when having bulk orders, as the receipt helps keep track of the contents of each parcel.

I myself have not had any issues with printing, although I use a relatively low-end commercial laser printer to do all my printing. The only color is black, and I've never tried printing Avery labels with multiple inks.

text: I have purchased so many pens over the years that seem a struggle to use, with ink that stops as much as it starts. These pens are a real pleasure: there's a lovely flow to them that seems steady and expressive. Very smooth. And the pen is comfortable, fitting my hand well. I could immediately tell the difference and could understand what the other positive reviewers were happy about. There are other decent pens out there, but these seem to be a step beyond. I bought a box of 36 on sale for just under $12. I liked them so much I went back and ordered a 2nd box while the price was low, coming in at slightly more than 30 cents a piece. The cost is still higher than some of the choices, but these seem so much better and well worth the difference. I think you will understand how great these are if you give them a try. The ones that I purchased and like so much also have the name "Atlantis" on them in addition to "Velocity Bold." I'm not quite clear on the double name and why the Atlantis part doesn't always seem to show up in the listing.  I have only recently acquired these pens, so can't really speak the the longevity of them. My husband always complains that his pens never last more than about a week. I gave him a couple of these to try, so maybe will update post this review. But regardless of when the ink might or might not run out, it's a lovely smooth experience till then.

I tried to wipe off the label, but it really doesn't come off all the way, rather leaving a sort of haze. After this first initial bumpy start, it seemed to write well; however, the writing tip is thick, not intended for a very fine line or small space use.
I do like the labels: there are a lot of them in nice large sizes. I did find, however, that contrary to what was stated, they are not so easy to peel up/off and straighten out. I did finally manage to do so, but they do stick pretty tightly, which I suppose, can be seen as a positive as well. My use was on plastic containers. My attempt to remove and adjust was right after initial placement. I'm wondering if trying to peel these off after a few months or years is even possible. I really don't know. In any case, satisfied with these, but not thrilled. Not having ever used other brands of these, I can't really compare the quality.

title: If You Type...You Need This NOW.

If your keyboard remains flat on the desk and doesn't have 'legs' on it to raise it, you need one of these. Don't wait until you feel pain to get one, because when the pain hits, it HURTS. And it could possibly affect your work. Be prepared. Avoid the pain. Get one of these NOW.

title: Must have for busy people
text:
I got this so my husband and I can plan our meals for the week. We get so focused on our projects that we will (and have) forget to eat and when the hunger finally hits us it's 10pm. We have alarms on our phones to remind us to start thinking about dinner at 6:30p every day, but then the game of "what's for dinner" begins. This awesome product helps us figure that out ahead of time.

The entire board is magnetic which means it latched onto our fridge and didn't want to let go. It was a little crooked at first and I had to peel it completely off in order to realign it. The board comes with four pens (red, green, blue and black) and the pens have two awesome features: they have dry erasers on their lids - which makes changing the board a breeze; and they are magnetic - this keeps them close at hand and not stuck in a drawer.

The package also includes a larger dry eraser, which is surprisingly magnetic as well. I didn't realize it at first because it wouldn't stick to the fridge but it does stick a little bit.. however, its magnet is not very strong so I'm not sure how well it will stay up when the door is opened and closed.

There are also four smaller decorative magnets included. The images on mine are a sunset, a castle, a dandelion and some odd ensemble of cartoon caricatures.. no clue what or who they are supposed to be. I'll be giving that magnet to one of my grand kids. Perhaps they'll be familiar with the picture.

The only negative is that, despite being shipped in a flat package (very nice touch, by the way), the upper left corner of my board is creased. The magnetic grasp of the board does not seem to be affected (it is not curled up away from the fridge or anything) but it is slightly annoying as it reduces the overall aesthetics of the board.

Overall, I am SO happy with this! My husband and I just finished filling it out for next week. The pens write on it really well and they don't run. If anything the tips are a little thick for the space provided. Let me just tell you now.. you will not be able to write as small and clear as the images included in the listing, at least not with the pens included. I used the blank spaces on the bottom of the board for planned appointments and my upcoming trips (I am a school bus driver and in addition to my regular route every morning and afternoon, I take our various teams to their away games) so my husband is aware of when I won't be home. I highly recommend this set for planning your meals and as a reminder board for everyone else in your house. For everything included, the price is very fair!

title: Perfect for cross-stitching
text:
I purchased these highlighters to use with my cross-stitching projects. I'm in the process of hand-making a personalized Christmas stocking for every member of our family. In each kit, there's a guide (kind of like a coloring book page) that has an outline of the design and has symbols for each color and type of stitch. Well, keeping your place and knowing exactly where you are is very important so I've been using highlighters to mark my progress. However, other brands have either been too dark (they cover or color out the detailed lines that are done at the end of the project) or they bleed and cover more than the area that I wanted to highlight making it confusing on where exactly I am or what I have already done.

I got hese Writech highlighters in their pastel colors and they are a dream come true! Being pastel, they color the blocks I want them to but not too dark to make it difficult to see the finishing stitch lines for later. They also don't bleed over to adjacent blocks - major bonus points! And they're retractable!! This was a huge deal for me as when I'm stitching along and want to mark a row off on my guide (something done every few minutes), I don't want to pause and have to use both hands to remove a cap. With these, I can simple stab my needle into the fabric, pick up the highlighter, click the end like a pen, mark my guide and continue right on stitching. Fabulous! Ive also had no issues with these highlighters drying out. The flaps that retract when you click to open and close them falls into place every time. And to finish it off - the ink dries fast! I don't have to worry about smearing or runs ruining my guide!

Bottom line... the retractable, pen-like clickers are great! The ink dries fast, doesn't run or bleed and the colors are perfect for being able to mark what you need to and still be able to clearly make out what's under the color. Highly recommend! When I use these up, I'll certainly be back for more! (I have quite a few more stockings to make so I'll probably be a lifetime customer LOL!)

title: Labels don't stick and printing ability doesn't last.
text:
We've had this label maker for a few years, but only use it maybe once a or twice a year. I tried using it a bunch when we moved to label our plastic tubs, but as others have noted, the labels don't stick to anything but paper. Which is kind of useless. So I ended up printing labels and using packaging tape to tape over it.

What irritates me more is the whole "doesn't need ink!" claim, like it'll last forever as long as you get more tape. After my printer started doing a shoddy print job, I looked up on how to get more ink and found out there's no ink or ribbon to be had. So I looked up instructions on how to fix this--and Dymo said I simply had to "clean" the printer parts with this little wand thing inside the cap. Ok. So I cleaned it as per instructions, and when that didn't work I tried every other way under the sun and it did absolutely nothing to help the problem. I have a whole reel of tape going to go to waste because of this.

Needless to say, I won't be buying another Dymo to replace this one.

title: Love These Pen(s)tels
text:
I absolutely adore these pens. They make writing fun! I decided I needed something different at work. Something that would make all the writing I do stand out in a very helpful way.

I go from one project to another regularly, not always able to finish one before something with a higher priority comes up. Using a different color each time I mark down what I'd just been working on. I can easily distinguish between all that I've written down at a glance with the rainbow of colors in my notebook.

The ink doesn't bleed through to the back of the page so I get to use both sides of the page and easily read it. I have a lot going on at work and making things more interesting with my different colored Pentels - actually helps me reduce stress by making stop for a few seconds each time I pick a new gel pen color. Those seconds add up over the course of each half hour. Since I have a habit of not taking breaks - these seemingly inconsequential moments of selecting a new color is soothing.

Being able to look over a page and see the fluidity of my writing broken only by the ink color shows me at a glance how much I have actually accomplished. I might have to Subscribe to these pens because I use them all the time now instead of just occasionally. I'll reevaluate things in a couple months. Stay tuned 🙂.

title: I Won't Be Ordering These Pens Again
text:
With nerve damage to my hand I need adaptive ergonomic tools to help me write. And I love to write. Well I had the opportunity to buy a pack of 24 BIC CRISTAL XTRA SMOOTH BLACK 1.0mm medium Ballpoint pens & a 24 pack of BLUE ones as ADD ON ITEMS. Unfortunately while the pens do write smoother then some, even when I press harder I still don't experience anything close to how well the BIC CRISTAL XTRA BOLD BALLPOINT PEN (1.6mm) writes.

I will not we using these pens. I will make them available for my friends and students to use. I already feel my hand hurting from using these pens, unlike when I use the XTRA BOLD (1.6mm) which Glide across the paper. I just need to move my hand to the right & cursive writing is effortless. The packaging was poorly done as well. All the black pens had fallen out of their smashed box while the blue ones remained intact in their box. I tried to return the unopened box of blue pens but Amazon would not allow it. Maybe because they were an ADD ON ITEM, but in actuality I don't know why.

If you all looking for a basic medium point pen that is cheap as an ADD ON product this item just might be for you. They write with a little prompting and continue until the ink is gone. With transparent barrels you can see how much ink you still have remaining. If you have no problems with your hands these pens should present no problem for you.

title: Wonderful Colorful Thin 1.6mm Pens
text:
Really love these new pens. I was hesitant, never experiencing 1.6mm in a thinner pen before. I have to use special adaptations on my pens due to nerve damage. I have ones I really like, but couldn't use because I preferred the thicker BIC VELOCITY 1.6mm pens. Well BIC has done something very wonderful and created thinner 1.6mm BIC CRISTAL XTRA-BOLD Ball Pens. I wasn't sure if they would write as smooth or with a thicker line. THEY DID!
I'm so glad that I ordered the 8 Multicolored pen pack. I have placed them in the car, my bag, my purse, upstairs and downstairs. I've even taken a few of them to work. I write a great deal & I need a pen that doesn't bleed through, especially my Steno pad pages or the notebooks I use at work. These pens are great when writing out checks, printing out addresses on envelopes or labels. I will definitely be buying them again.

title: Great Product for Adults Who Suffer from Hand Pain
text: I have nerve damage that affects my hand and I love to write, but trying to use a pen or pencil made my hand hurt so  much I found myself writing less and less. Then I researched ergonomic aids and this item came up. I loved them so much that I bought another pack and shared it with my mother who has arthritic hands. She said they definitely made a difference for her too.

title: Traditional Steno Pads, but not possessing hard covers
text:
I use Steno Pads daily for lists of my favorite authors, but mostly for Book / Purchase reviews on Amazon, as well as Goodreads. The back covers are thin, but I use them with a clipboard to have a hardback to write upright. I've also taped hard cardboard onto the inside back cover and then I don't need a clipboard. This also makes it possible for me to stand the Steno Pad upright on its own as I type out my reviews. It makes it easier to read than if the Steno Pad were lying flat.

I did try out the smaller 6x9 clipboards, but the Steno Pad didn't fit. Part of it was hanging off. These are a cheaper reasonably priced set of 12 Steno Pads. I do prefer harder back Steno Pads, but I used some ingenuity and packing tape to make the back covers of these Pads very firm. It's not a pretty DIY, but no one actually notices it, unless you point it out. I do recommend this 12 pack. The bargain price pushed these up to 5 Stars.

title: I prefer Black Pens, but really like using these particular 1.6 mm Blue BOX Velocity pens
text:
I have enjoyed BIC Velocity 1.6mm Bold point Black pens for several years. Since I am really a fan of the Bold 1.6ers, I decided to try the BOLD Point 1.6mm Blue Velocity pens. I enjoy it better than thinner pens. I think arthritic or people with nerve damage would find these pens easier to grip. In comparison to the ZEBRA F301 Stainless Steel 0.7mm Fine point these VELOCITY pens are lighter weight.

This is my first experience with these Blue pens and while I like the Black BOLD more, I really am enjoying writing with this Smooth gliding pen. I write a great deal at work & for pleasure away from work. This 12 Pack will be a nice addition to my Pen Collection. I will be using them everyday. With twelve I can have a few at home, a few at work, and a few in my bag, as well as one or two in the car.

I find myself being able to both write in cursive and easily print with these pens. The retractable point means less accidental ink stains on my clothes, in my bag, on the bed, the couch upholstery, or on my hands. I recommend without reservation to people who like writing with a thicker pen. It's a very smooth writing pen exactly what I need daily. I hope you enjoy using these Blue pens as much as I do.

Too bad it's bedtime I could easily write a few more hours with this pen. Not enjoying tonight's humidity though. I'm putting a few pens in my bag for work right now, as well as taking a couple upstairs. Have a good night - looking forward to using one of these at work tomorrow. Or maybe I'll stay up a little longer to write up a couple reviews of books I recently completed.

title: Sometimes you have to Gift yourself
text:

If you own a Dachshund you know they are busy. If you don't want a busy body in your house don't get one. They are hounds who love being outside and in the bedroom with you.

My little Miniature Wirehaired who has one speed - fast! I used to wonder if she'd ever be able to go up all the stairs to where the bedrooms are? She runs up at top speed. She weighs 8 lbs at 2 years old because she cat naps (literally with the cat) and then she's all action. Usually doing something that makes me laugh.

My daily thought is what is she going to do today? And usually I can't even imagine. It is such an adventure living with a Dachshund whether it's Smooth, Long haired, or a Wire. Standards, Minis, and Tweenies. All types of colors.

If you want to smile and laugh a lot you need to get a Doxie. If you can't get this calendar and enjoy their antics!

title: Beautiful calendar that depicts mostly Smooth coated Doxies
text:
Dachshunds come in many colors, two (really three) sizes: Standards, Miniatures, and Tweenies (in between sizes) and three coat varieties: Smooth, Longhaired, and Wirehaired.

This makes for lots to love for anyone who loves Dachshunds. In the past the Daily Box Calendar captured that diversity of types of coats. So when I purchased not only one but two calendars one for home and one for my office it was in anticipation of seeing several Wirehaired Dachshunds like my little Miniature girl each month.

I was shocked when in trying to show someone at work the difference between the coats and I could only find ONE Wirehaired in the entire calendar! What?! And there were only several Longhaired Dachshund pictures out of over 300 pictures...Really?!!

The calendar consists of mostly Smooths. Which is fine if Dachshunds weren't so diverse. So if you're a Smoothie owner and Dachshund lover you will enjoy the entertaining photos very much. The pictures are beautiful and depict the antics of silly & serious Doxies.

I just wish there were more Wirehaired and Longhaired Dachshunds to enjoy with their Smooth brethren. It's like a owner of a Chocolate Lab purchasing a Daily Box Labrador Retriever calendar and finding mostly Black with only a couple Yellow Labs and the picture of ONE Chocolate Lab. They love all Labs but it's so great to see your variety represented too.

I plan to give my second Daily Calendar to one of the many Smooth Dachshund owners I see while I'm out with my little Wirehaired. Someone who loves Dachshunds as much as I do, who will love & enjoy a calendar that depicts their low long baby in all it's tail wagging happiness.Of course I am keeping one of the calendars because though I have a coat preference I am still a Dachshund Devotee. text:
I was having trouble with my home phone. The cable guy fixed one outlet which took a long time. He recommended that I buy a base system like this since it could be attached to the line he repaired then the other phones just need to be plugged into an electrical outlet.

The only inconvenient thing is that they all have to be plugged directly into an electrical outlet. I didn't realize that at first so I tried plugging it into the electrical outlet in the wall system of my bed so I wasn't able to get it to work. That means that I had to put the base where it can be plugged in directly. I can't reach the phone directly from my bed anymore. But since the phone is cordless, I put the phone by my bed when I'm in bed in case anyone calls. I just have to remember to put it back into its cradle to recharge when I leave the room.

It was fairly easy to set up, save numbers to the directory, add numbers to the block call list, set the number of rings before the answering system picks up, and record my outgoing message. One of the best things is that once the directory, etc. Is set up with one phone, it automatically appears in the other phones. So even though the base and answering machine is in my bedroom, I can see if I have any messages and listen to them from the phone in my living room. And since the satellite phones don't use a phone line, I can put a phone anywhere I want in the house wherever there is an electrical outlet. This means that I can have a phone in my bathroom, if I so wanted.

The sound is very good, including the speaker. With my old phones, people had trouble hearing me if I was on speaker - especially with my mother who has trouble hearing. The number keys are also large, illuminated when the phone button is turned on, and easy to read.

So far I am very happy with this phone!

My parents have been married 53 years. And for over 53 years they have had a 'secret code' they write to each other in cards, notes, etc. When we 3 kids were younger - even up through our 30s - we would always try to figure out what the series of letters meant. As we've matured, seeing that series of letters (starts of "T.S.T.S.T.S...") became more of a cherished sight. And we don't want to know anymore; finding out would kinda ruin the magic, y'know!?! So I bought some THICKKKKKKK blank white cards and these markers, asked my parents to each do about 10 cards with their little message. I plan on having the cards matted, framed and give as gifts to my siblings some day (and there's extra for the grandkids if they ever want them when they're on their own).

The sharpies did the job: Nice, crisp, non-smudged letters. I couldn't be happier with a "marker" tbh

title: Just buy the erasable gel pens & save your $$
text:
I so wanted to LOVE this item! For me, though, using the pen that came with the RocketBook, the writing was like... you know how you use a gel pen and it's *thisclose* to bring out of ink, so the writing is 'spotty'? You find yourself shaking the pen and trying to finish the word or sentence or list you started without having to go back to the kitchen junk drawer or top desk drawer or your purse to find another pen? That's the way the writing was coming out on the page. So, off to the big box 'office supplies for twice as much... that was easy [money for them]' and I bought a package of the Frixion pens. It wasn't until I was standing there, forced to actually shop in person, that I realized that these Frixion pens write on ANY paper and erase with... 💡DUH!!... friction. Bought the multipack of pens, got home, tore the pack open, went to finish my list and the black pen in the multipack wrote just as cruddy. As did the navy blue, the royal blue, the red... all of 'em. So, I grabbed a clean sheet of paper and used one of my new pens (clickable with the rubber 'eraser') and they write splendidly on paper. They also 'erase' perfectly on paper.

Verdict: The RocketBook is not for me. I'm too ocd or too perfectionist or lack enough patience for a $32+ book with like 5 pages that makes all my lists and notes look like I have a dried out pen. I don't need the app, probably would have never used it anyway. So I sent the RocketBook back for a full refund. Maybe the book I bought was old and whatever film or whatever they use on the pages (to make them wipe away with water and the included microfiber cloth) was old 🤷🏼‍♀️ I won't say the entire product is worthless, because I'm not going to spend another $32 to find out.

title: Greatly regret buying this printer!
text:
The Epson ET-2650 was ordered Oct. 2, 2018, and delivered Oct. 4, 2018. It worked as promised in the description -- at first.

First issue: It drinks ink! I had no reason to think we used more ink than average until this printer. I quickly went through the first four Epson color ink bottles and was already halfway through the second box of Epson ink refill bottles when the unit failed, after only 4 months of moderate use. The description suggested the ink refills would last up to two years. I didn't expect the refills to last that long, but less than four months is quite a bit short of the predicted ink use. We don't print every day, and certainly not in huge quantities.

Second issue: From the time of purchase, I needed to clean print heads frequently due to the print quality being unreadable on parts of the page. I'd never experienced this with previous printers. Photo 2.

Third issue: This printer became unusable when it could no longer print documents from a website, like Amazon. Instead of the printer recognizing and printing letters and/or numbers, it substituted blobs of ink instead. End result, I had a printer that couldn't print receipts or other online information. This problem developed about two months after we purchased it. Photo 1.

Replacement policy: When I contacted Epson, the phone rep indicated that he thought it was possibly a hardware issue. To get a replacement printer, Epson would send a box for the printer. I was to mail the printer back to the company. Once they received the printer, they would send me a replacement. However I had to send them a check for nearly $200 before they would send the box.

I would have been happy to receive the return box and mail the printer to Epson, then waited for them to OK the return, and send me a replacement printer. That wasn't an option.

I opted to NOT send Epson either the printer or the money. Instead, I'm recycling the printer and have purchased an HP.

-- Former Epson customer

title: Good for Portable Printing Needs
text:
Documents are usually transferred and shared electronically, but there are still those times when you need to print. Having a printer that is easily portable and easily connectable is great when you’re on the run and this need convinced me to get this HPRT Wireless Portable Printer.

Setting up this printer requires a few simple steps. First, you need to open the top, take out the paper roll, and tear it to get it ready to print. You then feed the edge of the paper through the slot and snap the lid shut. Next, you need to go online and download the printer driver, then install on your pc. If you want to print from your phone, you just download the Hereprint app.

The best feature of this printer is its portability and its best use is printing from your phone, through the app. I already have regular printers at home and at work, so I don’t really need help in these places. But I often do need to print from other locations and I like that this small, skinny printer can be taken anywhere and that I can send documents to it, straight from my smartphone.

As for quality, this printer is best for printing documents. I have tried printing pictures and the quality is not the best. The other issue I have with this printer is that it requires rolls of paper, which means you need to have a supply on hand, and they are not that easy to find. I would prefer just feeding individual 8.5 by 11 inch sheets, but you can’t do that with this printer. You have to use a paper roll.

Printing will never go completely out of style. Printers are generally inexpensive nowadays and are available most anywhere. But portable printers are not widely available and thus a printer like this fulfills a specific need. It is limited in its ability to produce a quality print and the need to buy rolls of paper is a concern. But this is still a useful printer when you’re on the go and need to print.

title: Gets the Message Across
text:
Certain members of my family like their beauty sleep and they do not want to be woken up in the middle of a restful nap. If one or both dogs are with said person, the situation is even worse because even a quiet opening of the door can get the dogs barking and wake them up in the process. To help resolve this problem, I got a set of these Door Hangers, from CROWATTS.

There are several varieties of from which to select with this brand. I went with the one that was most practical for me: Do Not Disturb/Please Knock. I got the ones with the blue color and dessert, since they have a tropical look which fits the theme of our house. At first glance, it looks like a cocktail and pool in the background but closer examination proves otherwise.

What stands out most with these door hangers is their construction. You get a set of four and they are heavy- duty, thicker than most, with a vinyl- like feel. They won’t tear and are waterproof. You just slip them on a doorknob or door handle and you’re all set. There is a slit in the opening, too, to make it possible to fit them on most any door handle, but a doorknob seems to be where they fit best.

With the Do Not Disturb clearly on display, we can cut back on accidental room entries and the irritation of being woken up too soon from a good nap or deep sleep. These door hangers have more practical use than I first thought and I predict they will continue to make a difference for many months to come. I’m most impressed with the construction and this fact alone earns this product a solid recommendation.

title: Helps Guests Find You at Events
text:
When you’re at an event and random, mostly unknown guests are expected, it’s a good idea to make your presence known. The best way to do this is by placing some sort of sign, but if you just lay the sign on a table, they may not see it. A better option is a visible, pedestal sign, like this one from Burferly.

What you get with this sign display is a pedestal base, a sign holder, and an adjustable pole. Assembling is easy enough, but it would be better if the instructions were clearer. They are not the best, but like I said, it is easy enough and there are few enough parts that you should be able to figure it out.

One thing I like about this sign display is that it’s easy to place a piece of paper or plastic in the sign holder. You don’t have to slip it between panels, like with other displays. With this, it clips into place. Each of the four sides can be pulled back, and you then place your sign in the opening, then clip the four sides back into place. You can also rotate the sign to show vertically or horizontally.

This sign is adjustable from 31 to about 48 inches. I wish it could be made even shorter because if it could, I would place it on the table at certain events. It isn’t short enough for that. It is intended for the floor. Oh, another thing to know is that the manufacturer recommends filling the base with water or sand to make it more secure. I haven’t done that because for my needs, it is secure enough the way it is. But if you are displaying it someplace where wind or something else could knock it over, then adding water or sand would be a good idea.

It's good to have a way for people to find you when you schedule an event. This pedestal sign from Burferly is a good means for advertising your event and while I did have a few small issues with it, it’s still sufficient for most needs.

title: Identify Yourself with Ease
text:
I attend events as part of official groups/gatherings, and these events are often held in restaurants or taverns. It’s always good when new attendees can find the group, and the best way is to have a sign sitting on the table. This set of acrylic sign holders from MaxGear fulfills that need.

You get a total of three sign holders with this set. They are not glass, but rather acrylic which is good because it means they cannot shatter if dropped. Each holder consists of two pieces of acrylic which are joined together with two small screws at the top and two longer screws at the bottom, which are slightly angled and thus serve as a stand. You don’t need a screwdriver to attach the screws. You can fasten them with your fingers.

I have used sign stands like this in the past and they usually utilized a piece of acrylic on the bottom which extended outward and served as the stand. The fact that this stand is nothing more than two screws does make it a little less stable. But on the positive side, the use of screws means you can remove the long screws and place them a different way, turning a vertical stand into a horizontal stand. This way, you can accommodate portrait or landscape printouts.

These stands are intended for standard 8.5 by 11 pieces of paper. You can easily fit a sheet this size between the acrylic walls of the stand. You will notice there is still a little room to spare so if your sheet of paper is slightly larger you should be able to get it to fit. There is nothing to guide you to line up the paper just right. You have to eyeball it the best you can.

I organize several meetings and there has been more than one occasion when an attendee was wandering around the establishment, trying to find the group. With these acrylic sign holders, people can find the group without any trouble. They are durable and with a set of three holders, you can announce your presence in multiple ways, ensuring that passersby know who you are and what you do.

title: Keep Track of Future Dates with Ease
text:
I like keeping organized and I like having an array of different calendars to help me remember important dates, tasks to complete, etc. It’s always good, too, when you know what is scheduled to take place well in advance and this need convinced me to get this 2023 Wall Calendar for my home office.

Laminated for greater durability, this is a reversible calendar with one side showing the 12 months arranged vertically, the other horizontally. The accountant in me prefers the vertical arrangement because each row depicts the months for a quarter. But my practical side decided to use the horizontally arrangement because it fits best in my designated wall space.

This calendar is dry erase, and it comes with its own marker. The marker is black and it writes nice and dark, which is what I like. The individual squares for each day are not very big, so you need to write small and you need to use a fine- tipped dry erase marker. The included marker works, but an even finer tip would be better. Each day of the year shows not just the day of the month, but also the number of days elapsed for the year and the number of days remaining.

One of the included accessories with this calendar is sticky dots for use in attaching it to a wall. I decided not to use these and simply grabbed four push pins from my desk to use instead. Yeah, I had to punch holes in the corners, but you need to remember that this is a one- time use calendar. You cannot erase the numbers and fill them in with the next years corresponding dates. This calendar is a one- time use organizational tool.

Organization is good and having a means to organize for a full year is great when you have a busy family schedule. This 2023 wall calendar fulfills this purpose and I have already filled in many important dates for 2023. It will help me keep track of schedules, upcoming trips, etc and it has already proven its worth for the coming year.

title: Helps Keep me Organized
text:
I like to stay organized and one way I accomplish this is through the use of lists. I make lists for most everything, and that includes what I need to get done each day. It made sense then to get my hands on a paper planner made for the task, like this one from Rileys & Co.

With this planner, you get a grid for writing down and tracking what you need to do each week. I like that the sheets are large: 8.5 inches by 11 inches, which is the same size as a standard sheet of paper. There are exactly 52 sheets, so you have one for each week of the year.

The days of the week each have a large enough space to jot down what needs to be done. Saturday and Sunday have half as much space, so you may need to write smaller on those days. The bottom of each sheet has places to list top priorities, to do items, and general notes. I think I would like it better of the days of the week section had lines, for writing things down, rather than an open, blank space. Still, there is enough room to jot down what I need.

There is no adhesive on the backs of the sheets. You cannot peel them off and then stick to the wall, refrigerator, etc. These are intended to be torn off and used like you would a sheet of paper. For my needs, they work as expected and they help me keep organized better than I would if I was writing things on post- it notes, like I used to do. I recommend this, for better organizing your weekly tasks.

title: Make a Statement This Halloween Season
text:
My kids have reminded me more than once that our house needs more Halloween decorations. Most decorations feature jack-o-lanterns, witches, and other like figures. Rather than stock up on more of those, I decided for now to get something that lets my kid’s make a statement, literally: KUBOER Black Felt Coffin Letter Board.

Shaped like a coffin and black in color, this message board let’s kids and adults create their own sayings for display in or outside the home. It comes complete with 340 characters, including letters, numbers, various punctuation, etc so that you can say exactly what you want. This is a definite advantage with this set. I have purchased others like this in the past, but they didn’t have things like punctuation, symbols, or other things. With a set like this, you can truly say what you want to say.

The 340 characters come in the package attached to a plastic holder and need to be snapped off. I recommend snapping them off and storing in a plastic bag. This will help keep them from getting lost. Once you are ready to make a message, just find the ones you need and stick them onto the felt board. We have ours inside the house now, but we are going to move it to the front porch when Halloween draws near.

Halloween is a fun season for kids and adults. This Black Felt Coffin Letter Board from KUBOER is a great addition to your Halloween décor and a fun addition for the season. I would like it even more if it was a little larger in size, but it is still a good option for those who want to make a direct statement for all to see.

title: Fun Stickers for Motivation and Reward
