title: I'm Happy With This
text: My father carried a pocket full of change that he liked to jingle when he walked. When I was a kid if I got separated from him in a store all I had to do was listen and I'd hear him from quite a ways away. One of the coins he carried was a 1952 Irish penny (visible in my images) given to him by my grandmother for luck and prosperity when he married my mom. I've carried it in my wallet for several years, it's fallen out more than once. It gets sweaty, I had a US quarter in my wallet next to it that's corroded and stained from my sweat. I didn't want to damage my dad's coin, it's one of the few things of his I own. When I came across this coin holder I knew it would be far better than my wallet. The coin feels secure, it doesn't appear that it will slip out. While I'm fairly sure this isn't real leather it's nicely made and finished. The only bit I don't like, unfortunately, is the loop of material that holds the split ring to the case. It feels and looks like cheap plastic. I'll be keeping a close eye on it to make sure I catch any possible cracks or splits.

title: Decent Mailers
text: I've found these to be of decent quality, comparable to those sold at the grocery store or mass retailers. They claim these 6 x 9" mailers have a usable area of 5.5 x 8.5" but I've found it to be more like 5 x 8". Still a good amount of space if you're mailing small stuff. They do shed water though 'waterproof' they're not. Padding is typical for this type of mailer. The seal on the ones I've used has been great. Grips really well and once sealed you really can't open these without clear evidence of the fact. The kraft paper is easy to write on with pen or Sharpie markers.

title: Works So Far!
text: I bought my Canon MF3010 multifunction printer in 2012. 2012! I've been using the starter toner since then. For the last year I have been getting light prints even and some uneven prints. This is why I bought a laser printer, an inkjet would have gone dry and ruined a half dozen sets of print heads by now but a laser, like my last one, will sit for months even a year and print immediately when asked. This printer has been reliable to an amazing degree and I really didn't want to replace it or buy OEM toner at nearly the cost of a new printer when I was offered a two pack of these S.Smartomni toner cartridges to review. These were reasonably well packaged with soft caps on the ends of each unit and they were secured in good quality bags that were difficult to tear. No instructions whatsoever came with these units but I was able to carefully watch how the original came out and installed this exactly as the old one came out. It went in flawlessly. The printer took a moment to cycle up and recognize the unit then it printed almost perfectly, I ran off 10 pages of dense text documentation and there was one word that didn't print right. One, single, word. I ran off numerous full page high resolution images just to see how they'd look and the quality was spot on. Rick blacks, good gradients. Then I ran off another dozen pages of text. I'm quite happy with how this toner cartridge is functioning so far and since the starter pack lasted me nearly 8 years it will be quite a while before I get to the 2nd full toner cartridge.

title: Not Bad Door Stops
text: These door stops are decent. They've fit the three doors I've installed them on with no problem. The metal is shiny though a bit thin. If you're installing on a really heavy door you might consider two. Adjustability is good and hasn't been an issue for me. These get the job done.

title: Very Nice Card
text: We buy a popup card every year for a family member in another state. This looked beautiful. It opened perfectly and I tested it a dozen times to make sure it was durable. It works very well, lays almost perfectly flat and is just a piece of art to celebrate the holiday. Highly recommended.

title: Wish I Liked This More
text:
It just comes across as cheap across the board. Even the gift pen had broken and sharp mirror pieces glued to it. Some of the beading fell off as soon as I used it. It wrote horribly and scratchy.
The journal itself initially appeared to be okay but you can see how the leather was just stamped over and over than then cut out, poorly. Edges are rough, undyed and not finished. The interior isn't well dyed and is rough like poorly produced suede. The strap is the same poor material.
The paper is thick and rough which would be nice if it had a quality feel but it seems like poorly homemade paper badly bound in the cover.
Just not great but could be useful as a D&D journal or even a diary if you're not picky.

title: Loud, Annoying
text: I first tried installing this in my bathroom using the sticky pad adhering the stop to the tile floor and it's metal on metal. You can hear it 15 feet away in my bedroom clacking and clunking as it latches and unlatches. The magnet is pretty strong and after about a week, maybe ten days the adhesive pad started to fail and eventually the post came free leaving the adhesive disk stuck to the floor. That took some scraping to get off the tile completely. I considered putting this in bedroom with the screws and decided I just didn't want to deal with the noise. In a game room, cellar or professional situation this might be okay. I don't recommend the glue pad or using this in an area where you'd want peace and quiet.

title: Better Than Plastic
text: Okay, they're not "chip clips" they're office supplies but after four plastic bag clips broke in a week I decided metal was the way to go. They are stiff and take some pressure to open but so far even my 88 year old mother can use them.

title: Requires Strength to Use
text: We're mostly homebound due to disability so coloring is a frequent pastime for us. We go through and sharpen a lot of colored pencils. My initial impression was okay. Decent amount of space for shavings to collect. Good weight and size. But then we tried to use them. First and foremost you have to hold the pencil still while the sharpener works. For a battery operated device these things have a lot of torque! I had trouble holding the pencil still it was impossible for my elderly mother. They put good points on the pencils we tested it with, several brands of colored and a couple standard #2 pencils, but the sharpener never stops. I got distracted once and easily drove a brand new pencil to three quarters of its length in no time. I guess they're okay. If your able enough to use them. I struggled and my mom found it impossible. We'll stick with our older, corded, sharpener that's fully automatic. These were a disappointment.

title: How Do You Get a Pencil SO Wrong?!
text:
Pencils. . . Around 450 years in existence and Bic somehow gets it horribly wrong. How? I like different looking pencils. Standby yellow school pencils are fine but different is. . . fun. I game, D&D, Car Wars, etc. pencils are part and parcel of gaming life. I think it was during first or second grade when I first heard "Take out a #2 pencil." before some test. So, at fifty three years old I know pencils. I saw these with their dark grey barrel and black inner wood and they looked cool. Something fun to break out at the next game night. Then I got them. They're comfortable enough. The barrel actually flexes a little like there's rubber in the mix. They are neat looking and that's where it ends. Again, I've written with a #2 for easily forty five years. I know what a #2 pencil feels like when I write with one. These write nothing like a #2 pencil. It feels. . . waxy, the tip doesn't grip the paper, it slips along. It feels totally wrong. I know what writing from a #2 pencil looks like. What comes out of these pencils (I almost want to put pencil i quotes here) looks, and feels like trying to write on slippery thermal receipt paper. I was using an old Composition notebook that I've had for years. I could barely make out what I wrote no matter how hard I pressed. The words looked waxy or greasy. The writing was faint looking decades old and faded or like what a much harder pencil (#5 - #6) produces, except for that waxy, greasy feel when writing.
TL:DR? These are terrible pencils. I wouldn't recommend them to anyone.

title: Works Pretty Good
text: The applicator is a bit finicky to get to work. The plastic is a bit stiff and brittle feeling. But once you get it feeding right it works pretty good. I've stuck some notes to my 3D printer and inside the lid of a wooden box I keep hobby supplies in and they hold well. You can put down as little or as much adhesive as you want. A quick zip and you can make your own post-it notes. Used more and you can adhere paper completely and smoothly. I even tried some on the bottom of a 3D print with a crank handle and it sticks to my desk fairly well and has been repositioned numerous times and remains sticky. It's supposed to be refillable but the couple times I tried opening the case it felt like it was going to break. I'm okay with it being single use. Less messy than glue sticks.

title: Pretty Birthday Card
text: A very pretty and distinctive birthday card. My 87 year old mom loved it and has kept it out for everyone to see for several weeks now. Well made with different layers and design this stands out from the run of the mill birthday cards.

title: Good Pens, Nice Colors
text: A nice selection of colorful pens (we made multicolored Christmas greetings on our cards this year) that have rather comfortable grips and write smoothly and cleanly. Even a left handed person like myself can use these with little risk of smears on their hands.

title: Useful Label Maker
text: Okay, first things first, it says 20+ font styles but let's be honest here there's one font (kinda sad actually) that can be several different sizes, bold, italicized, underlined and combinations of those. Actual different fonts would be much more fun and useful but okay, it's still useful. The keyboard is easy to use and edit with although the emojis are poorly implemented requiring you to start at the 1st emoji and navigate through the selections making using more than one of the same at a time fairly annoying. I like that you can have multiple lines of text on a label. The sparkly blue label with white print the purple  Colorpop comes with is not easy to read and does not stick well to some surfaces such as the metal tubes on my mom's walker where they lasted only a few days before peeling off. Once I'm done with the color labels I'll get the less expensive, far longer rolls, standard Dymo labels. It's fairly rough on batteries and doesn't come with a power brick although you can buy one separately.

title: Mediocrity
text: I've bought 24 pound paper for my printers for years. I like the weight and feel. This, feels like at best 20 or 18 pound copier paper. It's not worth the trouble and effort of returning so I'll deal with it. Paper is slippery and thin, I didn't expect rag or linen but I had about 30 sheets left from my last ream which was a different manufacturer's 24 pound 96 extra bright paper and it's got a little textural feel, it's stiffer, by a great deal, than this paper from HP. When I buy a brand name I expect quality not paper that lags behind some no-name brand. The other brand had jumped nearly 75% since my last purchase. Had I known how mediocre this HP product was I might have splurged and repurchased it. I won't buy this again.

title: Astonishingly Beautiful Card
text: This card is beautiful, stunningly beautiful. The colors are vibrant. The construction perfect. The inner cream colored paper is a perfect backdrop for the exquisitely detailed paper feathers of the peacock. Even the cover is beautifully done with a cutout of a peacock in the dark paper of the front & back cover lined in the same cream seen inside. My mother loves pretty cards and this took her breath away. Most cards get displayed for a few days then get thrown away. This card she has proudly displayed on the coffee table where she spends the most time sitting. Best birthday card, ever.

title: Fun Colors Great Pens
text: They're InkJoy pens, you can't go wrong. They're comfortable to hold. The ink flows well and dries quick. We've bought and used the standard Blue in 01mm and Black in both .07 and .05 for years now. The larger diameter pens seem to write smoother but they also make it a little hard to write, for example, long names on a check or small spaces on forms. I'm good with the .07, these Candy Pop pens are 01mm and write like a dream. The different colors will be fun when it comes to paying the bills or sending cards for different occasions. They might even be fun for coloring, haven't tried that yet but I did just pay a bill in orange ink. The pen bodies are colorfully and cutely decorated. Have fun, change colors from time to time. Write a letter (people still do that, right?) in four different colors.

title: 3M Always Makes a Great Product
text: 3M mounting products are almost always great. These are no different. I used them to attach non skid contact paper on the bottom of a set of bathroom rails. Need another couple to level things but they don't feel as if they're ever coming off. Still need to add some for leveling but you get plenty in a pack.

title: Best Disposable Pen, Ever
text:
I tested a single of these a long while ago and almost cried the other day when it started getting scratchy and skipping. So I ordered myself a 10 pack of .7mm medium point (my original was a .5mm fine point). If anything I like the way the medium point writes even more than the fine point. I think the InkJoy pens are some of the best on the market and they're going to be all I buy for as long as they remain affordable.
The one odd thing. My mom also loves InkJoy pens and bought a box of 1mm and it's amazing the difference there is in the design between the two.

title: Fun & Pretty Decorating Project {Edited}
text:
These are a lot of fun. Reasonably easy to apply to the wall. You get two sheets of different butterflies. Actually you get teo of the same sheet. It would have been nice to have a greater variety to choose from but we made do with what we received and decorated a wall between rhe living room and kitchen where the can always be seen. A few of the smaller butterflies were used to accent a wall in my mother's bathroom. They look great in both places.

{Edit} - Our neighbor was over visiting and so these on the walls in both places and absolutely loved them so Amazon made another sale as we bought her a pack to use in her many crafting projects. The ones we put up BTW are all still in place and survived numerous days without power where it got as high as 88° with 100% humidity inside the house. So they've proved to be fairly durable so far.

title: Very Nice Note Pads
text: Decent quality paper. I mean all we use these for is keeping one around to keep notes and ideas down on and I keep another in a faux leather folio I use for grocery shopping. I used to clip a pen (to mark off the things I'd bought) to an older pad and that tore the sheets. I find it far easier to write on these white pages (our previous were yellow and school/wide ruled) with their much smaller college rule lines. This dozen pack of pads are going to last us for years. The price was good, the quality is fine. The sheets are microperforated and tear out clean and easy. Couldn't ask for anything more.

title: Great Pens
text: I've tried earlier versions of the Ink Joy pen and really liked them. I'd have to say they've actually managed to improve the 'writability' of the pen though to be honest I like the older styling of the pen body. It not a big deal and the pens still write fantastic.

title: Well Made Clipboard, Great For Grocery Shopping
text: I bought this for grocery shopping, a way to keep the pad dry, a place to keep my coupons and a pen. The blue is a little darker in real life than it is online but that's probably a lighting issue. It holds my shopping list and any coupons I happen to have. The only problem is I normally bring an InkJoy pen with me grocery shopping but it's too thick for this portfolio and holds the cover open. Luckily I was able to find one or two thin pens that fit and don't hold the cover wide open. It's great for grocery shopping.

title: Sturdy & Well Made Desktop Organizer
text: Thise comes fully assembled except for some four button feet that are easily pressed into place. The three drawers, even with quite a lot of weight in them slide open and closed easily. It's sturdy and feels well made. There are stops to keep the drawers from falling out. I can't call it attractive but it's suitable for a business or home office. It takes up quite a large portion of desktop real estate (make sure you check the dimensions and ensure you have enough room for this before you buy it) but i don't mind giving up the desktop space because this has allowed me to sort, store and clear the clutter that was taking over my desk. From packs of rechargeable batteries to cables of all sorts as well as a couple 5v chargers. I also found I have more micro SD card adapters than I ever thought I owned. But now all that clutter, including a giant 5-subject notebook stored on the open top tray. Very pleased with how well I was able to declutter my desk and there's still plenty of room left for more stuff. I don't have anything to compare this to but it certainly does it's job. Well worth having.

title: Decent Phone System
text: Replacing an older Panasonic phone system that was starting to show it's age. Handsets are a bit bigger. Ringtones are different. Subtle changes hefe and there but other than that these work great, have great range and sound good. Answering holder and secondary handset holders a bit on the cheap and light side but they work and that's what counts.

title: I Wasn't Impressed
text:
I'm not impressed. I really like the Ink Joy pens and how they write but if this is a medium point you could likely do surgery with the fine point version. This write a sharp, hard and thin line unlike any medium point pen and very unlike a typical Ink Joy pen. This unlike most Ink Joy pens had a removable, and easily misplaced or lost cap on the writing end and a large, soft stylus on the other end. Yes, you can cover the stylus with the cap as you write but if you need the stylus for anything it's covered. I think the design is poor. Some means of clicking the pen tip in an out could easily have been designed.
The stylus itself it rather large and I found somewhat clumsy to use on our 7" Fire, my 10" Samsung and my touch-screen laptop. As my mother said, "other than the fingerprints it's no better than using your hand." Plus there's the time needed to find and use the stylus while your hand is right there. Not a great idea.

title: Pretty Colors, Some Problems, Best For Kids And Teens
text: Not super impressed. The colors honestly are very pretty when you're careful and lay them down evenly which isn't as easy as it sounds. You have to be soft, slow and gentle to get large areas covered smoothly, cleanly and completely. They do go down nice if you take care but we found some of the pens were scratchy when coloring with them. Another problem we had, because the pens aren't marked and even though there's Basic, Pastel, Neon, Neon Glitter, Metallic and Colored Glitter. They all seem the same. The 'glitter' pens don't write/color in glitter the glitter as far as I can tell (the glittering being in the barrel of the pen far away from the ink was a big clue) glitter is just decorative part of the pen and not part of the ink. Trying multiple pens from different racks it was really hard to tell there was any real difference in the colors as far as metallic or neon and basic go. I had an easier time than my elderly mother coloring smoothly and with complete coverage but I still think a good set of colored pencils is far better to color with than ball-point pens. I think kids and teens would have more fun than adults with these.

title: Decent Set of Pencils
text:
Personally I prefer round pencils. Standard design 6-sided hextuple pencils tend to dig painfully into my hand and fingers. Granted they don't roll away as easily as round pencils do but I'd still take round over angles any day. My other problem with this set is there's no color guide included or available (confirmed by the seller) with the pencils or any color names on the pencils. The manufacturer's name and a number are embossed on each pencil but nothing to tell you what the color is. My 85 year old mother has a serious problem with the lack of color names or a color chart that corresponds to their numbering system.
That all being said, these do color very nicely and smoothly and you can put down a light color or darken it easily with just a bit more pressure. The tin they come in is two layers, 24 different colors per level and you can put the 1st layer in the lid while working to keep everything in one place. It's a good set of pencils just not a great set. A color chart with color names or having the name of the color on the pencil would easily bring this up to a four star review.
I received this item in exchange for my review.

title: Looks Great, Writes Poorly
text:
The pen itself is beautiful. The blue and chrome are stunning together. This comes with a felt sheath to store the pen in which is a little hard to get the pen into or out of as the clip is very tight. It does fit a shirt pocket, without the felt sheath, nicely even with a pocket protector. The pen has a nice heft, feels very well made and solid. . . and then you get to the bad part. When writing, and it's not just me I've handed this to two other people without a word and asked for their opinion and both of them said the same thing. The roller-ball grabs, scratches and stutters as you write which is too bad because it lays down a nice wet and dark line of ink that dries not quickly but doesn't stay wet all that long. But no matter how attractive a pen is when all is said and done a pen is something you use to write. If all you use it for is signing your name maybe you won't notice but I wrote an entire page as did a friend of mine and the way the pen writes is so distracting neither of us could enjoy using the pen. I even spent ten minutes scribbling constantly with the pen thinking maybe the roller-ball needed to 'break in' but it still did the same hitching, catching and stuttering. A pen that doesn't write well just isn't something to rave about. I was somewhat disappointed in this product.
I received this pen in exchange for my review.

title: They're Nice. . . But
text:
First off I'm just going to say this; I don't mind being asked to review a product and enjoy it at times. What I dislike quite a lot is receiving several notes in the packaging specifically encouraging I write a five star review of the product. On to the product. . .

The labels are a heavy gauge vinyl and stick well to dry surfaces. Removal and reuse was okay, I was able to get about three uses before the edges would stop adhering. The marker design is interesting. You can flip the tip, easily but a bit messily, from a round point to a chisel tip. The liquid chalk writes quite wet and takes a while to dry. Once dry you need to be careful how you handle the labels. Moderate pressure causes the chalk to halo and spread out. The slightest dampness, such as the humid environment in a 'fridge or damp fingers, will cause the chalk to badly smear. Oddly enough I found it almost impossible to completely remove the chalk from a label even using glass cleaner there was a white haze left behind.

Maybe with a more permanent white marker things would be better. I'd rather not be able to reuse the labels for less risk of smearing. The labels are attractive in an old timey way. I'd gladly buy more than mess around with trying to erase and reuse them.

I received this item in exchange for my review.

title: Never Buy This Scanner Because Of The Software!
text:
UPDATE 2
I spent tens of hours scanning photos. They were saved regularly, and the folders indicates that they were actually there. When I went to start organizing them tonight, they were gone, and WINDOWS cannot find a single one anywhere on mys system. The software was acting strange, and apparently it took out all the photos. That is a big chunk of my life that I will never get back.

Even tonight the sogtware refuses to consistently save test scans.

My original assessment was that this was a bad scanner because of the software, and I stand by it again. If you are scanning in more than a few photos, USE AT YOUR OWN RISK!

UPDATED REVIEW
I had extensive problems getting the scanner to operate and the software to install. I had to download the drivers to three different computers. I was never able to make it work with WIN 7 (old laptops I could place where the photos were) but did make it work with WIN 8 with tech support help. The Web site specifically states that the driver and software will work with WIN 7. Take it with a grain of salt.

Scanning was easy. I ran a calibration first and then scanned several hundred photos over about 8 hours. The results were good EXCEPT the white balance was way off on many photos. They looked sepia-toned.
Software was "not so good". First, they use a white on light blue interface color scheme. For a visually impaired person like myself, it might was well be white-on-white. Second, there seems to be no batch processing of photos. The white balance Quick Fix seemed to work wonders, but I was not going to do each scan individually. My corrections were done in Photoshop instead where I could run a batch process on all the photos.

Positives were that the hardware and software were able to rotate the scanned images to eliminate any feeding errors over 99% of the time. Scans at 600 dpi were fast and consistent. Having the scans start automatically when the photo was dropped into the scanner was a huge plus for this job. While some rotation did occur, there were only three misfeeds that required a rescan because the photo stuck in the scanner feeder.

Negatives for the setup issues and the white balance, but positives for ease of use, consistency, and speed. I will end up saving hundreds of dollars scanning the photos myself instead of using a service bureau.

title: Solid Performer For 35 mm Slides
text:
Okay, up front disclaimer. You are NOT going to get the same quality as a professional scanning service. YOu also fo not get the automatic slide feed everyone wants.

Out of the package, the unit worked well. I selected the correct holder for my slides, inserted my SD card (not included with unit!), set the film type (35 mm slide) and resolution, and started. While there is no autofeed, it is pretty easy to push the slides through manually. Positioning is helped by the LCD monitor, but I found it is not perfect. Expect some cut-off and some rounded corners with mounted slides.

I tried adjusting the brightness because many of my old slides were a bit overexposed. I found little benefit, so I went with the defaults and made adjustments in Photoshop instead. For reasonably well exposed slides, the defaults work well.

Picture quality was up and down. When I looked at some of the slides that appeared fuzzy or granular when I went to 100%m the originals appeared okay at 5X. On the other hand, I had several that were very sharp and well focused. I am still trying to decide if it is the Scanza or the slides.

Color saturation was a bit variable. Older, overexposed slides seemed to be lacking color and contrast even in good areas. Well-exposed slides were saturated with no obvious problems.

If you are interested in converting your slides to snapshots for on-screen slideshows and sharing, the Scanza is a good option. You can go through a few hundred slides in a day and get good results pretty easily. If you have many more, you should be considering a professional scanner. If you only have a few, I would try your scanner, if it has a suitable capability.

While branded Kodak, it is a Chinese product. It is meant for worldwide sales, so you can find instructions in virtually every major language.

title: Disappointing unit
text:
This is a very substandard unit for converting slides, in my opinion.

The problems start with the slide tray. It is vertical, so that slides tend to fall. It also is difficult to center and keep centered the slides so that portions are not cut off.

My bigger problem is poor color rendition. I have some very good, colorful slides that have been kept in archival quality holders that are still as pristine as the day that they were developed. The colors in the scans are washed out and can approach black-and-white.

Finally, I have far more noise in the scans than there should be. The unit uses a Zoran camera and a lamp to shoot a picture od the slide. This is about as controlled an shooting environment as you can get. There should be NO noise.

title: Looks easy, but a long learning curve (for some of us)
text:
I received this as a free review sample. Like J. Graham in her December 17, 2015 review I went toYouTube to check out some videos before I started using this pen. Unlike her, my results were not nearly as artistic. However, when researching how to properly use this I noticed a number of different pens and none had the ergonomic shape and design this one has. In fact, most looked bulky and clumsy, and I do appreciate how nicely this one feels in my hand and the logical layout of controls.

Obviously there is a learning curve to using this pen and the two sample packs of filament (one PLA and the other ABS) are not going to get you through that learning curve. I recommend ordering additional filament (the size must be 1.75mm) along with this pen, or - if you live near a Michael's - rolls can usually be purchased locally. I had to make a trip to Michael's to get enough to prove to myself that I could make something useful. As it turned out with a lot of practice and filament I was able to make a reasonably straight wire cube. I am embarrassed to reveal how long (and how much filament) I went through to achieve that modest feat, but suffice to say that I am probably never going to create an Eiffel Tower like the one depicted in the product photos.

If you do check out J. Graham's excellent and very helpful video review you will notice that she is reviewing an older generation of this pen. It's clunkier, but does come with templates that this one does not. To be honest, I would probably have never used the templates anyway, and I can tell by comparing the model she is reviewing to the one that I received that mine is lighter, more balanced and easier to manipulate.

Bottom line: if you have a steady hand and a lot of patience to master this tool you can create some interesting 3D models and works of art. I saw what can be accomplished with this in some of the videos that I checked out - and the artists all made it look so easy. There are folks who seem to be born with the knack and talent for such things. I am not one of them, but if you are this is a tool that allows you to create designs (both technical and artistic) that add another dimension to your creativity.

title: Quality is excellent, but not my daily ink
text:
I am more of a 4001 fan, but had to try this because - frankly - the packaging caught my eye. Since my 'go to' ink is [[ASIN:B0009WFNAQ Pelikan 4001 Ink 30ml Royal Blue]] I am going to base my comparison on it. First, why five stars if I do not plan to use it as a daily ink? One reason is the packaging and I am betting that much of the price over the 4001 is because of it. This makes a great gift, and there is a certain level of aesthetics of the bottle on a writing desk. However, the ink also has a nice, even flow that 'feels' better than the 4001 formula.

The color is a little too light for me, and the drying time is too long. In fact, if you are accustomed to a faster drying ink like 4001 this one will take time to get used to because it takes nearly twice as long to dry.

That said, the way this ink literally causes your nib to glide across paper is one of the most compelling reasons to consider it. I have switched to an F nib and 4001 ink can make it feel scratchy. This ink transforms my nib into a whole different creature - and one that I have grown to love. So, back to why I do not intend to make this my daily ink. Drying time is at the top of the list. The weak (to my eyes) share of blue is another. And finally, price. 4001 is in my budget and if Pelikan were to repackage this ink into more modest bottles and boxes, and drop the price accordingly, I would probably experiment with other, darker blues like sapphire or Tanzanite.

Bottom line: there is much to love about this ink, and it may - in fact - be perfect for you. It's certainly a quality product; a Rolls-Royce in many respects. Who knows, it may win me over yet because I do love what it does for my pen!

title: Just right feel for me
text:
I have recently started using this after nearly fifteen years of using an M400. My reason for switching is as I get older my preference is for a slightly larger pen that - for me - is easier to hold. I did try the M800 and it was not as comfortable. I have relatively small hands, so take that into account.

Performance of this pen is identical to the M400. which has never skipped, leaked or failed to lay down a moderately wet, smooth flowing line from the very first stroke after uncapping it. More importantly I have never had a problem with the filling system. It draws in ink perfectly with a twist of the knob and the piston is sealed with no air bubbles or other issues. This pen is exhibiting the same great, reliable performance in those respects.

Since the performance is identical the dimensions are what sets this model apart from its small (and larger) siblings. This one has an overall length of 5.24 inches (capped) and slightly over 6 inches when posted. The barrel is .5 inches in diameter and the pen weights in at slightly over .6 ounces (18 grams to be exact.)

The F 14K nib is smooth with no scratchiness or any other 'feel' problems that would mar the writing experience. I do keep mine well maintained during those rare periods when I am not using it and at least monthly I will flush it with distilled water. I also only use Pelikan brand ink, but that is more a personal preference.

title: My preferred ink
text:
I've tried a large number of inks and have settled on this brand. I also use the 4001 black ink with the exact results, so it's the formula and not the pigment that make this so versatile. I've used this ink in a wide range of pens from modern Pelikans, Montblancs and others to vintage pens that are turning 100 like my Parkers and Watermans. It works beautifully with each of them.

This ink immediately starts on the first stroke and has never clogged nor prematurely dried out on a nib, even after extensive writing and letting the pen sit uncapped for prolonged periods. This is a somewhat dry ink that works best on slicker paper, although it writes beautifully on just about any surface from high rag papers to card stock. In fact, I just tested it on the highly absorbent paper in this journal and it worked perfectly: [[ASIN:B00Q1QACJG VALERY Rustic Genuine Leather Handcrafted Writing Blank Journal Diary With Handmade Paper]].

Because of the dry qualities it has minimum bleed on pulp type papers and even on thin sheets does not show through if you are using light strokes. It's not so dry that it's scratchy. On the contrary, this ink allows your nib to practically glide over most paper types.

title: Inspires writing!
text:
I received this as a free review sample. If you are a journal writer, artist or even a diary keeper this is actually inspiring. Or for me it is.

Do note that if you use fountain pens there are some limitations. For example, the paper is a little too absorbent, so you will want a quicker drying ink. More importantly, you will find that this is better suited to fine nibs with little flexibility. If you own a modern Sheaffer with one of those 'nail' nibs this is a perfect journal. If you love writing with a vintage Waterman with a 'wet noodle' nib the paper in this journal will probably frustrate you. I found it to be perfect with a [[ASIN:B000CN5OLA Pelikan Souveran 600 Black/Green GT Fine Point Fountain Pen]] using [[ASIN:B0009WFNAQ Pelikan 4001 Ink 30ml Royal Blue]]. In fact, the color of the ink against the pages is as old school as the journal itself.

Every other aspect of this journal is a work of craftsmanship. The leather is distressed, the binding is rustic (to say the least) and the entire journal is sturdy. I am betting that if you are looking for a journal that will actually inspire you, this one will not disappoint. The only minus to it is it's so beautifully made that my first reaction was to not mar it with a mark. That defeats the purpose, so once you lay down that first letter or line you will find more flowing from your writing instrument.

title: Should have purchased this a year ago
text:
I finally broke down and purchased this cart after needlessly making double trips to set up for performances. Sine there are well over five hundred reviews already I will give my observations of a few key areas.

First, this does an excellent job of rolling over uneven surfaces as well as textured ones like cobblestone. Note that I do not load this anywhere near the weight capacity, so that may account for the ease of rolling. My normal loads are less than fifty pounds.

Second, it expands out and folds back in seconds. When I first received it there was an issue with the wheels smoothly and completely folding in for storage, but that problem went away after a few uses and has not resurfaced. Perhaps it needed to be broken in.

I stand 5'9" and the handle expands vertically to a height that is both comfortable for me and and easy to control the cart. If I could change anything it would be to add a few inches to the length and width, but as is it is still vastly better than any other hand truck or cart that I have used because it is compact. And, for my loads and use, sturdy.

To put my use into context I play 22-25 gigs a month and hand carrying all of the gear we use into and out of venues was time consuming and a cause of aches in my sixty-six year old body. Thus far this has not only diminished the aches and pains, but has also cut set-up and break down time by at least a third. To be totally honest I would replace this immediately if something were to happen to it, and am contemplating purchasing another as a spare.

Factor in the way I use mind when making a purchase decision because I am not stressing it to anywhere near its specified limits. Some other reviews have reported issues and you should also factor those in, but for me I am totally pleased with this cart.

title: These are great “junior” writing pads
text:
I work from home and really like having steno pads and these smaller “junior” pads around…both for work and my personal life. I have them all over the house where they are easy to grab when I need one.

Over the past few years, I have been frustrated with pads I have purchased coming with really flexible, limp backings. Not at all functional for me, since I use the hard backing as a writing surface…I’m sure many people do as well.

The backing on these pads is a perfect thick, hard surface to write against. The paper is a nice bright canary yellow and the lines are narrow, which is my preference. The paper is a good thickness…not too thick or thin.

The paper tears at the perforation nice and evenly.

For the price of this 12-pack (50 sheets per pad), I think this is a good value for the quality. It came in great shape and was packaged well with cellophane and a paper cover.

I am very pleased and will be buying these pads again.

title: A perfect steno pad with a sturdy backing
text:
I have used steno pads for many years and have always found them extremely useful for work and personal life…to makes lists, take notes, and help keep me organized. I also really like the line printed down the center of each page. It just helps keep me focused somehow.

Over the last couple years I have not been thrilled with the cheap backing on many brands of pads. The whole point it to be able to hold the pad and have a stable back to support your writing. When I found this Tops brand and saw the reviews, I decided to place an order. I was not disappointed.

The backing is sturdy cardboard and the paper is thick. You can easily write on both sides of the paper, if you want, without seeing ink. I also found writing with a pen easy on this paper stock.

There are 80 pages per pad…160 if you write on both sides.

The color of the cover will designate the color of the interior paper…so I bought a package with teal covers and the paper is a light blue. I prefer a color paper versus white, since I find it easier on my eyes.

Each page is perforated at the top and the spiral allows for easy page turning. I’m not sure I really need perforation, but it’s there if you want it

I find the quality to be excellent and will purchase again. I am tempted by the many colors!

title: The only hanging folders I will buy
text:
I work full-time from home now and have a need for some physical hard-copy filing…both for work and personal use.

I started out using those old dark green hanging folders from our office but soon realized they were falling apart and not at all pleasant to look at.

When I saw these “jewel tone” colors…I didn’t hesitant to order, knowing the Smead brand to be a professional product. They still have the same sturdy quality and these colors are so nice to see when I open my filing drawer.

I stopped using individual file folders and now use hanging files only. I will pull the whole hanging file out when I need to reference something and it holds up well. I also use the plastic tabs that I insert with file names and I’m always moving those around so I can see them better.

These folders also slide quite nicely on the metal file rack.

I see that the price has gone up on them, so it is a bit of an investment. Lots of nice color choices.

I expect these to last quite a while but would certainly buy again.

title: Best ink cartridges for my HP Envy printer
text:
I only use HP printers for my work, because they have always been reliable throughout my career. I work from home full-time and my company reimburses me for my work expenses. I try, however, to get a good price on whatever I’m buying…so I keep coming back to this particular product.

I like this convenient 2-pack of black and color cartridges, since it seems to simplify my shopping. I always have backups since you never know when your ink will get used up.

I prefer a black ink laser printer for most of my work, but I do have the occasional need for color printing.

I’m sure we all find these ink and toner cartridges painfully expensive sometimes, but we do what we have to, right?

As long as I go through the proper testing and adjusting (calibration?) when I put in new ink (the printer walks me through it), it usually is a simple enough process.

The one complaint I have about inkjet print is that, when I use a highlighter on my copies, it smears my ink...even after the ink has dried. I just know not to highlight if I can help it.

I do find this a decent value and HP products have always worked well for me.

title: I feed my HP laser printer what it wants
text:
I work from home full-time and have both a black and white laser printer and a color ink jet printer.

Most of my work is on the computer, but I need to print off emails throughout the day so I can reference them for each of my projects.

The laser printer is much faster and I don’t often need color printing. I just need fast and crisp printing so I can see what I’m doing...and I can highlight laser print.

We all know the pain of the expense of toners. As our printers get older, toner cartridges seem to get more expensive.

I can’t say this is a great value, but I’m not disappointed with the product. It arrives really fast, it’s well-packaged and easy to load. I also find it lasts quite a while. When my print starts to lighten up, I pull out the cartridge and roll it around a little. I can usually squeeze out a couple more days doing that maybe twice before that doesn’t work anymore.

I appreciate the prepaid UPS label for returning old cartridges. I used to have a Brother printer and they did not do this. Or they made you go to the Post Office. I just remember it being inconvenient.

I now just pop the used laser cartridge in the box, put on the label and put it in the car for the next trip to or close to a UPS Store. I’m happy to make that effort.

I will continue to keep buying and can recommend.

title: I have used this calendar for years
text:
This calendar is a great choice if you are looking for something not to break your budget. I work from home but don’t have a wall close by my desk to hang a calendar on…so I stick it in a rolling work cart I have by my desk where it’s easy to grab. I like that it’s light-weight since I do reach for it often, and that it’s not overly-thick and taking up room in my cart of standing files.

I keep a combination of work and personal notes (often reminders when bills are due) on this calendar. I don’t really have a lot going on in my life as far as appointments, but I am constantly grabbing it to enter reminders and it holds up quite well. I like the calming yellow and blue colors, the room for notes, the distinction of months, weeks, and days. The spiral also works well when flipping back and forth.

Lots of room for post-it notes that I use for reminders. The paper is thick enough not to bleed through. I use both ink and highlighters at times. Lots of room for future notes for the following year.

The size and quality are perfect for me and the price is right. I recommend and will purchase again.

title: Perfect solar calculator for my home office
text:
I work full-time from home and use quote software. Sometimes, however, I need a calculator to figure out certain pricing differences so I can email information to my team.

I realize we have calculators on our phones but you can’t “feel” where you are on the key pad…and no back button. Just not practical for work. Some physical calculators are just too small for me.

I love the size and feel of this calculator. It is well-balanced and stable (with its little rubber bumpers on the bottom). I frankly do not use a lot of the calculating features, but the back button is a great option. I also prefer a solar calculator and having no worries about changing batteries.

The shape of the buttons works well for me and often I can punch away without looking at the key pad.

Since it is such a reliable device, I bought a second one for downstairs.

I highly recommend this calculator and feel the value is great. I would purchase again if needed.

title: My favorite highlighter for work and personal use
text:
I’ve worked for years and have used many different highlighters and markers. Fat ones, thin ones, different colors, etc.

My main use is to “highlight” print…not write with them.

My work consists of different jobs that I receive over email. I print off the emails and highlight contact information, part numbers, pricing, etc. I then create my quotes on my computer, referencing what I have highlighted. It’s important for me to focus on just what I need and not get distracted with other information on the pages. That faster I work, the better my production…and the happier my manage is!

I think many of us started out with the yellow highlighters, but I realize I actually SEE pink better than any other color. My eye is just drawn to it.

These particular highlighters are my all-time favorite. I don’t want thick markers, but something with the shape of a pen for comfort. No rough edges. The chiseled point helps for better control.

I find the color does not bleed through to the other side of the paper, so would be good for two-sided printing or book pages. These last for quite a while, depending on how long you keep the cap off. I do not leave mine uncapped for long, just to keep them fresh longer.

I find this pack of 12 to be a good value and will certainly keep buying. I highly recommend them!

title: Worked great for a move and then for storage
text:
I bought these to store files in for a move and they worked great for holding my hanging file folders WITH file name plastic tabs attached. These containers really do hold a lot.

When I moved in, I just pulled out the files to put into my new home office built-in filing cabinets. title: Paper shredder with functions perfect for me
text:
I really don’t need a paper shredder all the time, but when I want it, I want it. Tax season, for instance.

I wanted something that was self-contained (not something that sits on top of a separate waste basket).

I wanted a window so I can see when it needs to be emptied.

I like the handle for removing the top.

Black ink

This pen fits all my needs. I used to get that little bump on my index finger from the all-plastic pens I was using. After using these new pens for a while, that bump and tenderness has gone away!

The design is everything I could want…even a slightly larger section where my thumb and index finger hold onto it. This pen is very well-balanced for me, which is important since I’m constantly picking it up throughout my world day to make notes while at the computer.

title: Toss Your Too-Small Bank Checkbook Registers!
text:
I’m old enough to remember carrying my checkbook and register in my purse all the time, because that is how we typically paid for daily shopping and bills. A few years back, I realized I wasn’t writing many (if any) checks, but I still wanted a register for keeping track of deposits, auto-payments, incoming bills, etc. The typical bank registers were and still are just way too small for my new system.

This larger register gives me what I want. There are plenty of pages and lots of room for making notations. I don’t even use the backs of the pages, since I like to add post-it notes for incoming expenses or deposits that I’m not yet ready to enter. There are certainly more pages with this version than on a typical bank register.

I like the spiral to be at the top (some books come with the spiral on the left side), so it does not get in my way while writing. Bank registers do not easily lay flat, while the spiral version allows for easier writing.

I also like that the register covers come in different colors, so I can keep the last one in my desk drawer and recognize which register is the current one.

I do wish, however, it came with one of those elastic bands to help keep the last pages grouped…but I just clip that section of pages together after everything has posted.

I also realize there are digital options for tracking bank expenses, but this still feels comfortable to me. There’s something to be said for writing things down and seeing a written account. We each just need to find our own comfort level for tracking our budget.

title: Writes Terribly and It's Uncomfortable to Hold
text:
The website propaganda states: "Commended for ease of use by the Arthritis Foundation." Considering that I learned years ago that the Arthritis Foundation cannot speak for all arthritis sufferers, including me, I should have known better than to order this pen because arthritics have diverse levels of disabilities. I have advanced systemic RA so my hands are in bad shape, but even if they weren't I found the Pilot Dr. Grip pen to be too thick since it has a 5/8" diameter at the middle (widest area) and a 9/16" diameter at the finger depression (too fat for my comfort). To replace a refill on most pens, the pen comes apart at the middle of the pen's barrel (where the silver tone ring is located). You would think that the Pilot Dr. Grip also unscrews in that area, but it doesn't. It comes apart at the tip, below the cushioned grip. A pen tip is not the most comfortable place for an arthritic to grab and twist so what were the manufacturers and the Arthritis Foundation thinking?. This pen is probably good for someone with non-disabled large hands who likes the feel of a wide girth barrel.

As a comparison, I like the thickness and feel of the Bic Velocity pen, which has a diameter of about 7/16". Similar to Dr. Grip, Bic Velocity has a rubberized cushion grip, but I find the Bic a bit thinner and easier to hold and use. The cushioned grip of Dr. Grip, unlike the Bic's rubberized grip, attracts dust like a magnet. For additional comparison, I also like the feel of thinner cushioned inexpensive non-gel pens like the Bic Atlantis and the Paper Mate Profile. So, why did I buy Dr. Grip? I searched for a gel pen with a comfortable hold and Dr. Grip popped up. I have tried other gel pens in the past and I wasn't pleased with the quality and flow of the gel. Dr. Grip also disappoints in that area b/c it skips as it writes. I have since looked for a gel pen under the manufacturer names that I mentioned above and found nothing that I'd like. A customer recommended the Uni-ball Signo 207, which looks stylish, allegedly writes smoothly and boldly, and accepts refills so I'm going to try it. Hopefully, I'll like it. Signo also has a slightly cheaper model (other than the 207) that doesn't take refills (it's disposable).

title: Good, but not for mobile devices
text:
Initially I was going to use this for video conferencing, however, my son decided that he could use it better for gaming purposes.

Pros:

1. Easy to use on a PC, you only need the USB cable, plug it in and you're ready to go. No drivers or software need to be installed.

2. You can use it on a gaming console such as a PS3/PS4, XBOX/ XBOX One, via the USB cable. However, it will register as a headset on the PS4 and therefore you cannot record party sound with a capture card.

3. The physical aesthetics are appealing, the surface and buttons have a good texture. Not that this matters much.

4. It has five microphone settings, four of which are single direction microphones and the last setting is an omni-directional setting which activates all the microphones. These settings can all be changed with the simple push of a button.

5. The microphone range is very good as I stood about eight feet away and the party on the other side heard me clearly. My son also uses the built in microphone for voice recognition when connected to his PS4.

Cons:

1. As noted by other users, it does not support mobile devices well. You would need a USB power source, such as a computer, and the audio cable. So it really doesn’t make much sense using it with a mobile device since you might need to get a PC to power it.

2. Sometimes the party on the other end can hear their voice echoing. I don't know if this is due to the VX-1 or something else on their side.

3. The volume is not very loud when connected to a game console. Didn't try it on Skype to know how loud it could get there.

title: Marvelous Printer - SUPER easy setup -printer has email address -  immediate Wifi recognition-
text:
Easy printer to set up. Once I took it out of the box , unwrapped it and plugged it in, this printer was printing within 10 minutes. The screen leads you through each step..no need to look at installation instructions. I went on my Macbook Air, pulled up a document and it printed. I did NOT have to install the software on my Mac or the printer. ( I am in the transition from a Windows 7 to a Macbook Air. Review is for either a windows or a Mac.)

This is , by far, the easiest printer that I have ever installed. I bought a Cannon wf printer 2 weeks ago, and it would not recognize the wifi , so I returned it. I am so very pleased with the simple no-hassle setup. A small child , who can read, could set this printer up. The only thing I was unsure of when installing was how to install the ink cartridges- the "case" that houses the cartridges looks different than the old printers. . But, don't worry, there is an automated video on the screen that shows you exactly how to install the cartridges. You do not force the cartridge in past when it wants to stop and there is no "clicking" sound when the cartridge is installed correctly. If the cartridge is in wrong, the printer will reject the cartridge- just push it in.

There is an Email assigned to the printer- a nice feature! Your printer has it's own email account- who needs a fax anymore? Send an email to your printer, or, better yet, give your printer's email address to others , and when they email the printer, the document will print AND you
get an email notification that a your printer received a document . That saves you steps! You don't have to open your email to send it to the printer !

Can scan to flash drive, an email address, your computer.

Found out I did have to download the HP drivers in order to scan. It was flawless..HP knew what my operating system was and took about 5 minutes to download. Now, I can clean printheads, see ink levels, scans, etc from my MacBook.

I had an Epson and a Cannon within the last month that constantly dropped the Wifi connection, after one print job. I had to reestablish the wifi connection multiple times, and that was frustrating ! For some reason, I thought I would venture out and try something other than an HP. I had always had HP's. That was a mistake ! HP really has the user in mind- from setup to operation of all functions. Kudos to HP for their design and easy installation.

title: Value and Quality
text: I ordered these pencils specifically for their colors and the little sharpeners in each pencil.  These pencils are refillable which is a huge plus.  WIth these pencils, I can sharpen them without them constantly breaking as my wood pencils do.  I love that I can get fine lines as the projects I work on are very small, 4 x 6 and 2 x 3 and various other small sizes.  The colors blend well with my other color pencils and watercolor pencils.  The leads are soft but *not* easily breakable allowing them to be blended easily.  I was surprised at the value and quality of these pencils.  If you know how to mix colors, there are sufficient colors provided in the set.  There are plenty of secondary and tertiary colors to allow for quality coloring book results.  These would be great for certain children's ages because they don't have to sharpen them like wood pencils and endure chronic breakage.  This constant breakage happens with my Chinese brand pencils especially and my Prismacolor pencils when sharpening but not so far with my Faber-Castell pencils and no breakage at all with these 36 mechanical pencils.  I highly recommend that one try these pencils first instead of paying large amounts of money for some of the other "top of the line" pencils or buy these as an adjunct to the wood pencils.  I believe one can never have too many pencils.  This set allows for versatility and excellent value coupled with quality.  Obviously,  I highly recommend this set.

Now we're home and criss crossing into Mexico weekly and living in a town where 80% of the community is Spanish first, English second.

These flash cards are helping me reboot my Spanish more effectively than picking up words here and there organically. My grammar still elicits tales of laughter from our friends, but that's fine.

title: Easy to use for small projects
text: I don't often laminate anything, but every now then something comes up and I realize I need a laminator. This unit is the right size for a small office that needs it infrequently. title: Looks good, actually comfortable
text:
My last DIY office chair was a disaster in 4 weeks. I think this one will be better after just one full day. The construction quality on this chair superior in every way. This just feels sturdy as soon as you sit in it and the bolts throughout are fitted properly.

I love the grey palette and the sleek design. The chair looks good and brings a hint of modern into my office space. The headrest adults and the chair lifts or reclines with little effort - but it holds it's position! I like it a lot.

title: Decent quality paper, works well in multiple printers

title: Useful in a small office
text: I am using these to keep printed copies of various State and Federal Studies available for fast reference. Sometimes, it is actually easier for me to grab a physical copy and go directly to the reference section I need than find the file in the computer. These folders fit in one of those little wire things on my desk and are easy to grab. Plus they travel well to out of the office meetings where I need the document, but have no internet access.

title: Nice holder for newspaper
text: I get two newspapers at my office and these little organizers are great for holding the paper when not being read. I keep one in my little lobby space for visitors having to wait. The holders fit well on side table and hold tourism magazines as well.

title: Not great with drywall & a heavy door
text:
This is probably fine for something like a screen door or even a swing window of some sort. However, for a heavy entry door, this is not great. The included hardware like the wall anchors is flimsy and thin - I actually had to buy better anchors because one these simply broke.

My problem is the magnet is so strong with a heavy door, that you have to actually pull hard to separate the door from the stop. Unfortunately, that causes the anchor to shift and wobble just a bit in the wall. Which leads to drywall damage. Over time, the entire doorstop will come loose or out of the wall entirely leaving a damaged area.

title: Sharp, fine line every time
text: I am persnickety about my ink pens, especially for work stuff. I hate black ink, I really dislike a thick line or fuzzy gel ink. These pens are working for me. The blue is bright without being ridiculous and the fine point creates a sharp, thin line that doesn't bleed over or dry fuzzy because too much ink came out. I will definitely consider buying these in the future when I've used the whole box.

title: Works fine in a small office
text: I have this on my desk to try to keep my daily to do list organized. It's working well and isn't so flimsy that it slides around the wood desktop. I think it looks nice - definitely better than the typical wire mesh versions.

title: Well made and stiff
text: File folders are something you can't live without in an office. These are definitely better than some of the generic folders we've used before. Each one is stiff and sturdy even when being dragged around in my tote bag to three meetings.

title: Bright, easy to see colors

text: Sometimes, hand writing notes is just faster than using a laptop or phone. I always have a notebook by my side and these are nice ones. They fit in my handbag and on the dashboard of the car comfortably. The structure of the notebooks is well done and they should survive some abuse.

title: Sturdy, well made
text:

title: Operating perfectly in harsh environment
text:
I'm using this printer in our RV to print stuff for a board I sit on. Just because we're in the RV full time, doesn't mean life/community involvement stops.

Since these are tight quarters, I put the printer away in a cabinet when it's not needed. So I'm packing it up, lifting it and moving it at least once a week. Despite that, it's printed without any trouble every time.

I've done a 15 page proposal for a new park including color photos of the site and it looks great. The photos are not blotchy or washed out. This machine works equally well as a simple copier.

I'm using this printer strictly with WiFi and printing from my Pixel phone and a Samsung tablet and a regular, old fashioned laptop when I must. The Canon app downloaded smoothly to my phone and tablet and it works without a bunch of drama. Overall, I'm happy with this printer.

title: Fine point tip, nice blue ink
text: These are very fine tipped pens. However, the ink flows smoothly and the pens write well without requiring any special handling. The blue is a crisp, bright color that certainly looks better than boring black ink.

title: Room to make notes, pretty
text:
I like this planner for several reasons. The floral pattern appeals to my feminine side. It also fits perfectly in my big portfolio.

I'm doing work with a local city and state park where everything is scheduled around the fiscal year rather than Jan-Dec. So this is exactly what I needed. The pages have plenty of room for notes and information and the binding allows it to lie flat.

title: Looks nice, holds a 10" tablet
text:
