My 10" tablet does for in this case, but it's tight and there's no real padding if you drop the portfolio. I do like that there's a full zipper so nothing falls out. Overall, this looks nice and serves my purposes well.

title: Clean, smooth writing
text:
I have no idea if the coating or whatever on these pens is truly functional or necessary. I mean, I don't think a major brand like BIC is going to make false claims, but there's literally no possible way for a regular person to test a plastic with antibacterial properties.

I can say that the pens do work normally. The blue ink is nice and it writes smoothly and cleanly. The pens are slender and fit easily in my purse so I have one whenever I need it.

title: Light hearted  cards for a terrible year
text: 2020 has been a rough year for everyone on the planet and Christmas looks to be strained this year. That means I wanted just playful, joyful cards to send to our loved ones we won't get to see for the holidays. Disney to the rescue. These cards are light hearted and sweet and have a smidge of vintage look to them. They are the right size for a single stamp so they are ready for your handwritten message, address labels and a stamp.

title: Pretty with traditional designs
text: These are your standard  Christmas cards. There's nothing fancy, showy or tasteless here at all.  The different designs are very traditional and nicely done. I like that the cards and envelopes are sized for a single postage stamp.

title: Useless as a magnet,  useless as tape
text: Grrrr. I wanted to attach this to a fridge in an RV so we could display our magnets from different locations.  Nope. This is just straight up garbage. The adhesive is weak and does not hold on any surface. We tried it on wood, plastic and metal.  Every piece fell off within 3 hours. Absolutely useless. Just for fun, i tried to attach stuff to the magnetic side - it holds the church key bottle opener,  but nothing else.  I just threw the rest of the roll away.

title: Great for on the go
text:
We needed a thin file to keep the documents in for a travel trailer. I wanted all of its paperwork in one spot, that could travel and stay separate from our car stuff.

This works perfectly for my needs. The pockets keep the insurance, maintenance records, receipts, registration and other stuff organized and easy to find. Plus it tucks neatly into the car seat pocket when we're traveling.

title: Look nice, great for small,  lightweight items
text: These are exactly what we needed in the travel trailer. No holes in the already thin wall and a clean,  silver appearance. These stick very well and are almost completely flush against the wall. We're only using them for hats, light leashes and silicone spoons - nothing heavy. I wouldn't trust these with artwork or anything over a 1lb or so.

title: Neat idea for tracking travels
text: We are trying to see every National Park over the next two years. This map is a fun way to note the ones we've been to and the ones we still need to get to.

title: Nice size and weight for on the go notes
text:
I've been researching RVs for a few months now - looking at the dealers lots and big RV shows and individual sellers. These things begin to run together very quickly and get blurred in my memory. I'm using this portfolio thing to take notes and hold various brochures and business cards for each model we like as we begin to narrow down the options.

It's light and easy to carry as I traipse in and out of the travel trailers and Class C units. The back is stiff and easy to write on while standing. There's space for the fliers, spec sheets and whatnot on the go. It fits comfortably in my tote bag and I like it.

title: Funny dinosaurs
text: I love this silly dinosaur card. It perfectly suits my husband's sense of humor and I'm looking forward to giving it to him on Valentine's Day. The physical card is sturdy and should stand up for display easily for a week or two.

title: Pretty cards meant to be mailed
text: You can always count on Hallmark to produce well made, physically sturdy cards. These are no different and will survive traveling in the mail. The Christmas balls design on the front is classic and lovely. I find the interior message is a bit generic, but still appropriate.

title: Great for equine records and easy access
text:
You can't really go too wrong with a big three ring binder. We have all of our horse records in binders for fast reference - their registration papers, veterinary records, show entry forms, show results, receipts, etc. It is just so much easier to access the info manually and all in one spot than messing around with files and software and which techno gadget works or if the WiFi is available or not.

These binders are big enough for a year of paperwork for one horse actively showing or three years for a pasture ornament. The rings open and closed smoothly and the binders stand up straight on the bookshelf.

title: Great for quick notes or written driving directions
text:
There are times when you can just write down whatever info you need faster than messing around with a tablet or computer. We keep pens and notepads in the house, the barn and the cars.

These are nice. The spiral binding at the top makes it easy to keep open on a car seat with written directions. There's plenty of writing space on each page for hurried notes or actual letter writing with the lines.

title: interesting and sometimes very funny
text: Some of these are pretty darn funny and some are ridiculous and some just emphasize the differences between the coasts and the rest of the nation. It's an interesting way to start the day off. There is no room for notes on these pages, so it's definitely a look at only type of thing.

title: Fun and uplifting messages
text: Sometimes, sending a card is just the best way to reach out and say something. Texts and emails are not warm or loving and there's something special about receiving a physical, hand written message. This set of cards is cute and fun and I have already mailed out three of them. The cards themselves are well made and stand up for display pretty well.

title: Delightful and gorgeous
text: Simply gorgeous in person. We have a big list for our annual Christmas card list, but there are four folks who are so special that I make a point to find extra beautiful cards for them. This card certainly qualifies. It unfolds perfectly into a delicate and super pretty Christmas tree. This is certainly a card you would display on the mantle.

title: Eye catching colors. They stick well
text: For knock offs of actual Post It notes, these aren't bad at all. The colors are bright and eye catching. Each pad has plenty of pages, but is small enough to fit in purse as well as a desk drawer. The pages do stick well and stay stuck.

title: Fast, lots of functionality for a variety of requirements.
text:
I'm a little surprised by some of the negative reviews for this printer. My experience has been excellent over almost a full month of use. This is a big, heavy printer that takes up its own table, so don't expect a little, compact unit. It's also more complicated to set up initially than a typical home printer.

We have a home network with two desktop computers, three laptops and two tablets sharing this printer. I work from home with a friend who brings her laptop a few afternoons a week and we use this printer for business stuff as well as the usual personal nonsense. Once we got it set up and the network all lined out, it turned out the best thing was to connect the printer directly via Ethernet to our router rather than relying on WiFi alone. I have added the printer to our Google cloud options and can now print directly from my phone and tablet even when I'm out at the horse barn.

The scanner works just like any other one and it offers an option to scan directly to a thumb drive - very handy for traveling and keeping emergency backups of necessary documents. You can also print directly from the thumb drive as long as you know the file name you're looking for.

I've been amazed at the high quality of the printed documents and they come out dry - even photos. Apparently, that's the difference between an ink jet and the toner based machines. No smudges. The inks for this printer are significantly more expensive than my old little HP, but the overall performance of this machine is better. It also prints very quickly. I'm pleased and have no real complaints so far.

title: Bigger tabs are easy to read
text: I like these dividers. The bigger tabs are very easy to see and to write on. The floral print is pretty and dresses up my horse vaccination record book. I'm using these in a standard three ring binder and they fit fine.

title: Not leather. Decent size journal
text:
I absolutely hate when these companies use the word leather in the product name when it is NOT leather. This is some chemically made plastic and while it is soft, it is not actually leather and looks like plastic. The very use of the word leather is deliberately misleading.

The book itself is fine - lots of blank pages and plenty of room to write on each one. The lock is flimsy, but it does work fine and they included complete instructions on changing the code. The moon design is cute without being childish. I always carry a journal when we travel and this should work for me.

title: Snarky tag for a snarky cat
text: I love the attitude with this snarky tag. Our smug Siamese cat likes to sit on the neighbors' porches and mooch attention or snacks. He has a reflective collar of course, but the printing on it with our address has faded. The tag makes it faster for people who don't know our kitty to understand he's not lost, he's just ridiculous.

title: Very useful at the horse barn
text: This locker/cubby bin is both sturdier and taller than I expected. That's good because it's being used at the barn to hold jackets, helmets and riding boots and it's holding up well after a month. It's not the simplest thing to assemble, so prepare to spend some time with it. It's also heavy - it took two of us to get it installed off the floor.

title: Very useful for remodeling
text: These are really nice markers. I'm using them in a remodeling project to mark spots for new electrical outlets, light switch boxes, cutting measurements and the like. Having a variety of colors has been very helpful - purple for outlets, red for switches, and so on.

title: Lovely set of sincere thank you cards
text: There's something deliberate and very personal about giving someone a specific Thank You card with a handwritten message on it. Saying thanks by text or email is just tacky and generic and means nothing. These cards are very well constructed and each one is different in message and tone. I will be happy to give these away to people we care about.

title: Perfect for the fridge and includes three markers and the eraser
text: What a great idea....a large, thin magnetic white board that fits perfectly on our fridge. Even the included eraser and markers are magnetic so they don't get lost. This is exactly what I needed so my Mother can see exactly how much each dog eats when she dogsits. The markers a black, pink and blue making it easy to highlight information. I really like this.

title: Very cute and worth giving to someone special
text: Super cute! The two little pop out/up cats inside are darling. The card is thick and sturdy enough to withstand multiple openings and passing around.

title: Cute and fun. Too big for the tree though
text: This is a large card and bulky because the plush Mickey head is packed inside it. Be prepared to spend more postage than normal if you're mailing this to someone. The Mickey Mouse ornament inside is really cute and a great way to get a kid started on the Disney obsession. The ornament itself is too bulky to really be suitable for a Christmas tree, but it would make a nice doorknob ornament for a child's room.

title: Very small cards and ugly logo on the envelopes
text: Sigh. This doesn't feel like Hallmark to me. These are much smaller than traditional Christmas cards - they make me think of the little Valentine's Day cards kids passed out in 3rd grade. The envelopes are flimsy and have a big Ink Studio logo on the back. It's tasteless and cheap looking.

title: Modern, fresh take on Christmas cards - nice quality
text: We always send Christmas cards and I take joy in selecting the right card for the right person and writing a personal message in each one. These cards are are prettier in person than on the net. The black and white lining and bow are modern and fresh and a tad unconventional for Christmas cards. The cards and envelopes are the expected Hallmark quality and should survive being mailed just fine.

title: Nice option for the kids on your Christmas card list
text: We do Christmas cards for family and friends every year and I usually send a second card just to the kids in some families on our list. These are too cutesy for our grown up cards, but the Peanuts them is perfect for the kids. The cards are fun and cheerful and exactly what I was looking for.

title: To the point with a bit of sass. Nice quality, blank inside
text: This is the usual high quality paper and artwork we expect from Hallmark. The message is a sassy way to tell someone close to you that you're thinking of them. The inside is blank so you can write your own message. My complaint is simply that this is, at most,can three dollar card, no way would I spend more than that on this one.

title: Nice everyday pens that don't smear or run
text: These are nice pens with the quality you expect from Paper Mate. The blue is rich, classic blue that looks nice. The ink flows smoothly and doesn't smear or run. I like these slightly fatter pens - they are reasonably easy to grip and write with.

title: Room for a personal note inside and envelopes that can be mailed
text: You can never have too many thank you cards and these are very nice. If you've received a gift or help during a time of loss, these Thank You for your Sympathy cards are exactly the right response. Each one is tastefully done and they open to a blank interior so you have room to hand write a personal note. The envelopes are sturdy enough to survive being mailed.

title: Well thought out design and pages. Room for scheduling and notes every day
text: "Very nice" was my first impression of this day planner. It's sized just right to fit on my desk or the passenger seat of the truck depending on my needs and it's easy to carry. The weeks are laid out with two pages per week so you have plenty of space to write notes and keep the schedule easy to read. It's exactly the layout I use for scheduling riding lessons for my students and keeping track of various horse requirements. I also like the plastic type of cover - hopefully when I dribble coffee on it, it won't fall apart.

title: Excellent size areas for notes and daily appointments - easy to see
text:
My husband keeps a spiral planner with him all the time for work. It's actually faster to keep notes, track mileage and appointments each day in the physical planner than his phone - no apps, no data needed and no accidentally erasing important information.

This one is a good choice for his daily needs. It's got each month broken into two pages with room n each day square for little notes. The other pages between each month have room on each day to write lots of notes, addresses or whatever you need in print large enough to actually read. The cover is a plastic rather than cardboard so it should hold up all year in the truck.

title: Cheerful colors for get well and thank you notes
text:
I send thank you notes and get well notes and just hey, how are you cards to friends all the time. There's something far more special about receiving a handwritten note in the mail than a soulless text or email. I keep a variety of different engraved stationary, pre-printed cards and generic note cards with envelopes on hand at all times.

This set is pretty basic, but does meet the requirements for a quick get well notes. The color selection is bright and cheerful with every hue you could want. The cards are thin, but not flimsy. The envelopes are pretty thin too and I don't really trust the seams, so I'm taping them closed before putting them in the mail. For basic, simple cards, this is a good box with a bunch in it - I could see using these for casual party invitations too.

title: Functional notebooks with creepy dogs as food covers
text: These are small notebooks that fit in a purse or the center console of a car - lots of little, oddball spaces where you might need to stash a notebook. The pages have a decorative border around them that eats up some writing real estate, but it's not a big deal - I'm just using these for grocery lists and such anyway. Personally, though, I really don't like the design on the sushi cover. It creeps me out - I know other people will think I'm crazy, but the idea of dogs and cats being represented as part of a human meal on a sushi roll really disturbs me. I know, I know it's a cartoon, etc etc, but it's as bad as looking at a tarantula or scary Stephen King clown to me.

title: Cute and perfect for the Star Wars fan family
text: I lost my father a few years ago. He and I were both (original) Star Wars lovers and the card would have made him very happy. I wanted it as a fun reminder of my Daddy. The sound plays with a press of the button on the front rather than as soon as the card is opened. It's just a fun, light hearted card.

title: Nice for tracking annual veterinary records for multiple animals
text:
For my purposes, these are excellent folders. We have multiple horses and 6 dogs and a single Siamese cat.... because we don't dare add a second cat lest Free Cat shred me in my sleep. I keep meticulous records for each animal and on each of my riding students, so organizing paperwork is always part of my day.

These file jackets are easy to use and great for carrying in the truck if needed. Keep them upright and nothing slips out or gets lost. That's kind of a big deal here when I'm taking an elderly dog to the vet - I have the last year of medical records at my fingertips. The files are sturdy and fit in my regular, 24 year old file cabinets.

title: Nice for adding a page to a cookbook or taping temporary stuff to the wall - like a Post It
text:
We don't do a lot of random taping around here, but there are times we need tape at unexpected moments. Like tapng up the assembly instructions for a computer desk so I could see them handsfree.

This stuff makes me think of the Post Its - it sticks, but comes off without drama. No marks or tearing whatever its taped to. It's actually very handy to attach a note card to a recipe page in an giant cookbook. (I always note any changes to a recipe and the results) Post Its work too of course, but this has other uses as well.

title: Standard note cards with tons of uses
text:
Index cards aren't a glamorous product, but they are a very handy thing to have in the kitchen, home office and even the horse barn. These are the usual stiff, white, cardboard with lines and can be used as recipe cards as well as note cards for any number of reasons.

I have them out at the horse barn with feeding instructions for each horse on one card. These can easily be swapped out as things change and can be paper clipped to the front of the horse's folder or attached to the white board with notices as needed.

title: Romantic, but not syrupy sweet message
text:
After 21 Valentine's Day cards for my husband, finding a new one with a good message has become tricky. He doesn't like the super mushy cards and I don't like the generic ones you might give a new boyfriend. This one is a reasonable medium ground for my needs.

The card is sturdy and stands well on its own. The message is nice and there's room to write your own personalized note inside. I don't like the watered down, drab colors on the card - the reds feel like they are edging into browns and grey in some places. It's not a big deal, but the card could be prettier.

title: Work correctly without bending unexpectedly.
text: For the most part, paper clips are pretty much...well....paper clips. These are the standard sized metal paper clips. They hold 10 to 20 sheets of paper comfortably, but that's probably close to the limit. I'm using them n my barn office to keep feed and farrier records for each horse sorted. Each box has 100 in it and for my needs, this multi pack is essentially a lifetime supply.

title: Very easy to use and upload to share. No storage for the pen
text:
I wasn't entirely sure what I would do with this gadget, but it was much too interesting to pass up. I'm a serious list maker - groceries, to-do, chores, errands, pros and cons etc etc. I do them on the backs of envelopes, in my cell phone, with Alexa, on my tablet, on regular notes and scraps of old receipts. It's a running joke with my husband that if it's not on a list, it's not happening. It turns out that this folio style smart notepad is exactly what I needed.

Once you connect via Bluetooth to your phone or tablet, this updates through the InkSpace app and just does its thing. From the app you save, download or send your notes/sketches or in my case, my lovely lists. I've been driving my husband crazy by sending his JPG chore lists for the horse barn and yard all weekend.

The pen is a tad wide, but you get used to it fast enough and it writes smoothly. There's an extra ink cartridge included BTW. You just write on the paper, click the button to upload to the app and go on with your business. My one complaint is that the pen is loose. There's no way to keep it attached to the folio case - tuck it into the inside pockets and the case doesn't close flat. If I take this out of the house it will only be a matter of time before I lose the pen entirely - no pen and the entire thing is rendered unusable.

title: Frozen ink slots, menu loops incessantly with one error message. Unusable
text:
I have a Bluetooth HP printer that works like a charm after two years, but it doesn't scan. I thought I would use this one as an upgrade of sorts, despite having had trouble with two previous Canon Pixma printers in the past.

Unfortunately, this printer is a failure for me. Just as persnickety and error prone as the other two I had trouble with before. I had it out of the box in five minutes and the packing materials removed and plugged it in. It immediately flashed an error code saying the paper cartridge was not installed properly. I followed the directions and for fifteen minutes the screen looped from the error code to the menu and back to the error code. Meanwhile, the ink slots are frozen and the belt won't move to allow me to even try to install the ink containers. It's simply unusable at this point.

The frozen ink holder problem is the same one I had with my first Pixma a few years ago - at least that printer waited a few months to act up. This will be the last Canon printer for me, I'll stick to the little HP printer.

title: Thirsty card just sounds like highschool puppy love
text:
I love cards and buy them for random reasons throughout the year. There's just something lovely about getting a sweet card in the mail unexpectedly and I try to pass that feeling on to our friends.

(Review of the Mahogany Thirsty Card)

This, however, just struck me as off. It's not unattractive per se, but it feels unbalanced and the decorations are just sort of scattered all over it. The message has a distinct immaturity as well. My first impression wasn't of love or adoration, but some poor, acne plagued, 14 year old boy trying to convince his first girlfriend of his undying love.

I asked my husband to read it without sharing my impressions. He laughed and said "are we in highschool?" So it's not just me. I won't be passing this one on to him for our anniversary.

title: Cute without being saccharine sweet. Sturdy enough to stand up on its own
text: What a cute, festive card. It has a very simple Happy birthday message inside that isn't too mushy. The little candles decorating the front cover are attached firmly and shouldn't fall of easily. But I don't think I would mail this card because those candles would be roughed up in transit. Like most Hallmark cards, this one is well made on thick card stock and stands up on its own for display.

title: Pretty, glittery angel that becomes a tree ornament. Too delicate to mail
text:
Out of the 65 people on our annual holiday card list, there are 15 who get individualized cards. Something special and chosen specifically to say how much they mean to us. This is one of those type of Christmas cards.

The front is a detailed, bright and glittery angel. The angel actually comes off the face of the card and becomes a tree ornament. Clever and pretty. Because the card includes that ornament piece, it's heavier than most and the angel is a bit delicate, this card isn't really suitable for mailing. It's definitely a give in person with a hug sort of Christmas card.

title: Sweet sentiment for someone special. Front house is a removable tree ornament
text:
Out of the 65 people on our annual holiday card list, there are 15 who get individualized cards. Something special and chosen specifically to say how much they mean to us. This is one of those type of Christmas cards.

The front is a really nice, thick house design with a lovely message. The house actually comes off the face of the card and becomes a tree ornament. Clever and pretty. Because the card includes that ornament piece, it's heavier than most and will definitely require extra postage.

title: Easy to program, highly visible adjustable screen. Works fine
text:
We keep a landline for several reasons, primarily because 911 services are sketchy with cellular connections. Also, we never give our cell numbers to businesses etc because they inevitably telemarket later and I don't want that harassment on my cellphone.

I like this phone. It's simple to set up, can be wall mounted and the number pads are big. The lighted screen is adjustable to allow for easy visibility and the print is large - enough so that I can read the call log without my glasses. I have the ringer on silent, but it can be set pretty loud if needed. The answering machine functions well and can be set to play the incoming message out loud or not - very handy.

title: Plenty of room on each day for notes. The cover design is busy though
text:
I try to keep a written weekly schedule for my riding students lessons and the other daily chores/errands that pop up. I used to use just my cellphone, but after a dropping it in a pond and frying the SD card as well as the actual phone, it was time for a physical back up plan.

This hardback planner is decent for my needs. There's lots of room on each day to write the schedule and additional notes if needed. It lies flat when opened and has a ribbon to mark your place when its closed. This book is a tad too bulky and heavy to carry around with me in my handbag so it's relegated to living on my desk. My one star deduction is simply for the cover art and random quotes scattered throughout. The flowers are really busy and distracting to the eye and the sayings are a little trite for my taste.

title: Ink flows like silk with no smearing. Easy to grip and use
text:
I love a good ink pen. I send cards, thank you notes and invitations to dinner on hand written, good stationery and linen cards. It's a Southern thing that was ingrained in me from childhood and I take pleasure in a personalized message to someone I care out. There's just no charm in a generic email or worse, a text message thanking someone for a gift.

These pens are easy to hold - not just the typical thin, slippery plastic tubes. Each color is crisp and bright without any smudges or wet spots. The ink flows smoothly and effortlessly and dries quickly. It's a breeze to write with these. I think the blue is definitely my favorite.

title: Sturdy, stackable with sturdy handles. Right for relocation of a home business
text:
I'm slightly ashamed to admit that it took me several minutes to figure out how to put these boxes together. Once I got the order of things, I realized that it's easy, I'm just a doofus.....The directions are printed on each box, so it's not exactly a mystery.

Once they are put together, the lid fits well - as long as you don't mistakenly tear off the tabs. The boxes are more sturdy than expected and this collection has 3 different sizes. I'm prepping for a move in the next month and these are suitable for all our horse business records, receipts, files and assorted paperwork. The large boxes are exactly what I needed for keeping the show ribbons and championship sashes clean and safe for transit during the move. The boxes stack well and are easy to label with a marker.

title: Scans very fast, but getting software & firmware updated takes a while
text:
I'll say this... The scanner is fast and it takes up almost no space. However, due to the small size, it's a little delicate and persnickety. If you don't have the paper in just right or if the scanner is unbalanced (like using it on the ottoman with the laptop) it throws an error message. That's not a big deal for me though.

The issue I have is the software. You have to go to the Epson website to get the drivers and the other optional software to sort your scanned documents or turn them into documents to edit. It took 15 minutes to download and install everything and then another 10 minutes to get the firmware updated and rebooted. So almost a half hour of messing with it before I could actually scan something. Then this morning Windows 10 didn't recognize the scanner and kept wanting to send me to my Epson printer - changing the name on both the printer and scanner solved that problem fortunately. I have it working now, but I am aggravated that instead of just scanning a floor plan change from my contractor, I had to mess around with software....again.

title: Perfectly sized for a handbag. Makes a great home renovation notebook
text:
Absolutely the perfect size and shape to carry in my handbag as a notebook. I'm in the midst of heavy research on the restoration of an old house, so I am drawing sketches, taking measurements, and making notes on the go. Honestly, it's proven faster and simpler to just write in this notebook instead of relying on a note function on my phone or tablet.

The cover is sturdy and has held up to bumping and banging around in my purse, random tables, balancing on a fence post top, and the hood of the truck. The little pocket in the back holds several folded pages - I currently have two surveys, a rough kitchen remodel sketch from my contractor and a couple of receipts in the pocket. I like the attached place holder ribbon for separation of sketch pages and actual notes. I can see ordering another two of these before we get this project finished.

title: Stylus is ok, ink is beautiful navy blue that flows perfectly.
text:
Deep, true navy blue ink that just effortlessly floats out of the pen onto your paper. I really prefer the Ink Joy line of pens and it sort of boils down to the physical shape and size of the actual pen that works best for you.

I hand write letters, personal thank you notes, get well cards and the like all the time. I'm part of a dying breed of women with customized, high quality, cotton blend embossed note cards and stationary specifically so I can send handwritten notes. I detest a flimsy, leaky, thin inked, splotchy pen.

This particular pen is decent, but the stylus tip isn't great. The shape of the pen has several ridges, almost an octagon, and isn't difficult to grip, but writing several pages will tire your hand quickly. The stylus works, but sometimes requires multiple taps on my phone compared to a single tap with a finger to make things happen.

title: Small footprint, HP ePrint App works perfectly with my cell phone, average photos
text:
Finally! Smartphone and tablet printing made simple. This little printer is not meant to be a fancy photo printer, but it does a decent job for quick pictures and it definitely works perfectly for documents and screen shots. The foot print is pretty small compared to my small Epson printer and it weighs so little that moving it around is a breeze.

Installing this and connecting it to my WiFi network took four clicks on the color touchscreen, entering our password and about 30 seconds for the printer to see it, connect and be ready to use. Download the HPePrint app from the app store to your phone, make sure your phone is connected to the same WiFi network as the printer and you're ready to go. Within 3 minutes I was printing photos straight from the gallery on my phone and a screen shot of an Amazon receipt. (I am using an LG V10 phone)

The two sample ink cartridges don't hold a lot, the screen tells me that I have already used about a 1/4 of the black ink in 3 days. I do like that there are only two cartridges though. The battery power only option works well and the printer isn't any slower than when plugged directly into the wall. My battery was dead in 24 hours with sporadic use throughout that period, but I didn't set the sleep and power off options - I just wanted it to cycle through. I really like this machine and I can see taking it with us to the next family gathering to produce real pictures instantly to share.

title: The best tape for shipping overseas & storage boxes in the attic
text: Solid shipping tape for mailing boxes (care packages) overseas and for sealing up storage boxes to put in the garage and attic. I use these on my own tape gun/dispenser thing with no problems. A single roll of the 1.88 yard Scotch tape can cost close to three bucks locally, so buying in bulk is definitely a money saver.

title: Pulls smoothly, the sharp edge cuts correctly & the tape holds boxes shut in the garage
text: I picked up a couple of these Scotch packing tape rolls with the self cutting ends locally and I'm really pleased with the entire system. The tape holds well on both regular cardboard boxes and envelopes for mailing and on boxes for storing stuff in the attic. I am finally cleaning out a ton of old clothes to be donated and sorting the holiday decorations into their own various labeled containers for storage. The tape has helped me with both projects and the cutting end means I managed to not lose yet another pair of scissors in the process.

title: Expensive & complicated, but looks great and they resist wear and tear pretty well.
text:
I got these to go with the Smead Life Planner System with the hanging file folders & big box. [[ASIN:B01D02X1Z0 Smead Life Documents Organizer Kit (92010)]] The quick fold tabs are new to me and I really like how they work. Essentially they fold in half and sort of stand up, creating a stiff "tent" above the folder that is easily visible and stiff. You attach the plastic tab in the little slots on the folder and it stands up without anything else needed.

This is kit comes with 45 of the plastic quick fold tabs and the sticker type sheets you print your own headings/labels on. You color code them for each section you're making. This is an expensive set up actually and it's more complicated than simply doing it by hand to be honest, thus the one star deduction. But...once it's finished and installed, the box looks great and the various files are easy to locate and keep organized.

title: Excellent backup plan for an emergency if you live in a hurricane zone
text:
This is exactly what I needed and couldn't quite figure out what it was that was missing from my homemade system. This is a solid box that is self contained and can be easily picked up and taken away - that's especially important if you live in an area prone to natural disasters like tornadoes or hurricanes. All of your critical information & records can be grabbed in one step and put in your car for evacuation with no searching or trying to make sure you have multiple different loose files.

The hanging files have labels that stand up to be easily seen and are color coded by generalized section - Purple is Health and that in turn, is broken down into multiple subcategories like Emergency Contacts (Pharmacy, Doctors, Dentist), Health Coverage (Insurance Policy Info etc). There are labels and manila folders for each of the subcategories in each section. Orange is "Ownership" and includes things like Mortgage information, Art Appraisals, and Car titles. You just organize your documents and file them as you choose. You can always add files and categories to suit your own life requirements - there is plenty of extra room in the box for that.

Of course you should keep the originals of really important stuff like wills, life insurance policies, passports etc in a safe deposit box or an actual safe, but the copies of those things or the information about the location of them in this handy box for quick reference or in case of emergency is a good back up plan. Having your health records on hand for everyone in your family and homeowners insurance policy easy to grab in a disaster could save you hours of trouble and maybe a lot of money at some point.

title: Absolutely adorable, interactive Christmas card for a child
text: This is beyond adorable. My soon to be three-year old niece will love this as her own personal Christmas card this year! The punch out Christmas Tree inside stands up on it's own once it's put together and then you use the included stickers to decorate the tree. What a great way to introduce a young child to the joy of receiving and sending personal cards in the mail.

title: Soft pink background highlights a beautiful cutout & wonderful message.
text: Beautiful. That's the first word that popped into my head when I saw this card and touched it. The detailed and delicate cutout on the front of flowers and butterflies is so well done, you really want to display this one where everyone can enjoy it. The background is a soft pink and doesn't scream "here I am!" like some pinks can - I appreciate that. The message on this one is heartfelt and sincere, but not overwrought. I have the perfect friend in mind for this card already, she always makes me want to be a better person just by spending time in her gracious company.

title: Understated elegance and sweet holiday wishes
text: This is an elegant and lovely card. Understated, but not without genuine sentiment and love. I like the gold and silver palette as a tasteful change from the traditional Christmas green and red. There is a bit of sparkle with glitter in the "friends" on the front and inside the words Merry Christmas are both glittered - but none of it has fallen off on my desk or in my hands. I already know exactly which couple we're going to give this card to this holiday season.

title: Adorable pup, nice accents with a ribbon & foil. Good for friends or family
text: I am a sucker for a dog on a card and this adorable Golden Retriever puppy made me smile before I even read the words on the rest of the card. The red foil and real ribbon accents are nice touches that lift the card a step above the dollar store rack in quality and appearance. The birthday sentiments on the message aren't too mushy, but sweet enough to give to a loved one or close friend. I can think of several of our "Dog Circle" friends who would appreciate this card immediately.

title: Nicely decorated without being overdone. Sweet sentiment. Will need two stamps for mailing.
text: Just enough embellishment to be fancy, but not so much as to be over the top or ridiculous. The silver hearts on the top are cut out from the underside of card, rather than a glued on applique or glitter - nice, no mess. This is an oversized card and sturdy, so if you're mailing it to your significant other, plan on using two stamps. I like that it stands up on its own with no wobbling around.

title: Perfect for your best smart alec friend
text: I love this card! I'm always on the lookout for smart alec cards for my long time friends and this one fits the bill perfectly. The glitter on the tiara didn't fall all over my desk when I opened the card or wrote on the inside, so that's a huge plus immediately. The message inside is a little strong for some folks, but this is a situation where you need to know your audience. I know my audience and my friend of 26 years will shriek with laughter and promptly put on the first fake tiara she can find at the dollar store.

title: Beautiful and well made. Sentimental without being overly sappy.
text: This is a beautiful card inside a card. It's oversized and heavy enough to stand up on its own for display. The front words are each on their own ornament style decorated cardboard pieces and glued to a piece of ribbon down the front of the card. The "lucky" theme repeats through the inside message and really brings home the "I appreciate you" tone. This is an oversized card, so if you intend to mail it, you'll need two stamps.

title: Sweet and simple with a smidge too much pink inside
text: This is a pretty birthday card for my Mother. Not too frou-frou, but not so plain that she will think I just grabbed a random card at the grocery store. The front has a fairly detailed drawing of roses enhanced by a bit of silver glitter - which is staying on the card and not falling all over my table by the way. Very nice. The words on the front of the card are a glued on velveteen material that gives the card a nice texture. My one star deduction is for the neon pink on the left side when you open the card. Whoa...that's just too bright. Brings to mind a 1950's bathroom sink.

title: Easy as pie to preserve antique family photos
text:
I wasn't entirely sure what to expect from these self laminating pouches. At 4 x 6 inches, the ones I tried are best suited for photos and small items you want to preserve rather than a diploma type thing. They are actually pretty simple to use after you read the directions - which include little drawings showing each step by the way.

I used them to seal some old photos that we don't have digital copies of and had no problems at all. Just take your time, center the photo, and smooth the top layer slowly and carefully to get a complete & bubble free seal. Pro tip - write any identifying information and dates on the back of the picture first and it'll be preserved for future generations as well. These pouches are a little pricey, but I will be ordering a box or two for some photos from my Grandparents' old albums before it's too late.

title: Fits the WF 3640 printer and is a bright blue.
text: This fits the Epson WF-3640 Workforce printer. The blue is bright and the ultra capacity cartridge does seem to last about 25% longer for my regular home usage than the regular cartridge - if you're deciding between this and the larger one. I use this printer and these inks for both regular printing and photos - everything looks good.

title: Meh. Old fashioned and a little dull. Sturdy though.
text: This is a nice enough birthday card, but I don't love it. It's kind of old fashioned and not in that retro cool way. The card itself is sturdy and stands up nicely so it could be displayed on a desk or shelf easily. The message is sweet and lovely - I don't think there's anything odd about it at all, perfectly suitable for someone you truly care about. There's just an overall impression of boring and meh when I look at this card. It's not one I would every pay for in a store or mail to a friend.

title: Nicely made & sturdy. Loving message without being over done
text: I give my husband lots of cards through the year, most are not terribly sentimental or mushy. This one will be the exception to the rule. It's just sweet enough and says exactly what I want to convey without being too much. The card itself is high quality and heavy card stock - this isn't a flimsy dollar store card. It stands up nicely on its own and the decoration on the front includes a small band of glitter with a rhinestone heart. This card would survive being mailed easily if you are so inclined.

title: Cute, well made, stands up without support. Quality card.
text: I give lots of cards to people that I care about - not just for birthdays or holidays. This is a nice one and one I am happy to add a personal note to & sign my name on with no shame for sending a cheap card that looks like a last minute after thought. The scoops of ice cream on the front are raised and textured and include a glued on sparkly "gem" piece at the top. The card stock is thick and the whole thing stands up nicely on its own when placed on a desk or shelf for display.

title: Cute idea that really works,not so sure it's worth the extra cost
text: More useful than I expected actually. The tabs fold away, out of sight when you swap from one to the other, so you can write on them and not worry about it. There's a sticky bit on the edge of the tabs that attaches to the clear plastic strip down the length of the folder top - it's reusable in the same way a traditional Post-It type sticky note is reusable. The folders themselves are sturdy, strong cardboard in red, blue, green and bright yellow. My one star deduction is for the value - these are pretty pricey when you consider that simply covering a pre-written tab with a blank mail label makes a regular folder reusable....for less money.

title: Timey-Wimey artsy look for holding your place on the page. Nicely done
text: This is a much nicer bookmark than expected. The artwork is gorgeous and goes perfectly with a similar Van Gogh theme Dr Who shirt I am giving a friend for Christmas. This bookmark has a tassel and is thick enough to hold your place in a book, but not so thick as to be bulky. It comes in a plastic sleeve - perfect for presentation or keeping as a collection item I suppose.

title: Plenty of room for annual financial record keeping. Nicely balanced
text: Ah...the new year is coming and that means new receipts and bank statements to keep track of for the tax man and that's where this binder comes in. It's more an orangey red than brick red, if that matters to you. The plastic is a bit textured which is nice, the clear cover is easier to slide open and slip a title sheet in. There are two additional pockets inside as well. The rings are pretty sturdy for my needs, but I won't be over-filling this binder. It does stand up correctly on it's own, so it's balanced properly.

title: Smooth binding, pretty floral pattern and smallish writing areas
text: This is a nice planner for basic functions. The spiral binding is coated so it doesn't snag the pages - I hate when that happens. The pages have a very pretty floral pattern throughout and the purple cover stands out so it's easy to spot on a crowded kitchen counter. My one star deduction is because the space to write in your appointments and activities each day is small. This is probably better suited for a single person's agenda rather than multiple people or a family schedule.

title: Surprisingly sturdy. Light, agile and easy to store.
text:
I love this step ladder and we've used it four times in 24 hours already! At three foot tall, this is the perfect height for routine household chores. Rubbermaid isn't kidding when they say it's ultra light either - under 9lbs and easily carried in just one hand. It's very slim when folded, so it's not too bulky or awkward walking down a hallway with the ladder in one hand and light bulbs in the other hand. It has rubber stopper things on the feet to keep it from sliding around on slick floors - these also protect my wood floors from scratches when we're climbing on it or scooting it around.

We have twelve and fifteen foot ceilings throughout the house with recessed can lights. The exterior lights are the same. Light bulb changing can be a circus around here. Yesterday, this ladder was stable in the front flower beds on uneven mulch while my husband used it to change the security light bulb along the garage wall. In the house, it was equally steady on carpet and wood floor for me dusting the tops of framed artwork. But the real reason for the five star rating is the fact that this ladder didn't budge when our six foolish dogs suddenly swarmed past, bumping into it at top speed when they saw a squirrel in the window. My husband was on it with both hands in midair changing a recessed light bulb and the ladder held steady - no wobbling!

title: No detectable scent, rich black that doesn't fade quickly, good markers overall
text: These are an excellent size for gripping if like me, you have a bit of arthritis in your fingers. The black is a deep, dark color that doesn't fade to light grey after a couple of hours on your board. That fading with other markers drives me crazy - I use a whiteboard to leave feeding instructions or medical care information about  specific horses in my barn and that information may need to be visible for several days. I am not able to detect any odor from these markers. The chisel edge is handy - I can write in cursive and it is totally legible with the thinnest edge, much faster that way.

title: Bare chested Capt. Mal and a good book..that is a very Good Day
text: A good book and a half naked Malcolm Reynolds peeking out at you....that is, indeed, a Good Day. I bought each of the other Firefly bookmarks as gifts, but this one is just for me. These are actually really good as functional bookmarks. The metal is thin enough to use without making a big indentation in your book, the tassel lends an elegant touch and the image is a classic reminder of the best Firefly episode of them all "Trash".

title: Well balanced, easy to every day, pricey....but worth it.
text: I stumbled on a set of three of these Cutco paring knives in a garage sale a few months ago for $3 each and I bought all of them. You can never have too many good little knives around. I realized tonight that I have not used my Wustoff paring knives once since I bought the little Cutco units. I cut up carrots and apples almost every day for the horses as well as the usual stuff you use one for. These are well balanced and easy to use. I'm now looking at the other knives in the brand.

title: Reminds me. of the Enterprise from Star Trek. Really useful in the kitchen for nutritional info on food boxes
text: I had to laugh when I put this together and turned on the two LED lights in a dark room for the first time. The entire unit looks like a little sculpture of the Enterprise Starship from Star Trek! That's a good thing though in my book. The lights are bright enough to see the inside of a dark toaster oven - looking for crumbs - and with the adjustable gooseneck, it's easier to hold & weighs less than a flashlight. Put together and used properly, this is a very good magnifier for reading, needle threading, button sewing, and jewelry cleaning. However, I have been using it primarily in the kitchen to read the fine print on the ingredients and nutritional breakdowns on food packages. The silver color blends nicely with our stainless appliances actually.  I received a free sample unit of this desktop magnifier to test and review and I have been very pleased.

title: Very cute & useful for home, barn, workshop and garage
text:
What a useful and neat way to organize stuff! I have never seen these liquid chalk markers or mini chalkboard labels before and was delighted to try a sample set for testing and review. The set comes with forty different reusable labels and the liquid chalk marker and this is more than enough for my purposes - especially since you can erase the labels and write something different on them later as your needs change. You do need to follow the directions and shake the pen for a full 30 seconds and tap the tip to get the ink flowing fully before using it, but once it's going, it's just like using any other felt type marker.

I am using several in our tack and storage rooms out at the horse barn and in the mud room at the house. My husband pounced on the rest of them for his work shop and the garage. Turns out the labels fit perfectly on a variety of varmint repellent products, fertilizer containers, and apparently, ammo cans. I received a sample set of labels and a marker from the seller for free to test and review.

title: Great Purchase
text:
I wish I had this product a long time ago. This is awesome. The one thing I wasn't clear on when I ordered the scale was what the lowest weight was it would weigh. Looks like it will weigh things that are even less than 1 pound. (I have nothing to use to see how accurate this product is at lower weights). This scale is also easy to hold on to while weighing.

Setup:
1. Hang the scale in an upright position and press the power button.
2. Keep pressing the power button to select your preferred unit of weight. Kilograms/grams/pounds/ounces
3. The screen will read 0.00 which indicates the scale is now ready to be used.

Caution: The digital luggage scale is not desinged for and should not be used to weight animals, babies, or children. If you have back problems or any health issues regarding the safe lifting of items, please restrain from using the digital luggage scale to weigh heavy items. Always remember to take care and use correct form when lifting.

Using the Strap:
1. Unclip the buckle.
2. Locate a handle or fixing on the items of luggage that is suitable for the scale's strap to connect. Please ensure that the fixing is centrally located and strong enough to support the entire weight of the item.
3. Securely fix the strap by passing it under the handle or fixing and closing the buckle. Please ensure the buckle is securely closed prior to lifting.

Weighing:
1. After correctly securing the luggage to the scale, gentle life the scale and a reading will be shown on the LCD display.
2. Once the luggage is stable, the LCD display will read "hold" and the data will be automatically memorized.

Please note: If the item is heavier than the scale can stand, the LCD will show "Err". Please try to lose some weight from the luggage to ensure the overload item / luggage will not harm the scale.

Power off:
1. Press the power button for 3 seconds to turn the scale off.

Please note: The scale has an automatic power off function which will shut off the device after 90 seconds of inactivity.

Notes:
1. When powering on the scale, please ensure to keep it in an upright position.
2. To ensure the accuracy, make sure to grip the handle tightly when weighing, and avoid interfering with any other part of the device or item being weighed.
3. Avoid any heavy impacts or rough treatment to the device.
4. To clean the device, use a soft cloth only. Do not use any chemical detergents for cleaning.
5. if the display reads (battery icon filled in dark), this indicates low power. Please ensure to replace the battery immediately.
6. For long-term storage of the device, please remove the battery to eliminate any risks of leakage.
7. Should you encounter any problems, please report it immediately to the manufacturer. Do not try to repair the device.
8. Do not immerse the scale in water.
9. Do not dispose of batteries in fire as they may explode or leak.

text: More comfortable than a regular foot stool, quite portable. Nice to rest my feet on while knitting. Read the cleaning instructions for the cover very carefully. Would be nice to have more color choices.

title: Beautiful looking and does a great job. No just strips, but cross cut.
text: I have had this shredder for about 4 months now and I am really enjoying it. Sturdy and does the job very well. No trouble with getting stuck. Have also used for a number of credit cards and it shreds them with no problem. Easy to clean with pull out wastebasket, Does leave some shavings on the floor , but not big deal. Very modernly styled, and looks nice in my home office. Just plug it in and it works. Hope it keeps going without dropping dead. Would definitively recommend for a home office with light but daily use.

title: Works fabulously
text: Really easy to sync up to my phone via Bluetooth. The app was very user friendly, and it prints labels lighting fast. Plus, it comes in such cute colors.

title: So cute!
text: I love these stickers for my planner. They're a really fun addition to it. I wish there weren't so many duplicate stickers, but for the price, I am definitely satisfied. I'll likely be purchasing more for next year's calendar and planner.

title: Not heavy duty at all. Command strips worked better for me
text: Hung a light canvas painting & it fell off the wall the next day. Would work better for posters & plain paper. Total waste of money. Ended up buying Command strips which actually worked.

text: was on my umpteenth paper shredder, but this blocks out my name and address and anything else I want to cover so I can stop buying paper shredders which never last anyway.

text: I wish I paid attention to how much comes in 1/4 of a cube. It's a really small box amount and you can't really protect more than 1 tiny item.

text: Works just like the HP cartridges. Only difference is the price.
