text: Could not get this to install properly on my laptop or desktop. It did work on 2 occasions.

title: Great envelopes!
text: Really nice and a great thing to send samples for my business in...

title: Great print cartridges
text: They have been working great. So I ordered twice as many

title: I was expecting boxed labels
text:
I was expecting these labels to be in a thin box, making them easy to tuck into the filing cabinet. Instead, you get a few sheets in a plastic bag. I feel the photo listed with the itrm is misleading.
I'm sure the labels will work for what I need them for, just disappointed in the packaging.

title: Plenty of labels and two colors
text:
You receive two rolls of freezer labels - one in blue type and one in red. I would guess you could easily choose to use one color for meats and one for all other items.

I have not had the opportunity to actually test how well they stay on once frozen, but will certainly be using these to label future freezer goods.

title: Nice set, easy to hold
text:
This is a very nice selection of pastel highlighters. The colors are not totally exact as the plastic cases, but fairly close.

I didn't have a book handy to test the bleed-through on, but tried it on a notepad. There was no bleed-through or color showing on the back of a page from a steno notebook, so that is a good sign.

The tips are very thin, so be sure to not push super hard when using these.

title: Colorful, easy to hold
text:
This is such a great thing to have if you have a home business.
Handheld, it is NOT cordless, which is the main downfall of this unit.

You WILL need to keep the instruction book forever, so know where it is! There are no button controls to do things like increase or decrease the beep of the scanner - there are BAR CODES for nearly any function inside the book. You have to SCAN what you want for your settings. Kind of odd, but it is what it is.

My inventory is currently packed, so I couldn't test it on my actual items yet. But I think it will be a handy thing for inventory control for small businesses.

title: Small, colorful and very useful
text:
These little things are SO handy!
The blades do not stay out - you push the blade out with your thumb via a slider button on each cutter.

They have already been put to so much use at our house. Perfect for opening those tyvek envelopes, taped boxes, etc. We even keep some in the kitchen to open plastic food packages.

There is a small hole on one end, where you can easily slip some thin ribbon or twine in there to hang up the cutter.

Overall, much more useful than I had actually expected. We use them daily.

title: Always the best markers
text:
I love Sharpies, just like so many others do. They are getting a little high in cost, especially my very favorite, the click-tops.

But packages like these allow us to have Sharpies in every room in the house, ready to go. I especially use them in the kitchen, as they work very well to mark mylar storage bags.

title: Great to have on hand
text:
Maybe I am weird (hush now! Ha!), but I really like having all sizes of rubber bands around the house. From big to small, there's always a good use for them.

This item is a pack of large, narrow rubber bands. These are NOT wide ones, just long ones. They come in four colors: red, blue, green and yellow. You could possibly use color coding for items you want to roll up. Maybe tarps, sleeping bags, old picnic cloths, etc.

These will be very useful around the house. Whether it is keeping a roll of trash bags under control, keeping a trash bag from sliding down into the can, or just keeping like items together, these large bands will be useful.

Go ahead and get some. You know you want to, or you wouldn't be reading this review. 😉

title: Great tape
text:
This tape is really great to have on hand!
It is strong, clear and easy to use. It doesn't leave marks on things that I've tried it on. When removing, you need to be very careful when dealing with a painted surface though - the adhesive is strong.

This has been helpful to hold things on the walls, act like quake putty, and even keeps rugs from slipping.

I would definitely buy this again.

title: Great to have on hand
text:
This is a great quantity of automatic pencils. They are recycled, which supposedly makes them awesome. But they are just auto pencil sticks.

When I worked in accounting, this skinny type of auto pencil would have driven me nuts. The lead feels a bit shaky, but it wrote just fine. The lead is also very soft, so gets used up quickly.

This a just fine to have around the house or to use for school. You get quite a few for the price, so they are a decent value.

title: A must-have around the house
text:
This tape is really great. I appreciate the two different widths of the rolls.

I have used this tape to hold rug corners on to carpeting. We've also used it to hold up posters and holiday decorations. So far, we've only had one time where it peeled off paint, and that was when my daughter tried to just tug the decoration down, instead of carefully peeling the tape off.

Overall, this is very useful stuff. Everyone needs at least one roll around the house.

title: No monthly photos, just a cover pic
text:
When I got this, I had thought there would be artwork on every page, but that is not the case. It is spiral bound, so you can easily flip to the next month.

There is plenty of space to write things for most people. It also comes with two sheets of occasion stickers to mark birthdays, appointments, etc.

You can choose to hang this up as the entire length of the calendar, or use the hanging wire to only show the current month.

Overall, I would not buy this calendar again. I prefer the option to see a nice picture, but it is only on the cover of this one.

title: It WORKS!  Not as frustrating as others
text:
We have used a LOT of different tape guns over the years. We've bought some just for moving, and bought others for shipping packages from our former home business.

This dispenser wins Dispenser Wars!

It was very easy to use. We did not have to fight with it all the time, which was a pleasure.

With so many dispensers, the tape slides off all the time, or won't cut right, making it annoying to use.

This tape gun also has a safety guard over its very sharp teeth. (Just tuck the guard in your pocket while you are using the tape gun so you don't lose it.) It came with a roll of clear box tape as well.

We only had the tape slide over a couple times with several boxes vs almost each pass with our other tape guns.

Overall, we are very happy with this one. Should we need more at some future point, we'll be back to buy THIS one - a lot less frustrating!

title: Pretty thin, but works just fine for recipe folder
text:
You get a box of 100 protectors.
These are somewhat thin, not super heavy-duty, but they get the job done.

I used these to organize recipes I had printed out from various sources, and put them in binders. I only have a few empty protectors left. They worked great, and I'd say they could hold up to four or five sheets each, should you need to.

I have used heavier page protectors to set up warranty sheets, to keep booklets and receipts together. I think this would be a little thin for that, but they were perfect for my recipe sheets.

title: Works just fine
text:
I changed out my filing system from hanging folders (I no longer have as much paperwork with which to deal) to plastic envelopes and these file pockets.

The pockets are easy to just slide stuff into that might be bulky. As an example, I have one full of photos I've found as we have unpacked mystery boxes.

They are also handy for keeping shipping labels together, as well as mailing forms.
No problems so far with these file pockets.

title: Well made, does a great job
text:
We had a few manual sharpeners, but as arthritis has reared its ugly head, not having to do wrist-twisting is very attractive.

This is a well-made sharpener with plenty of space that holds shavings. We've used it for regular graphite pencils, as well as colored pencils without problem. It actually sharpens the pencils, not chewing them up.

This has been a very helpful addition to our home office.

title: Works great
text:
I am one of those people who don't think you can have too many binder clips or paper clips.

That being said, you get a generous amount of small binder clips in pastel shades of yellow, pink, blue and green.

They have all worked well and seem to be well-made.

title: Cute assortment
text:
These are very cute. You get shamrocks in three shades of green.
They are perfect for decorating packages or envelopes.

title: Sadness...no green ones! Soft, squishy pencil grips
text:
I wanted to try these out to see if they might help my hubby, who had a stroke a couple years ago. I thought they might give him a better grip. I'll update on that when I can get some up to him.

If you were around in the 90's, these are like mini koosh balls. You need to slide them on to your pen or pencil kinda like putting on panty hose.

The photos in the listing show a bright green, but we didn't get even one green one. Our mix was dark gray, orange, pink, blue and a few yellow. So, not as colorful as we had expected.

It is actually pretty comfortable on my pen. It also keeps it from rolling away. But one warning... it picks up pet hair and fuzz!

title: Works very well
text:
I have long wanted one of those rollers that blots out personal information. I ended up getting a shredder instead.

So when I had the chance to try this, I jumped on board. What I did not realize is that this is not one of those rollers that is a random grouping of letters and symbols. This actually spells out "CONFIDENTIAL", both one big word and lines of repeating phrase. If you run this a few times in slightly different positions, it does a pretty good job of covering information.

It comes in its own plastic case, and is self-inking. No need for a stamp pad, which is the best thing about it.

title: Nice case, lots of room, very handy
text:
I have ended up liking this case a lot more than I expected to. I don't currently have a much-needed desk. This case has allowed me to keep my address book and steno note pads in one quick-grab case, all zipped up together.

An additional benefit for me is the handle. I have to use a grabber much of the time (ok, nearly ALL the time). Not a big deal, except I could never get my address book. It has a slick hard plastic cover and I could never get the grabber to pick it up. Now that everything is zipped into this case, I can easily grab it by the handle and take care of business. I would buy another one of these if there were more color options.

title: Just lovely.  Nice appearance
text:
I use poly mailers for some of my handmade items. I like to have a variety of sizes on hand, but larger ones can be folded over and sealed easily.

These bags are very nice looking. I normally use plain, solid-colored bags, but cannot deny the visual appeal of these. I love the black and gold combo, as well as the tone of the gold used.
I would definitely buy these again.

title: Sturdy, but not very wide
text:
Sorter folders are nearly always useful. These folders are a little less wide than I prefer, but they will still work ok.

The plastic is stiff and a little sharp, so be careful. But these would work well to keep receipts for tax time.

title: Very squishy and comfy
text:
This is a very nice chair pad.

I am always on the lookout for a comfortable chair pad, as I have severe OA in both hips, and sitting can be miserable. My husband is in a wheelchair full time now and between the two of us, we need all the chair padding we can get!

title: Nice looking set
text:
We all need pads for our desks/tables for our mice. The wrist guard is an extra nice thing to have. As someone who worked in front of a screen for a couple of decades, I wish something like these existed then. It is actually pretty hard on your wrists to have them on a hard surface all the time.

Anyway, this is a beautiful set. I've always had plain, generic-looking mouse pads and wrist pads. I have the black/white/gold marbled-looking set. I love them. So nice looking, while doing exactly what you need them to do...cushion your wrists and give your mouse a smooth surface.
Great set.

title: Get these!  So cute
text:
These are adorable stickers! I wasn't sure exactly how big they would be.
I used these as stickers on lollipops, but they are the perfect size to go on the bottoms of foil-wrapped chocolate kisses. You get two full sheets, so plenty for most uses. I did four bags of lollipops and had nearly five full strips left.

Great item, and I'd buy them again.

title: Really cute
text:
If you need to wear a badge or ID card every day, these retractable badge holders are very helpful. I used them for many years, but the only options used to be plain colors.

This is adorable. If you need this item, you might as well have fun too. Very cute.

title: They work great. Sturdy enough for most uses
text:
These are basic sheet protectors that will hold American standard sized printer paper (8.5"x11").

There are holes punched down one side to easily keep these in binders.
I like to use these to keep warranties, receipts and/or direction books for household purchases. If something breaks down, it makes it a quick search to find original purchase information and warranty dates.

title: Big cellophane envelopes with air hole punched in them. Weird
text:
Ok, I need to check out the details on another page. The page I see didn't have enough info.

These looked like cellophane envelopes in the size of a sheet of paper. Nope...that is the envelope folded in half. They are twice that big.

Ok. I can deal with that. I wanted these to put handmade fabric items in to keep them dust-free and clean until they are gifted or sold. I can fold envelopes over. BUT...these have a hole punched in them! No idea what purpose that is supposed to serve. However, it doesn't help MY purpose of keeping an item clean and dust-free!

These have a strip of adhesive on the open end to close them. But the hole makes these pretty much useless.

title: All three sections are ONE unit
text:
When I saw this, I thought it was three separate magazine holders. I had some craft magazines to corral, so gave this a try.

First off, know this is thin plastic. If you are hard on items or plan to cram a lot of magazines into them, don't bother.

The biggest surprise to me, once I opened them up, was finding out that these three dividers are just ONE piece. Why does that matter? If you planned on putting one or two of these on a shelf, you need to plan for all three in the same spot. I had to rearrange my bookcase to accomodate the size.

The pieces slide together. You'll need to be able to push hard, and follow the exact order on the directions.

Overall, it is a little extra storage space, but definitely not what I had expected at first. The stiffness and connection to each other has also made it a little harder to get magazines back out. If you have materials/mags you need to keep organized, but don't need to access much, this would work very well for you.

title: Beautiful stickers
text:
These are beautiful stickers!
I occasionally sell handmade items online, and I like to put thank-you stickers on the packages. These look great and really catch the light.

Perfect size and great looking. You can't really go wrong with these.

title: Six-star cushion set!
text:
This is an absolutely beautiful pad set. I was impressed by the quality of all the materials used, from the fabric to the buckles, to the pads.

You get a strong chair back pad, perfect for an office chair. The curve is great, the fabric is great and the adjustment buckles are strong. One odd thing was that the chair pad has a pocket to hold your phone on the left side. When in use, it would be incredibly awkward to put your phone in there - just unhinge your elbow and slide that phone in!

Other than that, this is without a doubt the nicest chair pad set I've tried. Very pleased with everything.

title: Not a wide enough core, but did a decent job
text:
I wasn't sure what to think about these. We use a lot of box tape. I have a metal desk dispenser, but I need one I can walk around with also. We have a handheld metal one, but it is awkward and kind of annoying - the tape tends to fold in about 1/8" on one side, no matter what we do.

These work much better than I had actually expected. They are all plastic but the steel cutting strip, which actually works well.

My only complaint is that these have a core that is too narrow. I always use 2" wide box tape. As you can see in my photos, the 2" tape hangs over the molded ring, so the roll slips around too much. If they'd widen the core, it would be much better.

title: Excellent for gift giving, bake sales or farmer's markets
text:
My husband is in a nursing home. I like to send in homemade treats from time to time. One request is a fruit-topped cheesecake pie.

These stickers are PERFECT for sealing the plastic pie-shaped containers shut (they don't seem to stay shut on their own).

I thought it was a roll of varied designs, but there are actually only two designs; one red and one black. That is perfectly fine...they do the job, and are just right to put on homemade treats. These would also be great to use for bake sales and/or flea market sales.

title: I don't see this one working very well
text:
Well, I am not sure how this is going to be 100% fireproof.

It is nice and thick, like an oily neoprene. It has a sturdy zipper as well. It looks to have enough room for most important papers.

However, I just don't see how this bag is anything but maybe fire retardant, not fireproof. There is a small opening at the end of the zipper. Fire wouldn't just stop because it should...it looks to me like it could pass right on into the bag at the zipper opening.

If you have super important papers, they should be in a safety deposit box at your bank, not in a cheapie bag at your home.

This is just my opinion on this bag. I am not going to set a fire to test it, so you'll have to draw your own conclusions as to whether you want to trust this bag or not. For me, it's a no.

title: Great tape, narrower roll
text:
Nano tape has to be one of my favorite things of 2020. This stuff is great.

This particular roll is not as wide as previous rolls I've tried, but that is just fine. Note that you should not underestimate the strength of this tape. It is STRONG. You don't need big pieces of it for most things either. (I used a piece about the length of a AA battery to hold up a battery box on a string of lights...when we took the lights down, it tore up the drywall. Be sure to use a hair dryer on the tape a little bit before trying to remove it.)

Great product and I recommend it.

title: They worked great. Convenient to have two colors in one pen.
text:
When I chose these, I thought they were just regular yellow highlighters. It was a pleasant surprise to discover that each highlighter is both yellow AND pink.

These fit comfortably in your hands. The highlighters worked well on the label without smearing anything.

Overall, these are really nice highlighters. Wish I'd had these back in college!

title: I love this stuff. Very versatile
text:
I don't know who invented this stuff, but good for them!

This "nano tape" is super useful all over the house. We've used it to keep an extra rug from sliding on a carpeted area, to put a poster on a wall, and to put up various autumn decorations. We currently rent, so want to take care of the place and not leave a lot of holes in the walls.

This stuff is sticky on both sides, but easy to remove. They claim to be reusable by just rinsing it off, but I haven't tried that yet.

I hope everyone tries at least one roll of nano tape. Great stuff!

title: They work just fine
text: I was a bit surprized to receive these folders just dumped in a cardboard box. They do not come in a regular office supply type of box. That being said, they seem to work just fine with my vame-brand hanging file frames inside my file cabinet.

title: Very runny, I don't trust them
text:
[[VIDEOID:647f30f7d16bdd37c5edf76b8b928338]] I don't know about others, but I don't buy home printers very often. I buy the best I can afford, and use them until they are worn out.

A couple years ago, I bought a very expensive Canon home inkjet printer. I use it to print patterns, as well as correspondence or shipping labels. It is no secret that ink costs a fortune. Most cartridges have dense sponges in them, which helps control the release of the ink so it does not spot on your printing project.

When I saw generic cartridges for my printer, I thought I'd see what the quality was like. I have to say, I was disappointed. While the sizing looks to be spot-on, there is only a tiny piece of sponge in these, and mostly liquid with the viscosity of water. It looks like water with food coloring in it. Yuck.

If you have a very old printer that you don't care about, these will probably work ok for that. With newer printers, you can actually void your warranty by using off-brand ink cartridges in them. Mine is likely out of the warranty period. I am choosing to NOT put these in my machine, as I can't afford to replace a printer right now. I truly do not trust what looks to be colored water not just running throughout the printer. Sorry, I can't recommend these.

title: Nice quality. Great for general purpose thank you notes
text:
There is a lost art of sending thank you notes. Too many people think texting "tks" is enough. Nothing beats a hand-written thank you note!

Whether someone has gifted you, done a kindness, or even a follow-up for a job interview, a written thank you note is wonderful to receive.

This box has a nice assortment of generically useful notes. All have the same very basic font, but the color variety is really nice. I look forward to sending some people notes, and making their day.

title: Very nice. Love it!
text:
This roll of tape is very thick and totally clear. It is wider than most of the other rolls, so it helps with wider or larger items you might want to use it on. You just cut what you need, attach, then stick the other side to your other surface. Super easy. This tape is also supposed to be reusable by just rinsing it off with water.

I haven't tried it on anything heavier than a poster yet, but it certainly waa perfect for that. We currently rent, so anything that doesn't damage the wall or door surface is a plus.

I am very glad we had the opportunity to give this tape a try. I'd definitely buy this again.

title: Really nice alternative to hang posters or lightweight items
text:
I had never used this type of tape before, but had seen it advertised on tv. I have to say, this surprised me.

The tape is very thick and totally clear. You just cut what you need, attach, then stick the other side to your other surface. Super easy. This tape is also supposed to be reusable by just rinsing it off with water.

I haven't tried it on anything heavier than a poster yet, but it certainly waa perfect for that. We currently rent, so anything that doesn't damage the wall or door surface is a plus. Very glad we had the opportunity to give this tape a try. I'd definitely buy this again.

title: HARD PASS on these cheap envelopes
text:
Wow.
I use poly envelopes often. They are great for keeping paperwork organized. I decided to try this set.

Well, I can say HARD PASS on these.
The first and biggest reason is that these are shipped folded up into thirds instead of just laying flat like normal envelopes! Yup, they were packaged by the manufacturer all folded into thirds width-wise. Crazy! They don't look like they'll take much pressure of a lot of papers either. These are apparently the cheapest of the cheap. But I am just amazed that the company decided folding these up in thirds instead of putting them flat in a envelope to ship flat. Grrrrrr. (A month later, and none have uncurled. It is crazy.)

So, you get a lot of poly envelopes for the price, but every single one is bent in two places. I have no words for how annoying this is. I recommend you shop elsewhere and avoid these.

title: Cheaply made, way too thin, no give
text:
Nope.
Hard pass.

I thought this looked sturdy enough to put files into. Nope. This was so disappointing.
It has the approximate thickness of the cardboard of a cereal box. It has a strange, fuzzy texture to it that wasn't pleasant.

It also has NO give at all, so if you try to put too much into it, it will just rip.

This one looks much nicer than it actually is. I really can't think of hardly anything this would be truly useful for, and cannot recommend it.

title: Worked great in my Canon inkjet printer
text:
I've used a lot of different brands of shipping labels over the years. Some are so thin, you just hope you'll be able to peel it off the backing without tearing.

Well, these shipping labels are not like that. There is enough "heft" to them that I have no worries about problems getting them from the sheet to the package.
They come two labels per sheet, 100 sheets per box. This means to extend your label count to 200, you need to set your shipping label to NOT print the receipt. If you do not, the receipt will take up the second label.

I ran a sheet through my inkjet Canon printer with no problems at all. I normally only put one label sheet in at a time though, to avoid inkjet jams. I cannot vouch for the ability to put in several sheets and do consecutive label printing without jams.

I also like that the entire back has text printed on it. Some labels are very thin, the backing plain, and printing in the wee hours of the morning can sometimes mean you printed on tue back of the label sheet! Ha! (Or am I the only one who has done that?! 😄)

In summary, nice quality, nice labels, zero problems with my inkjet printer, happy with this brand.

title: Cheaply made, ok for rare use, not ok for lots of use
text:
I bought two of these, because we will be moving soon, and I didn't want to put my tape dispenser around. I thought these would be easy to work with and save time.

I was wrong.
We've spent a LOT of time re-aligning the tape, as it shifts and moved every time you use it. The little metal guide that is supposed to hold the tape in place does very little.

We thought at first it was the cheapie roll of tape that comes with it. But nope...same results with the more expensive box tape as well.

If you have a lot of boxes to tape, save yourself a headache and get a more heavy-duty tape gun. If you only rarely need box tape, then this might suit your purposes.

But for now, we are muttering aloud every time we use these. The tape twists, gets stuck to itself or the dispenser, and is generally annoying to use.

title: Would not change a thing. Great function, design and appearance
text:
This was my first experience with the PraxxisPro brand. I needed an additional upright hand stapler for my home office, so came to my favorite online shopping place to find one.

I was drawn to the copper metallic appearance, which would go nicely with my metallic gold printer. The black base and copper metallic structure is a great combo. Good job designers!

Now to the more important parts - actual function and ergonomic feel.

I don't have super strong hands, and wear a medium glove, so I didn't want something that would take a lot of muscle to use. This stapler fills the bill.

While it was heavier than expected (and I worried it would grow hard to use), that has turned out to be just fine. The stapler sits up perfectly balanced on my desk. It is easy to grab, and stapling is very smooth. I've been using it for a while now and not had any jams or problems. I haven't tested how many layers it can go through. The majority of my stapling needs at home are pretty basic.

Overall, the function has been perfect, it feels great in my hand, has a small desk footprint and looks great. I would definitely recommend this handsome stapler.

title: ULTRA FINE POINT... more like a ball point pen
text:
Sharpies are awesome.
We all know it and love them.

After marking our hands trying to get the caps off the wide black sharpies nearly every time we use them, I decided to grab a box of clickable sharpies (retractable). They are so much nicer to use, even though they don't last as long.

What I overlooked was the word "ultra" as in ultra fine. These are NOT the regular sharpies, but more like a ball point pen.

Now, I use the ultra fine sharpies in crafting. I bought those by the box too. But these retractables will be replacing those too. I have trouble with some of my knuckles (cysts from repetitive motion) bending and they definitely do NOT like getting the caps off regular sharpie pens.

So, this was a very happy accident.
Just note the "ultra fine" before purchasing.

title: Great deal for pen losers like me
text:
Since everyone at our house uses capacitor pens on their phones, this was a good value.
I wasn't sure what we would truly get, but we received 103 pens, mostly three or four designs. But not worried about the designs. (They need me to help proof their setups!)

Since we all lose our pens or have outright killed the touch tips, it is great to have plenty on hand.
The pens have all worked, both the tips and as ink pens.

Great value, happy with the seller and the product.

title: Crisp lines, great photo contrast
text:
This is a really nice ink.
While this is our first Canon printer (used to be a loyal HP fan, but since they are not loyal to me, and no longer care about the quality of their products, I have moved on), I can definitely say we get much crisper prints from the Canon.

The pigment ink is the main one used for documents.
However, it also adds a really nice sharpness to photographs as well.

All thumbs up!

title: I really like the Canon inks - bright, true to color and makes great prints
text:
We recently bought a new printer and changed brands from our decades-long HP loyalty
(which was never reciprocated) to a new Canon wireless printer.

The new printer takes the 271 Canon cartridges. They are super easy to pop in.
I LOVE that you don't have to print out a new page every time you replace the ink,
which always wastes a lot of ink.

The photos from these inks is spectacular - you would never know they were off a home printer.
They are bright and color steady. Very happy with them.
They do get used a little faster than I'd like, so if you can, replace any original cartridges
with the XL size. I am not sure about the difference in the amount of ink, since the cartridges are solid black.
(Why won't manufacturers just make them clear so we can actually SEE the ink that's left?)

Anyway, a little costly, but I lovelove my Canon products. Glad I changed brands.
No regrets!

title: Very useful... great for recipe pages
text:
I am putting together my own cookbook of recipes for our low carb dietary changes.
I needed something that I could tuck one or two recipes into without getting them
dirty (I print out sheets on the printer). This fits the bill with a budget in mind.
I would have preferred side loaders so they would not slide out if I dropped the notebook,
but for the price difference, these were a great alternative!

They do the job just fine, and I am glad I bought them.

title: What's not to love about a dozen Post-It note pads?  Nothing!
text:
There is not a whole lot to say about Post-It notes.
If you have not used them before, you should. Buy these now!

If you have, you know how nice it is to have plenty of these around.
I buy them by the 12-pack. I pull apart one pad, then cut that in half.
I then stick them inside each of my cookbooks, so I always have a way
to flag a recipe I come across that I want to try. I just stick them inside
the front cover, and always have one at hand.

Decent price (esp if you don't have any supply stores in your area and other places
are sold out!), quick delivery.

title: Sturdy, strong, worth the cost
text:
Well, these notebooks are mixed blessings.

They are kind of heavy.
There are five tabs separating the section, There is a decent paper supply in each section.
The tabs can be taken out and moved if you need to.

This is very sturdy and unlikely to fall apart.
The weight could be an issue for some kids, but college age or for those taking online classes who don't have to lug it all over campus in a backpack, it is a great way to stay organized.
Very nice quality.

title: Not new colors, just repackaged already-available colors
text:
I love Sharpies and have more of them than normal folks would have! LOL
But, these were pretty much a waste. No actual new colors - they are just repackaged
in a way to look like they belong together.

Meh.

title: Quality pens at a reasonable price
text: These were purchased as a gift, but since the recipient was very specific in wanting this particular pen set, I'd say they are the best for the job!

title: Does the job well - aids in grip and keeps pencils/pens from rolling away
text:
Got a pack of these to help me hold pencils.
I have knuckle cysts on three of my fingers (I thought it was arthritis, but it wasn't).
Nothing that can be done about them, but these help me hold on to thin pens or pencils,
and keeps them from rolling off the table.

title: Canon has a fan - and the gray ink is GREAT
text:
We've had many brands of printers over the years, with most being HP, with their tri-color cartridges. It always was frustrating to have to replace an entire cartridge when only one color had run out.

This is my first time having a Canon printer, and I have to say that I like having all the colors separate so the color cartridges can be replaced as needed. They are a little pricey, but so far, very happy with them.
I am especially impressed with the GRAY ink, which truly gives a lot of clarity and depth to full color printing.
I bought the Canon both for the wireless connection and for the detail in the printing, as I plan to use it more and more for crafting purposes.

title: Canon has a new fan here
text:
This is my first time having a Canon printer, and I have to say that I like having all the colors separate so the color cartridges can be replaced as needed, rather than replacing a tri-color cartridge when only one color is empty. They are a little pricey, but so far, very happy with them.

We've had several other brands of printers, and three different HP printers. I hated the waste of the HP test pages that printed out in color every time you replaced a cartridge, as it used a lot of ink, and often would repeat itself 2 or 3 times. I also like separate color cartridges.
Well done Canon - you've won me over.

title: Glad to be able to replace one color at a time
text:
I've had Epson, Brother and HP printers. We recently got a Canon wireless printer.
This is my first time having a Canon printer, and I have to say that I like having all the colors separate so the color cartridges can be replaced as needed, rather than replacing a tri-color cartridge when only one color is empty. They are a little pricey, but so far, very happy with them.

title: Happy with Canon
text: This is my first time having a Canon printer, and I have to say that I like having all the colors separate so the color cartridges can be replaced as needed, rather than replacing a tri-color cartridge when only one color is empty.  They are a little pricey, but so far, very happy with them.

title: Quality tabs, great product, looks very nice on Bibles
text:
I bought these to put into a gift Bible.
The tabs are beautiful, and the silver edge perfect for blue toned Bibles.

They do take a while to do well... it took me an hour and a half to get all the tabs placed properly,
but I'm a little anal-retentive and made extra sure everything was lined up just right. They do come with
a tab template, but I preferred to set them up in my own spacing. Once you get the first 8 tabs, lining up
the rest is fairly simple. You just need to be very careful to only have one Bible page, not two - most are so
thin, it is very easy to put the tabs onto two pages without knowing it.

Excellent product. Great quality.

title: Great little clamps for your fabric projects
text:
These were my first set of this type of clip for quilting and sewing.
They are small, but have a great grip. This will work best for smaller projects.
If you have a thicker quilt with batting that you want to keep clamped while you work on it,
you'll want another size with a deeper "throat" on them. I've already ordered a larger set and
love those too! The colors are translucent and cheerful, and the clamps powerful enough to do the job.

Well done URBest. I can recommend these to anyone who sews or quilts.

title: Excellent folder, nice quality, cheerful colors
text:
I was looking for something that was simple, containable and colorful to hold all my tax-related receipts during the year.
I do taxes for my entire family, so needed something I could keep separated for each one and each purpose, but in a small space.
This will do the trick!

I received it quickly, set it all up this morning and easily filed/separated the stack of papers and receipts that had already started piling up for this tax year. The dividers are pretty sturdy (and even if they rip from the sides, they'll still do the job I need). The folder is a GREAT color - I chose the green, and it is indeed a bright, cheerful apple green. The color is translucent, so you can easily put a sheet of paper in front of the first slot if you wanted to give a quick reference as to what was in it.

It has an elastic band to hold the folder closed.
There's nothing to dislike about this one - get it! Soon!

title: Great pen, cost effective and writes smoothly
text:
I think I have Conehead blood coursing through my veins... I love mass quantities of things, especially office supplies!

One of my favorite pens used to be the Bic Ultimates with the sparkling cases. They fit my hand well and wrote smoothly.
But for some heinous reason, Bic discontinued them. I was forced to look for a different pen in a sufficient quantity that I could
forget where I left them all over the house and still have one within quick reach when I wanted to make a note or list.
This fills the bill!

The pens are actually very nice, no goopiness, and write very smoothly.
I now keep them everywhere, with several all over my desk area for quick grasping.
(I am both a doodler and a rabid note-taker.)
Well done Bic!

title: Nice notes, they stick well, do their job, and most importantly, are indeed yellow  '-)
text:
There is not a lot I can say about self-sticking notes that hasn't already been said.

They are small, perfect for sticking quick notes on almost anything.
They are made of paper, a nice quality paper (even though they are a different brand than the "leader"),
and they stick well.

The quantity is nice as well, because I keep them all over the house, as well as lose them on my desktop.
(Usually, at least one pad can be found under my computer keyboard.)

Well done Highland.
And thank you to the sellers who offer them on Amazon for those of us who live in The Boonies and have no stores in the area that actually carry these.

title: Two stickers per page - no plain paper on this one.  Fine if you don't print receipts.
text:
The labels themselves are very nice quality. BUT - what I am looking for are pages that are half sticker and half regular paper.
I print the receipts for the mailing labels as many online venues only keep three monthsor 90 days of mailing records.
So, while they are nice labels, I am wasting half the sheet by having to print the receipt on the label part. Then you have to trim them down to fit most envelopes, and there is no place to catch your finger - you have to start them by prying until you can get a corner off. Not hard, but annoying nonetheless.

Not sure if I would buy them again. Yes, I could print half the label, then change out paper and print the receipt portion, but I was not trying to create hassles or a longer time to print. I wanted to save some time. These don't save me a thing.

title: Works great for long-term storage and keeping things organized
text:
These work very well for keeping ornery papers together in our file cabinet!

I love the poly folders. The paper ones seem to get overstuffed, things fall out, they get bent, etc. These, on the other hand, work really great.
This is about the fourth package of them I have purchased, and am easing over to color-coding the folders as well (all the green ones will be tax info, for example).
I highly recommend them - they expand to hold quite a bit, stand up to abuse pretty well, and are easier to open than zip-style bags that pop open.
Two thumbs up!

title: Great project folders - perfect for medical sorting and project organization.
text:
I used to use these in the office all the time. After a recent round of a lot of medical/doctor/hospital visits for my husband, I found myself wuickly being overwhelmed with the sheer quantity of the bills from the hospital, doctors, radiologists, labs, etc etc. They ALL bill separately for your part of the cost, and with Obamacare guidelines, there is no longer just one account for your name - every procedure has a new account number. I bought these to try to keep the bills, estimation of benefits, doctor bills, etc under control. Turned out that I needed HALF of this box just to have one folder per account set up by these various entities! Good grief. 13 different accounts for the treatment of the same medical problem! Yikes...

These have been invaluable to keeping up with the accounts without losing my sanity. I am also going to recommend them for my daughter to keep her projects separate for her college courses. Don't know why I didn't think about them sooner... I tend to associate these with office use only, but they are great for home and school as well. Love them!

title: Add this to your line of defense against cyber theft
text:
I am one of the better-safe-than-sorry crowd, so I bought these to house our credit/debit cards.
The papers are thin like Tyvek, with a metallic lining that allegedly bounces any pocket reader attempts
to lift card information without your knowledge.

They arrived promptly, and were put to use. If they protect us from even one theft, then it was worth the cost.

title: Expired
text: These are old and dry. Not even one marker I got worked as supposed to.

title: We are very please with the product. We have several.
text: We purchased these because our cats like to slam doors and get locked in a room. Then they meow until someone let's them out. We wanted door stops that would not cripple us if we stumbled on them. So far our 2 cats have not destroyed them so this is a very good thing. We are very please with the product. We have several.

title: Horrible constant jamming!!
text: This is by far the worst paper I have ever purchased. This paper does nothing but jam my printer. I have purchased a variety of printer paper brands off of Amazon, so much that I decided to buy this in bulk to save on so much ordering. This paper had great reviews, including ones about 0 jamming (a problem I’ve only encountered with shiny card stock until I bought this paper). It’s not thick it’s just so thin and cheap that my printer must be thrown off when it takes a sheet off of the stack. Horrible don’t waste your money. I have a HP printer with copier. The first jamming encounter I thought it was a fluke and I must have put too much in but nope 10 minutes later another jam. We are on three jams in 25 minutes. Worthless paper, do not buy!

title: It's convenient, inexpensive, and I LIKE IT!
text: In a world where everybody seems to depend on their phone's calendar program, I can open this three-year calendar, with a paper clip guaranteeing that I will open it to the correct month, and flipping pages gets me to the following months, a lot faster than turning on my phone and running my calendar program.

text: High quality fast-drying ink and crisp print and pictures!
