title: Paper Shredder.
text: I am thoroughly pleased with the shredder. Does what I needed it for.

title: comfortable
text: works great for my hard office chair.

title: Non-adhesive Tape
text: This tape is just as it says “noise free”. I knew you had to loose something in this deal. It seems they do this by leaving tiny air pockets all over the tap. It’s great for noise, but if your main goal with the tape is adhesion, pass this one up.

title: Perfect for my reorganized pantry ...
text:
I purchased these to use on some white wire baskets in my newly reorganized pantry. I'm of an age where I'm starting to forget what I have and/or where I put it, so having some kind of labeling system is needed to keep me from purchasing too many duplicate items.

I'm using some pre-printed adhesive labels that fit these perfectly, and so far, the system is working nicely. It comes with pens so you can write your own labels, but this way, I can change up the labels easily by just peeling off the old adhesive label and adding a new one.

They fit the baskets nicely, with no breakage so far, and the clip-ons plus the adhesive labels are large enough so that I can see what I have on hand. I'll try to post a photo to show how I'm using these, but overall, I'm quite happy with these.

title: Perfect to help organize my new kitchen storage unit …
text:
These fit perfectly in the drawers of the Adeptus 6-drawer roll cart. I use one of these solid wood carts in my kitchen for extra storage and needed something for flatware and some cooking utensils. These organizer bins work perfectly! They’re sturdy, great quality, and a good value. The interior drawer dimensions are about 12.5” deep x 17” wide, so 5 of these fit in one drawer (each bin is 3” wide).

I ended up ordering the wider version of these bins, too. Very happy with them!

title: Probably the best boxes available ...
text:
I recently moved from one apartment to another inside the same building. Should be too much of an ordeal, right? WRONG! It was a nightmare and at least as bad as my previous moves (cross country included!).

So in planning for the move, I decided I wanted to get some decent boxes that I could use after the move for storage -- I now have a spare bedroom that I intend to use to store craft supplies, etc. These are sturdy enough to withstand the actual transport of "stuff" from apt 1 to apt 2, and still look as good as new to handle my storage needs.

Easy to set up, the integrated handles and tapeless features are great! Made things a lot simpler.

Will purchase again if needed. 5 stars.

title: Good quality tags ...
text:
I use these in my card making. I like to make a bunch of cards of a particular design, then use these tags to add the sentiment ("thank you," "Thinking of You," "Happy Birthday," etc.) when I need to send one.

I use rubber stamps/ink to print the sentiment on the tag OR use foil sentiment stickers, then add a small ribbon bow and add it to my card. I love the design of these white tags -- not *too* fancy, but classy.

Will purchase again when needed.

title: I absolutely love these pens!
text:
My preference is for fine-point pens, and these definitely deliver. I purchased the "Assorted" option -- 8 different colors -- and couldn't be happier!

The colors are vibrant and the pens are really high quality for the price. I use them a lot for sketching and Thomas Pavitte's "1000 Dot-to-Dot" books (yes, those dot-to-dot puzzles that we loved as a child, all grown up in size and complexity).

The ink doesn't bleed through (at least it hasn't so far), and so far no skips.

Will happily purchase again if needed.

title: Does what it's supposed to do ...
text:
Super easy to assemble, even for an old lady with mobility issues.

I use two of these in my "kitchen." I live in an assisted living facility, so "kitchen" is a gross exaggeration -- I have a 2-burner electric cooktop, an 11"x11" sink, a decent-sized refrigerator, and a microwave oven -- no counter space at all, and only one small overhead cupboard. They fit under the counter and hold a lot of things that would normally be stowed in cabinets: small appliances like a countertop grill, measuring cups/spoons, pans that I use in my air fryer, etc.

I wouldn't store anything too heavy in this unit -- but it's sturdy enough to hold a couple of pounds of potatoes plus the assortment of cooking utensils and small pans/dishes.

Definitely worth the investment.

title: Used for clothing with no issues ...
text:
I live in an assisted living facility where laundry service is provided and I have to have everything marked with the resident's name and apartment #. I've been using these labels for about 6 weeks and so far no problems at all.

I followed the instruction to attach the labels to the care tag (usually in the side seam of my tops and pants), at least 24 hrs before washing. I've had some items washed 3 times since applying the labels, and so far, there's no sign of any issues at all. (My stuff is washed in cold water and dried on "delicate," so that may make a difference.)

I DON'T use these on dishes, mugs, water bottles, etc., so that may be a problem area (judging by the reviews so far). But for clothing, they work just fine.

Shipping was quick with these as well.

Really, no complaints at all. They're working as advertised.

title: Very pretty, good quality ...
text:
I belong to a women's organization that uses the daisy (marguerite) as one of its emblems. I like having blank cards featuring daisies on hand that I can send as get-well cards, thank yous, "thinking of you," etc.

These are quite nice -- excellent quality, a good value for the price. Will order more as needed.

title: Great for "thinking of you"-type cards ...
text:
Although the product title calls these "sympathy" cards, they are absolutely appropriate for "thinking of you" sentiments. That's why I purchased them!

Because of the pandemic, I have a lot of friends whom I haven't seen in person for a long time. I like to send cards just as a day-brightener -- just to let folks know that they're on my mind. I used to make my own cards, but my dexterity has deteriorated over the years, so I looked for a set of cards that would be appropriate.

These really are perfect. I love the floral designs -- not too fancy, not too formal, more "down home" feel. And the touch of gold is just right -- not too much that it's overbearing, styled more casual in terms of font/etc.

The cards are blank inside so I can pen my own personalized greeting. The envelopes are lined (!) to match the overall floral pattern. And the stickers match the color scheme, too.

These are perfect for my needs -- no issues at all with quality, size, or anything. Would gladly purchase again if needed.

title: Very nice set of cards + box ...
text:
I used to make most of my greeting cards by hand but I'm at an age where my dexterity is faltering. I still wanted nice dimensional cards, though -- something a little nicer than the typical plain "flat" cards.

I grew up in Kansas City, MO, so I've been familiar with Hallmark Cards for decades (my uncle worked there as an artist for several years). I hadn't realized that they were making dimensional cards until I started looking on Amazon for a set of nice cards to have on hand.

I'm really blown away. These cards are beautiful! There are a lot of birthday cards -- at least half of the cards, I'd say. But there are nice cards for sympathy, wedding, "just because," etc. Each card is packaged in a cellophane sleeve -- a nice touch to keep the dimensional add-ons safe and pristine.

The box includes dividers and is large enough to hold a LOT of cards. It's also quite sturdy so I'm not worried about durability.

Very happy with my purchase. Hallmark comes through -- excellent quality all around.

title: Great for marking laundry …
text:
I had some health issues that landed me in an assisted living facility years before I thought I would need that level of care, but here I am. One of the perks is having my laundry done each week. We’re asked to label our clothing items, so I ordered a set of these just over a year ago. I was so happy with their performance that I just ordered another set.

They’re easy to apply, and so far, they’re staying on after dozens of washing. Printing hasn’t faded, either. Couldn’t ask for more. Nice product.

title: Good all-round high-quality printer paper ...
text: I've been using this Hammermill 24-lb inkjet printer paper forever, it seems like.  It's my favorite for just about everything.  The heavier weight and bright white make it great for any printing, from casual letters or notes to more formal reports and newsletters.  The price is consistent with local prices, too.  Will continue purchasing and using this paper as long as it's available.

title: Rubber grip is great -- so is the pen ...
text:
Imagine finding a super-fine point Uniball pen in nice pastel colors AND with a rubber grip! I've used Uniball pens for years, and when I saw this ultra-fine point version, I had to give it a try.

It's the typical Uniball high quality just with a finer point. The rubber grip is a big help for my hands -- I have arthritis that has gotten significantly worse over time, so I need some extra cushioning. The colors are fresh and a nice change from the typical black (yes, I have a set of these in black, too).

Overall, very happy with these. No issues at all. Will definitely purchase again when needed.

title: Nice and colorful ...
text: Not too much to say -- they're good binder clips, sturdy, nice size, good colors.  Quality is good -- the color isn't going to flake off, and since I like to color-code my projects/papers, the selection of colors is good.  Very happy with these.  Will purchase more of this brand if needed in the future.

title: Great for small kitchens ...
text:
I purchased two of these in navy blue to use in my kitchen to hold utensils that I use often.

I live in an "assisted living" facility, and the apartments have what is euphemistically referred to as a "kitchenette": 2-burner electric cooktop flanked by a small 11" x 11" square sink and a surprisingly decent sized refrigerator topped with a microwave. No counter space at all. I purchased a buffet server with a counter-height top that I use for counter space positioned about 4' parallel to the cooktop area. It also provides additional storage for cookware and small appliances.

Because of my health issues, I have to do any cooking seated, so having my most-used cooking utensils close at hand is critical. I have my two blue organizers on the refrigerator door right by the cooktop, so I can reach my spatula, tongs, pancake turner, whisk, etc. easily. So far, it's working just fine.

I may order another one of these to mount on the side of my toaster oven (a new acquisition -- you can do only so much with two burners and a microwave oven) to hold my cooking thermometer and other useful items.

No issues at all with the magnet -- it seems to be glued strongly to the back and adheres strongly to my fridge door. It's not very big which is why I purchased two, but the look is what I wanted and the color is perfect (my kitchen colors are navy blue and yellow with pops of orange).

Overall, very happy with this item.

title: Perfect for my drill containers...
text:
I’m relatively new to diamond painting, but I'm learning a lot about how to work efficiently and stay organized. Getting my drills organized at the beginning of a project is important, and for me that means getting them out of the little cellophane bags and into my storage system. These labels are the perfect size for my Harbor Freight containers, and I can remove them when I’m finished and ready to move on to the next project. I used fine-point markers to record the number and the DMC code when available.

You get a LOT of these so they’ll last a good long time. Very happy with them.

title: Just what I needed ...
text:
I'm living primarily "paperless" these days -- but there are always a few things that are available only in paper form that I need to keep "just in case," so some sort of a file system is necessary. Because there aren't that many documents involved here, I didn't want to invest in the whole "filing cabinet with dividers and file folders" set-up. I just needed something small that I could tuck away on a shelf in the closet.

After looking at a lot of options (a LOT of options), I settled on this one due to size (perfect) and appearance (I liked the pattern and colors).

It's perfect for my use. I'm using a few hanging folders to hold papers by subject, and regular file folders within the hanging folders to separate sources/etc (e.g., MEDICAL hanging folder subdivided into "Insurance," "Doctor Notices," etc.).

No issues at all -- everything fits perfectly, and I can store it as planned -- on a shelf in the closet.

Would gladly purchase another if I find I need more storage.

title: Easy to do, very nice designs
text: Very pretty and easy to do!  I wanted to try a small project before trying a larger picture.  Each of these designs took between 2-3 hours to make. You get everything in the package you need to complete the bookmarks.  I got into a sort of rhythm with placing the gems on the design, so it seemed to go much faster.  These will make great gifts.

title: Nice size --
text:
I got these to take on a cruise so I'd have a way to leave notes on my door or in my cabin. They're a good size, so I had plenty of room to write quite a lot (instructions to cabin attendants, for example), and they did a good job of staying "stuck" to the door when I needed to leave a note for visitors ("I'm in the Mariner Lounge -- see you there!").

The colors are vibrant -- neon bright. Quite happy with these.

title: No issues at all -- nice quality ...
text: I like to use card blanks for my handcrafted greeting cards since I tend to use white or cream as my background and then layer colors on that.  These are really quite nice -- a tad pricey, but good quality overall.  I read some of the earlier reviews and was a little apprehensive, but so far, I'm seeing no issues at all.  They're a nice weight -- not at all flimsy, but sufficient to support several layers of cardstock and embellishments.  Will purchase these again when needed.

title: Nice little ruler for card makers ...
text:
I make hand-crafted greeting cards and like to have a small ruler in my toolbox. Six inches works great as the cards I make are almost always 4.25" x 5.5". I had an earlier version of this same ruler that got misplaced while on vacation a few months ago. I'd had it for almost 8 years, so that speaks to the quality.

This new version is slightly narrower, but otherwise basically the same as my old one. It's still easy to read and the thin cork backing provides some security as the ruler doesn't shift around while scoring or trimming. Good price, too. Compact size, durability, accuracy -- all add up to a 5 star reaction.

title: WAY better than I thought it would be ...
text:
Well, color me impressed. The design is simple but it really works. The size is wonderful -- big enough to handle my 13" MacBook Air very comfortably. I got this to use both in the living room when sitting on the sofa as well as in the bedroom when I put my feet up to relax before bedtime. I also use it for some of my crafts activities -- the size is big enough to handle my 12" x 18" craft mat (I make handcrafted greeting cards and use various sharp things in conjunction with that activity). I can also use my 12" paper cutter easily, so it's almost perfect.

I say "almost" because, as others have noted, the surface is slick. My laptop is in a hardshell case that has rubber feet so that's not a problem, but the slick surface doesn't work that well with my crafty things. I ended up getting a set of 3 large "rubber bands" -- they were intended to be used on trash cans to hold the plastic trash bags from slipping down into the can. They were the perfect size and work great. Problem solved!

Definitely worth the less-than thirteen dollars I paid for it -- a great bargain!

title: Beautiful and classy ...
text: Very pretty cards, classy without being pretentious.  The off white background sets off the copper metallic design. Beautiful as is, but can be “dressed up” a bit with added metallic thread, mini sequins, etc.  Perfect for special folks.

title: Easy to keep travel docs organized ...
text:
I use a lot of these when I travel to keep my travel documents organized. I've been doing a lot of cruise travel lately which usually means flying to the embarkation port or from the disembarkation port, pre- and post-cruise hotel stays, plus numerous ports, onboard pre-purchased wine packages and dinners, etc. A LOT of stuff to keep track of.

I carry a 1" 3-ring binder with sheet protectors to hold the various reservations/documents and use sets of dividers to keep things in order and easy to "flip to" when needed. Each port of call has its own "section," pre- and post-cruise activities are in their own sections, etc. That means I'm using them over and over during a cruise (I do longer cruises, 28+ days). I use a label maker to produce customized removable labels for each cruise.

These dividers are perfect for my use. They're extremely sturdy, attractive, and the tabs are large enough to use printing that's big enough to read easily on the labels. At the end of a trip, I just remove the labels and set it up for my next trip.

These are cost-effective, too -- excellent quality for the price. Solid 5 stars!

title: Lots of paper clips ..
text:
A nice bunch of paper clips here. No, I didn't count them, but the container is fairly large and it's packed. There are three sizes -- the smaller two sizes are very similar (maybe 1/8" difference), but the large ones are definitely larger. They seem to be nice quality, too. The container has dividers that seem to keep them organized.

I go through a lot of these -- I'm my homeowners association treasurer and have to produce paperwork that can't be stapled for various reasons, so paper clips are the best alternative. These will last a good long time. No issues, really.

title: Classy looking name tags ...
text:
I purchased these to use as name tags for an evening social event at a local yacht club, paired with gold metallic markers for folks to use to write their names. They were a big hit -- very classy looking, suitable for men and women. More importantly, they stayed "stuck" (I've had some name tags that simply won't stay stuck -- they peel and curl until they fall off). Easy to remove, too, without leaving any residue.

Will gladly order and use again when the situation calls for it. Very happy with these. Five stars!

title: Nice storage solution for travel ...
text:
I've been taking some cruises lately and I've been refining my storage strategies especially for longer cruises. By longer, I mean at least 28 days long. That's long enough to necessitate the use of some sort of organizing system to keep dinner reservations, shore excursion tickets, and event brochures handy.

I've tried various solutions with varying degrees of success. Some are just too bulky to tuck into my luggage or they weight too much to be particularly useful. I've landed on a canvas sorter that rolls up and works for my shorter cruises (21-35 days), but I really need something with a little more storage space for my longer trips but that doesn't take up much luggage room ( (I have two long cruises booked: an upcoming 131-day world cruise, and a 68-day circumnavigation of South America next year).

This should be perfect. I've been playing with it at home just to see how it might work. I've labeled each folder according to how I might use it on the ship (daily activity announcements, dinner menus, shorex tickets, dinner reservations, event announcements, etc.), and it should work just fine. Even better -- it folds into "portfolio" that's about the size of a standard file folder (maybe just a bit bigger) so that I can just toss it into my suitcase without worrying about any damage.

The solid gray works fine, too -- unobtrusive, kind of melts into the background. And it seems to be sturdy enough to handle the amount of printed material I'll be dealing with on that 131-day world cruise. Very nice! Four stars.

title: Nice looking, but not so comfortable to use ...
text:
If you want a stylish very nice-looking pen to use only occasionally (to sign a check, etc.), this might be a great option for you. But if you want a pen that you can use daily for extended periods (writing in a journal, taking notes in class, etc.), yeah, not such a good choice.

The pen has no ergonomic features -- the barrel is smooth (no "grip," no textured area, etc.), which means that your hand will slide down the pen if using it for longer than 15 minutes or so. So you either have to keep repositioning the pen or grip it tighter, neither of which is a great option. I realize that adding even some thin rubber "grip lines" would likely spoil the sleek design, and maybe the target demographic for this pen is the "very occasional use" folks. But bear in mind that if you need a pen that will hold up to lots of use without causing your hand to cramp, this probably isn't the best alternative.

That said, it's a very nice looking pen in a nice presentation box, and would make a great gift (maybe graduation?). I give it 4 stars (I like it -- but only for LIMITED use).

title: Does what it is supposed to do, and does it nicely ...
text:
Another good offering from BIC -- this one a retractable gel pen with a medium point (0.7mm). I generally use pens like these for signing things (checks, forms, credit card slips, etc.), and I just want something that is reliable and works on a variety of papers and surfaces. So far, this one is performing just fine -- no skips, smooth ink flow, ergonomic rubber-cushioned grip, and quality construction (the metal pocket clip is a nice feature). BIC tends to price their products very competitively, and this is no exception. A good value.

Bottom line: 4 stars -- I like it!

title: Fine point, no bleed-through ...
text:
I'm not easily impressed when it comes to a pen, but these Finito pens definitely impressed. The point is VERY fine for a porous-tip pen -- a huge plus for me. The color is vibrant (I used the red to sign holiday gift tags) and the ink flows on with no skips. I tried it on printer paper -- and there's no bleed-through at all. No bleeding and no smearing, either. Really just about the perfect pen. There's a slight hint of drag -- it's a porous-tip pen, after all, so that's to be expected. I didn't find it a problem; others might.

For me, these are solid performers -- deserving of 5 stars.

title: Not exactly "heavy duty" - but suitable for light use ...
text: I'm the treasurer of my homeowner's association, and I like to keep each year's records in a separate file box.  I was offered an opportunity to try out this box and overall, I like it.  However, calling it "heavy duty" is a bit of a stretch -- the plastic isn't particularly heavy, but is adequate to protect a year's worth of receipts, bills, and forms.  The design allows me to take the box to board meetings -- nice handle, compartment for pens/pencils, etc.  Works fine for my use -- which admittedly is fairly light.  It's not going to take a lot of rough handling, but it's great for light day-to-day use.  Four stars.

title: Great to use “on the road” ...
text:
I have one of the big red ATG double-sided adhesive tape dispensers that I use at home fir my card making activities. But when I travel, I prefer to take something smaller. This Tombow applicator is perfect! Small and compact, it holds enough adhesive for 18-24 cards. I usually bring along a refill just in case I run out.

Easy to use and refill, it tucks neatly in pot my travel box. No problems at all — a first-rate product!

title: Classy file tabs, great for anything that needs a "marker" ...
text:
I've been using these to mark sections of a travel journal. I recently discovered the joys of cruise travel, so I do a chapter for each day / port. I tend to do longer trips (14-40+ days), and I try to section it logically (e.g., for the recent Alaska cruise, I had section for Ketchikan, Endicott Arm, Juneau, Gulf of Alaska, etc.). Sure, I could use less "flashy" tabs, but these are really nice and fit the gold/silver highlights I've added to the journal.

As usual, these are high quality - typical of Avery products in general. I use indelible markers (Sharpie Ultra Fine) -- works perfectly!

I'm preparing for a 38-day trip this summer through the North Atlantic, and I'm sure I'll purchase these to use for that journal. Definitely happy with these - solid 5 stars.

title: Who knew?  Great for packing long necklaces for travel ...
text:
I'm using these a little differently than intended. I have a lot of longer necklaces (the chains are usually around 30" with pendants that measure 1"-4" long), and I'm planning to take several of them along with me on a summer cruise. Problem: how do you pack long necklaces without the chains getting all tangled?

Solution: use these long narrow poly bags. I attach a cardboard tag to each necklace, then drop them pendant first into one of these bags, then staple the top of bag to the tag so that it doesn't fall off. Voilà! Problem solved! I'm taking a small stapler so I can repack them before the flight home.

These are great quality, nice thickness, flexible (I fold these up and pack in a small packing cube), and sturdy enough to hold up to packing and repacking. Will happily purchase again when I run out of these.

title: Great for card makers! ...
text:
I make a lot of handcrafted greeting cards, and I'm always looking for new products to incorporate into my cardmaking that will add a new dimension.

Enter these Milky Pop Pastel Gel Pens. As the package (and advertising) says, these really "pop" on dark paper. One of my favorite uses so far is to stamp and heat emboss a gold outline (usually a floral), then "color" the sections with these pens. It ends up looking almost like stained glass. (I'll try to post a photo later.) I've also used them with outline stickers in a similar way: color inside the exposed sections to mimic stained glass. The point is .8mm -- medium point, so not super fine but not "broad," either.

Very nice quality -- just what I'd expect from Pentel. Nice choice of colors, too (orange, yellow, green, pink, blue, lilac, and two white pens). These are getting a lot of use right now, and I'll likely continue to incorporate them into my card making supply arsenal. They're that good!

title: Good for card makers ...
text: I've been using this in my card making and it's working nicely so far.  It's not too thick, but just thick enough to show some dimension.  Easy to use, too.  Will likely purchase again when I run out.  I ordered it in the 5mm and 10mm width sizes and I use both depending on what I need for a specific card.  The photo shows the result for a small 5" x 5" card with a layered focal (the cluster of flowers is 3 layers deep, hand cut, and assembled using this foam tape).  Works nicely for my use.

title: Nice size for crafters, easy to print using Avery's templates ...
text:
I use a lot of Avery products in my crafting, especially when I need to produce a number of matching items (cards, etc.). These 2" round labels are extremely versatile and easy to print. I have an HP inkjet printer -- not top of the line, but it's a decent one. These feed through just fine, no jamming. And the Avery templates make it incredibly easy to design my labels for each batch of cards I want to make. I've used them for a central focal backed by colored cardstock or mirror board, and also for envelope seals.

No problems at all with these. I've come to trust Avery because the quality is consistent. Good stuff!

title: The same Sharpie pens we know and love -- with some new colors ...
text:
As someone who enjoys adult coloring (I've been at it since around 1992 or so), I tend to "collect" pens and colored pencils. I have several different Sharpie sets, both fine point, and ultra-fine point.

This set contains some new colors (check the photos on the product page that show the new colors). This is the "fine point" version, best suited for images with larger sections to color rather than some of the more popular highly detailed images that really do need that ultra-fine point. I've used these for more detailed work, but I have to be REALLY careful and apply with a light hand.

As with all Sharpie pens, these are alcohol-based, meaning they will likely bleed through most coloring book pages. But as they're permanent markers, they work on plastic really nicely -- like for marking plastic wine glasses/etc. at parties.

If you're looking for another set of Sharpies to replace an existing older set, this might be a good choice due to the new colors. Quality is as expected from Sharpie.

title: Easy to assemble, great size ...
text:
As someone who does a lot of crafts, I always have a bunch of stuff looking for a "home" that still needs to be convenient to my workspace. This cart is perfect! It comes in two colors -- black and silver. I got the silver one.

Assembly can be a little tricky -- make sure you have everything pointed in the right direction and everything will fit just fine. Took me about 10 minutes beginning to end -- and I'm a "senior citizen" with some limited mobility. Seriously, if I can do this, anyone can do it.

I'm using mine at the moment to hold crochet thread for my next several projects. I like to line up 3 or 4 projects with all the supplies needed along with the instructions. Having this on wheels means that I can easily move it from room to room.

I'm tempted to order another one or two: another one to use in my crafts room, and one to use in the kitchen. The size is great, and having 3 shelves works nicely. Good quality, certainly serves my needs perfectly!

title: A nice new addition to the Sharpie line-up of pens ...
text:
Sharpie has long been one of the primary pens of choice for adults who enjoy coloring. To meet the varying needs and demands of discerning colorists, Sharpie has introduced a variety of pens and points. This is yet another new addition to the Sharpie family of pens.

Unlike the familiar permanent Sharpies, these don't bleed through the paper as easily. They're not alcohol ink, but they do dry fairly quickly and they're water resistant. The colors are vibrant, and the twelve colors that come in this set are a good assortment.

So how are they to use? The tip is a brush tip, so you can get an extremely fine line or something thicker with just a little pressure. If you're not used to working with a brush tip, it might take a bit of practice to get it under control, but the results are stunning. I've used mine to highlight my travel journal from my cruise to Alaska last fall.

The inclusion of a case is a nice touch, too -- the instructions say to store the pens horizontally, and the case makes that easy to do. it's nicely made and holds the 12 pens securely.

Overall, I liked these better than I thought I would. Nice set, good colors, nice case.

title: Super quality -- great for card making ...
text: When they say "mirror" board, they mean it!  This is the shiniest most reflective silver cardstock I've seen, and it's perfect for adding sparkle and shine to my handcrafted greeting cards.  You get quite a lot in the package, too.  I used it for some holiday cards this year and have enough left to get a good start on next year's supply.  High-quality stuff, and it works just fine in my die cutter (a Sizzix Big Shot).

title: LOTS of excellent quality rubber bands ..
text:
I seem to go through a surprisingly large number of rubber bands because they serve so many uses. I use them mostly to package together packets of music for my choirs at the beginning of a rehearsal period. These are just the right size to hold 6-20 octavos together with leaving marks on the music. Then there the dozens of household uses — bundling up excess power cord to keep it out of the way, resealing bags of chips or crackers, attaching a pen to the kitchen message board, etc. These seem to be made of better material than my “usual” office supply store brand, and the size is perfect.

I suspect based on prior rate of usage these 3 packs of 1 lb each will likely last at least 5 years. It will be interesting to see how they age — many rubber bands get brittle and lose their stretch over time.but so far, I’m impressed!

title: Super boxes for handcrafted greeting cards ...
text: Got these to package some handcrafted greeting cards for a holiday fair as a fundraiser for a women's organization to which I belong.  My cards are 4.25" x 5.5" and often have multiple layers of papers and embellishments.  Four of them fit perfectly in one of these little boxes.  The quality is better than I expected -- the plastic is relatively heavy with clearly embossed fold lines that make assembly easy.  Would purchase these again if needed.

title: Great for organizing cruise docs while onboard ...
text: Took this along in a cruise to help organize papers, notices, menus, etc.  Someone on a cruise info forum suggested it as most walls in cruise cabins are metal covered in wallpaper or fabric, so magnetized storage pockets work well.  And so it did!  I was able to keep important info handy without taking valuable desk or nightstand space.  The daily “Where &When” fliers, daily menus, special offers from the shops or spa, shore excursion tickets/notices, etc.  stayed in place, no issues with detaching magnets.  I’ll be taking it along on my next cruise: 38 days transatlantic and return.

title: Absolutely perfect for Holland America luggage tags ...
text:
I got these to use on my recent 14-day cruise to Alaska on Holland America's Amsterdam They are the perfect size for the printable luggage tags you get after you do your online check-in. These plastic holders are sturdy, and the braided wire cables hold strongly with tight and secure screw-type joins. The hole at the top is reinforced with a metal eyelet, minimizing the risk of tearing.

Really well made -- actually better than I expected. Will be reusing them next summer for a 38-day transatlantic cruise through the north Atlantic to Norway. Highly recommended!

title: Perfect small clipboards (6" x 9")!
text:
These are really nice small clip boards. I really don't understand the reviews that complain about the size of these -- the size is right there in the title: 6" x 9". And they are exactly that size. Don't order these 6" x 9" clipboards if you really want 9" x 12" (to old 8.5" x 11" paper).

I got these specifically to use for coloring small postcard-sized drawings, stamped images for card fronts (I make hand-crafted greeting cards), and to hang on the wall to hold small items like receipts and tickets.

Sturdy, well made, a "low profile" design, and a retractable bit for hanging (it stays out of the way until/unless you need it). No complaints at all. These are perfect.

title: Nice heavier-weight paper and a true bright white ...
text:
I'm using this to create journaling "cards" for use in a scrapbook/journal I'm making to commemorate a cruise to Alaska this fall. I've designed cards of various sizes (2" x 3", 3" x 4.5", etc.), some with lines, some with small icons representing highlights of the trip and I wanted some "sturdier" paper to use for printing them. This is perfect.

The surface is smooth and works nicely with a variety of pens/pencils. Since I'll be gluing the cards into the pages of my blank journal, bleed-through isn't an issue, but just bear in mind that alcohol pens (BIC, Sharpie, Copic, Spectrum Noire, etc.) DO bleed through.

I may be printing some of my photos on this as well. The bright white works well with my ink-jet printer to reproduce the colors accurately, so it's a good lower-cost candidate.

Overall, it's very high quality paper. I really do like it and will likely be using it quite a lot for my projects.

title: Classy colorful writable repositionable tabs ...
text:
I go through a LOT of Avery Ultra Tabs! I've used them for marking music to help locate a particular piece during rehearsal (choral music, usually 25 or more pieces in preparation for a concert). I use them to help mark months in my homeowners' association financial reports and meeting minutes. And they work well when I'm reading and just want to add some notes and keep track of where I am.

I'm currently getting ready to take my first cruise -- a 2-week adventure to Alaska -- and I'll be using these along with magnetic hooks and small binder clips to keep the daily activity newsletters and menus organized and readily available. This is a tip I got from cruise-veteran friends: The cabin walls are metal that will hold magnets, so using magnetic hooks to hang lanyard/room key, daily documents, charging cords when not in use is an easy way to optimize space. Using these tabs makes it easy to identify specific instruction sheets, menus, etc.

Let's talk color. The actual colors/patterns of the set I got: turquoise w/ white lattice-work design; lime green with baroque damask design; and hot pink zig-zag pattern. Great colors! The tabs are sturdy but flexible, and stick securely but can be removed and reused. I like to make notes on the tabs themselves, and the size is great for that. I usually use fine point uni-ball pens for something permanent; pencil if I think I might need to change (like for my music, where I make notes about tricky bits where I need to watch the conductor more carefully ... )

These are nice tabs and you get 8 of each color -- I love them! Solid 5 stars

title: Nice medium-gold sticker paper, printable and die-cuttable ...
text: Works great with my Sizzix Big Shot die cutting machine to make labels and embellishments for my handcrafted greeting cards.  The gold color is nice -- not overly shiny, just a nice medium gold metallic tone.  You get 5 solid sheets of gold sticker paper and backing that work nicely in an inkjet printer, too (mine is an HP OfficeJet 3830 All-in-One).  Adds a classy touch to my cards, journals, and scrapbooks.  Love it!

title: Super sturdy and strong ...
text:
These double-wall boxes are super strong, capable of surviving a lot of abuse.

When I travel for the holidays, I often pack a "box" and ship via UPS ahead of time instead of packing a large check-in bag that I have to haul through the airport. The size of this one is about perfect in terms of shippability -- large enough to hold a lot of "stuff" without going over weight. It helps if I can use the same box to ship both to my holiday destination and back home after my visit. The double-wall construction of this makes it very suitable for the extra wear and tear of being shipped twice. I used one of these boxes to ship stuff from the Pacific NW to St. Louis and back over the Christmas holidays 2016, and it held up just fine.

The only issue I had with the first box I used was the flaps on one end didn't meet -- when folded according to the score lines, there was about a 3/4" gap. I was able to work around it by putting a flat piece of cardboard under the flaps and then taping it. I haven't tried any of the other boxes in the pack, so I'm hoping this was just a fluke. It's a relatively minor issue, really -- given the overall good quality here. I'd have no problem purchasing other sizes in this line.

title: Excellent quality, easy to use ...
text:
I make a lot of handcrafted greeting cards, so I go through a lot of "tape-style" adhesive.

This is a slight variation on the normal "snail"-type small cartridge glue runner. It has a protective tip cover to keep the glue from gathering dust, and it automatically advances the tape to the tip of the applicator so there's never a "dry" spot when you start to use it. It's also refillable, which is an advantage over other tape runners. The adhesive is permanent, so once it's stuck, it's stuck -- no opportunity for repositioning.

Tombow has a great reputation for craft supplies and I've used several of their adhesive products in the past. This is the same high quality and should work well for any paper crafting project.

Overall, I like it.

title: My favorite mechanical pencil ...
text:
I've been using this brand/style of pencil for years, and I've been totally happy with them. I like the fine point (0.5mm), and the twistable eraser. You even get replacement erasers in the package. The soft grip is a nice touch, too.

I returned to college after I retired at age 52, and found myself back in the daily grind of lectures and note taking. This is the pencil I used and the soft grip really really helped. They do wear out, but mine usually last at least 3-4 years, depending on how much abuse they get (in and out of backpacks, etc.). The two-pack is a great deal. Solid 5 stars -- I love them.

title: Versatile, strong, and lots of them!
text:
Good for so many uses! I use them with my crafts supplies, especially with my balls of thread that I use for thread (lace) crochet to hold the loose end so the ball doesn't unwind in storage. They're the perfect size -- relaxed, they're about 2" in diameter; 3" long if squished into a straight line without stretching. They're strong, too -- so far I've had no breakage at all, and no "duds" out of the ones I've used. You get a LOT in a package -- I'd guess hundreds for sure (it's 1/4 lb, and the package is fairly large-ish).

So far, I've found these to be fine for all my needs -- home/crafts as well as office. The size and strength mean they can fit a lot of items and bundles easily. I would happily purchase more of these if/when I run out, and will definitely consider other sizes if the need arises. Highly recommended and a solid 5 stars.

title: Coloring books come to the office ... on folders!
text:
With the current popularity of coloring books for adults, it was only a matter of time before these designs started showing up on home and office items. Enter these office folders -- complete with detailed line drawings for coloring.

There are four designs, and you get 3 of each for a total of 12 folders. Two of the designs contain inspirational sentiments; the remaining two designs are floral and circle/abstract. There's a nice variety of styles and detail levels which should appeal to most.

The quality is nice. The weight is typical of most common office folders. The folders are crisp white with oversized tabs (3 across). Printing is sharp with no misprints on any of the folders in my set. No issues at all regarding quality.

I've been enjoying coloring for years, so I was excited to have the opportunity to check out these folders. I tested these with alcohol markers, water-based markers, gel pens, and colored pencils. With the alcohol markers (I tested with BIC Markits as well as Sharpies), there was no bleed through but there was a little feathering (ink seeping across the lines). Using a slightly lighter hand solved that issue. With water-based markers (I used Staedtler Triplus), there was no bleed through or feathering but they take longer to dry than alcohol markers. Gel pens worked just fine but be aware that you have to let them dry or they'll smudge. And of course colored pencils work fine with no issues at all.

I'm using these for paperwork I need to take along when attending meetings. I bring a small pencil case with a few colored pencils and get pens, and I'm set to doodle when things get ... slow.

I really do like these -- they're good quality, useful, and fun to color.

title: Smooth as silk writing, comfortable in the hand ...
text:
I've used a few Paper Mate Inkjoy gel pens in the past and really like the smooth easy writing. This is a new set, more colors, and a different shape.

I received the 14-pen medium point set and the colors are really striking. I've played with all of them, and the ink color is quite close to the pen color (red is red, turquoise is turquoise, etc.). They're also quick drying -- much faster than earlier versions of the Inkjoy product. The size and shape are also nice -- I have severe osteoarthritis especially in my right hand (and of course, I'm right-handed), and the size and shape, combined with the comfort grip (a softer rubber-like material that surrounds the pen) really helps.

A note for those into adult coloring books: Not all gel pens are created equal. Some are better for writing, others are better for coloring. In my opinion, these are best used for writing, annotating journals or scrapbooks, etc. They aren't nearly as well suited to coloring in coloring books. For one thing, you don't get as much ink in these are you do in gel pens specifically designed for coloring. These will run out much faster. Also, they're retractable, which works great for writing and transporting a pen or two in your pocket or purse; not as much for quick access in coloring. They will work for coloring -- just like any other gel pen, they don't have as much of a bleed-through issue, and you do get a lot of colors that aren't as available in gel pens designed for coloring. But be aware that if used for coloring, they'll likely run out of ink faster than other brands.

That said, I really do like these, and will be using them often in my hand-crafted greeting cards and for annotating my journal.

title: Great for light office or home use ...
text:
I needed a stapler for home use, and of course came to Amazon to see what they had before hitting the office supply store. Found this one, liked the choice of colors, read the reviews, and decided to give it a shot.

VERY happy with this. The stapling mechanism has a different design than most staplers. You squeeze it, and toward the "end" of the squeeze, it sNaPs! the staple into the papers. I'm using it primarily to staple together pages of patterns and recipes as well as corralling some of my financial paperwork.

I got the green color -- it's a little darker than the photo -- more of a "kelly" green, but I'm OK with that. It takes standard staples and isn't difficult to fill once you figure out that you slide the BOTTOM section instead of the top to reveal the staple chamber. And it stores on the end (see the photo above), so it really doesn't take up much desk real estate.

I've stapled as many as 10 sheets of fairly heavy (26 lb) printer paper with no problems at all. I may purchase a second one to keep in my office, and have one in the kitchen to use with recipes and receipts.

title: So many uses for these ...
text:
I've used various sizes of these plastic "write-on" UltraTabs for several years for different purposes, so I'm happy to see that they've come out with a new "mini" size.

These I'm using to mark crochet patterns that I want to make for a fund-raising project. I can mark the pattern and write in the specific thread/color that I want to use, making it easy to remember what I had in mind when I selected that particular pattern. They're also reusable -- I write the thread type in pencil, so it's erasable, and the tabs peel off the book or magazine page with no tearing or residue, or loss of "stickiness" for the next use.

This set is the "neon" colors: pink/yellow/green/orange. They also come in pastels pink/yellow/lilac/aqua, and "brights": red. turquoise, orange, spring green.

I can also see using these in my cookbooks to mark "must make!" recipes including possible dates. They're small but really useful. Typical Avery quality, too -- really first rate.

title: Perfect for blocking small thread crochet items ...
text:
I used these as blocking boards for my smaller thread crochet items (coasters, small doilies, snowflakes, etc.), and they're perfect!

I usually draw a series of "guide" lines and/or circles on the white surface using an alcohol marker (sharpie, usually), then cover the surface with plastic wrap. I pin the wet item to the board using non-rusting pins, leave overnight, and voilà! it's blocked. The foam board is just the right thickness (3/16"), too, and light weight so I can easily move them around to keep them out of kitty's reach.

I've just ordered a couple more sizes of these for larger items. No complaints, no problems.

title: Worked fine in all respects ...
text:
I used these to make name tags for a brunch/conference, and they worked nicely. I have a decent low-end ink-jet printer (HP 3830) and had no issues at all with the printing process. The *only* issue I encountered was with using the template on the Avery website -- we had our own graphic/logo and I could not get it to work, couldn't get it placed in the "right" place, etc.. I ended up creating my own template in Pages (I'm on a Mac), and it worked just fine to print the 120+ name tags.

They were easy to "punch" out, too -- all laser cut, you just turn the sheet over and punch through the back (hard to explain -- the instructions are included). I was able to get all name tags separated and clipped to the sigh-in sheets.

We had no problem with the glue leaving residue or with it not being sticky enough to hold. Once applied, the name tags stayed put until removed.

I'll be recommending this product to next year's registration person for next year's event.

title: A touch of elegance ...
text:
From a practical standpoint, most binder clips are fine, regardless of color. And sure, you can get the mundane run-of-the-mill black binder clips for a very low price point. But if you want a little personality and elegance, you go for office supplies that are "different."

I purchased these to use for a conference/brunch meeting of ~100 women. I had name tags and sign-in sheets and needed something to keep them together. I saw these and knew they would add just the right touch to the festivities.

They are MUCH nicer in person -- really well made, the designs are nicely stenciled/painted, and the colors are a little deeper and more vibrant. The gold just sparkles, too. They were a big hit, with a number of folks asking where I'd found them. "Where else? Amazon!"

Can't find anything negative to say -- they really are nice, and I'll purchase more if the need arises.

title: Great for light or medium duty tasks ...
text:
I purchased a total of 9 of these to hold sign-in sheets for a large brunch/conference, and they were perfect. In fact, they are actually better than I expected. The high-density fiberboard is about 1/8" thick, smooth and strong, no "splinters," scratches, or sharp edges, with nicely rounded corners. The clasp is securely fastened, and the spring clip is strong and even (not lopsided). There's a pull-out hanger in case you need to hang these on a wall. Even more important for my use, every clipboard was identical -- all perfectly the same, same quality, etc.

For my purposes, they worked great. I probably wouldn't recommend them for any sort of heavy duty, but for light to medium tasks, they should be fine.

title: Definitely exceed my expectations ...
text:
I needed some clipboards for a large conference/meeting to hold the sign-in sheets, and decided to give these a try. Wasn't expecting much, really, at this price point, but I figured if they made it through the event, that would be good enough.

Well, color me surprised! These are really nice! The hardboard (high-density fiberboard) is sturdy, smooth, and 1/8" thick, with nicely rounded corners. I purchased a total of 9 of these (I needed 8 for my event) -- this six-pack and another pack of 3 -- and ALL of them were in perfect shape: no dings, no scratches, clip securely fastened, spring clasp perfectly aligned. Honestly, I can't find anything wrong with these at all.

I'm really impressed by the quality, and would recommend them without reservation for light- to medium-duty uses.

title: Perfect markers for "premium" coloring books ...
text:
I've finally found the pens to use for my nicer coloring books -- the ones with brilliant artwork but that contain images printed on both sides of the page. Alcohol markers bleed through (Copic, Spectrum Noir, BIC Mark-its, Sharpies, etc.), so unless you're willing to sacrifice the image on the opposite side, alcohol markers are more or less off the table.

These are water-based markers and are much less likely to bleed through or feather (seep outside the lines). You still need to be a little careful -- for example, you don't want to hold the tip of the pen to the paper for a long time as it WILL bleed through. Just color "normally," and you should be fine.

The 36 color set is perfect. You have enough variation within each color family to get some really nice shading effects. The triangular shape is really comfortable, too. I have severe osteoarthritis in my hands, so I have to be careful (I use "cushions" with my colored pencils). But these are really comfortable.

So glad I found these -- solid 5 stars from me. Highly recommended to my coloring enthusiast friends!

title: Excellent choice for home or light use --
text:
First things first: I'm using this with a Macbook Air 13" running OS X Yosemite (10.10.5) on a home network with router supplied by my cable company (it's an integrated cable modem + router). My background includes 32 yrs in IT (software development), but I'm NOT a "hardware geek," and I can be a little intimidated by some hardware. So I often approach installation/setup of new electronics with some trepidation.

This was probably the smoothest install/setup I've encountered. There is one issue which didn't impact the actual install/setup, but I'll get into that later.

From opening the box to printing my first page, I spent under 20 minutes. This included EVERYTHING: unpacking the printer, connecting all the bits that needed to be connected. powering it up, and installing the HP software on my Mac. You get a CD, but I didn't use it at all. I just followed the instructions and went to the HP website which led me step by step through the process. Also in the box are the power cord and the two ink cartridges (black and color). There is NO USB cable to connect it directly to your computer, so if you aren't planning to use the wireless feature, you'll need to furnish your own USB cable. Once it's powered up and the cartridges are installed, the printer will automatically print a test page.

I had no issues at all connecting it to my wireless network. Once I had entered my network's password (I have it stored in a keychain, so I didn't have to manually type it in), it connected immediately.

I went ahead and signed up for the HP Instant Ink 3-month trial. The price after the free trial period isn't too bad, considering the cost of the ink cartridges. I figure if I don't like it, I can cancel (there's no "contract" or minimum membership limits), and not having to worry about ordering ink on time is a nice convenience. I don't print a lot, really -- maybe 30 or so pages a month -- so this should work from an economical standpoint.

After finishing the installation process, I sent it a variety of documents, both black and white as well as color, text, photos, drawings, etc. -- 10 in all -- to test out the print speed and quality. I sent them in "batches," waiting for the printer to idle between batches to determine how long it took to "power up" to print. It definitely prints faster than I expected -- both color and black & white seemed to print quickly -- and the quality is good. Black & white quality is really excellent; color is OK -- not perfect, but I was printing on general purpose inkjet paper, not photo paper, and it was fine for my use. I don't print photos on my home printer, so the need for precise color matching isn't as great for me. It does a "good enough" job. Power-up from idle is almost instantaneous, too. Overall, I'm very impressed with the performance.

I also opted to install the HP printer "electronic help" that is supposed to integrate with Apple's Help function, and this is where things didn't work. You get only minimal product and usage info in the box, so you're supposed to install the more detailed help documentation during the installation process, which I did. Unfortunately, it seems to disappear into a black hole on a Mac running OS X 10.10.5 (Yosemite), because the instructions they include in the minimal "get started" guide that detail how to find it after it's installed bear no resemblance to anything I can find on my Mac. I spent the better part of an hour searching among the various Mac "help" functions for the list of commands presented in the HP 3830 "get started" guide -- they simply don't exist anywhere in the OS X Resources --> Mac Help tree. I finally went to the HP website, and even there it wasn't intuitively obvious where to find a "user manual" for this printer. I did finally locate one and downloaded the .pdf. Without the manual, you'll have to figure out how to use the document feeder, handle two-sided copying, etc. by trial and error.

Given that having a detailed user guide to provide guidance on more advanced features of a printer is kind of important, I'm knocking off 1 star. At a minimum, HP should provide a link to the actual .pdf user manual somewhere in the documentation. The link provided for "additional support" goes to the "Drivers & Downloads," "Troubleshooting," and "Support Forums" page. Clicking on "Drivers & Downloads" allows you to select "Printers," and after a couple more clicks on a couple more pages with more dropdowns, you'll eventually get to the page for this printer where you can select "User Guide." It shouldn't be this difficult. How about just including a link for the guide?

title: Charming artwork, soft colors -- in a handy size ...
text:
I remember using write-in planners and calendars, back in the days before smartphones and tablets. And "At-A-Glance" was always my planner-of-choice. Back in those days, most planners looked the same: fairly utilitarian, not much "style," plain, boring.

Things have changed.

This "Poetica" style might just be enough to get me back into using a non-computerized planning tool. This is a beautiful example printed on quality softly-colored paper, with "shadow" faded designs of birds, flowers, fish, and a few pastoral scenes. Each "quarter" is a different color (Jan - Mar is gold, Apr - Jun is teal, etc.), and each month is tabbed to make finding your way to the proper month easy.

Each month section starts with a 2-page spread of the entire month "at-a-glance," followed by a 2-page-spread for each week with plenty of room to record appointments, notes, etc. The planner covers 13 months (Jan 2016 to Jan 2017 inclusive), and ends with pages for "Important Dates," "Holidays" (a list of commonly celebrated holidays for 2016, 2017, and 2018), "Names & Addresses," "To Do," "For Me," and "Notes." I like that there's a LOT of room to record additional bits of information, but the planner is relatively small: just 5.5" x 8.5"

This will fit easily in my everyday bag, which means I'll be more likely to use it than I would by keeping it on my desk. I'm really impressed -- they've come a long way since I kept my schedule in a write-in planner, and I'm looking forward to using this in January. This would make a great holiday gift for someone who might appreciate the charming artwork and soft colors.

title: Great for those of us with sensitivity to "regular" adhesive tape ...
text: I'm almost hypersensitive to most adhesive tapes, but not this Micropore Paper Tape.  I spent 6 weeks last fall going through treatment at a Wound Healing Center,  and this was the tape they used when I indicated that I have a real sensitivity to "regular" adhesive tape (seriously, not fun -- blisters, rash, etc.).  It performs as well or better than most adhesive tapes and is easy to "mold" around curvy bits.  This size seems to work best for my use (occasional stasis ulcers due to CVI), and you cannot beat Amazon's price for a box of 6 rolls (at the time I purchased this, I paid less than 1.50 per roll).  Prices to change so watch closely for fluctuations.  Highly recommended.

title: Best color assortment of the lower-priced markers ...
text:
I've been doing a lot of coloring lately as a way to relax, so I've been collecting various markers, pens, and pencils to use. I chose this set over the similar Sharpie set because you get 36 colors as opposed to 24. I also purchased the BIC Mark-It Ultra Fine Point assortment as well.

So far, I'm reasonably happy with these. As others have mentioned, the caps often do NOT match the color inside. For example, there are NO real "pastel" colors in this set. What looks like it should be a pale peach is actually a flamingo pinkish orange; pale lavender is more of a medium purple, etc. So whatever you do, make a sample sheet ON THE PAPER YOU'RE COLORING. The shades tend to vary a lot from paper to paper -- it will look different on all-purpose printer paper as opposed to a page out of your favorite coloring book. Take the time to do samples.

These have a broader tip, and I got them to use on the more wide open spaces in some of the designs I like to color. I use the ultra fine tips for those small hard to color areas. These are alcohol, so they will bleed through most pages, and they can feather quite badly if you're not careful. Use a very light touch and stay away from the edges of the area you're coloring until you get the feel for how these behave.

I've used these for 8 or 9 different projects so far, and they haven't run out yet. Apart from the color issues, I'm happy with these.

title: Tiny eraser packs a big punch ...
text:
I use these for tidying up my coloring in highly detailed coloring books, like Johanna Basford's "Secret Garden." I color with colored pencils (Prismacolors), and occasionally go "outside the lines." This eraser is perfect for getting into those tight spots, and eradicating my mistakes.

It's gentle -- removes the pencil marks without scuffing the paper -- and the design keeps it sturdy so it doesn't break. It works like a mechanical pencil: you click the "clip" end to extend the eraser tip.

I purchased the 2-pack of erasers with the refills so I wouldn't have to worry about having it with me. I keep one of the erasers plus one tube of refills in my pencil case, ready when needed.

Very happy with this product, and recommend it to any who have taken up coloring with pencils.

title: Good sharpener for all sorts of pencils ...
text:
I'm actually on my second one of these -- wore out the first one after about 4 yrs of use. Yes, the blades will eventually get dull, but the price point on this little sharpener is low enough that purchasing a replacement isn't a huge deal.

I've used this on my Prismacolors, my Aquarelle watercolor pencils, my Staedtlers, even my cheaper RoseArt and Crayola pencils, and it does a fine job on all of them. I like that there are two sharpening "profiles": wide and narrow, as I alternate between the two depending on what I'm coloring.

A note about emptying the shavings: it can be a bit tricky, especially since there are no instructions at all. Here's what I do: first, it empties out the top, meaning you have to remove the entire top sharpening apparatus to open the shavings compartment. DO NOT attempt to do this by opening the lid and pulling on it. You will break the lid (as some other reviewers have mentioned). Instead, leave the lid CLOSED. Hold the unit tightly in one hand and use your thumb to gently push up on the top just above where the top sharpening unit joins the transparent plastic housing. The first time you do this, you may need to use both thumbs to push it off. Once you get it off, empty the shavings and carefully line the little "notch" at the rear of the top with the little "bump" at the back of the housing, and snap it back into place. After the first time, this will all be easier.

All told, this is a nice little sharpener -- works great with all my pencils, and lasts quite a long time with regular use.

I use these a lot for coloring (especially the [[ASIN:1780671067 Secret Garden: An Inky Treasure Hunt and Coloring Book]] and related items). I love the intensely saturated colors and ease of use. So far, I haven't found any "duds" (no dried out pens, etc.).

A word about cost: pay attention as the price of these varies depending on the listing and supplier. I got my set for less than forty dollars; right now (May 1 2015) it's just under fifty. Still, at fifty cents a pen, I'd consider this a bargain given the quality.

text:
There's a lot to like with this cart, and some things I wish were different. Starting with that, I wish the upper basket size was larger and could hold more weight. It is approx. 21" long, 13" wide, and 13" deep. If you either look up or are already familiar with 1-Gallon Arrowhead Water Jugs, you'll recognize the capacity as being able to put in 6 of these jugs edge-to-edge. (Incidentally, with one gallon of water weighing 8.63 pounds, if you did cart home all 6 jugs, you'd pretty much hit the weight limit, as the water would weigh about 52 pounds.)

It's sometimes a bit difficult to keep the cart driving perfectly straight. It tends to veer off on its own.

If you decide to walk fast, your foot might accidentally hit the brake, depending on your strides.

The cost is really very high for this small cart.

On the good side, the wheels roll quietly, the ride is smooth, it turns well, there is no bad odor coming from it, the handle feels nice, and you could easily put it in your car, if desired.

It's hard to know how many miles you can really put on the wheels before they wear down or break, but assuming you want a small-size cart that is not too heavy, and assuming you do not need to buy groceries for more than person, this is a nice cart that can do a good job.

title: UPDATE one month later - Had to "pick" to open
text:
SEPTEMBER 16, 2020-- I finally got around to setting up this Masterlock 5420D lock box. If followed the directions in the .pdf instructions sheet, set the combination to the last four of my social security number, and closed the box as directed. I couldn't open it using my combination, and thought I had essentially lost use of the contents --a mini garage door opener and a spare key. I shortly found that there are Youtube videos demonstrating how to pick this lockbox. I was able to get it open that way; it now seems to be working, but I wonder how common the knowledge is that it is so easily picked. CANNOT RECOMMEND THIS ITEM.

AUGUST 11, 2020 - I have no cons for this item, but will share a personal observation. title: 3M tapes have really good adhesion, this variant works well for storage
text: One problem you run into with some other tapes (though 3M is generally pretty good regardless) is that over time when used on storage boxes, they lose adhesion, sometimes coming off or forcing you to retape.  Obviously with boxes in storage, you do not always have temperature control, this tape holds up better than most on temperature cycles (hot-cold-hot...).  And as you tend to shuffle around some in storage, you do not want the box opening up unexpectedly on you.  The 3" hub form factor is pretty standard, you can use with Scotch ST-181 or 3M commercial tape dispensers (guns, like the HR80).

title: 3M/Scotch Tape Gun well made, safer to use, but blades not replaceable, so expensive over time
text: The 3M/Scotch ST-181 tape gun is well made, and has a retractable tape cutting blade which makes it safer to use than most of the cheaper alternatives.  Most tape guns have an exposed blade which is easy to brush against, injuring the user or someone else in the work area (or when you have the tape dispenser stored, between uses), or clothing or packages.  Duck and ULine also have OEM units with retractable blades, but you will have to shop around for those, the 3M/Scotch is much easier to find. The body of the ST-181 unit is steel, as is the cutting area and blade, blade slider and tensioner.  The tape roller is a hard plastic, as is the tape spool (which is adjustable, tension wise) and wiper.  Pushing on the wiper pivots the blade for cutting the tape.  The handle is plastic with a foam cover, it is comfortable, although over time the open foam can collect a bit of dust and dirt, gets greasy, can be hard to clean (a unit with a rubberized handle will generally be better in this regard).  The ST-181 can also use a variety of 3M/Scotch and other brand packaging tapes, the tape is threaded past a retention/tension device, over the roller and past the blade and clear plastic wiper.  You can start taping the box on the side, use the roller across the top, and then push down on the wiper as you go around the edge, this should cut the tape and press it down, with practice this goes all pretty simply.  Turning the small wheel on the tape hub lets you adjust how much tension there is, which is needed for different types of tape.  This works well with 2" wide tape on a 3" cardboard hub, from 3M and others.  Tape is replaceable, and sold in bulk.  There are a couple of tricks to buying this, 3M/Scotch sells it with and without one or two tapes, price those out as frequently with tape will be cheaper than without (which makes no sense, but...).  3M makes a lot of different tapes, it is generally a very good brand.  Shipping tape generally has better adhesion, storage tape holds for longer and is less susceptible to temperature swings.  The kind of caveat on this unit is that the blade is not replaceable, it is held on with two screws, but 3M does not sell replacements, so as the blade dulls with usage, you will have to replace the whole unit.  Normally the safety of the retractable blades and padded handle would make this a good choice for commercial, but the lack of replaceable blades means it should be used more for light office or home only.

title: A top-notch laser all-in-one printer
text: I have had a lot of printers over the years (IBM, Epson, HP, Canon, Lexmark, etc.), and had kind of gone away from HP a bit due to their software/driver problems (when they off-shored the development/support, the quality slipped quite a bit).  However, when printing Christmas cards, my Canon died, and I had been impressed with this HP model when I was helping my sister sort out hers, so I bought one (MFP M479fdw).  Software seems to work reliably so far, so I think HP has addressed that somewhat, granted it is a bit rough and crude in places, but it works.  And it works from both Windows 10 and macOS 11 (Big Sur), as well as from mobile (iOS).  The printer hardware seems to be very good, output arrives quite fast.  One of the problems you run into with cheaper printers (including some lower end HPs) is that they do not put much horsepower into the printer CPUs, and cost-reduce the hardware to the point that they are slow and do not hold up, but this version seems well designed and made.  Ratings from PC Magazine, Wirecutter, etc. generally have this printer at or towards the top, I would say that is accurate.  Print quality on text is excellent, graphics from web pages and similar also excellent, scans are very good (a custom flat-bed would be a tad better, but this is for an all-in-one amongst the best I have seen).  For printing high-quality pictures, you probably still want a Canon or Epson InkJet printer, but this one prints OK for a laser.  HP does not ship this printer with full duty cycle cartridges, but the ones they ship with will still do a decent number of pages.  Control screen is touch and good sized, gets the job done.  Unit is fairly heavy and large, so if you are using this on a desk, check the dimensions some.  The printer is not cheap, but it has excellent print quality and appears to be very well built, so HP has come back to where it once was, at the top.

title: You won't regret buying this printer.
text: My husband bought this printer for work. He works from home, so I've been able to use it frequently as well and so far I'm loving it. I will say that setting it up was a nightmare. I'm far from technical guru, but do have moderate experience with computers and have set up several printers over the years. The main issue was getting the software on his work computer that does not have a CD drive. You can download the software from the Epson website, but for some reason it was extremely difficult to do. After downloading I would get an error message saying it was unsuccessful. After fighting with it for 3 days I finally got it setup, and I honestly have no idea how I did it so I cannot give any tips for others in a similar situation. After the initial headache though, it's been smooth sailing. I love the borderless printing option, it really does print all the way to the edge of the paper with excellent quality. The ink is super easy to load, and will save us a bundle of money over the life of the printer. You get a LOT of ink! The scanner on our last printer was awful. The picture quality was pathetic. This scanner is crazy good!  We were both impressed with how well and clear the scanned images are. Same with the copier. I have no complaints whatsoever about this product and would absolutely recommend it without hesitation, although it'll be a lot easier to install if you have a CD drive to install the software. Once you have it set up, everything is very easy to use. The printer basically walks you through everything. If you can read, you can use this printer. The only thing my husband doesn't like is that you can only scan one page at a time and you have to place each page individually on the scanner/copier. He has to scan dozens of pages at a time, and he is used to putting a stack of pages in the printer all at once (the way you put blank paper in for printing). That's our fault though for not completely reading the product description before purchasing, so I certainly can't take away any stars for our own error. Overall, you really can't go wrong with this printer. I've been at my parents house over 100 miles away and can print things as if I were at home where the printer is. My only regret is not buying it 3 years ago.

I don’t quite know what’s wrong with my hand but if held in certain positions, it will get a cramp and draw up into a claw ( certain fingers), so my handwriting has become a mess and difficult at best for me.
I don’t have as much trouble with my handwriting looking as messy when I use this brand. It has just the right amount of ink flow for my problem.
The only cons I have to say about this is that I go through a LOT OF THEM. I’m constantly writing so maybe I just use more than a normal person uses but in all the years I went through school I just don’t recall running out of ink in pens like this.
I’ll keep buying this brand as long as I can afford to buy and find them. I just got my order of 75 count I hope they last me for awhile although I’ll be giving some to my daughter and I have other family members that will also use them.
If you haven’t tried this brand, give them a try and see what you think, especially if you have difficulty with your hands and need help.

title: EXCELLENT planner. Great layout and paper quality
text:
I ordered another planner before this and ended up returning it, as the paper was too thin and writing/highlighting bled through to the other side.

This planner on the other hand is near perfect. It's obviously of high quality, including the paper but also the cover, binding, and fact it comes with a spiral-binding bookmark that marks the well you're on.

It's obvious a lot of thought went into making a perfect planner. Days are laid out by half hours (excellent for scheduling) plus a box at the top of every day for overview/notes. There's punched tabs at the bottom of each page to remove at the end of the week to make it even easier to flip to the current week, even though the provided bookmark that snaps into the spiral binding is more than sufficient. The cover is thick and sturdy. Plus it comes with full-month overviews which are easy to flip to with recessed tabs. On top of that it has a password list, envelope for important notes, and a string bookmark for marking the month.

My qualms with it are minor and not even it's fault. The pictures in the reviews made the green option look turquoise when it is in fact the color in the main photos (not the planners fault obviously) so I wish I'd gotten blue instead of green - but ultimately no big deal. It also doesn't have hourly daily planning on Sat and Sun which is probably fine for 90% of people but as someone who works weekends it'd be nice to have those days laid out by hours as well. But still, not a huge deal.

I'll very happily buy this planner again next year, though in blue. It's overall excellent and of superb quality. You won't be disappointed with this planner.

title: Paper too thin
text:
I wanted to love this planner, it's got everything I was looking for: daily scheduler by hours (including weekends), month pages, lays flat with a spiral binding, cool cover pattern, month tabs. Unfortunately the paper is too thin, writing and highlighting shows through on the opposite side. That's not ok as it makes the reverse side sloppy looking and hard to read. Deal breaker for me so I'm returning it. Such a shame because otherwise it's great.

Just be aware also that it's HUGE. Much bigger than I expected. Not it's fault, I didn't read the dimensions carefully and I'd still have happily used it if the paper quality were better. Very disappointed such a great planner has such a fatal flaw. I mean for this kind of price you expect good quality paper. It's not cheaply priced, shouldn't be cheaply made. Boo.

title: Fantastic printer!
text:
So so so SOOOO pleased with this printer. I'd set aside an hour and a half to mess with it to get it set up an for a good mid-set-up frustration cry, it took less than 20 minutes to go from sealed box to spitting out shipping labels, even WITH a small cry out of relief in there.

The manual directs you to their website for the Android/oS app. The page just says to go to the app store and download an app which is very succinctly simply called "Shipping Printer" (icon is a black printer w blue paper). There's nothing else on their website of relevance to set up so save yourself some time and just download the app. As per a tip on here I just screenshot the label, rotate and trim it in my Gallery, and then once the app is open you just hit "file", pick your image, click the next arrow, then click print. Easy parcheesie. Idk if there's a way to bulk print or not, but at the bulk I'm shipping I'm not fussed to find out.

It spits out labels lighting fast, and while they could be a little darker they're still plenty dark and totally readable.

Another cool thing is it comes with a USB to USB-c (newer phone port) adapter so you can actually plug the printer straight into your phone if you don't have a computer, and connect that way if you don't have blue tooth or it's being buggy or whatev. AND it comes with a USB protector thing. And a good-size roll of thermal paper.

Absolutely no complaints. Feels well-made and sturdy and looks like one of those Glade aromatherapy smoke things.
