title: Stop reading and BUY THIS RIGHT NOW!
text:
The pendant is so so lovely and I'm really pleased with the quality! I've only worn it a couple days, but I think literally everyone I talked to while wearing it complimented it. I thought from the picture it was bent wire but it's actually casted-- that said the casting job is perfect and clean, which is great because most casted jewelry I've bought on Amazon is sloppy and looks much worse than the picture. This pendant looks exactly as pictured, maybe very slightly darker but still great and a fantastic buy for the price, and looks like it cost significantly more than it does. Sure, maybe the chain isn't amazing but it's really not nearly as bad as some reviewers are saying, plus it's good and long which I really like, and it even has an adjustable length part-- plus for this price what do you expect, a Tiffany chain? I'm just thrilled the pendant looks so good, I can easily put it on a different chain if I need to, but I personally like the chain.

I'm so very happy with this purchase and I'd make it a hundred times over, it's probably one of my favorite Amazon buys. Can't believe how many compliments it gets! If you're wondering if you should buy this, you absolutely should!

EDITED to add: This is still probably my all time favorite Amazon buy, I wear it almost every day since I got it and get compliments on it just about every time I go out. I wanted to add that I'm VERY sensitive to "cheap" jewelry, it gives me a rash and bad hives. I've kept this pendant on the chain it came on and had absolutely no issues, either with irritation or with breakage-- and considering I'm a pro horse trainer, lets just say I've lost some nice jewelry on the job thanks to cheap chains. I seriously have no idea why people hate the chain so much (maybe because it's a more rustic style chain than a "diamond necklace" style chain?), but I love it-- especially the length!-- and personally I couldn't think of anything about this purchase I don't absolutely love. I'm not one of those paid reviewers or anything (but seriously, how do you get in on that??) and I'm usually pretty critical in my reviews, I just seriously LOVE this purchase. I'll probably buy another to have incase I lose this one or need a last-minute gift.

title: functional value added gadget, very durable/sturdy base & arm, so easy to use
text:
Nothing new in terms of function. It is a bluetooth speaker that can easily control the phone via the controls on the base (no need to use controls on phone once paired). The speaker pairs very easily- no hassle. The speaker has a voice that will tell you when it is paired, turned on, etc.

The feel of this is sturdy. I am rather impressed by the weight. The arm is stiff and secure feeling. The grip pad really helps hold the phone, and further held in place by a little shelf. The arm is adjustable.

It all folds down into a rectangle. If you dont want to use the stand, you can just fold it back into place.

Everything has a flashlight these days, and this is no exception. I like that. Much brighter than anticipated. Has steady light as well as a flashing light. Quickly double click side flashlight button to turn on/off.

Can use to make calls and answer calls as it has a built in microphone. I havent used this yet to test the call quality because I almost never make calls.

Definitely adds volume over what my phone can offer. I like this for listening to podcasts. We're not talking cinematic sound, it simply provides a louder more room filling volume. Easier to hear over phone sound by far.

Came pre charged and was ready to go, however the directions asks for this to be charged for a couple of hours before use. Has basic USB-C port, so any cord you may already have will work. This comes with one USB to USB-C cord.

Has a spot to use for attaching to a bag. Will want to fashion your own cord or something to make it work. I would just feed a loop of cord through it and then use a carabiner to attach to backpack or whatever. Too bad it didnt include something to highlight that feature.

Comes with instruction manual this is clear and helpful. Most of it is user intuitive but it will benefit anyone to give it a good read through

I had given this product a lot of thought before ordering. I didnt want another goofy gadget that would never really be used. I was drawn to it being a stand and speaker combo which would make it nice for use on my desk, or now that I have it in hand, has been great for podcast listening while doing chores/projects. I considered using it in the car as part of a navigation system since I dont have bluetooth in my older car.

Anyway.., I truly find that it adds value, and am quite pleased with this order. Near perfect to me: 4.5 stars but am going with 5 stars since I like it more than 4 stars

title: strong & durable, super easy to put together (couple minutes), holds a lot, holds weighty stuff
text:

For the reviews that stays it falls apart, I imagine they didn't the pieces fit in snug enough. Make sure everything is pressed in as far as it can go, including handles. It is all pressure fit, no screws needed. Sits evenly.

The wheels work fine on tile floor. I use this in my kitchen. I always seem to have a small pile of groceries sitting on the floor in one spot. Not wanting to keep that going, yet knowing I could use a little extra storage space, I got this cart to hold miscellaneous items. I keep bottles of water, cooking oils, breakfast items, some excess k-cups, and whatever else I need it to hold. I have no concerns with it collapsing. I think I could load it up with laundry detergent or gallons of water and it would be fine.

Good size for my needs. I may consider another as I simply like it enough to want to use one elsewhere.

The measurements are in the product pictures, and yes the height includes the wheels and handles. Take a close look. Not sure why there are questions and comments when the information is clearly in the description.

I wouldn't pay more than the $23 I spent. If I were to spend more, then I would be looking into metal

Since mine is loaded up, it doesn't really roll. But I can scoot it across tile floor just fine. If truly needing a rolly cart, I'd go for metal or something more upscale.

title: have patience- takes long time to prime, bold colors, might leave haze when wiped off
text:
[[VIDEOID:d41afc4a49454093909a0ace01a3ab07]] They take awhile to prime. Shake shake shake, shake some more, then press press press, maybe shake a few more times. Eventually the liquid chalk works its way down to the pen tip. Tip can be turned around--- one side rounded, one side slanted.

Zips fully open. Easy to open, easy to close.

Because I have fun doodling on a wall hung chalkboard situated at our main house door. It was here well before we moved in (20+ years) ago, and with just two adults in the house, it really serves no purpose. So I took to making terribad art on it. I make some quick doodles every once in awhile for the sheer fun of it. Adding in more color allows me to more options. I enjoy the process of creating a images with chalk.

Overall, I like the colors, I dont like how long it takes to prime each one, and I have to do this nearly every time. Maybe thats the norm? Can leave haze on some surfaces, case wasn't as expected. I give them 3 stars because I think they (and my overall experience) have been"OK".

--have a full week calendar showing Monday- Sunday,

--The goal planning has a page labeled as "this month", then it has notes for "get it started", "quit it", "keep it up", and "notes".
--The checking in page includes a spot to jot down notes about "last month", then a couple of columns for notes on Wellness and Gratitude.

--Includes a few pages of blank note pages (front and back) at the end of the planner.

--Each page for the weekly has a bullet point/check off note section labled, "don't forget". Also can be found at each full month calendar (as well as a line for "monthly goal").

--Front page has list of Holidays for 2022 & 2023
--As well as a Yearly Overview calendar for 2022 & 2023

That's it! Sound good? go for it!

title: Super basic, weird layout,but is functional for its basic purpose: see the date across the room.
text:
This review is for the THREE month view calendar.
"Dunwell 2020-2021 3-Month Wall Display Vertical Calendar (11x26" Open), Use June 2020 - December 2021, 3-Month Display, Three Month Look Ahead Calendar, 3 Tier 3 Panel "

Width wise, it is a typical sized calendar.
Length wise, it is showing three months at a time. Each month on their own page- sized like a typical wall calendar but X3.

The blocks just have the dates on them in bold black, large print.
Blocks include popular holidays.

This is really an "At a glance" calendar since there is no room for writing- not really. Hang this up, and you can see the date from across the room for the next 3 months. Since it shows 3 months at a time, there is no 'month ahead, month behind' display.

Top of calendar is spiral bound with a little bump out for hanging. The month attached to the spiral is not perforated. The months attached below are perforated. I think just so they fold cleanly? It seems to be advertised as a feature, but you can't logically tear one off as the months proceed. And when you get to a spot that you want to tear off what has already passed by, then you would be tearing off 3 full months (which the top portion isn't perforated anyway). Weird point to make. Maybe I am missing something.

How it is displayed is a little odd to describe. When the 3 months are hanging down, it isn't always current, but the current month is highlighted in red (always in the center), and the other two months are grayed out. So basically you are getting the month ahead, month behind but they are same size as a calendar.
More specifically & for example: June, July, August shows on 1 full page (well, 3 pages technically). July is highlighted red (as though it were current month). It is situated at center (or second panel). This is the layout throughout. Once you get through August (3rd month in sequence), the next set is July, August, September (with August highlighted red as it is now the current month), then next 3 panels are August, September, October (with.. you guessed it.. September is highlighted red for the current month). It is fine, and no one would be confused by it. It is nice to always have the "month ahead/month behind" feature, so long as someone doesn't change it too early or too late.

When I selected this, I knew where it was going to be used, and what the limitations are. So, not what I have in mind for an actively used calendar in my kitchen, where we jot stuff down, but it is good for my home office where I just want to glance at a date. I never use it to write on since I have a planner for stuff like that. But sometimes I just want to glance at a date on the calendar, so that is why I have calendars in my office. This just happens to be the largest I have ever used since it provides view for 3 months. Doesn't matter that there is no room for notes.

Super basic, but is functional for its basic purpose: see the date across the room.

If that is what you need it for, then you will like this basic calendar. Just note how it works.

Since it mentions that it is also for seniors, please take note of how the layout is. Yes, the numbers are big and bold, but there in no where to jot down notes for them. And, I mean this kindly, from experience with having 80+ years old friends.. the format may be confusing to them. They will have to remember and understand that the pages must be kept up with in order to see month behind/ahead correctly. I am imaging bringing this over to my slightly confused geriatric friends house, and this would stress them out. So please know who you are buying this for.

title: greatly reduces all the aches & pains from tailbone pressure; works great on my computer chair
text:
This Luckylife gel seat cushion measures roughly 17" x 17" x 1"

I am a bigger person, and it seems appropriate to my size and needs. I use it on my office chair, where I am always wishing for a little more cushioning. My chair aggravates my back, and while I use a back cushion, it was dawning on me that a little support in the bum area would provide better care. I did try a seat cushion, but it was too thick and firm. It changed the way my chair worked, and I found that I rarely used it. When this cushion came up as an option, the information in in the product description as well as the overall look intrigued me.

The cushion is thin but dense. If you really needed a thicker cushion but still made of this material, I would just buy a second one and double up. The material used, TPE(ultra-flex polymer) is neat. It is a jelly like material in shape of honeycombs. The pad has a zip on cover that has little nubs on one side to help grip whatever you are using it on. Basically less likely to slide of your chair.

I didn't notice any major changes right away. Well, I noticed that it was comfortable to sit on and that it seemed to form to my body. It was after using it for a few days and being at my computer for long periods of time that I realized that I wasn't feeling the usual odd aches in my legs, hip, back. My back wasn't aching as I get out of my chair. So while I have only been using it for a week, it has been a good week.

So depending on your needs.. this might be good for you. If you need a more firm pad, look elsewhere. This is super flexible, and super squishy. I am not sure how it is working, but at least for my needs it seems to be helping. I think the too frim pads (or lack of pad) exacerbate an easily pinched nerve. This seems to cradle my body and alleviate the tension.

Also, it is somehow cool feeling. Not sure if is actually cool, or if it is the design (honeycomb) which may allow for more air flow?

The cover is super thin yet durable.

I read another review that said theirs stunk. I hadn't noticed anything, but I decided to pick it up and take a whiff. There is a faint, unpleasant odor. If it were strong, I imagine it would be unusable. But for mine, I didn't notice it until I sniffed for it.

Like I said, this pad happens to be working for my needs, in my computer chair. I would consider taking it to restaurants as most of the chairs offered really hurt my back (which stems from pressure on butt/tailbone area). Since this is lightweight and flexible, I think it could easily be carried in a large purse, or simply as it. Be comfortable where you can!

I am giving it a solid 4/4.5 star rating. It's still early on in my use, but I am enjoying it so far. It has been great to use. I hope it holds up and continues to be good for my tailbone. I think it is worth the try.

title: bookmark this for gift giving, every book lover is likely to welcome this little gadget
text:
This is the neatest little gadget. Maybe "gadget" doesn't do it justice. How about functional art piece? It is a small, lightweight piece of walnut that has been shaped and smoothed to provide a means to hold a book open easily and comfortably with one hand. It is one of those things that you don't know you need* it until you try it.

It is not a book weight. It is meant to be placed on your thumb (check sizes to determine your fit), and the slight pointy area will nestle into the book crack, and the length protruding from both sides will keep it wide open. I have felt no pressure on my thumb. IT may not be something you need*, but I like the added pressure it provides that the thumb doesn't have to take. It really helps with heavier or larger books, or books where the binding is extra tight and it takes extra effort to keep book open.

EDIT: I was first using this on my day time reading, where I tend to sit up and rest the book on my lap or propped up on a pillow (on my lap). The books were smaller/lighter and I had a heavy one in use. When I took this item to bed, for my night reading, I had/have a mid weight paperback, and I noticed that my thumb was feeling fatigued early on. I think it was positioning of my body as well as how my thumb was more apt to be angled, which changes how the pointed part works. I also tend to hold my book at the top when reading in bed, so it was odd feeling to switch. It doesn't change anything in terms of rating regarding quality or efficacy, just depending on how you hold a book, it may make a difference.

If you are like me and get sqwicked out at the feel of wood, know that this is so smooth that it doesn't both me at all. I would not be able to touch it if it was at all rough or had any texture. It s full on smooth.

It sure is small. Just a little over 3" long, and .5" thick. Very light.

If you have book loving friends or family, I highly recommend it as a gift. Or even as a teacher gift. This is not likely something they have, and I imagine they would like it. It would be great as part of a themed gift, or just as is. Pretty sure any book lover will enjoy this. It is attractive, it feels good to the touch, and it really does a fantastic job of keeping book open.

I have the size medium, and my thumbs are fat. The description says that the Medium (0.86 inches) is "for women with large fingers and for MOST MEN". I concur. My fat thumbs are about 2.75" around, and the center hole on this is just a tiny bit more than that. It fits like a ring that is too big, not that you will necessarily be sliding it down that far. But I am just trying to give you idea of sizing of the hole. Using a ring sizer it is around a size 13). Which is what you want- loose.. well, preferably not snug anyway for maximum comfort. Anyway, the wiggle room I have seems perfect. I have been using it near the tip, and have plenty of room left over. I imagine I could go to the small size, but I dont think it would make a difference. I would not want it snug. Medium is good for me.

From product description:
SIZE MATTERS! -
Small (0.78 inches) is suitable for MOST WOMEN and kids,
Medium (0.86 inches) - for women with large fingers and for MOST MEN and
Large (0.98 inches) - for men with thick fingers

title: detailed review of layout below; Organized and uncomplicated planner, great view of month, week
text:
Planners are personal, and it can be a challenge to find the one you want to spend a year with. I aim to detail the layout of this planner and provide the overall feel of it so you can decide if it is even what you are looking for. Then if it is, you can continue to read on for further thoughts of my observations/summary at very end. Ok so...

--The cover is a clear, thick plastic, followed by one page of card stock paper with design. Next page is,

--Personal Information page (lines for name, email, home, office, cell), on back of this page is a page of

--Reference Calendars for 2020 and 2021. Then..

--"The Story of the Planner That Will Change Your Life" (basically an "about" section regarding this planner), on back of this starts the goal setting theme of this planner. So a numbered sequence over the next 4 pages..
1. "Start With the Big Picture": (includes a paragraph of big picture thinking, plus blank lines to jot your thoughts down)
2. "Set Your Goals": (inludes blurb on goal setting, plus area to jot down various personal, family, financial, spiritual, work goals)- Also side bar for adding dates to accomplish this by.
3. "Design Your Days": (Daily planning; includes columns to describe morning and evening routines)
4. "Stay on Course": (Review goals, includes checklist for measuring progress)

THEN..
--Full monthly calendar for July 2019- two pages. Each full month calendar uses two at a glance full pages that you can see the whole month at once. The remainder of 2019 follows. Just the month calendars, not the dailies. No tabs. These are the "bonus" months in case you want to get started early on acquiring and using a planner.

--Starting in January 2020, each month has a tab to quickly access your month of choice. Again, each month utilizes two pages, so you can see entire month at once. The left side of the calendar includes a "Notes & To-Do" column, as well as a glance back and glance forward a month column (typical calendar feature). Holidays are included in small print. Those dates have a ribbon icon (great for at a glance to see which days have a holiday). After that..

--A full week is seen on the next two pages. Mon, Tues, Wed on left page, Thurs, Fri, Sat &Sun on the right page. There too holidays are printed as well as the ribbon icon. Each day (section/box) has a "todays schedule" printed on the left side of the box, and a "to do" section on the right side of the box. Along the bottom on the left page is a short column to jot down "this weeks top 3", just to the right of it is a quote/saying. On the right page you will see after Thurs & Friday, who has their own section/box, that Sat & Sunday share a space. Underneath these sections is a spot for "notes" and the other spot is listed as "gratitude". Rinse and repeat through December 2020.

--A few pages of "notes" (7 pages, one sided)

--last page is a list of holidays for the year.

--The planner wraps up with a back page that says, "Live Well. Laugh Often. Love Much. This is Life, Well-Designed".

--Another card stock page, then the back cover- clear plastic like the front cover.
___________________________________________

I like the larger size. This is 8.5"x11". It gives me more space to write. I found that sometimes I do not just need a space to write down what I have to do, but also what I have done. It is nice to look over prior pages and see all that I have accomplished. I utilize bullet points and check marks. Sometimes I am more productive in my day (personal and work) when I make a point to jot down what I have done, and crossing things off list on what I determined ahead of time that needed to be done. I feel a little more personal and accountable for my day. Often days go by in a blur, and it is all to easy to overlook tasks that need to be accomplished. Another thing is that it easy to overlook how much I actually do get done. So having something to look at and to interact with, I feel more connected and satisfied.

I would like to see this planner have a few extra pages for notes. I would also like to see a pocket. All that would require it to make the front and/or back cover be doubled and closed up on two sides (since one side is already closed due to binding). It would allow little scraps of paper, notes, envelopes, receipts, or whatever to be stored. I currently have a planner that has that area as an option to use like that, and I find i use it all the time. I also make use of binder clips, paper clips, and sticky pads to keep myself organized within the planner. So the addition of a pocket would just add to the experience. I will likely make my own for this upcoming year by using clear tape to make a pocket using the front cover and the next page which is made of stock card (thick paper, almost cardboard like).

Things that it doesn't have that you might be curious about: Doesn't include contacts page, moon phases, time zone map, nor count up/count down on days of the year. For example, my current planner tells me 298/67 (298th day of year, 67 days left). Not a deal breaker, just a little detail that some planners have.

My personal nit-picking: the front page after plastic cover is an attractive "frosted tile" design. There is a coordinating ribbon that states that it is a Day Designer 2020 Planner. Ok, so that is the branding, but it kinda doesn't need to be there. The back page is just the frosted tile design with nothing branded on it. I think it would be more attractive and classy looking if that branding ribbon logo was taken off the upper right front cover OR just moved to the back cover. Pretty much once you buy a planner, you know it is a planner-- so no need to say "planner" on it. Or at least not on front. My current beloved planner doesn't have that anywhere on front or back, and it looks better for it. Again, that I conceded that this observation and suggestion may be a nit picking one, and I do not weigh that (heavily) into rating.

Overall, it is set up how I like it- Ability to have a full glance at a calendar month (typical layout- Sunday through Saturday), followed by being able to view the entire week in the layout of Monday through Sunday (with Saturday and Sunday being clumped together). Plenty of space to write, and additional words and such aren't intrusive. Wire binding is wide enough to hold my mechanical pencil. It feels organized and uncomplicated. I am sure to be happy with it this coming year- although lack of pocket is a bummer.

Solid 4-4.5 rating. If I learn anything else, or experience anything worth sharing, I will be back to update.

title: monochrome super tank print only unit, connects via wifi/network, or ethernet or wired USB
text:
This review is for the Epson monochrome super tank ET-M1170 Print Only printer. Just black ink, Just printing. No bells or whistles. In short, works perfectly as described. Read on for various details and thoughts :)

This printer is made to be set up for wireless printing, and can also be connected via ethernet cable (not included) for wired network connection. If you prefer or need to have it wired to a desktop computer or laptop, then you will need a USB to printer cable- also not included. What is include for almost $300? printer, big bottle of ink, power cord, printed instructions, and installation CD.

Printed instructions state that if you do not have a CD/DVD drive, then and internet connection is required to obtain the product software. Other than that, the set up is easy enough. Read directions first, and remember.. don't drink the ink (yes, that is in the instructions!).

The instructions are well written and easy to follow. Basically, unbox and take off tape; don't get too handsy with internal parts (ie do not touch flat white cable, translucent cable, or ink tubes). Add ink- don't drink it, don't squeeze bottle. Plug power cord in. Follow instructions for "charging ink" (this will eat up a portion of your ink). Load paper. Install software- follow onscreen instructions to get it connected wirelessly, etc. Learn about mobile and voice activated printing, if you want. As well as registering product. Print test page, and you are good to go.

The "ET-M1170 Print Only" printer takes up some but not a lot of desk real estate. I like that it is a box without anything open or hanging off from it other than power cord. Paper trays are closed up, prints come out on top. The overall footprint is roughly 13.5"x14.5"x6".

But since it is wireless, it can be plugged in anywhere that you have a plug and a little bit of space. Currently, I have it in my kitchen as I find a better place for it to live. I like that I can just unplug it and store it somewhere for when it is not in use, if I so choose. AND, when I do plug it in and turn it on, there is no hassle with getting it to print. I had sat at my computer, elected to print a recipe, and I quickly scooted off to my kitchen around the where is was just finishing printing 6 pages. It took only the time from hitting print, getting out of my computer chair, stepping over a lab (ok, rubbing her belly real quick), and taking 20 steps to the kitchen and it was done.

Ink well is securely closed, and seemingly air tight. Ink bottle to tank connection is a pressure release. Once bottle is out, that part is mostly to totally closed up. Then there is a flip latch that locks over the port, followed by another basic cover which is part of overall casing design. So I dont see it splashing, ever. Not that I have tried, but I have moved it all over the house, and not entirely too carefully.

No info screen- just a few buttons. Very simple, which you may or may not like.

High-capacity 250-sheet paper tray; auto 2-sided printing; rear tray for specialty media. I have just used it to print basic stuff, primarily recipes. Lots of paper loads into bottom paper tray drawer. Prints come out directly on top. I have not yet had a need for the upper rear tray which I imagine is for single feed stuff like envelopes and special paper.

saying again.. THERE IS A LARGE CAPACITY PAPER TRAY ON THE BOTTOM. This is the main paper tray, you flip open front facing cover, pull out paper tray, make paper side adjustments to fit width, add stack of paper, close cover. The TOP rear TRAY is for special paper/projects. Less likely to be used. Also not noticeable until you need it. ALL prints land on top of printer.

There are options to have printer do its thing via voice activation. There is also a way to print using various devices from anywhere. I have this set up on my Google Pixel 3xl using Google cloud. Lots of options if you are so inclined. If not, it is perfectly fine basic printer. It prints clearly- both words and images. I wouldn't use this if your main interest is for image quality. It has a good enough rendering, but not super sharp. I use cheap paper, so that is part of it.

Why'd I get this? I wondered if having a black ink only wireless printer would be better than our Canon color printer/copier/scan combo that I almost never use because it is always low on ink- and always seems to be trouble to get it to print wirelessly. I just want to print. WITH THIS, I can just print. I have not yet had a problem getting something to print. That is a first in many many years. So my frustration level has gone way down since this came into my life. I can also carry out some projects that have been on the back burner, so to speak. There is a huge host of project and recipes I want to print out, but haven't had the desire to use up multiple small ink cartridges for my binder making hobby. I almost never ever need a color copy of something, so it is kind of refreshing to have a monotone printer whose sole task is to print me black and white goodies off the internet- with promise to to able to print 6000 pages before ink runs out. Only caveat being that the first ink bottle will produce less copies because a portion of the ink is used towards priming the machine.

It is a lot of money (to me), but everyone's working budget is different. This one is print only. Black ink only. If that is all you really need, then this might be a good option for you. If you really need to copy/scan/fax with color, and have a menu display, then I would look elsewhere. I don't see being unhappy with this if this is the style you want. So far, so good- for me. I'm at a 4.5 stars, but will give it 5 for now as so far it is doing all that it says it does, and set up was straightforward, with clear directions.

Supervised by my 17 year old kitten, I have some pictures during set up and of the printer over the past few days.

I keep up with my reviews, and enjoy trying to help others make informed decisions. Since this will need a lot more printing to really see how it does over time, I will continue to take notes and will come back to update as I learn more.

title: Functional little budget friendly planner
text:
This planner is pretty much as described in the listing. The front cover is a plastic pocket with a design card slid in. You can do as you want with this- keep it in, take it out- replace it with what you want, or use it to store a few extra pieces of paper. The next few pages before the calendar begins has a "quick reference" page that includes a spot to jot down personal information, emergency information, and family/friends information. Next couple of pages has a "yearly overview" and "holidays" listing. The next two pages are lined pages for contact information. Then it proceeds into the month calendar followed by weekly pages (2 pages- all within one view for that week). At the back of the book, just after the calendar finishes up there are 10 pages (front and back, + one side of a page) that are blank, lined pages for whatever. A one page thicker card stock completes the planner that includes a map of the United States, the capitol of each state, and the time zones. The wire spiral binding diameter is large enough to comfortably hold a mechanical pencil or pen. The planner comes with little sticky tabs with the months printed on them.

I typically use a mechanical pencil or an Ultra Fine tip Sharpie in my day to day use. I currently have a mechanical pencil attached to the spiral binding. However for the purpose of this review, I decided to try out a Sharpie so as to give you an indication of how the paper handles the ink saturation. While the paper is thicker than a typical legal pad, the ink of the Sharpie does bleed through. Not terribly, but enough to plan to just keep on using my mechanical pencil. This is not a negative for me, unless I was expecting it given the product description: "The planner is resistant to the most passionate artist giving reduced bleeding,"...
(I intend to include pictures)

In summation, I like this little planner. It is better than I anticipated, and I am using it daily to jot down what I need to do, or to keep track of what I did. I like that month sticky tabs came with it, for better organization and quick reference. I added in use of binder clips, a rubber band, a paper clip, and a stack of sticky notes to further assist me in making use of this planner. The larger full month view is set up like a typical calendar- Sunday through Saturday (I have seen some run Monday through Sunday, and that is the worst for a full month viewing). I really like that the weekly section is all within one view. On the weekly view it runs, Monday through Sunday, with Saturday and Sunday sharing a block. And that works very well. I have seen many that go into a second page, and that does not help a visual person like myself. If I can see it in an organized manner, then I can copy it to memory. This layout is solid, and happens to have enough space to jot down notes, and really use it in an active manner. Nice job!

title: 2022 book was better
text:
This is a pricy faux leather planner. I loved the 2022 book so much that I paid for this higher priced 2023 planner. I won't be back for 2024 at the current rate of increase.

The inside of the binder is the same as last year. I could use more pages for notes but it wasn't a deal breaker. However, the cost of the planner increased while the value of the cover drastically decreased.

The 2022 planner's bookcover was flawless. The faux leather looked and felt nearly real. The cover was perfectly adhered to the cardboard hardback. My very well used planner looks to be in perfect condition a year later. It was a professionally done book that looks and feels professional in my hand. Last year, I bought the gray.

Unfortunately, this 2023 binder lacks the same quality binding. The cover feels very cheap and thin. It's not adhered to the cardboard hardback at all; so, you see ripples in the cover when it's open and closed. I'm highly disappointed with the extreme lack of quality and professionalism. This 40 dollar binder is dollar general quality. It's a bait and switch. Now that they have all the great reviews, they didn't feel compelled to maintain or improve the quality with the higher price.

Next year, I'll just go into a store to make sure I get everything I'm paying for. This should've been 1/3 the cost or less. I'm very disappointing to say the least. Note, if you are solely concerned with what's inside the planner, you should be fine. But, I need the entire planner to reflect its cost and the very thing you see 1st is annoyingly sub par and I don't have confidence in its durability as a result. I no longer have faith in the company and won't be returning for a 2024 planner.

title: Beautiful mini printer that is truly mobile due to unique built in battery...
text:
[[VIDEOID:2d3d7f669ea9053d0f89c84295106dc5]] THE GOOD:
---------------
* In terms of build quality. This is solid. Good heft to it. The type of build quality you'd expect from Apple, Google, Samsung, etc.
* Aesthetically, the nice rectangular minimalist design is very pleasing to the eye.
* When you are done printing, the clear photo tray can be stacked on top of the printer magnetically. That is awesome! I reviewed another version by HPRT and when you're done with that, the tray is a separate thing that you have to manage. This Liene design is so much better.
* Built in rechargeable battery makes this tiny thing truly a portable printer! My other HPRT unit does not have a built in battery.
* Can print from PC with USB. This is the only option that doesn't require connecting to the Printer's Wi-fi hotspot. Which means the internet on your PC won't be cut off, you can multi-task.
* Can print from PC via Printer's Wifi hotspot.
* Can print from IOS or Android using the Printer's Wifi hotspot. However, unlike the HPRT, where you absolutely need to use their app, the Liene printer is not tied to any apps. You can print from any app such as Google Photo. However, more on this below in the important advice section.

THE BAD:
------------
* No AR feature. The HPRT has something called AR video printing. You print an image from a video clip, then the photo comes to life when you scan it. It's pretty cool, but it doesn't work half the time anyway. So maybe it's a good thing this printer didn't include it.
* I thought maybe all these ribbon cartridges are interchangeable, but unfortunately they are not. The HPRT and the Liene cartridges look almost identical, but the HPRT was slightly shorter and would not go into the Liene printer. I'm pretty sure as more of these printers go on the market, there will only be so many variations. Some brands will probably be interchangeable, and some won't. HPRT and Liene are NOT.
* No Bluetooth.
* Not a network printer. So whether on your pc or mobile phones, you can only print via the printer's wifi hotspot. So when you're printing from your phone or pc, you have no internet to multi-task. Again, the only option that doesn't require the printer's hotspot, is a direct usb connection to your pc.
* Paper and cartridge refill are sold as a set for just $20, and you can print 40 photos with that. So it's .50 a piece. But I'm listing this under bad because HPRT has their combo for $20 also, but they give you 54 photos. So it seems the Liene cartridge has a lower capacity.

IMPORTANT ADVICE:
-------------------------
* If you want to print from a different photo app on your android phone such as Google Photo. Be sure to install MOPRIA app from the android store first. It's a service, it's not an app that needs to be open. It's equivalent to printer drivers for windows. So it's like printing drivers for android. Do this and save yourself a lot of headache. Technically, this printer should be able to print from any android app out the box. That's what it advertises. Even in the manual, it says to go to Mopria website for help if you can't see the printer as an option. But once my phone was connected to the printer, I do see it as an option in my Google Photo, so I thought everything was fine. However, when I tried to print the photo. I would get printer error under the printer spooler notice. Once you get this error, this also messes up the Liene Photo App. So if you go back to the Liene app and try to print a photo, it will not work. Uninstalling the app, re-installing, restarting your phone, nothing will work. You will need to push the reset button on the back of the printer, it is right above the power input. Once I reset the printer to factory default, I was able to print from the Liene app again. Then I tried again with Google Photo, and again I get the printing error, and again the Liene app no longer works. LOL! So once again, I reset the printer, went through setting up the Liene app for a 3rd time, and everything printed fine. But now I install the Mopria app from the playstore, and everything is printing perfectly from the Google Photo app.

In conclusion, this is a beautiful printer with some drawbacks such as no bluetooth, can't add as network, and the manual could have been more useful by instructing us to download the Mopria app, but it also has features I haven't seen from other printers such as a built in battery, could magnetic stow away tray design. And although it was a headache to figure out, you CAN free yourself from the Liene app, just download Mopria first! You'll notice I mentioned HPRT a lot because these are my only two experiences. If I had to choose one, I choose Liene easily. Overall, I'll rate this 4-Stars.

The AR feature in which I described as magic in my review below worked for one day. LOL! What you do is you select a video clip from your phone in the HeyPhoto app, you trim a 15 second clip of your video, then you choose a still image from that video to print. Then when you use the HeyPhoto app to scan that photo, it'll play the clip. It's pretty cool, just as the advertised. But for whatever reason, this app has stopped working. We uninstalled and reinstalled app too, so now I think we lost the effects for the previous photos we printed. Still does not work. This product has given so much headache from day 1. It's still good just to print regular photos. I'm downgrading to 2-Stars.

JAN 26, 2022 UPDATE:
---------------------------
Okay, so just as suspected, my issues in my original review were all due to a faulty ribbon cassette. I've since gotten a replacement ribbon, and the printer is working fine. I still believe they should go back to the drawing board and re-write their manual to include troubleshooting tips. I've uploaded a video to show you the printing process. It lays down a single color film with each passage. The picture comes out quite impressive, but of course it's a little dull compared to how it shows on your phone. So I suggest you only print pictures that are bright and colorful on your phone. Those will show up best when printed out. The AR feature is also very neat. It's like a magic trick. I think with the invention of the smartphone, we are printing less and less. We just look at photos on our phones. So I think a product like this makes a lot of sense. It's for printing occasionally, and for something that won't be used often, it's nice that it won't take up much desktop space. I'm bumping this up to 4-Stars.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
-----------------------
Well, this has been a disaster so far. I got this printer because I really liked their little 3x2 zink printer. Now this 4x6 printer requires a ribbon. This is the year 2022, I don't think I'm the only one who is in the dark about ribbon technology. Not that I'm a young buck, but the last time I dealt with ribbons was in the 80's and 90's. What I'm getting at is there should be some introduction in the manual explaining how this ribbon prints on their paper, and a section on troubleshooting issues. None of this is in the manual. On my first print, the printer made all sorts of sounds, then the button started blinking red, I knew I was in trouble. The ribbon got all wrinkled and crumpled up inside. A troubleshooting section on how to remove a ribbon jam would have been nice.

This is a vine review, but I paid for their ribbon/paper package in order to test this out and write this review. I consider myself pretty good with tech, and I'm 99.99% sure this wasn't user error. When I removed the ribbon from its package, it seemed a little loose to me, but what can I do? Should I adjust it, should I tighten it, how do I do that? There doesn't seem to be any moving parts on the ribbon. Nothing can be adjusted. Troubleshooting tips didn't come with the ribbon package either. So I gave their product the benefit of the doubt, that nothing's wrong. I pushed the ribbon into the printer and I heard a click, so all is well. On the first print, everything got jammed up with no troubleshooting manual to turn to.

Bottom line, documentation needs to be better. They need to think in advance and anticipate these issues like every printer on the market does. This is 1-Star so far until I get this sorted out.

On the very first day with this GBC, the manual feed jammed. So the adjustment I need to make is to go back to opening envelopes again, unfolding them neatly and letting them pile up. Once it gets close to 230, I then let this GBC have at it. I don't trust myself to be that disciplined. LOL! I thought I could have the best of both worlds. I thought I could use this horizontal 230 sheet feature, but also continue with my usual habits of shredding entire envelopes. But I can't, the manual capacity of 8 sheet is just too weak. These digits are hidden, that's why you don't see them on your package. I then have to manually delete them, which is a hassle. title: If you're a newbie to barcode scanners, read my review...
text:
So with a lot of these barcode scanners, they provide you with a usb cable to connect to your PC for corded operation, or USB receiver for wireless 2.4. Many also have bluetooth connection, which this version DOES NOT have. However, the cradle feature makes bluetooth moot, so I can understand why that feature is omitted. There is also no usb receiver because the cradle is your usb receiver, it does double duty. You plug the cradle into your PC, and as long as it's plugged in, the scanner is wirelessly connected. Even better yet, when you rest your scanner, it gets charged.

Here are some noteworthy things for newbies, like myself. I've never owned a barcode scanner before, but these products all assume you have. I assumed like other gadgets, you download some sort of software or app to view the codes you've scanned. That is not the case at all. I found out through lots of googling and YT videos that they work like keyboard inputs. You can open any program on your pc where you can see the blinking cursor, such as word, notepad, excel, or even in a search browser. Wherever you put the blinking cursor, aka, insertion point, that is where the codes will show up. You can set it up to show up instantaneously the moment you scan, or you can use the scanner in storage mode, then upload everything later.

Because there are no apps or software to download like with traditional gadgets, all the settings and set-ups are done by scanning barcodes. Tera gives you a little manual with barcodes in it. Each barcode is for a particular setting, but it is not a complete manual. You'll need to go to Tera's site to download a more complete manual. Even still, the manual they have on their site doesn't seem to cover all the possibilities of this scanner. For example, you'll find out yourself that when you scan a USPS package, it'll add 9 digits/characters in front of the tracking number that's on your package. These digits are hidden, that's why you don't see them on your package. What should be 22 digits, ends up being 31. I then have to manually delete the first 9 digits, that is a hassle. Well, there is a setting which instructs the scanner to omit the first number digits, or the last number of digits. In my case, I'd like it to omit the first 9 characters. The barcode for this setting is not in the included manual. So I downloaded their bigger manual on their site, but the most you can delete is the first 4 digits. I contacted Tera about needing to delete the first 9 characters, and they emailed back with a barcode setting for me that will accomplish this. I asked them where did they get that code? They say they got it from other manuals that were made for other languages. SMH. LOL! So you see, their manual for the English market currently is incomplete. Now here is another issue... If I'm scanning a mixture of packages from USPS, UPS, Fed Ex, etc., omitting the first 9 digits will cause me issues with UPS packages. Because with UPS packages, there are no hidden characters that will show up, so you'll end up erasing the first 9 digits of the actual tracking number. So Tera told me if I want to go back, I have to put the scanner back to factory default settings. So the best solution is to actually buy two scanners. LOL!

I did purchase a different scanner by Symcode, that came with a more robust manual of barcode settings. It allowed me to hide up to 16 digits! That scanner is now my dedicated USPS scanner, and this Tera scanner is for UPS. If you're interested in that Symcode scanner, here is the Amazon link: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B092MB8BXZ/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

In conclusion, I really don't have high demands from these scanners. All I needed was the removal of some characters from USPS packages, which this Barcode scanner can do, but only after contacting customer support. The Symcode version had the answers to my needs in their manual. Like I said, this Tera has been dedicated for UPS packages, it's been put through the ringer, and it does a wonderful job. But I'll have to dock 1 star for their incomplete manual.

4-Stars!

title: If you're looking for a spacious platform scale to ship big boxes, look no further...
text:
Wow, this scale is magnificent! It took me a while to make my decision because I did my research. I needed something with a big platform, but I also wanted something reputable. I didn't want a white label scale from overseas. White label means a product is mass produced in a factory somewhere overseas. Then a bunch of sellers in the US buy the same scale, but put their own logo on it. That's why you often see identical scales on Amazon, but from different sellers with different logos. Once I visited Ohaus' website, my search was over. They've been in the scale business for over a hundred years! And the SD75LAM did not disappoint. Here are some noteworthy things:

* Heavy duty. This thing screams quality at 30 lbs. Not lightweight cheap stuff.
* The platform is truly 20.5 x 15.7 x 3 inches. No measurement trickery. I noticed with other scales, sellers will measure with the lcd unit attached, then it'll say in fine print, "actual platform dimension..." No trickery here. This platform is truly spacious. If you often ship boxes, small to large, you will love this. Luggage as well! We've been using an ultra-75 by ultraship for the longest time, and often struggled with balancing big boxes and luggage on it's 8x8 platform. In my pictures, that's a HD shipping box that is 21x16x15. We've been shipping a lot of those. This large platform scale has made everything so much easier!
* You can attached a supplied power adapter to the LCD unit, or use three C-size batteries and go cordless.
* Not for mailing letters, or anything below .05g. It will not register. You should still get a dedicated scale for very lightweight mail.
* In KG mode, it uses two decimal points. However, in LB mode, it uses only one decimal point. We ship medium size boxes using UPS and keep them below 50 lbs. So for example, in comparison to another small scale we have, which uses three decimals, If a package is 25.232 lbs, the Ohaus will say 25.3 lbs. This is perfect, doesn't really matter because when you use UPS, Fed-Ex, etc., they round up to the next whole lb. So you would need to buy a 26 lb. label anyway. But to get this precision is very comforting.

When I don't care for a product, I don't bother to register for their warranty either cause you got to give your email, address, phone number, etc.. After several sessions with this Ohaus scale, I went to their website and registered for my warranty. That means I love it! 5-Stars!

title: Excellent network scanner, no need to be near your PC...
text:
Truly a network scanner. I take my review photos in the garage. I plugged this thing in near my workbench, and set everything up without a PC. The onscreen instructions are self explanatory, but here are some noteworthy things...

* Scanning to your NAS: I hit a snag in connecting to my NAS. For whatever reason, the Epson will only take at most 20 characters for your NAS' password. My password had 24 characters, so I had to change the password to less than 20 to make it work.

* Scanning to 3rd party platforms like Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, etc.: You first need to register with Epson Connect, and add those accounts from within the Epson connect site. Once you do that, Dropbox will then show up as an option on the LCD. You cannot simply input your Dropbox credentials on the LCD like you can with a NAS. BTW, One Drive currently not supported.

* Scanning to Flashdrive: You can do this by plugging in a flashdrive in the back of the scanner.

* You can have 48 presets. If you want to scan to Dropbox, scan to your NAS, scan to different folders, have different page settings like one-sided or double-sided, etc. You can create presets so you don't have to input the same info over and over.

* You can also scan to your phone using the Epson Smart Panel app.

Very versatile, and a brand you can trust. We love it! 5-Stars!

title: High quality mobile whiteboard, please read my review if you are new to mobile boards like me...
text:
I've never owned a mobile white-board before, so some of my assumptions were different than reality. Here are two wrong assumptions I made, which I did not dock any stars for, since one should never assume. LOL!

1. The flipping action is simply to get to the other side of the board. It cannot remain horizontal like a table. There is no locking mechanism to keep it in table form. For some reason, I had assumed you could do that. Gather around with your generals to look at the map. LOL! You can't do that.

2. When they say adjustable... I assumed some sort of rail system where you slide the board up and down, and lock it in place anywhere from 59 to 70 inches. In reality, you can only choose between 2 height locations... 59 inch or 69 inch. Their stock photos say 70 inch, but their manual says 69 inch. Anyway, whenever you want to change from one height to the other, you need to remove 4 screws with an allen key they provide, or use your own screwdriver with an allen bit. Then reinstall the screws at the new height.

Despite my incorrect assumptions, I really like this mobile whiteboard. The bars and poles are made of some sort of metal and feels very sturdy and high quality. The caster wheels are plastic, but for something light like this, it is good enough. The caster wheels can lock too. The board has nice smooth corners molded by ABS plastic, and the fact that it's magnetic was a pleasant surprised. There are some accessories that the manual did not even talk about, but after playing with it for a bit, I realize they are clips/clamps to clip things to the board. I also found these little rubber feet that the manual doesn't discuss. I realized they are for you to cover the screw holes of the height location you do not use. View my pictures to see what I'm talking about. This item is 5-stars!

title: Retro looking device that prints really fast...
text:
[[VIDEOID:8721296286be9e253e7e0a4e6ba09249]] Oct 17, 2020 UPDATE:
-------------------------
I subtracted a star because I thought the manual didn't include any website, but I stand corrected. The web address is located on the second to last page. I did skim through that page before, I probably missed it because my mind was looking for an address with the word "Comer." The website is completely different than the word Comer. In any case, I will give this product 5 stars now.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
----------------------
Out the box, it caught my eye immediately. I wondered when was the last time I bought any tech device that was beige? LOL! I don't know if it was intentional, but I dig the retro feel. It looks like something from the 1980's, like some sort of bulky accessory to go with your beige Commodore 64. Or, a 1960's movie prop that's supposed to represent tech from the year 3000. LOL! The name Comer also seem to allude to Commodore. Anyway, love the looks! This thing was easy to set-up and it prints super fast! Watch my video to see how to set up a roll, and a demo of how fast it spits out a label.

However, something that's annoying is this company's lack of online presence. My computer did not install drivers automatically, but the package included a usb mini disc. Who uses cd/dvd drives nowadays? I don't, so I looked at their manual for a website, but couldn't find any. Then I searched online for Comer, but could not find anything either. So I resorted to searching "drivers" in the Amazon Q&A, and finally found an answer posted by their rep. I can't post the link, so just search Amazon's Q&A, and you'll see it. The website doesn't have the word COMER in it either, no wonder you can't find them. So even though I got this thing to work and I like it, I wonder why would customers purchase from an unknown brand who cannot be found online, versus from reputable brands such as Brother, Dymo, etc. If you want to sell in the US, make your website easier to find. How about providing a web address in the manual? This does not give consumers confidence that you'll be around in the future when they may need tech or warranty support. The product is fine, subtracting 1 star for the lack of online presence.

title: Not 100% accurate due to the possibility of user error...
text:
[[VIDEOID:f82da4a94fda65fac3db935b76c4c46d]] Right off the bat, something you need to know... this is not 100% fool proof in terms of detecting every bill you feed because the USER plays a vital role. This thing is pretty accurate, but if you experiment with it long enough, you'll start to see how it doesn't properly count from time to time. And it has all to do with how the user feeds it. Did you feed it with too much force? Were the bills aligned or staggered? In my video, I demonstrate how it can detect fake money (paper) among real bills, then I also demonstrate how it can count incorrectly. You'll see how I'm trying to re-create scenarios that would cause the counter to count incorrectly.

At the end of the day, if you're using this for your business, and it's a fast past environment, I recommend you run the bills 2 to 3 times to make sure you're getting a consistent count. I mainly want to use it for the counterfeit detection feature. For counting, we'll be counting manually and double check with the machine. We won't solely depend on the machine. This isn't something you could multi-task with. It's not a good idea to be talking on the phone while feeding the bills. For accurate counting, your undivided attention will be required. I'm very surprised there is no instructions or advice in the manual on how to properly place the bills.

title: A scanner as well as a conversation piece...
text:
From the hardware to the packaging, everything about this item feels premium. My intention was to make this guy my go-to scanner, but the truth is, this is truly for book archiving. For regular scanning, the process of clearing your table, laying your paper down, straightening it a little, then flip it over, then take it away, then lay the next one down, etc., is a bit tedious versus feeding your papers through a traditional scanner and be done with it. So what it is for me is a conversation piece at the desktop, but it also doubles as a nifty table lamp. I'll use it to scan papers occasionally when I don't feel like walking to my traditional scanner.

One important tip I do have... The first documents I tested out was some of the included Czur manuals. The pages have a sheen to them, so they were glossy/shiny. The glare caused the image to not show any text, so my first reaction was... Wow, this is terrible. Why would I do this, then spend hours on the software to fix things when I can just use a normal scanner? Then I realized the included side lights must have a purpose. The side lights aren't even in the listing stock photos, so it was a surprise. But it turns out, they are very important for documents and manuscripts with glare. For those type of documents, you'll want to use the side lights, your scans will be perfect with no glare. When scanning, you have to choose one or the other, both lights will not be on at the same time. The side light is pretty neat, it connects by a magnetic port, and it has its own on/off touch button.

Lastly, there is an included foot peddle and a black desktop pad to lay your documents on. The peddle is mainly for scanning books while standing. Your hands can continue flipping pages, while your foot taps away. As for the black pad, you're supposed to use it with the scanner. Supposedly, its material helps the scanner calibrate. I don't see anything special about it. There are no thin electronics hidden in it or anything. Just seems like a normal business or desktop pad you can buy anywhere. At my desktop, I have one of those huge black gaming pads that spans across the entire table. It had no problems scanning documents with this pad. I think any black pad will do, but I keep the Czur pad underneath this pad. This way it doesn't get dirty or messed up, and I can always move it on top should the scanner require it.

title: Good value for a 4x6 label printer...
text:
This type of printer is actually foreign to me. I didn't even know the lingo for the labels used in this type of printer was called "fanfold" labels. I've only had experience with the 4x6 rolls used in Dymo printers. So naturally, I also didn't know these types of printers DO NOT house the labels. The labels are fed from the back, but sit outside exposed. You can easily make a tray, or search for "fanfold label holders" on Amazon. Some holders double as a holder for the rolls too, so you can actually use the rolls with this printer as well. I still prefer my Dymo because it's less clutter. But this will be a good back-up for the desktop in my room. I've never had to print in batches, so to avoid clutter, I won't be setting the fanfold labels behind the printer. title: Awesome 600 dpi Network Scanner...
text:
[[VIDEOID:3b762caf92d3470f572b7f6b09bf3455]] This scanner is a pleasure to use. The 7 inch LCD interface is awesome, very intuitive and user friendly. Right off the bat, I want to correct someone else's review saying this thing is only 300 dpi. For some reason on the home screen, Plustek is not allowing us to scroll to 600 dpi, the most you can scroll to is 300 dpi, but right beneath is the "ADVANCED SETTINGS." If you go in there, you can see that the 400 and 600 dpi options are there.

Another complaint I read about is the speed. If you take the time to set-up your presets, meaning "often used jobs or settings," then scanning will be very quick. At the end of every scan, there is a prompt asking if you want to assigned current settings as a "Job," select yes or no. Anyway, you can save up to 6 of these jobs. I have one going to my email, one going to my network NAS, I have one set for 600 dpi for photos, etc. Watch my video to see how fast 5 pages set to duplex scanning at 300 dpi gets scanned and uploaded. Technically it's even much faster because once you grab all the papers, you can go about your business, you don't need to wait for the "Sending Success" notification. If you don't set up these "jobs," and always start from scratch with your selections such as dpi, jpeg or pdf, location, inputting email, nas IP address, dropbox, etc. If you have to go through those settings each time you scan, I can see why someone would complain it's "slow." Just save your jobs, trust me, this scanner is fast enough for your home.

I have a Scansnap Fujitsu 500XI, but I need to fire up the PC and open the software to use it. I bought it to digitize decades of family photos. But for just a few documents, sometimes I don't feel like going to the garage where my office is, and I'll let things pile up. Which is why this Plustek is now set on the entryway table where all the daily mail gets stacked. Now I can quickly scan something important and trash it, instead of letting it pile up saying, "I'll scan it later." Network scanners are expensive. I can't test or speak for office use environment, but for home use, this is perfect for us.

text: This is a great set of ink replacement cartridges. They are the same size as the original cartridges and produce the same color quality in your prints. Each cartridge comes individually wrapped to protect it while in storage. There is a wedge of triangular yellow foam included with each cartridge to protect the plastic attachment on the end. title: Great For Teachers
text:
This is a great set of dry erase markers that is perfect for bringing a little more color into the classroom. To activate the markers, you have to depress the tip a couple times against a hard surface. The ink then seeps into the tip and you are able to write. The instructions on the side of the markers say you have to wait for a minute, but the marker is ready to write faster than that. This system is good because it means the markers are less likely to dry out while you keep them in storage.

You are able to see through the body of the marker so it's easy to tell when it is running out of ink. This set has 12 colors and 5 markers of each color. In addition to classrooms, this set is also a lot of fun for children who can create works of art on dry erase boards and then quickly wipe them off and start again. It makes less of a mess than when they work with watercolors or paints.

It's nice having plenty of colorful markers on hand for lectures or for art projects. The markers leave sharp, highly visible lines. This is a great set that would be a thoughtful gift for any teachers in your life.

title: Affordable Replacement Ink Cartridges
text: This is a great set of affordable ink cartridges. These cartridges provide a print quality that is indistinguishable from your original cartridges. I included photos of each cartridge alongside a tape measure so you can verify that the dimensions are compatible with your printer. The set includes yellow, magenta, cyan, black and PG black. The PG black is larger than the other four cartridges. Note that the set does not include photo blue, but you can buy that cartridge separately. If you regularly print a lot of pictures, it is nice to have extra ink cartridges on hand for convenient replacement.

title: Quality You Expect from Xerox
text: This is a really great black and white printer that is ideal for offices and writers. If you like to print out a manuscript of a couple hundred pages, you need a printer like this. Toner cartridges last a much longer time than the tiny black cartridges that come with color printers. The printer can obviously scan in full color and the images are great to work with. The printer comes very well packaged and is sure to be in good working order after shipment. Take note that when you prepare the toner cartridge, you have to pull out a plastic ribbon from the side of the cartridge. Pulling the ribbon causes a little cloud of ink to be expelled from the side of the cartridge. This is not a big deal, but it's better to do this step over a garbage can or outside. Set up is easy and print quality is superior. This is a great printer for the home or office!

title: Get Organized With This Great Planner
text: Everybody thinks they are too busy to get organized, but it's amazing how much of a difference it can make in your life to simply write down your appointments. It takes a lot of energy to try to remember all your upcoming tasks, but when you write down your lists you're able to sleep better without worrying that anything will be forgotten. title: Get Organized With a 2020 Monthly Planner
text: This is a very well-thought out and organized yearly planner. I like having a planner like this so I can set it down beside my computer and write down appointments as they come up. It is amazing how much more energy you have if you don't try to spend time remembering all your tasks and, instead, rely on an active planner. I've used my phone in the past to get organized, but I stare at the computer screen all day, and there's something satisfying about writing down an important appointment in a planner by hand. title: Compact and Easy to Operate
text: This is a very attractive and compact printer. I like that it is available in a vibrant red rather than the typical boring gray or black of office printers. I also like the symmetrical square shape of this computer which is aesthetically pleasing. The quick start guide sends you to the Canon page where set up instructions are shown in a brief video. Installing the ink cartridges is very easy, they snap into place without any problems. When you are done installing ink cartridges and paper, you download the driver. The whole process takes about 15 minutes depending on the speed of your computer and network. The computer produces fine quality copies and text documents. Great printer at a good price.

title: Durable and Lies Flat
text:
I've worn through a carpet with my office chair before. The simple act of pushing a chair back to stand up and pulling it forward to sit down can absolutely destroy your floors. It doesn't happen overnight, but you'll see considerable wear and tear after a few months.

These days, my office is in a room with a wood floor. I restored the wood floor over a period of a few weeks. This entailed getting on my hands and knees and scraping, sanding, and painting the floor. I'm not inclined to lose all that hard work to scrapes from an office chair.

My main concern was that this item would have a curve to it when I pulled it out of the box. That turned out not to be the case as you can see in the above photo. The moment it arrives, you can uncoil it and have it lie flat. Be a little careful when you unwrap the item, it springs open and if you're cutting the plastic wrap with a knife it could be dislodged from your hand.

The material is durable and doesn't make noise when you pull your chair across it. One side is smooth and the other side has a texture. The size is as advertised. This is a good choice for a home or office.

title: Easy to set up, not high end but good sound quality
text:
Big number buttons on this are easy to see/ press. The buttons feel decent and not cheap. The screen is reminiscent of the old school first color cellphones that came out- very basic. As far as I can tell you can't upload your own screensaver but you can use one of the few they have on the handsets. The phones have all sorts of call block/ call screening features and the one oddity I see with those are that when I'm in the settings, multiple options under the call block setting have all the same function. You click like 3 different tabs and each of them do the exact same thing. Kind of weird programming. That being said, these are a great value when you break the price down and divide it by 4. The price per handset is fair for a good working device.

Sound quality on the earpiece and the speakerphone are both very clear, nothing like the first horrible speakerphone speakers back in the day. I think the speakerphone is even clearer than a lot of cellphones I've had. The earpiece isn't as clear as an expensive cellphone would be but for the price point, it's good and usable.

Things I love: Unlike old cordless phones, these take 2 AAA rechargeable batteries so if these ever go out- you can just swap them with new rechargeables! No more battery packs. Another thing I love is I can pair my personal cell and my work cell to it via bluetooth. I don't use a landline but I wanted the ability to answer my cell anywhere in the house and this was a great way to do it! It only allows you to hook 2 cellphones to it at a time FYI.

Things that could be improved: They could add a earpiece jack so you can wire an earpiece on this and clip it on your pocket. These also do not feature a clip to clip to your belt or pocket. I'm not counting against them for this as they didn't claim it had these features. Just features I'd love to see on these.

Another thing to know- these don't hook to the internet or anything of the sort so no auto-updating on the time most likely. You have to set the date and time yourself so it's not syncing with anything of course. Nothing new for most of us familiar with cordless phones but just figured I'd note it.

Overall, I'm impressed with the price point. It's not a super high-end phone set but all the handsets work perfectly and I set them all up without having to read the manual.

Problem: The film keeps wrapping around the rear rolls

This is a particular problem with lighter films, and it’s because of the effects of static electricity. You can gently pull the wrapped film off the rear rolls by running the machine in reverse.

To prevent the problem:
* Laminate in a continuous feed – The weight will help hold the film away from the rear rolls
* Leave a few inches of extra film between each sheet if encapsulating – This also adds weight, which mitigates the effects of static trying to pull the film back
* Ground your machine – Not only is this a safety issue, but it also helps drain off static from partial conductors
*Use tinsel – this is the most common way of neutralizing static, but make sure you choose one with a metal core, stretch it tight, place it 0.25 inches from what you want to neutralize and give it free airspace
