title: Beautiful design, except...
text:
This table is beautiful, sturdy, of a very nice design and quality. Very well thought-out. Which is why it is incomprehensible how they overlooked the fact that the book stand simply does not fit in the slot provided. I have noticed that there is a padded buffer tape running along the inside edge of the slot. I imagine if I peeled that tape off, the book stand would probably fit. But then, I would no longer have a proper, safe support for my phone or tablet, when I want to use those... Somewhat disappointing, especially since everything else about this table is so perfect. Even the book stand itself is of a fairly nice quality.

The legs of the table are sturdy and well-built. The supporting slats that go on the bed have tips that turn up, like skis. This keeps them from getting caught in the bedclothes.

The instructions helped too, because the legs are tightly folded against the underneath of the table and I couldn't figure out how to get them open at first. I didn't want to force things and possibly break them. I checked the instructions, which said to just pull hard (use more strength). So I did.

I love the size, the colors and the materials they used. The slightly textured, leather-like surface provides a nice grip, so things stay stationary and don't tend to slide around on the table-top when you are moving around or moving the table itself around.

I also really enjoy being able to tilt the table-top. It has a narrow lip near the bottom, which keeps papers and canvases from sliding off. Genius! It also comes with a piece you can insert into the bottom slot, to keep your notebook or laptop from sliding off. But I find that is not really necessary because the narrow lip that runs from side to side at the bottom does the job anyway. title: Using as a hospital bed table AND will definitely use it after recovery!
text:
I am shocked at the sturdiness of this table but also all of its features.
I am using it at home in a hospital bed.
The legs easily adjust up and down in height. It tilts nicely (3 positions) no matter the height.

The best part is the non-slip surface. Nothing slides around. We don’t put anything hot (such as plate with warm food) on it directly. We put a silicone pot holder between the plate and table surface. Flatware doesn’t travel. Stays wherever you sit it. I don’t put drink ware on it, so I can’t attest to that ability but that isn’t something the company says can be done anyway.
The table stays in the position you have set it until you change it. The up/down and tilt positions lock/unlock in to place easily. It isn’t a lightweight table. It has some weight to it but that adds to the durability and makes a statement of quality.

I will get a LOT of use after I recover by using it in my (adjustable) bed to do adult coloring books. I’m thrilled with the inserts on the tabletop and the drawer as this will be able to hold my needed supplies. No, the drawer is not big enough to hold a tin full of coloring pencils but there is enough room to hold the colored pencils you’re using on a certain portion of the coloring page you’re working on.
I easily use this to hold my ipad, in the hospital bed, so I don’t have to lay the ipad on my stomach where my incision is. That would be painful.
I bought it at a great price through a Amazon Warehouse sale in “Like New” condition and that’s how it arrived inside of the box as it is packed with the corners protected in styrofoam and then inside of a protective bag. The gorillas at the USPS decided to give it a go at destroying the exterior box but their efforts proved futile - thank goodness. I’m happy I got a deal on it BUT I would have been just as happy with my purchase if I had paid full price. If you find this helpful, please mark it. Not because I get paid by the marking but because it puts a smile on my face knowing I might have helped someone in making a decision to purchase based on what I’ve detailed in my review.

title: Mixed Review...Table size is not as advertised.
text:
False Advertisement: The tabletop is 58 and 3/4 inches long v 23.5 inches......bad...that is false advertisement and technically a breach of contract as it's advertised as 60 x24 inch
Assembly: You must get power drill to set it up. The directions tell you to drill while the table top is flat on the floor or table. DO NOT do that!. The holes don't line up! That is a major manufacturer issue. Best to do it towards the end. Step 4 tells you to drill holes...DO NOT DO IT! Wait till the very end. Logically you would do it then but the pre-drilled manufacturer holes may not line up. Mine did not. You will have to wait till Step 11 to drill those holes...which requires you to get flat on the ground on your back while under the table. One set of the pre-drilled holes on either end may line up with the white underbar. The other side of pre-drilled holes may not line up. If one side lines up, then drill holes with your drill on the side making sure they line up with the white bar......and that requires that you drill through the white bar holes. You will better understand when you get to Step 11 of the instructions. I had 2 buddies of mine...one is an electrical engineer and the other a mechanical engineer. They vouched for it because they said it was a manufacturer issue.

The sticker cable holders didn't stay on pass 1 day. So I will have to get 3M stickers .

Delivery: Delivery was expected in 2 weeks but it arrived the next day after I ordered. Awesome.

So far so good. The mechanics work as of now. But the table dimensions are smaller than what is advertised. Hopefully, it keeps working for a long time.

title: LOVE the Extra Space
text: As an educator, I was given two tables for desks.  I really needed some drawer space, so this helped me put all the smaller things closer to me than in the small file cabinet that's nearby. title: Cute Little Planner
text: This is the smaller version of the larger desk versions of an academic calendar.  I tend to like the bigger ones for my job as a teacher, but this is nice for home.  I put in small things like appointments and notes about repairs I need to have done around the house.

title: A Little Flimsy and Off-Colored
text: Be aware that the color is more pinkish-red than rose gold.  It doesn't match my other rose gold desk accessories at all.  I also found that this is pretty flimsy and I don't know that you would want to put anything to heavy on the shelves.  I'm just using it for papers though, so it works fine so far.

title: Works, but is Tricky
text: This stand is not the prettiest and is a bit bulky, but works well.  I want to say up front that there's nearly no way to put this together without an electric drill.  The screws are really long and they only get it started into the wood.  We could only put in each screw just a little bit and had to finish with a drill.  So far, it's working well.

title: Pretty and Dainty
text: I've been moved into a new classroom which will most likely be my "forever" home until I retire.  I decided to pick up some new desktop accessories to replace the ratty ones I've inherited from other teachers over the last two decades.  This is a small accessory, but works perfectly for a "to do" pad I have and to stack other smaller items.  I don't think you can stack heavy things in this, but it's perfect for notepads, sticky notes, or mail.

title: Feels Light, But Easy to Put Together
text: This is my second cart, as my first is the typical metal, three shelf cart.  My metal cart feels a bit sturdier and can even hold a bit more than this one, but I'm using this one for school.  I like the flat top on it for placing files. I'm not going to put too many heavy items like hardback books or textbooks and I think I'll be fine.  I like this cart, but you should know that it's not as sturdy as it looks.

title: Nice Size and Easy to Transport
text: This is such a nice little cart, that was fairly easy to put together and folds up so easily.  It holds quite a few items as well. The drawback of this cart is that it doesn't maneuver easily, as it only rolls front and back.  You can tip onto the back wheels to swivel, but that quickly wears off the pins in the wheels.  Before I knew it, the pin popped on one of the wheels, so now I need to replace it before I can use it again.  Honestly, I don't know how else to get the wheels to stay on more securely, so I'll be getting a few pins for the inevitability of them continuing to break.

title: Easy to Use and Adjust
text: Like many, I suffer from lower back and sciatica issues.  I have a standing desk, which has helped a lot, but when I sit, I'm always wanting to put my feed up.  I still do, to some degree, as this foot stool is still pretty low.  I think if you want to put your feet up higher, you'll need to get an ottoman.  I like putting up my feet a bit, and I LOVE the massaging capabilities here, but would even love propped up a bit more.  This is really nice though!

title: Really Pretty and Durable
text:
I've had one of these desk pads before and loved it. Through Covid, it got a bit too much hand sanitizer on it, so it has a weird finish on it. I don't think it would affect it at all, normally, but I was constantly using hand sanitizer or Lysol wipes, and the finish (after six months of school), is just a bit matte. I decided to get this one to replace it, as it will match my desk and decor a bit better. The other one is perfectly fine, but I'll put it at my TA desk and flip it over.

Overall, I love these mats. Be careful about signing things with a pen on it. Ink rubs off onto it pretty easily, so I sign things on the desktop and not the pad.

title: As Expected and Needed

title: Perfect Mail Organization

That allowed me to dump my mail until I can get to it all and holds the magazines and extra house keys on the pegs at the bottom. Well, that hasn't worked so well, so this is my solution for now.)

title: Great Desk and Table With Great Features
text:
I recently had a major surgery that left me doing more sitting than I'd like. I also teach online classes and needed a way to hold a computer off my lap (because I had a lap desk that has a padded back, but it was uncomfortable). This one worked perfectly! There really wasn't much to do other than take it out of the box, pull the legs in to a standing position, and figure out how high I wanted it. Honestly, I really loved that I could put my phone at the front of the desk in the holder there, then angle the desk down a bit so I could comfortably type. I also have used it to read on my kindle. Again, I had a type of lap holder, but it wasn't comfortable with my surgery. The desk was a nice substitute so that I could read comfortably.

I get that not everything needs to be made more comfortable, but for my work and my surgery, it served a great multipurpose. I can also see using it for my aging mother if I need to step in more as a caretaker and need to bring her meals, etc. Overall, it's great planning for the future and for unforseen events. Don't get me wrong though, I'll be using this when I work from home too!

title: SOMETIMES PHONES CAN TRY TO INCLUDE TOOOO MANY FEATURES!
text:
I generally do not want a cheap phone, and at this price, I consider it cheaper. I want a phone that is quality and the only reason I picked this is because it is MOTOROLA, a well-known dependable name.

My other phone is a Panasonic 6.0. I like it, except for few things. So I plug this one in, and get it charged up. And, holy cow! The booklet is like a BOOK. When I saw the thickness of the small booklet, I thought there might be different languages, but no, one language. There are a TON of features here. And, for me to get this phone working up to par and benefitting from the features..... is a long shot!

I like some stuff that I accidently discovered, like Block Number. and the Handset can be Speaker Hands Free. I had that once, then couldn't figure out why it wouldn't do it again.

I also did notice that I could not CALL BACK a number directly from the messages. I used to have that option. Also, I want to figure out HOW to not have beeping everytime someone leaves a message. I would rather check the phone's number of messages than have it beep.

So, my question is WHY do companies need to include a ton of features. I don't need a ton of features! And, if you have elderly folks in the home, forget them trying to set this.

All in all..... The phone has too many features, that will not be easy to work out. This phone will take me a long time to get it the way I want and the way I understand.

I like to "SEE" all of my notations at a glance. This booklet lets me see a whole month at once. Large amount of writing space for appointments. I place this by the computer to keep track of my online sales also.

The Calendar is in a book form, and it is hardcover material. I like that over lightweight covers. Durable! That's what I need for something that will be looked, opened and handled at all year. The binding looks stable. There are floral images on each page and on the cover.

What I also like are the Dividers..... protected! This is important to prevent dividers from curling up. Colorful dividers for several months at a time. That helps for quick look on where we are in the year.

Nice booklet form, well-designed!

title: This is a Really Fine Chair!  I love the comfort and quality!
text:
This is my second Ergo chair, and it is better than the first one. Hubby puts the chair together, and first thing he noticed was how neat the tools were placed.... in plastic. You can see all you got without scrambling in bags. The correct tools were supplied, and said even an allen wrench with a handle.

There is a nice set of gloves, white and they help you grip the tools. Nice addition to assembling. This company cares how you get this chair put together. Other than all that, assembly went great.

I love that the chair is sold, metal base, with good movable strong caster wheels. There is plenty of adjustments to the chair, so anyone can find comfort. Two of us will use this chair, so we keep it at a normal adjustment.

The spin is good, the feel is good. Head Rest adjusts comfortable and many levels to adjust.

Great chair. It is not only used for the computer/desk, but it is an extra chair for company to sit. Love the comfort, and quality!

title: Great!  Portable!  Take it anywhere in the home or office!
text:
One of the reasons I like this charger is that it is very PORTABLE. Take it to any room. I use a lot of pencils and need to sharpen them often. I can simply take this to either room that I am working.

I like to see when the shaving collector is full, and this is visible! Third, this offers a very sharp point, quickly!. And, all you do is charge it up. No electrical plug, no physical batteries. Chargeable. Love it!

title: Perfect fit,  good ink color
text:
I was a little nervious wondering if this would work. First, it fits right into the cartridge tray. Second, the color is nice and dark for the black ink. That is all I need is black ink, and I love that these cartridges last a long time!

Excellent!

title: LOOKS GOOD,  Sufficient,  assembled!
text:
This is a nice size of a locked cabinet. The color is dark gray, makes it fairly unobtrusive. It will work in any room. With the size, I can put it almost anywhere. It is lightweight, has a lock and three deep shelves. Perfect for my painting and craft items. Hubby wants it for the many drills he has for the new shed. But, nooooo, it is toooo nice for the garage. There is a list that comes with this on the many ways you can use it.

I like the size because I can move it around. And, if I needed to lock it, I could. I like this cabinet!

title: Comfort!  Light.  Developed a cheap squeak when moving on it.
text:
Had a little issue putting this together at the base of the seat. But, other than that, it is nice. I like the adjustability and the arm rest. I like that this chair is lightweight. Easy to push, pull and move around. It fits under the desk perfectly. Stays out of the way when needed.

This is comfortable. However, as I have been using it for a couple of weeks, it has developed a "cheap squeak" as you sit and move on it. I might have to use oil on it.

title: Strong, Compact,  Colorful AND  there is a magnet!
text:
What is nice about these clips is that they are very strong. Then, they are not long like most clips, they are compact. I use these on a variety of bags that need closure. The clips are easy to spot so I can find them easily. Keeping these clips on the refrigerator is a plus. The clips have a magnet!

Nice clips are strong, hold on numerous bags and the clip is short. Nice colors!

title: Very workable!  Make big marks or handwrite.
text:
I use a lot of markers. I create a small label for my business boxes and on this label. I write what is located in the box for shipping. I can make large size words so I can read them from afar....or I can use the same marker to handwrite a thank you note for the inside of the box.

That is how versatile this marker is. Then, What helps is to have a lanyard hook at the tip. I often lose my markers and if I don't have the lanyard clip, I can hook the tip cover to the shirt.

Colors are nice, bright and bold. The odor is there, so keep your nose out of it. Great markers! Multi-use, and great for marking on metal or wood.

title: Works good for me!  Unrolls smooth,  tape is strong.
text:
I try different brands of tape and am always seeking tape that is wide, easy to roll out, and most important stick. I found that pulling this off the roll is easy, good, doesn't split.

The tape is strong. Adhesive good enough. I pack shipping boxes and need a tape that has good adhesive and easy to work with. I am pleased.

title: TOP OF THE LINE SCANNER!  Powerful,  fast,  and great for an office!  Everything you need for scanning!
text:
This scanner has more features and great capability than I have seen. I would encourage this for a small business office or company to use. Most of the home scanners have moderate amount of capabilities and the homeowner doesn't even use what they are intended for. So, yeah, great for small business that has to scan important documents, receipts, etc. etc. I won't scan that much.

And, usually when you have great devices with features, gadgets, gizmos and more, the average person at the small business office doesn't use all the features available. But, it has a home in an office where multiple documents can be scanned..... and is used to its capacity.

It is easy to use, with a nice colorful display. I haven't had any trouble, nor page stops. It does its job fast! I have used the scanner to document my children's work....close to a hundred papers from the 80s. Then, I can view the PDF and have access to create folders.

One useful feature is the double-sided. But, make sure that you learn how to set it. I have scanned some receipts, and with smaller ones, I tape it to a regular sized sheet that will scan easier.

title: The Granddaddy of 'em All!
text:
This is quite a scanner, and I call it the "Grandaddy of All Scanners". I have decided to scan many many financial documents that are taking up file cabinet space, even though I purge periodically. Plus, I am scanning the children's school artwork from the 80s. I am even attempting to re-scan all their photos from childhood.

First of all, what I noted is that I can make a Sticky Note on the Photo that is scanned. Plus, I like when it puts a white frame around the pictures that are scanned. I am working with it, because there are a lot of computer tools to work with.

The scanning is superfast, and even though i don't require it that fast, you can sure get used to it. It even adjusts small cards or small photos.

This is all interface on the computer. This is great to work with it, save it into files, make adjustments with tools. The setup was simple, and this is a lightweight scanner, easy to operate. This scanner is not wifi, but apparently another higher model is.

I even scanned a rumpled paper with images, and the scan came out beautiful. So, don't try to straighten out all the kinks, because this will scan minus rumpled kinks.

Nice scanner, easy to work with, and with fine features!

title: Nice, looks good, lightweight,  and easy to set up!
text:
The first thing I realized about this, was how easy it was to set up. Generally, I go through a lot of stink, but ths was easy. There is a small easy to read and comprehend Touchscreen Face thing that lets you set up. Inputting of the two cartridges was another easy step, at least easy for me this time. I also have this for my laptop and will use on the Kindle Fire. But, mostly, I also inserted the disc to my desk computer and it was a simple process to get wifi connection.

The Printer is lightweight. Looks good!

What I have done mostly is scan items. The items will scan to your regular computer, which is what i needed. Once there, I had to open the scan into another program for easy editing.

The printing was nice, neat clear. I don't have an idea how much cartridges will be, but I guess I cross that bridge when I come to it.

title: Great Sticktuitiveness!  Cut without scissors!
text:
I use these for some large boxes, and what I liked most is that there is a perforated line that makes this an easy cut, especially when you do not have scissors handy or a tape dispenser.

The roll is large, and I use this alone. It is easy to find the perforation, easy to carry, and the it sticks great!

The print is bright red over white, easy to read on larger packages.

title: Images are not great, but they will do for what I need it!
text:
This printer looks nice, is not too large, and I was able to set it up for wireless printing. The difficult part I had experienced was puttin in the cartridges. The big sheet demo does not tell you what that blue square is for. I tried pushing it and pulling it, whatever it needed to do. I had the struggle because I could not get the second cartridge in. I also struggled with the others, because something was blocking my way to do this. It is a long story, but I finally got the cartridges in.

I did get it to set up easily. That was good, because that is the critical part. Messing with the paper trays was another challenge, but I got through that too.

I printed several color images on one sheet. And, for a color printer, they were not all that great. Now of course this all depends on your images that need printing. But, basically, my images on all white paper, were not that great!

Copying a document of black and white text was good! Very comparable to the original black and white text.

There is a nice userface, easy to navigate. As far as the printing processing time, it is as usual. Not too fast for larger images that were printed.

title: Good as the Brother!  Try it
text:
I replaced my Brother Cartridge to try this and compare. The fit into the cartridge slot was perfect. The ink is not exactly the same color as Brother, but you get a nice print color anyway.

If you do not need the finest quality of printing, this will work great!

I compared this to the printing of a photograph, and came with about the same quality of the Brother.

I do not have an idea how long this will last, but will post it as I find out. Received toner for review.

title: Excellent product for labeling all my tools that nobody knows what they are!
text:
These are great for labeling the stuff. I have a garage full of tools and when I leave this world to go to the Promised Land, I want to identify the tools that need identifying. There are plenty that no one knows how they are used, but me.

So, take this little white label, write on it, and bam, post it to the object. The material is flexible, easy to wrap itself around all kinds of stuff. And, it doesn't appear to take abuse, by fingerprints smudging the Ink or Sharpie. We will see.

They reposition themselves easily, are white for easy viewing, and great to write on. What I like is how flexible the label is.

What I prefer..... is a larger label.

title: Nice, excellent sizes, corrugated for strength!
text:
Corrugated cardboard is that wavy looking inner lining situated between the cardboard layers. This creates a heavy, more durable content. These boxes are perfect for shipping items, and if you are into boxing smaller items, or shipping, these work perfectly.

The boxes are strong, and survive the shipping process. The size is quite handy, and you can get many many different sizes. I use these, and other size, and continue to use Pratt.

title: Classic Pelouze Scale!
text:
If anybody needs a quality-made scale, these readout scales are the best. Sometimes I don't trust those digital readout scales. I prefer the mechanical version.

I previously owned a Pelouze, made in 1982, and it has always given me accurate readings. But, now, I need a scale that can read more than 10 lbs. This one goes as high as 50 lbs.

It is easy to read the numbers, it is lightweight, portable, and convenient to own for weighing packages. Excellent product.

title: Surprised!!  It has good screen image, nice and loud sound!
text:
This is a surprise to me! First thing, it is not that mini, but will fit on your hand. I worked with this and discovered that there is a rule number one: take the lens cap off to see, for Christ Sake! Once I did that, I could see a nice clear picture.

i have an HDMI cord for my Kindle Fire 8.9 and plugged it into the projector. I was able to play music videos and Netflix onto the projector screen. I turned off the lights and tried it on the white ceiling and it was clear. The sound is good, loud. You can also use earphones, which I did, but I couldn't find a way on the projector to turn the sound down.

The booklet does not help much, but I guess there isn't much to learn. YOu can hook this up to many devices. Keep it positioned so you do not block the air vent, because it will get hot.

As far as the stand, I couldn't trust it. It just doesn't do well, so place it on solid table top. All in all, I was pleased and quite surprised that the picture screen was large, the image came out clear, and the sound was loud and clear too! Excellent mini projector....

title: Thinner than Dymo, but work good!  Not recommended for Dymo.
text:
A great supply of shipping labels! Each roll has 450 labels, making it over 1300 in shipping labels. This is a nice quality set of thermal labels. They roll off and I have used them on a Zebra, but not on the Dymo as it is not recommended.

The labels are not as sturdy as the Dymo, and theses are actually slightly thinner and with an ability to rip easier than Dymo. They peel off easily, and work well as the roll for the Zebra. I can now make a decision on purchasing my own Zebra, but these do work good.

The amount is amazing for the price! Excellent choice you will make when you purchase this set of three rolls. I use these for various other reasons and they do just fine. Rizzo

title: Well made,  strong, and this company has many sizes!
text:
i have ordered several sizes of these boxes for shipping. They are not doubled walled, but they are strong! The box is well-made, and with the varying sizes this company has, you can always find sizes you need.

On the bottom of the box is the dimension of the box. But, yeah, try the different sizes. These are good for shipping and storing many things. Rizzo

title: Ah!  A full page!  Do as you need.
text:
The best thing about these Avery labels, is tthat it is a FULL Blank Page, meaning you can create what you need with this full page. Avery has been the champion of labels as far as I can remember. They create so many different formats for your versatile needs.

These labels peel off the sheet in a smooth way. They stick well. I have used these for various different projects. And I have even used them to cover up unwanted messages on shipping boxes.

I use these for shipping labels, printing two per page or more if you select different sizes of labels. All I have to do is print two 4x6 labels on one page and stick it on a box.

I can also go into Avery and create labels for different size projects or shipping. These are top quality labels..... Rizzo

title: May hold the grocery list, but the pencil slides down!
text:
So far, the board is sticking to the refrigerator. However, the items I place, like a pencil, tend to roll off. It appears to not be strong enough. I did have a 5x5 card stock paper, which held up, but the pen.... just slides down.

There may be more, and I will update as needed. I cannot imagine the sticky part, not getting dust and becoming ineffective.

Will update!...... Rizzo

title: If it works good, when it works good, IF NOT, then it is too sensitive, troublesome!
text:
I purchased a brand new one. I was wasting more labels than using them effectively. The Printer kept rolling out several at a time, I could not get it to stop. Then, I could not print from the computer page...

These machines are sensitive, and I could not rely on it to work properly and consistently.

It may work for some, but I could not longer take a chance.

title: A Party Conversation Piece !  Nice, workable, fun addition to parties
text:
These molds are a lot of fun for parties. What a great addition to any drinks. I have colored my water for the molds. You will receive four sets of Lego Molds. These are silicone ice trays, meaning they feel rubbery, and certainly are not stable if you need to fill with liquid and carry to the Freezer.

Give them a little tug at the bottom to empty the trays.

These are nice for any party, and will be a hit for the Lego Fun Club....

title: Laser Cartridge.....that's what I want!  Nice quaity print!
text:
The first thing I like about this printer is the LASER cartridge! I hope to get more performance time with this one, rather than my other Brother ink jet printer. This is a nice, heavy, attractive printer, wired or wireless. I am using wired this time.

The scanning is great, because you can scan TWO sides at once. and I got a nice printout of my pages, including the TWO sided printing. I haven't set this up for faxing, and sometimes I wonder how much faxing goes on anymore.

Haven't scanned yet, but the printing quality is great!

You can set this up easily, although I struggled with wireless for a bit. But, I like the simple interface, and following instructions from the CD operations is nice, clean, concise. Again, best thing is that this is a Laser cartridge, and I don't like my old inkjet. ...Rizzo

title: These mailers are about as good as one can expect for the quality and price
text:
These mailers are about as good as one can expect for the quality and price. There is a popular brand that I can't remember, but these equal those. The inside is black and outside is a very neutral color.

This size is large, and I have previously used 24x24, and this is the closest you will get to the largest size. If you are packing anything with a sharp edge, you jmay poke a hole, but otherwise, they hold up well.

You can undo the strip that secures them. These do not have a wide edge, in other words, you cannot expect it to expand. It is a flat edge.

Quality for the brand, large enough for huge items, sturdy enough for the elements of packaging....Rizzo

title: Strong!  Great size.
text:
These poly mailers are a great size for mailing large products. They hold out well. Great to protect your packages from the elements. The poly mailer is strong, and of a great size.

It is not easy to find these in anything larger than this. Rizzo

title: Great for working from bed or a big comfy chair.
text:
I often find myself working or studying from bed or my big comfy chair, and I had been using a dinner tray table, but when my doggo knocked the tray over with his big happy tail enough was enough and I made this purchase.

Not only is this lap desk/tray sturdy it’s really adjustable. The ability to adjust the height and tilt without the worry of the whole thing collapsing has been a godsend.

I have enough room to use my MacBook and still have room for a smallish notebook to take notes. Or there’s room enough for my textbooks for studying. It’s easy to keep clean as well.

title: More than I expected
text:
I wasn’t expecting too much when I ordered this planner, as I’ve ordered other like it in the past. So when my order arrived I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of the planner.

Why makes it even better is I’ll be able to use it for more than just a year, the quality and the fact it’s a binder means all I’ll need to do is get new planner paper when the year is over.

I absolutely loved the fact that the only company marking is the fox logo embossed into the front of the binder. My nickname is Fox so having just that logo makes me smile. (It also matches my wax seal stamp).

I’d definitely recommend this planner to anyone that wants a high quality planner that isn’t going to fall apart after a month or two.

title: Great product, worth buying again!
text:
I don't like these pencils...

I LOVE them!

I really wasn't expecting too much when I made the purchase. I wanted a set of draft pencils and found these. I honestly expected them to be cheap and not worth the money but I was really surprised when they came in the mail.

They are worth what I spent for them. The shape of them is unique and the material they're made out of is soft to the touch, which is amazing for someone like me who has sensory issues. They write smoothly and the lead doesn't break every other letter like some pencils I've owned in the past. These are definitely a product worth buying again. A bonus for me, they sent me a Mr. Pen moustache sticker which now lives on my MacBook, giving my Apple a moustache.

title: Great desk with one issue
text: This desk was so helpful when I had surgery and was pretty much in bed for a couple months. Even now I can sit in my big old recliner chair and set up my laptop and work and it is fantastic. The only issue I have with it, and the only reason it isn’t five stars, is that every time I pick it up to move it, at least one of the legs extends because the clip to hold it in place isn’t strong enough. Then I end up trying to balance it with one hand, while putting the leg back in before I can set it down again hoping that my laptop and mouse don’t go sliding off before I can get the leg back up. If the leg issue was fixed, it would be perfect.

title: Work great. No issues. Have purchased several times.
text: I don't have much to say - they do the job, they last quite a while without drying out (as long as you put the caps on tight). I have bought these same markers several times for different groups at work. No complaints.

title: Bought this as a gift. Love the paper and the general look but not how "shiny" the cover/back is
text: 4.5 Stars. Gave this as a gift so I haven't used it myself. Love the paper and the general look of the journal. It is a good size. The outside leather cover/back is significantly shinier than I realized but that isn't misinformation - the pictures they posted aren't wrong - it's just that in "real" light the leather definitely reflects which can give it a more fake (pleather) look. For me it would have been 5 stars if it were a more muted leather but that is just my personal preference. Also - and I saw this in other reviews but it is worth mentioning - I can see that if you use a heavy ink pen it could bleed through/show through the paper so keep that in mind.

title: I like it but it hurts! 3.5 stars
text: I bought the Silver version and I really like it. It looks great and I love that they give you the lanyard and the clip. I have only been using it a week or so, so I haven't experienced the issues that others refer to regarding the stones falling off but I have a few other issues that keep me from giving it more stars. 1) The retractable clip - the retractable "string" is about 2 feet long fully extended. Unfortunately, that is about a foot shorter than my previous one meaning when I have it clipped to my pocket or belt it is too short to reach the "key pads" that we need to swipe to get in the doors of our building so I have to unclip it from my person every time I want to use it (defeating the purpose of having the retractable part to begin with). Also, the clip is weaker than others I have used and when it is clipped to my pocket and I pull my badge to use it, the clip isn't strong enough to stay clipped to my pocket and comes flying off - again, defeating the purpose of having the clip. 2) The lanyard - I really like the way it looks but it actually pulls my hair out of my head and/or basically slices through my hair every time I wear it. The "gem" edges are sharp and when my hair gets in between two of them, good-bye hair! So I can't really wear the lanyard at all (unless maybe I have my hair up?). So....to recap - looks great, not the strongest clip or longest retractable string, and if you wear it too long you might go bald.

title: Great hooks! Exactly as advertised.
text: Exactly as advertised. I bought them to hang a big wall calendar and also to hang my heavy set of work keys, ID badge, etc. near my desk. They work great. Check the product description though - it seems some people are buying these to hang really heavy coats, etc. and the product description states "holds up to 13 pounds." Just a warning if you are looking to hang something really heavy.

title: Missing ink
text: After opening the Pen to check the Ink all of them were missing a quarter of ink. I am not sure if they were used or old and dried up.

title: Must have
text: Makes working from home so much easier in regards to comfort. It is very sturdy and easy to fold legs and put away when not using it. I would strongly recommend this if you work or study from home.

title: Can’t beat the price and quantity
text: I wish I would have known about this product earlier. I have been spending way too much money on buying brand name. It works fantastic and now I know where to buy my ink

title: Very detailed and durable
text: I purchased several of these to give out as Christmas gifts to my coworkers and family. Everyone including myself love this planner.

title: Perfect for notetaking on the clipboard
text: I normally would not write a review on pens, but I had to make an exception with these. He refused to use any other type of writing utensil. Even coworkers that use my pen complement on how smooth it writes

title: Awesome product
text: It’s great for holding id and credit cards when traveling and work id.

title: Smooth
text: I love these pens. The write smooth and last a long time. Several coworkers asked where I got them

title: Great price
text: Perfect for what I use it for.

title: Great product!
text: It's almost like a miracle! I use it at the office, the car and at home!

title: Great price
text: Great neck pouch for the price.

title: Great fountain pen.
text: Got them for my dad and he loves them.

title: Leg Room
text: The only complaint that I have is that I am a short person that has a tiny frame. Even we the desk is at it's lowest level, it is too high for me. I wish that was a way to adjust the legs to go lower for smaller people. My arms are uncomfortable having to work at such a high level.

title: This Thing Is Awesome
text: I’m currently a full time college student and I have my desk all set up but I bought this for when I wanna sit in bed or on the couch for class/homework and it’s perfect. Everything I need is right there and it’s compact and portable.

title: Nice!
text: This is perfect for me! I don’t have enough room in my bedroom for an actual desk, so this works perfectly. I can use it sitting on my bed, on the couch or the floor. It’s easily transportable and works perfectly for my needs!

title: Easy to adjust angle and height. Easy to store.
text: This is amazing. I’ve been using it to do artwork and it’s just perfect!

title: Exceptional lap desk
text: Well designed desk - angle adjustments and height are great.  Constructed of high grade materials.  Items do not slide around at low angles.  A little on the expensive side but it is not a knock off plastic desk.

title: Five Stars
text: holds a lot of groceries at the apartment

title: More Sharpies!
text: Bought these for journaling! Can use them on the narrow point for calligraphy writing, and use the lighter colors for highlighting pertinent passages you'd like to remember. A great addition to my pen collection.

title: Great Organizer for Desk Items
text: Got this for the top of our multi-shelf printer stand since my husband has retired and we no longer keep his work laptop there. It holds printer paper, tissues, some file folders, and other items. Very sturdy and easy to put together. Might have to tap some corners with a small hammer to get everything to line up, but really not a problem.

title: Love the Sizes and Shapes
text: Once my husband retires we are going to do an intense labeling of everything in the house, and these are part of my plan. We intend to buy more permanent containers for foodstuffs to keep them fresh and these will be used to label the containers. I tested a few chalkboard labels a few years ago and really like them for labeling food containers.

title: Pretty Nifty Metal Organizer But a Tiny Bit Difficult to Assemble
text: This is a nice strong metal organizer for business or home for use for sorting mail or keeping up with personal papers. You can put about half a ream of paper into each horizontal shelf and put two or three narrow hanging file folders in the back and underneath there's a drawer to hold office supplies, plus a magnetic pen holder for the side. It's easy to confuse the two different supporting metal parts (the metal "floor" and the "metal" back, and they aren't labeled, so I marked this down a star, but it's a nice little organizer. Going to use it for all our retirement papers and other bills.

title: This Was a Lot Smaller Than I Imagined
text: I ordered a medium size and this was still tiny, 5 1/2 inches across. It was also lighter than I was expecting. I was hoping to also use it to hold book pages open so I could transcribe passages out of them. It's not really heavy enough to do that on a paperback book; hardback maybe. Very pretty item and useful for reading, however.

title: I Don't Know How I Can Review These...
text: ...since Amazon never delivered them. I got a refund, and they're Sharpies, so I know they work well.

title: Inexpensive and Lots
text: Lightweight but useful labels to print out on your computer. I need these because our dippy substitute postal person keeps delivering strangers' mail to our mailbox and I am tired of writing "Return to Sender" over and over. I'm going to print labels instead.

title: Absolutely Adorable Pen & Phone Holder for Your Desk
text:
Just as pictured on the web. Holds pens, pencils, thumb drives, etc. and the owl's tail forms a little shelf so you can stick your phone there, too, out of the way.

I call this my "Robert Goren pencil holder" because he tilts his head just like the detective on LAW & ORDER: CRIMINAL INTENT. It's so cute.

title: Beautiful and Useful
text: Nice solid bamboo organizer! Puts together in a flash and nice and roomy, looks gorgeous--see! I have all these reference papers next to my computer, from old bills to printouts to tell me how to use functions on my webspace. Here they all are nicely organized!

title: Great "Crash Cart"
text: I got one of these on Prime Day, and it's wonderful. Husband has various medical problems including venous insufficiency and cellulitis in his legs, so he often gets blisters or sores. We had a collapsible tote next to the bed, but now we have this with all the medical supplies I need for these treatments on top and extras on the bottom. Everything now fits and it can be rolled into the closet when not in use! Nice and sturdy, too. I had seen carts like this before, but not with the dividers and the cups and the hooks. Really great for sorting medical supplies.

title: I Like the New Design of These Inkjoy Ballpoints
text: They have shaped the barrels more like the ones for the gel pens rather than using the old design, which broke easily. This is the set to get. You get two sets of ten colors, plus one extra black and one extra blue, which are the most commonly used. I use one set until it runs out, and then the other; I use the pens for journaling. I prefer them to gel pens because sometimes I use highlighter on them and the gel pens smear when you highlight them, even after they dry.

title: I Love Susan Branch's Beautiful Watercolors
text: I buy one of these every year to put out. Branch's watercolors are joyful and wonderful. I have saved pages from her old calendars and framed them and have them dotted around the house. So you have a beautiful year of monthly entries and then can use favorite watercolors to decorate your house later. Win-win!

title: Looks Nice But Too Small
text:
I got this because I notice in the photo that you can put two remotes next to each other in one slot. Well, they must be really teeny remotes because you can't double up any of ours in this holder except maybe for the Roku remote with the soundbar remote. Everything else like the Dish Network remote, the Blu-Ray player remote, etc. only one can fit to a slot.

Have put this in the spare bedroom to hold the remotes for the TV there, but there are fewer remotes than we have out in the living room, so it will work.

title: Gorgeous...Gathered All My Pens
text: OMG, got these today and had to sit down to review them. I've had my journaling pens scattered in four different containers on the coffee table. Now they are all together in one very handsome, sturdy container. I corralled the tallest pens in a pill bottle in the middle box so I could put the ballpoint pens with them, and the small Xacto knife and black marker are corralled by the cardboard roll inside some Coban tape in the right box. Everything in its place!

title: Not Magnetic Enough for Me
text: This will perhaps hold a photo on a fridge, but not much else. I was hoping this would be as strong as the little silver round magnets they used to sell at a local craft shop, but it is not.

title: Beautiful Copper Organizers
text: They call 'em "rose gold." I prefer to think of them as a bright copper. I have not used them yet, since I haven't cleared the space in which they will go, but I intend to use them as upright holders for tablets, which take up so much space lying flat.

title: Love These Labels
text: I have a friend who's ill who I send some packages to from time to time. These are perfect, especially if you want to reuse old shipping boxes. I no longer have to use a big black magic marker to block out IDs and bar codes under thinner labels, but can put these right on the packages and not worry that some confusing ID will bleed through.

title: Good Wrist Support
text:
Husband spends a lot of time on the computer (4 days a week 10 hours a day for work and then he is either playing a game or watching videos). His mouse hand wrist was starting to bother him. This has definitely helped, he says. It's soft but firmly supportive and it keeps his arm and hand at a better angle.

He would love one in blue!

title: Nice Variety of Stickers for Use on Planners and Calendars
text:
If you keep a planner or journal or even a paper family calendar, this is a great set of stickers for use with them. There are three packages of stickers: a 12-page seasonal pack with themed stickers (snow/winter for January, shamrocks and spring for March, flags and summer motifs for July--there's even a tag for Canada Day!, pumpkins and Hallowe'en for October, etc. ); a pack of different styles of list stickers--I'm always looking for these!!!!--with things like checkoff lists, meal plans, hydration, small monthly calendars; and a third that has assorted seasonal, event, and calendar stickers and two pages of motivational stickers.

The price appears very reasonable when you consider the prices of other brand-name planner stickers that you find in Big Box stores.

title: This Is So Darn Cute!
text: I didn't need another mouse pad, really, but who could resist the cute baby elephant in Harry Potter specs listening to his music on headphones? Every time I look at it, I feel good, and really, these days, isn't that what you need? This brand, this size has lots of different patterns, but this one is definitely the happiest.

title: More Colors! Perfect for Journaling!
text:
I had the Inkjoy ballpoint set and reveled in the fact that it actually had a BROWN pen, and ten different colors. I wasn't sure I wanted the gel versions, which had more colors, because I hate it when pens smear. But Inkjoy claims these new gel pens dry 3 times faster than the old type...why not take the chance?

Well, the colors are wonderful, I have to admit it. And I still wait a few seconds and they don't seem to smear. Just think, thirty different colors instead of ten for all my journaling needs. Now, there are 36 pens in this set, so I knew there would be a few repeats. I totally expected the repeats to be something like two extra blacks, two extra blues, maybe a red and a green. Instead there is an extra black and an extra blue, and then things like an extra salmon pink, light green, mauve, and blue grey. Interesting choice of extra colors!

title: Drawers for Pens and Paintbrushes
text: I have fastened these, using the sticky foam pads included, to the underside of the wooden drafting table I use for my painting. I simply had too many pens on the desk and have transferred some of them to these drawers. Very simple to stick on, and if that doesn't work there is also an option to screw them in, with the four small screws per drawer included. Won't hold heavy objects, but perfect for pens, pencils, thin markers, paintbrushes, water brushes, perhaps a light scissors, erasers, a compass, etc.

title: What's Better Than Post-It Notes? Stickier Post-It Notes!
text: We use Post-Its for so many things: temporarily labeling, notes to the postal carrier to return-to-sender the stranger's mail we get in our mailbox, reminder notes, labels on gifts I've put away to remind me who they are for, and more. Unfortunately Post-Its were made to be a temporary item and sometimes you need to keep it a little longer. So anything "super sticky" is preferential. This box also comes in eye-catching colors perfect for reminders. Love it.

title: Lost in Space
text: This is a darling card. My husband and I have been space program fans since childhood and one of our favorite programs is FROM THE EARTH TO THE MOON. I can't wait to give it to him.

title: Looks Much Nicer Online Than It Is
text:
I thought this would be a nice unit like the Knodel Bamboo Monitor Stand Riser (2 Tiers) I also received from Amazon. Alas, no. Oh, it's a clever idea that you can position the two portions in different ways (straight, corner, sideways) as in the video, but the quality of the product leaves a lot to be desired. The brown "finish" of the shelves is simply a veneer and you can see the lighter wood it's laid upon at every corner of the board. The instructions are pretty straightforward, but I advise you to use a Phillips head screwdriver with a lot bigger handle to make the torque of the screws a little easier to bear. At least three of the pilot holes drilled in the boards must have gone sideways, because when the screws were all put in securely I had three bulges in the wood that looked like they were going to crack if I had had to put the three screws in any more. Also, two of the boards came scratched, and I didn't pay attention and ended up putting one scratched board on "top" where everyone can see it.

The worst thing about this set of shelves is that its kept packed tight in its box using a terrible styrofoam that leaves tiny little flecks of foam EVERYWHERE when you unpack the box. They give you a cloth to wipe down the boards, but with all the static electricity around in the winter you'd no sooner wipe the top of the board than all the little flecks of foam accumulated at the bottom of the board. When I finished assembling the unit I had to vacuum it, the carpet, my pants, and anything else I was near to get all those little shredded pieces of foam. ICK!

title: Nice Little Bookstand, But Small
text:
My husband loves to cook, and sometimes we'll actually use a cookbook to do something. Several years ago we were given one of those plastic cookbook stands, but it was very big and awkward. This sounded smaller, so I got it. I guess I should have read the measurements more carefully, because it's a lot smaller than I thought. Not really made for the larger style cookbooks, but for a hardback fiction or nonfiction book.

Otherwise it's a really pretty book stand, made of attractive honey-colored wood with two sturdy pivoting metal "fingers" to hold the book open. If you have, like us, a room devoted just to being a library, you could even put this on a tall table like a plant stand and have a book open, like a small dictionary, as a display. Or if you do religious devotions each day, you could have it set on a tall table with the book stand holding your place in whatever book you are using for your devotions. Might be suitable for use in a little chapel and definitely in a small classroom.

Just be aware it's not for oversize books.

title: Many Uses, Not Just for Monitors
text:
I replaced a dog's breakfast of a canvas cube storage box, a small table, and a round cloth storage container with a two-cube system set horizontally. Two messy looking cube storage boxes went in each of the holes, and I put my portable CD player and old cassette tape player (I still have many dozens of cassettes with irreplaceable music) on top of the cube. I still needed a little more storage for some DVDs, so I put this monitor stand on top of the cube as well. It looks really cute with the CD player on top and then the stray DVDs underneath. Gives the the whole unit a little pizazz.

Anyway, it's very sturdy, nice looking wood, and you can store whatever in the two gaps left underneath: CDs, DVDs, a mouse or mouse pad, thumb drives, whatever.

title: Pretty Abstract Design and Sturdy Design
text: I usually get my bookends at Office Depot, but these looked so pretty I decided to try them. They are nice and sturdy and I love the abstract tree design of the upright part of the bookend. Each bookend has soft pads underneath so it will not scratch your shelves and it also keeps the bookend itself from slipping. A cut above the padded-bottom bookends at the office supply stores.

title: Useful Not Only for Students
text: Got these because of the scheduling and holiday stickers, which were very cute. I don't need stickers for classes, but the other motifs are very cute: books, reading, appointments, mindfulness, etc. are very useful for journaling.

title: Warm Hands Always a Plus
text: Husband likes this. He has circulatory problems and his hands are often cold even in the summer. He says it's a little small for his usual mousing radius, but it would be huge if they made it the size he wanted. Note that the little warming pad you put inside it cannot be microwaved; it has to be heated in hot water. So it might take a while to get warm to use. Hubby has a USB-powered hand warmer that he uses to warm the inside instead and then he can put his hand in and have it warm.

title: My Sanity
text: I started keeping one of these when I retired to record new things, but it turned out to be a godsend to pour out accomplishments and grief in during a year when my husband was in the hospital three times and I wrecked my beloved 14-year-old PT Cruiser. The publishers change the design every year and I really dislike the 2020 design so I bought another copy of this 2018 version for future years. I use it to keep track of my chores, things I've crossed off the to-do list, my exercise, what podcasts I've listened to, even to memorialize folks like Alex Trebek. I love these big planner journals and have bought much too many sets of stickers to go with them!

title: Impressed with Its Stickiness
text: We've had a "critter catcher" gadget to hang up on the wall for about a month. The adhesive that came with the included hanger died after one day. Tried 3M tape which usually does the trick and it fell off the wall within two days. This was my last hope and it works fine except when the dog jostles it (it's hung near the back door). It's lasted a week now. Appreciate that it can be used outside but haven't tried it out quite yet.

title: Just What You Need!
text: I keep masks next to the front door so that if someone knocks I can don a mask to greet the person safely. I had them in a plastic bag, but these cases are much nicer and sturdier. Two disposable masks fit in the case with room to spare. Could also be used to hold a handkerchief, perhaps a folded bandanna, some facial tissue, even emergency toilet paper when on a trip.

title: Cute Set of Stickers
text: I'm not a teacher, but couldn't resist journaling stickers that had books, people sitting in chairs reading, and other bookish things for women that didn't include stuff like high heels and makeup, or massage reminders. Most of these stickers can be used for other things like general appointments, to-do lists, etc. They're bright and glossy and will liven up anyone's planner, especially a teacher's.

title: So Useful for Many Things
text:
This is advertised as a "presentations" folder, but the moment I saw it I knew it would be useful for something else. Over the years I have ripped pages out of various magazines: autumn scenes, winter scenes, Christmas decorating ideas, etc. and now have a box full of them. This will be perfect to put the pages in.

Other uses: recipe pages pulled from food magazines, cross-stitch and other stitchery pattern magazine pull outs, inspirational essays, poems, funny articles, etc. from various periodicals. Very versatile.

title: For My Purposes This is a Winner
text:
I understand this is supposed to be some kind of binder for a business prospectus, but the moment I laid eyes on it I knew it would be useful for something else. Over the years I have bought magazines in the fall and in the winter for the autumn leaf and snow photographs. Once I finished reading them I would tear out my favorite photos. I had a whole box full of them. I saw this and thought it was precisely what I needed for these photos! With 60 pages I have 120 showing magazine pages, and any lesser or smaller photos can go in between two photos to be pulled out for viewing. I would have never thought of buying something like this, but it worked out perfectly.

Could be used for a cookbook of recipe pages torn from cooking magazines, cross-stitch or other stitchery patterns when you didn't want to keep the whole magazine, an idea book for home decorating ideas once your home is built or condo is purchases, etc.

title: Holds All My Pens and Looks Nice
text: Got these to hold a set of 18 colored pens I use for journaling and a set of black art pens for drawing. They each fit in a container with plenty of "wiggle room" and the clear lucite looks very attractive. These are square, sturdy, and just right!

title: These Are Gorgeous Bookends
text: I spent some time this morning putting them in places where they were needed. We have an extensive collection of books, so I also use the tops of the bookcases to store books. The tree design is very pretty and these are strong enough for all except really big books like those "Reader's Digest" big compilation books (history/nature/household hints) or coffee-table volumes. Very glad of the padding on the bottom that keeps them from slipping on the shelves.

title: The Ultimate Chill Out Book
text:
Seriously, you could use this journal to meditate by, just sitting and breathing deeply and turning the pages. There are 32 sheets (64 pages) of original design before they start repeating again, of dreamy-looking deer, flowers, butterflies, trees, leaves, and the moon. Just breathe in and out and turn the pages!
This pretty journal could be used for anything--profound thoughts, inspiration quotations, favorite verses of poetry, your own poetry, nature notes, tiny memorabilia, etc. But it really is beautiful inside.

title: The Labels Are Good
text: I'm using these to organize my closets, our pantry, and my craft room, and the variety and the different sizes of the labels are good. The two markers are rubbish. Go to a craft store or get some chalk markers from Penguin on Amazon. The value is good just for the labels.

title: Serviceable Labels
text:
These are matte-finish labels for laser printer, 20 to a page, and if you don't care about a semi-gloss finish on the labels as Avery usually does, these are fine labels. They run through the laser printer easily, and the laser ink does not smear on them as I have had problems with other laser labels. They stick really well, even to your fingers. Well worth the price.

The only downside is that Amazon Basics does not put any Avery equivalent number on these, and Word/Word Perfect usually gives you label choices in Avery label numbers. Just for the record, these are equivalent to Avery labels 5161.

title: New Tablets = New Cases = Something to Hold the Stylus
text: These are great; the stylus holder itself is tight and stiff so you don't have to worry about the stylus falling out, and the adhesive that sticks the holder on is super tight. Plus you have extras for other tablets or computers.

title: Fine Point Pens The Best Part, But Others Okay
text: This is a nice starter set combo of drawing/calligraphy pens. My only minor problem with them is something I often see in felt-point calligraphy pens--the tips on the 2- and 3-point calligraphy points are often quite stiff at first and sometimes skip part of the width. The fine-point tips are quite nice to draw with, and can provide a lot of fine detail. I am taking off one star because the description for these pens clearly state several times that they are "waterproof." Nowhere on the packaging does it say that; it says they are "watercolor." However, I did get them wet after allowing the ink to dry for one day, and they did not smear when I wet them, so maybe they are "waterproof."

title: Beautiful Effect With These Pens
text:
These are like paint pens in that you have to prime before using; however, the paint in these flows very quickly, only takes one or two pushes, the most three. Here's how they look when you print with them. All of the colors look good with the silver, except the yellow. I think it looks a bit off. I would have preferred a gold, or, since the "red" pen is actually very pink, a real red pen. However, these should have a very pretty effect for art projects.

Please note that you WILL see paint on the other side of whatever paper you use. I used heavy watercolor paper for the samples and it bled through to the other side, so don't use these on something you want to use the other side of, or, worse, have already used the other side of, like for a journal entry.

title: So Useful, So Many!
text:
I guess I didn't quite think about how many padded envelopes 125 were. When this box arrived I was quite gobsmacked.

On the other hand, the envelopes are great. They are a little smaller (maybe as much as one inch, or maybe just 1/2 inch) than the ones I typically get from Walmart or Office Depot, but they are nice and sturdy, and the adhesive that closes up the envelope is super-strong, unlike the others I have use. I usually reinforce the seal on those envelopes with shipping tape, but these don't need them. I have vowed, after years of spending ginormous postage on out-of-state Christmas packages, that my future gifts will be books, CDs, and DVDs so they can go media mail and be shipped in these envelopes.

They will serve me well.

title: Large Lap Desk With Room for Most Any Activity
text:
I seriously underestimated how large this would be. Even though it was shipped in a huge box I thought they'd just gone overboard with the packaging again. No, this is a nice BIG lapdesk, and, at 5 foot 2 inches tall, it is almost too big for me. If I sit down at our sofa with it, it almost comes up to my collarbone with the legs at their shortest. So if you are a tall person, you have found the perfect lap desk! Everything works perfectly, it folds up compactly (alas, not enough to go under our sofa, but under taller furniture, like a bed, for sure), and the work surface is enormous! If you were an artist trying to draw a portrait from a photograph, you can easily prop up that photo and still have plenty of room to draw on a full-sized drawing pad. There are several different angles of tilt as well.

I'll admit I bought this because last time husband was in the hospital, we tried to do stuff like watch Amazon Prime on my laptop and it just wasn't possible with that big, awkward table they give you in the hospital. This would be perfect for sitting on the bed of someone who is bedridden or in the hospital for a long stay, so they could prop up a laptop, color for relaxation between the nurses running in and out, read, do a small craft like beading or drawing, etc. I have it; nevertheless I hope I don't have to use it for the activity it seems perfect for!

title: Full Again
text: I bought the Epson XL-830 mainly for its scanning capabilities as when I retired I lost use of the all-in-one I was given for teleworking. However, while our Brother color laser printer prints fine for coupons and such, it was not as good printing little items to go in my journal, so I started using the Epson printer for that. Under my use, the ink lasted two years, so I guess that's good. This is a nice printer that prints beautifully with the Epson ink cartridges. Ink was no cheaper and was actually more expensive everywhere else, so I am satisfied with the purchase.

title: Just In Time!
text:
Husband's expensive not-two-year-old Serta office chair started squeaking and wobbling a few weeks ago and contributed to arthritis problems in his legs. The description of this chair intrigued, so I ordered it.

First Impressions: Wow, this is COMFORTABLE. I had a high-priced ergonomic chair at work and it was the world's most uncomfortable chair. I didn't know if I'd like this mesh seat and back. I guess it was the chair at work! This is very comfortable, and I like the tilt back right out of the box. Husband has put one of those egg cushions over the seat but he said he didn't need it. He loves the back support; says the curve of the back of the chair goes right into the curve of his back.

We did not put on the head rest initially. My husband is five foot eleven and when we fitted it, the top of the head rest came to the base of his neck. title: Teleworking?  This is a great printer for a home office.
text:
Working from home required me to have a better printer. My old one was an ink monster and drank the stuff like it was infinite. So, when I came across this printer I was like why not. Cannon is a well known brand and I assumed it would be a quality product. I have not been disappointed and the printer has exceeded my expectations. It is a great home office do it all printer.

The printer arrived with no damage on the exterior package. Unpacking the printer was very ease. Just open the box, grab the bag the printer is in and lift it out of the box. The printer weighs about 20lbs.

Note:
The dimensions in the ad are not marked properly.

Length across the front is 28.6”
Width front to back is 15.8”
Height is 12”

Setup:
Setting up the printer is very easy. Just remove the shipping tape at the various locations and power up the unit. Follow the direction on the printer screen and also, the written instructions from the box. Simply go to the website listed and follow the prompts. Setup took me about 15 minutes. The majority of that time was a 10 minute alignment process that was automatic.

The Cannon software can be downloaded from the website listed in the instructions or from the Microsoft store. There is a link on the website to take you to the Microsoft store. There is also an app on the Apple App Store for iPhones but the printer will also air print without the use of the app from an iPhone. I did print from my iPhone using both methods.

Filling the ink tanks:
This is very easy and during the printer setup process the printer will display on the screen how to fill each tank. In summary, you open the color ink lid, unscrew the ink bottle cap, flip upside down and fill the corresponding tank. The bottle lips are each unique so you can not accidentally fill the wrong tank. When the bottle is empty remove it and place the cap back on the tank and bottle. There was no mess at all and my 12 year old son actually filled the tanks.

Printing:
Printing is very easy to do. The program/app are intuitive and visually pleasing. Print quality is very good for its compact size and the inkjet prints pages quickly. I used most of the basic print features with ease and had no issues. The printer is fairly quiet and makes typical noises associated with an inkjet and printing.

Note if using your phone with the cannon app stay on the screen like it states. It doesn’t like if you exit the app while printing.

I found for a quick print job from your phone the air print function was faster.

Scanning:
Scanning is as easy as putting whatever you are wanting to scan under the top cover or in the feed tray and clicking the scan tile. It is similar process for copying. Now with that said there are options beyond the basic ones. Smart phone copy is a very useful feature where you can use your phone camera.

Overall:

I’m very impressed with the printer It is a quality product that is simple to use. It has many advanced features that with me working from home makes my job easier. Having larger ink tanks will definitely be a plus. The refills bottles are purchased individually at approximately 30$ each. So, approximately $120 plus tax. With that said it does state it prints 6000 pages black and 14000 color. Of course this was not tested out by me. I only wish the printer came in all black as well.

title: Perfect For Pre-Cooked Meals
text:
These days I have a home health care aide who comes by several days a week to help with cooking, cleaning, and the like. She'll generally cook up enough of my favorite meals to giving one serving that day as well as putting one or two servings in the freezer for the days she doesn't come over. We have these plastic reusable bento box containers for her to put the extra servings into. Though the containers have a clear top, once they are frozen, the tops get iced over a bit, making it hard to see what's inside. These labels are perfect in that situation. They make it easy to tell what is inside each bento box when there are several of them sitting inside the freeze. The labels also go through the microwave just fine as I heat those meals up.

I had never heard of water soluble labels before but that's an essential part of what makes these so easy to use. They really do completely dissolve in 20-30 seconds under running water, without leaving any kind of residue. So you don't have to try peeling the old labels off or stick label on top of label like you do with regular ones. This is one of those items I didn't know I needed until I saw it. Having used these labels for several weeks now, they have quickly become an essential part of my kitchen. So I very much have to give this product a 5 star rating.

title: A Solid Workable Stand With Some Issues
text:
Let's run through the pros and cons...
Pros:
- Once assembled, the stand is a solid, sturdy piece that does its job well.
- The finished unit looks really nice and should complement most decors.
- It works well as an organizer, giving shelf space to put things that otherwise just end up in a jumble migrating around on my desk.
- Putting a monitor on this stand raises it to eye level which makes more of a difference than I initially realized. It's easier on the neck and back as well as making the monitor seem brighter and clearer.
- The space under the monitor shelf is perfect for a soundbar speaker. When I put mine there, it actually enhanced the sound, deepening it and adding a bit more base.

Cons:
- Without a power tool, the assembly can be a bit hard, leaving the hand sore after screwing everything together.
- Assembling it by hand, not everything lined up well. There are small gaps here and there and the front edge of one side doesn't lay flat on the desk. Luckily though, the stand is sturdy enough that it does not wobble unless you push on that side hard.
- As several other reviewers have noted, the plastic cover for the cable hole arrived in several pieces. We were able to jury rig it back together so as not to leave a gaping hole in the shelf but the company really does need to do a better job of packing this item for shipping.

Bottom Line: This stand does have some flaws, enough to not make it a 5 star product. Still, the flaws are not major and the stand is useful enough for me to give it a solid 4 star rating. Anyone wanting to use it in a home office, a dorm room, or the like should do well with it.

title: A Solid, Useful Product With Some Minor Flaws
text:
"Sifting through garbage is a popular tactic for social hackers to recover information about the habits, activities, and interactions of organizations and individuals. Information retrieved from discarded property allows social hackers to create effective profiles of their targets."
-Social Hacking, Wikipedia article

That kind of hacking has been with us for quite a while now. The 1995 movie, Hackers, with Angelina Jolie, includes a dumpster diving scene where a couple of intrepid hackers go through corporate trash bins, looking for info to help break into that corporation's mainframe computer. As an old, retired guy, I don't have any corporate secrets to throw in my trash, but I'd just as soon not have my medicare or social security records sitting out on the curb either. So a reasonably priced shredder for home use is not a bad thing for me to have in this day and age.

There are some nice things about this Amazon Basics shredder. It's small enough to make for easy handling even as a 70 year old. Four wheels on the bottom make it simple to roll the thing out of the way when not in use. The operation is pretty simple and straightforward. Plug it in, turn it on, and shred things. It turns paper into such tiny confetti that trying to piece anything back into readable form seems like it would near impossible. So the shredder does its job well.

There are only a couple of minor flaws. Strangely, for a box on wheels, there are no hand grips on the side to make for easier pulling. That's not a big deal but if you roll the shredder under a table when not in use like I do, a handle would make it easier to pull back out. Another thing worth mentioning is that this doesn't seem to be a high volume shredder. On my first use I put something like 2-3 dozen sheets through it, one at a time, and there was a faint burnt smell in the air as I did so. So I would not try to put massive amounts of stuff through this thing. Again, that's not a big deal for me. As a retired guy, I'll usually only be shredding a few sheets at a time, maybe two to three times a month. So for small amounts of personal use, this product seems perfect. If you need a high volume shredder, check the capacity of this one carefully before buying and look around to see what else is available.

title: Worse Than Useless - It Borders On The Dangerous
text:
There are three significant issues for me with this floor mat. By far, the most serious is that the edges keep rolling up. Not only do the wheels on my desk chair get caught on those edges but twice I've almost tripped and fallen over a curled up edge. At 69 years old, a fall like that could easily break a hip or worse. Every couple of days I flip the mat over but by the next morning the edges have started curling up again.

The second issue, irritating but not life threatening is that the mat continually slides around on the floor. The last issue is cosmetic but very noticable. The black mat is an absolute dust magnet and looks terrible on the floor. Given my age, boxing this mess up and hauling it down to UPS to be shipped back is a non-trivial exercise, not worth the $30 involved. Still, I will not buy anything from this company again. The last floor mat I had was from Office Depot. It cost about the same, was of heavier, clear plastic, and had none of these issues. So after I throw this one out, I'll head back there for a usable floor mat that won't try to trip me.

title: The best designed bedtray!
text: I’ll admit it.  I’m obsessed with my bedtray lol.  It is so well designed that it had things I didn’t even know I needed.  Firstly it’s HUGE!  I’m an artist so I needed a big space.  You can adjust the legs and the tilt of the table very easily.  You can place your phone or iPad in the groove ONLY if you keep the desk flat.  Otherwise it just tips forward so don’t believe the pictures you see in the description lol.  It comes with a book/iPad holder that can be placed in the groove or stand on its own.  It also folds up and there is a place for it underneath the desk.  Since it does come with this book holder it makes up for the fact that I had to keep the bedtray flat to see my iPhone.  I can tilt the bedtray at any angle and the phone will still be upright.  So I love that I can have my reference image right in front of me.  The sleigh legs are probably one of the most convenient features of this bedtray.  If I have to get up I can just push it forward and it moves so smoothly on the bed.  My old one I pretty much had to pick the whole thing up to move it.  There is a little drawer on the left side where you can keep the silicone stopper.  My only cons are, I wish it came with a second silicone stopper or have a longer one.  The surface (I have the black version) is a little hard to clean when I got colored pencil on it and lastly, it’s heavy.  Though I don’t mind that it’s heavy because it just gives you confidence that it is a sturdy quality product.  It is expensive but I absolutely believe it’s worth it.  It is a game changer.  You’ll love it!
