text: Pretty basic letter sized calendar book. I have it 3 stars because of the quality. It has held up well and not fallen apart, but the pages feel thin and so do the covers. Also the book is so tightly packed that I have a hard time turning pages.

title: Sticker paper
text: This paper has a very shiny finish to it, but not clear shiny more like white. I tried to use it with my cricut to cut the images but it could not read the lines because of the shiny-ness of the item. I printed on a canon photo printer and had no issues then cut the images with my scissors. The look of the stickers is more of a white glossy vinyl than just glossy. The sticker paper isnt thin either.

title: Organizer
text: I'm currently using this organizer on my desk to store my multiple coloring utensils. I like this item because it makes those things accessible to me, rather than putting them in a drawer or leaving them in the box they came in. The item is a crystal clear acrylic material. It came with kraft sticker paper to protect it and was easy to remove. The only thing I dont like about it is the bottom containers are so slim and the way they are shaped, you cant fit as much in there are the other compartments. I was able to fit at least over 100 markers in there--and they're a  variation of sizes.

title: Labels
text: True to size. Decent quality, not thin. Adhesion works well. These worked with my shipping label printer (not sure of the brand, just something I found on Amazon). I would recommend this item.

title: Shipping label printer
text: I used this label printer with USPS and ETSY and it works fine. All of my labels have come out with good print quality. I had a little bit of a hard time setting it up, probably took about 20 minutes, but eventually I got it going. It's a good size so it doesnt take up too much space in my work area. Item is sturdy and doesn't feel cheap. I would recommend it.

title: Bling desk items
text: I gave this item 2 stars because of the quality. First let me say the items are sturdy and the construction of them seems well made, where they fall short is the decoration of the bling. If this item wasn't priced at $60 then I would have rated higher, but because it is $60 I expect much more when it comes to quality/ execution. All of the items have good weight to them and appear sturdy. My problem is how the bling is glued/ adhered to the items. The items seem to have been first wrapped or covered in a white material that looks soft/ squishy then the rhinestones were laid on top of that. I say that because you can see between the rhinestones where they were not all placed as tightly together and there were some gaps left. Also, the rhinestones seem to not all be the same size and color. Some look bigger than others and some shine brighter than others, as though they have a rainbow/ iridescent effect and the others are smaller and silver. Also, they used chain link bling for the perimeter of some of the items and then rhinestones to cover the rest of the areas and you can clearly see the difference. Some of the rhinestones are even laid on top of one another looking very tacky. So, although the quality is there, the execution is not and for $60 I find that unacceptable.

title: plastic binding come
text:
-feel somewhat flimsy
-could be sturdier
-shiny black
-when used with amazon binding machine, the combs kept popping off the hooks (possibly because they're flimsy)
-does hold pages together well enough as long as you dont manipulate it or try to take it off
-however it can be pulled apart easily, even after being binded to the pages

title: Comb binding machine
text: Let me start by stating that my review is from the point of view of a person who has never used a binding machine and this is the first time using one. First, there are no clear directions on how to use the item. IF you have experience then you would know, but for someone's first time, it's very unclear. There are small picture directions on the machine, but without words. The paper directions themselves are 1-2 pages long, each in a different language. Those 1-2 pages in english provide no clear directions either... just information about the product. I ended up looking up a video (not of this machine - because the amazon page wasn't available) to try to understand how to use the machine. I ended up figuring it out and began by using 8 pages of plain white paper. This machine seemed to have a problem punching the holes through those 8 pages when the capacity says 25. I had to press kind of hard to get the holes through. Then I placed in the binding comb (amazon branded), pulled the lever back to open it up and placed the paper on the ends of the combs and pulled the lever forward and I was done. Overall, it does work as intended and is sturdy, but the directions are lacking and the machine has a hard time handling even 8 pages.

title: Grocery cart
text: Very convenient item. Helpful so you dont have to carry multiple bags of groceries by hand. Very spacious; deep and wide enough for at least 4 bags of groceries (depending on how many items are in each bag). Is able to hold weight of bags as well. Easy to roll. I was a little confused on how to open it up at first because the bottom was not laying flat and I thought I had to do something special to get it to do so, but eventually it popped into place. I think this is a convenient item and would recommend it.

title: Shipping bags
text: These are perfect for lightweight items, especially because they will keep the weight of your item down, keeping the price down. The quality is good and they dont tear easily. The adhesive on the flap sticks well too. Overall, good quality product and true to advertisement size.

title: Dry erase board
text: I got this board for my son's room to help him begin writing. I gave it three stars because the material feels cheap, the markers are not of good quality and the board leaves smudges when things are erase. I hung mine on the wall with some command picture hanging strips and it has stuck well, and I'm sure that's because the item is lightweight. The markers write so lightly that the blakc looks grey unless you press harder while writing. I do like the eraser because both sides stick to the board. Overall, it's okay but I wouldnt recommend if you want something of better quality.

title: Bubble mailers
text:
-Sturdy
-Good and quality material
-protects items
-adhesion works well and stays closed
-Packaging does not tear easily
-Would recommend item

title: Acrylic pen holders
text: This item (in my opinion) is actually multi-purpose. You can use them to store a variety of things; really anything that fits and looks good in the container. They are crystal clear and the material is very thick and sturdy. I ended up using the larger one for a single rose and it looks beautiful with the water and red rose inside. I would definitely recommend because of the quality and the fact that you can use them for so many things.

title: Badge holder
text:
-plastic badge holders have a blue tint to them, not crystal clear or clear
-badge reel is sturdy
-silver color was the one I really wanted but someone did a poor job of rhinestone placement. The item has lopsided rhinestones, they are not lined up or placed correctly. Some look like they're falling off
-the black and pink one look nice, but that's because the background color is the same as the rhinestones so you can barely notice the imperfections (the silver one had a white background)
-overall they're okay. I only used the reel because I already had a badge holder and its working fine for me so far

title: bubble mailers
text:
-bubble gum pink color
-good thickness for protection of small, fragile items
-flap sticks well without much effort and doesn't come up once adhered

title: Mouse pad
text:
-Works great
-The colors are more pastel
-I'm not sure if the accent color is supposed to be gold, you can kind of tell, but it looks closer to beige
-The design does match the picture
-The design looks printed, but I dont know how good it can look on this type of material
-The backing is a grip like material and is black
-stays in place

title: Laminator/trimmer/hole puncher
text:
-Laminator was easy to use
-instructions were easy to understand
-Plug laminator in and choose 3mm/5mm thickness of item to laminate
-wait for it to heat and green light to come on, indicating readiness
-place item in with folded sheet side first
-allow item to slowly move through laminator
-make sure there's enough room for the item to come out flat, if not and you have to pull it up and out then it will cause bubbles and not laminate smoothly
-the trimmer is iffy. It cuts a straight line from time to time, but there is too much wiggle room allowing the line to go crooked
-also, its kind of difficult to lay the item and find a straight line to cut on since the measurement marks are vertical and you lay the paper horizontally
-the hole puncher is a 2 hole punch, works fine, but I'm not sure most people use a two hole punch unless its for documents going into a folder with the clasp on the top
-overall works fine, the only thing I dont like is the paper trimmer and that I was really looking forward to

title: Printer
text:
Printer was easy to setup. I set this up with google print on my chromebook and on my galazy s10+ through the epson printer app. The app is good for scanning and mobile printing, I mostly use it for scanning things to my phone. The printer is loud, but prints quickly. The copier is aligned to the bottom and back rather than the top and front. The copies look very similar to the original. I copied a pencil drawing and had a hard time telling the different between the copy and original. The color printing was bright in the beginning, but after a few weeks of use, it looks sort of dull. Especially the black, the black looks more grey than black. Two sided printing is quick as well. This printer seems to be targeted towards office settings because the "out of paper" notification shows up with 30+ sheets remaining in the paper tray. However, when using larger paper, the notification does not appear with even ust 5 sheets in it.

The ink was easy to fill, no mess. Ink seems to be affordable per the epson website. Black ink is 19.99 and color bundle is 38.99. Ink will last a while.

title: Printer
text: The printer was pretty simple to use. I took it straight out of the box, plugged it in and entered my wifi information into it and connected it to my chromebook with google print. It took me a little while, but I'm attributing that to cloud print because I have that issue whenever I connect a new printer. I still havent been able to get it fully connected, but was able to print a test page to see the quality and the print quality and color were very nice. The colors came aout vibrant, there were no lines or smudges or imperfections on the page. The touchscreen is responsive. I wasn't able to connect to the app through my phone or chromebook, however, for some reason it would not find the printer. I checked the price of the toner and it is pretty high, it ranges from $65-$103 for different colors EACH. However, the toner is supposed to last a long time so it could be worth it in the end.

title: Money counter
text:
-Counts money accurately and quickly, as it advertises
-The item has some weight to it so I wouldnt not consider it lightweight
-The flaps that flip through the money are pretty flexible, but sturdy
-Easy to operate, especially right out of the box
-Does detect money that isnt real. I just cut a piece of paper the shape and size of a normal bill and it was able to detect that it was fake.

title: Printer
text: The printer is a good size for small business; could even be used as a home printer, even though it’s monochrome, for simple print jobs or someone who isnt printing pictures or needs color. It was easy to setup connection to my wifi. I tried installing the software from the disk that was provided on a dell laptop with windows 10, 64 bit, however, it would begin the download process, but wouldn’t actually install on my computer. Once the initial download bar completed, nothing else happened. I looked in my downloads folder and other folders for the download, but nothing was there. I tried this multiple times and it didn’t work. Most companies will put the software on their website as well, but that wasn’t the case here. I was unable to find anything on the website. I couldn’t even find the specific printer/model on the site. So far, I am unable to fully test the product because the software will not install.

title: Utility cart
text: Easy to assemble. Instructions were clear. This cart is great for crafters of all kinds. There is room and storage options for papers, vinyl, tape, pens, pencils, smaller storage containers, and so much more. It manuever well and can travel with you (if oyu need to move around your home or area). It's lightweight as well.

title: Laminator
text: This product was very easy to use. There are laminated directions inside on how to use the item and how to change the cartridge. I havent had to change the cartridge because I'm just using the starter cartridge that was included with the item. I plugged the item on and turned the power on and it says it takes 3 minutes to heat up, but took more like 2 minutes and was ready to laminate. I inserted a normal 8.5"x11" paper inside. The process took a few seconds to laminate and cut the item. The laminate was very flat and had no bubbles. The cut was very precide and even as well. The item looks heavy and comes in a big box, but it's actually lighter than it looks. I was able to carry it easily. I would recommend this item.

title: Scanner
text: This scanner can be setup on a mobile device through the app store application or by downloading software onto the computer. I chose to do both to see how well it worked with each. The software setup takes a little while, probably about 30 minutes in total. At first, it was unable to locate the item (even with the cord) then I tried wifi and that still didnt work. I ended up going back to the cable and it worked out. Once I was able to locate the item within the software, I was able to scan documents. The scans comes through clear and quickly run through the machine and it saves a copy on your computer. I downloaded the brother app on my Galaxy S10 plus and, at first, had trouble locating the device on there also. I ended up realizing that if you use wifi, the scanner has its own wifi signal that you connect to (no internet) and then you can scan documents through it from a mobile device. That worked as well and came through clear and also saves the copy on your device. The item is sturdy and the functions and buttons are easy to understand. It is slim so it takes up very little space. I would recommend this item.

title: Adhesive paper
text: This item is somewhat easy to use. They are instructions in the booklet, but j found a video on YouTube that was a little easier to understand. The first try seems like there's a lot of steps, but once you've done it, it becomes easy. Once finished, the item is like a giant double sided sticker sheet. From my image, you can see where the shape of the item stops (you can see the square I cut). It's like a milky white against the marble background. Overall, it did adhere very well and actually looks nice.

title: Laptop tray
text: This laptop tray was much bigger than I expected it to be. There is a lot of room on the tray, you could fit a laptop, some paperwork, and mouse, and others on the tray. The legs fold in and adjust in length and slope. However, I couldnt get the right slope, it was either to low or too high. I was very confused by the divets at the front and back. One said it was for the laptop support, but looked upside down compared to the picture. Also, it is not sturdy. As I was on the bed, the tray did not provide support and the lowest length on the legs was still too high for comfort.

title: Pens
text: These are easily now my favorite pens. I am not really a fan of gel pens, but they have to be right for me to want to use them and these are the perfect gel pens. The grip is comfortable. They are click pens, which is easy to use. They write so smoothly and really just glide on paper. They work and dry best on regular paper; anything without a glosy finish to it. They are a deep blue color and have a blue band on them (I'm not sure if that is to indicate that they are blue pens). You can somewhat see them through the other side of the paper, but they do not bleed. Overall, great pens.

title: LED dry erase board
text: [[VIDEOID:f5a23cee25ecbb2fe83b43d585b5bbf3]] The dry erase board is lightweight. You can either hang it horizontally or vertically. The cord on the board has a clear usb adapter on the end. To plug it in, you plug the usb end of the power cord into the clear usb adapter and then plug that into the wall. You can use this clear usb adapter piece to change functions of the board. If you long press the button, it changes the display type, such as flash, colors, etc. The remote has a lot of buttons for different functions and colors. The markers that come with the board a liquid like. The show up really well on the board, but are kind of hard to wipe off. You have to wet wipe them first then dry wipe. If you dry wipe, it leaves significant streaking. The colors of the marker actually change with the different light colors. For example, the blue will show up light blue, but if you turn the blue light on, it becomes a darker blue. Overall, it's fun, especially for kids.

title: Notebooks
text: These are good memo notebooks, especially for those who work and need to keep notes handy or even just to keep in your bag or purse when you want things written down for a hard copy. The pages are like little notebook pages. The colors are bright and fun, gives you some nice options in colors. However, the booklets are pretty thin and dont have many pages, but there are plenty in the pack so I guess it works out.

title: Cube storage
text: This cube storage was very easy to assemble. There are no tools needed - only the mallet that is included, if you want to make sure everything is secure. There are directions that instruct you on how to assemble the item depending on the look you want. I choose to go with 3 and 3, sibe by side because I was using it in a kid's room to store books and games. It was sturdy enough for the materials I stored in it. Depending on the heaviness of the item, you can put a piece of cardboard or stronger material at the base of the cube so the cube doesnt bend from the weight of the item. So far, it's holding up everything I put in it very well.

title: shredder
text: There are pieces of tapes and tabs in the shredder that all have to be removed before using. When you plug the item up (with the attached cord) the area where the paper goes lights up blue. The on/off switch is on the back of the shredder. When you press forward or backward, the area then lights up green. You also have to oil the shredder with the included oil before using. It also comes with bags. The instruction booklet tells you what the shredder can and cannot shred and best practices for shredding. The basket pulls out easily for cleaning. There is safe sense technology, that if a object is detected near the top of the shredder and it is shredding, it will stop. It does shred 12 pieces of paper at once, as it indicates.

title: shredder
text: There are pieces of tapes and tabs in the shredder that all have to be removed before using. When you plug the item up (with the removable cord) the area where the paper goes lights up blue. The on/off switch is on the back of the shredder. When you press forward or backward, the area then lights up green. You also have to oil the shredder with the included oil before using. It also comes with bags. The instruction booklet tells you what the shredder can and cannot shred and best practices for shredding. The basket pulls out easily for cleaning. There is safe sense technology, that if a object is detected near the top of the shredder and it is shredding, it will stop. I have had no problems with it shredding any of the things that it says it can, it works really well and I would recommend it.

title: Desk pad
text: This desk pad is really large, it was actually too big for my desk and I have a L shaped desk that it large. There is some weird slogan printed into the left hand corner that says "To ask why we fight" and I'm not sure what that's about. It is easy to clean and liquid slides right off of it. I would say the quality is good and the color was actually really nice. However, the size of it and that slogan is why I gave it 3 stars.

title: Grid book
text: I absolutely love this book. I got the smaller sized one, but would love a bigger one. The outside is a deep purple and feels like leather. There is a elastic string to keep the bookley closed. There is also a purple satin like bookmarker. The pages are beautiful, they are so soft and make you write smoothly; the back of the pages are a little rougher and don't provide the same experience, but that's okay for me. There are also a few blank pages at the end of the book. The grids are great for creating bullet journal pages or even drawing. I would recommend this booklet.

title: Sticker paper
text: This sticker paper sticks really well and it actually peels up easily as well (depending on what you stick it on). I used it to print off some images that I had drawn on adobe draw and chose to stick one of them to a ceramic mug, but the positioning was off so I had to peel it up and readjust it, and was able to do so without ripping the sticker or part of it staying stuck to the mug. The paper was easy to cut to the shapes of my images as well. However, I gave it three stars because the print quality wasn't the best. I wasn't expecting it to be too great, especially because the paper is matte, but the colors were not vibrant. I did try it on high quality print as well and the colors came out a little better but still not as vibrant as I wanted them to. I'm not sure what this paper would be ideal for, maybe printing labels or something simple.

title: Pens
text: I think these pens would make great gifts or go with a gift basket of some sort. The patterns and colors can tell your unique style as well. I was thinking these pens wouldnt write so well, but I was totally wrong. These pens write smoothly and softly and the black ink is vibrant. They are really sturdy as well, and have some weight to them. They do not feel cheap at all. I would recommend this item.

title: Plastic envelopes
text: These envelopes work great for document storage, preserving documents, or just needing to organize and file them away. It comes with a lot more clear colors than the other colors. They are all transparent even though they are colored---you can see through them. I'm not really a fan of the velcro, but it works. These can fit large documents in them, I was able to fit 9x12 sheets. I used them to store my drawings that I'd done on paper and tracing paper for my paintings. You could fit about 30-40 sheets in them, maybe more.

title: expandable bookend
text: The bookend is sturdy and adjust easily. I was able to fit 14 books inside, the books ranged from about 100-300 page books of all sizes. I could fit more books in, but this was just the amount that I had on my booksheld. It does a great job of holding the books up... I havent had any problem with them falling out or forward.

title: Fine line pens
text: These pens have a variety of colors that are really vibrant. I used all of them to create some simple sketches in a sketchbook that I got from Michaels. They write really smoothly and feel soft too when writing. They do create really fine lines. These pens would be nice for writing or sketching. I wouldn't try to use them to color anything in because of the small tip (would take a while). I ordered them to sketch some of my paintings before I put them on canvas so I can see all the colors together and I think these will work perfectly for it.

title: Wire organizer
text: This organizer would fit normal size documents. It is sturdy and a shiny black metal color. It stands about 8.5 inches tall in the front and 12 inches tall in the back. The whole item is 9.5 inches long from front to back and there are 1 inch spaces between the bars. This organizer is pretty big, but would make good use for an office setting or home desk, if needed.

title: Paper trimmer
text: This is a nice little portable paper trimmer. It cuts sharp and precise. The blade cut smoothly as well. You could use it to cut smaller pictures, like wallet or 4x6 sizes. It's very light and that's because the bottom is hollow.

title: Scanner
text: I was excited to receive this scanner because the printer I use doesn't have one. This would also be very helpful for me while I'm on the go. Unfortunately, I cannot get this thing connected to ANY computer that I have. I first tried to set it up to my chromebook through the app, but I couldn't get that to work. I believe that's because this scanner can only be used through the usb cord. So, I plugged it up via the cord to my chromebook and still got nothing. Then I tried to connect it to my dell laptop and still NOTHING! I went online to the website and downloaded the software. Unfortunately, after a certain point, I kept getting an error message that the software couldn't be downloaded. So I uninstalled everything, deleted it all and tried again and still it did not work. At that point I just gave up and put the scanner away. Never got it to work or connect to any computer.

title: Printer
text: This printer works pretty well. The touch screen works well enough; there are sometimes where I have to touch the button twice for it to respond. The setup was fairly easy. I plugged it in and connected it to the wifi easily. The printer has an email address that you can get printed out and with it, you can email things to the printer and it prints them out. However, with pictures, the scaling is off... they come out smaller. It also sends an email to your personal emaile address (if you put it in) to confirm the print job. I setup the chrome OS app on my chromebook. For some reason it took over 30 minutes to finish setup. I ended up exiting out of the app and when i went back in, the printer was connected. Copying is very simple, however with colors they dont come out the same. The copy I made of the instructions, the colors didn't come out as vibrant as the original. However, I printed out a welcome sheet with features of the printer from the menu and the colors came out fine. It does print really fast. Within the app you can print pdf documents from your device, scanned files, photos from google drive and some social media sites. You can add accounts like google drive, dropbox, google photos, facebook, and IG.

title: Planner
text: This is a great planner, especially for those who need a hard copy of their schedule and have appointments that they need to keep track of. The front is just black with "2020" in the upper right hand corner. When you open it up, there is a clear pocket. Then follows a laminated yearly overview, "this planner belongs to" and yearly goals page, contacts page, and important dates page. Then the calendar begins, which starts with July 2019 and ends with December 2019 and are full monthly calendar pages. After that, follows 2020 and there are tabs for each month. Within those tabs is the monthly calendar pages (takes up two pages) then a breakdown of the times of day for each day of that month. For example, January begins with that Sunday December 21st and there is a vertical colums of time frames in 15 minute increments, starting at 7am and ending at 9:45pm. There is a vertical column for notes on the right hand side. Everythng is neutral colored, white and a grey-ish color. After December 2020, there is 5 pages of notes (front and back side). Then a laminated page with holidays and states and capitals on the back of that. Altogether I think this is a sturdy planner and great for people who need to list their appointments.

title: Stapler
text:
Update: After using my first stapler for about a week, I tried stapling two sheets of paper together and the staple and stapler got stuck to the paper. I eventually got the paper out but it had 3-4 staples in it. I tried fixing the stapler by pulling it apart, but could not. The staple head was stuck to the bottom and I could not get it loose. I eventually had to just replace with another in the pack. I'm hoping this does not happen again because a week's worth per stapler doesn't really work. I adjusted my review from 4 to 3 stars.

This item is made with good quality is and is very sturdy. Inserting the staples was easy because you dont have to open the entire top like a traditional stapler. You press the orange button on the back and the compartment pops out. You put the staples on top of that and push it back in. You can press to staple too, rather than picking the entire thing up to do so. It is also strong and can push through a lot of paper.

title: Document folders
text: My favorite thing about these document holders is the array of colors: there is green, yellow, pink, blue, and two shades of purple. They are not made of the thickest plastic, but sturdy enough for paper. I was able to put 65 sheets of paper in them and it held up. There is a small front pocket to put a label card in if you want. I used these to put my transfer sheets in. I used them for paintings and keep them because I replicate he images. I was able to fit 9x12 sheets in there as well.

title: Nice printer
text: The item was securely packaged. It had orange tape to keep parts closed/ together and four foam blocks to keep it in place. There are booklet instructions, but it also gives you a website where you can watch videos on how to set it up. The first thing you do is take all the tape off and plug it in, but dont turn it on. Then you fill the ink. There are still cartriges to put in, but you refill the ink with the bottle ink. It is sort of spill proof if you don't go too fast. They do fill quickly so you have to pay attention. Mine formed bubbles so I had to take it out and let the bubbles settle then see where the actual ink was. You dont have to squeeze the bottles either, once the ink is on the head it will come out. the black had about 1/3 of the bottle left and the colors were almost all used up. The levels are displayed on the outside which is convenient so you have a visual of where your ink is. During my setup (I connected it to my phone with the app, my chromebook with google cloud print, and my dell laptop), I had to turn the printer off about 3 times to reboot because it kept getting stuck on messages and wouldn't let me do anything. It was easy to connect to my samsung galaxy through the app. For my dell, I just had to go to the website and download the software. I dont have a cd drive so I didn't use that, but it does come with a cd-rom. I also connected it to my wifi, which was simple to do on the printer. The only problem I ran into was the it wouldnt connect with my chromebook. I kept getting an error message, but then you can select "web service setup" on the printer and it will print a page with a link for you to go and connect with the printer. So, it shows up in my cloud print now, but says its offline. There is a quiet mode, however it shakes my desk a bit when printing. There is also an auto shutoff mode, which is turned on when you first receive the printer. The printer prints out very clear and crisp pictures. It has multiple sizes. So far, I've tried a 4x6 and a 4x4 and gotten great results. The photo paper goes in the tray in the back of the printer.

title: Easy to use
text: This item was very easy to assemble... just place the top of the shredder on and plug it in. It's also easy to use... you just turn the switch to on. It shreds up to 8 sheets of paper, cards, and cd's. It has a lot of storage space. It has a lot of storage for the material also. I shredded as much paper to fill a bathroom sized garbage can and a half and it's only about half full. Also, the paper is shredded very finely so I'm sure that also accounts for the storage space. I shredded an old ID card of mine and it had no problems shredding it. I also shredded cardstock paper and some thicker laminate paper and the shredder worked fine. It also has wheels on it, making it easier to move. The front of the shredder comes off by just pulling it a little and looks like a small garbage can, so that you can empty it. I still have yet to try shredding a CD. I will update when I do so.

title: It's ok
text: The first thing i did when I got the notebook was opened it and tried to write in it. When I tried to erase it with the eraser on the pen, it still left a bit of an imprint so I would suggest writing lightly. The pen actually reminds me of an eraseable pen. When you put the top on the end of the pen, it covers up the eraser, which can be somewhat inconvenient when you need to erase a minor error, then you have to remove the cap, rather than just turning the pen over and erasing. It said it was tear resistant so i tried to tear the page (I really did) and all I did was crinkle it a little. I then downloaded the app and you have to create an account. The only destination I added was my email, but you can add multiple destinations like emails and drives. To transfer the page to your phone in the app, you essentially take a picture of it. You press the camera button in the app, fill the screen with the page, the app detects it and it captures the image without you having to press any buttons. Once it is loaded, it is a clear image, that resembles a document then you can sent it to any destination. The pen eraser would be for erasing mistakes or quick fizes, the cloth is to be dampened with water and used to erase an entire page, which it does. However, I'm not sure where you would keep a damp towel, especially if you're traveling with this item. Other features listed were searching handwritten text and grouping pages into once file.

title: Comfortable bond
text: I used this mounting tape to mount some of my acrylic paintings on my living room wall. Upon opening the package, I found the plastic that each roll was individually wrapped in was stuck to the roll so I had to use quite a bit of force to tear those off. The rolls were very soft. The tape is black and there is a thin red plastic sheet covering one side (this is the side to peel off obviously). I cut 2" strips and laid them on top of eachother to measure and the pieces did not stick to one another. I then cut those in half and used 4 of those squares (4" total) on each corner of the painting to mount it. I used more because I wanted all four corners covered. When you place the tape on the desired location, it molds to that surface. So on some of the paintings, the acrylic paper was folded over the back and stapled on. Therefore, I was applying the tape on half the acrylic paper and half the wood frame. The tape molded comfortably to that area and stuck right away. I only had issues with the corners not sticking, probably because I didn't hold it down for 30-60 seconds as recommended, so it made it hard for me to peel up the corners of the red film. Once all the red film was removed, I placed the painting in my desired area and held each corner for 30 seconds. Upon release, they did not move or fall. I will update on whether they slide or move from their initial location.

title: Gadgety, but NOT Practical
text:
I hate these.

First, the stickiness of the 'regular' Post-its are much stronger. With the originals, I can stick and re-stick several times to our bathroom mirror (helpful for weekly reminders and the like), as well as to my office door ("I'm in 248 today"). With these, they fail after one or two moves. Even when just sticking them to a single surface, you will find that they are easier to pull/fall off. I have tested them side-by-side, and the 'normal' notes consistently outperform these. You can see this yourself if you stick a normal pad of Post-it notes into the pop-up dispenser. You can pick up the dispenser with the stickiness of the normal notes, whereas the pop-ups come out 'cleanly'. Or just put them on a table side-by-side, like I did, and see which one comes up more easily.

Second, these are more expensive than regular Post-its. How so, you ask? Well, they are incredibly frustrating to use without a dispenser, so you really shouldn't buy them unless you also buy one of those. That will set you back another $5-10 on top of the notes (although it is reusable).

Finally, to use these with the dispenser, you HAVE to write on them AFTER you pull them off the pad. If you are posting them to a wall or other vertical surface, this generally means sticking them to a table or some such, writing, then moving them elsewhere. Since they are already weaker (see #1), this greatly increases the chances of them falling off by accident.

In short, these are 'neat' and 'gadgety', but not actually practical. Use these as a fun little party trick. Stick to the plain old "boring" Post-its when you actually need to make sure your message gets across.
