text: I'm determined to get organized this year and this is a great add on to my "stuff".  I did have to go back and reassemble it when I realized I forgot the top but it was easy to put together (should probably have looked at the instructions -- I assume there were some) but I put it together in a couple of minutes. It's very sturdy (no wobbles) and the sizes of each tray are high enough that taller things can stand up in them, without tipping over every time I roll it somewheres.

title: Went right in - worked perfectly.
text: No trouble inserting these and having them recognized. It was easy! Print quality is good, I can’t tell the difference between this the the OEM version and the price is way better.

title: Sturdy and durable.
text: These are bit bigger than I wanted but I knew that going in. They are very sturdy and have held up well. I’ve been using them when I travel and they’ve held up to heavy wear and tear on the outside as they get banged around and shoved into corners and pockets and they come out looking good. None of the pages have been damaged which means the covers are doing their job. The binding is smooth without any wire protruding and overall they’ve been great.

title: I like these.
text: I’m a little ocd about keeping things organized and I like the colored cards because I can ‘code’ with them. Some things are one color, other items are a different color and so on. These are sturdy and there are a good number of them. They did arrived scattered all over the bag so I’m not sure if they were originally in something that broke or they are just shipped in a messy pile. I did have to sort and organize them which I found annoying so hopefully that doesn’t happen to you. Otherwise, they are great.

title: Astonishing how handy this is.
text: I didn’t realize how much I could actually benefit from a label maker until I put this to work. I probably went a little overboard but it’s so nice to print a label quickly and easily. i didn’t have any trouble getting this going and in fact I probably labeled everything in range once I got going. It does make it easier and faster to find things so I’m going with the fact that this is a helpful household item (at least that’s my story - I’m sticking to it).

title: Feed nicely, stick well.
text: Just what I needed for my new label printer. While I swore I wouldn’t get any additional equipment, a dedicated label printer hardly counts as extra since it saves so much time and effort. These labels feed right in, the auto adjust and print out smoothly. I have had any jams, and smearing and they print nice and quick and clean and then go onto the package without any fuss and stay where they are put. Nice to have enough to not have to worry about labels frequently.

title: Handy addition.
text: You’d think a regular printer would be enough but not if you are printing a lot of labels. I had a bit of trouble setting this up the first time but once it was working I haven’t had trouble since. It’s small enough that it doesn’t take up any room and having a dedicated printer saves having to find labels and to try and get them into a regular printer. Makes life easy and that’s exactly what I wanted.

title: Great idea, lacks delivery
text: I wanted to love this and did love the idea but actually using it is a pain in the …… I’ve constantly had connectivity problems and that’s been the biggest problem. It may or may not work but if I can’t rely on it, what use is it? Even when I have it connected, there are times when it just doesn’t work! Arrrgggghhhh so very frustrating. I’ve had to look for alternatives. I still think this is a great idea, it just needs some work to make it usable.

title: Ah — a new office chair
text: Now that I’m working from my home office almost exclusively I spend a lot more time at my computer. It was time to find a better chair. The one I had was okay for a few hours but when I spent most of the day in it, it because obvious that I needed a replacement. This has a lot going for it but overall the most important thing to me is that it is comfortable even after long stretches of time. It was easy to assemble, it’s got enough adjustments to make it useable for me and it just works.

title: Went right in and work perfectly
text: My printer has been complaining about low ink for a long time and it finally stopped printing readable material so I had to figure out how to replace the ink. This was easy to do, these fit right in and the printer came online with no problem and now I can print dark enough that I can read what comes out of the printer and I don’t have to cancel out that stupid message “low ink” any more. Thank goodness!

title: Best lamp ever!
text: I love that this combines so many great features. I needed a desk lamp and didn’t even realize there were so many options available. Not only does this lamp have several lighting levels which is immensely helpful, it also has a wireless charging platform so my phone is handy and charged. The light has a very small footprint and is easy to position, easy to adjust and really makes it so much easier to see what I’m doing without sweating from the heat or getting a headache from the brightness of the light. Yes!

title: Wasn’t sure I’d like this but I do
text: I’ve been sitting at a desk seems like forever so while I was intrigued by the idea of a standing desk, I wasn’t so sure I would love it in reality. Turns out to be very useful. I find I’m not nearly as tired at the end of the day from standing as I would get from sitting. I do alternate now which seems to work best for me and I’ve got a fatigue mat that I stand on but with the lift feature, I can raise and lower it as needed. There is enough surface for me to actually work but not enough for me to load up a ton of junk so I don’t worry about things spilling when I raise or lower the desk. Hope this holds up for a long time, since I don’t expect to quit working and this specific desk has found a home.

title: Space saving and useful
text: I have another one of these at work and wanted one now that I'm working at home more. I consider this a "must-have" and use it frequently. It doesn't take up and room and can slide right into a small space so it's always handy. I use it for a ton of trimming whenever I need to make a label smaller or cut a piece of paper. If you line it up right, it makes a nice straight cut. You can only cut 2 sheets at a time (and 1 is better). It works much better than scissors and does a nice finished, even cut.

title: Very sturdy
text: This is a very sturdy cart with no wobbling and deep shelves. Assembly was easy although I missed the handle on the top (I put the top shelf on the bottom) so had to reassemble) but it wasn't a big deal. Went together really fast and I like that the shelves are deep enough to actually hold something without it falling out or slipping through.

title: Never thought I'd learn to love a medium point
text: As I've gotten older, I find that I MUCH prefer a gel pen for ease of writing. I generally get a fine point and got these by mistake. I'm never going back. I LOVE the medium point. I do write a little bigger but my writing is way more clear when I glide the pen instead of press the pen into the paper. These are nice, they write well, don't bleed, seem to last forever and have a nice feel in the hand.

title: Medium Point Gel
text: I wasn’t sure I was going to like the medium point but I find that I do like it. It’s easier on my hand to write with the gel pens but I’ve always used the finer lines so I was worried this would be messy. Turns out, it’s easier to write, less stress on my hand and I like that the barrels have different colors so I can easily spot them in the mess on my desk.

title: Easy plug and play
text: This was super easy to get up and running and works well. I admit to having a lot of trouble with the phone company which wasn’t this device’s problem but it almost didn’t get used. However, they finally made things work and now my phones all ring on one device that I can see and hear. Voice quality is decent not great but it does the job of combining multiple lines into one phone.

title: I love gel pens
text: I’m so over ball point pens - as I get older I find that the gel pens are easier to use (and I can also read my writing better since they are easier to write with). These are medium point which I wasn’t sure I was going to like (I usually use a fine point or extra fine point) but these aren’t obnoxious and they are super smooth. I saw that they are refillable but I’ve found in most cases the pens are cheap enough and the refills are so expensive (relatively speaking) that it’s just as easy to replace them. There are enough in this package to last a while and the blue ink is not a weird blue - it’s a normal blue ink.

title: Easy to assemble
text: Very easy to assemble and very moveable. This came well packaged and was super easy to put together. It’ rolls smoothly is easy to clean and doesn’t leave traces of ink when wiped off. It’s magnetic which I find very useful and it did come with a flip chart which I find less than useful but you may benefit from it - for me it takes up room on my board.

title: Huge, Heavy, does the job
text: This is easy to assemble - it's heavier than I expected but still manageable for a woman and it does the job - it's a double white board and blocks everything behind me for my zoom meetings. It's a bit white to do a good job with lighting but I've got a sheet covering it to make the background darker. It works, it rolls to move and I can write on it!

title: Very sturdy
text: This is very sturdy. It turns a regular desk into a standing desk and does what it's supposed to. It's heavier than I expected which is fine but just be aware you won't want to put it onto anything lightweight. I've got it on top of my regular (very sturdy) desk and use it to keep from sitting all day. It's an adjustment for me but has started paying benefits. I may look into a regular standing desk in the future.

title: Getting a lot of use
text: I've been using this quite a lot since I got it and find it very useful. I'm storing a bunch of project supplies in it that I occasionally need but when I don't, I don't want them all over the place. There are enough shelves to keep things organized and while it's not super sturdy, the things in it are light and it does roll fairly well. It has proven to be extremely useful, especially when I need something and go right to it.

title: Portable White Board
text: This is the white board I carry around with me to take notes on (which I then transfer to my "big" board). It's sturdy enough to prop against my desk or use on my lap or wherever I need it. It's been totally handy and stores in a corner or on the side of the desk. Wipes clean easily (even after the ink has been on it for a long time).

title: A few glitches
text: The instructions were terrible so I’m glad I didn’t have to rely on them to put this together. You do have to be sure to get the shorter screws to put on the top. As it is, I’ve got a couple of nail pops, they didn’t go all the way through but they are definitely there on the top. Also, when attaching the lift be sure it’s positioned facing the handle (fortunately I realized what was happening after I got the first screw in and could easily restart. Still now that it’s together, it looks great and works great. Nice size and my laptop is happy to have a new home.

title: Great for the kids to draw on
text: This is an endless source of joy for the kids. They can draw on them and time. Two per board— one on each side and I got a whole array of different colors of dry erase markers. The older one can practice his letters and numbers and the younger one can just doodle in whatever color they want. I did get two sets of markers so they wouldn’t have to decide who gets what but that may have been overly cautious on my part — so far they are sharing just fine.

title: Reusable Post Its
text: I’ve made great use of these when working on projects. The fact that I can wipe them clean and rewrite on them is great but the biggest advantage to me is that I can move them around when something needs to be rearranged. I’ve made extensive use of these when planning projects, in fact they are up there in my top 5.

title: Handy size
text: This is a nice little cart and very handy. I was all thumbs and it took me a minute to put it together but it's easy to use, rolls nicely and tucks away in a small space.

title: Fine lines and lots of color options
text: These work well on my white board and wipe away easily (even after staying on the board a while) which is a big deal for me. There are enough color options for anyone (even me) to be able to color code to my heart’s content and they produce a fine line that isn’t so narrow you can’t read it but it isn’t so wide you can’t tell what you wrote either. Can’t speak to longevity but so far they are holding up and I haven’t had any of them start to fade while using them, even if they are getting a lot of use.

title: This is "The One"
text: This is the perfect size for me to "journal" which is a laughing matter in my household. I forget to write things down or it's not handy but I'm getting better. I like the size of this. I've tried smaller and larger and this size is convenient -- big enough to handle and to read what I write and small enough to tuck into the size of a bag or my laptop case. Lined, sturdy and an elastic band to keep it closed so things don't fall into it or out of it. For me this is the best working solution. (Now I just have to remember to use it -- but I'm getting better).

title: Nice variety of colors
text: These are fine point so you can actually read what you write with them. I like that I have lots of colors so I can color code different sections or group things that belong together on the board. So far, no fading or disappearing so I'm happy.

title: Versatile printer, small footprint, easy setup
text: Good quality easy setup. I recently installed another printer by this manufacturer and I'm not sure why but it was HARD to install and setup so when I was getting ready to install this, I was already 'not happy'. This was surprisingly easy to install (especially after the last fiasco) so I was pleasantly surprised. The quality of print is very good and the speed is decent. As usual having color is a perk but sometimes the speed leaves a lot to be desired. This does a good job.

title: Working perfectly
text: This shredder has replaced several smaller shredders that we have around. We don't shred a ton but enough to make it worthwhile to have one. It's fast and easy -- just push and go. I'm using 8 gallon clear trash bags inside to catch everything and the hardest part was finding the switch (it's on the back, near the top and was against the wall) everything else was easy, fast and works great. We haven't had any jams or any trouble at all so hopefully that will continue. For now - 5 stars.

title: Nice once you manage to set it up
text: I think it ended up taking me two or three days (off and on) to get this printer set up. I started on my desktop but had trouble with the software so I switched to the install on my phone. It was NOT intuitive and didn't "automatically" set up. I had trouble getting it onto my network and had to keep coming back later because it wasn't easy. I've still had trouble occasionally with printing from my phone and it seems to be working just fine now but it was a pain to set up. I'm fairly techie and this was just frustrating. That being said now that it's set up, it's a fairly nice laser printer. It's relatively fast and produces great quality. (Be sure to reset the printer to single sheets if you don't want front to back -- that's what mine defaulted to). Footprint is good, once I got it setup it seems to be working fine and hopefully it'll stay that way.

title: Works Perfectly
text: I have an older HP printer that works like a champ and has a small footprint but it’s almost cheaper to buy a new printer than to buy new toner cartridges. I thought I’d give this “brand” a try and it’s just as good as the HP OEM toners. No glitches and the payoff is the same. I’m a believer.

title: Easy to read and great for larger hands
text: This was a bit hard to use at first because the keys are so very big. It was an adjustment but once I got it, I LOVE this. I can read it from a distance, it’s so very easy to use and doesn’t have a ton of functions that I have no idea what to do with or would ever use. Back to basics!

title: Holding up but a finer line than I wanted
text: These work great on my smaller white board but I was hoping they would also work on my larger one. While they do work, I really need something with a wider tip. I’ll keep looking for the big board but these are great for the smaller one and I like have color options.

title: Great size for having on hand all the time.
text: I started with a plan to journal but I can't bring myself to just sit and write "stuff" in a book. However, these have proven to be VERY helpful for taking notes and reminders while I'm out and about. It fits nicely in my bag and I find I pull it out a lot. I suppose if you journal it would be a bit small in size but that's what makes it perfect for me.

title: I'm still "planning" to journal
text: This appears to be a nice sturdy book that will wear well. I'm still trying to convince myself to journal so it's sitting on the counter. Maybe it'll be a gift. Not sure I'll ever get started, but if you do or are planning to but this is a good starter volume.

title: These are my favorites for larger projects
text: These have a 2 inch expansion and say they'll hold 400 sheets. I don't know about that because I'm not counting that many pages but while I like the flat folders for everyday stuff, I do work on some big projects and these are perfect. I do like the color although sometimes I have to try and remember which is which but by the time I've used a certain color folder for a while, I associate it with a project and can easily grab and go with everything I need at one time. Pendaflex makes a good product. I've tried look alikes and sometime the sides aren't assembled right and you have to tear them to make them work. I hate having to do that when I grab a folder, I want to put my stuff in and go. I've never had that issue with a pendaflex product and I'm tired of trying to guess whether the product will work or not. Sticking with what I know.

title: Reusable Post it Notes
text: YAY! Great add on - I use them to keep track of things on my white board (things that move around can just be restuck in the new place until everything is organized). I had some white ones that I used pretty regularly but the colors give me even more options. Love them!

title: Project Files
text: These are flat paper holders. I love these. I use them to keep things together rather than staple or clip and they hold enough for most of my projects to be included in one folder. I then batch a bunch of these flats and put them into an expanding folder so everything is easy to get to, kept together and can be hauled around. I did try the colored ones but couldn't remember what color was what and although I'd prefer that for easy grabbing, I can label these and it does the same thing.

title: Nice writing instrument
text: This has a nice, easy to hold barrel and the ink flows fine. I've got them laying around all over the place and haven't had any trouble with any of them. Fine product. However, they are billed as having a cord hanger. If that's why you are looking at these, guess again. The holder is on the bottom of the pen so if you remove the cap and try to put it onto the bottom of the pen - gone is your pen holder. There is a loop on the pen clip that would work but it's got a 5 star for desk top use and a 3 star for the cord holder.

title: They are Pendaflex
text: I broke down and ordered these because I was tired of slightly cheaper expanding folders that just don't last against the wear and tear of my life. These are tried and true, worth anything extra and just work fine (no glued edges you have to separate) and hold up mightly to my less than gentle handling. These are letter size and they expand and hold a bunch of stuff (probably more than I should stuff them with but - hey they can take it!) No more imitations for me!

title: Might work for you
text: This does help keep my chair from giving in more where I've been sitting but the fabric isn't overly comfortable. I would have preferred a smoother surface. Probably wouldn't have noticed in heavier pants but it's summer in Florida and I can feel the pattern when I'm wearing a skirt or shorts. It does help with positioning but I'll be looking for something else that's more comfortable. If the mesh pattern doesn't affect you, it will work but if you are fussy like me (hate the heat) I'd keep looking.

title: Keeps my knees up and my feet from dangling.
text: I'm vertically challenged (5'2") and often find my legs swinging which is extraordinarily stressful and makes sitting for a long period of time unpleasant to painful. This fits neatly under my desk and allows me to rest my feet so my legs are supported. It's lightweight and might work better on carpet but I've got it on tile floor and it's not too bad for staying place. It is not slippery so it doesn't go sliding away and once it's in position, it stays so it's been really helpful for spending time at my computer.

title: Great gift for struck at home kids
text: I sent one of these to my nephew - 3.5 yo and his little sister was so jealous I sent another for her (2 yo). The kids LOVE these and have spent hours playing - drawing and the older one has practiced his letters and they’ve been quietly entertained for hours with the temps way below freezing so they are inside all day. Their mother and father have thanked me several times and it’s proven to be a great gift, keeps them quiet - it’s particularly good before nap time and it’s a winner all the way around. I was surprised how excited they were to get them and I expect there’s some “it’s for big kids” charm to it as well.

title: Seems to help keep me upright in my chair
text: I'm short (5'2") and my feet don't usually hit the floor. I find myself stretching, slumping or hunched forward to get any work done. This went right under my desk and I already feel better. By getting my feet up a bit, I can actually sit back in my chair. Love it - I've tried others but they lift my feet too high, this has options and the slant makes it work for me. Its also soft, not gushy, but firmly soft and isn't cold so I can go barefoot too.

title: I need more!
text: It seems you can go a long time without a white board, until you’ve had one. This is a decent size and the quality is great. We haven’t had any ghosting - about the only complaint I have is that now I need an even larger one (just have to find a place to put it....) Not sure how I lived without one for so long. Definitely a Must - not something that’s just a “nice to have”. If you haven’t invested in one, stop waiting around. This is a great board and a great size.

title: Laser ready
text: These go easily through the laser printer without getting stuck or jammed. There are 2 half sheet labels on one piece of 8x11 paper. I have run them through twice, to get both labels used separately and haven't had any trouble with them. Print comes out clear and crisp, Labels are thick enough to use on my bypass tray and I haven't had a single problem with them. About the only thing I might complain about is that there isn't a gap between the labels so you have to bend the backing - which is not a big deal.

title: Announcement: I am going to start journaling
text: I've got a million things going on all the time and have heard several people speak recently about how journaling helped/helps them. Sounds reasonable so I ordered my books. They look nice, are sturdy and I carry at least one around where-ever I go - One day I might even start journaling but for now, I can jot down notes, I love the size of this - fits in a pocket and it's easy to spot when I lay it down somewhere.

title: Still on the fence
text: Well these do what they say they are supposed to. The problem I have with them is that first of all I have to remember TSM (that stupid mask)  which is the real problem. Once I'm out and about, it's not that hard but I'm not used to having to think of everything before coffee in the morning. This does work, I'm just not sure of the real need for this lanyard. I have a metal nose piece on my favorite masks and they don't just lay flat on the lanyard so I'm not sure I'm the ideal target market for this item. If your mask folds flat you should be okay and this isn't bad (it's easy to spot and easy to use) but if you've got a nose piece that doesn't go limp, you might want to double check that this will work for you.

title: Really like these
text: So far I haven’t had anything these marks don’t brush off of or wash off of. I like the options for different colors and I love that they are packaged in a hard box with spaces inside for each piece. No more crumbles and broken pieces. While the chalk is good and I like having different color options, the packaging makes it that much better.

title: Surprisingly resilient
text: I wasn’t sure about this since I planned to toss it into my carryon bag and it was bound to get knocked around but I’ve tried many other notebooks and all have been failures. This survived my first two trips with it. While I love my iPhone and use it for a ton of things, sometimes I just need to jot a note or take down a number and I like having a pad handy. This works well for me and I’m very happy with the quality and most importantly the durability of the cover.

title: Nice for mom and kids
text: Magnet drawing board: works great. A little smaller than most. I like that the shapes “click” in so the baby can’t pull them out to chew on. Very pleased

title: Didn't work for me
text: Apparently the printer makers are getting not-nice even more than before. It's almost cheaper to buy a new printer than to purchase OEM ink. The new printers seem to be hardcoded to only accept "their" ink. These didn't work for me and trying to buy OEM cartridges is almost as much as a new printer -- going to look for another brand or maybe an older printer?

title: Best thing ever
text: I’ve found this to be the MOST helpful thing I’ve ever added to my household. It allows me to work while watching tv or sitting up in bed or traveling without hunching over or trying to make do with a tv table or something along those lines. I’ve used it for both my tablet and my laptop and it’s the best thing EVER. It folds down so is out of the way when I don’t need it but pops right back up when I want to use it. I bought another one for my other home so I’m never without it.

title: A lifesaver
text: I’m homeschooling and sometimes the paperwork gets a bit out of hand. This has proven to be a lifesaver and keeps all the current and upcoming material organized enough that even when traveling, we manage to do “school” while on the road without teacher going crazy. I love that there are enough sections and that it closes securely so nothing goes flying.

title: Great scale
text: I don't have to weigh a ton of packages or letters but I do have to do it occasionally. This has a very small footprint, it hides away easily and I can get it when I need it. I can also see the numbers so it's a winner in my book. It has a power button and a tare button so that's pretty much all I need.

title: Pretty good labels
text: I saw a lot of reviews that these didn't work but they work just fine in my zebra printer. They aren't super thick but that's fine and the print comes out on them nice a clear. They are easy to install, easy to use and work for me.

title: LOVE that there is a back
text: I'm short on space so everything has to be squeezed in. This has proven to be a great organizer -- it's exactly the size of it's footprint - no extra "stuff" to take up room and there is a back so when I shove things into a section they don't go out the back (to be lost forever). Pretty sturdy I haven't worried and it has been full at times. Enough sections for me to actually get (or at last pretend to get) organized.

title: Love my white boards
text: I admit to being a white board junkie. I got used to using them years ago and now I'm not sure I can work without one handy. I'm very visual and having this propped in front of me while I'm working keeps me on track. It's a little awkward to move around because of the size but I can live with that and it's big enough that I can work through my problems without losing track of what I'm trying to do. Very handy to have and cleans up well.

title: Just Okay
text: If all you need is a lightweight, infrequently used shredder, this might work for you. I find it a bit flimsy and it's very slow to start - I can't just press the button and stick the stuff in. It only handles a few sheets at a time. For my needs I'll be looking for a bigger, better faster but if you only need to use if once in a while this may be enough.

title: Great little label printer.
text: So far so good. This took me a few minutes to set up correctly but once it was installed and running it hasn't been a problem. Prints quickly, recognizes label ends and so far no jams, no skips and no tangles. Just put the labels in, and off they come in a nice neat pile. I've been using sheet labels for a while in a laser printer but these are way more economical and easy to use.

title: Great Laminator, expensive film
text: The laminator comes with a laminated Quick Start User Guide in pictograph form.  I didn’t feel comfortable using the laminator by just reading the guide, so I watched a couple of Youtube videos that gave a demonstration.  I laminated two 8.5 x 11 sheets of cardstock in the Auto Feed/Auto Cut Mode.  It laminated perfectly without having to feed the sheets manually, and it automatically cut them uniformly. Then I laminated two 5 x 5 sheets of cardstock in the Manual Feed/ Manual Cut Mode. I fed each sheet separately. To cut, you must make sure you see the product before you push the Cut button.  I found a lot of wasted film between the 2 sheets, but with practice, maybe the second sheet could have been inserted sooner to avoid wasted film.  There is also wasted film at the start-up; the machine cuts off a length at the beginning before the sheet comes through.  I like the quality of the lamination, the ease of changing film cartridges, and the “no-effort” required to laminate a stack of 8.5 x 11 sheets.  But the cost of a laminating cartridge is very expensive.

title: Seems like a great replacement
text: My printer started telling me it was out of toner so I ordered these to give them a try. Of course the printer lied to me and ran on and on. It finally died and I pulled out one of these and inserted it into the printer. Great quality and so far no hiccups with the cartridge. I can't speak to longevity (yet) but I was leery going in and was pleasantly surprised. No shadows or splotches and no printer errors. Working great so far.

title: Easy to use gel pen - Mine are RED!
text: These work great and write wonderfully. They come with an easy grip handle and look like a regular gel pen. I can't tell if they are better or worse than the others but I did notice that there is a little red ring right around the pen so you can tell what color you are getting. In some pens its the color of the barrel but this is way more subdued but still easy to see. I like  to write stuff I want to see again in red so it pops up when I'm looking through a pile but I have to be careful not to make everything red. Nice smooth write. Good color. Nothing I can think of wrong with these.

title: Great markers, consistent highlighting
text: I love highlighters and you can find them scattered everywhere I work. I find them extremely useful for marking my place, separating things that are important from unimportant and even to mark areas and sections of documents for different reasons. For me, I also find that different colors work better for me because I like to be able to grab all the things related to one subject with ease. So this package of highlighters gives me a range of colors that I assign to different things. I prefer the BIC liners because for me they seem to last longer and give a brighter (more easily spotted) line. These work great and solve my need for organization.

title: Good wrist rests for keyboard and mouse
text: I spend a lot of time on the computer and find that these types of add ons are almost necessary. Between the keyboard rest and the mouse rest, you'll improve your ergonomics immensely. The wide pad sits right below my keyboard and allows me to rest my wrists without drooping and definitely improves my carpal tunnel problems. The mouse pad could be a little wider since I sometimes go crazy moving the mouse all over the place but it does the job. For myself, I prefer a mouse pad/wrist rest in one piece so everything is in "one". If you are a general user, at least using the wrist rest for the mouse will improve your movements. I wish I had a set of these to carry along with my laptop but they are just too big (long) to be carrying around all the time. I do have a wrist rest that I carry around so I do get that benefit. These work, you'll have to tweek the position to your perfect position and they are lightweight and easy to move around without sliding.

title: Great markers
text: These write well and erase well and don't stink! Pretty much perfect for markers. So far they've been holding up, I expect them to last a while but just the fact that they write clear and erase clear makes them superior to many of the other markers that are out there.

title: Works well only a short learning curve
text: Never having used this before I was a bit unsure but it didn't take me long and I was wrapping like a pro. This was relatively easy to use (a bit awkward and heavy at first) but once you get started you'll want to wrap everything.

title: Sheet Protectors
text: I use a lot of these and this brand is up to the regular standard. They keep the papers inside clean (and safe from little hands) and allow me to keep my papers up to date easily. I have been using them 2 per sleeve and they work just fine. Can never have enough of these. They are lightweight and clear so they don't blur your pages.

title: Portable white boards -- no more paper
text: Love whiteboards. They are better than paper in every way. You can tweek by erasing something and you can stand back to see what you've got. You can also rearrange them as necessary. These are two sided and the come with markers and erasers. The erasers are good and nice  to have but the markers aren't up to par -- not a deal breaker for me so this is a very handy set to have around.

title: Sheet Protectors for things you want to keep
text: I use a lot of these and this set is as good as any I've tried. I work around makeup and there are always splotches or smears appearing out of nowhere. With the sheet protectors all our important pages are saved. They are easy to use  and I've been inserting 2 pages into each one (front and back).

title: Big and Bold - they can't say they didn't see it
text: These are big, bold and bright. No one can claim not to have seen them. They are easy to write on (I've been using a Sharpie--big and bold background seems to require some statement making ink too) and so far have been sticking very nicely. While they haven't actually been in a flood or wind storm, they have managed to last through regular use, children and "blind" teens that can't seem to see anything else. I'm happy.

title: Awesome Quality
text: Very sharp looking. Almost too good for a pencil holder so I'm going to have to think about how to use it. Love the look (non-shiny silver) and the weight (it feels expensive). This would make a great gift for someone's office -- it really does look good. It arrived in a box that would easily serve as a gift box.

title: 11x17 Clipboard
text: HA! Do you have any idea how hard it is to find a clipboard that holds ledger sized paper and doesn't weigh a ton? Difficult. I was happy to see these. This is a 3 pack so I've got one for home, and one for work, and one for travel. I use them to work on spreadsheets when I can't sit in front of the computer any more and it's nice to have a clip board that actually fits. It's a very lighweight board, I'm not convinced it'll hold up to heavy wear and tear, but so far, so good and I know where to get them if these have to be replaced.

title: BIG keys and BIG display
text: Basic calculator with BIG keys and BIG display. I've noticed that as the people in my life get older the calculators get smaller and numbers get downright tiny. This solves the problem. Is lightweight, big enough to spot in the mess on my desk and it works flawlessly. It also has keys that are big enough for even the men's fingers and no one has complained about not being able to read it. YAY!

title: BIG digits and you can go back and see what you actually entered
text: I've been thinking about dragging out my old desktop calculator with a paper tape to allow me to go back and double check sometimes. I don't need it often, but when I do, it's annoying to have to drag it out or re-add the list to try and find a mistake. This shows up a few lines but you can roll back and look further back. I don't have to worry about paper, it's got a small footprint and does exactly what my old desktop  calculator does in half the size and with way bigger numbers so I can actually read it.

title: Letter size Hanging Folders
text: Standard letter size hanging folders that have 1/3 tabs and fit nicely into my file cabinet. They compare favorably with the brand that starts with a P and look like they'll hold up to the extreme wear and tear of living in my file cabinet. Great value and they seem to be working as well as the more expensive brand.

title: Good weight and durability and the price is right
text: So far, great folders. They are 1/3rd cut so they are easy to use and I personally love colored folders because I can often remember seeing something long ago based on the color of the folder. These appear to be the same weight of the well known brand starting with a P and the price makes these a shoe in.

title: Fun and easy to use (and useful)
text:
Love it. The apple is heavy enough to stay in one place and I finally have post-it notes when I need/want them in. It was a little tricky getting the front off the apple, but once I did, it clicked right back together and instantly post-it notes were available. Looks cute on my desk, makes getting sticky notes when and where I need them easy and the colors are brights so I can also find them again when I'm looking for something.

It comes with several refills and more can be purchased. I like the idea of having them within reach and being able to grab one as I go.

title: Very sturdy -- full sized
text: Full sized Wall File. Measure first but it will hold an office full of paperwork and is fast and easy to install. I didn't measure the length and expected something smaller, it's perfect for what I need, but I was surprised. Just a few minutes to install and very sturdy.

title: Big buttons, big numbers and solar powered.
text: So far, so good. The solar panel is fairly sensitive so it's reliable. The buttons are easy for me to hit without having to be too precise and the numbers show up so I can see them even without glasses and from a distance. Folds flat to store. Winner all the way around.

title: Writes nicely, feels good in the hand
text: Nice pen with a good feel and it writes beautifully. I'm a bit concerned about getting refills but I expect I'll be able to find them when it's time. If you still write (with a pen) this has a nice fine line and is very smooth. It feels good in my hand.  In these days of disposable everything, this is a nice addition to my desk.

title: Durable and useful
text: They fit perfectly both laterally and vertically and are very handy to have. These are comparable to the other brand and are well made and durable. Definitely a must have to keep organized in our "paperless" society. (Seems like I have more paper than ever). They are standard sized and come with 1/5th cut plastic tag holders.  Fast and easy to set up and handy to have.

title: Easy to Setup and Great Looking Output
text: This took about 10 minutes from box to working. The longest part of it was loading the disk onto my computer so it could print wirelessly. I used the mobile app to get it started and then popped in the disk and I was ready to go. It's probably the easiest printer I've ever set up. I sent some color pages to the printer and it did a beautiful dual side printing where the colors on the paper look just like the original did from my screen.  A simple basic laser color printer. This is a winner!

title: Big Board, Lightweight
text: This works for me -- it's big (3 feet by 4 feet) and double sided. When you write on it, it cleans nicely, leaving no shadows and it's pretty lightweight without feeling flimsy. I haven't quite decided where it goes (if I mount it on the wall, only one side is usable) so I'm considering options. At the present time, it's sitting on a table and leaning against the wall and is in use. So far, so good. The box was banged up and the board was set into plastic corners that broke all over the place but the plastic wrapped board is fine. The instructions show that there is a cap on the corners to hide the screw holes but those are not included on the one I got so if that's important to you, be sure and check.

title: Endless Color? or it seems that way compared to other printers
text: Fast and easy setup with no trouble. Also works with my iPhone, iPad, etc. Print quality is just okay but the fact that I don't have to go to the store once a week for refill cartridges makes my day. I haven't used it a ton yet so we'll see how long it lasts but for right now it gives me color and a decent output. I do see that it has some "nice" features that I'll have to explore but for now, I've just used it for printing and I did one scan which was fine. I'm not sure I find inkjets practical for making copies but this might do it--time will tell.

title: sturdy and sleek looking
text: Love that I can have my laptop and mouse on the same desk. super comfortable to use. No assembly required. Just opened the box and started working right away. I use it slightly tilt as it helps with my wrist. I am a student as well as working full time so I will definitely need to support my wrist with all the typing I will be doing.

title: Best ever - but wait for a sale
text: I’m obsessed with this bed desk! It folds flat, tilts to adjust, and is basically the best thing I’ve ever purchased. I bought it on Black Friday for about $65 and it seems to go on sale regularly, so as much as I love it, I don’t think I would spend over $100 on it.

text: I have lower back problems and unable to sit long. I prefer to lie flat on my bed while watching netflix etc on my laptop. This desk gives a decent height and angle to view. Depending on my angle, whether or not i have a pillow under my head, i may need to prop one between my laptop and desk. There is a stopper underneath that prevents the machine slipping, but it would have been more convenient to have side straps to hold down. Doesnt stop the functionality though. Recommended.

title: Locking mechanism is not working properly
text: Used this item with no problems for 5 years, average of once a week. Lately though the locking mechanism is not reliable - the step stool closes suddenly even with small weights.

title: Yes, they are mere rubber bands - probably from a rubber tree. As old-fashioned as can be.
text: The good thing is the price. 1 box will last maybe 2 years. So why not? Nothing worse than running out of rubber bands when you really need one, right?

title: Drawers don't come out. Unlike 3-tier similar units.
text: Being able to slide out a drawer and swap it into another location would be handy. For instance if you have 2 drawers of diapers and the top is emptied, then just slide out the top empty one and swap it with the full one below. Later, refill the lower one as might be convenient. Rather then reload the top from the bottom one handful at a time. Also if you are rearranging storage, simply swapping drawers around is much easier then unloading the source drawer and reloading the target drawer. Swappable drawers are present on the 3-stage units. Also no wheels but that I can understand due to the tippy height of this unit. (PS: is swappable not a legal word? And tippy? So why the squiggly red line?). So slightly disappointed hence 4 not 5 stars.

title: A commodity item. We all know what this is.
text: It is what it is. Useful. Prosaic. An office necessity. Satisfactory in all respects but hard to get excited about.

title: The medium is the message. The flag is the medium. The message is "Glory to Ukraine."
text: Small enough to be discrete. (Don't want to piss-off the snooty anti-flag neighbors) but just big enough to be seen. Do people know what it is, sky over land? I can only hope they do. If your heart bleeds for the Ukranians whose glorious defense has succeeded beyond all expectations (except their own) and which defense will go down in the history books, then put out this small, well-made, symbolic flag. Next to but slightly below your American flag, if you show such on days other than the 4th. Each displayed flag is a twit to Vlad the Invader. The more the better.

title: Inflated and kept inflated.
text: Yes, it is a small inner tube. Like for kids on the lake. As one might expect only much smaller. Inflation tool actually works nicely. Lotsa pumps but high appropriate pressure can be achieved within moments. Leaks? Bought in May now late July. Light use. No leaks. Good. Better than expected. BTW: Good luck to all those who need such a thing! Been there...

title: Very satisfactory. Big enough to be useful.
text:
Ideally, it might be 1 in higher. Ideally, the drawer might be 1/2 inch deeper to store the wireless mouse, Ideally, the click-stop height adjustments, which jam and require a whack to release, might be replaced by a friction plate tightened by a knob - yes, I know friction plates eventually wear and become slippery plates. But still. Old folks' old hands need something easier. Meantime we'll see if a touch of WD40 does the trick.
BTW: The plastic insert that holds a laptop in place does not fall out unlike the wooden versions. Nice! I tried and returned others.

Overall: If everything were perfect, there'd be no room for improvement and no one wants that! So for now, this is as good as I have found after extensive searching. Very satisfactory.

title: About the same price per ream as, say, Office Depot. But delivered. Very convenient.
text:

As to quality: standard smooth paper of good weight for ink jets. Very satisfactory. Just what one would hope for.

And so, yes, will buy from Amazon again in about a year when we likely run out.

I use the fridge handles when needed and step down carefully as 13" is a long step. Snap it shut and put away. When folded, stands neatly on its own. Take care!

title: Well, well, well - there is progress even in simple things
text: This is a clever tape dispenser that works better than any I have had in over 40 years at the desk. Trick is the moving armature that tilts up when the tape is pulled making the cutting bar more effective. Somebody at Scotch was working CAD and this is the result. Nice build, nice weight, nice finish, nice action. Think about replacing your old, un-thought of tape dispensers with this as a decade overdue upgrade. Make it a desktop treat...

title: Nesting leads to stress on the lower piece whose sides bend out and bind the upper piece
text: Cannot nest. Here's what happened: placed the longer piece in a rather shallow drawer (hey I did not build this place). Placed the shorter piece on top at one end. Noted immediately that the upper piece descended half-way into the lower piece. Thus the upper piece took 1/2 of the available space of the lower piece. Why so much? 1/4 inch tracking would be fine and preserve more space in the lower piece, rather than take away HALF of the usable lower space. But it gets worse! Placed 2 tubes of ordinary toothpaste in the upper piece while in the backmost position and slid it forward. The walls of the lower piece spread apart under this huge weight (joke) and the upper piece FELL into the lower piece as the lower side walls opened in the middle, binding all movement. Poor design, poor thought, poor engineering.

The holder stores nicely under the tray when not in use.  It can also be placed on a desk if you want to stand while using your laptop.  I wish there was a small drawer to hold a couple of pens and a note pad (when using in bed).

The only complain is the height at the lowest position is still higher than what I preferred. For it to earn an extra star, the stand should be an inch lower at the lowest locked position. title: Rickety, Unstable, and Doesn’t Roll with Minimal Weight
text: It assembled easily and drawers worked smoothly, unlike a similar style single tier version which I disassembled and returned immediately. However, after loading the cart with some very lightweight nail art supplies (no polishes!) it was very wobbly and less than stable. The wheels that are supposed to make it easy to move don’t! And if you do get it to roll, the entire cart feels like it’s about to self-destruct. I want to reemphasize here that the items in my art are basically things like little pots of glitter, nail decal cards, cotton rounds, and cosmetic wedges, and roughly 2 dozen little paint brushes! All told there’s probably less than 3 lbs of weight in mine! I honestly can’t imagine what good a portable storage cart is if it won’t roll and is too rickety to handle a certain amount of weight! I’m disappointed because I had high hopes for solving some of my storage problems, but it’s precarious and temporary at best! I’d be returning this too, but I already recycled the packaging. Waste of time and money!

title: Unstable and Drawers Won’t Slide
text: I was really looking forward to this cart to organize odds and ends that have been accumulating on the bathroom countertops. I purchased a 15 drawer version (2 tiers) at the same time for my nail art supplies at the same time, although the larger one was delivered a day earlier. I assembled it just the day before and as it turned out, that was a good thing, since no assembly instructions came with the 8 drawer cart. Everything seemed to be going together fine—until I started trying to insert the drawers. They were just slightly too large to slide into the slots! I loosened the bottom and top crossbars that connect the two sides and was able to get the drawers in with a bit of effort, but they could not be opened without bracing the cart and really pulling hard. Once I retightened the crossbars, it was nearly impossible. Fully assembled and appropriately tightened, the cart is wobbly and unstable and leans to one side or the other. The bigger issue is the inability to easily slide open the drawers, since that’s the entire purpose of a storage cart! I considered trying to figure out ways to get the thing to be functional; I had just spent all that time putting it together. In the end though, I decided that I would very likely only be wasting more of my time with no guarantee that it would work any better. So I took everything apart, repackaged it, and will be sending it back. I’ll get another 15 drawer model if I get another, but I’m pretty much over assembling (and UNassembling) storage carts for the near future! What good is a storage cart if the drawers won’t open? What a huge waste of time! And now I have to haul it to a UPS drop off site too!

title: Everything It Claims To Be
text: I purchased this primarily for the purpose of doing nail art while watching TV in bed. I also ordered the clip-on rechargeable light. Honestly, the things you could use it for are unlimited! Everything works exactly as described in the product information and it is VERY sturdy. In fact, it just might be THE BEST purchase I have ever made from Amazon! The only possible negative might be that it sits just below chest level even with the legs at their lowest level, but I’m 5’6” and I actually prefer having plenty of leg room. It’s a comfortable height for eating and working! I also like using the book rack and love that it has a spot underneath to slide into for storage. No need to keep up with loose parts! If you are in the market for a bed table you won’t go wrong with this one!

title: Excellent and Beyond Expectations
text:
I don’t know how many different pencil cases I looked at before ultimately deciding to select this one to store my Prismacolor and Fabre-Castellated Polychromos colored pencils. First, I liked the idea that there are 4 separate zippered sections instead of multiple pages of pencils flopped together. I can open as few or as many sections as I need without disrupting everything. The zippers work smoothly as advertised. Secondly, unlike the majority of other cases on the market, the outside is made of water-resistant fake leather, which additionally doesn’t pick up pet hair and is easy to clean. Finally, each zippered section is composed of two sides of rigid material that is sturdy and protective. I was able to fit approximately 43 pencils on each page. The first and last elasticized slots hold 2 pencils; the 13 inner slots hold 3. Loading the case was monotonous—I have A LOT of pencils—but I’m absolutely sure I will use them more often than I did when they were in the flimsy, spill-prone trays from the manufacturers! I am extremely pleased with my choice!

Having said that, there IS room for improvement. A large zipped pocket on the exterior would be helpful for storing erasers, sharpeners, and other supplies. Two pockets would be even better! It would also be nice to have the ability to attach a shoulder strap to make transporting the case easier. At present however, this case has my recommendation!

The colors of the flowers are realistic and although they don't look handmade like a watercolor does, it is as close as you can get without being watercolor. These are really nice cards.

title: If You Have The Desk Space, This Might Be Worth Having
text:
I have a thermal label printer. I don't have a lot of desk room in some cases, but when I want to print out a lot of labels, I set up a table top area where I could have my set up. This holder is perfect for that scenario.

ASSEMBLY
This assembles pretty well. It comes apart and is compact to store. When I want to use it, I put it together, and I have a great place to use rolls or folded labels.

FIT
This fits a decent pile of folded labels, but I do not do massive mailings with labels, so I cut my stack of folded labels down in half. It works great. This also closes up to accommodate my smaller roll of labels nicely too. They feed pretty well and so far no issues.

PERFORMANCE
This works well when I want to do a decent amount of labels from folded, or if I want to use a roll. I have had no issues with it at this point.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This goes together easily and fits both my rolls and folded piles of labels nicely.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is great to have so I can now use rolls for my labels instead of just folded ones. I will update if anything else happens I think I need to tell you about.

title: I Think My HP Printer Head Was Too Far Gone
text:
I had an HP Printer I LOVED. I had managed to clean the print head as new ones were hard to get and VERY expensive. The old cleaning kit was no good so I got this one.

PARTS ALL INCLUDED
This is not difficult to do, just have some paper towels ready. Everything needed came in the kid.

DID IT HELP?
I am sad to say that I think my printer head was too far gone. I tried to use this several times and it just would not clean out again. If you were to clean your printer head AS SOON AS IT IS SHOWING SIGNS OF CLOGGING then this would probably work. I think my printer head was clogged too long and it was not cleaning out properly.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you have a new clog in your printer head, this will probably work well. For my HP printer that had been clogged for quite a while, it just was not able to free it up again.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. I have a new printer - actually two of them- and do not need a cleaning yet. However, based on my HP experience I am putting this at 3 stars. If I have an additional experience with my newer printers, I will try to update this as I am keeping it handy in case. This time I will clean immediately.
