title: As Long As You Keep A Few Things In Mind These Are Wonderful
text:
We have some artists in the family, so when it comes to art supplies we have a very willing team ready to play with and try anything! Let's see how these measured up.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These pens come with a large selection of brightly colored inks. When it comes to a full spectrum of color, these pens cover all of the colors that we personally like to have on hand for art projects. The pens themselves come with a retractable push button on the top. When you first attempt to use them, there is a tiny little cap on the point which helps keep the ink from drying out or leaking. We kept these in a tiny zip bag for future times if we are not going to use them for a while. That eventually went by the wayside.

The points are fine and the contents are on the par with drawing inks- not the writing king.

WHAT TO DO WITH THESE PENS?
These pens are predominately set up for coloring, although you can write with them. Each color is a beautiful translucent color. These pens can be used for drawing fine lines, cross hatching, or filling in small areas of coloring books or drawings. The colors are bright and clear.

HOW DO THESE PERFORM?
These are beautiful pens. They are wonderful for coloring in SMALL areas of very intricate coloring books. Larger areas take an awful lot of ink. They do not dry as quickly as writing pens so you have to plan to TAKE YOUR TIME with these. they take about a minute to set. If you don't wait long enough THESE WILL SMUDGE.

ANY OTHER PROBLEMS?
These pens are great. If you remember to plan ahead and take your time with them so they don't smudge, they are beautiful to work with. Other than that, they really don't have any other issues, other than occasional fluctuations in ink flow but it is not that bad at this time.

BLEED THROUGH?

THE BOTTOM LINE
These pens are beautiful. They are great for coloring tiny areas, drawing, or cross hatching. You HAVE to remember to pause after each use or they will smudge. They don't take long to set, and the colors are worth the effort to take your time with these.

MY RATING
Five stars. I love these pens. I use them with drawing ink, markers, and some colored pencils too. My artist family members enjoy them as well.

I will update if there are any future problems. For now, these are really well liked in my house.

title: I Am BLOWN AWAY At How Nice These Are! PERFECT Canning Labels
text:
Every year I try to can some fruits and vegetables so we can enjoy some freshness in the following winter. Sometimes it is hard to get markers to stick, or to get jars properly labeled for various reasons. These labels solved them for me!

WHAT ARE THESE LABELS LIKE?
These labels are a matte white in color. They are laid out in a nice way on the sheet so they can be easily peeled off one at a time. They indicate that they are permanent in nature. I used these with inkjet, but they can also be used for laser jet.

HOW DO YOU USE THEM?
Avery online has the site listed on the package that you go to for pre-designed labels that you can use as a template, or you can design and upload your own.

CAN YOU DO EACH LABEL SEPARATELY OR THE ENTIRE SHEET AT ONCE?
Both. You can choose to write something different on each label, or you can decide to do the entire sheet.

WHAT DID I USE THESE FOR?
Although I could see these used for lotion, soap, or other labeled containers, I chose to use these on jar lids for my canning products. The jar lids sometimes are difficult to get markers to stick to, but the label is perfect.

Also, some people re-use jar lids and this solves the problem of how to write over last year's marker label.

HOW TO GET THEM TO STICK
I made sure to wipe the lids with alcohol dampened paper towel to remove any traces of grease or anything that would make the labels not stick. It worked great for me.

HOW DID THEY PRINT OUT FOR ME?
I used an HP Deskjet Pro 8710 printer and the labels printed out flawlessly. I am so impressed. I did not have to tweak a thing, something I am not used to with other labels or printer combos I have used.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want to have a way to label soap, lotion, or other containers these labels are wonderful. They are easy to use, printed out perfectly and stick well so that I know they will stick to my jars of food that I canned without peeling off too easily.

MY RATING
I LOVE LOVE LOVE THESE LABELS! Five stars. They really do work beautifully.

title: Handy Small Footprint Great Cutter- Blades Replaceable
text:
Do you know how many cutters we have gone through? No, of course you don't! Well let me tell you, it is frustrating to find a really good one. Let's see how this lines up.

WHAT IS THIS CUTTER LIKE?
This paper cutter is small footprint compared to some of them. It is loaded with measurements for just about every type of cutting I would want to do. The base is metal so I can even use it for tiny free form rotary cutting (with mat on it) on small areas of it or use it for marking fabric with a rotary marking wheel.

The side has a nice strong metal slider that has a plastic enclosed rotary blade housed in it. The paper is put under a clear holder. You slide the paper out to the proper place, and then slide the slider along the paper and it cuts quickly and neatly.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This cutter is one of the nicer ones we have had. It is easy to cut- and it does cut up to 10 sheets of paper very well. No jagged edges, no slipping of paper, and it really seems to be well set up.

ARE BLADES REPLACEABLE?
The nice part is that the blade in this can be replaced!

IS THIS MADE FOR LARGE PAPER?
This seems to be able to handle only up to about 12 inches of paper as a max,

THE BOTTOM LINE
For smaller paper cutting for scrapbooking, other paper cutting needs, this is a really nice handy cutter. It is not too big, yet is able to handle up to 10 sheets of paper well.

MY RATING
Five stars for this cutter. I like it. It is easy to store, and yet pull out when needed. I not only use it for paper, but have used it for fabric as well within reason- more for a strong back board for cutting tiny pieces and not so much for cutting strips.

title: Great For Using On Colored Pencil Projects To Separate Out The Colors I Need At Each Stage
text:
I do a lot of colored pencil work. One thing that I have a hard time with is when I am working on a project and have to put all of my pencils away for a while, I hate to have to put them all away and get them back out again when it is time to pick up my project again. This case really helped solve the problem!

WHAT IS THIS CASE LIKE?
This case is bonded leather. That means that the leather is ground up with a binder and re-pressed out and given a nice durable coating on the outside which is why it is a more shiny black. The case holds a bunch of pencils and closes with a cord around a round leather button closure.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This case is perfect for my pencils. I am able to put all of the colors that I am working with of pencils so that next time I pick up my project, all I have to do is pick up my case, and all of the pencils are grouped together already. When I am done with them, I can put them back in my cases and replace them with my next load of colors for my project.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice leather pencil case to use for keeping pencils I need for projects. It is bonded leather and seems sturdy enough to use over time.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS for this one. It serves the purpose and the bonded leather is not a bother like it is for me in some items.

title: Great Hand Held Stapler, Sometimes Needs Two Hands
text:
I do a lot of work with thick piles of paper whether it is reprinting sections of books for education, or combining a variety of paperwork in booklet form. I also put together boxes on occasion. This stapler seemed like a good solution. Let's see how it measured up to the tasks!

WHAT IS THIS STAPLER LIKE?
This stapler is a hand held stapler which comes with a box of 2000 galvanized staples. The staples are size 73 (10mm). The stapler itself comes with two anvils. One is for making boxes, and the other is for standard stapling jobs.

The stapler is easy to fill. It has a thick metal plunger with a loop on the end for easy grabbing. There is a spring down the stem and the end pressed up against the staples once they are slid into the stapler. The plunger hooks into place so it stays put.

HOW IS THIS STAPLER TO USE?
This stapler has to depend upon hand strength to work. It is not the type you press down so you can not use body leverage to help press it. I found that to staple very thick things that are hard to get through, I had to use both hands and press heavily with both to make it work. One handed stapling in those cases would leave the staple half in and not closed.

I found that I can staple together small books of paper- about 30 pages tops and boxes that are able to be penetrated by the staples. I had one box so dense that the staples would not go through, but I think it had composite in it.

BOXES
The corner anvil does help to poke through the corners of boxes to staple and works well. It is pointed and not flat and is easy to change out. You do need to have a good straight edge screw driver to change the anvils.

EVALUATION
For the type of stapler it is, it works very well. I prefer the type that you press down upon for thicker booklets, but this does the job very well up to that point and on boxes.

THE BOTTOM LINE
With two anvils, easily changed with a screw driver, this hand held stapler goes through somewhat thick booklets and boxes nicely, sometimes using two hands of pressure. It is easy to fill and maintain.

MY RATING
I give this five stars. It is well marked, easy to use and refill and makes quick work of what I want to do with it. When it comes to booklets that are very thick, I move up to my heavy duty table top stapler, which is to be expected.

title: I Bet You Never Thought Of This Use (Bonus Funny Story)
text:
I like to have paper clips around the house. LOTS of them.

There is a family joke at our house about them. (skip if you are in a hurry)

One time when our son was little he had a fascination with caps that you could pound rocks on and they made a popping noise. I found them at a store (they were VERY hard to find) and with him with me, I diverted him using the cashiers as a tag team and quickly sneaked the package up to the register all paranoid that he would discover them, but he didn't. He was hard to surprise.

I wrapped them in a hurry too and could not wait until Christmas. I really built up the gift to him telling him he would be SO excited.

He saved it for last, opened it up and there was a whole collection of boxes of ..."gem clip paper clips"

He said in a monotone voice, "Oh wow. Gem clips. Yeah. I really am excited"

I grabbed the wrong package and in my hurry to hide them never realized it.

WHAT ARE THESE PAPER CLIPS LIKE?
These paperclips are just under 2 inches long. They are sturdy and strong, but most importantly, they are polished metal. That is important to me and let me tell you why. There are 10 boxes of these.

WHAT DO I USE THESE FOR ? (I BET YOU NEVER THOUGHT OF THIS ONE)
Not only do I use these for holding papers together and twisting into a number of ways, but in my fish aquariums ( I have many), I use these to hold seaweed down in the tanks which don't do well with suction cup seaweed holders.

I unbend the clip and make it into a triangle with the opening in the bottom. I slip the folded seaweed or cucumber slice or other vegetable onto the triangle, and then bury the bottom in the gravel (or other substrate). The piece that I slipped onto the triangle floats upward and stays where the shrimp and fish can peck at it. When I am done, I usually throw them away before the water can cause the finish to peel off at all. I might get two uses out of them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
In addition to the usual uses for paper clips, I also find these invaluable for my fish tanks to provide fresh snacks for my fish and shrimp. Because I use them only once or twice before they can corrode, I do go through them pretty quickly.

MY RATING
I give these five stars. They might not be Gem Clips, but they sure have a great finish on them and I can get two uses on them before I have to use a new one for my fish tanks.

title: One of the BEST Planners I Have Ever Used- Encourages As Well As Helps Organize
text:
I have had the chance to use a lot of different weekly/monthly planners. I have had the opportunity to run three separate things in my home all of which need to have organization and record keeping in them. I am always looking for new and easy to use planners. Let's see how this one measures up.

WHAT IS THIS PLANNER LIKE?
First of all, I love the cover. It is textured fabric in feel that is a magenta red color. The corners are reinforced with metal gold edges. I LOVE that feature. Corners are the first to wear out. The spiral binding again is fantastic. A real plus for me.

The pages inside have tabbed markers in them. They are COLOR CODED! For us visual people out there, that is a huge deal! When you turn to a tab, the first page you see is the calendar that is broken into squares. At the top of the page are goals for this month- LOVE that feature. Then there is a block at the top which allows for big ideas you might have for that month.

On the right side there is an outline of what is important for the month with check circles so you can mark them off when they are completed. Below that there is a space to list pursuits and possibilities. Again, in plain view so you can refer back them as life gets busy.

After that you have pages which give you a weekly breakdown. At the top are three boxes for the top 3 things of the week. Then there is a quote. On the right side, there is an outline area where you can list what needs to be done right now- this week. There are check circles to mark them off when you are finished.

Below that is a space for looking ahead- things you want to write in for the future weeks. There are wins of the week (to keep you encouraged). Then there is a space for three items with a 7 circle progression below it so you can put up to three things that you need to evaluate in increments - showing again PROGRESS.

At the end there is a chart for
gift ideas
birthdays and important dates
phone and email lists
expense tracking
three year reference
holiday list
looking ahead ideas for the future
notes in both lined and graph format

THERE IS EVEN A SEE THROUGH THICK PLASTIC POCKET AT THE BACK!

HOW DO I LIKE THIS PLANNER?
I have to say, whoever designed this planner is gifted in understanding how to not only keep a planner, but include encouraging spaces in the planner which are easy to reference and keep focused on what is GOOD and not what you have not completed or measured up to. I really love this thing. In fact, I plan to change everything over to this new planner for the upcoming year. I like it THAT much.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you are like me and need to be uplifted with progress as well as have lists of what needs to happen and be done, this planner could be for you. Very easy to read, refer to, and find in a pile of things, this planner is beautifully laid out and very easy to use. I find it uplifting and encouraging as well as helpful for organization. I highly recommend!

MY RATING
One of the very best planners I have ever used. I give this FIVE stars.

title: A Bit Dark But Perfect For Ingredient Labels, Or Earthy Appearance Labels  (Also See Tips and Tricks)
text:
As someone who makes their own lotions, body butters, soaps, and other personal care products, I like to have a variety of labels handy so that I can label everything I make in an easy to read manner. These labels are an interesting addition to my label drawer, but they do have limitations.

WHAT ARE THESE LABELS LIKE?
These labels are smaller than I expected them to be. That means that the typing you put on them is quite limited. Also, detailed graphics are limited as well. The color is a dark nutmeg color. It is not the easiest label to read. It looks a little darker than it does on the photo on the listing as well as the package. The labels have a bend place so that you can bend on the sheet, and they come off more easily. These claim to print to the edge, but they do not have a claim as far as water resistance.

HOW DID THE AVERY PROGRAM WORK?
This is the first out of three Avery labels that I have had a difficulty with. These printed a bit offset toward the top of the sheet of labels. They are still able to be used, but easy to knock off center. The program is easy, but keep in mind, these are SMALL LABELS. That means that the typing has to be clear, dark, substantial, and easy to read. I uploaded my own graphics and used text from the program.

TIPS AND TRICKS
These labels are best used for a simple title such as "Detergent Free Soap" or "Body Lotion" etc. You can also use these for ingredient labels easily as long as you use a font that is dark and easily read.

HOW DO THESE PERFORM?
I made these to go on my soaps that are wrapped in clear wrap. They work really well. I also have used them for ingredient labels with good success. They came off the sheets well and were easy to apply.

TIPS AND TRICKS
Try printing out the finished labels on plain paper, and then hold the labels up into the light with the printed sheet behind the label sheet. That will tell you how accurate it will be. If it is off, use the nudging feature of the Avery program to fine tune it. Also, be sure to limit text and make sure it is bold or it might be too hard to read.

THINGS I WOULD CHANGE
I think that these labels are a little on the dark side for printing. I would like to see them just a bit lighter. Colors do not show up well on these, so if you use color, make sure they are more on the earthy side of things. Bright colors will show up muted if you make your own graphics.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although these printed a bit offset, they are nice labels for simple labels or ingredient labels. The color is a little darker than expected but have an earthy feel to them. They are easy to peel off and work well in smaller places.

MY RATING
I have given these four stars. They are nice labels but the printing challenges and the darker color got me to remove one star. Still worth getting them, just be careful how you decide to use them or you will be wasting expensive labels.

title: Fantastic Experience With These, Also Tips and Tricks
text:
I make soaps, lotion, and other body products. I really love having different labels handy so that I can design my own labels to fit on a variety of different package shapes and sizes. Despite a rather drawn out malfunction and replacement of my printer (long story), I am FINALLY able to write about these labels and try them out with my own designs.

WHAT ARE THESE LABELS LIKE?
These labels are white. They have a round shape to them with plenty of space between them that if you need to print partial graphics, they won't overlap onto other labels. There are 9 labels on a sheet, and a total of 72 in the package (8 sheets). These are water resistant, so if you use them on mildly risky containers (lotion, etc) then they will be pretty good. I would not put these on shower gel.

HOW DID THE AVERY PROGRAM WORK FOR ME?
Although I prefer to design my own labels in a graphic program, the Avery label program is pretty decent and quick. I chose the blank round label and imported information from another label that I had printed out earlier. The results were really nice.

HOW DID THESE PRINT OUT FOR ME?
As I have said in other reviews for labels, I have always had problems with Avery online programs printing out correctly with various printers. This time, however, my HP 8710 was flawless in how it interpreted the Avery online program and printed it accurately on the labels. The colors were bright and intense, and the labels printed out exactly as laid out on the Avery online program. I just imported my own graphics from my computer. Due to the personal nature of the labels, I won't be sharing a photo of these at this time.

HOW DO THESE PERFORM?
I put these labels on soap containers and so far they have held up very well. A little splash of water does not make them run, but I would not soak these at all.

TIPS AND TRICKS
I highly recommend that you test these labels with a PLAIN SHEET OF PAPER until you have the labels perfected for your printer. Just hold up the paper behind the labels so you can see if they are properly centered. Also, these labels can handle more lacy graphics than clear ones do. Just don't go too small or it will be hard to read.

THE BOTTOM LINE
When using the online Avery program, my own graphics, and the HP 8710 printer, I had flawless results printing these labels. Colors are bright and intense, easy to read, and the labels stay on well. Although they are only water resistant these will hold up to occasional splashes just not soaking.

MY RATING
These labels performed perfectly. I am very happy to have them to put on my lotions, soap packages, etc.

title: FINALLY My Printer Is Back - Great Labels For Certain Applications- Tips and Tricks
text:
You want to talk frustration? Try getting excited about printing labels, ordering several different styles to try out and having your printer go BERSERK leading to a long drawn out scenario trying to solve the problem and getting the printer up and running again.

Yes, that has been my situation for too long. But today- FINALLY - I was able to try out these stickers at last!

WHAT ARE THESE STICKERS LIKE?
These stickers are a square clear glossy label which is designed to go on top of a solid background so it shows up. There are 12 per page and they are designed to be permanent. There is an edge that is marked which is to be bent after printing so that the labels are easy to remove and place where you need them. There are 10 sheets in the package which means 120 labels.

HOW DOES THE PROGRAM WORK?
I used the Avery online printing program given on the packaging. You basically go to the avery website and go to the printing section. When you get there, you have the option to use your previous Avery projects on the same sticker (which allows you to edit eventually), upload your own graphics finished and saved to the avery file format, or you can choose one of the premade stickers from Avery for your own use and personalizing.

HOW WELL DID THESE PRINT?
I have to be honest with you, until I got the HP 8710 printer, I had nothing but trouble with various printers when using Avery templates. With the HP 8710, however, I am amazed at the razor sharp accuracy of the online Avery program when printing with these labels. I used a personal graphic that I designed, printing images that I designed from fonts that I like that are not on the Avery site, and then added some simple lettering from the site. The labels printed out PERFECTLY. Due to the personal information on the labels, I will not be posting photos.

TIPS AND TRICKS
Because these labels are transparent, you will need to keep in mind that you have to have BOLD lettering and graphics. That will allow the labels to be read more easily. Due to the see through nature of the labels, you can not have lacy or small graphics. They will be too hard to read.

WHAT DO I WANT TO USE THESE FOR?
My purpose in testing these labels is to apply them to containers, bottles, and soap packages for lotions, soap, or packaging for personal products. So far they have tested out well. No smearing or peeling from containers as of yet.

THE BOTTOM LINE
As long as you use bold graphics and fonts, these labels will be easy to read. When used with the HP 8710 and the online avery program the printing was accurate and easy to do. No adjustments were necessary. Labels were colorful and easy to read. They stay put well.

MY RATING
I am giving five stars because these labels are as advertised, print up well, and seem to stay in place nicely for me.

title: Great Sheets, Solid Performance, Would Buy Again No Problem!
text:
After finally finding my laminating machine, I realized that I needed some more sheets. When I saw these, I thought it was a perfect opportunity to see if there is a brand that I can use besides the ones that came with my machine.

WHAT KIND OF LAMINATING MACHINE DO I HAVE?

DID THESE WORK WELL WITH MY SCOTCH TL901 MACHINE?
I thought that these worked flawlessly with my machine.

For lightweight projects, these laminating sheets worked great in my Scotch TL-901 laminating machine. No problems with buckling or wrinkling made them a pleasure to work with. Items stayed in place well and the sheets were very easy to use. I would buy these again in a minute.

RATING
Five stars for these great sheets.

title: They Had Me At Neon Purple- GREAT School Glue!  The Kids Love It!
text:
I love purple. I really love neon purple. It is one of the most fun colors. And this glue? Well it is NEON PURPLE!

WHAT IS THIS GLUE LIKE?
In a clear container, this glue came in a container that is a bit taller than the photo. The glue itself is clear with a beautiful brilliant in your face neon purple color. There is a slight scent to it, but it is not overwhelming or really that noticeable unless you are looking for it. The glue is runnier than the typical white glue, but not so liquid in nature that you can not control it. I would say it has a good viscosity (thickness).

HOW DOES THIS GLUE PERFORM?
We put this glue on a variety of paper and cloth surfaces. We used canvas, thin cotton, regular printer paper, construction paper, and decorated paper. In all cases, if we applied the glue as directed- and spread thin- the object was dry in an hour or two. The paper dried faster than the cloth did. Once dry, the glue does indeed turn completely clear. Not only does it lose the color, but it loses its scent as well and becomes scentless.

I found this glue to be flexible as well as hold well once it is completely dry. I let the things dry overnight just to be sure. There was not any cracking or loss of grip once moved around.

CAUTION
I want to point out that it specifically says on the bottle that THIS IS NOT TO BE USED ON PHOTOS, BARE METAL, OR SUBMERGED SURFACES. You also should not use it on anything that will be heated up.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I love the color purple. This glue is great to use with the kids. The purple color is exciting, and makes the glue fun to use. I know that my daughter and son were both very impressed with this glue. It dries well, loses both color and scent, does not crack or break when bent and works well for basic school type projects that are not necessarily high end permanent projects.

FIVE STARS for this glue. I will update should I need to add any more observations over time.

title: UPDATED-You Should Be Aware Of Some Things, But So Far, This Seems Like A Good System Despite Hiccups
text:
(See UPDATE at the end of this review)
Due to the nature of this product, this review will be an ongoing interactive review for the next few months. First, I will outline the process that has to be gone through to start this program, the outline of what to expect as relayed to me, and my actual experiences with the process as it progresses.

In the following months, I plan to update this review with actual experience with this service and if it lives up to what it says it will do.

WHAT IS THIS PROGRAM LIKE?
The idea is that you buy this card for $9.99 and then you get one month free from buying the card. At the time of this review and my sign up, HP was running a special code SCHOOL3 which allows for another three months of free service. That means for the price of $9.99, you should be getting five months free.

WHAT TO DO FIRST
This service is as follows- you buy the card and you get it in the mail. On this card is a code for entering into the sign up process. At that point, you will be opening an HP Connected account. This is a hub account that all of your printers will go through with SEPARATE accounts for instant ink should you opt to use this system for more than one printer.

GET OUR DEBIT/CREDIT CARD OUT
You will have to sign up with your debit/credit card in order to open this program. I saw a space for a pre-paid card, but no one could tell me where to get one, not even at HP. I am sure they are around, I just was not aware of what sources to get them and no one I talked to knew what to tell me.

GET YOUR PRINTER READY
Once you fill out the information- name, address, and your printer- you will have to print out a paper from your printer using the e-print button. That will give you a code to enter into your sign up pages. Once that is done, then your printer will be set up for the instant ink.

WHAT TO EXPECT
At this point, once your information is entered, your enrollment should be complete. You can enter your codes for bonus months, and it should show up as five months of free service.

WHEN DO THE CHARGES START?
7-10 days after you complete enrollment, HP is going to send out some extra large capacity printer cartridges. These will come in every color you need. You only need to put one in when you are running out of ink in your present cartridges. The charge period for payment is not supposed to begin UNTIL YOU PUT YOUR FIRST HP CARTRIDGE IN YOUR PRINTER.

I was told by HP that it is recommended at that point that you put in ALL of your HP Instant Ink Cartridges into your printer so that they can track your ink usage and make sure you have ink ready.

WHAT WILL YOU BE CHARGED FOR?
You will be charged $9.99 a month for up to 300 pages printed on your printer no matter what- black and white, or photos. It does not matter. They will track your usage and then when it looks like you will need ink, only the cartridge that you will run out of will be shipped to you with a postage paid envelope to return the other one.

ROLL OVER
If you do not use all or any of your allotted 300 pages in a month, that will roll over to the next month - but not over 300 pages in any one month.
If you go over your allowances that month, then you will be charged like $1 for 25 pages or something like that.

MULTIPLE PRINTERS
On the HP Connected site, they have a place for you to enter additional printers into your Instant Ink account. I was told by one source that this meant as long as you did not go over the 300 page limit that you could do both printers on the same account. According to the HP customer service, that is not true. If you open an additional printer account, it goes under the umbrella of the HP Connected Instant Ink account, but requires a different payment method even though it uses the same email. Since I did not sign up another printer at this time, I can not talk of my experience with this aspect of the system.

MY FIRST PROBLEM
Well, first of all, I had a lot of problems trying to set up my account. The account was not recognizing the extra month that I was supposed to get with the enrollment card as indicated on the card. So, I had to call up HP and get customer service to help me. It was quite a process and took about 15 minutes to get some help. The site would not let me complete my enrollment and was not recognizing the extra month.

FIREFOX SEEMS TO GIVE PROBLEMS
For some reason Firefox browser was not working with the HP Connected page so with customer service working with me, I had to go to Internet Explorer which I usually prefer NOT to use. The enrollment worked okay on Internet Explorer, BUT my extra month was still not showing up.
The customer service rep had to manually enter my information All said and done I spent about an hour to do what should have only taken me a few minutes.

ANOTHER TIP
The HP Customer Service rep told me that if you do sign up for this system that you should be aware that if you are having a rush of print jobs expected in a certain month or period of time, you need to call HP so that they can make sure you have enough ink for you to do that. Because of no previous trends to show your sudden ink need, or if you have any internet problems, you might not end up with ink when you need it otherwise.

FUTURE UPDATES
For now I am rating this four stars due to the idiosyncrasies of this sign up system that I had to battle with. I will change and update my review as applicable based upon my experiences with this service over the next few months.

UPDATE FEB 22, 2017
I tested this service to the limit. I had some free months coming to me, but I was still using my old cartridges that came with the printer for a LONG time after signing up for this service. Would they honor their promise not to charge me until I put the cartridges in? Would they not bug me at all even if I took a LONG time to do it?

The answer is THIS IS A WINNER so far. I got my cartridges back when I first signed up for the program. title: Still Prefer The Epson LabelWorks But This Is A Decent Basic Label Maker
text:
I never knew how much I could use labels until I got my first label maker. I have used that for a LOT of different purposes and have found it useful. My previous label maker experience is with a more luxurious model from Epson. However, for quick little labels that I want to use on items on the go, I thought it would be handy to have a smaller sized label maker to take with me and use quickly for quick labels that I am not quite as concerned about perfection on. This label maker seems like a valid choice.

WHAT IS THIS LABEL MAKER LIKE?
Measuring 5 1/2 inches by 4 inches, this label maker is very portable. It has a clear LED screen that is just black and gray. It does not have back lighting to use in very dark areas, so be aware of that. There is a standard key board on this which makes it not have a huge learning curve for typing. The label maker only comes with one small starter roll of labels which means you will have to buy more pretty soon after purchasing if you plan to make any significant amount of labels.

The instruction fold out sheet is invaluable. I would highly suggest that if you get this, you immediately print it out via copier- more on that later.
You can control the font, designs, size, width of label contents, length of the label, and even up to two lines of text. The unit takes 4 AAA batteries which it does not come with. You will want to have them handy before you attempt to use this.

The back comes off easily to insert the batteries and the tape roll which is good. You don't have to unscrew anything or really struggle with tight fitting plates that don't want to come off. The keys are easy to press and are not too close together. The printer slot for the labels to come out is at the back of the machine, along with the cutter tool.

HOW DOES THIS LABEL MAKER PERFORM?
I have to say that I am spoiled by my current label maker, but this one is a decent contender for the smaller label maker needs. The instructions are mandatory for you to run this machine. I will say that one feature I like is that if you want to print out the different graphics that you can use on the label maker, you have the ability to do that. Then you can stick that label on the bottom or side of the unit in case you misplace the instructions.

I tried to make a variety of labels- from simple contents labels to more fancy labels with borders and design. Both worked beautifully. You can save a label or print multiples of the same label with this machine. You can also preview the label before you print it.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE ABOUT THIS MACHINE
There are only a few things I am not fond about with this machine.
1. You can not preview the graphic with the label- it only shows as the listing A1, B2, J3, etc.
2. You can only print straight labels, not the type that wrap around cords.
3. When printing deco labels with repeating designs, you have to have a resting period. This overheats quickly.
4. The labels are very flimsy and have a single back on them which can make them a bit tricky to peel apart

FEATURES I LIKE
1. You can print out the pictograph list on a label and stick to the machine for reference
2. Instructions are clear and make this easy to use
3. Keyboard is standard so no learning curve for typing text
4. Labels stick well to anything I have put them on including glass, frosted glass, metal, plastic, and wood.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although I really enjoy using my [[ASIN:B005J7Y6GS Epson LabelWorks LW-400 Label Maker]] much more than this label maker, I did find this useful for quick jobs. It does what it says nicely, and although the labels are a bit flimsy, they do stick well. I did like the feature of being able to print the pictographs on a label to put on the machine in case you can not find the instructions. I did not like that it lacks some features such as back light, printing labels horizontally or vertically, or to wrap around cords like the Epson does. I also didn't like the single backed tape vs the split back tape of the Epson.

If I had to make a choice, I would still pick the [[ASIN:B005J7Y6GS Epson LabelWorks LW-400 Label Maker]] with the tape bundle. I find the labels to be more sturdy and substantial. However, this is a decent label maker and I still give it four stars.

I will update as I use this over time to add any more insights or details that might be helpful in your buying decision.

title: Sturdy Enough For A Year Or So, But Not Quite As Nice As I Would Like For Long Term Use
text:
Recently, I have developed a need to have a variety of three ring binders for a class that I am taking. In order to make the best use of the binders, I have needed to have alphabetical dividers but I have also a need for a monthly category for another binder. That is where this collection of dividers comes in. For the sake of quality, I will be comparing the quality of these dividers with [[ASIN:B000086122 Cardinal OneStep Index System, 26-Tab, A-Z, Multi-Color, 1 Set (60218)]]

WHAT ARE THESE DIVIDERS LIKE?
The thickness of these dividers is like a thick paper. Compared to the [[ASIN:B000086122 Cardinal OneStep Index System, 26-Tab, A-Z, Multi-Color, 1 Set (60218)]] I would say they are half as thick. A bit of tugging and these would rip. The inside edge with the holes on it is moderately reinforced with a thin plastic layer on both sides. The Cardinal has a thicker plastic on one side only.

The title page is large enough that you can print what you want to label each number category with a sufficient title and description for each number. Although you can print it on the printer, I find that it is almost a waste of time because you can easily print in each section. The tabs are similar in strength to the Cardinal.

HOW DO THESE WORK IN MY BINDER?
Although only the test of time can tell how long it is going to last, but these dividers will last with constant use. So far they seem to be fine. I plan to update in the future after some time to let you know how well they last.

HOW TO CHANGE FROM PORTRAIT TO LANDSCAPE
The way to change these from portrait to landscape is that you take the title page, flip it over and then flip over the dividers and reshuffle them so that the 1 is on top and the 12 at the back (unless you like it backwards, of course). It took me a minute to figure it out, but it is simple enough to do once you get the hang of it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These are moderately strong dividers that serve the purpose for monthly records or anything else that can be divided into sections of 12. Reinforced to make it last longer, these are made from thick paper that is not quite as thick as say the [[ASIN:B000086122 Cardinal OneStep Index System, 26-Tab, A-Z, Multi-Color, 1 Set (60218)]], but they should last for at least a year of constant use. Although you can print only the title page on the printer (the tabs prohibit printing the dividers on a printer) , it seems easier to write by hand in each of 12 category labels.

I am rating these four stars. They are nice, I like them but they are not quite a sturdy as I would like. I will update as I use them over time, but for now, four stars. I will re-rate if necessary based on wear over time.

title: Good Value for Standard Binders For Home, Office, or School Use
text:
I recently enrolled in a class which requires me to keep a compilation of chemical data sheets, and properties lists and needed a good three ring binder. I wanted something that was easy to use and would hold up well. Does this fit the bill? I think so, but if I had to drag this around with me to a lot of places, I am not so sure. Read on..

WHAT ARE THESE BINDERS LIKE?
You get four binders in the pack which are packed as to prevent bending or damage to the binders. The binder themselves are white with see through pockets on front AND back so that you can clearly label them with papers to help you tell which ones are for what. There is also a see through pocket on the spine of the binder so that you can label them there with removable paper as well.

The rings are round rings NOT D rings. They are on the back of the binder, not the spine which helps them to lay a bit flatter. There are two inside see through pockets for loose papers which only go up about 1/4 of the way. The binder itself is easy to lay open and there is a tiny pocket on the inside spine which would hold something long and flat such as a small measuring stick or other flat object.

The quality is average. These will not take very heavy abuse, but would last through an average year of average use. If you are very hard on your binders, these might not hold up as well, but you do get four so they are easy to swap out if you need to.

HOW WELL DOES THIS PERFORM?
So far I have no complaints. It holds at least 100 sheets comfortably and the rings work well with good snap to them. They don't pop open with no spaces between rings that are not shut tightly like so often happens with binders of this nature.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This standard weight binder is great for compiling reference papers for classes or subjects in home office or school functions. It is sturdy enough for at least a year of use, although harder use may require something a bit more heavy duty. There are pockets in them for loose papers, easy pockets for paper labeling which can be changed at will and firm rings in them which keep papers held in place.

For what I am using these for, they will be fine, but if I had to take these to a lot of classes with hard wear, I am not sure if they would last without splitting or not before the end of a year. A semester use would be fine.

I give this four stars- one off because the inside pockets are too shallow to be of much use in my situation, and they are rather flimsy too.

title: UPDATE- The Love/Hate Soap Opera Continues -Unusual Use For This Printer Unlike Any Others I Have Had (AUTO-INK INCLUDED)
text:
(I promised I would update as I find more to report on this printer and I am back again at the end of August 2016 to let you know I found another reason to up my original low rating another star. This one is important. SEE UPDATE AT THE END)

-------------------------
I have been using HP printers for a VERY long time. I have also had the opportunity to use a lot of different brands of printers over the years, and have always come back to HP. HP has had issues at times, but for me, it has been an excellent quality printer for the most part. However, once I tested out this printer, I can see that something has changed.

I have really tried to like this printer. I will do my best to make this review as brief as I can, but I will also try to outline the basic observations I have made with this printer. I plan to update more in the future as I continue to try to work with this, as it is something I am going to have to find a way to cope with. My current printer (HP Officejet K550 dtn) is on its way out and HP no longer supports it or sells printer heads for it.

WHAT IS THIS PRINTER LIKE?
First of all, you need to be sure you have the space to put this printer. It is rather large. If you have one of those compact computer desks with a retracting printer shelf, get ready to move the shelf way down almost to the bottom, keeping the bottom shelf for paper only. The top needs plenty of swing space to lift as well if you need to scan something.

The screen on the front of the printer is very clear and easy to use. It is self explanatory when you set it up, guiding you through all of the steps. The printer comes with ink, basic instructions and a CDROM to set up the software. You can also get it online. This printer uses either wi-fi from your in house router that you have with internet or you can use the cloud online. You can also connect via USB port to a desktop or laptop if desired.

PROBLEMS I HAVE ENCOUNTERED
I have not tried to print photos from cameras or anything like that due to regular printer quality being so low, I am just trying to make it look decent for regular printing needs. I will update should I try to use it for photos.

INK
First of all putting the ink into the unit was frustrating. I have never seen such rickety sockets for ink cartridges in all of my years using printers- even the really cheap ones that I didn't like too much. This was ridiculous. There is a spring in the socket and the ink cartridge (which is also cheaply made) is supposed to press in and lock. The problem is that they don't always want to stay locked in. I had a problem several times of ink cartridges popping back out and the printer would not run. I have NEVER had that kind of problem with any printer.

SOFTWARE
The driver is really annoying. I am frustrated most of the time trying to use it. This printer is designed to be used by smartphones, tablets, laptops and a desktop. I have tried it with all four of these and the results are frustrating at best. Using android, it is very difficult to control the print and how it will turn out. Many times the pages are cut off and are not fit to page, and are really lousy looking. The laptop and desktop are also frustrating when used for online printing. I know there has to be more control somewhere, but it is not anywhere as intuitive and easy to use as it has been in the past. I do not have this hard wired into USB at this point, so perhaps things would be different at that point, but I am being hopeful here.

PRINT QUALITY
Besides being goofy looking, half cut off and adjustments not being easy to use, I have also had trouble with the ink printed on the page. When it does print, the quality of the print is horrible. I mean HORRIBLE. This looks like some of the lousy quality bubble jet printers I have used in the distant past (not all were lousy, just the lousy ones). The ink looks faded, very blurry and not strong colors at all like the other HP printers I have in my house.

PAPER FEEDING
I have been spoiled. In the past HP printers have had a tendency to be fussy with paper feeding. Usually a year or two of feeding paper and then they really mess up. The current printer I have had for 8 years has had NO problems feeding paper. If something gets jammed on the rare occasion (Bent paper or something) it is a snap to fix and it still goes strong. This printer, however, is a different story. It feeds paper okay, but then it feeds through multiple papers, or halfway paper, etc. I am not impressed. I am using the exact same paper in my very old printer and it feeds through fine- it is not the paper.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I can no longer buy printer heads for my beloved K550 Officejet printer, the best HP printer I have ever had. I would rather use that in a moment. The ink is vivid, colorful, crisp, and fast. The HP Officejet Pro 8710 is such a disappointment in comparison that I have a hard time liking it. The software is not as easy to use as HP software in the past and I am not very happy with it. The printer itself is easy to set up although the ink cartridges seem cheap as well as the sockets they are supposed to be pressed into. I have had problems with printing being fit onto the pages, ink quality, as well as paper feeding.

I will continue to work with this printer, since I am stuck with it, but I am so far unimpressed. Perhaps I will find some more positive things about it to report and I will update should that happen. At this point, I don't like to have to work so hard just to make a printer do what it is supposed to and has done without much effort in the past.

I am giving this two stars at this point, but it is open to change in the future should I have better experiences with this printer over time.

UPDATE May 31, 2016
As I said I would, I have continued to try to work with this printer to see if I might be able to get more satisfactory results. I have printed out a photo which I had at the exact same time on two different printers so you can see the comparison. The HP Officejet Pro K550 has such amazing definition, contrast, etc, that I could print the photo on draft print and it would look perfect. This was done with regular ink printing on that printer. Again, I could have reduced it down to draft level and it still would look good.

The HP Officejet Pro 8710 has almost no contrast, very grayish black, and a red tone to the photo which is awful. The K550 photo is much more true to life. The HP 8710 is not at all the level of performance that I am used to with HP printers.

I will continue to work with the printer, but so far, I am disappointed. Should I have the need to attach it directly to my desktop instead of Wi-Fi, perhaps it would be different. For now, it is not great. If I can find solutions to my frustrations with this printer, I will update to let you know. For now, I am used to MUCH higher quality printing from HP printers.

JULY 11,2016 UPDATE
I wanted to amend my original rating to bump up my review one star. I have had the opportunity to use and interact with this printer a lot more and have found that there are some things that I have come to like about it that I didn't get to use much before.

COPYING
The copying feature is really nice. The paper sits in the feed slot and makes the printer kick in to prepare to copy the page. All I do is pick what I want to copy (Document, Photo, ID) and then the machine pulls in the paper, scans, and copies it and returns it out of the other slot. The result is a lot better than the photo results were when printed and sent from the same computer desktop that I previously posted. That leads me to wonder if the problem is in the drivers for the printer or if it just seems to do better when scanning in itself as a unit. The results for simple lined diagrams, illustrations and print are nice and accurate, unlike my photo experiences so far.

INK
This ink is pigment based ink which is important if you are doing any kind of industrial labeling which needs to have permanency to it with those special labels.

FURTHER UPDATES COMING
I will continue to update as I have a chance to get to know this printer more as I interact with it over time. If I can find out how to adjust the problems I have been having with it, I will surely let you all know and change my rating accordingly. I am not one to give up so easily so if I can improve the way that it has performed so far, I will let you know and pass it on. It has potential to be a great all in one printer, and I hope perhaps I can find ways to get it to work better.

UPDATE JULY 24,2016 (THIS LOVE HATE RELATIONSHIP TAKES YET ANOTHER TURN)
I promised I would update as I found more out about this printer and I am about to explain why I updated and added yet another star to my originally low rated review.

Although I am still not thrilled with photo printing which is important to me that this printer does, it does do something else which is fantastic and has me thrilled to no end. I have had a need to print some high quality oil resistant labels. I could not afford to have them printed and wanted the creativity options to do my own. I came upon the [[ASIN:B01C78554S Avery UltraDuty GHS Chemical Labels for Pigment Inkjet Printers, Waterproof, UV Resistant, 2"x4",500Pk (60525)]] which sounded perfect for what I needed to do.

I designed labels which got me two out of each label on the sheet, but my stress was wondering how many labels would be wasted trying to make them line up as so many other printers have caused for me. Boy was I shocked when this printer printed them PERFECTLY like a CHAMP!

I LOVE this printer for these labels. It is a pigment based ink and causes the labels to be permanent and resistant to oils, water, etc. I could not be more happy.

SO, although this printer has frustrated me on a few things, it really is a champ on something I can not do with any other printer- print PERFECT labels that withstand water, oil, and corrosive materials without wasting labels with misprints. I could not be happier.

So, I have raised my rating to four stars as of July 24,2016. I still wished that it would print higher quality photos, but the labels make up for it and have earned it a higher rating.

Will add more should I find other things to report to you all!

UPDATE IN AUGUST 2016
I am still loving this printer for labels. Pretty soon I will be able to comment for you all on the instant ink aspect as I will be testing that part out as well coming soon. Since I have a need to print out all kinds of labels for my essential oils, creams, body products, and other soaps, I will be needing to replenish the ink more quickly. Will be updating once I have tested that facet of this printer.

Stay tuned for my love hate relationship with this printer. A REAL soap opera. (sorry, could not resist the pun there)

title: Brilliant Colors, Highly Pigmented, Handy To Use, And No Caps To Lose!
text:
One of the things I like to do when correcting papers or making notes that I want to stand out is have a selection of nice different colored pens that have different colored ink in them.

WHAT ARE THESE PENS LIKE?
These click pens are covered over half of the barrel in a soft grippy plastic that indicates what color ink is inside the pen. The front of the pen has a clear plastic front on it which is tinted with that same color but is see through. The ink itself is very bright and pigmented. The ink tube inside is filled about halfway up the pen, but is larger around than most ball point pens. There is a plastic tip on the pen to keep the ink from flowing when you first get it, so you have to remove it with your fingernail or something similar.

HOW DO THESE PENS WORK?
The pens are surprisingly smooth and write very well. There is enough drag so that I don't feel as if I am losing control of the pen, but not so much that it is hard to write with. The ink does not seem to blob up much when using, but I did notice that if you hit the writing just right, it will smear a tiny bit. It is not that bad, however, and I would not say it is a big problem. The colors are all very brilliant and heavily pigmented, making these look like the perfect marriage between ball point pen and gel pen.

WHAT I LIKE ABOUT THESE PENS
-colors are all brilliant
-smooth to write with
-grip well any spot on the pen
-don't roll off a desk
-no caps to lose

WHAT I DON'T LIKE ABOUT THESE PENS
-ink should be filled up a bit more
-tiny bit of smearing if hand runs over just right

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want a nice pigmented pen in brilliant colors that is easy to use, this click pen is a great choice. Although it smears slightly from time to time, in general, it is an easy pen to use and pretty classy looking. The inks are all pigmented and the purple especially is dark enough to be used for general writing when blue or black is usually preferred.

For the price of these pens I have rated them four stars due to the slight smearing from time to time and the ink not being as full as I would like to see. I would rather rate them four and a half stars if I could, however.

title: Great Colors, Traditional Ball Point Ink Look, A Few Skipped At First
text:
I have had a collection of pens from Bic in the past which were very similar in color of ink to the collection here referred to as Atlantis. My other pens were the crystal style pens with caps, but the ink was very similar. I used those pens constantly until they were used up. I missed having them, so these are a welcome addition to my household!

These pens are great for the ink. The mechanics are a bit hard for me to get used to, but so far they are working well for me.

WHAT ARE THESE PENS LIKE?
They come in a cardboard bubble package with all eight pen colors. The pens themselves have a rubbery grip on them and the top button that usually clicks on most click pens is a very smooth engagement. It is hard to tell sometimes if the pen has engaged or not- something that is a bit difficult for me to get used to. The ink colors are true to the color of the pens so they are easy to tell which pen you are grabbing- no guessing here.

HOW DO THESE PENS PERFORM?
These pens perform great. At first I had a few skip (orange-red and standard blue), but the more I worked with them, they did become smoother after a short while and work fine now with no skips. The pen ink looks just like ballpoint pens. These are not the gel type pens, nor are they thin markers just in case you were not sure. The ink does seem to be more smooth and even than traditional ball point pens, which is part of the claim on the package.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although this package is a bit on the expensive side for what you get, I do like the pens themselves. There is no cap to lose, the ink is very pigmented and does not seem to skip once I use the pens a bit, and the pens are all the colors of the ink- again excellent to use because you don't have to guess which pen you are grabbing. I debated upon four or five stars, but I was asked to review the performance of these, and in that category I have to give them a five. They are a bit expensive, but performance wise, I like them.

title: Why Do I DO This To Myself?  But Two Packs If you Plan to Use These
text:
I have been making business cards and other similar things for business for quite a few years now. Back when I first started to use Avery products, I might have had a few glitches with various printers and programs now and then, but most of the time, printing business cards was a breeze. They were not to awfully difficult to set up and print, having most of the cards turn out right except perhaps for the last row of cards, perhaps.

As time has gone on, however, I tend to get lulled into a sense of stupor, when I think that I can get business cards to print out successfully. I have tested them on two different printers. For some reason, the cards don't print out and line up the way that they should. Being that HP is one of the most common brands of printers, I find that to be doubly frustrating. I really don't want to have to work THIS hard to get simple business cards to print out. I really love the idea of two sided cards also.

This set of Avery cards is one of the most frustrating I have had to cope with to date.

The sheets of cards themselves are well labeled Front and Back so you know how to put them into your printer. They are thick and the perforations are not so flimsy that they come apart before you have a chance to print them out. Nor are they so hard to get apart that your cards look like they were torn from paper sheets. I am referring to the appearance of the PHYSICAL cards. The printed is another story.

I have tested these cards over and over in a variety of ways and to this point, I still have not been able to get a sheet to print out the way that it should. I have used the Avery program as it is with a few different printers, and I have nudged (for printer adjusting)on the Avery site, as well as tried to rearrange the graphics on the card to allow for any hidden marginal errors that seem to be throwing these cards into chaos when they print.

I can not do it at this point.

WHAT I LIKE
-Cards are heavy
-Perforations are sturdy
-Sheets are labeled well.
-Ink prints well on the paper (appearance not location)
-Gives me flexibility to hopefully print out unique cards as many as I would like (theoretically, anyway)

WHAT I DON'T LIKE
-Avery program does not lay out properly for my HP printers
-Program on Avery seems to conflict with my printer drivers sending them into freezing etc
-Sheets won't print out without printing another sheet afterward
-VERY frustrating to try to set up and print. Takes WAY too much time than it should
-Importing another saved Avery product is useless- better to start off fresh

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you are planning to use the Avery site to do your printing of cards, I HIGHLY suggest purchasing two packages- one for experimenting and one when you figure out how to make it work. No matter how many times I use plain paper (as suggested by Avery) when I think I have it right, on the card stock, it just does not line up right.

I know there has to be a way to get at least MOST of these to print out so I can use them, but I have not found it yet. These are great quality cards physically and I plan to do another layout using my graphics professional program and at least getting them to print out fairly well if I can do it. I have given these three stars because I really do love the idea of it, the physical quality of the double sided cards are great, but it is just the translating it from Avery site to printer to card that I am struggling with.

If you plan to do a quick and easy business card printing, you might want to rethink it and give yourself PLENTY of time and experimentation. If you are one of the lucky ones that gets this to print out perfectly right away- I envy you!

UPDATING
As with most of my reviews, if I have anything to add in the future or if I find a solution, I will update, re-adjust my rating and let you know about it.

PRINTERS USED
HP Officejet K550dtn
HP Envy 4500
