The magnets stick on the board securely.  The chalk does require some coaxing and a little water on the eraser to get it off the board.  It does come off clean with a little effort.  The quality seems to match the price point, but honestly, we have not purchased another of these, so I am not sure how comparatively it is priced.  Overall, well made and looks great.

title: A little rough around the edges,
text: I ordered the "Harbor Creek Days to Remeber Family Wooden Birthday Calendar Wall hanging' for review.  As we have been gaining new family members recently due to marriage and new babies, it was important for my wife to find a system that would work well to remind her of important dates.  when it arrived a few of the smaller pieces were chipped or broken, but with 100 of them these couple of causalities were not a big deal.  The front of the sign is a light oak color with the design cut/burned into the wood.  It has very rough edges with some chips, looks like it was cut with a dull saw.  The front also had a small ding in it.  For the price, I do not believe this has the quality that I would have expected it to.  Overall, It is a cute idea, but the look of this specific wall hanging is a bit cheap.

title: The rose color is a nice touch
text: I ordered this 'Rosework Rose Gold 2 Tier Letter Tray Desk Organizer for Women, Stackable Paper Tray Organizer' for review.  My wife's desk has a pink mat and other rose accessories and I felt this would match well.  It is a bit more expensive than some other sets of stack-able files.  Yet, the quality is better than others we have ordered. They feel durable and sturdy.  The rose color is a nice touch and aesthetically pleasing.  The only issue I saw with this set was that they were a little tight to connect.  However, once connected they do not move around as with some other stack-able file trays.  Overall, great product.

title: Much better quality Felt Boards out there for about the same price
text: I ordered the ‘Black Felt Letter Board 10x10 inches - 510 Letters and Storage Bag Included’ for review.  I have had the opportunity to review two other felt letter boards recently in this same price range.  This is the lowest quality board of all three.  The edges are unfinished and rough.  You could get a splinter if not careful.  As it is unfinished the frame is not stained as the description picture shows.  The plastic letters do not have tabs on the top and bottom of them, so when you stand the sign up the letters fall off.  Also, the slots are too wide apart so the letters do not fit in them securely.  There is a good variety of letters and punctuation marks.  The frame also does not have a standing leg on the back.  You must purchase a stand to set it up on a dresser or desk.  Overall, I was disappointed in the quality of this board.  Not one to purchase when there are others that are the same price and way better quality.

title: A little Disappointed in the Quality
text: I ordered a set of 'EnDoc's 5x7 Blank Greeting Cards Sets - Color Bright White, Heavy Cardstock Paper Weight -25 Cards and Envelopes' for review as my daughter has an upcoming birthday party and we always send out customized party invitations.  These cards a single sheet card, not meant to be folded and opened.  They are a bright white.  I was a little disappointed in the quality of these cards and envelopes.  They just do not feel like Heavy Cardstock.  They will work just fine for her birthday party or shower invites.  However, I do not feel these are nice enough for a wedding invitation.They are more economical than some other blank card sets, but you get what you pay for in this case.

title: Nice quality.
text:
I ordered the 'TOPNIKE LED Sign Standoffs 1"×1", Polished Chrome, Green LED Standoff Sign Holder, for Glass, Acrylic and Other Transparent Plates, Pack of 2' via the Vine program and would like to share my thoughts.
First off, I ordered these as a set of green yet as you can see in the attached images, I received white. This was not a huge deal as I plan to use these more as background lights for product photos. There were no instructions with my set but for their intended purpose it's not to hard to figure out how they are supposed to work. The light standoffs are a nice heavy build and the lights are pretty bright. The cable lengths from the light standoffs to the power splitter are only about 2 feet. The power splitter has 6 ports so it is possible to plug 2 more sets into it. From this splitter to the controller you get another 2 feet of cable and from the controller to the wall plug you get another 3'. If you were to use this kit as intended on a wall, these lengths may not work unless you modify and ad more cable. However for my indented use, the cable lengths are just fine.
It would have been nice if these LED lights were RGB however I think you could take a strip of colored plastic film wrapped around the light between the top and standoff base to create a colored lighting effect. This will actually be more effective with the white light. Overall the build quality of these lights is really nice and I think they are of great value for their intended purpose.

title: Works great
text: I had the opportunity to order a roll of 'Removable Adhesive Nano Gel Tape - Washable Strong Adsorption Double Sided Clear Silicone Traceless Tape' for review.  This tape is definitely sticky.  Unlike double sided sticky pads, this tape is flexible and stretches.  It has excellent adhesion and has held up in the spots we have used it.  it was difficult to get the backing off to get the double sided stick.  I like that it is clear and you do not see anything behind or through anything we have hung with it.  I am a bit worried that it may take the paint of my walls when it is removed.  It is probably best used on glass, metal or tile.  Overall, this tape works great.

title: Basic, easy to assemble Monitor Stand
text:
I had the opportunity to review the PAG Desktop Bookshelf Monitor Printer Stand Computer Riser Wood Desk Organizer for Home/Office/School. I would love to share my thoughts with you.
• This Desktop Computer stand is made of Melamine board.
• It is simply deigned aesthetically.
• The round plastic cover that you run cords through came broken in several pieces.
• Assembly was easy and quick.
• The quality of it does meet the price point. It is really basic. But, for $25, you could not ask for much more.
• A standard sized monitor will fit nicely.
• The added side shelves store books perfectly.
Overall this Computer stand functionally works for what it was made for. Again, it is basic, but worth it’s price tag. A little bummed that it came with a broken piece.

title: Nicely made cards with Envelopes
text: I ordered a set of 12 Hallmark Assorted Valentines Day Cards for Kids with envelopes for review.  Having a daughter still in elementary school, she needed some cards for her class.  These cards in Hallmark fashion are nicely made.  Having the envelopes make them a step up from the fold able valentines cards.  I thought the designs were cute, but my daughter felt they were a bit to "Cheesy" for her age (5th grade).  That being said, we will be ordering more Hallmark cards, as her class has 35 kiddos, just not this particular design.

title: Bright Colors
text: I had the opportunity to order a set of 8 Magnetic Dry Erase Fine Point Markers, low odor to review.  My kids are doodlers so we have several whiteboards and the markers always seem to disappear.  Each marker in this set has a magnet to attach to the fridge or other metal surface.  There is a round eraser on the top, although when you use it, it feels as though it might tear off.  The ink in these markers is bright and vibrant.  You have 8 different colors to choose from.  They write smoothly on a white board surface and they erase well, without leaving any residue behind.  My only negative thought about these markers is that they are not low odor.  They definitely have a pungent marker smell.  Overall, the quality meets the price point and my older kids will get lots of use out of them.

title: Really great quality
text: I ordered a set of Sorbus Clear Drawer Organizer 5-Piece Set, Multi-Purpose Organizer Bins to review, as our vanity drawers are a disorganized mess.  These are made surprisingly well.  The plastic is much thicker than other drawer organizers we have come across.  They are crystal clear without scratches or nicks. They are durable enough to take a few knocks off the counter before breaking.  They fit perfectly in our drawer and now our toothbrushes do not come into contact with our hairbrushes.  Overall a great value for the price.

title: Super cute, Vday Cards with Stickers
text: i ordered these Hallmark Kids Minecraft Valentine’s Day Cards and Stickers Assortment (12 Cards with Envelopes) for review, as I have a daughter in the last year of elementary and she loves Mine Craft.  These are cute little cards.  The set comes with 2 different designed cards and a set of stickers to go with each Valentine card.  They included the envelopes too.  When my daughter saw them, she said “those are cool”.  Just wish they came in a larger set.  These cards are way nicer than some of the cheaper, tear-away or fold-able cards.  Their quality exceeds their price point.  Overall, these are adorable VDay cards that most kids would love to receive.

title: Good variety of colors
text:
I had the opportunity to review a set of 60 Brilliant Bee - Permanent Marker– Bulk Pack, Assorted Colors, with Chisel & Fine Point Tips. The following are my thoughts:
• Having 60 different pen colors, this set has a wide variety of colors to choose from.
• The color of the ink may or may not match the colored cap. Some were lighter than the cap and others darker. I would recommend a test line to make sure the color is what you are looking for.
• The ink is well pigmented, and most colors are very vibrant.
• If you use lighter pressure, the chiseled tip strokes do look like they were made with a marker that is a bit dried out. However, if you use a slighter heavier pressure when using the chiseled tip, the stroke color is consistent and saturated.
• The fine tip works flawlessly.
• Used on a heavier paper, such as mixed media or watercolor paper these markers do not bleed through. However, when used with regular notebook paper they do bleed through slightly.
• The tips do not seem to shed. And keep their shape even after a bit of use.
• They do have a more pungent odor than other low odor markers that I have reviewed. They are not overly odorous, but they do have an odor.
• They do come in a box, that you can keep them all together in. But a plastic or Canvas case would be more suited to the price point.
• These do seem priced higher than other marker sets I have reviewed that are of equal quality.
Overall, this set would work great for a budding artist learning to use different mediums. They make good doodling or coloring markers. With that being said, I do believe there are other sets of markers that would work just as well, but that are a bit less expensive.

title: Smooth surface, nice quality
text:
I had the opportunity to review the Marvelux 35" x 47" Polycarbonate Chair Mat for Hard Floors and Very Low Pile Carpets with Anti Slip Backing.
• It comes shipped flat. It is much harder than some of the rolled silicone type floor mats. You do not need to set heavy items on it for a couple days to flatten it, so you can use it right out of the packaging.
• When taken out of the packaging, it did not have any plastic or chemical smell to it.
• It has stayed exactly where I placed after several uses. Both walking on it and also using my rolling chair on it.
• It is smooth, my chair glides smoothly across it.
• I have noticed that when standing on it the ends tend to curl up very slightly, as I used it on a low pile carpet versus a hardwood floor.
• It is a bit smaller than other mats we have used in the past, but it works great in front of my desk.
Overall, this is a good quality chair mat for the price. Although, I would prefer a bigger size, this has worked well when I am at my desk and need to get up or slide over to grab something at the end of my desk.

title: Adorable, way better than tear-apart, fold-able valentine cards
text: I ordered these Hallmark Kids Harry Potter Mini Valentine Card Assortment (12 pack) for review. These cards are definitely mini.  They are adorable.  When my 10 year old daughter saw them, she immediately asked for more to use for her school valentines celebration.  Halllmark makes a quality card.  The paper is much better than the tear apart valentines that fold.  Plus, these come with envelopes.  Overall, these are great quality mini cards.  Guess, I will be buying a few more sets for my daughter to use this Valentines Day.

title: Functions well for storing small items
text: I ordered this ANIZER Classroom Pocket Chart for Phone Calculator Holder Over The Door Hanging Closet Jewelry Organizer to review as we want to be more organized for 2020.  For the price and what this is made for it functions well.  The hangers are sturdy and hang perfectly over a door.  The fabric it is made from is pretty thin, but the vinyl pocket are clear.  It works great for storing small items and would work great in a classroom.  Overall, for under $10 you can not beat the functionality.  And although not superior quality,  the quality exceeds the price point.

title: Have to hold horizontally, even when writing with them for the fine points to work
text:
I ordered these Dingbats Atopen 6-pack Dual Tip Fineliner/Brush Pens for Calligraphy and Art Drawings (Pastel Set) for review. I asked my wife for her insight as she has multiple sets of dual tip markers and loves trying new products.

Pluses:
* The brush tips work well with a broad stroke
* They have both the brush tip and fine point
* The did not bleed through any paper that she used
* The caps seal tightly
* There is no noticeable smell
* They are water based, so they will blend

Cons:
* The coral is not really a pastel, it is more hot pink
* The fine liners do not write at all or as if they are dried up if you do not hold them up horizontally to write with them. My wife likes to write or draw with a slant, so these markers did not work well for her
* For the over $20 price, you only get 6 Markers, way to spendy in my wife's book. Especially since they are a bit difficult to use
* They seem to dry out quickly when using them, again this may be the slant issue

Overall, these markers' quality in my wife's opinion, just do not live up to the higher price tag. She has several other sets at the same price point but 3-4 times the markers and overall better quality.

title: Well constructed
text: I ordered this JEMIA Multi Compartments Collection 3 Independent Zipper Compartments Pencil Case in gray to keep sets of markers in and for review.  This case is good sized to hold a lot of markers.  It is made with smooth feeling canvas in a heather gray.  It has two separate large individually zippered sections, along with a smaller zipped pocket on the exterior front.  It is constructed well, the stitching looks good.  It feels solid.  My wife can easily throw this case in her purse or carry on bag when she travels.  The interior is not the most aesthetically pleasing color, but who cares, noone sees it. Overall, a great portable, durable pencil case.

title: Ink is not a dark black
text: I ordered this set of 16 Keebor Basic Low Odor Dry Erase Markers Chisel Tip Whiteboard Markers in black for review, but also to keep my kids supplied with whiteboard markers.  We have several white boards and because most of these type of markers tend to dry out quickly, we use a lot.  These markers have a chiseled tip which makes for better lettering.  The are very low odor, I barely noticed an odor at all.  They erase well from the whiteboard.  The negative to these markers is that they do not write in a dark black, the ink looks faded on the whiteboard.  Overall, for my the purpose of doodling, they function okay and the price is reasonable enough that when we go through them so much, it doesn't hurt as much.

title: Great quality for the price
text: I ordered this ACSTEP Office Desk Pad Pink,Dual Sided Ultrathin Desk Pad Protector for review.  When it arrived, I was pleased with the quality.  The PU leather is smooth and a mouse glides over it with ease.  The light pink color is very soft.  And if pink isn’t your favorite color it is reversible to a silver gray.  This mat is huge.  Lots of surface room for a laptop, mouse and anything you are working on.  If you accidentally spill anything on it, it wipes right off.  There is a stamped logo/saying on the upper left corner that says, “To ask why, We fight”. It grips well to the desk and doesn’t slip or move when is working on it.  Overall this is a great quality desk mat and the price makes it an exceptional deal.

title: Soft and comfortable.
text:
I ordered the 'Razer Ergonomic Wrist Rest for Full-Sized Keyboards: Anti-Slip Rubber Base - Angled Incline - Classic Black' for review.
This is another great product from Razer. This is not your typical gel wrist rest. The padding is perfectly soft and comfortable with just enough cushion for for your wrists. The width, angle and height are all well designed and really help with fatigue while using my keyboard. The grip on the bottom holds in place so that the wrist rest stays put and doesn't slide around. Overall this is a quality product and the perfect wrist rest.

title: Solidly made and looks beautiful
text: I ordered this PAG Wood Desktop File Holder Organizer specifically to review.  When it arrived, the box was heavier than I expected.  It was packaged well but comes un-assembled.  My wife was able to put it together quickly and easily.  The pre-drilled holes all matched up. The instructions were clear.  It comes with all the hardware needed, even including a screwdriver.  The pressed wood is solid, the walnut color is beautiful.  This is excellent quality.  It feels sturdy.  It is large and takes up quite a bit of space and may be too large for a smaller desk.  It works perfectly to sort and organize all my wife's sheet vinyl and lots of them.  Overall, my wife loves this Desktop organizer.  We are happy with both the aesthetic look and the quality.  Would definitely recommend this to anyone who wants a more solid wood looking organizer versus a metal or wired one.

title: Sturdy, durable cart.  Difficult to put together
text: I ordered this DOEWORKS Storage Cart 3 Tier Metal Utility Cart Rolling Organizer Cart with Wheels in black specifically to review. My wife has several work-spaces and likes to have a rolling cart to move her craft supplies with her.  This cart was difficult to get together.  The design should have made it much simpler, but some of the bars and bins did not fit as well as they could have for easier assembly.  The bins were slightly too small to fit snugly into the bars and you had to either put a lot of pressure on the bars or bins to get the screw the entire way through and get the nut screwed on correctly.  It did make it easier to secure one screw on each side and then put the screws into the other bars versus trying to do one side at a time.  Once together it is sturdy and as with some other carts my wife has used, this one does not come a part every time it gets bumped.  The Black metal is well painted, and it looks aesthetically pleasing.  Additionally, this cart has a handle that makes it easier to move about her craft room.  Her other carts lack this feature.  This is my wife’s fourth cart for her craft room, and this is one of her favorites.  The wheels move smoothly even on carpet.  The size is perfect to roll right under her craft table to be stored out of the way. And stores more than she thought it would.  Overall, the quality on this cart is worth the price tag, but in my opinion the difficulty and mis-fitting bins make me hesitant to purchase another.

title: Would work best in a classroom or office
text: I ordered this YOUNGTION Dry Erase Laminated Wall Calendar, Huge 24 x 36 Inches Erasable Undated Monthly Planner for Home Office School, Premium PET Film & Habit Tracking Grid, with Big Bonus Bundle for review.  Once we finally got it out of the rolled tube, we realized it was HUGE and would not work in our kitchen.  But we found use for it in my daughter’s bedroom.  This really is suited more for a classroom setting versus home.  It did take a few days of laying flat and having a heavy object on it to get it to lay flatter.  It still curled up at the edges, but with a few thumbtacks we were able to get it on the wall.  The dry erase markers work very well and erase without leaving any marks.  The date blocks are large and so writing out your appointments or events is easily done without feeling like you are squishing them all together.  The bonus holder, eraser, markers, stickers and jumbo tacks were a nice addition to this set.  We did not use the tack tape however; we did not want to mark our paint.  Overall, this is a great product, which just a couple minor issues.  Would work great in a classroom setting.

title: Love this magnetic planner
text:
I ordered this set of 3 Dry Erase magnetic calendar to review and use on our fridge. With three children and a wife who travels for work, we have a hard time coordinating our schedules. We love this set. The monthly and weekly calendars are the perfect size to fit on the side of our fridge. The space in each square is easy to note basic info on the monthly but then elaborate with more details on the weekly calendar. It is brightly colored and easy to see. It comes with four dry erase markers. None of which is black, but those are inexpensive to get. The markers that come with the set have fine points and are also magnetic to stick to the side of the fridge. Not to mention, the eraser sticks to the fridge too. Makes it so convenient to add or erase details on the calendars. The smaller to do sheet, is much smaller than the calendars, of course. But is plenty big to create a pretty large list. This set also includes ten round “occasion” markers for things like date night, birthdays, travel. All the pieces to this set stick very well to our fridge. It came flat versus rolled so the edges do not curl up.

When you erase, the board comes clean. You do not see that dreaded shadow of what used to be there. The markers do not scratch or indent the board either. Overall, this is a great Magnetic Calendar set. And the quality far exceeds it’s price point.

title: This is one awesome Stand up Pencil Case
text:
I ordered this iSuperb Stand Up Canvas Pencil Case for review. My wife is continually crafting even when traveling. She needed a case she could throw into her purse but be big enough to hold all her basic writing and small crafting tools. This is the perfect case for her. It is high quality, the seams are sewn securely. The pink canvas is a bright pink and is durable. It is padded thicker than other cases she has purchased. The interior is a soft gray and holds quite a few markers, pencils, etc. My wife was thrilled with the fact that it actually does stand and does not tip over easily. It has magnets that when the front cover is folded down it stays attached to the other half. The sides of the top cover are designed deep enough that her cell phone fits perfectly. This feature provides her the ability to view her image, instructions or videos upright versus laying flat in front of her when her hands are busy. Not to mention that when open, her supplies are easily accessible.

Seriously, this pencil case way outshines any others she has used. It is exactly as described. My wife absolutely loves it. With all the markers, pencils and pens she has we will buying a few more of these.

title: A little more expensive than what it is worth
text: I ordered this JEMIA - Blue Pencil Case with 2 Compartments and Handle, Mesh Pockets and Slots for review.  My wife loves crafting and has a huge collection of markers.  She loves to keep them organized in pencil cases.  This pencil case is a good size and holds a good number of markers and some smaller crafting/art tools.  It has one larger compartment and another with a mesh pocket and elastic holders in front of a pocket.  The zippers do not unzip fluidly and is a bit sticky.  The exterior fabric feels weird to me.  This may just be opinion, but it feels a bit cheap.  The interior canvas is thin.  The mesh is more grass green and the canvas sea green.  Again, may be a matter of taste but, I just think the colors clash.  For the price, I was expecting a much better-quality case than this one.  My wife has found Pencil Cases with better quality and with a smaller price tag.  Overall, this is not one that my wife would want to order again.

title: Easy to assemble
text: I ordered this Desk Organizer Stacking Letter Tray Stackable Paper Trays Black Mesh Office File Organizer for review..  It is made of a lightweight medal mesh but feels durable.  The black color looks good on my wife's desk.  It is easy to assemble.  It is a bit wobbly because the layers sit on each other with sliding the side handles into or over the previous shelve handle.  They do not snap in tight, so the top two shelves can wiggle a bit.  Additionally, I was hoping that my wife could just pull the top sectioned part up and off to be able to take her supplies with her when crafting; but when I attempted to take it off, the whole thing collapsed.  That being said, the quality does meet the price and it does function well for her needs.

title: Best markers we have used by far
text:
Ordered the Caliart 100 Colors Dual Tips Permanent Markers, Alcohol Markers, and Coloring Art Markers for review.
These markers come in a nice zippered Canvas bag, which allows you to take them with you and keep them together. With 100 different colors, you have a variety to choose from for any project you are working on. The dual tips, fine and Broad (slanted chiseled) allow you to either color in fine details or make larger brush strokes when coloring a larger area. Additionally, you can use both tips to create beautiful artistic lettering. My wife loves these markers. The quality supersedes their price point by far. I recognize that this set may be slightly more costly than other sets of dual tip markers, but for serious crafters or artists they are a better-quality marker. If you are looking for a starting set or want to get some markers for your kids, this might be overkill. Yet, my pre-teen and teenage daughters love this set. If only their mom would let them use them.
The ink has excellent saturation and the colors are vibrant. The ink flows without skipping when using them as some other brands do. They last when working on a larger project and do not easily dry out, which can be frustrating. The color is also consistent as you write or color with them. Honestly, I can not imagine anyone not liking these markers. My wife has already ordered 2 other sets. One smaller set and one larger set. Seriously, these markers are worth buying.

title: Letters stay where put
text:
This 2020 Upgraded Felt Letter Board Set 11x14' Double Sided Black Purple Changeable Message Sign Board for review. It is an exceptional value. The glittery letters are a bit more stand out than flat colored letters. They were easy to pop out of the sheet and there were only a few times the cut was not clear through. The letters and emojis stick extremely well to the felt. In fact, they stuck so well that I accidentally separated a letter or two when I pulled them off. The bonus emojis are cute and they too stick well to the felt. The letters are thick enough to look 3D on the board.
There are lots of letters and I have not at this point been short letters, but I would have liked more vowels. You also get punctuation marks, flowers and numbers. The little game that it comes with it is a fun addition. The stand is a bit tipsy and not very durable. I will probably replace the stand with a sturdier one.
Overall for the price, this a great felt letter board. We have had a great time playing with it. I am guessing my daughters will soon each want their own.

title: Great value for the price
text:
I ordered these iLable 8.5" x 11" Full Sheet Sticker Paper for Laser & Inkjet Printers[300 Sheets,300 Labels], for review as we wanted to create tags for Christmas gifts on my wife's Die-cut machine. The color saturation is okay, maybe a little lighter than expected. For black and white address labels they would work just fine. For the price they are definitely a great deal.
They were a little difficult to peel off the backing but they adhered well to the wrapping paper.

Overall, I will definitely be able to create a lot of stickers for all kinds of surfaces with 300 sheets in this set. And for the money they are of great value.

title: Awesome for crafts too!
text: I ordered these '14 Name Badge Magnets - Magnetic Name Tag Holders with Premium Strength Neodymium Magnets, 3m Adhesive on Front' for my wife to use for making crafts such as refrigerator magnets and they work perfectly for this. The 3M adhesive works great for plastic, metal and non-porous materials but for fabric, wood or porous materials it's much better to use glue sticks, super glue or an epoxy glue. I was surprised at how much hold the little magnets have but was actually expecting them to be a just bit stronger.  Overall I think this set is of a really good value to be used as name tag holders so not poke holes in your clothes like the old school name tag pins, or even refrigerator magnets.

title: Rustic Looking Journal
text:
I ordered this Coloabis Leather Journal Notebook for review because my wife who both travels and journals consistently. When we opened she was a bit perplexed at the design. It has several separate inserts versus one continuous notebook. One insert is lined and the second is unlined. It also comes with a Monthly plan insert, but it is not actually in the the cover so you can choose to put it in or leave it out.

It does have a plastic pocket and 2 slots for cards, ID. It also is not inserted into the cover, rather comes separate so you can also choose to use it or not. There are also some cardboard pockets on the flaps of the journal but I would not trust those with any cards of value. The cover is a light fawn colored leather. It is very soft and scuffs and scratches very easily.

The set comes with a pull string-fabric bag to store the journal in. Additionally, it included a relatively nice pen. They also added a cute little sticker of a Birkenstock. Overall, for the money it is okay. I would just worry that the pages may not stay intact or attached to the binding. It does have a rustic, wander kind of feel to it and that look may appeal to some.

title: Great value for the price
text:
I ordered this Yenhome Large Size Clear Transfer Paper for Vinyl 17.8" x 118" for my wife to use with her Cricut and adhesive vinyl. As she is crafting like crazy for the holidays, she had the opportunity to try this transfer paper for several projects. It did not work quit as well as some more expensive transfer paper but for the price it worked just fine. She was able to create some customizable signs and occasionally the transfer paper took a little extra time on a letter or two to get the vinyl to stick to it and then the reverse also it took a bit of extra care to be sure the vinyl released onto the wooden blank.

It was convenient to have the lined back to cut the paper into the correct size to avoid wasting it. And it separated well when removing the backing. Overall, this is a great economical option to the more expensive name branded transfer papers. I would definitely order more for my wife as she goes through a lot of transfer paper.

title: Fluid and Smooth lettering
text:
This Zeyar liquid chalk marker set is a great starter or basic set. The 8 colors are all bright and vibrant. They are easy to use and the liquid chalk writes smoothly and fluidly on a chalkboard or any non-porous surface. You do have to shake them for a bit before using and prime the tip, but compared to other chalk markers I have tried this is pretty simple and quick. The chalk does not leave a dust residue and wipes off completely with a cloth and a little water. The chisel tip makes it easy to artistically letter chalkboard signs.

This set would make a great gift for any crafter - pre-teen, teen or adult. They are a great value for the price and I will definitely be purchasing more of these in a bigger variety of colors as these chalk markers are the best ones I have found thus far.

title: Great little journals
text:
I ordered these Taotree Yellow Classic Dotted Bullet Grid Journal Notebook for review as my wife uses them to make lists, journal, take notes in, etc. She has used a multitude of brands of these notebooks. These are some of the better ones that she has used. She like the sturdiness of the leather covers. They are soft yet don't bend easily. The pages are not lined, but are dotted so you can write evenly on the pages. The pages are also very well made and durable. They do not easily tear out. The binding is solid. title: No USB connection necessary!
text:
I had the opportunity to order and review the new HP OfficeJet Pro 8025 All-in-One Wireless Printer, with Smart Tasks. My past experience with HP products has led me to stay clear from them because of all the bloatware software that is (in my experience) buggy. With that said, I would like to share my thoughts on this printer.

First off I would like to say that I am extremely pleased with the HP OfficeJet Pro 8025. Just the fact that you can set it up without having to connect it to your computer via USB cable first, was huge! My last HP Printer and Software was so buggy and would lose connection randomly until I moved it from it’s remote location and re-connected it to the computer via the USB cable. Then I would have to move it again to it’s remote location. Needless to say that was very annoying. The 8025 was super easy to set up via WiFi and start using right away with zero issues.

Setting up the WiFi was quite easy with the touchscreen and I never had to make any physical connection to the PC via USB cable. This makes me very happy! Setting up the HP OfficeJet Pro 8025 for my Windows 10 PC, Android mobile device and Chromebook was an absolute breeze. For Windows 10 you need only to install the free App from the Windows App Store (without all the unnecessary Bloatware). The Android device was just as simple as downloading the App from the play store. Setting up to print from my Chromebook was as easy as making sure that I was connected to the same WiFi Network and searching for printers via the printer settings on the Chromebook, then add the HP 8025.

At first set up, I did have some issues with the printer to where it would pull through several sheets of paper every time it would print test pages. This was a huge disappointment, however this issue has seemed to correct itself and it has not happened since but I thought it was worth mentioning. It totally could have been user error on my part when placing a small stack of paper into the paper tray for the initial set up process.

This printer has the capability to connect to your Google Drive and DropBox accounts (via the included “Apps” settings) so that you may print FROM them and Copy/Scan TO them. This was “fairly” easy to set up to my Google Drive account but I have yet to try DropBox as I don’t use that as often. This feature alone will make it so much more convenient for my daughter who uses Google Drive exclusively for her School Homework.

You can also send copies/scans from the printer, to email addresses. This is a little cumbersome through the small touchscreen but I do love this feature. Speaking of the small touchscreen - it will prove challenging for those with long fingernails but it is doable ;)

I also tested out the FAX feature that is included with the HP OfficeJet Pro 8025 and although this is a dying technology, it’s still used by many businesses as I have found. I am happy to report that the FAX feature works great, and though I won’t use it a lot, I am grateful that HP included this feature with this model.

The 8025 also has included "Smart Tasks" which basically allows you to set up (via the mobile app) tasks such as scanning a document and print directly to your Printer or send to Google Drive, DropBox, OneDrive, Box, Evernote, Quickbooks or an e-mail address. I use this feature currently to scan received invoices from my Android device and send directly to my Google Drive. It places this scan into a designated folder under another folder called "HP Smart". You can create several different "tasks" on the Mobile App to simplify things that you would do on a regular basis. This is an incredibly simple and useful feature that I will be using more often.

In conclusion HP has changed my views with this printer, and I highly recommend the OfficeJet 8025 for those in need of a compact All-in-One Wireless Copy/Scan/FAX Printer

text:
Delivered in one day. Appears to be exactly as advertised. So far feels comfortable to use. I'm enjoying the tremendous amount of "real estate" available. That is a huge advantage over other portable lap desks and trays.

Since I've been using it only a few hours, I'm not star-rating this laptop bed tray desk's comfort or sturdiness.

In my opinion this product needs an obvious improvement, namely the additions of additional, and taller stoppers.

Why taller? (Note, multiple stopper could come in various heights.) To accommodate products such as the AmazonBasics ventilated adjustable laptop computer holder desk stand, the Road Tools Traveler CoolPad®, and Steklo laptop stand adjustable aluminum computer riser, all of which allow for ventilation and reduced heat build up.

Why more than one stopper? Because I doubt that a single stopper of the current size is sufficiently strong to withstand over time the weight of a laptop when the table is tilted. And, to allow for varying positions of stoppers to accommodate multiple devices, such as a laptop and a smart phone and/or a tablet such as an iPad.

Also, for someone using this in bed or sitting normally on a couch, the leg spacing is fine. But, when one stretches out lengthwise on a couch, the tray's legs are so far apart that the leg nearest the front of the couch actually extends out beyond the couch's front edge. Each of the tray's legs could be positioned further inward by over an inch (2.54 cm) without any risk that the tray would tip over. Moving the legs inward would increase the places that the tray could be used.

Even without those improvements, my star-rating thus far remains at 5 stars.

text:

First, the "backer" for holding the photos in place does have little "L" brackets that snap into place depending on the size of your photo. (It supports sizes up to 6 x 8 inch). Theres a small screen to show what you're about to capture and a simple scan and save captures the photo to an SD card. That, of course, can easily be transfered to your computer for saving, sharing, whatever.

One thing that didn't occur to me... Many years ago, when I was taking a lot of 35 mm pictures, I would save the negatives... didn't know why, just seemed like the thing to do. But what can you do with them now? This unit will handle them. Theres a plastic slide tray made just for these old negatives - you place the strip inside and snap it closed, then slide in from the side and capture those shots as photos! (Not just as the negative of a photo) Nice!

As for picture quality, its pretty good - they do offer 2 resolutions and theres some provision for adjustments built it, but that seems a little tedious. Once in my computer, I'll be able to do a better job of "fixing" old faded images with software, anyway.

title: Have used lightly over 2 years. Still works but I'm unimpressed and don't recommend it.
text:
I bought this laminator - [[ASIN:B0010JEJPC Scotch Thermal Laminator 2 Roller System (TL901)]] - for $29.69 from Amazon in February 2015. It's so very definitely NOT worth the crossed out price of $80.49! It wasn't worth that then and it's not worth that now! So firstly, don't be misled by the crossed out price. I really wish Amazon would start policing these misleading crossed out prices! This laminator can currently (date of this review is 2/10/2017) be purchased through a well known online department store for $19.97 (with free shipping or free in store pick-up). You can also buy the newer version - TL902 - through another online department store for only $17.99 (with free in store pick-up). So, the crossed out price here is terribly misleading. Note: I can't 'advertise' these stores here, but go shopping with your browser and you should find it around or under $20 elsewhere as well.

After 2 years of use, here's my review of my experience with this laminator:

Pros: It still works fine with light use for the past 2 years. Also, I have found it can give nice results if you only want to laminate items up to 3mm thickness (so a photo by itself or with a sticker on back for instance). It will laminate nicely for a 10 minute period, without warping or scorching. So, it's okay for light duty laminating of items of limited thickness. Note: I've found mine needs to be set to the 5mm thickness if I don't want the lamination lifting soon after being laminated.

Cons: I bought this laminator to make bookmarks for gifts using varying layers of card and photos, and later to use in my small home-based business for the same. I also planned to do cards with pressed flowers, but my machine gives bad results for any of that. I'm now looking to purchase bookmark sleeves, after 2 years of trying every way I could think of to get good results. This laminator seems incapable of laminating nicely varying layer heights of paper and card or card and pressed flowers (up to 5mm total thickness). The issues happen when I use photo paper together with thin to regular thickness card framing and backing the photos, unless it's all a uniform height (so no framing with the backing card). When using the 3mm setting the lamination lifts pretty quickly leaving ugly results. When using the 5mm setting, it may look great at first, but within a day or less the laminating film starts to lift leaving nasty marks on the card around the photo or all round the pressed flowers etc. Furthermore, I've had to be careful not to laminate for more than 10mins, or it gets too hot and starts scorching.

Overall, I'm not pleased with this laminator. It does not meet my needs and I would not recommend it. However, it might be fine for you if all you want to do is laminate the occasional photo.

title: nice if you don't want to grind your own
text:
I bought this nib for an Al-Star. I wish it and other italic nibs were options instead of only F and EF. This nib gives a hint of line variation that makes cursive much more satisfying. I haven't tried the 1.5 nib, which I imagine would give an even greater line variation but would require a larger script size. With the 1.1, I can write very similar size to a fine ball-point pen, but with much better looking script.

Upon examining this italic nib carefully, I was surprised to find the tip is beveled instead of square. This would seem to make it difficult to get fine hairlines. I decided to start with an "F" nib and grind an italic nib the way I thought it should be. With a very sharp right-angle on the tip, I get finer hairlines and much better line width variation without an excessively wide nib.

Although I polished the nib up to a 12000 grit stone and a strop, neither italic nib (Lamy's nor my own) are especially smooth. The trade-off of a nib that can make fine lines is that it must be sharp and more likely to cut or tear-out paper fibers. It can be polished further, but eventually, the sharp angle is polished off and the finest line width is widened.

Overall, I'm pleased with the italic nibs. I prefer my own to the one being reviewed here, but either is much more satisfying than a ball-end nib.

title: extra chairs at our house for big people
text:
This might normally be a product for an institutional consumer, but I bought a couple for our house church. My family is of smaller stature (5'8", 5'1" and kids) so if any of us sit back in the chair, our feet don't reach the ground. We're also light (132, 99 lbs. and the kids about half that). Our own chairs are kid-size or middle-school size. We also cut-down our table and desk legs to fit properly. But when we have guests, some of them are much larger. We have a couch and upholstered chair, but we didn't want to fill up our house with furniture that doesn't fit us. These chairs accommodate more large people when we need to, and they stack to store when we're not using them. We may end up getting two more for a total of four.

The black fabric shows a lot of lint. Get a marl fabric, a lighter color or the polka dots if that is a concern.

The book rack results in a higher stack, but I think they'd still stack four-high with the racks. They're heavier and bulkier than typically smaller stacking chairs so it could be hard to pull one off the top of a high stack, but four-high with racks should be no problem.

These wider, 21" chairs are better for large people than the standard 18". They're also better if the chairs are not connected in a row. In rows, wide people can use part of the adjacent chairs. In our house church, we don't use rows. It's roughly a circle around a living room. Just imagine 12 to 14 people in a living room. In many people's homes that will take some extra chairs. These are better than just folding chairs. Besides these, we also use school chairs and a bean-bag because half our church is kids.

title: The printer will not print black if I select black-only ...
text:
Review after 9 months:

- Constant print alignment problems
- Smearing
- Skipped lines
- Heavy color ink usage even though I almost never print color or pictures
- Black ink runs out fast even though I use the faded-grey draft mode for more than half my prints

The quality problems are so persistent and grievous that I can't imagine using this for business. I use it primarily to print worksheets for my two kids, and UPS return labels. Every time I try to use it for something where quality matters, it disappoints.

If this was truly low-initial-cost printer (40 dollar job), then I would accept getting what I paid for. While this is still an inexpensive printer, the ink costs add up quickly and I will have to consider dumping this since it cannot print anything decently and is too costly to print casually.

Note: The printer will not print black if I select black-only if even one color cartridge is reported empty. I'm disappointed that the Epson is deliberately set up to stop printing black just because a color cartridge is out and did not allow a workaround to print black only. Shame.

I've found the scanner produces poor image quality. I would like to scan my children's artwork on paper, but I get better results taking a picture of it with a camera. I suppose the scanner function works adequately if you're just using it to replace fax.

Printing can be good quality if the right "inkjet" paper is used so it doesn't bleed too much. I think this is the first inkjet I've had where I won't regret having it instead of a laser printer, but I also wouldn't replace the lasers at the office with anything like this. It's definitely a home, personal or small office, low-productivity printer, and it has limited page sizes. Personally, the thing I miss the most is double-sided 11x17, but admittedly that is another category/price-range.

I have done some photo prints on this, which I would not plan to do regularly. This is not a photo printer. I used photo paper to print some proof-of-concepts for an offset print project. The print quality was quite good, but the printer left roller marks with many tiny pin prick dents on the paper. There may be an adjustment for this, but it's not worth it to me to figure out. It was awkward enough just changing paper sizes and orientation with the poor user interface. For photo printing, I still prefer a laser-exposure mini-lab type system (Fuji Frontier etc.) - In other words, I send it out to a service.

I frequently have alignment problems with the printer. I get places on the page where the image is shifted left or right. I've run the print head alignment utility several times but it still has alignment problems on occasion.

text:

title: Excellent product to use with Google Voice to get very low-cost home phone service
text:
Awesome product for what I consider a really customer-friendly price. I used this to get myself practically free phone service at my summer home, saving something like $30/month that I was paying the lousy cable company. (Now I'm planning to use the Obi202 to receive voip calls at my main home.)

The set up is really easy, their instructions are clear and easy to follow, and the website offers a ton of additional help. Here were my steps:
0. You need internet service with decent bandwidth.
1. Get a Google Voice number (free from Google)
2. Buy the Obi200 from Amazon.
3. Plug in the Obi200, connecting it to network (using ethernet cable) and cordless phone main station base (phone cable). (Test it as suggested.)
4. Go to obitalk.com, create account, add your device (using the product id), configure device and connect to Google Voice.
5. Wait a couple of minutes, make test call to Google Voice number, answer call.
6. Smile happily.

I connected two different Gvoice numbers to this unit, and calls to either number come through as promised. You can configure up to 4 such voip services, but of course can only use one at a time. The Obi202 enables two line simultaneous use.

Note: I was having trouble receiving calls and thought something was wrong. It turned out that the old telephone I was using at first to test wasn't working correctly with this box for some reason. (It wasn't worth investigating further, since it worked immediately with the newer phone set I was planning to use anyway.) So if you have any trouble, make sure you troubleshoot thoroughly, don't immediately blame the box or the configuration.

PS: If you want to register your number for e911 service (so that your address shows up when you dial 911), check if your county uses smart911 (smart911 dot com).

title: Excellent shredder for personal use, in a compact size
text:
This is an excellent shredder, I can recommend it without hesitation. It does a great job, without any fuss, and without too much noise. Multiple sheets aren't a problem: but note that when they say "8 sheets", they mean 8 sheets of relatively thin (20lb) paper, so your bills and junk mail will probably need to be fed in smaller quantities.

This is compact in size, smaller than the other two shredders I have (Fellowes and Amazon Basics), but should be fine for most personal use. If you want to shred a lot of stuff regularly, you might want to get a bigger shredder.

The safety features are adequate in my view. (I think it's hard to hurt yourself with a shredder, but I suppose there are ways to do it.) Emptying the bin is easy -- and note that lifting the shredder top off does activate the kill switch. I generally pour the shreds (carefully!) into brown paper grocery bags, and put them in my recycle bin.

Also note that this model (H-8C) does not have the CD/DVD shredder slot. (Credit cards can go in the regular paper slot.)

title: Excellent labels, but note that they're not a complete half-page size.
text:
Works really well with the USPS print-and-ship labels: if you choose the label & receipt option, the label prints on the top portion, which you can peel off, and the receipt prints on the bottom, which tears off at the perforations in the middle. The label peels off and sticks on easily and cleanly on an envelope or box.

The one thing I didn't like is that the label on top doesn't take up the full half-page: it leaves a border around the edges. With the similar Avery 2 labels per page version, each label is a full half-page, no borders.

Unfortunately, Amazon's return labels aren't formatted to print neatly on label paper (at least they weren't the last time I returned something). To use this kind of label paper I have to use a screen snipping tool to cut out the label and paste it carefully into a word processing form --- I use MS Word, but anything else like Google Docs will also work. (If anyone has a better solution I'd welcome a tip in the comments.)

title: Excellent labels for printer use
text:
These are excellent shipping labels, although they do require a bit of setup to use correctly on a printer. I've used them for Amazon returns, UPS, FedEx, and USPS shipping without problems: they print neatly, stick onto packages securely, and are a whole lot better (and easier!) than printing on plain paper and using glue and tape.

Note that Avery also sells a very similar (identical?) 8126 "ink jet" label, I've used both quite successfully on my laser printers.

Avery does offer templates on the website, but for something like this you really don't need to bother, you can just create a very simple template yourself in your preferred software by drawing a thin dividing line exactly halfway down, and reducing the margins to 0.5in or so. (Note that Amazon doesn't give you a return label form that you can print directly onto this label paper: I wish they did. I do a cut & paste in MS Word, which works, but is more hassle than it should be.) Make sure that you're selecting the correct printer options (turn off duplex, use manual feed, set paper type to label or thick paper). title: useful to assist in learning Mandarin
text:
I believe these cards can be useful to help one learn Mandarin, especially the written language. They have the word written in Traditional and Simplified characters on one side, then it in Pinyin and English on the other side, along with a simple phrase in all four beneath that. The words are grouped together (Greetings, Questions, Colors, Food & Drink, Verbs, etc.), and there are downloadable audio files so you can hear how the words/phrases are pronounced.
The drawbacks? I wish the words/phrases were also phonetically spelled out, as you may end up pausing and replaying the audio tracks several times to figure out the pronunciation (Pinyin doesn't exactly translate into how to say it unless you're very familiar with the accents). Also, the audio files run into each other, so it's a bit tricky navigating them until you do nail down each word/phrase. That's why I feel these flash cards may be better for understanding the written language (characters) than the spoken language.

text:

The main thing about the HP Tango is you have to have the smart app on your phone or tablet to use this - there's no US or any cables other than the power cord. It's easy to download and it walks you through the set-up, and you can install it on multiple phones (or use an email address it gives you to allow others to send items to print). title: decent shredder for the price
text: We already own a shredder, but it doesn't do the cross-cut so were happy to try one that does. The Sentinel Pro FX1800P does chop up the paper better than shredders that just cut in a straight line, but it doesn't do the small 'confetti' that some other, higher end ones do- they're over an inch long but better than a long strip. It's still a bit noisy, but we're used to that for a shredder and don't plan on using it while someone's on the phone or watching a movie, and it handles large loads of paper without overheating or slowing down, which helps to get the job done all at once. You have to keep watch on the paper since the top is fixed and you'll have to open the front, pull out the bin and press down on the scraps rather than be able to lift the top part off to press down to get more room like you can with other shredders. Other than that, I do like the light overheat functionality, and it has the usual reverse and and auto stop-start functionality. All in all, it's a nice, functional shredder for the price - maybe not one you want for a busy office if you're going to run it a lot while people need to talk in the background, but great for the home or if you can run it from time to time without bothering people.

(3) The pages themselves are thicker than your average loose leaf paper. I bought fine tipped markers off Amazon to color code my planner and they don't bleed through the pages which is perfect.
(4) I like that it's not just your typical calendar (Jan-Dec). It starts in the middle of the year and goes all through the middle of the next year. That just works for me better.

Overall, I really like this planner! I would definitely recommend it!

title: Excellent boxes for Christmas gifts
text:

I've survived on scavenging for years, but I figured just purchasing appropriately-sized boxes would be better. It definitely was; I was able to use these for more than half of all gifts given this year. Since they are all the same size, it has the additional benefit of making wrapping easy, since you use the same format for each gift. Multiple recipients decided to keep the boxes so they can re-use them for their own gifting purposes.

Easy to fold, certainly sturdy enough for a gift box. The only things I don't like is [a] the seams are a bit thin at places - sufficient for a gift box but maybe not robust for other purposes, and [b] the way it folds, there are little cardboard tabs which protrude a bit from the edges of the box, so you cannot get perfectly smooth wrapped edges. So would recommend for most one-time shipping/gifting purposes.

title: Great for protecting a rubber band ball that might end up in a hot attic
text:
Recently I pulled out some old storage tubs and found an old rubber band ball I had made as an adolescent, about 6" in diameter. Many of the outer rubber bands had held up, but some had melted/broken over the many years of it being in an attic, so despite being a grown adult I wanted to protect my creation from further deterioration. For this purpose I purchased these rubber bands as an outer layer. While this goes against my long-established policy of never using wide rubber bands for the ball, needs must when the devil drives, and the properties of these seemed too advantageous to pass up. Most other rubber bands of this dimension or quality are black, which is obviously unsuitable for this purpose.

These are perfect for the job. They easily stretch to cover the 6"+ ball, though near the end the ball was well over 7" and I was approaching the limit. Zero broke on me, or even felt anywhere near breaking - which was a common experience I had when making the ball all those years ago - and all felt very secure and quite elastic. There was little variation in size - a couple outliers were clearly 5" and not 6" bands - but all the rubber bands fit over the ball, though it was quite a bit of a workout after going through all four pounds of them. The generous powder coating and wide form factor made stretching them over the ball much more comfortable than they might have been, as it gave each band more surface area to grip onto during the process.

I only dropped a star because they are quite expensive for what you get. Probably fine for people using these for ceramic molds, but for a rubber band ball it's a bit of an investment.

Would recommend for rubber band balls in the 6-7" diameter range.

title: Ink stays black, even over time
text:

Other than that, they are the same, writing is so-so but not smooth for someone who is accustomed to higher-end pens. This may have to do with the specific kind of ink needed in these cartridges to make them usable in a wider range of environments.

Anyway, if you want a blacker pressurized ink cartridge, this works. Otherwise, probably not a huge advantage over the standard Fisher ink.

title: Much better than graphite for marking
text: Like its white counterpart, this black chalk is far better than graphite since it can be easily brushed away when you are done with the project. It is harder and more brittle than graphite, which means you have to be more careful with it, but the tradeoff is obviously worth it. As you would expect, it works perfectly fine with the Bohin extra-fine chalk mechanical pencil, as I now have one pencil with white chalk, and one with black chalk.

title: Better than pencils, but a bit hard, a bit brittle
text:
I purchased this - along with some black chalk refills - after working with an old white marking pencil for many years. The pencil was annoying to use - it was very hard and left marks after the fact. These are better - much better at making fine lines - and easier to handle as well. If you are working with dense fabrics and need the extra detail, they are well-suited for that purpose.

For me, though, I think they are a bit too hard. I am working with linen and corduroy and I still have to go over the lines a couple times to make them visible, it's a balancing act between going too soft to be seen and so hard the chalk breaks. I've worked out the technique, I think, but I'd prefer if it were maybe a bit larger diameter chalk and a bit softer. That might just mean I need a different kind of chalk pencil, or maybe those triangular tailor chalks instead of these.

So far as I can tell, the chalk comes right out if you rub it, but if you are even a little careful it stays put. Only once have I had a line become too faded to see while I was still working. No complaints there.

So I suppose I'd recommend for denser materials, even if it doesn't work for me.

title: Work very well for 18650 battery holders.
text:
I purchased these to hold spare 18650 cells in my hiking and work bag, and they are of the perfect dimensions to do so. I added a thin rubber gasket to the lid and the base to make the tubes water-resistant and shock-absorbent respectively, and the battery has minimal play inside. The top has deep-enough ridges to make tightening and untightening it easy.

Some tubes of this kind are unacceptably fragile for almost any use, but these seem tough enough to survive in a padded bag. They aren't "survival grade", and would probably crack if subjected to significant stresses, but I was able to tighten down the lid and loosen it without damaging anything.

Can't speak to their ability to hold pennies, but as noted they are decently durable and the screw-top fastens down securely, so would recommend.

title: Great heavy-duty shredder for a variety of materials
text:
I purchased this for my father for the purposes of shredding a formidable volume of old papers, documents, junk mail, and bags - he uses the resulting shreddings to make paper logs. I've run quite a bit of material through it myself, including several old technical texts and books, without issue. The machines draws it in, cuts it up, and carries on without a hitch. I've only tripped the thermal safety once, and only when shredding full books. Every time I've jammed it up - which is infrequent - I already knew I was pushing the limit of what it could handle. I would prefer it didn't trip *quite* so quickly, but it is reasonable.

The system can easily handle 15+ pages, magazines, thin box cardboard (think cereal boxes), full envelopes, printed papers, the whole deal. Much better than his previous shredder, which was a robust but still fairly-low volume unit. The shreddings aren't particularly small - it isn't suitable for high-security applications - but the output is small enough that you can turn it into compost or burn material relatively easily.

However, if you aren't shredding a large amount of material every week - in the range of five to ten pounds - it might not be worth the price you end up paying for a unit like this. For the purposes I described, however, would recommend.

title: Ideal for scribbling out labels
text:
I use these for just one purpose - scribbling out labels on boxes. I work in an IT department and we are constantly receiving things and shipping them out again. Regular Sharpies are sufficient for this, but they have a fairly narrow head and so require a lot of scribbling to be effective.

These Pro versions are much better. Better coverage, thicker ink, better all-around experience. They feel durable and are large enough to easily grip and control even with gloves on. They last a decent amount of time - larger labels consume them more quickly, of course, but I can knock out dozens of smaller labels with a single marker quite easily.

While I only needed one to replace a lost marker, I would recommend ordering the 4-pack, as it is a better value by a considerable margin.

Would recommend for office/warehouse use.

title: Great for scribbling out labels and bar codes
text:
I work in IT, and I have these markers for one reason: scribbling out old shipping labels so we can re-use the boxes. Regular sharpies are fine but that's a lot of scribbling, especially on some of the boxes we get in - they can have several hand-sized labels scattered across the surface. This XL sharpie with the wide chisel tip makes very quick work of everything. Only thing it can't write on is those special oleophobic labels they sometimes use on boxes, and pretty much nothing sticks to those, so you just have to tear them off.

Odor is strong, but fades rapidly. Dries quickly enough, though I'd give it a couple minutes if you are wearing white pants. After drying, it doesn't appear to rub off. Tip is tough and doesn't wear down easily. Cap is tight and seals well - don't leave it off though, or the marker will go dry quite quickly. Marker seems to be quite durable - though here in IT it spends most of its life in a desk drawer, I think this could survive on a warehouse shelf, feels pretty tough.

Would recommend - I would have have purchased this two times times now, and will do so in the future.

title: Beautiful paper and construction
text:
Great notebook for just about anything - the paper is very smooth, absorptive, has a little drag but not too much. I have seen almost not bleed-through except with a sharpie marker. High enough quality that you don't necessarily want to use it for random scribbles, but the dual-ring binding and stiff backing means that it works great for every sort of project where you need to bring it around with you. Perforations and date/title fields are very nice to have as well.

I'd really like to see a 3mm grid version, but 5mm should be fine for most.

title: Great little pack of replacement blades
text:
Exactly what you expect, replacement blades for the smaller of the x-acto knives. These are great - though they are a bit tricky to separate from one another, due to the oil and whatnot. It might be worth getting one of those dispenser-packages instead of this box. Not an issue for me - I don't go through that many blades myself - but if you are pulling new ones every day it might be a bit of a chore.

Blade quality appears to be good, and there are plenty of them in the pack, so would recommend.

title: Great, light-weight tape gun for office use
text:
I bought this for use in an IT office to tape up packages, as the ones we had were all heavy, old things that constantly lost the tape and failed to trim it properly. This is great in every respect - it is light, but feels completely solid, the lever keeps the tape in place, the blade is adjustable so you can nudge it forward, making trimming the tape extremely easy. It was an absolute upgrade and does everything I want it to do.

Would I recommend this for the squad of fourteen 250lb gorillas on the warehouse floor? Maybe not - though I don't doubt its constitution. But for anyone else looking for a tape gun, this is the way to go.

title: Better on carpet than the alternative, but still not perfect
text:
I purchased these for my computer chair - which is a custom one I made from an office chair base, a plywood platform, and the passenger seat of a 2000 Impala Sedan. Nice chair, all things considered, but a bit heavy for your typical office chair wheels, even on a fairly dense carpet. the problem was mostly that the wheels refused to rotate, or roll, with any consistency. So I installed these instead.

Installation was very easy for 4/5 wheels. Literally just popped the old ones out and these in - didn't even need any tools for my chair, despite the wheels being all original.. The fifth gave me an absolute bear of a time and required two prybars, a screwdriver, and caliper grease, but I think that was a problem with the socket, since whereas the first four wheels went right back into the sockets, I had to use a diamond file to clean up the edge of the fifth socket to get the fifth wheel in place.

After install, my opinion is that it is better, but still a problem on the carpet. The wheels require force to rotate when you change direction, though less than with the standard casters. They roll much easier though. I'm not exactly gliding around, but the improvement is notable.

The major thing to remember is that these will add height to your chair, I would say about a half inch over standard casters, maybe a little more. So if you already have little room for your legs, this might give you a bit of a squeeze.

All in all - I would recommend this kind of wheel, and probably this brand as well. It won't make carpet like hardwood, but it will still help.

title: Always ready to go, for all kinds of paper
text:
We all hate grabbing a pen that doesn't work - especially these days, when the only reason most people grab a pen at all is because they want to quickly jot something down. Typical ballpoints are completely hit-or-miss in this regard, sometimes they work, sometimes they don't, sometimes they work for a few seconds and then fail or fade out or become gunky at the tip.

Not so with the Precise V7. I've been using these (or the V5, which has an Extra Fine, instead of a Fine tip) at work for months have never had a case where it didn't work the moment I put the tip to paper. I have never picked one up and had it come out dry, not even once. The flow is very consistent - you aren't likely to run into problems with fading or smearing on this one. I write in all-caps and find it to be quite suitable to my purposes. I don't typically use these for long-form writing, only notes, so your mileage may vary if that is your use case.

Generally, if you want a pen which will always be ready to write, it has to have a completely sealed cap - no holes, and no clicky-pens. This fits the bill. If you want something which can make fine, clean lines, this is what you want. If you instead want more exact lines, with more control over the flow, I recommend the V5. I purchased a 12-pack of each and left a pen in all the places I'm likely to need them at home and work, with plenty to spare in storage.

Would recommend.

title: Great for scrawling out bar codes on boxes
text:
I bought these for a single purpose - to scrawl out labels and barcodes on boxes so I can re-use them for shipping. I purchased the Sharpie Pros for work - I'm in IT and am constantly receiving and shipping items to different sites. I was using standard Sharpies and whatever other markers I could dig up from various desks and closets, but they were inadequate, barely covering the barcode or going dry or leaving only a very thin line, requiring lots of scribbling. These avoid all those problems and allow me to quickly scrawl out the barcodes and labels from the previous delivery, ensuring there will be no technical mistakes in the shipment. The Pros work on everything except the special hydro/oleophobic labels they sometimes use at UPS - I haven't found *anything* that sticks to those yet, so I just have to tear them off. For the rest, these markers work well.

Being in IT, durability isn't much of a concern for these - they just sit in a desk when not in use - but they feel pretty durable, I wouldn't have any typical concerns.

I also tried the Milwaukee Jobsite markers here on Amazon. Those work well too, though their tip is narrower and the ink isn't quite as thick. If you find the Pros don't work, they might be a solid alternative.

title: Great for crossing out labels when re-using boxes

I purchased/tried quite a few markers and I wasn't happy with any of them - they are either too thing, or too light, or dry out too quickly. I didn't want to use paint markers because I need the ink to dry very quickly, within a few seconds, with no chance of rubbing off. So I purchased these instead and I use them only to cross out labels so I don't have to rip off the barcodes. They work quite well on everything except those special hydrophobic/oleophobic labels UPS sometimes uses which repel pretty much everything.

I also purchased the 4-pack of Sharpie Pros. I *think* I like those a little better, mostly because they have a broader tip and what I think is blacker (more opaque) ink, not sure. I like having both because where one doesn't work, the other sometimes will, the Milwaukee is rated for a greater number of surfaces than the Sharpie is. If you have to choose one or the other, maybe go with the Sharpie Pro, but these are good too.

title: DON'T USE WRIST RESTS!
text:
This is true of all wrist rest pads. Don't use them!

ANY pressure applied to the bottom of your wrist will only make carpal tunnel syndrome worse.

Use NO pad. Keep wrist just barely elevated above tabletop. It should not touch anything. If you let the Carpal tunnel area rest on the pads, all you're doing is compressing the muscles and tendons in that area, making it even more likely to get swollen and sore. So stay away ftom these devices. The only time to use them is momentarily when you're not typing.
Yes it might feel good for a minute but then it'll get worse and you'll need the wrist rest pad more and more, until eventually you need surgery. So stay away and you'll never need surgery!

title: Bright white labels are quite the bargain
text: A few years ago, when it was first introduced, I purchased a few of the Amazon Basics multipurpose copy/printer paper reams and loved them because of their bright white color and smooth texture.  At that time, it was produced in France but I believe it is now made in Thailand.  Being in the market for round printing labels, I first searched for Avery products because they are my favorites and despite having more labels than any person needs to have in all sizes and shapes, I did not have any of the round 3/4 inch labels which I wanted to decorate the bottoms of Hershey's Kisses.  The price for the Amazon Basics labels was so much less than the others convinced me to take a chance on these and I've been rewarded with bright white matte labels which work perfectly for me using the Avery 4220 template.  These were made in Vietnam but I created the designs and printed them in the USA.  I first did a test of a half sheet of my designs on plain paper, held it up to a light over a sheet of labels, assured that they lined up, then printed.  The ink from my inkjet printer was transferred without a hitch and I'm very happy with this purchase.  For the record, I've seen comments for this size labels that people use the Avery 4221 template so that was the one I first tried and it just didn't line up properly.  I'm not sure how I ended up finding the 4220 or if there's really any difference, but I have perfectly printed labels.

title: Just bottles of ink, each in a box, all in a plastic bag
text: No instructions.  No gloves.  Nothing to put underneath the printer. No smock for you to wear.  I paid for ink and I received ink.  To my surprise, removing the seal from the bottle is the most difficult part and I was fortunately already gloved up, doing it at the kitchen sink when I discovered that it wouldn't just peel off.  Paper was already placed underneath the printer, my clothes were impervious to staining, paper towels were next to the printer, and the cap on the tank was lifted up and placed on its holding spot.  (Lift it up, doesn't screw.)  Unscrew the outer cap from the ink bottle and carefully tilt it into the tank, gently squeeze until the ink reaches the fill line.  Lift the bottle back, wipe it off, recap if there's ink remaining.  Place the cap onto the filled tank and check again for messes.  Check everything and wipe up any drips or dribbles.  Be sure to check dark areas. like where the cap was placed and the printer case.  Repeat with other tanks as needed.  Check your clothes.  Remove your gloves.  Reset the ink levels on the printer in Maintenance and test your printer, cleaning the heads if necessary and check alignment.  I've had no problem with the ink printing clearly and will repurchase without a doubt.

title: Newfangled labels are unlike any others I've used
text: As of today, Avery.com/print offers 111 templates which can be used for these dissolvable labels, but you can simply write on them with a pencil or pen.  I like to print my labels, particularly if I'm presenting a canned good as a gift.  Like most other Avery labels, these have a code printed on the package, but there is no clear date of manufacturing, so you would have to contact Avery to determine their coding.  I don't expect to need that information because I'm using these labels right away.  Before I applied one onto a jar, I felt compelled to test what is meant by "dissolvable."  I removed one corner from one of the five sheets of labels and stuck it on a jar.  I then ran the jar under cool water and to my surprise and delight, the label really and truly dissolved underneath my fingers.  It washed away without the use of a sponge, soap or even warm water.  It felt sort of slimy and was then gone!  Now these labels look like none other I've used.  They are not a true bright white, but they are whitish.  Printing on these is exactly like my other Avery labels and because they are fresh, the printing was clear and remained clear.  I've experienced printing that just did not take on old labels, so I am careful about using fresh labels now.  If you do not need to use FDA approved adhesive safe for indirect food contact and labels which dissolve in water, you do not need these labels.  They are not cheap and they will dissolve if you put them on an envelope and they encounter rain in their delivery to the recipient.  These are perfect for canning or food storage purposes and that's exactly what I'm doing with this package of 90.  They were made in Mexico, south of the border.

title: Best for sending and then being recycled, not reusing
text: Each envelope weighs about 20 grams or .7 ounce including the removable seal cover strip.
