title: Every person who sees it wants one
text: I recently got a standing desk with a white glass top and have found that the ability to write directly on the glass with dry erase markets was a time and paper saver. It's so easy to wipe off the writing with the sweep of a tissue or micro fiber cloth and keep working on a clean desk. This easel life's exactly the same capabilities in a small format and I'm finding it perfect in the kitchen. The secure clip can be attached to any edge, I use it on the top for most cars or don't use it at all of I need the entire surface with no paper being held. I can print a recipe, clip it on the glass easel and make my notes on the board. Entree the notes into the computer when I can, then wipe them away and have a pristine glass easel. I also use this for taking notes during phone calls and then transcribe them later. It's saved me a lot of paper lately in my numerous conversations with Verizon Fios. It was comforting to sit in an oversized chair with this on my lap as I wrote my notes with this in the closed position. The plastic backing is rigid but does not add much weight. I am not a big fan of the enclosed marker so I use my preferred brand with darker ink instead.

title: More impressive than I'd expected, a rather complete introductory set
text: I am a big fan of anything that introduces young persons to art and Faber Castell has hit it out of the ballpark with the quite complete set which also introduces them to color.  Let's face it, too often kids want to play with makeup, not realizing they are exploring texture and color, and at a price that rivals makeup marketed to kids (notably girl targeted), they can experience the texture and color on paper.  They even receive little vials not unlike those we can get at department stores which contain cosmetics samples, yet the kids can create their own shades and use them later, then wash out the vial and do it again.  A mortar and pestle helps them learn what happens when colors are blended together into powder form and see what happens as water is added, thereby learning about hues and shades.  This includes brushes and paper to get them started.  I do have to say that this is a suitable set for adults as well as children, and would be a really nice addition to an adult day care facility for producing art and creative expression.

title: Low residue in addition to low odor
text: In my experience, any dry erase markers do not last long, they tend to dry out if not used often.  I've also found that most have been of the low odor ink formula, and although I don't know for a fact, perhaps this is a reason they do not remain moist.  Nevertheless, I really like these pens for several reasons.  The rubberized grip is definitely easy on the fingers and if my hand is wet with water or moisturizer, I can keep a hold of the marker.  The point is what is called fine, but don't confuse this with the mush finer tips as you would find in a permanent marker.  The ink is solid, flow is even when the pen is new, the cap stays on when snapped on with a little pressure, and I've been able to rig up a hanger attached to the pocket clip of the cap which I've hung next to the mirror at our front door.  I can write directly on the glass face of the mirror and erase it with a tissue or fabric as required.  It's a good option for those who need to write on white boards, glass or mirrors, and I appreciate that they were made in the USA, even if some of the materials have been outsourced.

title: Red button is more depressed than all others, none sticks
text:
I will rate the Canon P1-DHV-3 a weak 4 star rating, 4 for the actual calculator and a -1 due to the terrible manual. I accessed the PDF version of the single folded oversized page online at the Canon website that is printed on the box and printed a copy which looks to be a reduced version of exactly the same paper, so now I have one clean and unfolded pair of papers in addition to the folded and wrinkly large sheet.

As for the actual printing calculator, it is better then the last one I purchased, a Casio that is about 20+ years old and still functional, in that it is clean and new and close to the same size. It uses the same size rolls of paper, some things never change, but be aware that this one comes out of the box with one of the small test rolls. If you intend to print on paper, stock up because the included roll is about an inch diameter and that includes a thick cardboard core which leaves you with about 1/2 inch maximum thickness on the roll. The ink roller is a replaceable CP-16, good to know if you print a lot. Included in the box is a set of 4 AA batteries but there is no AC adapter in the box, so you'll have to purchase that separately. It plugs into the rear of the unit, behind the paper holder wire. I do not care for the wire due to its small gauge and lack of any holding contraption to keep the roll in the calculator and not unwound on the floor behind the desk if it's been knocked over. This is a pet peeve of many printing calculators for me because I've experienced the flying paper roll too many times. It seldom occurs with full rolls, but these little ones seem to grow wings as the paper is depleted and the roll becomes lighter.

Functionally, this calculator does what is described, having the currency conversion and cost-sell-margin functions escalate it to the level above basics. Because the paper roll flows so freely, I would not call it a "Handheld" printing calculator as it's described on the box, but with a little creativity, I will be fabricating something to keep the roll in place so that I can use it in the hand and not on the desk to try it out. It is described as "Desktop" on Amazon and that's what I'd call it.

title: Adhesive is good, inkjet prints well without smearing
text: My only criticism of the Avery full sheets sticker paper in beautiful gold is that the backing could use more slices to allow for quicker and cleaner removal after smaller sections are printed. The paper is thick, so with care, destruction can be avoided, and if you are not a perfectionist, you might not mind anyway.  Since I often have problems with Avery templates printing not so perfectly onto precut shapes, I'm more satisfied by cutting my own with a blade after printing.  I've been having fun with these and appreciate the exposure to a full sized sheet of sticker paper.

title: Simple labels are a good foundation for your creations
text: Yes, the Avery labels print to edge, but only if you successfully align the sheets in your printer and have adjusted the template document you are printing. title: Photos pop, for document printing I still use another printer
text: For printing photos, my preferred printers are Canon. I don't use this one or the little one I've had for a very long time for documents, though, because I have others which employ inks that aren't as costly. With Canon, I always go with their cartridges, never taking a chance with generics or off brand. The TS9020 gave me no problems during setup and since mine is the white version, I am especially careful to keep it clean. I hope the white doesn't yellow over time as many plastics tend to do, and will note that this printer is heavy on the cheaper plastic components. I tried the duplex printing to assure that it works, but won't use it often since I use the printer typically for photos. Because I like the ink quality, I also use this for inkjet label printing. I've only used this for a couple of weeks and my ink levels are still good, after printing photos on both glossy and matte photo papers. I enjoy printing wirelessly from the phone but prefer to use a computer with a larger screen and more editing options. The cost of the 6 ink cartridges is in line with other Canon cartridges, I guess, but with the greater number, the total cost is higher. Like most home printers now, all parts are delicate, so I'm cautious, even when touching the easy to read screen or using the card reader.

title: Delicate artwork and paper
text: If you like delicate feminine artwork,  it's likely that you will love the pale labels which fit small bottles. The patterns do not work well of you need to cut these down,  so be sure the measurements will suit your needs. Rounding the right angled corners is not an option. The paper is like glossy premarital address labels which many of us receive by the dozens from charities soliciting donations and the adhesive is about the same. These are not great for oil based contents because the adhesive is weakened over time. They are really pretty in a classical sense, I just find them weak in materials. title: Smart design
text: The shape of this eraser fits more comfortably in the hand than a traditional blocky style of chalkboard or whiteboard eraser.  Much more comfortably,  and the ends of it can be used in crevices with ease,  so I can have better access into areas inside the edge of a frame.  With two different surfaces on one removable section,  I can use the one I need,  then reverse it when I need the other side.  There is also a section with a piece of blue microfiber fabric which we all are familiar with,  the kind we use for washing,  drying and polishing our cars,  homes, boats and pet's faces and paws. Keep the old ratty ones with holes or stains because they can be cut to the shape of this eraser and stuck to the textured area under the existing microfiber.  I expect the one included to eventually ravel away at the pointed ends because of their narrow form.  This is a very smart,  space saving little tool for home or work.

title: Good supply for occasional use, creates professional impression
text: It's been many years since I've sold on eBay, but do occasionally need to send a package or large envelope and a receipt.  For those times, the Avery shipping label with receipt all on one single page is a convenient supply to have on hand.  I can use the usps, paypal, ebay or stamps.com sites to print these and include the postage in the stamp or I can use what I have designed pretty quickly using word.  These are not as cheap as separate address labels and receipts printed on plain paper, but you get what you pay for with these.  A professional impression is created and if you recycle packaging materials, the label does cover up previous labels or ink very well.  I like the two part label/receipt option for occasional, so this package of 50 is great for my needs and pocketbook.

text: Just as expected,  the black vinyl letters are positioned on their sheets to maximize space and reduce waste of black vinyl. title: More sturdy than expected and has more purposes than a simple locker structure
text: To my surprise, we are using this Five Star very tall stand that is designed to be used in a school locker since it was retired from the school lockers which are on a hiatus. title: Cinder block wall struggles
text:
I used the blue Loc-tite wall putty (for lack of knowing exactly what to call it) last year to hang posters on my classroom walls. I took everything down in the spring, just before EOCs, because you have to remove or cover anything content-related ;and of course everything I have is somehow related to the content I teach). But nothing fell off the walls last year. Bought new blue stuff and hung posters this year — and within a week, the first pieces began falling. I surveyed colleagues and got a host of answers, from drilling holes for nails to hot glue and more. But this stuff seemed to be the most consistent…and successful (short of drilling holes). So I ordered two rolls — because it was out of stock in all the stores around me (which seemed to corroborate the idea it is good for classroom decor).

I cannot speak to ease of removal — apparently the pieces I was using, which are roughly the length of the end of my thumb, mean it will never come down. 😂 But I can tell you that in the past month, nothing I have hung with this tape has budged, whereas the few remaining things I hung with the blue stuff finally gave up the struggle and fluttered to the floor. (Oddly enough, it never happens during the day where I see it; I always find something facedown on the floor when I unlock the door in the morning. 🤷🏻‍♀️)

It remains to be seen if my posters come down in pieces, are permanently affixed, or if I can somehow remove them safely…but at least they are staying where I put them now.

title: Run out of ink too quickly
text:
I bought a three pack of these pens to use for grading essays. When I started on the most recent batch — 64 students, and most essays were two pages, hand written — I had a pen that was partially used. It ran out before I was halfway through, so I took out a new one. That one just ran out, and I still have five essays to go.

While I like the feel of this pen in my hand, and I like the smoothness with which it moves across the paper, I cannot recommend it because of the startling speed with which it runs out of ink. I have never had a single pen not make it through one stack of essays, much less not be able to do it with one full pen and another partial one. And there have been years when I had closer to 90 students in the course.

title: For the teacher who moves around
text:
I have to “float” between two classrooms and the teacher’s lounge during the day, because we don’t have enough classrooms for every teacher to have their “own.” But when you have supplies you purchased for your classes, they need to go with you. For me, that means games to help my AP Lang students practice argumentation, highlighters for color-coding essays when they do self-evaluation, index cards, post-it notes, handouts for the students, my teaching materials…and whatever else is on the menu for that day. I did not want the large media cart that some of the teachers who move around a lot rely on; I’m fortunate enough to be in “my” room for all but one of my classes, so I move once or twice a day (including to my study carrel in the lounge for my planning period) so someone else can use my room when I’m elsewhere. This cart is small but sturdy (space is important when you have 34 student desks in a classroom and need to maneuver past them), and the wheels even have a locking feature. The bottom of each tier is solid, and that was important to me; I didn’t want the mesh/open-weave style, to have to free paper clips and staples from the holes all the time.. You can hang clip-on cups off the side (a lot of the craft stores sell them) if that is how you organize smaller items, but I favor the pencil bags that zip…so I don’t have any exterior cups at the moment.

I liked it so much I got another one for my office space at the house.

title: Just what I needed for teacher organization
text:
I have been trying to find a way to keep up with the various categories of paper for all my students. I have a rolling briefcase with multiple sections, and the “regular” file folders I have been using do not hold up to either the volume of papers to be graded and returned or to the daily in-and-out of the bag. The beauty of these is multifaceted for me.
1) Number of folders. With six colors and three of each, I have a set of folders for each class (5 classes/2 preps) plus an extra set for the miscellaneous things I need to track. (So I have a “To be graded,” a “To be returned,” and a third folder for keeping up with the handouts for students who were absent so that I’m not digging through other stacks when said student returns and asks for the work they need to make up.)
2) Bright colors…I love color-coding, and I can grab the set of folders for any particular class at a glance.
3) Durable. These folders have had to hold upwards of 90 pages each at times and have been in and out of my bag daily for weeks now, and they show no signs of wear. And my labels (from a label maker) adhere perfectly.

Even if this set were to only last for one school year and then need to be replaced, they are well worth the price in my opinion; I give them quite a work out!

title: Looks good, doesn't hold up

My first day was January 8, and I had five classes (high school). I used this book for attendance and for grades. I liked that the cover was not just a solid color, and I liked that the blocks were slightly larger. And you couldn't beat the cost.
But like most things, you get what you pay for, it seems. I took this out of my rolling briefcase each morning and put it back at the end of the day. If I was grading papers at home in the evening, it came out and was replaced before I went to bed. Within three weeks, I was running into my local office supply store hoping to find one of those generic record books with the solid cover because the cover to this was falling off at the plastic coil, and several of the pages were also beginning to separate from the coil. Before I made the complete transfer of data, I had ended up removing the coil altogether and holding the pages together with a trio of small binder clips down the edge where the coil should have been.

text:
I used this well made, heavy duty lift cylinder to repair my 2001 Steelcase commercial office chair, that I use in the garage. A couple years ago, I tried to repair it with a cheaper cylinder, but it was no match for the heavy piece of American metal, that is the Steelcase. The Office Oasis lift cylinder quickly hoists up my garage chair like nothing.

One odd little bonus is that my lift cylinder came with some thin white gloves, with the "Office Oasis" logo on them. Curious bonus, but a bonus just the same I guess. I did not use the included collars at all in the cylinder replacement process, but they seem well made should you choose to use them.

If you are like me, and don't want to putz with collars and allen wrenches for such a simple task, a large pipe wrench (the bigger the better) and WD40 are your friends when removing your old cylinder from the mechanism bolted to the seat of your chair. There are You-Tube videos which go into further detail. If you spend more than 20 minutes trying to install this thing, and you cuss more than twice, you are doing something wrong. title: Great pencils for little hands
text:
I got these pencils for my kids because the regular pencils they were using were always in need of sharpening or were nowhere to be found. To not delay homework, I bought a package of these and put them in a cup near their homework station. The kids were thrilled when they saw them and now we never have to worry about not having a sharpened pencil or lack of eraser. These pencils works great and the thicker 0.9mm lead works great since it doesn't break and the eraser erases without leaving any marks behind. These are the perfect size for my 7 and 10 year old's hands. We are super happy with these pencils and wouldn't hesitate to purchase them again. Although with this many, I'm hoping they last a while.

Update: 8/31/17
While the pencils are still great, one problem we've had with them is the eraser. After using the eraser for a bit, it gets pushed down and get pierced by the plastic pencil lead holder. We have more than half of these pencils that the erasers are completely unusable because they keep getting pushed down when you try to use them. The pencils still work great but now we have to use a separate eraser when using them. Most pencils have a metal fitting where the eraser fits so as to prevent this issue but these pencils don't have that. I have updated my rating from 5 stars to 3 because of the eraser issue. It's a pain because the kids really need an eraser to work with their pencil when they are doing homework and all of these now have unusable erasers.

The pockets only hold 5 pencils comfortably and since there are 13 pockets, I could only fit 65 pencils in this wrap case.  I tried putting 6 pencils in some of the pouches but they don't lay flat if you do that and it is not as easy to see the colors when are layered upon one another.  Also the little leather thing at the end of the cord immediately fell off when I opened my package and I didn't even notice it until later when my son found it lying on the floor.  This might be a decent pencil wrap case if you have 65 pencils or less but if you have more than that, they will not comfortably fit in here. title: Great for storage
text: I needed a place to store personal items in my dorm room, and to replace another plastic drawer unit that I had for a while and was not cutting it anymore.  I actually needed two, but did not want to purchase two in case they didn't work out.  So I just purchased one and if it met my need, I would get another one.  After I placed the order, lo and behold, someone had left a gently used one, exact brand, model and color, in the "free giveaway" area of the dormitory, this one did not have wheels.  I claimed it, gave it a little cleaning and it was good as new.  It fit perfectly in one of the spots where I was planning to put it and I have it storing all my extra toiletries and personal hygiene items.  With bars of soap and bottles of lotion and shampoo, it can get pretty heavy, and all 3 drawers are full.  It is very sturdy and can handle the weight, I also have a small fan sitting on the top.  Since it worked out perfectly, I am glad I just purchased the one on Amazon, which I will use as a nightstand next to the bed and put a lamp on it and use it to hold my phone and glasses and other items while I am sleeping.  The extra storage drawer space I can use for pretty much anything now, maybe all my tech gadgets and books. title: Useful item
text: This can hold two regular size/thickness ID cards with a paper card in between.  The flap is good for keeping the ID's from falling out in the event the holder gets turned upside down.  The flap doesn't open on its own, it sort of clings to the plastic under it.  I wouldn't use this ID holder if you have pull the ID's in and out a lot (like a CAC with a chip in it).  The sides of the holder would start to tear in that instance.  If you use it for ID's that you just flash or as a proximity key, then it would hold up well with that use.  The flap is also useful if it rains or snows the water wouldn't leach into the holder and get everything inside wet.  The holder is pretty light, it doesn't add any significant weight around your neck if you use it with a lanyard, and it doesn't make noise if it hits against something, unlike the hard plastic ID holders.

title: Exactly what I needed
text: This ID/Badge holder is exactly what I needed.  It is a good quality, heavy duty holder.  The pen loops are very convenient and a better way of holding my pen instead of in a pocket.  I do not use the actual lanyard because I am required to use a lanyard with my company's logo on it, but it is a good quality lanyard that I will definitely use if the occasion comes up.  The sleeve itself can hold multiple IDs and some necessary paperwork folded in a certain way to make it fit. There is also a sleeve in the back that you can put other things that do not need to be on display.  I had one of those "ziplock" plastic ID holders before that didn't last very long, it started tearing after a few weeks of everyday use.  This ID holder seems like it will last way longer than that.

title: Helps for click and ship
text: It works.  It weighs my boxes the way it should so I can Click and Ship with the USPS.  Because the readout is on a cord and not on the actual scale itself you can easily see the readings when there is a large box on the scale.  You can switch between pounds/ounces and kilograms.  It says the max weight is 110 lbs, but I have yet to try it for boxes that heavy.  The surface area of the scale itself is pretty small, so if you have a large box you may have to place a stable, stiff platform on it and zero out the scale before actually weighing the box.

title: Helps save time
text: Used these for USPS "Click and Ship" to ship a lot of boxes over seas.  After weighing the boxes (see my review of Weighmax 2822-50 lbs capacity, Postal Shipping Scale).  I was able to pay for postage online and print up the postage and addressed shipping label on these, with the customs declarations right on the single label, no additional forms or labels needed.  As long as you click that you don't want to print the receipt in the USPS website, you can print out 2 shipping labels per sheet.  The glue on the label is pretty strong, but I like to put some clear shipping tape over the edges and over the address itself in case the box gets wet for whatever reason.  Best thing is that you can arrange to have the USPS pick up the boxes or just leave them at the counter at the post office, no standing in line.  These could also be used to print things other than shipping labels.

title: It did its job
text: I used these to ship perishable food to Afghanistan.  I put the food [frozen prepared meats and sausages (not pork)] in with some gel ice packs.  (See my review of the Polar Tech TP12/MS Ice Brix Viscous Gel Moisture Safe Refrigerant Cold Pack) and it got to their destination still chilled.  Of course this all depends on the reliability of the USPS and the handlers at the military base end, but it took about 9-10 days to get from my home to its destination (first box 9 days, second box 10 days).  The food was still good and we had something different to eat for a few weeks that was better than the usual fare we had.  I put this box into a plain brown box before shipping because I didn't like the markings "RUSH-Perishable" on the outside.  I would have liked to see them sell the same box with no markings on the outside at the time I purchased it.  If they did, I couldn't find it.

title: Great for "Click and Ship"
text: I use it when I "Click and Ship" with the USPS.  I can pay for the accurate postage online because I weigh my packages and boxes at home and print out the postage and pre-printed address labels, and I just leave it in the box at the post office, no need to stand in line.  Or you can have them pick it up.  Well worth the price of a scale, especially during Christmas time when the lines are out the door at the post office.  The top of the scale has a piece that flips open to accommodate larger boxes and it also can measure in either grams or pounds.  When you weigh something it freezes the measurement for a short time so that if its a large box, you have time to move it and write down the weight before it disappears.

They’re also so small that it’s extremely difficult for me to read the menu selections even with my glasses ON! I have had Panasonic phones in the past, and they lasted for almost 5 1/2 years before giving me any problems! I’m looking forward to having a phone system that will work with my iPhone too, and the other features, so I hope the next one will be better for me than this one was.

title: A great buy! Pretty and a lot less expensive than the plain white ‘name’ brands!
text: 150 Very pretty napkins for about $9.00! This is a great deal and too good to pass on! I have always bought the plain white ‘name’ brands, like Bounty or Vanity Fair, etc., in a Walgreens, CVS, or another regular store. They usually cost about $5.00 +/- for a pack of 50 napkins. With these, the price is much less and you also get colorful napkins that are perfect for the kitchen. You would think that the quality would be compromised for being so cheap, but it's not. I have been using the same one now for several days and it's still not ready for the garbage! Granted, I haven't used it to eat a messy dinner, but it works well for my coffee, tea, and other beverages, and protects my white Corian kitchen counters and wood table. Even if you wanted to use these for a sloppy meal, so what? - they are so inexpensive that it's not a shame to throw them out. The pattern is on the 4 sides that show when the napkins are open, and the other side is plain white. These aren't the softest around, but would still be ok to wipe your mouth. The pack of 150 came in 2 plastic-wrapped packs of 75 in each. None of them were damaged or wrinkled, like some others are when you get them off the shelf in a regular store! To me, that says a lot about the care and quality control by the manufacturer. I have some of these in a holder on the kitchen table, which looks much better than the pure white ones (I used to keep those in a cabinet or drawer! I would definitely recommend these to anyone who is looking for these colors. They are even appropriate for a party or other occasions. I am the first person to write a review, even though the little bit they have were all 5*’s. *** Since I buy items that are not familiar to me on Amazon based on the reviews of others, if you find this to be helpful please mark it as such for future reference, thanks!

title: Useful for a variety of things and very low cost without sacrificing quality!
text: First of all this set of tiny notebooks is less expensive (.50 cents each) than many others that are similar sold on Amazon, as well as the ones usually sold in a CVS or Walgreens (that is if they even have this kind, which they normally don’t at the ones by me). The pages of these don’t have the metal spiral that make a paper mess when tearing a page out or get stuck on something else with the wire ‘binding’ or the ‘post its’ that have the sticky backs. The quality of these is actually very good and useful for a number of things that some other reviews mentioned. I bought them for taking on my yearly month-long cruise, using one for each place I visit, not only the various ports but also each city/town that I see on the shore excursions. Until now I had been relying on my camera for the pictures of everywhere I went to (but it didn’t help me to remember some interesting facts as told by our local tour guide. Since my last cruise I found that I had trouble remembering what I saw and did in a lot of ‘similar’ towns, getting mixed up with quite a few of them (i.e. Portofino, Positano, Sorrento, Taormino, as well as a number of others.) This year I am going to pack a bunch of these little notebooks and use each one (like a diary) for each day, as well as every place I visit. The information that is given by our tour guides is something that I can write down too, making it much easier to remember when I return home and download the pictures to my iPad. Having 6 different colors in the set and 4 of each makes it easy to coordinate too, depending on the use of them. I would definitely recommend these - they really are great and have so many uses!

The color of the one I bought is so pretty but it’s not the same color as shown online. This color is a soft blush pink and isn’t neutral enough to go with every color decor. The quality seems to be good and it does easily swivel 360 degrees. Although it’s not real leather it looks as if it is - until you touch it. The design is not overdone but it adds a little extra touch to the appearance. As someone who has a bad case of OCD (I can also be a bit too critical at times) I can honestly say that this is a great buy and it I wouldn’t have the need to put any little felt (or rubber) pads on the bottom to keep it from scratching my furniture. (I do add these to almost everything that I buy that comes in contact with glass, wood, granite, etc.) My only reason for possibly returning this is due to the pinkish/blush color - while it doesn’t look good in any of my rooms that have TVs downstairs I do have this color in my master bedroom upstairs. title: Works well!
text: This was the 2nd one that I’ve tried - the first was a different brand and I couldn’t get any of the plastic cards to open. This pack of 5 plastic card holders wasn’t easy to open but I eventually got them all opened. I doubt that I’ll ever use them all unless they break over time. I wanted a horizontal card holder rather than a vertical one and one that wasn’t covered by any type of vinyl, leather, etc. for one purpose only. I am going to use this for my cruise key card - I have seen a lot of people on the cruises that have something like this around their neck. I am always digging in my purse or tote bag looking for it and at times in a pocket of my pants, shirts, jacket, etc. I’ve even left it in my stateroom and had to find my butler or housekeeper to use theirs to let me in. This is also going to be a lot easier for getting off and back on the ship - it always gets scanned when doing so. My purpose might not be the same as someone else but I would definitely recommend this if anyone has a need for a clear card holder and lanyard that is thin and comfortable to use! text:
This perfectly fits my Uplift 30x60 desk.
I got a great deal for a used Uplift reclaimed-wood standing-desk for $350 with all the bells and whistles/accessories added of a $1400 brand new Uplift desk.
Yet I did not think of protecting this great desk deal. I spilled hot tea on it one night, quickly cleaned it up over a minute, yet didnt realize some tea prob got through the cracks in the panels of wood and the next night realized the wood had expanded/warped upwards so much in those areas.
I bought this to protect against future tea spills. and it looks like it will do the job.
One side is very clear (but feels stickier, so I assume this should be the bottom), and one side is more patterned/blurry (feels very plasticy so easier to slide things like cups, etc on your desk, so i assume this should be the top).
The reclaimed wood pattern is a tiny bit muffled/blurred but still looks great (the muffled side's pattern is kinda nice too since you don't have to worry about keeping it scratch-free/spotless). Note: there was a small 'streak' on the clear side of the desk like a few other reviewers mentioned. Didnt bother me since the clear side is going to be hidden under the muffled side if you choose to make the muffled side the top.
I wonder if its always meant to be placed that way.

Quick tip for a tea spilling incident like mine: I was able to flatten the raised/warped portions of the panels of wood where the tea spilled by placing ten 10 lb weights on top of it in varying locations of the panels over 4 days and finally got the desk where its mostly flat/even across the surface again. (so basically 100lbs total focused on one area, just need a few sheets of paper placed under the weights so the weights don't dent the wood at the hard edges of the weights).

And every year, at review time, my husband comes to me and asks me: "what should I write?". And every year it goes like this:

Wife: Did you write down this?
Husband: Uh, no, I forgot about that.
Wife: What about that? You did that, right?
Husband: Oh yeah, I'll put that in.
Wife: You could mention that other thing.

text:
Wanted some time to pass before I did my review so could really test it out.

Decided to get rid of my copper wire landline after decades, as barely used it, cost too much to justify keeping it, but didn’t want to lose the ph#, & figured good to have a backup. The set up online was easy, I plugged my old Panasonic phone into it, & immediately opted out of Premier, as I don’t need the extra features. I have Ooma’s VM set to the max (59) seconds so my other phone picks up 1st & it goes to that answer machine, where I can hear who is calling, since that feature is only with Premier otherwise. I didn’t pay for caller ID with my old phone company, but now have it with Ooma basic (& love it), plus other phone features that I couldn’t use before.

The only slight negative I experienced is that when I requested the porting, my order was confirmed for $39.99 with zero fees/taxes, but after porting, suddenly there was almost $7 added for local & federal fees/taxes & I only knew about it when I checked my credit card bill. I had done screen shots of my original order that said zero taxes etc, & I called them to let them know they didn’t have prior disclosure/authorization to charge this, & they said would credit the extra charges back to my card, which they did in a couple of days. I had to call for 1 other minor thing also, & the customer service has been great both times.

I have no regrets at all switching, & I’m very happy with my decision to use Ooma. In fact wish I’d done it a long time ago!

title: Not a serious but not terrible yet
text:
Caveat: I've just bought it.

Pro: affordable, does what it says it will, especially as the A.D.F. works correctly.
Con: it feels flimsy, toy-like, and the paper feed sticks out the front instead of being clothed decently in a cassette. This last actually matters because duct, pet hair, and dusty pet hair can easily get into the paper-path and screw-up not only the printed copy but worse, the print-head. The first matters because it feels like it will last two years of infrequent use at best. Also: the multiple colours in one cartridge mean that you will buy cartridges sooner, that is when you run out of any of the three colours…but all printer ink is a rip-off anyway, though this is particularly bad. Also: I find step-by-step, manyal, set-up easier than using an application.

Summary: if you print infrequently and have limited funds, fine; avoid if you have to print every day or a lot every month or so: spend $100 or $150 more and get a good printer.

title: Don't waste your money
text:
Before anyone buys this printer they need to know what they are getting into. This is the most unreliable printer-scanner-copier I have ever owned. After 4 months of light use one day it just stopped working. Would not even shut off, was giving an error message, claimed something was stuck inside though I had not recently used it to print.
I had to cancel 2 evenings of plans to sit on the phone with HP. The first night I was given a heck of a run around, including things like telling me to replace the firmware even though it was the most up-to-date available. I live in a small apartment and was expected to dig the printer out and find another place to set it. It was just ridiculous. And the evening ended with the woman stating that the error code said it was a hardware problem. Really, you waste my time like that when what I have told you already tells you that the problem is with the hardware. The woman can't help me, I have to call back tomorrow night to a different number (but no further instructions).
So the second night I call the second number only to be expected to be able to guess who I am to speak to when I encounter a computer. I end up on the phone with someone who can't help me who finally forwards me to the correct person. In the end I am informed that I have to give them a credit card number in order to get a replacement printer. I am told that they will not charge anything to it, but they actually did charge money to it right then and there. So I am dealing with a liar.
What I receive 4 days later is a used printer that they think will work, and I have to get the old printer back to them. The used printer I now have squeaks and it doesn't work right. I never had these problems with my previous printer. The printer can't seem to stay connected to the router. Since I use one printer for 2 computers I don't want to hardwire the printer to a computer.
The scanner will just suddenly run at times even though I have not hit the "start scan" which means I end up with extra messed up pages in my document. The scan program will suddenly stop working which means the document stops. If you need to step away from the printer to get something from across the room that you wanted to include in the scanned document, forget it. The printer will shut down the document before you get back. If you don't own Adobe Acrobat you won't be able to repair the messed up files it creates.
I have to turn off the printer, turn off the computer, wait for this and mess with that. This machine just wastes your time too much. Now I have to set aside another couple of evenings to try to deal with them again concerning the new piece of garbage they sent me. (since when do you replace a problem piece of hardware with someone else's used piece of hardware that was returned because of a problem??? a new printer would be much more appropriate)
HP is a big name, but they certainly are not a good company, at least not any longer. It was obvious that they were outsourcing the phone calls out of the country since no one I spoke to spoke English as their first language.

title: From 35 Spam calls/day to only 4—in just 10 days!!
text:
SANITY SAVING!! We had suddenly, on 10/5/21, started getting TONS of spam calls on our land-line (which I still love to use since it’s so much clearer to hear from than my iPhone 12)…all with NO message left & most #’s were NOT repeated so I didn’t want to waste any more of my precious 250 allotment of “Blocked Calls” my Panasonic phone allows, on such. I continued to dutifully report each of these #’s to the government’s DoNotCall List…until I couldn’t keep up as the phone was Spam Ringing 35 times/day!! So I ordered this easy-to-use gadget & turned OFF my ringer plus all the voice ID announcements. AND changed the greeting to say that we can no longer hear the ringer & if the caller chooses to not leave a LEGITIMATE message—that their number WILL be blocked AND reported as SPAM.
Each night since it was installed, I have continued to write down all the spam info from my phone’s ID list, then I quickly scroll through this gadgets’ list to compare #’s so I can see where it’s being blocked from…as this gadgets’ innate blocked program does NOT show those #’s on it’s ID list. I happily tap the BLOCK BUTTON when I see a fresh spammer.
Sooo for a wee bit of consistent work for only 10 days & 87 of my hits on The Button…now only 4 Spam calls a day are getting through! I might soon be able to turn back on the ringer & ID announcement!! Sure hope Panasonic stays on top of this growing nightmare and keeps building better blocking programs for these inconsiderate creeps to add on to this SOON!! Thank you for our serenity once again!

title: Good competitive ink tank printer
text:
This printer is quite amazing. I have this and the competitors ecotank model and I can safely say they are both good choices and depending on what you need this printer might be a perfect match for you.

Let us start with the price. This isn’t a cheap printer by any means. At this price point you are open to a fair number of competitors for inkjets and even some low-cost laser printers. It does lack a few features seen in some competitors which might be a deal breaker. An auto document feeder for the scanner being the main feature I would have liked to see.

This has a lot more maintainability in mind components though and that’s nice to see. The purge ink tank is easily replaceable along with the print head. I know most people won’t spend the money on a new ink head, but the maintenance cartridge is nice to have since this style of printer can purge a fair bit of ink. Be prepared to set aside a little more space for this printer though. It has the ability to bring in documents from the back and that combined with its overall footprint makes it a little bulky when compared to my ET-3850.

I do think the print quality isn’t as good as some of my past cartridge-based Canon printers. Definitely not a photo quality machine, but then again it doesn’t really claim to be. I would say it’s on par if not slightly bet than my ET printer though. I am interested to see how it deals with longer periods of inactivity. The issue of print heads getting clogged because of dried up ink is something I have faced on all my past ink jets so let's see if this one manages better.

Overall, I’d say it is a good high-volume printer and if you don’t scan a lot of large documents then this will be perfect for you. I know this model is new but see if you can get this on sale as its competitors often are. If size is a constraint, then some of the competitors are a little smaller footprint, but you really can’t go wrong with this for a home office or small business.

title: Life Coach Yourself!
text:
Do you like to make lists?

Did you forget what you ate for breakfast yesterday?

Do you like purple planners?

If you answered 'yes!' to all of these questions then you should get this planner!

I have a love and obsession relationship with planners. When I die, one of my friends and family will find that I had written in, 'dying' on one of the days in a planner.

This planner is pretty nice. It has spots for a lot of lists and aspirational planning ahead. It has a full page of US holidays to keep aware of and spots for contact information.

Each of the monthly spreads is entirely blank, so if you go awol from your planner for a month or two (it happens, right?) you can pick up without having a huge amount of wasted pages.

There is one built in bookmark, it is thin and practically colorless, why colorless?

there is no pocket for a pencil or pen, which I find myself absurdly annoyed with.

All in all, this is an okay planner.

I think this might be better than my old sharpener that had the pencil sharpening opening on the side so that sort of mimicked the old style that I remembered being secured to the countertop at my old Elementary school.

This is a small reservoir for pencil shavings, so you do have to empty it frequently, but it is very simple to do and I haven't had to reach a qtip inside to sweep out any clumps.

The sound is just as loud and obnoxious as you remember, but that is the downside to using an electric or battery powered sharpener, they just are so piercing.
