title: A Fun Filled Family Project, or a Struggle for Domination?
text:
Worked great until it didn't. My Xyron came new in the box with no User's Guide, so I was forced to turn to the good folks on YouTube to learn my way around what is probably the easiest-to-use paper crafting product ever developed.
What has come to be referred to in hushed tones at our house, "The Great Adhesive Rebellion," is the night we tried to troubleshoot a defective replacement cartridge. Those things are brutal and unforgiving. Marketed as "a simple, one-step, drop-in process," that simple self-contained cartridge goes rogue, adhering to everything within a thirty foot radius except the targeted item nestled in the input tray. The handle stops turning. Sticker paper clings to the machine's interior. The mysterious roll of cellophane shivers and quivers and tries to wrap itself around everything at once. It's like some passive-aggressive squid wandered into our living room and engaged us in some fairly innocuous, though highly complex duel to the death. No matter what we youtube'd or researched or attempted, the maliciously wound cartridge blocked our every effort to restore function to my Xyron. As he dragged himself away from our project to scrub up in a tubful of fingernail polish remover (even the whorls of his fingerprints were cemented together), he proclaimed over his shoulder: "Waste. Of. Money." He does not appreciate the challenges posed by paper crafting, apparently.

title: Perfect for time management and staying in check
text:
I struggle with time management, a plan to work on a task for 1 hour turns to 2 or 3, and before I know it the day is over and I've only completed half the tasks I've planned for the day.
The quality of the planner itself is nice. The cover is a faux leather cover is nice, and doesn't have that fake leather smell which is great. The beginning has a vision chart for things like health, business, family, friends, etc., vision board, mind map, yearly goals, and 3 month goals (which pops up 4 times total through the length of the planner, so that you can keep up with them). Each month starts with a monthly spread, followed by 5 weekly spreads, ending with a monthly review spread for reflection.
I love this layout. It's well designed, and flows. I go through a lot of planners, because I wind up not liking the setup. But this one is perfect. Only thing I would change is the tone of the paper to be ivory, but that's personal preference. I'm sure it won't bother some. The paper itself is thick and the text is a subtle but dark grey color. I love that, because if it was black text, it would have been jarring against the stark white paper. I haven't had any show through, or bleed through with the pentel gel pen I use for planning. I haven't used any other pens in it though, so I can't speak to it being bleed through safe.

Negative?: The only thing I don't really like, but won't keep me from using it- is that the paper is a jarring white. I'll get used to it though.

Verdict: Overall, this planner is perfect for keeping myself in check, at a great price for its quality. The weekly spread layout with time slots are large enough to write in a little blurb on what I need to do during that period. I write in what I should do at the start of the day, and I keep the planner open to make sure I stay on track, writing a check or placing a sticker down next to it if/when I stuck to my task. I hope I can stick with this. If I do fall off planning, it's great that this planner is undated! I can pick it right back up and start again.

title: Great to use as a business planner
text:

I was originally planning on using this for my personal use, but after looking through it, I knew it would be perfect to use for business planning.
The planner itself is okay quality. In regards to quality, the cover is the best out of everything for this planner. It feels like a coated cloth material.

Negatives:
Mine arrived with dents in the first 40 pages of it, and some of the corners weren't cut all the way, so I needed to separate them myself. The paper reminds me of what nice quality coloring book paper feels like. Smells like construction paper from when I was a kid.
I'm not used to the stark white paper. I much prefer ivory paper, and I didn't think that the white would be so jarring. I'm going to get used to it, I have to- because I really like the layout of this planner.
It does indeed lay flat, and I love that it has 3 ribbon bookmarks to mark the most important parts of the planner.
Overall, I still am happy I got this because it's already starting to get myself more organized in my business. I took away a star because quality control could be better, with the corners of some of the sheets not having been cut through all the way. For the price, quality control should be much better.

If you don't have felt or foam on hand, I would suggest not pressing the extender tray directly up against the edge of your desk if you don't want any scratches, dents, or nicks on the edge of your desk.
Despite that, I still really like this desk extender. It folds down and out of the way, which is great for my small office area. The surface is smooth and has a cool sleek design.

There is a little ghosting when I use my micron pens, but it's faint and I don't draw on the backside of my pages anyway (also want to note that my plain moleskins have higher ghosting). I only use pencils and microns for my sketching, so I can't say how this paper does with other mediums.
Since the notebooks are blank, they're versatile. I'm using one of them as my bullet journal.
I'm glad I got these, the price is great for quality sketchbooks.

title: Strong magnets for book clips and fridge magnets
text:
I'm using them for book clips and fridge magnets. They are pretty strong, with no problem at all sticking/unsticking from the fridge, and they hold a good amount of pages between two magnets.
They arrive neatly in a resealable plastic bag, with 4 sheets. These are a great value overall, I'm very happy with this, and will definitely repurchase when I run out!

title: Not just for business cards
text:
These came packaged nice, each stand wrapped in plastic to avoid any scratches, and none of them had any.
It's a very stable stand, perfect for my business cards. It's good for displaying other things too, I'm using my other stands to hold smaller stickers that I have.

title: High quality, durable mat
text:
This office chair mat has a good weight to it, with a nice texture. I was curious about what the texture would be like since the listing photos are just computer generated images, not actual photos. I've added photos to show what the texture is like to help with anyone whose wondering about it.
It rolled out flat as soon as I laid it down on my floor, and it has solved my problem I've been having with my chair getting caught on my tiled floors.
The quality of the mat is really nice, it's thick, and the texture is like a basketweave that's smooth with just a little bit of tooth. Doesn't feel weird under my toes.
I've had it for a while now, and it's stood up to my pups rolling and lying on it by my feet while I work for 15 hours some days. It's held up to long days, and it still looks like new. It vacuums extremely well. I much prefer this type of mat over the felted mats I've been seeing.

title: Not a single issue with printing
text:
I'm always on the lookout for a cheap alternative to the branded labels for my 4xl. I got this one for the low price and because it was a 4 pack.
I'm currently in the middle of my last roll, and can happily say that I haven't had a single issue with printing on these rolls. No skipping, no problems where it would start printing in the middle of the label, and then onto the next one, no issues with not being able to feed the roll in and registering.
I mean, I've had these issues with the branded ones!
So, I can say that I'm a very happy customer, and will be coming back to purchase more once my roll is close to the end.

title: Great for organizing with durability that paper folders don't have
text:
I got these to organize clippings and documents for work. The transparent folders are perfect, so it's easy to spot what I'm looking for when I'm in a rush. I've been using them quite a bit after switching them into them from my old paper manila folders. I haven't experienced any rips at the seam, and I haven't bent any of them accidentally even with being rough with them.
These plastic folders are transparent and shiny. I was expecting them to have a frosted matte look to them after viewing the listing photos, but I was wrong. Most of them arrived with scratches on them, and that would have been a deal breaker for me had I needed these for presentation purposes, but I don't. For the low price these are offered at for 50 pieces, I think this is absolutely worth it for keeping myself organized and on top of things.

title: Finally!  Support!
text:
I've been going through so many different support cushions to ease the pain from sciatica, and I finally found it with this!
It arrived vacuum sealed in a box with a protective sticker on it.
As soon as I took it out of the vacuum sealed bag, it expanded almost completely. I let it sit for a few minutes, and it was ready to go. When I sat down on it, I was blown away buy how dense it is. I was half expecting for the pillow to deflate a little like all the other cushions I've tested out, but this kept its form. I immediately felt relief in my bum, and was able to sit for a few hours in my chair without feeling the typical pain I normally get from sitting for long hours at my desk.
The removable washable cover has a non slip bottom, so it doesn't move around on my chair, and the included straps that are also removable, keep it from falling off my chair too. Because of the supportive cushion, it raises me up a few inches which I appreciate since I'm quite short. The photo of the cushion on my chair is what it looks like after being used for a month. The other photos are what it looked like straight out of the box.
I sit straighter, and my bum and back don't hurt as much now, so basically this little cushion has made my life better. This has got to be one of the best purchases I've made this year.

title: Good for organizing documents
text:
I got these to organize documents, manuals, and whatnot around the house. The plastic is nice and durable, and have a frosted look to them. They snap open and shut without any problems. I'm storing them all in a box, so I can't say if they actually fit in a binder, but the included rings are helpful in keeping them all together.
I like the variety of colors, It made organizing even more easier by categorizing by color. The included labels in the front pockets of each envelope are very helpful in marking what's what.
These have made getting my things organized very easy!

title: Great paper quality, little to no bleed thru
text:
I like the larger size of this planner, so I don’t feel like I’m cramming all my words into each time slot.
The quality of the planner itself is really nice, the cover is a soft and smooth material, and the pages are nice with little to no bleed through, not too thin, not too thick.
It offers two book marks, so I am using one to mark my weekly, and the other where the note pages are in the back. The pocket in the back is a nice touch that I see in many notebooks, so I appreciate it.
At the end of the day, I enjoy the size and price. Would buy it in a heart beat if I ever lost it.

title: Good organizer. Poor finishing.
text:
Bummed mine came chipped in a few places on the top and side piece where the vertical organizing part is. I originally was planning on putting this on my desk, but I would be able to see the damages, so I found a spot to put this on my shelf to hide both the spots that arrived damaged, so all is good- but still worth mentioning.
It arrived flat packed, so you have to put it together. I don't mind that, and it comes with everything you need to put it together. Once all the pieces are screwed together, it's very sturdy and has quite a good weight to it.
The clearance on each shelf is 2 7/16 inches in height, and 8 5/8 inches in width. So, you can't fit anything larger in width than your standard 8.5x11 letter size paper. On the bottom shelf of mine, you can see how legal size papers fit with some of it hanging off the front.
I'm using this to organize some of the different paper types that I use. It's good for organizing. At the end of the day, it does what it's supposed to do. Would I repurchase this if I ever need to? No. the paint is bad on this, doesn't reach the edges, as shown. I had already put everything together when I noticed the poor painting, and it wasn't worth taking apart to return.

title: Great for organizing my paperwork. Not waterproof.
text:
I’m using these to store documents and other things like photos and receipts. I started using them right away, and all of the zippers work fine.
I like the frosted look of them, they look nice have a soft look to them.
One of the pouches arrived with a crack in the center about 1/2 in below the zip edge. I’m not really bothered by it, but I wanted to mention it in case that kind of thing would bother someone.

These pouches aren’t really waterproof, since there are little openings at each end of the zip closure. But they still are great for keeping dust and your paperwork or whatever you want to put in there organized.

title: Great paper organizer
text:
I got this to replace an old cardboard organizer I had that was falling apart. It came packaged neat with instructions, and was very easy to put together.
Once everything is out together, it’s very sturdy. I’m not worried that it’ll fall apart with use, and it can hold a lot of paper. It’s very pretty, not your standard black mesh organizer. It’s muted sage green color and cut out design compliments the aesthetic of my office, I love it.

title: Perfect for small spaces!
text:
I was looking for a storage shelf for my bathroom in a very slim area between the toilet and the wall, and this fit the bill. It fit perfectly in the spot I was intending it for.
It arrived packaged well and smart. All of the parts were within the cart bin. There are instructions, but they’re not in English- BUT, they are visual instructions, so you don’t technically need the text. You could always use google translate for it if you really need it. But, if you’re a handy person, you don’t need the instructions.
The actually shelf bins aren’t very sturdy and the sides can be bent with one finger. This doesn’t bother me, as I’m using it to hold toilet papers, etc. the plastic does bounce back after it’s been bent. I don’t know how well this will fair holding plates and such, as shown in the listing photos.
Overall, I’m happy with it. The shelf works where I need it, and the cut outs design on the shelves are really cute and make it look airy.

title: Great thick cushions for my short arms!
text:
I’m quite a short person, so I never found armrests in office chairs comfortable bc I’d have to lean down a bit to get my elbows to sit on them.
Now, with these, they sit perfectly! No more hunching down to get some arm relief.
The way the arm rest of my office chair are made it a little difficult for these to stay still; so I crisscrossed the Velcro straps as shown, and now they’re nice an tight on there. One of the cushion cover tops is a little warped looking, but as of writing this now, it smoothed out from use.
I really like them, they’re soft and cushiony, and they are thick- AND you can wash the covers! Love love.

title: Everything's together now
text:
This was very helpful for me, particularly since it arrived while I was in the middle of a move. I was able to get all of my important documents and valuables together and organized in this box.
It's made very well, and the outer fabric has a nice feel to it. I feel better now, knowing that all of my important things are in one place- and that place is water and fireproof. The lock is a nice touch, although it is a portable box, and made of fabric that could easily be cut with a knife to get into. But, I wasn't looking for a safe, so that doesn't bother me. I just needed something that I could tuck away out of sight for all of my important things, and this does that. If anything were to happen to the house (knock on wood), I can quickly grab this and run out.
This is definitely worth the money, and I'm glad I got it.

Using on my stone tile flooring. Does what it should and stays put. I like that it’s thin and smooth, so my chair wheels don’t sink in and rolls smoothly over the surface. Before the mat, the wheels of my chair kept getting caught in the grout of my flooring.
I’m still moving furniture around, so I didn’t peel off the clear backing, although you can reposition it. I just didn’t want to go through the hassle of having to clean my floor AND the back of the mat again. But, regardless of the fact that the backing isn’t off yet, it doesn’t move around on the floor when I’m rolling around on my office chair.
Overall, good buy and great price.

title: My go-to daily carry pen
text:
I love this pen. I have had it for about 4 years at this point. It is a frequent go-to pen in my work bag and one of the few ball point pens that I've ever bought refills for.

What I love about this pen:
-The finish is silky smooth (though mine has acquired a small amount of wear around the rim of the tip which is hardly noticeable at first glance)
-The weight is more substantial and fairly balanced.
-The knock is smooth and quiet. It is also spring loaded, so it doesn't flop around when the pen tip is extended.
-The ink is smooth. I would compare the ink in this pen to the Bic Atlantis (but this has a nicer body) for smoothness of flow. The ink in this pen is slightly more black and almost has a gel quality, but quickly dries.
-I like the .7 refills, but there are additional larger and smaller size options that fit this pen.

The only thing I don't love about this pen is the plastic jewel. It isn't something I HATE, or something that would be worth breaking the clip over. After some time, the sharp angles wear down and it becomes less prominent. It isn't really a big deal.

I would 100% recommend this pen to anyone looking for a good daily carry pen. Plus it looks and feels nicer, I find that people are less likely to swipe it (since it is clearly a pen that the owner would miss).

These pens are great and Amazon's price is awesome (I bought them at a specialty store for almost twice the price). The colors are vibrant and perfect to expectation which is nice. The colors are easily differentiated on paper despite the fine tip.

So far, the only paper I have found that these pens that don't work great on is midori paper for some reason.

title: Great pens, but can cause some hand fatigue.
text:
I love these pen/markers! I have been doing a lot of coloring in my Johanna Basford coloring books and these have been great for getting into tiny details! They are awesome pens. The ink is vivid, consistent, and the pens won't dry out if left uncapped for a while!

The only thing I can complain about with these markers is that there is a fair ridge where the cap meets the body that is uncomfortable when coloring for a long period of time. Moving back makes it hard to have as much control of the pen and further forward is really narrow. I do find that I have fatigue after hours of working with these pens and my middle finger hurts from where the ridge digs in. Other than that, these pens are awesome!

title: Great journal!
text:
This notebook is great. I find the new notebook chemical smell that Midoris tend to have is less chemically than the brown covers. I love the simplicity of this notebook/journal system and that I will be able to use this thing for years to come. I think it is a great investment for anyone who wants a long term, customizable, rugged (yet classic), looking notebook, journal, or planner!

If I could change one thing about this notebook, I would make it slightly taller so I could use a lot of other brands of small notebooks. That being said, scout books do fit and come in packs of three.

title: A beautiful, clean, and classic pen!  Oh and it writes great!
text:
I love, love, love this pen. It is beautifully designed. It looks so clean and classic! You can't beat this pen for it's looks.

It gets better. This pen writes super smoothly! It holds a ml of ink, so you can write for a nice long time. I love the flow of ink from this nib. I haven't found an ink that doesn't work great! I find this fine nib to be only very slightly finer than the Lamy Safari/Vista medium nibs. I am still super thrilled with this pen. There isn't one thing I don't like about it! I expect to love this pen for years to come!

title: Better than cartridges and reliable
text: I got these for my Lami Al-Star and Vistas.  These are great.  They take up ink with no issue.  The only things I wish is that they had a bigger capacity and came with a black end.  There are black ended converters, but the fit of those is reported to be a little looser in the pens I have (and they do not include the alignment tabs that these have).  The capacity isn't too big of an issue.  A fill of ink still lasts me a good week with my daily note taking habit.  Plus, the smaller capacity gives me a chance to clean out pens more frequently and try other inks.  And they are definitely a better option than cartridges if you ask me!

So far, I’m not finding any issues. I’m going to keep going with my project and if I find any of this changes, I’ll update the post.
If these cartridges continue to work this well, I will no longer be spending $100 on a set of ink cartridges for this printer!

text:
Okay, I should have admittedly looked at the picture better before buying these for my young child. 🤦🏻‍♀️

Pros:
💕 Prismacolor is a high quality colored pencil and language barriers do not change that fact.
💕 $10 for 24 pencils of this brand is a good deal.
💕 They arrived quickly.
💕 The toucan on the box is Kawaii.

Cons:
👎🏻 I bought these for my young child’s art class. She does not speak Spanish and the pencils only state the color names in Spanish. Unlike say, Crayola who puts both English and Spanish on most crayons. She is already going to be learning French and ASL so I wasn’t planning to teach her Spanish ATM.
👎🏻 I was not warned in the discription that these pencils have NO English on the packaging or on the pencils.
👎🏻The package is trash and not something they can be stored in for long -like the metal case typically found with Prismacolor (to be fair I assume this is a major reason they were cheaper.)

👩🏻‍🦱 Overall: I am left feeling pretty angry about the lack of English on the pencils. I really wish they had BOTH languages. If this were the case I would be accepting with no other English on the box (even though there was no warning in the description.)
However, since I do not know what the colors are called without Googling (and there are 3 brown shades for example so the names are helpful) I find the price to not be as great as I had originally thought. My time is vauluable and Googling the translation for each of the 24 penscils and then making English labels AND labeling them will take a bit of time.

⭐️If they were say $4.99 and not $9.99 (and they warned me in advance I’d need to translate for my child), I’d be willing to buy again.

⭐️At the set price of $9.99 with no explanation- I would opt to find a better seller and even pay MORE for an honest discription of what I’m getting.

🤓Just a note, I order things for my kids from 🇫🇷 France, Japan 🇯🇵, and Germany 🇩🇪 and have never had a product not contain information in more than one language. 🙄

text:
I'm not going to lie, we have to replace this printer every 15 months or so after it has printed nearly a half million sheets of paper. I also use an HP laser printer at home and according to the reviews, it has about the same lifespan, at a much higher price. Thank goodness my home office needs aren't as demanding and in all honesty, I think the two manufacturers are about the same in performance, longevity and print quality and speed. I like the HP software somewhat better, but I don't think it is worth the extra $100+ for a printer of equal quality.

Toner Lock Bypass:
Open the toner access door on your printer.
• Press the Secure and Cancel buttons at the same time.
• Use the arrow buttons to select the correct toner yield of the toner you are using
TNR-STR = Starter cartridge
TNR-STD = TN-820 standard yield
TNR-HC = TN-850 high yield
TNR-S.HC = TN-880 super high yield

It's a fast printing workhorse at a budget-friendly price.

I had a Travelmate cushion since 2017. Still helped, but wanted to replace it for more cushion.

Found out it had CHANGED. The new one wasn't as good on first day as old one from almost five years ago.

Based on reviews, decided on this Kolbs cushion.

Let's start with CONS first:

Packaging -
I KNOW many said theirs was NOT folded in HALF. MINE WAS. And it was folded at the factory, because all the info was inside the plastic it was in. THIS does NOT help the memory foam in the middle.

Comfort -
Feels thick, but within minutes, I was feeling the computer chair underneath. I put my OLD Travelmate back on, and it was more comfortable.

Price - for price expected it to have more cushion where I needed it and not to kind of deflate once I sat on it for five minutes.

PROS:

Thickness - It does feel thick. Once I sit on it, more on the SIDES than where I want and need the cushioning, but is thick.

Material - fabric is nice, soft.

Quality - Seems well-made

And again re comfort, other reviews have mentioned just wish was more comfortable or supportive.

BOTTOMLINE: MAYBE if you're one of the lucky ones that gets it NOT folded in half, that might make a difference. I am not a big woman and this should be more comfortable than it is.

title: EDIT:  I ordered this in 2017 and again in Feb 2022 - WHAT YOU SHOULD KNOW
text:
EDIT: I ordered one of these in 2017. I think it was on sale, I got it for exactly $7 less, or it could just have gone up in price.

PROS AND CONS between the FIRST one and the one I JUST got this week.

PROS re FIRST ONE:

It was really great. Made a big difference and I have bad discs in my back.

It came in a box, NOT ROLLED up like a roll of paper towels and was good to go out of the box.

Foam was perfectly balanced and cover fit really well.

CONS:

Well, not sure I can really call this a con re the first one, after over four and a half years, it wasn't as thick. Still offered some comfort, but wanted to get another EXACTLY like it.

NOW for the one I JUST got.

PROS:

THICKER (AFTER letting it sit and fluff for two and a half days) AND that's where pros end.

CONS:

PACKAGING - This should NOT be rolled up and expected to expand evenly. Even after two and a half days of just letting it sit, I could run my hand over it and feel rippling. It did NOT expand evenly. Cover sagged a bit in places.

COMFORT - IF you had never had the one I had first, you might find this comfortable. Within minutes, not even hours, of sitting on this, I feel it's thicker in some places than others. Right side expanded more than the left. Yeah, not ideal.

I'm not that heavy, so I can't imagine someone very large finding this super comfy for long.

BOTTOMLINE: IF you get one that is NOT ROLLED UP tight, if you get it good to go, you will likely like it more OR maybe some came from a different factory. ALL I know is for seven dollars less, the one I got in 2017 was more comfy up until I got this one in Feb 2022, than this new one is NOW.

CAVEAT EMPTOR.
I DID read a LOT of the reviews, both positive and negative, to see what I might expect.

I didn't want a cushion with grooves in it, either too soft that would flatten fast or too hard. I am in my sixties and just wanted more cushion especially for my hip and backs of my legs (I put my feet up on an ottoman).

Got the cushion yesterday, unwrapped, and yes, did notice an odor, but not surprising, reviews had prepared me.

I couldn't hang it outside, so put on a hanger with clips by it's tags and hung in a room I don't use much. This morning, most of the odor seemed gone and decided to try it out. And oh, it didn't have creases and did seem to have expanded well.

I have on a few layers of clothing between me and the cushion. I noted a few people mentioning the mesh fabric not the most comfy.

PROS:
FITS my armless computer chair perfectly and cushions the backs of my legs near my knees, which I wanted. SO GLAD I GOT THIS LARGE size!

VERY COMFORTABLE - granted, I have only been sitting on it a couple hours (and I get up and down, so usually no more than an hour goes by before I am up doing something), but it is JUST what I wanted - MORE CUSHION for my bones and legs!

DOESN'T SLIDE - I do have it on a nice fabric computer chair, not a slick chair, but I just tried moving back and forth and the cushion stays put.

ABILITY TO EASILY CARRY AROUND - I got for this chair, but good to know I can move it to another easily.

CONS:
THE COVER AND TAKING IT OFF - It doesn't seem easy to just take off and clean. I have thought of taking a piece of fabric and adding a bit of velcro on the ends to just attach to the sides of the cushion, so I could easily just wash that. It might make it more comfortable if I were wearing shorts to cushion against the mesh cover.

THAT'S IT FOR NOW. I will post again after I have used this for about a month, whether I still notice the positives or any negatives.

GLAD I GOT IT and at the price I paid.

title: Easy to Install, Quick Speed, Great Quality Touch Screen Printing!
text:
LOVE IT! In the few years sine I bought my Canon Wireless Printer, technology has come a long way. Some of the features you wish you had the most are now integrated and easy. For example, I love printing from my iPhone! One touch and I can print a 4x6 photo right from my phone. Or I can print a document bigger with a couple of clicks from my phone. I love the touch screen--so easy to use. And it prints FAST! Several times faster than my old printer without sacrificing quality at all. I also love that the print cartridges are only 2: black and color. (The Canon had 5!). It does make me wonder if I'll have to throw the whole color cartridge away even if all the colors inside aren't empty, but I guess that's what you get for the ease of one color cartridge replacement.

One thing I don't love is that it seems to take you through a few more screens to get to frequently used things like enlarging an image. And sometimes I'm not sure if I've chosen it or not as it doesn't return to the home screen after selecting it. But it's a small thing and I'm sure I'll learn to adjust to it in time. Overall, this printer is so much easier to use than my Canon, I really enjoy finding excuses to print stuff!

title: This is a great little planner, very useful
text:
I wanted a planner that was bound (I found out that spiral bound planners are not necessarily the best choice (at least for me as I take it out of and put it back into a purse or pocket).
What do I like about my new planner?
--As I open it up, there are calendars for 2019, 2020, AND 2021! Nice!
--This next point may or may not fit your needs: there is a two page calendar for the month or a month-at-a-view at the beginning of the month entries, where main points can be entered into boxes. After this month-at-a-view, the calendar is presented basically in a week-at-a-view format, with two small monthly calendars for the current month and the subsequent month included.
--The paper is smooth and of a high quality, nice to write on, and is similar to quality paper in more expensive note pads--this was a real treat! Who knew that it would have great writing paper?
--After the end of the year, there are 14 pages for "NOTES," a very welcome supplement.
--Two narrow color coordinated ribbons facilitate keeping track of the current date or where important information is located. The ribbons appear to be securely glued into the spine of the planner. Having two ribbons instead of the normal one ribbon is a nice idea--thank you!
--There is a sufficient room to write in the day's appointments, addresses, or additional details. If I need to add more information than fits into the day's allotted area, I add a post-it to the calendar.

There are two small areas where I would find a change helpful:
--I would prefer that front and back were the same color, or at least that the back was not black; I find it difficult to locate black items in a--how should I say this, sometimes purses. or briefcases or backpacks resemble a black hole or vortex, where the contents are invisible and basically disappear. The colored (turquoise) side is very pretty and is in a nice light color, and is easy to locate. However, just turn the planner over, and whoops--it vanished down the black hole/vortex in my bag. Joking aside, it is much easier to spot the brightly colored side than the black side. I wish both the front and back were of the same color.
--The other little challenge concerns the elastic that you use to hold it closed. Well, I started using my new planner on April1 (not a joke), and a few days ago (it is still April) the elastic band slipped out of one of the holes, and there was no way to stick it back in the hole so it could hold my planner closed. So it is starting to be difficult and frustrating to keep it closed, unless I use an all purpose rubber band to secure the planner. This works really well until I slip it off the planner so I can write in or read the contents, and then my rubber band has gone somewhere else (into the vortex perhaps?). Hey, life isn't perfect, right?

Suggestion for future design:
--make the front and the back the same color.
--have a more secure way of gluing or attaching the elastic into the back of the planner. I have this nice little hole and can actually look through the hole from the front to the back. I could thread some light weight cord through the hole, but then one would have to tie and untie the cord, not nearly as nice as an elastic loop.
--I would like pen or pencil loop at the side of the planner.
--A personal information page at the front of a planner is something I have become accustomed to using, so wish it were included. It is obviously not required that one fill in the information, however that personal information enabled a grocery store to return my calendar to me after I accidentally left it in a grocery cart (this happened to me several years ago, and could happen to anybody at any time).

Overall, this is a well made planner, and I plan to order the same kind for next year. Now about that elastic band problem! I hope that this particular detail is redesigned.

text:
I received this product for free for my honest review. I was not paid for my review.
The HP OfficeJet Pro 7740 Wide Format All-in-One Printer has a B I G footprint. I had been using a little laser Pantum Printer that was about 8x13 to this color printer that is 23x28 when fully extended for the use of the wide format. Big difference in size and in weight. And in functionality.
The old printer was unable to print in color or fax in color, copy in color or scan in color. It was a monochrome laser printer that was inexpensive and this new HP is hands-down the better printer.
As with many HP printers that I have owned in the past, it takes XL cartridges that can print up to 1600 – 2000 pages, depending on whether you are printing in color or black and white.
The smaller cartridges print 700-100 pages; again, dependent on color usage.
Whichever size cartridge you use, it will take a total of 4.
Color pages take at least 10 seconds and black only takes at least 9 seconds to print.
The printer has a 2.0 usb that is compatible with usb 3.0 devices. In addition there is a host USB, Ethernet, wireless and 2 modem ports.
There are two paper trays.
You can make 99 copies at a time.
The printer, by itself, out of the box, weighs just shy of 43 pounds.
In the box, you get the printer, phone cord, setup black and color cartridges, cd-rom and power cord.
The cd-rom includes HP Dropbox, Hp Google Drive and Microsoft DotNet.
The printer also has mobile printing capability via HP ePrint, Apple AirPrint Mopria, Wireless direct printing and Google Cloud Print.
Scan software supports Bitmap, JPEG, PDF, Rich Text, Text and TIFF.
The printer can has a flatbed that measures 11.69x17.
You can scan to PC, memory device or email.
You can print up to 11x17, with duplex and two sided printing.
The other drawback, other than the size of the beast, is that the programming LCD panel, which is incredibly small at 2.65”.
This printer could easily be used for business capabilities and has the capacity to print 11x14 signs professionally.
Due to the size of this guy, I am having to completely arrange my office so it will be easily accessible. Getting it out of the box will need two people, yes it is heavy and not easy to lift up by yourself. I did it though. title: Dry Pens.  Test them- Write on high absorbing paper or cardboard.
text:
Take your chance. Test all pens before return period. Mine were dried out.

When I tested one at first it seemed ok. However, ALL the markers were dried out when put to any test. They would not flow on cardboard or any paper that absorbed. It first seemed to work on shiny low absorption paper so I was fooled into thinking they were ok.

I bought them for moving boxes. When I finally needed them a month later, I have to go over every letter ten times to make it look black enough and easily legible. This should work with a single pass. Frustrating.

With any normal writing it was dry, and did not flow. Going super slow sometimes works ok.

I am 100% sure, ALL my markers are dry. At best, they only work for a few slow words then stops flowing properly. Wont work on cardboard at all! Dry.

Yes, my fault that I did not challenge all the pens before the return period. Yet, I never bought dried out NEW Sharpie pens befores. First time for everything.

I threw away the packaging, but I doubt there is a manufacturing date. If there is, check it!

title: For light mounting Only
text:
I have this on the wall for remote controls. It looks almost invisible from far away, while before, I had some thick black velcro on the white wall. It looked tacky.

The remotec ontrols stick, but will knock off way easier than the thicker old black velcro. There is a huge difference with this thin velcro compared to the thicker kind as far as adhesion strength.

Example: I think it takes 5 to 10 times the strength to pull the remote straight off with the thicker black type I have.

So, there is no comparison between traditional thicker velcro strength and this one. The only question is if the value of the clear and thin properties outweighs the needs of adhesion strength. Because, it really looks good, almost invisible on white.

I guess all I can report, is its strong enough for my remote controls as long as I don't brush by them, as they knock off easily.

title: Doesnt Smell, Comfortable, Sturdy- EXCELLENT PRODUCT!
text:
Let me answer all the questions I had (based upon reported problems with other mouse pads) that made me determine that this a great Mouse Pad
(I owned this 5 months and use it 8 hours a day)

But first, my one and only gripe- all else is positive:
My blue laser mouse (Microsoft Wireless Mouse Model 1383 Mobile 4000) tracks with a slight drag. The soft surface makes it not flow as freely as I would prefer. Over very long periods of intense work, it feels slightly tedious and tiresome. But, this might be preferential. To some, this drag might aid with accuracy over a more fluid and free mouse movement. My next pad will be of the solid, slick surface type.

1) Does it smell like chemicals? Answer: No. I am very sensitive to smells. Many mouse pads and urethane type products reek of foul chemicals and I fear may actually be toxic. I returned a mouse pad because it leached a nasty chemical smell and gave me a headache.

2) Is the wrist pad comfortable? Yes. This answer will vary with ones taste. This is not very soft, as some pads bottom out from pressure and act like they are not there at all while the other extreme they are hard as rock (worst case scenario to me and some reported this to be too hard). This one is firm yet giving. Almost perfect for me. It could be a little softer but not any harder to make me happy. If you are very sensitive to firmness, probably pass. I am sensitive to firmness a little- I prefer soft than hard. I use this for hours and never had a sore wrist from the pad. The wrist pad material feels like a quality, firm, spongy foam.

3) Quality? Simply, excellent. It doesn't curl up, no fraying edges. It has substantial weight and is thick. I think it will last many years. Other than the dirt, it looks brand new after 100's of hours of use.

4) Size? Its just long enough for my large hand with no room to spare, lengthwise. Another half inch to an inch longer would be better. I have to choke up a little on the pad with my wrist back toward me as to not run out of room. My palm almost straddles the wrist pad a little. Not ideal but really not a problem either. I don't really notice, however, I would be more comfortable if i could extend forward more. Do you have big hands? Try to look for something a little longer, but if you can't find something else of quality and affordable, buy this one. The other great attributes makes this a winner and I personally wouldn't trade quality, comfort for length while giving up the latter. The pivot of my wrist to the tip of my middle finger is 8 inches. When holding my mouse, my wrist to the tip of my small mouse is 6 inches. Mouse wrist pad base to the far tip of pad is 7 inches. Pad is 8 inches wide (plenty wide) total length of pad is 9 inches including wrist pad. Wrist pad is 1 inch thick and doesn't visually deform under the pressure of my wrist but gives just enough to not feel rock hard and yet feels a little soft.

4) Grip? Excellent. This pad will not slide around. If you want to move it, you probably need to pick it up to relocate it. I like it to be easily movable, relocatable on my bed, so I keep the plastic wrapping on it so it will slide its position on my bed but never slides when operating. I peeled off the backing plastic wrap shipping protector and it gripped my bed so well I carefully put the plastic sheet back on and it stayed on. Very Grippy!

This is the best mouse pad I ever had. The 3 year warranty stands up to me because i don't think I will need it. Its extremely well made, especially for the price. It is easily worth twice the price. It seems almost impossible to find real quality and especially quality and economy these days in anything.

*I have no affiliation with this brand and I did a lot of research and bought this mouse pad based upon the reviews and the company's claims and product parameters. The only thing where the claims may not hold up for everyone, is that the pad might be too hard for some peoples wrist and the soft surface could cause enough drag to make their wrist get sore. But both these concerns are very marginal and I suggest getting this and trying it. For the life of me, I could not find a better mouse pad especially at near this price.

title: USB Version is Ok, but ALL Purpose Desk is Best!
text:
I have two different Sofia + Sam Laptop Desks and I will compare both in this review... The USB one vs. All Purpose Lapdesk
1) I far prefer the All Purpose Desk. It has a larger surface area for working and distributes the weight on your legs more evenly. It is also not as high as the USB one, which I prefer. There is also less of a slanted surface. It does not come with a usb lamp.
2) The USB one is about 2/3 the size of the All Purpose Desk and far more slanted. It is heavier and feels more weighty on my legs. The USB light is a handy feature to have, but I never use it because the light doesn't shine very well or disburse the light well enough to really make use of it. I always use my overhead or table lamps instead.
3) All in all, both have equal wrist pad height and gel, but the All Purpose version is significantly longer than the USB version, which is beneficial for those doing computer work all day or with carpal tunnel complaints.
At night, in bed, my husband and I stack the USB version on top of the All Purpose version for perfect viewing height of the laptop. Add in a sound bar and you have a cozy night ahead of you. I really like Elegiant's Sound Bar the best.

title: Become a Star Student!!!!
text:
I just completed my FNP NP clinical rotations and schooling and this literally was the best purchase I have ever made before starting my master's program. Although the print is EXTREMELY tiny, one full page- back and front- is EVERYTHING you need to ask a patient during a physical exam's history and physical, including OLDCARTS, allergies, family history, review of symptoms, lab values, whole body review during physical exam, plan and assessment. Truly a life saver for any student or practitioner.
For my school, I had to write a detailed write up for every patient from top to bottom and I used this notebook as my record keeping. It was extremely helpful for keeping Typhon notes (some schools require you log patients into the computer using ICD-10 codes). I found that over time, this book housed everything handy to keep me timely and efficient during my clinicals because I used to so often that the notes were like second nature to me.
My only two gripes about the book include: 1) the print is really small and almost imperceptible for those that don't have 20/20 vision and 2) the book was just slightly too large to fit into my white coat, which was a huge hassle.
Yet, the Dean of my school (top 3 in the nation) praised me for using this book during a simulation in front of the whole class because I knew all of the right questions to ask during my first semester whereas most students were still finding their groove. I am not meaning to brag at all, but meaning to say that this book gave me a significant leg up in school. He even mentioned to the whole class after the simulation that everyone should obtain this notebook!

If I was a printing business cards or logos for a living, I might pony up the money for HP for the final end product.
Because the cartridges have a tiny funky chip on them over the regular chip reader to make them more compatible with the HP printer, I am careful to slide it in for fear or knocking it off, but I've used about 10 of these cartridges and never had a problem with that, it just takes a little extra nudge to get it locked in. One time I did get like a "dud" on a multi pack. No trouble shooting would make the printer read it for more than. Two pages. The sellers were very responsive 3-4 months out when i finally popped in new cartridge and sent me a replacement.

Can't give enough kudos to sellers that are actually there for you, you just gotta remember, it's a two way street. Some things they can't control. You have to give sellers an honest chance to work thru trouble shooting, and be willing to meet them 1/2 way sometime to resolve an issue.

I just put it in my printer this afternoon and it did work. It was very easy to install and I didn’t have any errors popping up. So far so good. The price is amazing and as long as it stays at this price. ($25 for a double pack of XL) I’ll definitely continue to buy it. Assuming I don’t have any issues as I continue to use it.
I was only buying epson brand for the last several years but it’s too darn expensive. With the coronavirus pandemic, money is extremely tight and when I can work, it’s from home. So it’s important that I’m able to print what I need. Also the ink printed like it should on paper, so no issues there either.

This is a very early review but I’ll edit this if my opinion changes in any way in the future.
I didn’t give it 5 stars for this reason but I’ll come back in a few months when I know how good it works, and to give an estimate of how many pages I can print with just one cartridge. Although it will vary depending if their full pages of not. Needless to say I’ll update it whether good or bad.

text: These are worth whatever price I pay. I used these daily on my desk and love that they are refillable. And when the corners wear out, toss it and order and new one. The paper is heavy, but not too. And it takes any type of pen well.

title: Very good note-taking pen
text: I use various types of paper during the day, but more often than not, I'm writing on a desk pad with removable and refillable pages. I keep these for up to a couple of months to refer back to them, and I've discovered pencil almost disappears and ink fades. I picked up one of these pens while out shopping a while back, was impressed, so ordered a bunch.  They last far longer than I thought they would and that makes them economical as well.

title: Strong paper
text: I used these daily on my desk while I'm on the phone. I can doodle on them, but more importantly, I can use all sorts of pens and pencils on them. I save the pages for reference for a month and folded into fourths, they fit into a filing cabinet quite well.

title: Good quality clips
text:
If you are anal like me, and like to color code things, these are for you. More importantly, these are high quality binder clips that are 1" wide, and normally classified as small. They are perfect (and a lot less money) and compare easily with the brands sold at the Big Box office supply places. And remember, a lot less money!

Price and quality are right - what else are you looking for?

title: Never a problem with these
text: This is the first time buying this particular packaging, but it is not the first time I've purchased Inktopia's refilled ink cartridges.  These are much less expensive than going to the manufacturer, and after learning how to get rid of the error message, everything works fine.  The message will tell you that either a. the cartridge is too full or b. it is an off brand cartridge.  Either way, you just clear the message. On my printer, you do that by clicking on OK. On others, I've seen that you have to X out of the message.  Once I've done that, I cannot tell that this isn't a manufacturer's cartridge and have never had a problem with them functioning in my printer.

title: Nice page size calendar
text:
Beyond what my notepad and calendar could do, I needed something that could be referenced for minor items that we all forget. But I wanted something I could stand up and put with the books at my desk.

I've used this for a little while now, and I believe it will work out fine. There's enough space to write on the days...there is one full month for every two pages. The pages are 8-1/2 X 11, and it is a soft-bound (soft-cover) so it will withstand being opened and closed often. Color me pleased that I found this here when I needed it.

title: Not much to say except...love cats?
text: This is just cute and a perfect gift for ANY cat owner or just plain lover of cats.  We all know, if you own a cat, then they get themselves into predicaments that are without logical explanation. This calendar puts a photo and caption to almost every one of those tricky little situations.  It is an enjoyable gift that will keep giving until the next Holiday season rolls around.

title: Great Gag Gift
text: This is for a woman who works in an all male (and totally clueless) office.  I can see her putting these notes on dirty dishes left all over the kitchen, to the coffee pot when they left it boil down to nothing, to the refrigerator where what's inside might just kill you or cute you, hard telling.  Great gag gift.

title: Not all are perfect
text: I bought these thinking I use enough of them, I was justified in buying them a bunch at a time. In a way I wish I hadn't.  The first one was literally falling apart when I started to use it.  The tape was tangled inside the holder, with absolutely no way of straightening it out.  So out of 6, I actually only got 5. Even for five, the price was good.  And so far, the second one out of the package is working fine.  The tape seems to stick well, and it certainly works well when I write on it.

title: Pass on these pens!
text:
UPDATE: I'm on my third pen and am slowly losing any praise I had for them. First, it is impossible, once you erase a line, to write over it with the same pen. In fact, if you try, the pen skips and sometimes just refuses to write. That negates the effect of having an erasable pen. No thank you. Add onto that, there appears to be not much gel in these pens, or the gel goes faster than ink would in the same size pen. I'm on my third and won't be using these again. I know there are erasable pens out there, and I'm going to search out some with ink instead of gel, because I think that is what is causing this problem. Don't waste your money on these if you actually think you're going to be erasing and writing over anything, because you'll have the same problem I've had.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: The last time I tried erasable pens and ink, I was totally disappointed so these were a nice surprise. I do most of my writing on a desk pad when I'm on the phone and it is nice to be able to erase something if it isn't correct. These erase cleaning (as long as you don't have a really heavy hand when writing, then they'll erase the ink but the impression will be left on the page). The first one out of the box doesn't skip and the blue is a bluer blue than most blue ink any more, which I appreciate too, especially when I have to put my wet signature on something and can't use a black pen.

title: Expensive but Worth It.
text:
I have a desk pad that I use constantly. I don't doodle. I take notes on it while I'm on the phone, then I fold up the pages and keep them in a folder until a certain amount of time has passed. I tried buying "cheap" previously - in fact, I tried other pages, other than Doolittle, but I keep coming back to them because of the quality of the paper. I write in both pencil and pen, and marker at times, and this paper doesn't rip, doesn't tear, and doesn't bleed through.

Yes, the pages are more expensive than you can get from a dollar store, but you get what you pay for. And in this case, I'd rather pay a bit more than have to deal with pages that leak through and tear easily.

Update- I'm on my third order of these refills. I'm still pleased, and now that I'm using both gel pens and erasable gel pens, I'm even more impressed. There no bleed through, so I can actually flip these over and use the other side of each sheet for notes.

title: My go-to favorite
text:
Even though I've been known to buy cheaper tape at times, Scotch has always been my go-to when heavy-duty packing and taping is going on.

First, the best way to use this tape is with a dispenser. If you try to use any kind of packing tape without a dispenser, I can tell you that you'll be frustrated long before the last box is taped.

I already have the dispenser and these fit perfectly. I've used 3 rolls of this so far and have no complaints.

title: Loves these pencils
text:
I HATE running out of lead in the pencils I use, and when I discovered these disposable pencils, I almost did a happy dance (not quite, especially since I was in public at the time). They suit me perfectly. I can put 3-4 into my tote bag, along with my "idea book" and if I'm stuck somewhere and have time to kill, out my pencil comes with the notebook, and I'm ready to rock and roll...or write. Depends upon how you look at it, I think.

I have no clue how many pieces of lead these hold, I can't tell you how long they last. What I can tell you is that I've used them for the last few years and have yet to be disappointed in them.

title: Very nice notebook for my use
text:
I use moleskin notebooks like this as a journal of sorts, and since I've used them before, already knew that if you use a pen or marker, there will be bleed through. Markers, especially, will make a mess. But since I usually am using a mechanical pencil or a fine point pen, I haven't had much of a problem with bleed-through. However, when I'm using a pen, I can usually only use one side of a two-sided notebook page, and that is something that all buyers should be aware of.

These are a perfect size for a backpack or tote bag. In fact, one tote that I sometimes use is a bit narrower than others I have, and these notebooks fit into it perfectly, saving me the hassle of having to switch out the totes before I can carry my "idea books". Because that's what I use them for. And they are perfect for that. The notebooks are lightweight, the covers are extremely durable, and I can sit with one on my lap and make notes for however long I need to without any problems.

I will definitely purchase these again. I have deducted one star from this review because of being able to use only one side of the pages when I'm writing with a heavier ink pen. Otherwise, these notebooks would have received five stars.

title: Sturdy expanding file
text: I didn't know what to expect from this file, as I've never ordered something like this online. Other than copy paper, my other paper purchases have always been in person.  I'm pleased. It appears sturdy, it held all the papers I needed to file in it, and a few extras.  The band that wraps around it to keep it closed did the job, so unless something terrible happens to it, I'm going to say that this will work well and it is sturdy enough for large documents, if you should want to file them.

title: Not my first desk pad by Doolittle
text:
This is about the third deskpad I've purchased from Doolittle over the last few years. I stay with the same brand because they're identical. The paper is just the right thickness, it is easily removed and tossed if I don't need to keep it, and this is my preferred way of making notes while on the phone. This pad is refillable and I've found that to be a huge time and money savings over the individual non-refillable pads you can buy that have fewer pages, usually.

When this one arrived, I was not disappointed. It is just like the last one! I love consistency in a product.

title: Standard notebooks
text: Don't expect these to have an ultra-strong cover or be anything other than basic notebooks. That is exactly what they are. I use this type of notebook in my job to make notes that I keep for a long length of time and these are an inexpensive alternative to buying them at a big box store and spending twice as much on a set of 5.  As long as you don't have high expectations for them being a sturdy substitute, they'll work fine for most uses.

How you can possibly give a well made card, with a cute picture and cute text, a one star rating is beyond me. Perhaps you should go spend twice as much at a card store then.

In my case, I LOVED these cards. And I was pleasantly surprised at the quality since the price was extremely reasonable. And just as an added note, everyone who received them has commented on how cute they were.

These were the first cards I've ever purchased from this brand, but they won't be the last. In fact, I'm browsing their offerings looking for all-occasion cards now!

title: Love the shading ability
text:
I ordered these after reading the reviews and knew that I had to be gentle when sharpening, otherwise I would break the lead in these pencils.

I've used these for a few days now. I tend to use coloring to break the tension of my job, and since I work at home, this is my "lunchtime" activity. Yes, I did have the same problems others had with the broken lead, but with a lighter, gentler hand on the sharpener, I only had that problem once. The rest of the time, I was able to sharpen them and not have the lead break.

But honestly, I think I would put up with the lead breaking because I wanted to be able to shade with the pencils I purchased, and these fit the bill. I love the colors and I love that the colors blend nicely together. And it isn't "work" to get them to blend. And with 152 pencils, I'm still imagining the different color combinations I can come up with.

Would I recommend? Yes. Would I say to be cautious when sharpening and to use a gentle hand? Yes. There is always improvement to be made with pencils. Especially soft core pencils. These are a less expensive alternative to the Prisms, etc., that are sold. And I'm happy with them. I'm not a professional, I'm not looking to make "frame worthy" art, I use this as a stress reliever and to take my mind off things it shouldn't linger on. In that regard, these work very well. :-)

title: Well made case
text:
This is the best made pencil case I've ever seen. My luggage pales in comparison to this. And it holds a boatload of pencils. Originally, I bought this because I have coloring pencils, drawing pencils, and graphing pencils and nowhere to carry them. They're all in the case now, and I still have two entire sections to fill.

This case has a wrist-strap with it, but I can't see using it, as the case, when even half filled is rather heavy and bulky, not something I would hang on my wrist. Overall, it was a great value for the money. In fact, it is almost too well made for what I'll use it for. :-)

title: Love the cover
text: I use one of these daily, and always have one on my desk for all the notes I take and make to myself during the day. This type of notebook allows me to do that and, unlike sticky notes and all the other crap, doesn't get lost because everything is in one place.  On this particular notebook (and this was the first time I'd purchased this brand and type), the cover is plasticized somehow. I'm not sure that it is completely waterproof but when I set my iced tea glass on it today, the sweat from the glass didn't soak into the cover. Or at least not before I found a coaster.  That's unlike other notebooks I have here.  I'll order this brand/type again. The color isn't important, so the supplier choosing it for me doesn't matter.

title: What's not to love at 20 cents a pen?
text:
Update: It has taken me about a year to go through these pens. Out of the box full, I threw out 55 pens that were not writing, or were falling apart. I was about to re-order when I saw the price had more than doubled. So I'll go back to ordering pens online that are budget friendly.

I received this box yesterday, in the nick of time. If it hadn't arrived I would have had to make a run out for refills or stick pens, or something to write with. I have a pen in my hand 8 hours of the day. I buy refills for gel pens in packages of 20, I buy stick pens in packages of 50 or more. When I saw this offered, I thought why not? Even if half of them work, it is still a great deal (unless you can tell me somewhere I can buy a stylus retractable pen for less than 40 cents each).

It is interesting the differences in the boxes as I read the reviews. In my box, about a quarter of them (25 or so) are not printed at all, half of them are obvious misspellings, and the rest are just printed pens. Most are stylus pens, with a few that are not (and that doesn't matter to me one way or the other, but it makes it handy when I have my Kindle available). I took two handfuls out of the box, at random, brought them to my office with a blank sheet of paper, and they all wrote. And all were black ink. I'm sure I'll find one or two that won't write, or some that have blue ink, but over all these cost me around 20 cents each, most (from eyeballing it) are in working order. And as I said, even if HALF of them were defective, it would still be a good deal. And I'll do this again, because I can tell you that this supply will only last about 3-4 months, unless I'm going to buy refills - not. I'll just come here and order this again. Color me very, very happy with this purchase.

text:
At the time I bought it I thought it was expensive and kind of frivolous and wondered how I could justify it. Having had it for months (years?) now, I have to say it was more than worth every penny.

Whoever designed and engineered this printer were consummate experts. This by far the most intuitive, reliable, straightforward, accessible printer I've ever had. We're doing a renovation right now and living in a small room that continually gets cluttered and desk fills with stuff. The Rollo thermal laser printer gets shoved around. Sometimes power or USB disconnected. The labels get moved and or torn. It doesn't matter.... I connected it. Remove the old paper (easy!!!) slip a new piece of paper in, push the button, it aligns and syncs it in just a couple of seconds, light goes green. To set it up on iMac with printer prefs just means selecting the Rollo driver from the list. Whalla!!! It just works! It works great!

I thought I would save a few bucks over the brand names like Quartet and or UBoards. Those boards run about $130ish so I was looking at a solid 25% savings. I figured why not, its just a piece of tempered glass with some thin gauge sheet metal on the back, how much different can it be? I wouldn't mount a 11" x 14" picture frame with that trash let alone a huge piece that weighs more than 20 lbs. I really wanted this to work so I ordered some third part offset mounts from Amazon and it was slightly too big. I am so disappointed. this thing took forever to arrive and then I waited another week to get the new hardware. All for nothing. I am still surrounded by 100's of sticky notes. Lesson learned. You get what you pay for. I am returning it and will be buying one of the brand name boards.
Dear Manufacturer,
This COULD have been a great product but you decided to save a few pennies on mounting hardware. I realize you sourced this from some factory in China (says so on the box) but is anyone managing your brand and the quality of the products you attach it to? I mean quality hardware would have cost you less than a couple of dollars. These small details are what make the difference when sourcing something. How did you not have specific specifications on your mounting hardware. Did anyone even bother to check the hardware shipping with this board? A little attention to detail would have gone a long way.

title: This book does have some nice, practical tips for helping track and reduce spending ...
text:
This book does have some nice, practical tips for helping track and reduce spending and even begin saving. There are certainly tips that everyone can use, but much of this is common sense. Don't spend more than what you make. Don't have tons of credit cards. Buy used. Use coupons. Make a budget. If you are looking for some ideas on where to get started, this is a great comprehensive book that is going to give you that. The author gives practical straightforward tips that--IF FOLLOWED--can help you save some money, but don't expect this to be a get rich quick with no effort sort of thing that never works anyway. Even if you follow all the tips and go above and beyond, not everyone is going to retire a millionaire. It just doesn't work like that. But you don't have to work until you die just to pay off half of what you owe either.
I enjoy the straightforward way in which the book is written, but I did find quite a few stereotypes in the book regarding women and gender roles in marriage and the "typical" way to live your life and goals. That's great if you were lucky enough to have parents who set you up for success and lived in and upper middle class neighborhood and went to college with little to know debt, got a great job, then met your spouse, bought a house, and had 2.5 kids in a Leave it to Beaver neighborhood. But then you wouldn't probably be reading this book. An example is the section on engagement rings. If you are reading this book looking for financial tips, you probably shouldn't be looking at spending thousands on an engagement ring. The author then throws in a paragraph stating that men's rings are less expensive so the woman just has to make sure to pay off the credit card before the wedding. This is pretty stereotypical and definitely heteronormative. The whole section is really toned to imply that the bride to be shouldn't be with you to buy the ring, she shouldn't know how much it cost, and the man is responsible for the majority of the decision. All this is after a section about how the couple should work together to make financial decisions before the wedding.
Overall the book can be helpful, so I will give it 4 stars with the disclaimer that as with everything you need to take it with a grain of salt and figure out what is really feasible and applicable in your life and your situation.

I received this product at a discount for my unbiased review.

title: Mesh Stretches! Could be deal breaker.
text:
Waited six months to write this. Glad I did. Be sure to read about the stretching before you buy...

1. Put the arms on backwards, L on R, R on L. Otherwise you can't get close to your desk.
2. The adjustability of the arms is excellent, up/down, forward/backward and angle.
3. Easy to assemble.
4. Looks great, professional appearance.
5. Headrest doesn't come close enough to your head to offer real support. This is subjective; your mileage may vary.
6. Mesh material is, as expected, very breathable.
7. POTENTIAL DEAL BREAKER: Within six months, the mesh has stretched to the point my head hits the plastic frame of the headrest, and my butt is almost touching the metal/plastic parts underneath. For reference, I'm 185 pounds; I would expect this would not be too much for an office chair to reasonably support.

Maybe I just got an unlucky run of the mesh material? If the stretching stops—which I don't think it will—the chair will remain usable, although the headrest already is not. If you're less than 140 pounds, you may not have to worry about this. But at 6'1" and 185#, I'm by no means overweight and really didn't expect the material to stretch like this.

Hope this helps you.

They never erased, they only left gaping holes and smears all over my papers. So when I got a specific journal book that said I need these pens because they could be erased. I laughed derisively. But then I got the pens...and miracle upon miracle...THEY ERASE! I don't know why it's so satisfying to erase a pen mark, but it really brightens my day. (This may also let you know how my days are going.)
I also love the bright colors this set comes in and I use them for my note taking in my classes. The only thing to really remember is that you have to let the ink dry before you start erasing or it may smear and then that may take you back to a darker time...a time without erasable pens. Buy these things! They're the best!

title: Best invention since sliced bread
text: Iv been moving my whole life , I think I’m up to 50+ moves. My Vietnam vet dad moved us a lot growing up . Then I married a service member and continued moving often . I’d discovered this stuff about 10 years ago and fell in love . When I saw this was available I did not hesitate and ordered it as fast as I could . I’m very happy with this product. It makes moving so much easier . It’s one of my favorite emergency items to keep around . I used it to attach a mattress to the top of my vehicle !! I used the wrap like rope and went thru the door frame to get it secured . It made it possible to close my door on the film and to add extra security I rolled the back passenger windows down and just went thru the cabin to make a secure wrap around the mattress and the roof of my vehicle . I did get some looks from people who couldn’t see the clear film holding the mattress to my roof and probably thought I was just being crazy. It was not a long drive . It worked so well , it didn’t move at all . Using the front and rear roof frames to secure it front and back was perfect . I’m use to using the rolls without handles so getting actual handles was kinda cool . They didn’t work super smooth but they did work . I think they might need some lube to work better but I’m not sure what would be safe to put on the plastic and not cause it to break down or make a mess. I’m gonna do a lil research and see if I can find a way to lube the handle pieces so they are smoother . If not then oh well , not a big deal . I ordered it for the wrap not the handles . Overall I’m very happy with this wrap and would but it for anybody I knew moving to make it easier to secure boxes or keep parts for opening on desks or dressers . In a pinch it can be used as a rope or to hold things like bolts . You can do a lot with this stuff.

I gave this 4 stars instead of 5 for 2 reasons- first, the holes on the right side of the chair did not line up well. I would have had this chair put together much faster if it wasn't for this. After some trial and error, I had to complete the left side first (back and arm) in order to be able to pull the pieces together tight enough to make the holes line up on the right side. Even then it was a struggle. The other reason is that it can with a slight tear on the very back of the seat piece. It was covered once the back was put on, but it does raise concerns about the longevity of the chair. This is for a home office with limited usage, but I think if my dogs jump on it, it may tear. I will update this review if there are any issues. Overall, not a bad piece. Slightly overpriced for the issues. This was my first time putting a chair together.
** update** Although the size of this chair is great for me at 5' tall, my husband (6') mentioned it being a little small for him. The seat is narrow and short. The adjustable height makes it versatile for eating on as well, and the slanting top is excellent for resting my iPad on for just reading. Unlike some tables, it can be moved directly over your lap without limiting your ability to move your legs and change position. Yet it folds up into a nice flat unit that can be tucked between the bed and the wall very nicely. If you work and/or eat in bed a great deal, you'll love having this versatile, dependable table.

Update Oct. 2,2021 -- I used this table for hours every day for almost 3 years. I frequently changed both the height and slant. Only now, after almost three years, is the latch for the slant feature getting a little undependable. It still works, but I'm buying a replacement just to be safe. This is a reliable table that is very easy to use with plenty of room for a laptop and mouse. It's an excellent buy. I couldn't be happier.

title: For the price it's totally fine.  A bit thinner than standard packaging tape (2.0 mil vs. 2.6) - but it works just fine.
text:
For the price, it's totally fine for packing up and shipping boxes. Don't expect thick, amazingly perfect tape. Your standard packaging tape is around 2.5 mil thick - this stuff is 2.0 mil. It still does the job. It's also not crystal clear - it's got a slight yellowish tint to it - but when separated from the roll and applied to packaging you won't notice one bit - it's appears crystal clear when applied to packaging.

So is the price low? Yes. Does it work fine? Yes...no complaints here!

title: Absolutely worth the price!  Best wireless printer/scanner for $99.  Apple Airprint works great - well worth the money.
text:
Holy smokes I love this thing! I had been using Epson WorkForce printers for 5 years now, and I love them because generic ink was cheap to replace. But recently my Epson printers had trouble printing with new OSX updates. I was also sick of the cleaning I had to do to keep up with the ink system.

I had always avoided laser printers, but they've gotten so much better recently. Replacement toner for this Brother printer is only $14 here on Amazon.

I was looking for a nice wireless printer/scanner combo that worked on my home network for printing basic documents and shipping labels CLEARLY, and a printer that would print directly from my iPhone without needing additional drivers. This Brother delivers!

As others have said - it doesn't print graphics or pictures too well - you'll see small lines through printed pictures, but I didn't purchase this printer to print pictures or color, so I don't really care.

I got it for only $99 as a refurbished unit here on Amazon, and it even came with a toner kit in the refurb kit (I didn't know this, so I purchased a replacement - so this felt like a bonus).

Setup was super simple. Google Drive also automatically detected it and asked if I wanted to set it up for internet printing through Google Drive - this also only took a minute, and it works great.

So long and short - it works great - I'm blown away for only $99! People report Airprint issues, but I've had no issues with Airprint at all - works great on my home network.
