title: Cheaper, Better, Faster than any Inkjet After a Year - Read my Tips!
text:
Short Version (TL;DR):
This printer is great, but you should download and install the latest Brother software and drivers. DON'T use any drivers that Windows tries to automatically use. Those default Windows drivers might "work" but you'll end up with poor quality and color in your images. It'll look like the images have tons of blurry JPEG compression artifacts and the colors will be washed out. The Brother drivers will fix all of that and will result in great-looking prints and more flexibility in your print options. The wireless compatibility could be a little better, but probably works with most routers / Wi-Fi access points.

Also, MAKE SURE you use laser printer paper! Not all printer paper is made equal, regardless of what your teenage son might tell you - it is not some scam. Quality laser printer paper should cost roughly the same as the inkjet or "multipurpose" paper you buy now, but will not curl as much and it will also help preserve the life of your printer. You can put it to the test if you don't believe me.

Long Version:
Bought this a few months ago from a local office supply store that was clearing out inventory, and it's worth every penny. I don't print a TON of color - just every once in a while, and the color cartridges would still go empty in a couple of months or start resulting in streaking (requiring head cleaning, which drains the cartridges even further). Replacing those ink cartridges could be about $60-$70 for the "high-capacity" cartridges. When I did the math, I was spending about $400 - $500 dollars a year on just my Epson Artisan ink (Claria - I don't buy generic anymore) alone.

Since toner doesn't have the same problem of drying up or being wasted and lasts a lot longer (something I know from being in IT support), this printer will pay for itself in about 8-9 months. Honestly, just about any inkjet printer will cost more than this printer after its first year of use and will give you headaches when you have to fix the inevitable streaking (I've owned a dozen inkjets by every major manufacturer and they all do it eventually).

Here's how people's lives are with lasers and inkjets:

Laser printers:
$400 Initial cost - "Ouch! Laser printers are so expensive!"
Print #1 on day 1 - Looks great.
Print #1000 on day 500 - Still looks like the quality from day 1, and you haven't had to replace any toner yet - awesome! Your cost is still $400.
Print #2000 on day 800 - Same great quality, but time to change the toner, which means a couple hundred bucks. You've owned it for over 2 years and now your investment is $600.
Year 5 - You may have to replace the drum. At this point, you've printed thousands of streak-free sheets, and invested about $1000 between the initial cost, the toner replacements, and the drum replacement.

Inkjet printers:
$100 Initial cost - "Nice! Why would ANYONE buy a laser printer when you get such great quality at 1/4 of the cost with an inkjet?"
Print #1 on day 1 - Looks great.
Print #100 on day 40 - Guess the starter ink cartridges need to be replaced, so that's another $60... installing them uses up some ink, so some of that $60 is already wasted.
Print #250 on day 100 - My red cartridge is out already and my yellow is almost empty? I guess I'll buy just those two cartridges for $30 total.
Print #500 on day 250 - Gotta buy a whole new pack for $60.
Print #750 on day 330 - Another ink-shopping trip. $60.
Print #751 on day 330 - Why are there ink drops on my prints and streaks? Head cleaning time.
Print #800 on day 340 - I -JUST- bought ink a week ago - how can the cartridges already be half-empty...? Oh right, the head cleaning...
Print #1000 on day 500 - Glad I didn't buy the laser printer. Inkjets are so much less expensive - I've only spent... let's see... $100 + nine total replacements of the cartridges for $60 each, and a few single-color cartridges... wait.... I've spent over $600 on this inkjet in just 500 days???
Year 5 - I've grown numb to the recurring cost of ink cartridges because doing the math at this point makes me feel bad, but I think it's somewhere around $2500 which sounds impossible . I tried the cheap "compatible" ink cartridges at one point and since then, the printer has never been the same. "Oh yeah, sure, [family member who's visiting], you can print your airline boarding pass on my printer. Don't worry about the streaks - that's normal - oh I guess maybe you can't print that if the streak messes up the boarding pass barcode. I guess it's time to buy another brand-new inkjet and throw this one into the garbage..."

Now, I'm not a huge user of every feature on this particular printer. I honestly just use printing and scanning. The quality results for both activities have been consistently great - the scanning quality and resolution is great and it scans pretty quickly. The print quality is precise (great if you want to print out accurate barcodes or anything that needs to be scanned) and the colors are accurate. In some cases, I've run across images that are poorly-prepared and they don't print well, but that's going to happen on any printer of any type and any manufacturer. The normal user will likely be very happy with the quality of every print (assuming they've installed the Brother software).

The network scanning works well and is pretty convenient, but it does require a tiny bit of setup. The Brother setup utility takes care of that setup for you and doesn't seem to require a lot of technical knowledge to work. There are some nice advanced features, with a web-based interface, but it's not going to be useful to most average users, in my opinion. More tech-savvy users might appreciate the ability to configure shortcuts and such.

Print speeds are okay. There ARE faster printers out there, but to me, getting another 2 pages every 60 seconds is not worth another $100 to me. The MFC-9340CW is likely going to be fast enough for most people. Also, be aware that advertised print speeds are basically the "fastest possible" print speeds that typically use the lowest quality prints. This is the same for all printers. If you want to print good-quality Word documents or web pages that have some images mixed in there, your realistic print speed is going to be about 1 page every 4-6 seconds, so maybe 10-15 pages per minute once it gets going.

The toner installation is a breeze. I actually thought I was doing it wrong at first, because I figured there would be more to it. Nope. It's just ridiculously easy.

The only thing I didn't really like was that the Brother software is a little on the heavy side in terms of resource consumption (assuming you load up everything it offers, but not everything is required). So if you're a tech-savvy person, you might want to choose the custom route when installing the software and only install the basics. I'm generally not a fan of printer software that has utilities that run in the background all the time (Epson does this with their inkjets), but it's not the end of the world and they don't take up any CPU after loading.

Overall, probably 4.5 stars out of 5.

text:
I used the jumbo Command hooks to hang a curtain rod and curtains. (I can’t add holes to my walls) I used 3 jumbo hooks for a 60” window. I used a lightweight curtain rod and it rests perfectly in the hooks (if I had a smaller rod like 5/8 or 1/2 smaller, it would have gone all the way down into the hook, but I like the larger 1” rod size) I did not use the adhesives that came with the hooks as they only hold 7.5 pounds, I ordered the 16 pound picture hanger adhesives from Command Strip. I applied the stronger adhesive to the back, pressing for a few minutes and making sure it was really secure on the hook. Next, I placed the hooks on the wall. After a minute of pressing, I removed the hook (they click on) and applied firm pressure over the adhesives then put the hook back on. (so I could be sure the adhesives were firmly on) I waited 24 hours before placing the curtains and curtain rod on the hooks. If your walls are slick or have older paint, they suggest wiping with an alcohol wipe before applying. This is a great renters option!!

Update- months later and the rods are still up!

title: Drawer won't open, and knob is broken
text: This could be quite functional and very useful, but it's not super well made. The wood is very thing and easily scratched and splintered. It arrived with the knob broken off, the screw sticking out, and it will not open no matter how hard I pull it. Won't even wiggle. It's jammed tight.  I tried to use a butter knife as a thin lever to pry it open, but it chipped off pieces of the wood instead- it will just break apart the front panel of that drawer into pieces of thin, cheap wood before it will open the drawer. title: Very roomy
text:
This feels like fabulous quality. It even smells good, not a chemical smell, but that sweet bamboo/crass smell of bamboo wood products. I had more trouble than other reviewers at putting it together, but I am extremely clumsy at that sort of thing and not at all good with schematics. I do think a couple of things could have been clearer in the instructions- like the fact that the pegs are optional. There are two sizes of boards that make up the slanted dividers/shelves, four pieces of one ,smaller size, and two of the larger. They each have guide holes for screwing in two pegs to make the dividers, but there are not enough pegs to put them in every single piece that has holes for them, so I thought I was doing something wrong. Once I realized the pegs are completely optional so it does not matter whether or not you put them in the larger or smaller shelves, it depends entirely on your needs things went better. I like that the shelves themselves can be removed and reorganized with a minimum of bother- they just slide in and out of grooves, no screws or other fasteners. The ball bearings on the lazy suisan base seem to be high quality, it spins smoothly and evenly and feels really sturdy. It holds a lot of things, but not a thousand pencils.

I like the reduced foot print on my desk, but I did find that because the pencils and pens stick so far above and beond the dge of the shelf, it needs more space than I realized between the unit and the wall.

Overall, this is a solid, quality tool for clearing up your desk surface and keeping your tools for arts and crafts or cosmetics well organized but in plain sight so you can quickly find what you want.

title: Nice whiteboard!
text:
Three major lists in our house; things to do, shopping and what's in the deep freeze. Alexa keeps track of the shopping list. The other two need a physical record. Otherwise, we can't keep up. I recently grabbed a notepad and recorded the 'to do' list. Because it has been out of sight, it's grown quite long. If it's 'in your face', you're more likely to work on it and get things done.

Then, what is in your deepfreeze? Do you still have that Fruit Cake from Christmas five years ago? I am guilty of buying stuff with good intentions and forgetting about it. I have ribs and brisket for smoking, two years old. I have all the makings of a good beef stew. And, there's much more. When planning the family meals, I need to SEE what I have available, to make the best of what we have and not waste anything. At one time, I had a small whiteboard on the fridge, with the list of the deepfreeze contents. It worked very well.

I ordered this magnetic whiteboard from YES4QUALITY based on three factors. First, the concept of an improved surface that doesn't stain like the older ones did. Next, was the size that best fit my fridge. Finally, was the price for the unit, including markers and eraser. I am happy with all factors.

It's a great quality product. It adheres to the fridge perfectly. The markers work very well. The markings erase very easily, even after many days. it's exactly the size I needed for my new LG three-door fridge. The markers and eraser stick to the fridge very well and don't fall off when you close the door.

I'm ready to put my lists on the board now. I'm very happy with this purchase. Five stars.

title: Best labeling gadget ever!
text:
I'm a drone pilot. I have a fleet of drones that require FAA registration and identification. The FAA requires that your license be clearly displayed on every aircraft you fly. I've tried every kind of label maker out there. The labels always find a way to peel off or get damaged.

Enter the TIKTONER handheld printer. It's easily programmed. It prints clearly and quickly. The printed data is water resistant and scratch resistant. It prints on nearly any surface, porous or not. It has a rechargeable LiOn battery. No cords to worry with. It includes an app that you create your label with and a memory card designed for just this purpose.

I'm now printing my FCC license directly on my drones. It doesn't get any more permanent than this. I'm very happy with this purchase.

title: Entertain like you mean it!
text:
We have been wanting to have a TV on the patio for entertainment, for quite a while. We like to throw little get togethers, cook outs and the occasional soiree. We have an extended patio, seating for 16+, two fire pits, a huge grill/smoker combo and great lighting.

It was my idea to permanently mount a TV designed for outdoor use, under the awning. Then, wifey suggested that we put one on a stand. As luck would have it, we attended a party where the host had a TV mounted on a regular stand and put it in the 'VIP tent'. That cinched it. I decided that we would have our 'outdoor' TV on a rolling stand, along with a soundbar and subwoofer. I already have an 'extra' TV. I bought a 55" to go in the garage. The 48" that's in there now will be perfect for this purpose.

After doing some research, I decided on this one from VIVO. It's not the cheapest. It's not the most expensive, either. But, based on it's design and function, it's the best for our intended purpose. Reading the description, I first thought that the uprights were telescopic. But, they are fixed. The height of the TV is adjusted by the mounting rings attached to the uprights. That's fine with me.

For our purpose, the TV will be mounted at the highest point. Using specialized brackets (purchased separately), the sound bar will be mounted above the TV, making the whole thing about 6' tall, and the subwoofer on the stand's built-in shelf.

This stand from VIVO is very well designed, built with top quality materials. The finish of the final product is perfect. I can see how this stand would be used in institutional settings, like public school's media departments. It's very sturdy and will withstand a lot of rolling around with heavy loads.

The casters are small, strictly for smooth, hard floors. They won't do well on uneven surfaces like coarse stone face paving. Extra care should be used when moving the fully loaded set up from place to place. Two people should do the moving. The leg spread is good enough to keep the whole thing well balanced and not tip over. All four casters lock, to keep it stationary on sloping surfaces. They include a bubble level. Keeping the bubble inside the black lines ensures safe positioning. Running the cables through the uprights keeps things nice and tidy, and tangle free. The TV mounting hardware is standard. It's the same type you would use to wall mount a TV.

Mounting the TV was a breeze. You can see that I also used another mounting bracket for the soundbar. There were no issues incorporating that in the setup. I set the subwoofer on the built-in shelf. All the wiring was tidied up behind the TV. The power cord and connecting wire from the sound bar to the subwoofer are run in the uprights and keep the whole thing clean, tangle free and very professional looking.

I am pleased with this purchase. I'm happy to give it five stars.

title: Treat it for the quality that it is.
text:
I needed a cart like this for my drone shop. I've seen several like it in stores and online. This was a quick pick, based on function. And, sad to say, I don't think I could have found the same thing at a lower price. That doesn't mean that I think that it's worth the price I paid. I don't. There's probably $20 worth of cheap plastic and low quality steel in it.

It has wheels, two of them locking. But, don't anticipate rolling it around very much without damaging it. It's not that sturdy. All of the drawers are light weight plastic with cheap little chrome plated plastic knobs. I am going to reinforce the knob screws with flat washers. Otherwise, the knobs will break out of the drawers after a few pulls.

The framework is the thinnest possible tubing and C-formed tracks. As long as this unit is stationary and you don't overload the drawers, it will hold up. That's what I'm doing. I have it parked where I'm going to use it and it will never move.

Assembly was quick and easy. I got it done in about 15 minutes, while I was watching a movie. The unit's top is a nice shelf and just snaps on to the frame work. it comes with an Allen wrench, which is all you need to complete the assembly.

Overall, if you treat it as the fragile thing that it is, it will serve you well enough. Just don't expect it to hold up well, under any kind of heavy or abusive kind of work. I think that it's over priced, for what it is. But, it's kind of in line with other products of it's type.

title: For universal application of stuff to your drones.
text:
That's the only reason I ordered these Velcro dots. I have a series of clearance lights, marker lights and FAA approved Anti-Collision Lights that I need to move between drones, based on which I am flying at the time. I keep the lighting in a separate drawer in my work shop. And, these Velcro dots handy in my 'glue and adhesives' drawer.

The lights in the picture came with some VERY strong double sticky foam tape dots. The drone in the picture is a DJI Mavic Mini that weighs less than 250 grams. The only way DJI could make this little guy so light was to substitute hard plastic and resin body parts with thin plastic and soft foam parts in the structure of the rotor arms (among other weight cutting measures).

Only a close inspection of the Mini will give you a true appreciation of what DJI had to do. It will also give you a greater sense of how fragile the aircraft really is. Using any kind of PERMANENT adhesives to fix something like auxiliary lighting to the aircraft is a HUGE mistake. Attempting to remove any of those adhesives will only damage the aircraft.

THAT is why I bought these Velcro dots. They are very small. Don't need big ones for this job. They are very low profile. Really don't need anything that stands up a lot. And, they are very light load rated. Don't need very strong rated Velcro for this job. The lights are VERY light weight, compact and they need to be added and removed to the aircraft with little effort or resistance. The lights, when attached with these dots, stay in place very well. But, are still easy to remove. Perfect.

These Velcro dots are EXACTLY the right solution for this application. So, for me, I am very happy and can comfortably give them five stars.

title: I wish I had this when I was in Puerto Rico for 6 months!
text:
[[VIDEOID:d22154b10fa742f30d63c4a4590d5d22]] As part of my work, I often travel to some of the US protectorates, like Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam, etc. Sometimes, like my time in Puerto Rico, after hurricane Maria, I can be there for months. I know a little Spanish. But, not enough for me to communicate effectively with the native people who don't know any English. I used the app on my phone as a translator a lot. But, it didn't have enough skills to get me through. And, I found that I was burning A LOT of my phone's battery just trying to have conversations with folks.

My wife suggested that we need to learn more Spanish. Especially since we're getting our house built here in central Texas and most of the labor here will be Spanish speaking with very limited English. So, I had enough cause to go ahead and get a REAL translator.

Now, with this Langogo Genesis translator, we can both learn just about any foreign language we want, we have an instant, always with us, interpreter. Did you know there were like twenty variations of Spanish? There are, and Genesis knows them all. In total, she knows over 100 languages. Ever want to know what the technicians are talking about while you're getting your mani-pedi? Take your Genesis with you. She knows Vietnamese.

It's super easy to use. No real set up required. Genesis automatically connects with the best signal while outside and can be connected to the strongest WiFi anywhere else. The controls are simple. Just select the language to translate from and to, she does the rest. Genesis will translate, speak the second language and give you written text IN THE SECOND LANGUAGE. I tested the Chinese and Japanese. I got the text of both those languages clearly displayed on the screen.

The display is clear and easy to read and the screen is also touch sensitive to allow accurate control without a bunch of buttons.

The volume can be dialed up loud enough to be heard over loud ambient noise. The microphone is sensitive enough to pick up the softest voice.

The silicone cover (accessory) protects the body of the Genesis very well. The wrist strap can be worn or secured into your handbag to prevent loss or theft.

This is the type of device that any professional traveling overseas should have in their pocket. Very pleased. Five stars.

title: Be Careful Pens Bleed
text:
I am not an artist and this is my first time purchasing gel pens. The pens were very affordable so I gave them a try. I tried them on my color book made for adults and they bled. I tried them on cards made to color and the bleeding was worse on the card stock. Part of the problem is me and my lack of experience. I have since learned that the type of paper used can make a big difference. Also, one should color top to bottom and from left to right (if right handed). The ink in these pens stays wet and must dry completely before you color the next section or it will smudge.

I gave this set of 24 gel pens 3 stars because all of them worked, the colors stayed true when dry, and the case is very handy.

I deducted 2 stars because the ink acts like paint, bleeds, smears easily and needs an exceedingly long time to dry. I have to dry each section over night before coloring the next area to minimize bleeding and smudging.

I would not recommend this set as a gift and would not give it to children because of the potential mess of wet ink.

UPDATE: Had a friend visit and we tried the gel pens on Psalms cards to color. She is very experienced and her work also bled and smeared. She thought about buying some for herself but changed her mind after trying them. I upgraded to 5 stars after finding a technique that works.

text:
These look good. And they work well.

The only issue seems to be with all the rubberbands since about 2016. They all crumble to goo or dust when exposed to air. Yes... Normal air. Don't leave the bag open or load your rubberbands cups anymore.

These last a little longer than the plain rubberbands but not much... And not Luke rubberbands pre-2016.

My business buys rubberbands by the pound to wrap up our printed products. However since 2016 we found the rubberbands now break down in normal air. They bond with the paper products and tear the paper when trying to remove. They turn to dust on the vinyl products and leave behind a gooey film.

The regular rubberbands we're lasing only 3-5 days before this was happening. These more expensive black rubberbands last a week or two. At least it's long enough for our customers to pickup their prints.

We started noticing this problem when we would come in to the shop and projects that were rolled and rubberbanded we're laid out open and the rubberbands we're clogging our vacuum.

title: Tape okay, annoyed by dispenser.
text:
The tape works just fine. Not great, but fine. It's not the stickiest, but it also doesn't tear things if you accidentally touch paper to it or glue your fingers together.

But the dispensers are useless. The edge isn't sharp enough to cut the tape, and the entire mechanism just falls apart and stops working almost immediately. The attached photos are of the second roll in the pack of 3 almost immediately after opening, the second time I used that roll (which had been sitting safely in an enclosed cabinet waiting its turn while I used up half of and then temporarily misplaced the first roll).

While a tape dispenser is a nice thing to have, you should not *have* to have one in order to use tape, especially relatively expensive tape, and you should especially be able to at least use the disposable dispenser one time before it simply falls apart.

The first time I used the roll was even more frustrating because I couldn't get the tape started since it serrated edge wouldn't cut it and I had to use scissors. I have a lot of pain and stiffness in my hands from a medical condition, and get more frustrated than I should when little things don't work, especially when I am already tired and in a lot of pain-- this product definitely did not make my life any easier and I'm disappointed in the quality.

This size band was perfect! They're super stretchy, which made them really easy to put on. I could easily put three of my own fingers inside the band to open it wide, and it easily fit over their feet. The bands were big on the 2 week old LF Ameraucana chicks, but not so big that they fell off, and they're still comfortably wearing the same bands now 8 days later. I anticipate that when it's time to remove them and put on a larger band I won't have any issues due to how stretchy they are! I am really happy with these, and would definitely recommend as a VERY easy way to mark LF chicks from around 2 weeks old!

title: Like, the best pens EVER!!!
text: My favorite pens EVER!  I tend to be a heavy writer and fine point pens just don't work as well for me.  I'm partial to thick lines that don't indent or scratch the paper as I write with with no missed spots of ink because the roller ball refused to roll since I press down when I write.  These pens deliver what I need; smooth, even lines with no indents, blobs, or irritation at how they (don't) work well enough.  These pens are the best I've ever found (for me) to write with.  Enough so that I hid the box so the rest of my family can't take them and I refuse to allow anyone to use/borrow the one I carry with me.  I realize how that sounds and I promise I'm not really a weirdo, huddling in the corner, holding on my preciousss, while warning others away.  Mostly.  It's just, they really are that good and definitely worth what I consider a rather exorbitant amount of money for a disposable pen.  I disagree with some other reviewers however; the ink doesn't dry immediately so it can smear - A LITTLE - but it's not so bad that it's all over the paper and can be circumvented by patience as long a you aren't a lefty.  Most people will never even notice or be bothered by how a writing utensil functions.  I do, probably more than I should, but whatever.  These pens are fabulous for me because they allow me to avoid that teeny-tiny irritation I get when I am forced to use an inferior pen.

title: Skipping is an issue initially... and it doesn't go away. Frustrating.
text:
Gorgeous, but I didn't want this pen to just look at it. I expected it to lay down ink when I wrote with it, and that hasn't been the case. Skips, and kind of inexplicable skips. Hard to get the ink flowing again after just a few seconds. Sometimes the flow would stop in mid-stroke. I did not anticipate being disappointed with this pen.

Nicely balanced, fits in the hand (I could stand a slightly larger pen). The cartridge was very easy to install, and once I got it to write things were going well for a short time. I set the pen down for a moment and returned to find it dry. So I tried various tricks to get the ink flowing again, mostly involving saliva and swearing in alternating yet equal amounts. I tried various kinds of paper I had on hand, from very nice smooth sketch book paper to printer paper to junk mail envelopes. The. Pen. Skips.

Hours later: I've picked up the pen and written with it several times over the past few hours, and stored it point-down for a while. Given it a couple of shakes hoping that would get the ink flowing between the cartridge and the nib. Less skipping. I ran across a web page and suggests using the edge of a piece of paper and fitting it between the blades on the nib. Haven't gone that far yet. Now the pen seems as happy as a clam in mud at high tide. Maybe it just requires some breaking in?

I'll keep evaluating the pen. If it writes, I'm happy. If it skips, there's a problem. Especially if you considering giving this pen as a gift. You'd want it to write when the recipient went to use it.

---

The top fits over the lip on the bottom, so it doesn't rattle and everything fits. You have to turn the reasonably strong (ie not punched out of tin) key to fasten the top, however, which seems goofy. If you don't, the top will hang open if you try and pick up the box by its handle. You'd expect a clasp of some kind which contained the lock. I probably should knock off a star from the rating for this design decision. But overall the box functions just fine. There's a built-in set of channels to hold standard hanging folders, not just a mess of file folders. But the fact that you need to throw the lock in order to pick it up leaves me scratching my head.

text:
I have no existing physical issues that drove me to get one of these. My SUV is twelve years old, and I still love it, and keeps going and going, except for the front seats. The great leather on the seats is fine except for the driver and passenger seat bottoms. I don't want seat covers, I just want cushions to make the seats last. As I studied the chair cushions on Amazon, I went with this one, after reading the reviews.

At first I thought I ended up with a booster seat! I was sitting way too high, and I didn't think I would like it. But I found it was backwards! lol

Once you get it right, the gap part in the back, and bring the Everlasting Comfort near the front edge seat so that it's right behind your bent knees, IT IS AWESOME!! Your butt sinks to where you are at a normal height, that's great! I felt like my butt and my thighs are hovering above the seat because there is no more hard surface under your body. The tailbone is suspended in air, and put all of that together, driving is really comfortable now. I just flew across the country, and the airline seats are really hard, and I kept regretting that I didn't bring the cushion!

Nobody bought this for me, I bought it, and I'm getting two more, one for the passenger seat, and one for my desk chair at home. If my car's seats hadn't worn out, I may never known about this cushion. But I'm glad they did! This little guy is wonderful!

title: These labels are great and would get a 5-star review if it weren't ...
text:
These labels are great and would get a 5-star review if it weren't for the TONS of time, ink and paper wasted on the included template. I downloaded the design software as suggested by Avery. Easy to obtain from their website and very easy to design what you want on the label. Avery suggests printing a trial on their template. This is where things went wrong.

I spent HOURS trying to get the labels to line up with the template. Thankfully I finally realized just leaving the template in the scanning bed of my multi-function printer and making a copy and telling my computer to print from the other paper tray (it's times like this I love, love, LOVE my HP Officejet 8600 Premium with not one but TWO paper trays!) so I didn't have to keep manually feeding the original through the auto-feeder. Anyway, on to the template complaints...

Seriously, I kid you not when I say I spent hours on these labels trying to figure out why I could NOT get them to print centered. I dug around on the internet trying to find ways to align my printer thinking it was the problem and found nothing. I printed templates every way I could think of thinking perhaps the alignment was somehow off when those were copying/printing but no, they were just fine. I literally broke this down and eliminated every possible variable in the equation before finally deciding to just risk it and print out a sheet of the actual labels.

Guess what! Yes, they printed. Centered and all! What's wrong here? The template provided by Avery is JUNK! Just make sure you perfectly center your design in the software! I recommend printing just label #1 through 1 so you're not wasting a bunch of ink if for some reason you have a disaster. If the first one is good, cross your fingers and go for it on an entire sheet!

I sure wish I had read all of the other reviews saying the same thing about the template before wasting half of a day trying to figure out what I was doing wrong. It wasn't me!!

title: Does not come with an AC adapter, wastes some label space
text:
I had experience with brother label makers at work and there they were a poor substitute for the $100 label makers that are usually made for such applications. I bought this on sale for myself expecting poor results, but this turned out to be better than expect. The sample label cartridge tape back comes in two parts and were much easier to remove than the single backed paper that I had used previously. What used to be the hardest part of making labels, is now easy.

What surprised me at first was that there was no AC adapter included. This was not a big deal and it is actually in the description (now that I actually read it), so I put in six AAA batteries in.

The only downside so far is that this seems to waste label space. I usually expect all label makers to waste some space, usually at the begging, end or both. But when you're printing multiple label copies at once there is usually less waste between each one. But not here. Printing multiple copies at once it inexplicably gives the same spacing between each label. So if one label looked like this [---label---] multiple labels will look like this [---label---][---label---][---label---]. This is not the case with my $100 work label maker, which might waste space if printing one at time will not do so when printing multiple labels at once, the end result looking more like [---label-][-label-][-label---].

On the bright side the label cartridges are cheap (in contrast to my $100 work label maker cartridges which are three times as much) so the wasted label space is not a big deal. But I would not use this for work, it just does not have enough features.

The $100 work label maker I was referring to is actually this model [[ASIN:B00IELD1O4 Brady BMP21-PLUS Handheld Label Printer with Rubber Bumpers, Multi-Line Print, 6 to 40 Point Font]]

My experience with inkjet refilling has not been the same. I had inconsistent results even though I supposedly followed the same method. Definitely no more worries about cartridge memory and dry print heads. I got rid of my inkjet printer and will stick to this process from now on.

I figured this label maker would be better, but I was surprised by how much. The labels are much higher quality, I do not have to struggle with peeling the labels off the backing any more. When I make a mistake in positioning, I can just peel the label off without it degrading. The best feature is that labelling cables is now easy and produces a professional looking results.

We still have the brother label maker, but considering how much easier this is to use we just leave it behind.

The downsides to this thing is that it's rather large. The accessories are expensive and the only case available is the expensive and bulky hard case. title: Works great but wifi setup was more painful than it needed to be.
text:
I love Canon printers. They last forever if treated right. The last one I got was in 2011. I had to buy this one because a family member broke the print head of my last Canon printer while they were trying to clear a paper jam from the wrong place...

This printer works great, it prints quickly, great quality images and prints, easy cartridge loading and the scans are in better resolution than my last Canon printer! Love it.

The only thing I didn't like was the wifi setup. I'm pretty tech savy, but I could not get the easy wifi setup to work. I tried a desktop hard wired to the router and a laptop that was connected to the router via wifi. Both cases I could not get the easy-wifi screen to show during the setup phase on the PC.

So I ended up having to do a manual entry on the printer it self. Idk why, but they made manually entering text as un-intuitive as you could possibly make it. It was like texting on a late 90s flip phone but worse. But eventually I got it to work and everything all set. Thankfully you only have to do this wifi setup once. For this I had to take away one star. Canon, please look into your software or at least make manual character entry a bit more sane.

title: Great printer - loving it
text:
I got so tied of buying inkjet printers time and time again only to have them die after a couple years of use from slew of issues I almost never print out photos so color printing isn't a huge deal to me. So I decided to pony up the cash for a decent toner-based all in one printer. My hope being that I can get away from the constant problems I had with inkjets headers always clogging on me and the ink packs never getting me very far. MAN did I choose well, this printer is great.

I can print out a page in 3 secs flat and subsequent pages in 1 sec. That's faster than every inkjet I've ever owned. The print quality is perfect. Very crisp.

The double sided printing is fantastic. It doesn't drastically slow down the printing process like most injets. The quickest inkjet I owned did double sided printing at a rate of about 22 sec per sheet. This printer manages about 4 secs per double sided sheet.

Setup is stupid easy. You can tell a modest amount of care went into the software and on screen steps of the printer. I was able to connect the printer to my laptop and PC in about 20 mins (60% of which was me getting use to the button controls).

One thing that would be nice here is a full qwerty keyboard for entering in wifi passwords. The old school texting style works but hard to get use to. But at the same time that's a lot to manufacture for a tool that's only used once in a blue moon. So I can get that design choice.

Scanning is nice and quick too. Very good quality, no complaints there.

I'm very happy with this printer. I'll check back in 6 months for an update as to how things are holding up. I'm interested to see if my toner cartridge lives up to the specs!

title: LOVE this Punchless Binder
text: I bought this punchless binder to keep some important medical papers in. So far, I'm happy with it. The only slight issue is, it can be a little challenging to figure out how to open and close the binder. My binder did not come with directions and I was afraid of moving the closure too quickly and breaking it. Fortunately that did not happen and I figured out how to open and close the binder. I like the bright blue color, the side pocket that holds additional lose papers or business cards and the ability to have all the papers closely clipped together so you won't lose them.

title: Beautiful colored snapping folders
text:
This product comes with six different folders. Two folders are a baby blue color with a white grid design, two folders are pink with purple short lines and two folders are an orangish/pink color with some letter designs on the outside. Each of the folders comes with a snap tab to close and keep your documents safe. They also come with a small piece of paper inside, which I assumed was possibly to use to put in front of any documents you did not want anyone reading through the slightly transparent folders, or to keep safe during the shipment.

The folders are quite pretty and a nice way to hold pieces of paper or documents. However, they are not quite large enough to hold a tabbed folder. My one wish for these folders is that they were just a bit thicker. I'm not sure how well the clasp will hold up and will look forward to seeing how long they last.

Again, lovely folders and they go very well with the Yoobi 12 piece tabbed folders - just not possible to put a tabbed folder inside, unless you cut the tab off. Which in retrospect- if you have sensitive information and you want to keep it safe, this would be a good way to store it, as the folder (minus the tab) would fit easily into the tabbed folder and keep your documents safe from prying eyes.

title: Beautiful folders to get organized with!
text: I'm in the process of getting organized and fell in love with these folders. The files are quite pretty and come in a package of 12 folders. Four folders are a light pink with purple lines and purple tabs, four folders are an orange color with an orange sherbet colored tab and symbols on the folder, and four folders are a combination of the orange, orange sherbet color and pinkish purple and purple. The colors are lovely, the only issue I had, which made me mark them down from a 5 to a 4 was the sturdiness of the folders. My folders arrived and the tabs were slightly dented in and the top folder had white showing through the end of the purple tab. Again, lovely colors, great if you're looking to organize your office and looking for some nice, pretty folders, but at this point a little unsure of their overall stability, since they arrived slightly damaged.

The only problem I had was one of the small magnets came out of my orange dry erase marker after taking it off of the fridge 2 or 3 times. Other than that I am fully satisfied with this product. Initially, It takes a little bit of scribbling to get the markers working. The erasers work very well and all the markers conveniently have them on their caps. Erasing is a breeze and I don’t see smudged residue if I erase with a little bit of pressure.

Edit: If you allow the ink to dry and remain on the board for longer than a day or two it is a bit difficult to wipe the writing off. The markers leave minor color on the board but it wipes off easily if you clean the board with water and a rag.

Compared to my Corsair MM350 this one is about half the thickness, and compared to my SteelSeries QCK+ XXL its about 1/3. title: Great set if you like the brush tip markers, complements other Hand Lettering set
text:
If you are a fan of calligraphy and hand lettering this is a great set, it includes primarily brush tip markers in cool colors, one chisel tip and one .05mm nib illistration marker. Also includes a 2H turq pencil for sketching and a magic rub eraser.

If you already have the other Prismacolor Hand Lettering set (with yellow background on the box) this set is a nice complement to it, as there is very little overlap between the two sets (only the chisel tip and .05mm marker). Even the pencil and eraser are different between the two sets (yellow set contains a 2B pencil and kneaded eraser, this set contains 2H pencil and magic rub eraser)

For beginners I would probably recommend the other set to start with instead of this one because the brush tip markers have a steeper learning curve to use well than other types, and this set only has one size chisel tip and no flat tip markers. Both this one and the other hand lettering set offer a great assortment of tools though, I don't think you can go wrong with either one!

title: Pen/ink are mediocre but still a nice gift set for beginners
text:
Pros:
-Very nice gift packaging, excellent presentation
-Nice assortment of items, I like that it includes both cartridges and bottled ink
-Ink dries faster and bleeds through less than most fountain pen inks
-Jotter pen has a very nice upscale look despite being Parkers most affordable fountain pen
-Excellent cartridge system with larger cartridges than other brands and a reliable secure fit in the nib

Cons:
-Ink lacks boldness of other fountain pen inks
-Ink is very fussy about type of paper used, moreso than any other ink I've used
-Medium handwriting nib doesn't feel as smooth as my others
-Pen feels too light and grip is too small, uncomfortable
-Limited selection of replacement nib styles

If you are looking for an impressive looking gift set for a beginner fountain pen user, or someone you think may be interested in fountain pens.. then this is a great choice. Everything contained within has a very high build quality and top notch aesthetics, it looks like a much more expensive pen than it is. If you are more concerned about function than form however I would suggest you look at other brands, as the writing performance of Parkers pens and inks aren't quite up to par with others in the industry in my opinion (even their very expensive models)

I like hand lettering and calligraphy so I have a number of different fountain pens and nibs from Pilot, LAMY, Manuscript, Jinhao, etc.. While the jotter is not necessarily a bad pen, I would definitely say it is my least favorite of all the pens I have. Despite its metal construction it is lighter in weight than many of my plastic bodied pens and while I love its sleek looks I find it uncomfortable to hold due to its small/thin grip.

I also have mixed feelings about Parker's quink ink.. as the 'qu' prefix implies it is a quick drying ink. As a lefty who has to be very vigilant against smudges, I do appreciate that it dries quicker than other fountain pen inks and that it doesn't bleed through paper as much. However, their quick drying formulation comes at the cost of being less bold/saturated than other inks and also being more sensitive to the type of paper you are writing on. If you have used fountain pens before you will know that all of them are somewhat sensitive to the type of paper.. but this parker ink is by far the most sensitive I have ever seen. On some papers with poor wicking characteristics it basically won't write at all, and on others it looks very janky and fuzzy due to bleed out. If you use the right paper, the performance is pretty good and it lays down smooth but still doesn't have the same saturation/boldness as other inks I have.

title: Good mouse pad but not my favorite

I also have a steelseries QCK XXL mousepad which is basically the same dimensions as this one on my other computer, and I prefer the steelseries since it has normal flat edges (and I've had that one for like 4 years with no problems so I'm not really worried about it fraying).  Also, this corsair pad did have a really strong chemical smell upon first arriving, it had to air out for several days before it totally went away.. never had a mousepad with that problem before.

title: Good starter set with great ergonomics
text:
This is a great beginner sewing set with pretty much everything you need for measuring and cutting. Fiskars has a reputation for making quality cutting tools with good ergonomics and this set lives up to their reputation. The scissors and thread snips are both very sharp and easy to use. The ruler and sewing gauge are both well made, pliable but not too flimsy, with lots of markings for measuring anything you need.

The seam ripper is especially awesome as I've never seen another seam ripper with an ergonomic handle before, I have several other seam rippers and they are all notably less comfortable to hold compared to this one!

The only thing in this set that is somewhat disappointing is the measuring tape, it works fine but its small round design is somewhat awkward to hold, and you can't lay it flat on anything for marking.. also when you retract it, it retracts *really* fast and can slap you or pinch your finger if you aren't careful.

If you are looking to get started with sewing and need these essentials then this is a great kit and recommended.

title: Quality markers, but only 3 colors.. not 6
text:
Sharpie metallic markers are great for marking on a variety of surfaces just like normal Sharpie markers but with an added metallic effect which makes them pop on darker surfaces especially. One thing to note with these is that unlike normal Sharpies they must be stored vertically with the cap facing down or else they will dry out relatively quickly.

My only qualm with this product is that we only recieved 3 colors (Emerald, Sapphire and Ruby) whereas the product images make it appear that all 6 variety of metallic Sharpie are included. The Silver and Gold metallic sharpies are my favorite so I was bummed that they were not included.. but reading the product description more carefully it does indicate that only Emerald, Sapphire and Ruby are in the 36ct. set. The images are misleading though, so do take that into consideration and read the description carefully if you are looking at the 36 ct. set.

title: Functional and attractive printer for Small Business or Home Office
text:
This printer has all the features you'd expect from a small-business focused unit. I haven't used the fax feature but the scanning works well and the printing is top notch. Set-up was very easy, install the toner cartridge, plug it in, set up wifi and it was recognized as a network printer by my computers right away with no need for installing drivers (Windows 10 devices, may require drivers on other platforms). I especially like that the touchpad swivels, makes it very easy to use whether the printer is placed on a high shelf or at desktop/counter height.

My only issue with the printer is that when power save mode is on it occasionally will not wake up from sleep properly and has to be manually restarted by holding down the power button for 5 seconds to restore the network functionality (Scanning and printing via cable still works, but the wifi networking will not function until it is power cycled). This doesn't seem to happen if eco/power save mode is disabled. I'm not sure if this problem is a hardware issue with my specific unit or a firmware issue but for now I'm just running it with power save mode off.

Aside from that one issue, this is a solid printer with a very attractive design, it's a fairly large printer but looks very sleek and attractive compared to our old Panasonic all-in-one printer which was boxy and beige.

As such, it is only really useful on heavier items that are not very dense and provide a lot of surface area to spread the product out on. title: Lasted 14 months
text:
Update: 5/17/22 I contacted the seller, and after sending pictures and answering questions about the use, location, etc., they wrote me back and noted that I had placed the wheels of under desk file cabinets on the mat, which I should not have done. Also, the carpet's thickness was a little too thick for this mat, and I should have ordered the mat for a plush carpet. However, they would replace it for no charge. Which they did, and it arrived today.
I consider the carpet a low profile, but it must have contributed to the cracking, etc.
The Company responded quickly to my emails. They took the time to review in detail my pictures etc. And they sent a new mat even though I was past the warranty limit. A high 5 for good customer service and standing behind the products they sell.
Thus, I am raising my rating to a 4 and suggesting to all who buy a mat for carpet thicker than glue down to buy the plush carpet mat. It is only a few dollars more, and I suspect it will last. If this one fails, that is my plan. And I will be buying it from these folks.

For the first 12 months, it worked fine. The mat is on wall-to-wall low pile carpet on a standard rather thin carpet pad. I use a 5-wheeled office chair. It is at my desk and is used a good part of each day. About the 12th month, I heard a crack and looked down to see a small crack under one of the front wheels. It is now April, just about 14 months since the purchase, and there are numerous cracks with the first one that I heard and then saw, about 8 inches long with a small chunk broken out. The chair pad is fast becoming unusable.
I am very disappointed to have a $100 pad breaking up in less than 15 months. It was installed as directed. Used as expected for an office pad. If you are looking for a chair pad that will last for longer than a year with daily use, this may not be the appropriate choice.

title: Excellent 3 year pocket calendar
text: I have had the one year calendar by the same folks and love it. This three year one will fit my needs better but with all the quality, size, and features I need. It is compact, sturdy, filled with features and good looking as well. A month on two facing pages, an elastic band to keep you on your month, and two cords to let you go forwards or backward to mark other months. Plenty of note pages plus an envelope type space at the back to carry cards, notes, etc. To top it off the cover material looks like real leather and it has a convenient pen holder on the side. These folks have thought of everything for a very good price.

title: Why didn't someone think of this sooner?
text: I have used pocket-sized monthly planners for a number of years. The combination of features in this one is perfect. A two-page spread for the month which is where I start and then a weekly set of pages follow. So the picture of the month is ready and the details are recorded in the following day spaces. But it doesn't stop with just the layout. There are taps for the months, marker cords to help you get to a specific page quickly, a leather type cover that looks and feels very real. A small pocket in the back and of course the pages for notes, addresses, the preceding and following year calender, special dates, etc. They are all there in a well made, not too large, pocket planner. But wait...and the price is half I have been paying for a flimsy plastic cover, monthly only, no note pages, cheap-looking, and poorly made one. If I could give this one 5+ stars I would. Hope they will continue to make these for years to come.

title: Comfy chair, easy assembly, attractive finished product
text:
Assembly was super easy and straightforward, I followed the instructions, but if you've put together office chairs before, you already know what goes where. I didn't time it, but it couldn't have taken more than 10-15mins to assemble, and that's only using the provided tool - if you have a power driver w/ hex bits, you can easily shave 5mins off that estimate.
Once assembled, the chair looks very nice and elegant/clean and the color of the cushion looks like it won't show stains easily.
It's a bit on the narrow side, but with a weight rating of 250lbs, I'd say it's just right. I tested it out and it held my bulk without trouble, though I wouldn't feel comfortable using this regularly due to being 35lbs over the limit. The back is comfy - I much prefer mesh to padded; and the backwards lean is just right, enough to shift position but not enough you'll feel like you're going to go head over heels.
I bought this for my mom (a school teacher), so she'll both be using it a lot and getting in and out of it constantly - if there's anything extra or special to note (good or bad) I'll add an update.

title: Excellent labels
text:
Phomemo is my fav brand for labels because of ones like these. They're plastic base (waterproof) and the thermal coating is extra rich. The label size is nice for a lot of applications and it's surprisingly bigger than I anticipated.
Price is great for 300 waterproof labels.
Protip - you can use these in other thermal printers, you just need to convert the rolls to smaller ones. You can use a drill with a dowel to make your own rolls at any diameter. Just make a split in the end of the dowel to hold the labels (using tape is a nightmare) and be sure to roll in the correct direction.

text:

The surface material is soft on bare feet and the size of the mat is just the right width to keep under both feet and long enough you can slide forward and keep your feet on it or slide back and keep the chairs rollers on it.

title: Not supported by Play Store

I do not want to put a 3rd party app on any of my personal devices and I'm not buying a burner just to use.

title: Excellent entry level green laser
text:
10mW seems just right to see the beam in a well lit, indoor environment. It's extremely clear at night (astronomy for instance). The actual dot is bright!
The built in kaleidoscope in the cap is pretty cool, but I wish the cap was easier to remove (manufacturer - please use magnets next time).
I'd prefer a USB-c port for charging, but the built-in usb-a works fine. It needs a battery meter. And the button is a terrible design - if you lose the button guard, there's nothing to keep it from turning on in a pocket or bag. I'd greatly prefer a switch or smart button. A tripod receiver would also be awesome.

title: Big upgrade to plastic storage bags
text:
I typically use zipper freezer bags for storing small / multi-part things, but I started using these and they're SO much better.
The zippers are really tough (I'm not gentle). The bag is a closed mesh, so they'll keep things clean & dry. The mesh is light enough I can still read labels through it. It's pliable and easy to fold around cases.
The size is just right for documents and most small/medium electronics. Colors included are both varied and attractive and make organizing easier.
Definitely buying a 2nd set when I've made use of the ones I have.

title: Poly labels are so much better
text:
Waterproof is the obvious biggest advantage, but poly is also nearly impossible to tear, and removes easily in one piece, usually without leaving residue behind.
Print quality was better than expected on the printer used - black is nice and dark. The roll is not perforated.
Labels fit in my printer great after converting (rerolling). The roll is too big around for a mini-printer, but it's really easy to convert your own mini rolls using an electric screwdriver and a dowel (put a split in the dowel to hold the paper, tape is just a pain).

title: Built better than I anticipated
text: The case construction feels really solid & durable. The plastic coated wire is a great alternative to chain-link or uncoated, braided wire. I haven't pushed it to breaking, but I was able to pull pretty roughly on it without problem. The spring is strong enough to hold a multitool or keys without them pulling themselves out. The little triangular clasp that holds the badge holder and keyring in place opens up easily enough, so I was able to attach tools directly to that, bypassing the extra length of the keyring. If I need another set of retractable leashes, I'll be coming back to this listing.

title: Disappointing for what it could be.
text:
The hardware seems great, but it's unusable without the app, and the companion app sucks - options are extremely limited (*), I can't import static or gif images, and it doesn't support any type of live data transmission (time & temp for instance).
(*) For entered text, there's only 1 font, and emoji support is sketchy. Animations for text are reminiscent of welcome signs from the 90s. For all customization, there're only 7 color options, despite it appearing to be RGB. Custom "art" is building a panel, pixel by pixel, and animations are stacks of these.... I can't art worth a darn, so doing anything custom will require a Minecraft-art app and a few hours of time.
There are a few things I can use this for, but to really have fun, be creative, and (most importantly) get customer's attention, I'll be needing something much better.

title: Effective but not great
text:
Should really be listed as a receipt printer - it doesn't get hot enough for dark print on labels. The "calibration" for the labels doesn't work to line them up, it prints slightly askew, and there's a weird pattern to the printed areas. Printed sample pics are receipt paper (dark one) and labels, I've also attached the original screenshot for comparison. Like most of these printers, there's no driver, so you can't print directly from word/chrome/etc - you have to screen shot what you want printed then bring the pic into the printer software, which is a lot more annoying than the manufacturers will admit.
This is useful in the meantime, but I'm still looking for a "good" portable thermal printer.

I will probably find a way to pack it, but it is quite large and will be difficult to slip into my backpack for my next flight. title: Good shredder with a couple of minor issues
text:
I rarely have opportunity to give less than 5 stars to an Amazon basics product, but this one isn't quite as good as some of there other products. The main problems I have with this shredder are that the bin seems quite small. The other problem is that shredded paper often sticks in the bottom of the shredder, causing the shredder to keep running. When that happens, you have to manually turn it off, pick up the shredder head and pull the paper out. It seems to happen more if there is paper in the bin that it does when it's empty. Heavier paper also causes the problem.

On a good note, it has plenty of power and does an excellent job of shredding. I have shredded CDs, DVDs, credit cards, and paper as it is advertised to do and it does it without any problems (except for what I mentioned above). Overall I'm happy enough with it not to send it back, but there could be some improvements.

title: PROBLEMS FROM THE START BUt GOOD CIDYOMER SERVICE
text:
This is my second B4600 printer. My first one presented few problems. The support service was excellent in the case of the few calls I had to make. I replaced it when the drum wore out.
The newer model B4600 has been very disappointing. While I have had it for a long time, it has been used little. After a few months, I began to get spurious messages that there was a paper jam. Since this was intermittent, the support staff convinced me that these were my fault. I tried different papers and re-loaded the tray. Soon after the warranty period was over, the paper jam messages became increasingly more frequent. The support staff provided different and conflicting messages as to how to fix the problem. I did not want to replace the printer, so I kept using it and, after a period of correct operation, had to open and shut the lid, turn off the printer-- whatever changes worked. Then, one day, I fixed the problem myself-- almost by accident.
All was well for a while, but then ( a month after installing a new toner) I began getting error messages that there was no toner! Oki support then insisted that I had to buy another toner ( cost of $60.) as the one OEM that I had did not work with this printer.
I am now on hold for 50 minutes in trying to reach another person for support!
I don't recommend taking a chance on this printer. There may be some which are as flawless as my first B4600. but, if you get a "lemon" there are endless frustrations ahead.

Addendum:

After emailing Support with details of my dilemma I received an almost immediate call from Customer Service. They are mailing out a replacement toner cartridge and assure me that this should fix the latest problem.

I was pleased that my problem was listened to and understood.

They even over-nighted the part.

Thus, I am adding a couple of stars
