My previous Canon printer had none of these features and was significantly more cumbersome to use. Actual printing and scanning performance is fine for this price level, but not super-sharp in either area. The printer is fine for home and school use

title: budget-quality holiday cards with fancy lined envelopes
text: These are budget-quality holiday cards. The paper isn't real thick or glossy or colorfully printed. Size is smaller than expected for this price and quality level. There is lots of blank space inside the card for writing a personal note. The envelopes are are lined, making them fancier than the cards themselves.

title: medium quality Christmas cards
text: These are Hallmark's budget-quality Christmas cards. They are not as large, thick, or glossy as their premium cards, but the price is more reasonable. The ink is shiney and there is some glitter, which some people may find tacky on a Christmas card. These are nicer than the really thin cards that you find for cheap prices at discount stores. 3.5 stars, considering price and value.

title: [rollerball pen] very nice luxury pen, better for people with smaller fingers
text: Pens come in a variety of weights and diameters. At this price range, I advise that you buy somewhere that lets you try the pen out before buying to see if it is comfortable for you. This pen is thinner than other luxury pens that I have tried, perhaps making it better for people with smaller fingers. It has a nice balance and weight to it; it has a solid feel without being too heavy. The pen is beautiful and build quality is excellent, as I expect at this price. The ink flows flawlessly, as I expect from Waterman. Refills are not cheap, but not so expensive that I would be tempted to use inferior generics.  This is a great pen to have at my desk, either at home or at work. At this price, I'm not going to carry it around with me and risk losing it.

title: expensive, easy to install on my HP M253 printer, works perfectly
text: This toner is pricey, but should last last a long time. Very easy to install on my HP M253 printer - open the door, pull the old cartridge out, and drop the new one in. Works great with sharp dark black printing.

title: [Mickey Mouse Clubhouse] pricey but cute for a special Mickey Mouse fan
text: The Mickey Mouse Clubhouse card is an average quality birthday card with a built-in audio player that sings a short song. It's a cute attention grabber for a special kid. Don't know how long it will last before the battery gives out, but the child will probably be bored with it by then.

title: budget-priced drawing set for students and artists more than professional engineers and architects
text: This is a functional portable plastic drawing board with a decent set of plastic drawing tools.  When I think of "drafting", I think of professional drawings for architects and civil engineers where accuracy is extremely important. This set is not really professional quality, but it may be OK for quick field drawings. It is good for students, especially if they need to carry it to class. It is also great for artists who will use the tools more for assistance than for precision.

title: [ADS1250W] very fast clear scans, hard to keep paper straight, not too hard to install on Microsoft Windows
text:
This is a nice compact scanner. Great for desktop use when you have limited space. Also great for travel, although a carrying case is not included.

Installing the scanner took some time. I am using this on Windows 10. I had to install Windows drivers as well as desktop client software (hundreds of MB total, so this will take a lot of time if you have slow internet). Then I had to upgrade the firmware in the scanner. Make sure you use Microsoft administrator mode to install the firmware. The Brother software tool reminds you about administrator mode constantly, but Microsoft Windows doesn't make this mode real easy to find. I use the scanner wirelessly and the Brother installation software guided me through the steps for setting this up (not hard, but there are a lot of steps).

Once the software is installed, the scanner is easy to use. I created a desktop shortcut using the Brother desktop app with my favorite settings (150dpi JPEG to save space, full color mode since monochrome doesn't work very well, save to a new folder on my PC). I can drop a stack of papers into the scanner and run the shortcut and all the papers are scanned and uploaded into my folder in a surprisingly fast amount of time. The scans are all sharp and clear. The scanner is smart enough to produce sharp black text on a white background (when my source documents look like that), not an ugly gray background like older scanners often do. If you are scanning more than a couple of papers, this auto-feet is tremendously faster than a manual flatbed scanner. My main complaint is that scanned documents are not always perfectly straight (which is usually easy to do with a flatbed scanner). The scanned files often have crooked black borders that are cumbersome to edit out (by rotating and cropping the images in a photo editor).

The scanner also has lots of fancy modes to upload your scans to network servers or email directly from the scanner. Those modes may be useful in an office environment, but at home I always want to upload to a folder on my PC.

title: nice hard-cover surveying book for the price
text: This a very nice surveying book for the price. Heavy smooth paper is easy to write on and doesn't bleed. Paper has printed columns on the left-side pages and printed grid on the right-side pages, as shown in the photo. Heavy hard covers are very sturdy to protect your book even after you fill it up and shelve it. A few pages of engineering formulas are printed at the end for people who still read those :-)

title: sturdy 3-pocket portfolios
text: These plastic portfolios are much sturdier than cardboard if you plan to use them regularly. You can't put a lot of sheets in each one, but I would use 3-ring binders for that purpose. Not real fancy looking, but works great for the price.

title: design is kind of clunky and long term durability is questionable, but price is cheap
text: The binder grips my tablet with velcro'ed on plastic corners. The design is kind of clunky and long term durability is questionable. For the $10 price, I suppose I can't complain too much.

title: aspect ratio doesn't work well with Android tablets
text: This case might work OK with ipads, but not so well with Android tablets that usually have a longer aspect ratio. The border of the case hides about 1/3 inch of my screen at the top, which is very annoying since Android system notifications are displayed in that area.

title: great reusable adhesive tabs
text: These tabs are great. Easy to apply. Adhesive is secure enough to cling to paper, but also peels off easily with no residue or damage and they are sturdy enough to reuse. I use them to organize my sheet music in music classes. I suppose you can also use them in cookbooks, reference books, etc.

title: very good budget-quality binders
text: These are good budget-quality binders. The covers are not as thick and sturdy as better binders. The clasp holds securely and I like the offset design that opens at the top so your papers are less likely to fall out accidentally. There are full-sized clear plastic pockets on the front and back and smaller pockets inside. The inner pockets are too small for holding much, but the outer ones are great for cover sheets. For the price, these binders are fine.

title: small block erasers are less than half the size as the large erasers, why is the price the same?
text: The small colored block erasers are less than half the size of the larger white block erasers. According to my kitchen scale, the small eraser is 12 grams vs 28 grams for the large eraser. Both sizes cost about the same 45 cents per eraser ($2.80 for 6 small erasers or $1.90 for 4 large erasers). Both work great for cleanly erasing pencil writing on paper without damaging the paper. I don't see any reason to buy the smaller size unless your pencil case is really space-limited or price gougers are charging much higher prices for the large erases than the big box stores are charging.

title: very nice binder for 2-hole punched papers
text: If you use 2-hole paper, this is a very nice 2-ring binder. Just be aware that it only has 2 rings and is not compatible with the more common 3-hole punched paper.

title: nice slim relatively inexpensive field book
text: This is a nice slim relatively inexpensive field book. Cover is a somewhat stiff, somewhat flexible coated cardboard; not hard cover like some notebooks. Paper is durable, but not real thick. Grid lines are great for graphs and columns of numbers. 32 sheets of paper makes for a slim book that fills up quickly, but easily fits in a jacket pocket with minimal bulk.

title: lightweight plastic body looks and feels cheap to me
text: This pen comes in a nice gift box and it writes very smoothly, but narrow diameter and lightweight plastic body make it look and feel very cheap to me. Long writing sessions with this pen are not comfortable for me, though maybe someone with smaller or less strong fingers may prefer it. If I were to buy a pen for myself or give one as a gift, there are many nice looking solid metal pens in this price range with smooth-writing ink cartridges.

title: good weight and stiffness, ballpoint writing does not bleed through, made in the USA
text: These are good index cards. The cards have a good weight and stiffness. Ballpoint pen writing does not bleed through. Writing with a Sharpie is slightly visible from the other side, but it does not smear on the front of the card. The 3 pack includes 3 packs of 100 cards, each pack individually plastic wrapped. Made in the USA.

title: [starter set] nice cheap pencils if you like very thick lines, great to have spare leads and erasers included in the set
text: 1.3mm leads give you a thick line (most pencils are 0.5 or 0.7mm thickness). I use these pencils when I have to read my writing from a distance, eg notes on sheet music. The pencils look cheap, but they work well and seem durable enough. Including the extra pack of leads is great since Amazon doesn't sell these leads in single packs (only 6-packs, which is too much for personal use). The extra erasers are handy, but I wish they gave us 5 for the 5 pencils instead of just 2.

title: Very handy eraser if you make a lot of small mistakes
text:
Very handy erasers for correcting small pencil mistakes. You have to hold the eraser at an angle and use the corner of the tip; the click mechanism doesn't grip well enough when try to erase holding it completely upright. Erases very clean without damaging your paper like the abrasive pink erasers do. We got the 3-pack with black, red, blue holders (the erasers themselves are all white). For some reason, this 3-color pack for $3 is much cheaper than the 3-black or the blue-pink-purple pack that Amazon also sells. For bigger erasing jobs, the bigger Pentel rectangular block erasers are lot easier to use.

Refills are available, but they are so expensive on Amazon that you may as well buy 3-pack of new erases for $3 total and discard your old holders.

title: fun bright colored printer labels
text: This is a fun kit. You get 2 sheets each of 5 different bright colors, with 15 labels pre-cut on each sheet (each label is 2 inches  x 2 5/8 inches). Blank ink prints best on these bright paper colors. You can use Avery's website to print your labels or download templates for Microsoft Word or Adobe Photoshop or Illustrator. Avery labels do cost somewhat more than generic labels, but the paper quality is always better (doesn't curl or jam our printer).

title: Thin erasers are great for small corrections.
text: Thin erasers are great for small corrections. We also have bigger Pentel erasers for large scale erasing. Pentel works really great for the price.

title: China-made clone of Sharpies
text: These pens are about the same size and shape as Sharpies, except that the caps are a little different. They work about the same as Sharpies with smooth bold writing. These pens are made in China, while my Sharpies are made in the USA.

title: not as smooth and crisp as gel ink pens, but smoother than most ballpoint pens
text: These pens are OK. They write more smoothly than traditional ballpoint pens, but not as smoothly as the better gel-roller pens that have gotten so popular in recent years (Pilot, Uni-Ball, etc). If you like the look and feel of ballpoint ink on your paper (instead of the super-crisp gel ink look), then these Atlantis pens are worth a try. The ink is less prone to clumping than most ballpoint pens, though it is not as continuously smooth as the gel pens. Pricing for pens jumps around so much from week to week that I will not try to judge value; you can go price shopping for yourself. I do advise that you stick to the name brands, however, since build quality of the off-brands is often very poor.

title: [markers and coloring booklet] clever, if pricey, coloring book kit
text: This is a clever, if pricey, coloring book kit. The pens cost about 50 cents each, so you can judge how much you are paying for the booklet. Ultra-fine Sharpies are great. You get a wide variety of bright colors. The fine points are easy to control and don't bleed much. The coloring book is very small (7x5 inches), but finely detailed, so coloring each sheet does take a while. The book paper is thick enough that the pen ink does not bleed through to the next sheet. The 3D glasses work better for some people than others (not so well for me), but even without them, the finished pictures are bright and cute.

title: great little color laser printer - great print quality, lots of wireless printing options (including from Kindle Fire)
text:
Love this printer so far. Despite all the functionality (wireless printing, double sided printing, color laser printing, etc) size is pretty compact. It is heavy, though (30 pounds), so make sure you have a sturdy desk. Wireless printing lets me print from my laptop, Android smartphone, and Amazon Fire tablet.

Setup is all wireless. Using the screen on the printer, you can enter your WiFi network name and password. Then from a Windows or Apple computer, you can download and run the drivers to configure the printer. The printer didn't respond for me at first, but turning it off then back on fixed the problem.

On my Android smartphone, I installed the "HP Print Service" app from the Google Play store, then I can just share documents to that service and it prints them. The HP app does not exist in the Amazon app store, but the Mopria print service that is pre-installed on the KIndle Fire mostly works. Printing from my PC works normally even though the printer is connected wirelessly (through WiFi).

The printer is very fast. Print quality is crisp and the colors look great. No jams yet with the double-sided printing (cross my fingers).

One small complaint is that the paper tray is very small, especially for a wireless printer that is shared by multiple people. The description says it fits only half of a standard 500 sheet ream and I think that is generous. We use standard 20 pound paper and don't try to put more than 1/3 of the ream in the printer for fear of jamming it.

title: 115 count box is great for families
text: This is a giant box of Sharpies. You get a wide variety of colors, and just as importantly, a wide variety of pen tip sizes. The slimmest ultra-fine tips are a little thicker than a ballpoint pen all the way up to the chisel tip which are marking great for wide areas. Twin-tips save space when you're on the go. Neon colors are great for highlighting. Metallic colors are great for writing on dark backgrounds. 115 pens sounds like a lot, but everyone in our family of 4 uses these and I'm sure we'll use most of them up before the ink dries out. Sharpie pen caps seal well so the ink does not dry out quickly.

title: works great and costs a little more, like all Avery labels
text: Avery labels always cost more, but usually give you more features or better quality than the competition. In this case, I couldn't find any other kraft-paper full-sheet labels. Kraft-paper does give you an interesting look for homemade gifts, etc. You can use the templates on Avery's website to design your labels or just use your favorite graphics editor. Templates aren't that important for full-sheet labels. As with other Avery labels, these rarely jam my printer and the sheets don't curl when I print on them. 4 stars instead of 5 because of the price.

title: good value tablet stand, but may be too big for a 7" or 8" tablet in portrait mode
text: These stands look cheap (and are cheap), but they work OK for the price. Big knobs let you fold the stand easily to carrying it in your bag. Size of the stand is good for a 10" tablet. It is too wide for a 7" tablet in portrait mode (eg while reading books). An 8" tablet is also too small in portrait mode unless it is in a bulky case. The stand is fine for smaller tablets in landscape mode (eg for watching videos).

title: very easy to print curved text on these circular labels by using the Avery website
text: These are great circular printable labels. Kraft paper gives you a more natural look than plain white. The apps and templates on the Avery website let you easily print curved text around the edge of the labels like the labels in the photo. Yes, you can find much cheaper generic labels, but especially for clear and metallic and colored labels, the Avery brand product is noticeably better quality with more durable films that don't warp or curl as much during printing. The curved labels print cleanly and peel off easily without curling.

title: too expensive for everyday use, not for refrigerated items
text: These labels do work, but there are a lot more caveats printed on the package than what you see in the product description. "Not for use in conventional ovens. Condensation can begin the dissolving process. Recommended only for one-time freezer use or for non-refrigerated items.  Store labels in a cool, dry place." Not being able to refrigerate packages with these labels is a huge limitation that is not mentioned on the website. Pricing is also extremely expensive at $15 for the little package of 30 labels. These might be useful in special situations, but not for our everyday use at that price.

title: sturdy chairs, a little expensive, seat height is low compared to our other office chairs
text: We ordered a single chair. It came in a huge cardboard box with no internal padding. The box was pretty beat up in shipping, but the chair is fine. It is ready to use out of the box with no assembly required. The chair is sturdy and stable, with a deep base so you can sit back comfortably. The plastic seat has a matte finish which is harder to clean than smooth plastic, but maybe more scratch resistant and less slippery to sit on. The only issue we have with these chairs is perhaps a personal preference. The seat height is advertised as 17 inches, but the seat is at the front where it is highest. The seat slopes down towards the back and is only 15.5" high at the back. Other chairs in our office have seat heights that are 1" or 2" higher, so people used to the higher chairs will feel awkward at the shorter chairs, especially when seated at a desk or table.

title: easy enough to scan 35mm slides, but image quality is mediocre
text: We have a bunch of Kodachrome and Ektachrome 35mm slides from back in the day. The slides still look great when viewed on a light table. I had tried scanning them into my computer using a home-quality flatbed scanner, but aligning and cropping the images was such a hassle that I got bored quickly. This Wolverine film scanner takes care of the aligning and cropping with the mechanical slide scanning mechanism. Unfortunately, the image quality is mediocre, even compared to the flatbed scanner. Contrast and dynamic range are both poor so images look washed out and grainy. The scanner has some basic exposure adjustments, but they don't help much. The user interface is clunky, but there are so few features that you can probably figure it out from the user manual. If you need a few quick-and-dirty scans to put up on your family blog or website, then this may be OK. If you're trying to preserve rare family photos, you should also look into professional slide scanning, which can be reasonably priced.

title: teenager is disappointed by very limited customization capability
text: The teenage daughter was not impressed by this "customizable" binder. From the description, she was expecting a regular view binder with templates allowing her to completely customize the graphics on the front, back, and spine of the binder. Instead, we got a basic-quality binder that is pre-printed with various emoji and a pocket on the front that allows you to insert a photo or print out one of the images from the Avery website. See attached photo. This may be interesting to a small child with limited computer skills and just wants to insert a snapshot of their best friend. Someone with more computer skills may interpret the product description differently and be disappointed.

title: Works OK, but feels flimsy. Unknown if ink can be refilled.
text: Average quality ballpoint pens. Stylus tip works well on my phone for pushing buttons, but you cannot do 2-finger gestures (like zooming or rotating), which limits its functionality. I could not find any source for ink refills. The pen feels kind of flimsy, so maybe they expect it to break before it needs refills? This might be a good gift for a child who will lose it before the ink runs out.

title: writes smoothly, dries quickly, does not smear easily
text: These are nice ballpoint pens. The write very smoothly. Bold is advertised as 1.6mm thick, but I do not know what that means. It certainly is not the width of the written line, which is only slightly thicker than a traditional medium ballpoint pen. The ink dries very quickly and does not easily smear or smudge. The 3-color assortment pack appears to always be black, blue, red. Clear plastic pen bodies look cheaper than these cost.

title: budget quality binder, latest batch (July 2017) has rings mounted on the back cover instead of the spine
text:
This is a cheap binder ($1.70 when I bought it), but the word "economy" in the title tells you that right away that the quality is commensurate with the price. The binder is functional and should last for the semester, which is all I'm asking of it. 4 stars because it does match my expectations at this price level. The cover pocket is useful for dropping in a cover sheet, but Avery also has a version of this binder without the front view pocket for 20 cents less. [[ASIN:B000I5W7RQ Avery Economy Binder with 1 Inch Round Ring, Blue, 1 Binder (3300)]]

I noticed some other purchasers are complaining about big ugly difficult-to-remove stickers on this binder. The binder I purchased in April 2017 did not have any stickers at all, thankfully.

Update: I bought some more of these binders in July 2017 and the new ones have the rings mounted on the back cover, while the old ones (from April 2017) had the rings mounted on the spine. I prefer the back cover mount since pages are less likely to fall out, but these still are round rings, not the straight-slant rings that you find on more expensive binders (that keep your pages more even).

title: budget quality binder
text: This is a cheap binder ($1.50 when I bought it), but the word "economy" in the title tells you that right away that the quality is commensurate with the price. The binder is functional and should last for the semester, which is all I'm asking of it. 4 stars because it does match my expectations at this price level.

title: nice heavyweight chair mat
text: This is a nice heavyweight chair mat, much heavier and sturdier than my old mat that this replaces. Too thick and stiff to roll or fold, it comes in a giant flat cardboard box. I'm glad I didn't have to carry that home from the big box store. Dimpled bottom surface holds the mat steady on a carpet, but it can scratch a wood floor. Very satisfied with this product. 5 stars.

title: nice sturdy shredder
text: This is a nice sturdy shredder, quite a bit bulkier and heavier than our cheap old shredder. Shredding is a little slow, but very reliable. It cuts your paper into strips about an inch by a quarter-inch. Pop-out waste bin is easy to empty. Since the shredded paper pieces are so small, the bin holds a lot of shredded paper. No complaints here. 5 stars.

title: Very nice heavyweight packaging tape
text: Very nice heavyweight packaging tape. Very sturdy as well as sticky. Just 1 layer of this stuff seals most of our boxes, compared to 3 layers of cheap tape. No thickness is specified in the description or packaging, but this tape compares well to the 3 mil Scotch packaging tape that we have been using. Yes, heavyweight tape costs 2-3 times as much as cheap thin tape, but it works so much better that it is worth it.

title: cheaper than other 20 pound papers sold on Amazon, but finish is not as nice
text: We have been buying Georgia Pacific or Hewlett-Packard brand 20 pound white printer paper from Amazon Prime. Those cost about $5/ream when you buy the 3 or 5 pack. This AmazonBasics paper is $4/ream. While it is also 20 pound paper, the finish is not as smooth and even as the GP or HP papers. You get what you pay for. For personal use, the cheaper paper is fine with us. Interestingly, the AmazonBasics paper is made in France, while the other 2 are made in the USA (if you care). AmazonBasics 10-pack comes in a big heavy box that does get beat up in shipping, but the paper inside seems to be OK.

title: 4 stars because the quality and functionality are better than we were expecting for this price
text:
This kit includes 20 different color pens in a nice metal storage box, all for $11. At that price, we are not expecting professional artist quality equipment. I think what we did get is a nice set for older kids or adults to play with. If your young kids like coloring, why not pull out this kit and color along with them? The kit has a very nice selection of colors. The colors are bright and vibrant on paper. The pens are fine tipped to give you much better control than typical felt pens. The ink does bleed a little, but much less than other felt pens and not too bad, as long as you only draw on one side of each sheet of paper (because the ink does bleed through). The pen caps seal well to help keep the ink from drying out very quickly.

A few criticisms: the round pens roll around too easily if you lay them on a table instead of back in the box. The pens are not marked with color names (even Crayons have printed color names). The pen caps are supposed to show the ink color, but some are much darker or lighter than the ink color.

4 stars because the quality and functionality are better than we were expecting for this price.

title: cumbersome to install, some ergonomic issues with daily use
text:
We set this up to run wirelessly with our Macbook. Installation was much more difficult than the HP printer/scanner that we installed last year. After getting stuck several times trying to use the way too skimpy instruction sheet that is included in the box, we searched for and downloaded the real user manual from the Canon website. We also had to download lots of drivers and other support software, which was very time consuming. Once we got it set up, print quality is very good. Photo printing also works well.

One ergonomic problem we have with this printer is that you have to remember to open the front lid before printing, which is a hassle if you are printing wirelessly and the printer is in another room. Another problem is if you want to print on non-standard paper (e.g. photo paper or an envelope), you have to insert the paper through the back of the printer, which is a huge hassle if your desk space is limited and you have placed the printer against a wall.

title: cute card for Valentine's Day or a love note that sort of looks handmade
text: If you want the handmade-look, but don't have the skill or time or materials to pull it off, this is a handy alternative. The front cover piece is made from a variety of different materials that are glued in place to give you some 3D texture (see photo). The inner note is a single printed piece of paper that is simply pasted in place, so you could easily remove that and add your own. These cards are a little pricey and if you search Amazon for handmade Valentine's cards, you will find lots of alternatives at various price points. It nice to have choices.

title: good value office-quality printer paper
text: This is nice office-quality printer paper for the price. You can find cheaper paper at discount stores, but that is usually poorer quality (18 pounds and not as smooth or white). The cheaper paper is noticeably thinner and less attractive and more likely to jam your printer. Better quality 24 pound paper is also commonly available, but at a higher price, so we only use that for special presentations. We've been using the 20 pound Georgia Pacific paper that is also sold on Amazon Prime for a similar price. Quality is similar to the HP paper and both are made in the USA. Price does fluctuate, especially if you have coupon or subscription discounts, so my advice is to buy whatever is cheapest.

title: good quality spiral notebook, but $12 price is too expensive
text: This is an above average quality wire notebook. Paper is slightly better than average with smooth bright white paper that is a little heavier than what you get in the $2 school notebooks. The plastic cover is thin and flexible, but should still be much more durable than the thin cardboard covers on the $2 notebooks. Blue-green color is not too obnoxious (not as bright as the photo). Unfortunately, the price for this notebook is $12, which I think is unreasonable. Mead has $6 "business quality" spiral notebooks in this size that I think are just as nice as this $12 notebook. For $12, you can find notebooks with hardcovers and nicer bindings.

title: lots of fancy print options, but for indoor use only
text: This is a nice labeler with lots of fancy and some silly print options. 2-line printing on a single label is very handy. The backing paper is very easy to remove from the labels, which isn't the case with some other label printers. The labeler requires 4 batteries, which are not included. There appears to be a power port on the side of the labeler, but the product description and manual do not say how to use that. I hate disposable batteries. Maybe we'll try rechargeable batteries. The product description does not say, but the Brother web site says the M-tape-labels that this device uses are for indoor use only. Presumably, that means that the labels will be destroyed by rain or by washing. That's too bad. The laminated labels used by some other Brother labelers are more robust.

title: expensive, but sticks well in wet or greasy environments
text: These labels are kind of pricey ($20 for 10 sheets, 12 small labels per sheet), but they do work as advertised. If you need to label tools or other small items that regularly get wet or dirty, these labels do hold on. These labels are easy to write on with most pens, though you should of course use a waterproof ink. Cheaper labels self-destruct when they get wet or greasy.

title: this "cash box" doesn't make sense to me
text: Maybe I'm not the target audience for this "cash box", but I hate this box. First, the upper cash tray is too small and drops down into the box easily. When that happens, pulling it back out is really hard because it is just barely too small. If the tray is full of money, expect some of that to go flying when you try to jerk the tray out. Second, the compartments in the tray are not shaped like dollar bills. What's up with that? Only the one large compartment in the back can hold paper money. Are all the other compartments for 6 different kinds of coins? Third, the handle on the top of the box does not recess into the box so if you have more than one of these boxes, you cannot stack them. Fourth, the lock is really really flimsy. You could probably pry that off with a pocket knife or screwdriver. This box might be OK for a child trying to keep their allowance money out of the hands of their siblings, but I cannot imagine a business working out of this.

title: great for patching bicycle inner tubes; easier to use than the glue tubes that come with patch kits
text:
This is not the same "rubber cement" as Elmer's school glue. This rubber cement is designed specifically for patching rubber tires. I use it for patching bicycle inner tubes (using vulcanizing tube patches) and it works great; just as well as those little tubes of glue that come in tire patch kits. This large can with built-in brush is so much easier to use than those little glue tubes. The brush built into the lid of the can lays down an even layer of cement very quickly and easily. Let it dry for 5 minutes then apply the patch. Works perfectly every time. If you are patching a bunch of tubes (even over several months), the price for this can is economical.

Steps for patching a bicycle inner tube (follow this very carefully and the patch will last for the remaining life of the tube):
1. locate the hole in the tube
2. mark the hole with a pen
3. sandpaper the area around the hole to remove the slick rubber skin on the inner tube
4. if you completely sanded off your mark from step 2, mark it again
5. apply an even layer of rubber cement over and around the hole, somewhat larger than the size of your patch
6. wait 5 minutes for the cement to mostly dry
7. remove the protective skin from under your patch
8. stick the patch to your cement spot (you did cement a larger area than necessary so the patch edges are completely in the glue area, right?)
9. press the patch down hard, all around the patch including the edges (finger pressure is OK, but a rolling tool is better)
10. I usually let the patch dry for a couple of hours, but if you need to ride right away, putting it back in the tire and pumping it up will usually work
11. if you haven't used the tube yet, pump it up after it dries for a couple of hours and let it hang somewhere, then check it the next day to make the tube is still full of air, meaning your patch is OK
12. 95% of the time this procedure will work and the patch will last for the remaining life of the tube
13. in the other 5% of the time, you screwed up (maybe not applying enough cement or not centering the patch over the hole) or maybe there was another hole in the tube somewhere. If I can find a 2nd hole, I will patch that, too. Otherwise, I just throw these tubes away instead of trying to figure out what went wrong.

title: light action, lightweight, high-capacity, jam-free stapler
text:
This is a pretty nice lightweight stapler. Despite the "compact" in the product name, this is a pretty big stapler (6 inches long and 3 inches tall). Mostly plastic construction makes gives it a lighter weight than typical all-metal desktop staplers that you have to slam hard to staple more than a couple of sheets of paper. This stapler has some internal spring action to give you high power with just a light touch. It's so lightweight that you will probably want to hand hold this stapler rather than slamming it on your desk like you would with a heavier stapler. Of course, the plastic construction probably means it is not as durable, especially if you drop it on the floor.

No staples are included in the box, though it does use standard sized (but not high capacity) staples. It does not accept a full strip of staples. Seems to work fine with cheap staples that I already owned. The drawer to install the staples is a little finicky, but not a big deal once you get used to it. As other reviewers are saying, the price is surprisingly high for a paper notebook. School-quality notebooks of this size cost only a couple of dollars in big box stores and "deluxe" business-quality notebooks can be had for less than $5. I can see paying this price for something like an address book (if you still use paper address books) that you would use for years (the covers are sturdy enough for a lot of use), but not for daily note taking (where it might only last a couple of weeks).

6. It has an attractive appearance.

8. It has a reflective strip on it that makes it easier to find in dim light (such as during a power outage).
9. It has handles to facilitate carrying it.

CONS

1. The manufacturer claims it is water resistant—this is useful, but it is NOT the same as waterproof.

title: Works well
text:
I have used this toner for about 250 pages so far, and I have had no trouble with it. There is no problem with its interaction with my printer, and the quality of the print is clear and dark.

I own a Brother HL-L2300D laser printer. It is compatible with the standard yield Brother TN-630 and high yield Brother TN-660 black toner cartridges. This product is advertised as being similar to both TN-630 and TN-660, with emphasis on TN-660, because the product description claims it will print up to 2600 pages and that it includes two TN-660 black toner cartridges. Brother TN-660 is advertised by Brother as providing up to 2600 pages. Brother TN-630 is advertised by Brother as providing up to 1200 pages. If you print in a high DPI, you will, logically enough, get less pages than that per cartridge.

This product includes a helpful user guide and, as promised, includes two toner cartridges.

It is worth noting that a toner cartridge has a shelf life of 24-36 months. Over time, the ink can dry out, settle and clump, which can cause the printer to clog. There is no way to know how old this toner is at the point you purchase it. But that may be the case as well with actual Brother toner.

title: Sturdy, large dispenser
text:
PROS

1. Sturdy construction of acrylic.

2. Functions just like any typical tape dispenser.

3. It holds 1/2-inch, 3/4-inch or 1-inch tape rolls.

3. If you prefer a modern, angular design, and you have quite a bit of other acrylic office equipment already, this dispenser might work very well for you.

CONS

title: Awesome set of mechanical pencils
text:
PROS

1. Very attractive silver colored pencils, with a black finger grip.
2. The set comes with six mechanical pencils, 20 additional erasers, and six packages of additional lead, with 12 pieces per package.

title: Works very well
text:
This sturdy, clear-plastic, protective holder for a CDC Covid-19 vaccine card works perfectly. As you can see from the picture I’ve attached, the card fits in it exactly. The top is a peel-lock closure, which holds the card securely.

title: Cute, cartoon elephant mouse pad
text: I use this cute, little mouse pad on a small desk, and it fits perfectly. It is well made, comfortable, non-slip, and the cartoon elephant is adorable. All in all, I am quite pleased.

title: Convenient package & bright yellow color
text:
This is a very convenient way to purchase yellow highlighters. The manufacturer offers a dozen of them in their own convenient, plastic storage case. The markers work well, and their color is bright and clear.

For anyone who needs highlighters for school or work, this is an excellent option.

title: Sturdy and functional, a few design flaws
text:
Before ordering this laptop stand AKA portable desk, I purchased one in a similar style, but it was made of a much flimsier plastic. This stand is far sturdier and better built. The legs are made of a durable plastic, and the desk top AKA tray is made of aluminum. The latter is 16.5 inches wide.

As an additional, excellent feature, which the other portable desk did not have, this laptop stand has two built-in fans to cool a laptop. The power to run the fans comes from a USB cable that plugs into the laptop itself. Since my old (2011) laptop tends to get very hot, this is a much appreciated feature.

The overall design of this stand is well thought out. There are two legs which have two joints separating them into three parts. This extra joint allows the user to position these legs in multiple ways. The instructions illustrate at least 10 different potential setups.

This laptop stand comes with an attachment that supposedly the user can place a mouse on. That is the one part of this stand that does not impress me. There are no instructions included on how to install the mouse attachment, and I personally could not figure out how to do it.

One other issue with the design is the lip of the flat surface at the top of the stand, that is, the desk top. The lip is not tall enough to fully support a laptop and hold it in place if you have the desk top of the stand tilted forward. It is only sufficient if, for some reason, you choose to position the desk top so it is perfectly flat. If the desk top is tilted at all, the laptop will slide off the desk.

title: This isn't really tape, but a form of weirdly applied glue
text:
I had no idea exactly what this product was when I ordered it from Vine, because there was no product information, either on Amazon itself or that came with this product. Because of the product's name, I was expecting it to be some type of glue, and since glue always comes in handy around the house, I went ahead and ordered it.

After the product arrived, at first, neither I nor my husband could figure out how to use this tape by simply examining it carefully. But since then, by trial error, we have figured out that this product isn't actually tape in the sense of the normal way you would use tape. You rub the edge of the adhesive/tape on a piece of paper and it leaves a residue of stickiness. You can then stick that piece of paper to another piece of paper. It's almost as if it is allowing you to create a Post-it type sticky note out of a regular piece of paper.

I'm not sure what this tape could be used for other than to glue a piece of paper to something else that is made of paper. I did not find that it is strong enough glue to be effective for much else.

title: Very comfortable
text: In addition to being very comfortable, this wrist rest is quite attractive. It has a sleek, modern design, and the black color is dark and rich. The non-slip feet are an important feature. It is far too easy for a wrist rest without that ability to slide around.

title: Seriously flawed
text:
This is a set of three business-card holders in classic, black, mesh metal. In color and style, it will match any other black, mesh office devices you already own, such as a letter tray or a pencil holder. However, as a business-card holder, it is seriously flawed.

There is no lip on the edge of the shelf portion of this holder where the cards have to sit. That lip is crucial in order to keep the cards from sliding off. All but two other brands offering a similar style of card holder here on Amazon, logically enough, have a lip.

text:

This is a very useful and convenient product that would make an excellent gift for friends and family.

title: Works really well
text:

By the way, I looked up 3M's patent, and it expired in 1997. All that 3M retains for rights to "Post-it" is that name and the original notes' distinctive yellow color, which continue to be registered company trademarks. Imitations use alternate terms like, in this case, "sticky notes," or "repositionable notes," and though these sticky notes are yellow, it is a lighter color than the trademarked yellow.

I have only one slight criticism as I compare this stapler with my Swingline: I personally find the action of this stapler when inserting a staple into paper to be a bit less smooth than my Swingline, full-sized stapler.

title: It's a nice item, but overpriced

It is a simple matter to pick it up to transport it, as one might pick up a small box or any other small desktop item which has no handle. It's not heavy. It weighs less than two pounds. Granted, the handle allows you to pick it up with one hand, so there is that convenience factor. But truly, how often does one need to move a desktop organizer from room to room?

In sum, this organizer is a nice item but, in my opinion, it is overpriced. Unless you have money to burn, I don't think it's worth the cost. You can get something very similar for less than a third of the price, just without the built-in carrying handle.

I received through Vine the "assorted" choice, with one red, one blue, and one black pen. For those who like red and blue, the colors are bright and clear.

I like these pens well enough that I would definitely buy them again.

title: An adequate shredder for intermittent shredding if you use it properly
text:
This shredder can shred staples and paper clips attached to the paper you want to shred, and it can also shred credit cards. It cross cuts and it can run for up to three minutes before the motor starts to overheat and it shuts itself off and has to cool down for 30 minutes--which is rather inconvenient if you procrastinate and store up a lot of documents to shred at a time. It holds up to 3.6 gallons before you have to empty the bin.

I've owned another Fellowes shredder almost identical to this one for many years, and over time I've learned the rules of the road for this type of inexpensive of paper shredder:

1. Do not put too many pieces of paper in at a time! The manufacturer states it can take up to 8 sheets of, presumably, standard copier-paper type weight. Note that the standard name for this type of paper is called, "20 lb. bond." This is because standard office copy paper weighs 20 pounds for 2000 sheets. If you are shredding a credit card or card stock type paper, then to avoid jamming, you should only put in one sheet at a time.
2. Don't let the sheets of paper you are shredding feed in crooked. It is crucial that it be inserted straight or it can get jammed.

The biggest enemy to successful shredding is impatience! If you break the above two rules, you'll inevitably create a paper jam.

This is a satisfactory product for intermittent shredding and is a perfect size to go beside or under an office desk. It weighs 8.6 pounds, which is heavy enough that it will not easily tip over, but it not too heavy to lift and carry around if that becomes necessary.

title: Nice product but extremely expensive
text:

1. I had not used dry-erase markers for years, because way back then, the only markers available had a terrible stench. These markers, however, certainly have a much lower odor.
2. These markers have a unique feature; they are, as advertised, see-through, so you can see for yourself how much ink is left.
3. There is a good variety of colors to choose from in this package.
4. The chisel tip allows for more flexibility than typical wide-tip dry-erase markers, such as for writing on a smaller style of white board.
5. They don't dry out while there is still ink in the cannister.

Here is the obvious negative:

The price is enormously expensive. A quick search on Amazon reveals other low-odor brands with many positive reviews which are a fraction of the cost of this brand.

title: Attractive, flexible, functional classroom desk
text:
This portable, folding, classroom desk has a pleasing, contemporary style, with fluid, curving edges, rather than a conventional, rigid, square shape with harsh corners. It weighs only 14 lbs. and is easy to lift and move around. It has an adjustable height from a low of 22 inches to a high of 29 inches. It is suitable for either right-handed or left-handed students. The desk top is laminate, which cleans easily, and it has an attractive, light-maple color. The legs and base are of silver-colored metal.

This desk is designed to be grouped together, in combination with other desks just like it, in creative formations that foster collaborative classroom projects.

Though this desk is primarily designed for classroom use, it would make an excellent desk for a child's room. The rounded edges are a crucial safety feature for a young child, preventing potential injury from a child banging its head against dangerously sharp desktop corners.

All in all, an excellent product.

title: You must use the built-in eraser on these erasable pens
text:
I tested all the different colors of these pens. There is black, navy, blue, green, purple, red, violet, pink, orange and gray. The gray is such a light color it is barely visible, but the other colors are bright and easily read. These gel-ink pens have a smooth flow, and the tips are a fine point.

When I read on the package that the ink of these pens is "erasable," I immediately tried out a regular eraser on this ink and immediately discovered that the ink can only be erased with the special eraser built into the end of each pen. The good news is that, unlike a regular eraser, these erasers do not dissolve into messy crumbles. Which is a good thing, because if they did, they would not last as long as the ink in the pens.

It occurs to me that pens like the black and blue ones in this set should NEVER be used to sign a legal document, since they can be erased.

These pens will not work in the way that colored, fine-point markers do, for art projects. But if you or some child or adult you know likes to play with colored pens, they might enjoy these.

title: Excellent, felt-tipped pen
text:

My main use for felt-tipped pens is for filling out legal and medical forms that I have to scan. In my experience, a regular, black, ballpoint pen does not produce a dark enough script for my scanner to read well. It appears very faint. This particular felt-tipped pen works perfectly for that purpose. It shows up excellently on scans.

I am happy with this pen and would feel no hesitation recommend it to friends and family.

title: Outstanding product!
text:
This is a set of two TV tables, and they are of excellent quality. What I like most of all about them is their sleek, contemporary design. It makes all the other TV tables I've owned or seen in the stores look quite clunky in comparison. They look terrific in my family room.

I got the tables in the black color, and it is a lovely, dark, matte-finish. A very nice feature of this product is that you can choose between multiple bright, lovely colors.

These tables are constructed of polypropylene on the table top, which is very easy to wipe down and keep clean, and they have a powder-coated. strong, steel frame. The legs have non-marring, non-slip ribber tips, which is an important feature. These tables are lightweight, a mere 7 pounds, and they fold up easily for storage. They adjust to three different, convenient heights, which you can tailor to the size of the person using them. Their dimensions are as follows:

Lowest position: 26"W x 18"D x 25"H
Highest position: 26"W x 18"D x 28"H.

Note that, for comparison purposes, 28 inches is the height of a standard desk.

The manufacturer states that this table can hold up to 30 pounds. I doubt that the typical use for such a table will ever call for it bearing that much weight. I have owned another brand of TV table for years which was advertised as capable of holding up to 50 pounds, which I never put to the test because it looks much, much flimsier than this sturdy table.

Finally, the cost for this set of two TV tables is extremely reasonable compared to the quality of the product.

All in all, I find this an outstanding product and I would not hesitate to recommend it to friends and family.

title: Quite overpriced for what it is
text:
This is a very nice, casebound journal/notebook. Unlike a typical notebook with lined paper, it is not spiral bound and does not have perforated pages, so they cannot be easily torn out. The cover is thicker and more durable than most spiral notebooks, and it is smooth in texture. Instead of using traditional 8-1/2 x 11-inch paper, it is made with 9 x 11-inch paper. The paper itself is much higher quality than a typical spiral notebook, though it is lined like a spiral notebook versus unlined as most journals are. This journal/notebook itself is not very thick, only 80 pages.

This journal/notebook is a rather odd addition to the high-end journal and notebook market. It's not nice enough to be a classic, hard-bound journal, but it's too fancy to be considered a typical school notebook. For what it is, a hybrid of the two, it seems extremely overpriced to me. For the cost of this journal/notebook, I would personally prefer to own a really nice journal. You can get some quite elaborate ones for as little as $10, such as this [[ASIN:B01AKFMPH0 vintage leather journal]].

I rate this journal/notebook as follows:
Quality of paper: 4 stars
Quality of cover: 4 stars
Attractiveness of product: 3 stars
Value for money: 1 star
Overall: 3 stars

title: Missing important features I've come to expect in a disposable, ballpoint pen
text:
These ballpoint pens with medium point and black ink are advertised as having "ultra smooth ink." Based on that selling point alone, they deliver. They do in fact write more smoothly than other ballpoint pens I own.

As far as I can see, this is their only positive. There is nothing special about the design. It's just a plain pen. Worse, they lack a crucial feature that I have been accustomed to seeing in disposable, ballpoint pens for at least 15 years, as a matter of course. That feature is padding in the grip to prevent the formation of a painful callus from writing. These pens are also not retractable, which most inexpensive, ballpoint pens have been for many years now as well. Instead they come with an inconvenient, easily lost cap.

All in all, I would not personally purchase these pens again.

title: Great labels
text:
These are great labels. I haven't put them to the tests that some people have so I can't testify to their durability, etc., but they look and adhere great. I stuck them on a bunch of my tools and tool cases, where they show up well and are very readable.

The purchase was a little weird and took longer than it should have because the labels arrived misprinted. I ordered them with my name and a number (my employee number at work) on them; our employee numbers (at least at this point in time) start with a zero, and the printer/seller omitted the leading zero. In some cases I suppose a leading zero would be superfluous and could safely be omitted...but not in this case (someone at my workplace looking at a five-digit number without a leading zero would have no idea what that number signified, while the leading zero makes it instantly identifiable as an employee number)...and a print order should be printed exactly as the customer ordered it regardless. So I had to contact the seller and request a reprint. The reprint was sent out in short order...but by ordinary First-Class mail, so it took as long again to get from California to New York as the misprinted first set had. Bit of an inconvenience.

In the end, though, I got the labels I'd originally ordered and they were high-quality and satisfactory in every other way. All's well that ends well...

title: Professional opinion
text:
I don't know that there's a perfect staple remover; every design seems to have its drawbacks, and that's true of this one too. But I've used staple removers of this general type that are not as well-designed as this one and don't work as well.

I work at a company whose business is scanning huge quantities of documents for its clients, and I'm one of the people who does the actual scanning, as well as prepping the documents for scanning...and believe me, that (the prepping especially) involves removing one heck of a lot of staples. You could almost say I'm a professional staple remover (it's definitely among the essential tasks of my profession). My company supplies staple removers of this type, but they're mostly more generic ones (and undoubtedly less expensive) and don't work quite as well. The metal blades you push under the staples don't taper outward the way these Bostitch ones do, and the magnets are on the opposite end of the tool from the blade, so you have to kind of flip the tool in your hand to use the magnet. This last is truly a tiny thing if you're possessed of any manual dexterity at all, but if you remove (and in the process scatter) a high volume of staples, you might appreciate that you pick up and hold this tool the same way whether you're removing staples or collecting them with the magnet. It's one of the small pleasures I derive from using this thing.

And speaking of scattering, this tool really doesn't do that much; i'm sure that tapered blade, as well as the placement of the magnet, has something to do with this. I actually use the magnet most often to clean up the staple-y mess left for me by the person working at my station before me. Staples do fly sometimes while using this tool, but not as much as with other designs.

Removing a staple from a thick sheaf of paper can take a bit of strength with this tool...as I imagine it can with any staple remover. Some issues are just endemic to the way staples work.

Paper rips, too - I think it's safe to say that's always going to happen a lot with this kind of staple remover. Fortunately that's not a big deal in my line of work as long as the torn paper doesn't take any printed information with it.

I like the ergonomic shape and the grippy little rubber pads that help me hold onto this thing even if my hands are dry, like now, in the wintertime. I like that there are three in the box, and that two of them aren't black - I take the red one to work. That way i can always spot mine and grab it before I move to a different station or leave work. (I discovered after I bought these that the company does have a few of these mixed in with the cheaper ones, but the company's ones are all black.)

So while these are not the magical staple removers I suspect everyone's looking for (I know I was) that never, ever rip paper nor leave behind any indication that a staple was ever there, these are pretty darn good. Just have realistic expectations and you'll be fine.

title: Attractive and seems well-designed
text:
I only just received my pair of these so I can't speak to their durability (plus I don't anticipate ever having to use the retractable aspect of them in my situation), but it seems a well-designed item. The cord reel operates smoothly - more smoothly and quietly than the rough-feeling and -sounding one in the holder I replaced with this one - and there's a little rubber grommet around the cord that serves as a bumper/shock absorber to soften the landing of the hard plastic...thingy with the triangular ring through it that holds the clear plastic snap strap that you pass through your...*other* badge holder (the part that the badge is actually inserted into).

I'm finding that badge holders are a difficult thing to write clearly about. 🤔

Anyway, this one is very functional, with two different ways (carabiner and belt clip) of attaching it to things, a cord of what seems to be an adequate length (I can extend it from my waist almost to my full arm's length, and I have long arms) and it looks very elegant and, for my purposes, does the job beautifully. I highly recommend pairing it with Fallen One Black Hard Plastic Open Face Id Card Badge Holder Horizontal and Vertical Dual-Use Double Sided Hold 2 Cards, also available here on Amazon. That's an elegant and well-designed badge holder that you'll especially appreciate if you need to remove your badge from your holder frequently to access any kind of reader that requires you to insert your card into it.

My thanks and compliments to the manufacturer. I've been buying a lot of stuff on Amazon lately, especially since February, and not all of it is of optimal quality (yay, easy Amazon returns!), so it's especially nice when something does indeed seem to be.

title: I love this thing
text:
This is an excellent ID holder for my purposes. It's lightweight, seems durable and very well-designed, and holds my government PIV card securely - the card snaps gently into place when inserted - while keeping it as easy as possible to remove the card from the holder for computer access. My only disappointment was not the fault of this holder, but of my bureau's choice of lanyards: they supply lanyards with thick plastic hooks that don't allow this holder to hang down the way it's intended to, causing it instead to stick off the hook at either an upward or a downward angle. No worries though - I simply replaced the bureau-issued lanyard with the handsome and functional Heavy Duty Retractable Badge Holders with Carabiner Reel Clip and Vertical Style Clear ID Card Holders, 24 inches Thick Kevlar Pull Cord that I found here on Amazon, and now my badge hangs elegantly from my belt.

The silly design of those bureau lanyards caused me to wind up with a much nicer solution for myself; the only thing I'm still sorry about is that I bought a ten-pack of these great badge holders, thinking I'd give them to some of my favorite people at work...but all those people would then need to replace their bureau-issued lanyards with something else at their own expense in order to use these, or indeed any badge holder with a standard-sized rigid opening to pass a fastener through. So I wound up with nine more of these holders than I need. But I guess I can give them out anyway, just with caveats.

These holders will work (though they might hang at a slight angle) with the standard metal clips found on most badge lanyards, and are ideally paired with a lanyard or other mechanism with one of those standard clear plastic snap straps found on many badge-holding mechanisms. That's what my new retractable things have and the holder hangs perfectly level (those snap straps are what the designers of this holder had in mind when they designed it).

Enjoy! I definitely am.

title: Was wonky upon receipt, but no longer
text: When I first received this unit, set it up, and powered it on, I was greeted by some kind of techy troubleshooting or configuration screen that I wasn't expecting (see photo). And that was some months ago now and I no longer remember what I did to get out of that and back to the proper display intended for the ordinary end-user. I probably turned the machine off, unplugged it for a while, plugged it back in and turned it on...and if I did anything else, I'm afraid that, as I say, I no longer remember what it was. But whatever I did, it did eventually get me out of that techy screen and back to the expected end-user display, and the printer's been perfect since. It's not a speedy-fast machine; if you need fast printing, this is not the machine for you. But other than that I can find no fault with this printer.  It's even printing longer than I might expect on the original, included toner cartridges. Nice.

title: Mostly great
text:
These are great pens; I only wish I could find these same pens in a medium point with Uniball's Jetstream ink. The fine point can tear the thin duplicate paper I have to write on at work, and I don't think the ink dries as quickly as the Jetstream ink does. Uniball's Jetstream pens, on the other hand, won't tear the paper I write on, but neither do they have the awesome hinged mechanical pocket clip that these pens do, that causes the point to retract when you put the pen in your pocket. My ideal pen would combine the best qualities of both these pens.

But if a very fine-point pen is what you're looking for, and you don't need your ink to dry very quickly, you can't do better than these pens.

title: Not for me.
text:
These are just fine for what they are; it just turns out that they're not particularly useful for me personally. A little too big and stiff to carry comfortably in most pockets and yet too small to write comfortably on, particularly because of their vertical, book-style binding...plus I guess I just don't like to write with a pen much anymore. I've become a good denizen of the 21st century, writing pretty much everything down in various apps on my phone (most of which is then accessible from both my phone and my computer - it's convenient).

I'm no great fan of graph-paper lines on writing paper either, but that's all I could find.

Field Notes books are probably great for some people; I'm just not one of those people. Maybe they're a hipster thing?

title: no wonder...
text:
it's no wonder this stapler's so highly rated - as soon as i saw the box I recognized the style of the packaging because it's very similar to that of my Zojirushi rice cooker. these products are made in Japan, one of the few places where they still understand the meaning of the word "quality". joy!

I bought this stapler for my home office without really thinking much about how infrequently I staple things at home. And, not surprisingly, I didn't use it. Wanted to, but had no opportunity! So now I've taken it in to work, where I staple a lot of paper every single day. I haven't yet gone all the way through my first cartridge of 5000 staples, but I've probably gone about halfway through, and this stapler is working flawlessly. I love it – I look forward to every opportunity to staple things together – and it hasn't screwed up once yet. One time I wound up with a mangled staple and thought I'd found the stapler's page limit, but no: I'd just placed my staple right smack on top of another one already in the stack. The machine's quiet and powerful and the flat-clinch staples are fantastic. There is zero risk of anyone poking a hole in themselves on a staple driven by this machine - the finished staple is as smooth on the back as it is on the front.

I'm sorry to hear of a couple of people's bad experiences with this stapler; all I can figure is that either they're reviewing the wrong stapler by mistake or they somehow got refurbished or otherwise second-quality machines, because the rest of us are clearly liking ours a lot.

title: Usable and cheap, but some real flaws
text:
Well, you can't beat the price, and they are usable, BUT these labels do have several problems:

(1) The Amazon listing AND the package say that the labels are 2-3/4" x 1/2". However, they are actually just a tiny bit smaller than 1-3/4" x 1/2" -- so, they're actually a full inch smaller in width than what is listed and what is indicated on the package. (Of course, if you're accustomed to using Avery 5167 labels, and/or if you can do math and look at the illustration of the label page on the box, you'll realize that the 2-3/4 claim has to be wrong.)

(2) The listing and the box both claim that these fit the template for Avery 5167 labels. Not true. They're close, BUT the left and right margins on these label sheets are about 1/8" wider than an Avery 5167 sheet, and the gutters between the columns of labels are narrower. Thus, if you attempt to use these as 5167's, your left column of labels will be printed too far left on the label, and your right column of labels will be printed too far to the right side of the label. In order to get them to line up, you have to print your sheet of labels to a document and manually adjust the postioning of your columns.

(3) Some of the labels aren't cut all of the way through to the backing sheet, so they don't pull off the sheet with clean edges.

(4) This is a more trivial, personal preference issue, but after printing I like to peel the margins and gutters off the sheet, leaving just the labels. I find that this makes removing the labels much quicker and easier, so it saves me a considerable bit of time when I'm doing a whole bunch of labeling. Avery (and Office Depot, for that matter) brand labels have an edge of exposed backing around the label material to make it easy to start in a corner and peel the margins and gutters off the sheet in one quick, easy motion. These don't -- the label layer extends all of the way to the edge, so the only way to peel off the margins and gutters is to remove a label first and then peel margins and gutters off piecemeal. Also, because of the issue with not all of the labels being adequately cut through, peeling off margins and gutters also tends to peel off some of the labels.

All in all, these are usable, but whether you consider the extremely low price to be worth the trade-offs is going to depend a lot on what value you place on your time.

title: Choose ones with a different magnet location
text:
So I wanted to like these and they work well just as a marker but the reason I bought these was for the magnet so I could keep them on my fridge. The problem is that the magnet is on the top which means when you’re hanging them, the ink flow goes down inside the pen so when you go to use it it doesn’t have much ink. It would be better if it was made so that the magnet was on the bottom and the pens hung upside down so that the ink would flow towards the tip. I’ve tried hanging them upside down on my fridge but due to the position of the magnet they tend to fall off or flip around.
They should make them with a magnet either in the center or on the bottom instead of on the top. Update: the company contacted me wanting to give me a refund but also asking me if I wanted to take down my comment. I refused because I do actually use the pens. I bought a magnetic fridge cup so I could put them upside down and in future I can use any kind of dry erase pen. But I feel like it is manipulative to ask me to take down my comment. Not a good reflection on the company. I only pointed out an improvement. I do still use the pens for now.

Second: the sheets don't curl like the other brands which many times can not feed into the printer correctly. Third: The quality of the print is absolutely stunning. title: Great Price - Excellent Results
text:
I generally use Glossy sticker paper for my Etsy/eBay biz, but decided to go to the next level with holographic sticker paper. I didn't even realize there were such a thing as printable vinyl with this finish. Getting into the sticker scene is no easy task as everything has to be dialed in perfectly. Standard white glossy paper can sometimes be temperamental, and cutting blades have to be set just right or your stickers go right in the garbage.

I was so thrilled when these sheets printed on my Canon Pro 100 which uses dye, not pigment which was surprising. Very clean results - zero bleeding/smudging. I set my Cameo auto-blade to 7 and did a double cut and boom - they came out perfect on my first run! Even peeling them from the mat was easier than standard glossy! Ordering again!!

title: A Sticker's Best Friend
text:
So, yeah, it's a bit tricky to work with at first, but after a few cuts, you'll have a system of your own down pat for the perfect coverage. Cut out enough to cover a sticker sheet, and start from one end as you SLOWLY unroll the clear sheet down the sticker page, while using your hand(s) to rub back and forth as you continue to unroll, in order to make sure no air bubbles or creases appear. When you cut a sheet of this, it will curl so be patient, and you will have a few failures along the way. Once a crease appears, there's no way backing out or correcting it, so each time you want to laminate your sticker sheet, you have one shot at it, so you need to be on target. Most times, air bubbles can be corrected while laying the sheet down, but once it's completely covered, it's becomes a lot more difficult to flatten these annoyances out.

The whole process takes about 2 minutes. Once completely covered, just drop it into your cutting machine (I've been using my Cameo 4), and slice away (don't forget to increase your cut force/blade). I have mine set at Blade: 6, Force 33, speed 7. I haven't done kiss cuts yet, as I am only working with die cuts. After you punch out your stickers, behold the sheen, strength and ultra water proof-E-ness. For a test, I slapped standard glossy and matte "water-resistant" stickers on a glass, along side the same stickers covered with this VVivid laminate. Popped it into the washing machine. The result: The standard gloss sticker's were runny, while the matte's color completely washed out leaving a faint memory of what once was art. The stickers treated with VVivid were 100% perfect. Now I can sell these without being paranoid.

title: Good bang for the buck.
text:
OK, what I like:
1) It doesn't curl badly when removing sheets from the package. Another brand I purchased recently had such curling problems once it hit the air, that it couldn't be fed into my printer. These worked with my Canon Pixma Pro 100 without a problem.
2) The colors are vibrant - no problem there.
3) You get a good amount for the price

What I'm not crazy about:
How does a company list these are tear resistant? The resulting stickers are so thin, if you even breath on one it will rip. For example: I peeled a sticker, it was stuck to my finger (like stickers do when you first grab them), and when I went to pull the sticker away just to place it on a surface, it easily ripped right in half with no force whatsoever. A number of stickers torn while I was simply removing them from the sheet.

Adding clear vinyl did the trick in making these more tearproof and waterproof. After using the paper for a week, I raised my stars to 4. It turns out to be a better deal than most.

title: You gotta fiddle with it...
text:
OK. Firstly, this is EITHER plug in via USB-C -OR- stuff a bunch of AA batteries into it. It isn't rechargeable.

Secondly, the app you need is called "Print Master." Don't scan the QR codes, just search that name to download, trust me. Print Master is pretty easy to use, but you have to register. I had trouble because the confirmation email kept going to my spam folder. I'm a little confused as to why you'd need to register this at all. There are a lot of pre-loaded icons which are funny and somewhat useful. There are preloaded words which are useless because you can just type in whatever you want. There is a fair selection of fonts as well. You have to reselect your label size each time, so don't toss those numbers out. Theoretically you could use a photo or image from your phone, but unless you designed a tiny icon, this isn't useful as the labels are so tiny.

Thirdly, you have to load this juuuuuuust right to get your label centered. This is the trickiest part. I found that if you position the forward edge of the label on the exact center of the black roller you should be ok. I have a picture showing just that. However, the paper roll moves around AND you have to be careful when using the cutter to remove your label that you don't yank the tape out of position. If you are making several labels just peel them off and don't tear them or you'll have to reset the position again and again.

I picked this to try out because it was very cute looking and it came with lots of extra labels and I wanted a label maker. I don't think I'd buy it again or get one for anyone as a gift. I'd find a more reliable one that didn't take so much fiddling. I do like that it is thermal, so no ink refills. I will probably use this a bunch more, but with the weirdness of the paper-loading, and the difficulty in figuring out what the app is and registering, I have to give it only 3 stars.

title: Excellent Value, Easy Set-Up
text:
We bought a laser printer to get away from the expensive inkjet issues. If we want photo prints we can always go to WalMarts.

From delivery to printing the first test page was a mere 20 minutes. There's a few things you can do in advance to make the process fast and relatively painless.

First, go to Canon's website and download the drivers and scan utility software. These come on the included CD, but if you don't have a CD drive you'll need these.

Second, take your time unpacking the printer and removing all the packing tape. Follow the quick install guide carefully. Shaking the toner cartridge is not necessary. Turn on the printer but DO NOT touch any buttons!

Third, decide if you're a wireless or wired user. If wired, you'll need to order a separate USB cable. Most users will have a router with a WPS button. Hold the WPS button down and follow the printer screen instructions. Only takes a minute to connect.

Now you can install the drivers. Once installed the printer will spit out its first test page. Woot! Printed paper! Don't forget to install the scan utility.

I printed a few PDF documents...fast, quiet, and excellent resolution. Scanning through the ADF was a breeze as well. The printer recognizes items placed in the ADF and manual feed tray instantly and adjusts accordingly. I also tried a label sheet marked for inkjet/laser printers. No problems, but I did notice the label sheet was a tad warmer than an inkjet sheet.

All-in-all, an economical AIO laser printer for home and light office use. The only feature it lacks is faxing.

title: Excellent for Big, Tall, Beastie Men! (and ladies)
text:
My last big, intensive use chair lasted me 4 years. Instead of cloth I went with leather this time around, plus a lot more padding on my buttocks, thighs, and back. This Hercules chair seemed decent with good reviews...in the cart it went.

Here's a few tips when unpacking and assembling any chair of this size. First, take your time. It ain't a race. Locate all your parts, spread them out and get all the packaging junk off them. Second, if you have your own tools...ditch the hex key. This chair uses a 5mm Hex bit. I used a ratcheting driver with the hex bit. Made everything so much easier. Lastly...use the box to assemble the chair off the floor. Look at my pics. My large carcass doesn't do well lumbering around the floor like a stranded walrus. Your knees, back, and self esteem will thank-you.

On to the chair...

It's big and beefy, just like us! Amble padding on the bottom, back, sides, and arms.

The up/down and lock control works as it should. There is no play when the chair is locked in its upright position. When unlocked the chair has a nice, relaxed flow when arching back. Some chairs make you feel like you're going to tumble over backwards, not this once. It's being able to sit upright at my desk and type, like I am now, then slowly lean back to contemplate the meaning of life.

The lumbar adjustment knob works well and you can feel the difference in the adjustments.

The armrests are adjustable and easy to do. It seems like they move approximately 1/2" each click, so you can get your arms just right. I like my arms to just barely go above my desk for typing and other close in work. The padding isn't too thick or thin, feels just right to me, plus it's more dense than the chair bottom which is good for pointy elbows.

Assembly was about 45 minutes. Instructions were clear, all the parts were intact, and no missing pieces or screws.

Most importantly, how does this beast feel on my carcass? Plenty of cushion all the way around...back, buttocks, thighs, arms...everywhere. I'm usually working 8-10 hours daily, plus some weekends when my boss acts like an airhead. So far, no sore areas, no stiffness, and no numbness. I like how I can tilt all the way back with my feet off the floor and just relax. Fan me with a palm frond, feed me peeled grapes and I'll be in heaven!

All-in-all, it's a heck of a chair. Very comfortable, easy to put together, and budget friendly.
