title: Not your average card
text:
This card is for a special, special occasion. If you're looking to elevate a gift or a note then look no further. The cards by PopLife are the 3-Star Michelin of cards.

They are well made with thick and durable paper. When you open this card the balloons pop up with a message. I gave it to my grandmother for her 89th birthday and she loved the card. She ended up removing the balloons to have them as a keepsake little display.

This is more like a diorama and less like a card. I had the same positive experience with a dinosaur one from them too. My son loved it.

These are cards I would use for a special person or when I want to liven up a gift card for a young kid. They feel like a card you'd get from a little artisinal boutique on a posh little street.

title: Perfect for shipping my soaps
text: I make homemade soaps and lotions. These mailers are the perfect size for shipping most of my orders - usually two bars and a lotion. I have not had any reports of a damaged product since using these as well because the padding is sufficient. They protect what I am putting inside of them, stay sealed, and are lightweight enough to not impact shipping fees too much. That is really all I am looking for in a mailer. The added bonus of the white color is they are easy to write an address on and have it show up clearly.

title: Good for home workouts and teaching remote
text: I used to use these around my classroom for kids to make word-webs and do larger group activities. When things switched to home I often used these behind me to write down examples, vocab words, and explain things. The paper is large enough that you can really put some good notes and images on it. I also found myself using it for home workouts. I'd write the workout on it in huge writing and stick it up on the wall. I liked that it eliminated putting holes in the wall with thumbtacks. The adhesive also doesn't pull paint off the walls. This is a must-have for any home classroom!

title: look good but poor storage option
text: I like these cards for all-purpose type of things. They are great for putting with orders I ship out from Poshmark, random gifts, and work events. They don't have a message so I wouldn't use them for a birthday or holiday. The wide array of artwork on them looks good and well done, and isn't cheaply printed. The one thing I find weird is having to fold the cards yourself. I don't mind because they take up less space, but I would rather pay a little bit more to have them pre-folded in a box like all of my other cards. Once you rip the plastic bag they ship in you don't really have any place to keep them except loosely stacked where they can get dingy.

title: a fun add-on to a bday gift
text: This birthday card was tossed from our car during one of the new "drive-by" birthday parades. It was so cute though, if my son got this I'd probably keep it on display in his room as a little decoration. It's well made and is perfect for anyone who loves dinosaurs and fossils. It's a decent size with an incredible level to detail for a card. The card stock is sturdy too. One thing i noticed though is if you mail it it will definitely take two stamps, so keep that in mind!

title: My favorite pen
text: I LOVE Sharpie Pens. They're like the only non-red pen I use. I usually get them in packs of four but was really excited to see a larger pack offered. They are so smooth to write with, and have an inky, rich, non-smudgy black ink. They make my handwriting look a lot better than most other pens. I keep a bunch at home, work, and in my purse so I can always find one. It's probably the first pen I've borrowed from someone, asked what it was, and ended up making the switch to it for myself.

title: simple and does the job
text: These mesh pencil cups work well on my desk. They are wide enough to not get top heavy and tip over if I put heavier items in them like scissors. I like that they are mesh so I can see what is inside each one. What's nice is that they match the other Amazon Basic mesh desk offerings. My file organizer and drawers are the same material so it gives my desk a cohesive look.

title: Kind of bulky
text:
Pencil Cups
Desk organizer
I didn’t like that this had assembly required, I assumed it would be ready to go on my desk. It didn’t take long to put together it was just not what I expected. Once assembled it was larger than I thought and the “file holder” is a bottomless and sideless hanging rack, I wish it had a bottom or sides so files that aren’t in a hanging folder could go there as well. The desk dividers are fixed so you can’t adjust the spaces between them, but the middle section is wider and fits a small notebook or journal. The drawer opens smoothly and the mesh is smooth with no rough edges.

title: Funny
text:
This funny congratulatory card is low-key and subtle without over the top flourishes and poems. "You did the damn thing" is how friends talk to one another, without the flowery language this card is to the point and is good for accomplishments big and small - promotions, starting a small business, hosting an event. The illustration of a trophy too leaves it open for a plethora of events.

The card itself is a high-quality print on thick paper with a matching envelop, with a bright blue and green background.

title: love the color schemes
text: These posters are such pretty colors they look really cute in a stack on my desk. I like that they are different colors because I am mark up my text books with them and each color represents a different reference or a category. Posts are a staple so you might as well have fun with the colors

title: High quality, a good gift for an academic
text: This journal feels very high quality, it ships in a sturdy black case that makes it ready to gift. Upon taking it out I loved how vividly orange the leather cover was, and the yellowish tint of the paper. It looks like a classic notebook, something timeless and well made, that you can carry around in a leather satchel. The paper doesn't bleed through when using an inky pen on it, and the size makes it easy enough to tote around.

title: Stylish watercolors
text:
These thank-you cards are rich shades of blues, greens, and pinks. They look like hand-painted watercolors on the outside and are blank on the inside so you can write your own note. The brown Kraft paper envelopes elevated them so they feel like you purchased each one individually from a paper store, not a boxed set.

I love the blues and greens used on this, they're such pretty jewel tones. They would work for any occasion, from thank-yous to coworkers, close friends, or acquaintances for bridal showers, baby showers, weddings, or birthdays. Loads of room to write in!

title: Better for students as opposed to teachers
text:
This is an academic year planner, which is perfect for teachers. It has a monthly overview section, as well as a detailed weekly layout. I like to use this for a rough sketch of lesson plans, and to have a physical reminder of what classes I will have that day. It's nice being able to look at the whole month and see meetings, and the week for a quick overview.

One thing I don't like is that for an academic year planner, it has no place to write your bell schedule, and no folder to hold a printed out copy of it. My old academic planner would show each day of the week at the top of the page, and have 5 slots under it for each academic period. This made is so easy to plan out my day. This planner could have been formatted like that, taken up the same amount of space, and been more useful to teachers.

The pages aren't reinforced where they meet the spiral binding either. Since they are thin paper I am sure some will begin to fall out.

This is more-so geared towards students writing down assignments, not teachers trying to organize lesson plans.

title: A well-made card for friends
text: This card feels very sturdy, the front is two sheets of paper glued together so there is weight to the card. The floral print looks like it's silk-screened, and looks retro in a stylish 1950s or 1960s way. It is reminiscent of a Lilly Pulitzer dress in a way, with similar tones, contrasting blues, and loose line work. The glitter is selectively applied, which only adds the details. It is deliberately placed in the corners of the card. The inside is a heavy weight paper with a positive message and some continuing floral details, yet there is plenty of room to write a note. It looks like something from a boutique paper shop!

title: Paper jams
text: This printer prints high-quality photos, and the wifi/bluetooth interface is great. Easy to set up and I love being able to print from anywhere rather than having to fire up my defunct desk top. But the paper ALWAYS jams, so while I can print from anywhere, I usually go downstairs to find that it's jammed and unable to print.

title: Good for photos
text: These print good quality pictures, and seem to last a long amount of time. No complaints so far.

text: I received the Blue Sky planner in size 5" x 8" and it’s perfect for my needs because I’m trying to pare down, consolidate, and lighten up. Even with the firm plastic covers, the laminated inner covers and laminated tabs, this weighs just a bit over 7 ounces. But it’s sturdy enough! title: Easy To Change Out The Old Cartridge
text: I like the fine point! It's not hard to unscrew the pen, slip out the old refill and slip this new one in. This is definitely cheaper than buying a new pen and it's probably better for the environment. A "win win" situation. (Be sure to remove the protective plastic nib before trying to use the new refill!)

title: A Pleasure To Create With! Smooth Flow. Rich Colors.
text: These Sharpie S-Note Markers gave me hours of relaxation. They're very satisfying to use since the fine chisel tip gets into small areas and the broad side of the tip allows for fast coverage. The tips are similar to calligraphy pen tips. Love the smooth flow! One can write attention-getting notes with these pens! Or create your own birthday cards or artwork. Jewel-like colors can be applied fully saturated, or more transparently with a quick, light stroke. Draw, underline, highlight, and create with 24 precise tips.

title: Stick A Huge, Clear Message Just About Anywhere
text: This is a TWO PACK. There are 30 sheets per pad. They're huge (25" x 30") and they're lined, making it easy to leave a neatly written message or instructions or HAPPY BIRTHDAY where it will be seen. Perfect for the classroom or presentations! On the reverse side, up at the top is a wide band of adhesive that will stick to walls, doors, refrigerator, glass, and other places. It sticks and it also lifts off easily. The cardboard at the top, that binds the pages, is designed so that it will fit on a variety of easels. The paper is a sturdy enough weight so that most inks won't bleed through.

title: Making My Own "Post-It" Notes With This Tape
text: This is a cool little tape dispenser with tape that can be repositioned. I put it on the back of paper -- some small (3"x3") and some larger sheets (8.5"x11") wrote messages and adhered them to the desk (the paper won't fly away in a breeze) and the refrigerator. You can even make a pile of these papers and lift them off of the paper below, as you can with "post-it" notes. The tape breaks off easily with a sideways motion after sticking it to whatever it is you wish to adhere it to. It measures 15mm wide by 12m long (about half an inch by thirty-nine feet). I also used this on a light piece of cardboard and stuck it to my fridge -- it bonded well -- and I was able to lift it off easily. The dispenser is easy to use and it's refillable.

title: Protect Valuable Documents & Give Presentations
text: These are heavy-duty plastic document protectors that will also be perfect for making presentations. This comes with two types -- one is a 3-tab system and the other is a folder with 6 inserts. Easy viewing through the transparent, yet substantial plastic. Very durable and flexible letter size protectors. Package Include: 4 of the six pocket file folders and 6 of the 3-tab document folders.

title: Things Overheard In New York & Los Angeles
text: Three hundred and sixty-five days of humor! I can definitely use this! My husband and I laughed our way through nearly every quote. It's remarkable to note the difference between themes from New York and Los Angeles. I like how they include exactly WHERE these remarks were overheard -- it provides good context.

title: Plenty Of Space For Planning
text: I like the tons of white space for writing in everything that must be planned and remembered. It's large and attractive with gray and white chevron design and pink tabs, numbers, months and headers. Tabs are laminated and so are the covers. The back cover has holidays listed for 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 -- great for long-term planning! It has heavy duty translucent plastic outer covers and the entire planner is sturdy in its spiral binding. Fantastic for planning weekly and monthly from July 2019 through June 2020. with two bonus months of May & June 2019 in the calendar section.. Five large, blank NOTES pages at the back.

title: Good Sized Calendar Pages
text: This is a good-sized, slim planner that'll take me through December 2020. This has plenty of writing space, monthly calendar grids, and 2020 Holidays listed. It also has several slim perforated tear-off notes and the back has an inner pocket. The cover is a pretty blue and there's also an elastic band for keeping this closed.

title: Make Every Day A Five-Star Day!
text: A planner for work and play, accomplishes and joy! This is a delightful planner that  encourages one to think about goals, track spending, drink enough water and also to factor in play and joy and to know when it's "Pizza Day," and "Send A Card To A Friend Day," along with all of the traditional holidays and observances. Every day you can rate your day, too, with one to five stars. Plenty of blank "Make It Happen" pages for jotting down one's objectives, intentions and purpose. I love the cover art!

text: [[VIDEOID:960937a60cb7d31c5fb55f4bdd37e13e]] This is easy to use, easy to empty. Heavy duty blade, and A SPARE -- nice feature! Versatile for a variety of pencils, including colored pencils. I like the sleek design.

title: The Finished Cart Is Well Worth The Effort!
text:
I love the finished cart (by "finished" I mean assembled) and let me tell you, it required a bit of thought and quite a bit of elbow grease for me to put this together.

The first step is to screw up the wheels. I did this with a plain old Phillips head screwdriver. I couldn't get all of the screws sunk.

Then, following the very clear direction sheet, I assembled all of the slats (i.e. panels) and began to screw the eight panels. At that point, my husband lent me his cordless screwdriver and the job went much easier. (I'm a woman in my mid-sixties.)

After putting in all of the screws most of the way (or part of the way), I went back with the cordless screwdriver and was able to tighten all of them up. I think there are 72 screws! So, it required a bit of labor, but the assembled cart was well worth it!

I love the quality and finish of the materials. I love that bamboo is natural and eco-friendly.

This is a sturdy cart and it rolls like a dream. It will be handy to roll everything out to the barbeque -- meat, plates, utensils, etc. -- and roll it all back in after it's cooked. But applications for this cart are practically unlimited; would make a fantastic art cart.

This looks good next to my kitchen cabinets and it would also look great with white cabinets, other colors and probably with stainless steel.

title: Smooth Flowing Ink. Fun Colors! Great Comfort Grip!
text:
Good basic pens in a variety of super colors.

My favorite thing about them? The grip. I love the rubber grip at base of each pen.

My favorite color? Black! It shows up the best. Purple is good, too and I like the dark blue. Gold will come in handy for signing special cards. The two turquoise don't seem all that much different and the two purples are quite similar. Also included are Red, Pink, Orange, Greens, Blue, Brown. (See photo, if they allow it.)

Medium point and very smooth flow. Writers might like these since there's little resistance, allowing thoughts to flow seamlessly from mind to hand to paper. Teachers will love them for correcting papers -- colors other than red for giving feedback -- a welcomed relief! And kids will love these!

title: Full Color & Photos & Inspirational Quotes Plus Plenty Of Space For Appointments, Thoughts, Inspiration
text:
I love that this is made from 100% post consumer paper. I also love that for the size and the thickness, the heavy-duty (faux leather) plastic cover and the metal ring binder, this isn't too heavy, weighing in at less than one pound.

I love the graphics: full color with a nature photo on every calendar page. This is the first planner I've ever owned that prints the numbers that add up to 365; for instance, on Tuesday, January 23rd there are two numbers next to the 23: 023/342. It's the 23rd day with 342 days remaining. (For people with date sensitive objectives: tick tock, tick tock, you know exactly how long you have to meet your deadline!)

Even with the full color photo and an inspirational quote every day, there's still plenty of space in the long columns to keep track of appointments or your own inspiration. Each column is numbered (hourly) from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. with six lines for "Things To Do" at the bottom.

A lot of thought has gone into the weekly/monthly graphics for easy planning. Week begins on Monday, one weekday per column, printed monthly indicators in different colors.

Blank pages at the back for name/address/ phone/fax/ and memos. 2018/2019/2020 calendar on the same page at the back. Important dates and a USA map with our six time zones.

I love it!

title: Rich Gold
text:
I created a rich gold background in the medallion shown in the photo with one of these Prismacolor Verithin gold pencils.

It's a pleasure to lay down color with one of these. When sharpened to a fine tip, it has a bit of "tooth" at first as it grips the paper. As the tip dulls, it's easy to spread the gold around. With the tip sharpened, it's easy to do fine details.

When viewed directly, it's apparent that it's gold; almost a coppery-gold. When viewed obliquely with the light glancing off, there is a burnished quality and it looks like a very rich gold.

title: Out-Of-This-World Wireless Printer With Fax, Scan, Copy Functions
text:
So far we're thrilled with this HP OfficeJet Pro!

My husband did the set-up:

1) Unboxed the copious, protective packaging materials. 2) Plugged it in. 3) Downloaded app. 4) Followed directions and immediately started printing remotely from his ipad.

He is extremely happy with this printer. He's not only used it remotely from his ipad, but also has used the double-sided copy machine function (duplex feature) using the touchscreen on the printer. This prints both sides of double-sided copies at once. It's very fast.

I've used this to print from my ipod touch. I downloaded the app and installed it in a couple of minutes. I was able to print immediately from my ipod. No problems!

Print quality is excellent.

Of the main functions (copy, scan, fax, wireless printing, two-sided duplex printing) we've used all but fax with seamless results.

This does mobile printing from anywhere. I haven't used this feature, but I will update this review when and if I do. I would not anticipate any problems based on the ease of use with our remote devices, so far.

Print jobs can be managed directly at the printer, too. My husband has used this feature for his duplex copies by tapping and swiping the touchscreen attached to the printer. Flawless results!

We have even printed from our desktop Mac, but only in black and white because we have not updated our OS.

Paper sizes supported: A4; A5; A6; B5 (JIS); Envelope (DL, C5, C6, Chou #3, Chou #4); Card (Hagaki, Ofuku Hagaki)

The product manual on the HP Website is easily accessed. Great online support, in fact!

This replaces our HP Photosmart Printer which we've been satisfied with for years.

title: Nice Ledger Book
text:
This is old school. Doing the taxes a few years back, I got so frustrated with online records. There's never a foolproof (not this fool, anyway) way to transfer data from one kind of thing (online orders and receipts, e.g.) to another kind of thing (online accounting). And if you get audited, you need to be able to show the paper records, which you also have to scan and upload. And everything has to be added up with a tape-type record. And my husband has two different businesses that he runs as a sole proprietor.

Got it so far? Original contemporaneous paper record. Running account. Categorized. Dated. ALONG WITH your accounting program reports. For me, the easiest thing is to keep a running ledger that I can check my numbers against at the end of the year. I just take everything as he gives it to me, enter it in the ledger by date in ink (because that's a contemporaneous record produced in the ordinary course of business, i.e. evidence), enter the info in the program, and keep the deposit slips and receipts with the ledger in date order. At tax time, I run the reports, check my numbers, and I'm ready to go.

text:
My first look at this thing provoked trauma memories from when I was an executive assistant back in the 80s fresh out of college. This behemoth is every bit as intimidating looking as the monsters that used to jam up and start smoking, resulting in visits from repair guys and exasperated looks from angry bosses who never in a million years would have been able to figure out how to run one of those things.

Surprise - it's three decades later, and this gentle giant does more than any of those nightmares did - at least the ones in the smaller offices - including FAX. You would think faxing would be a thing of the past, but trust me, if you ever have the need to deal with a government agency, there will be a fax number and you will be expected to use it.

It's easy to set up (once you get it out of the box - it weighs like 70 pounds). Printing is fast. Really fast. So far, there's nothing I don't like about having an all-in-one color laser printer. Everything that I would have expected to be a pain (paper jamming, toner issues, software problems) has been stellar. However, the size and the price are probably overkill if you aren't running a lot of paper through your home or business.

title: Terrible Paper Loading
text:
I bought this because it was dirt cheap and both of my other color printers turned out to be possessed by the devil the week my kid's science report was due. Seriously. There was ink vomiting. There was gibberish. Okay, not seriously, but there was no color printing going on in this house, and a cheap replacement ink cartridge turned the innards of one printer entirely cyan.

My husband said, "Don't buy a printer. We'll go to ******'s (you know the place)" First of all, "we"? He works all the time (tirelessly, and I am grateful - he is the best guy in the world), and the kid is not driving yet. Secondly, this printer cost about twice what printing the required number of copies would have. So, I only feel bad about the plastic, the carbon footprint, and having more stuff at a time that I am trying to have less stuff (looking into donating the old printers to a lace that refurbishes them).

Setting up the printer was a two button job: one on the printer, one on the router (it's an ORBI, if you care). Not only do my Macs see the printer, my Windows10 computers ALSO see it. My Windows10 computers see nothing - NOTHING! that isn't plugged directly into one of their plentiful-compared-to-Macs ports. But they see this. Print quality is good enough. And I still have a ton of toner after printing what I needed to print.

I know that this model has well-described issues. If it does one more job like this, it has paid its room and board. If it doesn't (and judging from other customers' experiences, it might not), we tried. Also? I hate the paper feed situation and wonder how this could possibly have happened. Hate is a strong word, and I do not use it lightly. How is it possible in this century to have a color laser printer that does not have a good paper tray? One star off for the lack of a paper tray. One star off for the uncertainty re: longevity,

This met my needs at the time I bought it, but I don't recommend it.

I was at Walmart and bought this set of pencils for my 7 year old daughter, with no intention of using them myself. As I watched how beautiful and vibrant her artwork was, I decided to try them out. Unbelievable! Sometimes artists can assume that they have the best known supplies, and be shocked to find there's better things out there, this is what happened to me, I assumed that the faber castells were the best on the market. In my opinion these prisma colored pencils are the best I've tried yet. They colors are so vibrant, the blend beautifully, and they lay on the paper effortlessly. Every artist should have these, don't always assume that your more expensive pencils are the best out there. In my opinion, these pencils are the number one quality pencils out there. I am HIGHLY satisfied. Since buying my little one these, I immediately ordered the 150 prisma color set, another of the 24 set, the portrait set and the manga set. Now, I know the 150 set has all of their colors, but I ordered the addition sets because these are my new favorite pencils and I wanted to have extras on hand. I say, if you're unsure, order the 12 set, then base your decision from there whether you want to invest in the full set. I can assure any artist they will want to make that investment.

title: I bought these on a whim.
text:
These sheets were on a lightning deal, and I am always looking for easy ways to decorate repurposed items. These vinyl sheets fit the bill. I was skeptical about how long they might take to dry with the inkjet, but I found that within 5 minutes these were dry and ready to cut. I placed them on an old gift box I had revamped into a pen holder. Be sure you have the right placement before sticking these on because the adhesive is top notch. Once they are on, they are on. I waited until I was finished placing them before hitting them with a coat of spray on triple thick, which is something I suggest you do if you are placing them outside. I did this because I wanted them glossy instead of matte, and to prevent any water from potentially ruining my work.
Would I buy them again? In a heartbeat!

Does it need to come in the oversized heavy, book-like packaging?  No.  I’m guessing they were going for the Apple experience on that.  It would be nice if they gave it a simpler packaging though which would help reduce the cost.  I’m guessing these probably cost about 50 cents a pop to make.

title: Decent, if not great gel pen, but the clips are awful.
text: As the title says these are decent gel pens.  Others are much better though especially when you consider these Sharpie ones aren’t exactly cheap.  The ink looks nice and it flows ok, but if you’re using these in any environment where you may have moisture (outdoor first responder note taking etc) the ink smears like crazy (as do many others, but at least are cheaper).  But the worst thing about these pens are without a doubt the clips.  If you will be using these from a pocket I would advise you to steer well clear of these.  I’ve used many brands of gel clip pens over the years and it’s extremely rare that a clip ever breaks.  I had to stop using these at work due to this.  I’ve had them snap off in as little as two days.  I think if you stare at the pen the clip will break off.  That’s how terrible they are.  Sure you can still use the broken pens at home, or at a desk, but if you’re storing them in a pocket it’s a huge pain.

title: My favorite work pen
text: I’m a first responder and I’ve used many work pens over the years.  This is my favorite one.  The ink is opaque and bold and dries very quickly.  Be advised that the ink isn’t waterproof though so don’t buy these if that’s what you’re looking for.  I work outdoors and have used these in rainy conditions and they’ll bleed around like most others.  But they do perform slightly better in that regard than many other pens I’ve used.  But as far as the ink drying during normal writing it’s nearly instantaneous so that’s great as you won’t smudge it around with a hand, clothing or anything else.

text: This is a nice set if you’re looking to try out these colors for making a purchase of a larger bottle. It’s even a decent value if you’ve several inks and won’t need to rely on these smaller bottles for extended daily use. The bottles do contain enough ink to fill several pens or several single pen refills though. While not dry I don’t think Iroshizuku inks are the absolute wettest in general although some can be fairly wet. The inks do flow very well and I’ve not experienced any hard starts or skips due to them. They make some wonderful colors though and the presentation of the full sized bottles is superb. These smaller ones aren’t shabby either.

title: A nice pen for beginners and experienced pen users
text: A great value for the money. It’s a nice design no matter what finish option you go for. Pen comes with a quality nib and I’ve had no flow or hard start issues with the two I’ve purchased. The fact that it comes with a converter, albeit a small squeeze type, at this price point is very nice and something you won’t find much. Opt for the Pilot twist convert if you plan on using exclusively with bottled ink for a nicer experience. While not necessarily a negative, buyers should be aware that the nibs, like most Japanese pens, run a tad smaller in size than most western ones. If you like a super fine line stick with the “fine” nib which in my opinion is like an extra fine. The medium nib will get you a bit wider, but still in the realm of a western fine. If you like to write very bold or even more medium to bold you may want to watch some video reviews to be sure you’ll end up with an enjoyable purchase.

title: Knocked off a star because one of the cartridges was empty

title: Comfortable, well-flowing beginner fountain pen
text:
Since this was my very first fountain pen, it took a little getting used to, but now it is the only thing I want to write with! I also get compliments about how fancy it is.
PS-don’t forget to flush it out with water before filling. I was impatient and just filled the pen first thing, but the ink did not flow as well as it should have until I rinsed it out.

title: Images a Delight - but use good lighting when coloring!
text: I use postcards quite often to correspond with family across the country and am always looking for new or unique cards. These postcards were beautiful drawings of items or designs found in India, and the only concern about these postcards is that the drawings were in very light grayish outlines. To stay within the lines and SEE the designs well enough to color them in with pencil you must have good lighting. I don't recommend markers at all, even thin ones, as the original artwork is so delicately outlined, you will lose the image. Other than that, the images are beautiful and  would be a delight to color.

Now, a few months in, the nib only comes out a short distance, and I really can't write with the pen. It seems like a flimsily made piece of junk.

(Glad I didn't go for the 800, as the 600 is pretty large.) No problems with the nib. I'm glad I bought it, but...my favorites are still my Lamy 2000 and Pilot vanishing point, both of which cost a lot less. They are not as fancy, but are very cool pens (especially the Lamy, which I fell in love with at first sight, and the nib is great)
and they write just as well. The Pilot especially writes like a dream. So, the Pelikan is a great pen and I'm glad I bought it, but it's not necessarily a BETTER pen then those that cost less.

I did have to push on it pretty hard before I heard the little "snap" that meant it was firmly in place. Are some people not pushing firmly enough?  It looks as if there is plenty of room for the plunger and it actually looks as if the converter could be a little longer and still fit. It's great that I can now put bottled ink into my beautiful brass sport and not have to deal with the inferior Kaweco squeeze converter. I am going to buy a few more of these. Why doesn't Kaweco make a converter of this type?  P.S.: I am not associated with a pen store or company and paid full price for this product.

Kaweco really needs to develop a decent converter for the sport line, as I sent away for the one they are selling and it is completely useless. title: Aso- Gao my go-to everyday beautiful blue!
text: I write with fountain pens roughly about 95% of the time, I have some more costly pens and some trusty very affordable ones (Like the Pilot Metropolitan)  Pilot Iroshizuku inks are premium, in the quality of the ink and beautiful packaging. Aso-Gao is my go-to everyday blue ink.  It is a beautiful deeper blue with a hint of purple behind it. It is a subtle blue, not an in your face bright royal "LOOK AT ME" blue.  Aso-Gao is a take me seriously, but know I'm not boring blue. All of the Pilot Iroshizuku inks are rather wet, so even with a Pilot/Namiki Extra fine nib, you will get a very smooth and pleasant writing experience. I highly recommend this ink. Unless you are using a fine nib, preferably Japanese this ink needs a paper that is smooth but not absorbent, or your writing will feather all over the place. Though with my fine nib Pilot Custom 74 or my fine nib Metropolitan it will write without feathering even on regular college ruled paper.

title: I love this pen.
text:
Brief back ground.
For a long time, my Platinum 3776 I bought back in 1980 was the only fountain pen I've used regularly. Before that, two more fountain pens, one was Pilot(Pilot Short) and I don't remember the other one.
I've been very happy with my Platinum 3776, so I had no doubt in what I could expect.
My first impression on Plaisir(white pearl finish, fine nib).
1) light weight, for me, a pen can't be too light.
2) Nice finish, very pleasing color. I later found out that the finish is extraordinary durable. I was expecting some sign of wear after repeat of cap and un-cap, by the experience from other pens. After two months of regular use, no sign of dullness. It still shines like new.
3) Stainless-nib, it works just as good as 14 k gold(as my 3776 has) nib. It felt a little rough at first but by the time first cartridge was finished, it was noticeably smoother. It's almost as smooth as 3776 now, which has impressed anybody tried it. The nib is not flexible, just like all other general purpose writing nibs. I won't be hesitant to choose another stainless nib if I was given a choice between gold nib and stainless nib.
4) Cap & Seal: it really works! I had problem with 3776 for needing a priming (writing something on the paper until the ink flow becomes consistent after it was left a few days unused). There's no need for such worry. It writes with full flow of ink from the first letter on the paper. It's a remarkable improvement over the older models.

Cons?
Some of you may find some cheapness about it, like the band around the cap. It is a cheap pen, it can be bought at $10.-. I have no complaints as long as functionally good.

I'll get another one of these or a few of Preppy with different ink colors.

If you have never tried fountain pen before, any fountain pen, you'll like how it writes compare to other types of pens, Unlike other types of pen, what fountain pens do is just sliding over the paper with no resistance unlike other types which requires you to push the tip down on the paper and smear the ink on the paper. Another advantage is evenness of the line thickness. If you've been dissatisfied with your hand writing, fountain pen makes your hand writing look much better.

title: The pencils themselves are quite nice and functional
text:
I found 4 pack of these at one of those dollar stores. The pencils themselves are quite nice and functional, I have no complaints.
As other reviewers noted, it's the leads I have a problem with.
I'm guessing it's about 4H(compared to all other HB from different makers I have, see chart below), you can barely see what you wrote on the paper. The good part of this is that it lasts about ten times longer, if you have enough patient to use them that long.
You probably would want to throw away the lead and load the real HB instead.
I think the pens alone, without the leads come with, are worth the price.

http://static.jetpens.com/images/a/000/079/79021.jpg

By the way, the leads are 100mm long and that makes it more torturous if you decide to use them up.
And 100mm is not the longest as Papermate claims to be. There are 110mm available at AliExpress and they have much better feel than the free leads come with the pencils from various makers(Papermate and Zebra).

If you want to know how much of waste it leaves at the end, it's about 14mm, which is about the average for pencils not designed for minimizing the waste but still is a lot of waste.

title: Horrible engineering
text:
I went into a store looking to buy a Zebra M-301 0.7mm mechanical pencil, came out the store with 7 pack of this instead.
I thought the price was right at $4.- a pack instead of $5.99 for a 2 pack of M-301.
Like other reviewers say, the lead core breaks so easily because of the metal piece comes off from the plastic part attached to it.
Two parts are connected only by the friction, as you write the metal sleeve wiggles and it comes apart from the plastic part every time you click to advance the core(see photos).
It would have taken only a few days of repeated test use to find out the flaw at R&D level but Zebra engineers neglected to do so.
The solution I came up with was pretty simple but requires a precision work. To put a minuscule amount of Super Glue with something like tooth pick(I used a pencil point instead) onto the thinner part of the plastic where goes into the metal part. It worked like a charm, and the metal part hasn't come out yet(fingers crossed).
Since I like everything else about the pencil, I kept them and repaired all the rest before I even used them.
M-301 is more compact and has no rubber grip(knurled grip gives no significant advantage over smooth body, just as slippery), which is better for carrying and would cause damage less likely to the shirt pocket.
On the other hand, Z-grip is better suited for the extensive use at the desk because of thicker barrel and rubber grip, giving more comfortable feel(at least to me). The length of Z-grip is about 1cm longer than M-301.
Both take longest core, 110mm, but don't have enough length for the spare. If you use 60mm (most common in Amazon) exclusively, this is not a problem.
The product should be marketed as complete without need for any modification.
I even think Zebra should recall all Z-grip and protect their reputation rather than keep selling as it is and damage the brand name.

I would not recommend this product.

title: Much Better than Lamy Safari
text:
Over the last year I got interested in writing with fountain pens. I started with Pilot's Varsity in a medium nib. After using those, I jumped to using a Lamy Safari with a fine nib because the Pilot medium was just a little too broad. It turns out, the Lamy fine is about the same as the Pilot medium. So, I bought another Safari with an extra fine nib.

At the end of the day, the Pilot Varsity is a good pen. The Lamy Safari in fine is OK, and the Lamy Safari in extra fine is not that great. It skips and scratches and is just not that usuable, especially if you print much.

The Pilot MR in fine, on the other hand, is a really good pen Even better when you consider the cost. For me the nib is the perfect width. It writes smooth and it seems to glide over the paper. Ink flow is great. Honestly, after buying this pen I regret buying the Safari pens which were more than twice as much. It works great for cursive, print, and the occasional sketch.

If you are thinking of a first fountain pen, this would be a great purchase.

title: Better than the silver extra fine nib
text: If you have the choice between this one and the silver extra fine nib, definitely buy this one.  The ink flow is smooth and it doesn't seem to scratch the paper as much as some of the other extra fine nibs I have used.  For some reason I can't explain, the silver version of this nib just doesn't work as well.  It scratches the paper more and the ink flow is just not as consistent as it should be.

title: Buy the Black Extra Fine Nib Instead
text: At the time I ordered this nib I also purchased the Extra Fine nib in black at the same due to limited stock.  Unfortunately, this one is inferior to the black one that I bought at the same time.  I was so surprised at the difference, that I actually switched the nibs on the pens they were on just to make sure that it was the nib and not some issue with the pen itself.  The black one seems to have less of a scratch effect to it and the ink flow is much more consistent.  I would consider the black nib very good while this one is just OK.  Neither is as good as some of the Japanese nibs I have used.

title: The screen protector is of a nice thickness and seems like it would take a bit ...
text:
I purchased the anti-glare version of this screen protector and so far it has worked well. Unlike some screen protectors, this one is cut to fit precisely over the screen without coming up short. I took my camera out and shot on a bright, snowy day and the anti-glare film to seem to help to reduce glare and reflections on the screen making it easier to see the images both while shooting and reviewing. The screen protector is of a nice thickness and seems like it would take a bit of abuse.

My only issue was that installation was a little trickier than I had thought, but that was probably due in part to the design of the screen and my rush to put it on. Initially, I put it on with the removable tab in the bottom-left corner. Due to the shallow channel between the screen and the trim as well as the trim around the buttons on the left side of screen, this made it difficult to get it completely flush on the first try. If I were to do it over again, I would probably install it with the removeable tab in the upper right-hand corner where there is less to get in the way. YRMV.

One thing I can say, is that Expert Shield had emailed me before I actually got the protector to let them know how I had liked it since I was one of the first to buy it. I responded back with my installation problem and the fact that my initial attempt left me with a misaligned screen protector that I was having trouble removing/repositioning. They in turn replied with some tricks of getting the protector back off and back on again which did the trick. So, kudos to them for being responsive to the customer.

Overall, I am very pleased so far. Given the lack of other options, I would recommend this product if you are looking for a way to protect your screen on your XE-2.

Now while I am here I would like to mention some things about fountain pens in general. Why do some get many five star rating yet a few people only give a one stasr. I thiunk there are a number of reasons.
1) The PAPER the reviewer used. A pen may react differently to different papers.
2) Not knowing how to get a pen started. I like to use the converter fill it up then back off so one drop of ink falls on a paper.
3) Perhaps to a lesser degree its the ink used. I ordered Parker ink because I got as Parker pen. Maybe another brand would work just as well but I dfont want to chance it.
4) The way the pen is held. The angle and orientation of the nib.
5) Maybe, from what I have read, the pen shoud first be flushed with cold water, perhaps there is some oil from manufacturing in the pen.
6) Product variability. Maybe you were unluckily and got the lemon of a bunch.
7) For a really good evaluation the pen shoud be used a while first.

If any others would like to add to this please do.

The ink flows smoothly. The colors pop on the page. It is easy to hold and write with. Overall, just a great set of pens. I will definitely be putting this on my wish list for future purchase.

title: Very sturdy
text: This book stand is very sturdy and it looks nice on the desk or shelf. It is easy to use. It stays in place. It keeps the pages set. I like to use it for cookbooks but it works well for other uses as well like displaying a nice book as decoration. Overall, I'm pleased with it.

title: Works well
text: The LLPT Double Sided Adhesive Roller works quite well. There are no stray parts. I can see where the adhesive is on the paper. If there is stray adhesive, I can rub it off. It does secure the paper. Overall, it is very easy to use and effective too. I do wish there was just a bit more on the roller, but it is comparable to other brands so that's a minor thing. I will still consider for future purchase.

title: Standard and that is fine
text: This JOYEUX lined journal is a standard journal and that's fine by me. The weight of the paper is good for most pens. The lines are clear and the paper is an off white which is easy on the eyes. The binding is good and the cover is sturdy. It works exactly as I need so it is a solid 5-star for me.

title: Like it
text: The price point is a bit high for the size of this organizer so I would have to really think about it if I were to purchase in the future. That said, I do like this PACKGILO Wooden Storage Box with 4 Drawers. It is a nice size for me desk area. It came assembled with no missing parts. The drawers open and close smoothly. The writing on the drawers is a little off-trend these days, but it can be sanded off and the item repainted easily enough. Again, it is the price that gives me pause for a future purchase, but overall, I do like it.

title: Very fine line
text:
The tip of this ball point pen is very fine which I appreciate when I need to write in tight spaces. The pen does seem to require me to scratch on a scratch paper to get the ink started if I haven't used the pen in a while, but after that, it is good to go.

I do like the color/art on the casing. It is bright, cheerful and easy to find in my purse. Overall, I do like these pens.

title: Cute and cheerful
text: I selected this Kawaii Journal Notebook (A6, Blue) for myself but it ended up with a grandniece who is enjoying it a lot. It is cute and cheerful. The clasp closes nicely. The size is perfect to slide into a pocket in her backpack. She's very happy with it so I am too.

title: Like it overall
text: I have a few quibbles on the changing features on this Labelife Label Maker Machine with Tape. It isn't quite as intuitive as I thought it would be and the instructions are a bit confusing. That said, I am getting the hang of it and I do like how it works. It arrived in good time and responsibly packaged. It had everything needed to set up. Once I got used to how to format the font etc, I went to town on creating labels. Overall, I quite like it.

title: Very good fit for the laundry area
text:
I selected this utility cart as I hoped it would fit between the wall and our washer-dryer combo. I'm trying to declutter and organize so I wanted a smaller cart that would help us store items but not take up too much space. This rolling cart fit that objective.

It was very easy to put together. The wheels are a little wonky but that's fine for our needs. We just need it to roll front and then back. So overall, we are pleased with this product. It is a good fit for the area that it was intended and it fit the objective of why I selected it.

title: Works for me
text: The print quality is what I expected for this Phomemo Mini Pocket Printer- M02X Inkless Printer so in that sense, I am happy with it. It is easy to use and install/pair with my phone. I like the thermal feature so I don't have to worry about ink. Instructions were easy to follow. Overall, it is what I wanted and expected.

title: Really liking the paper
text:
Now that I'm getting to use this House of Daisy Dot Bullet Journal with Gold Foil Enlightened Lotus cover, I am really liking it. I can't really find a fault with it. I'm setting up for the new quarter and I use a lot of markers and pens. The paper is smooth and not showing any bleed-thru. Compared to the journal that I am using for the current quarter, I can really tell the difference.

I still prefer the B5 size, but they can get pricey so this A5 size with this good quality paper is a best case alternative. The price point is comparable to other brands so this is a brand that I'll keep in mind for future purchase.

title: Really like this size and format
text: I took these composition notebooks to the office because it is 6 pack of notebooks. They are a hit. The size is great. They like the open space at the top of each page. It is easy to flip through and put away. The lack of rings at the top is also a big bonus. Had I known how much I would like the format (or how fast they would be snapped up), I would have been more stingy and kept more for myself. That said, the price point is reasonable so I will purchasing another pack soon.

title: LIke it best for cookbooks
text:
I selected this book stand to help me when I needed to type out letters and other work tasks. It sits stable on a desk and I could adjust the angle.

That said, I use it mostly for cookbooks when I'm trying new recipes. I've tried more recipes from my various cookbooks since I've received this book stand than I have in a couple of years. I just put it on the counter or table and put in the cookbook to the pages that I need. The stand keeps everything nice, neat and readable for me. When I'm done, I just flatten it and put it away.

For that reason alone, I am pleased with this product and I am getting a lot good use out of it.

title: Very convenient
text: I appreciate the Eulps Ergonomic Computer Arm Rest for Desk. It doesn't require any tools to put into use. It is sturdy. It provides support that is needed. I like the ability to put up and then put down. It is so convenient to use and it makes working at my desk a lot more comfortable.

title: Effective
text: The Scotch Super-Hold Wide Tape wasn't quite what I had expected but that has turned out to be a good thing. The tape is wide but still easy to work with. The adhesion is effective. The amount on the roll is generous. Overall, it is better than I had expected and I will consider for future purchase.

title: Great size for storing paper
text: I love this set of iBune 4 Pack Scrapbook Paper Storage Boxes. These storage boxes have helped a lot in my quest for organizing the scrap-booking materials. They are clear with useful size dimensions. The snap locks also work well. They fit in my bin perfectly as well. I don't have any complaints at all. A solid 5 star for me.

title: Functional and sturdy
text: These multi-functional geometric ruler set is working well. We like that the rulers were marked (High school and junior high school). We like that they each have a plastic sleeves. The rulers have been in use for about a month and seem sturdy and accurate. In short, we're pleased with the rulers. The price point might seem a little high compared to standard rulers but for the use that these are getting, we find that it would be worth it.

title: Cute and pretty
text: This journal notebook is a hit. The size is perfect to carry in a purse. The pages are nicely decorated. The cover is as kawaii as described. The young one who received this journal to use LOVES IT and that is what matters.

title: Getting good use out of it
text: I have gotten similar items like this office pen and desk organizer. I generally liked them at first but eventually, they became less useful/workable for me. In this case, I've had it in use for almost two months and I'm still liking it a lot. I like that I can move the units to where I prefer. It is easy to keep organized. They are easy to clean which is important to me. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product.

title: Already in use
text: The person who got this SULIRUN1981 2022 Planner A5 Weekly & Monthly, January to December with Calendar Stickers has started to put it into use now that we are closer to 2022. She loves the weight of the paper and how smooth it is to write in. She likes the organization of the pages as it is to her preference. She also likes the stickers. The size is also to her preference in that that it is big enough to write in comfortably but not so big that it becomes bulky to carry with her. It is, in her opinion, the perfect planner and she looks forward to using it in 2022.

title: Like the size
text: This dotted journal is my favorite size (B5). The paper is just a tad lighter gsm than I prefer but the B5 size makes up for it. I also like the softcover. Hardcover is nice for support, but I generally write at a table or desk so it isn't as needed for me. The softcover actually works better for how I write in that it is just more comfortable. Another thing I like is that the dots are not heavy but they are not light either so I can find them when I am using them as a guide. My previous dotted journal's dot was too light and hard to see. This is perfect for my eyes. Overall, I really like this journal.

title: Dries fairly quick
text:
I am starting to go back to liking ball-point pens over gel pens and that's due to ink smear of gel, but this Pentel EnerGel ICE Retractable Gel Pen's gel ink dries fairly quick so I am liking it a lot. It has what I like about gel pens (nice flow of ink to page) but reduces what I am not as keen on (gel ink needs to dry or it will smear).

It is a comfortable pen to hold and control. It looks good on paper. It is a Pentel which is a brand that I like. Overall, I am liking this pen a lot.

title: Generous amount of paper
text: I do like a couple of the packages in this 4 package bundle more than the other two, but all of them are very nice. They work well for how I am planning and creating pages for my planner and journaling pages. They work well with other pieces that I have in my collection. They do bleed a little when writing on the paper with gel or ink pens, but it works fine with ballpoint pens. The amount in the set is generous at 240 and overall, I am enjoying and using this set of paper with its vintage vibe.

title: Works as expected
text: This item works as expected. I like that it is firm and keeps its shape. I also like the extra pad when more height is needed. It does help me keep better posture in my chair which helps me overall.

title: Generous amount of sheets and stickers
text: This set of Habit Tracker Planner Stickers is very generous. I was able to divvy out to family based on what they like to use for their planners. I prefer sticking to weekly tracking. The adhesion for the stickers is good. The graphics are clean and stay in place. It is definitely worth the try.

title: Beautiful journal
text: I do wish the dots in this dotted were just a bit darker, but that aside, this  Scribble & Dot | Bullet Dotted Journal - Gold Bee is beautiful. I love the cover. The paper is so smooth to write on. The paper is thick but not too thick. It does keep any bleed-thru to a minimum but the paper is still easy to flip through. It is sturdy and elegant. Just a really beautiful journal.

title: Useful for household's need
text: I selected this 2 set of accordion file organizers becuase I liked the A6 size. I didn't want a letter-plus versions since I needed something to help me organize receipts and letters to keep where I could store upright in a drawer. It was a good decision for my household as they are the right size for what we needed. The 13 slots also work well and the securing with the cord is good as well. Functionally, it is exactly what we wanted.

title: Nice and neat
text: The Refillable Glazed Printing Craft Paper is nice, neat and works well. I use it in my budget binder for planning and notes. It isn't fancy but it gets the job done.

title: Useful set
text: This planner sticker set is a useful and pretty set. The stickers are a good size for planners. The color is vibrant and the graphics are crisp. I like that the stickers are designs that I feel like I will use when the holiday month comes around. They aren't too cutesy yet they are still fun. I like this set a lot.

title: Good size and keeps things in place
text: I really like this LUXACO Mouse Pad. The Navy color is great in that it hides pen marks. I like that it keeps my keyboard in place. The downside is that the mouse can get 'stuck' if I'm a bit heavy on it but I'll take it because I like my keyboard to be steady on the desk. It is a good size and it is easy to clean. It hits all the marks for me.

title: So far so good
text: I am printing more now that I work from home so finding alternatives for print cartridges has become a challenge. That's why I selected this product to try out. It is working out so far. It is holding up well. No leaks. Easy to put in. Prints evenly. I also like that it was responsibly packaged. It was protected but it was overdone. Overall, I'm quite pleased.

title: Love the cover
text: I love the cover of this Scribble & Dot journal. The green is so vibrant and the simple gold detailing of the Monstera leaf. It is simple and so pretty. The paper is 160 gsm so it doesn't bleed too much. It holds pretty well. The only reason why I can't give a 5-star is the dots are a little too light. Otherwise, it is such a nice journal.

title: Like the support
text: There are two things that I like about this ergonomic foot rest: (1) feels good on my feet and (2) feel like I have extra support. The first thing is something I hadn't expected but it does make a difference since I work at home and I don't wear shoes at home. It is nice to have something soft and pleasant under my feet. The second thing is what I was hoping. The support keeps my position in alignment. Maybe it is mental but it helps and I can feel the difference. I'm glad that I finally tried once of these foot rests.

title: Can see why Posca markers are popular
text: I was curious when I selected this set of Posca Paint Markers (Extra Fine Point). I had heard that Posca Paint Markers were good so I wanted to see for myself. I am impressed. They do have an intended use so like other brush pens, the better the paper surface, the better the markers work. So I kept that in mind and when in use, they are really nice. The color is vibrant. The pen is easy to handle. These are extra fine point so the coverage is a little different but for me, being new to the markers, it works well. I am glad that I got the opportunity to try this line out and will definitely consider for future purchase.

title: Compact and useful
text: The Alfion Desk Adhesive Tape Dispenser is compact in that it doesn't take up much space on the desk. It is light but sturdy. It is easy to use. The tape rolls smoothly and the metal cuts effectively. It functions really well. I'm pleased with it.

title: Simple design and easy to use
text: Some journals have elaborate closures that make them annoying to use. That's not the case for this journal. It is simply designed so that is easy to open and close. The variety of design on paper is also nice. It has graph, dotted, lined and plain paper. The size is compact so it is easy to tuck into a purse. A nice little journal.

title: Pretty
text: This little journal is pretty. The paper works best with a ballpoint pen but for journal writing, that's my preferred pen so it works okay for. I like the bookmark as well. It makes a nice gift set. It is a good size in that it isn't too big. I can concentrate on using it mainly for journaling and not planning. Overall, I like it.

title: Helpful to have it
text: I'd be using a cutting mat but finally gave it and got a real desk mat. The pink color is cheerful. The size is functional. It is easy to clean. My keyboard doesn't go sliding. The mouse has a level are so it responds better. I'm glad I finally gave in. It is very helpful to have this deskmat.

title: Works as needed
text: Amazon Basics LCD 8-Digit Desktop Calculator is a basic calculator. It is light and useful. I take it with me for grocery shopping and it works like a charm.

title: Looks nice
text: The VINTAGE LEATHER JOURNAL SCRAPBOOK for Women & Men, Leather Bound Junk Journal looks nice. It took me awhile to get used to the paper. It has a different texture but I'm getting used to it. It has a nice presentation and would make a good gift.

title: Looks good but not useful
text: It looks good but it wasn't useful. The drawers were stuck. The wood is a bit unfinished and I got a splinter rying to get one of the drawers to come out. The wood is very light and soft so it doesn't even make a good paperweight. If it is just for decoration, it would be fine, but as a functioning item, it was disappointing.

title: Nice and simple
text: I like these Thank You stickers because they are nice and simple. They don't clash but they still stand out just enough to be noticed. They adhere well. They are a generous amount. They look good and readable. Thank You stickers don't need to be fancy. They just have to simple, look nice and be readable. These stickers hit those marks.

title: Nice quality
text: I like the quality on these postcards. They have a nice vintage look. They are sturdy enough to survive the mail system. They are easy to write on. All in all, a good postcard with a pleasant image. It works well for scrapbooking, especially when the journal paper is a bit thin and needs more support.

title: Generous amount with nice sharp quality
text: At 600 pieces, this set of mini-stickers was more than I could ever use. I ended up passing them out for others to use. The stickers are mini but they have a nice, sharp quality to the image. There is a nice variety as well with barely any repetition. A nice set of mini-stickers at a reasonable price point.

title: Lanyard clip is a bit wonky but
text: Lanyard clip is a bit wonky but once it is on, it is good. There's nothing fancy about  TSAIYOGA Vaccine Card Protectors but they work. We don't wear it, but we do keep it in our bags and if we need to wear it, we can. Overall, it functions as needed.

title: Smooth writing
text: Surcotto's roller pen (black) works well for how I write. It is smooth. It doesn't require a lot of pressure. It is as quick drying as expected, it still dries pretty quick and the ink looks good on paper. A very nice pen to use.

title: This cat lover loves it
text: I love this cat stationery set. There is one sticky note that I'm not that keen on, but that's just one item in the set. The rest is getting used. I like the little note book. I like the 'things to do' pad probably the best. The stickers are cute. The sticky notes, save for the one, are also cute. This cat lover loves it.

title: Look pretty and easy to use
text: I love this set of magnetic bookmarks. They look pretty and are easy to use. They don't get caught on other things due to stick out of the book. They are seem a nice addition when gifting a book. Such a simple thing but it makes for a bright sight during the day.

title: A bit of cute perfection
text: When I selected this cute dog planner sticker set by PPAPPAPPIYO, I was curious but didn't have any expectations. I was happily surprised. The variety of the stickers is fantastic but honestly, it is the cute dog that sells it. The design just makes the sticker pop on the page. It is whimsical and fun and produces a smile. Each sticker is a bit of cute perfection.

title: Works on most surfaces
text:
I like Zebra pens and I do like this ballpoint pen. It is smooth. That said, I have found that there are a few surfaces that it doesn't like. I have this bullet journal that I got from a local store a few years back. Once I started using it, I realized why I had put off using it but too late, I already did the page planning so I was committed. I thought this ballpoint pen would overcome the journal's weird paper but it skips on the paper. The pen also doesn't like the label paper I use for block correction.

Otherwise, I like the pen. It works for my regular notebooks and work notepads. Since that is where I will use it mostly (office work/location), it gets a 4-star from me.

title: Pretty
text: This Faber-Castell Metallic Highlighter Set have pretty colors but they aren't very good for highlighting as they have quite a bit of bleed-thru. I do like to use them for art journaling where the color is being used intentionally so I have prepped on how I want to use the markers similar to when I'm using watercolors so I'm pleased to have selected the set. That said, I can't go above 3-stars only because the set is marked as highlighters and they don't quite meet that function.

title: Easy to use
text: Finally got to use this label printer. It is easy to use and set up. Also, it seems pretty sturdy and stable. The label feeder tray is also a nice addition. It works as expected almost right after installation.

title: Works as expected
text:
There is only one thing different from what I'm used to with the BOMEI PACK Transparent Office Tape with Dispenser and it was that the sticky part was facing up and I'm used to it facing now. A minor thing since my plan was to take it out of the plastic dispenser and put the roll on my tape dispenser (yay! it fit perfect!).

Otherwise, I'm quite pleased with this tape. It works as expected. It is the clear type of tape that I prefer whether for gift wrapping or journaling or anything that I would use it on. Simple and functional which is what I wanted and got. I'm happy with this product.

title: Nice support
text: Soundance Ergonomic Mouse Pad with Wrist Support has good support and it does make using the mouse a lot more comfortable. I don't feel the fatigue at end of day as much as before I had this mouse pad. I selected this product out of curiosity and so glad that I did.

title: Nice notebook
text: My favorite bullet journal is from RETTACY so when I saw this A5 blank notebook, I figured it was worth a try. The paper is nice and smooth. I like the soft cover. There's no wasted pages. I'm using one of the two books for sketching wihch is filling up pretty fast so I'm glad this was a set of two. All in all, I'm liking this notebook.

title: Nice set
text: I have to admit that I might like the pen set more than the journal; however, I can see why the Leuchturm 1971 bullet journal is popular. The paper is nice. The dots are consistent. The pages are numbers. I generally don't use content pages, but I can see why people would like them. There is some bleed-thru from the pens that I use but with pen set that it comes with, it works fine. Overall, a very nice set.

title: Generous
text: This set of planner stickers curated and sold by AMAZING TIME is very generous in count. There is enough variety that I can find a type (ex: budget) to use at some point. It should last awhile. The adhesion is good and I like the colors. Nice, functional and, again, quite generous in its count.

title: Simple and neat
text: Camidy Identity Theft Protection Roller Stamp is simple and neat. It is easy to use and covers well. I also really like the cap. In this day and age where mail and papers can't just be thrown out, this little item comes in handy.

title: Simple yet beautiful with wonderful paper
text:
I used my dotted journals for planners, sketching, journaling, etc. The B5 size has become my favorite size even if A5 is the most common. So when I saw this Dingbats journal at B5 become available to select, I grabbed it.

It is my first Dingbats journal. I'd heard some good things about the line but honestly, it was the size that got my attention. Seriously, though, I see why it has fans. The cover is simple but striking with the woven fabric hardcover with the simple embossed bee. I'm glad that it doesn't have the 'contents' pages that some brands have because I find that to be wasted pages. The paper is fantastic. Smooth to write on and almost zero bleed thru and I tested with the markers that generally cause the most in other journals.

It is so nice that I'm tempted to be stingy on using it but it is meant to be used so I'm enjoying it. I'll definitely put on my list for future purchase when I want to treat myself to something special. This Pro version is a bit pricey but I think the quality makes it worth it as far as I am concerned.

title: Works well and like the cap
text: I like the Unjoo Whiteout Correction Tape. Correction tape is generally easy to use and this product follows that behavior. I do like the small cap that goes over the tip. Sometimes the white tape curls up but it is easily smoothed back onto the paper. It is a simple item, but I use it a lot so I'm pleased with this product.

title: So pretty
text: I have to admit that I have another dip pen that works a tad better, but this SIPLIV Glass Dip Pen is just so pretty to use. It is calming and comfortable and I need both of those "C's" is my life these days. It does work well and I do like the blue ink that the pen came with. It would make a great gift for someone who likes interesting writing tools.

title: Snaps are a little stubborn but I like the look
text: I really like the look of this  Leather Journal/Notebook that is re-fillable due to binder rings. Generally, I don't like binder rings but I'm good with them on this size. The one that I'm not as keen on is that the snaps are a bit stubborn when trying to close, at least for the one that I received. I can live with it though because it may get easier with use and I really like the look of the item. It is plain so as long as I take care of it, the look will always be "in style". It feels good to use too. So I am liking this item quite a lot.

title: Works well as a writing journal
text: The paper isn't quite as thick as I would like so I'm not using this classic dot journal with brush pens or art. I'm using it strictly as a 'write 3 pages a day' journal and it is working well. The paper is fine to the touch. It takes the ballpoint pen well. The dots are just noticeable enough to use to guide me but not so noticeable as to be distracting. I like the hard back and that the pages lay flat. It makes it easier to write in. Overall, a nice writing journal. I like it.

title: Nice set
text: I have to admit that it was the pens that came with this black paper notebook bundle that made me try it out. I do like the pens too (name brand and good quality) but I also like the black paper notebook. I have to admit that I write what I need and then tear it to put in my art journal or planner. I'd never really understood why there was black paper notebooks but I get it now. The notebook does have a lot of pages but I think it is a reasonable amount for how I plan to use it. A really nice set.

title: More useful than expected
text: I had selected iCakper's notebook binder because the plastic binder pockers would help with corralling receipts. That's what the idea was. I am not using it for receipts. Instead, it has been much more useful with corralling notes, stickers, cut outs and general loose items that I would throw here and there. I still could use it for receipts at some point because the amount of plastic binders that it came with is generous. I also like that the closure is magnetic so I'm not fighting to close it. It just hits the right spot and closes. Such a simple product but so much more useful than I had expected.

title: Pretty good
text: The Smead Cloth Expanding File works pretty much as expected. It is advertised to expand to 2 inches which is about right. The snap closure on the one that I received is a little finicky but it does close. I like the letter size. It says that it is navy but looks more steel grey and I'm a-okay with that. The only thing that kept it from being a 5-star is the odor that took awhile to go away. Otherwise, it is pretty good.

title: Generous and functional
text: The Qualsen 24 pcs Mesh Zipper Pouches is a generous amount and the pouches are a good and useful size. Since there are 4 colors, I'm able to color-code what I'm using them for (Blue - Work; Pink - Mail to review; Yellow - Stickers; and Green - TBD). I like cord on the zipper tab as it makes it easy to hang. Simple product and quite useful.

title: Comfortable pen that writes well
text:
I use gel pens a lot for one reason or another. When I saw the Paper Mate Profile Ballpoint Pens available, I selected it because it made me realize that I didn't have any black ball point pens. I only had gel, brush pens, and calligraphy pens.

I really like that it came in a 4 pack. I like how comfortable the pen is to use. It suits how I grip pens almost perfectly. The ink is consistent so I don't have to press very hard and it stays nice and neat. Honestly, it reminded why ball point pens are standard as it works well on a good number of paper surfaces. It reminds me to keep a supply of ballpoint pens, especially black ones.

title: Works like a charm
text: The ExcelMark 3/4" Security Roller Stamp works like a charm. Just roll it over the area to block out and the text is blocked. I looked on the other side of the paper and it obscures completely. I'm still trying to figure out where I need to re-ink if/when the ink runs out, but otherwise, I like this simple but effective tool. It has saved me time with the shredding scissors and I appreciate that muchly.

title: Good for notes and journaling
text: I'm using this lined notebook for training notes. It works well for me because of the sturdy cover and the pages can take a lot of highlighted and sketching to go with the notes. The cover has a humorous sketch that is a nice change of pace. Overall, I quite like it.

title: Like it
text: I like this Gorilla Tough & Wide Mounting Tape. It is easy to use and easy to remove. I change my mind a few times (or more) and it was easy to remove and adjust. There are a few surfaces that it didn't work but that was expected. Overall, it works as I expected and I like it.

title: Works as expected
text: This set of notebooks from Yoobi work as expected. The lines are easy to see. The size is standard. The pack of three is economical. It doesn't have binder holes or tear out perforations but that's fine for me since I wouldn't use to tear out and put in a binder. For me, this set of notebooks as I expect.

title: Cute stickers
text: This set of stickers from bloom are great for my planner. I have a bullet journal so I like the pop of color from these stickers. They adhere well; they look cute; and there is a nice variety. It is a nice set of stickers.

title: Easy to assemble
text: The CORFICH 3 Tiered Rolling Utility Cart was super easy to assemble. I think I had it all put together in 20 minutes. It comes with all the hardware needed to put it together and all the hardware worked which is nice. The size is standard. It is plastic but a sturdy plastic. The color is neutral blue so it blends well into the decor. The cups that snap onto the shelves is a great addition. It is convenient and useful. Overall, a good item and I'm satisfied.

title: Pens are great
text: I love the pens in this Noted by Post-it Brand Office Essentials Set. I also like the Notes book and post-its but the pens really make it a 5-star for me. Just a nice set overall that can is useful and giftable.

title: Love the pen
text: I really love the pen in this quill pen and ink set with journal. The ring binder journal is okay. I knew what I was getting when I selected this item although ring binder journals aren't my go-to journal type. That said, I like the paper. The key, though, is the quill pen. I haven't tried all the tips but what I have tried is a dream. The writing is smooth and the pen easy to use. It is actually kind of addicting to use. I like it a lot more than I had expected.

title: Liked the traditional postcards
text: Fancyoung 32Pcs Set Travel Sights Landscape Postcard Greeting Cards Souvenir Gifts is an interesting set of cards. It is a good paper quality. Thick and not prone to bending. I do prefer the traditional pictures of the sites. I wasn't as keen on the cards with regular tourists or the picture of the lady walking her dogs. I guess it is to evoke 'home style picture taking'. I can understand a picture of a tourist bus but a picture of the tourists as the focus? Or the lady walking her dog? That just seems like taking pictures of people without their permission. Anyway, there are a lot of pictures that I do like (the ferris wheel, the carousel, the macarons, the Eiffel Tower, etc) and they do outnumber the 'odd' ones so I like it overall.

title: Functional and consistent
text: The Amazon Basics Self-Inking Date Stamp is functional and consistent in its stamping behavior. It is also convenient to use and the stamp is nice and tidy. The only reason I don't give it a 5-star was the lack of directions. Obviously, I figured out how to put the stamp pad into the stamp but it was a little messy so a little direction would have been nice. Otherwise, I'm liking this date stamp. It is neat, tidy and functional.

title: Works well
text: The biggest challenge that I have for these labels is that my eyes aren't as good as they used to be so finding the edges for the labels requires a little extra light. The borders between the labels are wider than expected but I guess that was needed for the size and layout. I'm not complaining though; I can always find a way to use the borders as 'correction tape.' So overall, the labels work as expected and have good adhesion and I'm satisfied with the results.

title: Post-Its are still the best
text: I use other brands than Post-Its and it can be up-and-down on consistency. Post-Its are so consistently good. This set reminded me of the consistent quality. I like the variety and the neutral colors that are easy on the eyes. Mostly, I like that it sticks and if I pull the note off, there is no residue left behind. The set has a generous amount of notes that looks neat and tidy. I'm a fan.

title: Not quite working for me
text: I am not sure what it is, but I cannot get this item to stick. I've followed the directions. I've tried the mounting strip that it came and then two others. Yet it keeps dropping. And before I mounted, I did clean the area under the desk. I like the design and the concept, but for some reason, it just doesn't quite work for me.

title: Functional and convenient
text:
The Tiyafuro Acrylic Desk Organizer was what I was looking for to help deal with my pens, pencils and other stuff.

And I have a lot of 'other stuff'.

So this organizer is functional and convenient for me. It fits on my desk. The amount of compartments is just the right amount. The top shelf is useful for smaller items like correcting tape and glue sticks. The middle shelf is used for everyday pens, mechanical pencils and brush pens. The third shelf is for pens that use for my journaling. Bottom shelf of compartments is for memo pads and tape.

I really like it. It is organized and easy access. Just what I had hoped for.

title: Looks good but it sometimes ignores what I press
text: I like the look of this RUSSELL+HAZEL Acrylic Calculator. It looks pretty on the desk. That said, it has its quirks that I haven't figured out yet.
