No matter how much I clean out the paper in the house, there are just some items that can't be thrown out. Yet, they do need to be organized. I like the sorter isn't huge so I still have to be mindful of what is being saved. The color separators help with additional sorting for category. This is definitely a help.

title: Comfortable in all right places
text: The MDL Furniture Ergonomic Office Chair High Back Mesh Chair with Adjustable Headrest and Armrests, Tilt Lock, Lumbar Support Mesh Desk Executive Office Chair (in Black) is working out great. It took about 30 minutes to put together. It is comfortable in all the right places. Usually, it takes awhile to get used to a new office chair in finding the right height and tilt, but this chair was easy to adjust and get used to and the 'lumbar support' part of the description is more appreciated now that the chair is in actual use .  Quite pleased with this product.

title: Streamlined and uncluttered
text:
I really like this Emily Ley 2019 Weekly & Monthly Planner, The Simplified Planner. At 8-1/2" x 11" is a good size and I l like bright stripes and colors. It makes it enticing to use. What I like best though is that it is truly simplified. It is separated by month and weeks with a helpful tab. The days are have a "My Day" section for appointments or notes for day and a To Do list section. It is a simple layout that I really like in planners. There isn't extra pages or stickers which I give extra points because sometimes it just seems a waste.

There is a page called "Simplified Prep-Work"/The Simplicity Challenge filled with bullet points of simplicity tips that I actually find mindful and useful so I don't mind it. There is one page for notes that follow; then a list of holidays; and a bucket list. At the back, there are 4 years of months (2019 to 2022) followed by 2 pages of future planning for 2020. I also like that it doesn't have contact pages because I never use those pages.

Again, it isn't fussy which I like and it has everything that I like to have in planner.

title: Nice and smooth
text: I like this set of PILOT Frixion Clicker 10 Pens Assorted Pouch. They write smooth. They have good color (except maybe one of the greens which is a bit light). The ability to erase is nice and a bonus is that the eraser (the top end of the pen) doesn't really look like an eraser. It is the only effective eraser for the ink. If you try to use a standard eraser, it doesn't work. That's fine for me. Overall, I like the set and given that I like to use different colored pens for note taking, this is nearly perfect for me.

title: Nice to have item at home
text: I don't think I'll use this Mead Laminator, Thermal, HeatSeal PRO Lamination Machine very often, but it is easy to use and seems well made. It is a nice size. It was big enough that I was able to laminate a photo of my mother when she was just out of high school as well as a drawing of my father when he was in grade school. Both items are treasured so it is nice to have the originals  protected. So I have found uses for it. My only concern is the cost of supplies. It is something that I would consider for future purchase. One never knows though. I thought I would never go back to a vacuum cleaner with a bag but the best vacuum cleaning I own at present requires a bag and I gladly purchase them. The more I find uses for it, the more I am likely to justify the additional cost of supplies.

title: Good basic planner
text: AT-A-GLANCE Weekly / Monthly Planner, January 2019 - December 2019, Large Planner, Badge Stripe (5148E-905) is a no-frills planner. I like its simplicity. I'm addicted to planners but I like them for specific uses. For work, I like basic planners with few bells and whistles because I can get distracted by it. Bells and whistles are fine for personal stuff, but for work, I like the planner clean and simple. This planner fits that description. I also like the size and the tabs so I can get to the month that I need quickly. The only thing that I wish it had was more lines per day, but the space per day is good so I can work around that. I look forward to using this in the upcoming year.

title: Just how I like it
text: I do prefer the monthly calendar set closer to the weekly of the month so that is the only 'drawback' that I can find and it is a minor one because I like everything else about it. I like the days on one side with the checklist, goals, etc on the other because I like to use planners for more than appointments and this layout works well for me. I also like that the ring binder is compact and proportionate to the thickness of the pages so it doesn't stick out. That alone makes up for the monthly calendar 'drawback' noted at the beginning. When the rings are too big, I often find they snag on other stuff and I end up not taking the planner with me and then I stop using it. This planner is just how I like it.

title: Interesting design and functions nicely
text: This Scotch Tape Dispenser Clear Tape Dispenser as a record player is functional and interesting looking. The main thing is that it functions well and I like the design. I thought it might be a little awkward to use because I'm so used the standard design but this was easy to get used to and I like that it has a cover that I can snap shut. It will help manage dust. Aside from the functionality, the vinyl record player look is a conversation starter. I have this at work and quite a few people have commented on it. The list price is a higher than the standard tape dispenser that I got recently but for the interesting design, I would consider it for future purchase.

title: Nice and classic looking
text: Mind Reader Desk Supplies Organizer For Letters, Pens, Pencils, Phone and Desk Accessories, 4 Compartments in faux leather is that kind of item that you are pretty sure that you don't need but once you have it, you're glad that you do. The small compartments are the perfect size for post-its and other miscellany like paper binders and clips. The longer compartment works for pens, pencils, scissors and the surprisingly always needed, staple remover. It does look nicer on the desk than plastic organizers. A classic touch is my impression.

title: Helps organize the desk area nicely
text: I like the size of the trash can from this Mind Reader 4 Piece Desk Organizer Set. The pen/pencil holder is also a good size. I thought the item with the three slots was for mail but it says that it is a notepad holder and it can be used to hold notepad, perhaps steno-size notepads at the largest. I still like it for mail because I still use snail mail. The memo pad holder is nice for post-its. All in all, I used all 4 items either as described or for something else and it does help organize the desk area nicely.

title: Works well to help unclutter and organize desk documents
text: I really like that I didn't have to put anything together with this Mind Reader Mesh Desk Organizer 5 Trays Desktop Document Tray. It is all one piece and it does work for letter sized file folders, mail, letter sized paper, and other miscellany. I think the only 'downside' is that top horizontal shelf starts to bend in if there is certain amount of weight. I put an standard office tape dispenser and stapler on that area and it started to bend. That's a minor thing though because it works well for what I need in that it helps me unclutter and organize the desk more so I like it.

title: Easy to put together and use
text:
Upon first putting together Mind Reader's Desk Organizer with 4 Sliding Trays, I thought "Oh no, the legs don't match in height. No biggie but still..." But really, it was easy to fix. In putting it together, I had tightened one side in a way that caused the crookedness. Once I loosened the connection where it was crooked and adjusted, it was fine.

The point of that is that it was easy to put together and easy to fix when there was an issue. The sliding trays can pop out on the other end so I have it against the wall so there's an additional stop, but otherwise, I like it quite a bit. It makes me wish I had grabbed the 3 draw version for work as well.

title: Standard and affordable
text: Binder clips are a fairly straightforward office supply item and these AmazonBasics Binder Clips in medium do the job that binder clips are expected to do. They are the standard black and silver and feel the usual kind of sturdy. The amount of boxes in the shipment was quite generous so we're pleased in that respect as well. It is worth a look for future purchase as the price per box breaks down in affordable comparison.

title: Like the size
text:
I was curious about the 'mini' in the PENTEL Med 8/Pkg -RSVP Mini Ballpt Pen Ballpoint Pen and the pens are smaller than the standard, but I kind of like the size. I'm already partial to this pen in its regular size. It is a colorful set and while the orange pen is always the problematic one in a set, there are others that make up for it. By problematic, the orange always seems a bit too light for what I need in a pen but that's a personal preference.

As noted, I rather like the size as it is easy to fit in my pen and paper pad pouch that I keep in my purse. The pens writes well which is the main thing. It is a kind of novelty thing but I find it to be a convenient novelty so it would be something that I would consider for future purchase.

title: New adventure begins
text:
It has been a long time since I encountered the first series of Cardcaptor Sakura so when I saw this offering, Cardcaptor Sakura: Clear Card Vol 1 by CLAMP, the nostalgia was strong and I selected it.

This series starts with all the fluff and cute that I remember. Not that all CLAMP series are cute and fluffy but this one does both in spades. Sakura, Syaoran and especially Tomoyo are cute and fluffy and sparkly. It opens with all being well in Sakura's world. She's starting middle school. Syaoran is back from Hong Kong.

It is all very sweet and a bit slow in its contentment as it re-introduces the cast. Then it picks up the action when Sakura has a dream that the Clow cards are turning transparent or clear. Of course, when Sakura tells her friends of her dream, I love that Tomoyo boldly (and hopefully) states the obvious that it could mean the return of the Cardcaptor! Tomoyo is spot-on and the new adventure kicks off.

This is a series for a young audience. For myself, I don't think I could continue reading the series as it is just a bit too sweet and fluffy for me, but for my grandniece and her friends, this is just what they enjoy. It is a bit of adventure with a sweet heroine and her friends. The art is detailed and clear. The characters likable and engaging with an adventure that is familiar and comfortable.

title: Good size for what it is needed
text: Elan Publishing Company E64-8x4S SewnField Surveying Book is the right size to carry in that the pages are big enough to write but it isn't so big that it gets unwieldy to carry over time during day. It is only 32 pages but for its purposes, it works. The description says it is water-resistant and I can say that is true since it rained while I using it. The paper isn't water-resistant but the cover does a pretty good. It isn't water-proof but it is resistant enough to give time to put it away.

title: Works for what I need it to work for and it fits my (limited) storage requirements
text: I don't generally use trimmers but when I work with one, I wonder why that is because they work so nicely. That's why I decided to try Swingline 1112 SmartCut Compact Personal Rotary Trimmer." It is a compact size so I figured it would be easier to store. I don't ever do more than 5 sheets so I thought it would work for me. On both counts, it does work for me. It did work fairly well on my firm bed that was doing double-duty as an counter but  it is best to use it from the table or desk to get best results. Overall, I like it for what I use it for and it fits with my storage requirements as well.

title: Easy to use (and read) and convenient too
text: It has been awhile since I've had a desktop calculator so it took me (embarrassingly) a bit of time to figure out the decimal and rounding functions for this Victor 6700 16 Digit Extra Large Desktop Calculator. Once I read the back of the packaging (which I appreciate because it was easy to read and not in tiny type), I started coming back. After that, I started to wonder why it took me so long to get another desktop calculator. It is comfortable to work with and to read with the extra large face. I forgot how nice and convenient it is to have one of these items.

title: Nicely packaged item
text: I have a set of colored pencils for adult coloring books. Not that I'm particularly good at coloring (even as a kid, I wasn't) but it is a fun way to pass time and I like this Adult Coloring Book + Leather Notebook Journal because the area to color isn't big. It is just in the header section so it really is a fun way to pass some time while using the journal for whatever reason (journaling, note taking, doodling, etc). It is a nicely packaged item and just the right size for a purse.

title: Definitely worth a look
text: I thought I left a review for this but I guess I didn't. I really like these dissolvable labels. I'm not the only one because I showed some ladies at work how these labels work and they like them too. It is more applicable to them because they are more likely to make stuff for the holidays and this would work for them. The price isn't too bad either. So it is definitely something to think about.

title: It has peel & stick and I like that
text: These envelopes have 1of 2 things that I like in an envelope. It doesn't have the security design but to be fair, I don't expect that in the larger envelopes like this so the peel & stick feature is what makes it a good consideration for future. I don't like the "lick & stick" envelope. Even if I'm using a sponge water bottle to help seal, the sponge on the water bottles can get sticky and gross fairly quickly so the peel & stick in still the preferred way to go. At my work, we still send a lot of documents out the old fashioned way so this is a good size for documents. I like that it came in a box of 250 as well. That should last about a month. Overall, a pretty good item to have.

title: Ease of use sells it for me
text: Avery Dissolvable Rectangle Labels are exactly as described. You can put them on a jar or plastic container and it will dissolve upon washing. It is a rather convenient thing especially for someone like me where taking home lunch and storing in a shared refrigerator requires labeling so it doesn't mysteriously disappear. It is a little pricier than using a post-it or piece of scrap to tape on, but the ease of use is what sells it to me. It is just the right size and it sticks on and then washes off so I'll definitely consider buying in future.

title: Has the two features that I want in an envelope
text: There are two things about this envelope that I like and because it has it, I'm fine with anything else about it and that is: 1) security tint and 2) peel and stick. The former is a "must" as far as I'm concerned because I don't like contents, even non-confidential, visible through envelopes. The latter is a nice-to-have that is very close to being a 'must' and the reason is that one never knows how long an envelope has been around so the moisten and stick envelope is a little off-putting. Since this envelope has both the former and latter, this works for me, even if the size is a bit non-standard for me. I can work with the non-standard size because paper folds to fit.

title: Like the top spiral bind and the full size
text: I had forgotten that I like top spiral notepads until I got this item. I really like the full size of it too. I can get a full use of it for what I had intended to use it. Definitely will purchase again.

title: Very much a 'do it all' planner
text: I'm a sucker for planners. I love them and I can have several to use for specific purposes: menu planning, work planning, home planning, health planning, gardening, etc. Then there are some that I like enough that I take it with me and use it for all kinds of reminders. The "Orange Circle Studio 2018 Do It All Planner, Aug. 2017 - Dec. 2018". I'm a fan of the 18 month planner. I like the layout and footprint. It isn't too big nor too small. I like the weekly planner format. I prefer horizontal but this vertical layout is nice with its five sections. I can use the five sections for specific topics. The "To Do" and "Shopping" tear out sections are plentiful. The stickers are cute too. It really is a "do it all" planner.

title: Versatile
text: The 4-star is with a caveat that one of the pieces that helps connect the tray to the rod was broken. I opted to leave the tray off so my "Mind Reader 'Valet' 3 Tier Rolling Coffee Cart with Free Condiment Organizer" is now a Mind Reader 'Valet' 2 Tier Rolling Coffee Cart with Free Condiment Organizer." I'm pretty sure that I could use a super glue to fix because the piece was still in the box and it was a clean break, but I actually like the height of the coffee cart with the 2 trays. It gives it more flexible of use. It was easy to put together. I would recommend putting it together in the exact order of the instructions because once the cylinder rods and the trays are connected, they don't want to be disconnected. The only time I needed my Philips screwdriver was for the drawer handle. All in all, I like the coffee cart as I received it. It works as a coffee cart; a printer cart; a temp table while sitting on the couch; and a side table. Very versatile with a simple, unobtrusive design.

title: Works as I had hoped
text: It works as I had hoped. I will still probably use the shredder for certain items like bank statements and such, but for other items that I just want to mask the address before I tear it up, this works as I had hoped.

title: Like the hardbound version and in my preferred planner horizontal format
text: I have another Erin Condren planner but it has the large spiral. That was the only thing that I didn't quite like about it (it made writing nearest to the spiral a bit awkward). This 18th month planner is hardbound which is nice as is the ribbon page marker and the gold edging finish on the pages. I prefer the horizontal layout for the day/week planning so that's a win for me. The notes section in the back is a plentiful and pleasant surprise. Usually there is only a few pages of blank pages at the back of planners but this planner has a couple of pages of lined, dot grid/graph, and blank each. I generally use pencil for my planners so any issue with pen ink bleeding to another page is moot. Overall, a very nice item.

title: Just right size for me
text: This "AT-A-GLANCE Notebook, 7-1/4" x 9-1/2", 80 Sheet Small Notebook, WorkStyle Take Care, Pistachio (WS50240423)" is exactly the style of notebook that I like. The size is just right for me in that it is small enough to fit in my bag but big enough to write the amount of stuff I want to plan for the day. Plus it has a to-do list section which is always a good thing for me. It also reminded me that my favorite planner was an At-A-Glance calendar with little birds on it so I put it on my wish list so I can get one for the July 2017 to June 2018 academic. That reminder is enough to make me give this item an extra star. It is a little pricier than most notebooks but for me, it is worth the extra.

title: Perfect size for me to carry in bag to keep notes through the day
text: I received this notebook yesterday and already I'm really liking it. It looks nice. It has the stiff covers that I like and the lines on the pages is the college ruled height that I prefer. Best of all, it has a manageable spiral that doesn't get in the way of writing. I wouldn't have noticed this until I recently got a notebook with a large spiral binding and it makes it unwieldy when writing on one side of the notebook. I use different types of notebooks for different purposes and this type of notebook is perfect to carry in my bag to keep a record of things to do and remember throughout the day.

title: works for me
text: I'm really liking this daily organizer. I can use it for home and work as a way to plan my day and have reminders. It is compact and light so it works well for my needs. Will definitely be looking at buying another when I'm close to the last pages.

title: Perfect for what I needed it for
text: I ordered this item on a weekend and it was in by mid-week so I'm quite pleased with that aspect, but in the end, the product is what matters and I love it. It was super easy to put together and bonus points for the Phillips screw driver that was included. That was all that was needed to put together the [[ASIN:B017CD6JYS Adjustable Natural Wood Desktop Storage Organizer Display Shelf Rack, Counter Top Bookcase, Beige]]. It looks great and it has a nice real wood fragrance. It works exactly as I had hoped and I am quite likely to purchase another one or two.

title: Nice and fun activity
text: I'd heard that coloring is a calming activity so when I saw this, I thought I would give it a try. The Prismacolor Premier Coloring Kit with Colored Pencils, Art Markers and Adult Coloring Book is a nice collection. The pencils are smooth in use. The coloring has many activities which is nice. I didn't expect to like the pens but they were the surprise to me. I'm not sure if coloring is a calming activity as I'd been told but it is fun and this collection has been a nice, fun surprise.

title: Didn't expect to like the color but I do
text: I have to admit that I selected this item thinking they were just regular mechanical pencils. It wasn't until later that I realized that they were colored lead. I was a little disappointed because I didn't "need" colored pencils but I am really glad that I made the mistake because now that I've tried them, I like them a lot. It helps that I like the design of the mechanical pencil. It fits just right in my hand. The lead is smooth when writing too. The color, especially the purple, is a great look on the paper. It stands out well. I didn't expect to like the green but it is a good contrast as well. Although I can use regular lead in these pencils, I think I may actually try to find the color lead when replacing is needed. The only 'ding' that I could find is that I wish it had a couple of replacement erasers but that's a minor thing.

title: My favorite planner notebook
text: This is one of my favorite planner/notebooks. I received a copy to try out once and I was sold since then. It has the notes section and then the list area so I can divide up my notes the way I want to use it. I can use it as a project planner or as I use it now, as a daily planner. One side I use to track health and fitness stuff while the main section is used to keep track of daily tasks, errands and notes to remember. It is a great price and I will be sad if this item ever goes out of print so please keep it around for a long time.

title: Some nice features on this marker
text: I like the chisel point of these dry erase markers. I prefer it to the standard point. The low odor is also a good feature. The semi-clear end on the markers is a neat feature as well. It has been awhile since I used the EXPO brand for dry erase markers so this was a nice re-introduction to them. I will definitely keep them in mind for future purchase.

title: Nice planner
text: The "Erin Condren 12 month 2017 Life Planner" in this watercolor floral print is a nice planner. I do like the 3 sections for each day yet it is set up as a weekly planner. It saves space while sectioning nicely. For someone like me who likes to section my planning (ex: Work, Home, Surprise or Meals, Exercise, Medications/Testing), this will work for me. Since I expect to take it with me, the only downside is the exposed spiral. I prefer bound or covered spiral so it won't catch material in my bag. That said, the spiral is of a quality that doesn't appear it will catch material. Overall, I look forward to using it regularly in the coming year.

title: Nice pen
text: It was humorous that when I received the "PILOT G2 Pen Stylus", it took me more than a few minutes to figure out that the clip on side of  the pen is what extracts and retracts the tip of the pen. I kept pressing the top of the pen and thinking, "Oh no, it is broken!" but oh relief, I finally realized it was the clip. Which gave me a good laugh and the pens work which is great because it is a nice smooth working pen. The ink is the right weight that I like. It isn't too fine but it isn't too thick either. I like it a lot.

title: Very nice
text: More than anything, I like the size of this "Mead Cambridge Meeting Notebook / Journal". It is a full size page. It also doesn't have the spirals so it is easy to keep in a bag without worrying about the binding snagging on something. I appreciate the amount of lines and the space to put a date (a small nicety). I give an extra star for the teal color. Normally color isn't a big deal to me but I'm in a teal mood this season so it gets extra points.

title: I like it
text: I received this a few days ago and finally got my office/desk space organized to put the "Breeze Point Fabric Message and Memo Bulletin Board with Ribbons" in a good spot. My son said he wouldn't want one for his desk area as he didn't like the shiny ribbon, so it is something that if you get it for someone else, you have to keep in mind what his/her taste might be. I really like it. The main color is neutral and even the ribbon (to me anyway) is the right contrast of color without looking garish or loud. I like that the design isn't too fussy and it holds the messages/pieces of paper snugly so for someone like me, it works well and it is reasonably priced.

title: Nice
text: When I selected this item, I just saw that it had the pockets. I hadn't noticed that the dividers also had a design on it. I liked that surprise. Plastic dividers are always nice. They keep well. I liked the designs because they make for good visual separation from the dividers that I already have which are plain. Overall, a nice item to have.

title: Nice unit
text: I received this item a few days ago which was two days earlier than I had expected so that was nice. It didn't come in an Amazon box and for security, the extra packaging would have been nice but it was nice to not have to deal with extra waste so that's a wash. The printer itself was easy to set up and since my son and I both have new PCs, the wireless feature is really nice, especially since my room has zero room for equipment so I was happy it could be set up in a different room and I could still print. We likely won't use the faxing capability but the scan capability was nice. Haven't delved too much into it but it was fairly straightforward as was the copy capability. My one concern is the concern that I always have when it comes to home printers and that is cartridge replacement but I'll get that bridge when I need to cross it. For now, I'll enjoy this item. It looks nice. It works nice.

title: Nice item
text:
I wasn't sure what I was getting when I selected these fold tabs and even when I got them, they looked neat but I wasn't sure if they'd be of significant use. Man, was I wrong. I brought them to work so I could use the printer to print on them. I put them on some folders and I thought, "Interesting." Then the person who reviews supplies saw the tabs. I never thought folder tabs would be so exciting. She loved them and wants to find out how to get them and said they would be so helpful because she hates sitting down to view the folder tab (she has a two file drawer).

So, in honor of the company supply person, I give this item a 4-star.

title: Fits the space nicely
text: I was in need of a white board only for my office space and this fit the bill perfectly. I also really liked the 4 dry erase markers. The standard is often to include a black marker so the four color variety was nice. I'm not all that picky about the magnets but once I had the board up in my cubicle, I have to admit that the rainbow colored magnets were a nice touch. Maybe not a necessary touch, but still nice to have a pop of color when you don't expect it.

title: It works
text:
Binders are binders for the most part and generally, I like ACCO Brands stuff as I buy their brand on the regular. I don't want to say that I'm disappointed in this binder because again, a binder is a binder and it does have the flat 3 ring that I prefer, but it isn't quite the standard that I'm used to with respect to ACCO/Wilson Jones. This is a new binder but it already has many bubble in the cover. The ring latches are good on opening but a bit wonky on closing. Not a big deal because it is easy enough to snap the rings shut. I just prefer to use the latches after years of getting skin stuck when snapping ring binders shut (ouch). HOwever, at least the ring line up nicely and close securely.

I still love ACCO Brands and this one is okay. It was just a little less than what I had expected.

title: Simple in that "why didn't they think of it sooner" way
text: These SMEAD Pick-ATab file folders are kind of neat. I selected to try it out because it is that time of year to start organizing for the rest of the year. I like that these file folders were various colors (blue, red, yellow and green) rather than the standard manila color. That's the initial reason that I selected it, but having the selectable tab is simple and brilliant in that "Why didn't they think of this sooner?" way. I'm not surprised that as of this review, there is a limited amount of stock left (I'm sure amazon will replenish quickly) because it is a decent price. Definitely put it on my wish list.

title: Nice coverage and variety and it is truly is low odor
text: I will probably never use the bright yellow marker but I do appreciate it just in case that I do end up using it and overall, I love this set of dry erase markers. We used them for a brain storming meeting rather than the regular markers and everyone was commenting that there was no odor. We liked the amount of colors available so everyone got their own color to use to add info to the board. Honestly, for the price, this may be our new go-to dry erase markers.

title: Good option for a home office
text: I like the size of this stapler more than anything. It is just the right size for my hand. It isn't the smoothest stapler but it gets the job done. I like the color as I won't lose it on my desk. I have another stapler that is very good for my office, but it also cost quite a bit so for the price on this one, it isn't bad for a home office where you just want to staple a small amount of items.

title: Very useful
text:
It is rather humorous (sort of) that I selected this item with a niece in mind but while she thought it was nice, she dropped the 'you are old, auntie' bomb on me that the lockers are her school are mostly for show because they are encouraged to not use the lockers (thefts, security, etc). So now I know why she and her friends lug bags of books to and from school.

So I ended up scrounging around to find someone who might be able to test it out and voila! a friend of mind who uses the local Y and has a locker there said "Hey, I'll try it out for you!" and while it is a just a bit big for the locker, she was able to slide it and she loves it. It really does help organize and maximize space. I thought the little drawer was unnecessary but she likes it because she puts her swimming goggles and cap in it.

When I asked for a rating, she said 5 stars and wondered why she never thought of getting something like this sooner.

title: Nice and streamlined
text:
I love these kind of calendars and I was having trouble finding this particular type in the local stores so I ended up buying one that is 'sorta' like this ACCO Brands student planner. I like it okay but when I saw this one become available, I knew I would snatch it up.

The cover is never important to me but I do like the colors and design of this one, but still the most important part is the flow of the entries. I do like the calendar tabs for separation. A small thing but I like the little check-circles on the daily entries rather than time ranges so you can use the daily entries as a checklist too.

There is one page at back for faves and websites plus a few additional pages of reference like the elements table but it is kept to a minimum. The planner is to plan, not to a planner/cheat sheet/address book/notebook. I like that because I used to rip those additional pages out because I never used them and it made it unnecessarily bulky and that's not the case with this planner. It is nice and streamlined and clean to use.

title: Mouse is a lot more responsive when using this pad
text: It is easy to forget what a good mouse pad can feel like. With optical mouses, it is easy to think "I don't need a mouse pad" and for the most part, I haven't used one for awhile but this "Turtle Beach Large Drift Fast Premium" mouse pad is so very nice. Large sized is an extra bonus but the responsiveness of the mouse is noticeable. My son took the mouse pad as he has the gaming rig and he noticed the same thing in that the mouse is noticeably more responsive and he has another mouse pad because he prefers to use them. He definitely likes this one.

title: Good set; really like the finer point of the markers
text: Normally, my son doesn't have an opinion on the markers while I have a ton of opinions but since he did have an opinion, I'm going with his: He likes this set. The finer point of these markers make it easier to write on the board. The eraser seems to do a cleaner job. I never realized that used to bother him until I got this set. The spray seems the same as others we've used so the items that make the set a cut above is the markers and eraser. Although I think for him, it is the markers. He's definitely sold on this finer point type. I like the set as well. I wanted to take it to work to use with the white boards at work but I guess this set will be staying home.

title: Love these things
text:
I am already a big fan of ACCO Brands Quartet whiteboard. I have a two boards that are combo whiteboard and bulletin board and I love them. I use them at work as they fit perfectly in my cubicle.

This item was received yesterday and it is staying home as it is a smaller size but one thing I like over the previous items that I have selected is that it comes with hardware that is designed to be used for hanging in a cubicle like mine with the fabric covered partitions. Nonetheless, this one is staying home for my kitchen. I could have used the screws and plastic holders that came with to mount to the dry wall but my home-made method of choice has been to use two black clamps/clips and then hang on two ACCO push pins. The board is light enough and the pins do less damage to the wall. All that said, it is nice that ACCO provided these options that to hang: 1) self-stick; 2) cubicle hooks and 3) screws/plastic for drywall mounting. Along with the two magnets and black pen, it is a nice package and I will definitely get a lot of use out of it.

title: Very nice to have
text:
I received my Amazon order in good time, but given the volume of office supplies that we receive at my company, we were given some complimentary items to try out (yay for end of year mini-parties) and this item was one of items so I grabbed it before others could. I didn't realize it was the same item until I got home to compare it and it is the same AT-A-GLANCE Meeting/Planner Padfolio.

I'm not sure why it is called a "Meeting/Planner" because it just looks like a nice folder to keep a notepad in but whatever they want to call it, I'm fine with it because I do like the look of it. I like these kinds of folders because in some meetings, we aren't at desks so I like having the folder to stabilize the notepad while I'm taking notes.

I like the organization of the notepad itself as I'm a sucker for graph paper over lined paper. I'm not as keen on the check boxes at the bottom of the pages but once it runs out, I can replace with the graph paper notepad. Notepad is the standard 8.5 x 11 size.

I do like cover. It has a nice feel and I like the stitched edging. Stylish but not dated looking and slim enough that I can slide it into my tote bag. Now that I will have one to use at home, it'll be good to take to the grocery store for shopping lists (yes, I'm one of those people at the store with their list, adding up the prices and blocking everyone from the item on the shelf) and other errands.

title: Sticks
text: About three years ago I packed up our house and had some of the best tape for adhesion. Recently when I was re-packing to take some things to donation I noticed that the new tape I bought doesn’t stick ad well. Intried this tape and I am very happy with it and trust it to keep my boxes closed, top and bottom

title: Works Great
text: This is a great makeup pencil pencil sharpener! It has both sizes most commonly used in makeup pencils. It does not feel cheaply made and compares with my higher end one that I can't find! It is a great replacement sharpener and I'd purchase again!

title: Easy to use
text: I actually had to use only one side of this tape. I had an adhesive portion of a shower caddy that wouldn't stick to the shower panel (plastic coated). No matter what I used the caddy fell off the wall. I used this to tape around the part that wouldn't stick to the wall. It worked SO well. The shower caddy hasn't fallen off the wall again. I know anything else I choose to use this tape on will stick, also. I will always have some on hand from now on.

title: Great Refill
text: I really like the Pilot G2 gel pen and have several. Instead of buying more, I opt to buy the refills. They are a great price and work beautifully.

title: Works perfectly
text: I’ve been packing, unpacking and repacking with this tape for a couple of years now.  It had never let me down as my boxes are securely taped until I use a razor knife to cut a packed box open!!

title: Beautiful Gliding Gel Ink
text: These refills fit a variety of my older gel pens - especially the Avant Next purple click pen!  I ran out of purple ink and wanted black ink as a replacement.  This refill fit perfectly and the ink glides over my acid-free paper.  I am so glad I bought them!!

title: Quality
text: I have a leather case that uses these style writing pads. They are exactly what I expected and work great in the case. Sturdy and well made, not flimsy.

title: Strong, sturdy boxes
text: These boxes are very strong and sturdy and excellent for organizing.  I use it with makeup and brushes. I also use in the kitchen and office. They are versatile and since this is about the 5th time I've ordered this brand, they seem to be long lasting and keepers!

title: Quality
text: Worked beautifully without skipping! Great refill

title: Good Ink
text: Great cartridge at an excellent price.  It works in my older model HP without any trouble and the ink flows smoothly during printing.

title: Great writing instrument
text: I love, love, love this fountain pen.  I had two - one a fine point and one a medium. I liked the medium better so bought this additional one for backup! All pens, the ink flows smoothly and are a dream to hand-write with. So much better than skipping ball point pens. I'm so glad I bought that first one a couple of years ago.

title: Well made quality product
text: These are a quality, well-made card lined as a "to do list". They are not flimsy so they are perfect for putting in your purse to carry to the grocery store. I found the find spacing a little difficult to use because I have big handwriting but other than that, I would highly recommend them as they are a quality product.

title: Top Quality
text: As usual, these are top-quality, well-made note cards

title: Cute Cards
text: These are cute holiday cards. They aren't quite as thick or the quality I'd hoped but the message and snowman were just right to express my message.

title: Awesome Notecards
text: I love these unruled note cards.  I am always jotting notes down and creating shopping lists.  These work great for that.  I can tuck them in a book and pull out when I need to jot down something I learned.  As shopping list it fits perfectly in my purse and are strong enough I can mark out what I pick up at the store.  This is my second purchase and won't be my last.  I love they are made in the USA, too.  I will outfit my office with her products!

title: Great journal, silky paper
text: I love the Eccolo journal/notebook. I love the size and the smooth paper.  The cover is faux leather but great quality. I have a lot of these journals because I can't walk away from them when I find a good price (smile).

title: Perfect
text: These ink cartridges are super easy to use.  They pop right in and the ink begins to flow easily.  I remember some I had years ago that required a lot of pushing before it would fit in the fountain pen - these are far easier to use.  I always buy two boxes at a time because there isn't THAT much ink in them and I write a lot so never want to run out.

title: Love the smooth paper
text: I love Eccolo journal/notebooks.  The paper is so smooth.  The faux leather is done very well so you really can't tell it's faux (smile).  I buy Eccolo all the time and this is just another perfect one added to my collection!

title: Very Good Tape!
text: I have been packing up for a move and realized some of the boxes were losing their tape. It just peeled away from the box. The boxes were not being moved; the tape just peeled off.  So I bought this Duck brand and have been very satisfied with its "sticking" power and ability to keep the box CLOSED. I've bought two now and none of the tape has peeled away from the box. GREAT product.

title: Works great
text: This tape works great.  It is "stickier" than the other type I was using and STAYS.  I want to know my boxes of delicate tea cups will arrive safely without the bottom falling out - this tape works great for giving me that confidence!  I've ordered several and every one of them works great at sticking and holding!

title: Works GREAT
text: I've been packing up the house for a move.  I was using another type of strapping tape and noticed that where 'd taped up the bottom of a box with it was already coming loose - before I even filled the box.  I came on here to see if I could find a stronger tape and tried this one - YES!  It works great, is a bit "stickier" than the other type and STAYS.  I want to know my boxes of delicate tea cups will arrive safely without the bottom falling out - this tape works great for giving me that confidence!  I've ordered several and every one of them works great at sticking and holding!

title: Great Product
text: It arrived in a plastic bag because it was far too large to put in a box.  That didn't bother me because it arrived safely but if someone were rough, it would pop the large bubbles.  The bubble wrap itself works perfectly to wrap my fragile china and glassware.

title: Works for packing to move
text: I'm using this filament tape to tape up boxes for packing.  I occasionally see the end of one that's come loose so you do need to press it onto the box.  It seems to be holding well, even heavy boxes.

title: Easy to use, no mess
text: These refill cartridges are very easy to use - so much more than in the past when I always made a mess! I recently got back into using fountain pens and these cartridges make it so much nicer to use and refill!

title: Easy to refill and use
text: I just got back into using fountain pens. A lot has changed since I last used them and it is all for the better! These pens come with a squeeze converter that means you can use a bottle of ink with great ease. The refills are also very easy to insert and use, no mess. I had forgotten how much I used to love using fountain pens and I'm so glad I gave it a try again.

title: Good Refill
text: I bought a unique pen for hubby. When it's came time for a refill Amazon had the right ink refill. It has more than one available and was easy to insert. Works beautifully.

title: Great journal
text: I like the saying on the front of this journal so much I will purchase more to give to friends of mine. Eccolo paper is smooth and the ink glides across the surface. It has become my go-to journal and note-writing notebook. I always feel special because these journals are quality and obviously well made.

title: Quality and Comfort
text: This is exactly what I hoped it was - a cushion large enough to fit on a dining room chair. It also works great in a car seat, especially on a long trip. It comes folded in a box but unfolds quickly within an hour or so. It is very well made, a quality product. I am going to purchase a couple more to keep in the second car and my office chair.

title: Great Book
text: This is a great journal, plenty of places to write - all on that excellent acid free paper. It is well made with a hard cover. I bought several of them to give to friends and to have one for next year, too! Quality in a small package.

title: Pretty good.  As expected.
text:
For this price folks, what do you want. They write very well, and take the adapter (included) or international tubes.
Love the weight. Caps stay on better after a few uses. The pen writes easily with fast writing or signatures (me). But I wish the nibs were more fine. I've ordered replacement fine nibs I hope will fit.

title: Great value... nice pens.
text:

title: Awesome Pen. my (F) writes like a (M)
text:
strongly debated between a medium and fine nib. i kept watching videos comparing the two but boy was it tough. I’m a (M) nib guy and in the end am very happy i picked up a (F). People werent joking that it writes a little broader, specially with wetter inks.

i went with a (F) nib and inked it with iroshizuku tsuki-yo. it writes pretty wet and broader than what a fine nib should be.

you’ll notice on smoother Rhodia paper, its as broad as the Pilot Custom Heritage (M) nib. the pilot custom (m) feels more like a true western (m) nib (my pilot mr fountain pen (m) is much less broad). the Lamy 2000 with the iroshizuku ink definitely writes broader than the Lamy Safari with Lamy black cartridge ink. i’m sure if i swapped to a dryer ink, it’ll be less broad, but for my uses, this was the thickness i was aiming for.

on cheaper paper, like my Lemome journal, it feels right at home and has the same broadness as my (M) Platinum Century 3776. the pilot custom is the broadest on this paper. on the lemome paper, they are all less broad than the rhodia paper.

Writing on the lamy 2000 is smooth with tiny bit of feedback. its not buttery smooth like my pilot custom, but does feel smoother than my platinum.

overall really love the pen and looking forward to putting some pen mileage on it.

title: It's "ok" - maybe just me
text:
Ordered a blue moonman t1 with (m) nib. What came in the box was the moonman fountain pen, which looks great. the nib that was on it was a Jin Hao (M), and packed seperately was a moonman nib which i'm assuming is a (f) nib.

I have a buncha jinhaos so was disappointed that it wasnt a moonman nib, but i'm now reading that there isnt really any MM nibs in a (M)? so the jin hao's probably there as a substitute.

THe jinhao nib was not smooth, unlike my other jinhaos - case of QC? was pretty scratchy, despite the tines aligned

I swapped to the moonman nib and barely much inkflow. eventually found out it was two things:
1) misaligned tines
2) the tines were tight

When i resolved the misaligned tines, barely had any inflow - found out the tines were really tight. took a thin piece of plastic film and ran it between the tines to see if i can get it less tight and viola!

the it's an (f) nib, i think i ran with too thick of a plastic shim - it now writes almost like a medium (less broad than the jinhao (M) nib - which is fine, it's what i wanted. also the aluminum section makes it a bit sliperry so i'm not always indexed correctly for writing.

The pen coulda been a 4 or 5 star, but cuz of the time it took for me to tune it and the slippery alum barrel, it gets a 3.

title: Reliable, Wonderful FriXion Quality
text:
I'm a bit of a pen-holic and fine FriXion pens are some of my favorite.

This set of three (all with black ink) is wonderful, because of the pretty pen designs--checkered pastel pink, lavender, and blue-green pen bodies. They're excellent quality for the price and are refillable. The ink flows smoothly, the .5 line is perfectly thin, and you can erase easily with the rubber "eraser" on the top.

The rubber grip makes the pens comfortable to write with and the pocket clip/clicker functions smoothly and is sturdy. Highly recommend if you're looking for a great, erasable pen.

title: Great Pens: Fine Lines, Smooth Writing, Show on Dark and Light Paper
text:
Zebra Sarasas never disappoint. These are excellent pastel pens that write well on both dark and light paper (excepting the white on white paper, of course).

The .5 tip gives a consistent, thin line. Right out of the box, they wrote smoothly. (After removing those little leak-prevention tips!) They have the sturdy, spring-loaded pocket clip Sarasas are known for. They also have a comfortable rubber grip. The see-through barrel makes it easy to keep an eye on the ink level, so you'll know when you're running out.

I highly recommend them.

One small thing to note: I like to keep my pen sets in their original packaging, but Amazon made that impossible for this one. They placed a bright orange "don't break the set" sticker over the front and a sticker with a different barcode over the one on the back of the package. Neither sticker was the easily-removable kind (leaving the surface sticky and ugly), so I had to ditch the package.

text:

The highlighters are wet writers and do take some time to dry, so they're not my go-to highlighters. Instead, I use them for fun (for example, in letters and art pages in my journal) I shared some examples of my most used pens (with at least 30 seconds of drying time before I highlighted over them). There is some smearing, but not enough that it bothers me. Of note: since it's Clairefontaine paper, ink does take longer to dry and doesn't fully absorb. I chose it because it's also great for showing colors/sparkles.

There is A LOT of sparkles, which is hard to see in the photos. The sparkle is clear and definitely easy to see in person. I love these and highly recommend them if you like unique/sparkly writing tools.

text:
EDIT 3/2/2020: Yep, the other reviewers are correct - these do dry out very quickly. But I'm thinking for the money, for the light color, and for the fact that they don't bleed through the pages, I can just buy more.

As a college student, I do a lot of reading and a lot of marking ... but I needed some highlighters that didn't bleed through the paper. The most commonly-available brands seem to be the ones that bleed through the most. Personally, I am not a fan of "dry" highlighters (they're basically crayons ...and some can be really oily and messy).
These highlighters, by contrast, are JUST RIGHT (Just "Write"? Ugh. I'll stop). Granted, I use them on normal printer-paper and normal notebook paper, but none of the colors bleed through. The blue and teal have just the slightest impression on the reverse side of a paper, but compared to the common-brands that you get from your local office supply store, the difference is night-and-day.

FOR THOSE LOOKING TO USE THESE IN BIBLES: I'm not sure if they would bleed or not; I personally wouldn't use ink in mine, but...for every other kind of paper, they work perfectly! Can't recommend these highly enough.

title: Great Nib in Several Positions!
text: Reviews of the Lamy left-handed nib have varied -- some people say they are useful and some don't.  This seems to be related to the way you hold your pen as a left-handed person.  I find that I hold pens in three ways: 1) At a roughly 45-degree angle, 2) Choked up on the pen in an almost vertical position, and 3) Between the first two fingers of my left hand -- also in an almost vertical position (see photos).  Using a Lamy Logo pen, I found that the original fine nib was great in position #1 (45-degrees), scratchy and wrote poorly in position #2 (vertical), and useless in position #3 (between fingers).  For me, this LH nib is great!!  It writes well in all three positions.  It is still a bit scratchy on paper in position #2, but you will see from the writing sample that the outcome is great on paper.  I have not been able to find a fountain pen before now that lets me write in the slightly odd position #3.  This is THE ONLY nib I have found so far that lets me write this way, so I am quite happy with it.  FINAL VERDICT:  BUY this LH nib unless you always write in the 45-degree position #1 in the attached photos, in which case you may not need it.  Highly recommended.

title: Beautiful, writes well, all metal, kind of heavy
text:
Okay, so I was really excited to try this pen out when it came. I met the guy at the door and probably concerned him with my excitement (to be fair, I'm usually away when my pens arrive).

I used it right away, testing it out on a notebook that the North Dakota National Guard was handing out at an event (good quality paper for fountain pen writing, btw). Not a feather to be found anywhere. It did splat a little on the first quote, so I wrote out four more quotes to see if it repeated the splat. I think it was from the fact that it had just been filled, and I didn't completely wipe the excess ink after filling it.

The surprising part was that while it did feather on the cheap cardstock from the dollar store, that feathering was surprisingly minimal.

Overall, it writes well, it's beautiful, and it's all metal.

If I had any sort of issue with it, it's that it is heavy. I bought it for myself, but it may be chosen as a gift for another some day because it's just a little heavier than I prefer my pens to be (though that remains to be seen as I use the ink up that's in it - Noodler's color Nightshade if anyone cares).

title: Smooth, almost no feathering, cool looking
text:
Yooo
This is a nice pen!
Okay, so it has been my experience that fountain pens that run roughly $17 or less typically tend to have a heavier ink flow, which results in more feathering on the page, even on the higher quality papers. This pen doesn't have that.
It really is quite a nice, sleek pen with a nifty change from other pens in that it has a black nib.
If there is any complaint about the pen, it would be that my aunt, who used it for some paperwork, said the place you grip it was a little more smooth than she's used to in pens. But even she, who hasn't used a fountain pen since high school, found it quite a pleasure to write with.

title: Pretty, smooth, and generally nice
text:
This is a very pretty pen! After getting it, I immediately pulled it out and filled the converter with ink. Not my best move because if you fill the converter and then pop it into the pen (instead of pulling the ink through the mechanics and into the converter as the instructions say), you will splat in on your hands. Because physics or science or something.
Once I got the ink flowing smoothly and consistently (again - follow the directions), I found that the ink flowed very quickly and very smoothly. That being said, because it flows a little faster than most pens, there is a possibility of greater feathering depending on the type of paper used (as an aside, it writes really nicely on dot-matrix paper).
The pen is a screw-cap, so there's no real risk of it popping off, and as a bonus, it has threading on the top to screw the cap on when you're using it, eliminating the risk of popping off when you're writing (or perhaps fiddling with it in class or a meeting). Additionally, it takes a standard cartridge, so even though I almost exclusively use jar in, I am able to bring a cartridge with to in the event I run out of ink.

title: Nice flow, lightweight, lovely
text:
This pen is just so nice
I know I say that about a lot of fountain pens, but this one is especially nice. It's very professional looking and writes really well. There is minimal feathering on cheap paper, none on the nice quality paper. I took a leap of faith on the converter style and have no regrets as of this review.

The pen is thin and very lightweight, so writing with it is a breeze, and the ink flows rather nicely.

The only weird thing is that writing with it somehow makes my handwriting look more like my grandma's.

title: Omg so pretty!
text:
This is such a nice pen. I ordered this for myself but ended up offering it up as a birthday gift for my friend. I regret that decision and will probably have to order one more for myself.
It writes really nicely and smoothly. It's all plastic, so it's super lightweight. I don't know what they did, but the way the pen writes, it writes perfectly whether you're buying the cheaper ink or have the expensive stuff (I started with the Manuscript ink, then wrote with the ink it came with, then tried out some Noodlers - purple if that matters to you).

title: Great in spite of the learning curve
text:
I don't love the lack of clip, and there's a little bit of a learning curve when you fill it for the first time (unfortunately I couldn't get a solid video of filling it as my kids wouldn't stay quiet and out of the way).

That being said, it writes really nicely, holds a good amount of ink, and since it's clear plastic, you can see when you're close to needing more ink.

Also, the shade of purple is really pretty.

title: Different, but not a bad different
text:
Okay, so, overall, I rather like these pens. They're a lot lighter than I'm used to (I mean, they're all plastic, so...), which makes long-term writing easier.
The flow is heavier than many of the other fountain pens I've written with before, so if you plan on buying it, be prepared for that. All it took for me, however, was an adjustment to the amount of weight I put on the pen as I wrote.
Fair warning: It's a piston-style pen. If you don't have ink, get some before you buy this pen set. Also, it's a little bit of a learning curve to get ink into it. You have to have the nib completely submerged and do this in-out kind of activity to get the ink to go fully through the feed and into the pen. But the upside is that it holds more ink than the standard ink converter, so it'll last a long time.

title: Lovely, but...
text:
It's a really nice pen. The ink flows nicely, and it's a pleasure to write with.

However, if you aren't experienced with fountain pens, I wouldn't recommend it.
It doesn't take standard cartridges, so if you don't plan on keeping a jar of ink handy (or one of those fancy portable ink bottles that cost, like, $80). Otherwise, you'll probably be shelling out extra cash for nonstandard cartridges.
Additionally, the opacity of the ink converter makes it next to impossible to tell how much ink is in the pen.

I got the green one and the purple one, and both are lovely shades of their respective colors.

text:
Note: My review is for the A5 cover.

As with everything there are pros and cons. A big pro is the price. For a fraction of any other non-leather cover, this Lihit Lab one is a great deal. I didn’t care for the bookmarks initially but I have been using them and it’s nice to have the option. I keep a LT1917 hardcover notebook in mine for bullet journaling and it works/fits perfectly, like they were made for one another. The pen sleeve in the front protects my fountain pen and I keep a cheap pen and mechanical pencil in the Velcro pocket, which is handy. Please be aware that if you bulk up those outside pockets with markers, sticky notes or anything else, it’ll create an uneven writing surface on the left pages. I keep mine pretty minimal so it’s fine. The interior pockets are great for anything credit card size (top pockets) and the one underneath is index card sized.

Honestly the only negative I have is that the elastic closure band is already becoming looser and I’ve used this cover a month. Other than that, the fabric is easy to care for and wipes clean with minimal effort. Sturdy and inexpensive, decent overall purchase.

title: Good, reliable ink cartridge
text: I use these in my Vanishing Point pen. They work great. Very easy to remove the old cartridge and put the new one in. Sometimes it takes a while for the ink to start flowing again, but it eventually does and then works just fine. I would say that this ink dries almost immediately. I’ve used it on cheap copy paper and quality paper (TRP; Stalogy) and it performs decently on both. It’s not waterproof so be mindful that it can smear if wet. I did refill a cartridge I cleaned out and put one of my bottled inks in it, but I ultimately prefer the convenience of the cartridge in my VP. I still save my cartridges so I can use my bottled inks in another Pilot fountain pen that’s also compatible with these cartridges. One more thing: the inks in these tend to dry light. I have Blue-Black and it looks more straight up blue. I also have Sepia and it looks like a washed out reddish brown color. The black tends to be dark when you start writing then becomes lighter as you go. Not sure if this is the case with everyone, but I thought it worth mentioning. I’m not sure why other reviewers say they don’t get a lot of writing with these pens. I write daily with it and a cartridge usually lasts me about 3 weeks, which considering the size of the cartridge, I’d say that’s a very generous amount. 0Recommended.

title: A6 no longer available - why?!
text: These little notebooks are fabulous. So bummed!! The paper in these notebooks is great quality and stands up to fountain pen ink (I’ve had no bleed thru, no feathering, no ghosting with a medium nib). The older notebooks I have don’t have any signs of aging or the ink fading, nothing. These are just solid, a well-made, perfect thin notebook. I can’t imagine why they discontinued making the smaller A6 sized ones because those were my go to for slim inserts. I wish I’d bought more and hoarded a stash. Northbooks, if you read this review, please—PLEASE—consider bringing them back in the A6 size. I know it’s not a first world problem, but I’d appreciate it very much. 🙂

title: Not my favorite
text: I've got to be honest: the Pilot Metropolitan is the most overrated "cheap" fountain pen on the market. It was my first experience with fountain pens a few years ago, and I sold that first one with no regrets. Believing maybe it was the nib size (I used to have a fine, and have since found I prefer a medium nib), I took a chance on this one. I loved the orange flower design on the barrel and well, it's a pretty pen. I inked it once and when the cartridge was empty, I cleaned it, dried it and back in the box it went. I'd have to say, in terms of starter fountain pens, you should go with a TWSBI. Their nibs write a lot smoother right out of the box, and I've never had any hard starts with a TWSBI pen, unlike this Metro and my Lamys. If you're particular about staying within the Pilot family and you have the means to do so then spring for a Vanishing Point or a Decimo if you can, which are still very easy to use with cartridges even for a beginner.

title: Great Pen for the price!
text:
If you are a beginner or someone more familiar with fountain pens, this is a great pen to get started with or try something new. This pen is lightweight coming in at .6 oz. It is 5.5 inches long with lid closed and 6.5 inches with lid posted, the lid is also snap cap. The nib is steel and you can change the nib and the body of the pen is resin/plastic and a matte finish. You can use Lamy cartridges or converters for different ink. Its a nice solid pen, has smooth movement across paper and is easily one of my more durable pens that I own and use daily. When compared to my Pilot metropolitan or Jinhao dragon pen I feel like it is a nice medium between weight, writing and quality. Always a nice addition to the fountain pen collection as well.

I've read concerns from other reviewers specifically for this seller that made statements these are fake Lamy safari fountain pens (I went ahead and took the risk with this seller because I knew it was going to take several weeks before I could get the pen from a pen company I trust (GPC) because they were closed due to Covid-19) and it is a legitimate concern that I see asked on most pens, given they have a high rate of counterfeit and knock off versions. These pens however are not fake and it was apparent the person was not familiar with Lamy manufacturing process and key features of real pens vs. fake. I hope the information below will help folks feel more confident in their Lamy safari ventures whether you get your pens from this seller or another seller.

Information on how to best spot a real vs. fake Lamy Safari fountain pen
- A real Lamy pen will come inside two boxes. A black Lamy box and a silver Lamy box. (Granted some special editions may have a special box or packaging, however its your lucky day because there is more than one way to verify a genuine Lamy safari pen!)
- Your pen will be found to have a cardboard ring with "remove" on it to separate the barrel from fully being attached (older pens had writing on the inside as well, but newer ones do not have the writing on the inside of the cardboard ring)
- You will have a blue ink cartridge inside, it does not come with a converter (it is very rare that it will unless you order it with it separately)
- Your new Lamy pen will probably show some blue ink (This is not a indication it was a used and returned pen) it is due to the fact that part of Lamy's manufacturing process before shipping is testing the pen with blue ink
- The Lamy logo will be clearly seen at the end of your pen (Fakes will not be as pronounced), will have "Germany" on the bottom of the pen and have a cross or plus indention with a small hole in the top or finial of the lid (Older versions was just a filled in circle with the small hole)
-When you attach your barrel you will be able to see through the window (where you see the ink cartridge) of your pen no matter how you put your barrel on. Fake pens you typically will have issues with this and have parts that block this window.
-The O-ring around the barrel will come off easily on a fake
-There will be some scratch-If its really scratchy or ink is not flowing well, look closely (preferably with magnifying glass) to see if the nib tines are misaligned. There may also be the factor of how you are holding the pen as well. Also the writing on the nib is pronounced and has Lamy and the size on the nib as well

And guess what folks, these pens passed the test!

title: Nice quality notebook
text:
This is my first Rhodia dot book. Overall I really like the book and chose this one over others, because personally I didn't like the orange elastic strap on the other versions. The dots are clear enough to see them, the paper seems to be a good quality and bleed through is very limited. Dots measure 41 vertical dots and 27 horizontal per page (If you plan to use two page spreads, be aware on some pages the dots may be slightly off ) and it is a hard bound Italian leatherette cover. It also has a expandable cover in the back that can easily be missed.

Shadow/Bleed through
I've used the prisma-color pens .005, .05, B, & C and those will not bleed through. You can see some shadows of what's on the previous page, but it is minimal and I didn't feel that it interfered with the next page of info. If you choose to use a prisma-color marker on the other hand, these WILL BLEED. I went ahead and took a chance as others said Rhodia doesn't bleed (I'd say probably with most pens/markers, but obviously there are exceptions) but because prisma-color markers are so saturated, even a quick sweep will bleed through. The only paper that I have found that prisma-color markers do not bleed through is Bristol paper (I believe this is ivory according to the listing, which I have never written on). Crayola markers do not bleed through. Also, something to take into consideration, if you use colored markers near the sewn part in the center, you might have some bleed through, through the tiny holes and from the ink traveling through the thread.

The picture I've included shows the bleed thru of my black prismacolor marker with a single quick stroke and the amount of shadow you can see from the crayola and prisma color pens (The squares are pictures I taped in). I took some double sided tape to tape the back of this page and the next together to "fix" not seeing the bleed thru on my next page.

title: Its okay, just not for stairs
text:
So I wanted to get a few grocery trips in before I gave my review. I was honestly going to give it a 2 star rating, but to be fair the cart is functional if you are not going up stairs. So my review comes from buying this cart primarily to help carry stuff upstairs (and its advertised as such anyway).

So to begin with I was impressed that assembly takes seconds. All you have to do is pop on the wheels and your set.

The packaging says up to 65lbs, however even rolling around 20-30lbs of groceries upstairs (18 to be exact), made me just want to go ahead and make the extra trips. It does roll up stairs, but not without alot of effort, which could make you lose your balance (I'm in my 20s and fairly strong, so I definitely would not recommend this to the elderly or those who are at risk of falling or cant lift very much weight. You might be okay with something like a light load of laundry though).

The handle is just right when you are pushing the cart, but it feels a bit short for me (I'm 5'5) when pulling it.

As far as durability, the cart doesn't do very well trying to turn corners and it appears to put a strain on the wheels, but if you're going straight it does okay. Also weight affects turning ability too.

Overall, this cart is better suited for climbing over curbs and going in straight lines.

title: Its okay, but convenient...

The ink doesn't come with any instructions, so if you are new to these cartridges you will unscrew the neck from the pen barrel of your fountain pen, firmly insert your cartridge by putting it in straight, and you should feel or hear a click when the cartridge is fully inserted. You can't squeeze the cartridge because it is stiff, so you may have to give your pen a few gently shakes to get the ink down.  What I don't like about this product is that the ink doesn't seem to flow as easily as the Pilot Namiki cartridges, but the ink does seem to last a little longer, but not by much. So you will still go through the pack rather quickly and they won't last as long as having a bottled ink, but again they are convenient if you are on the go.

title: Good product, especially for those on the go
text: I like this product, because it is easy to change out and not messy and useful for when you are on the go. The ink doesn't come with any instructions, so if you are new to these cartridges you will unscrew the neck from the pen barrel of your fountain pen, firmly insert your cartridge by putting it in straight without turning or twisting (the larger end with the valve cover is what will be pointing down), and you should feel or hear a click when the cartridge is fully inserted. You can give the cartridge 2-3 squeezes and the ink should start flowing through your pen with ease. If it doesn't, then there may be an issue with your pen nib, or you haven't given enough time for the ink to flow (but it shouldn't take very long). One thing to take into consideration when using the cartridges is that you will go through them quickly (nib size could affect this too), especially if you write a lot with your pen. I use these cartridges with my Pilot metropolitan (fine nib) to write case notes with and went through a cartridge in 11 days. So you will go through the pack rather quick and they won't last say as long as having a bottled ink, but again, they are convenient if you are on the go.

title: I really like this pen!
text:
I absolutely love this pen. So to get started, lets clarify what is the size point of the nib? The listing says fine, the community says medium or fine. Well the nib is labeled as fine, but for comparison it is not as fine as say the pilot metropolitan, but it is also not as medium as the Jinhao 1200 (gold pen with dragon & red eyes). So it lands somewhere in the middle of those two and you can see the difference in the picture that I've added. It's slightly bolder than the fine, yet not as bold as the medium.

Next this pen weighs in at a whopping 3 ounces. If you own the Jinhao 1200, it weights 2 ounces. Even though this pen is heavier, I actually like it better than the Jinhao 1200, because the weight feels more evenly distributed. In the Jinhao 1200 a good portion of weight is in the cap and more towards the nib. The weight distribution in this pen however makes it more comfortable. Where your fingers rest when holding they touch part of the dragon design and for some this may be uncomfortable when writing. I am currently using the Jinhao international cartridges with this pen and it writes wonderfully. I can write at a normal angle and it does not skip. That being said, I think if it is skipping then it may be one of a few things either the ink being used or there may be an issue with the nib itself.

The "jade" is fake in case you are unsure. I can't quite tell if the ball is plastic or if it is glass like a marble. It does shake when writing, but I plan on either putting a dab of clear glue under it or some other method to keep it from shaking. The box that it comes in is very nice. The box I received is not what is pictured, at least on the inside. It does not have the insert in the middle, its just flat with a ribbon to hold the pen. (I've added a picture of the box). Overall though I am happy with this pen and it seems to be of good quality.

title: Nice pen for the price point
text:
This pen is a lovely sturdy looking pen. When observing it online the design appears like it may be rough and uncomfortable, but it is actually very smooth. The pen as a whole is a bit heavy, and according to my scale is almost 2 ounces. Most of the weight however is surprisingly in the cap and without capping the pen feels nice in your hand. The line point appears medium/bold.

Things to be aware of:
This pen does not come with any instructions, something I really liked having with my Pilot metropolitan. So if you are new to fountain pens you'll need to check here with other buyers or search on the Internet for care instructions.

Initially I considered giving this pen 3 stars because when writing it was skipping. It does take a little bit to get good ink flow. I am using the Jinhao international cartridges and you can't give them a little squeeze to get the ink flow because they are very stiff. I found that slowing my writing pace down helped get the ink to flow better and then I was able to write at my normal pace. It does come with a converter, so using bottled ink and other brands could influence your inkflow experience as some inks are thicker/thinner than others.

I don't recall reading in the description if it the pen was identified as a pull cap or screw cap, but it is a pull cap. I initially had some difficulty pulling the cap off, but it just takes more force to pull than what I am used to. When replacing the cap you'll hear a nice solid click. Capping on the end of your pen isn't quite as secure, but you can push the cap down far enough it will hold on to the pen and not fly off.

Edit* I recently tried noodlers bullet proof ink with this pen and I have noticed that the ink flow is much better than using the Jinhao cartridge with this pen. So I stand by the statement that using different inks could improve inkflow.
