title: Amazing Value for Sketchers
text:
I bought these to see if they'd be suitable as a "first sketchbook" for students in sketching workshops that I teach. Wow, are they ever!!! I'm going to stock up not only for my beginner sketchers, but also for myself!

The paper is not "thick"...it feels like the same weight as you'd get in any less expensive sketchbook. However, it performed well beyond expectations. I tested several things as you can see in the picture. NOTHING except the Sharpie bled through to the other side. There is some kind of sizing in the paper, because the very juicy watercolor swatches flowed and blended very nicely across the surface. It acts sort of like hot press...sorta slippery, no real tooth to grab the pigment. But still...the granulating Cerulean Blue did granulate somewhat. There was a tiny bit of buckling but not much. The colors stayed bright! I would say this paper could handle direct watercolor pretty well as you might splash on for an urban sketch but don't expect it to handle a lot of glazes or reworking...it's really not meant for wet media so the fact it can handle a juicy wash is a nice bonus! Using a water brush with the Flair marker also resulted in no bleed through. The gouache in the upper right corner dried so fast the paper really didn't react to it. Graphite erases beautifully with a soft polymer eraser. My mechanical pencil's .7mm lead felt very nice and smooth on the surface of the page.

I think this is a perfect sketchbook for quick sketches in graphite, ink, direct watercolor with light touch, even gouache. Perfect size for a purse or small pack, and what a bargain.

title: Best in Show
text:
I looked seriously at a LOT of planners here on Amazon before choosing this one. Its simplicity and quiet design appealed to me. The fact that it doesn't waste a novel's worth of pages talking about how to organize my life and be grateful also appealed. I don't need a life coach in a planner, just a useful time organizer and motivating tool...so I have no desire to pay for a bunch of pages to be looked at once then never again...ESPECIALLY when it comes time to buy a replacement planner after I fill this one up. That one of the things that kept me from purchasing another Best Self planner, besides comparative cost for function offered by this planner. The Priori planner has exactly three coaching pages at the front, if you need more than that, the planner's design might be so complicated that you will spend half your day keeping up with your planner rather than actually doing the work or other tasks you've planned.

I originally thought I would have preferred this planner be organized by Month, then Weekly pages for that month, followed by Daily pages after each week but on second thought now that I hold it in my hands, I like how all the Monthly pages are together, then the Weekly pages, then the Daily pages. I can use the three ribbon place markers to mark the current month/week/day easily enough...plus the current organization will make it a lot easier to page through all the months for big picture stuff, or all the weeks one after the other to notice trends, habits, etc.

I am very pleased with this planner's price and design. Can't wait to start filling it up with plans and scheduled stuff to help me achieve my goals.

If you're a fountain pen user, as I am, please see my comment in response to the question about how the planner does with fountain pens.

title: Twice the tape...
text:
Ok, first of all I get it - it's a label maker and a pretty low priced one so it's not going to be 'high tech/high quality'. But (showing my age here) the cheap old-school, simple, less-plastic-used-to-make-the-thing, not-so-pretty label makers of yore at least put sufficient pressure on the tape so as to form a nice crisp letter. This one does not. The letters have a white haze around them and the letters themselves aren't embossed enough to stand out from that stretched-tape haze. Yes you can read a word, but why bother putting out a label maker that doesn't make that word stand out?
Probably worse than the quality of embossing is the horrible letter spacing - the spacing between letters would suffice as a space between entire words. So you have W O R D S instead of WORDS. (Spaced farther than shown as comments parses extra spaces.) Pretty much this means that you'll be going through tape twice as fast - not quite economical as the $9.95 price would lead to believe.

title: it is important to know that this is NOT a flex pen
text:
This pen writes like a dream. Really smooth with little to no feedback in the medium nib. There are a few things to keep in mind before buying this pen.

1) this is NOT A FLEX PEN. It is able to create line variance because it is a soft nib, but it does not flex like many people expect. The videos that show it off as a flex pen that flexes a lot or very easily usually have modified nib. With that in mind don’t push too hard or you will ruin the nib
2) this is the cheaper version of the Falcon. The more expensive one is made of metal, this one is plastic or resin. It still looks and feels great but is a little light.
3) just like any other gold nib, the nib is softer than steel nibs and softer than glass. Be careful using a glass ink bottle not to scrape the nib across the glass.

If you set your expectations for a wet noodle flex nib, you will be disappointed because that is not what this pen is meant to be. But this pen is amazing and I recommend it to anyone who is ready to take the next step from beginner cheaper pens to gold nib pens.

The good:
Nice weight, they feel substantial without being heavy
They hold a LOT of ink.
I have not had any leaking

The bad:

title: Not as Useful as Expected
text:
Upon opening this planner, I discovered that all the months that are printed on the pages for looking at the whole month are exactly the same. The first day of every month is the first, as if all months begin on a Monday (or Sunday depending on the publisher). The rest of the undated planner is more useable. It can be used as any undated planner.

As inexpensive as it is, I wasn't expecting much. I figured if I didn't like the layout, I could use the vinyl cover for a B6 journal I have. Technically, I can use it for this. However, the heat-sealed seam for the zipped pocked is torn. The vinyl itself is thin and doesn't appear as if it will hold up to months of use.

When I look at a monthly overview feature, I want a day to coordinate with which day of the week it's on. It isn't worth returning due to its low price. I might be able to find a use for it, but not as I had intended. It would work for planning a week's menu or keeping a weather log. The year at a glance could be used to write down birthdays and other occasions that occur annually.

title: Best. Embroidery. Pens. Ever.
text:
These are the best embroidery pens ever. I said what I said and I'll stand by it 'til the death. (Probably. Pretty sure.)
But seriously, these are great for embroidery. They write smoothly and clearly. They write on fabric well without too much drag. The markings last well, but not forever. Run an iron over them and *poof* the pen marks are gone. It's like magic, in fact, I'm pretty sure they'd work as a magic trick for an enterprising illusionist.
I love them, I bought the whole set, because they work so well, even though I really only needed one color. I trace my design, stitch, iron and I'm done. No more chalk rubbing off, no more trying to scrub off the markers that were promised to wash right off super easily and then didn't. No more struggles tracing the pattern. These are the best. title: Favorite Fountain Pen
text:
So, I've had a variety of fountain pens. Vintage ones. Cheap ones. Fake ones. Expensive ones. Pretty ones. Ugly ones. Fine ones. Broad ones. And they've all ended up being just not quite what I wanted. They'd either not write smoothly or clog or just be a lot of upkeep. This one is different. This one is perfect.
Ok, ok, fine. Maybe not perfect, but nearly perfect. It writes beautifully. I've had no issues with keeping it writing smoothly. Maintenance? What maintenance? Seriously, cleaning it now and then with running water and you're golden. And it already comes with a converter, so you can use your own ink! It feels nice in the hand. I've had no issues with leaks or skipping or anything. It's even pretty, so very, very pretty. It is very nearly perfect.
I did purchase the medium nib, so the line is a little thicker and sometimes I wish it were finer. That is my only compaint. But then...I could just buy one with a fine nib, so maybe it really is perfect!

title: I LOVE this pen—Great value, Great look
text:
I'm no professional, but I've been using fountain pens for over 4 years now. I love them because they force me to write lighter (so as not to ruin the nibs) and I can write a lot longer with them since I'm not straining my wrists. I also love them because they are REFILLABLE—v eco friendly—and the ink glides way smoother than ballpoints. (Heck they're classy too and I like to feel fancy tbh)

I was using a Pilot Kakuno fine nib fountain pen for years and I really liked it. It was super light and the nib was very fine, but I found it was a little scratchy on my paper and hard to hold sometimes. I like the Pilot Metropolitan because of its smooth writing and its weight. I initially thought the weight would hurt more than it helped, but turns out Pilot knows what they're doing and the weight allows for much smoother, ergonomic writing. It's easy to push and pull the nib across paper and have it do exactly what you want it to do.

Overall, the Pilot Metropolitan is a great pen for casual or beginning users, like myself. This particular retro orange color is also so heckin fantastic.

title: Astounding Value and Excellent Fountain Pen for Any Price!
text: I wrote this review for Goldspot Pens, where I purchased this wonderful gem. Here is what I said: "This fountain pen by Pilot is an *amazing* value. As a fountain pen collector for many years, I have owned very high-end pens that do not write as well or flow as freely as this one does. It's very comfortable to hold, and has a substantive feel because of the brass barrel. The finish is lovely--uniformly vivid red color, and a nice contrasting pattern on the ring that encircles the barrel. The nib is quite elegantly finished for an inexpensive pen, reflecting the classy lines and structure of the more expensive Namiki fountain pens that Pilot also produces. The fine workmanship I've always expected of Namiki pens is also seen in the high quality of this pen by Pilot. I give it my highest recommendation as a workhorse, everyday pen, or a starter for a new fountain pen user. The new user who writes with one of these will be a fan of fountain pens for life!"

title: REVISED review: Turns out to be junk
text:
I reviewed this phone shortly after purchasing it at a large box store and said I thought it would be OK -- didn't measure up to the old Uniden, which is no longer made, but it appeared to be the best on the market. If this IS the best available, then...well...heaven help you if you buy less than the "best." This phone is one of the most annoying devices I've ever used. It does work to block calls, and that's good -- though my freestanding call blocker works far better. But what makes me want to drop it into the deep end of the pool is that its handsets constantly run out of juice, blatting LOW BATT'RY LOW BATT'RY LOW BATT'RY at you, at all hours of the day and night. You get FIVE handsets, but PANASONIC ONLY PROVIDES FOUR HANDSET CHARGERS!!!!! If you place one of them on the charger on the home base, it sits there and beeps. BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP ad enragingly infinitum! Fully charged or not! At all hours of the day or night.

This thing is junk. I am going to port my landline number over to my iPhone and throw the Panasonic where it belongs, in the garbage. I need a phone in every room, should I fall or suffer a health emergency and have to call 911. Guess those phones will have to be cheapo clamshells with different numbers for every phone.

My late father, a WW II veteran, used to brag that America has the highest standard of living in the world. Supposedly that was one of several things this country went to war for, he thought. NOT so, Dad. Not anymore!

title: Reliably Loveable
text:

title: They're Turning Me into a Pen Nut...
text:
Dang, but I love these cheap Pilot pens! The things are turning me into a fountain-pen collector. :-D I've held forth on models in other colors. By and large, I'm finding the quality is consistent: one works just about as well as the next. And "as well" is operative: ink flows smoothly, consistently, and pleasingly. I think I like the fine nib better than the medium, but that's a matter of taste. If you use a type of paper that's not unduly absorbent ("sketch" paper as opposed to "drawing" paper, for example), the medium nib is fine. If the paper is somewhat absorbent, the fine nib is better, as the medium nib will disgorge too much ink.

Gotta have one in every color!

title: One Heckuva Pen for the Price
text:
This is the second of two Pilot Metropolitan pens I purchased at the same time. This one has a medium nib, and the other, the red variety, has a fine point. I found them both very pleasing. Of the two, I REALLY love this one, because I like the way the medium nib dispenses ink. Remembering pens from the Good Old Days, I expected this a medium nib to squander vast quantities of ink and to create a sloppy-looking document. But no: apparently the Japanese idea of "medium" is close to the US idea of fine. On a good piece of paper, this medium-nib pen glides right along -- extremely smooth and pleasant to write with -- and it makes a nice, neat line. Even compared to my old Waterman, purchased back in the day when I could afford pricey accouterments, this inexpensive pen performs handsomely.

Whenever I like something this much, it's the kiss of death...so I probably will buy one or two more of them in the near future, before they go out of style. If this thing lasts, then it's worth considerably more than it costs. IMHO.

title: So far, excellent value for the price!
text:
I bought this red pen and another by the same maker in black for a couple of dollars less. Given how inexpensive the things were, I'm REALLY surprised at how pleasing they are. The red pen has a fine nib, and the black one has a medium nib. On a lark, I also bought the package of three small bottles of Pilot Iroshizuki inks in red, teal blue, and green. The blue ink went into an old and very nice Waterman pen I had laying around. The red and the dark green ended up in these new Pilot pens.

The Waterman is...well, a Waterman. The ink flows beautifully and angels sing when you write with it. But what's amazing is that these low-budget Pilot pens are working just as smoothly and just as pleasantly as the expensive Waterman! In fact, I'd say the black Pilot pen with the medium nib writes and flows even better than the Waterman. To my astonishment, I might add.

How long this state of affairs will last remains to be seen. But even if they only survive a few months, given the price I'll be happy enough.

title: Big improvement on the competition...
text:
This year I tried a different brand for the wall calendar that lurks by my office door, where I'm forced to check what I'm supposed to be doing that day every time I walk in and out. For several months, I pined for my old calendar. Finally, in a burst of sentimentality I ordered up a 2017 Lang calendar to replace the one I'd foolishly ordered last winter.

SO much better. The Lang calendar's grid has large enough cells for you to enter several events. Each monthly grid shows last month's and next month's calendars in miniature, so you don't have to flip back a month to figure out what day the 26th was. And the last page of these calendars has space for you to enter reminders for NEXT year. So repeating reminders and events that happen after December 31st can be stashed there and entered after you get the following year's calendar.

And the artwork can't be beat.

title: Was Disappointing but Customer Service Is Exceptional
text:
Pros: Nice balance. Pen is a little stockier than some, but is comfortable for short periods in my hands. If you're looking for a stick pen this isn't it.
Cons: Perhaps a little heavy, especially for older hands. Wouldn't be able to write the great American novel or even a long letter without the hand tiring. Also the ink skips terribly and that is the true reason for the abysmal rating. The ink in this leaves gaping spaces, regardless if the stroke is a curve, upstroke, downstroke, or a cross bar. My Pilot G2 pen writes flawlessly and effortlessly and costs much less. I'm hopeful that maybe the ink was just old and will try a new refill to see if it solves the skipping problem. If not, the pen is totally useless at any cost in my opinion.

Edit 9/21/19 - Customer Service was good enough to refund the purchase price of the original pen, less the cost for shipping that was built into the cost of the pen, and they did indeed send another pen with a second replacement ink cartridge. Excellent customer service. At the same time I received the replacement ink refills I ordered. Sooo...I went to swap out the refill and lo and behold the spring that goes inside the pen was missing. I have to laugh. Sometimes when things go wrong, it just continues to go wrong. Well, fortunately I'm a pen hound, love stationery and all things related to it, and I had some old pens that probably should've been thrown out ages ago, found one with a spring and voila. Pen now writes perfectly. So....after some thought, my original one star rating should've been for the ink refill itself, as that was the real issue with all the skipping and whatnot; the pen itself is well made, looks nice, has a good feel. It's a pleasure to use it as a writing implement. I'm happy. I can see myself using this long into the future.

Most companies will only let you choose one logo/motto/statement that will be engraved on all the pens. The fact that each pen can have a different saying on it is awesome to me.

*engraving - the pens are engraved. You can feel the grooves of the engraving if you run your finger over the text. It is not a decal or sticker as I've seen with some cheap customizable pens

4. Quality: these look and feel way more expensive than they really are. No quality issues so far. I will update my review if I find any issues.

**update** I've had them for several weeks. The gold accent color faded very fast! It's now an awkward rust looking color. This is pretty much my only complaint. Otherwise they are still decent pens. None have broken, cracked, etc.

5. Refills: each pen has a refill and then you receive 10 additional refills. I HATED the cheap gel refill. I am a pen snob though. I won't write with just anything. I played around with pens I already have and found out this pen will take UNIBALL SIGNO gel refills (which are my fav pen anyhow, so this is a game changer). You're welcome. I included the UNIBALL pens in the photo so you can see which pens I'm referring to...

6. Amount of pens: I've been looking for executive-looking pens that can be customized for a while. Most pen companies have minimums of 30 or 50. This is a great deal for just the right amount needed for personal use.

I'm already considering ordering more with the names of my leadership team engraved on them as part of a "thank you" gift.

title: I take notes all day in a journal and this pen is a joy to write with
text:
This was my first fountain pen purchase with the intent to get something decent for an everyday writer for business notes. After many reviews and many looks at different options I decided on the Pilot Metro Retro along with Pilot black/blue ink.

I have been using the pen now for about 1 month. I take notes all day in a journal and this pen is a joy to write with. I also sign many letters throughout the day and this is the pen of choice. I went with the fine nib because I like to write small and I was concerned of the potential bleeding. There is no bleed on the journal paper, cannot say the same for standard copy paper, but the bleed is minimal and doesn't stop me from using this pen all day every day on just about any paper that I would use a ballpoint pen or rollerball.

1) It will drip ink if you shake it or hit it too hard on paper. Using this pen makes you a more patient writer and forces you to write with the skills you were likely taught when you first started writing, including holding the pen correctly. If this is the first time you are writing with a fountain pen, chances are you will get ink on your fingers holding the pen. Be patient, the more you use it the less it will happen.
2) store the pen up-write and try not to shake it while you are not using it. As an example, when you take it to a meeting, put it in your shirt pocket, not your pants, in your hand or in you bag while you travel/walk to the meeting. Moving too much will make ink come from the tip. The good news is that if it does happen, the pen doesn't leak through the cap, at least it hasn't for me
3) use good ink. It comes with one black ink and a squeeze converter if you want to go that route. I like the cartridges myself and they are reasonably priced and easy to find on amazon.
4) don't let anyone borrow it, you will likely not get it back because they will likely want to keep it. After trying it, one of my co-workers bought same model, different color and nib within a couple of days of trying it. It took a couple of days because they too researched and after reading all of the reviews and trying mine, there was no question that this pen was a great purchase.
5) the body of this pen is made of metal, not plastic. It is solid, sturdy and has nice balance.
6) I like everything about this pen. No negatives

title: Great Printer for Students
text: I love this printer!  Yes, I had trouble setting it up ... BUT I am 55 years old and not tech-savvy.  I'm doing good to pair my Beats By Dr. Dre with my cell phone.  However, my neighbor, who attends university with me, came over and had it going in under 5 minutes.  If you know what you're doing with modern computers and electronics, this shouldn't be too hard for you.  I used the CD, as my laptop has a CD/DVD drive.  And so far, it's really dependable.  I don't have any issues with the "deep sleep' feature some people mentioned.  I just leave it on, and go for days sometimes without printing.  I bought one of the high-yield toner cartridges, too, and even though I use it (I'm a philosophy/history major), my neighbors use it (special ed major and a grad student in nutrition) the cartridge it came with is still going.  With a high-yield cartridge and the cost of paper, the cost per page comes out at 2 cents per copy, and our university print lab charges us 8 cents per page.  And done of us are doing anything that warrants color printing.  I do want to emphasize that this is the perfect printer for students who just want to print assignments, lecture slides, and study guides for their own use.  I also like the fact that I can print my essays here in my apartment, edit them without having to state at the laptop screen, and then save my eyes for editing.  I really love this printer, it wasn't difficult for my neighbor to set up (although he really knows his stuff; he built his own computer, but I know a lot of classmates who do that, too).  Most students are probably as computer-savvy as my neighbor.  At any rate, this is a great printer, and it saves myself, and my friends, money that could be charged to our student accounts.  If we need color, we just go to the Print Lab and pay 16 cents a page.  It's monochromatic, so if you want color prints, look elsewhere.  For our purposes, it's great. Also, I want to say that my neighbors have a printer, and it does print color, but as soon as one color of ink runs out, they can't print anything until they buy new toner.  That's why they use mine.

title: Whimsical Fountain Pens
text: I really love these fountain pens!  Since the nineties, I've used fountain pens.  I still have my Parker Sonnet, but it's a vintage, it has gold trim, an 18 karat nib, and it would cost hundreds to replace it.  Someone stole my Waterman off my desk when I worked as a paralegal in Chicago.  Walked into my office while I was downstairs grabbing a latte and stole it off my desk.  Although I love the flexibility and flair of an expensive fountain pen like the aforementioned, pens are among the small items which pile up as life's collateral losses.  However, these Pilot pens are surprisingly smooth, substantial, and fun to use.  I have five of them--all colors except the orange--and they're fun to use for everyday writing.  As I am active in the local university, these pens are the ones I keep in my bookbag, along with plenty of cartridges.  These pens come with an easy-to-use ink reservoir, a squeeze-bladder-type cartridge, and they take the Pilot Nakimi cartridges.  In my experience--I've been using them for a few months now--they are dependable and easy to maintain.  My sole criticism lies in the inability of the cap to stay fixed upon the barrel while writing.  It often falls off during class when I'm taking notes, so I've learned to place it to the side.  It's such a minor point, in my opinion, that it doesn't warrant a four-star rating as opposed to a five.  Again, I really enjoy these pens.  The medium nib delivers a narrower line than my medium nib Parker, but that has to do with the flexibility of the gold.  Stainless steel is not so soft, but these pens write so smoothly I really don't notice hand fatigue.  As a German Philosophy/History major, I do a lot of writing, and I like to sketch out my essays longhand.  If you like gold-nib fountain pens, but don't like the several hundred dollar risk you take every time you leave your home with it or pick it up to write (I once dropped one of mine and they ALWAYS land on the nib, which destroys it, and you pay at least $100 for a replacement) try one of these whimsical little pens.  They are perfect for everyday use, for those who move around a lot, or for beginners.

I love this pen. But who's to say that the mundane cannot be elevated to high art? Why must we settle for something less than the complete unification of the sacred and the profane? But also, I've written many new poems with this pen, because the ink flows organically from it, as if you really were dripping your thoughts on paper.

title: Japanese Pens Are Good, These Mexican-Made Ones Are Terrible!
text:
I love Sarasa pens and have used them for years and years. When I lived in Japan, I tried all their styles and colors and really thought of them as a quality pen. They still are and Japanese-made Sarasa pens are a reliable workhorse of a pen that I can't ever get enough of. Imagine my surprise when a new type of rapid drying ink was available in 0.5mm (my favorite size) AND at such a low price! I ordered right away.

I noticed that these pens tout a 0.5mm line width but actually write out at about 0.7 to 0.8mm. To check and make sure, I wrote out the same sentences with these pens and older, Japanese-made Sarasa 0.5mm pens I still have. I also used 0.7mm Sarasa SE pens made in Japan to check. Sure enough, these pens are wider than advertised. They don't write as well as the Japanese made ones and with the line width, they are not as good to me for daily usage. Repeated calls to Zebra aren't being returned, but I will try to get a response from them. If not, then these are going back to Amazon.

The Mexico-made pens are of inferior quality. Most of Zebra's RDI Sarasa line you can find in stores, along with their cheap ballpoints, are made in Mexico and the poor quality really shows. I will only buy verified Japanese made Sarasas from now on and will never give another penny for such cheaply made pens.

A good alternative to these inferior pens are the Papermate 0.5mm gel pens. The bodies are made in China, but the refills themselves are from Japan. They are as smooth and as wonderful as the Japanese-made Sarasas and they aren't expensive.

text:

First of all, the label attaches securely to the glass spice jars, but if you need to reposition a label, you can do it with no loss of sticking power. The labels themselves are just the right size for the tall spice jars. Although they are too big for the half size spice jars, I just cut them in half. Also, it is easy to wipe off the writing with a little pressure but simply handling the jars as you would when using the spices would not mar the writing. So Perfect! So Cute! Rarely do you get a product that ticks off all the boxes. Note that this set did not come with a chalk pen. I read that other people had problems with their chalk pens, so I bought two different kinds. My favorite for this small label was a fine point - the Bistro Chalk Marker. The other Chalk Pen by "Super Chalks" was slightly thicker which would be perfect for any label larger than the spice label. Note that neither chalk pen worked out of the box even when I pumped it. The easiest way I found was to pull out the point and turn it around and replace it into the pen so that it would come into direct contact with the chalk and soak it up. Then the pen worked.

title: Great buy for the price, but you get what you pay for.
text: I bought this due to the sudden need to laminate quite a bit of homemade home school activities for my 4 and 6 year olds during the Covid-19 quarantine.  I did not want to spend a lot of money because I was not sure whether I would actually get as much use out of this to warrant a higher price.  For the price, this is a great purchase.  It heats up fairly quickly and works well.  I have laminated probably about 50 sheets now, and I have only had one or two pieces that needed to go through again due to not melting the laminating sheets properly.  My main criticism of this product and one that I would pay extra money to have fixed is that because there are no guides or a tray to hold the input, it is easy to have the sheet you are laminating go in at an angle that causes one side to get "crunched" up and ruined.  A secondary problem is that even if you get the sheet in straight, if you don't support the sheet you are laminating, the paper inside the laminating sheet can move around a bit as it sits at an angle towards the floor.  (I hope that makes sense.)  Other pros are that the profile is very slim and it's a pretty good looking piece of equipment.  Given the choice, particularly now that I see how much I am using the machine, I would probably purchase a slightly more expensive laminator if it had guides and a tray.  Otherwise, this is a solid buy.

title: Wonderful Set and Wonderful Pens!
text: I Love these Sakura Micron pens.  I have just newly started journaling and these have been a great product for that.  I bought this set because I wanted to try out different tips and I found this set to be a good value.  These pens are generally not inexpensive (although I think they are worth it) and for someone who either knows they want this assortment of tips or for someone, like me, who wants to try them out but doesn't want to pay the piece-by-piece price at the local supply store (which was more expensive for me), I would definitely recommend these.  The assortment is great and the fact that they are all black helps you to really experience the different tips.  The ink is a great black that does not bleed (in my Moleskin and Leuchtturm journals),dries fairly quickly and the pens have a great hand feel and are nice for both drawing and writing.  Would highly recommend these.  I found them to be a great value.

title: Solid office pens
text: These pens are pretty much exactly as described.  The tip is a nice very fine tip.  The colors are standard but very pretty.  The grip and feel are nice.  I deducted one star because I ordered these upon someone's suggestion that they would not bleed through the pages of a Leuchtturm 1917 squared journal I used for bullet journalling.  The black pen does bleed (I have not used the other colors much).  I also think the tip is a little too fine to be comfortable for my writing style.  They feel much finer than a fine tip fountain pen for instance and I worry that if I press a little too hard, the tip will puncture the page.  That said, this is a personal preference and I also did not see a claim that this pen would not bleed so I can't severely fault the pen--it just wasn't great for what I was looking for.  Otherwise, if you would like an assortment of very fine tipped pens in a roller ball style and in pretty but standard colors, these are a good option.  I think these would be good for the workplace or for school as opposed to art projects.

title: Solid pen and great price point
text:
I had just purchased this same pen in a fine point (which I also really like) and decided I might use medium point more often. I obviously liked this pen (in fine tip) enough to purchase a second. Some reasons why:

- the squeeze convertor that comes with the pen (nice extra that allows some more flexibility although I have not used it yet)
- the cheery color options that make the serious feel of a fountain pen feel fresher and more accessible
- the weight of the pen (it's just heavy enough to be right for writing but not so heavy it overpowers or fatigues the hand)
- the width of the pen (similar to its weight, not so wide that it feels uncomfortable to write with--note that my hands are on the smaller side--but not so thin that your hand tenses after using it too much)
- nice ink color options available with this pen
- great price point
- generally nice feel of the pen in hand and of it writing

I will say that I prefer this medium tip to the fine, but this is so subjective, so I don't think this detracts from either pen. Ultimately, I would highly recommend. If it's useful to anyone, I bought this primarily to use in my bullet journal, but I ended up using it more often in just daily writing. It's a nice experience and adds a little something. It has not replaced my other rollers or other types of pens, but for me, I did not anticipate, need or want it to, so this was fine for me. I would really recommend this to anyone interested in adding one or a few fountain pens to their pen arsenal.

title: Good stool, but feels slightly unsteady
text:
I purchased this for use in our laundry room for easy access to tall cabinets. I wanted one of these step stools because I remember them from the library and they always seemed very sturdy and easy to use. I love that this comes in various colors. The red is lovely and looks very much like the picture online. In terms of the feel, I was not completely sure about it when it arrived. It felt slightly less solid than the ones I remember from the library days (or even from the barnes and noble). List of pros and cons below:

PROs:
Great color and look
Convenient for a room where the stool does not need to be folded up/put away
Easy to use--wheels glide and stop easily

CONs:
Slightly unsteady feel when stepping up
Stepping area feels slightly small and could make you feel off-balance if you don't have something to hold or lean onto.

title: Good value for a great pen

title: Absolutely love

title: My new favorite pen
text: I absolutely love this pen. It looks fabulous and writes beautifully. I am even thinking about buying one for my coworker who does calligraphy.

title: Used and Cracked
text: I bought 3 Pilot Metropolitan fountain pens as gifts. Two of them were fine, but one came used and with a crack in the plastic nib holder. There was already some ink in the converter which had leaked during shipping, and the crack in the nib area made the ink leak out onto fingers every time the pen was used. I bought a replacement from another company and will return the damaged pen. I tried to clean it and see if there was any way to salvage it, but the crack can't be fixed. It was very disappointing to receive a used pen as a gift.

title: Fantastic daily driver
text: Fantastic pen especially for the price. At $10 you’d think it would be made for novelty, but is easily passable as a daily driver. The job is smothe, great ink flow, and the metal body exudes quality. It also comes with a squeeze converter that’s convenient to change inks with.

title: Very good quality. Should last a long time.
text: Really high quality pen case. I’d really like to see a larger case as well. I removed the notepad and use the band for storing calligraphy nibs and some ink cartridges. Overall, I’d readily recommend this case to anyone.

title: Good pen, definitely worth buying new.
text:
I bought this to save money on pens going forward with my degree. I run through a pack of pilot G10 pens in roughly a month at university. This pen writes the same way, but ink is unbelievably cheap. It’s definately the best option for someone that wants to use a fountain pen, but doesn’t want an ornate display.

The pen is 5/5 stars, in my opinion. However I bought one used and it came very messy with orange ink all inside the box and over the pen. I easily washed it away, but it’s frustrating that it wasnt at least emptied before being put back in the box.

title: Very good pen to write with.

title: Sturdy and cute

title: My Favorite Pens--and Choice in Color

These pens write neat, non-clumpy, and while the .38 is too thin really, the .5 is PERFECT. This way I don't waste the really light ones because I don't use them for coloring but for writing. title: Lovely color!!

I'd happily buy more of their ink.

title: A must for online teachers
text:

Boards stack together well and fit in a dollar tree organizer.
Because of their sturdiness, they weigh more than traditional whiteboards. Users with hand or wrist issues may find them difficult to hold upright for long periods of time.

title: Fountain Pen Friendly Pocket-sized Notebooks
text: Excellent quality. Ive kept a Field Notes book in my wallet for years.  When I began using fountain pens, I replaced my Field Books with these.  No bleeding, and very little ghosting.  Nibs glide smoothly with no missed strokes.  I would prefer rounded corners to the square currently offered on this book.

title: Smooth flowing Ink

title: Extra wide form factor is great for labels
text: We use this size to correct labels on folders. Yes, kind of old fashioned, but still necessary in a professional office. Works well, doesn’t come loose over time, even here in humid South Florida.

title: Card arrived undamaged in transit, no wrinkles.
text: Bottom line is that if we’re going to order a greeting card online, it must arrive without any damage from transport. This card arrived in pristine condition, ready for use.

title: Well packed, arrived in good condition
text: I’ll get the obvious out of the way, I bought this card online during the worst of the pandemic, back when you couldn’t just go to the store and look at cards. It arrived well packed and in pristine condition. All I could have asked for.

title: Great upgrade for Jotters
text: I got these to replace the standard ball point cartridges in my Jotters. It’s a significant upgrade. The ink flows very smooth and dries quickly. Similar to the performance of that very famous Japanese pen that sells like crazy at the office supply stores. But, in a much nicer pen body.

title: Does the job and easy to clean
text: These transfer ink without being too messy and they clean up well enough. Would have liked a metal tip, but these will get the job done.

title: Sturdy well made easy to use
text: Traditional document creating tools like this are getting very hard to find. Fortunately this one is up to traditional standards. It is thick enough to hold up to use but still clear and easy to see through. The markings are crisp and well defined. A little frustrating to pay this much when these tools used to be $5 or less, but times change. This appears to be the same tool these folks have made for decades, and that’s a good thing. Yes, recommended.

title: Very well made, holds up well
text: We just bought another set of these after having some for three years now. We put them out for the major flag holidays and leave them up for a few days at a time. So our flags have probably been out a dozen times for a total of about 40 days. Weather here in South Florida can be brutal during the summer, with intense sun followed by powerful thunderstorms and high winds. Our flags still look pretty much the same as when we first unpacked them. Definitely recommended.

title: Converting to blue, this pack makes it easy and inexpensive
text: I keep Jotters everywhere I might need a pen. I can buy the Jotters in four packs, but they come with black ink and I prefer blue. This value pack of blue cartridges is the perfect solution.

title: Great set of Jotters, real value
text: If you like Jotters, this is a great set, great value for four Jotters. I have these scattered all over, next to phones, on the nightstand, by my computer. Great to have enough to put one everywhere without spending an arm and a leg.

title: Great for grading
text: My niece is a school teacher and she loves her Parker Jotter. I got her these for grading and she tells me they’re just great. I too use a Parker Jotter and have one of these for marking up documents. Find them to be well made and reliable.

title: First quality paper for fountain pens
text: If you’re a fountain pen user, you need to buy this paper. Rhodia quality is very well known and their reputation is well deserved. I get well defined strokes without feathering or bleed through. Outstanding paper.

title: Fits perfectly and works as advertised
text: I own a construction business and have to visit job sites all the time. This inset enables me to use my Cross pens anywhere, anytime. These space pen cartridges really do write on anything. Great upgrade for my Cross pen.

title: Rhodia quality, great for fountain pens
text: If you use fountain pens, you need this paper. Excellent quality. No bleed through or feathering issues. Strokes appear sharp and well defined. This is also good with particularly wet writing gel pens. But really, this is fountain pen paper from the jump and it shows.

title: Very good pad holder for your Rhodia pads
text: I really like this pad holder and almost gave it five stars. However, the pen loop is too small. My Parker Jotter just barely fit into the loop. I don’t have a single fountain pen that would fit into the loop. Considering the whole point of buying Rhodia paper in the first place is to have fountain pen friendly paper, this is more than just slightly annoying. However, the holder does provide a secure fit for Rhodia top stapled pads and the material is of excellent quality. I do recommend this pad holder as one of the best I’ve seen for Rhodia pads.

title: Great assortment
text: If you have several Lamy fountain pens and like the convenience of cartridges, this is a great assortment. Also good value for the money.

title: The business friendly Metropolitan
text: Most of the Metropolitan pens have such loud shiny graphics, you’d never use one in a professional office. This Houndstooth version is the exception. It can be used in an office without issue. I gave it four stars instead of five because the Metros use proprietary cartridges and the converter it comes with is opaque rubber so you can’t see the ink supply. As a result, this pen is limited in terms of ink options and not as practical as some of the other pens in this price range. The nib is very good and the pen is well made. Most buyers will be happy with it, but you need to be aware of the limitations.

title: Very easy to keep clean
text: I got this for my Faber Castell Essentio. It fits well, nice and secure. The plunger seal is tight, very easy to clean without getting a lot of seepage into the screw chamber. I haven’t had any difficulty getting it to fill to 90-95% as some reviews have mentioned. However, I do cycle my converters multiple times when filling in order to get them as full as possible. I guess a little patience goes a long way. This product is recommended.

title: Perfect for fountain pens and wet writing gel pens
text: My niece got me a very nice leather notebook holder on Amazon for Christmas. The leather binder is a side-load type and is international A-5 size. I got this notebook to fit into the leather holder and it fits perfectly. As with all Clairefontaine paper, it is exceptionally good quality and works well with fountain pens. No feathering, no bleed through, it yields very crisp well defined strokes that dry quickly. Even better, since I use this for work, every page is micro-perforated for easy removal. However, the pages are quite secure if you intend to leave them in the notebook long-term. Highly recommended for people that use metric size paper and fountain pens.

title: High quality but limited starter fountain pen
text: The Metropolitan series pens from Pilot draw rave reviews, but living with them long-term exposes the limitations of this pen. Pros first then cons to follow. This pen is well made, has a nice smooth flowing nib, fits most hands, is durable, and comes with a converter (basic model) and a cartridge. For the street price of around $20 it’s hard to find a better starter pen. However, this pen uses only proprietary cartridges in limited colors, also the included converter is a rubber sleeve so you can’t monitor your ink supply. The cap snaps securely but has no seal, so the ink supply dries out quickly. The shiny metal body with loud graphics isn’t compatible with most professional environments (interesting that the home market Japanese version called Cocoon is more understated in design.) If you’re experimenting to see if you like fountain pens, this is a very good choice. But, if you know you already like fountain pens, get a Grip (seriously, get a Faber Castell Grip for $20 on Amazon) as it has an even better nib and uses international ink cartridges. Yes, this pen is recommended, but you need to be the right customer and understand this isn’t a long-term relationship.

title: Great gift set!
text: Iroshizuku inks are outstanding, with great colors, consistent flow and performance. The colors are rich and vivid from even extra fine nib pens. The inks are a bit on the wet side and may cause some feathering and bleed issues on low quality paper if you’re using a fairly broad nib like a western size medium or larger nib. This set is a great introduction to Iroshizuku inks, and I’ve bought these twice as gifts for people starting out with fountain pens. The Yama Budo in particular is a very cool color, a rich burgundy red that is such a deep shade of red that it in no way resembles the shiny red we associate with grading papers. It’s great for personal letters. This product is highly recommended.

title: Great nib, solid writer
text: Faber Castell pens are known for their outstanding nibs. This Loom is no exception, very smooth writer with consistent ink flow. The fine is pretty close to a Japanese fine in line width, but writes a little wetter, similar to most European nibs. In my opinion this gives the best features of both international standards and makes for a very enjoyable writing experience. The pen is fairly compact and the aluminum barrel is light and well balanced. The cap is a very tight fit, with a locking ring to hold it securely in place. Surprisingly, the cap doesn’t post well, the fit is loose and the cap tends to fall off easily. So this pen is clearly meant to be used unposted. The metal grip has concentric rings to aid in forming a secure hold, though the metal grip section is on the slick side. In this price range, there are very few pens as well made and even fewer that write as well as the Loom. One very nice feature of Faber Castell pens is that they take standard international cartridges, so there’s a lot of ink options available. The pen doesn’t come with a converter, but any standard size converter will fit. This pen is recommended.

title: Buy the Essentio instead
text: Faber Castell is discontinuing this pen. The replacement is very similar, and called the Essentio. The new pen is ever so much better. The nib on this pen is not as fine a writer as you’d expect. Also, the feed runs on the wet side. The result is a pen that writes fuzzy lines with too much feathering and bleed through on most paper. The pen is very heavy for its size, and the solid metal end finial makes it too tail heavy even with the cap unposted. Posted, the plastic cap doesn’t add much weight, but makes the pen ridiculously long. The pen looks good, but just isn’t up to par as a writing instrument. In contrast, the new Essentio pen that replaces the Basic in the Faber Castell lineup is perhaps the best fountain pen on the market for under $100. I have that pen as well and rate it 5 stars.

title: Fantastic ink! Great alternative to basic black & blue
text: This is a top of the line ink from Germany. It meets international standards for archival ink. The color is a rich brown with a bit of nutmeg red in it. On the page it goes down fairly wet but dries quickly without feathering or bleeding through. I’ve used it on both premium paper (Rhodia & Clairefontaine) as well as standard copy paper and even pulpy notepads. This ink is basically bulletproof. Yes, it costs a bit more than some brands, but those inks aren’t waterproof or archival like this is. For business use, this GVFC ink is a superior choice, and a nice departure from boring black & blue inks. One tip to pass on, after you ink up your pen, cap it, let it lay flat, and wait 24 hours. You’ll notice more saturation on the page. I think that because this is a fairly wet ink, it needs a day for some of the excess moisture to evaporate from the fins on the ink feed. At least it works that way here in humid South Florida. Your experience may differ. This ink is very highly recommended.

title: Caution! Not product described.
text: Be careful! This product isn’t what the description says. The product description say these are for Rollerball pens. No! These are the long version of the standard size fountain pen cartridges. Waterman’s Serenity Blue ink is wonderful, just about bulletproof reliable in every fountain pen I’ve used it in. But if you’re in need of rollerball refills look elsewhere on Amazon.

title: Great ink sampler, these are exceptional inks.
text: The Iroshizuku inks from Pilot seem to be almost universally excellent in quality and performance. I have tried seven of them and they have all been outstanding. Picking just the right color, especially common colors like blue can be a real challenge. There are so many subtle variations that can only be truly evaluated in person on your paper by your own eye. This sampler set enables you to try three of Pilot’s most popular blues without buying those big bottles. It’s a great choice for anyone, but I have found it’s even better as a gift. I’ve sent these to several people so they could experiment. Judging by the response, I’d highly recommend this set as a gift for a fountain pen newbie along with a good starter pen like the Pilot Metropolitan.

title: Good for fountain pens, good quality paper.
text: My experience with this paper has been very good. My fountain pens have worked well with this paper. I haven’t had any of the issues mentioned in some of the other reviews. I will say that I use fine and extra fine nibs most of the time and I select my inks based on their performance with most papers. The people who talk up the European and Japanese papers are correct in terms of quality, but those papers generally don’t come in standard American sizes. So if you need US sized paper like this Strathmore, there are very few options. Fortunately, this pad is readily available and gets the job done. It is nice for letters and memos. The colors show well on this paper and I haven’t had problems with feathering. The folks who’ve complained, well I’d say if you want to use wet writing pens and inks have the good sense to not use paper with a high cotton content. Don’t blame the paper for your poor choice. If you want premium letter paper in a handy pad format, this is a very good choice. Highly recommended.

title: Very good mid-level pen from Lamy, almost great
text: This pen is a dramatic step up from the Al-Star and Lx pens. I would have given it five stars, except the Lamy Studio is a little less expensive and is a better pen. That said, the Scala is a very nice pen. To begin with it just looks fantastic. The application of the beautiful color onto the aluminum metal body is very even and looks like a much more expensive pen. This is a very heavy pen. It appears to use chromed brass at both ends. Unposted, the balance is very good. Posted, it’s very tail heavy as the chrome end cap is quite heavy. The pocket clip is a little wiggly. The nib is the same one you find on the Safari and those are known to have some consistency issues. I’d expect an upgrade at this price point, but it’s the standard nib. The converter is a different model and was supposed to come with the pen but mine didn’t. Amazon did take care of me on that score, so not really a problem. The chrome grip section can be a fingerprint magnet, but wipes clean easily. In use, the pen feels great and fits in well in my office environment. If you really are a Lamy fan and keep an eye on the prices, this pen is a very good option.

title: Great ink, very reliable, superb color
text: I have thoroughly enjoyed using this ink in many different pens from several manufacturers. It feeds reliably, is smooth, doesn’t have feathering issues, is never blotchy, dries quickly, makes clean sharp strokes on almost any paper. The color has drawn many compliments from others. Highly recommended.

title: Best option for Metropolitan series pens
text: This converter is ever so much better than the squeeze converter that comes with the Pilot Metropolitan. The clear reservoir allows you to monitor your ink supply. It’s easy to clean. The metal balls do keep the ink mixed. It fits snugly into the pen’s grip section. It holds about two weeks worth of ink in regular use. The five pack is great value if you have more than one Metro. Highly recommended.

title: Works well, stays firmly in place
text: The entry level Lamy pens are mostly used in general carry type situations. They get tossed about, which is usually not a great idea with fountain pens unless you enjoy cleaning up ink stains. The dedicated Lamy converters have a pair of mounting pins molded into them so they lock into the Lamy grip section. It’s a simple idea, but it works very well. Overall these converters are well made and work reliably.

title: Perfect for Safari, Vista, Al-Star & Lx series pens
text: This is the revised converter Lamy makes for the Safari, Vista, Al-Star & Lx series pens. It has the locking pins that fit into the slots molded in the grip section of these Lamy Pens. It makes for a very positive connection so the converter doesn’t come loose in the rough and tumble of general carry and use. Holds about 35-40% of the ink amount in a Lamy cartridge. Works well, cleans up easily. Recommended.

title: Ideal converter for Lamy Studio pens
text: Lamy has updated their converters recently. This converter is the correct model for the Studio, Scala, and other mid-level Lamy pens. The Lamy Safari, Vista, Al-Star, and Lx series pens use a converter with pins extending out from the sides that fit into a receiver slot in the grip section. The next level of Lamy pens don’t have those slots and the Z28 type converters won’t fit. You need this one for your Studio type. My experience has been that it fits well, not too loose even though it doesn’t have the locking pins. Holds about 35 to 40% of the ink as a Lamy cartridge. In general use I’d say you can expect to refill it from the bottle about twice a month.

title: Very good general use (everyday) fountain pen that travels well
text: The Procyon is a good step up from the Preppy/Prefounte/Plaisir series of pens from Platinum. This is a mid-level fountain pen with a good nib and quality construction. The slip & seal cap system actually works as advertised, keeping the nib and ink supply from drying out over extended periods of time. I find that it writes well without feathering even on poor quality paper. On good quality (fountain pen friendly) paper the lines are very clean with crisp well defined edges. The nib is definitely an upgrade from their entry level pens. I experienced very little feedback even when writing on copy paper and notepads. I have more than one Procyon, and find this Deep Sea Blue model is very businesslike in appearance. If you travel with a fountain pen, you know that leakage is an issue on planes. This pen works extremely well with Platinum’s proprietary Blue/Black ink cartridges which are far more travel friendly than a converter. The only warning I would give a buyer is that like most Platinum pens, this one takes about 24 hours for the ink feed to really saturate when you first ink it up after purchase or a thorough cleaning. It’s not an issue when changing cartridges, just when the feed has been completely emptied out. So, don’t rate the ink flow based on the first time you use it, wait a day to evaluate the pen. I gave this pen 5 stars and do recommend it for business and everyday use. I would rate other pens in this price range better for home use. Because of the excellent slip & seal tech and the good nib, this pen lives in my iPad bag and has been bulletproof reliable.

title: Excellent ink - one of the best standard blue inks available
text: Excellent standard blue for office/school/general use. This Lamy ink is very smooth, stable, doesn’t have feathering issues, dries quickly, and looks good. I have two higher end Lamy pens that I put these cartridges in. Considering how impractical it is to travel with a bottle of ink and a converter, these cartridges are a real go to option. Purchasing them in bulk like this from Amazon made for good value. Large cartridges provide ample ink for a good two weeks of normal daily usage. Highly recommended.

title: Nice color but too wet/runny on the page
text: I really wanted to love this ink. The color is great and as someone with lots of Lamy pens, being able to use their large-proprietary cartridges is important. However, I found that unlike the standard Lamy blue, this ink was too wet and runny on the page. It feathered on everything short of top of the line hard finished paper. Since the standard blue doesn’t react that way on normal office paper, I was genuinely surprised. So, if you’re only going to use this on very high quality paper, you’ll most likely enjoy this ink as the color is very vibrant. Otherwise, there are better options available. In keeping with Amazon policy, I won’t name other brands here, but Amazon does sell better Turquoise inks for this pen. You’ll have to get a converter, but the standard Lamy converter for this pen is quite good.

title: Beautiful color - great value
text: This ink is a beautiful color, very vibrant and well saturated. It has strong Cyan elements to it, but definitely fits in the Turquoise range. Writes smooth and even with a seemingly wet flow, but doesn’t have feathering issues. The ink dries quickly and remains stable. This isn’t a permanent ink, but I’ve had no issues with smearing or smudging in normal use. You get plenty of ink in the bottle, like all Noodler’s inks it comes filled to the brim so it’s a good value. I did find that it dried up fairly quickly in my pens, so you’ll need to monitor your ink supply if you put this in a pen that leaves the home/office. I consider this ink to be a very good choice and highly recommend it.

title: High performance ink - very adaptable
text: If you’ve heard about the tremendously reliable performance of Waterman’s Serenity Blue, you’ll know what to expect from this medium green ink. On paper, the ink is noticeably darker than what the onscreen images show. It has a hint of blue in it, but is not a teal. This is a true green, about midway between a forest green and a spring green. There is a little color variation depending on pressure and line variation. I mostly use this ink in a Japanese fountain pen with a fine nib (a Platinum Plaisir with the special cartridge adapter Platinum makes that enables international cartridges to be used in their pens). I have tried it in several different pens ranging in price from $20-$200 and it has been flawless in them all. Flow is even, good color saturation, dries quickly, and doesn’t feather even on copy paper. If you’re looking for something you can use in an office that differs from the bog standard blues and blacks, this ink is worthy of a try.

title: Interesting color scheme, quality but scratchy nib
text: The dark green body and gold accents work well together, making for a classy looking pen. Even though the pen is made of injection molded plastic, it doesn’t look cheap. The gold accents are subtle, not overdone. The pen takes any short size international cartridge. I put both Waterman and J. Herbin inks in this pen and got very good results. On low quality paper the EF nib doesn’t run too wet or feather, but it is decidedly scratchy with a lot of feedback. On high quality paper, the strokes are almost too fine, like a lot of the Japanese nibs. I prefer the Kaweco fine nib, but was looking for an everyday carry (EDC) fountain pen that wouldn’t feather on notes and copy paper. This pen does fulfill that role quite well so long as you are prepared for the strong feedback. I have experienced no feed issues, ink flow has been very consistent and even. This pen is recommended.

title: Interesting color - good ink - will feather
text: This is kind of a difficult review to write considering my overall experience with Noodler’s inks. The color on this ink is very interesting. You need to use a thicker nib (at least a euro size medium) in order to get the benefits of the dark overtones along the edge of the stroke. Unfortunately, even though this is part of Noodler’s semi-permanent collection I found it to be a little wet on the page. So it really is going to be paper dependent as to how well this ink performs for you. Bottom line is that this ink will feather on low quality paper. Use it on good quality paper with a fairly broad nib and you’ll get a beautiful stroke with a saturated red center and black edges.

title: Pages not removable
text: The product description is wrong, these pages are not perforated/removable. That’s the bad, and it is a serious consideration because it’s the reason I bought this notebook. Now the good. The notebook is very thin, easy to carry in almost any bag or purse. The paper is of very high quality and is certainly fountain pen friendly. The ruled lines are well spaced and there’re 22 lines for writing on each page. The cover is coated paper, like what you’d find on a milk carton, but even thinner. There’s two staples in the margin holding the pages in and the book together. Durability will be iffy if this notebook gets knocked around too much. A good project/task notebook or general notes type book. Provided you’ll be carrying it in something to protect the notebook.

title: Easy to grip, better size than std model
text: Parker built a better Jotter, with this XL version. I’ve been using Jotters for over 40 years. Always liked them, but also found them to be a little too thin. Over longer writing sessions, my hands would start to cramp up from squeezing that skinny pen body. Now that the XL is available, the Jotter feels like it always should have, much easier to grip. Still have to press a bit with ballpoint cartridges in it. I put a Parker gel cartridge in this pen and it gave me the best of both worlds. A good quality business like pen with smooth flowing ink that shows well on any paper. The pen is made entirely of metal and you can feel the quality. Highly recommended.

title: Nice gift starter pen
text: As a gift starter fountain pen, this Waterman pen is a good choice. It looks nicer than the competition at this price point <$20 and has a smooth nib. One good feature is that unlike most starter level pens, it uses standard international cartridges. I put a J. Herbin cartridge in mine and it writes very well. Waterman’s own Serenity Blue also performs well in this pen. Even though this is listed as a “fine” size nib, it writes more like a medium. Even with fast drying inks like the one’s mentioned above, it is almost too wet on inexpensive paper like note paper and legal pads. This is especially true if your writing is very small and tight. You’ll be okay, but must take care not to let the pen drag too much. On good quality paper the performance is excellent. For the price, it looks sharp, is well balanced, has a smooth consistent nib, and offers many ink choices. Doesn’t look or feel like a starter pen. Recommended.

title: Better than Std model
text: This special edition of the Kaweco Sport is a better choice than the standard black model. The chess board pattern does a nice job of breaking up the shiny plastic look of the normal Sport and it doesn’t show scratches as much either. Like all Kaweco Sports, this one has a very nice smooth steel nib, gold colored in this case. The gold colored trim, logo, and finial ornament all show very well against the black body. The fine sized nib has good ink flow, but doesn’t write too wet on low quality paper. On fountain pen friendly paper it makes a sharp clear stroke. I have this pen in both fine and extra fine. My experience is that the EF is a little too scratchy low quality paper and writes too fine on good paper. This version with the fine nib is recommended.

title: Very good all purpose pen
text: This Kaweco Sport is a very good everyday carry type pen. The Extra Fine nib is a bit on the scratchy side, but it lays down a fine enough line that you can use this pen on standard quality paper. I find even on pulp papers it doesn’t bleed or feather. The ink supply is even and the nib doesn’t skip. These Kaweco pens, being made of plastic, are prone to showing scratches. I find the chess pattern does a good job of hiding scratches and will keep the pen looking good longer. The gold trim really looks good with the black body. This pen would also be a good starter pen for someone new to fountain pens. I put J. Herbin inks in my Kaweco pens. I have a couple of them and the Herbin inks perform very well, it’s a good combination.

title: Great step up from Safari pen
text: The Lamy Al-Star is a great step up from the plastic Safari. I like the balance of the aluminum body and the more subtle appearance as well. The Safari is a great pen, and the ergonomic grip is amazingly comfortable. However, being all shiny plastic it just isn’t exactly office ready. It looks like what it is in Lamy’s native European market, a student’s starter pen. Enter the Al-Star, with its anodized aluminum shell. The more muted colors and more refined appearance are a much better fit for a work environment. This is a great next step up on your personal fountain pen journey. Highly recommended.

title: Great choice for business traveler
text: I love the Iroshizuku bottled inks from Pilot. However, a converter can be a problem on airplanes. Also, just try taking a bottle of ink through a TSA checkpoint! Covid won’t be with us forever, and taking a fountain pen on a business trip means using cartridges. Getting these 12 to a box is great. The Namiki blue is a good business standard blue, largely indistinguishable from Cross, Parker, Lamy, etc. It doesn’t feather on copy paper, dries quickly, flows evenly. Good option for your Pilot pens.

title: Great upgrade from Safari/Al-Star series
text: If you already have a Lamy Safari/Al-Star and are looking to upgrade, this is your pen. Even though it’ the same nib series, the Studio slightly outperforms the Safari/Al-Stars because the ink feed is superior. The strokes are a little finer and there’s less feathering on standard paper. On higher quality paper like Rhodia or Strathmore Cotton, it really shines. As for feel, the balance is great unposted, a little tail heavy posted. The larger diameter grip is easier on my large hands than the grips on the Safari/Al-Star. I’ve written for an hour straight without cramping using this pen. I’ve only used it with Lamy Blue cartridges thus far, no bottle inks. It has been flawless. Considering this can be had for the same price as the LX version of the Al-Star, do yourself a favor and buy the Studio. Very highly recommended.

title: Great ink! Get’s lots of compliments.
text: I use this in one of my Pilot Metropolitan pens. It is smooth, it dries quickly, it doesn’t have feathering issues, and the color is gorgeous. I actually get compliments from people, asking about the ink because they like the color so much. Highly recommended.

title: Stick with the Metro and save $
text: The Cocoon is the Japanese home market version of the Metropolitan. It has a body color band at the separation point instead of the more colorful graphics on the US version. The Cocoon also comes without a converter. So... you pay more money for the same pen and no converter. All the talk about the nib is smoother on the Cocoon is just so much propaganda. It’s the same nib, it’s the same pen. I have three Metros and this Cocoon. They all write the same. I bought this because I wanted to avoid the cheesy graphic, it didn’t fit in my professional environment. But that was a silly waste of money on my part. Do yourself a favor, buy the Metropolitan. As for the pen itself, just like all the Metros, it’s a great pen. I have purchased several more and given them as gifts.

title: Big upgrade for your Jotter
text: These gel refills provide the best of both worlds. You get the ink performance of the best Japanese gel pens in the higher quality pen bodies made by Parker. Just like the rest of the world, I love Energels, but they don't look good in the professional/executive environment I work in. I use a Parker Jotter XL as a goto pen and these gel cartridges are outstanding. As an aside, I'm also a fountain pen user, but they don't always travel well. This gel ink performs very well and is a lot more convenient. Highly recommended.

title: Very high performance ink
text: Tired of feathering on standard quality paper? Want a business friendly color that isn't the standard black or blue? This is the ink for you! I have used this Noodler's ink in several different brands of pens and multiple nib sizes. The results have been remarkably good. Waterman Serenity Blue is known to be almost bullet-proof in terms of compatibility with most fountain pens. When I A/B them in my pens, the Air Corp Blue is very close in almost every way. The Air Corps Blue is more water resistant than the Waterman and it is an unusual color. The amount of ink you get for the price is also very favorable. Take it from an experienced fountain pen user/hobbyist, this ink is highly recommended.

title: Black EF writes finer than silver EF
text: I was surprised to find that there is a performance difference between the Lamy silver EF nib and the black EF nib. One would think they're the same other than color. However, there is a clear difference in the way they write. The silver EF nib writes wetter and feathers more than the black EF. Also, though both are on the scratchy side, the black nib is smoother on low quality paper. They both perform well on high quality paper, but the black writes a finer stroke than the silver. I have several Lamy pens and a supply of extra nibs in both fine and extra fine in both colors. The results stated above have proven out over multiple nibs of both colors. The decider for me was when I changed out the nib on my Studio. Switching from a silver EF to a black EF produced superior results with both Lamy Blue and Noodler's Air Corps Blue (a very high performance ink). I also noticed that the silver EF nib was slightly longer than the black EF nib. I think this may be the reason the silver writes a little wetter. Seeing these results on the Studio was telling, because the ink feed on the Studio runs a little drier than the Safari/Al-Star series. So if your interest is to get as fine a line as possible to reduce feathering and be able to use more absorbent general use type papers, buying the black replacement nib is worth the extra money. FYI, based on my testing, I agree with the other reviewers here that there is little discernible difference between the Lamy fine and extra fine nibs in the silver color. However, I did see a visible difference with the black. Probably because of the coating system used to produce the black coloring of the nibs. In terms of comparison to other pens in this range, the black EF isn't quite as fine or scratchy as the Kaweco EF, but it does slightly outperform the .03 size steel nib from Platinum. It is about equivalent to the Pilot medium nib. I would also say it is roughly equivalent to the fine nib in the Platinum Procyon. However, the build quality of the Lamy is superior to all of the above. So my advice is to buy a mid-scale Lamy like the Studio at the best price you can find on Amazon, regardless of nib, and then buy this black EF nib for it. You'll come out money ahead and have a great pen.

title: Great for home office
text: Good Value, works well in my home office.  Would recommend

title: Great for very fine lines
text:
So far good wet erase pens. They work well on my blank yearly calendar that I use to track when the monthly obligations / income / scheduling happens. Dry erase are fine in certain applications but if you need to go back and add something what I've found is that my hand would smudge the dry erase. The only way that I could smudge the wet erase is if I have wet hands or if there is sweat.

Haven't had them long enough to tell about length of use. Clean up is a breeze, damp cloth, quick wipe and your done.

Would recommend.

title: Works well
text: Easy to assemble. Read the instructions. works well for me. Would recommend.

title: Not exactly what I thought
text:
Like usual, Diamine inks flow very well. I may have to try this ink in a fountain pen that has a much broader nib than a broad. The ink color is interesting. I have tested on plain copy paper and fountain pen friendly paper from Vietnam. I haven't tried it on Rhodia paper. The ink seems to fade into a shade that is reminiscent of pencil lead but on areas where I paused a bit longer is darker.

I do like the ink. Recommend.

title: She liked it
text: Ex seemed to like the item.

title: Good replacements
text:
Please verify the converter your replacing. I didn't and then they hung around for a while until some other fountain pens came in and then those fit my new pens.

Definitely recommend

title: Great for smaller laptops.
text:
Overall a decent unit. Works well for smaller laptops but it's not deep enough (front to back) to have a larger laptop completely supported on the bottom. Side to side is still good. The padding on the bottom of the lap desk is good but the distribution of what feels like Styrofoam beads is a bit off for me. When I am using it, with my thighs parallel to the floor, it leans away from me so the top of the lap desk isn't flat. If I put my feet on a block that's about 6 inches high then the top of the desk is level. I could turn the desk around but then the wrist padding is also reversed.

The addition of the handle is a nice touch.

Could be a outstanding unit if small adjustments from the manufacturer were done. Honestly, I'm torn. there are many good points, but some not so good points. If your a person that is willing to purchase and modify it, then it could work well.

title: So far so good
text: Good value. Great that it's magnetic.  Got this for proctored tests where they don't allow paper.

title: Good business card holder for my biz
text: Its a good purchase. To stay organized

title: Had to buy multiple sets to make complete words
text: 5hey did not stick to my vendors tent, so i used as stencil instead to paint & bling the outline of the letters

title: Good purchase
text: Great use for my Biz for making wallets and clutches

title: Nice
text: Wonderful stub nib for inexpensive.  Get a con-40 or a con-50 converter to go with it.

title: Decent Black
text: Decent black for writing.  Not bulletproof but for the money a good solid ink.

title: Lighter shade of red
text:
I thought that I would try this Waterman Red since I do like their blue and black. This red isn't super saturated which gives it a translucent effect on paper. I didn't test this on fountain pen friendly paper. Did use it on copy paper as work though.
Works well as more of a high lighter style use than for a writing ink.

title: Good buy
text: I should have started with this book.

title: Wicked!!
text: A fountain pen that works like a ballpoint?  Sweet!!! Use with drier inks since it does run on the wet side.

title: Light
text: Very light ink, do not use on less than fountain pen friendly white paper.  Also use a very wet pen. Other than that the ink is very well behaved.

title: A YES
text: College Daughter.

title: Solid middle
text:
Monteverde did a good job with the formulation of this ink. It actually has a good ruby color. To get more pop of the color the usual applies of fountain pen friendly paper, clean pen, etc. Solid middle of the spectrum in regards to wet/dry. Well behaved in all the pens I tried it in. Personally my preference is towards the darker reds and while this is a good color overall it's still a touch to translucent when dry. If that makes any sense.
Overall good ink.

title: Darker oxblood than other brands :-)
text:
Took a shot with this ink. I do have other brands of ink that have the same name and I thought that perhpas this would be a different shade. I was right. This ink is a darker red with a tinge of brown so it more aptly fits the name of oxblood. The usual applies, clean fountain pen, fountain pen friendly paper for best results. Drying time is fairly quick but not quick enough if your a lefty. Well behaved in the pens that I have tried it in. Does feather some on common 20lb copy paper usually found in offices. That said, it is dark enough that you might get away with using it as a way to add emphasis on something without being to.. flamboyant. If you catch my drift.
Fairly wet ink which works well with the dry Asian pens that I usually use for a daily carry.
If only they had a larger bottle.. Maybe one day.
Overall is a good ink.

title: Works
text: Direct fit which is nice.  Genuine Canon product so no worries about compatibility.  Still stinking expensive though.  It's not as bad as other printers but still pricey.

title: Decent ink
text: Diamine. Well behaved. Not a bad color. Feathers on common copy paper which is to be expected. The color.. To really pop it needs a lot of ink on the paper and then drying time is increased.

title: Good Value
text:
I am into fountain pens. There are times that I gift a beginner pen to someone. Can't really gift them a pen without ink so that is what I got them for. There are fountain pens available that take a proprietary ink cartridge but those usually are not a beginner pen anyway. Value is great, presentation.. well it's just like it looks like in the picture (smile)
The down side is that there are some of the cartridges that seem to have a thicker plug and they are much harder to install properly in the pen.
