Ink color is a solid black. Nothing to be excited about. Feathers minimally on common copy paper. But these work well on getting a newbie exposed to the world of fountain pens.

title: Not bad
text: Nice vibrant color of blue.  I bought this on the recommendation of someone else in the fountain pen world.  Have to say that it's a solid performer overall.  Tends to feather on non-fountain pen friendly paper and has a bit of a dry start but once flowing works well even in an fountain pen made in Asia.  Nice touch with the bottles where you can set them at basically a 45 degree angle to help with the re-filling of a fountain pen.  Would recommend most definitely.

title: Not bad, not bad at all!
text: Decent it overall.  Especially when you look at the cost per millimeter.  Not water resistant.  Does feather on non-fountain pen friendly paper. For me I found that using this ink in a wetter fountain pen worked better.  Good black color, no sheen but sometimes a bit of shine.  BE CAREFUL when you open the bottle.  Can spill.  If I knew it before hand I may have scored it with a x-acto knife.  Will need to have other bottles to pour into.

title: Amazing ink for the price..
text: First time using Parker ink.  Nice deep black, works well on fountain pen friendly paper.  Feathers some on non-fountain pen friendly paper. Wicked nice price.  Does have some lubricating properties which changes the feel of the pen as you write.  Have no idea of water fastness when dry as I haven't tested that yet nor have I looked up the properties of the ink on the manufactures website.  Over all good ink.

title: Close.. Oh so close
text: Diamine is good ink overall, usually well behaved, decent drying times, nice selection of colors.  Maybe this is someone else's red that they have been looking for but darn it, it's not mine.  Some color variation on fountain pen friendly paper, and a tiny bit of sheen.  The bottle I got isn't as bright as the ink swatch would lead you to believe.  It's a straight up red.  Just didn't push my button.. you know?

title: Interesting color
text: Very interesting color.  Like usual, Daimine is a well behaved ink even in the fountain pens from Asia which usually runs small on writing surface of the nib compared to the rest of the worlds pen makers. Some feathering on non fountain pen friendly paper, would not work for staid business use. Back to the color, it's like a smoky violet.  Really no color variation and no sheen that I could detect. Fairly quick drying.  One thing I did notice is that if you have a very wet writing pen, one that slings a lot of ink.. you might be able to pass this off as a black but doing that the shadow / bleed through is pretty severe. Overall, not a bad ink.  Worth a shot for the money.  If perhaps you have a fountain pen person in your life, could work as part of a larger gift basket thing.

title: Not bad
text: This is definitely sturdier than many expandable files I have used in the past.  The materials are pretty stiff on the outset, so do not be surprised if you may have to spread it to add files / folders and it wants to return to it's compressed state which makes pulling files / folders out a little tougher.  I'm basing the durability on the thickness of the materials.  Overall, I've seen much worse for more money.

title: Add more backing
text:
Cork board, usually used for sticking notes or important info on with thumb tacks. This does do this but from the construction, this is not meant to be used regular like. Put some notes and leave them because the backing for the cork is flexible. Another thing is use as short of thumb tacks as possible. I used some longer ones and I could feel when they punched through the cardboard backing while the cork is moving away from the thumb tack. This could be ok for someone to put notes on it and leave it for a long while but attempting to use it other wise.. I would not suggest that.
In the spirit of transparency, I received this for free in exchange for my unbiased opinion of it.

title: Good option
text: Really good replacement for file folders offered other places and if you happen to have someone that is a visual person, it's nice to be able to group things by color. While they aren't the most heavy weight I've ever used, they are not the lightest either so I estimate that with use probably get 3 years or better out of them.

title: Really like this color
text: This is a very good color.  Nice dark blue/black with hints of red.  Could pull it off in the office and with the hints of differing colors.. Also gives you a nice pop of color that isn't really expected.  In typical Diamine fashion, well behaved, not to wet or dry, I wish that the cost per fill was a little lower but unless your like me and write long hand letters this color of ink could work out.  On common non-fountain pen friendly paper, has a little more feathering than other Diamine inks but on frountain pen friendly paper.. Oh it's nice.  Fairly quick drying, but remember this is NOT a water resistant ink.  Overall good stuff, recommend.

title: Might work for a highlighter ink.
text: I thought that I would like this ink.  I mean, it is from Diamine, which the ink does behave well in the pens that I tried it in.  Minimal feathering on non fountain pen friendly paper,  Perhaps on a non white paper the color would pop more, or maybe it's my eyes.. I don't know honestly.  But for me, the color was light enough that I was having a hard time picking it up on white paper.

title: Small business folks, y'all need to take a look at this.
text: These are a fabulous idea!  I mean, using vertical space for files?  For the monthly / weekly paper work totally killer.  Not so much I figure for long term paperwork storage.  It's nice because you can see much more of the folders than a typical filling cabinet which is great because then you can add more description to the folder.  The included over the door hooks is a nice addition and with the grommets, I could see being attached to a wall as a semi- to permanent installation.  They are made from a good heavy canvas and the seams look good.  Because canvas is a fabric you will get some motion and I am sure that over time there will be some sagging.  Overall, wicked cool idea, doesn't take up floor space, door still opens fully.  Definitely take a look at these.  And they are a two pack?!?!

title: Nice bright blue!
text:
There had been some bad press a while back about Private Reserve inks. However, every single one of their inks I have not had any issues with what so ever! Very nice bright blue, would work well in a business setting but still give you a little punch to make you writing stand out. Well behaved ink in all the pens that I tried it in. Works great in the pens that seem to run on the dry side, but when you get a pen that writes wet.. there are at times to much ink going on the paper. I would like to add that Private Reserve now has a web site with color swatches and a list of ink properties per ink which does help in the decision making tree. Additionally, for those folks who like to support small businesses.. Private Reserve is that.
Overall, good ink!

title: Another Black..
text: Diamine is well behaved ink overall.  As is Diamine usual, very nice color, worked well in all fountain pens that I have tried it in. Some feathering on the less expensive, not fountain pen friendly papers but does well on fountain pen friendly paper.  Fairly quick drying overall.  Nice ink.  Maybe not be fast enough drying if your a lefty.

title: Good for a temporary solution.
text:
48 spaces is pretty good but watch for clearance between your pens. It's genuine hyde of the naga, which means it's easy to dust, What I have done is placed it on a book shelf and utilize it that way for fountain pen control.
I really don't know if this would work for traveling purposes. It .. it's on the flimsy side and dang it if I got loaded with pens in a suitcase... I'm kinda doubting its "umph" you know?
For the money.. eh it's ok. I'm not saying it's "bad" it's just not what I thought it would be.

title: Whoa Nelly!
text:
This is a very interesting color! Depending on the paper / lighting it can appear neon reddish/pink. Works great as a underlining ink. Seriously, you cannot miss it! But.. for me anyway on white paper, It is just to much on the eyes if there is a large amount of it, say like in a letter to a family member. I plan on trying it on a non-bleached paper (brown) and see what the results are. I am also thinking that reducing it with water and using it in a brush pen as highlighter.

Fairly well behaved in the pens I have tried it in. Occasionally in less expensive pens it shows a dry start. Not often mind you but enough to be aware, you know?

title: Interesting shade..
text:
If you have read my other reviews of Noodlers, you already know that on non-fountain pen friendly paper there is some feathering, however Bad Green Gator isn't as bad as some of the other colors. Would not recommend for business correspondence unless you have some really cool peeps your working with. Nice shade of green and it appears to be a true green rather than a green-black, or a green-red or whatever. Has a nice punch of color without being overwhelming so works very good for personal letters.
Price per fill is where in my opinion Noodlers has an edge over some of the other inks.
Fairly well behaved in the pens I have tried it in. Like any ink, good pen hygiene is a must. Would not recommend going for long periods of time with a pen inked with this that is not being used.
Overall would recommend.

title: Good stuff here
text:
Maybe I am biased, but this mileage log book has some very good things going for it. First off is the size. Yes it takes up more space in the glove box but that is a small price to pay for the size of where you write your business travel details! I admit that I am one of those "large writing" people. I had tried a different brand of log book and the spaces were so small that I was always writing into the space above or below. Accountant no likee. Enough separate entry areas for a full year, plus some. 400 actually. Obviously, if you have multiple business trips per day on a vehicle then you may want to look for a different solution in tracking business miles.
Paper is of decent quality. So far it has been good on gel, ball point and fountain pen inks and being spiral bound helps with having the pages actually lay flat for when you write.
I was so impressed with the first one, I got another one for future use.

title: Where to start?
text: I liked the size of the overall booklet but the paper that the inner pages are made out of is weird.  I am into fountain pens, and as part of that, you learn about paper and ink and such. When every single ball point pen I have tried on this, skips. Everything from a dollar store stick pen all the way to high end needle tipped roller balls? Then add in the size of the boxes to write things in is on the very small side, and the worst part is that the lines on the paper do not line up from one side to the other side. Very hard to use, very confusing when things don't line up.  I don't know if perhaps I received a pack that got missed for QC or what.  Will not be reordering.

title: Nice, mellow, soft, black.
text: This is a black that is soft and mellow.  Very nice color over all.  Would work well for personal correspondence since it is in the hue range that isn't jarring to the eye.  Recommend

title: Sweet blue
text: Perfect stealth ink for business use.  It's blue which is acceptable business wise but it has a little twist in how vibrant the color is.  Good amount of ink for the price.  Well behaved in the fountain pens I have tried it in.  Personal preference here but larger nibs give a wider line which gives you more punch in the color.  Recommend!

title: Nice green!
text: This color is a nice middle of the hue spectrum of green.  It's not a green/black, it's not a blinding neon green, it's just green.  Of course there will be feathering and bleed through on non - fountain pen friendly papers but recent bottles of Noodlers ink does keep that at a minimum.  Good color for hand written correspondence. No way for business use. recommend

title: Love or Hate can't ignore Noodlers
text: Noodlers is a well behaved ink overall.  Of course there will be feathering and bleed through on non - fountain pen friendly papers but recent bottles of Noodlers ink does keep that at a minimum.  This color is a nice maroon that isn't to to red.  Would be great for a full personal letter but wouldn't recommend it for business use unless for perhaps strike - through or bullet points. Worked well in all my pens that I have tried it in.  Good value overall.  Recommend!

title: Diamine, what's not to like?
text: Diamine is a well behaved ink overall.  Of course there will be feathering and bleed through on non - fountain pen friendly papers but Diamine does keep that at a minimum.  This color is very pumpkin.  Would be a bit much for a full letter but for underlining or strike-through it does really well. And since it's not your typical red hue, it's very eye catching.  I would recommend Diamine in general for modern fountain pen usage.

title: Amazing Quality
text: Pilot, very good brand in the fountain pen world.  The fit and finish on this is amazing compared to the price.  You may want to add a twist style converter a CON-40 or a CON-50 which for me is handier than the squeeze style converter that come with the pen.

title: This is not a "prime" delivery
text: Not a bad fountain pen overall.  Direct from China so be aware.  Very light which is good for gifting to someone with some fountain pen experience.

title: Very bright
text: Diamine ink.  A well behaved ink in the fountain pens that I have used it in.  I found that the punch of color was better when I was using a larger sized nib.  Very bright almost neon orange/red.  Works really well for strike through editing / underlining/ checking off a list.  Does not pick up well if your attempting to copy the document.  But the search for the "right" color ink is something that drives us fountain pen aficionados. I use it as a means to check things off a list.  Can not miss that color. Would recommend as a well behaved ink.

title: Noodlers...
text: Price per milliliter is crazy low.  One of the best values in fountain pen inks right now.  Typical stuff with any ink, fountain pen hygiene is important, feathers on non-fountain pen friendly papers, for me larger nib = larger line size = larger punch of color.  Nice black but darn it, just not the black that I was looking for.  For the $ per milliliter so low and the color, would recommend.

title: Dark brown almost dark chocolate
text:
Diamine ink. A well behaved ink in the fountain pens that I have used it in. I found that the punch of color was better when I was using a larger sized nib.

Just in case someone is looking at this for a gift for a fountain pen person in their life : Quick recap of the 3 things that go into having a wonderful experience with fountain pens. 1st is the ink. Does the ink flow nicely? Good color? Is it saturated ink or a particulate ink? Match the ink to the pen basically. 2cd. The pen, nib and feed are so important, does it write wet? Dry? That info will help determine some of the properties of the ink. 3rd. Paper. When it comes to fountain pen ink and it's physical properties the paper needs to have certain physical properties as well beyond just the weight of paper. Generally speaking the majority of modern inks will "feather" on non-fountain pen friendly paper E.G. copy paper, legal pads, etc. If you really want to knock the fountain pen aficionado in your life socks off, go ahead do the research, get some fountain pen friendly paper along with a selection of different fountain pen inks. You will be much appreciated by them. And every time they use that paper, or the ink, they will remember who gifted it to them.

Sorry about the aside, back to the Macassar Diamine ink. Nice color, like other inks larger nib size = larger punch of color. Warm dark chocolate, with hints of brown. Good all round ink. Just not what I was looking for as far as a deep rich warm black. Anything by Diamine is overall decent ink. Recommend.

title: Very nice color
text: Diamine ink.  A well behaved ink in the fountain pens that I have used it in.  I found that the punch of color was better when I was using a larger sized nib.  Very nice dark color with hints of blue green .  I do use it but other fountain pen folks will get it when I say "Close but not what I was looking for"  Like the grail fountain pens, finding that 1 color of ink that you are searching for is something that drives us fountain pen aficionados. Would recommend as a well behaved ink.

title: A very nice red with hints of brown
text: Diamine ink.  A well behaved ink in the fountain pens that I have used it in.  I found that the punch of color was better when I was using a larger sized nib.  Very nice red with hints of brown.  I do use it but other fountain pen folks will get it when I say "Close but not the red I was looking for"  Like the grail fountain pens, finding that 1 color of ink that you are searching for is something that drives us fountain pen aficionados. Would recommend as a well behaved ink.

title: Well behaved
text: I get it, I do, there is a lot of stuff that floats around concerning the owner of Noodlers ink but this is a decent ink.  Well behaved in most pens that I tried it in.  Good color, not a sheening ink, but does throw down a nice line on fountain pen friendly paper.  Typical of fountain pen inks, on not so fountain pen friendly paper there is some feathering.  When you look at cost per oz or milliliter actually, it's a fair deal.  Plus if your like me, I have enough to provide samples to others.

title: Diamine.. Solid quality ink
text: Diamine does good ink.  Well behaved on fpuntain pen friendly paper.  Works better with wider nibs to really get the effect of the color.

title: Nice red, not bright but not blood, but close
text:
Diamine. Well behaved inks generally speaking. Red Dragon is a nice deep red with hints of brown. Has a wee bit of sheen on fountain pen friendly paper when dry, but it's not a sheen monster like some of the inks from Organic Studio. Flows well in all the pens I have tried it in. Everything from a EF Asian to a B European, the down sides are the size of the opening in the bottle. Bigger nibs / pens are a wee bit tricky to fill sometimes, and I was hoping the this red would have been the red that I have been looking for. I must say that the difference between the color swatches seen on the computer screen to IRL is very marked. On the screen the swatches (I compared different images from several different sources) appeared to be that fresh hemoglobin that was just starting to oxidize, but it's more brownish than that.

Alas, my search for the red I seek continues. However, I would recommend this ink. Just remember to follow proper fountain pen hygiene with all your pens.
Wouldn't use this for business correspondence but for everything else.. You betcha!

title: Decent for the $
text: Lamy, good pens, work well but take proprietary converters.  The Broad nib is great as it lays down a nice big line of ink with writing.  I don't know why, but Lamy changed their warranty on this pen.  It used to be a life time but on this one, it's reduced to 2 years.  Overall a decent fountain pen, don't forget to order a converter with it though since it doesn't come with one.

title: Something to add to the rotation
text: Really good saturated ink. Well behaved, some feathering on non fountain pen friendly paper but that seems to be very common in my experience so far.  Does well on fountain pen friendly paper with reasonable drying time.  The interesting thing I found with this ink is that it increases the amount of tactile feedback I experience.  I inked a jinaho x750 with a #6, M nib, which is a fairly wet pen, and I was pleasantly surprised by the feel.  I will need to test this ink in some other pens to see if what I felt is a property of the ink or not.  Nice color with a visual of being so dark blue it appears black with shifting to a blue.  Not really a sheening ink. Over all, I would recommend.

title: Manhattan project ink
text: Nice black.  Semi water proof. Very super saturated so proper pen hygiene is a requirement. It's not a black black but a decent one nonetheless. According to Noodlers this is a recreation of an ink that was used in the facilities for the Manhattan project. Flows well.  Over all a decent ink.

title: Would be a great graduation gift.
text: Nice large pen with a good weight to it.  Needed a lil adjusting of nib when I received it.  Flows well but remember that the Asian medium nib will usually run smaller in size than a European or American nib.  Overall cannot complain regarding fit and finish.  It looks and behaves like a pen costing multiple times more.  It does come with a converter which is a nice touch.  The Jinhao international ink cartridges will fit no problem.  Perhaps a little over the top for business use but still a great looking pen.

title: A violet for a non-violet kind of guy
text: Usually not a fan of purple / violet inks but this one is so vivid even on non-fountain pen friendly paper that I am pleased that I bought it.  Like all Noodlers inks, it is super saturated so proper pen hygiene should be followed. That said, it seems to be a nice wet ink, flows well in my Lamy EF nib pen.  But it's not "bullet proof" as some of the modern inks are.  I haven't tested water proofness but for writing personal correspondence it works really well.  Typical of fountain pen ink on typical paper there is some feathering of the ink but does well on fountain pen friendly paper.  It's also cool that it's a recreation of an actual ink used during World War 2.  I recommend.

title: It's good to have spares.
text: These will not fit every fountain pen out there.  But they do well in the asian ones I have tried them in.  Very handy to have spares on hand.  Didn't fit my Lamy Safari.

title: Good brand!
text: Jinhao.  I know, I know, there are fountain pen snobs that dismiss Jinhao's as junk but so far my experience has been positive overall.  The fit and finish are very good, the nibs on the x750 are the same size as what is in the 159's.  And you have to remember that the nibs on Asian brands runs smaller than their European or American counterparts. That said, this pen, has a really interesting color to it that while subtle does catch the eye of folks out in public.  It has performed well with all the inks I have used in it so far (6)  Everything from Noodlers to Diamine with some Pelikan thrown into the mix to just see.  Great value for the money.

title: Beautiful pen. Just amazing fit and finish for the ...
text:
I haven't inked this pen yet. Beautiful pen. Just amazing fit and finish for the price. The one I received has a fine nib, which for those of you who are just starting with fountain pens, the nib sizes (actual measurements of where the nib meets the paper) generally runs smaller in nibs that are of Asian origin. While nibs and pens of European or American in origin will generally run larger than their Asian counterparts. That being said, even among nibs that are marked the same from the same manufacturer, there will be variation. This is just one of those things. That's why there are times that a medium nib pen could write more of a fine line than a fine nib pen of the same manufacturer.

I am debating on whether or not to ink it or leave it just for the beauty of the pen in a display case.

title: Good color, still experimenting.
text:
Still experimenting with this ink. Works fantastic with a glass dip pen that has enough surface area to hold a fair amount of ink. I looked up the ink properties on their site and supposedly it's ok to use with a stainless steel nib pen, so I tried it in a Jinhao 992 F nib pen that I have had for a while. This pen usually does not have any issues with any of the other inks I have thrown at it. Obviously, the writing experience will change based off the physical properties of the ink you are using. In this pen, usually there is enough feedback that you know your writing but it's not feeling like it's dry. With this ink, it felt dry. I think I will try it in a medium and see, or perhaps go to a broad.

The color is striking. I wouldn't use it for business but for personal correspondence, it would be a good choice.

title: Good ink! Exceptionally Reasonable priced.
text: Very nice ink in a cartridge.  Works well and with the cost being so reasonable it completes the whole package of gifting a fountain pen.

title: Good Value!
text: Jinhao's.. A really good value and really good fit and finish.

title: Five Stars
text:
Jinhao is a good brand. They will surprise you with the fit and finish and performance.
Update: I have inked this beast of a pen and I am even more impressed with the fit and finish. This pen with Organic Studios Santiago Sea Blue is buttery smooth. I never thought that such a large pen would have such a fantastic experience of writing. I would highly recommend this model. Just remember it's a large pen!

title: No loose leaf here!
text: Fountain pen folks, This is a really nice for writing. I like it because there are times that I like to have a line to follow, and the sheets are perforated for easy removal. (if needed)  The only single thing.. The left margin seems to me to be larger than needed. It works well with all the inks I have which isn't a surprise considering its Clairefontaine. I understand that it's a speciality paper but there are sometimes that the $$ for it... sigh.  Overall I would recommend this product.

title: Pilot converter.. Good stuff
text: Nice converter!  I like that it has agitators included. It fit my metropolitan with no issues at all.  I wish it had a bit more volume for ink.

title: Fountain pen friendly.. Little thin
text: For all you fountain pen people these work out for a pocket sized, fountain pen ink friendly notebook.  Like most fp friendly papers, there is some shadowing in the back side of the sheets.  They have printed a ruler on the inside of the back cover and areas on the inside of the front cover for name address etc. Plus "project name, location" which is a nice touch.  I wish that there was more sheets per notebook.  By my count there is 24.  Which if your like me will go really fast.

title: Worth a look
text: Noodlers inks is a overall a good ink.  This one works for me in a larger nib size pen.  It has a nice color variation on better (fountain pen friendly) papers versus the less expensive copier/note pad papers.  The color variation happens based off the drying time of the ink on the paper and how much ink was put down by the pen.  Color varies from yellow to a dull goldish to a orange. For a non shimmering ink this does pretty good color change wise.  For the amount of ink and it's price... If your looking for something that lets you change things up I would suggest this.

title: Interesting color
text: Very cool color !  Usually when you mix a rose color with a black color you get variations of purple. Which you do have in this ink. However, to the eye the ink on paper will go from a rose-ish, to a purple, to near black depending on how much ink is being put to paper and how fast or slow the paper absorbs the ink. Obviously, low quality paper being used with this ink you will get feathering if your trying to get the darker end of the ink to show.  Wouldn't recommend this ink for archival purposes, but Noodlers already has that covered,  but for general writing this ink does well.  Currently the pen I have inked with this is a Jinhao 450 Medium nib. I cannot say that the pen "loves" the ink or vice versa but the pair are very well behaved even after using it as a pocket pen for several days.

title: Safe bet
text:
Bought to go with the Pilot fountain pens purchased for Xmas gifts. The cartridge style of inking a fountain pen works well for ease of use for a non fountain pen enthusiast. But I am hopeful that they will become one!
Nice color. Rather a "safe" color suitable for business use. No feathering on even really inexpensive papers. Fairly quick drying.

title: Its Noodlers! Great price per fluid ounce
text: Noodlers.. When it works its wonderful. This is a very decent ink. This is a very super saturated ink which is good for that shock of color on the page. Great color. A little feathering on common copy paper, but not much.  Would work well as a daily use but in my case I left the EF pen untouched for a week and I figure the ink dried in the nib/feed.  Got it going again after a quick dunk if the nib/feed. I do not know if the drying out was due to the pen or the ink.  Once I get it sorted will post update.

title: Good gift
text: Bought as Xmas gift. They have reported back that they really did like it. Do not have any direct experience

title: Good gift
text: Bought as Xmas gift. They have reported back that they really did like it. Do not have any direct experience.

title: Great color ink
text: Great ink! Great color. Nice price for the amount of ink you get. Be careful when opening the bottle, its filled to the very top.  Update: 1-23-2018  Very rich and saturated.  Even with not the best quality paper, very minimal feathering.  I am considering using this in a Asian EF nib because of how well the ink flows.  Let me explain, Asian EF nibs are smaller generally than a European EF nib and with such "slick" ink I want to see what will happen.

title: Decent pen, not really flexy
text: I like that the ink volume is huge! Feels nice in the hand, 4 stars because the flex nib seems stiffer than I had thought a flex nib would be.  However, its flexible enough to add expression and flair to my writing with the ink width being variable based on hand pressure and speed of writing.

title: Good ink
text: Really nice ink. My Lamy EF Safari loves it. No skipping, good color on the page. Will get more when I run out which will be a while since this is a large bottle of ink.

title: Fantastic color
text:
So far this is a really good ink. However, I've only inked one pen with it. Thats why the 4 star rating so far. The color is great! It takes a moment to dry on the page and while it looks like a very deep red while wet. As soon as the ink dries it goes to a dark copper color. I have a hunch that this ink will perform well in my other fountain pens.
As I try it in different pens I will update this review

title: Less mess than a converter
text: Spouse loves them.  She doesn't like using a ink converter to fill her fountain pens that she claimed from me.  The only issue really, is where to look for which color the cartridge is, since the package comes with 12 black and 12 Blue.  The ink colors are great. Nice and vibrant.

title: Good pen!
text: Great pen, writes well, with large bold line of ink.  Does not work well with a lubricating ink, needed to go to a "dry" water based ink.  Good feel in the hand, but for me still need to post the cap on the barrel for my hand size.  Please note this pen has weight to it which I personally like.  With lighter pens I sometimes feel like my writing gets jerky and worse than usual :-)  Converter does come with included agitator which was a surprise considering the price point of this pen.  I will perhaps update this review as I get more time with the pen.

title: Good fit
text: Very well constructed, piston seal is great, this is a twist style, just remember it's a left hand threaded twist.  Nice tight fit in my Lamy.  Have used it in my Lamy and used the Lamy as a daily pocket pen for some weeks now and I haven't noticed any leaks.  I would recommend this for folks with Lamy fountain pens.

title: Sketching in pen? Look here
text: The ink flows well and is a very nice black.  But it's not the inkiness of space black. It dries well even on inexpensive papers. The pen is a "dropper" style which is really cool since the pen I received has a clear plastic body which is nothing but a huge ink reservoir. It's really nice to have a clear visual on how much ink you have without needing to take the pen apart. It's a black ink, It has a very nice color and dries on the matte side of things. The bottle of ink is HUGE.. I am expecting to have this ink for several years before I'm needing to reorder. Cheap copy paper doesn't do any ink justice so if your using that as you test bed it skews your results because of the brighteners within the copy paper, the ink appears lighter in color than it actually is.  Same weight of paper, but without the brighteners(same brand of paper as well) the perceived hue is much closer to what you see in the bottle.  However, I used some 32lb, 25% cotton paper and the color is much better.  I would have given this set a 5 star but because of the bottle design, it's kind of a drag that without some syringe and needle work I can't use this ink in my other pens.

title: Very striking ink
text: Very blue ink, It has a very nice color and nice sheen.  Now this ink is not "bulletproof" so if your letter could get wet.. Maybe do not use this for that letter.  It's also what is considered a "dry" ink, which I take to mean that it dries quickly on the page without feathering . I have noticed that it's very paper dependant. Inexpensive 20lb copy paper doesn't do this ink justice.  Because of the brighteners within the copy paper, the ink appears lighter in color than it actually is.  Same weight of paper, but without the brighteners(same brand of paper as well) the percieved hue is much closer to what you see in the bottle.  However, I used some 32lb, 25% cotton paper and the color is just gorgeous.  If you are looking for a nice bright blue ink for your fountain pen I would seriously consider this ink.

title: Great Ink!
text: Noodlers inks.. While not "bulletproof" it's water proof.  It's a joy to use in my Lamy Safari fountain pen.  Depending on the paper you use, it stays in the range of a robins egg of blue hues.  I like it very much, the only little thing is that until it's fully dry, it will smudge.  which is a small price for such a nice flowing, very striking color of ink.  I have also learned that for the "opps" that happen from time to time, common ammonia is the solvent to use for clean up, and apparently, to flush your fountain pen, followed by a warm water and soap bath.

title: Folks with hand issues take a look
text: Extra light is a understatement.  By feel, this pen is about the same weight as a #2 wood pencil! Even with the extra fine nib, the ink flows very well, and even with it being a hooded nib (which usually means a stiffer nib in my experience.  Which I admit is not that massive)  there isn't any undue scratchiness. The ink bladder is very interesting to say the least.  However, once I figured out how to load it with ink. what a large reservoir for ink!  Just like the Jinhao, I gave it a good wash with soap and water, let it air dry and loaded it up with dark green pelikan 4001 ink.  Very good writing experience.  The pen body is short for my hands so I do need to have the cap posted for comfort.  Not for the weight issue but just because it's short and I like my writing instruments to be able to fully rest in the crook of my thumb. One other little thing, for me to fill the ink reservoir I needed to remove the metal casing from around it. Overall the Hero is a good pen, would be really good for those who like a very very light pen that writes well.  This pen has caused me to consider purchasing another Hero, hopefully in a longer body.

title: Quality beyond the cost
text:
Very good sub 10$ pen. I did some research and found out that a good wash with soap and water helps things tremendously. After I did that, I let everything dry and then loaded up some pelikan 4001 brilliant red ink and tried it out.
It did take a moment to get the ink flowing but once it did it could keep up with my fastest writing, I was able to change the width of the line with very little pressure so the nib is very responsive. However, the pen does have some weight to it and with the cap posted it could be a little top heavy for some people. The body is short for me. To have the feeling that it's in my hand properly I need to have the cap posted.
Gorgeous colors though. It looks like a fountain pen that cost many multiples than it actually costs. Overall I like the pen, it wrote very well for me even with the dry ink. I am planning on going with a "wet" ink sometime in the near future and seeing how it does with that. If there is a model Jinhao releases that is a bit longer in the body I will definitely purchase it.

title: Surprising
text:
First off.. A lifetime warranty? Second off its very very light so if heavy fountain pens aint your thing. I loaded Noodlers blue eternal and it writes wonderfully. The nib is very responsive to changes in pressure it lays down a line so nicely and with changing pressure and speed it is like having multiple nibs all in the same pen.

Will update as I use it and if there are any issues

title: Nice instrument for writing
text: Love the experience of writing with this pen. Way better than any ball point or felt tip writing implements that I have ever tried.  Heavier weight paper does help with the experience. Two small issues. 1 the body of the pen is a wee bit short for my paws. 2 had to clean the nib after running out of ink. Swapped ink cartridges but.. Still had to clean the nib which was simple. Soak in warm water,  don't know if thats common with fountain pens, or specific to this one. Thats why not a 5 star. Darn close.. But just short

title: not bad, not bad at all
text: Nice shredder. The 12 sheet capacity I think is a little much due to the way the motor lugs. Anything short of that it does very well.  If your looking for a decent shredder for household use this may fit the bill.

title: Very cool planning aid
text: Having this as a planning aid is great!  Kinda bummed that I needed water based markers but overall not a issue. It's a nice bonus that a marker is included. Being able to have things laid out for full year is  really nice.  Yes it takes some time to get everything written down but after the initial time spent then it's just a matter of like five minutes once a month for obligations to pay, etc.

title: Great pen!
text: I collect pens…lots of them. This $13ish pen writes superbly and I love it over more expensive pens. The nib is extremely smooth, ink flows well, and the fine nib allows me to write small. I have several pilot pens and I’ve never been  disappointed in the least.

title: Writes beautifully!
text: I have some cheap calligraphy pens and they are just that -- cheap! It's hard to find a nice calligraphy pen so I am glad I found this nib. I am a big Lamy fan, but didn't realize this nib worked on the Safaris (which I have too many of); I thought they were only for the Joy pens. Anyway, writes beautifully and I am very happy with my purchase.

title: Great little stamp!
text: I looked all over for a bicycle stamp and there aren't a lot to choose from (and none in the US). I chose this one and it's perfect! High quality and does a great job. Arrived much quicker than I expected too...took maybe 2 weeks, if that.

title: I like!
text: Great little templates for writing! This helps make my letters more uniform. Great for cards, envelopes, crafts, etc.

title: Great Nib and Great Quality!
text: This nib works great! I have had trouble with some Lamy pens and nibs purchased on amazon so I typically buy from gouletpens or jetpens, but I took my chances with this one. I was also hesitant because it's more common to have drag when the nibs are extra fine/fine than medium/bold ones. I am quite happy because I purchased it on amazon and I purchased an extra fine nib, and it works GREAT! Very, very pleased!

title: Love it!
text: Great pen for such a great price!! Ink flows consistently, writes smoothly, and then pen is pretty!!

title: Great!
text: Works great! I have a lot of Lamy pens and therefore a lot of these converters. They work quite well!!

title: Great pen!
text: Great pen!! Fits nicely in my hand and with the way the shape is designed, I can hold it snugly, easily controlling the pen. It is a very find tip which is great to write small or if your drawing fine detail. At first I thought it was a little scratchy, but it's really quite nice. When there's enough ink on the pen, that helps to eliminate the scratchy feel.  The pen is very pretty too!! Well made!!

title: Great!
text: Works great with my Pilot pens! Easy to use, easy to clean...I actually find it easier to clean than other brand converters because the opening is wide so ink washed out easily. The plastic is of very good quality.

title: Ok...
text: Very cool concept, having storage on top. I like to be organized and to file things, but my only complaint is the latch is very very flimsy and I foresee it breaking easily and soon. It came off the first time I opened the box, but I was able to put it back on for now.

title: Works great!
text: Works as it's supposed to...fabulously!!

title: Fabulous Pen at a Great Price!
text: I love the Lamy Safari pens! They work flawlessly (very smooth, ink doesn't skip). I am a pen snob and have some more expensive pens, but these are really great pens and compare to the more expensive pens. I have the fine and medium nib. The difference between the 2 is very subtle, but I do like the fine one a little better cause I prefer finer line with most of my pens. Finally, I'd like to try the extra fine...that's my next purchase.

title: The best!
text: I am a pen snob! I collect fountain pens and calligraphy pens and can spend all day at a specialty pen store trying and comparing their fine pens. I got a $5 AvantPro pen at Staples with this ink and it's MY FAVORITE PEN! It writes so smoothly, the ink never skips, the point is fine...I just love it.

title: Smooth at all angles and ink flows evenly.
text: This is a great pen.  The nib is smooth at all angles, the ink flows evenly.

title: A Little Powerhouse!

title: Pilot Metropolitan Retro Pop - great value and quality
text:
The Retro Pop, and all Pilot Metropolitan pens, are excellent for both beginners and long-time fountain pen users. Since it can't be purchased with the extra-fine (EF) nib I bought an inexpensive Pilot Penmanship with EF nib and swapped the nibs. I write quite small in my journal and work log. The EF has made a positive difference.

Pros: Relatively inexpensive. Attractive. Balanced. Crisp line on good paper. Smooth flow. Does not leak unless dropped. Easy to change nibs with other Pilot nibs. Cap fits well on the barrel when writing.
Cons: Cannot buy with extra-fine (EF) nib. Slick--somewhat easy to drop. The clip is fairly sturdy and tight but will not prevent the pen from falling from a shirt pocket when the shirt material is thin.

title: Lamy CP1 is outstanding
text:
I've had the CP1 a few weeks now. It writes a smooth, extra fine line (equivalent to the .38 mm Pilot G2 throw-aways I'd been using). I write ten-to-15 pages of small, single-spaced text per week. One fill of the very convenient converter (included) will last about two weeks. I'm using the black Noodler's Ink. There was some minor skipping on the second day, after leaving the cap off for a few hours, but twisting the converter to eliminate the air bubble easily restored the flow. I've not had the issue again (about two weeks).

The size, weight, and balance are just right for my hand. The entire pen is the right length to fit in a shirt pocket (no leaks). I've written in four different notebooks, on printer/copier paper, and in the margins of some of my books. There's been no blobbing, streaking, or bleed through. I'm entirely pleased with this pen and look forward to never having to buy another disposable.

I'm curios as to whether the CP1 will leak in an aircraft. The next time I fly, I will take it in a zip bag, just in case. If it doesn't leak at 36,000+ feet, I may have to declare it a nearly perfect pen.

title: It arrived today and this is the first fountain pen I've ever purchased that wrote beautifully out of the box without scratching
text:
I simply adore this pen! It arrived today and this is the first fountain pen I've ever purchased that wrote beautifully out of the box without scratching or needing adjustment. Here are the pros and cons as I see them:
Pros:
-The gorgeous trendy colors! I bought the purple and the the color is exactly what it looked like on the site.
-The body has a nice weight to it, without being heavy. I prefer the weight of the pen with the cap not posted, but I an still write easily with the cap post on the end. The body feels cool in my hand and the Pilot log is minimal and doesn't detract from the pen itself.
-The nib writes perfectly right out of the box and the slit in the feed and the air hole in the nib were perfectly aligned so there were no problems at all drawing ink for the first time. I bought a Lamy Safari on Amazon two weeks ago and I could never get it to draw for this reason and had to send it back. It is clear to me that Pilot took the time to do some quality assurance before packaging my pen.
-The case is great! I admit to sort of "babying" my pens and when I am not using an empty one, I like to store it in a case.
-The price is outrageous for such a great pen. I starting using fountain pens so I could enjoy the variety inks available and because of the sheer novelty of the instrument, but I also enjoy not putting another plastic pen in a landfill. I use Pilot's iroshizuku inks in my pens.

Con:
-I'm not sure this is a con because I haven't had any troubles yet, but I don't care of the squeeze fill/ink sack mechanism. I get the feeling that I'm not getting as full of an ink load with it as a cartridge or a converter. I'll eventually get the converter recommended here on the review section.
-Proprietary cartridges are a bit unnerving simply because I like to use the Waterman cartridges when I travel by air. I haven't use this cartridge yet, but it is a good size cartridge.
-The clip is bland for such a pretty pen.

On the balance, I'd recommend this pen to anyone who is interested in entering the fountain pen market or (like me) were eager to find an inexpensive desk pen for work that wouldn't be soul crushing to lose. I will probably get the teal colored pen eventually.

title: I was unexpectedly disappointed in this pen after having read so many positive ...
text: I was unexpectedly disappointed in this pen after having read so many positive customer reviews about Lamy pens.  I have several heavier fountain pens at home but I wanted something lighter and narrower for an every day pen at school.  I like the design of the pen, and especially the grip.  The lid fit nicely and the color was fun.  Unfortunately, the slit in the feed was so poorly aligned with the air hole in the nib that despite multiple adjustments, I simply wasn't able to draw more than a couple of drops in to the converter.  I'm completely accustomed to adjusting my own nibs since most pens scratch a bit more than I'd like.  When I tried to draw ink the first time, I got nothing but a dry converter.  After adjusting I was able to manage a few bubbly drops.  That's when I examined the alignment.  Had this pen been properly aligned, I would have kept it.  I'm so glad to hear that most of you have had better experiences.

I will add Unibene to my drawing pen arsenal which include Cross and Uniball. I bought the 6 black and 6 blue Parker style . I mixed an eyedropper of Brown 41 with same amount of General of the Armies and it seems to help the 41 flow but needs more testing..also it made for a strange slate gray /brownish /greenish color . if that makes any sense . The General is a nice color for writing and I like it for drawing. I have a vintage Esterbrook superfine nib and General works very well producing fine hair lines out of that nib. One must keep in mind that different inks have different flows or is it just viscosity? That with nib style and paper choice makes fountain pens a unique experience that can take some mastering.

The notes always appear in the note function. Tap on it and then select the particular notebook you want. You can title and group them. It navigates the web smoothly and easily displays your emails. You can even view YouTube videos reasonably well. I like to view videos in split screen mode and take notes. Only 4 stars just because it's not as user friendly as I would personally like, but I highly recommend it for its versatility. Definitely my goto e-reader/tablet now. Love it.
