text: Got these for games for my cousin's bridal shower - her colors were plum, black, and grey. It was nice to be able to order black pencils in bulk at a reasonable price. I'll reuse them at work and in my craft studio - the ones that people didn't leave with. They write nicely and look sharp (no pun intended)!

title: Great for garden planner gift
text: Got this to put inside a garden planner for a friend - to hold garden markers or seed packets, or writing utensils, etc. It was perfect for the gift, not sure if it's still working properly, but I assume so.

title: Love it!
text: Perfect for keeping my daily food log! Pocket to hold odds and ends in the back. Love the tan color.

title: Give yourself a little class.
text: Not a expert in fountain pens. Having said that, if your not a collector and just want a great fountain pen, these are fantastic. Come in a variety of styles and tips. I prefer the fine tip (nub) as medium seems to look a bit more like a marker. Leaves that wide appearance as opposed to the razor thin one left by a fine nub. Just personal preference. Ink refills are cheap. Certain things stand the test of time and really can make you feel like you’ve got some class. A nice hat, good watch, a money clip and a nice fountain pen are items you should wear everyday.

title: Five Stars
text: Original ink, expensive but it works every time

title: finally a stylish, easy to use fountain pen!
text: I l o v e using a fountain pen and it has been years since i gave up on my grandfather's old fountain pens. This was a total impulse buy and it has a great look, writes beautifully, has ease of changing ink cartridge. I really use it fairly infrequently, but reach for it knowing it won't disappoint!

title: Great pens. I have a large collection of pens
text: Great pens.  I have a large collection of pens, probably $25,000 or so and these cheapies are the best ever!

title: 000 worth of pens this is the best out of the box I have ever used in ...
text: As a collector of $5,000 worth of pens this is the best out of the box I have ever used in fifty years!  You’ll love it!

title: Pilot ink cartridge works better than Parker ink
text:
I started using this pen with the included 1 black ink cartridge and the writing was smooth, ink dried instantly, no smudging. After the cartridge was dried (so much fun I wrote a lot), I replace with squeeze converter and Parker bottle ink. The ink flow struggles, writing became scratch, and ink smudged easily.
Just ordered Pilot ink cartridges and am waiting anxiously for them to arrive so I can enjoy writing again.

title: Love my HP stamps!!
text: I ordered 1 book for myself from USPS when they first became available. I just used up my last one and was really sad that they were no longer available. Cost more than USPS was originally but cost less than what I could find on Etsy. Arrived in great shape -- the seller took the time and effort to make the packaging sturdy so they stamps wouldn't bend. I'm not a collector, but I think it's good to note for those of you looking to add these stamps to your collection.

title: The nostalgia is real. Love these gel pens...still!
text: Work just as great as they did when I was a kid. Best gel pens and lovely colors

title: In my experience non-HP ink cartridges have been fine. This ran out almost 3x faster than HP ...
text: In my experience non-HP ink cartridges have been fine. This ran out almost 3x faster than HP ink and other non-HP ink cartridges.

title: Bleeds like crazy, be careful
text: I feel fancy when I write with it :) It's not as calligraphy-ish as I expected after reading many reviews online and viewing writing samples. Very heavy pen. Bleeds like crazy, be careful. VERY bold, not quite medium point.

title: Useless cartridge??
text:
I like how these pens write and love that they can use regular fountain pen ink.

What in hell is with the empty cartridge that has no bottom? It's just a tube, and could have caused a Very Serious Inkcident had I not noticed its pointlessness.

Also standard international cartridges DO NOT FIT this pen.

Sigh. Back to looking for a cartridge rollerball that does take international standard cartridges and/ or converter, which is in my under $20 price range. (J Herbin's roller has its own issues- squeek, squeek, squeek)

title: WOW THIS STUFF STINKS
text: I've read many comments about Noodler's pens having a 'special smell,' but have not noted that in the dozen or so inks I've purchased from that company. This one is so smelly that not only can I smell it (with long-covid anosmia) but can't be in the room with it. Not helpful when I'd bought it for marking papers!  It's not just me, either: my partner who rarely can smell things (not COVID related!) sniffed this from two rooms away and commented...unfavorably. I'll need to find a nasally-insensitive home for this as it's well past the return date, thanks to final exams.

title: Does not fit a5 planner
text: Bought for an A5 size planner; holes do not line up : (  though recommended by Amazon when buying the planner.

title: Meh
text: I keep a bunch of fountain pens for students who need to borrow one in class- they are generally intrigued by the old tech. These were very spotty for startup and kept losing flow for no discernible reason. (I have a bunch of "real" fountain pens and can make adjustments.) Kids kept wanting to shake them to increase flow...which worked. On my floor, desks, walls. Overall not thinking I'll buy these again.

title: Great
text: Use to refill cartridges for Canon pixma and tanks for Epson ecotank. Also occasionally for ((cheap)) fountain pens

title: Great
text: Have used to refill Canon pixma printers and Epson ecotank without problems

title: Not so sticky
text: Purchased for mailing home student awards certificates and medals. The adhesive is not strong; each envelope needed tape to stay shut reliably, even before handing them over to postal carrier. Overall would buy again though.

title: Great so far
text: Easy to replace the broken old plastic wheels on my desk chair; super smooth rolling. I hope they last a long time!

title: Worth the price but not buying more
text:
I personally prefer broader nibs (italic actually) but these are OK for writing fast--almost like a gel pen. Mine do tend to leak into the cap and blob from the nib, mostly using Noodler's inks- but what do you expect for the price? Keeping the converter-cartridge full limits this IMO.
EDIT: may well buy more. After a lot of hard use (teacher) I've had only one die- weirdly the section got jammed in the cap??? but the others are still going strong, and they have greatly outlived single use plastic pens with the extra bonus of almost unlimited ink choice. (No sparklies 😔)

title: Not so shimmery; clogs
text:
I love the color but get very little shimmer with the several fountain pens in which it has been used- my preference is for medium or wide italic nibs, so I don't think it's a function of line width, and also swirl the pen before writing. It is quite cloggy as well.... Maybe ok in dip pens?
I won't be buying this again.

title: SERIOUSLY STINKY and NOT PERMANENT
text:
I LOVE Pilot's Wytebord ink refills for dry-erase-- they work well and DON'T STINK so I was hoping for less stinkiness from the permanent ink.

Nope! It seems to be a near-lifetime supply of stinky green permanent ink. But it triggers migraine for me : (

Also there was no little plastic pipette as pictured.

UPDATE: A school bag, synthetic gsbric, on which I'd used this, to touch up faded color, is now BLEEDING green ink on skin and fabric it touches- no hard rubbing or friction, just carried across a room after drying for OVER 2 WEEKS.

SKIP THIS INK.

title: Steelcase ok- no retaining clips
text: Used these to replace the finally-collapsing original casters on my inherited Steelcase chair (got the desk too! vintage @1960). Easy-peasy to pop out the originals and pop these in, but there is no retaining clip on these casters' stems, so the wheels fell out on the way back to the floor! Minus one star. Overall a good buy and I would recommend. They work well on carpet so far.

title: One works well. No response from seller
text:
Per seller's request, emailed that one fountain pen skips horribly despite full cleaning and typical adjustments. Two emails, no response.

Had both pens worked equally well, this would be a 5 star review. One defective plus two ignored emails equals two stars. Lame.

title: Avoid
text:
Why is there a rating for warmth??

Yes, these are thinner. Which would not be a problem except for their tendency to ripple AND PLEAT in a self-feeding laminator- which has never done this with other brands of film.

This film is NOT CRYSTAL CLEAR either. A second run through the laminator helps but it's still not good enough for keepsakes.

Of you dont mind cloudy, inconsistent results AND babysitting your projects to prevent some of the ripples and pleating, try this.

I'd advise against, though.

title: Meh
text:
I do prefer calligraphy / italic nibs on fountain pens, and since I lend mine frequently to students I buy the cheaper plastic ones. These are sturdy enough for what they are, but the nibs don't write consistently, which I find frustrating. Perhaps a bit of tuning and more adjustment will help.
I can't speak to the ink cartridges supplied as I use bottled inks with the converters.

title: Sharp
text:
As others have indicated, the metal corners are very sharp. In my classroom I've used strong magnets with 1/2" hooks to hold the item to my whiteboard, and position the hooks to cover the corners so kids (and adults!) don't get scratched.

I anticipate this will function long beyond my retirement in 13 years.

title: Colleague approved
text: Bought as a gift for a colleague. He has given up his red stick pens for the fountain pen I gave him (pilot metropolitan) and this ink. He says the red is dark enough to not be looking like dripping gore, but saturated enough to be easily noticed.

title: Leaks. Scratchy. Won't buy again.
text:
While I do like the variety of italic nibs in this pack, I find the nibs are *very* sharp & scratchy and have a fairly defined "sweet spot" outside of which they don't write / draw well (of course, not in my normal holding position).

The ink colors included are unremarkable, and the 2 I've loaded for use to date LEAK (yes I know how to install a cartridge).

Look elsewhere for easy to use italics- I much prefer the Pilot Metropolitan stub italics I've bought, FYI.

title: Burgundy
text:
I had hoped this would be more purple than red, but it comes out the color of a nice red wine. I'd rather drink my wine! Written with a Hero 5028, 1.9mm italic nib.
FYI the purple ink is Baystate Concord Grape and the paper is just a regular Office Depot lined pad, written with Noodler's Charlie.

title: Migraine trigger -avoid if sensitive
text:
I am a migraine patient and a gardener. Actual real growing violets do not trigger my head, nor do dried violets, but this ink does- in under a minute. I seriously doubt the "hydrosol" assertion on this basis- other ink does not have this effect.
The color is nice.

title: Skippy; cracks- does not live up to its reputation
text: This pen skips. Its "sweet spot" is really narrow. There are lots of hard starts and erratic ink flow. I wish I'd just put the same $ to a metal Jinhao or Baker etc. that would actually work and last longer than a week of light use.

title: Love the stub
text: I like this stub nib more than the regular tipped medium Metro nib, but have found this one dries out faster for some reason. Namely, my regular Metro was vacationing in a jacket pocket for a few weeks and started right up, but this cute stub version needed a quick nib dip in H2O to get going after one day.... with the same ink (Pilot black cartridges, from the same box).

title: Quite dark
text: Generally I love Noodler's inks - even the BayState ones! - but I wish this purple were brighter.... with some dilution it feathers less on cheap school copy paper, but it's still nearly black. "Stealth purple,"  if you will... Being a BayState ink, I keep it in the Charlie eyedropper which came with the ink, with no problems.

title: Does not feed ink; skip this one
text:
Fits my Jotter but holds very little ink.

Edit: it does hold a reasonable amount of ink but does not release the ink to the feed properly: the slide has to be manually advanced to make the ink available. This is *not* an acceptable option!!!

Find another option!

title: Not my favorite
text: I was prepared to like this pen but have been disappointed. It's lighter and feels cheaper than expected- the section especially- and the converter doesn't hold enough ink for a not-many-notes hour-long meeting. It was filled with Monteverde Caribbean blue 😎 but ran out before the first page was filled. Medium nib seems Fine to me.

title: A reasonable introduction
text: For those who aren't familiar with fountain pens or don't want to mess with cartridges or bottles of ink, these are OK. I don't find them "fountainy"  enough to buy more but the students to whom I gave them like them....they write pretty much like the g2 gel pens. Apparently they can be reined if desired...

title: As expected
text: Generally fine but difficult to install on new Pilot Metropolitan- too a bit of force to pierce the tip.

title: Inconsistent
text:
I've used two of these so far.

One is fine almost two weeks in -some hard starts and not sealed at the end so...eyedropper fail, at least initially.

The second only lasted 4 days of light use. That one was well sealed at the end so it was fine eyedroppered. However, with Sheaffer Skrip ink in it, it clogged on day 4 and the feed snapped beneath the nib when cleaning...gently. Seller (ds) not at all helpful about clearly defective item. Not holding my breath for better quality out of the remaining units, which is a shame as I'd planned to use them for student prizes.... They like my Herbin scented inks...

title: Great ink- low odor, glass bottle
text:
This ink is awesome for extending the life of your dry erase markers and lessening plastic use. The glass bottle can be used for something else (paper clips, needles,etc) it recycled.
The pipette included is flimsy, though, and cracks easily along the seam. I just dip mine now, rather than using a pipette.

title: Perfect for milk
text: Fits 4 regular gallon bottles of milk perfectly. Helpful when bringing groceries in from the car.

title: Love this color!
text:
I'm a purple fan, and this puce/magenta ink makes me happy. I have used it for taking notes for myself, and for marking student papers. The kids like the color too!
This bottle ought to last a good long time. Bottle is very full, as others have noted is common for Noodler's inks. Some staining on my fingers - wasn't paying close enough attention when filling- washed off in a day.

title: No problems
text: Bought for myself and to include with fountain pen gifts. No problem with installation or function to date.

title: Environmentally friendly AND highly functional
text: These refill inks are great! The colors are rich, the ink smells very little (unlike most single use plastics like Expo) and erases fine with a dry rag or board eraser. I've found one bottle lasts a LONG time, and my markers are in very heavy use - high school language clasroom.

title: Nice but harder to erase than black
text:
I love the Noodler's Waterase inks.

This one is a bit harder to wipe completely off than the black but is still great and WAY better than the toxic stink of expo etc.

The colleague with whom I share a lecture hall can't stand it, though.

I will say the highlighter pen with which it comes dried out fairly easily, and its tip isn't broad enough to be seen from the rear of an average sized room (@30' square). I filled some metal 'paint pens' and their bullet point has better visibility.

More colors please!

title: Nice ink
text:
Using in refillable markers for student mini-whiteboard practice and classroom board marking. Slightly damp rag will wipe off ink easily and NO STENCH! Reducing plastic waste and solvent odor from markers. Mild alcohol scent is not bothersome.
Thank you, Nathan Tardif!
Please, more colors???

title: Pale
text: This purple is rather watery, not nearly as saturated and vivid as I wanted.

title: Nice- vibrant colors, works much as expected
text: Great price for so many cartridges. I love the color, more magenta than pink, in my Jinhao x750 pens. Sometimes it doesn't flow perfectly but that isn't a deal-breaker for me. Gave a bunch to a student with a fountain pen as a graduation present & she loves the set.

title: NOT NEW but otherwise fine FOR A MONTH
text:
I bought this set thinking to use most of them as gifts. Imagine my surprise when checking the dark blue/purple marbled one, prior to wrapping it, that it had already been used! The converter was about half-filled with a dark blue ink....which had dried on the nib. NOT HAPPY that I received used merchandise, and especially that the gift I'd planned to give can't happen. MINUS 1.5 OR 2 STARS.

On the plus side I do like the one I'm using myself (which does seem to have been new). It's fairly heavy and writes fine with the Jinhao cartridge ink I bought for it. I've not used the converter so I can't speak to it. It's nice that each pen comes with one, and the boxes are pretty good also.

EDIT: the purple one has its color peeling off after very little light use by a careful adult. Minus another star.

title: Nice pen but
text:
I've got another of these and like them for cost, weight and performance.

2 stars off this review because this one had a converter but no ink cartridge. As I don't currently have any bottledink, I can't use my new purple pen 😞

title: BROWN
text:
This ink is NOT PURPLE.

Well, the Romans would have called it purple- but their purple came from crushed sea snails.

Yuck.

title: No bad smell; some colors pale
text: Bought to reduce toxic smelling items in classroom. Minor alcohol smell dissipates quickly. Colors less vibrant than hoped, especially orange and green.

title: Overall WAY better than Expo / "normal" board markers
text:
Purchased this lot to remove the xylene-toluene stench of "regular" (Expo) type markers from my classroom.
These smell faintly of alcohol, which dissipates quickly.
They write well enough on a slant (sometimes lines are faint or striated when holding the marker at a more usual angle) and ink can be seen from 5.5 meters back from the board (back of my classroom). They erase cleanly with a dry or damp rag. They can squeak as you write though....but not like squeaky chalk of the olden days!
Will update if any issues arise re. usable life of the marker (though they are refillable).
Never received the refill ink, however, though I did contact the seller multiple times. 4 stars for markers, minus one for no refill ink.
UPDATE: the screw-on collars/caps can crack fairly easily if handled carelessly by students or colleagues. So far not a deal breaker for me because the freedom from solvent stench is wonderful. However, minus another star for flimsy brittle plastic.
UPDATE 2: seller resent the missing ink. Adding one star back! (Minus one for brittle plastic- not the seller's fault)
My students *much prefer* the nonstinky markers to the horrible toxic ones!!!

title: Didn't work
text: Paper printed only magenta tones though cartridge was full & printed plain paper just fine. Returned.

title: INVISIBLE, USELESS MARKERS
text:
Yes, they are low odor.

Unfortunately they are WAY low visibility also; not functional AT ALL for classroom use, so I may take them home for grocery & chores lists.

AVOID THESE MARKERS.

title: College son loves
text: My college age son loves this and actually uses the planner. Hoping it holds up; he's been using it for about a month.

title: Not worth $10
text:
Tried this cleaner for my writeyboard whiteboard; doesn't work any better than the easier-to-find, cheaper E brand- though it is less smelly

EDIT: what I've found works best is NOT Removable but some fairly hot (not quite boiling) plain water. Murphy's Oil Soap is the best occasional cleaner. Nothing really gets an old, ghosty board "like new"

title: Ghosting. Hard to install. Bubbles. Costly mistake
text: While when clean, the Writeyboard is a better surface for projection & writing in class due to its matte surface, it does not erase cleanly (proprietary markers OR Expo), requiring constant wiping with smelly cleaner. The board was hard to hang- and yes, we read and followed the directions. Bubbles are visible under the surface a month in, and I doubt it will last a semester-  $100 per semester is too much to make the classroom projection/notes surface less glaring and more friendly to those especially sensitive to glare. I will not be purchasing this product again.

title: Great purchase!
text: My students never seem to have a blue pen. This way I can "lend" them one without breaking the bank....

title: Plan for it to last until retirement!
text:
Replacing a near-identical sharpener for my classroom; that one lasted 18 years, 3 moves, and thousands of kids. Hoping to bequeath this to my successor in 2033 (oh wow).
Weirdly, 21st-century students have to think about how to use a "real" pencil sharpener!!!

title: OK but not great
text: Good graphic and size but stamps maybe twice before needing re-inked.  Thought it was self- inking but it just has a felt pad in the base...."pre-ink"?

title: Excellent
text: MUCH BETTER THAN REFILL INK SOLD HERE BY ⭐INK. COLORS PRETTY TRUE, not too hard to use but expect some stained fingers. If possible consider prying off the whole top section of cartridge to be refilled (mine are Canon 240 and 241) then taping top back on for greater ease and cleanliness. Don't forget to keep them upright though!!

title: NOT 4"!!!
text: The exact dimensions of "jumbo" seem to be variable. These are just big (average) color-coated paper clips-  I wanted 4" as one answer indicated. Nope, closer to 2"

title: Good price.  OK otherwise
text: Bought to laminate classroom reminders, labels and a repositionable (with added magnets) date card. Does not wipe clean with dry-erase markers (expo) and stained/ needs replaced after 5 weeks, even though cleaned daily with liquid board cleaner.

title: as expected
text: as expected

title: Work great, great colors, don't dry out
text: Absolutely love all my mildliners! The colors are fantastic and I haven't had a single marker dry out in the year or two I've had them. They dont bleed through on almost anything, though some cheaper papers will show through if you go over an area more than once. Even in my Bible (thin pages) it doesn't bleed through, although ghosting is impossible to avoid on those types of pages :)

title: Okay ish if you have a skinny or fancy pen. Do not plan on using with pens that have grips.
text: Admittedly, I was disappointed in this. The elastic loop will work nicely for a very thin pen OR a very smooth pen (my staedtler fineliners were perfect, and my pilot metropolitan fountain pen goes in nicely) but if you don't use fancy pens, don't bother with this. Its well made, but its a pain with most walmart pens, or anything with a grip on it. It might also be that I didn't attach it to my journal just right, but I don't think I will buy a pen loop again. I would rather pay the extra $6 for the journal with pen loop attatched than to buy this separately and have to chance putting it on wrong.

title: Great ink, works perfectly with Pilot Metropolitan Fountain Pens
text: fits perfectly in my pilot metropolitan medium nib fountain pen. Its hard to say a lot about ink cartridges, but I'm pleased with these. I'm still new to fountain pens and the amount of ink they use, so I don't know if its normal to go through a cartridge so quickly, but I needed to replace my first cartridge after less than four weeks of daily journaling. I've never gone through another pen so quickly, but I also used this a lot more than I have exclusively used another pen before.

title: Beautiful, well made
text: This pen is a great beginner fountain pen, although admittedly, as I am still a beginner, I don't know what qualifies as an excellent pen. In any event, this pen has a nice weight to it and has a beautiful finish. I have not used the converter yet, only cartridges, but it writes wonderfully and hasn't leaked on me yet. I personally like a finer print, so I wish I had bought the fine nib instead of the medium, but if you like bold print, you will love this pen. I do still love it for some lettering practice, and will continue using it in my journal until I purchase a fine nib pen.

title: Like a gel pen that doesn't smudge!
text: I love these pens! Take it easy on them to help them last a while, but they write very well and dry quickly. For someone not extremely experienced with different pen types, these are like gel pens that don't smudge. LOVE LOVE LOVE them. Very comfortable to use for a long time-- Germans have done well again!

title: Perfect for a new bullet journalist!
text: Absolutely love these journals, this is one of three we have purchased and the color (Emerald) is beautiful. Great pocket in the back to store my stickers and a small ruler. The elastic closure holds up well even after months of daily/heavy use. The journals are so well made, and the dot grid is great for writing, sketching, or whatever journaling needs you have in mind. The paper is not white, which may bother some, but it doesn't phase me at all. The pages are all numbered and there is a 3 page index in the front. These are features that make this ideal for bullet journaling.

title: Fun to write!
text: My grandkids love this smooth styling pencil— won’t do homework without one!- keep them coming!!

title: Excellent pen in all ways but price point
text: Unexcelled in performance ! Except price!

title: Only once!!!
text: Ordered a dozen pens and only abt 7 write w/ enuf ease and flow to be useful in journal— I won’t be suckered by a price point to buy these again!

title: Five Stars
text: Excellent quality. - and fun to write ! G

title: Simply the finest
text: Excellent smooth flow; the finest fountain pen I have ever used!

title: From A Man, This Is Great!
text:
Coming from a man, I can honestly say that this Bible is not just for ladies. I got one from the BH Blogger program but my wife has had one since they launched and has loved it. I even sit down with it from time to time.

The design is amazing and the study helps truly are helpful. They provide good clarity to passages and devotional points throughout that really add to the staying power of what you're reading. As is always the case, the text is the most important, but the additions and supplements are really what make this Bible different from all others. Not to mention that it is joyful to read/study.

title: My new go-to pen.
text:
I have collector pens and a wide variety of "regulars" and I can honestly say this is one of my favorites. It's nothing too fancy, just a good size body and weight and a great length that allows it to sit well in the hand.

Not to mention the nod to the great with the houndstooth!

title: Dated Appointment book
text: A decent and well made appointment/notebook.  The whole thing is laid out pretty well. It is well-constructed, and offers a lot of space for notes, dates, etc.  I wish the paper was thicker, as I use a fountain pen, and it bled through a lot.

title: Very sturdy, thick paper, and lots of features
text:
This feature packed notebook offers a very thick and sturdy cover and spine. A lot of things in here to help you plan your year and your life. Pages to track habits, and pages to doodle in. Monthly at a glance pages are undated as are the weekly pages. You can start this any time.

This is good for those who like structure, but if you are looking for something like a bullet journal, you may want to look elsewhere. But this is a nice sturdy and heavy duty notebook.

title: Great monthly planner
text: Lots of good features in this notebook. Good heavy paper, suitable for fountain pen users.  Easily adaptable to your specific needs.  Well made and quality pieces.

title: Good Stuff
text: Good stuff. Well made. Lots of storage.  Holds items securely.

title: Solid organizer
text: A solid organizer. Sturdy and easy to set up.  It collapses when not in use, but expands to a solid, sturdy box when in use.

title: Good beginner fountain Pen
text:
Very good beginner fountain pen. Comes with so many cartridges, you won't have to buy your own ink for a while. But I DO use my own ink, so I used the converter that is included with the set. There is one converter for each of the nibs, and the nibs are easy to swap out and change.

Pen is solidly built, well made, and writes very nicely. A good beginner fountain pen.

title: they do just what I need them to do.
text: These made cute gifts for the girls in my office.  The images are clear and super cute.  Highly recommend.

title: Nice and solid, but a wee bit wobbly.
text:
A nice piece. Well made, and HEAVY for its size, and indicates quality construction. Hinges and pieces are all solid and tight. Opens up and has retaining bands to hold your book which feel good and hold it tight. Rotates on the bottom, but because the rotating part of the base is a bit small, it does wobble ever so slightly, but not much to diminish it, but enough to downgrade it to 4 stars instead of 5.

Would stil recommend.

title: Comfy, but small
text:
Comfy, and supportive. but very small. I was surprised how small it was. Sitting on my office chair it took up only about half the space.

Other than the small size, it is nice. Would be good for a car or smaller chair, but not so much for an office chair.

title: great little gift
text: These are a great little gift for any cat lover.  I got them as stocking stuffers.  Highly recommend.

title: Great markers
text: Good set of markers. Vibrant colors, Goes on smoothly. Erases cleanly with water or other cleaning liquid.  Built in small erasers, though I would still use a standard eraser.  Magnets hold to board, but could be stronger.

title: great for my kids
text: These really help us keep chores in order. I update it at the beginning of the week.  I use both wet and dry erase markers and both clean will with some water or glass cleaner.  I would recommend to any family that needs some help getting organized.

title: Works great in a variety of typewriters
text:
I used this in my Olympia Electric and it works well. Bright vibrant red, and deep dark black. Quality made, installs in moments. It also fits my manual Underwood.

Highly Recommend.

title: Nice notebook, fake leather
text: Nice notebooks with fake (faux) leather, but it looks nice, and feels nice in the hand.  Nice paper, pretty much bleed proof.

title: Really cute!
text: Got this for my son who loves Harry Potter (as do I).  It looks like something a wizard would carry.  Nice craftsmanship.  book feels heavy in your hand, and look antique.  Paper is very thick and resists bleed through by fountain pens.

title: Nice quill set, though more than most need
text:
I guess because I've been watching Harry Potter, this came up in my feed. Pretty neat set. Comes with several pen options, including the quill. There are quite a few assorted nibs for the pens, and they are easy to change. Most of them, though, will go unused because I do not know how to do calligraphy.

But I do own fountain pens, and though these are not fountain pens, they are what is called "dip pens" Pens that you dip into the ink to write with. Like oldie time quills. And for that they work very well.

The inks are very nice too, and can be used in your fountain pens if you so desire.

title: Great markers and container
text: Markers are great. They work well. Very colorful. The container has a very heavy duty magnet so it holds fast wherever you put it (on a magnetic surface).

title: They are rubber bands.
text: Rubber bands.  It bounces, it is pretty and if you need something useful, you remove one of the bands and you can tie things up.  What else is to say?

title: disappointed
text: I was really excited to use them in my bullet journal.  The pen end works well.  The ink does not bleed through notebook paper.  The dotted lines work pretty well although I found it hard to get a straight line. It takes a while to get the stamper primed with ink so you'll want to practice on some scratch paper.  The heart and flower patterns are hit and miss.  Frustrating for an adult so I can't imagine a child using it.

title: One of the best "budget" fountain pens
text:
I have about a dozen fountain pens. All are considered the budget level, ranging in price compared to the Lamy Safari, but this pen stands WAY above all these.

The pen is very nice, though it feels a bit light in your hand compared to other pens. In this regard it feels a bit cheap. When you write with it, though, you notice the difference.

The pen writes very smoothly, with an even flow of ink and smooth action. The NIB is super high quality. It comes with one blue cartridge, and additional cartridges are available. You can also get a converter to use with your own bottled ink, but you have to buy that separately. Hence why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5. It should come with a converter. As it is, I am waiting for one to be delievered and I have a nice assortment of inks to try, but cannot yet.

title: Nice quality books. Would like dotted pages first for bullet journal. Good for fountain pens
text: Nice book. Well made. Quality construction. Cover feels smooth and elegant leather/leather-like feel.  Pages are think and hold up to a variety of inks.  Works well with FOUNTAIN PENS!!!  Colors do not bleed through. There are a few pages that are lined and have date spaces, and the back 1/4 is all dotted pages.  As I use a bullet journal, I would have preferred to have these bulletted pages FIRST but this will do.

title: great for family organization
text: They all fit well on my small refrigerator.  There is plenty of room for lists, events, and notes.  There is a lot of traffic going past ours so I use wet-erase markers so we don't lose any information.  Come clean with water.  Occasionally I clean it with 70% ISO alcohol to get any residue off.

title: Pretty good, but beware fountain pen users!
text: Overall, pretty good. Nice quality material, and good paper. Easy to write on without smudging. Except if you use fountain pens. You may get a bit of bleed through or smudging if you don't allow it to dry.

title: Very pretty and nice
text: Very nice lanyard.  Very nice colors, well made, good stiching. A quality product.

title: great whiteboard
text: I am very pleased with whiteboard.  I also got the matching corkboard.  They look great hanging in my kitchen and are very functional for a busy family.

title: great cork board
text: I am very pleased with this cork board.  I also got the matching whiteboard.  They look great hanging in my kitchen and are very functional for a busy family.

title: Nice, and gets a lot of compliments
text: I really like this. I was just using ga plastic cup for my pens, but this is so much nicer. I get a lot of compliments on it. Very sturdy, well made and looks like a real typewriter.

title: Great planner for busy families
text: Having a household with 2 kids and two working adults, it is quite handy to have a nice high quality planner. IT's dry erase and magnetic, we stick it to our family whiteboard and it shows events, meals, and schedules for the week and is very handy.

title: Very nice cushion
text: I got this for my classroom seat.  It's doing hell on my back, and since I sit a lot during various activities I needed something.  This cushion seat for my chair fits very nicely, has ample support and I feel less tired at the end of the day.

title: Really nice bells
text: Got these for games I do with my students. They are very nice. Look good, and sound good. Fits the bill.

title: Decent beginner fountain pen
text:
This is a decent fountain pen. It comes with the converstion kit so you can use it right out of the box with your own bottled ink, which I do.

There are two nibs, but you can obviously only use one at a time, when you remove one to fill it, you simply pop off the little tank and converter, and put it in the new nib and screw the new nib in.

They write pretty well, but I found that the one you aren't using tends to dry out. I wish there were cap so you can keep the unused one fresh.

I also found it leaks sometimes, more than other fountain pens.

title: A wonderful whiteboard: A must for teachers and parents who are asked to be teachers
text: [[VIDEOID:1c337d1821fee0c8783def39857a2457]] A really nice white board. Easy to put together, use and roll around. Writes cleanly, and erases nicely.

title: Surprised by comfort
text:
Like so many memory foam products nowadays, they come in a vaccuum bag that you simply open and it expands. It doesn't expand as much as I would have thought, but it is still very comfy.

Nice material and well made, it has a strap to secure to your chair. Feels very nice to sit on.

title: Nice selection of little bags
text: Nice selection of little bags. Nice assortment of sizes. I use them to carry my different pens, markers, and the such. I also use a couple to keep my wires in place.

title: colors are ok, a bit washed out
text: Not bad. Easy to use, and hold. Decent colors, but some of the brighter colors are a bit washed out compared ot other brands, but they write evenly and smoothly and erase very cleanly.

title: Good quality note pad
text: Good quality note pad.  Paper is nice, doesn't bleed with standard pens, but got a bit of it with my fountain pen.

title: For whom the Bell tolls?
text: The Bell tolls for Thee!  A nicely made bell, loud, adn consistent action. Very nice. Use it in class to get attention.

title: Nice looking but too big
text: I don't know who made these, but they are way too big. They stick out of the side of the binder by abour 1/2 inch or so.  Not acceptable.

title: Great Chalk markers
text: Great chalk markers. Beautiful vibrant colors. Easy to use, can switch between pointy tip and chisel tip. Cleans up with water and a rag. Very nice!

title: Super Duper Markers
text:
These are so much better than the ones you get from the office stores, or what is supplied at work. These write very well, have a great quality of color along with a wonderful selection. They write nice and feel very good in your hand. The box is a very nice way of displaying them.

they erase super clean.

title: Decent enough, but the writing scuff off
text:
Very good idea. nicely made. Easy to write on, and easy to clean. Sturdy and should last a long time. My only fault with them is that when you use them as flashcard, often the writing beings to scuff off with use. It's not the fault of these per say, but just due to how dry erase works.

I think they would work better with wet erease markers.

title: Great gaming mousepad
text: This is beyond a simple mousepad, and is more of a whole desk sized pad. Very well made, comfortable and lots of good ways to use it.

title: Great pencils!
text: Good set of pencils. Well made, quality pencils that write nicely, sharpen nicely, and erase cleanly.

title: Great books, good quality paper
text: Good notebook. Very well made, with good paper, good for use with nice pens such as fountain pens or markers. Doesn't' bleed through much.

title: great markers
text: Comparable to Crayola!  Kids didn't complain.  It does wash easily off of clothing and skin.

title: fun card
text: good quality card.  would purchase again.

title: Awesome cat mousepad
text: A nice mousepad. Nicely mad, soft and supportive.

title: METALLIC CHALK PAINT
text: These are metallic.  I didn't see that in the product description.  They work great.  Easy clean up. The container they come is great!

title: Very nice pen case, good to keep them organized
text: Great case for your pens. I use them for my fountain pens, and it keeps them all where I can access them and use them. Keeps them from knocking around and getting lost.

title: Great color and writing
text: Great color and good coverage and color. Flows smoothly.

title: A fantastic, well made fountain pen
text:
A great fountain pen. Very well made. Feels very sturdy and heavy for it's size. Fits comfortably in the hand. Comes with an adapter for bottles of fountain pen ink, but NO disposable ink cartridges.

It says "fine nib" and I almost didn't get it because I don't prefer fine nibs. To me, this nib is more medium, so don't let it only have fine and ultra-fine choices deter you.

The pen writes smoothly and cleanly. Feels good in the hand. The converter that comes with the phone is very nice.

title: A beautiful pen that feels good and writes really nice!
text:
This is a beautiful pen. I've been writing with Pilot Metropolitan, and this is far superior and roughly at the same price point.

The pen is elegant and has a nice weight to it. The whole thing is constructed well and comes in a beautiful leather box with the pen, blue and black ink. Included with the pen, already installed is the converter to use with a bottle of ink of your choice. This is what I did because I prefer to use this over refills, but you do have refills on hand to keep in case you run out of bottled link.

The cap comes off and is replaced with a very sturdy feel. The pen is nicely weighted in your hand. It writes beautifully with wonderful ink flow and the nib just rolls like melted butter over the paper. Very elegant and a wonderful pen for newbies to fountain pens, or those more experienced. I got the green one, and the color is a wonderful glossy hunter green.

If you are thinking of a pen for yourself, or a pen for a gift, this is an impressive pen at this price point.

title: Sturdy and durable
text: Sturdy and well made. Just what I needed for my Covid-19 home office.

title: Great paper!  the lines are very understated
text:
I almost regretted buying this because I traditionally wrote on unlined paper. Traditional lined notebook paper, the lining is too dark. this is very understated but still helps guide you in your writing. the back is not lined.

the paper has a nice feel to it. It feels elegant, but not too heavy. I use a fountain pen, and the ink does not bleed through, and is absorbed and dries very quickly. I would highly recommend it!!

title: Super easy to use. Great way to fill out pen
text: This is a great way to load your pen up with the ink of your choice. This converter installs in mere seconds and is very easy to use.  Much better than that rubber bladder that comes with the Pilots.

title: This this is fantastic!!
text:
This thing is fantastic!! Really well made and pretty. And it is comfortable. The best part is that it allows you to hold your soft or hardcover book open much more comfortably than before. Great for reading for yourself, but also if you were going to read to a child, you can turn and face the book toward the children and they can see the book too. Gonna get a few more for gifts!!

It also came with a very nice wooden letter opener!! A great touch!

title: Great fountain pen pink.
text: I really like this fountain pen ink. I"ve tried other brands that did not write as smoothly and did not have water resistance. This ink is great. Very dark black, and flows nicely.  It dries very quickly and doesn't smudge. I love my fountain pens, and this ink adds to the enjoyment.

title: A little smaller than I thought, but very nice
text: A very nice map. Very beautiful and detailed, you can scratch off individual countries on the map, or just scratch off the flags at the bottom. Very nice to track where you have traveled. A bit smaller than I anticpated, but very nice.

title: 3 of them didn't work
text: The Ruby, Sapphire, and Emerald colors did not work, right out of the box. We will try to store them upside down, but they are dry. Would not recommend.

title: You can't beat this pen!
text:
Really a great beginner/intermediate fountain pen. Very heavy, and feels good in your hand. The medium nib I find is my favorite, the fine nib is a bit too thin for me, especially if you are writing on thinner paper or have a heavy hand, as I do.

Easy to refill, as it has the bladder refill device already inserted, or you can use disposable cartridgtes (it includes one). But i find refilling it offers you the best choices for ink type, color, etc.

Really a nice pen.

title: Decent, but not great
text: This is ok, not great.  It is a bit flimsy and feels cheap.  The pen tray doesn't stay on well, and mounting can be a bit tricky.  The quality of writing is very nice, as you can use dry or wet erase markers and the writing comes off nicely with a eraser or wet cloth.

title: A cheap pen. Better ones are out there
text:
I was disappointing with this pen. I write with fountain pens exclusively, and this is not a great pen. It's not BAD, but it's not great. Very flimsy feeling, cheap. It took forever for the ink to come down to the nib, and it writes just as good as a dollar store pen.

But if you are looking to give a fountain pen to a true newbie or a kid, this may be good.

title: Nice journal, but need more dots
text:
Nice journal. Padded and well constructed. Paper is great, smooth writing and doesn't bleed through. I use a fountain pen, and that's good.

My problem wit it is that the pages are only dotted on one side. The back side of the pages are NOT dotted. What's up with that?

title: Very nice badge holder-For my 5 point Constable Badge
text:
Got this for my 5-point constable badge. It's a pin style badge, and this badge holder holds it exceptionally well. It holds the badge nicely, and has a clip for your belt, or a chain for around your neck.

All the materials seem very well made, sturdy, and of the highest quality. Super nice. Look no further!!!

title: Nice pen
text: Nice pen, writes well. Smooth writing and comfortable to hold.

title: Elegant and beautiful notebook
text: You'll feel like the elder Dr. Jones, with his grail diary with this beautiful and functional notebook/journal.  Leather is soft and supple, and the paper is nice to write on and won't bleed. Looks nice for keeping notes, keeping a diary, or using for sketches. Very nice.

title: Heavy duty and high quality
text: Heavy duty quality product. There is a calendar and a chore chart. Made with heavy duty material. You can write on with a dry erase marker. Writes nice, comes clean nice. Very good product.

title: Really good fountain pen for the money. I suggest the medium nib
text:
Good fountain pen for the money. I suggest getting the medium nib, as the fine is a bit to fine. I write in a bullet journal and sometimes the ink coverage isn't the best. The medium is still finer than most medium fountain pen nibs, and writes darker.

Comes with an ink cartridge, or the billow reservoir for filling with your own ink (suggested).

title: Perfect for what our family needs
text: This is a big magnet that attaches to your fridge, where you can put events, reminders, and notses.  IT's made of heavy duty magnet with a glossy white front divided into days of the week, plus a spot for notes.  Very well done, easy to read. Easy to write on and erase. A must for busy families.

title: Great and useful planner-and a little bit of fun
text:
Great weekly and monthly planner. Has all what you expect in a planner; weekly pages for short range planning, and big two page monthly pages that show the entire year. Think heavy pages good with all sorts of pens and markers. Colorful and fun with interesting graphics that make this a little fun.

Good well made planner.

title: Nice desk blotter, glossy pages smudge, but resist stains.
text: Nice, well made. The paper is a bit glossy, and some types of ink and pens will smudge a bit, but what is great about the semi glossy pages is that minor spills don't soak in. I hate older pads I've had that get stains on them. This helps with that issue, and is great to have on my desk.

title: I use for my Workforce 840
text: Good ink for your Epson. Easy to change out, and lasts a fairly long time. Good price too

title: Well made, easy to mount
text: This is a nice board for office or home use. It is a nice size, not too big, not too small. It attaches very easily to your wall with the included 3m mounting tape.  It comes with one dry erase market and 2 magnets.  There are no push pins included for the cork board. Overall it is well made, but the cork board feels a bit flimsy.

title: Not needed, redundant, but with a nice plastic case it does keep them all together for your planning.
text:
Really not very useful, any more than an index card. These are thinner, and any thicker pen will bleed through, so if you are using a sharpie be cautious. The case is decent, if it doesn't break on you.

The plus side is that it does have a decent layout. The pages are all like graph paper, and the case can sit on your desk holding them all very neat, but overall, why do you even need this?

title: Four Stars
text: nice and small travel sharpner

title: Two Stars
text: I found it difficult to use and adjust.

title: Four Stars
text:
enjoy using a make believe fountain pen
would like more varied colors

title: Five Stars
text:
writes like skating on ice
smooth and glides easily

title: Easy way to stay in touch with friends
text: Adequate space to write a message to my friends and family.  No need to hunt for an envelope, just write and send it off.  Makes me happy and gives my friends and family, I believe, a treat to hear from me.

title: Cursive Made Easy
text: I have three of these pens and am pleased with each one.  Fountain pens have always been my choice for writing letters, notes, cards, etc. and this series is perfect for all.  The pen is well made, easy to change out the cartridge and flows easily across the page while feeling comfortable in your hand.  If, like myself, you enjoy cursive then this pen will make you very pleased with the performance.  No, it isn't expensive; but at a good price for a terrific writing intrument.

title: Journal Perfection
text: This journal is high quality, a very convenient size, and my favorite feature is the paper.  I use a fountain pen to do my journaling and with this book there is no bleeding.  My pen glides easily and I don't have to worry about the ink showing on the reverse side.  The small pocket at the back is very handy for keeping notes, items that I want to check out, small articles I find that I want to keep and is generally a very nice feature.  I was a bit skeptical about using a dotted page as I have always used lined, but the dots allow for neat and even entries.  Now if my ability to write down my thoughts and observations were as good as this book it would be even better.  Great product at a fantastic price and I highly recommend this item to all who want to record or just doodle, have fun.

title: Fun With Book Ends?
text: My collection of books is considerable and I like to keep them neat and orderly.  Book ends must be strong enough to hold big books without being so heavy that you can't lift them to place them.  These are the perfect combination of both of these requirements.  Simple in design, but if you're a Dr. Who fan they are super special.  The price was very good and I am very happy with the job they do with even my larger books.  They come in red too and those are super fun!

title: Beautiful But
text: This is a beautiful pen, easy to hold, easy to fill and not a bad value for the money.  The one thing that doesn't work for me is that the nib is not smooth, it seems to drag on the paper.  I've used fountain pens all of my life and they are my first choice for creating documents.  This pen just doesn't flow easily across the paper and that is a bit of a problem for me.  It will be used regularly, but it isn't my first choice.

title: An Alternative To Manufacturer's Pricey Cartridges
text: My HP Pagewide printer/scanner/fax is amazing and I am super pleased with it.  I was not pleased when I found out how much the cartridges cost, something I should have checked before I made the purchase.  The HP product is an amazing machine and I am very happy with it.  When I found the Kingjet cartridges I debated whether or not to take a chance on not using the original replacements.  No worries as the cartridges work perfectly, cost so much less and I'm very confident they will be my go to source for refills.

title: Art and Quality
text: I received a Christmas card this year that was made by Papyrus and thought it was one of the loveliest I'd ever seen.  When I looked on Amazon and saw the note cards I was delighted with the variety.  Knowing the quality of the product I'd seen I ordered a box and have since ordered another of a different design.  In this day of e-mail I still like to hand write notes to friends and family.  The Papyrus products are beautiful and are of excellent quality.

title: Quality Without Being Costly
text: The Pilot line of Metro pens is fantastic at a price that won't break your budget.  It has a nice feel in your hand, is easy to refill and writing with it is a delight to anyone who loves cursive.  I have three, in different colors, and each one gets used each week.  Different color ink makes each task fun.  Fountain pens have been a life long favorite and this line is perfect at a great price.

title: Great Fun For Organizing and Reminding
text: These are great stickers and are just what I need to make my Day Timer work for me all year.  The quality is very good, they stick very well, easy to remove from the sheet, colors work for added impact and a terrific value for the money.

title: Not My Idea of Great
text: I'm a lover of organization and set up my Day Timer each year very carefully.  Using the stickers makes special events stand out and reminds me of cards to send, appointments, etc.  For the money you don't get much and what there is of each event is not much fun.  Very disappointed.

title: Good But Not Great
text: I am a big fan of fountain pens and use them on a regular basis.  This pen is okay, but has a drag that can become annoying if writing a long letter.  The color is a major turn off, in the picture online it looked like "velvet" and that was what caught my eye. The pen is purple, but not a good shade of purple.  Very easy to change ink cartridges and having the converter is nice when I want to use bottled ink.  All in all it is a good pen for the money, but it isn't my go to pen.

title: Good Investment for Storage
text: These binders are perfect for any items that you wish to keep safe and neat.  The price is good and they will afford you the organization and protection you desire.

title: Cute With Quality
text: These cards are just as cute as in the picture.  The quality of the paper used is superb and the size is just what I wanted.  I will definitely consider this seller again when I need cards.

title: Best Binder for the Price
text: These are very basic, but for my quilt pattern collection they are perfect.  They are just a tad flimsy so constant handling would be rough on them, but for binders you need to hold collections that you look at once in awhile they are perfect.

title: Fountain Pens Are Fun
text: I love cursive and with Sheaffer's wide variety of nibs it is possible to create beautiful writing with ease.  The ink cartridges are wonderful and allow you to change colors when the mood hits you.  Amazon offers so many varieties at such great prices that I have purchased three pens with different nibs.  Still a quality product even after all these years.

title: Fountain Pen Lovers Best Friend
text: I love using fountain pens, but I remember the days of filling them from a bottle of ink.  That indicates that I'm older than dirt.  There are beautiful fountain pens available, but it is hard to beat Sheaffer on all points.  These ink cartridges are the main reason I have Sheaffer pens, super easy to pop in a new one with no mess.  Also having the cartridges available in many colors makes it fun without spending a fortune.  Outstanding product from Amazon.  I tried to buy these cartridges at a large brick and mortar store and they looked at me like I was bonkers.

title: Perfect Pocket
text: Exactly what I wanted, good price and quick delivery.

title: Organization Made Easy
text: I collect patterns, quilting patterns, and this product is outstanding for keeping them organized and protected.  There are other products available to do this, but Avery has produced the star of the bunch.  When I spend $9 for a quilting pattern I want it kept in perfect condition and this product allows me to do just that, plus I can organize the patterns so that I may easily find just what I need.  The price that Amazon sells this product for is perfect when you need a large quantity.  Avery produces good office products and this item is a perfect example of that quality.

title: delivered on time and as expected
text: works as expected

title: Ink runs out super quick. Is a bit on the messy side
text: Writes well. Ink runs out super quick. Is a bit on the messy side. I have had more than a few times getting ink on my fingers from placing the cap on the end (as the product picture displaying the tip shows) the cap gets filled with ink for some reason and then leaves ink on the base of the pen - that you will be holding to doodle, scribble, and scribere :)

title: It’s so transparent I use to lose it
text: The days of losing tape are over. Someone gifted me a desk dispenser. The first roll has been working out great. No complaints.

title: Love this brand
text:
I have purchased several of this brand—Joyeux.
It’s the name of Lancelot’s sword in one of the Arthurian Legend books. I had to buy one, and one and another one. Some lined some not.
I write with fountain pens and the paper is wonderful. Smooth, not scratchy and so far no bleed throughs.
The cover is a quality feeling faux leather. The elastic band as a closure is a nice feature, which I use . And there’s a pocket on the inside back cover. It contains a few labels for organizing. I have not used either feature. However, I am impressed with the pockets construction. It also is something I think most people would probably overlook. So if you don’t put too much in it, it can be your little secret. If you’re still into that or uhhh, need something like that. I would and have purchased them again.

title: Works great if you know how to use it
text:
These erasers aren’t Silly Putty pink erasers. Imo a gummy eraser is a great FIRST step tool in erasing colored pencils. Especially the soft core types like Prismacolor. I had a terrible time with the rolling technique. Now I just tear off a small chunk, press it down onto what I want erased—1-2x, more if need be. Then if need be use a white eraser.
Pay attention to how it looks before pressing or rolling it on any page. You can transfer things from the eraser onto your paper.
I saw an art hack that worked on washing them vs tossing out. I will find it and update with washing details.

title: Good buy
text: I like white erasers over the standard pink eraser. This brand individually wraps their erasers. The erasers work well. No complaints. They were a little smaller than I had expected. But their size wouldn’t stop me from reordering this brand again.

title: They’re pens. They write well. Or is it good.
text:
These are “gel” pens. Pen is a pen is a pen….
But it’s by Sharpie. I’ve been a pen freak since childhood. Their looks, the way they write, the feel in my hand. I like this pen. I bought a 4 pack on a whim. It’s comfortable, has a nice even flow of ink and is retractable. I can’t say anything on ink drying time. It’s not a factor that makes or breaks a pen for me. I would purchase these pens again. Sharpie you have certainly come a long way from being a smelly black marker.

title: It’s always the write time for this pen
text:
I ordered the red version had expected a pen with a metal body. Initially was disappointed. But once I swapped out its fine nib for a medium, and inked it up. A fondness for it started to grow.
It’s lightweight. Feels good in the hand—with cap posted or un posted. Writes well. It was a good pen to have pen when I’ve had to get a lot written done quickly.
The Explorer can use both sizes of the Pilots ink cartridges. A large Pilot cartridge comes with the pen. It also comes with a converter, the CON B bulb squeeze—isn’t the greatest. If you’re going to stick with ink cartridges, Don’t give it another thought.
If you’re going to or regularly want, to ink this pen, want to play with other inks or intend for it to be your, ‘go to’ pen. Get the CON 70 converter. I went brick and mortar for mine. I read too many reviews about people getting bad pen converters online. Go brick and mortar. Pilot cartridges GO in Pilot Pens.
Pilot Converters GO into Pilot pens.
I’m happy with this pen. I use it for a lot of writing and I use bottled ink. I use the CON 7.
I prefer my inks in the bott

title: Love this color
text: I I inked up a Pilot Metro with this ink. It lays down well using a fine nib. If I had a medium available to me, I think I’d use a broader nib. It looks good but I think a little more line would make it look better. Til then . I’m grooving on it with the tools I have. I really do enjoy the color.

title: Hooked by the company’s name
text: I have returned to writing after a several year hiatus. Admittedly this journal sped up, my process. I write in this book and several others, I’m using fountain pens exclusively. The ink lays down well and dries evenly. There’s no bleed thru nor does my nib collect fiber from the pages. Hope the quality remains high. And that Amazon continues to carry them while it does.

title: Not a rich deep turquoise, an okay greenish blue
text:
I loved how this ink color looked—in the samples provided online, in the bottles online. I bought it because I just had to write with it. I first used a small nib pen. The ink laid down well. It dried quickly. Fully dried, it looked green. I changed to a medium nib pen. Ink laid down well again. Again dried quickly. The color was an okay greenish blue.
It doesn’t look like the rich, vibrant ink samples, nor is it a “deep turquoise blue.”
No change in paper, pens or nib sizes could help this okay, unexciting greenish blue ink.

title: Works great
text: Met my expectations—Tape rolled off easily and stuck.

title: Great pen for beginners
text:
For starters, the pen is quickly ready to write. Just load a cartridge and give a couple shakes—be sure to do it over paper to catch any ink that comes out.
I’ve had it for two months. Use it almost everyday. Writes great with no leakage.
My only complaint is the cap. When it’s on the pen the weight feels good but it’s not balanced well for writing. It hangs heavy over my hand. The backwards pull quickly tires out my hand. So I write without the pen capped. Initially it felt a bit small not capped but that sensation went away after a few more sentences.
I love the pen, its bright green color and metal body. Imho it doesn’t look or feel cheap. Would definitely buy again.

title: Go to Fountain Pen.
text: Fantastic fountain pen. Writes like a dream. This is the second one I've purchased. I prefer the EF point. Excellent.

title: An absolutely wonderful pen! I am a bit of a pen ...
text: An absolutely wonderful pen! I am a bit of a pen snob, collector, appreciator... and this pen loves up to all the positive reviews. I can't wait to order the medium nib. Quick drying, works well for leftys!

title: Great for hall passes
text: I use these in my DYMO printer to print hall passes to our after school program. Kids are always in my room after school, and the ASP requires a pass when they come late. Also the pen smells horrible... don’t normally smell my pens but I caught a whiff of something on my hands then smelled the pen. HORRIBLE.

A few days later... yeah the pen I have inked with heart of darkness is not as black as I first thought. This ink as it drys starts turning a bit gray. It's obvious next to another sample I was comparing to with Lamy black ink.

title: It's a good notebook. Helpful size. Great price and arrived quickly!
text: I just received this notebook. Like a couple of other customers, I too LOVE Cambridge notebooks...for many years, but there's nothing wrong with this Mead Cambridge. It's a quality notebook and arrived pretty quickly after my order. I vividly recall paying quite a bit more for products that were labeled "Cambridge". This was very low cost and I think I received a book of a higher quality than the price charged. I'm not going to compare the spiral quality, etc. to others. That's been done and sometimes quality is in the eye of the beholder. I do a lot of writing with fountain pens. I just tested this book and didn't have any bleed-through. Will that always be the case? I don't know. Time will tell. I just saw a cheaply priced book, a name I knew from school, and for practicing letters or jotting down thoughts, it looks like this notebook will do just fine and again I'll say... look at the price. If you prefer another brand, then buy that one and don't order this cheaper notebook and complain about the quality. I've whittled down my lists on notebooks as the higher priced at an average of $16/book. Those higher priced books, as of yet, haven't equaled this Mead Cambridge, plus the higher priced ones are almost always are smaller in size - such as A5 and smaller. Just as with fountain pens, no one is always going to like everything someone else does. If you need a utility notebook give it a try. If you don't like it... then you're not out a lot of money. I've paid more for books of a lesser quality. Think about it... and give it a try. There is nothing "wrong" with this notebook. It's just a matter of preference. You might find that you are pleased with both this notebook's quality AND it's price! Oh, and mine came in a padded envelope. I've had small orders shipped in boxes too large for the contents before but maybe Amazon is becoming less wasteful.

text:
This pen is beautiful! There's no doubt about it & I bought it on looks. A month later, it finally arrived today & I was so excited! But I've used it for a few hours & I'm VERY DISAPPOINTED. The ink flow is awful. I can't get 1/2 way descent ink flow without having to push down so hard that I'm afraid the nib might break. Plus the force needed really hurts my hand. The item sheet says this is a medium nib but it writes like an extra fine. I get much better flow from the Pilot Metropolitan Fine Nib. I would think it's just me but I have the same problems with my Gullor. It's not the ink because it writes beautifully in another pen. This tip of the nib looks even more fine than my fine point pen's and the feed was out of place a bit.

This one looks pretty but I can't use it the way it is. I didn't try the converter because that won't make a difference. My only hope is to find good nibs to replace them both. I am really upset that it doesn't work well. ☹️ I had hoped this would be my "go to" pen because it is really so beautiful. But because of problems with both the Gullor and this JinHau, I've removed a set of JinHau pens from my cart. I'm afraid I'll have the same problems with the four I'd planned to purchase. title: Quality Paper for A Great Price
text:
I recently got an affordable TN, and while the inserts (that came with it) had what felt like substantial paper, it was slightly coarse (not fine and smooth). It can't really be seen upon inspection, but when I started using my fountain pen, the ink would find the tiniest creases between these coarse bits and make feathering-like lines that happened sporadically.

So, I picked up these Newstor inserts instead and I no longer have that problem. This paper is but smooth. The ink sits where I put it and there's no more of these tiny tails/spines shooting out from my letters or drawings when the ink found an invisible crevice. I also noticed that the covers had similar qualities when compared to the poor set that came with my book - the poor set had thick stiff covers, and the Newstor ones seem thinner, smoother but not lacking in strength.

I'm sticking with these inserts from now on. They're a great price for a good value.
