title: Easy to assemble and very sturdy + solid
text:
The keyboard tray is the last step of my ergonomic setup. I have an adjustable monitor stand, a new ergonomic task chair, and a standing desk- adjustable height of course. I have purchased another adjustable keyboard tray and have reviewed it, but ultimately kept this one. I will try to address some of the issues that others have reported.

The brackets and clamps are very sturdy. There is rubber material on each side of the clamp surface that comes into contact with the desktop. There is a bracket that screws to each clamp and there are 5 pairs of screw holes in each bracket for each of the five levels. The description claims that from the highest to the lowest setting there is a 4.5 inch range, but it's really about 2.25 inches, which annoys me. The size of the tray is listed as 26.8 x 11 inches. Front to back is actually 10.5"; there is a curved edge which shortens the usable size.

The tray surface is a textured plastic material. Although my mouse does track on it, I would recommend getting a mousepad as the surface is rough. There are tracks on each side of the tray and pushing it in and out is smooth. If I rest my arms on the tray there is virtually no flex or movement. When I slide the tray in and out it remains level.

Some people claim that the description of the height range is not accurate, and it's not (listed as 1.5- 5.75"). For a reference my desk is about 0.7" thick and on the 5th or lowest setting (most room) the tray sits 4.75" below the desk. On the 2nd level from the top the tray sits 2.85" below. The actual height of tray will be affected by the thickness of your desk- A thicker desk will have less room. If you have a very high desk and need to lower the tray, the maximum clearance measuring from the top surface of the desk to the top surface of the keyboard tray height will be approximately 5.5 inches.

Some people claim that there is a lot of wobble or that the the tray tilts as you slide it in and out. Mine does not tilt at all. I suspect people did not tighten their hardware enough, or mixed up the screws, or placed the brackets inside out, or mixed up the left and right hardware, etc. I tried to recreate the wobbling and tilting and I only could only do this if I loosened the screws. I think that these issues are attributed to user error. It's also possible that QC is not perfect and some trays are leaving the factory with less than ideal manufacturing tolerances, though I still think it's PEOPLE!!

Some people claim that the screws are too short. If however you have the tray at one of the upper height levels a longer screw will hit the track on the side. Therefore, the screws are the proper length!! You can see what happens in the photo when you use a longer screw- it sticks out. A longer screw will not make it sturdier.

So my cons:

1. The front to back distance is only 10.5", (listed as 11"). I would have liked to see 12" like some other models- more room for a mousepad or a second keyboard.

2. The adjustable distance is not listed accurately and does not have as versatile as the description claims- there is a range of about only about 2.3" instead of 4.25". This is not actually a problem for me because my desk height is adjustable. But if the tray hits your legs on the upper setting or is too high on the lowest setting you are out of luck and there is no further room to adjust it (this is unlikely I think, unless your desk is an odd size).

3. The sliding track on the right side is a little stiffer than the left. When I pull on the left side I can feel it moves just a little easier. I may take it apart and see if there is a problem- maybe some debris in the track or perhaps I tightened one side too much. I can also lubricate it, but it does not really affect the operation and is hardly noticeable, so I may just leave it alone.

So I spent days going through the different clamping keyboard trays on this website, and I really think that for most people this is the best option. You need to measure you desk and make sure things will fit properly, but this item is well made and versatile. I would ignore the 4% or 5% negative reviews as I think these can be attributed to user error. If somehow it does not work properly or does not work out you know you are covered for a return.

UPDATE: I purchased a second unit for work and this one is just as solid as the first one- no tilting or wobbling, etc.

UPDATE # 2- One side of the slider track was considerably looser and had less tension than the other. I'm not sure if it got worse or I just noticed it more, but after a week I contacted Amazon and asked for Vivo's contact info. While I was on hold they called the company and connected me to customer service and then a technician. I explained the issue and they sent me new slider brackets the next day. I receved them in about 3-4 days. The issue was with the left one- there was not enough tension. The problem is solved and I could not be happier. No matter how good a company or a product is, some items will leave the factory with defects. What matters is that customer service and support is there when you need it. I though I was going to have to speak to someone who could barely speak my language, or that I would wind up playing email tag for a month and never get the part that I need. I am amazed at how efficiently my issue was solved. Thank you Amazon and Vivo!!

title: Good, but not great
text:
I've been wanting to get one of these for a while and having a keyboard tray is really the last step ergonomically for my desk setup. It frees up the desk space and places the keyboard at the perfect height.

I chose the 27" model instead of the 20", even though my keyboards are smaller at 12-15 inches. I wasn't sure how well the mouse would track on the plastic drawer and I wanted to leave plenty of space for my mouse pad. This was a good idea. I also have two keyboard on the tray- one in front and one in back,, because I frequently switch between them.

Assembly took about 5 minutes and there are a total of 8 screws to assemble the clamps and brackets.
The C-clamps and brackets are super well made and sturdy. The keyboard drawer however is rather cheap and flimsy. I am not a fan of the texture, finish, or the lip on the front of the drawer. There is a piece of plastic that sits in a groove on the under side of the tray. This piece of plastic screws into the brackets that attach to the C-Clamps. As the drawer slides in and out you can hear and feel the plastic surfaces rubbing against each other, and this also adds to the feeling of cheapness. If you rest your arms on the tray it does flex a little bit (I imagine most do).

One reviewer (I don't remember if it was this tray or a similar one) was very upset that the clamps left marks on his wooden desk surface. There is a textured, rubber-like material that sits between the clamp and the desk surface, and I think this is what made the mark on his desk. I have a desk mat and this is what it is clamped to. Also my surface is black and a laminate material, so I would not be concerned. If you however have a fancy desk, it would not be a bad idea to put a piece of felt or something between.

There are 3 height settings for the tray and my tray is at the highest setting (with the least amount of clearance between the tray and the underside of the desk. It looks like the the thickness of the desk will affect how much clearance you have, but there are still 2 other setting that can be chosen. For reference my desk is 0.75" thick and there is exactly 3" of clearance at the current level.

If you are deciding on a model to get I STRONGLY ADVISE YOU to choose one that is adjustable. If you do not you are stuck with whatever predetermined height your tray comes in. In choosing a model this is in my opinion the most important feature of all. Most models will list the specs and you can measure you desk and determine at what height your keyboard will be at (most desks are around 30" high). I am a nut for ergonomics and I have a fancy chair (height adjustable of course), I have a standing desk which is also adjustable. The height of the tray is also adjustable as is the monitor. I am still not sure exactly which height I want to type at, but I have the luxury of pushing a button and raising and lowering the desk.

I have ordered another model with similar dimensions that has a metal track on the sides as opposed to the plastic groove underneath. We will see if it is smoother. One thing I will mention is that the tray STAYS IN PLACE when you type. I have noticed that for reviews on many models people complained that the draw would slide in as they are working, so perhaps a tray with a little more friction such as this one is more desirable.

One thing that this tray is lacking that I've noticed on other models is vertical edge on the back of the tray. They keyboard does not move, but when you slide the tray in and out the mouse sometimes falls off of the back of the tray.. These vertical edges were designed to prevent this. I thought it was ugly so I chose one without.

I hope that my remarks make your choosing of a keyboard tray a little more painless. I will include a few images as well.

title: Chair is for a shorter person like me-  Most comfortable chair I have ever sat in!
text:
I consider myself an office chair connoisseur and have owned about 10 and spent thousands. I am a big fan of the leather executive type chairs. However, they do not really give enough upright support if you are actively typing or working at your desk. They are usually for reclining and the chair position itself is kind of reclined.

The biggest issue I have had in the past is that most chairs are designed for taller people- my feet wouldn't touch the bottom, the seat is too long and the end digs into my thighs, and they didn't support my back in the right areas.

I purchased this from Staples and sat in every chair in the store until I decided on this one.

Pros:
-My feet touch the floor on the lowest setting and I can raise it higher if I choose
-The mesh is very breathable. You won't sweat on a hot summer day like plastic or leather. It supports your bodyweight different than leather. It is the tension of the fabric that supports your weight- like patio furniture
-The chair doesn't did into the back of my knees or under my thighs- the seat is the right length for my short legs.
- The chair is very upright- but comfortably so which I wanted.
- It is very comfortable to recline. The tension is adjustable and it supports all the right areas of the back, neck, and shoulders.
- Headrest is very comfortable. It is fixed but can be rotated up and down. Supports my head/neck in just the right spot.
- The armrests are very comfortable and adjustable. They are sturdy and don't wobble. They are not hard plastic like many of the chairs I tried. They are kind of a stiff foam type of material. An issue I've had with other armrests is as the padding wears out the hard plastic or metal beneath becomes very obvious. I like this texture and support/cushion.
-Cost!!! The retail price is $229 and it was on sale for $159. Many similar chairs I have seen are $3- $500.
- Appearance! The chair is very sharp looking. Would look great in a modern office setting or at home in your den or living room.

Cons: (very difficult to come up with any)
- Assembly was very easy- about 15 minutes. Instructions are simple because assembly is simple. However, the headrest took an additional 15-20 minutes. The holes in the headrest that the threaded screw holes in the back were ever so slightly misaligned which made it very difficult to line up the screws to thread properly. It is also difficult to support the weight of the headrest as you are lining up the screws. After trying several times I wore away enough material to line up the screws. This can happen at this price point- and I'm sure it happens at the $1k price point too!
-The base of the chair is a silver-grey that clashes a little with the red color of the chair. Black or graphite would have been a better choice.

By the way you CAN adjust the seatback and armrest width (many complain it's too narrow). When you secure the screws the holes are actually slotted. The back can be moved farther away from the seat and the armrests can be moved wider.

I just want to stress again that this is for a shorter person- I am 5'4 to 5'5 ish. If you are like 5'10 or taller the headrest and lumbar support may not line up properly. I WOULD HAVE SPENT MORE THAN $300 ON THIS CHAIR!!!

title: KEM cards have a very unique feel to them unlike any other playing card
text:
I've used these cards for years. They were always a pleasure to use. My preference was however for Dal Negro Trevisio. They were a little thicker and a little bit stiffer. They feel like paper and are very pleasurable to hold in the hand.

However, I've been using KEM cards and my biggest complaint was how they slide on each other. They are ever so slightly more flexible and smoother which make them easier to shuffle and handle. These are my new favorite and I'm a little disappointed that I have 25 other decks of cards which I like less than these. I'm happy I tried them all, but the KEM are my favorite. Now your subjective favorite can change just like your favorite painting on the wall. Besides being the most pleasant to handle and shuffle, they also have the most pleasing back design. Every poker house I have played in has used these cards, although sometimes in the bridge size, but that says something.

Edit: at the moment my favorite playing card is Dal Negro Trevisio. Here is a little tidbit of info. I recently opened the red deck of KEM cards. They felt stiffer cuz I thought they were new. Taking a caliper I could see that this red deck was 0.76 mm thicker than the blue counterpart (52 cards only). Whether this is normal meaning the red is always thicker, or there is variance between every deck I don't know. I would love to hear responses from others. The blue cards were new, meaning only opened and shuffled and never used for a game. I like to buy and try most cards, fearing I may be missing out on something I haven't tried.

Edit: The quality of these cards has changed in recent years. My last decks purchased sat in the original box, and inside another box for 18 months. My original deck which is about 15 years old is stored with it and is perfectly fine. The new ones are all cracked. If you've seen a photo that is 50 or 60 years old and the images is cracked all over- this is what it the surface looks and feels like. I cannot return them, but I will never buy them again. Obviously something has changed in the manufacturing process. Buyers be wary.

title: Nice cards, easy to handle, but not my favorite.
text:
I love the back design on these cards. They are also easy to shuffle. I don't like how one or two cards buckle under just a little pressure. However, I prefer the Italian cards like Dal Negro and Modiano. They are stiffer and more textured. They are more of a pleasure to handle and don't bend as easily. My KEM cards just sit in the case because I am usually using other cards. I love collecting decks and having options. I'm happy to oblige somebody if they like these, but my preference is truly for Modiano.

These are slicker so they slide together more easily when shuffling as well as rifling, but when push comes to shove I just love the substantial feel of the other cards. This is all very highly subjective. The only way you are going to know what is for you is to purchase 3 decks or so of the best rated cards and see for yourself if you like stiff, slick, textured, thin, thick, etc.

text: I started out with the A4 size notebook version of this, it has very good and smooth paper for fountain pen inks. The overall build on the the ones made in Poland (by a different manufacturer) is just awful. While the paper is the same, only the German-made ones seem to have the coating that is what causes the paper to be smooth for fountain pens. By far the worst thing (unless you exclusively use fountain pens (in which case the lack of paper coating would be worst)) is that the Poland-made ones have elastic bands that have long pins that poke through holes in the back cover to form a "T" shape that allows the bands tho stay in place. What's so bad is that these pins can stick out of the edges of the notebooks, make it annoying to keep the band from developing twists, make the band relatively loose, and (by far the worst part) cause the notebook to have two rather massive bumps in the top and bottom corner that you can feel and see either under your utensil or under your arm. title: it took me a few days to really love this pen
text:
I admit, it took me a few days to really love this pen. Initially, I was actually a little disappointed. The pen has written perfectly from the beginning, and the wood is gorgeous, BUT the plastic grip section of the pen feels very cheap in comparison; especially compared to the less expensive Sailor 1911 Standards and such. The plastic has obvious manufacturing seams, from the injection molding process, and I think that for a pen at this price point, those should NOT be visible. They can even be felt, if you run your hands along them at the right place.

However, once I got past the section, and began to evaluate the pen as a whole, I enjoyed it immensely. The pen has fantastic balance, posts well, and the wood is amazing. I would guess it is Bombay Blackwood, also known as Indian Rosewood. I am no expert on wood though. All I know is that the grain on the pen is gorgeous; it's hard to do a wooden pen well, but Sailor managed. The nib wrote very smoothly, with a touch of feedback (like most Sailor nibs, this writes how velvet feels). Evaluated as a package, it feels well crafted and like a high quality product. The name "Sailor Precious Wood" does not seem like hyperbole when I'm writing with this pen. It would have gotten a five out of five if the section plastic were better. There appears to be some sort of coating/lacquer/something on the pen that serves as protection from the elements, moisture, and apparently posting.

I would recommend the pen at this price, and also at it's full price, but ONLY if you like wood. High quality wooden fountain pens aren't as common as one might think, and this is a well executed example. I will probably sand down the seams of the injection molded section to enjoy the pen more, but even if I did not, the pen is just wonderful enough that I would still recommend it despite that flaw.

The other thing is that I can swap out the nibs in the Jinhaos with these Zebra G nibs and they write so much better than the Noodlers flex nibs.

I have been desperately wanting to improve my handwriting and wanted a pen that could give me that old fashioned, calligraphy style lettering . These Zebra G nibs totally do the trick!. I am able to write very fancy now ;>).

WARNING: Depending on the INK you are using and/or pen you may have to play around with getting the ink to flow. If you store your pen upside down it shouldn't be much of a problem, but if you find the ink has "dried up" just open your pen, if you have that style and "force feed" (very gently mind you, not too much) the ink back into the nib and write a few lines or gently tap the nib on a scrap paper to get it flowing again. ALSO for some reason using this nib and or the ink WILL BLEED on certain kinds of paper so be warned. I think it is more about the nib because I am using the same ink in a different pen and it bleeds far less, so just a warning. (can't use regular notebook paper)

Other than that, I am toying with getting yet ANOTHER Jinhao 450 and put another one of these nibs in that one too (with a different ink). You get 10 nibs to a box and I only had to replace it once when I accidently dropped my fountain pen on the floor and I think I messed up the nib.. no biggie.

text:

The pages are too thin for marker, but any dry medium or acrylic paint would work on this paper. The tooth of the paper is not as rough as I would like, but works with the mediums I use. The books lay flat so that you can draw something two paged. This book would work as a journal with a dip ink pen also, which is almost what I used it for.

Good art book for a decent price.

title: Plenty, but flawed
text:
[[VIDEOID:8c64ec2baaede3ce0825d4267f6f6115]] I ordered these tacks for stretching the canvas of paint-by-numbers purchased on Amazon. I have stretch frames here, and so stretched the canvases on, using staples. It worked, but not so well as using tacks. This box of tacks was perfect!
The tacks that are soldered correctly, are strong. There were a small percentage that had a failed solder point, but the ones with a successful solder point were strong. In the pictures with the failed solders, you can see a bent pin. The pins are very sharp, and most are flawless making easy to push into the wooden stress frame.
I feel this box is a great value for the contents.
As noted in the video, not all pins are perfectly centered, and the solder point makes a dimple on the dome of the push cap. If using these for dragon egg type art projects, the dimple and non-uniform style of center point will make them not the best choice for dragon egg crafts.
I feel that both the reject pins and tops would make excellent scraps for steampunk design creations.

title: Thick paper, correct size, messy asthetics
text:
[[VIDEOID:9f5341903e9cf99a8a07ae1ee86c4363]] I have several of these journals for drawing, writing, painting, dreaming... I love them! The pages are thick, the craftsmanship is very nice, truly handmade. Other sellers have provided the identity of my book's craftsman. I loved that touch. THIS company does not include that information.
I can use watercolor and acrylic paints with ease on these pages, as well as marker, colored pencil, and quill pen ink (Noodlers) and have no bleedthrough.
When sketching, I am disappointed when I have my rendering near complete, then ink its final form, and erase the pencil lines. Even with a soft high polymer eraser, and gum eraser, the paper will lose its surface dye, and come up in little fluffy of Cotton, like the old lined yellow scratch paper from grade school did. I don't like this about the paper. The distruction of the paper surface means that my watercolors will absorb differently. Vexing.
Another problem - which is purely esthetic - is that this paper edge choice is nice for creating the style of a vintage handmade book, however it looks sloppily done. Some pages are merely a quarter the width they should be, others are so wide they get bend when the book is bound up. I believe that if the labor of making antiquated pages is going to be put forth, an effort of keeping pages more uniform and within the binding would make the price point more reasonable. To me, a messy looking, fake vintage book in an inferior(but likable) leather binding for $30 or there abouts is ridiculous. I would expect fairly even and gilded ends for that price.
Overall, the book suits my needs, my disappointment is minimal, and should I find one for around $12 less money, I would buy one again.

title: Drafting and sketching - nice set!
text:
I have several mechanical pencil sets, however, this one I was very please with. The pencil design is not flimsy, and all pencils are clearly marked for lead size. Refilling each pencil is simple. There were two erasers in addition to the extremely small erasers that come inside each pencil. These interior pencil erasers are good for fine detail erasing, but the larger erasers are needed for eliminating pencil when rendering a final in ink.
What I was surprised and happy to find in the case, which holds all tools in the kit, was a pair of sharpeners for the thickest sketching lead pencils. These small sharpeners can be pinched between thumb and index finger being held firmly to quickly put a point on the heavy lead. An excellent addition to a mechanical pencil kit. These could be used on any large and soft lead pencil lead, such as a color pencil, if you don't want to have to wear down the pencil with a full wooden sharpening. I was happy to have a pair of these.
Overall, this collection is not $100 draftsman pencil quality, but the set gives an artist, draftsman, scientist, mathmatian, accountant, engineer, or student a great set that will last if kept in the case and proper care is taken. There is enough lead to last quite a while with every day use.

title: Trusted company of quality ink
text:
These ink packs, and this particular ink company are trustworthy. I had this printer for work prep at home. The ink quality was fantastic. The reason I purchased the printer itself was because I found E-Z ink company, and their products for this printer. The price for the milage you get for the ink is unbeatable. This is not my first purchase of these inks from this company. Every batch works well, and the inks last. I would trust this company for any compatible inks. I have tried other companies with previously owned printers(an epson), and the ink clogged the jet, and ruined the printer. The ink is clear and the programming chips on each ink cartridge are compatible with programing and are recognized as the correct color, and a new ink. This isn't always the case with other companies.

Depending on paper type and quality, and what resolution of printing you are doing, inks can be used slowly, or quickly. These inks, with word documents containing some charts and graphs, and colored headings, lasted for many reams of paper.

I am happy with my purchase. There is also a color only package that I will purchase in the near future when I make a printed photo album. 👍🏻

title: Journal with bag - lousy dye
text:
On first recept of the journal, I was pleased with the softness of the leather, and the style of the extended cover and longer wrap chord. It is a little timely to undo with one hand in the video, but it makes it certain it will not suddenly open when you don't want it too. It also can be tied in a way that will allow you to know if anyone has "used" it without permission.
The color is awful. I am uncertain what method they used to dye it, but the ocher color looks like it is straight out of the litter box, and is uneven and even "patterned" throughout the pages. The color is darker on the edges which leads me to believe it was died AFTER the page sizes were made. Also the pigment patters make it appear to be dyed while bound in the smaller bound packets that were later stitched to the cover. I disliked the color so much so, that I almost returned it. Not an aged brown like advertised. It us a yellow-brown-green...ocher. a walnut color would be much more pleasant with the cover, and natural looking.
The paper i nice for all pen types. I like glass calligraphy pens with Noodlers Ink. I have written, drawn, and "colored" in the book with a caligraphy glass pen. It does not suck up the ink or catch the fine nib. It is smooth. The paper does have a gridded look, so I am uncertain what paper making method is used. I am not accustomed to a textured paper of this kind, but it did not make a difference in use.
The book has fantastic craftsmanship, in that knots are not obvious, and the journal is solidly held together(see video). The leather is marred easily, but there are directions included as to how to remove indents and marks it picks up. The soft surface is unusual.
My favorite part of this purchase was the small cotton bag. I like books to stay covered. All reading books have dust jackets in cellophane, and journals are in boxes or bags. This bag is an easy bag made for the size of the book. It only fits the book, and is a bit snug. If you use the journal to store clippings or mixed media art, your journal will outgrow your little bag. This is a con for the journal. It is great for gifting the journal, but not for using the journal. I will crochet a cover for it at some point.

To sum it up:
Pros:
Well made
All inks can be used on paper(all media likely can be used)
Nice size
Nice gift
Cons:
Gift bag too small for long term use
Dyed color is horrid
Dyed pages are low quality with patterns
Would I buy it again? For a lot less money, I would buy it again. The quality of the dye job on the pages is inferior, as was the color choice and method. This is a book that meets the expectations of something under $15. I have purchase larger books with paper that was not quite as fine, but not inconsistently dyed, and not dyed an ugly color, for under $12. I think the price point for the problems with the book is the deal breaker for me.

title: Thick, well made, OOAK journal
text:
[[VIDEOID:a63c7900fbdbf802dce68522272486d1]] I had purchased a different brand with similar dimensions. It was the 8"x6" journal(rough size). I loved it, but this one came up in a suggestion when I was going to leave a review for the other book - which was excellent also. However, THIS book has a much nicer design for the leather strap and rivet to hold the strap in place, I need to add a picture of that come to think of it, and was TWICE the thickness. Yes, twice. THIS blue-black looks like it was pulled right from the midnight sky on a new moon. Gorgeous. It isn't so dark as to effect drawings.
The paper is smooth, and does not have the gridded look of muslin cloth, but rather the old fashioned method of making paper, where you could even add seeds and plant matter for recycling for compost. It is beautiful. The dying took place prior to making the page sizes because the dye is not darker at the torn edges, which authentically more pleasing. Glass pens, gell pens, felt pens, and other writing tools all will work on this paper service. When I set up to write or draw in this book, I will add a photo, video to show the results with the tool.
I paid slightly less than $24 US dollars because a lightening Deal/Daily Deal was being offered, however, once receiving this monster, I would have paid the full price of $29.99. The size and quality makes it worth it.
CON: The only thing I can pick on about the book itself is that the sections are bound in a manner that leaves giant open spaces at the binding point between the booklet sections inside the tome itself. It isn't the prettiest think when it flops open to the binding and you see the leather and tying and big gap. However, this is a known binding method, and I appreciate the craftsmanship I can see in this area of the book. Someon's hands, not a machine, put this together. A personal card with your artisan's name is included with your book. I will keep that forever. Someone on the planet made my book. That makes it special.
Wish: I wish this book came with a small draw string cloth bag. I have a reptile bag it will likely fit inside of, but something like that to protect it when traveling would have been a nice addition with the company name silkscreen on the bag. The smaller size biiks will likely travel - mine will- and the bag would have been a nice touch. title: Balanced smooth pen - excellent price.
text:
I purchased this red color, and a gold in the series. I have to say that for the price, it is a step up from other $14 dollar pens I have been using. I have not attempted to make one dropper fill yet, but it is on my list of things to try. I think these would not require the 'O' ring, and may just convert with some HEAVY grease. I will.poste if I convert and it is colossal fail or success.

title: Great little tool for scanning books or any type of symbol
text:
This scanner was purchased to scan book barcodes into a data system. It sees the codes and is compatible with the software. The only downside is that I cannot carrry the scanner to the shelf and scan the books, I have to bring all of the books to the computer because there is no wireless feature for this tool. Also, a stand would make this device much easier to use since it is not wireless and will be stationary for its purpose.
So,
function: five stars
Usability: four stars
If I could have it a 4.5, I would. It is light, so there is no fatigue from using it like some battery powered scan tools that can hold data. The cord is fairly long, so if I get the computer on a technology cart, it can reach most shelves and it is nearly "wireless" if plugged into a laptop. The code recognition is quick as well. When plugged in, it makes a loud beep through the device to let you know it is functioning. The laser is not on until the trigger is depressed, which is nice for leaving it plugged in - less battery drain, and no laser bar on a wall across the room.
In all this is exactly what I needed so I do not have to use a phone app for the data storage program and use data on my phone to scan. I will be.able to scan any other images that are available, such as information websites incuded in some books because this tool.picks them up as well.

title: Not a typical Parker pen.....
text:
The pen is made of a very light plastic, not the typical metal or heavier guage plastic of a Parker pen I have purchased in the past. What makes me a little curious is that this pen came with one ink cartridge, AND when I opened it, there was a converter inside already in place. Hmmm. Typically they are not included...but maybe they are now. I have not purchased on in a while, and never online.
When I put the cartridge inside, I pressed the nib to get the ink flowing. Nothing. I tapped the top of the pen to see if it was a bubble in the chamber, or if the bead had not floated away from the bottom. An ink splater came out on the paper. I figired I was now set to write. Still no ink came out. I applied enough pressure to separate the nib sides, and I could see no ink flow. I was disgusted. I put the pen upright and will take it apart tomorrow to see if it was not properly assembled, or if there is more going on here. I am disapointed to say the least. This may have been a bad run of pens - I will no more when I disassemble the pen. Every Parker or other lesser brand pen, even a child's student model with a bladder was ready to write as soon as I took it from the package and put in a cartridge. If anyone has a solution who purchased this pen, I would love a comment. This pen also took over two weeks to arrive.

Update: after taking the pen apart and reassembling it, the pen writes well!! I have increased from a 1 star to 3 stars. If the pen were not made out of thin plastic, and were a bit more reasy to use out of the box, I would give it a 4. So, for the price, and if you are willing to wait, the pen works. With a light touch, it is nearly fine point. With the slightest pressure, this pen will make blobs, and uneven lines. So, light deft movements when writing, and it works well. It will move smoothly over medium quality to fine quality paper. I am much happier than I was initially! A product just needs to work, and I will be pleased; the pen now works, and I use it daily.

title: hand held sharpener that works well
text:
I have seen the many pictures of broken pencil tips, a broken sharpener, and the statement that this sharpener will not sharpen Crayola. Well, I can only afford Crayola and no name pencils. This is not an electric sharpener where you jam the pencil inside and get a lethal tip. This is an artists tool. The pencil has to be lightly inserted, and turned against the sharpened edge as if you are shaving chocolate, not chipping tree brush. For extreme fine work, I agree that an artists hand held fine art sharpener, or an expensive eyeliner pencil sharpener you will get a more lasting fine point. Note that the razor is able to be replaced, and when it gets dull from shaving wood, which has a dulling effect, replacing the blade is your best option so that it does not ruin your expensive pencils.
I have ordered two now because I have a travel bag of pencils, and that sharpener is old. I would not hesitate to recommend this sharpener to people who know how to use hand held sharpeners, and have not dropped their pencils on the ground fracturing the led and believing the sharpener to be the cause. Colored led is very fragile, especially with the softer led types.

title: It's beautiful! Sturdy! Writes well! MY FIRST FP

It writes smoothly, and comes with 1 free plastic pen cartridge. Or, if you get bottled ink, you can load it up by dipping into the bottle and squeezing the top of the pen to activate the converter inside (see tiny manual).

I wrote a long, long letter to my friend last night with this pen. It was just as easy as writing with a regular pen - something I was worried about, as a newbie. The ink flowed out well but didn't splatter. I was able to write smoothly and consistently as thoughts came to me, without any hiccup.

If you're debating whether to get this pen or not, especially if you're an intimidated newbie like I was - JUST BUY IT! I got the Pilot Namiki Ink in black to go with it.

NOTE: It is perfect for my small hands. If you have large hands, this might not be the pen for you.

Sadly, 10 days after I opened my second Lemome journal, the binding split. I had heard this was an issue but never experienced it personally. I don’t be buying another one of these journals. 😕

This journal is just perfection. I am on my second one and just can’t say enough about it. Here’s what I love:
- the spine pen loop is amazing, efficient, smart, and space saving
-the pages are so incredibly smooth
-No ghosting!!
- the 120 gsm is perfection...not too thick, not too thin. I sent back my Archer and Olive and the new Scribbles because the pages felt like cardstock.
- the dots are not too light not too dark, they’re just right.
-the cover is incredibly satisfying to touch and hold. This may sound silly but think about how many times you pick up your journal...it should feel good.
- the bookmark is handy as is the back cover pocket

Here’s what I don’t love: Nothing to say here.

Here’s what I would maybe suggest:
-I would like more color choices. I plan to be a lifelong Lemome user so I need more choices besides brown and black. That being said, I bought a small patch and glued it to the cover to decorate it. It’s now personalized.
-I would prefer page numbers but it’s not a deal breaker

title: It's mostly really good!
text: This mechanical pencil has the right balance and weight (heft) to it that I find far exceeds the feel of plastic ones. It's mostly metal which I really like as well, except for one weak link in the design.  If you drop it on a hard surface, and it lands on the writing end, it can break some kind of plastic sleeve that resides in the barrel. If this sleeve breaks the pencil is rendered useless. This has happened twice to me.  I'm  on my third Graph Gear 1000. I put up with what I consider a design flaw in the pencil because I do like the "feel" of the pencil. I'm very careful now about trying to avoid dropping the pencil. For the expense of the pencil - it is more expensive than your typical mechanical pencil, it seems to me this "plastic sleeve" in the barrel could be either better designed, or made of metal.  One feature of the pencil I really like is that the clutch that holds the graphite in place allows the graphite to be placed back into the pencil. This saves me getting poked with the sharp writing end when I carry the pencil in my jeans pocket.

title: Works as described and worked well
text:
This is easy to use. It is a bit glitchy - the sliding feeder tray sticks sometimes so you have to sort of push the slide through. But this does not happen all the time, and when the slides are feeding normally it is quick and easy. I did not find the slide holder (where you put individual slides in and close the tray) to be useful. It took too much time to open the tray, insert the slides and then slide the tray into the machine. The easiest way, for me, was to use the slide feeder. I think you are supposed to be able to stack several slides in this and then feed them into the converter. However, I put slides in to the tray one at a time, slid the lever across and out pops the slide on the other side. I can see the picture and decide it I want to “capture” it to the SC card or not. Very easy and quick. I did hundred of slides and it probably took me 3 to 4 hours total. I have transferred them to my computer with the SD card and the quality of the pictures is good. I used the 10 pixel resolution, however. And I did not run out of room on the SD card.
The first SD card I got with the converter did not work. The converter could not read the card. I emailed the company and they replied right away to say they would send another SD card - which they did, again very quickly. So I have to say that customer service is A+. There are much more expensive converters out there, but this worked well for me. These slides are about 50 years old and the only slides we have. We don’t take slide photos anymore, so I don’t think we will be using the converter in the future. So we didn't want to spend a lot of money on a one time use item. This was perfect. Did the job easily, quickly and with satisfying results. I recommend it. The only reason I am giving any of the above areas 4 stars is that it is a bit “sticky” in the feeder tray. I think the color resolution is good, but I can’t really tell. Some of the slides are blurry - but who knows after all these years if that is due to the converter or the photographer! Overall, this is a good choice if you just want to get slides onto your computer for storage.

The ink cartridge is the international standard cartridge and can be filled with any bottled ink like Noodlers. I would only use ink for fountain pens. I know from experience that anything else can ruin the pen.
The cap screws on when posted.

I spent hours just petting my dragon.

text:

This is a really nice pen if you work on it. Still it wouldn't be good if you expected everything to go well right out of the box.

Nice and large, which is suitable for my taste. The cover’s color and texture are a classy touch. The paper is slightly cream-colored, which is more pleasant to write on, and the dots are lighter than other journals I have though still visible. The pages are left with right angles rather than rounded, as many brands of notebooks do.

One downside is that the elastic closure does leave an impression on the cover, which might bother some folks. It is super soft and also creases easily if textured items are left pressed on it. Storing it in a backpack will likely result in a lot of dings scuffing it up very quickly. It doesn’t sit quite as flat as I’d like, and the ink of a black gel pen can be seen on the reverse though it doesn’t bleed through. The paper is a decent weight, super smooth, and not too flimsy.

I’m giving it four stars because, for the price category, it’s pretty average. I usually use Molskein for sketching, and it doesn’t quite hit that standard. The cover stays scuffed if you drag a fingernail across it, and I can’t see it standing up to the abuse of being banged around during travel. It would look nice on a desk, though!
