text: Above all... excellent package! the pencils looks nice and have a high ended feeling, about the quality, the colors are fine and the range is very good. this pencils are not creamy as they seem, they are hard but still this are good. A bad thing, they have bloom and a waxy finish if you put pressure.

title: The do the job
text: They work and look nice

title: Great color, vibrant
text: Great color, vibrant, good for sketching. Wish the leads were just slightly softer as they do break without careful handling.

title: Not sure of what to do when the blade dulls but for now it's a good complement to my sliding cutter that does have replaceable ...
text: Ordered it a couple weeks ago and have already put it through three projects cutting heavy paper with no trouble. Not sure of what to do when the blade dulls but for now it's a good complement to my sliding cutter that does have replaceable blades. Keep in mind the handle is packaged separately in the box.

title: Was not expecting this at all!!
text:
So quiet, so smooth, very impressed.
Don’t hesitate. The best I know.

title: 1,2,3 easy to assemble and comfortable
text: This is exactly what was looking for. Easy to assemble 1,2,3 and it was ready. I use it at my workbench for drawing or working. Sturdy and rolls well.

title: Very nice and inexpensive too!
text: I bought these pen displays to put in an antique secretary display my antique pens. The pen displays are exactly as described and look great too! I would recommend them to anyone wanting to display their pens/pencils in a very nice, inexpensive way.

title: ... i had thought they would be but very very pretty! and the magnetic clasp is strong too
text: The beads were smaller than i had thought they would be but very very pretty! and the magnetic clasp is strong too. I recommend this product.

title: Very smooth to write with!
text: Beautiful color and drys instantly! I love it! Very smooth to write with! I will be ordering more colors!

title: Not What I Hoped For
text: I really wanted to like this pen, but the quality of the lines produced was very dissapointing. I experimented with several inks and the Picasso was consistently duller looking than with my other fountain pens. The line it makes is thicker than I'd like and the flow is unreliable. Very dissapointing considering that it's a very elegant looking pen.

title: Really good quality
text: These are really good quality shipping boxes. They're cut and scored cleanly and the corrugated cardboard itself is thick enough to be durable and looks really good.

title: Works well, a little thin
text: We're using this as a whiteboard on a whiteboard -- as a smaller note panel. It works well, erases cleanly. A couple of minor things for which I'm deducting a star: It's really thin, and it was shipped without cardboard in the package, so it arrived creased in a couple of places, and there's no way to get the creases out that I know of. They don't look too bad, though, so we're going with it. The other thing probably relates to its thinness, and that is the magnet backing isn't very strong. But it does stay put, and otherwise it looks good and works well.

title: Comfortable and works well
text: Just the right amount of cushioning to be comfortable. I'm not a big fan of memory foam since in my experience it just seems to go flat and not offer a lot of support. But the foam in these rests is firm enough to work nicely. The non-slip bottoms on these rests are a nice feature too.

title: Little one in our family loves these!
text: A little one in our family loves these! He calls them "round chairs" (we got the round version) and has played and played with them, stacking them and carrying them around and spreading them out and sitting. The colors are bright and cheerful and the bottoms are a gray slip-resistant fabric. They are shipped compressed and expand when the package is opened.

title: Good heavy duty packing tape
text: Good quality heavy duty packing tape. Works well. Sticks nicely. It has a little solvent odor out of the box, but that dissipates quickly after opening.

title: Looks like classic Kraft gummed packing tape
text: This tape looks like classic kraft gummed packing tape, but it's more convenient because it's adhesive and you don't have to wet it. It tears to length easily, so you don't need a special dispenser.

title: Nice bulletin board
text: Nice bulletin board with a lovely color fabric on one side and natural cork on the other. Mounting hardware for flush mounting to a wall is included, but I opted to drill a couple of holes in the back side of the frame and put a couple of short screws in and tie wire to them to hang it like a picture. I secured the bottom corners with some of that tacky memo-hanging putty stuff. Looks great.

title: These work nicely
text: These oil-based paint markers are good quality. They work best on non-porous surfaces (plastic, metal, glass, painted surfaces), but not as well on porous surfaces like fabric or cardboard (they're not as opaque on porous surfaces that soak up the pigment). They have a metal shaker ball in each marker for mixing. Since they are oil-based they have a solvent odor when using, but that's to be expected.

title: Works better than memory foam
text:
I came to realize that memory foam cushions are pretty useless, at least for me. They go flat when sitting on them. Sure, they'll return to their original shape, but when compressed they're not cushiony. (Same goes for memory foam shoe insoles. They just go flat.)

So I thought I'd give this cushion a try. And it works really well. It compresses some, but it doesn't go flat. I figure it must be comfortable because I don't think about it much when sitting on it. Most all the listing pictures show it without a cover, but it does come with one.

title: Good quality envelopes
text: Good quality security window envelopes. And none of the flaps were "pre-stuck" in the box.

title: Good addition to a sketching kit
text: Dividers like these are a great tool for marking out proportions on a sketch. These lock in place better than plastic ones I've tried.

title: Great addition to a sketching kit
text: The small set is a great addition to a field sketching kit. It's a great tool to easily lay out some parallel lines. To make one even more portable and suitable for smaller sketchbooks, you could trim the "wings" off and narrow the width.

title: Love this pen
text: I love the fude (bent nib) point on this pen. It's great for laying down expressive lines when sketching or drawing. I like the simple design and durable barrel. I loaded mine with Platinum Carbon Black ink and it works well, though it's a little hesitant to start sometimes. It's a waterproof ink that will handle watercolor washes without running once it is completely dry.

title: Good replacement
text: Nothing to complain about. It's a good-fitting remanufactured ink cartridge replacement and it works great. And saves money.

title: Spiral fill works great
text: This is a review for the spiral fill. It works great, expanding as you lift it out of the pack and shake it. It comes in several individual packs, so you don't have a problem with too much getting expanded all at once. A good use of recyclable packing materials.

title: LIght duty only
text: These boxes are cut and scored cleanly and fold well, but should be considered for light duty and non-fragile shipping only. The cardboard is pretty thin. The advantage to that is some weight savings.

title: Works well
text:
Great machine for small-run booklets or making your own notepads or sketchbooks.

This binding machine works well. It punches round holes cleanly. I didn't try to make it punch through more sheets at a time than it's capable of, so I got nice results. I noticed the seller recommends using chipboard backing sheets no thicker than 30 pt., and punching them one at a time. It's easy to find videos online on how to use one of these machines. Most of them work about the same way. The included coils will bind books or notepads up to about 1/4-inch in thickness. I didn't use the included specialty pliers to cut and bend the ends of the coils. I just used small wire cutters and small pliers.

When I made a couple of 4"X6" top-bound notepads, I found the four-inch width was too narrow to hit more than one of the internal alignment guides, so it was a bit of a challenge to position the sheets so they'd punch squarely. I just aligned them manually and still got good results.

There is no lock to hold the handle in the down position for storage. I used a long zip tie that I ran around a cross bar on the bottom of the machine to secure it.

title: Nice brown color
text: This ink is a nice brown shade and is water resistant when dry. It will stand up to watercolor in line-and-wash sketching. It has a slight alcohol smell in the bottle, but it's not noticeable when using in a pen.

title: Puts a very nice point on pencils
text: I like the easy operation of this pencil sharpener. Charge it up, then stick a pencil in and it takes it from there, sharpening it, then pushing it back out. It does wobble a bit when sharpening, but not much. It will accept pencils up to 8mm wide. I also like that you can adjust how sharp it makes the pencil points. With colored pencils, for example, you might not want a completely sharpened point that might break easily. And this vertical sharpener doesn't take up a lot of desk top real estate.

title: Nice smooth finish
text: Nice smooth finish, not glossy. It allows your hands to slide from side to side instead of pivoting at the wrist. The non-slip pads on the bottom work very well to keep it in place. Angle and height feel about right, although sometimes I put a little extra padding on top. It protects your wrists from the edges of a desk or table too.

title: Nice mailers
text: Nice mailers. The white exterior looks great. Good sturdy thickness, and well made. They fold nicely, and the interior dimensions are a full 8-by-8-by-8 inches.

title: Good quality
text: Very good quality poly mailers. The adhesive strip closure is nice and strong. The material is 2 mil thick, kind of light, but durable and it could save little on shipping cost. And the color is nice.

title: Nice bubble mailers
text: Very nice bubble mailers. They're not super thick, but they're well made and they'll do the job. Love the color choices too. We got the teal color and they look great.

title: Great for DVD or game shipping
text: These are sturdy enough for mailing DVDs or video games. The sides are perforated so the height is adjustable to fit the number of DVDs or games being shipped, up to four per box. Very convenient if you're shipping or mailing a few.

title: Works great
text: Great document camera. It comes with a USB-C to USB-A cord (about 6 feet long) for connecting to a PC. It's powered via USB. It does not have a microphone. It still could double as a web cam if you use a separate audio source. The built-in LED is a single light and is quite bright, maybe a little too bright when the camera is close to the subject, but the camera works well in ambient light too. Picture brightness is adjustable. It has several built-in resolution settings and a couple of different focus modes -- auto and fixed, and built-in rotation and mirroring adjustment. It focuses as close as about four inches from a document. The built-in zoom function doesn't work with the higher resolution setting. The base is heavy enough to hold the camera steady. BTW it works with Linux.

title: Nice Parker quality
text: Interesting barrel color choices available in this line of Parker fountain pens -- orange, green, and violet, the three secondary colors on a color wheel. Of course the pen itself is high quality, with good feel in hand and a smooth writing medium size stainless steel nib. The one I received came with two black ink cartridges and a converter (the slide-fill kind, used for refilling and using with bottled ink). I filled it with some Waterford brown ink, and it lays that ink down smoothly and evenly.

title: Cool retro looking thermal small label printer
text: The first thing to know about this printer is it is not for printing full size mailing labels. It prints small labels, about 1.25 X 2 inches. It has a cute retro look, and it makes cute sounds when printing. It doesn't connect to a PC. It works through an app on a portable device. It's wireless, battery powered, and recharges through a USB cord. It does come with a roll of printing paper labels. Since it's thermal, no ink is required. It's black and white printing only, and not high resolution. But for small labels, it works great, and it looks really cute.

title: Work great
text: Anytime you order Sharpies and they arrive fresh and loaded with ink instead of nearly dried out, it's a win. These arrived fresh and fully charged with ink.

title: Good boxes, true to size
text: These are good mailing boxes. Good quality corrugated cardboard. I checked the measurements -- they are a full 5x5x5 inches on the inside. Actually they're just a little over five inches, which is a good thing.

title: Cool mechanical pencils
text: The auto-rotating feature that keeps the lead turning as you write is inventive. As other reviewers point out, the blue one comes with black lead, so you'll need to remove that and install blue lead from the package. The blue lead writes nice and dark, the red lead not so much. It would be nice if the red wrote as dark as the blue lead.

title: Glossy plastic
text: Nice clipboards and they work well. Just to let you know, these are glossy plastic with a very smooth finish. They're pretty reflective and they do show fingerprints. The clips are nice and springy, and the 6x9-inch size holds half-letter size sheets nicely.

title: Good notebook cover
text: Really nothing to complain about here. It's a simple and well made notebook cover, water repellent (not waterproof). It has a good quality zipper, and a place for four pens and pencils, as well as an extra pocket for loose notes or other flat things.

title: Great cart for shopping and other uses
text: I had this cart assembled in minutes. The larger wheels simply snap on by pressing a button, and they can  be removed just as easily when you need to fold the cart and store it flat. It's a pretty large sized cart, and the handle can be adjusted in height. The stair wheels work well. It's well made. It could easily be used for a laundry cart or cleaning supplies cart.

title: Really good whiteboard
text:
I had this kit together in about an hour. That includes the time I spent trying out the optional lower whiteboard mount position. I opted for the higher one.

There are only two sizes of screws, so assembly is pretty simple. The instructions are clear enough. It comes with assembly tools.

It arrived well packed with no shipping damage that I could find. There was a little crease in one of the channels that surround the whiteboard, but it's very minor and the both sides of the whiteboard itself were fine.

The casters roll easily and are durable. They're metal contruction with rubberized non-marring wheels. All four of them have locks.

The whiteboard pivots on a couple of axles that rest in slots in the side tubes. It can only be locked in a vertical position.

It will hold up to 12 letter-sized pages (8.5 inches by 11 inches) in portrait orientation on each side, a total of 24 using both sides. Push-pin style magnets are handy for that.

title: One of the better lap desks
text: I've bought and tried several lap desks over the years. Most of them wound up tossed away or sitting on a shelf. This is one of the better ones. The design is well thought out. The cushion height is great, and so the way the middle one will fold back to double the height of the back one. The device slots are handy. And so are the fabric pockets on the back cushion. I also like the rubberized mouse pad and the integrated wrist rest. And it's not too heavy. Good lap desk.

title: Good binder
text: Well made binder. The hinge parts seem strong. It does have translucent pockets in the inside front and back covers, as well as the outside. The D rings allow pages to lay flat, and you don't have to hold up the binder and shake it to center the pages in order to close it. You can just close it. The lever does open the rings easily. I find it easier to close them just by squeezing the rings together. And the front cover can be folded all the way back behind the binder. I like that it's made from a material that won't stick to copy machine or laser printing toner.

title: Quality tape, sticks well
text:
This packing tape fits standard dispensers and tape guns. The adhesive seems to be a little different than brand name tape, because the tape comes off the roll smoothly and pretty quietly compared to brand name tape. It's hard to tell, but the tape itself seems to be a little thin, but I tried tearing it and it seems just as strong as brand name tape. I also gave it a bit of a test. We're in a heat wave with high humidity, so I stuck a strip of the tape on a corrugated cardboard box and left it outside overnight to see if it stayed stuck. And it did.

The only negative is that this tape does have a bit of odor when the wrapper is removed. It's not a bad odor, but it's not really pleasant either. I'm just keeping the tape and dispenser in a storage container with a lid.

title: Good quality strong clips
text: The large size accomodates stacks of paper over a half inch thick. The clips are well made and the wire handles bend a little but spring right back to shape when using. They're strong enough and the quality is good, however, I did notice a tiny bit of paint and rust marring on some white paper on first use. I suggest clipping them to some coarse fabric like denim or canvas or some thick cardboard and pulling them a couple of times to clean them first.

title: Really like the 1.0 bold point G2
text: I really like the 1.0 bold point G2 pens. They're smooth writing and of course bold. It would be nice if Pilot would make bold point refills available in turquoise color too. Teal is nice, but I also like the turquoise.

title: Great for fountain pen lovers
text: Great pens if you like fountain pens but don't want to spend big bucks for top dollar brands. These are sold as disposable, but people have come up with clever ways to refill them. You can look around online if you're interested in that. If you're new to fountain pens, note that the ink is not instant dry---it takes a few seconds before it's smear proof. And they will not write on smooth non-porous surfaces. And the ink is definitely not water resistant once dry. If you want water resistance, choose a marker or pencil for that.

title: Good alternative to burning boxes
text:
Like a lot of people, I'm kind of a stickler about not throwing things away with readable personal information. Until recently I shredded some things and burned the rest---including the cardboard boxes with sticky labels that can't be shredded---in a fire pit in our yard.

Now our state's environmental division has issued a ban on all outdoor burning of trash for the summer. So I decided to give this roller stamp a try.

It works great! Sometimes it takes a couple of passes to get a an address or bar code completely obscured, but it does work. And it's easier than using a hair dryer to remove sticky labels from boxes before recycling. Just roll over the bar codes and addresses and done.

The roller comes with three ink refills, a nice addition.

title: Fun and well made
text:
It's kind of fun to check the accuracy of kitchen and postage scales. I was surprised to discover that a scale I thought was inaccurate was actually very accurate.

These calibration weights are well made with a polished chrome finish. A little off-label idea for the large (100g) one is to run the top under very warm tap water and apply it to a mosquito bite for a few seconds to relieve the itching. It holds it's heat longer than a spoon, which is the traditional tool for that trick.

title: Biodegradable and convenient
text:
I like this honeycomb kraft paper. It's space-saving because unlike bubble wrap, it stores flat on the roll until you use it. You just stretch it and it forms into cushioning wrap. It's biodegradable too.

It doesn't claim to be acid free, so you might want to wrap some items that might be affected by acidity in an acid free tissue paper before wrapping them with this packaging.

title: Good academic quality markers
text: These are "schoolhouse" quality markers at a good price. They're not premium quality, the paint is a little thin, but they're really good budget markers.

title: Good quality
text: Good quality labels with good adhesive. Works well in a thermal printer and produces sharp results.

title: Small footprint, sharp printing
text:
This thermal printer has a small desktop footprint and produces sharply-printed labels. It comes with a label caddy tray that accepts both roll type and folded type labels. The tray actually has a larger desktop footprint than the printer.

Note that this is a wired printer, not wireless. It requires a power supply (included) and USB connection. A USB-C adapter is included.

title: Interesting paper for pen and ink
text:
I'm giving this paper five stars because it is a high quality, smooth finish paper. It's printer paper, and not tailored for pen and ink, but I got it for pen and ink because I read a few remarks online that it's good for that.

I tried three colors of Varsity disposable fountain pens (black, turquoise, and red) and the results varied. The black ink didn't feather much at all, resulting in a thin line. The turquoise feathered a lot. The paper seemed to be pulling a lot of ink from the nib. The red was somewhere in between, with a little feathering.

I also tried three colors of ultra fine Sharpies (again, black, turquoise, and red). The black did okay, but the paper seemed to dry out the turquoise and red pens almost on contact. Maybe in this case the paper wasn't absorbent *enough* to start the ink.

I tried Pilot G2 gel pens (same three colors) and got good results, but the paper is so smooth it seemed like it wasn't giving the roller balls a lot of traction, so there was some minor skipping.

These comments may sound like complaints, but I'm happy with the paper and will continue to use fountain pens with it. And maybe gel pens sometimes. And of course mechanical pencils. The paper's smooth finish works very nicely with those.

title: Just right for US letter-sized paper or books
text:
The interior dimensions of these boxes are a smidgen over 8.5 by 11 inches, which is just right for US letter-sized paper or books. The extra space allows room for the side tabs to be inserted. The interior height allows for a stack of pages or books about 1 and 7/8 inches tall -- just shy of 2 inches. You might could make a full two-inch stack fit, but the top might stick up a bit.

The corrugated cardboard material is sturdy enough for shipping, the die-cutting is consistent and the boxes fold easily (they're shipped unfolded in flat bundles).

title: Good paper, vivid prints
text:
This paper does make vivid color prints. And since it's very matte, the prints appear detailed and are glare-free. Some things you should know about:

- It's thick paper. It might not run well through some inkjet printers. I had success by stacking some regular printer paper behind it in the feed tray.
- Some minor streaking from the inkjet printer head passes is visible on the print. I was using a standard printer, not a photo printer, so your results may vary.
- There is a good side and not-as-good side with this paper. It's easy to tell the difference once you make a test print: the good side is much more colorful. Unfortunately both sides pretty much feel the same, and there's no watermark on the paper to identify the back. So I think the thing to do is to remember which way they're stacked in the original package---which, by the way, is just a transparent plastic sleeve with a cover page and a cardstock backing.

I'm going to go ahead and give it five stars because the printed colors are vivid, and I think a photo printer might yield even better results.

title: Smoothest writing G2 gel pen
text: In my opinion this bold 1.0 version of the Pilot G2 is the smoothest writing version of the G2. The ink colors in this five-color assortment are burgundy, purple, teal, blue, and black.

title: Great pen and pencil organizer
text: This thing comes fully assembled and ready to use. It's small enough for most desktops but still holds a lot of pencils, pens, or other supplies. It's well designed with a rotating base. My artist friend likes loading colored pencils in it with the points down so it's easier to see the barrel color of each one.

title: Not the colors I expected, but they're really good pens
text:
I expected to get the "fashion color" assortment. I got something else---black, red, green, dark blue. The blue is so dark it's difficult to distinguish it from black.

Here's the deal, though: These Bic Gel-ocity pens are really smooth writers, even in the "fine" (0.5mm) variety. They don't feel scratchy on paper. I don't know if it's the ink or the pen itself, but they're good pens. And 36 pens is a lot of pens! By the way these are snap-on cap pens, not retractables.

title: Great binder rings
text: Great rings for presentation cards, note cards, or letter-sized documents when you want to be able to fold them completely back for reading. The rings are well made and work well.

title: Quality leather, very well made
text:
Lots to like here. The leather is indeed very good quality. The build quality is very good. And it is real leather, and it smells like real leather.

The pad holding sleeve is open top and bottom, which means the organizer can be set up either right or left. There are plenty of storage spaces, credit card slots, three pen/pencil loops, and a couple of zippered compartments. It will hold a slim book, a tablet, a pad, pens, pencils, cell phone, and other items.

It's the kind of leather that can be treated and renewed and softened. An inexpensive alternative to neatsfoot oil is olive oil. And olive oil won't darken leather as much as neatsfoot oil or mink oil. However, olive oil has to be reapplied more often. Just put a few drops on a microfiber cloth or paper towel and rub it into the leather areas. Wipe off any excess. Allow the organizer a day to dry.

The only nitpicking complaint I might have is that the amount it can expand is limited to about an inch---that is, if you still want the zipper closure to work. I think a wider zipper could increase that. Otherwise this is very nice leather folio/organizer.

title: Great photo print paper if your printer accepts heavy cardstock
text:
This glossy photo paper is thicker than most photo print paper. It's postcard thick. Since our inkjet printer is rear feed, I thought it would handle it. It did accept and print a couple of sheets, with beautiful results. However, it struggled a lot when accepting any additional sheets. And the sheets that did print had a faint guide wheel crease embossed in them, probably indicating what a tight squeeze this thick paper was in our printer. I'd recommend you check to make sure your printer can handle heavy cardstock before you order.

The paper quality and finish are outstanding. Both sides of the paper are glossy, but one side is a little smoother than the other. That's the side you'll probably want facing up in your printer.

title: Nice looking bulletin board
text: This bulletin board is reversible---fabric finish on one side, natural cork on the other. It comes nicely packed. Mounting is pretty straightforward. It comes with the hardware (screws and wall anchors) and simple illustrated instructions. And it comes with snap-in corner pieces to hide the screws and provide a nice finished look.

title: Good quality
text: These are well made journals. They look great, and they will lay flat when open if you give them a little back bend. The 128 pages are actually 64 sheets, counted front and back. The line spacing is a little over 1/4 inch. There are two slashes printed at the top for writing in a date if you choose to. The paper is like a good quality 20-lb printer paper. The claims of no bleed-through or ghosting may be a bit exaggerated. See the photos. Sharpie Ultra Fine markers did bleed through a bit, but then Sharpies will bleed through most any average-weight paper. Pilot G-2 Gel pens had zero bleed. I don't think the paper would hold up to water-based media. The expandable pocket on the back cover has satin fabric-like expanding ends and looks durable. As I mentioned, they are well made, and they come nicely packed and individually shrink wrapped.

title: I really like the mini size G2
text: Some people might find a short-length pen or pencil uncomfortable to write with, but I like the mini size G2 pens and mechanical pencils. They fit in most any pocket or EDC bag. The gel pens are smooth writing.

title: Good quality
text:
I'm not a hundred percent sure the gummed adhesive will seal these envelopes securely for mailing, but they also have a clasp, and I usually stick a piece of packing tape across the flaps of clasp envelopes to cover the clasp and make sure they stay sealed.

Otherwise these are well made and the thickness of the kraft paper is about what you'd expect for a 6x9-inch envelope.

title: Great pens
text: I really like the compact size of these mini G-2's. They write smoothly, and the turquoise color ink is dark enough to be legible even on green paper.

title: Good quality wire paper clips
text:
The first thing I did was test the quality of the wire of these paper clips by unbending and bending a couple of them. When the wire is poor quality, it will break after only a couple of bends (work hardening). These are made of great quality wire. I bent and unbent them several times, and though they got a little stiffer, they did not break.

The wire is slim too, which will make these handy for opening media trays in devices.

The finish is smooth, and they're sure to stand up to repeated use.

title: Easy assembly, looks great
text:
I had this storage shelf unit assembled in about 15 minutes. It was easy. It goes together with four small wooden pegs and four screws. A screwdriver is included in the kit. You could add glue to the wooden pegs to make everything stronger, but I just assembled it without glue.

The back panel on the one I received had snapped in two, but since it fits in a slot in the back, I didn't even bother to glue it together. The slot holds everything in place sturdily and it doesn't even appear to have snapped.

I got the model with the top tray, and I recommend that one. It adds more usefulness. The top tray comes preassembled, and is held to the top of the cabinet with four fairly strong magnets, a nice touch. You wouldn't want it sliding off and spilling your pens and pencils and other supplies everywhere.

The interior dimensions of each level are a little under 13.5 inches wide and 9.5 inches deep. They will easily hold 8.5"x11" letter size paper, and also hold 9"x12" paper or envelopes. They are not wide enough for legal size paper (8.5"x14").

It's a good kit. Everything fits, it goes together easily, and looks great when finished.

title: This one hits the sweet spot
text:
I don't know how many lap desks I have ordered and tried out. I know I already had three on hand before I ordered this one, and that's not counting the ones I threw out, and also not counting the one I made myself with a thin sheet of plywood just sitting on a pillow.

I know that previous ones had the same issues for me: First, that bead foam filling in the padding. It always seems to lose its loft and bunch up and pretty much goes flat. And the cushion bags are made and attached in a way that makes replacement or adding beads very difficult. I think that's the main reason I threw out a couple of lap desks.

I also found I wasn't too fond of sectioned lap desks that have one part that will tilt independent of the rest. I just didn't use that feature much.

So I found this one and ordered it. It really hits the sweet spot. It holds a fifteen-inch laptop easily. And it will hold a full size keyboard, the kind with a built in ten key pad. The padding underneath is a firm foam---no beads---in a fabric that can be wiped clean. It doesn't get hot. And it's one piece. A simple design, and I'm already using it practically daily.

Incidentally, there's really no room for a mouse on this lapdesk when using a full size keyboard on it. So if you use it for that, you'll need a place for the mouse nearby.

title: A little thin, but they print beautifully
text: These 2.5-inch round kraft brown labels are a little on the thin side, but they print beautifully in an inkjet printer. We haven't tried them in a laser printer so we don't know how the adhesive would hold up to the heat. A friend who has a paper flower hobby home business tried printing her logo on them and the results were great. They even show colors well despite the brown kraft paper tone. The packaging does not list the template number for these labels but Avery 22856 works, or you can set up your own template in Microsoft Office or LibreOffice.

title: Great little boxes
text: These are a thin corrugated cardboard (not chipboard) and are lightweight but sturdy enough to be used for shipping and mailing small items. They're also great as the inner box when double boxing delicate items like porcelain figurines and such. The similar 4X4X4-inch size boxes fit nicely in this 5x5x5-inch size box for that purpose. The white finish gives them a bit more elegant look than unfinished corrugated boxes.

title: Great little boxes
text: These are a thin corrugated cardboard (not chipboard) and are lightweight but sturdy enough to be used for shipping and mailing small items. They're also great as the inner box when double boxing delicate items like porcelain figurines and such. This 4X4X4-inch size fits nicely in the similar 5x5x5-inch size box for that purpose. The white finish gives them a bit more elegant look than unfinished corrugated boxes.

title: Good journal
text: This is a well made dotted-paper journal and it will open completely and lay flat, which is a nice feature for taking notes or sketching. I would point out that though the paper in this journal is pretty heavy at 100 gsm, there are other journals available with even thicker 120 gsm paper. Which you prefer is up to you, but with this journal I would avoid water-based media or inks or pens that are prone to soak through paper, and stick with ballpoints or gel pens and pencils. It has an elastic band to hold it closed, and an elastic pen/pencil loop. It also has three placeholder ribbons, a nice touch. Another nice touch is the pocket on the inside of the back cover is expandable.

title: Great set of binder pockets
text: These translucent PVC pouches/pockets are thick enough to be durable. You get four credit-card sized divider pouches, four photo-sized divider pouches, and four "bill sized" pouches that are single pouches without dividers. The prepunched holes line up perfectly with the binder rings. There is no zippered pouch for pens and pencils, but there are three bill/money pouches without dividers that will work okay for that. They have a simple flap closure on top that will keep things from falling out.

title: Nice, well-made journals
text: The paper is thick and smooth just as advertised in the listing, and the grid is an unobtrusive but visible gray. The binding is very nice. The pink color of the cover in the black-and-pink set is a coral shade. The pen loops are a little snug but it will probably loosen with use over time. Overall these are well made journals at a good price.

title: Awesome all-in-one machine with versatile scanning options
text:
I had this office quality monochrome laser printing/scanning/copy machine set up and operating in less than 20 minutes without a hitch. A software CD is included, but it wasn't needed for setup. Once we had it connected to our WiFi network, our Mac iOS and Linux computers recognized and operated it as a printer right away. The Mac recognized the scan function too.

Speaking of scanning, this machine does both sheet fed scanning and flatbed scanning/copying/faxing. All functions are operable directly from the touch screen control panel (which is simple and intuitive) as well as from your computer.

There are several connectivity options, including corded via USB or Ethernet cable, or WiFi wireless. The most secure means to print documents is via corded connection, but Lexmark includes "full spectrum security" as an option.

I didn't put a timer on it to see if it really prints 42 pages per minute, but it is fast, and the print quality is of course laser printer sharp. And it does two-sided printing.

There's a lot to like here. The only minor negative is that it is a monochrome printer (black toner only) and not full color. But I owned a color laser printer for years and was never too impressed with its color output or reproduction. I think ink jet printers are better at that. Laser printers excel at super sharp and cost effective black and white printing, and laser printed pages are water resistant---they don't smear and spread if a bit of water drops on them like ink jet ink tends to do.

title: Big home office shredder
text:
This crosscut shredder is a little bigger than a tall kitchen trash can. It's not a toy. It's suitable for office use. It's heavy and has a strong motor. The bin holds a lot of shredded paper. The shred pieces are about 1/4-inch by one-inch. It will shred plastic cards and CDs or DVDs.

A couple of things I really like about it: It comes fully assembled, including the casters. It's also NOT top heavy, which I found to be the case with another shredder. You unbox it, remove the tape securing the bin (which is the slide-out kind; you don't have to lift off a heavy top section), plug it in, and it's good to go.

The only minor negative is it does make a little noise. But it's not enough to complain about.

Good shredder.

title: Nice set of marker pens, and they're erasable
text:
If you're new to Frixion pens, like I was, the ink is thermo-sensitive, and will disappear when heat is applied. All it takes is the heat from friction of a hard eraser (friction, Frixion, get it?) and whatever you wrote will vanish. You don't have to rub hard, just briskly, and it will work. Interestingly, you can make the ink reappear---to some extent---by putting whatever you wrote on in a freezer for a while.

Each of the marker pens in this 10-pen set has a hard rubber end on the cap to use as an eraser---actually just a heat generator. The eraser itself wears down little if at all. It's sure to outlast the ink supply in the pen. The manufacturer still calls the ink "gel" ink but these pens write like most any regular marker pens.

Some crafters use these pens to mark fabric, then use a warm iron to make the marks disappear. A hair dryer will work too.

This is a fun set of erasable marker pens, they do write in a fine line, and the colors are nice and bright.

title: Pentel white erasers are the best
text: Pentel white erasers work. They erase cleanly. I bought a couple by another brand name manufacturer and they just sort of smeared the pencil graphite around without really erasing. But the Pentel brand eraser effectively removes almost all the graphite without tearing or damaging the paper surface. You can get them as pencil-end (the kind that stick on) or in block form. The retractable erasers are handy and pocketable.

title: Okay, but not for heavy items
text: This 1/2" bubble wrap is made from rather thin plastic. The bubbles pop easily. I'd recommend using it for lightweight items only. Heavy items would likely flatten it in transit.

title: I painted one turquoise before I found this one
text:
I love Pentel Twist-Erase 0.7 mechanical pencils. I love the grip, I love the eraser. I load mine with Uni-ball 2b diamond-infused leads, which make a nice dark line that's still erasable.

I wanted a turquoise Twist-Erase though. I had no idea Pentel made a turquoise version, so I painted one turquoise. The top one in the photo is the one I painted. When I discovered Pentel did make a turquoise one, I ordered it. I'm not sure which one I like better. I like them both.

If you decide you want to paint one a custom color, here are a few tips: Disassemble the pencil: Pull the barrel apart, unscrew the tip, pull off the pocket clip and the rubberized grip. Mask the area the rubberized grip covers, and stuff the barrel openings so no paint gets inside or on the eraser or on the tube that holds the leads. Sand the barrels lightly with fine grit paper. Sand some of the diameter off the lower barrel where it goes into the top barrel---if you don't, the paint adds thickness and the fit will be too tight when you reassemble the pencil. I used bamboo skewers to hold the barrels while painting.

Use a good quality spray paint. I used Rustoleum 2X Ultra Cover paint (I think I used the shade called Seaside). A couple of light coats will do it. Then be patient and wait a couple of weeks for the paint to bond and cure fully before reassembling or using the pencil. A little paraffin wax rubbed on the part of the lower barrel that inserts into the upper barrel will help the pencil operate smoothly after reassembling.

title: Cute, well made, nice design
text: See the pictures. This is a really cute pop-up holiday card, lots of decorative details, evocative of a snow globe. Love the duplex paper envelope, a nice detail. The card took a little experimenting to open up. It's not that difficult though -- you just pull up the clear layer from the top. Two perforated tabs on the bottom of the card can be folded in to lock the card in the open, display position.

title: A bit of a step up from similar carts
text:
I already own two similar rolling carts, and this one from Amazon Basics is a bit of a step up. Assembly was a little easier than the other two. The frame snaps together instead of using screws. Only 12 screws are required to mount the trays to the frame, and all the screws are the same size. (2 extras are included, by the way.) The casters screw in, and that's it. Done. Necessary tools are included.

Two other things make this a step up from similar carts: a metal pegboard on one side with three repositionable accessory baskets, and two metal storage tins with magnetic backs and clear lids. The metal pegboard is easy to install and needs no hardware or tools---it hangs by tabs from the trays.

It comes very well packed and includes picture-book type assembly instructions. I had it assembled and ready for use in about a half hour. Here's a tip: lay the cart frame on its side when installing the trays. It makes putting the screws in a lot easier.

title: Beautiful smooth writing pen
text: The Blue Wave rollerball pen is beautiful. The etched wave design adds elegance. The blue lacquered barrel has a lovely satin finish and has a great in-hand feel. And it's possibly the smoothest-writing rollerball I've ever tried. It lays down ink like a fountain pen. It comes in a nice box so it would make a nice gift too.

title: Lovely fountain pen set
text:
This is a lovely fountain pen set, complete with cartridges and a converter for refilling with bottled ink (included), a microfiber cloth, and a detailed instruction booklet. And it all comes in a nice box that makes it a great gift too.

The pen has a light feel. I was surprised that it's stainless steel; the light weight makes it feel more like aluminum. As far as other in-hand qualities, if you have large hands it is a little short without the cap on the end. But the pen does feel smooth.

The line thickness when writing is about medium. I compared it to some pigment liner pens and it just about matches the thickness of the .05 pen. It's not bold or too fat a line, but it's not a fine point. The point doesn't feel scratchy on the paper when writing.

Overall a really nice set.

title: Easy assembly, sturdy, looks nice
text: Assembly of this cart was pretty straightforward and easy. The thing to remember with all kits like this is to not overtighten the screws, just snug them firmly. The wheels roll easily. It's a handy, sturdy cart and looks nice.

title: Love the design and build quality
text: This is a step above most plastic crates you find for sale. The plastic is heavy duty, and the design of this crate is well thought out. It's solid and sturdy when unfolded.

title: Great little set, great box
text:
A couple of reviewers have already mentioned the box this set comes in, but it is a cute, colorful box, with divided sections. It really is much like a gift box or presentation box.

All the pens and pencils in this assortment are Bic quality, of course. Most all have soft grips. There are two highlighters, four ballpoint pens (two medium, two fine point), two mechanical pencils, and two gel pens (one blue and one black).

Great little set, and a great box.

title: Good accessory
text:
It's a good accessory for transcribing notes or documents. It's not so good on a big monitor. The document winds up parallel to the monitor and hanging way out to the side of your field of view. It might be better if there were another hinge in it that would allow the user to angle the document more inward. It also might be better if the clip that holds the documents or notes were rotatable so the user could level it up. If there's any incline to your monitor the clip is inclined too.

It's nice that it came with two Command strips. I installed it upside down the first try, so having that extra strip for a do-over was handy.

title: Assembly is a little challenging but it's cute
text: Assembly is a little challenging because the instructions are pictures only and the parts aren't numbered. I eventually got things sorted out. It took about a half hour to put together. Quality of the finish is good, it seems pretty durable, and it's really cute once assembled.

title: Hold up to repeated bends
text: Good quality wire that holds up to repeated bends. We used them to make white ornament hooks, and they worked great for that.

title: Great for colorful sketching
text:
Great set of pens for sketching or coloring. Colors are bright and the pens write smoothly.

The ink dries fast, but it's not waterproof. It will spread or smudge a bit if it gets wet.

These are capped pens, not retractable. There's a little protective coating on the point to remove before first use.

title: Compared to National
text:
Here's a side-by-side overview of this Oxford Greentint narrow ruled 8" X 5" notebook and a similar National brand one:

- The overall dimensions are the about the same, except this Oxford is 1/4" taller.
- The Oxford's cover boards are thicker and stiffer. The National's covers are thinner, but a little smoother and the inside surfaces are coated.
- The paper weight is about the same, which is lightweight. Testing with a Uni-ball Deluxe Micro black pen, the Oxford's paper seemed to show slightly less soak-through.
- The Oxford paper is a slightly lighter shade of green than the National.
- Being spiral bound, both brands will fold back and lay flat.
- The holes for the spiral wire binding are round in the Oxford, slightly oval in the National. The National has 31 holes, the Oxford has 32. Did you need to know that? Probably not, but I counted them anyway because why not.
- Both brands have 80 sheets.
- Both brands have the same number of lines, and the lines (narrow ruled) are spaced the same (1/4-inch). Most of the 1/4-inch extra height in the Oxford goes toward a slightly taller top margin. The Oxford's lines are finer and a bit lighter in color.
- The Oxford says made in USA by TOPS products. The National says Rediform Inc., and made in Brazil.
- At this writing, the National is a little more expensive.

The listing title says "Ampad" (which is also a TOPS brand), but the picture shows "Oxford" brand, and that's what I received. If you search "Oxford green tint notebook," this listing won't appear in the results. This listing is actually kind of hard to find no matter what search terms you use. I think I found it through "customers also viewed" on another product listing.

title: Very good seating
text:
Yes the rubber footing squeaks when you move around. And if you're wearing polyester pants, the seat might feel a bit slippery. But overall it's a great stool for active tasks. It leans (slightly) when you do, and the height is quickly adjustable. The seat is generously wide, so there's plenty of support.

Assembly is simple. There are only three parts---the base, the post, and the seat--and they just push together. There is a protective cap on top of the post that should be removed first. Underneath the cap is a button. The instructions show not to push that button. I assume the post would immediately extend if you did.

The build quality seems very good and it does feel and look like it's durable. Overall a nice stool.

title: Good quality
text: Same quality as some older, nearly identical folders in our files--even the color matches. The folder paper is the same sturdiness, and the rails are coated metal so they'll hold some weight. And they come with plastic tabs and inserts. Good quality folders.

title: Works well
text:
This shredder has a lightweight plastic bin and is narrow from side-to-side, and the the weight of the shredding unit makes it top-heavy and a bit front-heavy. It's not exactly stable on a carpeted surface. Just a small bump from behind will knock it over.

It does better on a hardwood floor, but I still positioned it against a chair, with the front toward the chair.

It draws some amps when it's under load, so you don't want to plug it in a very light-duty circuit or one that's already loaded with appliances or such.

It works well, though. It's not quiet, but it's not too loud. It makes a little paper dust, but not much. And it shreds paper into pieces about an inch long and a quarter-inch wide (the exact size is in the listing information). Three sheets at at time is about the most it can handle. You can hear it working harder with three sheets.

Like all shredders, the manufacturer recommends regular oiling.

title: Doesn't bottom out
text: Since it's made of two layers of foam (furniture foam topped with memory foam), it doesn't bottom out like some cushions made entirely of memory foam. That's its best feature.

title: Great little all-in-one printer
text:
The Canon TS6120 is an excellent printer. It's small--surprisingly compact footprint for an all-in-one printer--so it doesn’t take up too much space.

Unpacking and setup was relatively easy. I say relatively, because setting it up for a Mac required visiting the Canon site and downloading the software. Ink cartridges (it takes five of them) are easy to install. WiFi is easy to set up too.

Printing over WiFi does take a little longer than over a USB cord (which isn't included). But it's still pretty fast.

Something some might regard as a negative is that it lacks a USB port for flash drives or an SD card reader.

Overall its a great little printer.

title: Good scanner
text:
Just to be clear since it isn't in the listing title, this is a duplex scanner---that is, it will scan both sides of a document at once. It's a sheet-fed scanner, best for stacks of loose documents, rather than a flatbed scanner.

It has a small desk footprint (when closed up), measuring about 6 by 12 by 7 inches, and it weighs about 8 pounds.

It will scan items as small as 2 by 2 inches (and it will scan business cards), and handles standard and legal sized documents. It will actually handle much longer documents (up to 200 inches long or longer, depending on resolution settings) as long as they are no longer than 8.5 inches wide. More on specs in a bit, but first I'll tell you about my experiences testing its operation.

We ran various items and stacks of documents through it, mostly with success. The one stack of documents that gave it problems was a 40-plus page stack that was printed on noticeably lightweight paper and had been tri-folded to fit standard envelopes. As it worked its way through the stack, it introduced a few Z-folds into pages (and didn't scan those areas) and eventually jammed. And that jam revealed what is to me a flaw in software or function---it did not notify the computer that there was a jam. The "scanning" window just stayed open as if everything was going fine. If you've set the thing up and are in another room operating it via WiFi, you wouldn't know it had jammed until you noticed nothing had happened for quite a while.

Clearing a jam requires opening and closing the front of the scanner without powering it off, so you can resume scanning from where it left off. Otherwise you'll have to start over.

The scanner also clattered a bit when scanning the lightweight documents. Otherwise it operates smoothly and relatively quietly.

The outfeed tray can become a bit of a mess with lighter weight unfolded paper too, and some documents might wind up on the floor.

The bottom line of this is that if you're scanning big stacks of documents (up to its 50-sheet capacity), you're probably going to want to keep an eye on the scanner. I guess in that case the benefit of wireless connectivity is at least you don't have a USB cable tethering your device to the scanner, even if you do have to stay near it.

We tried running some snapshots through it, grouping them into stacks by size, and it scanned them beautifully. We also tried some letter-sized art prints, and they scanned nicely too. Native resolution can be set up to 600 dpi, and 1200 dpi interpolated.

(A little note here: If you scan snapshots, make sure they're free of adhesive, or they'll muddy up the scanner. And avoid those thick Polaroid type photos. They're a little too thick for this scanner. Scan those on a flatbed scanner instead.)

As the listing title says, this scanner comes with an impressive warranty: Three years with next-business-day replacement.

It doesn't come with a software disk. An internet connection will be needed to download the software. The quick start guide is clear, and we had it up and running in less than 15 minutes. We tried it on a Windows and Mac PC, and it worked fine on both. We used the included USB cable to set up its wireless connection instead of the automatic option.

The scanning software takes a few minutes to figure out, but it's not too difficult. There's a simple mode and a more complex mode. And you can set up different "jobs"---sets of settings so you can just click on the job for various scanning tasks.

The software has some nice features like skew correction and double-feed detection, which you can set on or off.

Here are some of the specs:

Connectivity: Wireless 802.11 b/g/n1 or USB 3.0.
Operating systems: Windows 10/8/7, Mac OS X 10.9.8, macOS 10.12.x.
Optical resolution: 600 dpi.
Maxiumum resolution: 1200 dpi interpolated.
Monochrome bit depth: 1-bit.
Output resolution: 50 to 1200 dpi.
Effective pixels: 5100 x 9300
Scanning speed: Letter size: 35 pages per minute/70 images per minute.
Capacity: 50 sheets.
Daily duty cycle: 4,000 sheets.
Card thickness maximum: Less than 1.24mm with emboss.
Consumables: Roller assembly kit, 200,000 pages.

I'm giving it five stars instead of 4 because I don't think the issues with the lightweight folded paper are worth deducting a whole star. If there was a 4.5-star option, I'd go with that.

title: Nice and convenient
text: I like them a lot. They give good wrist support. The only thing I might complain about (and only a little) is the foam supports in the wristbands are rounded on the bottom, so it takes a little getting used to the feeling that your wrist is balanced on a rocker and wants to tip over to one side or the other.  But I got used to that, and they work very well, so no biggie.

title: Yay, no more cartridges!
text:
No more cartridges! Yay!

Years ago I splurged on a color laser printer--an HP 2600n---because the price per print was low compared to inkjet printers of the day, and because the resolution was sharper.

I kept the 2600n around and continued to use it even though it's no longer fully supported in Windows 10.

Now that I've tried the Epson ET-2650, there's only one reason to keep the old laser printer around now, and that's for an occasional print that might need to be water resistant.

The Epson ET-2650 inkjet beats the old laser printer in every other respect. The resolution is better (about twice as good), it has a built-in scanner, built-in SD card slot for direct printing, built-in wireless connectivity (Wi-Fi), the price per print is now way lower than the laser printer, and no more inkjet cartridges!

The Epson ET-2650 uses the Eco-Tank system. Instead of cartridges, it has refillable ink tanks. And it comes packed with enough ink for up to 4000 prints. Up to two years worth of ink, according to the packaging, and of course depending on how much printing you do. A whole set of refill bottles for the Epson costs about the same as two remanufactured toner cartridges for the laser printer (and they only yield up to 2000 prints each).

Setup took a little over an hour. Unpacking took about ten minutes--there are a lot of pieces of tape to remove from the printer. Then the tanks had to be filled. That's a potentially messy job--the quick start guide recommends wearing gloves and putting paper underneath the printer in case there are any spills. I spilled only a drop or two.

Then the printer has to run an ink charging process that takes about 20 minutes. Following that, you download and set up the printer drivers. There's also an included driver CD.

The automatic network setup did not work for me. I had to connect the Epson to our network manually using the printer's control panel. After that, the software detected the printer and setup went smoothly.

Even though I unchecked the customer research participation program box during installation, the software was still installed on my computer. I removed it manually. (Update: After a recent software update, I discovered it had been installed again. I removed it again.)

The Epson's quick copy function reproduced even very fine print and colors were a close match.

The desktop footprint is about 12" X 18" and it stands a little over 6 inches tall. It's not too heavy either.

A power cord is included, but no USB cord, even though it does have USB connectivity.

Great printer. I'm looking forward to getting a lot of use out of it.

title: The Best Wireless All-In-One Printer
text:
I know it may look like just a simple wireless all-in-one printing device, but there’s something really special about the Epson WF 2760. It works – every feature and every function works exactly as described. It’s as if Epson really wanted to make things right for some of their marketing decisions in the past (mostly when it came to ink cartridges), and they succeeded.

This all-in-one can be set up in a matter of moments by unpacking it, removing the blue tape, powering it on, installing the FULL SIZED ink cartridges and connecting it to your Wi-Fi network via the touchscreen menu on the printer itself. From there you can go to any Windows device, choose Add Printer in the start menu, then select this one (as long as you're connected to the same network) and start using it immediately. I didn’t have to install any proprietary software in Windows 10 to get it to work. I signed up for an Epson Connect account to register the device, opted out of the newsletter, and set up all of my cloud print services from there. More on that below.

By the way: You don’t need to even sign up for any cloud services if you’re not going to use them. To set up your printer with more features on your PC, just type its IP address into your browser and edit them from there. (You can find the IP Address in the printer settings menu on the Touch Panel.)

Here is a list of some of the features and why I think this is the best inkjet printer on the market:

1. Ink cartridges are high quality, reasonably priced and they last. It comes with 4 full capacity cartridges that I’ve printed dozens of pages with in full color, and my ink levels are still reasonably high. No more printing 10 pages and having to buy new carts immediately. A set of standard capacity Epson replacements are about 40 bucks, but the best part is you only need to buy the color you need. They stopped with the “you're out of black so you'll need to replace magenta as well” stuff. Also, when copying or printing in black, you only need to have enough black ink – the printer doesn’t lock down when you run out of cyan but still need to print black and white.

2. Print quality – Described as laser quality – I have to say they nailed it. I haven’t done any photo printing (there are other models that specialize in that) but standard and color docs look super sharp and vibrant.

3. Cloud print services – This is HUGE! Without installing any software on my Windows 10 PC I signed into the printer by typing it’s IP address in my browser, signed into my Google account, signed into my new Epson Connect account, and even set up an email address *****@print.epsonconnect.com to send docs or forward emails to for printing.

4. Cloud scanning – another awesome feature that works. You can set scans to automatically upload to a specified folder in Dropbox/Onedrive/Evernote/etc. You can also set up email addresses for the scans to be sent to. You can have multiple options in case you want one sent to your work account, or another sent to Dropbox as a backup. I have one set up just for receipts and it captures everything and uploads it to my deductions folder in Dropbox.

5. Printing from mobile – either by the Epson iPrint app (which you can also trigger prints via NFC, or by Google Cloud, Airprint, etc.) you can print full-sized docs from your mobile device. I set this up in minutes via the Epson app – really nice interface for Android, and really effective.

6. Auto 2-side printing – for super efficient paper conservation

7. Large paper tray – holds 150 pages

8. Wi-Fi direct – cool if you don’t have a wireless network or want a more secure way of printing. (This is helpful if you have roommates that like to prank you by printing multiple copies of the Star Wars script…. Bryan.) You can also connect via USB and go off network, or even print via NFC while in Wi-Fi Direct mode.

9. Auto Document Feeder – This is cool. Need to scan/copy a stack of papers? No problem. Set them up in the ADF tray and it immediately recognizes there is a stack there. Good for scanning contracts, other docs, etc.

I didn’t have a use for the fax function because I do that via an email service, but if you have a hard phone line it will handle that too.

I really love this thing. 5 stars. Awesome device.

title: Nice budget mini binder
text:
Nice budget mini binder. It's a three-ring binder sized for half sheets (5.5 inches by 8.5 inches). But 7-hole paper -- the kind used in planners -- fits in it nicely. The rings are 1-inch and hold up to 175 sheets.

The covering material is white vinyl with a clear layer that serves as pockets on the outer three sides. It looks reasonably durable. There are inner pockets on the front and back, but they are a single layer of vinyl and won't hold more than a few sheets or cards.

As the item listing says, it's basic, but it's nicely made.

title: Nice
text: Very smooth writing and a visibly darker line than HB leads. I think they're pretty strong and perhaps only slightly more breakable than HB, if at all. The lines are a little more difficult to erase, but with a white plastic or vinyl-type eraser they still erase pretty cleanly.

title: Excellent stapling pliers
text:
The mellow yellow color seems a shade to the green side -- kind of a chartreuse. That's not a complaint. It's still looks very nice.

As far as build quality and operation, these are simply great stapling pliers. We were a little skeptical of the "50 sheets" claim, but we tested them on multiple folded paper and even magazines, and they worked every time. Well, almost. The only time they didn't work was when the magazine was thicker than the length of the staples, but it wouldn't be fair to call that a failure.

They're well made and sure to hold up for years of use. And with the colors, they're cute too.

title: Good slide and film scanning solution.
text:
The results from 35mm color slides are very good, but I wouldn't call them great. There's a little loss of sharpness and resolution, and some sketchy contrast issues (a little too much whiteness it seems at times), but some of that can be recovered with a sharpening filter and contrast adjustment in photo editing software, and controlled somewhat by adjustments to the scanner. So for most of us, it's just fine.

For the price, though, and when you consider the alternative is a very expensive high resolution film scanner, the results are great!

What it appears to be is not actually a scanner, but a little self-contained digital camera with a built-in light source. The slide-in holders work well, and after I learned the buttons and digitized a few slides and negatives, I got quite efficient at it. I digitized a box of around 200 old slides in what seemed like no time. Results were great with negatives too, including 110 pocket camera size.

I do wish it handled larger format negatives (35mm is the max), but products like this can't be all things. Overall a good cost-effective solution to digitizing slides and negatives, if good, but not super-detailed quality is acceptable to you.

title: Not so good results with 5mil and cardstock
text:
The one I got didn't get hot enough or apply enough pressure to do a good job with 5mil pouches. It left unsealed stripes and a pretty large unsealed border around cardstock. I found the Fellowes M5-95 (which is just a few dollars more) does a much better job with 5mil.

With either machine, the tip other reviewers have about putting a book or something under the outfeed side to hold the pouch level when it comes out of the laminator is a good one. That will keep it from warping or getting wavy while it's still hot.

title: Very nice results for the price
text:
I ran a side-by-side test with the AmazonBasics laminator, which at this writing is about 10 dollars less.

And there is no comparison. The Fellowes M5-95 performed much better.

I tested using 5mil pouches and pieces of cardstock. The AmazonBasics laminator just doesn't seem to get hot enough or apply enough pressure with the rollers to get a clear and clean result. It left a 1/8-inch unlaminated gap all around the edge of the cardstock, and there were streaks where it appears there just wasn't enough heat to make a good clear seal. Even making two passes through the machine didn't result in much improvement.

The Fellowes laminator made a good clear seal on the first pass through, and the gap around the cardstock was much smaller -- only about a 16th of an inch, and it was even all the way around, indicating even pressure by the rollers. I don't think any budget-priced home laminator can completely eliminate that gap. But these results are very good.

A couple of tips when using either laminator: Put a book or something on the outfeed side of the laminator, level with the bottom of the slot, to give level support to the hot pouch as it exits the machine. This will minimize warping.

Secondly, don't trust the green light. Give the machine a couple of extra minutes to heat up.

And finally, leave a little border when trimming laminated pieces. If you trim right to the edge of the laminated piece, it will eventually delaminate at the edges. If you like that look, make extra copies so that you can replace them from time to time.
