These are very good highlighters and I would recommend them.

title: This works well
text: This is a comfortable memory foam chair seat. It's perfect for sitting long periods of time. It's especially nice when for drives. If you have ever had any type of sciatica pain, this helps with that a lot. It's a very light weight pillow with memory foam so it reshapes once stand up. The cover is removable for easy washing. It does what it says it does!

title: My go to notepads
text: Love these!  I use these for everything from daily and monthly to do lists to jotting down recipes and to go orders. These pads are excellent!

title: Nice board
text: This is a very nice pin board. It's sharp looking made with either cork or felt. It comes in a nice aluminum frame. The installation is incredibly simple. It comes with everything you need to attach it and also 12 push pins to get you started. This would be great in a busy household to keep track of just about everything or a dorm room. It's a very nice board and since it comes in three different sizes and colors you do get a good choice.

title: These are terrific index cards
text: This is a lot of index cards for a good price. The size of these cards is 3 by 5 inches. They are a good thickness being made from 11 pt. economy weight paper. Writing on them is nice and smooth so they are ideal for anything from recipe cards to cataloging books old school style. They'd be great for school or work projects as well. Very good deal.

title: Erase well and write nicely
text: I really like these. I have been using them in everything from  journals to adult coloring books. It's true that at times they seem to be a little too faint perhaps but I like that they are erasable because I am a terrible stay-between-the-lines type of person in both the above mentioned tasks. I'm an oaf like that. These erase nicely without leaving anything behind. This is the first Frixion erasable I have tried so my interest has been more than peaked to check out others now. Back to these though. I find that the thickness of the marker/pen, 0.6mm, is a good thin thickness for what I am using it for. I do like these and think that they are worth checking out.

title: Very sturdy
text: This is fantastic. It's extremely strong. This will take care of all your important papers and you can have confidence that they will be safe. Since they are already tabbed alphabetically all you have to do is start filling it all up. This file is heavy duty so you can store it without having to worry too much about it getting crushed or messed up. It's great! I really like it and trust it with all my important papers!

title: Brilliant
text: This is a great versatile letter size desk tray organizer. It's incredibly well made and is a solid piece. It would be great for so many things. It works wonderfully for holding folders, important papers, even as a daily mail drop. Although I have every intention of using this at my desk, it's currently housing a few pieces of produce in my kitchen because I needed something in a pinch and it fit perfectly and it's working beautifully for that. So you see, it's versatile! I really like this and may wind up getting another one if the kitchen one stays.

title: Very well made
text: This mesh 3-tier organizer is impressive. It's made from a good solid steel that just upon looking at it let alone picking it up you know the makers meant business. It's so well made. This can either stand up or be attached to the wall so that you can use it in the space that is most convenient for you. It holds quite a bit in each of the three tiers and it's simple to see what you have in each one. This is a great addition to any home, home office, or anywhere you need to keep important documents.

title: Post-it notes for everything
text:
This is a great pack of assorted Post-it super sticky notes. The mulitipack has assorted sizes and colors. The sizes included are 1 7/8 in x 1 7/8 in, 3 in x 3 in, 4 in x 6 in.
I'm probably one of the most forgetful people I've ever met so I stick Post-it notes up all over the place. Mostly for my benefit but also for others. If I have a note up the family can't say I didn't tell them something or another! It's a fail safe.
Whether you use them for this reason, for noting notable pages in books, for school, etc. this pack of assorted notes is the perfect pack for getting things done.

title: Well made and practical
text: These mesh pencil holders are incredibly sturdy. They have more weight to them than you would think by looking at them. Definitely well constructed. They hold everything from pencils and pens to markers, scissors, and more! I'm using one on my desk that holds all those mentioned. I have one in my kitchen that holds all those little kitchen things like rubber bands, mini food clips, a few pens, well more odds and ends. The last one is holding post its, paper clips, stamps, etc. I find that I'm a boring person but if you put your mind to it you could find far more exciting things to put in these because they will hold them. These are great!

title: Very nice pen
text:
This is a very nice pen. It's a comfortable pen to hold on to and write with. It's good and lightweight. The ink rolls out smoothly and glides over the paper without smudging or blotting. The body of the pen is plastic not metal although it is a scratch proof plastic and it looks very good. This pen can use Quinkflow ballpoint refills (which is what is in the pen when you get it). You can also use Parker gel refills as well.
This is a very nice pen and one that should last a very long time.

title: Works great
text:
This works great. It sticks and holds perfectly to the refrigerator. The eraser, board, and marker all stay up though I do put the eraser and the marker above the board for extra help just in case.
So far, my husband has been having a ball with leaving messages on it so the eraser has been getting a lot of use and it does erase well and completely.
It's a very good board that does what it says it does and works very well. I haven't had any trouble at all with any of the parts of it, though I haven't tried using any of the hanging options other than the magnetic for the refrigerator.

title: Very convenient
text:
This is excellent! It's one of those things that you just wouldn't think of but someone out there did and I for one am so happy they did!
This Post-It note dispenser is the ideal addition to any desk setting. It's weighted making it very sturdy. It has a divided section in the back that you can put the things you need to have close by (scissors, pens and pencils, paper clips, etc.). The size sticky notes it takes is 3 inch by 3 inch. It's so easy to fill and just so convenient once you have it you won't know how you managed to keep you space so organized without it.
I love this and I think you just might as well if you've gotten this far in this review. It's such a great product!

title: Very cute card
text: This card is just too cute. I have a slew of family members this card (39-ish) would be perfect for. I think it's hilarious. It's also well made. Hallmark uses great quality card stock and even their envelopes are of very good quality and match their cards just a bit on the inside. I go back and forth with the price though. It might be a bit over priced but on the other hand it's very good quality and cute. Plus isn't that special recipient worth it? So, for those reasons, it's worth it.

title: So cute!
text:
The Santa on these Happy Ho Ho Holiday cards is so cute! He and his poinsettia are so clearly printed on this nice thick card stock that it makes this boxed Christmas card set perfect! The inside of these cards is blank so that you can personalize each and every card you send. Adding that little touch will make each recipient feel that much more special during the holiday.
These cards/note cards are adorable and well worth the little bit extra to make the recipients day brighter!

title: Very funny little calendar
text:
So funny! That's the first thing that comes to mind when it comes to describing this 2020 daily calendar. I didn't look at too many of them of course because I didn't want to spoil them all for the upcoming year (or, superstitiously inclined at times, bring about too much bad luck in the coming year.
What makes this calendar so funny is that you can picture yourself in the situation where you are the one overhearing what is said and how you would react to it at the time (if you could follow that). I also like the bi-coastal approach to it. It's hilarious.
This would make a great gift as well as a keeper for yourself. I like this a lot.

title: Beautiful card
text: This is an adorable little card! Make sure you read over under the description about the size of the card. It's not a very large card. It's actually rather small. Oh, I guess you don't have to read it there. I could just tell you here. The card is  4" x 5.5" and it comes with a matching envelope. Size aside, it's a very cute card. The paper is nice and thick so it's not going to rip right away and it has that nice pop out middle part that makes it perfect for putting on display, or the recipient to put on display. You can see the card at the top of this page and it looks even nicer in person. You and the person who you give this card to are going to love it. I'm still just always astounded at the cost of cards (I want to add 'now days' or 'anymore' but how old would that make me sound? probably my age!) so it's likely worth the cost though I'll still think it's a little too pricey.

title: Beautiful cards.
text:
These holiday cards are stunning. The cards that I received have raised gold lettering on off white card stock. The envelopes are the white lined with what looks like gold foil. They are so pretty! Simple yet elegant. The inside reads, 'All the wonders of the season, all wished especially for you.'. These are the types of cards you could send to anyone from your closest friend to a business colleague.
The cards come in a sturdy box. There are 12 cards and 12 envelopes. These cards are really beautiful and I can only imagine their other ones are as well.

title: Excellent!
text: This is a great stapler set for the cost. The stapler works perfectly and it comes with staples and a staple remover. It's a very nice basic stapler that does just what it's supposed to do. It is ideal for students, home use, and those that don't have to staple more than 20 sheets at a time. The stapler is very easy to load and it is resistant to jams. It's an all around good stapler. It's a terrific steal of a deal!

title: Adorable!
text: These pens are so very cute! The pen is quite heavy which is nice. They look good and write as good as they look. The only drawback is that you might want to get yourself some ink refills because they are filled with itty bitty ones. I'm bad at guessing sizes but maybe 2 to 3 inches of ink in them. However, for how cute they are it's probably worth just getting some refills. They are adorable.

title: Great for reminders
text:
For someone who would forget their own head if it wasn't attached these are tremendously useful. I have placed these all over the house (well, there are five of them so in five locations anyway) where I most need reminding. There is one by my phone downstairs (yes I still have a house phone), one by my desk upstairs, one in the kitchen by the fridge, one by the sofa (you never know where you will be when you need to remember something), one by the upstairs phone in the bedroom, and one by the stove. Now I can just clip notes right in them when I need to remember things that I need written down rather than spoken on to a device. I do like to write things down at times rather than have siri, google, or alexa remember everything for me. These are so great for that and I use them constantly. Having MS my brain can be a slippery slope at times and if I didn't write things down and post my little notes all over the place I'd be hard pressed to remember to do a lot of things!
So, if you ever just need to remember things, these things are great and you can put there anywhere since they have a sticky side to stick on anything! Then you just clip your note in and you are set to remember your thought! It's really great. I love these!

title: Great planner!
text:
This is just a fun idea for an undated agenda calendar. The "I Adulted!" theme of this book is a great one to use at any age. It comes with stickers that you can use to add to the days where you did something you might want to memorialize with a sticker or maybe someone else did one of the things there is a sticker for and you want to stick it right on them, you have the power now! Plus the undated planner is nice as you can start it whenever you want to and aren't limited to starting at any prearranged start date.
The one thing about this calendar is that it helps to have a great big dose of sense of humor when you get this. It's mostly just a fun thing. I looked at it a lot before getting it to make sure it was a good fit for me. It is also a thing that you may find for someone else as a gift if you know someone who could use such a thing. It's all great fun plus it has the practical side of actually being practical with the daily agenda pages.
I really like this!

title: Perfect Little Notebooks
text:
I have nothing bad to say about these two pocket notebooks. Absolutely nothing. These are exactly what I need.
I love these little pocket size leather cover journal type notebooks. They have so many need little extras. A pen holder loop on the side that most pens should fit in, an elastic band attached to the back cover that will keep the journal closed, two bookmarks to help you keep important pages easier to find and two inside pockets to keep important papers/business cards/etc. in. Just to name a few things.
These also have a decent amount of paper in them. They have 80 individual sheets (or 160 write on with front and back usage) and the very best thing about them? They are so easily carried around wherever you go or placed in assorted areas in your home without taking up a lot of space. I am a list writer and jotter downer of many things so I like to have everything from little sticky notes to journals like these all over the place so I always have something to write something on no matter where I am from the kitchen to a restaurant. With these you can fit them in a purse, tote, or pocket easily enough and also in a nightstand or that junk drawer where all those things wind up and no matter what you can always find a pen (as long as you remember to put one in the pen holder on the journal).
These are great notebooks. Convenient and practical!

title: Excellent Cards!
text:
The designs on these cards are so pretty. The insides are blank so that you are able to write a nice heartfelt thank you to a special person who deserves it. It's so nice to get a personal note in a world where personal (handwritten) notes seem to be a thing of the past. These cards are the perfect way to make someones day.
There are 36 cards in all with 6 different designs. All of the designs are watercolors and all are very pretty. These are excellent cards to have on hand because you never know when you'll need them!

title: Enjoying this so much!
text:
This is a really good electric eraser. It's incredibly easy go use once you get used to it, which doesn't take very long, and holds a charge for a long time. With a bit of practice, you can really get into shading using the different size erasers and by adjusting how you apply pressure etc.. Having a rechargeable is even better! This comes with a decent amount of erasers to get you started as well 40 big and 100 small. This is good because they do tend to run down quickly.
This is something that everyone who enjoys drawing for fun, work, both, or any other reason should consider trying. It's very helpful and fun to use. I like it a lot.

title: It works!
text:
So far, I can give this a four star!
This is an interesting little device (in certain places it claims this is a silver-2 pack but it is just a one pack. Perhaps the "pack" should have been/is meant to be piece. There are no instructions in the box so make sure you mark this page in case you need to reference it for some reason. This magnetic door stopper is stainless steel and you are supposed to be able to install it using just the adhesive tape you get in the box. This does work and it works well enough. I think that if you are going to use this in an area of high traffic or where people are just rougher with doors you may want to consider using the screws that come with it. There are holes on the one part that they go in. It might be practical to use those too.
It's a neat little door stop and it works well. I'm not sure of it's longevity yet but I do like it!

title: Great Cards!
text:
All of these cards are nice. They are decent quality, cute enough, and you get a good amount of cards (12) with envelopes for a good price. These are the types of cards that are just nice to have on hand. They aren't extremely personal like a card would be if you went and picked one yourself from the store out of the single cards but they also cost a whole lot less! I like these cards.
The designs on these are quite cute (you can see all four at the top). You get four different designs and three of each design. They have cute writing on the inside (you can see this on the pictures on the side at the top). I think these will make terrific cards for just about anyone you want to give a standard card to. They still look really nice and they serve their purpose quite well. I like them and will likely buy more packs like this.

title: Very good!
text:
These are terrific. They are quite heavy and very well made. These would look great for displaying company marketing materials, specials, definitely menus and specials of that kind, and anything else you can think of. These are durable and they even come with a cloth to wipe them with so you don't risk scratching them up. Another great use that I have found for these is to hold paper recipes keeping them 100% safe and not lost for the duration of a recipe. Very convenient and perfect.
These are some of the best acrylic sign holders I have used and I also love the bases on these. They are very sturdy and incredibly easy to put on and off. I recommend these to anyone interested. They are very good.

title: Huge and Fantastic
text: This is brilliant. It's very large and it covers an entire space. It's relatively thick and my mouse loves it as it can be used anywhere on it. I love that it protects the desk so well. It doesn't seem to leave any marks when you move it so you can change it's spot whenever you'd like.  If you are looking for a quality desk mat then this is one to consider. I'm not sure what to say about it that isn't said in the stuff above.  I'd sound repetitive but I gave this 5 stars because it's really good at doing what it's supposed to do. I really like mine!

title: Very Pretty!
text: My 9 yr old  daughter loves it.

title: Works, But Doesn't ...
text:
I have YET to find the perfect calculator. I had one back in the late 1990’s, but it died – no, I couldn’t replace the battery.

This has a nice “stand”, big buttons, on/off buttons, and large display.

The problem for me is the GT button that requires me to “clear” the total before moving on to my next set of equations. I much prefer the simple 9+9= 18, then hit the “C” button to clear, as opposed to 9+9=18, C, GT (twice). Otherwise, I end up with even more results. That might just be the way people like to do it. I don’t.

I find using my iPhone’s calculator a lot better for simple equations, as well as my computer’s calculator which I can adjust height and width on. I can even make it take up the ENTIRE screen of my computer.

At almost $13 – I have had better ones. And, I am not impressed with this.

title: Great Gift for Anyone or Yourself
text:
For under $10 (with tax), this is a pretty great pen. I love to collect pens (and use them), so this was a stellar standout for me.

Lightweight, not bulky. Comes with four (4) refills. I love that idea. Too often I’d get a favorite pen and have to cannibalize one for a refill or spend time and gas looking for a refill.

This is also gift ready. Comes in a tin and the pen is in a leatherette sleeve. The refills are in a sealed bag with caps on them.

It writes well and smooth; looks fancy too. Very comparable to pricier pens on the market.

For the price, packaging, and refills – I’d definitely call it luxury.

Definitely pleased with this.

title: Classy and Affordable
text:
As someone who LOVES pens - this is a near-to-perfect set for me. And, if you don't mind "breaking it up" - you could keep one and give one to a friend, sibling, parent; especially since they are refillable (Parker-type refill). And, the $20 tag (as of this review) is pretty reasonable. These look very classy and comparable to higher ends pen brands.

AS OF NOTE - these are BALL POINT, not rollerball. I saw rollerball in a review and ALMOST passed on this set. Glad I didn't.

These do have some "weight" to them. They are twist-to-use and write well.

As far as the packaging. The sleeve on my set slipped right off. I did work with it, but there is some slippage.

Despite that, this makes an excellent "any occasion" gift.

title: Cross Lookalike Pens
text:
These are a more economic variation of the iconic Cross pen. And, these even take the same type of refill.

Individually packaged for giveaways, goodie bags, or for your own use.

Black ink is versatile for home or work. And, for around $9, you get six (6) pens.

Terrific value. Very pleased with them. Kept three, gave three to my mom. Since they're refillable, no need to keep any more than that.

title: Cheap and Colorful
text:
I actually prefer black ink, but … this set was actually too good to pass up, and the reason I use black is pretty outdated.

As a kid in school, I preferred BLUE ink and other colors until the teachers had a fit about pink and purple. I used the darker versions, but … either blue or black.

That changed in the 1990’s when my mom went to work at a hospital and it was BLACK INK ONLY. So … that’s what happened. As a result, and even after her retirement, my preference remains black ink.

That said …

These are a darker blue color and really show up. The pen is SUPER lightweight, and very easy to hold. They can be refilled adding to the life.

They can, if not careful, easily break. As I’m harder on my items than most people – I had NO issues using these.

Given the blue ink, I’d suggest these for school kids. It’ll definitely last them a while and so many colors to choose from.

title: Stylish and Great Goodie Bag Gifts
text:
At the current price of $11.99 for a set of six, that is an average of $2 per pen. Each is individually wrapped and makes a great goodie bag gift or any occasion “bag” item.

There are three finishes, and two of each. I liked this because I could share easily with my mom and not have to “pick” through my favs.

Now, the downside …

These take a PARKER-type refill. However, the PARKER brand will not fit them. A “non-name” brand will likely fit. I have three types, excluding the 4-piece set that came with this. All of the “generic” ones I have fit.

Overall, I still like these pens – they write well, have some “weight” to them, and look like expensive pens without the price tag.

title: Double the Inspiration
text:
Due to recent and very chaotic events, when I got these bookmarks, I didn’t pay attention to them and thought it was a set of two identical ones. After all – that’s what I got. I got two of the Prini ones.

One was lightly “printed”, the other dark and bold.

The wood is durable, and suited for a hardcover book, definitely not a small paperback.

For the price, they aren’t too bad.

The string with the gem/bauble seems cheap though.

title: Affordable and Super Cute
text:
I’ve seen pens like these at stores like Office Depot and Staples – those “tempting” items near the registers.

And, they average about $2.99 upwards depending on how fancy they are. I have seen some like the “pouf” go for about $4.99. This 8-piece set, at the current price of around $15, averages to $1.87 per pen. That’s cheaper than the $2.99 low figure.

I absolutely LOVE the rose gold feature.

Now, seven (7) wrote in black, one in blue (I changed that one even though I was giving it to my mom). The refills vary from a short Cross-type to a Parker-style.

Each type of refill is available here on Amazon.

The velvet pouch is a classy touch.

I gave the plain twist, plain crown, and heart pens to my mom. We each already had a crystal one, so I put that to the side for a “just in case”.

They all write well, easy to hold unless you get sweaty hands. But, I don’t tend to write too long with metal pens as it is.

Overall, I LOVE this set and it would make a great gift for any occasion. And, each pen would be great for gift-giving in goodie bags.

title: Mermaid Pens
text:
Anyone seeing my profile will know – I LOVE COLLECTING PENS.

They can be a cheap BIC stick from a hotel, or ones like these.

I like unique pens.

This is a pretty good selection, and if you give them out – something for everyone.

I like that they’re refillable with a Parker-type refill, easily purchased here on Amazon.

As one person pointed out – the texture. Not a grip per se, but a matte finish that is easy to hold. They have some weight to them being a metal pen, but it isn’t overwhelming – unless you’re writing for hours.

Overall – I love them!!

title: Fashionable and Functional
text:
I love PENS. I love to collect pens. I’m a bit odd like that.

Anything sparkly, I like. So, getting these was a “no-brainer”. And, four pens at the current price of $9? Cheaper than the office supply stores. That’s an average of $2.25 per pen. I’ve seen these sell for $4.99+

They do tend to stick when you get them, and have a slight funky odor.

Comfortable? Not for long term. I’d say a quick “to-do” list or signing one’s name on a document.

They are refillable (Parker type ball point).

They could also make a great goodie bag gift, mini “door” prize, or a stocking stuffer.

Pretty pleased with them.

title: Cute, Not Practical
text:
As a fan of certain movies, I enjoy seeing "quill" pens being used. However, in most cases - they are not practical.

These are colorful replicas but have far too many flaws to be a practical alternative:

** The "cap" is small, easily lost, and cannot be replaced
** Pen is thin and not easy to old
** Pen nib (the metal part that connects to the pen that ink comes out of) is small, producing thin strokes
** Ink was black in all five (5) pens, but not too easy to see

They are individually wrapped for goodie bags, gift-giving, or stocking stuffer. And, at OVER $2 per pen - not worth the price due to lack of being refillable.

title: Mustang Fan
text: Beautiful calendar for the fan of the Ford Mustang. Officially licensed. Great gift.

title: Car Enthusiast Calendar
text:
This is definitely designed for someone who enjoys the mid 1960's to mid 1970's muscle cars.

I have a few favorites, so a calendar like this is perfect for me.

The price is a tad high, but given this is officially licensed by Dodge, Chevy, and Ford - it might be worth it.

title: Small, But Effective
text:
I have a love/hate affair with erasers.

If they’re too tiny – they don’t work; too big – they tend to break or have issues collecting “dust” or other particles. Bigger ones are also sometimes awkward to hold.

These are a compact, but usable size. But, probably suited for ages 8-14.

Despite being different colors – there is no real difference so depending on kids – there’s a color for most everyone.

The paper sleeve is a bit hard to get the eraser back into. Depending on your tolerance for difficulty – I’d remove it.

Does it leave writing behind? That’s difficult to say.

I use it with 0.5mm mechanical pencils that tend to write lighter and I don’t “press” down with my pencil that hard. I also use these with PaperMate EverStrong break-resistant HB-2. As I tend to write with only “sharp” pointed pencils, my marks don’t get that dark. The PaperMate pencil is one I have little trouble with erasing.

It also doesn’t tear the paper – unless you’re a roughie with it. I’ve seen some people erase like they’re scrubbing a floor or sanding a piece of wood.

This is a pretty huge box, and as a home user – I won’t need to buy anymore anytime soon. Honestly, if you have a school-age kid or a few – this is great! For teachers? It’ll be great for a class of 30 for probably a semester, depending on how many the kids go through.

While I don’t need them anytime soon … I’d definitely get them again.

title: Calculator
text:
I got this because I liked the big numbers and the color (pink).

But, it is definitely a tad "complicated" to use. Seems newer calculators have this GT feature and you have to spend more steps clearing it in order to perform a new equation.

Also, it tends on the pricey side.

I've seen calculators like this for sale at Staples around th$4-$6 mark.

Cute, but a no-go for the future.

title: More Fun Than Function
text:
These are definitely cutesy. They're easy to hold. Write well? Not really. Most of the time they scratched the paper.

They are not easy to refill either.

Okay for the price, wouldn't get them again.

title: Decent Set
text:
This is one NicPro set that I wasn't too happy with.

Not that it had anything to do with the performance of the pencils. It had more to do with the overall value.

For close to $14, there are

After a previous experience with the NicPro brand, I saw this set and HAD to get it. While it is close to $14 (as of this review) - the customer gets SO much in this bundle:

3 0.5 mechanical pencils
3 0.7 mechanical pencils
3 tubes of 0.5 lead refills
3 tubes of 0.7 lead refills
1 tube of eraser refills (about 9 erasers)
3 erasers

Now that may seem like a good bargain until you start shopping the brand. There are bigger packages with a better value.

Overall, I do like the pencils. The lead reminds me of the late 80's/early 90's pencils that didn't smudge or smear.

It is a fair value, but if you're looking to get your money's worth ... I'd keep looking.

title: Great Variety
text:
After a previous experience with the NicPro brand, I saw this set and HAD to get it. While it is close to $14 (as of this review) - the customer gets SO much in this bundle:

13 differently designed 0.5 mechanical pencils
13 differently designed 0.7 mechanical pencils
3 tubes of 0.5 lead refills
3 tubes of 0.7 lead refills
1 tube of eraser refills (about 9 erasers)

I'll admit this -> depending on the pencil eraser, I RARELY use it. I have an OLDER Pentel Quicker Clicker (about 30 years old) that STILL has 3/4 of the original GREEN eraser to it. So, refilling the erasers is NOT a big deal.

I honestly chose this brand of pencils because of how the lead writes. While the 0.5mm is prone to breakage, I haven't had that many issues with it. No more than I would of the late 80's/early 90's pencils of similar lead with no smearing or smudging. Which is why I LOVED mechanical pencils of that time.

Overall, a VERY good buy!

title: Basic Mechanical Pencils
text:
Nothing is made like it used to be.

That out of the way ...

This is, as of this review, about $8. What is included? Something I haven't seen:

Pencils
Eraser
Lead Refills
PENCIL ERASER REFILLS

I'll admit this -> depending on the pencil eraser, I RARELY use it. I have an OLDER Pentel Quicker Clicker (about 30 years old) that STILL has 3/4 of the original GREEN eraser to it.

How do these pencils feel?

They're about as comfortable any mechanical pencils out there.

They write well, and since the lead is 0.5mm, it is "lighter" than most. Trick is to NOT extend the led so far. The lead does remind me of the late 80's/early 90's type that didn't smear or smudge, part of why I LOVED mechanical pencils.

These work, aren't too heavy duty though. And, given what is included - a pretty good buy.

title: Mess
text:
Some like to highlight sections of the bible, I haven't, but I'm not against it.

However, the pages of a bible are thin, and some inks or highlighters can bleed through. These, as some have noted, are waxy and can be a bit problematic.

The pens are not the best; but do give A for effort when it comes to the little zip bag.

This isn't something I will get again.

title: What Do I Use These For?
text:
When I got these, I was in the middle of a move. As it turned out, I won't be moving for another 10-11 months now. That's good.

That said ...

While the "roll" of wrap might wrap a frame, the squares BARELY wrap a cell phone. I managed to use them as "inserts" for certain cups, which was about all.

I definitely wouldn't get them again.

title: Great for Organizing
text:
I've been using sheet protectors since I was in Junior High - so over 35 years.

I've used all brands: Samsill, Avery, office store brands.

These work just as well as others. I love being able to sort projects by color. The only drawback is you might need more than one pack for larger projects.

The packaging could be better for sorting.

Great price considering everything.

title: Pretty But Expensive
text:
I've used and relied on planners since about 2009. They're essential now to me.

The undated ones are good because I tend to see a planner, think "that's the one", see another and that "WAS" the one :(

That said ...

Undated planners are great, for me.

This is a bit on the pricier side, but it is by Yoobi, a company know for their philanthropy.

Overall cute, didn't come with pen.

title: Perfect Pencil Set
text:
This is definitely designed for an artist, but these can by used by anyone.

Pencil “leads” ranging from small (.05mm) to EXTRA LARGE (2.0mm) for every occasion.

I love that the set comes with special sharpeners for some leads, extra leads, erasers, and eraser replacements. Also, a great variety of colors too!

Definitely a FANTASTIC value.

I’m partial to the .05, and the lead reminds me of the late 80’s/early 90’d. It didn’t smear, smudge, or get “dark”.

Very pleased!

title: Comfy Pens
text:
These are very comfy and slightly affordable pens. They’re pretty affordable coming in at about 83¢ each. Of course, the brand has a bit fancier ones for the same price, which is why the 4-star.

The pens are definitely ball point, refillable. The nib is a bit less standard, but a standard refill will fit.

Comfortable, easy to write with. I split the pack with my mom so we ended up with one of each color.

title: Fancy Pens Without the Fancy Price
text:
First of all – these are indeed BALL POINT pens. I say this because some companies say “ball point” and they’re really rollerball or gel. But, these are definitely BALL POINT.

That out of the way …

These can be refilled, though finding a suitable one might be difficult. The “nib” is a bit different, but a standard refill (in same length) will fit.

Function? Write like any other retractable, grip ball point pen.

Comfort? Very

Price: About 83¢ per pen, which is VERY reasonable.

I love the idea of having doubles – my mom and I were able to get one of each design.

Definitely love these!! They’re like ones that the office stores sell at the check stand.

title: Light Up Journal
text:
This pink (more like purple) light up diamond journal isn’t just for kids. It makes a great gift for anyone who likes diamonds (my birthstone) and purple (my favorite color).

The pages are nice, thick (especially for gel or felt tip pens).

There is no way to manually turn off the lights, they cycle off on their own. That leads me to my ONLY issue – no way to replace the battery on this. So, when the lights stop – that’s it.

It is cute, but not quite worth the nearly $13 it is as of this review. More like a $10 journal.

title: Just Okay
text: These didn't hold up well at all. They're more for a generic trimmer and not brand names. Price is good if you have a trimmer than can use these.

title: Durable Comp Books
text:
When not on sale, composition books can be pricey. I’ve seen them around $3.50, so 2 for $7.99 isn’t a big jump.

Though to be honest, I usually wait until Staples/TruRed has them for 50¢

They’re not as durable as these ones, so that puts the TruRed brand out. The paper for these books is no bleed – unless you’re really using water-based inks.

While these are superior – as money is have a low buying power – I’ll stick to the ones on sale.

title: Cutesy, But Not Functional
text:
These are, without a doubt, the CUTEST set of note pads. I got the bear one.

But, that’s where it ends.

I love the long list, and the two square ones. I haven’t seen a practical use for the tree or log.

I use them to mainly write down where I have to go if I run multiple errands.

My set were super sticky, difficult to tear off. Yet, when I wanted to stick there somewhere in my car to easily reference – it was as if there was NO adhesive at all.

Worse, on some occasions, even gently peeling the one piece off tore the one I was trying to use and the one connected to it.

For almost $20, that isn’t a good deal. I still like the cutesiness of them, but wouldn’t get them again or recommend them.

title: Colorful CaseDurable pen/pencil case. Colorful, easy to use.
text: Durable pen/pencil case. Colorful, easy to use.

title: Cute Diary ...
text:
This is a solid diary. Well-constructed, beautiful (and refillable) pen. Even has a lock.

What keeps this from being a 5-star product is the lock. It is awkward to unlock and relock due to the narrow "hole" in the belt.

Makes a great gift. And, for under $15, is pretty fairly priced.

title: Parker-Type Refill, Good for Most Pens
text:
What can be said? For less than $7, there are 10 refills which comes out to 70¢ each. I remember getting a generic 2-pack at Walmart for 99¢, so there isn't much inflation here.

These work, write well.

Definitely would get again.

title: Flimsy and Pricey
text:
About 20 years ago, I saw something like this at Walmart. It was during a "Back 2 School" sale. It was the Dexas Clipcase 2 Storage Clipboard with Rounded Handle, Blue"

The "clipboard case" was hinged at the top, heavy duty. Inside was roomy. It was longer as it had a handle which is where the pens/pencils could be stored. Far sturdier than this, which is surprisingly "wimpy".

That cost me less than $8, and I STILL have it today. Here on Amazon, it is priced a bit higher, but so glad to still it is STILL available. I recommend that case over this one. This has no handle, and the clip closing it is inferior.

title: Cute Chinese New Year Money Envelopes
text:
These are what they say they are. Definitely colorful, sturdy, and reusable.

Got these for book photos and the color is stunning. Very pleased with these.

title: Conflicting Information
text:
I got these because I LOVE the Kawaii design. And, I love cats.

That said ... these start off with "4pcs Cute Cats Ballpoint Kawaii Pens" then transition to "Quick Dry Gel Ink Black Pens"

Which are they?

As someone who uses a LOT of pens, owns a lot of pens (I'd say in the 1000's) - I know the difference between BALLPOINT and GEL. These are clearly finer point GEL, which I do not like. I do not like it when sellers put conflicting information in the description.

They are over $2 per pen, and there is NOTHING spectacular about them. The clip is a cat tail rather than a standard clip. Nothing else. These could be something in a $1 store.

title: For Fans of Stranger Things
text:
As someone who LOVES to collect pens – I look for pens to feel unique, be comfortable, be durable, and be REFILLABLE in some way.

These are unique, slightly comfortable, and slightly durable.

But, they are not refillable.

The set runs about $7, so that is $3.50 a pen. And, that is a bit much for something I cannot refill.

These are definitely more towards the novelty use.

title: Not What They're Supposed to Be
text:
Right off ... I REALLY wanted to like these pens. Really.

I got the fruit ones, and they remind me of pens from the 80's/90's. So, there was some nostalgia there.

The first set I got was broke, so I got a replacement. Those came and were PERFECT.

So, why the 3 stars?

Not so perfect. The plunger (or some mechanism) sticks to retract the pen/refill. And, the refill/ink - it is GEL ink not BALL POINT. One of the refills is also TOO short.

I really did want to like these, and I am almost SURE I can find some compatible BALL POINT refills. I just wish the listing was more accurate.

title: Works ... Okay
text:
In the course of packing, as well as shipping, I’ve used MANY brands of tape – and different types:

🖤 Duck Tape (Silver)

🤎 Brown Paper (U-Haul)

🤍 Clear (this, Duck Tape brand, Office Max, Office Depot, Staples, Rotch, ProMaxco, Double Bond)

I mainly use them for packing my boxes for moving or storage.

And, some of my stuff is heavy, so I NEED durable tape.

That said …

This is pretty good, but it has a problem with tearing easy. There is some tightness and hesitation. Depending on the scissors, it is easy to cut through.

Durability? It seems durable at the beginning, but I have questions about it lasting.

I honestly wouldn’t get this again. While it is cheaper than the Staples brand, and has more to it (Staples is 56.4 yards), the Staples is 3Mil compared to this and FAR more durable.

title: Useless Tape
text:
To quote one reviewer – “SAVE YOUR MONEY”.

Since I am in the middle of packing to move, tape is something one can NEVER have too much tape.

And, being that I live in an apartment, I want to pack as quietly as possible. Tape is noisy.

But … it is not so noisy that I would really spend money on this.

Of the three dispensers, one didn’t have the “cutter”. The tape didn’t “sit” well within the dispenser and flopped around.

The tape was super thin, so definitely not to support the bottom of a box regardless of the weight of the packed items. It barely stuck to the box.

It is quiet, but not practical, especially at the price per roll. One (1) roll is about $9 and not that much on the roll. The three (3) rolls price comes out to just shy of $5/roll. Still not worth the price.

I use the tape mainly for “inventory” lists.

title: Fancy Pen Without the Fancy Price
text:
This is a fancier type of pen without the heavy price-tag. It takes a simple “Parker” type of refill which can be found here on Amazon.

The gift box is lovely, but FAR too big for the pen which causes it to move around and “rattle”.

It makes a great gift and is pretty affordable.

Writes beautifully.

title: Simple Grey Pouch
text:
I have to laugh at my own silliness here. In the case of these “grey” KECYCEYN pen/pencil pouches – they’re all the SAME grey color. There is no variation in them.

I ended up with five (5) of them. Then again, I do need them for an unplanned move:

Charcoal Grey
Silver Grey
Shadow Grey
Graphite Grey (this one)
Grey

While priced at $11.99, I’d say they’re probably more like $8-$9. And, the three (3) compartments? Not quite.

The top one has two (2) sections with elastic holders for pens or pencils. The netting area can take smaller things – correction tape, erasers.

The MAIN compartment holds quite a few pens or pencils depending on the thickness and designs of the items. Calculators are not something I would consider to carry in this. Size is a consideration, as is the calculator’s battery from being accidentally turned on.

I love the durable and sturdy material. It can last quite a long time depending on the care.

title: Simple Grey Pen/Pencil Pouch
text:
Since I am moving (not a planned one, but one that is necessary) – I want to organize all of my writing items – pens, pencils, highlighters.

So, I got quite a few of these. I thought there would be variations of the “grey” pouches, as it turns out – there was nothing despite them being available in the following colors:

Charcoal Grey
Silver Grey (this one)
Shadow Grey
Graphite Grey
Grey

They all run about $12 (as of this review). And, it makes sense they’re ALL identical because they’re by the same company – KECYCEYN. And, yes I actually have all five (5) listed.

As far as being 3 compartments – I wouldn’t exactly say that. I define compartment a bit differently than perhaps they do.

The top “compartment” reveals two identical sections with elastic holders for pens or pencils. The netting area can take smaller items (correction tape, erasers).

The bigger “main” compartment holds quite a few pens or pencils depending on the thickness and design. Fancier “fashion” pens (such as those with gems or crowns on top) might reduce the amount this can hold; this also holds true for markers. Calculators? I’m not sold on that idea. It would depend on the size of it. I have a few that would NOT fit in here.

A small square of post-it notes might fit in the zippered area of the main compartment.

Durable and likely to last an entire school year – depends on how well the student cares for it.

I’d feel better recommending this if it were around $8-$9 as it doesn’t seem like it is worth any more than that.

title: Grey Pen/Pencil Pouch
text:
Don’t be fooled by the various versions of this. I ended up getting FIVE of these. And, while they all have a different “color” of grey listed – they’re ALL identical (makes sense because they’re by the same company – KECYCEYN).

Charcoal Grey (this one)
Silver Grey
Shadow Grey
Graphite Grey
Grey

They all run about $12 (as of this review).

As far as being 3 compartments – that depends on your definition of a compartment.

The top zippered “compartment” reveals two identical sections with elastic holders for pens or pencils. The netting area can take small items (correction tape or erasers).

The bigger “main” compartment definitely holds quite a few pens or pencils depending on the thickness and design. Fancier “fashion” pens (such as those with gems or crowns on top) might reduce the amount this can hold. Same for markers. As far as a calculator – it would depend on the size of it. I have a few that would NOT fit in here.

A small square of post-it notes might fit in the zippered area of the main compartment. A standard protractor or 6” ruler as well. Nothing bigger.

It is durable and would definitely last an entire school year – then again, it might depend on how rough the student is with it.

I do believe it is a tad overpriced. I’d feel better recommending this if it were around $8-$9.

title: Better Off Buying Name Brand
text:
If you’ve EVER seen or heard of Paper Mate FLAIR pens (original) – these are an off-brand version.

Both the PM and this one (Apogo) state they’re 0.7mm (Medium). The problem? This one ISN’T. It is more like a 0.5mm, but not 0.7mm. – 1⭐

These claim to be felt tip pens – but in reality? Not even close. They’re closer to rollerball if anything. – 1⭐

I found similar colors of my preferred pens and a corresponding color in this brand to compare as I KNEW something was off.

Notice the BOLDness of the original pens – it is the MEDIUM point, 0.7mm as advertised, and is FELT TIP.

This one? Barely writes at all. And, the pen I tested from my stack is OVER at least 2-3 years old, and been used multiple times. This one? Right out of the package and looks like it is dying.

That wasn’t the only “dead” color either … the magenta (or as close as I could get) was like that too.

Again – 1⭐

There is also the SERIOUS issue of the cap. The “original” ones snap TIGHT. These? The cap, once off, is loose and falls off quite easily which can dry the ink out even faster – 1⭐

Conclusion? If you’re looking for FELT TIP pens – go with the original. Not only are they FELT TIP; they’re far more reliable, bolder, and write better. Definitely wouldn’t get these again and absolutely do not recommend at all.

title: Sweet Gift for a Girl of Any Age, But a Bit Overpriced
text:
This is a SWEET little gift set for a girl of any age (some of older gals still liked to be called girls, at least I do).

The pen is adorable, the journal is cute (I do prefer lined journals more), and the gift box is incredible – though the logo on front could be a bit off-putting.

Still, it is gift-giving ready.

Why the four stars?

I took one off for price. Pens like this can be found at an office store for about $4. The journal and gift-packaging are not $10, the journal is more like $3, packaging around $2. Closer to a $7-$9 value, but not $15.

Otherwise … still a lovely set for any gift-giving occasion.

title: Storage Baskets
text:
Some things work – some things don’t.

I have a LOT of stuff I need to keep close, but LITTLE room to keep it in.

Seeing these bins, I thought – PROBLEM solved. So, I requested them, and eagerly awaited their arrival.

Upon arrival I noticed one thing – the lack of ENGLISH instructions. In fact, there was a SUPER SMALL square “insert” with pictures and obviously NOT ENGLISH instructions.

The square insert was HARD to see, so someone who has vision issues – they’re out of luck. –1 ⭐ there.

Next … unwrapping them. Fairly easy enough. Assembly? Fairly easy. Staying assembled is another. While they snapped into place easily, they wanted to SNAP out even easier. –½ ⭐

Durability – this comes more from staying assembled rather than what they can hold.

I was going to use one of these as a “TBR-R” (to be read & reviewed) stack holder. Of course, as I stood the books up, I knew I couldn’t stack on top of it, but I didn’t mind using one on its own.

These books weren’t HUGE and HEAVY hardcovers – we’re talking the size of a small Harlequin book or a 325-page Revell book; limit 5. That right there – wobbles and the storage basket starts coming undone if moved. Not good if it gets bumped. –½ ⭐

Last feature – price. The bigger baskets (9.8" x 6.5" x 3.8"), the ones I got, are $23.99 for a set of 5. That’s $4.80/per basket 😮

Absolutely no way! These are, at best, dollar store quality. I’d say $2 each, but not close to the price of a gallon of gas per basket (FYI: my “home” station is $4.999 – $5/gallon). –1 ⭐

I cannot justify paying a “gallon of gas” for something so flimsy, has no instructions, and is a piece of homely looking plastic. That is another thing – the aesthetics. These are definitely not really good looking.

That said … if you have low expectations and a good budget, you likely won’t mind.

title: Pretty Design for Cheaply Made Item
text:
I ALWAYS hate being the dissenting vote. But, popularity was NEVER my thing in school, as an adult – really not my thing 😉🤣

Moving on from there …

The buying of school supplies fell to my mom until I reached middle school. Then she let me have a go at it – hand me the money, take me to the store. Usually, that was Kmart. Yes, I know – only three stores left – none in my area. So strange that as of 10 years ago they were in the area.

That said …

I’ve bought school and office supplies from (in the order of how it went):

🛒 Target
🛒 Walmart
🛒 Staples

When I was younger – my mother would let me keep what was left over so I could buy books.

As a result – I learned FAST how to budget my money. Get my needs for less so I could get my WANTS.

Now, I do love fashionable and cutesy items. But, justifying the price tag – not me. I go for functional, durable, and affordable.

These do not qualify as that at all. Yes, they’re fashionable, which I’ll get to. But, these are, at minimum – functional.

While these “function” – they are not durable. They’re “chipboard” – not even wood, so the durability effects the longevity of them. If you need to be mobile with these – they’re not going to stay “fashionable” as the design is WRAPPED on, almost like a contact paper over cardboard. And, the “wrap” can easily tear during use.

There are two clipboards for almost $13, that comes out to about $6.50/each. That is a NO-GO for me.

I say these because Office Depot has a floral plastic one for $4.50. True, it is only ONE design – but durable, functional, and affordable it is. This saves over $2 per clipboard for a total of $4. And, that is enough for a small – large coffee or drink while you’re out and about.

There are the clear plastic ones that run about $5.50 each, and again – meet the durable, functional, and affordable criteria. Not much savings, but even at $2 ($1 per clipboard) – that can get you two (2) $1 drinks at a burger place.

While I KNOW the plain wood ones are just not attractive, there is a 6-pack for a little over $13, averaging about $2.20 per clipboard. And, you can always wrap it with some cutesy contact paper (like this is).

Don’t get me wrong – these aren’t the worst I’ve used, but when the price of NEEDS increases, the WANT has to wait or go for the max benefit.

This isn’t something I would get again and definitely don’t recommend.

title: Too Expensive for a Cheap Product
text:
I’ve been buying school and office supplies since I was in middle school. Yes, my mother would give me the money and take me to the store so I could pick out what I needed. I got to keep what was left over which usually went towards of all things – books. (If you read my reviews – you know I am an AVID reader).

So, as an adult, I KNOW good values and where to get what I need.

While this is “cutesy” – it doesn’t justify a nearly $7 price tag.

It is what is called “chipboard” – not even wood or plastic. It is a wrapped design that can easily unwrap and fall apart affecting the durability.

Office Depot has a floral (though one design) plastic clipboard with a similar clip for about $4.50. Plain wood ones (same clip) – a 6-pack for $13.19 ($2.20/each); and clear plastic multi color ones go for $5.49.

The OD ones will definitely last longer and be far more durable for less money. I could always wrap the plain wood ones with contact paper for a cutesy design; or decorate the back of the clear ones with stickers.

This isn’t something I would get again and definitely don’t recommend it.

title: Not Unless I REALLY Need Them
text:
Standard “view” binders. You can slip in a coversheet so you know what is in each binder, or dress it up for classes. I got them for some “PDF” books I needed to print along with some reference material.

At 1” they claim to hold 200 sheets of paper. Avery and Samsill 1” binders hold 175 – I’m going to say 175 to be certain. I have gotten more pages in the other ones too.

A bit flimsier than the other brands, but work as well as other binders I’ve owned. They are made in the U.S.A.

These binders come as a 6-pack for (as of this review) $25.99. A pretty dismal value:

🛒 Staples – Samsill 6-pack – $23.49 (average $3.92/per binder)

🎯 Target (sells individually) – Avery – $13.14 (6 x $2.19/each; nearly half the price of Integrity)

With Target and Staples, I can get FREE same day pickup. And, Target will bring it out to my car. I know I usually have errands 2-3 times per week, so it isn’t an “extra” trip. In addition, I’m saving anywhere from $2-$13. That’s enough for a soda or a lunch with dessert.

They all work the same. Though, I’ll wait for the SUPER CHEAP BACK2SCHOOL sales. They get even cheaper at that time!

title: Workable but not a Value ...
text:
First off …

These are great standard “view” binders. This means you can slip in a coversheet so you know what is in each binder, or dress it up for classes. I got them for some “PDF” books I needed to print along with some reference material. They work for that purpose.

At 1” they claim to hold 200 sheets of paper. Most of these (Avery, Samsill) hold 175 – I’m going to say 175 to be certain. I have gotten more pages in the other ones too.

Thes a bit flimsy; but work as well as other binders I’ve owned. They are made in the U.S.A.

These binders come as a 6-pack for (as of this review) $25.99 (average $4.33/per binder). That definitely isn’t a good value at all even looking at over $4 per binder. That is until you shop around and release it’s pretty dismal:

🛒 Staples – Samsill 6-pack – $23.49 (average $3.92/per binder)
🎯 Target (sells individually) – Avery – $13.14 (6 x $2.19/each; nearly half the price of Integrity here)

I can pick the Target ones up tomorrow (it was closed as of the writing of this review) and it’ll be brought out to my car, same as Staples (though I'd have to go in there). No waiting for shipping at all. I can get them when I'm out; and save money too, anywhere from $2 – $13 (approximately).

They all work the same, so I definitely would pass on these unless you don’t have a Target or Staples in your area.

And, just wait until the BACK2SCHOOL sales. They get even cheaper then!

title: Classic BIC Stick ... Only Better
text:
BIC pens have ALWAYS been a staple in my home growing up. Between them, Scripto, and PaperMate – I NEVER went without a pen.

I will be honest, I have FAR too many pens on my desk – promotional ones (business, hotels, casinos, medical …), so getting these was a bit overkill. Still … I have ALWAYS had an affinity for the stick pens. (They’re also good to use to refill some promo BIC stick pens).

That said …

These write JUST like the classic pens I used growing up, and they’re the SAME size too. They are made with 74% of recycled plastic which is a LOT better than the pens I used growing up.

Even the packaging is 100% recycled which definitely makes this an even better product all the way around.

The pens (as of this review) are 200 (4 packs of 50) for about $27, that’s about 13¢ per pen – not a bad value for an eco-conscious one.

I would DEFINITELY get these again – if I ever NEED pens … especially with all the ones I have.

title: Great Eco-Conscious Pencils
text:
At about 21¢ per pencil, from a brand like BIC, these are a great value. In addition, they’re also made ecologically better than other pencils of the same type.

As one would expect – they write like a pencil with 0.7 lead. They are disposable, but could be refilled.

The eraser? No quality there – that’s completed expected. My mother used to say that if I didn’t make mistakes, I wouldn’t need an eraser. Funny, but not practical. But, there are big erasers sold that can help with that. I never NOT have a big eraser when I’m writing with pencil.

That said …

The box is a bit weak and can easily bend or rip.

Would be great for anyone of any age. Great set to start the school year off with.

Would likely get again if and when I need pencils … which won’t be for a while with this group and what I already have.

title: Cute, But Watch The Price!
text:
These are really cute highlighters, and definitely great for inspiration.

They can’t really be used long term because of how small they are. They are difficult to hold and the cap can't be put on them.

Colors are pretty cool.

BUT ...

The problem I had was 6 TINY highlighters for just over $14. That’s a bit out of reason. While Stabilo Bros. are a great brand – not at that rate. If I was supposed to get 6 packs of them – then I didn’t get the other 5 packs. And, I did wonder so I contacted customer service. According to the rep, it was indeed a 6-PACK of 6 count. They ordered a replacement.

What arrived? Another 6 count of highlighters (1-pack). I’m sorry – but over $14 for 6 MINI highlighters is not acceptable. I definitely wouldn’t get them again or recommend them.

title: Cutesy, But Not Worth the Price
text:
I pretty much LOVE getting school and office supplies – I also need them and go through quite a few of them.

One thing I seem to misplace a lot (and I don’t know HOW I do it) – clip boards. I just seem to misplace them. So, I try to have a few at my desk or in my bedroom. Yes, I often need a clip board in the bedroom – makes book reviewing a bit easier.

That said …

Durability is a MUST. I don’t care if it is a plain, brown clip board or a fancier one like this – MUST BE DURABLE.

This certainly meets the fashionable and functional test.

However, the quality – that’s debatable.

When I got this, the front was definitely as shiny and clear as shown.

The problem was the harsh feeling on the back. Felt sticky – and, I noticed – it was a plastic protective film. That was the worst experience – trying to pry that film off.

I thought that would give the clip board the shiny, smooth symmetry for both the front and back.

No. The back was now slightly dull (like it was WITH the film) and the texture was “unfinished”. Any paper I set it on – clings to the paper. Definitely not idea. That caused this product to lose a star for the film cover/texture.

Another lost star was due to price. As pretty as this is – it definitely doesn’t grab me at almost $14.

title: Pricey Storage Tubs
text:
I’m probably the dissenting view here …

But …

For nearly (as of this review) $48 – you get two tubs with no lids.

However, these are NOT as sturdy as they look. They’re very wobbly and can easily “unfold”. They’re not for heavy items.

They stack on each other, but do not have a lid so not ideal for moving.

As other places have cheaper and more durable “totes” – I wouldn’t get these or recommend them at all.

Definitely not practical for moving, only for “storing” inside a house.

title: Good Affordable Highlighters
text:
These are good highlighters for everything … BUT … the bible given how thin the pages are.

They are retractable and do a pretty decent job of highlighting text. Good for narrow and thin spaces.

Price – very reasonable given the cost of the major brands.

Overall, a good offering from Mr. Pen.

title: Cheap Multi-Color Pens
text:
These remind me of the souvenir pens I’d get back in the 1980’s when I’d go to amusement parks or even water parks. Yes, even water parks sold pens.

These are, to be fairly honest, cheaply made pens that cannot be refilled.

However, at around $11, that is about $1.83 per pen. A bit pricey for the “cheapness”.

The colors write moderately well, though depending on the lighting and paper – they are fairly light.

The pens are better suited for younger kids to tinker with and to put in goodie bags for them.

Not something I’d get again or recommend.

UPDATE (4/10): The seller did respond that this is a 12-pen set, thus the per pen price is MUCH lower than what I stated so I did update the rating based on the price per pen.

title: Over-Priced and Half The Book
text:
I can NEVER pass up school supplies – highlighters, pencils, pens, and composition books.

One reason is that as a book reviewer, I NEED to take notes for my reviews. And, as a writer, I tend to need the stuff for notes as well.

For close to $5, as of this review, this is a set of TWO (2) Mr. Pen composition books. Each has 50 pages, averaging $2.50 per notebook.

The reason for the 3-star review is how RIDICUOUSLY overpriced it is.

Affordable?

Here’s the problem …

Every June-September (depending on location), places like Staples usually have Back 2 School sales and they are REALLY GOOD sales.

I mention this because last year, I went (skipped 2020 obviously) and got quite the haul – paper, spiral notebooks, pencils, pens – you name it and they had a sale for it.

One deal at Staples:

Composition Books, 100 pages for 50¢ each

Those books, same size in width and height as these, have DOUBLE the pages these books do. For $1, I can get TWO (2) 100-page books in either WIDE or COLLEGE ruled pages. Why would I pay FIVE (5) times that for HALF?

Even MEAD has a wide rule composition book, 100 pages for $2.79. That’s less than 30¢ more for TWICE the amount of pages.

I’m sorry, the mustache sticker isn’t a good enough draw to pay more money for.

Honestly, if you NEED these books right now – Staples has the TRU RED Composition Notebook, 7.5" x 9.75", College Ruled, 100 Sheets, 4/Pack for $10.49. That’s about $2.62 per notebook. While slightly higher than this set, you are getting DOUBLE the amount of pages per notebook for about 12¢ more. And, at least you can have extra on hand.

If you like wide ruled, that 4-pack is on sale for $5.49 ($1.37 per notebook).

But, if you tend to go through them like I do – take the $5 you’d pay for this set, and hit the BACK 2 SCHOOL sale as soon as it’s announced. You’ll get more for your $$.

I definitely couldn’t recommend these and wouldn’t get them again.

title: Fashionable Pencils
text:
Triangle pencils are NOTHING new. At least not within the last 25-30 years.

I remember back in the 1990’s, there was the YIKES! brand. In fact, I still have about 2-3 around my home.

About 10-15 years ago, I got some Ticonderoga Tri-Write pencils. Amazon sells 12 (a dozen) here for less than $3. Those come with erasers. These do not.

These come with a SMALL eraser that works, but it won’t last through 12 pencils at all. The sharpener is small, and doesn’t collect the shavings so you will need to stand over a trash can to sharpen the pencils.

They’re cute and colorful – functional? Absolutely. The graphite, while #2 is definitely lighter and doesn’t leave streaks or smudges.

Value? This pack runs $6.99 (as of this review). That’s not a good value at all. I could EASILY get 2-3 packs of the Ticonderoga ones.

If you’re looking for value – I’d go with the older brand. You want fashion? These will work.

title: Overpriced Pens and Journals
text:
This is a rather “generic” pen and journal set.

To be honest, these remind me of dollar store finds put into a “set”. The pens are definitely generic (not even a brand name on them). The spirals are plain.

They would make an interesting “goodie bag” item. But for the current price of $7.68 – it’s TERRIBLY overpriced.

There is nothing about this set that stands out for it to average $3.84 per pen/journal set.

Definitely wouldn’t get again or recommend.

title: Worldly Pen Cup
text:
I have a LOT of pens. And, I use a VARIETY of cups:

🖊️ Coffee Cups
🖊️ Mugs
🖊️ Small Buckets
🖊️ Pen Cups
🖊️ Old (cleaned out) Candle Jars

So, this is definitely not out of my style. And, it is a cute little globe.

Heavy? This thing could cause damage if thrown at someone (not that I am recommending that – just a warning).

It can hold about (depending on width, grip/no grip) about 27 pens without “squishing”. I went by various widths, and pens with grips. There was no slouching and no crowding to get a pen out. Each person’s experience will vary.

The current price is around $25, and it would be a decent investment.

As far as gifting – this is not really “gift” ready. The Styrofoam crumbles easily and can get messy. It does arrive in a plain white box though.

Overall, I do like it, just wouldn’t get it again.

title: Good Gift if Improved
text:
Right off, this would seem like a wonderful gift: journal holder with 2 books and a pen. The gift box is gorgeous too. One would think this would be a great gift. It is, and it isn’t. It truly depends on how “picky” someone is.

A lot of reviewers are right about the “creases” on the cover – this “damaged” area tend to cover the width of where the string is despite a protective “paperband” around it during transit. The pen is not exactly cheap, it is on par with pens of this nature often found at places like Staples by the register for about $2.99-$3.99. But there is nothing really special about it.

The journal set has really NO place to store the pen, unless it is the “elastic” on the “buckle” in front.

If that is the case … if the nib is not retracted, it could lead to ink stains on the cover.

The books are held in place by elastic and can be replaced. One is a dotted notebook, the other is lined.

Priced a little over $11 as of this review – this is definitely not worth the price. I would say for around $9-$10 it might be.

This isn’t something I would get again or give someone.

title: I'll Stay With The O.G.
text:
When I bought my first printer in April 2003, I quickly became aware of HOW expensive ink was and still is. Since then, I've owned SEVERAL printers and/or all-in-one machine and different brands:

🖨️ Epson (2) (had to replace one 6 months after I got it (2003-2004)
🖨️ Lexmark (2004)
🖨️ Brother (2005-2007)
🖨️ Kodak (2) (2007-2010)
🖨️ HP (currently 3; 2 are in service, 1 is being “stored”) (2010-current; obviously satisfied with the brand)

Most of the printers were on the “expensive” side of the initial purchase with the ink being cheap.

The Epson printers I had were fairly inexpensive, ink was slightly reasonable. Quality? Great for documents, especially when using higher quality paper. Photos? Not so much.

Lexmark was a pricey printer, cheap ink, printed HORRIBLY. The black was more greenish. Never again.

Brother was more affordable on both sides, but still not great for photos.

I’ll give Kodak this – they had a good thing going: $9.99 for black, and I believe $14.99 for color. Photo and document quality were great. I couldn’t complain – except … their printers BROKE. Literally BROKE.

HP … my 209a was a dream, ink was getting up there in price though. I got an 8610 and with it came a 6-month free trial of HP INSTANT INK. I started it in February 2016, still a happy customer six (6) years later.

Last year, I got an HP Laser Jet, it had a three (3) month trial of INSTANT INK. Still on the plan and love it.

For the past few years, I’ve seen these “compatible” types of cartridges. And, let’s face it – the printer companies tell you NOT to use non-brand ink.

I got these to test two theories:

#1 – Is the printer that smart and will my printer break?

#2 – Are these JUST as good as the branded ones?

The answers?

#1 – Yes, the printer is that smart. It will know they're not legit cartridges and warn you. And, no, the printer won’t break if you install and use them; though note that using them might violate your warranty.

#2 – No, these are NOWHERE near as good as the O.G cartridges (in my case – HP)

They do fit the machine. The problem is, in using them, I can’t allow my computer to receive updates, including security ones. Sorry, but right off – no go for these no matter how much I save.

The quality? Started off great. I decided I’d print something complicated like a downloaded (superb quality) picture of a book cover.

I’ve owned my HP 8610 since February 2015. I’ve installed I don’t know HOW MANY cartridges. So, I know this HORRIBLE quality wasn’t on my end. True I've had a bad pic here or there, but not this bad and not from NEW cartridges.

I printed three pages of this “book cover” – each time the quality declined even worse at the bottom. The top starts off good, but this is how it ends.

It could’ve been a bad batch, but I am not risking my printer or network security to try it again.

I’ll stay with what I’m using and go from there. At least HP's cartridges are guaranteed and work with my machine.

title: Perfect Pen Set
text:
I absolutely LOVE collecting pens. I am more partial to ball point pens than gel or roller ball though.

But, this set was FAR too cute to pass up. The current sale price of about $16 is pretty attractive. Even the non sale price of about $18 is pretty fair as well.

As described – this is a two (2) pen set – one (1) ball point (blue); one (1) rollerball (pink). I do wish it was the reverse, but that is me.

The “window” gift box is pretty and definitely makes it attractive for an any occasion gift.

The pens are “metal”, so they have some weight to them. While I love them, they do get uncomfortable to hold for any length of time.

The ball point is a twist action, and twist off to replace. The replacement is a standard “Parker” type ball point refill. The rollerball is refillable, but I don’t know which refill would fit it best.

The ball point is smooth on almost all paper surfaces. The rollerball best functions on smoother paper.

The lovely set has hearts on it. Not engraved, but not printed either.

Overall, I absolutely love THIS set! I wouldn’t hesitate to give it as a gift or recommend it.

title: Not Exactly Professional
text:
If you’re looking for a basic letter envelope – these might work. For under $5, they are not a bad value.

Everyone else has stated what I noticed:

✉️ The box isn’t adequate for storage
✉️ The envelopes are thin
✉️ The “security” lining is not secure
✉️ The brand “watermark” on the front doesn’t allow this for professional use (I can use a correction tape to mark over it though)

I can use them; I wouldn’t get them again though.

title: Inspiration That Sticks
text:
I actually get these for book photos on social media. They’re also cute on a laptop as well.

As far as durability – depends on where you stick them. There are some flaws, those can be overlooked depending again on where you stick them.

For the price, it’s a good value. I definitely wouldn’t hesitate to get them again or recommend them.

title: Cute Colorful Ball
text:
🚫🏀 RIGHT OFF – THIS IS NOT A BOUNCY TYPE OF BALL – THESE BALLS HAVEN’T BEEN “BOUNCY”. 🚫🏀

If you’re expecting that – it won’t happen. This is a rubber band ball – a ball shaped out of rubber bands. I’ve known about these and even made a few back as a kid. It is perhaps the BEST way to keep your rubber bands stored in my opinion

These are not, as the seller advertises: “red, yellow, blue and green”. They have pastel colors as shown in the photos: orange, pink, purple, mint, yellow, and white. It is as shown. I didn’t mind that as I enjoy most of the colors on the ball. I got it more for its function.

The ball comes in a light and wimpy cardboard box. Easy to discard of on the recycling bin.

I have not counted the bands as I don’t want to dismantle the ball. I use only what I need when I need it. It does look to be a decent quantity. They are also only “one size” – a decent medium size. Can wrap around a wrapping tube 2-3x depending on the tube size.

These are thicker than the office rubber bands I’ve bought. Do they work? Just as good as ones purchased in a store. I’ve had no real issues with breakage. I haven’t tested it past a few loops on some items.

I do LOVE it and wouldn’t mind getting another one as the price (under $7) seems fair.

title: Easy to Use, Sturdy
text:
In August (2021), I got a Scotch Thermal Laminator (TL901X) as I wanted to do my own bookmarks along with other items.

[NOTE: do not laminate the CDC COVID vaccine cards in case you haven’t had a booster or a future one is required. There are card holders and protectors for it here on Amazon]

I also got the 3 mil laminating pouches (TP3854-100) to go with it.

When I saw these, I did have to wonder if they were similar to or better than the ones I got. Obviously I didn’t have a need to write on them, but, I thought I’d try them.

They are a bit thicker than the 3 mil pouches despite using the same setting. These didn’t tend to curl as bad in the laminator I had, so that was a bonus.

Pricewise? I’ll opt for the ones I got as I don’t need to use these to write on. I think, from other reviews they would be good for that purpose though.

title: Basic, But Complicated
text:
I have a love/hate affair with pencil sharpeners. They’re necessary, but finding the “perfect” one is elusive – electric or manual. Which one?

That is definitely complicated.

In school, the manual ones were like Charlie Brown’s kite-eating tree. To get a new pencil sharpened, I’d have to sacrifice 1/3 to ½ of my pencil.

Electric ones could be bad. Battery operated tend to work be slightly worse than plug-in.

But, from the early 1990’s until around 2010; we had a plug-in electric sharpener that was awesome, so much so I even had one. After so long, they tend to stop working.

In/around 1997/1998 – I ended up with a Yikes manual sharpener. I LOVED that, but it got packed away. I brought it out a few years ago, and the ONLY thing wrong? The bottom suction part wouldn’t “stick”.

When I saw this, and having a better opinion of manual sharpeners, this looked like a good idea.

And, it is … to a point.

There are some striking issues:

✏️ Lack of directions. This is a more complicated sharpener to operate given a “hold this, pull this out” deal. You don’t know, because there are ZERO directions (no insert, nothing on the box) (-1 ⭐)

✏️ Lack of “suction” on the bottom. This has to be manually held down, there is nothing to ADHERE it to a surface (no nails, no glue, no suction). Definitely not ideal for a classroom with students lining up to use it (-1 ⭐)

Is it worth the current price of $9.14? With those issues? Not so much.

It does sharpen well, just not ideal for certain situations. I definitely wouldn’t get another one, and as far as recommending it – I couldn’t even mention it.

title: Sharp ... But, Only to a Point
text:
Growing up, I used all kinds of pencil sharpeners. I’ve had, depending on which one I’ve used, a preference for them.

For the LONGEST time, I hated the rotary ones as they were infamous for pencil-eating (much like Charlie Brown and the Kite-Eating Tree). So, once my mom bought a REALLY good electric one back in the early 90’s – those were ALL I would use.

I really, and still do, detest the small manual sharpeners. I refuse to use them.

I ended up, about 30 years ago, getting my own electric sharpener. Sadly, both of those oldies died a few years ago.

Today’s replacements? Very questionable quality, durability, and functionality.

I love the battery-operated electric ones as they’re easy to take on a trip or outing.

That said …

Last year I got a battery-op operated electric sharpener from Staples. It “kind of” works. It sharpens the pencil, but there are issues with it. Given the price, I can’t complain too much. My mother’s Staples sharpener – works like a charm.

This little Amazon Basics? For the price it is a bit … on the fence for me. But … I LOVE the dual power availability.

This can EASILY plug into your computer or laptop’s USB ports. If you have limited ports, I’d suggest a HUB. I usually use one. Or, it can be connected to a power strip/tower that has a USB outlet.

Does it work?

It is quiet. It has a LARGE shavings capacity for a relatively small sharpener. It does sharpen the pencils, but not to a “pointy”-point. It isn’t dull, but there is room for SOME improvement.

Unlike another sharpener I got from here on Amazon, this did come with instructions.

For the price, it isn’t bad.

title: Overpriced Journals
text:
First of all, let’s talk about pages vs. sheets when it comes to journals.

Journals are much like books (fiction, non-fiction, textbooks) – both sides are used, basically two (2) pages but only ONE (1) sheet of paper.

Like the book I am reading – it is 418 pages, but in reality, it likely only has 209 sheets of paper between the covers; and the story starts on page 11.

These journals have 80 sheets for a total of 160 pages.

Depending on why you’re getting the journal will depend on whether you can use both sides of the paper. When I’m taking notes for book and product reviews – I HAVE to use both sides. I usually use pencil for the notes. When I was journaling and writing in a diary, I’d use pen – and yes, I’d use BOTH sides of the sheet. Of course, it depends on what kind of ink you use. Gel and water-based tend to show through more than regular ballpoint ink does.

That said …

These are a basic journal – nothing you couldn’t find for around $2-$3 at an office supply store, Target, or Walmart.

The cover isn’t “hard” like cardboard based; it is a durable (but flexible) plastic cover.

The pages are not thick, but not tissue thin either. I love the fact there are different colors so I can organize notes.

My only issue is that these are a bit over-priced and there is nothing really special about them.

They’ll work for what I need though.

title: Home or Professional Use
text:
Working in the fast-food industry, “prep” was a daily job. From sauces, to meat, to cheese, to just about EVERY food item that was used – they had to have dates.

One place I worked at used ROX (as shown in the picture):

Received
Open
