eXpires

Very self-explanatory. Only these were used for the HUGE gallon size sauces: butter garlic, barbeque, hot sauce.

The R date was the date the item arrived at the store, usually from the corporate office’s “commissary” truck. The O was the date it opened. The X – when it expired. Not the date that was listed on the bottle, the amount of time allowed from open to “possible” spoilage. Usually that was a month.

Though we didn’t have stickers like this. I wish we did. We had to write on the side with a Sharpie. Sometimes that got messy and the ink would smudge. While not major to some – we could’ve gotten in trouble for it.

Typically found (hot sauce) (like seen on picture):

R – 12/25/2021
O – 1/05 (we’d know it was 2022 right off)
X – 2/05 (despite the bottle read an “expired” date of 12/31/2022)

Actual “mileage” would vary. Usually, the hot sauce was gone WAY before that.

For the price, this is definitely a LOT of labels for home use, but worth it if you’re a bulk-buying and food prepper.

I have come to rely on these stickers with leftovers as well.

title: Quality Recycled Notebooks
text:
When it comes to recycled items and environmentally friendly products, I’m often at odds with the value vs. the “do-good” feeling.

Let’s face it – depending on how much you make, how much savings you have – affordable is a subjective term.

Last year when the mask restrictions were relaxed, I wandered into Staples. It felt good to have some “nostalgia” back – “life before the pandemic” and all. And, it just coincided with the back-2-school sales. Uh-oh.

I was able to get spiral notebooks for 25¢; comp books for 50¢; and 8”x10” notebook paper for 75¢. Hard to beat deals; actually “can’t beat these at all deals”. Naturally the spiral books were 8”x10”, and the comp books were slightly smaller – not as small as these notebooks though.

Therein is the problem – size, price, and environmental thinking. It is hard to want to pay approximately $2.30 for a notebook that offers less.

These are 5.5”x8” notebooks with 100% recycled paper. The paper is thick, durable, and bleed proof (mostly). These are the perfect size for a medium sized purse.

The covers are pretty durable and made with 80% recycled material.

The only problem? Is this post-consumer waste or pre-consumer waste.

What is the difference?

♻️ Pre-consumer waste is a material that was discarded before it was ready for consumer use. Pre-consumer waste is commonly used in manufacturing industries, and is often not considered recycling in the traditional sense.

♻️ Post-consumer waste is material discarded after someone uses it.

That said, the books are cute and come in a recyclable box. Are they worth the price? Not for me considering that I usually shred or save the notebooks depending on the material I put in them.

title: Cheap Sharpie Markers
text:
If I didn't know better, I'd swear these were the normal Sharpie marker. The barrel and cap are the same, the tip is the same, the smell? Not the same.

The cap is VERY sturdy when it snaps on, so it can be a bit of a pain to tug off.

Otherwise? They write like the more expensive counterpart. Longevity? I've had issues with the name brand. But, getting two (2) dozen pens for about $6 is a pretty good deal. If and when I need them again, I will likely get these.

title: Works, But Not That Well
text:
This SORT of reminds me of the paper cutters from school – shape, function, and difficulty.

This doesn’t cut that well and has some alignment issues. I did, after a learning curve, get it to work better.

Mine had flaws other reviewers pointed out. Knowing them ahead of time, I had something to work with.

This isn’t perfect, but it works when you figure out HOW to work it with the flaws.

Another thing? The guillotine arm is a bit hard to lock into place for storage.

title: Dual Highlighters
text:
These are a great idea ... if you use both colors equally.

I usually use highlighters for keeping track of my book reviews, my own stories, and to-do lists. These work, for the price. Not practical for me. I prefer the Sanford highlighters as they last far longer and are, for the money, a better value.

title: Address Labels
text:
The product I got is the 30 per page, 3 per row, 1 inch label.

These are comparable to the Avery 5160 label and that company offers a FREE downloadable template. Easy to use, easy to save. Or you can fill your labels in on their website.

These performed remarkably well in my Inkjet. My LaserJet wanted the day off. Refused to be acknowledged by my network.

These peeled right off, stuck to envelope. Bright, clear and easy to work with. Far cheaper than Avery or even the generic office supply store ones. The only issue I have – packaging. The cardboard they’re in doesn’t work well.

title: Sweet Christian Giftable Bookmarks
text:
3.5 Stars

Okay, I’m going to be honest – these are NOT the greatest bookmarks in the world because of quality.

They do require some assembly, I managed to get all of them done in about 10 minutes due to sorting and untangling the small cords.

That said …

Here are the “problems”

🔖 Cross is not stone, enamel or enamel type on metal
🔖 Cross is a bit too heavy for bookmark (tearing can occur)
🔖 The “charm” cord is tricky to work, those with vision or dexterity issues might have problems

What is nice about this set? The bible quotes on the bookmark, the idea of them being giftable (though you’d have to furnish your own box or gift bag), and the price is pretty decent given the fact there are 12 total bookmarks, two of each bookmark. There are enough cords and charms for all.

Practical in use? It varies. If you use them a lot, there is a chance for them to get torn and lose the charm.

Not something I would get again though.

title: MONTHLY Planner
text:
Like someone else, I thought this would be the standard planner: month first, followed by week with days.

NOPE

It is ONLY a monthly planner.

The cover is durable and flexible, will work well for someone at their desk or they can slip it into a laptop bag, or backpack.

The pages are thick. Wouldn’t use a sharpie or liquid based inks. Pencil, pen, and Flair-type felt tip pens work well.

For nearly $10? Not worth it for me given the fact I prefer a “daily” planner as well.

title: Cutesy Novelty Pens
text:
These are exactly what they state – novelty pens in the quantity stated. For less than $11, you get six (6) pens. Average price? $1.83.

These are VERY thin, a bit hard to grip, and not refillable. As far as durable? Not too much. The packaging is a bit rough and the “top” can easily break off when trying to get it open/out.

To me, they are not really practical. It is hard to write for any length of time with it.

Yoobi does give an item for an item bought. Depending on how much you view the contribution, these might be worth it. They’re not worth it for me.

title: Big and Cute Push Pins
text:
I use push pins for just about everything.

I use smaller ones for picture and document frames; larger ones for décor items. They do the work and don’t damage the walls too bad. After 13 years where I am, when I move some serious renovating is bound to happen.

FYI: the complex I live in has renovated units twice.

Anyway …

Push pins are definitely my go-to for décor purposes. I hate the ones in the paper backing. After they’re opened – they get all over.

These? They are in a cute little tub with a screw-top lid. Perfect for storage and can sit on on desk or in a drawer.

Price is pretty reasonable. As of this review they’re a little over $5.

Pretty pleased, would definitely get them again.

title: Basic Planner - Nothing Specatacular
text:
I’ve been seeing giveaways for these planners on Instagram and when I got to get one through the Vine program, I was thrilled.

In all honesty – this is a pretty planner, but not really worth the money. I can get one like this for $10-$13.

Like most planners – it has a spacious monthly calendar before the weekly/daily section. Most holidays are listed. Thick paper, room for notes and contact information.

Given the fact of how basic it is, it is great for reminders and appointments (I’d suggest using pencil in case it changes). I use it for my photos and blog-post reminders and it works.

Overall, I likely wouldn’t get one of these again.

It does make a great gift though.

title: Colorful Correction Tapes
text:
I’ve been using correction tapes since around 1997/1998. I used to get the TomBow (usually refills) at Walmart.

Naturally, I did not want to go back to correction fluid. And, being carded at Walmart for it (I was 22 at the time) – that stopped me right there. My mom might want to use it, I won’t. It’s also too messy and dries up too fast. Remember the thinner liquid sold separately? (I also got carded again for correction fluid about 4 years ago).

These work just like the TomBow did and my usual BIC correction tapes. I do like the cap on the end to protect the tape.

For the price, this is a decent value. Colors are fun.

title: Sweet Undated Planner
text:
As planners go, I love the idea of an undated planner. I also LOVE the January-December planners and not the July-July academic ones.

Often, as soon as they are available for the new year, I’ll get a planner. I love them as a Christmas gift.

Often I’ll get one of the first batches out as I do dislike waiting. And, then I’ll see a planner I REALLY want. Ugh! That means giving the unwanted one away, passing on the one I like, or … modifying it for the next year. Which, I recently did. That was easy due to having stickers, washi tapes, and correction tapes. Looks great for being modified.

An undated planner actually prevents all that stress and extra work. It leaves the organizing to the person for the months as well as whatever holidays/special days they want to add. Obviously the main goal of an “undated” planner.

They can also use it for the next year or save it for another time. It can also be regifted in case the person cannot use it.

This is sweetly packaged for gift giving – and an anytime gift, given that is undated. Birthdays, anniversaries, wedding, graduation – anytime.

It is more of a journal binding than the spiral binding I prefer so it doesn’t lay flat as well as I like. Durability is questionable given how often it is opened, closed, moved, etc.

Pages are thick. No bleed through from regular ball point ink or fine tip markers.

Overall, I do love this and will definitely get the full use of it.

title: Great Novelty Pens
text:
Most of the times I enjoy going to Staples to get some good bargains.

Why did I start my review like that? Simple – by the checkout counters, they usually have pens like this in a display. They range from around $1.99-$4.99 depending on the style. I bought a diamond topped one from them for $3.99; a crown topped one for $2.99.

Even at $1.99 a pen; this six-pack would cost $11.94; this set here on Amazon saves over $2.00.

You have choices of all of one color, or a multi-color pack.

These really make great stocking stuffers or goodie-bag items. They’re easy to refill, look for the mini-Cross type refill here on Amazon.

They are easy to hold, not as heavy as they look, write well, and definitely unique.

Would love to get more and definitely recommend them.

title: Simulated Vintage Journal
text:
Being a fan of Charmed (the 1998-2005 series), I wanted my own Book of Shadows (BOS).

Finding a suitable replica journal was a bit of a challenge. Of course, nothing is going to be 100%, so I opted to make my own.

A decent “vintage” appearance journal is one step, getting “aged” paper, that is another.

While this has some solid binding, vintage appearance, the paper is not really “paper” per se. It appears to be some kind of cotton type item. Definitely would need more than a pencil or ball point ink pen.

The book is thick, but cannot add pages to it. Comes in a great gift bag.

While cute, stylish, and definitely vintage looking – this isn’t something I would get again or recommend. Not sure how I will use as I can’t even tape anything into it because of the “paper” fiber.

I’ve used it as a photo prop and it works quite nicely there.

title: Just Like What the Office Stores Sell
text: This is nearly identical to what the office supply stores sell, and priced identical as well. Works as good as any other packing tape. Easy to use as well.

title: It Works, Just Doesn't Work For Me
text:
The idea of a reusable (fabric) box is somewhat interesting. Most all of my regular boxes get reused over and over. Some are at least 20 years old. So, the reusable factor isn’t a BIG deal.

For almost $24, this gray fabric box is snazzy enough to be in a living room or home office, even a bedroom. It isn’t heavy duty though. If you have hanging files, this won’t work that well either.

It comes with ONE “see-through” inventory card pouch. Unless you’re close to it, it won’t be seen.

This isn’t something I would get again or recommend.

title: Good Idea, Price is Wrong
text:
I got this more or less for my mom and it is JUST LIKE a set of pink ones I got. For the price of this one (when it was available, it was $6.99) – I got TWO pink ones.

This works like those do:

A nice little “wallet” to hold your vaccination card in for easy presentation. The cards fit perfectly in them. And, the holders are stylish, easy to find in a purse or other bag. Some jackets have big enough pockets for them.

This is great for parents who need to carry their child(ren)’s cards, especially those who are not yet old enough to carry their own cards. You can also slip in your driver’s license in case you just need those two together.

While pleased, do feel it should be lower in price given the other options out there.

title: Card Holders - Great for Parents
text:
These are nice little “wallets” to hold your vaccination card in for easy presentation. The cards fit perfectly in them. And, the holders are stylish, easy to find in a purse or bag.

I like the idea of being able to carry two cards for parents whose children are not yet old enough to carry their own cards. You can also slip in your driver’s license in case you just need those two together.

For less than $7 you get two of these and they’re sturdy.

Keep one as backup or give it to a friend.

Definitely pleased with this!

title: Colorful Pens, Needs Instructions & Warnings
text:
Let’s face it, we see these types of pens at the checkout counter of office supply stores (Staples … sound familiar).

I know I am FOREVER looking for my favorite color and combo.

Pens like this usually go for around $3.99-$4.99.

These, unfilled, run about $2 each. They’re a decent value.

These are unfilled, come with a cute stopper – on instructions, you’re on your own there.

I used fine and chunky glitters to fill the tubes. The stopper wasn’t that easy to work with, so I DON’T RECOMMEND using a liquid in it.

The top doesn’t connect well with the pen barrel and I had to GLUE it together. Again, no instructions to tell you exactly HOW to do this.

They do make good gifts.

I do like these and am pretty happy with them overall.

title: Great for a DIY Planner
text:
These worked really well (along with some dated washi tapes) in converting a spare 2022 planner I had to a 2023 one.

These worked well, stick VERY well. And, there are many to choose from. There are enough for all holidays. Some are missing. Some stickers are large and others small.

For the price - these are a good value.

title: Hallmark Christmas Cards
text:
Hallmark has been the standard for most everything Christmas since WAY before I was born. Established in 1910, the company made its first Christmas cards in 1915 – that was less than 2 years before my grandma was born (February 1917).

So, they are, as stated on Wikipedia: “the oldest and largest manufacturer of greeting cards in the United States” – they’re likely EXPERTS in the field by now.

They are pricier than the other mass-produced box cards out there. I remember getting CUTESY sets of Christmas cards from Walmart for $3-5 box (about 24 cards/envelopes) back before 2010.

Now, a 10-pack of Hallmark cards runs about $8 at Walmart. And, it seems those “cheaper” ones are gone. Too bad, they were cute. I still have some as I seemingly accumulate Christmas cards every so often.

Back to these …

Mine came in a brown box with a label photo of the cards on it.

There are 10 cards of each of the 4 designs, and 40 plain red envelopes. No need to go looking for a coordinating envelope. The envelope flap is LIGHTLY stamped with the HALLMARK logo.

The cards are simple in design – non secular. Red, blue, green, and slate blue cards with gold edging.

Given how much cards run today – just under $18 (before tax), this is a pretty good value. Great for co-workers, friends, even family.

Honestly, even if you don’t hand out many cards this set will do you for SEVERAL years. I barely do 5 cards a year so I know it will last me. A long time. Also, it doesn’t help I have two different packs from last year, a stash of the old Walmart ones, and about 2-3 boxes of cards someone else gave me.

title: Pens With Heart
text:
I’ve often found pens like this in the checkout area of major office supply stores (looking at y’all there Staples). They’re typically about $2.99-$3.99 (around $3.24-$4.32). And, right then and there? That’s not so bad. I mean, it is a cute pen, am I right?

That is until you see this deal:

8 pens/$13.64 (as of this review PLUS my county/state sales tax of 8.375%).

Single pen? About $1.71, So, right off I’m saving $1.53-$2.61 per pen. Total savings? $12.24-$20.88.

100% a great deal already. And, since there are two of each pen this set is great for:

🖊️ Besties
🖊️ Mom/Daughter
🖊️ Sisters

They each come in a velveteen sleeve which can EASILY be separated to give out individually or packaged as a set for a gift.

They write quite well and refills are easy to find here on Amazon. They take a SMALLER Cross-type. There are a few sellers I’ve bought from.

The only reason for the four stars is that the pens I got were a bit “dull” as if they were dirty or wiped with grease.

These are great and LOVE them. Lightweight for a “metal” pen.

title: Good "Promo" Type Pen
text:
As soon as I pulled this out of the package, I KNEW this was familiar. I had a pen JUST LIKE THIS one.

After looking in my “carry” bag, I pulled it out. Yup – same pen style, weight, design (this one is ROSE GOLD).

This is IDENTICAL (with the except of the metal color) to a CHEVROLET pen I bought at a NASCAR race.

I paid roughly $20 for the Buttoni pen and thought it was wonderful.

This RG one has NO inscribing on it but is identical in the bottom barrel design, weight, and length to the Chevy pen.

This one is about $5 less though.

Believe it or not, these can be found for as little as $5 a pen through other companies.

It writes pretty solid despite how heavy it is. That’s one of the reasons I don’t use my Chevy pen much.

Either pen makes a great gift. This isn’t anything too special though. And, knowing where else to get them – pretty pricey too.

title: Great Idea, But Using it is a PAIN
text:
This reminded me of those PURPLE mattresses being sold and talked about. So, keeping that in mind (and no, this is NO relation to that company) – I decided to get this.

It is pretty big, so bigger or more “ample” rears won’t have to worry about lack of space.

This also sits up HIGH, as in 1-2 inches.

The problem was that with my office chairs, I tend to lean more forward. My main desk/office chair already has that issue. This compounded it.

As far as softness – no chance here for that one. I felt like I was sitting on a rubber raft.

Comfortable? Not that either

Does it do what it claims? I wasn’t able to sit on it long enough to really see a benefit. My mother sort of liked it – she was able to tolerate about 10 minutes with it.

At nearly $30 it isn’t a bad value, though not for me.

title: Multi Use Highlighters
text:
As of this review, these highlighters are about $11, and I’m sorry – that is a tad too pricey for me.

They do work as promised – dual tips. This is especially great for small and big text, small and big work areas. Also, they’re great for marking projects.

Quality I’d expect from the Pilot brand.

title: Gorgeous But Not Practical
text:
As a lover of books, if my books are new – I try to keep them new even after reading.

If they’re used – depending on how bad they are, I try to prevent further damage.

When marking one’s place, I definitely do not mark the book. Receipts, old gift cards, and business cards are good. Bookmarks are preferred.

This is a beautiful, classy, giftable bookmark. Beautifully packaged for gift-giving and definitely a stunner. Well worth the money. I’ve paid more for one at a bookshop.

This is definitely not recommended for smaller paperbacks or bigger ones. I’d suggest hardcover books are more appropriate.

It’s gorgeous, but not practical for the books I read.

title: Correction Tape
text:
My first introduction to correction tapes was in the late 1990’s with TomBow. I had a wide and thin tape holder and would buy the refills.

Now, they’re just one piece and disposable.

As I hadn’t been able to find the refills (one was a huge green one, another was a small purple one) – I switched to the BIC correction tapes. Those are reasonably priced.

These?

For a four pack, it is around $4.25 so a little over $1.06 each. That is definitely a bargain. They work just as well as the name brands.

Easy to hold and use. Definitely wouldn’t hesitate to get them again.

title: Definitely a Huge Wall Calendar
text:
This definitely fits my wall and I LOVE it! I had one like this last year and it definitely was durable. The paper – the wire – everything.

The only problem with this is the wire and loop is a bit small for the calendar.

Other than that, for the price? Easy way to track family appointments.

title: Fits Most Parker-Type Pens
text:
A cheaper version of a Parker-type refill. Good value considering that a 2-pack of Parker refills are about $10.

I used to get a pretty decent generic 2-pack for about $1 back between 1997-2000. Given that “inflation” – the price (as of this review approximately $10) is pretty decent.

Easy, smooth, bold flowing ink.

Highly recommend and would buy again.

title: More for Fashion Than Function
text:
This is one of those sets that is fashionable, but not quite functional.

For about $19 you get the following:

📎🖊️ Stapler
📎🖊️ Staples (1000 count)
📎🖊️ Staple Remover
📎🖊️ (2) Diamond Topped Pens
📎🖊️ (4) Medium Binder Clips

The stapler has an acrylic body and the staple remover has the acrylic top and bottom.

All very fashionable and matches my metal rose gold pen/pencil cup.

So, why the three stars? Function. Mostly function:

📎🖊️ Stapler – the “top” keeps popping up. After putting two of the staple strips in, the stapler continues to “pop” up

📎🖊️ Staples (1000 count) – these are pretty good. Sturdy and fashionable.

📎🖊️ Staple Remover – this came with one of the acrylic pieces broke off. I was able to glue it back, though it isn’t too fashionable. I put that on the “bottom”.

📎🖊️ (2) Diamond Topped Pens – best part of the set. Twist to use, bold and black ink, easy to refill. I already have several like it.

📎🖊️ (4) Medium Binder Clips – these work like they’re supposed to

The stapler is the biggest reason I got this set. It works, but for the price of this set – it is very disappointing.

title: Pricey Notebooks
text:
For around $19 as of this review (average about $4.75/each) you get four (4) dual spiral notebooks in plain colors:

📓 Dark Blue
📓 Black
📓 Blue
📓 Beige

They are solid and durable. Lay-flat design. Top cover can “fold-over”.

Paper is smooth for pen or pencil. Erasing doesn’t tear, no bleed through for ball point pen (didn’t try liquid-based pens). Perforated for easy page removal.

They ARE NOT 3-SUBJECT as stated on the wrap shown in the picture. They are single subject.

As far as “pages” go … there are 100 sheets, double sided – so indeed, 200 pages.

These are incredibly basic and a tad overpriced for me. I’ve bought $5 journals at Staples, Office Depot, and Walmart that were definitely more decorative (these don’t come with anything to decorate them with – you’re on your own).

I honestly wouldn’t get them again, and don’t recommend them. I certainly wouldn’t get them for anyone I know.

title: Easy Peasy Bookmarks
text:
These are a SUPER affordable way of keeping your page in a big hard cover, bigger paperback, or in a spiral notebook. Easy to use, and a lot of colors in case you are working on a project and want to section items off.

I don’t recommend these for smaller paperbacks, but they could be used.

Overall, a great value! Love them!

title: Only for Specified Pen
text:
I accidentally got these thinking they would fit some of my older novelty pens with the smaller refill. They do not.

They are only for the specified pen.

After testing them (using just the refill), they write quite well – smooth, easy flow, no smudge.

If you have the pen these go for – great value on the refills.

title: Avery = A+ Products
text:
First glance at the price of this 3-ring binder and someone might want to say it is overpriced – it isn’t. It is actually cheaper here than on the Staples website. And, as it is from the Avery company – it is definitely a high-quality product.

Very durable, easy to use. Hold quite a bit.

Not sure about the “antiviral” and “antimicrobial” claims, but this is definitely a good product. Wouldn’t hesitate to get again or recommend.

title: Great Refills
text:
I own a LOT of pens that take a Parker-type refill. So, these are ALWAYS a need in my own, they’re honestly essential.

For my Parker branded pens (I have 5 total, my mom has 4), we use the name brand. That can get pricey when doing that for ALL of those types that take the refill.

When I saw these, I decided to try them.

The packaging is standard for off-brand refills. I will say they are not packaged well.

Overall, do they work? Yes and no.

I have a few “Parker”-type pens that this refill is too WIDE for. Yes, others? It fits as if it was the refill that came with the pen. Fit is a slight issue.

Performance wise? They’re awesome. Write well, dark and vibrant ink, no skips.

For around $6, you get a pack of 12 – either all black or black/blue mix. I chose the all black. And, as far as value? I remember when there was a brand called A&W (no, not the root beer place) that sold these refills (and others, like Cross) 2 for 98¢ at Walmart. That was back in 1998, so the price is very reasonable if not “retro”.

I definitely would purchase these again, but ask the seller to package them a bit better for the warehouse.

title: Lovely Set of Journals
text:
Overall, this is a truly lovely set of journals. They are not lined, so if you’re looking for that – it will be a problem.

The covers are velvet-like with embossed phrases. Good to give as a set or individually. The ribbon bookmark is a beautiful touch.

Paper is thick, durable. I wouldn’t use liquid-based inks due to smudging. Not so much bleed through though.

The box they come in, while pretty, is too thin and unstable to hold both journals.

For almost $14 for 2, these are average priced journals. I’m sure some shoppers might get a better value elsewhere.

I’m not too upset with them, but I wouldn’t get them again.

title: Cutesy and Great for Christmas
text:
These are those types of pens usually found in the checkout section of the office supply store (Staples, I’m watching you …)

And, typically they’re sold as a SINGLE unit for roughly $2.99-$4.99. Right off, getting eight (8) pens for around $13 – that’s a savings right there. Each pen is around $1.62 each.

This pen has three different “packages” to choose from:

Multi-Color A – Black/Matte Silver/White/Blue for $8.99
Multi-Color B – Rose Gold/Gold/Silver/Pink for $8.99

Honestly? Get Multi-Color C (all eight of the colors) for $12.99, you’d be saving $4.99.

Why?

These make great gifts, especially stocking stuffers. They write great. And, even though they’re metal – they’re light-weight. There is a color for everyone. Refills are easy to find here on Amazon (2.75 in, I prefer MengRan).

I ended up giving my mom the “Multi-Color A” set, keeping “B” for myself.

Great deal! Definitely would get again!!

title: Classy Pen Holder
text:
I am not one for wire pen holders. Main reason? Depending on the design – pens slip out and fall out. That’s not holding it, that’s dropping it.

These on the other hand? Gorgeous, thin spaces between “bars”, and durable. Good gracious is this durable! Not too heavy when filled, but after adding about 18 pens, and 10 of them with the crown and “diamond” accent tops – it gets weighty. It current is holding the following:

1 – Twist pen in slim box
3 – Parker Jotter pens
3 – Miscellaneous twist pens
1 – Parker 51 (2021 edition) twist ballpoint
6 – Crown topped twist pens
4 – Diamond topped twist pens

I think I could, safely (without scratching or crowding) get two more pens in this holder. If I took the boxed pen out? I’d say 22 comfortably.

Good for office, home, home-office use. Makes a TERRIFIC gift for a pen enthusiast.

Bargain wise? The two-pack: GOLD/ROSE GOLD at $7.99 is a MUCH, MUCH better value than the single GOLD at $6.49. Spend the extra money and get the 2-pack. I gave the GOLD to my mom and kept the ROSE GOLD for myself.

I wasn’t too fond of how they were packaged: wrapped in bubble wrap separately, in a bubble pack. No box.

I can’t blame the seller for Amazon’s packaging. Would recommend seller use a box for these to be sold in to keep them safe.

Would definitely get again though!

title: Gorgeous, Refillable, Gift-Giving Worthy
text:
These are the types of pens that are sold by the checkout at an office supply store, or very close to it. You know, impulse purchases?

This could EASILY go for $4.99, and I’m sure someone has purchased one (1) or more at that price.

These run about $2.40 each which is a terrific value. They’re refillable (almost always a plus); refills are easy to find on Amazon (again, another plus), they’re gorgeous, and they make a GREAT gift.

Goodie Bags
Stockings
Prizes

Whatever the occasion.

Durable as well, not cheap in any way. Comfort depends on how often one writes with a metal pen. They do write quite well; ink is dark and vibrant.

My mother and I saw the seven (7) which is one of every color. Since Christmas is coming up – yup, we’re each going to get a set.

So, yes, I would get these again – I’ve already placed an order.

NOTE: These are the refills I have used and trust:

MengRan 2.75'' Ballpoint Pen Refills,Standard D1 Ballpoint Pen Refill (10 ct) ($4.99) [these are preferred as I like the black ink)

15 Mini D1 Ballpoint Pen Refills Compatible with Swarovski Crystalline Pens (Brand: Pen Savings) ($9.99) [better bargain, but ink isn’t as “vibrant”]

Refills come with the removable “heads” as each twist pen is made differently.

title: Cute, But WAY Overpriced
text:
I’ll admit it – these are pretty. Who could resist these flowers? And, these are the PERFECT size for note-taking.

They can be wrapped back or lay flat to write in. The paper is smooth for ball-point or pencil. While the paper isn’t too thin, I wouldn’t recommend liquid based inks in case of bleed through.

So, why the three (3) stars? The value as well as the material. While the cardboard is durable, it isn’t too sturdy and can easily get dinged in a purse or bookbag.

At nearly $18 (before tax) for this set, that comes out to around $4.50 per notebook and definitely WAY overpriced for me. I’ve gotten books like this at Staples for $1-$2.

I definitely wouldn’t get these again or recommend them.

title: Pretty ... Pretty Cheap
text:
I love cutesy little pens, and these are cute. They have a huge “fake” plastic gem on top, and little gems in the top of the body.

They definitely write smooth, dark black ink.

But, what gets them down to three stars? They’re “cheap”.

Cheap in not only inexpensive, around 83¢ before tax; but cheap in material. These are NOT metal. These are plastic, and they are not refillable.

Better for teens than adults. And, definitely more suited for giveaways than an actual gift.

title: Beautiful Pens
text:
These stylus/ball point pens are like personalized promo pens that some businesses or people give out.

Individually wrapped pens make for great gifts, stocking stuffers, or prizes.

They’re light-weight metal, standard type of pen refill (which isn’t too easy to find). They do write quite well, dark black ink.

And, they’re less than about $1 each. Beautiful colors and something for everyone.

title: Promo Pens Without the Promo
text:
As someone who once had a business, as well as someone who LOVES pens, I have often received samples in the mail for pens and other PROMOTIONAL items.

Every so often, companies send me a pen, and I test it.

I’ve gotten pens like this before and there is an author who sends one (the green one) with every book she sends me and I definitely appreciate it. They are comfortable and write quite well. No issues with skipping or dull ink.

These are great to have on hand. The top has the stylus tip and of course this is a refillable ballpoint.

As far as value goes – it depends on how many of these you need and want. These cannot be personalized. Those can be found through National Pen Company or Amsterdam. Usually the more you buy, the less it is per pen.

If you want non-personalized, these are a pretty good deal.

title: Similar to Novelty Pens Sold in Stores
text:
Just before the mask restrictions went back into effect in my area, my mom and I went into Staples after PROMISING ourselves we were only in the area to get something from Target. (FYI: During the mask restrictions, we’re mainly pick-up and curbside types; just our preference).

Yeah, right – only in the area for Target?

Staples had a FANTASTIC BACK-2-SCHOOL sale that we JUST COULDN’T RESIST.

In the checkout area, we saw some SUPER cute pens – metal, twist, crown. So, we each got one. They were $2.99. Wrote well, and I LOVED it. A first for me as many metal pens are too heavy for me.

Flashforward a few months, and I see this set here on Amazon. 10 of these pens for about $14 before tax. Yes, that is – after tax in my area – about $1.51. The other one I got was $3.24, nearly TWICE the price of one of these.

This set, the pens are IDENTICAL to the pen I got a few months ago. Same type of Cross type, twist refill; same type of crown with hidden gem; same weight; same pen only different colors.

They write well with no issues, durable, wrapped individually in thin plastic for gift-giving or as rewards.

For the price? These are a WONDERFUL value.

Would definitely get them again. These are the refills I usually get for these types of pens – Jovitec 24 Pieces Replaceable Ballpoint Pen Refills Smooth Writing 4.5 Inch (11.6 cm) and 1 mm Medium Tip (Black). They are, last time I checked (this weekend), about $6 before tax. And, the refills I bought in 2018? Still working today.

Actual Cross brand pens get the CROSS refill.

title: Functional, Has Issues
text:
For roughly $15, this planner is cute and functional, but has some problems. I’ve spent less money for better ones, and to give you an idea … I’ve spent $10 (before tax) for a 6-ring planner at Barnes & Noble. We KNOW how pricey they can get. And, that wasn’t a sale price either.

Anyway …

This is as basic of a planner as you can get. It touts a “leather” cover, but it is more like leatherette (fake leather, faux leather, pleather, and synthetic leather, although in the furniture industry, leatherette is the most common name). The cover is definitely lighter than most leather books I’ve been around.

The paper is smooth so it will be easy to write on with a pen or pencil. However, I would avoid felt and liquid bases inks as the paper is on the thinner side. Not as thin as notebook paper, but thinner than some journal/planner normally is.

The dual wire binding is standard for most wire-bound books, but the way this is bound and set up, there are some issues closing the book.

The stickers are a nice touch for organizing paydays and other special days of the year.

There is a SMALL pocket in the back, but the thickness of the pocket is relegated to barely the two sheets of stickers, so it REALLY isn’t functional. I’m assuming the phrase on the pocket is supposed to be inspirational but is HORRIBLY riddled with typos.

The elastic strap is a normal thing for most planners to keep them shut.

Overall, this is functional for my needs. However, it isn’t nearly nice enough for a gift due to the issues that it is plagued with.

It is the standard size for desk use, putting in a drawer, or in a medium sized purse.

It isn’t something I would get again or recommend.

title: Overall Good Deal
text:
First of all – these lots are usually overstock, overprints, errors, or possibly returns. I know because I’ve gotten two lots like this from another seller, and three from Farry’s (2019). And, they have been slight misprints. All worked and I found some cute pens from places I’d never been to.

I did find a pen from a place where I lived.

With that said …

You won’t get a quality selection with these lots, and the pens shown are usually for representation.

These are basically what they say – plastic, ballpoint pens. There may be 5-10 of a certain one. I usually got the sets for refills for other promo, medical, or souvenir pens I had from 5-20 years ago. Certain refills are not sold at all. Or, if they are, they’re too pricey.

Overall, 100 pens for $24 equates to 24¢ per pen/refill. Not bad.

In this lot, I ended up with one (1) non-functioning pen, 6 gel (3 blue, 2 black, 1 red), a pen/screwdriver/LED flashlight, and a multi-color pen. 14 of the pens wrote blue ink, 76 were black ballpoints.

Even the 75 would come out to 32¢ per pen.

Yes, I had OODLES of duplicates. That’s great if you want to give some away, lose one, one breaks, or you need the refill.

With regard to customer service – aces. I informed them to let them know of the gel pen issue, they offered a suitable replacement which I got on 9/11 which was four (4) days after I got the 100 lot.

Very pleased. I got the selection “Jim” showed. I honestly can’t complain.

Would definitely get a lot like this again, but do recommend the seller make sure they are all ball points.

title: Meh ...
text:
I love collecting novelty, yet functional erasers. And, I thought these would be cute. I liked the idea of a “brush” to sweep the debris away.

There are SEVERAL design issues that truly affect this.

The cap for the brush is easily knocked off during use, the eraser can fall out, the eraser is a bit stiff and can tear the paper, and the slider clip is a bit difficult to use.

Eight (8) erasers for about $9 is not a great value.

Honestly, I wouldn’t get them again.

title: Small Starter Kit
text:
I will start off by saying – this is NOT going to pack up an entire kitchen worth of dishes.

It is, however, a good starter set, or one to boost supplies you may have.

The bubble wrap is sturdy, standard size. And, perforates as well as stuff I’ve used from Office Max, Staples, or even Office Depot. And, I’ve been using those brands at different times since about 2002.

The FRAGILE stickers are a nice bonus. There are 20, so five boxes for me as I place them on all sides. Learned to do that after some movers thought it funny to “hide” boxes.

Short story – I used to place typed inventories on one short and one long side of a box. On a move, the movers turned the boxes so I couldn’t see what was in them. Oh, and these people expected payment too. After that? ALL FOUR SIDES get a sticker and an “inventory”.

The tape included in this? Not really useful for boxes. I use 3 mil packing tape. I would use this tape to secure the bubble wrap though.

For about $14 before tax, this isn’t a bad starter or booster set.

title: Sweet, Super Affordable Pencil Set
text:
When I was a student I flip-flopped back and forth between liking mechanical pencils and regular ones. Today, my FAVORITE pencil over all is the Paper Mate EverStrong pencil. It writes light for a #2, is easy to hold, and works and has surpassed Ticonderoga as my go-to.

That’s not to say I don’t still like mechanical pencils. I still do. I have some #5 and #7 leads. I’ve got some that are brand-new, and others over 25+ years old. So, to say I’ve used and owned a LOT of pencils since I was a student (even going back to say 6th grade) – is an UNDERSTATEMENT.

Anyway ...

If something is cheap – it’s usually cheap for a reason, and usually that isn’t good. I’ve experienced a lot of bad “cheaps”.

That disclaimer out of the way …

For less than $7 – this is a SUPRISINGLY high-quality set. Seriously! I’m not getting anything out of this deal by saying that! Well … I did get something – this set! My goodness.

Four super cute, durable, grip mechanical pencils. These are by no means “cheap” quality. And, they’ve got such SUPER cute prints.

Extras? Well, you get extra lead refills. Not one pack – four! Yes, four! One for each pencil. I gave my mom the green pencil with the white dots and a pack of lead refills.

This set is great because it includes something a LOT of manufacturers seem to forget – erasers! There are eight (8) – 2 for each pencil – eraser refills in a tube.

All of this is SWEETLY packaged in a sturdy case.

Definitely makes a great gift for a pre-teen to teenager. And, I’ll wager some adults might like it too.

So, for the current price of $6.75:

4 – pencils
4 – 15+ count lead refills (one pack I counted 22, could be more or less)
8 – eraser refills
Sweet storage case
Cutesy moustache sticker

Absolutely worth the money, and if they had other designs, I’d likely get another set!

title: Fancy, Colorful Pens
text:
These aren’t going to be “national” gems or worthy for a vault.

But, these sparkly and colorful pens will stand out.

For $6.99 (before tax), there are FOUR (4) ballpoint pens. That’s roughly $1.75 per pen, so a VERY good value. I’ve seen pens similar to this at office supply stores (Office Depot, Staples) being sold anywhere from $3.99-$6.99. And, in the past, I probably would’ve paid it. Not today though.

These take a “Parker”-type refill which can easily be found here on Amazon and for a good value. I’ve paid $9 (plus tax) for a 20-pack (MengRan 3.9'' Ballpoint Pen Refills, Medium Point, Metal Tactical Pen Refill, Black Ink, Pack of 20 – my favorite “go-to” refill for non-Parker pens).

So, these are refillable. Ink is a standard dark black. Writes first time, no skipping.

Weight – they’re not light weight, but they won’t weigh your hand down. Easy to hold and write with. They have a bit more metal to them than other pens.

The colors are vibrant and you get four (dark magenta, rose gold, light gold, and blue) – easy to split up among family or goodie-bag gifts. And, since Christmas is less than four (4) months away – stocking stuffers is another suggestion.

The glitter only has minor rub off, nothing that would look like an explosion. It also adds some texture to the pen and gives it a “grip”.

These are definitely well worth the money.

title: Pretty But Needs Work
text:
I’m REALLY on the fence with this set. This is definitely not 5-star quality, then again, 3-stars is a tad low. It’s about 3.5/4 stars.

On one hand, it is a great set – eight (8) pieces of double-sided paper with four (4) coordinating envelopes.

There are only THREE (3) different colors, and two (2) different styles per color. One paper style is what PaperDirect would refer to as a “frame” (design all the way around the borders), and a letterhead (design on side, sides, top, bottom, top & bottom).

The quality of the paper is great, unless it is exposed to extreme dry heat (shipping/transit) or high humidity.

Granted these are cheaper than PaperDirect by virtue of the double sided design, also price.

The envelopes? Those are a problem for me – they are side open. And, the sides are not that well constructed. In addition, they seem tricky to work with.

While not as dazzling, there is a beautiful “vintage” set which offers 60 sheets of paper and 30 envelopes for $1 less. Unlike this one, it is lined and only single sided though.

There is no storage packaging (ie: box, etc) for this. Once it’s out of the poly-wrap, it is difficult to get back in without tearing the wrap or having the adhesive stick to the paper.

I’m going to go with 3 stars. It is definitely not giftable at all.

title: Classic Jotter
text:
I will admit one thing – the 1970’s ,1980’s, and definite the 1990’s had a LOT of interesting pens. Some good, some classic, some we needed to forget.

But, the Parker Jotter – they were CLASSIC. And, still are.

Believe it or not, this style has been around since 1954. The one I remember is metal or chrome. And, I think we have one around here in my household.

And, an astonishing fact? It is Parker’s second-highest selling pen. Over 750 million have been sold worldwide. That is pretty amazing.

According to the website they’re available as a fountain tip, rollerball, and ballpoint. And, for the record? I got a “gel” jotter – the refill is the same size as the ballpoint so it was EASILY converted to the preferred ballpoint.

In 1955, Parker introduced “colors” –> turquoise, coral, blue, charcoal, gold (mustard yellow) and grey-green. The plastic barrel was introduced 10 years later, 1965 – which is what this “retro” model looks like.

These are obviously the 1960’s retro version. There are also a 1950’s and 1990’s version as well.

They write perfectly, easy to refill, easy to hold, and basically inexpensive to own considering they are priced $6 (low end) to $20 (high end). $13 for two pens isn’t a bad deal considering that.

These pens have also been featured in media (TV and movies) as well. One famous movie – “Goldeneye” (1995) – “A specially modified version of the Parker Jotter plays a role in the seventeenth James Bond film GoldenEye. This version of the pen was modified by the Q character to incorporate an explosive device which is armed and disarmed by clicking the plunger three times. Continuous arming, disarming, and rearming the pen by a character unaware of its explosive nature plays a major role in the film's climax.”

I definitely wouldn’t hesitate to buy another set, or two … or three. There are a LOT of different colors out there!

They make a great gift as well.

title: Not Quite Hitting the Mark
text:
Hallmark is the PLATINUM of greeting cards with American Greetings the GOLD standard.

And, when I see HALLMARK, I think of a premium card.

This card (Watercolor Mountains) is a generic, gender neutral and relationship neutral card. That works! In fact I like it for that reason.

This can be for a friend, neighbor, co-worker, service worker, or someone like a delivery person you want to celebrate that. And, the design is gorgeous.

The bad thing? The quality.

While the cardstock itself is quite durable, it comes off as two pieces of cardstock glued together. The front “juts” out on the side quite awkwardly.

The inside, while a great greeting, is on a piece of paper that is glued on the left side, leaving the right side “flapping”. There’s seemingly no purpose to that design. There is enough room for the interior greeting on the card itself.

This car isn’t worth more than perhaps $1.99. It certainly isn’t something I would give to anyone.

title: Not for Sale in the USA, but Work in the USA
text:
Normally, if a pen takes a “Parker” type refill, I get the cheap versions which work wonderfully. After all, those are usually souvenir or promo pens. If it is a TRUE Parker pen, like a Cross pen – I do prefer the branded refills. I’m just a snob in that manner.

And, to be incredibly honest – as long as the refill works, I’m totally cool with it – wherever it comes from. But, it is very concerning when you order what you see:

TWO (2) 3-pack refills, packaging as shown (likely a stock photo from Parker)

And, you end up with:

THREE (3) 2-pack refills, packaging different than what was shown (the package I got, my own photo of the product)

I really like to get what I ordered and what is SHOWN.

How it started? I got some Retro type Parker Jotter pens, and I wanted to change the refills. One was a blue gel, the other was a ballpoint blue. FYI: the gel jotters can be “converted” to ballpoint ones. The refills are the same size.

I wanted ballpoint black. It’s a holdover from my mom’s days working at the hospital. Despite her retirement 5 years ago, the practice is a holdover.

Looking for refills, I saw a great deal for two 3-packs of Parker branded refills; six (6) total. After all, close to $12 with tax sure beat a 6-pack for $21 with tax. Obviously I bought these. However, I didn’t look to see it was a:

THIRD PARTY SELLER

The six (6) pack sold by Amazon is about $7-$9 more. That should’ve alerted me.

Anyway …

When they arrived, I noticed the packaging was different. Okay, a re-brand? That happens. Sometimes old stock gets resold at lower prices.

That was until I saw the back of the product “card”.

They had India prices on them, along with the date of manufacture. At least they’re “fresh” (March 2021). Still doing okay, I popped them in the pens, they all worked. I even tried the ones I didn’t need to make sure.

So, what’s the BIG deal then? The “FOR SALE ONLY IN INDIA/NEPAL” markings on the pen refill. The part on the card that states that is MARKED OUT IN BLACK. That really has me uneasy on this “deal”. The seller went to lengths to hide it on the card, but they couldn’t hide the markings on the refill.

I compared them to a refill I got that came from a more expensive Parker pen (Parker 51 which I got back in April), and that refill is MADE IN FRANCE.

How did these India/Nepal ones perform? Right off they worked. I even compared it to the Parker 51’s black refill. The India/Nepal ones did write a bit darker, so I was impressed by the performance. They do fit the jotter as well as the 51. Compatibility is NOT an issue.

Amazon was nice enough to refund me over the discrepancy considering these are NOT AS SHOWN, but not as advertised either.

It is rather interesting how these got from India/Nepal to here. Since these were actually sold by a third-party, fulfilled by Amazon, I am assuming the third party had some “India/Nepal” stock.

I would state that these are a good value given those issues. If you’re concerned about the origins, then you will want the ones sold by AMAZON which are more expensive. I did find a 6-pack for about $20.

I’m still leery of these. But, they do work and are PARKER branded. Would I buy them again? I’m not quite sure. It will depend on overall performance. But, at least I would know what I am getting.

title: Classic
text:
Some of these classic-type pens I wasn’t able to get when they were originally around, so I LOVE the retro designs.

I honestly didn’t look at this and found out it was a GEL pen. Ugh! But, as of note, I did convert it to a BALLPOINT with a refill from another Parker pen and it worked without a problem. That was good thing.

As far as the price, there is a 4-pack of these for about $16, so in value – it isn’t a very good deal.

It is light-weight, easy to hold, and yes – plastic. That’s the way things go. I don’t remember these being expensive pens.

If I were to invest in these – I’d go for the 4-pack.

Great for any kind of use.

(As of note, I did use a similar pen to review as mine hadn't got here and I accidentally reviewed it before I had the actual pen)

title: I'll Take Traditional Boxes
text:
Looking to get a bit better organized, when I saw this, I thought it might be a little nicer to store some stuff in my already crowded living room.

The color isn’t something I’m wild about. But, I figure something is better than nothing.

This is listed (before tax) at $23.95, and that is a BIT much for my liking.

Does it work?

The lid is SUPER heavy, so that is where the wood comes in. Honestly, the top will outlast the main box portion. So that lid is definitely worth 5 stars alone.

But, since it isn’t just the lid I am getting, I went on to the body.

I wasn’t wild about the “fabric” bottom. It seemed a bit too “flimsy”. I added the other bottom to it, and that still didn’t restore my confidence. I added some items to it, which were heavy, and thankfully didn’t have that far to go with it.

The top, without using the side rails for hanging files, is EXTREMELY huge for the box with the OVERHANG. And, that makes it a bit difficult to handle when moving if you don’t use the rails.

This definitely isn’t worth the price. I definitely wouldn’t get it again or recommend it.

title: Gorgeous, But Too Thick
text:
This comes as no surprise to anyone following my social media accounts or even my reviews on Amazon … but …

I LOVE TO READ!!!

And, as a lover of books, I tend to want to keep my NEW ones as new as possible even when I read. No offense to those who are a bit more “loving” towards their books. It hurts to see bent covers, torn spines, even dog-eared pages. If I get used books and they’re more “loved” I try not to damage them any further than they already are.

As far as those “inserts” in certain books, I only crease the spine enough to get it out of the book.

When reading the book, a bookmark – of any kind – is my preferred page keeper. I’ve used receipts, business cards, even a playing card (ones that aren’t part of the suits or a joker – usually the “info” one).

I do have quite the selection of bookmarks, but I’m always on the lookout for more and definitely unique ones.

The metal ones, even smaller ones, are sometimes too bulk for the small and larger paperback. Yet, they’re often impractical for LARGE hardcovers.

This wooden one looked like a great idea for the LARGE paperbacks and hardcovers.

It is – to a point. Durable, well-made, strong, and absolutely stunning – it is a bit TOO thick for my liking. That isn’t bad, but it isn’t good for me.

The price is a bit above what I would be comfortable paying for. It would make a great gift.

It isn’t something I would rush to buy, but it isn’t something I would refuse though.

title: Small, But Mighty
text:
This is a basic calculator, good for the times when you don’t want to have to worry about using your phone or the one on the computer.

Small enough for keeping in a desk drawer, but no so big it takes up a lot of room. For the price, which it was listed under $6, that isn’t too bad.

title: Can't Lose Your Place With These
text:
I do a LOT of reading. In fact, a lot of my reviews are for books. And, taking care of my books is a priority for me. I can’t stand to really hurt a book –> dog-earring to mark my place, folding the cover back to read it, cracking a spine (unless I’m removing those blasted mail-in cards). It hurts to see a book mistreated.

So, I rely on bookmarks. When I didn’t have them, it was either a receipt or business card.

These are great, colorful, and work with or without the ribbon. Though, I did put the ribbons on them. Caution: those can easily fall off. I used a trick – nail glue. A dot at the “tie” part and viola! The ribbon stands up and doesn’t fall off.

I was worried these wouldn’t work in smaller “pocket” paperbacks. They do, along with the large ones. I select the matching color and size – they work great. I do like you can take notes on the back, but as I tend to re-use bookmarks (and there isn’t enough room), this isn’t a concern.

For about $9 (pre-tax), you get 30 bookmarks. That’s about 30¢. And, these are certainly worth that. They are durable (as long as they’re taken care of – no tearing, ripping, smashing, etc).

I wouldn’t hesitate to get a back up set or give these as a gift! Great party favor to slip in a goodie bag!

title: Overpriced and Barely Works
text:
While these do work – to a point – they’re a bit overpriced. I’ve seen cheaper sharpeners at Staples, Target, or Walmart for around 50¢. These run about 83¢ before tax.

The container doesn’t hold much in the way of shavings either.

I honestly wouldn’t get these or recommend them, not at this price.

title: Great Quality, Not So Great Value
text:
These are the basic 3-subject, spiral notebooks that I remember from when I was in school.

The 3-pack price is about $15 before tax, and that comes out to $5 per spiral. And, while these are great in terms of quality; those looking for a bargain would be better served by purchasing a 5-Star Mead one from Walmart for about $3 before tax. That is a savings of $2 per notebook.

In terms of durability – these are usually a one-time use and disposed of after.

If I needed them again, I’d probably head to Walmart or even Target.

title: Basic Photo Paper
text:
This is just like standard photo paper sold by many places. It worked well with my HP 2610 PhotoJet printer that I got about six (6) years ago.

There was no bleeding, no bunching, worked well.

No jamming. Would likely get it again.

title: Packing and Storage
text:
This is on par with the store brands (Office Depot, Staples). It works for sealing and packing whether for mailing or storage.

It is a pretty sturdy tape.

I wouldn’t hesitate to get it again.

title: CDC Vax Card Holder
text:
With the debate of “how do we know someone is vaccinated” – I don’t know about others – I got a card like what is shown. The card has both dose dates, lot numbers, my name, birthday, and location listed.

These clear holders are great for keeping the card from warping, tearing, or getting wrinkled. Easy to open and use, clear plastic, durable.

My card easily slips in it, I can put it in my wallet, and I can show it when needed to “prove” my vax status while keeping the card safe.

You can attach a lanyard to it if desired.

There are 10 of these so you won’t run out if you have small family or need to replace them, and the 10-pack is $4.99 before tax, so each card holder is 50¢. Not a bad deal.

I highly encourage getting these as an alternative to laminating a card that might need an update or “booster”.

title: Basic Sheet Protectors
text:
These are the absolute BASIC /economy sheet protector. They are very thin and durability is questionable.

Honestly, I would spend the money and get the more durable ones if you need to store documents for a long duration.

title: Low Cost Laser Printer
text:
Since I got my first computer back in 2003, I have wanted a laser printer. However, they were far too expensive. Until now …

This printer is less than $180. It is also a copier which is pretty handy for home use when you need to copy something for mailing or to give to someone. Which was one of the reasons I wanted to get something like this – copying as I used to do a TON of it back 15-20 years ago.

It is very compact, which is a bonus because my place is SUPER small. Not quite a tiny house, but it’s not big either. This could actually fit on top of my 3-tier bookmark.

Is it a noisy printer? Yes when you’re on top of it. My mom was sleeping in her room (which is above where my “office” is) – she didn’t hear my 225 page print job at all. And, at her age, she’s not a heavy sleeper either.

As far as fast? Yes. Far faster than my inkjet printer was when it was new (and it’s still fast).

Noise, performance, and size – this printer is perfect!

Connecting it to my network? Easier than my current printer. Yes, this is wireless. I had the fun time of setting up a new laptop while setting this printer up. They both connected to my network fast and with little effort. No, I don’t work in IT either, and my laptop isn’t “state-of-the-art”. I followed the prompts and viola – connected.

FYI: my home network is a Sprint MiFi (MEEGO) hotspot. So, that isn’t that great. Either I’m really good (lol, which I don’t think so), or the HP devices were that easy to set up (more likely the possible answer).

Now, to address the elephant in the room:

** YES – you MUST have an internet connection. This should go without saying.

I have internet anyway as I obviously order from Amazon, check emails, post on social media, and run my blog. My home is NOT set up for a wired connection either, so “wireless” is a MUST-HAVE.

** YES – you must have an HP+ account to operate this. This is clearly stated in the product’s information at the top.

That does NOT preclude you from using store-bought HP toner cartridges though. While it is under warranty, I would NOT recommend using third-party cartridges. Those can and will void the warranty.

Is HP+/Instant Ink work the money? Obviously this is research related. Individual printing varies.

I have been an HP Instant Ink customer since 2016 and have never had an issue. I’ve NEVER run out of ink, got my money’s worth, and have been able to see my pages vs. ink used. I get ink WELL before I need it, they recycle the cartridges, and I can see how many pages I’ve printed as well.

I have been with the same plan since then for my 8610 InkJet (300pages/mo for $9.99/now $11.99). It only increased by $2 and I get up to 900 pages to rollover (so I can save 3 months worth of pages for bigger jobs). The ink tanks seem to last FOREVER so they don’t send you as much. I have saved a LOAD of money with the plan.

Since this printer takes a toner cartridges, those plans vary. Currently I’m going with the 400 page plan for my 6 month trial. I’ve printed over 230+ pages with the cartridge it came with and I still have about ¼ left.

There are lower plans – or go with no plan.

Overall, I wouldn’t hesitate to get another printer like this, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it either. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend HP+/Instant Ink.

No, I am not an HP employee – never have been.

title: Cute, Sturdy, Reliable
text:
I’ve been using Zebra pens for well over 20 years. And, I’ve enjoyed most of the ball point ones.

This 5-pack did not disappoint. The colors are lovely, the pens are lightweight and very easy to hold. The grip is stiff, but I do have a very light grip so it isn’t a bother. Even my nearly 70 year old mother loves the pens and has no complaints with them at all.

These are yes … plastic pens. There’s no surprise there. Most pens are plastic, these are a harder type and not that easily broken. They are solid and durable unless you tend to throw them, run over them, or purposely break them.

Are they 1.0? Yes. As a ballpoint pen, they are. I’ve used many different brands (PenTech, Pentel, Papermate, Bic, Parker, Cross), and these are definitely a MEDIUM ink pen as fine is 0.7 or lower.

Gel inks tend to write more heavily or broadly than ballpoint and be gauged as 0.5 or 0.7.

In a separate listing, a 5-pack is about $7 per pen making these about $1.40 per pen and they are work that.

I am very happy, would get them again, and wouldn’t hesitate to recommend them!

title: Pretty, But not Durable
text:
While this is a cute little 2-pack of journals with colored edges, the pros outweigh the cons on this set.

The inside paper is lined with areas to mark the weather, day of the week, memo number, and date – pretty good for keeping notes in at least.

The paper isn’t thin or thick, it isn’t slick either. It also isn’t rough. Depending on what kind of pen you use, it might bleed through. Ballpoint ink is probably a 100% safe bet. Anything like felt, gel, or rollerball? I’d probably pass. If you use pencil, I wouldn’t erase too much or the paper could tear.

It is hard to lay down flat and write in.

The cover is a bit on the weak side. At least mine was. Thin leather over cardstock. Not the best construction, especially if it is going to be used quite a bit.

For the price (almost $12 before tax for two) – it isn’t that great of a value.

title: Good Pens, Not Sure About Protection
text:
I’ve used the BIC stick pens forever … and I mean forever (let’s say over 35 years) and they’ve been around longer than that.

I don’t share my pens and if the purpose of the PREVAGUARD is to protect the pen, keeping them to oneself is a better idea anyway.

As far as writing – the same as the standard BIC pen. Ink is smooth, pen is easy to hold.

Not much of a value though.

title: Only Half Works
text:
With the pandemic, a lot of things have changed, especially the way we use office supplies.

As a result, BIC has recycled an idea that I saw back around 1997/1998 with another company – anti microbial pens.

I normally LOVE BIC pens as the ink flows superbly, they are easy to hold, and long lasting.

This one? I love the clic pen, but … the stylus doesn’t work. It doesn’t work on my Samsung GS8 or my iPhone 11.

This writes like a standard BIC click stic, but as far as being a great pen? They need to work on this a bit more.

I cannot attest to the efficacy of the PREVAGUARD coating.

title: Not A Good Fit
text:
This is not a good fit for me. And, at nearly $55, it should be. I got this to use with my new laptop while I was sitting in bed. And, that is definitely not feasible.

The problems are numerous:

#1 – It either sits too high or too low. Leave it as it is – too low, flip the one side it is too high

#2 – Wrist rest is too high for a slimline computer (like my HP 17)

#3 – It fits if the computer is 17”, my 17.3” one is a bit too bit

#4 – The “phone” holder does not hold my iPhone 11 as shown. Phone tends to fall out

#5 – The external mouse area is problematic, mouse tends to “slide” when lapdesk is on the lap

For the price, I definitely wouldn’t get this again. I definitely wouldn’t recommend it either.

title: Pricey for Cheap, Thin Tape
text:
Thanks to the pandemic (yes, a bit of sarcasm, sprinkled with some gratitude), I have quite a bit of time on my hands. And, that time is helping me get a few things done I normally wouldn’t.

One of those things – going through my stuff and organizing it.

And, needed for that – tape. While I might empty some boxes and enough to have some extra to re-pack items, tape is essential to closing them up. In addition, I also “label” my boxes.

Rather than write on the box, especially if it has a lot of contents; or keeping a numerical master list (and ending up with 3 #3 boxes or two #6 boxes) – I end up typing up a list on paper and putting it on all four sides. Why? No matter how I place the box I can see the content list.

And, I use tape for that as well. So, I tend to go through a lot of tape.

This is definitely not suitable for shoring up the bottom of the box or taping it closed. Thankfully I have heavier tape for that. This tape is better suited for my “labels”.

I even used it to package up a few Amazon returns (was sent a broken item and wrong item) and had to use quite a bit of tape to seal them.

This is the price I’d expect for heavier duty tape. For this THIN tape? It’s a bit too pricey.

I’m glad I have this as I can now extend the heavy duty tape for the boxing and leave this for the labels.

I wouldn’t get this again though or recommend it … unless you’re using it for labels.

title: New Pens From an Old Idea
text:
It seems that a pandemic is a good time to recycle an old idea.

While some may have seen them back in 1997/1998, for those that didn’t – there was another company that sold ANTI-MICROBIAL pen. I didn’t seem them after 2001, but I liked how they wrote.

With the exception of the PREVAGUARD coating, these write just like their not coated counterparts that I grew up with.

For the money, they’re a pretty solid deal.

I would get these as opposed to the BIC CLICK STYLUS. Despite having both a Samsung GS8 and an iPhone 11 – the stylus on those pens didn’t work and were about 2x the cost of these.

title: Write Well, Not Sure About the Feature
text:
BIC is NOT the first company to experiment with an ANTI-MICROBIAL pen. There was a company back in the late 1990’s that did. Those didn’t sell well and lasted less than about 3-5 years. I honestly saw them in 1997, but by 2001 they were gone or hard to find.

Obviously due to the pandemic, one thing that needs to be safe – office supplies.

I guess this is BIC’s contribution to shared supplies, particularly where a customer might need one to sign in – for example when I got my vaccine at a pharmacy. Despite filling out paperwork, they had me sign stuff. Of course they let me keep that pen :)

In addition, there are other places where pens (and even pencils) are needed. Even if they are used by one person, they should be safe.

These write just like the BIC stick pens I grew up with – easy flow, dark ink, easy to hold.

I can’t verify the efficacy of the PREVAGUARD coating though.

All in all, these are good pens.

title: Pretty Good Envelopes
text:
I don’t really write people much, and because of online bill paying and paying with phone apps; I don’t have the need for envelopes much anymore.

That said …

There are times when envelopes come in handy.

And, with the pandemic – the ones that require “licking” – OUT! They were out for me before the pandemic for several reasons:

** Didn’t stay closed. Too little “spit” or too much and the envelope flew right open. Tape was always required.

** Bad gum. Sometimes the “gum” on the envelope was nasty. Though there were times I loved getting the mint flavored ones.

** Cutting my tongue by licking an envelope. Yeah, I’m that person! I can manage a paper cut on my tongue.

These come with a sturdy self adhesive. Rip the tape off and smooth it out. And, the security print is definitely a plus! Better than most.

All in all, a good value.

title: Portable Sharpener
text:
This is pretty much an “OKAY” pencil sharpener. It works better than some, not as good as others. The plus side is the size.

It can take batteries or the USB charger.

For the price (currently pre-tax of $14.99), it is a moderate value.

title: Below Standard, But Price is Good
text:
I’ve always preferred to put my documents in sheet protectors rather than punching holes, as more often than not, the holes tear the page. I am either re-printing the document or taping it back up.

While I was use to the Office Depot, Smead, Office Max, or Staples brands – I usually think that sheet protectors are standard quality. I know some are far thicker than others, but often the cheaper ones are still good.

Don’t get me wrong, for the current price of $13.49 (before tax) for 200 is a great deal. I’ve often paid $10 per 100. But, these are a lackluster quality.

They won’t stand up for a longer periods of time. I’ve had some sheet protectors, even the lower quality ones, for well over 15 years. These? I’ll give them two years – tops.

They’ll work for short term use though.

Not something I’d rely on for long term archival.

title: Works Great, Worthy of Parker, Price is Not Right
text:
I’ve never owned a Parker 51 or one of their more expensive pens. This is currently listed at $79. To examine whether or not it is worth the price, let's examine the following:

#1 – The gift box – This is a BEAUTIFUL and sturdy gift box. It will definitely hold up for storage and perfect for gift giving.

#2 – Presentation – The pen is held by overlapping loops of elastic, and there is a LOOSE ribbon over it. There is no certificate of warranty though.

# 3 – Construction – Metal top is stamped PARKER with their signature style. Bottom portion is a harder plastic, but definitely not resin. No instructions either.

#4 – Refill – The pen does contain an authentic PARKER QuinkFlow refill in medium, black, ball point. It is smooth writing and generally PARKER pens are very reliable and write smoothly, more because of the refill than the barrel of the pen.

#5 – Durability – This is going to be subjective to one’s own expectations. It is a solid pen that will last as long as it is cared for and not abused.

Overall, I will say that at the price, it isn’t what I would consider “worth the money”. At half the price I would question it. I would say this is probably worth around $25-$30, no more.

title: Writing in Style
text:
These are IDENTICAL to a pen I got at Staples for $2.99; they’re also IDENTICAL to the Disneyland 60th Anniversary one I have that ranges between $18 and upwards to almost $85 (depending on the seller). Don’t get me wrong – I LOVE my Disneyland pen, and the other one.

This set of five (5) pens for around $10 (including tax) is a BARGAIN! Less than $2 per pen. Unlike the ones I got, this set comes with five (5) refills – one for each pen. And, the refills can easily be found here on Amazon.

Twist action like the famous Cross style.

Writes smooth, cutesy. Makes a great stocking stuffer, goodie bag item, any occasion gift, or just because you want a fancy pen.

I definitely LOVE them! Then again I love collecting pens.

Pleased with this and wouldn’t hesitate to recommend them.

title: Sturdy and Private
text:
These are anything but basic catalog or document envelopes.

Security interior, sturdy construction, tamper sealing, with easy to open pull tab – these are the ultimate in envelopes.

These aren’t too pricey. At around $15 before tax, that is about 15¢ each.

As I got them for organizing documents, they’ll do the job just fine.

title: Okay Notebooks
text:
I had never heard of the Hamelin brand of notebooks until I saw them here on the Vine program.

As I am CONSTANTLY going through composition books and note books for my writing as well as book reviews – I thought these would be pretty neat.

They are … to a point.

BASICS:

** Spiral Bound

** Nice “smooth” paper (pencil and pen won’t “catch” on the fibers – issue I’ve had with cheap paper)

** Dark Lines (have had some paper with “barely visible” lines)

** Sturdy Cover

** Perforated sheets to take a note elsewhere or remove a note no longer needed

EXTRAS: an app that can scan the paper and search within notes. I did download the app and try that feature. It is somewhat easy to use if you’re good with tech stuff, if not – pass on it.

Over all, for over $4 per spiral before tax, these aren’t really worth the cost.

title: Only Half Works
text:
I use a LOT of pencils for book reviews and other notes. As a result, a pencil sharpener is a necessity, a good one at that.

My electric ones date back as far as 1990, yes, over 30+ years old.

Recently, I got three (3) desktop battery-operated ones. Two barely lasted two weeks. They had replacement parts, so each one lasted a month. That is they stopped sharpening the pencil. I was lucky just to get the “lead” exposed.

The last electric one I got – it didn’t even work as an electric one. Brand new pencil started off great, just until the graphite was exposed, then a dull point. Took the batteries out – used as manual.

Sorry, but if I wanted a manual, I’d get something cheaper … like these.

This is, at first glance, a good package – 4 pretty sharpeners and 4 erasers.

The erasers are the BEST part of the package. They erase clean, without tearing.

The pencil sharpeners … colors for just about everyone. There is a cap covering the top of the sharpener and a cap at the bottom to hold in debris. Cute idea so that shavings don’t exit the top of the sharpener in transit.

There are, unlike most, TWO different slots – one for the little kids’ pencils (the thick, chunky ones), and a slot for bigger kids’ pencils (the regular pencils).

The big (thick/chunky) slot – don’t bother. It literally tore the pencil up. I used all of the sharpeners with bad results.

The main/regular one? This is where it got tricky.

I have a lot of new-type pencils, and older ones (some over 25+ years old).

And, I had luck with only ONE type.

The types I used:

** Bic Striped (New design) – FAIL

** Berol Eagel Recycled (Slick-type) – FAIL

** Ticonderoga EnviroStik – Pass

** Papermate EverStrong – Pass

The blue sharpener didn’t want to work at all, the orange and pink worked, green was in between.

Overall, the only good thing – the erasers.

At the current list price of around $7 (before tax), I wouldn’t get this again and would find something else.

title: Great Pens!
text:
Over the course of my life, I’ve used DOZENS of pens and many different brands – Papermate, Scripto, Pentel, Pilot – too many to really name to be honest.

They all have their strengths, they all have their weaknesses; and of course there is the “personal preference” to take into account.

Like the black ones I got – these are not metal per se, so much as metallic, likely thinner steel if not aluminum. That doesn’t affect their function at all. If you use it for long periods, the lighter weight pen won’t weigh your hand down.

The pen clip is a bit wide and can be awkward when using the pen. But it is definitely going to stay when clipped. The “plunger” is big enough for big thumbs or fingers.

The grip isn’t squishy, but is comfortable. Makes the pen easier to hold and grip as well.

The ink flow is superb much all of Papermate’s pens. There is a plastic tip to protect it, but that is easily scraped off.

I’ve always liked the Profile line from Papermate, and this is no exception.

title: Bold FLAIR Pens
text:
Color pens and markers are ESSENTIAL for me when I’m taking notes for book reviews, organizing notes, and organizing my writing notes.

I have been a fan of the FLAIR pens since I was a teen.

This is one of the NEW products from PaperMate, a THICKER version - BOLD. Easy to see and easy to use. They’re great for any project.

They’re easy to distinguish from their thinner counterpart with the white contrast to the color top as opposed to the WHOLE pen being the ink color.

I didn’t care for the goldenrod color, and the lime was a bit odd. But, I had 10 viable pens. For the current list price of $21.55 (before tax) that is about $2.15 per pen, so a bit on the pricey side.

If you want max colors, I’d go for the 16 count. That, the last time I checked, was $24.56 (before tax) that is roughly $1.54 per pen as I only liked 13 colors. Still a bit high, but not too bad.

I do like them. Very pleased with them and would definitely recommend them.

title: Gorgeous Gift for a Reader
text:
This is an absolutely stunning bookmark. It makes a beautiful “any occasion” gift with the gift box and packaging.

It is a bit heavy, so I wouldn’t use it in a small paperback. I would think a hardcover would be better.

title: Might As Well Use a Manual One
text:
Being that I have limited desk space, and also wanting something without a cord (and portable), I opted for a small sharpener like this one. It even came with a replacement blade.

That lasted less than a month before I got another one – just like it. After all, when a product fails it could be an anomaly. Two products? Maybe another anomaly, but they’re still BAD.

I saw this and it is one of my second favorite colors (#1 – purple). So, I was excited to get it. After all, most of my sharpeners are between 25-30 years old. My 30 year old one died a few days before I got this. The 25 year old one? On its way out.

This arrived and immediately I popped in the batteries and decided to “re-sharpen” some pencils. That didn’t work. Okay … maybe my version of sharp is different than others.

Tried a brand new pencil – the first one? Stopped right at the “emergence” of the lead. I popped the batteries out of this and opted to “manually” sharpen it. That worked.

But, perhaps it was the material the pencil was made from. And, the pencil was over 14 years old. (I stocked up back in the day and found it in my desk drawer).

Popped the batteries back in, grabbed one of my standard pencils – Papermate Everstrong HB#2. Again, same issue – only to the “emergence” of the lead. Popped batteries back out and finished off using it as a manual sharpener.
