That worked. I was able to begin a new pencil in electric mode, but had to finish off as manual. Very time consuming and certainly not practical. Either it is battery operated or manual. And for almost $12 (as of this review) – no way would I get it as a manual sharpener. Not for an adult, or child. It really isn’t worth it.

This isn’t something I would get again. I definitely don’t recommend it.

title: CONFIDENTIAL Indeed!
text:
Hearing about identity theft back in 2000, I really didn’t like throwing away stuff that had my name and address – even junk mail. So, my mom and I would often rip it up. That was a temporary solution.

By 2006, we invested in a shredder, particularly a cross-cut one. That was definitely a bonus. But, there were the box labels from packages. We decided to used a BROAD TIP Sharpie Marker (what we affectionately called the box marker one). That was an added layer if we couldn’t peel the label off to shred (we put it between a sheet of folded paper).

Over the last five years, we’ve shredded and marked stuff out. Trust me, if you get a TON of mail and packages – you might want to think about that.

This is a great little gem to have if you don’t have much mail or packages. It does tend to bleed through regular paper, and you can sometimes make out a bit of the print.

Definitely pleased with this and I’ve already located the refills. I’ll see how well the pricing does as opposed to a 4-pack of Sharpie markers. Though I’ll probably till still need the markers.

title: Not Worth The Money
text:
A lot of times I use highlighters for projects and I tend to go through a TON of them.

As I usually get the “bold” ones, I thought these might be better being that they had two different tips – broad and fine.

The idea of two different tips, multiple colors, and a 2-pack of them was a GREAT idea.

The problem – the “FINE” tip isn’t too fine, the broad tip is small. The colors yellow and peach cannot be seen on the paper (especially bright white), and the caps are a bit hard to pull off. Unlike most highlighters – you cannot put the cap on the end, so it can be easily misplaced, which would lead the marker to drying out.

As far as value? I honestly prefer my Sharpie liquid ones. They’re easier to work with, cap fits on end, I can see the level of ink, all colors are easy to see – even the yellow.

These might work for kids in school, but definitely not for grown-ups.

Overall, for the money, I’d pass on these.

title: Excellent Pens!
text:
I have been using various brand pens for over 35+ years – Papermate, Scripto, Pentel, Pilot – too many to really name.

They all have their strengths, they all have their weaknesses; and of course everyone has their personal preference.

These are not metal, so much as metallic, likely aluminum. That doesn’t take anything away from their function though. It might make it easier to use over longer period of times as it won’t be heavy.

FYI: I used to LOVE heavy metal pens, until I wrote for a long period with them. Led to hand cramps and finger cramps. Nowadays? I’m a plastic barrel/promo pen type of person.

The “pen clip” is a bit wide and can be awkward when writing. But it is definitely going to stay when clipped. The “plunger” is big enough for big thumbs or fingers and easily exposes or retracts for easy writing.

The grip isn’t squishy, but is comfortable for long periods.

The pen tip is definitely a medium point, and the ink flow is superb. There is a plastic tip to protect it, but that is easily scraped off.

Overall – these are some REALLY great pens. Then again, I’ve always liked the Profile line from Papermate, along with other pens.

Easy to refill as well – though you might have to invest in another pack of pens to do so, but find the cheaper profile ones.

title: Meets the Same Standards as the Other Brands
text:
I’ve used NUMEROUS types of highlighters in my life. Standard was always FLOURESCENT yellow. And, that screamed as it was.

I’ve used Sanford, Sharpie, no-name, and others. They’ve all worked.

Lately I’ve been using the Sharpie liquid ones to see how low on “ink” I am getting. And, for the price of these – they’re comparable.

These are very good – full size, and have quite a few different colors to choose from for different subjects or projects. I wasn’t happy with the Red Apple and on arrival my MINT was leaking. I’ve long since cleaned it up and it seems to work fine. The colors, except the one, are true to color of the barrel.

The cap not only pops on the end for storing while using the highlighter, but it is designed to lock on to seal the highlighter.

These are NEARLY perfect except they’re not easy to hold for long term use though. They’re a bit “slippery” and wide.

The box they came in was solid and durable enough for storing or popping in a desk.

Other than the “handling” issue, and the one marker's "leak" – these are perfect!

title: Pretty as a Pearl
text:
These are similar to the ones found in souvenir shops, office supply stores, and I even have a DIAMOND ONE from Disneyland’s 60th Birthday (2015). They’re all the same – big gem, in this case pearl, with a twist design to use.

They are BIG and definitely top heavy. So not designed for long term writing.

They take the smaller “Cross” type refill which is easy to find here on Amazon and very inexpensive.

This five pen set features five BEAUTIFUL cotton candy like colors; and they would make LOVELY stocking stuffers, gifts for goodies bags, or great giveaway items.

As this is currently listed around $10 before tax, that is $2 per pen. That’s cheaper than I’ve seen in stores. And, while I love my Disneyland one – it ran between $13-$25 depending on where you got it if you got it outside of Disneyland.

title: Impractical Calendar
text:
Normally, I’m not too picky about a calendar – free ones especially. If I’m paying for a calendar – I feel like I do have a RIGHT to be picky.

While I got this through the program, and trust me a positive review is never required or requested – this is currently listed (as of this review) at around $14. And, honestly I hate to be the person that screams – DON’T BUY THIS. But, seriously, there are better and far more complete calendars out there. This is definitely not worth the money.

Here’s why the two (2) stars:

#1 – Only MAJOR holidays listed. That’s it.

For example – while Easter is listed, Ash Wednesday, Passover, Palm Sunday, and Good Friday are NOT. These are tied right in with Easter.

I can ALMOST excuse religious holidays being omitted (Ramadan, Yom Kippur, Rosh Hashanah, etc.) – what about New Year’s Eve? OMITTED.

My planners, free calendars (Cisco Systems, Pharmacy, Insurance Company, Promos) – all of them have these days listed.

#2 – Daylight Savings Time Begins/Ends – NOT LISTED.

#3 – Seasons: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter – NOT LISTED

#4 – No moon phases listed

#5 – Misc. Holidays are omitted – Chinese New Year, Mardi Gras, GROUNDHOG DAY, Cinco de Mayo, even Kwanzaa.

BUT BLACK FRIDAY is sure listed!

#6 – The WEEK goes Monday- Saturday, not practical to align with most calendars or planners

#7 – Lack of picture attribution which makes me wonder if these were stock photos put together

# 8 – The small squares; no room for making notes at all.

The only good thing? The material is a bit sturdy. That’s about all that it has going for it. The hold where it hangs is SMALL, so only a push-pin works. Though I use them anyway.

Not to be rude, but I have NO idea what kind of thought went into this, what the purpose was of not including this stuff, what it was designed for, and why the high price.

This reminds me of the calendars found at the $1 store. I’ve had a few of those that were a bit better in quality.

title: Colorful and Sturdy
text:
First off, these are PRICEY!! Currently listed at $12.95, that’s roughly $4.31 each. So, as far as a bargain, these are not that.

Now, they are STURDY. The covers are not really “soft” per se. They are more of a plastic coated cover that is around the strength of a credit card, or if the card was “halved”. Not easily bent or warped.

The paper has NO margins. It is thick, slick and easy to write on, easy to erase, without tearing and smears.

The designs are gorgeous and easy to separate projects or notes for. Small enough to slip inside a purse, eBook case, and/or bible cover for easy note-taking.

Makes a great gift or get them for yourself.

title: Beautiful Bible Cover
text:
I hadn’t really thought much about bible covers until last year when I started doing bible studies.

I got one, and loved it, though it is FAR too big for my devotional bible I got 20 years ago.

As I got a newer bible (my “study” bible), which is bigger and thicker, I thought this might not be big enough …

I was wrong. It is roomy and has a lot of pockets for pens, a small notebook, even bookmarks.

Very pleased, great quality, and am sure it’s durable unless you get too rough with it.

Makes a great gift too!

title: Good Spiral Notebooks
text:
One thing right off – the price. I’m a stickler for a good deal, and the PRICE is screaming … “NOOOOOOOOOOO!!!!” and that’s where they lose stars – the price.

These are, as of this review, $11 before tax. That is $2.20 per spiral and in all honesty, I remember the days of the 10¢ ones, which wasn’t too long ago at a sale at Staples.

While these have perforated pages, which are great for those who have a “frilly-fit”, the paper is standard quality as is the binding. Nothing I’d pay over $1 for though.

As I have seen other spirals with different color covers – these are similar in that with five different colors for coordinating projects or assigning to multiple people. Paper is thin, and smooth for easy writing with either a pen or pencil.

Not my first choice for spirals, but they’re solid.

[FYI: “What is a frilly-fit”. When I was in school, most teachers PROHIBITED using torn spiral paper due to the “frillies”, the paper left over from the torn spiral holes. I was required to have SEPARATE notebook paper for that. Even wireless paper was discouraged because of the strip of paper that connected the main sheet to the “binding”. Thus if they saw us tearing paper from spirals or wireless, they’d have a “frilly-fit”.]

title: The "P" Must Stand for PERFECT!!
text:
I got my first P-Touch machine about 15 years ago and LOVED it. The sad thing – I couldn’t afford the tapes for it. That’s the downside right off.

And, of course I’ve long since forgotten where it where.

When I saw this, I decided to get it, though it is NEARLY double the price I paid for my first one.

I LOVED how this came with everything to use it right out of the box:

** Machine (obviously)

** Manual (always good to have, and I am keeping it handy for the font, symbol, and frame charts)

** Tape (pretty nice idea, but the tape is CLEAR so it might not be seen on certain surfaces/items)

** BATTERIES!! Yes, it came with the required six (6) AAA batteries and that is definitely worth mentioning. Nothing like getting your new “toy” and have to get batteries for it [FYI: back in the day I USED to have a TON of each type of battery, but … never used half of them and they went to waste – not always a good idea to stay “stocked”]

This is rather HUGE for a labeler. As I told my mom – it’s like a mini typewriter. But, it is sturdy.

This is easy to use, set-up, and type with. Inserting the batteries took the longest only because of the “wrapper” they were in. Tapes are EASY to pop in. I barely consulted the manual before I had my first label done – with a chosen font, symbol, and frame.

The “backing” of the label splits in the middle, rather than peel off from the sides.

The keyboard? Super easy to touch and use buttons. They’re also angled for comfort, though I doubt anyone is going to be spending a LONG time on here typing.

This is great for labeling kids’ items, your own items, and getting organized.

I definitely recommend one of these in every household (of course finances permitting, totally get that). Really happy with this!

title: Large Calculator
text:
This is WAY pricier than I would’ve liked, and WAY bigger than I thought (it is practically ¾ the height of a standard composition book). But …

I…LOVE…IT!!!

This runs on the usual solar and battery power. The difference? This has an ACTUAL, easy-to-access & easy-to-replace battery. It takes a AAA battery. That’s all. The battery door slides off and on. No screws and no searching for some number button cell that likely you can’t find except for some obscure battery store.

With that said …

This has TWELVE digits. That’s 100 BILLION (100,000,000,000).

The features on this calculator? Well worth the price tag:

** BIG BUTTONS. No accidentally hitting the wrong button/digit. And, there is even a BACK (>) button if you do.

** BIG display with “commas” at the top for seeing the millions and billions

** The DOUBLE zero for 100+ calculations

** Angled display for easy viewing

Definitely pleased with this and highly recommend it!!

title: Works Great, Good Value
text:
Going to school (and later in life) I had NO end of writing instruments I’ve tried – regular and mechanical.

** Papermate

** FaberCastell/Eberhard-Faber American

** Empire (I miss those “plastic” like regular pencils)

** TICONDEROGA (the gold standard)

** Pentel (I had a SUPER fancy metal one that even had its own “cap”; two piece that formed a stunning one piece; think it was called “KERRY”)

** Eagle Office Trends Color (much like the Empire; pencils were regular #2 graphite, outer was various colors)

** Yikes! (same as Empire-Berol)

** Berol (I think they were part of the Empire/Eagle Family)

** Staedler

** Pentech

** BIC

** Pilot

** Cross

** Off-Brands (some were wacky designs)

And, I’m sure I missed quite a few.

So, there is NO brand I haven’t tried. And, they’ve all had their positives and negatives. Some were far more loved than others (and those are the ones I can rarely find)

Then there is the 0.5 mm vs. the 0.7mm. I was more of a fan of the 0.5 myself.

These are the 0.7mm and very basic. For less than 35¢ (before tax), this will do whatever job is needed – work, school, home. If you lose one, yeah it might be bad but not financially catastrophic (only if it is your LAST pencil and you can’t afford anymore).

The eraser, for any pencil, is actually generous. I’ve seen some mechanical pencils with TEENY erasers (why even bother); and this is about the size of an eraser on a regular pencil. Longevity? Don’t bother. I usually use a regular eraser. I’ll end up needed it later anyway.

Longevity of the pencils? They’re not easily breakable, but not indestructible. They’ll do the job, but don’t look at it being a classic keeper.

Pretty good value. Definitely pleased with them.

title: Snazzy Pencils
text:
I’ve had ALL kinds of mechanical pencils over the past 35 years – plastic, metal, twist, push-type, even the “lead tips” ones.

First of all none of the pencils I’ve had has had an eraser worth using. This has a VERY teeny tiny one under the cap. Though to be honest, even when using regular wooden pencils, I’ve ALWAYS kept a regular eraser near me. I find that MUCH easier.

This doesn’t retract like a pen. None of my previous mechanical pencils ever have. This uses the same methods as my older ones – pushing down the top while pushing up the “tip” at the bottom.

I honestly prefer the 0.5 thinner lead, but these work as well, they’re just thicker.

While these are not a heavier metal, they have a metallic like bottom, with a metallic type over plastic coat.

For the price, they’re pretty decent. I truly enjoy them. Designed more for adults than school kids.

title: Too Pricey and Not Too Functional
text:
This is one of those “ideas” that start off great, but fail to work – at least for me.

My set came with a set of light grey, medium grey, and a dark brownish/grey/black pens (like the ones shown in the top picture of the description) which obviously don’t go with the blue and green theme of the set. And, there is . The first two pens, even on the white paper of the notebook can barely be seen. The darker one does better for the notebook; none of them seem to work on the “daily” post-it notes.

The daily post-it notes are DARK paper. I used a #2 pencil, the darker pen of this set, and a Papermate BOLD Flair pen. The Papermate pen had the better chance of being “seen”. The pencil could barely be seen, the darker pen of this set was iffy. Depending on the lighting, it would be best to use a BLACK thin type Sharpie or a FELT tip pen such as the Flair. The note pages peel off the pad quite easily, but don’t stick too well.

The notebook is average size, easy for popping into a medium size purse, keeping by the bedside, or at the desk.

I do love that it isn’t spiral in case you need to tear a page out of it. Lays flat and is easy to work with.

For nearly $17 as of this review – this is NOT a good value at all. One could do better buying items individually.

For around $8 you can find a 5-pack of super sticky post it notes, albeit they wouldn’t have lines or the DAYS of the week like this one. And, for the remaining amount of $9, you could find a decent pen (or pens) and journal.

This would probably work better if it were less money and the pens darker to see on the post-it notes, or a lighter color of the notes.

title: Bold Pens
text:
As someone who takes a lot of notes for book reviews and other projects, color coordinated and using BOLD color pens to keep notes is essential.

This is one of the NEW products from PaperMate. A fan of their regular FLAIR! pen for decades (as in since I was a child), these are the THICKER version. Easy to see and easy to use. They’re great for any project.

They’re easy to distinguish from their thinner counterpart in that while the tops of these have the ink color, the bottoms are all white.

There were three colors (goldenrod; yellow; and some kind of avocado green) I didn’t like. So, that left me with 13 viable pens. The colors are vibrant and true to what the cap is.

At the current price (as of this review) of $24.56 (before tax) that is roughly $1.54 per pen, so it is relatively HIGH (in my opinion) for these pens.

They should last as long as their counter parts; and I do like them. Very pleased with them and would definitely recommend them.

title: Not Too User Friendly
text:
As I am doing more bible studies, I find that quickly locating a particular “book” is expedited with the use of these tabs.

I got a set a month or so ago, and really liked them. They were heavier than I thought and resulted in a few “torn” pages. They were SUPER sticky and once on the page – forever on the page. They were also about half the price of this set. Yes, I only got one set, but they were quite durable and easier to apply.

As I do have another bible and wanted to fit it with tabs, I saw this set and thought they might coordinate well with it.

They do. That’s one thing in their favor. Also, this set gave me TWO full sets of bible tabs, and two full sets of matching blank tabs to create my own tabs.

These do not come off either. When stuck – they’re stuck. They also tear very easy from the sheet or in applications. One tore completely in half.

Also, without proper “scoring”, they’re difficult to line up properly when folding over. Some of my tabs are a bit “off”. Also, the guide that came with this did NOT line up with my bible. Instead of getting six (6) “placements”, I got five (5). The other set had a better guide.

They will do the job, but I definitely wouldn’t get these again. For the price they could be a bit more durable and easier to place.

title: Pretty, But Not A Good Value
text:
Admittedly “value” is in beholder’s wallet. Still, for nearly $3 per pen, these aren’t what I’d call a great value.

They are pretty, somewhat functional, and take the standard “Cross” type pen refill that can easily be found in inexpensive multi-packs here on Amazon.

I cannot write with them for any length of time, so they’re more fashionable than functional.

They are gorgeous and could make a great gift for someone who doesn’t mind these types of pens.

For the price and functionality … I’d pass them up.

title: Gorgeous Markers
text:
At about $1.25 (before tax) each, these metallic/silver outline markers are gorgeous. Some remember these types of markers from the 1980’s. I personally didn’t have a set, but do recall seeing something similar.

CAUTION: they tend to BLEED through standard type paper. So, they’re more suited for card stock paper.

On white paper – they’re all visible. And, I actually checked them as soon as I got them.

Easy to use, and all but the brownish/black is gorgeous.

Those who are artistic or enjoy doodling are sure to love these markers.

title: Better Than Nothing
text:
Since my printer (HP - Photosmart Plus 209a) was WELL past its warranty period. As in the thing is OVER 11+ years old … I decided to get some replacement ink for it and use it as a back-up.

The first problem, finding part of my cord. The second part was getting the ink installed.

The ink worked okay, and had it worked better, it’d be a stellar value. The 2-sets of ink was definitely a game changer.

According to some it is perfect, others had a bad experience. I could’ve just had a bad batch.

Thankfully I have my newish printer (bought in 2015) and with being on the HP ink plan, I’m good on ink.

title: Ideal for Grocery Management
text:
Having worked in fast food, I’ve been around these types of labels and really wanted them for home use.

They’re definitely ideal for keeping track of not just leftovers but when condiments, dressings, and other items are opened.

The only problem is that they can be difficult to see.

title: Great Affordable Highlighters
text:
I love these highlighters! The dual tips are great for not only highlighting, but making notes with the smaller tip. I love the colors!

The packaging is a bit less than desired as it is hard to store the pens in, but I can keep them in a cup on my desk, or use a pen pouch.

And, the price is quite reasonable compared to major brands.

title: Cute & Quiet
text:
For the price it is currently at ($7.99), this is a decent sharpener. I like the “shorter” sharpen as opposed to the LONG standard one.

This is dual power – battery and manual. Works great.

The only problem? The tool carrier doesn’t last long. I had one just like this, but I had to replace the part that sharpened the pencil in less than two months.

Since this is the same design, it will likely happen again.

I definitely wouldn’t purchase this at $39.99 though.

title: Work Well, But Why Yellow??
text:
I don’t use gel pens that much. They’re mainly for taking notes, color-coordinating project due dates.

The price on this is a bit off-putting. Still, these work and write well – except for the yellow pen (don’t really know why they’d include it).

The grip is fantastic and better than leading name brand gel pens.

Overall, they work for what I need them too.

title: Anti-Bacterial Pens
text:
I am definitely on the fence with these pens. They’re from BIC, so they write pretty good. They’re comfortable and easy to work with.

With regard to the antibacterial plastic … this isn’t the first time I’ve been around such pens. There were some from 1997/1998 that touted that claim (Microban). Unless you have special equipment, there is NO way to test the theory on these pens.

The price is one thing that really sticks out. For five (5) dozen pens, it’s roughly $28. That’s less than $6 per dozen.

This gets a pass from me.

title: Great for Reports
text:
These report covers are more for business and professional use rather than academic use. They do require the use of a 3-hole (standard paper) punch to insert the paper into the prongs.

And, they definitely hold the amount of paper they do. I've actually put in about 60 pieces of 20lb paper and had SOME room left. But, that is my own personal experience.

They're durable, and I've definitely pleased with them. They'll suit my needs!

title: Just Like I Remember
text:
Oh, how these bring back some “good” and “not-so-good” memories of school reports.

Honestly, it wasn’t doing the reports I had issues with – it was these things. My mother REALLY despised these (and science projects). Don’t get me wrong – it wasn’t that she didn’t want to spend the money on supplies, she just though some teachers went OVERBOARD with the projects and reports.

These are SIMILAR to the ones from the late 1980’s/early 1990’s. In fact, they’ve DEFINITELY improved.

The old ones? The plastic “report cover” was FLAT. Absolutely flat, as opposed to these “triangle” spine ones. The slider bar was often difficult to get on (it sometimes would fall off or slide off as it was going on). These? The triangle plastic cover spine fits right into the triangle slide bar – easy peasy.

The old ones? I was able to squeak more paper into them.

These? Barely the 25 pages states. I was using 20lb paper though, which I believe is standard.

These will work for smaller reports though, and these slider bars are VERY secure unlike the ones from my school days.

I love the colors in this set. And, I’d probably get them again for any future projects. Right now, the four pack is about $5 before tax, so that’s a good deal!

title: Tricky Tabs
text:
These "bible" book tabs are AWESOME! I love the colors and I love the fact they come with a "guide". And, it makes bible studies very easy when looking for different "books".

Also included are blank ones, albeit they are more "slick" than the bible tabs. These REALLY DO STICK to the paper, which as we known is already thin. So, once they're on, they're on.

That is another problem - they're TOO thick and can easily tear the paper. Caution must be taken. I've had to tape a few pages/tabs already.

Overall they're good. For the price, I wouldn't mind getting a set for all of my bibles.

title: Not Fancy, But Functional
text:
This isn't a fancy calendar, but it is functional and suitable for the family.

I put this in the kitchen and the "wire" hook makes it much more durable for use. The price isn't too bad either. Definitely a great bargain!

title: Gorgeous Pink Journal
text:
As someone who not only uses journals, but collects them, I couldn’t pass up an opportunity to get this. And, it is in pink which is my second favorite color (purple is my #1).

Absolutely thick and great paper so certain inks won’t bleed through, 195 numbered pages, table of contents in the beginning to mark notes or reference the pages, inspirational introduction, and a ribbon bookmark complete this journal.

Great gift for any occasion – birthdays, anniversaries, graduation, Christmas, Hanukkah, Easter, Valentine’s Day, “any day” gift.

title: Sometimes Doesn't "Stick" The Landing
text:
With the Christmas season in high swing – one thing my household needs – tape.

So, when I saw this, I decided to get it.

Six pack of tape seemed reasonable.

My mother and I went to use it on some craft (brown bag) type wrapping paper – it kept peeling off, popping off, and wouldn’t stick. It just wouldn’t stick. We resorted to clear PACKING/MAILING tape.

When used on other wrapping papers, it didn’t do as well, but definitely not as bad. It can be a chore to “tear” off from the dispenser.

It isn’t a bad tape, but I do prefer my Scotch brand.

title: Money Card Holders
text: While some money card holders can double as regular gift cards - these cannot. They are adorable and more suited for children or teens.

title: Great Pens
text:
I am not new to the Zebra pen line and have been using them for well over ten (10) to fifteen (15) years.

They do have one drawback – lack of refills.

These are ball point, retractable pens. They write right off, of course after you remove the plastic nub from the tip.

They’re durable and last quite a while, depending on the conditions.

Recommended for school or work use. My mother used to use this brand when she was working. She was a clerk in a hospital so you can imagine how much “writing” she had to do.

These will last quite a while, and you get the bonus “flight” pens which, despite looking metal, are light weight and so easy to write with.

title: Pretty Cards, Average Value
text: These are standard "boxed" holiday cards from Hallmark. They are very pretty and have matching envelopes. They are an "average" value. Some stores such as Target and Walmart might have a better value though.

title: Pretty Neat for a Charitable Idea
text:
Yoobi is the brand that gives back, so I don't mind the extra cost. As long as it is comparable in a way ...

These are like smaller composition books without the margins, black band, or thread binding. They're pretty decent for home or work notes, but not for use as a composition book.

Given the price, they aren't a very good value.

title: Cute Little Journals
text:
These are some cute little journals to keep on hand for notes – car, purse, desk, almost anywhere.

They’re sized just right, durable, and slightly fashionable.

title: Beautiful Anytime Daughter Gift
text:
One thing my mother and I LOVE to get is personalized goodies. While her name is easy to find, mine isn’t. So, sometimes we settle for MOTHER and/or DAUGHTER.

Knowing I have a planner and a journal, this is something I would (and really asked for) as a gift.

Simple, yet conveys a heartfelt sentiment.

Looks classic and is refillable so it can be used for years.

title: Great to Mark Fragile Item Boxes or Other Items
text:
I usually make my own labels, but when I saw these, I thought I would get them.

They are pretty decent size (not too small or large), and easy to see on boxes due to the red background. Easy to apply, you do have to push it down to get it to stick.

They can be used for mailing or storage. I’m mainly using these for my fragile item storage boxes.

Pretty pleased with them.

title: Basic Mechanical Pencils
text:
These are definitely “basic” mechanical pencils – no frills, inexpensive material, small eraser.

They are the 0.5mm/#2 lead and can easily be refilled. They come in six (6) different colors, four (4) of each.

Definitely enough to get one through the school year or to keep on hand for projects.

title: Functional Pencil Case
text:
Rarely does a pencil case really live up to expectations for regular pencils. Most of them, like this, are designed for mechanical pencils and pens.

And, as far as those go – this does the job. There are some “slots” for pens or pencils and the bottom can hold quite a few pens or mechanical pencils depending on size.

I have not yet found a use for the inside zipper pocket as it seems far too small to hold even an eraser.

Solid choice for any one who is going to school or needs this for travel.

title: Stunning Pen - Great Gift
text:
Don't expect longevity out of the refill as these are SMALL refills, but ... these do come with extra refills. And, you can find refills online, especially here on Amazon.

This is an absolutely gorgeous pen which is "weighty" to hold. It can easily be a gift for any time of the year, for me? Stocking stuffers!

Classy but affordable. Even with tax? Less than $3 a pen!

title: Standard Calculator
text:
This works for a simple desk side calculator.

I didn't use the case as for me, it opens the wrong way. The display is big, but there is no OFF button. Has a LONG display digit placing for larger calculations. Buttons are soft touch and easy to use.

Mine does function with a dimly lit room, then again the "battery" might be fresher.

Pretty decent for the price.

title: Close to Artist Pencils
text: These are as close to professional artist pencils as kids can get. Easy to use, hardly any "debris" from use, and sturdy (nearly non-breakable) materials, these are perfect for amateur artists or beginners.

title: Affordable and Durable
text:
Growing up I had ALL kinds of pencils – novelty, mechanical, even brand names that have long since left the market – Berol (Eagle & Yikes), Empire, etc.

And, even though I am no longer in school – I still need pencils. Durable, affordable, and user friendly.

As I have stockpiled SO many kinds of pencils, I rarely buy them anymore.

But, seeing this – I HAD to get them.

They work better in an automatic sharpener as opposed to a manual one. And, I prefer my desktop “short” shorten sharpener.

Durable? These are. Of course I am sure a really determined, strong person could break them, they are not easily broken with stress or by dropping.

The erasers are standard, but let’s face it – you will need a separate one (I have TONS of those).

The “lead” works on both types of paper, but preferably on slicker types.

The value cannot be beat. Six (6) dozen for less than $12 (remember sales tax) is a great bargain, less than $2 per pack and they will last!

title: Cute Comps
text:
I take a LOT of notes with various projects and sometimes a composition book is my best friend.

This 4-pack is super cute, and also the purchase benefits charity. Love that about Yoobi. These are smaller than most (70 pages versus 90), but I LOVE the colors. Each one for a different subject (or task).

The paper is "slick" so that makes writing on it a breeze with pen or pencil.

Definitely recommend these and wouldn't hesitate to get them again!

title: Beautiful
text:
I had been seeing bible and book covers on social media and thought it would be a great way to store what I need for reading and taking notes.

This is a BEAUTIFUL bible/book cover. Mine came with three bookmarks. This has pen and notepad pockets, and comes with a LOVELY ribbon bookmark attached.

The material is colorful, soft, and durable.

The gold-tone zippers also have crosses on them.

This would make a beautiful gift for a teen, young girl, or anyone who is involved with daily devotionals, bible studies, or wants a safe place to store their bible.

title: Fancy Portfolio
text:
This is more or less Yoobi’s answer to the “portfolio” or fabric trapper without the 3-ring binder. It is roomy, as I have at least 4 “workbooks” inside the main compartment. Each one is anywhere from 200-260 pages. Though the workbooks are fairly small.

Inside the main zipper is another workbook 250 pages. In the front I have a small 2-pack of Yoobi coordinating notebooks. Each one less than 60 pages.

So, this is ROOMY.

As far as durable, it depends on the rugged conditions it is exposed to. I know that elementary school and junior high were not kind to my school supplies. Also, the “blush” does tend to show dirt a lot more than a darker color.

This suits my needs, but as an adult I won’t be putting it under the rigors of a school environment either.

This is more than 3 stars, but no more than 4 – 3.7 actually.

title: Some Ideas Always Plan Better Than They Turn Out
text:
Yoobi is one of those brands, because of what they do, that I usually try to procure their products before choosing other brands.

This pencil case matches the “blush grid” design. And, it is ROOMY.

However, it is more or less designed like a mini notepad holder and better suited for mechanical pencils and pens. Regular pencils will tend to dirty the inside fabric if not tear it.

It is definitely roomy enough for plenty of “extras”, so there is no worry about being caught without a pencil or pen.

It is pretty good for the value, especially when coordinating with the other Yoobi school supplies.

title: Glittery But Not Sturdy
text:
Liking all things glittery and that I LOVE to collect journals, this was definitely a no-brainer. It being from Yoobi the “giving” school supply people, this was a gifted gift.

But, as soon as I got it, I thought about potential “punctures” and damage to the cover which could cause it to leak and damage the journal.

Thankfully the journal has a slip-cover so you can remove it. But, that does take the “design” out of it.

This is definitely not practical for younger children, and definitely cannot be placed in a bag due to possible puncture damage.

The pages are wonderful, smooth, and thick.

Best used as a table journal or bedside one that doesn’t have sharp objected nearby.

title: Charitable, But Basic Pencils
text:
These are pretty much the standard #2 lead (graphite) pencils. Shaped in a gentle triangle, these are easy to hold and use.

With regard to sharpening – they work quite well in an electric sharpener, but not so well with a manual one.

As far as a value, there are five dozen pencils (60 – 20 of each color), so for around $11 (with tax) that is around $2 per dozen which makes this a great value since it is a charity based initiative.

title: Great and Durable Binders
text:
I got these to get more organized.

They are not only "large" in width (as some are barely paper size); but they are strong and durable. These would definitely last most of a traditional school year.

And, the different colors makes it super easy to get and stay organized.

title: Dual Tip Chalk Markers
text:
I got these for a blackboard I have.

This is a great selection of colors, including gold and silver. The gold one didn’t work as well as the others – it was runny and leaky. The others worked fairly well.

They were a bit rough to get started – shake and smash down.

But, I was pleasantly surprised by the colors being visible, including the darker ones. I have not used the dual tip (and there are no instructions), but that is okay.

If they were a bit easier to use, I’d have rated them higher.

title: Filing for Charity
text:
Strong, sturdy, and supports charity.

These file folders are great for getting organized and the colors are vibrant and bold.

They do pretty well for household document organization and would likely hold up to a full school year as well.

title: Multiple Colors
text:
Yoobi is a charity based initiative that gives an item for an item purchased – every item purchased. Even these colored pencils.

They’re a pretty good deal for how many is in here.

They come pre-sharpened and ready to use. But, the quality is a bit lacking.

When coloring they tend to build up “residue” which has to be blown or dusted off so that it doesn’t smell or collect on the drawing.

They sharpen better in an electric sharpener opposed to a manual one.

Pretty standard compared to lower priced brands. Good for those just starting out with their love of art.

title: Really Small, But Colorful Highlighters
text:
When they say “mini” – they mean TINY! Those with bigger hands might have a problem getting a handle on these. They're not easy to use.

They’re definitely not for long term use. Designed more or less for short term. And, I would state they're better for a child to use as opposed to a teen or older student.

The pastel colors are very light, some are almost unnoticeable. The other darker colors are vibrant and noticeable.

Perfect to tuck in a purse or small backpack though.

title: Charitable and Functional Notebooks
text:
These dual pack notebooks are great for desk use and travel use (smaller one is good for a purse).

They coordinate with the rest of the Yoobi blush grid items.

A unique feature is that both of them have a clear zipper pocket in front. Though once you’re done with the notebook – either you keep it or toss it and that wastes the pocket.

Another bad thing is that the paper is hard to turn because of the small dual rings.

title: Cute Journals
text:
This is a wonderful three pack of sewn-bound journals.

Great to have on hand for small notes, diaries, or general information.

Also great to give as a gift for any occasion.

title: Little Sharpener, Big Point
text:
This is probably the cutest, lightest, and most portable sharpener I have ever had. This can easily slip into a purse or backpack for travel (business or pleasure).

And, it can be a manual (you twist the pencil by hand) or mechanical (using battery operated feature). And, the door to the “shavings” is lockable – right to lock, left to unlock. Easy out and easy back in.

It isn’t whisper quiet, but it isn’t loud either.

And, it comes with a bonus “tool carrier” (sharpener unit); which is amazing as I’ve never had a sharpener come with one.

This sharpens pencils in what I refer to as “short” style as seen by the pencil in the images.

Definitely wouldn’t mind getting another one.

And, the mushroom on the package is just adorable!

UPDATE: While cute and useful, it was not durable. I went through this one and another one in less than three (3) months time. Definitely NOT worth the money.

title: Non Secular Christmas Cards
text:
Standard holiday cards that are non secular – only reference to the holiday is MERRY CHRISTMAS on the front, “holiday” type greeting inside. All same design with matching red envelopes.

Perfect for card trades at work or school.

Mine were packaged in a poly sleeve with little flair.

Would recommend for those who want a simple card for the holidays.

title: Not Laptop Friendly
text:
This set is definitely designed more for a desktop computer than a laptop.

Since I didn’t have a need for the wrist rest, I decided to put it to the side and wanted to try the mouse pad. Mine needed to be replaced after seven (7) years of service.

A few issues with the mouse pad:

#1 – it is definitely not compatible with a laptop. The bump is far too high and thus creates an unnatural angle

#2 – the material is not suitable for use with current “mice”. Mine is a LOGITECH that was manufactured in the last five (5) years. It isn’t “optical” per say, but the mouse pad hinders the use of the mouse.

#3 – it does have a “stick” bottom. It stuck to my desk. While this can be good so it doesn’t slip, it also makes it difficult to move if needs be.

The design is beautiful, but it just didn’t work out for my needs.

title: Too Big
text:
I don’t know quite where to begin with this review and I am honestly shocked at this item.

I got these dividers as a way of organizing my papers, notes, and other things. Obviously one expects they would fit a standard 3-ring binder.

Getting three (3) packs looked like a great bargain – these are anything but.

UPDATE: They are still rather large, but I finally found some 3-ring binders to put them in and they do work.

One look at them after I took them out of the box they came in and I was leery. But, I opened them and put them in a 3-ring binder.

Quality is good, the fit? Atrocious. Sadly atrocious.

They don’t exactly fit the binder. And, by don’t fit – they stick out at least half an inch. And, it wasn’t like I just sat them in there – I put them in the rings and closed the binder.

The front pocket looks like it would not hold but two sheets of paper. There is also no way of labeling the tab. Yes, you can write on them, but the tabs are slick and any ink could rub off.

Durable is about the only good thing I can come up with for these. I’m sure for some they’d do in a pinch. I recommend spending the money and getting the name brands as I know they work – I’ve used them numerous times.

title: Not a Bargain
text:
These are definitely not a bargain.

Remembering my old school days, and the fact I still have some items around, even after 20-30 years – I’m truly appalled by these binders.

I don’t expect premium quality. But, these are incredibly cheap binders.

The construction doesn’t seem very durable, and I know as someone who was once a student – this would barely last a quarter (9 weeks), and I’d be lucky for the semester (18 weeks). And, I was usually gentle with my supplies. I can’t see these lasting the rigors of school – especially going to school in a backpack or just being carried all over.

The folder inside is more like a slick, thick piece of paper with a flap over it. It wouldn’t hold much, perhaps like a note, but nothing more.

The colors are more like a mauve and light purple, which are pretty.

These are a hard pass. I’d definitely spend more money and get the better quality binders.

title: Beautiful Planner
text:
As a rule, I prefer the January to December planner over the “academic” (July 2020 – June 2021) ones.

This is definitely a terrific planner.

Perfect size for desk usage, not too good for popping in a purse.

Pages to track goal progress, monthly appointments, daily appointments, tabs to get to the months, and it also lists the major holidays.

The spiral binding allows for the book to lay flat or “bend” it back. Also the spiral binding is wide thus the pages don’t bunch up.

The only thing lacking is a pen loop.

Otherwise this is a darling planner that would make a great present!

title: Short Term Planner
text:
This is a pretty cool idea – an undated planner.

The bad part? It is only a SIX (6) month planner. Though if one is converting from academic (July – June) types to transition into a January – December planner, this could work.

It is beautiful though – great gift for a man or woman and comes in a wonderful sturdy box suitable for wrapping.

The heavy leather bound book starts off looking fancy – for causal or work purposes it is definitely solid and durable.

I love the inclusion of the markers, stickers, and the tapes (whatever they are – they are pretty though).

The paper is pretty thick so that markers will not bleed through. There are pages and “sections” for every aspect of life.

If it weren’t for the fact it was a SIX (6) month planner, this would rate a LOT higher than it does.

title: Beautiful Journal
text:
This is a beautiful, non-date, perforated journal. Good for taking notes at a desk, or on the go.

It’s sturdy, and gorgeous! Perfect gift for any occasion.

I love the idea of the three ribbon placeholders. That makes sectioning the book much easier.

It could benefit from a pen loop as most journals like this have one.

All in all – no complaints.

title: Small Anything Notebook
text:
NOTE – this does not come with paper. You can find refill packs here on Amazon along with the “agenda” type refills. Look for the A6, which is the smaller size. Despite the number, the A6 is smaller and a perfect fit.

I got this to work more as a note taking book than an agenda/planner as I have a planner already.

This is easily stowed in a purse, backpack, or desk drawer.

This holds an entire pack – the one I got that is. That contained 200 sheets of paper.

This has a single pen loop and room for cards.

Makes a perfect “any time” gift for anyone of any age.

title: Great for Packing
text:
Having some “time” these days, I thought I’d go through some storage stuff.

The problem? Having enough supplies, and tape is one that tends to run out faster than anything.

That is usually what I use the tape for – sealing boxes and adhering “inventory” lists on the box.

This does the job. Pretty affordable, I’ve had zero issues with it.

I’ve read some issues with “lifting” – and I’ve had that from the office supply places as well as major tape brands. It could be the climate, then again it could be the box or tape.

Either way, this is a pretty good deal. These are the “smaller” rolls, and 18 is going to do me quite a while.

title: Basic Eraser
text:
These are pretty basic erasers which are good for students (3rd grade to college) as well as adults who need them for their work or hobbies.

They’re pretty easy to use and don’t mar or tear the paper.

I have had erasers that completely and cleanly erase pencil marks, but these are not that bad.

Individually wrapped to hand out or for storage. Comes in an AMAZON BASICS box with no frills.

title: Perfect Letter Board
text:
I do a LOT of Instagram pictures – mainly for books. And, one of the items I use is a letter board.

I had one that was a letter tile board. However, unlike this one – that didn’t come with many “letters”. Some words were impossible to spell as I didn’t have enough letters (buzz; bookkeeper). And, some of the tiles didn’t fit the board so it looked crooked and awkward. I also didn’t have any numbers.

This one? Perfection!

I have PLENTY of letters, everything fits in the space, there are emojis, script letter forms, and numbers. While they were on a plastic “bracket”, the set came with clippers and a file for easy removal.

And, it was definitely easy removal. I barely needed the file for the letters.

I also love that this set came with not one, but TWO burlap-type drawstring bags. That was another minus for the old board – no storage for the letters.

The base of the other one was a peg which hardly fit. This one has a detachable base and cane be hung up on the wall by way of an already attached bracket.

This is absolutely perfect for my needs and I wish I could’ve gotten this one first. I definitely recommend it for anyone wanting to add a “letter board” to their décor or communication or just fun.

title: Perfect Planner
text:
As someone who lives by a daily planner – finding one for my needs is often a challenge. Just when I find a good one, the next year it has been discontinued.

I try to go for the January to December ones; and it is hit or miss in finding one that has everything I need in it. Academic planners (usually June to June) are in abundance, but don’t always coincide with the previous planner.

A lot of them have stuff that isn’t needed either.

After locating a six month calendar (thankfully undated), I found this 12 month undated calendar. It is GORGEOUS. Larger than I like, but just perfect otherwise.

It is colorful, of course undated, and has inspirational phrases every single month. I enjoy the “gratitude” sections, and the colorful stickers help to completely personalize this. There is also plenty of space to make notes as well.

It makes a GREAT gift for any occasion because it is undated.

I honestly hope this is around the next time I need a planner because this is definitely my go-to planner from here on out.

title: Great Grip
text:
Pencils have become my “go-to” writing instruments for taking notes. I alternate between regular pencils and mechanical pencils for different reasons.

When using any writing instrument (pen or pencil) for any length of time, a “grip” is often a much needed bonus.

These are standard 7.0mm lead pencils I some vibrant colors. It is easy to find one’s favorite color(s) in the stack.

They function like all the other pencils out there, but the edge of the grip towards where the thumb joint would be (depending on how you hold the pencil) might be uncomfortable when using it for a long period.

Pretty good value for the amount of pencils.

Although I don’t need any more right now – I wouldn’t hesitate to get them again!

title: Interesting Concept
text:
Mechanical pencils are nothing new. Ones with grips are a newish idea.

Shake to advance? That’s completely different and definitely NEW.

As someone who uses a LOT of pencils in what I do – when I use them for a prolonged period, I want something comfortable. It’s also great when I don’t have to stop to sharpen a pencil. This is also a better idea for slipping a pencil in my purse or using in my bedroom.

The colors are pretty standard in this set. So, if one is sharing, someone might find their favorite color.

The barrel width is a bit wider than most mechanical pencils, and definitely wider than a normal pencil.

The eraser is a tad thin and not practical for use. Thankfully there are spares with this set, along with extra lead.

The grip extends all the way up on the back of the pencil with a small grip in front. There is a see-through window to watch the “shaker” weight.

The lead can be advanced by the top plunger or by shaking the pencil. I found the plunger idea is better for advancing the lead. Using the shaker results in too much lead being advanced and I’ve had to “push” the lead back to a reasonable level. Too long and it is going to break.

Overall, they’re pretty sturdy and great to use – but if using for a prolonged period, the pencil will get heavy due to the weight.

title: Nothing to See Here
text:
One thing about most gel pens – the vibrant, colorful ink.

So seeing these colors and having an abundance of ideas – I thought to snag them. They come in a cute little box and the colors look so pretty.

So, if this product scores two five star ratings in the categories, why the three star overall?

It isn’t performance or durability.

Instead, like my headline – there is nothing to see here, there, or anywhere to be honest.

These are extremely FINE tip, and may scratch certain textured papers.

The colors are pretty, but when it comes to writing with visibility – these don’t do very well. I used them on white paper; they may perform differently on black paper. If that is the case – that should be notes somewhere.

Overall, I was really disappointed as I had so many things I wanted to do with these, but they’re not that practical.

title: Standard Gel Pens
text:
With the various projects I have, I find it easier to keep track of them with different ink colors. It makes it easier to spot the projects and their priority.

While I prefer ball point, gel pens tend to stand out and provide better visual prominence.

These are as good, if not better than the standard ones sold by major companies and retailers.

Like the major ones – these have a grip for easier holding and writing. Writes smooth on “smooth” paper, I haven’t tried it on courser paper though.

After removing the “tip”, the pen writes right off.

The packaging is no frills – and perhaps easier to open. Pretty decent value to what is out there. I wouldn’t hesitate to get them again.

title: Standard Pencils
text:
I take a LOT of notes for the various projects I do – and one since sometimes things change, or I change my mind – pencils are essential to what I do.

For me, most pencils are the same. They function the same – graphite, cheap eraser, sharpen, use, re-sharpen.

Some are comfortable, some are not.

These, while I don’t know what lead they are (they write like #2), they have a unique finish that acts like a slight grip.

I prefer a manual type sharpener, which I find gets pencils sharper. This particular pencil didn’t fair well using the manual sharpener. It was coarse and difficult to manage.

The pencils faired a lot better with an electric sharpener, though they didn’t get as sharp.

Overall, a pretty decent value. They’re not as colorful as some I’ve seen, but they’re not the worst I’ve used either.

Thank you to the VINE program!

title: Much Like the Game, Few Tiles to Work With
text:
Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing an item to review. A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

Being an avid #Bookstagrammer, I often have to do “stylized” and unique pictures for the books I get. And, I have a lot of fun trying to think of ways to remain creative. With the “props” I have … I think I do fairly well.

But, of course, I want to try to up my game here or there. I’ve been seeing a lot of boards like this on Instagram. I’ve also seen the old type with the “peg in” type letters.

Needless to say, I was pretty happy to see it on the program. I was ESTACTIC to see this on my doorstep after ordering it! I had SO many plans … yet … there was some disappointment as I unpackaged it.

The board has a wobbly little peg to prop it up, and that didn’t fit – at first. So, I worked it into the hole on the back of the board to shape it, grabbed a 100/180 nail file, and carefully shaped the peg. It worked beautifully. But, where I was going to store it, I didn’t want the peg to fall out and get lost behind a bookcase. So, I used nail glue and stuck it in. That might be a problem if/when I need to pack it, but that’s another problem for another day.

The second issue – the tiles … I better not need to spell POPPY – I only have TWO (2) of the letter P tiles.

I went and counted the tiles – and while I have 100, some letters are only 1-2 in quantity. Forget spelling BUZZ or BUZZER as I only have ONE (1) Z. While there are two blank tiles – that doesn’t look very aesthetically pleasing when doing a project. Aesthetics are important for photos. I use the blank tiles for the # symbol for the hashtag.

Some of the tiles are THICKER than others. This is problematic when the “rows” are not adequately wide enough to accommodate the thicker tiles sticking in. While the top row might accommodate the tiles, the second and fourth rows may not. This causes uneven height issues.

I will likely have to purchase another or two of tiles to insure I have an adequately amount for future projects.

This cute idea has so much potential, but is only a three star reality.

title: Zodiac Bookmark
text:
Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing an item to review. A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

One of my FAVORITE hobbies; outside of trying to create my own stories; along with photography … READING.

I read a LOT of books. Last year – 76. This year? Close to 92. I started keeping track last year in March, so … that’s the reason for the slight YTD (year to date) difference.

With reading comes the need for a good bookmark. Some books I’ve won have come with them, some I get as promotional goodies from a launch team, but for the other books I have? I need something to mark my place. And, while I have some – I often keep buying bookmarks that are interesting. I’m also the kind of reader who tries to either color coordinate the bookmark, or get one that matches the “theme” of the novel.

Being that the best bookmarks are personalized – either with name, month of birth, or like this one … zodiac – I absolutely had to get this. The zodiac sign is printed on both sides of the little ball though it is NOT transparent or see through.

This is not the kind of bookmark that can be used with a small paperback as it could damage the book. The larger paperback books might be questionable, but this should be able to be used in a large hardcover book without any issues. Or even a journal book.

It’s also perfectly packaged for gift giving and is the best kind of gift to give a reader for any occasion. With Christmas being four (4) months away, this is also ideal for a stocking stuffer.

title: Throwback Erasers - Still Cute, But Now More Functional
text:
Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing an item to review. A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

I tend to take a lot of notes for “work” as well as writing – reviews, planning blogs, or even my own writing. And, a good eraser is ESSENTIAL BUSINESS EQUIPMENT.

Depending on the pencil “lead” (graphite, actually) and the paper texture – erasing a mistake can come with problems …

If the paper is slick and thick, not too many worries unless the graphite is really dark. If the paper is thin and “coarse” – no matter how light the graphite is, erasing is a challenge. Am I over thinking this? Nope. Just someone who hates to have to erase something and the paper tears or what I am erasing doesn’t seem to get erased.

Add in the fact that these resembled the 80’s type novelty ones (which I still have a few of those around), I thought they’d be a pretty good idea.

Unlike the 80’s ones – these have NO scent. So don’t expect apple, lemon, or strawberry scented erasers. These are cute, but functional.

These worked erasing text made by a Ticonderoga #2 pencil on a slick-type paper.

I made a few notes to test the erasers and the text erased very clean and didn’t tear up the paper. Some erasers don’t even erase the text completely before tearing up the paper.

I also tested them (again, using the same pencil) on a “coarser” type of paper – like before, the text was erased, and the paper didn’t tear.

There was still some “imprint” but that was only visible because of the camera and lighting.

Compared to other erasers, including ones from the manufacturer of the pencil, these erasers (at least the three I tested) performed remarkably well.

Given the cuteness, one could use these as a “BACK 2 SCHOOL” goodie bag type item, or stocking stuffers.

title: Basic Journals for Notekeeping
text:
Thank you in advance to the VINE program for providing a complimentary review item. A positive review was not required or requested, and all words are my own.

As someone who takes a lot of notes for my own projects as well as reviews for books, I am always looking for journals to use. And, these are a PERFECT size to do that with! I can easily tuck them into a backpack, medium purse, or in a desk drawer.

They’re basic – no frills. College ruled lines and don’t have a lot of pages.

Depending on the person’s need, these would definitely work for occasional use.

I’m definitely happy with them and SO glad I got them!

title: Cute Little Inspirational Journal
text:
Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing the item to review. A positive review was not required or requested, and all words are my own.

As someone who does a lot of writing, and note taking for reviews and someone who collects journals (even “inspiring” ones) – I couldn’t resist this one! I just LOVE that quote on the front! This isn’t a tiny journal book; and definitely not a large one either.

The size (6½” x 8”) makes it perfect to dump in a mid to large size purse, it has perforated sheets in case you want to remove a page or need a quick piece of paper for notes, and it has “color-coded” pages to section things off. The big rings give the user ample room to turn the pages. This has been an issue for me with some journals – lack of spiral space to turn pages. After a while they tend to get bunched up and it makes the journal unusable.

The back and front covers when combined, make a sturdy surface to write on if a desk or table isn’t handy.

This would also make a PERFECT gift:

** Graduation
** Birthdays
** Anniversaries
** Christmas
** New Job

Overall, I’m pretty thrilled with this little journal.

title: Versatile Bags - Necessity in my Home
text:
Looking for small bags to store some craft supplies in – I found these here on Amazon. Some of the items were tiny beads or string I’d cut for future products.

What started with crafts has morphed into food storage, as well as storage for small jewelry items, erasers, other supplies.

I use the smaller ones for medication to take up to my room as I really don’t want to haul a huge pain reliever bottle up and down the stairs every single day. Nor, do I want to purchase multiple bottles. So, I put a few tablets in a bag and take it up to put beside my bed.

The 3x4 and 3x5 bags are great for storing spice mixes for recipes. I use mine more or less for my chili spices as I make my own from the regular spices.

Rather than mix up the spice batch for every pot, I mix up a few “bags” at the beginning of the month and have them ready for when we want chili.

These work well with keeping the spices contained and I don’t “smell” them either (the spices that is).

Another thing I’ve used the bags for – condiments. Not kidding. I’m not a “tree-hugger”, but I do tend to get a lot of packets of condiments to save money here or there.

Sometimes I’ll use half a packet. Rather than to throw it away – I slip the unused portion in a baggie (usually the 2x3 size), and pop it in the fridge. Next time I need the condiment – it’s right there. This is a great money saver as well.

I’ve been using them for three (3) years, so I’m definitely happy with the quality. They’re shipped directly from Amazon, so delivery isn’t an issue (nor is available stock).

title: Colorful and Functional Dividers
text:
I got these for multiple projects that I had to print, and these do what they’re supposed to – divide the sections. The tabs are big and colorful. The dividers aren’t exactly wimpy, but they’re not “super durable” either. They’ll do the job if used and treated gently.

One thing I liked, but didn’t have a need of – the landscape mode. The last time I bought dividers (incidentally this brand, but a different style) – that wasn’t a choice.

And, the “printing template” from their website was easy to use. I didn’t use the PDF version as it would’ve left “lines” on it. I opted for the WORD template.

I HIGHLY encourage printing a sample of how it looks, stick the paper back in to see how the Table of Contents (TOC) would look when printed. I did this and had NO issues.

As I have been a fan of this brand for well over 20+ years, and used a differently style, I’m happy with these. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend them or buy them again should I have need of them.

title: Standard Paper
text: Standard all purpose paper. Haven't had too many jams or issues with it. Works pretty well, and easy to open.

title: Dr. Grip Refills - Can Also Use In Other Pens
text:
These are the ballpoint refills that fit the Dr. Grip ballpoint pens. These do not fit the gel or roller ball ones.

These are also used in various other pens as well. One I’ve found is the Zebra Orbitz. I have a Patriotic one and a Camo one that this refill fits. There are countless other non-Pilot brands it fits.

These refills run the course. Before she retired, my mother used to use the Bottle2Pen recycled ones (mad from plastic bottles). She would run her pens completely out of ink. You couldn’t see the ink. The B2P took this refill so she went through quite a few of them.

Works right off, and in my mom’s case, they worked to the nib/nub of the refill.

The value is average. I say this as I remember getting these at Walmart for $1. So, paying twice that isn’t too much of a value. But, I’ve seen worse.

title: Easy to Use with Attached Hub
text:
Getting ready for Christmas in my home, means wrapping. Wrapping means tape. And, after getting a few rolls this week, I went looking for my tape dispenser since my handheld one was too small for the rolls I got (the Scotch brand ½ - 1296 inch ones).

But, I’d lost the “hub” (black center piece that holds the roll). Having an Amazon gift card balance, I opted to first look for the hubs. Couldn’t find them (and didn’t want to shell out too much money). Instead, I found this tape dispenser (at the time less than $5 with tax). And, it had a BONUS – attached tape hub.

My mother (now retired) used to order office supplies at the hospital where she worked. After some of her co-workers kept throwing the hubs away or losing them – she decided to order some tape dispensers with attached hubs – much like this one. And, she was quite pleased with them – as that stopped a lot of “losses”.

With Prime shipping, I decided to order it.

Glad I did! I’m absolutely thrilled with this. It’s small, fits on a crowded desk and works!

Bonuses:

* Has enough sand to weight it down, but not so much I can’t hold it in my hand

* It fits my roll! Silly me, I did get the ½ inch tape (1296 in) rather than the ¾, but it still works (both tape and dispenser)

* Ease of use. This thing is easy to use! And, I’ve had a LOT of different tape dispensers over the decades.

* The attached hub! LOVE it.

After inserting the roll, my mother decided to look at the dispenser and loved it!

She also provided a helpful hint with this – MAKE SURE THE HUB IS SNAPPED INTO PLACE. You should hear the SNAP when you push it down. Otherwise, the roll is going to bounce up and down (maybe even fall off) every time you use it.

This is slim and actually snazzy looking, especially for the price I paid. I’ve put it to use in prepping for Christmas and haven’t been disappointed. If I am – I’ve got the 30 day return window.

And, no – in most cases, the tape NEVER comes with a dispenser. If it is part of a package deal; then most likely. But, even on this box it clearly indicates that tape is not included. It’s shown with tape so the customer can see how it looks and how to gauge it for their personal use.

If anyone bought it as a package deal - tape and dispenser, and didn't get either one - that is more of a customer service issue than product issue. I'd immediately contact the seller for a refund and/or replacement. If that doesn't work - contact Amazon.

I’m pretty pleased, and if this remains at a low price – I might get a few more after the holidays.

title: Standard Tape
text: Standard tape. I ended up (by accident) getting the 1/2" (thinner) tape. It still works. No real issues from the Scotch brand. Works for most all your adhesive tape needs.

title: Affordable and Durable Planner
text: Sturdy planner, great little gift. This can easily fit in a purse or desk drawer. Basic and easy to use.

title: Good For Mailing or Storage
text: Bought this because I needed packing tape. Average value. Works better than some. Strong though, definitely not thin.

title: Environmental Pencil
text:
Ticonderoga EnviroStik pencils are made with premium wood from responsibly managed forests. They work just like regular pencils. They’re the common #2 lead (actually graphite). The #2 on this pencil isn’t too bad and doesn’t smudge much which I find surprising. They sharpen quite well in either an electric or a manual sharpener. I have an excellent manual sharpener (Yikes! Brand). It’s old, but it works even better than my mom’s electric sharpener.

As I use cap erasers, I don’t use the pencil erasers much – but I have used this one and it erased clean. Seems solid.

Like most of their “designer pencils”, I have a problem with the lack of lead selection. I prefer #3 lead since I don’t need them for school or work. When I do use them for writing or making notes, the #3 lead works better for me. That’s the only thing I would change is the availability of the lead for the designs.

These are environmentally friendly, and the cost is on part with the other designer pencils from Ticonderoga.

title: Best Correction Tape I've Used!
text:
I’ve been using correction tape products for well over 10+ years. I started with the refillable Tombow MONO CX (thick) and the thinner PXN (which used to be a purple/white device). It worked pretty well. But, finding refills was problematic after a while.

I tried to find other suitable replacements – correction pens or another type of tape – nothing worked.

Several years ago, I tried some BIC tapes – and they were awesome! Just as easy to hold and use as my Tombows, and less expensive too. So, the BIC ones became my go-to-brand. I used them when I’m making lists or after finding a mistake after I’ve printed something.

Since I was running low, I was pleased to discover the 10-pack was available for subscribe and save. I prefer the various colors of the 4-pack (yellow, orange, pink, blue) – the 10-pack has five (5) orange and five (5) blue tapes.

title: Eco Version of the Classic
text:
This is the Eco version of the classic BIC stick pen. It performs just as well as the classic one. As far as value, the classic is a better value, but these are not that much more expensive.

I got them as refills for other BIC stick pens that I like to use.

title: Perfect Classic
text:
These are the timeless, classic stick pen. They perform perfectly the first time. Great for students, secretaries, anyone who uses a pen at work. Light and easy to hold.

I got them to refill some older casino/hotel pens that I just love using.

title: Patriotic Pride Pen
text:
This pen is a great way to show your patriotic pride, and be comfortable while writing. It’s easy to use and light weight. It is also easy to refill. It comes with blue ink, but I easily swapped it with a black refill (I was able to use the Pilot Dr. Grip).

I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this as a gift for military, former military, law enforcement – or anyone who wants to display their patriotic pride.

title: Dr. Grip (and other pen) Refills
text:
First of all, these are the BALLPOINT PEN refills for the Dr. Grip pen (and other pens that use them). If you have a gel or rollerball –THEY WON’T FIT. PLEASE REFER TO THE PICTURE AND YOUR ORIGINAL REFILL.

With that said …

These are the PERFECT FIT for the Dr. Grip pen as well as the Pilot B2P (bottle 2 pen). I also have other promo and “special” pens these refills fit in. This also fits the the Zebra Orbitz Retractable Ballpoint Pen (American Flag Print).

I don’t know about other people, but these refills have lasted quite a long time for the pens I have refilled. These refills are the same quality as ones that could be found in major office supply stores.

I haven’t been disappointed in these refills. I’ve bought five 12-packs since I found them on here, and I will continue to buy more.

title: Write Bright!
text:
Dr. Grip ballpoint pens (as well as pencils) were introduced in 1995 and have been commended for “Ease-of-Use” by the Arthritis Foundation.

They first introduced with the black and blue barrels. As the line expanded, Pilot offered more styles and colors – gel pens and different color barrels. Of particular interest to me was the “brights” collection. When they were introduced I was able to get a purple, blue, and green. I couldn’t get a pink one. After years of searching – found it here.

It works just like the original Dr. Grip pens, only they’re in “bright” colors.

For “long term” writing (stories, notes); they’re not comfortable – at least to me. They’re a bit too heavy and bulky. I honestly prefer the thinner “promo” type pens for long term. For me, the Dr. Grip pens are better for short term writing – making lists, signing checks. Not even my 68 year old mom uses them for long term writing.

This is not to say they’re not good pens. They are extremely durable. But, my mother and I haven’t seen much difference in hand cramps from using promo pens, stick pens, or these pens.

Each individual will vary as to whether they like them or not. I am still extremely fond of them though.

title: Printing at Home
text:
This isn’t the same quality as the prints you get from online print services or pharmacies you can pick up from in an hour.

However, for the money and for memories – it isn’t too bad. Some might find the photo paper to be better, some might find it worse. It depends on one’s preference.

I use it for pictures I’ve downloaded from my theme park visits and they look great. Saves money. Private, convenient, and fast.

title: Cute, Durable, Refillable, Charitable
text:
These are not cheaply made pens at all. They are sturdy metal pens best suited for high school, college, work, or at home use. They are refillable with a standard "Parker" type refill so you won't be throwing it away after the ink runs dry. They're thin, but don't have a comfort grip. The design is "slick" rather than matte. Gripping might be an issue for some people with arthritis or other dexterity issues.

Yoobi stationary offers a "buy one, donate one" program. The actual item donated varies by classroom need. So that makes this a bonus purchase.

title: Good Value, Variety; Good for Those Who Just Need a Pen; Good for Refills
text:
I've purchased two of these lots and haven't been disappointed. I've gotten exactly 100 the first time, and 101 this last time.

Yes, they were not ALL retractable. Some had grips, others had stylus types. There were some twist pens, there was a stick pen. But, they were pretty decent pens, especially for 13¢ each. Some were like souvenir pens that you'd get from a hotel, one was even a souvenir from a lighthouse in Maine. I loved the Margaritaville Resort (Orlando) pen in this last lot. I got university pens (top yellow is from Northern Kentucky University), a sorority pen, medical type pens, even a "cell phone holder" pen. Some of these "finds" went into a "personal collection" rather than for the purpose they were originally purchased for (see below).

As these lots are thrown together - the lack of variety or the type of pens in it is to be expected. One lot was all black, medium ball point ink. That was fine. One lot had about six blue ink pens. Either way, I wasn't disappointed.

They're great for students, restaurant workers, or anyone who needs a pen but doesn't want to spend a ton of money on them; and especially for people who don't want to lose their favorite pen when at work or school.

I usually get lots like these as refills for other promo and souvenir pens I own as these pen lots are about the same type and/or style of pen I'm trying to refill. And, I can't seem to find refills for the pens. In addition, a 13¢ refill (roughly $13 per 100 pens) is a hard bargain to pass up.

I'll be buying another lot pretty soon.

title: Beautiful and Functional Planner
text:
This is not only a beautiful planner, but a functional one as well.

This comes in a beautiful gift box for gift giving, but it is a little snug to get out. It is small enough to place inside a desk drawer or a medium to large purse.

The material isn’t exactly plastic, nor is it leather-type. It is slick though. The colors on the front are vibrant. It makes a perfect gift for a graduate, mother’s day, even for father’s day as it is “neutral” with regard to the color scheme.

Rigid construction to withstand daily use; lays flat to write in. It also has two different color “place” ribbons for marking your place. The months are “cut-out” tabs for easily accessing different months for planning.

For easy closing, there is an elastic ribbon to fit around the planner along with a pen holder, which is really cool, along with a pocket in the back for receipts or event tickets.
