title: Lines are slightly wider than college ruled
text:
This review is for the Dark Green set of 3 Lined Journal Notebooks from EHWINE.

The notebooks are identical. Each is dark green, with a stamped owl decoration on the front cover and WERTIOO stamped on the back cover. The notebooks have an elastic closure, one ribbon bookmark, one folded pocket on the inside back cover, and an elastic pen loop.

The first page of each journal is a Personal Memoranda page that I dislike. Who is going to write down their driver’s license number, savings account numbers, or credit card numbers?? The next three pages are yearly calendars for 2023, 2024, and 2025. Then the rest of the pages are lined. The lining is slightly wider than college ruled.

I did a bleed through test with a Stabilo 88 fineliner; there is faint bleed through, but not enough to keep me from using the back of the page.

The value of this set is amazing! It’s like getting three for one, and there’s some color variety and the cute owl on the covers.

title: Gorgeous color; dots are very light, fineliners bleed through pages
text:
This notebook from Annecy is nearly perfect!

The rose gold cover is a gorgeous shade of pinkish gold with a metallic sheen. It looks very pretty under the light. Most of my notebooks are black, so I always appreciate a unique cover. The journal has a pen loop, another plus for me. I take notebooks with me wherever I go, but I don’t like carrying a bag, so I need a pen loop.

The notebook has two ribbon bookmarks, an elastic closure band, and a pocket on the inside back cover. The only branding is Annecy’s logo on the back cover. A sheet of label and spine stickers is included, too.

The first three pages are index pages, with tables for page number and description. The rest of the pages are numbered, and the numbering starts properly, #1 after the last index page.

There are only two things I don’t like about this notebook.

One: the dots are so faint I can barely see them. At first glance, the pages look blank. I use dotted journals all the time; I’m not used to putting my nose practically on the page to make out the dots. They are a very, very light gray.

Two: the paper is thin. I did a bleed through test with a Stabilo 88, my preferred journaling pen. I can clearly see what I wrote on the back of the page.

title: No instructions, poor construction
text:
I have the Black Frame + Black Board version of this Desk Shelf Organizer. The boards are MDF or medium-density fiberboard; I had quite a few chips and scuffs on mine, which really stood out against the black. The edges have a gray strip, like a bezel, and that is also stark against the black.

The organizer doesn’t come with assembly instructions. It’s not hard to put together, but a diagram in the box would be very helpful. I had to look up a picture of it, so I could figure out how to use the clear plastic brackets.

The brackets fit into pre-drilled holes on the bottom of each board, four brackets to a board. The upside-down U on the bracket hooks over the side of the frame, ∩ fitting over the sides. Because of how the brackets hook over the frame, you can’t put one shelf on the very bottom. That leaves 3¾ inches of space between the two shelves.

The shelves do not fit tightly, which I don’t like. If I try to move the organizer by holding onto a shelf, the shelf lifts off. Instead, I have to pick it up by the frame to move it.

For me, the organizer is just okay. I wish the construction were better, and that the shelves fit tightly onto the frame.

title: No cable management
text:
This stand does quire assembly. Putting it together isn’t hard, just a little awkward. A Phillips screwdriver is needed.

I don’t care much for the mouse storage rack, but it’s integrated into the side of the stand, so you can’t take it off. My daily driver mouse (MX Master 3) is too thick to fit in the rack. The bottom depth of the mouse rack is just under 1½ inches.

The keyboard side does not have any cable management, which is a downside. Not all keyboards have detachable cables! Because I don’t use the mouse rack, I ended up looping the cables around the shelves and into it.

However, all those quibbles aside, I do like this keyboard rack. Since getting into split keyboards, I’ve acquired a small collection that I switch between. I can’t store them on a vertical rack, so they took up a lot of space on my desk. This horizontal rack frees up some space for me, and keeps the keyboards relatively safe. I currently have a Ferris Sweep, Corne, and Iris sitting in the rack, and it’s working well for my needs.

title: Firm memory foam
text:
The measurements are accurate, 9.5 inches long by 3 inches wide, but I suspect this set of Memory Foam Armrest Chair Pads from Western Comfort will be short for most office and gaming chairs.

On my office chair, about 3.5 inches of the armrest are exposed. That’s okay with me, it’s not like my arms take up the whole armrest. But it does look a little silly.

The memory foam is very firm, not squishy. When I press with all my hand strength, it barely indents. I prefer this level of support. But if you’re looking for pillowy foam armrest pads, this isn’t the set.

The velcro straps are long, so you can cut them to size once the armrest pads are fitted on your chair. The velcro holds securely, I’ve had the armrest pads on my chair for almost a month and haven’t had to tighten the velcro once.

title: Drawer pulls on bottom of drawers, lightweight plastic
text:
This review is for the Narrow 4 Drawer, White/White Storage Unit from IRIS USA.

The storage unit requires simple assembly, but no instructions were in the box. The frame and drawers are easy enough to figure out. The frame snaps together and the drawers slide inside. But I couldn’t figure out how the front panel pieces went onto the drawers.

I don’t like the panel pieces at all. I’m actually not using them. With the panel pieces on the drawers, the only handle to open them is at the bottom! That’s why I took them off. Putting the drawer pulls on the bottom of the drawers is awkward, and makes it difficult to open the bottom drawers. It goes against muscle memory; every time I wanted to open a drawer, my hand went to the top of the drawer. Without the front panels, the drawers actually have a lip on the top that functions as a drawer pull.

The only downside to not using the panels is a gap between the frame and the drawers, so dust can drift inside.

I have the white storage unit, and the plastic had a lot of random dark gray spots. Like it was dirty, but when I washed it, the spots didn’t come off.

Overall, the unit is quite lightweight. It’s not suitable for anything heavy.

title: Stackable organizer

title: Cute organizeer
text:

title: Tiny stacking organizer cube

title: Glittery covers are nice, paper is very thin

title: Great option for split keyboards
text:
I’m using two of these Adjustable Armrests from Radlove. I have a split keyboard, the halves shoulder width apart. I’ve been trying to find a good armrest/wrist rest option, and I think these are the best I’ve tried. The armrests allow me to hover my hands over each keyboard half, supporting my elbows so my arms don’t get tired.

The armrests swivel and move with the motions of my arms, so that’s why I really like them for my split keyboard. And reaching for my mouse is easy, I don’t have to take my elbow out of the armrest. When I’m not typing, I use the one armrest for my mouse arm and it’s supportive.

The armrests are quite adjustable. The height, position, and angle can be adjusted. The elbow cup rotates 360° and doesn’t have a set front or back, so it swivels with the movements of your arms. The height is a bit too easy to adjust in my opinion, I wish the mechanism was stiffer so I don’t accidentally change it. Changing the height is done by moving the armrest up in the air, and a button on the arm releases the height setting.

The arm has two segments that give you some room with positioning. When I first mounted them to my desk, I put the armrests right where my arms were. But the clamps hit my legs. I have the clamps open to the maximum width to accommodate the width of my desk, so that means 3 inches of the mounting screw sticks out the bottom of the clamp. All this is to say, I have the armrests mounted on the edges of my desk and they reach the middle just fine.

My desk is 2 inches thick, with a metal frame underneath. The mounting clamps fasten to my desk.

title: Runs large, not compressive
text:
In my experience, the Smart School Body Sock runs big. I’m a 5’5” adult woman and have the body sock in size large. It’s too big on me. I do not feel any compression anywhere. The body sock is so big I can walk around the house. If you or your kiddo do walk around while wearing it, the body sock is slippery on tile or wood flooring.

The material is smooth, a stretchy mix of 85% polyester and 15% spandex. There are no tags on the inside, but there are seams. I don’t like the snap closure at the neck, the black material is a little rougher than the body sock, and the snaps don’t always stay closed.

I have the Dinosaurs print, which is bright and vibrant and cute. I washed the body sock on gentle cycle in cold water, and dried on low heat. It washed just fine, no fading or shrinking.

title: Design spans front and back covers
text:
I use hardcover notebooks like this all the time, but 95% of my journals have plain black covers. Boring! So naturally, I was drawn to the printed covers on these notebooks from YAGNAA. Each notebook has a different elk design, and maybe I’m showing my age, but they remind me of notebooks from the book fair when I was a kid.

The designs span the front cover, spine, and back cover. For pictures that have gold elements, like the black notebook, the gold is matte. Not shiny. The elastic closure, pen loop, and bookmark match the notebook. Yellow for the two notebooks with yellow in their pictures, and red for the one of the elk with very impressive antlers.

YAGNAA is printed on the back of each notebook and on the first inside page. The notebooks have lined pages and a pocket folder on the inside back cover.

The pack of 12 fineliners is okay. The tips are 0.4mm, the ink doesn’t smear. The color variety is okay. I don’t know if the colors are random or set, but my pack had: 2 blues, 2 greens, yellow, pink, orange, purple, red, brown, peach, and black. For writing, the fineliners had minimal bleedthrough, and more if I colored a spot or design.

Overall, I think this set of notebooks is great if you’re looking for variety with bujos or journals.

title: Chair wheels making imprints
text:
The DESKU Octagon Gaming Chair Mat comes rolled up, so I laid it out for a day, with heavy objects on all 8 points to flatten it out.

I like the shape a lot! Enough of the mat fits under my desk so I can roll right up to the edge of my desk without having to wedge the mat under the desk legs.

But the mat doesn’t cooperate well with carpeting. A disappointment, since the description says it’s for carpet. The carpet in my house isn’t super plush or high pile, just your normal carpet. After a few hours, the mat is already buckling from my chair. There are wheel imprints in the plastic.

The edges of the mat rise up from the carpet if I sit too close to the edge. The mat has plastic spikes on the underside, to help it keep from moving on the carpet. Not something I want to accidentally poke my toe or foot against because the edges are in the air.

title: Reminds me of spending hours in ICC
text:
I have the “90x40 sheshou” design in the Envysun Gaming Mouse Mat. This design features Sylvanas Windrunner fighting Sindragosa in Icecrown, with the Lich King in the background.

Any Warcraft fan will instantly recognize the design. The scene reminds me of my days playing one of the best expansions and raiding ICC.

The colors are bright. The mouse mat looks even better in person than it does in the pictures. The blues and purples are vibrant, and Sylvanas’s red eyes really pop.

The mouse mat is big, there’s enough space for a laptop, external keyboard, mouse, and other desk stuff. The back is non-slip, and it doesn’t move on my desk. The mouse mat does smell strongly of rubber when first unpacked, so I let it air out for a few days. Upside down, and with objects holding down the corners to straighten it out (it comes rolled).

The edges are bound, I didn’t have any unsewn or rough spots.

title: Cover picks up marks
text:
I have the Dark Green color in this dotted hardcover notebook from WERTIOO. The cover, elastic closure loop, and ribbon bookmark are dark green. The cover has a debossed tree as shown, and WERTIOO is debossed on the back cover. That’s the only branding I noticed.

I don’t love the cover. It’s made from polyurethane leather, aka artificial leather. It has a slightly gummy feel to it, and it picks up marks and imprints like crazy. The notebook ships wrapped in plastic, but when I unwrapped it, the notebook already had marks.

The pages are dotted, and the dots line up pretty well across the spine. By that, I mean the dots on the left page and the dots on the right page are usually in a straight line.

The first page is a silly Personal Memoranda page, with sections for information like your driver’s license number or credit card numbers. I say silly because I can’t imagine anyone writing those numbers down in a notebook someone else might find! The next three pages are yearly calendars for 2022, 2023, and 2024. The inside back cover has a pocket folder.

Aside from the cover, I like this journal. I use notebooks like this all the time, so I appreciate having some color variety for cover options.

title: Smooth, consistent color
text:
The tips on the Colourcolor Fineliner Pens remind me of felt-tip markers. They don’t look like the tips on the rest of my fineliners. But that’s not a bad thing.

The Colourcolor pens put down smooth, consistent ink. They glide across paper, no scratching. The colors match the color on the barrel.

The ink dries very quickly. I’m left-handed so I always do a smear test. The ink did not smear at all.

Bleed through is minimal for writing and lines, but obvious bleed through when coloring in a block or area.

The colors are quite light, trending towards pastel. I can see all of them on white paper, but some colors are harder to see than others, like the two yellows and the very light green. The color choices are a little odd to me. Six of the pens are pink or purple, so a quarter of the set.

The lids don’t have clips; they have a raised dot to keep the pen from rolling on a desk. The bodies and lids are smooth, white plastic that is slippery in the hand.

title: Runs January 2023 to December 2023
text:
The PAPERAGE 2023 Weekly & Monthly Planner has weekly and monthly spreads, a spread of 2023 and 2024 calendars, a year long tracker, and 25 dotted pages. There are 2 ribbon bookmarks, a folder on the inside back cover, and a sheet of cover and spine stickers.

The planner runs from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2023.

The planner starts with all the monthly spreads and then all the weekly breakdowns. There’s no tab to easily flip from month to week, but you could use a ribbon bookmark for that purpose.

For the monthly spreads, they have a blank section on the left page for notes. Each day square measures 1⅜ inches wide by 1⅛ inches tall. I do wish the month labels were in a bigger font, the days of the week are larger printing than the month.

For the weekly spreads, they always start on Monday. Each weekly spread has the days of the week on the left page and a blank dotted page on the right.

The paper is 100 gsm, it feels slick and smooth. I did a bleed through test with a Stabilo 88 fineliner, I had very faint bleed through. Not enough to keep me from using the back of a page.

title: Binder clips work as expected
text:
This is a pack of 50 small binder clips from DUIJINYU. The pack is a good value, just under ten cents per clip. I was just looking at binder clips in a big box store, and a comparable box is more than double.

I received 50 clips, one was broken. I’m not fussed, that can happen in any multipack.

The clips measure ¾ inch, with a capacity to hold 50-60 pages. They can hold fewer pages too, this small size is quite versatile. I use them to hold file folders shut and to keep my calendar flat, but obviously, they have a lot of uses.

The binder clips just work!

title: Luxurious black page journal
text:
I have the BKB-3 design in this dotted journal from BUKE. That design has a black cover with the phases of the moon. The moons are holographic silver. The pages are black with white dots. There are two ribbon bookmarks, black and gold, and a pocket on the inside back cover. There is no branding on the cover or inside pages.

The journal comes in a nice gift box. The box has a silver foil design on the top, a tree and the planets. But the box was taped shut, and when I removed the tape from either side, part of the design came off. The journal inside is wrapped in tissue paper.

The journal also comes with 3 sheets of planner stickers and a sticky patch with an elastic pen loop. I really like a pen loop but it can ruin the aesthetic, so I appreciate having the option to add it if I want.

The pages are dotted, and I really like that the dots line up across the pages. By that, I mean the dots are aligned in straight lines from left to right, even across the center. Sometimes the dots are off from page to page, but that’s not the case here.

Overall, this is a very nice black paper journal!

title: 24 pen set has okay color variety
text:
I have the set of 24 pens. The color variety is okay. If you’ll be using the pens on white or light paper, 4-5 of the colors are very light on white paper.

These artPOP! Fineliner Pens are very similar to my favorite Stabilo Point 88 Fineliners. The writing experience feels identical. The nib width is the same, 0.4mm.

These pens put down smooth, consistent color. They do smear. I’m left-handed so I always do a smear test. With these pens, I have to give the ink a few seconds to dry or my writing will smear.

The lids close with an audible click, so I know the lids are on tight. The barrels are triangular-shaped, but it’s a very subtle, rounded triangle shape that feels comfortable in the hand. The top and bottom of the barrel are round, and I like that a lot. That way, the lids have round openings, so there’s no matching up triangle points to get the lids on.

I don’t care much for the storage tin. It’s big and takes up space, and the pens don’t stay very well in the red liner.

title: Also great for split keyboards
text:
I am actually using the MOLMO Ergonomic Wrist Rest Pads with my split keyboard. They aren’t as thick as Brilas, so they are a good match for my low profile Corne. The heels of my hands rest on the pads, and then I can float my fingers over the board.

I have the wrist pads positioned horizontally, think -- and not |, one in front of each keyboard half. The wrist pads are larger than each keyboard half, but that gives my hands plenty of room to roam over my keyboard.

Each wrist pad has a slight slope, with the front slightly lower than the back. Or the back (where the logo is) slightly higher than the front, depending on how you have them positioned. The slope is so slight that I don’t notice it, even with the wrist pads laid out in a horizontal position.

title: Ribbon bookmark is different color than cover
text:
I have the “Sky Blue” color in this dotted notebook from Soomeet. The cover and elastic closure loop are sky blue, but the ribbon bookmark is brown. The front and back cover are plain, there is no branding. The cover is hardcover, but it’s a little puffy, it feels more like a slipcover than the usual hardcover notebook.

The inside pages are plain too, no branding. The pages are dotted, with dark gray dots. The inside back cover has a pocket folder, and inside that pocket is a pack of index tabs and three sheets of alphabet stickers.

The paper is 100 gsm. I had very slight bleed through when testing with a Stabilo 88 fineliner. The bleed through wasn’t enough to keep me from using the back of the page, it’s barely noticeable.

title: Plastic envelopes
text:
At first, I wasn’t impressed with these plastic envelopes. I thought they were flimsy and thin, and that they wouldn’t last. But first impressions aren’t always right, and that’s the case here. These envelopes from Jasilon are better than I thought!

The envelopes are two inches longer than a piece of computer or notebook paper, so they can hold many sheets of paper. I put a stack of notebook paper about half an inch thick, and the envelope still snapped shut.

The snap closures are my main concern. Some of the envelopes are permanently wrinkled where the snaps are, so I wonder how durable the plastic really is.

I have the Assorted Color option, and received: 4 clear, 2 red, 2 yellow, 1 blue, and 1 green.

title: Gives me nostalgia!
text:
I have the “90x40 yilidan” option in this mouse mat from Envysun. To put that into inches, the mouse mat is 35⅜ inches long by 15⅞ inches tall. It’s a nice big mouse mat, I have enough room for my laptop, split keyboard, mouse, and drink.

The picture of Illidan brings back my Warcraft raiding days. Black Temple was one of my favorite raids, so I like the nostalgia whenever I look down. The picture is clear, it’s obviously Illidan on a fel-infused backdrop.

The backing is non-slip rubber, the mouse mat stays in place on my desk. It did have a strong rubber scent when unpacked, but after I let it air out for a few days, the scent disappeared. The edges are bound, I didn’t see any loose threads or missed spots.

title: Colors are bright
text:
This pack of 8 sticky notes is a good value. The colors are fluorescent, so a little brighter than pictured.

The sticky notes measure 3 inches by 3 inches. Each pad has 100 sheets, I actually went through one pad and counted every sheet to verify.

The sticky notes stick … one time. The adhesive isn’t super strong or super sticky, so if you put one in the wrong place and need to move it, the note likely won’t stay stuck. But they work great for the first application.

I tried an ink pen, a gel pen, and a Sharpie Pen, and all wrote on the sticky notes.

title: No branding, sturdy notebook
text:
I have the “Burgundy” color notebook from CToN. The color is deep red, with a matching ribbon bookmark. The elastic closure is a slightly darker red color.

The front cover, back cover, and spine are plain. There is no branding on the outside or inside of the notebook. There is a pocket on the inside back cover. I found a sheet of cardstock inside that pocket. The sheet has what looks like spine and cover stickers, but they aren’t stickers, just printed cardstock.

The pages are lined. The lines are the same spacing as college ruled. The top and bottom lines on each page are darker than the rest.

The paper is 100 gsm, I had very faint bleed through when testing with a Sharpie Pen.

title: Monthly spreads from January 2023 to December 2024
text:
The PAPERAGE 2 Year Planner has some useful extra pages in addition to the 2 years worth of monthly spreads for 2023 and 2024. Additional pages include a password list, lists of holidays for both years with space to add your own important dates, goal pages for both years, habit trackers*, contacts, and 17 blank ruled pages at the end.

*The habit trackers only have dots for 30 days, which seemed a little strange to me since some months have 31 days.

For the monthly spreads, the blocks for each day measure 1¾ inches by 1¾ inches, with 7 ruled lines for each block. There is a notes section on the right page, and small calendars for the previous and upcoming months. The monthly spreads run from January 2023 to December 2024.

I really wish the different sections and months had tabs, so I could quickly flip to a section or month. The pages don’t always turn easily, the binding is narrow, so if you try to turn too many pages at once, they get stuck.

The covers are not super sturdy, I honestly doubt they will survive 2 years of use. They feel like thick cardstock. The outsides might have a vegan leather layer, but the insides are polka dotted cardstock.

title: Pen loop is a plus
text:
These dotted notebooks from Compera are a little smaller across than similar notebooks, the width is about half an inch smaller. The given measurements of 8.3 inches by 5.1 inches are accurate, but I didn’t realize the slight size difference until I had one sitting on top of my other bujo notebook.

The notebooks have “Compera” on the lower right front and back covers, and on the inside front page.

The notebooks have a ribbon bookmark, an elastic closure, a folder inside the back cover, and a pen loop. I love the pen loop, I always miss when notebooks don’t have it. That pen loop is essential for me if I take a notebook on the go.

The pages are dotted, with gray dots. The paper is 100 gsm thick. I did a bleed through test with a Stabilo 88 fineliner and could clearly see each letter I wrote on the back of the page. I’ll still use the front and back of each page, I just wish the paper was a touch thicker.

title: Great notebooks other than first page
text:
I have the “Black/Green” color option in this set of hardcover notebooks. The colors are true to the pictures. The covers have a slight texture. The notebooks have an elastic closure, one ribbon bookmark, a pen loop, and a pocket inside the back cover.

Each notebook has the tree design debossed into the cover. There is no branding on the front cover, back cover, or inside the covers.

The first 4 pages of each notebook have printed information. The first page is a “Personal Memoranda” page which is a bit weird to me. It has sections for information like your passport number, driver’s license number, savings account number, credit card numbers… I can’t believe anyone would use this page! The next 3 pages are yearly calendars for 2022, 2023, and 2024.

The pages are lined, the lines are very slightly wider than college ruled paper. The lines are dashed, printed in dark grey so they aren’t super stark.

Overall, the value is fantastic for this set of notebooks.

title: Scratchy tips, smooth ink flow
text:
I like fine point pens for making trackers in my bujos. I go through them regularly, so I like that this is a 12 pack of 0.38mm pens from Uni-ball. All of the pens are black.

The pens put down good, steady ink, but they are scratchy. When I tried the pens on very thin paper, they actually indented the paper. I expect a smoother writing experience with a rollerball pen, I don’t expect to hear the pen tip scratch across the paper.

I’m left-handed, so I always do a smear test. The ink smears very slightly, not bad at all. There’s barely any bleed-through on the average calendar or planner.

Other than the scratchy feel as I write, I’m pleased with these pens. The ultra-micro tips are great for thin, precise lines.

title: A5 notebooks have pre-printed headers
text:
I have the A5 size in this 4 pack of ruled hardcover notebooks from Compera.

The pages are lined, the lining is the same width as college ruled. I do not like the header at the top of each page. The description doesn’t mention this header. Each page has three weather icons (sunny, cloudy, rainy); the days of the week (Mo, Tu, We, Th, Fr, Sa, Sun); and space for the date (__/__/__). I make my own headers for each page based on what I write on that page, so I don’t like having these pre-printed. Every notebook has these page headers.

The notebooks have “Compera” debossed on the lower right front and back covers, and “Compera” is printed on the first inside page.

Each notebook has a ribbon bookmark, elastic closure, and a pen loop in the same color as the cover. I particularly like the pen loop. The inside back cover has a folder.

I did a bleed through test with a Sharpie Pen, and was able to see each letter I wrote on the back of the page. When I tried an ink pen, the bleed through was fainter.

title: Ink color matches barrel color
text:
This pack of 18 retractable gel pens from Loddie Doddie has some nice color variety, though 6 or 7 of the pens are difficult to see on white paper. The ink color matches the color of the pen body, and the colors are pretty accurate.

Each pen has a blob of wax on the top, the wax needs to be removed before the first use. This isn’t unusual for gel pens, but I’ve never seen such big blobs of wax before. The wax was hard to fully remove from the pen tips, some pens still have bits of wax and the ink is getting stuck on the wax.

Most of the pens wrote smoothly, a few skipped. Fortunately for me, the ones with inconsistent ink flow were the lighter colors.

The pens have a nice hand feel. The barrels are about the size of a Sharpie Pen, with a satin finish that isn’t slippery.

title: Inconsistent ink flow
text:
I thought this set of 24 gel pens from Loddie Doddie was just okay. The set has four different styles: neon, pastel, glitter, and metallic. There are 6 pens of each style, and all the pens fit inside the plastic carrying case. The case has a slot for each pen, and latches shut.

I tried all of the pens on white paper. Most of the pens wrote okay, but some did not put down smooth ink. The glitter pens aren’t very glittery and the metallic pens aren’t very metallic. That’s good if you want subtle effects, and not good if you prefer bold glitter and obvious metallic sheen. Four of the pastel pens weren’t visible on white paper, but I expected that. The pastel pens are better suited for dark paper.

The caps close with a click, so you know they are fastened. The caps don’t fit on the back of the pens very well, they pop off.

The writing experience with these pens is just okay. I would only use them for writing, not coloring, since they don’t always put down consistent ink.

title: Good paper thickness
text:
I have the Grey color in this notebook, it’s a really dark grey that almost looks black. Only when I put it next to a black notebook is it apparent the color is grey. The elastic loop is the same color, the ribbon bookmark is a lighter grey.

The notebook has no branding on the cover or inside pages. It has a folder pocket on the inside back cover.

The pages are dotted, which is my personal favorite. It looks the dots are dark grey, so you can see them, but they aren’t super stark. The paper is a good thickness; when I did a bleed through test, I could barely see my writing on the back of the page.

There are different sizes mentioned, so I’ll specify this notebook measure 5⅜ inches across and 8½ inches tall.

title: Smooth gliding, do not pick up hair
text:
These wheels are a huge upgrade on the basic wheels that come on most office chairs. I couldn’t believe the difference when I swapped the wheels -- my chair glides around SO smoothly now. It’s like upgrading from roller skates to roller blades.

On my chair, changing the wheels was very easy. I flipped the chair on its side, pulled out the old wheels, and pushed these into place. My chair is an unbranded gamer-style office chair. The wheels did add about an inch of height to my chair. For me, that was a plus, but it might not be if you have your chair set at its lowest height.

I have plush carpet in my office, so I use a hard plastic mat under my desk. These wheels glide like butter on the mat. They don’t work well on carpet, but no wheel works well on plush carpet.

Maybe best of all, the wheels do not pick up hair. My hair is elbow-length and I shed more than any pet. My old chair wheels were pretty disgusting, all gunked up with hair. I checked these new wheels after two weeks and there’s like, two hairs wrapped around them.

title: Has a pen loop!
text:
I have the Light Blue color in this hardcover notebook; the pictures made it seem like the light blue had a slight metallic sheen. It does not. The color is a flat, matte light blue. The elastic ribbon, pen loop, and ribbon bookmark are the same light blue.

The notebook does not have any branding. The cover and interior pages are plain. The pages are lined, and a bit thin. When I did a bleed through test with a Stabilo 88 fineliner, I could clearly see what I wrote on the back of the page.

Otherwise, I think this notebook is a good deal. I really like that it has a pen loop, and it also has the usual folder inside the back cover.

title: Good diamond painting storage solution
text:
I have the Green color in this diamond painting storage book. All versions are the same, just different color covers. The green is like a seafoam green, translucent but frosted. I can see a hint of the diamond painting right behind it.

This storage book is an easy, practical way to store diamond paintings. The clear sleeve pages can hold canvases up to 40x30cm. Each page can hold two paintings. There are 30 pages, so this book stores up to 60 paintings.

Before trying this storage book, I piled my paintings on top of the bookshelf, it was the only flat place where they wouldn’t get damaged. Okay, but not ideal. This book is much better, and it’s also useful for storing paintings you’re working on! The canvases fit inside even with the protective film on, so it’s a nice way to keep them safe when you aren’t working on them.

title: Color-coded file organizer
text:
In the hope of being more organized the next time April 15 rolls around, I wanted to try a file organizer with several pockets. I stuff all papers and receipts in one folder, but then have to spend a few hours sorting it out before I can even begin to work on my taxes. No fun.

This file organizer is exactly what I needed! The organizer has 7 pockets, each one is a different color which is perfect for me. The pockets can be labeled, you can put a sticker on the tab or slide a label into the tab slot.

Basic labels come with the organizer, but the letters of the alphabet (A, B, C, etc.) are not something I’ll use. But it’s easy enough to make my own, so that’s fine with me. I just like that you don’t have to use stickers, as stickers can be hard to remove.

The organizer closes securely. An elastic loop on the flap stretches over a button on the body of the organizer. If the elastic were to break, you could easily replace it, the elastic isn’t hidden behind a layer of plastic.

I keep saying “organizer” but you actually get 2 organizers, so this is a great deal.

title: Only black marker shows up
text:
I have the 8 X 6 Inches size in this Small Desktop Glass Dry-Erase Whiteboard. I thought that size would fit perfectly under my laptop stand, and it does. The bottom of the whiteboard has a slight angle so you can see what’s written on it; the angle is not adjustable. The bottom also has 4 non-slip rubber feet to keep the whiteboard from moving and scratching the surface.

The box includes 4 dry erase markers: black, green, red, and blue. The marker caps have built-in erasers. There is also a small eraser and a marker tray to attach to the whiteboard.

Unfortunately, black is the only readable color. I used the green marker and could barely see what I wrote. I know the marker works, I tried it on a different whiteboard and could see it just fine.

If natural light -- sunlight shining through the window -- lands on the whiteboard, the text ghosts badly. Ghosting doesn’t happen with artificial lighting, but I’m still disappointed I can only use one color of marker with this whiteboard.

title: Nice cover design for notebook
text:
For me, the notebook is the star of the “Starry Sky” set from Qihonger. I have so many plain black notebooks that I’ve started decorating them with stickers, just to have some variety. The notebook in this set has a gorgeous cover: a holographic silver moon surrounded by small holographic silver dots and gold stars and constellations. The design is on the front cover, spine, and back cover. A+ for the cover design.

The notebook has blank pages, and the page edges are gilt. The set is packaged in bubble wrap and the gift box has cutouts for each item, but there’s a noticeable ding on the gilding on my notebook.

The set includes two rolls of celestial-themed washi tape, a white roll and a black roll. Both rolls of washi tape have holographic foil in their designs. The rolls are 1⅛ inch wide.

The bookmark and gift box don’t impress me very much. The bookmark’s chain is very thin. Personally, I’d prefer the ribbon style bookmark that is common to notebooks like this. The gift box has a foam layer with cutouts for each item, and while the design on the lid matches the notebook, all of the text is Chinese, so I have no idea what anything says.

title: Pages are numbered
text:
I have the Sky Black color in this notebook from JIALINY. The cover is glittery! Red, blue, purple, and green glitter on a black background. The glittery is sparkly but not obnoxious. Depending on the angle and light, the glitter looks matte and not shiny. It’s a nice effect. Also, you can’t feel the glitter, the cover is smooth.

The cover doesn’t have any branding. The first inside page has JIALINY on it. The notebook has an elastic loop closure, two ribbon bookmarks, a pocket on the inside back cover, and a small flap folder on the inside front cover.

The pages are already numbered. The numbers are printed at the bottom of each page, in the middle. There are two table pages before the numbered pages start, but they are on opposite pages. I don’t know about you, but I like my indexes side by side. Here, the first table is on the right side, and then you flip to the next table.

title: Good hardcover notebook
text:
I have the black version of this lined journal notebook from JOYEUX. The cover is matte black, with JOYEUX debossed on the back cover, near the bottom. The ribbon bookmarks are black, and so is the elastic closure strap.

JOYEUX is also printed inside the front and back covers. The inside back cover has a folder. Inside the folder I found a sheet of spine and cover label stickers, which was a nice bonus.

The pages are lined. The paper is 100gsm. I checked for bleed through with a Stabilo 88 fineliner, and could not see my writing on the back of the page.

Overall, this notebook is a great value. I use notebooks like this constantly, so I’m always looking for good ones that aren’t super expensive.

title: 50 colors, not all are translucent
text:
This set of sticky index tabs has a lot of color variety! The set really does include 50 different colors of tabs. There are 3 styles: rectangle, flag, and triangle ends.

The flag and triangle tabs are all bright colors, some are even fluorescent. There are 2 packs of each style, and all of them are translucent. They look opaque in the package, but once you peel one off the stack, they are translucent to see any text under them.

The rectangle tabs have the most color variety, but not all of the colors are translucent. There are some dark blues and purples that are opaque. There are 40 different colors of this style, they are broken down to 10 colors per pack, in 4 packs. The tabs come on clear plastic rulers that can clip into a notebook.

I tried several tabs of each style. One-half of each tab is sticky, so they stayed stuck to the paper. They remove easily without leaving behind any residue. I was able to reuse the tabs a few times, they still stayed where I put them.

title: Non adjustable; rocking foot rest
text:
This under the desk foot rest is not adjustable. The angle and height are fixed. However, unlike other foot rests I’ve tried, this one is usable on both sides.

One side is a normal foot rest, with raised massage beads for each foot. It has non-slip feet, and does not slip on carpet or a chair mat.

Flip the foot rest over, and it rocks. Literally, you can rock your feet on it. The rockers are non-slip, too. I use the rocking side the most and it doesn’t slide on my plastic chair mat. This side also has raised massage beads for each foot.

Both sides are hard plastic, so you could easily clean the foot rest if using it with shoes in an office.

A little assembly is required, to snap the legs onto the foot rest. The box includes 4 screws, to screw the legs on. The legs snapped on so securely -- I had to use my body weigh to push them into place -- that I didn’t use the screws. After a week of use, the legs haven’t budged.

title: Dots off-kilter
text:
I have the Grey Elephants design in this hardcover notebook from SETTINI. It comes with tissue paper wrapped around the cover to protect it from dings.

The elephants are debossed into the front cover and they are cute. Settini is debossed into the back cover and printed on the inside of the front cover. The one ribbon bookmark is grey, so is the elastic closure. The inside back cover has a pocket.

The pages are dotted, which is my personal preference. However, the dots do not line up across the pages. Imagine the journal open flat, the dots should be a straight line from the left page to the right, like - - - - - -. Instead, they might be (left page) _ _ _ - - - (right page). I’ve included a picture to better show what I mean.

For a journal this pricey, I expect better attention to that sort of detail. The cover is cute, but I spend most of my time using the pages inside, and those off-kilter dots are going to annoy me.

title: Angle/height settings don't lock into position, collapses too easily
text:
I like how tall I can make this footrest. I have it set at 10½ inches, which is almost double the height of my other under desk footrests. I have a bad habit of sitting like a pretzel in my office chair, usually because I can’t put my feet high enough. So this higher footrest makes me less likely to pretzel up.

The footrest is also nice when I want to sit back in my office chair with my legs out, almost like I’m reclining.

The height is adjustable, and so is the angle of the footrest portion. This is good and bad. Good because you can probably find a combination that’s comfortable for you. Bad because it’s way too easy to change the angle or height. The settings don’t really “click” into place. Bumping it the wrong way with my foot is enough to make it collapse.

I have a clear, hard plastic mat under my desk, and this footrest has scratched it all up.

If you use the foam cushion on top, it covers the massage beads. The massage beads are just hard plastic bumps.

title: Rose gold is metallic; paper is thin
text:
I have this notebook in the Rose Gold color, which has a metallic sheen on the cover. Depending on how the light hits it, the cover looks pink or champagne gold. It’s pretty and for me, a nice change from all the black notebooks I have.

The cover doesn’t have any branding or logos, which I like. No branding on the inside, either.

The paper is thin, only 80gsm. When I flipped through the pages, I could see the shadows of my fingers behind the pages. I did a bleed through test, writing with a Stabilo 88 fineliner. I could clearly see the words I wrote on the back of the page, so there is bleed through.

I wouldn’t recommend this journal for artwork, not unless you’re using pencils. There would be a lot of bleed through with any types of fineliners or markers because the paper is thin.

title: Fantastic storage idea
text:
I have a ton of storage solutions, but somehow I always need more room on my desk, especially for small items. This 2 pack of storage baskets from Aurynns is a fantastic idea!

The baskets clamp onto the side of your desk, adding a handy spot for light items: cords, pens, etc. The baskets can clamp onto any table, actually. You aren’t limited to the side of the desks. The clamps have soft foam pads on the part that touches the desktop.

The baskets fit desks that have a metal frame underneath, as long as there’s about an inch of desk overhang before the frame starts.

Assembly is easy, screw the clamp to the basket, and repeat for the second. I like that the clamps are removable, this makes storing the baskets themselves much easier if I don’t need them for a while. I can remove the clamps, nest the baskets inside each other, and put the clamps inside the baskets.

title: Good weekly planner
text:
I have the “Blue” version of the 2022-2023 Daily Planner from Thefefan. I liked that cover design, the blue and teal marble print with gold, but I was disappointed that the gold is matte, not shiny. The gold is printed. The blue and teal is a bit less vibrant than pictured. The cover is hard.

The planner has an elastic loop to keep it closed. The first few pages are for reference, such as a section for your name and address, spaces for emergency contacts, friends and family, and a list of holidays.

There are tabs to easily flip to each month. The months start with a monthly spread and then the weekly breakdown. One thing I don’t like is that the weekly breakdowns start on a different day for each month, depending on what day the 1st falls on. For example, September 2022 starts on a Thursday, and then October 2022 starts on a Saturday. I prefer the weeks start with the same day every time.

I do like that Saturday and Sunday each have their own block, rather than sharing a space like other planners I’ve had. Each day has 7 lines of space. For the monthly spreads, the blocks for each day are small, about 1 inch by 1 inch.

The paper feels thin, but I didn’t have a lot of bleed through when testing with a Stabilo 88.

The planner runs from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

title: Small ties are great for thin cables
text:
I have the “36pk Cord Ties” size in this pack of Velco brand cable ties. This set includes three sizes, 12 of each size. The small is 3” long, ¼” wide. The medium is 5” long, ⅜” wide. The large is 7” long and ½” wide.

The round end allows you to get a good grip on the ties, so that you can wrap them as tightly as possible around cords. The velcro holds securely, as I’d expected from VELCRO.

I like the smallest size quite a bit. It can be hard to find cable ties that can wrap to a very small diameter and then securely hold that small size. The small ties are great for skinny cables, headphone wires, etc. I particularly like them for keyboard aviator cables, they hold the desired size of the host side cable and there’s not a lot of bulk from extra tie to spoil the aesthetic of the aviator cable.

title: Small for a refill kit, but good quality bands
text:
This loom band refill kit from Hismo is on the smaller side for a refill kit. The 12 band colors are true to the pictures, and then you get a few accessories. The charms are random, you might not get the ones pictured.

The kit includes a Y-loom and a hook, so you can make a simple design with everything in the box. There are instructions with pictures, which is helpful because the translation isn’t that good.

The bands themselves seem to be quite good. I tried several in every color, none of them broke. I didn’t pull out any broken bands, either.

The container is nice, it latches shut so there’s much less chance of it popping open and spilling.

title: Lots of color variety
text:
I have the 18-Pack option in this set of highlighters from Zosxi. The set is a fantastic value, both for how many you get and the color variety.

The highlighters are double ended, they have a chisel tip and a fine tip. The lids for both ends click closed with an audible snap, so you know the lids are secure. The chisel tip lids have a pen clip.

The highlighters write smoothly, no smearing. I could read the text I highlighted, even when using the dark purple highlighter. For the darker colors, there can be a little bleed through depending on paper thickness. I used the highlighters in an Eccolo notebook, no bleed through. My mom used the highlighters in a word search book and had bleed through with the dark colors, the paper in that book was very thin.

title: Ideal for dark paper but work on white paper
text:
The Zebra Pen Sarasa Clip Decoshine Gel Pens are different than the ones pictured and shown in the video. I received a 9 pack of pastel metallic gel pens. The pens have a solid black body with a metallic grip, push clip, and clicker in the color of the ink.

The pens are ideal for black paper but do show up on white paper. I swatch tested all of them on notebook paper. There is slight bleed through on white paper, and 4 of the colors look very similar.

The pens are fine point, 0.5mm nib, which is nice for everyday writing. A lot of my gel pens are 0.9mm or 1.0mm, so I like the finer tip on the Zebras a lot. I tried all of the pens and none were scratchy, they all put down solid ink.

The ink did not smear when I did a smear test.

title: Quality issues
text:
I’m always on the lookout for pens to use in my bujos. I like colorful pens for making and decorating layouts, and also writing by hand. Most of the time I use Stabilo 88 or other 0.4mm fineliners, but I have fond memories of felt tip pens, so I thought I’d give this set of 24 a try.

Unfortunately, my experience was less than stellar. Out of 24 pens, I had problems with 8 of them. One third of the pack!! Eight of the pens were scratchy or didn’t put down steady ink. Three of that eight had loose lids, the lids literally fell off when I took the pens out of the box. The lids don’t stay on those pens, so no wonder they were dried out; no amount of pressing will make the lids fasten securely.

The barrels are a slick plastic that is slippery in the hand. For the pens with lids that stay on, you can hear an audible click when the lid is fastened.

The pens have a .7mm tip, they are actually comparable to my favored 0.4mm fineliners. The .7mm tip isn’t that much thicker, my eyes can’t tell a huge difference between them. Nearly every single color bled through on notebook paper. On 105gsm paper, the bleed through wasn’t as noticeable.

title: Organizer with 6 compartments plus 1 drawer
text:
I have this organizer in the Grey color option, which is a silvery mesh. I have the Large size, which is approximately 11 inches long, 5½ inches wide, and 5 inches at the tallest point (the back).

The large organizer has 6 compartments plus 1 sliding drawer. The back compartment can hold letter size paper. The width of that compartment is just over 1½ inches, it holds a lot of paperwork!

The sliding drawer comes all the way out of the organizer, which is handy. That makes it easier to clean, and if I have paperclips or small items in the drawer, I can put it on my desk, use what I need, and then put the drawer back.

The organizer has non-slip feet on the bottom, to keep it from sliding all over your desk. The construction is pretty good, it doesn’t have any sharp edges. But my organizer arrived with the side dented in. The dent doesn’t impact using the organizer, but did throw off the alignment of the four small compartments. One is now slightly bigger than the others.

title: Dotted pages
text:
I have the 2 pcs option for this set of dotted bullet journals from Irmanas. I think the value is good; I use notebooks like this every day, for a variety of projects, so I can never have enough of them.

The notebooks don’t have any branding, which I like. I didn’t see any logo on the covers or inside pages.

The notebooks have elastic closure loops, one ribbon bookmark, and an elastic pen loop. The pages are dotted, and when I tested them with a Stabilo 88, I didn’t have any bleed through.

I’m using the notebooks for bullet journals, and for my purpose, they work well. Dotted pages are my personal favorite for making layouts and trackers. I only wish the notebooks had a pocket inside the back cover, I actually do use those folders.

title: Ink did not flow consistently
text:
As of April 2022, this is a pack of 24 Liquid Ink Rolling Ball Stick Pens. There are 12 colors, so you get two of each color. That’s good, because not all of the pens worked. So having a backup pen in the same color turned out to be handy. I also noticed that not all of the pens had the same amount of ink in the barrels.

I swatch tested the pens on notebook paper and also used one in my bujo. On notebook paper, the pens bled to the back of the page. Every single color bled through. In my bujo, which has 120 gsm paper, the darker colors bled through.

Other than the yellow pen, all colors are usable on white paper.

I tried a purple pen first, and it was a joy to write with. I barely had to touch the tip to paper for the ink to flow, and the ink flowed smoothly. I even thought the pens might be nice for coloring. Then I did a swatch test, and not all of the pens were so easy to write with, I had to clean the tips for two and they still didn’t write very well.

title: Tons of color variety
text:
This pack of 25 highlighters from Zosxi has a ton of color variety! I’ve never seen a brown highlighter in my life, but this pack has brown. And grey, and teal, and red, and all the neons… you get the idea. The color options are great. A ton of choices to use for studying, doodling, bujos, or anything else.

The highlighters have a chisel tip and a fine tip. They write smoothly and do not smear. I used a light yellow highlighter over a fineliner marker, and even that didn’t smear. The tip picked up only a hint of the marker’s color.

The caps close with a click, so I know the lids are really on and the markers aren’t going to dry out. The highlighters come in a plastic case you can reuse for storage.

I used the highlighters in my Eccolo notebook and had no bleed through. Even when I tried the darkest colors -- grey and brown -- I couldn’t see any trace of them on the back of the page.

The highlighters are made in China.

title: A good value but inconsistent quality
text:
I like that the Artle Gel Pens come in a plastic case that can be used for storage. The case has a sticker on the back showing all of the different colors and styles. There are 12 glitter pens, 12 pastel pens, 12 neon pens, 12 metallic pens, and 12 glitter neon pens. Each style is in a different section in the case. However, the case is difficult to open; I really thought I was going to break the plastic tabs.

The pens are hard to take out of the case, too. I also thought I was going to break the pens … the barrels and caps are very thin plastic. The cap for one of the pens was broken already; there wasn’t any plastic inside the case so it must have broken at the factory.

The pens actually feel cheap in the hand. The quality is inconsistent. Some of the pens write smoothly, the ink flowing nicely. Other pens scratch across the page, putting down patchy color. The quality issues weren’t grouped by the type of pen, and by that I mean there were good and bad metallic pens, good and bad glitter pens, etc. The ink levels were inconsistent too, with noticeable differences between pens.

However, the value is good for this set. I’ll use these for coloring books or everyday writing where I want some color but quality isn’t super important.

title: Strong enough to hold 3 to 4 pages
text:
I have the “Ocean Patterns” style of the LASOCUHOO Magnetic Bookmarks. The patterns are oceany and marbly, all shades of blue and teal accented with faux gold. The designs cover both sides of the bookmarks.

The bookmarks have a matte finish, which looks quite nice.

The magnets are strong enough to hold 3 to 4 pages. They clamp tightly on 1 page, I just prefer to put them on a few pages to lessen the chance of accidentally tearing a book page if I grabbed the bookmark wrong.

The magnets cover nearly the entire bookmark, leaving only a small spot in the middle, the “hinge.” The edges aren’t all neatly finished, but for what these are and the price, the value is so good I can overlook that.

I can think of a ton of uses for these, as regular bookmarks and also in my bujos. As small and flat as these bookmarks are, they’ll be great to use as tabs for marking sections.

title: Adjustable, can hold up to 3 pens
text:
I have the “Rose Gold” color in this Adjustable Pen Holder. The color is really pretty in person. To my eye, it’s more of a soft, metallic pink than rose gold, but I still like it. The elastic band is a matte pink that nearly matches.

The elastic band is adjustable. The sliding buckle allows adjustment to fit the size of your journal. The sliding buckle does make a little bulk inside the front cover, so the front cover won’t sit flush against the inside pages. All of my journals have the elastic closing band that fits over the front and back covers, I can still use that, the buckle on the pen holder doesn’t interfere.

The pen holder fits 2 to 3 pens depending on the size of the pens. I can fit one Sharpie Pen and one Stabilo 88 in it. The capacity isn’t quite as big as it looks, but it’s very handy for notebooks that don’t have a pen loop. I like that I can move it from notebook to notebook.

The pen holder has “diodrio” debossed on the front, at the bottom.

title: Translucent barrels to see how much ink remaining
text:
In the Assorted pack of 12 gel pens from Penagic, there are 4 shades of red and pink, 3 shades of blue, 2 shades of green, and 1 each of black, orange, and purple. The labels on each pen have the color name, and the insert in the cap matches the ink color, too.

The description mentions brown, but I did not get a brown pen in my assorted color pack.

The pens write smoothly most of the time; I did have a few hitches in ink flow when trying out all of the colors.

I did a smear test and had very light smearing, only when I purposefully ran my finger across a word I just wrote.

I like that the barrels are translucent plastic, so I can see how much ink is left. But I didn’t find the barrels very comfortable to hold. They are round and smooth, almost slippery, so it’s hard to grip the pen to pull the cap off or put it on. The caps close with a click so you know the pen is securely capped.

The pens are made in China.

title: Soft covers, perforated pages
text:
I tested Papercode’s “Thick No-Bleed Paper” by using a Sharpie Pen, in purple. I could clearly see what I wrote on the back of the page, both letters and a colored square. The bleed through isn’t enough to keep from using the back of the page, but I was expecting not to see anything after Papercode’s claim.

The leatherette covers on both notebooks had a very strong scent when I took them out of the plastic. The scent has stayed, and I get a whiff every time I write in a notebook. It’s a chemical-y, plastic-y scent.

The pages are perforated. I can see the benefit, but for me personally, I don’t really like it. I was holding the journal open flat to try and get a picture of the bleed through, and I stressed the perforation on that page.

The branding is unobtrusive, only PAPERCODE debossed onto the back cover. Each notebook has two ribbon bookmarks (one white, one gray), and a folder on the inside back cover.

title: Tiles are random
text:
The letter and emoji tiles are RANDOM. For example, the pictures show 👀 and 😎, both of which I actually wanted.

Instead, I got: 😂, 👌, 👍, 😘, and 💋. (Face with Tears of Joy, OK Hand, Thumbs up, Face Blowing a Kiss, and Kiss Mark.)

For letters: A, E, I O (2), U (2), F (2), G, H, L, V, W, and X.

What the heck am I supposed to spell with those options??

The pencil case and tiles are silicone. They are super flexible, I can bend the pencil case in half. The tiles don’t really snap on, the edges do peel up a bit if you fiddle with them. For kids, I’d tell them to be careful the tiles don’t fall off if they play with the pencil case.

The silicone is the type of silicone that’s a dust and hair magnet, but the pencil case and tiles are washable.

I was able to fit 8 gel pens inside without stretching the case. There’s room for a few more and the extra tiles. Because the silicone is so flexible, you can overstuff the pouch and still have it zip.

The back of the pouch has a band to fit the pouch over the cover of a notebook. I tried putting it on one of my bujos, and the band fits an 5.7 by 8 inch notebook. The silicone band stretches a little, but not too much.

I really like the concept of the WAFF Personalized Pencil Case. With the customizable emoji and letters, it should be fun for kids and adults. But I really feel that WAFF needs to emphasize the emoji and letters are random.

title: Squishy foam
text:
The Carpalax Glide Wrist Rest takes a few days (or longer) to get used to using. The first few days, I wasn’t sure if it was making a difference or not, and to be honest, I’m still not sure. But now that I’ve gotten used to using it, not using the wrist rest feels strange.

The best thing I can say about the wrist rest is that it really does glide with the movements of your mouse hand. I use a desk mat that covers nearly my whole desk, so I never run out of mousing or gliding room. I tried it on the plain top, no mat, and the wrist rest does glide but with a little noise. The bottom of the wrist rest has four smooth “feet” which help it move easily.

The top is made from a soft TPU rubber supposedly mixed with cooling gel. I don’t feel any cooling effect but the wrist rest isn’t bulky and doesn’t cover a lot of your hand/wrist, so it’s not going to overheat you. The top is not quite as firm as I’d like. I have a similar wrist rest and when I compared the two, this one from Office Hub PRO was squishier than my other one (otherwise they are identical). Because this one is softer to start with, I feel like it will compress down after too much use.

This wrist rest isn’t one size fits all, I think they are sized for dudes. I have small hands (women’s size small gloves) and my wrist is also small, the wrist rest is just a bit too big. It’s still usable, but I have to fuss to get the right positioning every time I pick my hand up.

title: Magenta is more of a pink color
text:
I have this Delmas 33 journal in the “Magenta” color option. In person, the magenta is pink. A bright Barbie pink. To my eyes, the shade of pink clashes with the gold edged pages.

The gold edged pages are neat. This is the first time I’ve seen a journal like this with fancy edged pages! I did notice a little shimmer on my fingers if I touched the pages.

The inside pages are black, which is my favorite part. I think black journal pages look so cool.

I tried out my white gel pens, Uniball Signos. The paper seems to soak up more ink than my other black page journals -- I had to trace over each letter at least twice so the color was solid. I also tried white and silver metallic markers, with the same results. The markers write smooth and solid on other types of paper.

The page style is dotted; the dots are a very stark white. Depending on what sort of layouts you like to make, the dots might interfere with designs or sketching. A light gray would be more subtle.

title: Armrests with arc design
text:
The Ergonomic Armrest Pads from BEAUTRIP are shaped differently than other chair armrest pads I’ve tried. I think the “arc contoured design” is one of those things you either like or don’t like. I’m personally not a fan, which is why I’m using the armrests with the curve at my elbow instead of my wrist.

I haven’t noticed any cooling effect from the gel top. The black mesh is very open on the top, so you see the white memory foam and the blue gel. If you’re picky about appearances or aesthetics in your office, these armrests are really noticeable.

The memory foam is thick and dense, it doesn’t squish down.

I’ve had the armrests on my office chair for about a week. I haven’t needed to adjust the velcro straps, they stay in place. The armrests on my chair are 2¼ inches wide.

title: Good bujo notebooks
text:
As far as I’m concerned, there’s no such thing as too many notebooks. I stockpile them like a squirrel. Even better when there are color options! JOTTI has a lot of color options, which is really great if you have a few notebooks going at one time. Being able to color code notebooks by type of project is very helpful for me. The value is good, too.

I picked the Silver color. The color isn’t as metallic as I expected, it looks more like a matte, flat silver to my eyes. Still pretty. The silver color actually shows up best in the logo -- the notebooks have the “jotti” logo debossed on the front cover, back cover, and spine. The logo is also printed inside the front cover. Honestly, I’m not a fan of the logo everywhere.

The paperweight is 100gsm. I normally use a Stabilo 88 or Sharpie Pen in my notebooks. When I tried both, I had slight bleed through. The line spacing is a tad thicker than college ruled; the lines are actually rows of tiny dots that look like lines but aren’t as visually harsh as a solid line would be.

The elastic closure loop, the elastic pen loop, and the ribbon bookmark match the color of the notebooks. On my silver notebooks, all are silver. The back cover has a pocket.

title: Coming unglued out of the box
text:
The picture sort of makes it look like you get two mouse wrist rests, but the picture is showing both sides, top and bottom, of the rest. You get one wrist rest.

The wrist rest is made of two pieces glued together. The slightly soft TPU molded wrist part and a hard sliding base. I know it’s made of two pieces glued together because on mine, the top is separating from the bottom. Glue flaked off as soon as I took it out of the box.

The wrist rest really does glide with the movement of my hand and arm. That’s probably the best part about it for me. I use a large desk mat so I’m always on a mouse pad. I tried it without a mouse pad and it didn’t glide as smoothly.

Does it reduce wrist pain? Eh. It does keep the base of my palm from touching the desk, which makes a straighter line for my wrist.

It took me a few days to acclimate to using the wrist rest. I think it’s better for heavy mouse users. I type most of the time, so I’m constantly taking my hand away from it, and then when I reach for the mouse, I have to adjust the location of the wrist rest again. It’s so lightweight and glides so easily that picking my hand up from it nudges the wrist rest just out of the optimal spot.

I have small hands; women’s size small gloves, and I think this is definitely sized for men’s hands.

title: Cobalt Metallic Burst
text:
I have this Southworth Planner in the Monthly Format style (January 2022 - December 2022) and in the Cobalt Metallic Burst. The cover has a metallic rose gold print and the inside accent colors are various light shades of purple.

The planner has some helpful extras, such as a list of holidays for 2022 and 2023, a yearly overview for 2022, and 11 ruled pages at the back for notes.

The monthly spreads have a section on the side for extra notes or to-dos. Each day box has 7 lines of writing space. The planner lays flat when open.

I did a bleed through test with a purple Sharpie Pen and had some bleed through. I could clearly make out what I wrote on the back of the page. Even a normal ballpoint pen had some bleed through. Not enough to keep me from using the page, but I did want to note it in case you’re someone who likes to color in your planner or use markers.

Before each month is a 2 page “Checking In / This Month” spread. I like the idea of this, but I wish Southworth hadn’t labeled the sections already. The sections include “Get It Started, Quit It, Keep It Up! Wellness, and Gratitude.” I end up crossing out the sections and using the 2 pages for notes instead.

The cover is a soft cover. I used a 2021 version of this planner for the whole year and it held up, but I didn’t take it out of the house, it was my at-home appointment/calendar book.

title: A5, Charcoal
text:
I have this Scribbles That Matter journal in the A5 size, in the Charcoal color. The cover is black, with a black elastic closure and elastic pen loop. It has two ribbon bookmarks, one gray and one black. The dots, page numbers, and index pages look to be printed in gray ink. The inside front cover has a table to make your own symbol key.

The Charcoal A5 journal has 214 numbered dotted pages, 2 blank front pages, 4 index pages, and 2 pen test pages. The paper is 120gsm. I used the included pen on the pen test page, it’s a 0.4mm fineliner. For normal writing, I didn’t really see bleed through. If I colored in a sketch, I had bleed through for spots where I pressed harder with the tip of the fineliner.

The journal includes a white cardboard slipcase, it has a sort of whimsical print with an assortment of different objects. The journal fits inside with a pen in the pen loop. The branding is very unobtrusive, only “STM” on the spine. “STM” is also printed on the inside back cover, on the folder. The “ruler” is junky, it’s just a thin piece of cardstock.

The fineliner marker has a triangle barrel, which I don’t find comfortable to hold if I’m going to write a lot. But I do like the grippy section on the pen cap, it’s a small thing, but so many pen caps are smooth and hard to remove.

Overall, this is a nice bujo notebook, with some thoughtful design elements.

title: Black pages are so cool
text:
I have the STARRY NIGHT journal in the Black color option, in size A5. The black journal has black inside pages. It looks so fancy and cool, I’m going to have to find a special use for it.

The whole presentation is luxurious. The journal comes inside a white cardboard slipcase, the slipcase has a design printed on each side. A ship on waves on one side and two hands with planets on the other side. A white gel pen is included so you can start writing right away, a Uni-ball Signo. The journal has an elastic pen loop and two ribbon bookmarks, one gray, one black. The journal cover is debossed with a cute shooting star print on the top of the front, spine, and back. “Starry Night” is on the front, “STM” on the spine.

There are 4 unnumbered index pages, 150 numbered dotted pages, and 2 pen test pages. When comparing the notebook I got to the pictures, both here and on the STM site, I noticed the inside front pages on my notebook are different. My notebook doesn’t have the pen test pages in the front, nor does it have “the following scribbles belong to / date journal started / date journal ended.”

The Starry Night notebook is super nice, probably the fanciest bullet journal I’ve ever used. The black pages are just 😍 for me. Notebooks with black pages always catch my eye when scrolling layouts on IG, but they look even cooler in person.

title: Line spacing a touch wider than college ruled notebook page
text:
I like that JOTTI offers so many colors! I can’t tell you how many black notebooks I have, and since I usually have a few started at a time, it’s super easy to get them mixed up.

I have the JOTTI notebooks in Silver. The covers have a very slight metallic sheen. Not quite as metallic as I thought they would be, it almost looks like a matte silver. “jotti” is debossed into the front cover, spine, and back of each notebook.

Each notebook has an elastic pen loop and elastic closure, both in silver. The ribbon bookmark is also silver. The inside front cover has “jotti” printed on it and the inside back cover has a pocket.

The paper is 100gsm. I wrote with a blue Sharpie Pen and a dark green Stabilo 88, both 0.4mm nibs. I had slight bleed through with both, but not enough to keep me from using the back of the page.

The line spacing looks to be a touch wider than college ruled. I’ve included a comparison picture with a college ruled notebook.

title: Have slight friction on paper when writing
text:
This pack of 12 rollerball pens is a great value!

The pens feel nice to write with. The ink is dark and goes down smoothly, no skipping or messy drops of ink. I’m left-handed so I always do a smear test. If I drag my finger over something I wrote a second ago, the ink will smear very slightly. But for normal writing, without intentionally trying to smear, I did not have any smearing.

The tips do have a slight drag or friction against paper when writing. It doesn’t interfere with writing, but I kept noticing it.

I used the pens in my Eccolo journal and had almost no bleed through. For normal writing, I had no bleed through. If I scribbled something out or colored in a sketch, then I had very minimal bleed through, but nowhere near enough to keep me from using both sides of a page.

The .35mm tip is thin and crisp, I really like it. I’ve included a comparison picture with the .4mm fineliners I normally use.

The pens are made in China.

title: Adjustable, plastic is cleanable
text:
This foot rest is height adjustable, which is my favorite thing about it. Adjusting the height is done by loosening the knobs on either side, then tightening them again when you have it in the desired position.

I like to have it at the highest height of 7.5 inches at the top, which is the most comfortable for me. But if someone else were to use my desk, they could adjust the height for their comfort.

The knobs hold the legs on, so that’s the only assembly needed. The foot rest can be stored flat when you don’t need it, or if you really wanted to travel with it.

The feet have foam padding that is non-slip on plastic chair mats and also non-slip on carpet. If I push against the foot rest, my chair actually rolls backwards, the foot rest doesn’t move.

I don’t even notice the small bumps on the surface of the foot rest, but I always have socks or slippers on in my office. The whole foot rest is plastic, so it would be easy to clean if you used it with shoes on.

title: Poor quality of materials
text:
Where do I start with this chair?

Assembly is not very easy. The instructions are not clear; they are one page with close-up pictures. Usually when I’m not sure of a step, I can look at the picture and figure out what to do. But these pictures are useless because they are close-ups and don’t show the entire part or entire chair. I had to redo steps more than once because I couldn’t figure out what way a part went on.

I’m sitting in the chair right now and I’m honestly paranoid the back is going to come off. Compared to my other office chairs, the back for this one is held on with one T-bar. The top of the T screws onto the back piece and the bottom of the T slots into the chair seat bottom, with one screw holding it in place. That’s it!!! My other chairs have several screws holding the back piece to the seat.

The footrest is why I wanted this chair. But it’s very difficult to slide in and out. I have to get out of the chair and yank it out, or really push it back underneath the chair. If I lean too far forward in the chair with the footrest out, I feel like I’m going to tip over. The footrest actually hits right below my knees, and I’m not very tall!

The quality of materials is low. I had to vacuum after assembling the chair because so much paint flaked off the different parts! The stitching on the faux leather seat and back is loose in several areas. Not all of the wheels swivel, so I can’t wheel around in the chair. The chassis looks like a kid welded it. There is a flimsy cover piece that hides the messy welding, but the instructions don’t show it, so I didn’t notice until too late. I had to clean foam off the screw holes for the armrests.

The seat feels like a rock, and the back feels like a slab of wood. The “thickened headrest and cushions” are not very thick, I don’t notice a difference between them and the rest of the chair. The thick roll that sits between the seat and back is annoying, it pokes my lower back and I’m stuck with it, it’s not removable.

Overall, I’m not impressed with this chair. It’s not comfortable and the low quality right out of the box is disappointing.

title: Slight bleed through
text:
This 3 pack of PAPERAGE comes well protected. The notebooks come in a medium-weight cardboard box, and then each notebook is wrapped in shrinkwrap. This helped prevent any bending or scuffs during shipping.

The notebooks do not have any external branding. PAPERAGE is printed on the inside front and back cover. Each notebook has one black ribbon bookmark. The back cover has a folder pocket, inside the pocket is a small sticker pack with 3 block stickers and 3 spine stickers. This was a nice little bonus to use for labeling the notebooks.

The notebooks do not have a pen loop.

The dots are faint, better viewed up close. If I hold the notebook a foot away from my face, I can barely see them. When I’m writing in the notebooks or making a tracker or bujo layout, I can see the dots just fine.

The paper is 100 gsm thick. I tested a Sharpie Pen, a Stabilo 88, and a PAPERAGE 0.4mm fineliner pen. On the back of each page, I could see the letters and the scrawl of color for each pen. Not enough bleed through that it would prevent me from writing on the front and back of a page, but it was noticeable.

title: Comparable to other similiar notebooks; good option
text:
I have a stockpile of Eccolo Graph notebooks, so I couldn’t help but mentally compare them to the HULYTRAAT Classic Grid Notebooks. In the HULYTRAAT notebooks, the grid is slightly larger and a lighter shade of grey.

I use Sharpie Pens and Stabilo 88 fineliners for my bujos and writing. I had very minimal bleed-through with both, I really had to look to see it.

The HULYTRAAT notebooks do have less pages than other notebooks I’ve used in the past -- only 160 pages. I noticed the lesser number when I sat down to number the pages to use for a bujo. I kept 4 blank index pages, which left me with 154 pages to use.

The notebooks look and feel nice. HULYTRAAT is debossed on the outside of the back cover, it’s practically invisible -- no obvious logo. The construction is sturdy. The back cover has a pocket and there is one ribbon bookmark (grey). I do wish there was a pen loop, I find myself missing it.

title: Lining is nearly identical to college ruled notebook paper
text:
I put a generic college ruled notebook next to the HULYTRAAT Classic Lined Notebook. The spacing between the lines is virtually identical. I couldn’t quite tell how wide the spacing would be from the pictures or measurements, so I wanted to give a better mental picture.

The top line of each page is slightly wider, if you like to make a header or title. The last line of each page is a full space.

The inside pages have a sort of … book scent to them. It’s not strong, but I do notice it whenever I write in the notebooks.

I use Stabilo 88s and Sharpie Pens for writing, I had very minimal bleed-through. Nowhere near enough to keep me from using both sides of the page. Speaking of pages, these notebooks have less pages than my comparable notebooks. I didn’t think much of it until I started numbering pages, and only had 154 after leaving a few unnumbered for my index.

I like these notebooks. They are sturdy and well-constructed. They don’t look like random notebooks, y’know? HULYTRAAT is indented on the back cover, otherwise the only branding is on the inside cover. The covers are smooth, not rubbery like my Eccolo journals. There is one grey ribbon bookmark.

title: Nice bujo notebooks
text:
For the past few years I’ve been using Eccolo notebooks for my bujo, I picked up a bunch when a big box store when out of business. I’ve used almost all of them, so it’s time to look for a new bujo notebook.

I like the dotted grid in the HULYTRAAT notebooks. The dots are light grey, very subtle. If I hold the notebook away from my face, I can barely see them. But the dots are there when I need them, a good guide for making layouts and trackers, and making sure I’m writing reasonably straight.

I typically use Stabilo 88’s or Sharpie Pens, I tried both to test the bleed through. My Stabilo is pine green, my Sharpie Pen is blue, and I had minimal bleed-through with both. Not enough to keep me from using the back of the page.
