The notebooks do have a scent to them, I noticed it every time I wrote in one. It’s kind of like a library book smell. I’m hoping that once the notebooks air out a little, I won’t notice it as much.

I like how the cover feels when I touch it. Smooth, without the slightly rubbery, grabby feeling my Eccolo notebooks have sometimes. The notebooks have one grey bookmark ribbon and one pocket on the inside back cover.

The branding is unobtrusive -- HULYTRAAT is imprinted on the back cover, in black.

title: Comparable to Stabilo 88s
text:
Stabilo 88s are my preferred bujo pen, I like the 0.4mm nib. The Paperage pens have the same nib size, 0.4mm, so I couldn’t help but make a mental comparison between them and the Stabilos.

The barrel is about the same size, though it does feel a little different in hand because it’s a round barrel. The caps fit securely, with an audible click.

Writing feels the same with both pens, the ink flow is smooth and steady. I’m a leftie so I did a smear test and had very light smearing on the last letter, if I intentionally dragged a finger over it to test.

The set includes 18 pens. I did a swatch test of all the colors on a white notebook page, and 3 to 5 colors are very, very light on white paper. Yellow, salmon, orange, light green, and fluorescent yellow are hard to see. The set doesn’t have names or identifying numbers that I can see, so those are my made-up names. Either way, a few of the colors are very light.

A few of the colors also had a noticeable scent to them.

title: Medium Pile Carpet -- this mat is amazing!
text:
I have the Oculus Office Chair Mat for medium pile carpet. It is amazing!!

Before this, I was using a flimsy mat to protect the carpet, one of those frosted plastic ones with spikes on the bottom. I had to adjust the mat multiple times a day, it would shift on the carpet and get stuck against the legs of my desk, making a big ridge I tripped over. The mat also had ruts from my chair, and if my chair ran off the edge, I would have to pick my chair up because the wheels got stuck underneath the mat. So annoying!

I’ve had none of those problems when using the Oculus mat. No ruts, no ridges, no edges getting stuck under the chair wheels. Seriously. I put it underneath my desk and chair and I don’t even know it’s there -- it just works.

Rolling my chair back and forth now is so easy. No need to push off my desk to move over the ruts and no need to adjust the mat five times a day.

The mat ships flat, and both sides have a protective film to protect it during transit. Removing the film can be a little tricky, I used a razor knife to carefully peel up an edge.

The mat is clear, completely transparent. It’s visible on the carpet but it’s not an eyesore like the frosted mats.

title: Seasons version
text:
I have the “Seasons” Large Desk Calendar from Cranbury. The borders around each month are themed, red and blue stars for July, snowflakes for January, and so on.

The calendar includes two identical sticker sheets, with stickers for things like “Payday” and “Gym.” The stickers are small enough to leave plenty of room to write in the day blocks.

The blocks are nice and big. They measure nearly 3 inches wide and 2¼ inches tall. Each box includes 4 lines, plus blank space next to the date.

The day blocks also show the day number of the year, as well as the days left. Example: July 31: 212/153.

At the bottom of each page are mini calendars for the whole year.

I wrote on the calendar using a regular Sharpie marker. There was no bleed through to the next calendar page.

title: Heavy, well-made lap desk
text:
I wouldn’t consider this lap desk from Kavalan to be super lightweight -- it weighs almost three pounds. I notice the weight every time I pick it up. The lap desk is solid and well-constructed, but it is heavier than other lap desks I’ve used before.

The two bolster cushions underneath the lap desk provide adequate cushioning for your lap while allowing air to circulate. The bolster cushions are stuffed with foam beads.

The wrist rest on top is soft, it feels like it's made from foam. The wrist rest is one inch tall, so it does keep a laptop from sliding off, but puts my hands at a downward angle. If I have to type a lot, that gets uncomfortable.

The distance between the wrist rest and the pen and phone slot is 8¼ inches. I have a 13-inch MacBook Pro, and the hinge edge of my laptop hits the pen slot. The pen slot is raised, it’s not flush with the surface of the lap desk, so my laptop sits on the top of that slot.

The construction is really nice. Other lap desks I’ve used in the past had a wrapped paper coating on the top to mimic a wood texture. On this lap desk, the plastic top has the white oak texture. The edges are neat, the cushions are well sewn, no loose threads or rough spots.

title: Add comfort to office chair
text:
I’ve had the LargeLeaf Extra Thick Cushions on my chair armrests for about a week. I sit in that chair about 4-5 hours a day, so I’d approximate that I’ve used the armrests for about 35 hours so far. I can see a slight slope in the memory foam from where my arms rest. So I’m unsure how long the cushions will stay extra thick.

That said, the cushions have significantly increased the comfort of my chair. My elbows aren’t sore at the end of the day anymore. I also noticed the added height of the cushion keeps my mouse arm in better alignment.

I have a gaming style office chair, with armrests that are about 3½ inches wide. The LargeLeaf cushions fit the armrests without any overhang. They haven’t budged in the week I’ve had them on my chair. Each armrest has two velcro straps that are 11½ inches long. The straps are long enough to accommodate a lot of chair styles, but that means there’s a lot of extra strap hanging off the cushions. I tucked the extra length between the armrest and bottom of the cushion.

title: Size is not accurate
text:
I have the “RGB Mat-L” color option in the Katoggy Gaming Mouse Pad. This option has an LED border with 14 lighting modes.

The mouse pad measures 10 inches by 14 inches. This is a different size than the description, which says “5x12 inches.” At 10x14, the mouse pad is in-between a traditional pad and a desk mat, which makes it an awkward size on my desk.

The LED light is powered by USB, a braided micro USB cable is included. To cycle through the colors and modes, you press the button at the top. The small instruction sheet lists the colors and modes and is accurate. There are 14 options, though one is lights off so I’d say it’s more like 13 options, 7 static colors and 6 lighting modes (wave, flash, breathing).

I don’t like that the company’s name is printed on the power/control panel, but that’s a minor annoyance.

The surface of the mouse pad is waterproof. I dropped water on it to test and the water beaded up. Because the mouse pad is an awkward size for how my desk is set up, I’m using it as a coaster so the waterproof surface is good for me.

title: Only one lead, not three
text:
The BIC PrevaGuard Mechanical Pencils are standard #2 mechanical pencils. The lead is 0.7mm and writes smoothly.

The description says “includes three 0.7 mm #2 graphite leads” but each pencil has ONE lead in it. I checked all of them.

The pencils are not easily refillable. The eraser comes off as expected for a mechanical pencil, but the barrel of the pencil is closed. I took a picture, but in case it isn’t visible, you can’t stick a new lead into the back of the pencil. A new lead would have to be fed into the writing tip, which would be a pain.

The PrevaGuard line “contains built in protection to suppress bacteria growth.” Notably, this agent protects only the body of the pencil -- it doesn’t protect the user.

title: PrevaGuard only protects the pen
text:
This 12 pack of pens from BIC performs exactly as expected. The pens write smoothly, no ink splotches or blobs or anything like that.

The caps fit tightly, a plus for me. I try to carry my own pen everywhere now, and keep backups in my truck and bag. So I prefer having the cap for less chance of leaking.

The barrel is slick and a little slippery in my hand.

I feel like “PrevaGuard” is a tad deceptive. The front of the box says: “Pen contains built in protection to suppress bacteria growth.” But on the bottom, in small print: “This product does not protect users or others from disease causing bacteria, viruses or germs.”

title: Thick paper, should stand up to a year of use
text:
I like the Southworth Academic Planner quite a bit. The color is described as “cobalt metallic burst” but to my eye, it’s more of a bluey purple, or blurple. The colors used for the month tabs and accents inside the planner vary between blue and purple to me, depending on the light. Whatever the color really is -- I like it, and the accent colors aren’t too dark. I can clearly read whatever I write in the bluey purple areas.

The planner has monthly and weekly spreads. The weekly spreads are horizontal, with Saturday and Sunday sharing a row. Each weekly spread has space at the bottom for to-dos, with pre-printed ticky boxes.

A monthly check-in spread is included before the start of each new month. The check-ins include spots for: wellness, gratitude, get it started, quit it, keep it up, and notes. I personally wish the section titles were left blank, as those won’t apply to everyone. But I can cross out the printed titles and write my own.

The paper is thick. I tried bleed through tests with a Sharpie Pen, a Stabilo Point 88 Pen, and a Crayola Gel Pen. On rows that had the bluey purple printing, there was no bleed through. On rows that were plain white, there was very faint bleed through.

Overall, I think this is a good planner and will last for the year. The spiral actually got a little bent in shipping (it shipped in a bubble mailer) but I was able to straighten it, so I feel confident that I can toss this planner in a bag or backpack and have it withstand normal daily wear and tear.

title: Supports most of one's back
text:
I’ve tried several different lumbar support pillows for my office chair. Most are the rectangle variety, which just aren’t comfortable and support only one small area of my back.

This pillow from Samflykaka is different in that it covers nearly my whole back, from lower shoulders to lower back. It has two stretchy, adjustable straps so that you can situate the cushion where you want it. I have some cutouts on the back of my office chair that makes it easier for me to position the cushion exactly where I want it -- I can thread the straps through those cutouts.
But the straps should work fine with most office chairs.

The foam is a little soft for me, and the cushion thins out and narrows at the top, by my shoulders. I had to add a second pillow for my shoulders and neck, because the top of the Samflykaka is not supportive.

But I do like the supportive nodes in the lower back area of the cushion. They sort of stick out from the cushion -- not in an uncomfortable way! -- and cradle either side of the spine.

Overall, this is a good lumbar cushion. It has helped make sitting at my desk more comfortable.

title: Has 11 light options
text:
The Buibong mouse pad actually has 11 light options: red, green, blue, purple, cyan, yellow, white, multi slow speed, multi fast speed, multi medium speed, and off.

The instructions and order of the colors is actually printed on the back of the spot where the power cable plugs in.

All light changes are controlled by a single button. The description says to press the button twice to change the brightness, but every single time I tried to do that, all I ended up doing was changing the color. I couldn’t adjust the brightness of the light at all.

But that’s okay for me -- the light is bright enough as is, visible day or night.

The mouse pad functions well as a mouse pad, I’m a big fan of big ones like this. Plenty of room for my mouse, laptop, and even big enough that I can use a corner as a coaster.

The mouse pad has a very strong rubber smell when removed from the box. I’m hoping the smell fades after it sits out for a few days.

title: Smooth pens, have a thick barrel
text:
This assorted 12 pack of Amazon Basics Rollerball Pens includes 3 of each color: red, blue, green, and black. The pen tip is 0.5mm.

The pens write smoothly, and the ink flows well. I’m left-handed, so I tried to see if the ink would smear as I wrote -- no smearing.

I tried the pens in my Eccolo bujo, there was a little bleed through. I could clearly see the words I wrote, in each color of ink.

The only thing I don’t like is how thick the body of the pen is. For comparison, the pens are thicker than Sharpie Pens. I noticed the thicker barrel as soon as I took the pens out of the box, and also while writing with them.

title: Good whiteboard, bad wall hanger design
text:
I have the Ivory Black version of the AmazeFan Whiteboard. The total size of the whiteboard is 22.5 inches wide by 17.5 inches tall. When folded together, the total thickness of the whiteboard is 1.5 inches.

The usable whiteboard space is 21 inches wide by 16 inches tall.

The whiteboard surface works great. Dry erase markers write smoothly and erase cleanly. I tested with a different brand of markers and a different eraser too, with the same good results for writing and erasing.

The eraser cannot be stored inside the whiteboard, but it has a magnet so it can stick on the surface. Other brands of markers will likely be too thick to be stored inside, too.

There is no latch to keep the whiteboard closed when it is flat.

I do NOT like the wall hangers on the top and one side of the whiteboard. The wall hangers are small pieces of metal, with a triangle top, that slide along the frame. I noticed that the wall hangers get stuck between the hinge and frame, so that the hinge sticks out. I think this is dangerous, as kids could get their fingers or clothing stuck on the metal.

title: Nice colors, erasers aren't durable
text:
The XSG Magnetic Dry Erase Markers are nice! This pack of twelve is a great value and includes some nice colors.

Colors: red, orange, yellow, grass green, green, royal blue, blue, deep purple, magenta, brown, dark brown, and black.

The markers have 1-2mm fine tips, which I prefer for writing on my whiteboard. Some of the colors, such as orange, were closer to 2mm while others, like deep purple, were in the 1mm range.

The markers write and erase cleanly. They are low odor, and again, I noticed some colors had more of an odor than others. The odors weren’t annoying and didn’t last long.

My main complaint with the markers is the design of the eraser. The erasers are foam heads on the tip of the cap. When opening the markers you cannot hold the eraser bit or the foam will tear. I almost ripped an eraser off, I was holding the cap with my index and middle fingers, and had my middle finger around the eraser.

The back of the box says the markers conform to ASTM D4236. The markers are made in China.

title: Surface sticker not applied well
text:
The Knodel Lap Desk is a bit smaller in person than I was expecting. The measurements (13.4 inches by 9.4 inches) are accurate, but it still looks small. I was planning on using with my 13 inch MacBook Pro; the lap desk barely fits a 13 inch laptop. If you have a bigger laptop, this lap desk will be too small.

The amount of stuffing on the underside of the lap desk is quite generous. The tag doesn’t say what the stuffing is, but I’m assuming it’s some form of foam beads, based on what I feel. The padded portion is about 1.5 - 2 inches deep, which is nice. I know from a similar style of lap desk that the padded portion will eventually compress with use.

I like that the lap desk has a ledge to keep whatever is on top from sliding off. The elastic band on the upper left corner is handy too, to help keep a notebook open.

The surface of the lap desk is some kind of sticker. On the Black color option, the sticker has a slight woodlike texture. But the wrapping around the corners is not very neat. The corners are bumpy and unsightly.

title: Lightweight, stays in place while using
text:
I’ve tried so many makeshift options for a foot rest under my desk. A crate. A monitor stand. Stacks of books. Stuffed animals. Let’s just say that none of them really worked, or were comfortable.

This foot rest from Fikowo is amazing. As soon as I put it under my desk and tried it out, I was actually comfortable!

I have tried the foot rest both ways: flat and upside down so that I can have a little movement by rocking my feet.

I have tried the foot rest on carpet and on a plastic chair mat. It stays in place on both surfaces, even though it’s very lightweight.

The foot rest comes with two covers, a mesh one and a velvety one. I didn’t want to lose one of the covers, so I tried putting both on, the velvety one over the mesh and they fit. The covers are machine washable and dryable.

title: Muted colors but works well
text:
I have the “Forest” color option in the iCasso Desk Mat. I know the image is of a misty forest, but the colors are still more muted than I expected. Based on the product photos, I expected the green trees to be brighter, and the background trees to not practically fade into light gray top.

Muted appearance aside, I like the desk mat. I never liked mouse pads, but I like these because they are so big and cover almost the entire top of my desk. I don’t have to worry about the mouse running off a small square. The desk mat doubles as a coaster and desk protector. The underside is grippy, like a normal mouse pad, and stays in place.

The mat is thin, so there’s not a hugely noticeable bump between it and the edge of the desk. It is thinner than my name brand gaming mouse pads, but I don’t notice a difference in performance.

The mat does have a strong rubbery/plastic scent when removed from the packaging. I had to let mine air out for a few days before I could use it.

title: Makes a big difference
text:
The Fuzaws Foot Rest has made my time at a desk more comfortable. Before using it, I tried random items I found around the house, hoping something would work as a foot rest. Nope.

This is one of those things I didn’t know I needed until I tried it. A stack of books is no comparison to this foot rest. My feet always dangled, so I would sit cross-legged in my chair, and then I’d be sore from scrunching up all day, or my legs would be tired from my feet dangling.

Literally the second I tried this foot rest out, I noticed a difference in comfort. It’s the right height and firmness.

The foot rest works on carpet and plastic chair mats. It has a grippy texture on the bottom, so even though it’s lightweight, it stays in place pretty well. It’s so lightweight I can easily move it with my feet if needed.

The foot rest includes 2 covers, a mesh one and a plush velvet one. Both covers are machine washable and did not shrink in the dryer. Both covers fit on the foot rest at the same time, so I’m “storing” the mesh one underneath the velvet one.

title: Messy construction
text:
The Knodel Lap Desk is an okay lap desk. It works for its intended purpose but has some unsightly construction issues.

When I took the lap desk out of its box, I noticed strings of hot glue still sticking to the surface. I assume the ledge to prevent a laptop from sliding off is hot glued to the surface. I can see glue sticking out from underneath the bit of plastic.

I saw a few other splotches of glue on the surface, too. And the pen slot has white spots on the rounded edges, like the plastic was distressed. So does the plastic ledge.

Do these things impact my use of the lap desk? Well, they bother me visually, and the glue bugs me because I can feel it. The construction issues do make me wonder how long the lap desk will hold up.

The lap desk does fit a 13 inch laptop with about 2 inches to spare on either side. There’s not enough room to use a mouse on it. The lap desk is 16⅞ inches across and 12⅞ inches long on each of the curved sections. It is 12 inches long in the middle.

The lap desk was made in China. I did not notice any smells when removing it from the box.

title: Lumbar cushion is not as good as seat cushion
text:
I’ve tried a few seat cushions in this U-shaped style, hoping to make sitting at a desk for long periods of time more comfortable. This cushion from DREAM ART is the best one I’ve tried. The memory foam is dense and doesn’t shrink down to nothing when I sit in it. The cushion itself is heavy, maybe 2-3 pounds.

The seat cushion actually gives me about an inch of extra height in my desk chair. The cover is removable for washing, with a soft plush top and a grippy bottom to help keep it in place in the chair.

The lumbar cushion is not as good. The one I received only has one strap instead of the two pictured. The strap is in the middle of the cushion.

I have a gamer style chair in one office, so I was able to weave the strap through openings on the chair to get it to mostly stay where I want the cushion. On a normal office chair, the cushion tends to slide down. If your chair has a curved back, this cushion is even harder to keep in place, since the back of it is flat.

The back cushion is not as supportive or firm as I would like, so it’s less useful. Its cover is also removable.

title: Glitter cover can be reused on same size journal
text:
I’ve spent the last few minutes playing with the glitter on the Yoobi Journal with Liquid Glitter Cover, so I’d say this is a pretty good idea. Moving the glitter about or tilting the journal this way and that to make it float is soothing when my brain doesn’t want to work. It’s also a good way to procrastinate without getting too far away from the notebook.

The glitter cover is actually removable and can be transferred to another journal. I tried putting it on an Eccolo journal that is the same size as the Yoobi and it fit. Just be careful if you do take the cover off, as the plastic isn’t the most robust.

The cover on my journal actually came with a loose bit of plastic on the end. The cover is still sealed, so the liquid glitter hasn’t leaked out, but I can’t tell if the plastic is a stray bit that didn’t get trimmed or if it ripped before getting to me.

The journal is as expected, a hardcover journal with college-ruled pages. The covers do not have any pockets like other similar journals I have. It has a matching aqua ribbon bookmark.

title: A nice step up from a basic yearly planner
text:
The Southworth 2021 Yearly Planner is a nice step up from a basic yearly planner. The planner has monthly spreads and a check-in/goal spot for each month. Extras include a list of 2021 & 2022 holidays, a yearly overview for 2021 & 2022, and 11 blank ruled pages.

I like the idea of the monthly check-ins/goals, but I don’t like that Southworth picked sections for me. The pre-labeled sections are Wellness and Gratitude for the preceding month. For the upcoming month, the sections are Get It Started, Quit It, and Keep It Up. I would prefer to note or journal what I want to remember or keep track of, but I am coming from a bujo perspective, so I can see how others might find it useful.

The monthly spreads include a lined section on the side, useful for quick notes or to-dos. The boxes for the days of the month are 7 lines long, which gives lots of room to put down appointments.

I wrote with a black Sharpie Pen (what I’m most likely to use in the planner) to test bleed through. I could just make out what I wrote, but the bleed through wouldn’t keep me from using the page. Thicker markers or brush pens will bleed through more.

I’m not sure how long the cover will hold up if you plan to take the calendar on the go with you. It is a soft cover.

Overall, I like the Southworth Planner. The green and pink color scheme provides a nice pop without getting in the way visually, and the fonts for headings and holidays are readable.

title: A lot of bleed through
text:
The 12 pack of AmazonBasics Retractable Permanent Markers includes orange (1), aqua (1), pink (1), purple (1), blue (2), green (2), red (2), and black (2).

The clicky button on top pushes out the marker tip, and the clip on the barrel retracts the marker tip. The marker tip doesn’t stay out unless the clip is flush against the barrel. So I *think* this will prevent the pen from writing if it’s clipped in a pocket or purse.

The pen tip is thick. The nib is at least 1.0mm.

The markers don’t smear. I tried to smear the ink as soon as I finished writing “smear” and there was no smearing at all.

There is a lot of bleed through when using these. I did a test page in an Eccolo notebook. I could clearly read every single letter I wrote, and there were pink, blue, purple, and green dots on the next page.

title: Good for bujo
text:
I have the Misulove 10 Size set. The pens in that set have silver bodies and lids.

I’m using the pens in my bujo, for writing and making a few lines, so that’s my perspective when it comes to reviewing them. I wanted a set of black with varying nib sizes to make trackers. For my purpose, the pens work well.

The nib sizes are only on the caps. I wish the sizes were also listed on the bodies of the pens. The bodies are thick. For a comparison, the Misulove pens have thicker bodies than a Sharpie Pen.

I tried the pens in a generic pocket notebook. All of the pens have bleed through -- the thicker the nib, the more bleed through. The brush pen had the most bleed through.

I’m a leftie so I tried to smear the ink as I wrote. I used the 1.0mm size to test and had very little smearing. I sniffed the page after I wrote and didn’t notice any strong ink smells.

title: Great clips, magnets weak
text:
The kizmos Magnetic Plastic Bag Clips just work! I always need more chip clips since I usually manage to break one every few months. So a bag of 15 clips is a great value for me. I’ve already used a bunch, on chip and cereal bags. The clips make a tight seal; my food hasn’t gone stale.

I also have to admit, I like the bright colors in this set. I’m a magpie for anything translucent, so I like all of the colors. The clips come in a mesh bag, so I did wash with soap and water before using.

My one complaint is the magnets. They aren’t strong. If I put a clip on my refrigerator, the clip slides right down the door.

title: Had it 2 days and ripping already
text:
This lap desk from QIELIZI is just okay. As of September 2020, the description mentions “a perfectly sized compartment for a smartphone, tablet and pencils or pens,” but the top of the lap desk is flat. There is no compartment.

There is no anti-slip ledge to keep a computer from sliding right off if you tilt the lap desk too much.

The lap desk has a black binding that attaches the flat top to the cushiony section. On mine, that binding is already ripping and I’ve had the lap desk for 2 days. In that time, I’ve used it for maybe 2 hours total. The binding is ripping right at the part where my hands sit, so it’s extra annoying beyond the durability concerns.

title: Good big mouse pad
text:
I like this mouse pad from Xinmade quite a bit. I never used to like mouse pads since I always ran off the edges of them, but since trying out big mouse pads, I’ve become a convert.

This mouse pad measures 31.5 inches by 12 inches. That’s long enough to put my laptop on it, use one end for a coaster, and still have plenty of room for my mouse.

It has the usual rubber backing to keep it from sliding on the top of my desk. The edges are all finished; the hem is smooth.

I’ve taken off one star because I have a construction issue on the right side of my mouse pad. The edge has a sharp spot where the rubber is ripping, like it got caught on a needle. The spot doesn’t interfere with me using the mouse pad, but I’m worried it could become a bigger hole.

The mouse pad did smell like rubber when I took it out of the box. I’ve had it sitting out for a week in the open air and it still has a slight rubbery scent.

title: Not very padded, actually 9.5 x 11 inches
text:
The actual dimension of the Limnuo Bubble Mailers is 9.5 inches by 11 inches. I put the flap down where it would be sealed with the adhesive strip to get the height measurement.

The envelopes are not very padded. I would use them to mail books or small, unbreakable objects. I wouldn’t use them for anything fragile or too big.

I do like the bright teal color of the envelopes. It stands out and is fun. My address labels stick just fine, and the envelopes seal well. I always add tape anyway, because I’m paranoid.

I put a 750 page paperback in an envelope, to test how much it could hold. The book (HP 7) measures 5¼ inches by 7¾ inches, and is 1¾ inches deep. The envelope barely closes.

The usage of these mailers depends highly on what you need to mail. As I mentioned above, books would be okay, but anything fragile could possibly break since there isn’t a lot of protection.

title: Wing lids are so-so
text:
The IRIS USA Letter and Legal Size Wing Lid File Box are great for storing old tax returns. Really, they’re good for storing any sort of files or paperwork, or anything else you might need to store, up to 25 pounds.

The Pearl color option is a milky white that is somewhat transparent. I can mostly see what’s inside a bin. For example, if I put a box inside, I can make out the color of the box but maybe not all of the text.

I don’t really like the wing lids. The style is handy, since each side is connected to the box. But the lids don’t close securely. The tabs just sort of fit together and provide a decent closure. I expect a lid to snap into place to signal a tight closure. But on these boxes, the lids pouf up a bit in the middle where the tabs meet, and I feel like dust will get into the boxes.

The boxes do stack. The lids have indented areas to fit the feet of the box on top.

title: Love the extended size!
text:
I love this mouse pad! I quit using a normal size mouse pad years ago because I always ran off the sides of it.

So I really like that the iCasso Extended Gaming Mouse Pad covers almost the entire top of my desk. I don’t have to worry about running off the sides anymore, my laptop doesn’t slide around, and I don’t have to use a coaster for my water cup anymore.

I’ve been using it for about two weeks, and I can’t imagine going back to not using it. The big mouse pad is just one of those things I didn’t know I needed.

The mouse pad doesn’t slip or slide on the desktop. It’s fairly thin, which I personally like. I don’t like to feel the edge between desk and mouse pad. The edges are soft and finished. The bottom is the usual rubbery mouse pad back.

I have the Tea Rose color, which has a gray background with white and pink flowers. I’m not the biggest fan of flowery stuff, but I actually like this. The lighter colors help me find stuff on my desk in dim light!

title: Not really heavy duty, but does hold well
text:
Would I call the KingTac Clear Packing Tape a heavy duty tape? Not necessarily. The tape “feels” thin when putting it on cardboard, and by that, I mean I can’t really feel the ridge between tape edge and the cardboard.

If I compare the KingTac tape to a roll of 3M heavy duty tape, the KingTac tape is thinner by sight and feel.

The tape does cut easily with a pair of scissors.

The description says the tape is 1.9 mil thick, while a product photo shows the tape as 2.7 mil thick. I’d definitely lean towards 1.9 mil thick. Though I can’t measure for sure, since one mil is a thousandth of an inch.

I used the KingTac tape to put some cardboard boxes together. The tape does hold securely, the edges don’t lift, and it seems pretty clear on the box.

Now, I’m always paranoid when I ship something and over tape. The KingTac tape is a good value for me that way, since I’m getting over 1,300 yards for a reasonable amount.

title: AmazonBasics Flex Style Correction Tape Applicators, 6 Pack
text:
I can’t help but wonder if I received a bad batch of the AmazonBasics Flex Style Correction Tape Applicators. Out of six, four have tape that already came off the plastic, or leave streaky, messy cover ups.

I’ve used similar name brand correction tape before, and have generally had good experiences when trying AmazonBasics versions of name brand items. But these … are not a good experience. I tried hard pressure, light pressure, careful alignment of the applicator -- everything I could think of, and the correction tape is still a mess when applied.

As I said, out of the six in the box, four did not do the job, so even though this seemed like a great value, it turned out to not be one for me.

title: AmazonBasics Fineliner Pens, 24 Pack
text:
I recently discovered the Stabilo Point 88 Fineliner pens and love them for my bujo and writing by hand. The AmazonBasics Fineliner Pens are almost identical to the Stabilo pens, down to the shape of the pen shaft.

But in my opinion, the pack falls short in color options. Out of 24 pens, 11 are a shade of pink or purple! That’s almost half!

Other colors include blue (2, light and dark), teal (3), green (2), brown (1), orange (1), red (1), yellow (1), gray (1), black (1).

The light blue, gray, and one of the light pinks are difficult to see on white paper.

The pens don’t bleed through on my Eccolo journal. Depending on the shade/how hard I press, I can see a bit of color, but it wouldn’t keep me from using that page.

title: Desktop Printer Stand
text:
Quality wise, the IPARTS EXPERT Desktop Printer Stand didn’t score well for me. One of the metal sides has a piece of metal stuck inside it, so it makes a bell-like noise every time I move it. The other metal side had a rough piece of metal hanging off. The bars on the metal sides aren’t flush, they have gaps and nicks on the metal.

The wooden shelves aren’t flush with the metal sides, either, and also had some nicks despite being packed in styrofoam. The screws for the shelves didn’t sink in straight, so I worried they would pop through the particle board. Luckily that didn’t happen, but I still worried.

The feet (wheels are also provided) also don’t screw in straight. I ended up not using the feet or the wheels because I wanted the unit to be balanced, not teetering. I advise being careful when putting the feet in, since two of the feet had sharp edges and nearly cut my fingers.

For assembly, some of the parts were mislabeled. The two particle board parts, 1 and 3 in the instructions, were swapped, so it took me a minute to figure out that something was wrong when I started piecing it together.

Without the feet or wheels, the stand is only 11” tall.

title: Sharpie S-Gel Pens
text:
Sharpie Pens are my favorite for my bujo, but sometimes I want a pen with a finer tip than is available in the Pens. I tried the new Sharpie S-Gel Pens, with the Fine tip, which is 0.5mm.

I’m left-handed; the S-Gel Pens smear if I’m not careful. It’s not too bad, but for me, the pens don’t live up to the no smear promise.

They do live up to the no bleed through promise. I tried the pens in my Eccolo journal and there was no bleed through.

The pens write smoothly. I really like the fine tip, it’s just what I need for when I want to cram a lot of writing into a small space.

title: TomCare Cube Storage System
text:
The TomCare Cube Storage System is pretty easy to put together. I used the included hammer once before it cracked and splintered, so I ended up pushing the shelves into the connector pieces by hand. Getting a good grip to do that was a little tricky, but not impossible.

The gray plastic material of the shelves looks thin, but so far it seems durable. I’ve stacked probably 20 pounds of stuff on the shelves already and the cubes show no signs of bowing.

I think the cubes would make great storage for dorm life, since they’re easy to put together and take apart, and don’t take up a lot of space for travel. Or for anything else, really. The different configurations mean the shelves can fit about anywhere, so it’s easy to find a space for them. I put mine together 2 wide, 3 tall, and had extra connectors available if I wanted to do a different setup.

title: LapGear Sidekick Lap Desk
text:
The base of the LapGear Sidekick Lap Desk is filled with pellets, which settle around your legs, so the lap desk doesn’t rock too much. The lap desk is lightweight too, so it’s actually comfortable to use it for an extended period.

I use mostly the lap desk sitting on the couch. It’s almost high enough on my lap to help prevent hand strain if I do a lot of typing there. The grippy silicone strip keeps my laptop from moving about while I use it.

I tried the lap desk in bed, putting it against my legs. It doesn’t perform as well if I’m lying down; the support bar in the front isn’t high enough to hold the laptop from falling forward. But that depends mostly on the angle at which I use the lap desk.

There are a few snags in the fabric underneath the lap desk, so I do worry about how well it will hold up, as the fabric does feel thin to start with.

title: Yoobi Blue Journal
text:
I stock up on hardcover journals like this whenever I find them on sale. I have a shelf full of black ones, as that’s the most common color. So the bright blue of this Yoobi journal caught my eye immediately.

I didn’t realize the Yoobi journal only has 80 pages. I have an Eccolo journal (very similar size, 5.5” by 8.5”) that has 186 pages.

The cover on the Yoobi journal isn’t quite as sturdy as my other journals. The sides of the cover were actually damaged in shipping, and I feel like I could easily bend the cover.

The paper quality is just okay. I tried a Sharpie Pen (blue), a gel pen (blue), and a Tombow Mono Drawing Pen (black). All had bleed through. The gel pen smeared even after I’d taken the time to take pictures to include with my review.

I don’t like that the Yoobi journal doesn’t have an included elastic loop to hold a pen. There are no inner pockets on either cover.

Compared to other similar journals, this one doesn’t quite live up to my expectations. It’s just okay. I do like that Yoobi says an item will be donated to a U.S. classroom, but there’s an asterisk to note “Actual item donated is based on classroom need and may be of equal or lesser value than item purchased.”

title: Orange Circle Folio and Agenda
text:
The gray and rose gold color scheme of this folio is what first caught my eye for this set, and in person, it’s quite pretty. In the product photos, it looked to me like the rose gold floral printing was raised from the gray surface, but it’s not.

I’ve had a few Orange Circle planners that are described as “leatheresque” and so far, they’ve all had different textures. The texture of this set is nice to touch; I can tell it’s not leather, but it’s not cheap or gummy feeling or anything like that. The cover of the agenda is very soft and bendy, something to be aware of if you plan on using it without the folio.

The agenda is designed for function, which I appreciate. Some Orange Circle planners have too many interior decorations for the calendars to be usable. This one has plain pages. All the monthly spreads are at the beginning, followed by weekly break downs. The paper is lightweight; I tested a Stabilo, a Sharpie Pen, a Tombow Pen, and a gel pen. All had bleed through. Even the printing, such as the dates and mini calendars, is visible on the page back. The agenda has no inner pockets.

The folio my favorite part of the set. I like that I can use it with another similar sized notebook with it. I tried an Eccolo journal, 5.5” by 8.5”, and it fit, even with a pen in the folio and a pen in the folio. I was actually looking for something like the folio, that I could use to carry my journal and a few pens, so this is great for me. But I do wish the pockets in the folio were stretchy, or had a little give. Right now, they’re tight, and I’m worried I’ll rip them.

Overall, this is a nice set. I really appreciate that the folio is usable even after the agenda runs out in 2020.

title: Clear Keyboard Stand
text:
I’ve tried this keyboard stand for a short amount of time and my wrists already hurt, which isn’t a good sign for me. I’m actually typing this review using it, and I’m trying to be quick.

The stand is a good idea, but since the height isn’t adjustable, it’s going to work for some people and not work for others. I have one keyboard in my house that doesn’t have a wrist rest, so I thought this would help relieve strain, but the angle is just too high for me.

The minimal lip to hold the keyboard in place is nice, certainly smaller than some I’ve seen, and it does securely hold the keyboard on the tray. If you have a large keyboard, it likely won’t fit on this stand.

There are two flexible plastic rubber strips inside the box to prevent the stand from slipping. Mine were unattached and I nearly missed them, because they’re clear. Just a warning before you toss the packaging!

title: Orange Circle Studio 2020 Leatheresque Large Tabbed Spiral Agenda,
text:
I have two Orange Circle calendars that have “leatheresque” covers. But the covers are completely different. This agenda calendar’s cover is hard, similar to a hardback book. The other planner’s cover has a soft texture that feels more leather like. I have no idea what “leatheresque” is supposed to be, but I DO like this cover. It’s durable enough to have a good chance of lasting until the end of 2020.

The planner is too large and heavy to be portable. I plan on leaving it at my desk, so it will work for me.

On the inside, I like that Orange Circle has concentrated on functionality. Some of their calendars have pretty printed backgrounds, but those can make it difficult to actually use the calendar. This planner has tabs for each month; I do wish they were made of sturdier cardboard. In the section for each month, there’s a page for notes, the monthly spread, and then weekly spreads.

The planner has a few extras, such as appointment stickers, a few gridded pages, and a folder. I wish I liked the appointment stickers more, but they’re a reason I’ve taken off a star. The stickers are printed in metallic silver ink, so depending on the angle, I can’t always read them. The stickers are also situational; I won’t have a use for more than half of them.

The appointment options include: nails, hair, birthday, doctor, date night, pay bills, sick day, day off, anniversary, dentist, car service, girls’ night, vacation, party, concert, vet appt., movie night, celebration, meeting, family event, deadline, don’t forget, volunteer, and hooray.

title: Orange Circle Mini Monthly Planner
text:
The outside of this planner looks luxe, with the shimmery gold cover and font. The cover isn’t stiff or soft, somewhere in between, a fake “leather” that will bend but still protect the calendar pages.

The font color used inside the planner is gray, which can be difficult to read. The dark watercolor backgrounds for some of the months don’t help. It’s difficult to read gray text on a blue/purple background, for example. I’ve noticed this problem before in some other Orange Circle planners. Sure, it’s pretty, but makes the calendar hard to use.

Unless I put something on top of it, the calendar stays open at the binding. It doesn’t lay flat but stays open about a quarter of the way.

title: Orange Circle Studio Monthly Planner
text:
“Just Right” is the perfect name for this Orange Circle Studio Monthly Planner. It’s just right for those who want a monthly planner without a lot of extra junk.

The “Bella Flora” design has painted-style flowers on the front and back, and faint flower prints inside. Sometimes the designs behind calendar pages can be too dark, rendering the calendar useless. But here, the backgrounds for the monthly spreads are very light, the faint flower prints adding a pop of variety. This is a big plus, since I actually want to use the planner, not just look at it.

The planner lays flat when opened, another plus.

The useful extras include a pocket in the back, one (front and back) full notes page, and a few perforated notes pages (4 pages front and back, split into 3 sections), and a list of 2020 holidays.

title: 3M Monitor Whiteboard
text:
I like the idea of the 3M Monitor Whiteboard, but not the execution.

I keep to do lists in various Text Edit docs, which means they get covered up on my computer screen. I wanted to start using a whiteboard so the list would always be visible, plus I like physically crossing an item off, even if I erase the list later.

The magnetic mount can be attached to either side of your monitor; the box includes two command strips. The magnet feels pretty sturdy, so I don’t worry that the whiteboard will fall off if I bump it. But I do not like that the mount sticks out from the monitor when the whiteboard isn’t in place. I’d prefer it to fold back, out of sight, when not in use.

The included dry erase marker has a very weak magnet to stick it to the whiteboard. The marker definitely needs a stronger magnet, because it falls off if I so much as look at it wrong.

The document clip at the top of the whiteboard could also use some finessing. 3M says it can hold ten pages, but I had a tricky time getting two pages into it. A proper clip instead of a little slit cut into the plastic would have been better, in my opinion.

title: Folding Lap Desk
text:
This is a pretty nice lapdesk that offers some adjustability in height and angle. The description is misleading because this desk is all plastic. The top is a teak wood print/laminate.

The desk is large enough to use a 15” laptop and mouse. It’s designed for a right-handed person; the clips that hold a laptop from sliding are on the left side. On the right side, the thick plastic rim is cut back and there’s a leather-like padding. I was hoping to use this desk to write by hand too, but the hard plastic under my left wrist won’t be comfortable for very long.

The width of the desk makes it better suited to working in bed, or even sitting on the floor. I was hoping to use it in an armchair too, but my chair is too narrow, and because the legs fold underneath it, the desk won’t balance on top of the chair’s armrests.

title: IRIS USA Storage Tote
text:
I want a dozen more of these IRIS USA Utility Totes! They are awesome.

I had planned on using the totes outside in the barn, but they look so nice, especially stacked, I’m keeping them for indoor use instead. I can shove a ton of stuff in here, put the lid on, and fill up the next tote.

When empty, the totes aren’t super heavy, so I don’t have to worry about the weight of the tote plus the weight of stuff inside being too much for me to move.

I like that the lids have a way to lock them, or you could use the holes for straps/bungee cords.

The totes did have a strong plastic smell for the first few days, but once they aired out, it went away.

title: AmazonBasics Heavy-Duty D-Ring Binder - 1.5"
text:
I’ve usually liked AmazonBasics items, but I don’t feel like these particular AmazonBasics Heavy-Duty D-Ring Binders are, in fact, heavy duty.

There’s only one lever to open the rings, which feels really flimsy to me. The rings themselves are thin.

I ended up using these binders to store papers I don’t anticipate needing often, since I feel if I were opening and closing the rings frequently, they would break or loosen. For that purpose, they’re adequate.

title: Medicare/Card Holder Protector Sleeves
text:
I wasn’t actually sure if Medicare advised against laminating Medicare cards. According to Medicare’s site, “the Social Security department advises against it because the card might have built-in security features that could be compromised by lamination.”

When my mom received her new one, she took it to an office supply store and the employee there said he’d already done 50 that week! So clearly not everyone knows or cares that you aren’t supposed to laminate them.

The card holder sleeves are individual, not connected. But the sleeves don’t fit into many wallet pockets, so that’s something to be aware of.

Inserting and removing cards is easy.

title: Epson DS-80W Wireless/Wired Scanner
text:
This Epson DS-80W scanner is very portable, great for taking places if you’re tired of using your phone as a quick scanner. The quality of the scans is definitely much better than using an app, but then I’d expect no less from Epson.

I don’t need a scanner every day, so I also like that it doesn’t take up a lot of space. It has both wireless and wired connectivity AND is usable on Mac and Windows. The Mac software looks like it belongs in 1999, but hey, it works so I won’t complain too much.

My main quibble with the scanner is how easily pages get jammed. There’s no wriggle room on a normal size piece of paper. I had to watch and carefully guide every sheet I scanned or the page would wrinkle and start to go sideways.

title: AmazonBasics Mesh Six Slot File Organizer with Double Tray
text:
I definitely didn’t expect the AmazonBasics Mesh Six Slot File Organizer to be as large as it is! To give you an idea, it’s taller, wider, and deeper than my 15” MacBook Pro.

I personally wish the file folder section had a back, so that if I were to put the organizer against a wall, I wouldn’t have to worry about papers falling out of folders and between the desk and wall. The double tray section does have a back.

It’s pretty well made, but the mesh “slots” could bend easily, if enough weight was leaned against them. My unit arrived with one bent section. It’s not too bad, but enough for me to see that there’s the possibility of the sections bending over time.

title: Zinmark Office Chair Mat
text:
This mat is anything but heavy duty. I’m using to protect the carpet underneath a ~60lbs gaming chair. The mat moves every time I roll the chair in and out. I have to pull the chair off once a day to move the mat back where I want it.

I’ve been using the mat for about three weeks; it still has an unpleasantly strong plastic scent.

title: Brother P-Touch Cube Plus PT-P710BT
text:
I really like that the Brother P-Touch Cube Plus is wireless and that I can print labels from my phone! This makes it truly portable, once it’s been charged. Charging is easy, via micro USB, so if you needed a recharge while out, those are quite common. The Cube does need to be charged prior to the first use.

Pairing the printer with my phone (LG V20, Android Nougat) via Bluetooth was easy. If you can pair Bluetooth headphones with your phone or computer, you can figure out how to pair the Cube. After downloading the Brother iPrint&Label app, I was on my way to making labels in minutes.

Once I started making labels, I kept thinking of new things I needed to label … this is my first label maker and I suddenly understand why they are so popular. And because all I need is the Cube and my phone to start making labels, I won’t be dissuaded by having to pull out a bunch of cords and hooking things up.

The app has a lot of options to fancy up the labels. Symbols can be included, or even pictures from your phone, barcodes, frames applied, etc.

My only concern is the cost of replacement tape. When I selected Auto Cut as an option, the Cube spit out a small piece with each label, wasting tape. A small piece, but it added up. There’s an option for “Chain Printing” which eliminated that problem. So definitely experiment with the different printing and cut options to get full use of the Cube.

title: C-Line Rainbow Document Sorter, Letter Size
text:
I thought this document sorter would be helpful for organizing my tax information. I have several different categories of paperwork. So instead of tossing everything into one folder and going through it at the end of the year, I thought I’d organize as I went, using the different colored folders for different categories.

My plan was foiled by two things.

One, there’s no way to label the folders. Because the elastic closure fits over the top corners, you can really only add tabs to the middle of the inner pockets.

Two, the document sorter doesn’t fit in my file drawer! The sorter is approximately half an inch longer than a normal file folder.

title: Paper Mate InkJoy Gel Pens Fine Point (0.5mm) Capped, 14 Count,
text:
I use these Paper Mate InkJoy Gel Pens in my bujo, so I like that they have caps. I haven’t had any problems with the caps not staying on. The variety of colors is pretty good, blue and purple being the best represented. I color code my writing notes, so I appreciate having some shades that I can’t find in my favorite Sharpie Pens.

I’m left-handed and did have a little smearing when I test wrote with the pens. The ink doesn’t dry instantly, but it is quicker than older style gel pens. Honestly, the writing style, hand feel, and look of the ink when dry reminds me a lot of a Sharpie Pen. So if you’re a fan of those, you’ll probably like these.

The ink flows smoothly. I’ve been using them for about a week every day and haven’t noticed any problems with ink flow. They have a hint of bleedthrough.

title: Scotch Wall-Safe Tape, .75 in x 800 in, 2 pack, Boxed tape for use with dispenser
text:
This Scotch tape doesn’t leave a sticky residue on walls when removed within a few days. But it doesn’t have great holding power -- I had to use several pieces to keep a single sheet of paper on the wall.

The tape doesn’t have a lot of stickiness, so it isn’t suitable for other taping activities.

title: Scotch Brand Wall-Safe Tape
text:
This Scotch tape might remove easily from walls without leaving behind residue, but it’s not very sticky! I had to use several pieces to hold up one sheet of paper.

This tape is also not suited for other common tape tasks. I didn’t have normal Scotch tape, so I thought I’d use this to tape the flaps on a lightweight cardboard box. The box popped open thirty seconds after I taped it. So beware that this tape is very specialized.

title: Orange Circle Studio 2019 Large Leatheresque Weekly Agenda, August 2018 - December 2019, Gunmetal
text:
At first glance, this Orange Circle “Leatheresque” Weekly Agenda is very slick and nicely designed. I’m a fan of the gunmetal grey cover with the holographic 2019. The pages are gilded in silver and there are two silver ribbon page markers.

From the display pictures, it might seem as if the agenda is hardcover. It’s not -- the cover is quite soft and bendy. I question how well the planner will hold up over a year and a half. If I were to take it everywhere with me, I think it would get beat up quickly.

Calendar layout wise, I like what Orange Circle has done. All the monthly spreads are at the beginning and then the weekly spreads follow. Usually I see something like August monthly, then August weekly, then September monthly, and so on. The weeks start on Monday, not Sunday.

I tested bleed-through with a Sharpie Pen and a Tombow Drawing Pen. I could faintly see both on the back of the page, but it wasn’t bad.

title: AmazonBasics D-Ring Binders, 3-inch, 2 pack
text:
I like 3” binders for holding account statements, since I can store a lot of statements without having to get rid of old ones. AmazonBasics are exactly that, a good value.

The binders have an outer clear plastic overlay so you can customize them. There are also two inside pockets. I do wish the inside pockets were taller, as pages inside the pockets slip when you turn the binder sideways.

I have about 300 pages in one binder right now, and it’s holding up very well. I don’t feel like it’s going to break under the weight, and there’s room for a few hundred more pages.

title: Mind Reader 4 Tier All-Purpose Mobile Utility Cart
text:
The Mind Reader Mobile Utility Cart is very easy to assemble. It took me about 15 minutes; the instructions are clear and the two necessary tools are included.

If you have trouble getting the cart to be square and level, do not tighten the shelves all the way as you add them. Wait to do a final round of tightening until all the shelves are in.

The cart is lightweight; I can easily pick it up when it’s empty. I wouldn’t store anything too heavily in this, or conversely, anything too small. The basket “shelves” have such an open grid that it would be impossible to store small items in the cart without adding a liner or plastic container to keep them from falling out. The top shelf of my cart had a few scratches when it arrived.

The cart rolls reasonably well on carpet, and better on a hard floor. I didn’t notice while I was putting it together, but two of the wheels can be locked, to keep the cart from moving too much when it’s in place. If you don’t need to move it at all, you can skip installing the wheels, as the cart can stand without them.

title: Mind Reader 3 Piece Desk Supplies Organizer, Black
text:
My mother loves baskets so much I could probably buy them for her for Christmas. I originally picked this 3 piece set for myself because my desk is a den of chaos, but she got to the box before me and now won’t give them up. In her words, “They’re adorable! They have feet! They’re good sizes!”

In my house we’re ultra careful with everything, so the little grips on the bottom of each basket that are intended to keep the baskets in place on a slippery desktop are also useful to keep surfaces from being scratched. The mesh of the baskets is fine, so even small items should stay inside and not fall out.

I have taken two stars off because the baskets have shoddy, inconsistent construction. I’ve included a collage of photos showing how the sides don’t match up and how the plastic on the edges of the corners/sides isn’t flush. The baskets are uneven and wobble, but not enough that you could easily knock them over. I noted construction flaws on each basket.

title: Erin Condren 2018 Hardbound LifePlanner-Watercolor Splash Quote, 5x8
text:
Like a lot of other people, I’m really picky with planners. I always start out with the best of intentions, but mid-January I give up and go back to a hodgepodge approach of online calendars, notes, and appointment cards everywhere. I’ve recently transitioned to using a bullet journal for writing, so I thought I’d try again with a planner.

At first look, the Erin Condren LifePlanner is gorgeous. I have the watercolor splash planner, with a white background, teal and pink watercolor splashes, and silver accents. It’s very slick: the pages have silver edges, the months are in calligraphy, and there are pretty, inspirational quotes every so often. The hardcovers are actually very sturdy, which is great for if you’re trying to add appointments or tasks in the car or on the go.

I use Sharpie Pens for all my writing needs, there’s a very slight hint of bleedthrough, but it’s not enough to be too noticeable or annoying.

I like the layout approach of the planner: each month has a monthly spread, and then a weekly breakdown. That’s fine, and useful. But what I didn’t like was that February’s monthly spread was after the week of January 22-28. I get that’s probably to save pages, but every time I tried to look for February’s monthly spread, I had to keep paging through January’s weeks and that annoyed me very quickly. I also wish the planner had an pocket in one or both of the covers.

title: Orange Circle Studio 2018 Just Right Monthly Planner, Aug. 2017 - Dec. 2018, Time You Enjoy Wasting
text:
I really like the design and thought put into the Orange Circle Just Right Monthly Planner. It’s got some graphic oomph behind it, so you aren’t staring at boring white pages for the whole year. If you’re like me and absolutely horrible at decorating stuff in the current trend of bujos and planners, this is worth a look.

The planner spans from August 2017 to December 2018, and the spreads are monthly. The day boxes are roomy enough to list plenty of appointments/things to do.

Resources include a list of 2018 holidays, moon phases, a one page calendar for 2019, a page for birthdays/anniversaries, several note pages that are perforated for ripping into lists, and a pocket.

The size, 7.5 inches by 9.75, is a little weird: it’s slightly too big for me to carry every day, but a little too small to sit on my desk. The cover is a stiff cardboard that is less bendy than flimsy plastic, but not as firm as a hard Moleskine.

And while I really liked the graphics behind the monthly spreads, I wish they had been just a little lighter. You can see from the picture I added to my review that I can barely see my blue marker at the start of August, because the green background is so dark.

title: AmazonBasics Classic Notebook, Large
text:
Let me start this review by saying I’m not a notebook or pen snob. I started using a Moleskine because the hard covers keep it from getting bent in my bag, and the covers also provide a decent writing surface if I’m in bed or out and about. But I don’t really like paying $15+ for a notebook!

The AmazonBasics Classic Notebook is a worthy alternative, although I do wish it was slightly less expensive. $13 is still steep for a notebook in my eyes.

I use Sharpie Pens for writing in my notebooks, usually in blue, black, or purple. They do not bleed or smear, but I can faintly see the writing on the back of the page. This is true in AmazonBasics or Moleskine, so I didn’t find the paper quality to be different.

Basically, the AmazonBasics is a near clone of the Moleskine for me, and a few dollars cheaper. The notebook’s size, features (inner pocket, ribbon bookmark, and elastic closure), and general feel are very similar. If you’re looking for a cheaper alternative to pricey notebooks, I’d check this one out.

title: Avery Durable ID Labels 6791
text:
So far, I’ve found quite a few good things about these labels, and have only one complaint.

Each label sheet identifies which template to use, in case you have a bunch of different Avery labels and mix them all together. Avery includes instructions on how to print labels, namely feeding the sheets into the printer one at a time, and not printing more than 30 sheets in one go. The instructions are helpfully printed on a bright green page that you can’t miss.

The package helpfully shows the exact size of the label, so you don’t have to guess at the size and can easily find what size is right for you. I think these are a great size for putting on small boxes, tools, that sort of thing. I don’t need to trim them down.

I didn’t test print, as that’s not how I’d use the labels, but I know Avery and Microsoft Word both have templates. According to how I’d use the labels, I wrote on them with a Sharpie Pen and had no smearing.

As for my one complaint, I did have trouble with the labels sticking on plastic bags that were full of oddly shaped objects. Obviously, the labels stuck a lot better on flat surfaces.

title: Avery Durable ID Labels 6792
text:
THE GOOD:
--Each sheet of labels identifies which template to use, in case you had a bunch of different Avery labels and mixed them all together.

--Avery includes instructions (helpfully printed on a bright green page) to tell you how to print labels using your own printer. Mainly, feed the sheets into the printer one at a time, and don’t print more than 30 label sheets at a time.

--The outside of the package has an actual size picture of the label, so you don’t have to imagine measurements.

--I didn’t print test labels, but wrote on them with a Sharpie Pen. There was no smearing.

THE BAD:
--These labels seem quite expensive. I’m doing a lot of organizing, of all sorts of things, indoors and out, so I need something durable that will hold up in almost any condition. I’m not an office products junkie, so I might be off, but I do think $20 for labels is pricey.

--I did have trouble with the labels sticking on plastic bags that were full of oddly shaped objects. The labels wanted to peel off.

title: At-A-Glance Weekly and Monthly Planner 2016
text:
I’ve tried a ton of apps, but I’ve never found one that does exactly what I want for keeping track of appointments and activities and blogging and other random stuff that I have deadlines for. So I’m going old school and going to a paper planner.

I haven’t yet used the At-A-Glance Weekly Planner, since it doesn’t start until 2016, but here’s what I’ve observed so far:

GOOD:
++The cover is better quality than other At-A-Glance products; this one is heavy and won’t pick up marks and scuffs as easily as other At-A-Glance planners I’ve tried.

++The binding is spiral, which means the planner lays flat. But sometimes when I try to close the planner, the cover get stuck in the binding and I have to shake it free.

++The pages are thick enough for me to use Sharpie pens -- there’s no bleed through.

++There are tabs for each month, so it’s easy to flip to a particular month.

++There aren’t any cutesy phrases scattered throughout. It’s a planner, plain and simple.

BAD:
--There’s a month spread before each set of week breakdowns. The month calendar starts with Sunday, but the week calendar starts with Monday.

--The main text color of this planner is light grey. I’m 29 with good eyesight, and I’m having a hard time reading the tiny dates in a fully lit room. This is a huge con. The grey is very difficult to see, and has been used for everything from grid lines to the bonus material in the back. The text color should have been black!

The light grey text color brought my rating of the calendar down, since I think it will really irritate me and cause unnecessary difficulty over the next year of using the planner.

title: Epson Expression Home XP-420 Wireless Color Printer with Scanner & Copier
text:
The Epson Expression Home XP-420 Wireless Color Printer with Scanner & Copier is a reasonably priced wireless printer, but I’d only recommend this if you aren’t going to print a lot of pages. This is the kind of printer that guzzles ink like I drink frappuccinos.

I checked Office Depot for replacement ink, to the tune of $68 for the four pack. Amazon has the ink for cheaper, but if you’re in a pinch and need ink, you could be out a lot of money.

For this review, I tried wireless printing from my phone (Galaxy Note 4, Android 5.0.1) and scanning to my laptop (Mac Book Air, 10.9.1).

What I did like about the XP-420:
—The control panel on the printer tilts up so you can see it.

—The scan quality is good.

—I thought the Android app (Epson iPrint) was incredibly easy to use. Even someone non-techy should be able to use it, provided they pick the right app (there are a lot of results for Epson in the Play Store). In fact, setting up the printer on my phone was the easiest thing I did with the printer. All I had to do was install the app, and pick “Select a Printer.” The app has a lot of information, such as showing how much ink remains. The app is integrated well into Android; I could paste a web URL into “Web Page Print” or I could share a tab from Chrome with the app and have it pasted in automatically. The app can also connect to Box, Dropbox, Evernote, Google Drive, and Microsoft OneDrive.

What I didn’t like about the XP-420:
—When you set it up, you *must* have the ink cartridges inserted to initialize the set up. I didn’t like that I couldn’t set it up just to be a scanner.

—The printer top doesn’t open all the way, so it was a bit awkward to put the ink cartridges inside.

—Entering a WiFi password is *annoying*, especially if you have one with lots of numbers and uppercase/lowercase letters. It took more than a minute to put my password in.

—If you want to scan to a computer, you need a USB cable (Type A Male to Type B Male), which isn’t included. This isn’t necessary if you want to scan to Facebook. Finding the USB slot was annoying; I found it hard to see since the printer’s black on black. I had to use a flashlight to plug in my cable.

—The printing quality is just okay. I printed 4x6 photo of a rainbow rose, and the printout wasn’t very vibrant or bright. The Android app let me pick the size of photo, but I couldn’t pick where the photo would be on the page.

An oddity:
—I set up the printer on my wireless network first. I installed the Epson software on my Mac, setting it up as a wireless printer in the configuration. Then I plugged in the USB cable, since you need it to scan to a computer. The first time I tried to scan from the printer’s control panel, it couldn’t find a computer. Why? Because I had the scan menu option open already on my Mac. (System Preferences > Printers & Scanners > Epson > Scan Menu). Once I closed the scan menu, I was able to scan from the printer’s control panel.

But I preferred the System Preferences/Scan Menu, because I could pick what to name my file and where to save it (among other options). When you scan from the printer, it saves to the Pictures folder on Mac and doesn’t let you pick a filename.

Overall, the XP-420 printer is okay. I wouldn’t recommend it if you’re going to print photos and color pages every day -- you’ll empty your wallet buying replacement ink cartridges. The printing quality could be better, and while the app is easy to use, it could have more options on setting up photos to print.

title: AT-A-GLANCE Meeting/Planner Padfolio
text:
The AT-A-GLANCE Meeting/Planner Padfolio does look nice at first glance. It’s sleek, and while the cover isn’t leather, it still feels nice. I do think it would mark up easily, as there’s some sort of stain already on mine when I got it, hidden underneath the cardboard wrapper.

I like the copper stitching on the outside — it’s a nice accent. Inside there’s a small pocket (described as a flap pocket), but it’s too small to be super useful. Also, you can see the outline of the pocket from the front of the padfolio.

The biggest problem with this padfolio? It’s way too flimsy! There’s no way you could take notes with this on your lap. I can fold it in half — that’s how little support there is. I have it sitting on my bed as I write this review, and just a finger press on the paper makes the whole padfolio buckle. This would only be useful when you can write on a table or desk.

The included paper is okay, nothing fancy. It’s divided into graph paper (with really tiny squares) and a spot for a to-do list at the bottom. The pad is replaceable, which is good because I think most people would prefer standard ruled paper.

title: Do NOT BUY!!
text: Very unhappy with this order the book had no liquid in it and was dry and hard returned it and never got a refund or new item back very disappointed in this and would not recommend buying this book

title: Fun teacher gift
text: I found the puns delightful. Kiddo rolled his eyes and groaned so double win.

title: Not very secure but it is useful
text: Got this for my husband, who stores his on random pieces of paper throughout his desk. Now its all in one spot and much easier to locate a specific password. However, it says password on the cover. It couldn't be more obvious what that notebook is for. Certainly something you need to either keep in a safe or hide very well.

title: Works well, but a couple markers were dried out on arrival.
text:
Kiddo hates chores but loves checklists so this was a good way to help him stay on track without me nagging him 19 times a day.

If you are wondering about the exact colors of the chore charts: one is blue and the other is red. It looks like it might be pink in the product pic, but it is most certainly a very defined red. So if you were worried that one was for boys and one was for girls, they are both just basic primary colors of blue and red.

Chart worked exactly as I hoped. Erases well, clear with a durable print. The markers work best if you store them tips down, otherwise they (like pretty much all other white board markers) will dry out faster. Unfortunately for us, two of ours (the black and the green) arrived already completely dried out so I deducted a star. The eraser is magnetic, but will only stick to the chart if you have the chart hanging on something metallic. Our chart is stuck to a white board and the eraser stays on the chart just fine. Otherwise it will fall of the chart if you just have it hanging on a wall, as the chart by itself is not magnetic enough to hold it.

title: Adhesive gives out in under a week, unless you plan on using super glue, don't bother
text:
Nice variety but like many of the magnets of this type the adhesive is awful. Sure they stick fine for a few days but then they eventually just fall off. And whatever they are holding up also falls to the ground.

The magnets are apparently stronger than the glue (they aren't really all that strong but they are better than the ones that only hold a sheet of paper). I'm going to have to super glue them onto the back of kiddos lap board. He likes to store it on his larger white board and this lapboard didn't come with a magnetic fixture. I was hoping these would be an easy solution, but I can't have his lap board come crashing to the ground every few days when the magnets adhesive gives. Oh well.

title: Big hit!
text:
Huge hit at the valentines exchange. I did make sure all the caps and tips were screwed on tightly, several were so loose they were almost off and one was missing a top but I found it loose in the bag. So before giving these out, make sure they are tightly secured.

Worked well and the kids love them.

title: Best of both worlds
text:
Work requires visible badges, so no just putting in a pocket or clipping to my waistband. The badges also work as keycards for the doors. So we have to wear around our necks but its a pain to slip if off every time I need to go through a door. It's that or bend oddly at the security panel to make the card reach.

This combo deal is perfect, I wear around my neck but has the convenience of a retractable one so no bending down to swipe. Love it!

title: Heavy duty, but unforgiving
text:
Heavy duty is right, these things feel like they could be used as a weapon. Super solid, more heft than I was expecting, retractable feature works well.

However, due to all the metal and general shape with the dog ears they are not forgiving when it comes to bumping into things like your desk or car door. For utility sake I will stick to the soft round plastic versions just to protect my paint. Now if I were ever in a fight, I'd want these O.o

title: Great for organizing in a small space
text:
Great for travel or if like me you want to keep your important documents all in one spot but don't have the space for a file cabinet or safe. I kind of chuckled at the combination lock, I mean really if someone wants to steal your stuff they could easily just take the whole bag. But if you are just trying to keep people from snooping this would do the trick.

Well made, love the flamingo print, not sure how "fireproof" it actually is but it does seem decently water resistant.

title: Wonderful pack of gift tags
text:
There are soooo many tags in this packet I will be set for many Christmases to come. Woohoo no more digging through my drawers for the "free" gift tags sent out by charities every few years.

Good price, great print quality. They are not super thin, but not the really thick expensive foil type either. Use a ball point pen to write on or they are going to smear because of the glossy finish. I like the variety of images, something for every age group.

title: Perfect fit
text:
Fits my vaccine card perfectly. You will want to measure your card first to make sure you have a standard 4x3. My understanding is some sites used a different size. For the most part though, 4x3 is the norm.

Now I can leave in my purse without getting worried it's getting all banged up.

title: Thin
text: It works, but its thin and certainly not "heavy duty".

title: Great quality dry erase
text: Nice and bright, width is perfect for distance learning, not to thin but not fat like a sharpie. They don't dry out super fast either like his previous set with the puffy erase ends.

title: Kiddo approved
text: Super cute and the magnet holds well enough to stay put. Kiddo was very excited and loved how they stuck part way out.

title: Never enough dry erase pens
text: My son goes through so many dry erase pens for distance learning. Particularly the black ones. This was a great deal and they work well. Tip is a nice width for working out math problems without looking like a sharpie. As with all dry erase pens I suggest storing them tip side down, rather than tip up, or flat. It prolongs their lives.

title: Great for distance learning
text: I had no idea how much space all the school supplies take up until kiddo started distance learning during the pandemic. This thing is great because it fits SOOO much, has a lazy Susan set up so you can easily reach everything, and each little compartment comes out so he can just take what he needs to his desk, then bring it back when he's done. Makes keeping things organized so much easier.

title: Great for Elementary
text: Going into 4th grade, wide ruled paper is on his school supply list. This paper is decent quality and the price is about mid-range at $15. You could probably find cheaper if you shop around, but it is in line with other same size sets I see currently listed.

title: Some confusion
text:
Kiddo is 9 and will be starting 4th grade at the end of summer. He missed almost a third of the year in second grade because our school shut down due to the pandemic and his teacher just couldn't handle the switch to distance learning. So they basically had nothing for the last three months of school. The following year was 100% distance learning which came with it's own crazy but at least was more structured with a more tech savy teacher. Sooooo basically kiddo may or may not have missed some foundational skills just due to the craziness of the pandemic. I assume many parents are in the same boat.

I got this set and the one for the year before hoping to fill in any gaps over the summer. Unfortunately the grade levels were a bit confusing and instead of being for the summers between 2nd and 3rd grade and 3rd and 4th grade, they were actually one year past each. So, this particular workbook set is for skills he hasn't even gotten to yet, since it is for the summer between fourth and fifth grade.

It is however structured just like the third grader one we completed. As such has the same concerns I had with that one. First being, if you are not familiar with how the lines work in the workbook your kid is going to revert to kindergarten sized printing and just skip the little half space they are actually suppose to use. So do yourself a favor and look up how they want you to actually use the lined spaces, its not intuitive.

Second and my biggest issue and reason I dropped the star, there is nothing to prompt the kids to write in the writing journal. It's just blank pages of lined paper. You have to come up with your own writing prompts or hope their idea of "write after each chapter" isn't just them scribbling surface level nonsense to get it done. If this had actually guided them through the story and made them think deeper (a key skill for early readers) it would have been 5 stars, but as-is, four is being generous... I almost gave three.

title: Mixed bag but good for summer
text:
I have been using this over the summer with my son who finished third grade and will be starting fourth grade in the fall. For our purposes it gets the job done. However I'm not exactly over the moon about it either. It seems like the workbook is the real value and the other two things are filler.

Workbook: 4 stars and well thought out. I am NOT however a fan of how big the lined writing space is. Maybe it is part of their larger program or we are just using it wrong, but it gives them kindergarten age space to write in between the lines and as a result his handwriting is regressing.
