They should be working on writing smaller (like wide ruled size) not larger at age 9.

The Book: 4 stars it is age and reading level appropriate. The story is endearing and interesting enough to hold his attention. My only complaint is that the print is a bit smaller than most books (enough I had to bust out my rarely used reading glasses). The small print makes it easier for him to get lost and he has reverted back to using a finger to help hold his place. A small regression but not a huge deal.

Writing Journal: 2 stars. We tossed it out and switched to a wide ruled notebook. The lines are HUGE and since there are no actual writing prompts to go with the book, its unnecessary. He was back to writing giant half inch letters like he was 6. I really don't understand their method, little hands should be working on fine motor skills not writing twice the size than they would in a classroom. Also, its just a blank journal, there are no tie ins with the book.

Overall: I like the workbook but on its own it is not worth $15. I feel like they knew that so someone got a good deal on a bunch of hamster books and tossed the blank writing journal in there with it. There is no effort to make the book and journal a structured lesson. You the parent have to come up with what the kiddo writes about, because if you tell a nine year old to just write in a journal after each chapter with no other guidance, you are going to get little effort and a ton of chaos. So each chapter I have been asking him to write about his favorite part of that chapter or what surprised him or confused him, and then make a prediction on what will happen next. It's repetitive and does little to make him think outside his own take. So, I feel it is a real missed opportunity.

title: Kiddo approved
text:
My son has been eyeing my collection of gel pens I use for adult coloring books. He was over the moon to get his own set of fancy pens, even more excited that they smelled super fun.

These actually write even better than expected, don't let the bright kid packaging fool you.

title: Adorable
text: Well received and non-gendered so a nice card to just stick in a drawer and wait until you need it.

title: Fun and well priced
text: Most of these popup cards are almost twice the price so it was nice to see a reasonable one from Hallmark. It's cute and my mother in law really got a kick out of it.

title: Big hit
text: This got several ooo's and ahhh's. Well made and it pops up surprisingly high.

title: Perfect fit
text: I keep my vaccine card in my purse and was afraid it was going to get beat up in there. This protector envelope is perfect. It's not overly bulky, although I don't really need the lanyard part but its fine. Also, it fit my card perfectly. I saw a couple other reviews said it was too small for their card, so the CDC cards much come in a few different sizes. My card fit perfectly though so I guess you should measure your card first before ordering just to be safe.

title: Nice set for the price
text:
We have gone through a ton of dry erase markers this year during distance learning. I like these because they have an eraser on the end and its one less thing for kiddo to have to keep track of. I do wish they hung upside down better to keep them from drying out. We just kind of corral them in hanging with the tips down using some magnets.

Otherwise they work as expected. The tip is finer than a kids marker but not as fine as a felt tip pen.

title: Great set for distance learning
text:
Kiddo loves the color variety in this pack and that they aren't as thick when trying to write as his other white board markers. I wouldn't call it a super fine point but it's much thinner than a sharpie.

So far they have held up well, but I recommend you hang them with the tip down to help keep them ready to write and not dried out.

title: Perfect size for papers
text:
Perfect size to replace a paperclip. These little mini ones hold about what a large size paperclip does. I also have the next size up "small" but find them too big for office use. They got repurposed to the kitchen for chip clips.

These came well packaged and with a container to keep them in. It's a pretty flimsy thin plastic container, but it will get the job done.

title: Beautiful and Delicate
text: This card is as close to genuine art as I've seen a popup card be. The tree is so delicate and beautiful, I almost don't want to give it away. Very well made, high quality card.

title: Hahaha it's sooo loud, I love it
text: My mom is going to get a kick out of this card. It is over the top. Loud blasting "You're Simply The Best" with lights and a popup bouquet. It's amazing in its crazy.

title: Love the reinforced edges
text: Distance learning and working from home has really made us up our office supply game. These reinforced folders were perfect for ensuring they could handle the wear and tear on younger hands and not fall apart at the seams.

title: Meh, they work but so do must all clips
text:
Not the clips that are pictured. These are black on the inside not painted the same color as the clip. Not a huge deal, but I do get annoyed when they use pics of someone else's product instead of their own.

They come boxed by color in the most annoying to open packages. Which means there is no storage container to keep them in once opened. Other similarly priced clips at least come with a clear container to keep them in.

title: No more forearm or wrist pain.
text: Took a few days to get use to but now I love it. No more wrist pain. I did ding a star because the odd angles at the edges make this difficult to position at an angle.  However I've managed to make it work and really like not having to dig out my wrist support when my arm starts hurting.

title: Mine arrived scratched and damaged
text: It is alright quality but seems a bit overpriced for a very plain not so heavy book end set. Mine also arrived deeply gouged and scratched from being poorly packaged.

title: Durable
text: Well I now have enough dividers to last my 8 year old until he goes off to college. These things are so much more durable than the cardstock ones we were using before. He can be a bit overzealous when looking for work sheets and had torn more than a few. These plastic ones however hold up like a champ.

title: Great neutral cards
text: We are sending out Valentines cards this year; instead of kiddo seeing friends, due to the pandemic. These cards are just perfect, no oddly mushy messages that always seem so weird on kid cards. Nothing gender specific, just nice fun wishes for Valentines.

title: Mixed feelings
text:
Pros:
-Compact and easy to stay organized
-Great fine point on the markers
-Handy clip on eraser with bonus pen holder
-I like the size, not too big, not too small.

Cons:
-Feels a bit flimsy
-Markers aren't really that "intense" as the name would suggest.
-Eraser works but the board stains easily. You will need the occasional squirt of expo cleaner to remove all the marks. My other whiteboards do not stain as much.
-Non-magnetic, nothing sticks to it and it doesn't stick on anything for easy storage. I actually put a bunch of lightweight adhesive backed magnets on mine so I could stick it to a larger whiteboard for easy storage.

*Possible con: I'm unsure if there are refill markers that fit the clip-in holder. They feel about the diameter of standard bic ballpoint pen, so none of the other markers I currently have would fit. This might be something the manufacturer can speak to. A quick Amazon search left me without any obvious refills that would fit the holder.

As for price point, it doesn't have one at the time of this review. I wouldn't pay over $15 for it, with a good chunk of that price being the markers.

title: Pricey but always well received
text: My nieces and nephews have reached the age where they no longer want fun toys and cute pj's. It's all about the gift cards. So, I like to dress it up a bit with a fancy card, call me old fashion. It doesn't matter that they are teens, even the nephew gets a kick out of Auntie's cool cards. Yay!

title: Good for larger books, great stocking stuffers.
text: These are hysterical, and great for my larger hardcovers. For smaller paperbacks they are a bit heavy but still usable. I think they are a hoot, kiddo claimed the cute doggie before I even got a chance to unpackage them. Perfect stocking stuffers!

title: Meh
text: They look great but that's about it. They have no heft and do not glide. It feels like you are writing with a pencil, scratchy.

title: Great for short term use
text:
These are perfect for short use. Meaning I know they will only be used a few times before I erase and write something else. For kiddo they are perfect for honing in on some third grade concepts during distance learning.

They are a happy medium between being slightly harder to get clean but also slightly harder to smear while using. I would not recommend them for terms you want to go over many many times without erasing and changing up. A couple times they were getting a bit stained, but a few squirts of the expo brand cleaner and they were good as new.

As long as you have realistic expectations on how durable a "dry erase" flash cards writing will be, you won't be disappointed.

title: Perfect!
text:
I know its a silly thing to get excited about but this is the best white board calendar I've come across. It actually has enough space for all the days even if the 1st starts at the end of the week. Markers write well, eraser erases well. I would say if you want the markers to stay dark, make sure you hang them upside down.

No complaints, love this set!

title: Great quality, actually break less
text: Kiddo is distance learning this year and holy moly does he go through pencils. These actually do break less than some of his cuter but less durable pencils.

title: Great for school
text: I got these for kiddo to keep at his desk at home during distance learning. They are perfect, just the right number of colors to have variety but not overwhelm like when he pulls out his full craft supply. Sharpen well, not prone to breakage. They aren't soft enough for adult coloring but great for kids.

title: Fun colors but dry out fast
text: Nice fun colors that initially write very well on a white board. However, they are not the longest live and a couple are already starting to dry out after only a couple weeks of use. I think if they could hang upside down and the magnet were placed on the other end it would help extend their life.

title: Nice consistent ink
text: So far these pens have not disappointed. They write well, make a clean line, and are smooth and blot free. I like the fun colors.

title: Misleading packaging and description... only 10 colors (there are two of each color to make 20)
text: This is a two pack of 10 markers each. Not 20 non-duplicated colors as the description states. Both the packaging stating 20 colors and the product description stating 20 non-duplicated colors is inaccurate. This needs to be fixed by the manufacturer or pulled by amazon for being misleading.

title: Clips aren't the best, but the lanyards work very well inspite of it
text:
I have another set with the bulky metal clips and even though they work better I like them less. they are heavy and stand out and pull on the mask too much. These lighter plastic clips are preferred. However, a couple of them are a serious pain to fit on properly. I think it's more of an issue with the loop in the lanyard end not being big enough, but I have one of the set that just doesn't work. Had I purchased these rather than received them for review I would have set back for a fully functioning set.

My advice check them all, make sure they work, send back if any issues. They really are very nice if they are sitting in the clip properly.

title: Worked great for distance learning
text: These folders are a decent weight and worked exactly as I hoped to hold kiddos papers and stuff for school. Usually we get the plastic ones so the hold up in his backpack but since we are distance learning this year (pandemic) I figured we could go with the paper kind. For that purpose they are perfect.

title: Highlighters are a great value, the box is terrible though
text: The box is garbage, just assume you will be storing these in a different container. That aside they are great, work as I'd expect, and you get a ton of them in so many great colors for a very low price. So I'm going still stick with 5 stars, just don't expect to be able to keep them stored in the box they come in.

title: Other than the magnets, 100% love
text:
This has been great for distance learning. Kiddo can respond in zoom quickly with it, and when we don't need it he can just put it up on his larger white board because of the magnets on the back.

The only thing I didn't like was the two smaller stick on magnets it came with. They had a tackey coating that made them "sticky", when I removed it the under magnets were rough and would have scratched the whiteboard. So I threw them out. Still a 5 star product when rating the actual board and marker/eraser set.

The magnets on the back that let it stick to our bigger white board are much softer and won't scratch the board thankfully.

title: Write well, grip isn't that soft though
text: These write very well. Nice and dark compared to some of my cheaper .7mm mechanical pencils. I did ding a star though for the "comfort" grip that isn't really all that soft and not at all ergonomic. They could have done better there, otherwise a great mechanical pencil.

title: Meh
text:
It works, but it's not great.

The eraser arrived cracked, the markers are smelly enough to clear a room, there is a slight ridge across the board although it is not as badly creased as another reviewer received. The marker tray attaches with sticky tape rather than sliding on like the better boards, so you cannot move it and once that tape goes so do all your markers.

Lastly, the plastic wrap to protect it was put on before they attached the metal frame, so it's frustratingly impossible to get all of it out of the seams. Making it look sloppy.

I do not recommend, there are way too many white boards out there for this to be a good choice.

title: Not what is pictured...
text:
The calendar you get is not the one pictured. As you can see in my pic, the number area is very dark. So dark in fact you cannot add a number with a dry erase marker and see it. So you have to write it next to it, which looks stupid. If I had not received this free for review I would have sent it back.

Also, some months (like August 2020) actually require 6 rows to fit all the days. I opted for leaving off Saturday the first, and just numbered from there.

The markers are fine, not the best but not terrible either, and so far do not seem to stain. The eraser works but its magnet is very weak and it has fallen a couple of time. But only when the board was bumped. One positive, the calendar did fit very well on my 36x24 white board/felt board combo.

Overall though, I do not recommend, and I do not appreciate the bait and switch.

title: Well made, easy installation
text:
This went up super easy.

It's sturdy, well made and works as described. The calendar and markers are from a different product, but if you want to add a magnetic calendar like I did the size is 12"x17".

title: Works as expected
text:
This stuck to the side of our fridge perfectly. The markers work well, and they erase easily and completely. The included eraser is the perfect size.

I did deduct a star because the magnets in the markers are a bit iffy on staying attached to the actual marker and I had slight (very minor) skuffing on the bottom edge of the mat.

title: Works well, super easy to use.
text:
Much less "aggressive" sounding than the one I had at work. That thing sounded like it was out for blood and while it was a bit of a rush to use, it was too loud. This one is a mellow stapler, it just happily does it's job without behaving like it is plotting your demise.

If you have never felt threatened by overly aggressive office equipment then I envy you. THE FEAR IS REAL.

title: Meh
text:
Print quality was only so-so on the darker cards, and all of them are a bit too thin for my liking.

If you aren't super picky and just need these for one time use they are fine.

title: Kiddo approved
text:
Our son loves these for drawing and I love that he hasn't dried them out.

He has killed more markers by forgetting the cap than I can count. These are great and the finer tip is better for drawing now that he is older.

title: Great to have on hand
text:
Nice bright primary color birthday cards.

Perfect for boys, girls, kids, adults. I like having them on hand because these things always seem to pop up.

title: Always nice to have on hand
text: Perfect to have on hand for the unexpected birthday or one of the many kid birthdays that pop up in our circle.  Great assortment for all ages and genders. Silly and fun, love the colors

title: Nice basic good sized mouse pad
text:
Works well, no frayed seems, love the generous size.

It's got a bit of an odor, but not nearly as bad as others I have gotten. Aired out in a day or so.

title: Functional as expected
text: Not sure on the price point as one wasn't set at the time of this review, but it's graph paper and works as one would expect. No complaints.

title: Cute set
text:
I like to put little sticker sheets in cards to my younger nieces and nephews and these are the perfect size for that. Some will also be used for kiddo this coming school year because it looks like we will be doing more distance learning as the pandemic is still going strong at the time of this review.

Great for either purpose. Nice mix of boy, girl, and neutral pages as well.

title: Cute and fun
text: Cute for sure, although these are kid quality erasers and not as good as my favorite hi-polymer ones from Pentel. Kiddo liked them because of the case and weird roll up your mess bit at the end. That part doesn't really work that great, and I am pretty sure he is going to snap these erasers at some point as he can be overly forceful when erasing.

title: Huge! Great for distance learning
text: I didn't read the description well enough, imagine my surprise when these giant things came. However, we made great use of them for distance learning while kiddos school was shut down during the pandemic. They stuck to the wall well, but didn't damage the paint when removing.

title: Great value, nice storage container.
text: Great price and all the clips work as expected. I really like the container they came in to, nice and durable so it's not going to collapse in on itself like my last one did, ugh.

title: Not really that big, but it does the job
text:
This is described as "Large Size Double Seat Cushion" but it fits about the same area as a dining chair. Front to back it was okay but width wise it is a bit narrow. It's also a little thinner than expected, but I'm using it on a firm but still padded computer chair, so it is good for that since the chair itself also has some cush to it.

It is a grid type seat cushion rather than a memory foam one. They feel totally different, but I've found the grid ones stay a bit cooler even if they lack that sitting on a cloud feeling.

title: Even cooler in person
text: Love love love the case. The plastic pages are a bit on the flimsy side and two were already ripped at one of the holes when we got it, so I deducted a star. Otherwise a very well made binder. I love that it zips up so there is no chance of losing cards that slip their sleeves if its upside down.

title: They write extremely well
text: Wow what a surprise. These are my new favorite pens and I can be a bIt of a pen snob. They glide and write so smooth. They don't feel super high end or expensive, but the way they write is just amazing. The price is great, and so are the pens.

title: Very thin, do not feel like they will last
text: These are so thin that they flex if you try to use them as a writing surface. The clip that keeps them shut seems questionable as well. May last one school season but I wouldn't expect much more of them than that. A bit disappointing, I usually like AmazonBasics stuff, but on this I would pass.

title: Nice staple to have on hand, a bit flimsy
text: I like to have stuff like this for when kiddo makes cards for relatives or for invitations. They are a bit flimsy though, not terribly so, but they aren't lined and ugh the taste.

title: Great value
text:
These work really well and the comfort grip is a nice bonus over some generic bare bones ones I got a staples. Everyone in the house likes them, particularly kiddo who is really the one that uses pencils the most. They erase really well, although I would prefer that the eraser not be the cap to keep the lead in. If he erases it down to a stub it makes it pretty hard to pull it out to refill. I had inquired if there were eraser refills and the community was super helpful and said yes, they are a standard size.

As far as graphite quality, I prefer a softer lead and found the ones that come with these to be too hard and "scratchy". No one else in the house had that issue though, so it is probably just me and my ridiculousness. As for colors, there is a nice variety. The colors are vivid and really pop.

title: All the kids oooo'd and awww'd
text: Such a fun card. Pops up easily, well made.

title: So fun
text: Huge hit for the kiddo that got it as a birthday card. Well made and popped up well.

title: Super fun
text: I love these pop up cards, I wish they didn't cost so much but they really are spectacular when opened.

title: Was much loved
text: My grandma loves red birds so I sent her this card to say hi. She loved it enough to show it off to all her friends at the assisted living facility.  I don't care how old you are, being the favorite grandchild for the day is always a win.

title: Huge hit
text: This card was a huge hit with my grandma. She is in an assisted living facility that doesn't allow flowers in the rooms, so this was a well received bouquet.

title: Perfect size for 15 inch laptop
text: This fit in front of kiddos 15" laptop perfectly. I put his laptop on a cooler because it was getting to hot, but that raised it up off the desk enough it was bothering him. This was a perfect solution.

title: Subtantial and well made
text: Nice set, I love metal rulers. The wood and plastic ones tend to get dinged and not keep a straight line. Kiddo already claimed the flat one for school. These feel sturdy and not all thin bendy like some cheaper sets.

title: Great rug protector
text: My desk chair was tearing up the rug in the office, this has solved the problem. Although now I roll so easily I keep banging into stuff lol.

title: Great for the price
text: This is a nice office staple, and also good to have on hand for the school projects that seem to pop up out of the blue. These are basic old school binders with the round shaped ring and the plastic sleeve in the front to slide a cover page on. They seem pretty durable for the price, great size for a presentation.

title: Adorable
text: So cute and display worthy. Came just in time for my cousins baby shower, many ooos and ahhhs over how it pops up, I love this new line of cards.

title: Cute but overpriced at $13
text: Charming and something nice to send that isn't just a basic card. Displays well on the mantle. I did ding a star for the price, $13 for a greeting card is a bit much. I mean this is nice but thats pushing it.

title: Not the most durable, but well priced
text:
If it wasn't for the low price I'd give these 3 stars instead of 4. But for the price they are a good value. These are not rugged or for extended use. These will get you through the semester/school year, but that's about it. Very thin and I was a bit disappointed that the colors weren't more varied, about half look very similar.

However, there are a ton and they are very well priced.

title: Nice sized and easy to read, keys are meh
text:
This is a nice calculator with some great features.. etc etc etc. As far as doing math and being able to see the keys it is wonderful. The price is nice to.

However the keys feel wobbly. It is easy to miskey if you are going quickly as they lean to either side. This is not a calculator that you go oooooo over and want to just keep clicking away. However, it is a good value for the price.

title: Good value, paper is a little thin
text: Decent basic notepads. I did find the paper to be a little thin, but not unbearably so. Great for the price.

title: So fun!
text: Absolutely adorable, I can't wait to send it out this year. Great Hallmark quality, so cheery. Love it!

title: So cute, great value
text: One of my all time favorite cards. Considering it stands up and works as a cute little display the $5.99 isn't bad. Ugh some of those annoying singing ones are sticker shock if you aren't expecting it when you get up to the cash register. Luckily not only does this NOT sing but its well priced.

title: Smaller than expected, but a nice little card.
text: Sweet little card. I say little because it is only 4.5"x5.5". Making it a bit smaller than a typical full sized greeting card. Otherwise it's good Hallmark quality.

title: nice and bright
text: These are nice and brightly colored. I think they are good value for how many you get, although the paper isn't quite as nice as post-its. The adhesive is decent. This is a good bargain buy.

title: Nice matte finish for easy writing and printing
text:
These were nice quality. I liked the matte finish, ink dries faster and doesn't smear like it does with a glossier finish. The box they come in is terrible for storage though. Doesn't really lend itself to re-closure, which kinda stinks. The name tags themselves stayed stuck on kiddo and I this afternoon without coming off. When I did pull them off they came off cleanly.

Lastly and maybe most importantly, they are a standard size and proved no problem using the Avery print site and also Microsoft Office Word templates (I used Avery 5395 as the template).

Hope that helps!

title: Pricey but well received by my car enthusiast husband
text:
I got this free to review and thought it was adorable. I loved pop up stuff as a kid, back in the days when it was crape paper and super flimsy. So I was pleasantly surprised to see that in the past few years (err decades) they have upped their game in the popup card world.

Hubby loves old cars, much to my dismay. Not that I hate the cars themselves, but ugh our garage will be a mess full of car parts and tools and an old '56 Chevy till the end of days... This card did not disappoint, he got a kick out of it, enough it got tucked into his bottom desk drawer where he squirrels away sentimental stuff he thinks I don't know he stashes. Hehe.

I did dock a point when I saw the price... $13, eeek. I mean it's a nice card but yeowch that is pricey. Half that price would be a better value. It's all paper, it's not like it revs or makes sounds when you open it. If it did all that maybe...

title: Love having these on hand
text:
Nice little notes of "you can do it".

Some of the cards are obviously geared more for kids but not all of them. I like to send things like this to my grandma when she is worried about a procedure or friends going through a stresser (job change, etc). Just a little thing that lets them know they are being thought of. Anyway this was a great well-priced assortment.

title: Beautiful
text: These are even prettier in person, the product pics do not do them justice. They come with kraft paper color envelopes that self seal.

title: Great generic cards for those oops moments
text: What I love most about these cards is they are not age or gender specific. I have a 7 yr old and we get invited to kid parties and I can't tell you how often I forget the card. Now I don't have to worry, boy/girl 8yrs old or 80yrs old, I'm covered.

title: They are clear once you put stuff in them
text: I got these and was immediately disappointed. I was like oh great all my stuff is going to be blurry and hard to see, because they aren't 100% clear. Then I put a doc in it and poof like magic totally was fine. Like other reviewers, I question the "heavy-duty" descriptor, but otherwise these seemed to be as described.

title: Binding damaged, Liquid glitter cover not a good idea for backpacks
text:
[[VIDEOID:e5ec7358b2f2bae9c0417b56685a52e5]] Nice journaling size at 8x6inches, but that cover is just an accident waiting to happen. They weren't kidding when they said liquid-filled. The cover isn't that thick and it's not going to take much to cause a leak. Fortunately it comes off easily, as its just a book sleeve, but what you are left with is just a pale pink boring journal.

Sadly, the binding on mine came already half detached, which does not bode well for longevity. I love the built in ribbon place keeper. Honestly, if it were a bit sturdier it would have been a lovely journal. As it is though, its a meh 3 stars.

title: Great Minecraft party favors
text: Huge hit as party favors at kiddos Minecraft birthday party!

title: Great buy for journaling
text: [[VIDEOID:1cb05001ddf74428de4bed7d2cb4c194]] I bought this to journal in and it’s so beautiful and well made! I love the soothing glitter effect and the pretty ribbon to save your page. My little one loved mine so much I ordered one for them as well!

title: Super fun and glittery!
text: My daughter absolutely LOVES this notebook! It’s super glittery and you can move the glitter around because it’s in water. I will definitely be buying more for next year.

title: All the fluid leaked out before arrival.
text: It came with a hole in it and had leaked the liquid out all over the box. So a lot of the pages were wet. My daughter just took the whole cover off and is still going to try and use it. But it was disappointing that it came already pretty ruined unfortunately.

title: No liquid in cover
text: There was no liquid in the plastic… it was just glitter stuck to the cover with plastic over it. Not fun for a 6 year olds gift….

title: Horrible journal
text: The gel was dry and lumpy, ordered a replacement item and received a other journal in the same horrible condition. Worse purchase ever. DO NOT PURCHASE!!!!!

title: Lots of beautiful cards!
text: Gorgeous cards! This set of cards is of good quality and they are beautiful too! In this day and age there’s always someone I know fighting an illness and these cards are great for spreading warm wishes and healing vibes. You get so many in the pack too!

title: Perfect fit, nice, bright ink
text: When I first installed these in my HP Envy I got a message that said the cartridges were recycled but compatible (I can’t remember the exact wording.) They fit perfectly and work great. The ink is nice and bright! Very happy with these.

title: Works well, wish it charged
text: I really misunderstood this listing but that’s my fault. I thought that this was a chargeable pencil sharpener, but it’s not. You can keep it plugged in via USB or keep batteries in it. But it doesn’t charge. That was a bit disappointing, but I guess it’s just the way I read the item details. Anyway, the sharpener works well nonetheless. It’s a homeschool staple for us.

title: Can’t make it work
text: The directions are straightforward and easy to follow. The app is also simple and easy. However, when it came to the actual printing, nothing happened. A blank sheet of paper came out every time. I can’t get it to work. I’m following the instructions, so I can only assume that the machine is malfunctioning. Disappointing.

title: My new must-have!
text: I ordered these disposable towels because I can never find a clean washcloth in this house. They work so great for taking off makeup and washing my face. They have a bit of a texture for grabbing dirt and oil. They’re incredibly soft, so much better for my sensitive skin than a washcloth. I’m going to order these again and again. I don’t think I can live without them!

title: Lovely Notebook Set!
text: This spiral bound hard-backed floral notebook set from XYark did not disappoint. I love the handy and portable A5 size and the college rule line spacing is perfect for writing and note taking. Both the cover and the spiral coil feel sturdy and well-made. The paper inside isn’t the best quality but it’s not bad at all for what I’m going to use it for. This set could be purchased to use on your own or it could even be given as a gift.

title: Great price!
text: I have lots of fancy handmade journals but I wanted something a little less expensive that I could really write and doodle in and not feel like it had to look perfect. I love this little journal. The pink color is so cute and the elastic closure is handy. It also has a good feel with the buttery soft covering. There’s an envelope on the very back page that has some extra stickers and tabs that goes along with it. I got a little giggle out of the typo on the front paper. I can only assume they meant “legendary.” Great value notebook!

title: They stay put!
text: These lined 5 x 8 sticky notes are perfect! I love the pastel colors and they’re very sticky and stay put. They even came with these neon sticky tabs that sort of feel like ultra thin plastic and look translucent. Can’t wait to mark my pages with those. Very happy with these large sticky notes!

title: My desk is clear and organized!
text: This desk organizer with accessory storage looks great on my desk. The rose gold color is a bit more pink than gold but I actually like the way it looks. It’s easy to set up and the drawer works really well. I like that it comes with the extra pencil cup. Great for organizing desks or any cluttered surfaces.

title: Works Great!
text: I ordered this to use for my son’s chores. I like how there are several options for displaying—magnetic, table display, and a little hook for hanging it on the wall. I chose the wall hanging method and it works great for us. Wipes clean easily too!

title: Inky!
text: These gel pens are smooth and oh so sparkly! I love the continuous inky line. Doesn’t skip.

title: Really Cute Card
text: These cards are adorable and my mom even ordered some after I sent one to her. Good buy!

title: Beautiful, great value
text: This is a beautiful, floral stationary set with a lot of little bits included for the price. It would make a lovely gift for those old school types of people who still like to send letters and thank you notes. I thought the stickers were a nice added touch. This box is a great value.

title: Great product!
text: I ordered these because I’m so tired of damaged walls in our house! I like the brushed nickel and they’re super easy to install. The price is very fair to preserve your walls! Great product!

title: Amazing Quality!!!
text: My husband does role playing games and this is the perfect journal for his game master persona. It is breathtakingly beautiful and very well made with such an attention to detail. The paper is thick and pulpy and the old looking latch adds to its middle earth appeal. I absolutely love this thing!! It comes with this fancy pen but mine was broken on the inside. I’m not even sad about it because I wasn’t expecting it anyway and the journal is so perfect I couldn’t be happier.

title: Good Value
text: These are perfect to store and organize collectible cards. My nerdy husband has an abundance and it will be nice to have them put away finally. The clear plastic is sturdy and just like what I expected and it’s slotted to fit a three ring binder. Good value.

title: So cute and fun!
text: These little notebooks are so much fun! I love Yoobi and how they give to classrooms. The little zipper pocket opens smoothly and the pouch is large enough for pens or pencils and erasers. Love these adorable notebooks!

title: Great Grip!
text: This is such a cute pencil set for young kids. The ladybug sharpener is so adorable and works well. My first grader has some issues with his motor skills and these help him to grip the pencils properly. I’d recommend these for anyone!

title: Pretty and Functional
text: When I ordered this I thought it was green and white but apparently I’m blind because it’s clearly pink and green. I don’t mind the pink at all and this organizer is nice looking and does just what I need it to. I work from home and I’m always losing things so this is a great way to keep it all together.

title: Fun and Inspiring Cover
text: I think this notebook looks better in person. It’s hard to tell how pretty it actually is from the picture, but trust me, it’s gorgeous! The mesmerizing cover is just the thing for inspiring creative thoughts to write within. I also really love that the company gives back to schools. Very happy with this product!

title: Makes Note Taking Fun!
text: I work from home and there's nothing like good old fashioned pen and paper to keep my tasks and to-do lists in order. I know it probably doesn't make much sense, but if I have a fun, nice looking notebook I'm apt to get more accomplished. I love the college rule spacing and the all the interesting doodles. Very happy with this product!

title: Smooth and blendable
text: Great colors and great pencils. They are very smooth and blendable. Also the design keeps them from rolling off the table. These would be great for adult coloring books.

title: Pink, glittery and lined pages. What’s not to love!
text:
The glitter cover appears to be well made (so hoping) but more for a teenage girl. However,
I needed a book to keep a hard copy of various information and the $ was good.
Overall, pleased with the purchase. Good price for a sturdy backed lined journal.

title: A little sparkle to learning
text: Bought this along with the pink one for my kids for back to school. Prettier than pictured and they love it. Will certainly bring a better start to an otherwise different school year. Would definitely recommend purchasing

title: My go to pens, with refills.
text: These are my go to pens. There are so many colors as well as refills just incase you run out of one color which I like. Great set of pens for the money.

title: Very cute
text: Super cute, moving glitter journal.. I am super excited to use for writing. I also want to add that this has a ribbon bookmark so you don't lose your page which is a plus for me. I will be buying another.

title: Not worth it
text: Too expensive for quality of product.  Ended up returning it

title: Convenient, pretty, quality ink
text:
As for the cartridge, these will fit all Waterman pens, and to my experience, all pens that take a standard cartridge. It’s important to note this is not reversable. Not all standard cartridges can work with Waterman pens. The barrel for some (not all) of the Waterman pens is a little thin for some (not all) of the standard cartridges on the market. You can put these into a longer pen end to end to have a spare on hand. I do this all the time with my Mont Blanc. For the Waterman Lady Charlotte, to my knowledge this is the only compatible cartridge and I’ve never found a compatible converter. To refill that, this is your only option.

These are convenient to just throw in your bag or briefcase and have spare ink on the go. I’ve taken this in a backpack full of books to college, I’ve taken them in a purse on airplanes, I’ve even thrown them in my gym bag next to my sneakers, and I’ve never had one rupture or give me any trouble at all.

The barrel is soft enough to squeeze. Yes, I know that’s a bad way to start the pen. Yes, I know you can flood the nib that way. For me, sometimes, that’s the only way I can actually get a pen I’ve let sit for over a decade to write again. I like that this provides that option as a court of last resort.

As to the ink, this is a beautiful shade of blue. Waterman has limited its line (as least at the time of this writing) to sensible colors one might find in the office. There is purple and brown and that’s about as crazy as it gets. This particular color is fine for any professional setting and is easy on the eyes for long writing sessions.

It's not water resistant or archival. To my knowledge only Dokumentus and some (not all) of the Noodler’s line are, but those only come in a bottle. That’s the main trade-off here. Cartridges give you convenience and converters give you options. That said, I’ve used Waterman ink for decades and I’ve not noticed any fading, even looking back at things I wrote in the 90s, unless I left the thing for weeks at a time in direct sunlight. If you’re writing a letter to go in a time capsule to be opened in a hundred years or more, you might have an issue. Or, well, whoever opens the time capsule might. For more mundane purposes you’ll be fine.

I should also add, some of the waterproof, archival inks, while perfectly fine in newer pens, aren’t totally safe for some (not all) vintage pens. This is. If you have a very old Waterman, you are probably best off with this or the same ink from a bottle. And if you have a lighter-colored pen, those waterproof inks are hard to clean off if they get on the barrel. Generally, any stain with those will be harder to clean. This is easy to clean off the outside of the barrel and somewhat easier to remove overall. There are always trade-offs.

It's also important to note that some cheaper inks can damage a pen beyond repair, which, when you’re using a $10 pen is one thing, and quite another when a replacement will cost you hundreds of dollars. This is a good, safe option for a prized pen.

The ink dries quickly, which is good for left-handed people using a left to right system like English, right-handed people using a right to left system like Hebrew, situations where you’re going quickly from page to page, and drawing. Noodlers has one that dries faster, but only slightly, and again, trade-offs.

Overall, if you want a nice ink, safe for your pen, in a convenient cartridge you’re sure will work for your pen, you found it.

title: Sturdy; well made
text:
These are cute.

The key thing to remember is that the bookmark is 2x6 measured to the outer edge. The inner pocket is a smidge smaller. Maybe trim the photo insert to 1.75 x 5.75 to get it to look nice. That’s the measurements I use and it’s fine with that. These are sized well enough you can fit photo paper, 140-pound watercolor paper, or cardstock without an issue. I didn’t try anything thicker than that.

The tassels are sturdy. They are easy to attach and they’re not prone to falling apart or shedding.

This makes for a fun, quick project and a great way to show off your best photos, especially landscapes, paintings, and lettering or calligraphy projects.

title: Great ink, fresh cartridges
text:
These fit the Pentel pocket brush pen, no problem. The cartridges came completely filled -- no signs of them sitting around and evaporating. The ink flows well, is quite dark, and is waterproof. I've used gouache and acrylic on top of it once in a while. This provides a nice amount of ink, though granted because of how much is used at a time if you're using it as a sketch pen, it will run out quickly, so it's nice that this comes with so many.. As a calligraphy pen, a single cartridge lasts quite long time. The packaging is sturdy, so no chance of a stray cartridge falling out of the box in transit.

The only downside I see as, as far as I know, this comes only in black. If you want variety of color, you need to look to a different pen. Kuretake makes some great ones, but they are far more expensive. This is partly an issue of the brush pen. It's not compatible with any converters, which would have solved this issue, and partly an issue with the ink not being offering in a greater variety.

title: Great pencils, but using the indicator is tricky.
text:
[[VIDEOID:a4997719ad2db3246f3784cfcf1ffae6]] This has a nice grip, making it comfortable for long writing or drawing sessions.

There is a small indicator near the tip where you can keep track of what type of lead you have loaded. It has indicators for 2B, B, HB, and H. Granted, Pentel has 4B in their Ain Stein line, but there is but so much room on the circumference of a pencil, and these are the most common degrees. To change it, you twist the pencil, but that will loosen the tip, so it will be easy for that to slip off whatever you set it to. You need to hold it in place, and tighten just the small tip to secure it back again. Screw the entire thing off, set it, and screw it back on once and you'll see what I'm talking about. Or watch the attached video. That this isn't immediately obvious (or at least wasn't to me) is the only thing I don't like about these pencils.

It comes with 3 HB leads preloaded, so you'll want to pick up refills. I recommend their Ain Stein, and as of the time of this writing, Amazon offers a variety pack in terms of degrees of hardness.

I like that the end retracts fully, not just the lead but the more fragile tip. Simply press on the clip as though to attach it to something and it will retract. This helps protect the pencil from damage while in transit. Press down the click top to extend it again. The clip sports a strong spring loading mechanism, making it great for clipping onto something.

These come in 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9 mm and I love them all.

title: Great for smaller books
text: As advertised, these are quite small. They aren't great for the larger books I have, those hardcovers or technical books that approximate the size of a textbook. For mass market paperbacks they're absolutely perfect. I've never seen a metal bookmark like this that fits so nicely in those. The craftsmanship is fine. I didn't see any bent, chipped, or damaged in any way. The loops for holding dangles are strong and secure.

title: Limited edition, beautiful, writes and draws wonderfully
text:
This is my second of these. I picked up a medium nib and liked it so well I picked up a fine nib as well. I'm surprised these are still in shock as they are a limited edition from I think two years ago at the time of this writing and those tend to sell out quickly. Both of this year's Al-Stars, released maybe two weeks ago, are already out of stock, at least for the time being. I'm glad this one is still available though. I like it. I hope it one becomes part of their staple lineup.

The Lamy Safari are popular among the urban sketch crowd and the ink drawing crowd because of the clean line they put down, the low price, and the comfortable grip. They're good drawing pens as well as writing pens and I use them for both constantly.

The only things I don't like is that the converter is sold separately. Amazon tends to carry them, so at least they're convenient to pick up. The ink cartridges are proprietary, and while they come in some amazing colors, and Amazon has some nice multi-color sets on offer most of the time, it would have been nice to use those amazing colors in other pens and use other cartridges in these pens. But that's a nit pick.

The Lamy Safari is a go-to pen for me, and this is one of the better colors.

title: Study, problem free
text: This is a trouble-free brush. I've bought it a few times because I lost one and gave away two, but I have never had one break or give me any problems. It's good for a large surface. It doesn't shed. It doesn't give me issues. Honestly, it's a tool I hardly think about. It does what it needs to do so easily and so invisibly that I don't have to pay it any attention, which is ideal.

title: Nice, a little trouble to get it started, packaging not as pictured
text:
It didn't come in the packaging photographed. I understand why they need to use their own packaging, but in that case they should photograph their own packaging. I am dinging a star for that, as it impacts how giftable this is.

After installation it was spotty at first. There were missing lines and white streaks throughout the printout. I reached out to Epson and they suggested run the nozzle head check and cleaning the print heads four times in a row, and if that doesn't work wait six hours and do it again. I tried that and after the fourth cleaning it worked perfectly. I can't say for sure that's a problem with the ink, and I'm certainly not dinging a star for that, but in case it is, and it case it happens to you, that's how to fix it. I should add that relatively minor inconvenience is the worst of it.

After getting everything sorted, this was wonderful. The ink prints beautifully, doesn't smear easily, and lasts a very long time. I'm using this for printing photos, printable junk journals, and large maps for a D&D campaign.

title: Fun, reliable pen. The go to for urban sketchers everywhere.
text:
This is my second time buying one of these because I love this one and somehow, despite the bright red color, managed to lose the first one.

This is the go to pen for urban sketchers. It's not the only pen capable of what this does, so I'm not sure why it's so ubiquitous, but it is certainly a capable pen. It lays down a good line without skipping. The ink flow is excellent. The ergonomics are great for a comfortable hand. Perhaps that's the reason, that comfortable grip. This is commonly used as a school pen in Europe to teach kids their handwriting exactly because it's so easy comfortable and well balanced, making it easier than say something with a hooded nib where you need to mind where you grip it. In any case, for writing or drawing this is a favorite of mine for a few reasons.

One, that nice ink flow. Sadly, these don't come with converters and the ink cartridge is proprietary, but there are a lot of options on the cartridges and the converters aren't that expensive and are readily available on Amazon.

Two, the colors. These are fun pens in an assortment of awesome colors, from grey and silver and black to mango, strawberry, pink, and lilac. They look great. Mind the lighter colors don't stain from the ink however. I have to clean my mango and cream pens fairly regularly.

Three, the comfort. For a long session these are great.

Fourth, the line. It's hard to find an extra fine in the US. Amazon typically has them, usually through a third party, but last I heard Lamy wasn't directly importing them. The bold is a huge line, great for signatures and the like. The extra fine is close to a Japanese fine. It's not the thinnest line I've seen. Pilot Namiki takes the prize there. But it's nice. I like the fine and medium points as striking a decent balance between precision and weight.

The craftsmanship makes these an excellent writing experience in an affordable pen. If this is your first fountain pen, you won't be disappointed. There are a lot of other entry level pens on the market at this price point that leak, skip, and won't give you nearly as good an experience.

title: Super soft. Easy to blend.
text:
My main concern with these was the ability to sharpen them. Anything 6B and softer can be hard to sharpen. I’m finding a few of my electric sharpeners, in particular the Staples branded (Amazon lists it as Staples 356332) can handle these without being pencil eating monsters, but as expected, several others, and most of my manual sharpeners, just break the point as they go. Sharpening by knife, if done carefully, also works.

The graphite is super dark, and an absolute joy to draw with. It smudges perfectly, and is extremely easy to blend. I am having a lot of fun with it. This is capable of extremely deep, dark shadows, and it's not that hard to use a light hand and get a lighter color with these, which makes it very easy to blend soft gradients. I did the trick of rubbing it against a sanding block to get dust charcoal, and it’s outstanding for that. I was able to easily tone a paper to the darker edge of medium with this, no problem.

These are a joy, and I might bring them to my next urban sketching outing this spring as little gifts for my art friends. I bet they’ll love them.

title: For the James Bond in your life
text:
Ever need to build a perfectly level piece of furniture, defend yourself in hand to hand combat, then stylishly write your memoir? Then this is the tool for you. I can barely think of any common sense situation where you need a tungsten tip, a level, a screwdriver, and a fountain pen in the same tool. Now for odd or cool factor, this rules. I plan to bring it to DnD.

The level is perfectly readable as is the ruler. The ruler so much so you could use it to sight measure for drawing, especially if you're doing a pen and ink drawing. There are four different rulers and I've included photos because aside from centimeters and inches I'm not sure what the rest are.

The screwdrivers are small, but large enough for fixing say a spinning wheel. A little too large for eyeglasses. About right for computers. You could add an SSD to your PS5 and check the TV stand is level all with the same pen.

The stylus is for the iPad tablet world. It won't work on something like the Kindle Scribe or the convertible HP laptops. It works well for its intended devices. I can use it for drawing in Procreate on the iPad.

The attack tip feels sharp. I can assert it can crack a walnut open. I don't know what else I'll ever use it for. Or at least I assume it's an attack tip. It's advertised as a feature and it feels as hard and sharp as the attack tips on pens at the local martial arts store.

The pen itself writes nicely one you start it. It comes with six cartridges and a piston converter. I'd put the nib at European medium. It flows well, no skipping, no leaking. Put it down for a while and it still flows perfectly. Because of the of extra functions of the pen, it's a screw cap and you can't post it.

Overall, I love the fun factor here. I'm not sure I'll actually use it for more than a pen, maybe a ruler for art.

title: Tons of ink
text: They aren't kidding on the size of this. So far I've gone through about a thousand pages and it hasn't given up the ghost yet. It costs more than many other cartridges, but it prints so much more it's worth it. I like not having to change the cartridge. It just prints and that makes me happy.

title: Great
text: This ink is easy to install, long lasting, and good quality. It's expensive as inks go, but that's true of all Epson inks so far as I can tell. The number of pages you can print on one cartridge makes up the difference.

title: No issues
text: Huge journal, well made. No problems I could find. The binding is good. There isn't any significant bleeding. I needed something with a lot of pages and this fit the bill perfectly. I'll be buying more of the same. It's great.

title: Versitile
text:
This fits on the larger Scribbles that Matter (B5) with no issue. It fits on a standard A5 notebook, no problem. It is elastic enough to work on a B6, but I feel like it looks too big on that. The issue is not functional, but asthetic.

The pen loop is identical in size to the STM. It's close in color to their teal as well, making this an excellent pairing. I am able to fit a Lamy or similar size pen in there wihtout a problem, or a smaller Bic size pen if I use the cap to grip the loop, but a simple #2 pencil is too loose.

The clip expands an impressive amount and on a lark I tried clipping a pad of 50 sheets of illustration paper. It holds and does so securely. The small pocket is too small to hold a check (for anyone who rememebers those) without folding it. It is large enough for a business card or credit card, but there isn't a lot of space to hold much and the more you put in the pocket, the less you can put in the clip. I would have added an opening along the side rather than this pocket. It would be more practical in terms of being longer and out of the way of the clip.

It's elegant. It has excellent craftsmanship. It's really nice. I can see this as a permanent addition to my bullet journal.

title: Much stronger than I thought it would be
text: This is much better than I thought it would be. I’m following a YouTube video on making a box for a journal, and the way the wooden lid is attached to the wooden box is to use a strip of this as a hinge. I thought that was crazy, but with this brand at least it actually works. It’s surprisingly strong, adheres well, and is easy to use. I’m a lot more impressed with this than I thought I’d be.

title: There are better options for less
text:
I didn’t read carefully enough and thought it was going to be A5 based on the price point. It is actually the smaller A6. I won’t ding it for that. It was my misreading.

This is slightly lower in quality than the smaller Moleskien notebooks and about twice the price. It’s the same quality cover and paper. The closure elastic is about the same as is the bookmark. This has a three-page table of contents in the front and a pocket on the outside of the front cover. Moleskein has a more secure pocket on the inside back cover with the opening pointed towards the spine. Both has perforated pages towards the back.

I found this disappointing.

title: Beginner Friendly
text:
I'm fairly new to using book binding cloth. I mostly do sewn junk journals, Copic stitch books, and mini scrapbook albums, and I'm trying to branch out. I found this to be easy to work with. It cuts easily. I can mark it with a pencil no problem (I went with a 2B for a darker line). It takes glue cleanly and easily and it doesn't warp or twist in on itself. I would say the feel is similiar to quilting cotton in terms of how easy it is to get it to lay flat.

At the very least I can say it is pleasant to work with and beginner friendly.

title: Convenient and well designed
text:
This comes with a straight needle, a curved needle, an awl, and a sampler amount of waxed bookbinding thread. If you’re considering this as a gift for a child, they will need more thread after one or two projects. While it comes with some instructions, they are inadequate. There are so many videos online on YouTube or on dozens of crafting educational sites, it hardly constitutes a problem for most users. Just something to be aware of. If the goal is to reduce screen time, there are ample books on the subject.

The single row of holes has a slight indentation in the shape of a V. This makes lining up the spine of the book so much easier if you’re doing something like a junk journal where you’re sewing through the spine rather than side stitching.

The main body of three holes has a bar that can hold the pages secure for popping the pattern you want, again making the task much easier.

Is this strictly necessary for bookbinding? No. I’ve done many projects already without it. Does it make the project easier and help you get better results? Absolutely. Having moved to using it, I would not want to move back.

title: Best of breed
text:
I went low end last time I bought a paper cutter and ended up wasting time and money. I should have just bought a Fiskars from the start. This cuts well, even through cardstock. The guideline makes it easy to line up exactly where the cut will happen. Replacing the blade is quick and simple. The measuring lines on the board clean and easy to read.

If I were to complain about anything, it’s that the arm for measuring is a bit stiff and hard to fully extend. That’s the worst of it. Everything else is perfect.

title: It can’t cut typing paper
text: I know I need to press down to release the safety blade. This can’t cleanly cut typing paper. If you start in the middle it works sometimes. If you start off the page and try to cut through, it tears up the edge. It’s the worst paper cutter I’ve ever seen.

title: Better than I'd hoped
text:
I’m using these to print maps for a D&D campaign and there is so much to love.

First, the paper is stored in a resealable hard cardboard box, which is important here, because who uses a hundred sheets of this at a time? The box seals securely with a tab in slot closure and makes this easy to store.

Second, the paper is much thicker and nicer than standard printer paper. It feels like good map paper, or if you remember the paper coloring book style placemats we had at diners as kids it’s similar to that. It’s sturdy and substantial.

Third, it’s a good matte finish. It could have supported a glossy finish with the weight of this paper, but that would not have worked for me.

A few ends were dinged in transit, but they straightened right out by simply going through the printer.

I don’t foresee running out of this any time soon, but when I do, I’m picking up more of the same.

title: Really nice mini pens
text:
They write well. They won't last as long as a full size pen. That's true of any pen this size. There simply isn't as much room for ink. Compared to other pens of this size, they're a bit above average. They don't feel comfortable for long writing sessions, but again that's a factor of the size and it can't be avoided.

They are beautiful. They are exceedingly compact. The main reason I bought them was for a sort of joke gift for my D&D group, little "portable office" projects using the Club Scrap pattern and made from these pens and a manila tag as the main items. They needed to be small and cute and they are. For my purposes, they were perfect. I have seen some with a chain to put on a keychain, which adds a bit to the portable factor, but if that's not a feature you need, then there are fabulous.

title: Fabulous
text:
It’s fantastic.

The side pocket, closed with a snap, is large enough to hold a spare legal pad and plenty of pages. I was able to get two pads in there with a smidge of space to spare.

On the left side, the top zippered pocket ends at the sew line. Personally, I’d have preferred it go all the way down, and it feels like sewing the barrier there just wastes space, but if you want easy access to smaller items then it’s perfect.

The card pockets are just large enough to make sliding things in and out easy without causing wear on the padfolio, but no so large as to worry anything will fall out.

The cable wires are taut enough to use for storing pencils or pens without a clip and they won’t fall out. The top one is the better one for that as the bottom will come into contention with the snap. It’s functional for it, but not as good.

The business card holder can hold a deck of playing cards. It holds closed with a modest-strength magnet. The oval cutout is just a cutout, no plastic or anything to keep small items falling through if you want to use it for something like that.

The pencil holder in the spine isn’t as good a pencil holder as the cord holders. It’s a loose elastic band and will only work for writing implements you can clip on. A good old #2 isn’t going to do that.

The clip holds the pad securely, and the entire thing works perfectly laid back of folded open. I absolutely love it. It’s elegant, functional, and awesome.

title: Close securely and the chain seems sturdy enough
text:
All of them work, though I had to scribble a bit with one to get it started. They lay down a black line, not super rich in color, similar to what you’d see with a cheap bank pen. This is what I had expected.

They are perfectly small enough to fit on a keychain. And they close firmly enough not to fall off in your bag, briefcase, whatever. The chain that holds the pen is kind of thin, but sturdy enough for the purpose. I’m not worried about it breaking.

You can post the cap, which is great but a bit unexpected, since I would think the common use would be to keep the cap attached to the keychain while using the pen. But it is nice that that works.

The pens are reasonably comfortable for their size. They’re kind of cute. They’re convenient. They would make great stocking stuffers. Overall, nice pens.

title: The more convenient, higher quality technical pen from Rotring
text:
If you’re looking at this as a way to upgrade from the Microns, you’ve picked the right pen. Rotring offers two technical pens – the Isograph and the Rapidograph. AKA, the awesome pen and the stinking pile of why.
The Isograph is the one that refills with Rapidograph ink bottles. The Rapidograph, which does not take Rapidograph ink bottle refills, uses cartridges. The primary advantage of a cartridge over bottle filling in any other pen is the convenience of changing cartridges on the go. These are such a pain to try to take off, you really can’t just pop a new one in while sitting on a bus or whatever. What you can do is top off the Isograph’s ink supply before you leave, or refill the Isograph from the bottle, as that is neat and super easy. You drip the ink into the wide-mouth bladder from a needle tip applicator on the bottle.

Beyond the refill system, both pens behave the same and are common considered the best on the market (rightfully so). They lay down a smooth, clean line. They are precise, don’t leak, don’t give trouble, and work brilliantly.

About the only problem I’ve had with this is if I have it open for any length of time without using it (and here I mean two or three minutes) I have to close it and shake it to get the ink to flow again. But once I do, it’s fine, so I certainly can’t ding it a star for that.

Overall, while I still like the variety of colors I can have at hand all at once with the Microns, I love the smoothness and clean lines this pen can create. The 0.5 is a substantial line from a technical pen and I absolutely adore it.

title: Wothless garbage
text:
Where to start with all that is wrong with this thing. I guess, the first thing I should say is it wouldn’t even print after a few minutes, and I had to send it back. I got maybe two pages out of it, and then all I could get were error messages, including the one about the ink absorption pad. Two pages.

It doesn’t support airprint, by design. You have to use their app to print from your phone or tablet. It says it does on the Amazon page, or did at the time of this writing, but if you drill down to the footnote, it says that’s only on supported printers, which this is not.

It has no screen, so to get to the abundant error messages (really, this vomits error messages better than it does anything else) you need to go check them in the app. If you don’t have a phone and just want to use this for printing from PC, you might be out of luck if something goes wrong. I couldn’t find the messages on my laptop, but I didn’t look for very long. It’s not obvious at least.

About the only thing I liked about this printer is Amazon made returning it easy.

title: A Mighty Beast of a Printer
text:
There is so much to love here. A few issues, granted, but they are far from show-stoppers.

The first issue I have is with the print trays. There are technically three if you count the back. If you fill it with larger paper, say legal size, then the tray is forced to stick out from the machine. This is a trade-off to let me machine be otherwise more compact, and I can respect the decision. I put the legal paper is tray one (top front) and let the receiving tray cover it, which it does nicely. I put the letter-size paper in tray two (bottom front) and that closes completely. As far as I can tell looking at the menus the largest paper, the A3+, can only be loaded in the back tray. I’m fine with that, just surprised. I think the trays would be large enough, but the menus won’t allow for setting that size anywhere else.

The second issue is the weight. This is a fifty-pound monster. Taking it out of the box is listed as a two-person job.

I would have liked for this to support the mega printing ink tank option, but that might be asking a bit too much. To disagree with Nicocallie, yes it comes with ink, in standard-size cartridges as is typical for most printers, and yes the cartridges do last for a reasonable number of printouts. I printed a fifty-page document without a causing a substantial dent in the ink supply. I plan to replace with the XXL and XL cartridges, but for the standard size these seem to be about average.

Setup is simple. If you have an older app, it will ask to upgrade to the latest. The free upgrade is definitely worth it for the added ease and features. The app will recognize it and help connect it to wifi. After that, you can print single or double sided. It supports airprint. It supports email to print, and you can customize the email address. You can even trigger scanning a document via Siri. It lists the paper size alongside the printer tray for your convenience. It’s weird that you can’t put the ink in until mostly done with the setup, but that’s an oddity not an issue. It was smart enough to put setting up the fax until last, because let’s be honest, most users don’t do that anymore.

The print quality and speed are excellent. I’m impressed. It’s a surprisingly quiet printer. I triggered a printout, then thought something was wrong because I didn’t hear it go off from across the room.

This is a powerful monster of a printer. I love it.

title: Aside from the lack or remote printing, it's perfect
text:
The lack of remote printing is the biggest weakness of this printer. This is common in Canon printers, so far as I can tell. There is no option to email to the printer, as there is with Epson and HP. Yes, I recognize the lack of security in e-mail, but I email to print Spanish vocabulary lists and knitting patterns I found online. I thought perhaps the Selphy app (more on that later) might solve this, but no, if the tablet and printer are on different networks, the app won’t print.

The app is, itself, another weakness, except in one thing – setting the printer up on wifi. The app can easily connect to the printer, link to the wifi the tablet or phone is on, and simply ask for the password. After that, wait a moment and it’s done. On the downside, the app won’t let you swap between single and double sided printing on a document basis. This is handled with a simple option in Airprint (again, more in a moment). Most of the maintenance options in the app do nothing but redirect to the printer’s web page, which is a pain to log into as the login often fails for no clear reason. It’s easier to do it on the printer’s screen.

The maintenance on the printer’s screen, on the other hand, is quite simple and efficient. I’ll say the excellent design here easily offsets the flaws in the app.

The print quality is the biggest strength of this printer. I use this to print photos for a scrapbook, so I need a quality print, and this does an excellent job of it. The colors are good. The printing is clean and sharp. The printing is quite fast, especially when it’s just text.

The ink tanks are the main selling point here, and of course, they are excellent. They’re easier to fill than any I have had before. Simply press the bottle onto the ink chamber, let the chamber break the seal on the bottle and it will make a solid seal and the ink will flow right down. The chambers each hold an entire refill bottle, and for the black ink especially, that’s quite large.

I have seen some modern Canon printers with the same mega tank capabilities that, for no clear reason, can’t support Airprint. To anyone who has any concerns about that, this supports Airprint with no issues.

I have seen some modern Canon printers that advertise being capable of double-sided printing, but the execution of such is that the user is instructed to print the first side, take the paper out, turn it around and print the other side. Granted, this is double sided, but I’d argue every printer is capable of that sort of double-sided printing. This printer handles it properly in the classic sense of it pulls the paper back in by itself to print the reverse side.

This printer is not without its flaws, but I would say on balance it is excellent. If remote printing is critical, you might look elsewhere, but if you are only going to print while on the same network, there is a lot to recommend this one.

title: Meticulous attention to detail
text:
They come packaged securely enough that even the 6B isn’t broken. Woodless pencils are prone to snapping in half or worse if you drop them. The softer the pencil, the greater the risk. 6B is kind of fragile, so the fact that these are consistently intact on arrival is impressive. They’re smart. That one is never on the end. It means they’re not in the pack in order, but sides, where there is a greater risk of impact, is where the HB and 2B sit. The 4B and 6B are protected between these two. It’s that kind of attention to detail that makes these so excellent.

These are amongst my favorite woodless pencils for a few reasons. First, they lay a good line. I haven’t encountered any rough spots with these where the graphite seems off. I have with other brands.

Second, they’re labelled. I know that’s a small thing, but it helps when you’re trying to get a sketch done quickly to know at a glance what kind of pencil you have at hand. And again, it’s that meticulous attention to detail. Yes, the label is on the far end, furthest from the point. Would you expect anything else?

These are quite simply perfect.

title: Lovely, but thin
text:
These are decent. My main concern with these is that they seem thin and flimsy, especially since I use them for junk journals. I need a little more heft in my materials. These are somewhat see through. If I put an index card written in a black ink inside for example I can read it through the envelope.

The adhesive is weak, but acceptable for making and people using them for crafting are likely to just use bookbinding glue.

They measure exactly 8.75 x 5.75.

They’re good, not great.

title: Sturdy, but too thin to use as flashcards
text:
The thing I liked least is that these are substantially thinner than I expected. They’re pretty transparent, so they’re no good for flashcards. I wasn’t planning to use them for flashcards, but enough people do that I’m dinging them a star for that. There is definite bleeding and ghosting with these.

They have a cold press texture, which is odd. I’m used to a smoother finish for index cards. Not a negative or a positive, just an observation.

They are well made, and for my purposes they score well, and they hold together in a handmade scrapbook perfectly, despite being so thin. I was able to accordion fold one as an insert to then glue panels to. It is sturdy enough for the purpose.

title: Top quality
text:
I go back to this brand over and over because I’m always satisfied with the results. These feed into the laminator no problem. They seal perfectly. They don’t crack. They don’t peel. They don’t give me any trouble. I have never run into a bad pouch.

The inside seam is even, making it easy to use it to level whatever you want to put in. I use this primarily for photos, but occasionally I laminate index cards as part of a D&D campaign. It can handle either with no issue.

The box is sturdy enough to use for easy storage for a long time. Honestly, I’m getting tired of some products like this that can’t be stored in the box they came in. This doesn’t give that problem.

title: Good at this price point
text:
These are great at the price point. If you’re looking for the parchment with the dried out feel and distressed edges that makes a crinkling sound when you fold it, the stuff you get at the high-end shops at the renn faire, this isn’t it. If you’re looking for nice paper that you can use in your D&D campaign for notices and letters, that has the appearance of parchment and adds a cool factor but doesn’t break the bank, this is it.

It feathers a little, I think by design. That’s actually a plus here as it lends to the authenticity of parchment. It doesn’t bleed. It can handle being put through an ink jet printer no problems. It has a smooth hand. I like that the edges are tinted and the center is lighter, easier to use.

You can take a distressing tool to the edges for a more authentic, aged look. It handles that no problem and looks pretty good.

title: Streamlined, inexpensive, sturdy and strong
text:
This is good at punching through a stack of pages at once. I maxed out at 15 and I think it can go more, I just didn’t have more I needed to do.

It has a clean lineup bar. It opens easily to clean out the punch dots. It punches cleanly, no hanging bits.

It’s small enough for easy storage and strong enough for most everyday uses. This one is a great buy. I like it.

title: Quality is great; quantity is not as advertised
text:
As has been pointed out, the count falls shy of the advertised 180. I got 144 envelopes and 156 cards. The quality of the envelopes is excellent. I measure them at 3”x4.5”. They are thick enough to handle some wet media without a problem like a light bit of watercolor or an acrylic impression from a gelli plate. Not much more than that.

The cards are light cardstock with rounded corners. They come in at 2.75” by 4.25”. They can handle a decent amount of ink without bleeding. A fountain pen won’t bleed. A paint brush application of ink or a heavy use of marker might.

There is also a very cute set of raised stickers, gem shaped in a variety of sizes and colors, a dark grey dual-tip marker, a silver gel pen and a gold gel pen. The gel pens are fairly faint. The dual-tip has a fine bullet point and a chisel tip.

For my purposes, these are fine. The only issue, and the only thing costing it a star, is that it’s not the quantity advertised. For my project, it’s enough.

title: Excellent pens; the case has a host of crafting applications
text:
I’m going to start this with I’m not an architect. I bought this for sketching in Inktober, monsters and still lives, not blueprints. So I will be reviewing from the perspective of someone into arts and crafts. If you are into those, I’m going to assume you are into multiple crafts, and after I talk about the pens themselves, I will talk about how the features built into the box can be used for other types of crafting, because for me, this is a multi-crafting tool.

The pens make a useful mix of lines from extremely thin to a moderately fat line. If you’re coming at this from a fountain pen background, think a Japanese manufacturer’s extra fine (Namiki for example) is about the same as the .20 and a European manufacturer’s medium (Waterman; Mont Blanc; Lamy etc) compares well to the .50. The .30 reads like a Lamy fine to me. Side note, if you’re coming at this from a fountain pen background, you need to shake it to start it, which I know feels counterintuitive. The other counterintuitive bit is this doesn’t take cartridges. That would be the Rapidgraph pens.

The .20 needs quite a bit of shaking to get started. Once started the ink flows well, and I have seen no issues. It handles on a variety of surfaces, including rough press watercolor paper. I thought the rougher texture would give it issues, but it didn’t have any problems.

The pencil is nothing special. Just a normal 0.5 mechanical pencil. It comes with a pack of spare leads. It takes a common eraser as a replacement (similar to the Pentel). It does have a nice, comfortable grip.

The white plastic eraser is also not much of note for good or ill. It’s not my favorite, but it is serviceable.
The ink is nice. The bottle isn’t prone to leaking or spilling or making any kind of a mess. This is a dark, rich black ink. I like it. From what I’ve seen, Koh-I-Noor offers a greater variety of colors in their Rapidograph line.

It’s strange to praise the box it came in, but in this case, it’s warranted. First, there is a protractor. It’s squared at the corner and the angle lines go straight to the edge, so this is nice for something like marking a 45-degree cut for quilting or scrapbooking.
