Definitely higher in quality than I would have suspected from the price point.

I don't know why the description says calligraphy. It most definitely is not that.

title: Ample room
text:
It can fit the iPad Pro 12.9 inch, barely, but it fits.

There is a pocket in front for papers or whatnot. It's about 9 inches wide and 8 inches deep, approximately.

For the inner left side, there is a zipper compartment running along the top, about four inches deep. Lower down there is an open flap running the full width and roughly 7 inches deep. In front of that, there is a flapped compartment on the bottom left, large enough for an iPhone XS Max in its case and a similar pouch with no flap on the bottom right.

For the right hand side, There is a full size compartment in the back, suitable for most tablets. The iPad Pro 12.9 will fit without its case there. With it's case, it does not fit. In front of that is a smaller flap, perfectly sized for 8 1/2 x 11 paper.

In front of that is a pouch running all the way down, so about 7 inches. In front of that is a webbed pouch coming in around four inches. In the back is a zippered compartment that encompasses the entire side of the case.

The zippers are well made and secure. The handle is secure.

The bicycle logo in front is odd, but cute.

I'm going to see if they have one in a smaller size for the iPad Mini. This is a very useful case.

title: Great for hard to sharpen art pencils
text:
The bad. This thing requires four AA batteries, not included. The top is a little hard to get off to put them in.

And that's the sum total of everything wrong with the sharpener. Now for what's right.

It's a helix sharpener, which I've heard before is great for easily broken points. Whether that is true in general or not I cannot say, but I can say I had some Soft charcoal pencils this got done on the first go. I won't hold the first one I tried against it. It took two goes, but only after my hundred dollar Staples sharpener made a mess of it. I had some really hard to sharpen pastel pencils I couldn't even get right with an Xacto knife. Again, first try worked. So I can say with confidence that this particular sharpener is fabulous with hard to sharpen pencils.

It's relatively quiet, so I can sharpen my pencils while watching TV and still hear the dialog. I wouldn't do that with someone else in the room because it's distracting, but it's not too loud as some (cough, Staples, cough) sharpeners are.

It's clean. I don't get shavings until I open it to get the shavings, not even if I turn it upside down (I've been taking it along with me a lot). It can store quite a lot before it needs to be emptied. It's lightweight, and it fits in my travel kit. I've used it with Polychromos, Lyra, Luminance and Prismacolor successfully. It will not work with Caran D'Ache Museum Aquarelle, as those pencils are a bit fatter and won't fit in the hole.

title: I'm stunned at how awesome this journal is
text:
First, this is thick. Each page is substantial. In the picture, it has about half the pages of the purple hippo noto (500 pages) next to it, but is about two and a half times the thickness. The spiral notebook under it is 300 pages. That gives these pages a heft and a quality you don't often see in a journal. I'd say, page for page, it's about as thick as a mixed media sketchbook, though I haven't tested how well it handles wet media.

The pages are hand crafted, or at least seem that way to me, and they are yellowed for an antique look, but unevenly, as a book would normally yellow unevenly over time, so if you want to do very realistic work in them, understand the paper isn't entirely uniform. The pages are deckled, and beyond that, they are sewn in a little unevenly. This comes across as a design choice to enhance the experience of an old, hand sewn book. That said, they are quite secure with leather ties, which again, plays to the old hand sewn book motif.

The binding strap is very secure and really cute. I love playing with it.

I hope these are available forever. I never want to not be able to buy more. I love them.

title: Setup can be a bear, but after that it's great
text:
This was a trick to get set up. I ultimately paired it, well connected via WiFi to it, with a Windows tablet. You need to install the software. It doesn't much guide you what software that is. Go to the website and grab whatever is the latest. After that connect to it as though it were it's own WiFi hotspot (not terribly unusual) and you're good to go. Wired connections take priority over wireless, so you can't scan wireless if you're connected even if you trigger the scan from the wirelessly connected device.

Pressing the scan button, for some reason, did not scan. I find this particularly odd. You need to go into the software and click scan from there. I was unable to get the scan button to do a darn thing, but the software does an awesome job of it.

Once you get past the weirdness of setup, it's a great portable scanner. It holds a good charge. It recharges via a nice, standard micro-USB cable. It produces quality images. It scans quickly. It's really all you'll need for portable scanning. I love it.

title: Huge
text:
This is huge, much larger than I thought it would be. Think artist luggage, not something you'd toss in a backpack for a day of sketching in the park. Indeed, you could probably fold an easel and put it in the big pack in the back. It definitely holds a 9x12 canvas with room to spare.

The only thing I didn't like was the loops to hold paintbrushes were way too big. I can fit about six brushes in each loop and must unless I want them to fall out. Also the strap is really short.

I like the plastic bags that hold paints. I like how adjustable it is for all sorts of purposes. You can make two of the inner bins I guess I'll call them, deeper or more shallow by moving the Velcro bottom. I use that to store acrylic mediums, so I have it as deep as possible and can fit two bottles of gac, flo, gloss medium, matte medium, and a slow dry with no issue in one of them. Like I said, big.

title: Holds artwork without letting it sag.
text:
What I like best about this is the hard board inside. I think it's cardboard. It lets me stand the car without letting the artwork sag. I'm doing one class now that wants us working on 18x24 pictures and another that is using 9x 12 and this lets me store my work from both.

It's study. It's roomy. It's exactly what a needed. I just wish it had a shoulder strap. That lack alone cost it a point.

title: Outperforms its price point
text:
The stainless steel pen looks like a higher quality pen than the price point would suggest. The others look more in line with it. I'm most fond of the stainless steel.

It does not come with a converter, and Parker does not use standard converters. Theirs are proprietary. That said, they are relatively inexpensive and widely available. This pen comes with a single blue ink cartridge. What I like best about the Parker cartridges is that they have a little ink reserve on the bottom, you can tap for extra ink once the pen runs dry -- kind of an emergency supply. It won't last very long, but will generally get you through a meeting or a class. I'm not that fond of the color selection, however.

The pen writes perfectly smoothly -- again, outperforming its price point. No skips. No blotches. No leaking.

I've been a pen fan for decades, and I find this one a great workhorse of a fountain pen.

title: Good quality
text:
Four of the colors (the two whites, the green, and the yellow) work substantially better on black, or at least dark, paper. I use a very dark grey. The other four (orange, pink, blue, and purple) work equally well on black or white paper. The colors are richly saturated. The ink flow gave me a little trouble at first, but once the pens got started, they worked perfectly. It's unusual for gel pens to have to "start" like that, but not a big deal.

These are fabulous for a bunch of purposes. If you want to do any kind of lettering where the width of the pen does not need to vary, then this is a good choice, especially for casual, festive projects, cards, that sort of thing. It's great for Bullet Journaling (or BuJo if you prefer). It's fun for visual notetaking, if you work in color, to add some pop to your headlines, drawings, or icons. Icons particularly pop if done in a different color. And of course, traditional arts and crafts, especially paper crafts, benefit from the clean ink flow, excellent coverage, and beautiful pastel colors.

My only complaint is two white pens. I don't use white often enough to justify that. I would have preferred a different color. Peach is nice.

title: Solid, fast, reliable
text:
This is fairly powerful workhorse of a printer. It does a good job on the large format paper, and the small. You can air print to it. You can email a document to it. It can sheet feed scan (double sided as well) or just scan on the bed. I've printed some pretty heavy jobs on it, north of 300 pages for a novel I'm working on, and it printed it fairly quickly and held it all on the tray until it was done. I'm used to a little bit of a mess after a while as they tray of most printers can't handle that and just start jamming or spewing paper everywhere. This one does a good job. I've also printed full color documents, and the colors are vivid and sharp.

I've been putting this one through its paces for quite a while to find something to complain about, and so far I have failed. About the worst I can say is, it has a fax. People still fax? I mean, it doesn't get in the way but... fax? With a dedicated fax line, no less? I guess someone might want that feature, and maybe a telegraph, and a butter churn or something.

As I said, I've worked it very hard and have yet to run out of the ink that came with it. I'm impressed at that.

title: A fabulous set
text:
These lay an even line with good color saturation. They are excellent microliners, providing a good selection of quality pens at a good price (32 at the time of this writing). The triangular grip makes them easy to hold, whether you are gripping them as though to write, or gripping them overhand to lay a subtler shaded line with the side of the pen.

This is good for people who like to draw, people who like to do bullet journals, or people who like to color. Also good for people who use multiple inks to stay organized.

title: not much color saturation
text:
They're okay. I usually expect more color saturation from Tombow. These run very pale (you can hardly see the color from the thinner tip) and feel a little dry to me. Tombow in general is quite excellent, but these markers not up to their normal quality.

They are good if you want to BuJo and need some pale highlight colors.
They are good if you want to annotate a bible or something (though I would think a bible would be annotated in a bit more of a serious palette, but then people come to their bible highlighting with a grand variety of mindsets)
They are good for highlights in a more serious piece of art, but that would be mixed with other markers from other sets, not these alone.

By themselves, they are okay, but I'm not as impressed as I thought I would be.

title: A great starter set.
text:
There is A LOT of ink here. If the ink shown in the picture were all the ink provided, it would certainly be sufficient, but inside the box there are many more cartridges. I'm thinking it's at least a six month supply with very heavy use. They were generous with the ink. There are no converters, and you'll more than likely want them eventually (once the massive ink supply runs out). The big weakness with these pens is that view window is totally open, so you can't do the trick of making it an eye dropper pen (which lets you use the entire barrel to store ink). That's usually popular with calligraphy pens, though having tried it, I don't favor it; even pens designed as eye dropper pens tend to leak when they're half empty anyway.

The three pens cover a range of lines from so fine that there is barely a distinction between broad and narrow lines to so broad it can give the appearance of brush lettering with the ease of a pen. The medium one is the one I use most often.

I found the included instructions to be sufficient, but not ideal. I'd pair with [[ASIN:B00Z3G1XQ6 Simply Calligraphy: A Beginner's Guide to Elegant Lettering]] This book calls for the Pilot Parallel, but I find these pens superior. You'll want the medium nib for the wide ruled notebook paper suggested in this book. I have not had much luck touching nib to nib to get the inks to flow together, but that could as easily be something I'm doing wrong; I can't get that trick to work with the Parallel, nor with the Tombows, and I know it should work with those.

The included paper is of high quality but low quantity. You're going to want to refresh that right away. For learning, simple typing paper will do so long as it doesn't feather too badly, or common wide ruled notebook paper. There is no reason to go for expensive paper until you're ready for your first project. If you can't see the difference between the thin and thick lines, it's likely the paper bleeding. I've had that before, and no pen can overcome it. It's simply a factor of how the paper takes the ink.

The pens feel nice in your hand. I wouldn't say they're warm pens, but not cold ones either. More neutral. I was worried about the ridge at the view window, but I don't notice it while I'm writing.

title: Wacom vs LiveScribe: Battle of the Digital Pens
text:
The obvious product to compare this to would be the [[ASIN:B0195Y00Y2 Livescribe 3 smartpen]]. I've used both, and they both have their own strength and weaknesses.

Price
At the time of this writing, Wacom is the clear winner in that category.

Pen.
For both you are going to use the pen that comes with it. Wacom's pen, since it isn't do the bulk of the work, is much lighter and feels better in the hand. The LiveScribe pen does have a soft tip to use as a stylus, which is nice. Still, for comfort alone Wacom wins this category.

Ink
Both have proprietary ink (Wacom claims you'll get the best result using theirs, so I'll call it proprietary even though other inks fit). Wacom limits you to black. LiveScribe has blue, black, and red. Nothing amazing going on here. It'll all show up as black in the app anyway. LiveScribe wins here.

Paper.
LiveScribe uses specialty paper with pretty much invisible dots that guide it to where it is. You can go back and edit a page as many times as you like to, switching between pages at will. If the page shifts, it doesn't matter, because, as with plain writing, the only thing that matters is the relationship between the paper and the pen. If you use the same designation paper (one subject notebook, number 1) without first archiving the old, the pen will get confused. That's what the numbers are about with the LiveScribe. You can use a one subject number 1 and a one subject number 2 at the same time. A wide range of sizes, including post-its are available.

Wacom does away with all that confusion. Put any old notebook in there and it works. This size works with the ([[ASIN:B003UCL77U Rhodia (16559)]], which is a great notebook. The catch is, without the dots to go by, what matters is the relationship between the pen and the tablet beneath it. The paper can't shift. You're limited to paper that isn't too thick and that fits on the folio. There is a stitched line that is a guide, and anything written outside that guide won't be picked up. Beyond that, anything goes. You have to push the button between page flips, which means no going back to edit. If you mess up and forget to push the button, you can split the page based on the timeline, the assumption being you wrote everything you wanted to on page one before moving on to page two. Since that shows you what remains, this works fine if you're splitting two pages, but not so much if you have ten pages of notes where you forgot to push the button.

Wacom requires the folio at all times. LiveScribe lets you carry a tiny notepad and the pen and it works great.

I think LiveScribe wins here.

App.
Both do handwriting recognition. Neither can handle my handwriting, but that's not surprising, neither can most humans. I've had some folk who can produce recognizable text try, and both are about equally successful on those samples. Both can export to a host of services, such as Evernote. LiveScribe doesn't charge a subscription to the app. Wacom had unclear subscription terms at the time of this writing (it was free for three months on the site, the app said my account war free until July and it's currently October, and looking for what ongoing prices will be resulted no data anywhere). Wacom has better apps for editing images after the fact.

It's a hard choice, but for now I'm going to say Wacom takes the win.

Audio.
LiveScribe has it. Wacom doesn't.

Folio
Wacom's padfolio is much nicer than LiveScribe's. I really like it. Of course LiveScribe's is totally optional, but it is a nice enough folio to merit a mention, and a point in Wacom's favor. I would have liked a strap to hold it closed, but that's nitpicking.

So, that's pretty much a feature by feature breakdown of the two. I know I use my digital pens all the time, and I'm always on the lookout for tools that help me stay organized. I think the Wacom will make a welcome addition.

title: A few design issues, but overall an excellent printer
text:
Overall, I like it a lot.

The print quality is astounding. I was entertaining some senior citizens and printed a photo for them. They were astounded that it was just like a "real" photograph, aka film sent out for processing. I think that is the best way to describe it though. When printed on photo paper, it looks just like an old style film photograph. .

It might be that I'm printing photos rather than documents, but I'm finding the set up cartridges run out of ink quickly. This needs six cartridges. On the color side there is black, magenta, yellow, cyan, and photo blue. On the black side there is...well... black. Yes, this does mean it has two separate black cartridges. I would order spare ink right away.

At the time of this writing, if you order the ink from Canon directly, you get free shipping and an insane amount of free photo paper (I restocked everything and they shipped ten packs totally 450 sheets in various sizes). However, if you need it fast, Amazon ships much more quickly. They do sell XXL, which I'm hoping lasts a very long time.

You can print remotely using cloud print (the app needs to be on the same wireless network to print) but here's where things get a little strange. The machine automatically turns itself off. This is great for power saving, but it does not automatically turn itself back on if you cloud print. I like my HP because I can email a document to it and it will come to life and print for me, then go back to sleep. It does give a few hours, but not a full day. You can print from your phone, or from cloud print. I use both a lot. I wish it had a sleep mode similar to the PS4 where you can shut it off, but remotely turn it on. I think that's its biggest failing.

When you print, it automatically lifts the front panel and extends the print tray to catch the paper. When it shuts down, it retracts the print tray, but does not lower the front panel. That's a little failing on form, fit, and finish, but not a big deal. All of this, the protruding, the printing, the retracting, is very quiet, but the automatic shutdown beeps, and I dislike that because it usually does it in the middle of the night after I've printed in the evening, and the printer lives in my bedroom.

You can scan to various cloud services, including Drop Box and Evernote, right from the printer. Initially configuring it is a pain (I'd have preferred that be handled in the app rather than the tiny panel display) but once it's done, it's quite good. You can, of course, scan to PC or to the app.

title: Came nearly out of ink
text: Most of the pens came nearly out of ink. The first line is already skipping. The pens that are working, work very well. The that would be the pink and the purple.

title: Too pale
text:
They are listed as bright and bold, and I wouldn't call them either. They run more towards the pastel range and are very pale. Three of the colors are so much so, they simply don't show up, neither on white paper nor on black. I tested them on student grade art paper, which is designed to take pencil well and has with any other pencil I've tried.

They have excellent blending and layering, but likely won't appeal to serious artists. Doodlers and the coloring book crowd won't like how pale most of these colors are. BuJo users will have a similar issue with the lack of pigmentation. You can't even highlight with the palest.

They can go in a pencil holder, which is important because they will shorten to nubs twice as fast as regular colored pencils. It is certainly a nice assortment, and were they simply bolder, I would have loved them.

title: Good, but needs a little care to use
text:
I use these for bullet journaling, and they are beautiful. The colors stars shiny and appear wet. The colors are fabulous, with extremely strong pigmentation, and a good, smooth flow. Sakura is known for quality, and this product is one of the reasons why.

The only trouble is, they do stay wet for a very long time. These are maybe the slowest drying pens I've ever seen, so plan careful so to not risk smearing the ink (I do a right hand tasks column, before the left side notes and events with any pen but this) and let the page sit open a few minutes, else it will stick to the facing page. Definitely not for left-handed writers.

title: Quality notebook
text:
This one has a small box on the top for a date or a very short subject header. On the page is a series of small boxes to the right third so perhaps to use the side column as a to do list, or any kind of list really. It's good for bullet journaling if you like the page partly laid out like that. I rather use it for Cornell note taking (I highly recommend checking that out if you've not done it -- it's very effective in class, in meetings, pretty much anywhere you take notes.

The paper quality is excellent. It handles fountain pens very well. I've abused it a lot, and it holds up.

Excellent for a day planner or for general note taking.

title: Nib is so bad it won't write
text: Noodler's pens are popular with people who like adjusting their own nibs, because these nibs most definitely need adjustment.  This one is so bad, I can barely get it to write at all.  I went through one refill, put it in the pen case, and may never pull it out again, unless I get into nib adjustment and want to practice on something I can't ruin any worse than it already is. They make great ink, but this pen is horrible.

title: Good, but meant for the pencil crowd
text:
I like it, for the most part. It's meant for pencils, not pens, but with some doing it can hold a reasonable array of pens.

For length, a fresh out of the box Blackwing is the exact length of the insert. For size, I can fit a Pentel ink pen in, but as has been said, I need to occasionally skip a loop. This is definitely designed with the pencil in mind.

The only concern I want to bring to a reader's attention is that one seam separating the elastic bands came broken. Now I had planned to intentionally remove a seam so to fit a Higgins ink pen (and with a seam missing, it fits just snugly enough to work) so for me that was a bit of serendipity at least, but an indicator of workmanship of which to be aware.

Even filled I was able to use the mesh compartment on the top, but either because it is a tight fit, or because something pressed against the soft outside in transit, it left deep groves in a kneading eraser.

title: Fun, sturdy case with adequate storage capacity
text:
This is a fun case, and extremely well-made. The zipper goes all around, so you can open it pretty wide if you need to. The teeth are a zipper as well, but without the mechanism to close them. The sit inside the case and are merely decorative. The stitching and the fabric are both very sturdy. It's been stuffed nearly beyond its capacity a few times and the cat had a go at destroying it, but it's held up impressively well. A few pulls from the cat, but that can hardly be avoided. No holes though, which means pencils won't put holes in them either, though they can poke through if you jam them in tightly enough.

For size, it's about large enough to hold 20 of the fat Sharpie markers. That seems a good compromise between adequate storage and not too large a case. The eyes are charmingly uneven. This is a fun case for a child or an adult who had times she's rather not be adulting.

title: Make a long-lasting pencil point.
text:
If you've never tried one of these, you must. It makes, well, a long point. Like write and draw all day, never stop, and the pencil needs no sharpening kid of long point.

It is fully enclosed, so no mess.
It has an automatic stop, so no difficulty in using it.
It makes a great pencil point.

It comes with a pair of replacement blades, but so far I've been grateful I haven't had to try them. Replacing the blade scares me.

title: Remarkable notebook
text:
This compares favorably to the Moleskein of the same size.

It takes fountain pen ink very well, with no feathering. It might be designed with the pencil in mind, but it's perfect for ink as well. It provides a very smooth sheet, with excellent, crisp lines. Like the Moleskine, it has an elastic strap to keep it closed, a back pouch, and a sewn in bookmark. Rather than the history of the notebook on a card in the pouch, it has the history of the pencil and an amusing list of "Places You Might Find a Blackwing 602" on the back end page. If it seems the book is an afterthought, it is because of the well-earned legendary status of the pencil. It improves on the Moleskine in that it has, not only a pencil loop, but an included pencil, and not just any pencil, but the Blackwing 602. If you have not yet tried this pencil, and you are at all interested in luxury writing instruments, you need to try this pencil. It's amazing.

If it seems the notebook is just an accessory for the pencil, that's because it pretty much is. The main goal is to give that legendary pencil a worthy surface to write on, and it succeeds that goal. My only complaint is that it does not come in a variety of colors, and I want a collection of these I can easily differentiate at a glance -- an unlined for a sketchbook, a lined for a writing book, a lined for a journal, etc. Maybe in the future they will offer that, but not at the time of this writing.

title: Great pencils
text: One of these showed up in an ArtSnacks box, and I fell so much in love I had to have the set.  They are ridiculously smooth and comfortable.  Artist students who have trouble getting even shading might especially like these. I found that especially easy with these.

title: Should be a staple in every office
text: These are a staple marker, and the green is very nice, very proper for the office, not too dark and not too bright.  It makes for a professional dry-erase board presentation marker.  Each pen has an ample supply of ink (I lose them before I dry them out) and the box has an ample supply of pens.  These are the larger pens, of course, so they won't fit in the dry erase clips of the smaller boards.  They're a big pen with a big chisel tip meant for the larger boards.  I use them all the time.

title: A true luxury drawing pencil
text:
I blend a lot when I draw. It's more like laying some graphite then painting with the tortillon. These produce the best finish. They're dark -- I think about a 4B -- and they lay a clean line when used point down and smooth layer when used point sideways.

What I like:
The eraser is long -- 7/8 inch -- and you can extend it and even replace it at need.
It lays a fantastic line and holds a point very well.
It has a good barrel and feels comfortable in the hand.
It has a faceted barrel and won't roll off the table (I am tired of chasing after runaway pastel pencils).
It blends very easily and leaves a lovely finish.
It's a good-looking pencil.

What I don't like:
You can't use it in a pencil extender because of the odd shape at the eraser end.
You can't put a cap eraser on it.

This is, for most folk, a drawing pencil not a writing pencil. If you use it to write, it will likely smear. It's supposed to (or rather it's supposed to blend easily, but to the pencil they're the same thing). The Blackwing Pearl or Blackwing 602 is a better writing pencil, and of the two I'd suggest the 602.

title: Fabulous pencils
text:
I did not believe the hype on this pencil. I mean, how great can a simple pencil be, right? Pencils are pencils. Then, on a lark, I tried it. And now I believe the hype on this pencil.

Taking this thing top to bottom, first is the eraser. Now, I will say you can't pop an eraser top on this thing because of the odd shape. It will just split after a little use. However, you don't need to. These erasers are replaceable. You just pull the thing out and put in a new one. The eraser is pretty long -- most of it is inside the pencil -- and you can just pull more out to lengthen it until you need to replace it. For an exact length, the eraser fills the metal on top for as far as the metal is flattened to its shape, aka about 7/8 of an inch. I took it out and measured it.

The only downside is the unusual shape of the eraser means it won't fit into a standard pencil extender.

The barrel is faceted, which makes it easier to hold and less likely to roll off the table. It has a warm wood and feels nice in the hand. It has a good grip.

No special care is needed in sharpening these, which is good because I can't seem to sharpen the ones that do need special care (6B and softer or soft charcoal) without loosing a good inch on them. These I just stick in a mechanical sharpener, a twist sharpener, whatever, and they come out fine.

The lead is softer than a typical HB pencil, but not by much. The line is a smidgen darker, when exactly the same pressure is placed on both, but there is more difference from pressure than from pencil. That is, a standard #2 can make a darker line than this with a heavier hand and this can make a lighter line than a #2 with a lighter touch, but the lightest this makes isn't quite as light as the lightest a #2 can make and the darkest this makes is darker than the darkest a #2 can make, if that makes sense. I'd put it as a B maybe, just one darker than an HB. It matches my Faber Castel B for line anyway. But these designations vary brand to brand. The line erases well enough with a light hand, but is tricky to erase if you press hard, which is, I guess, typical of pencils. This is their premier writing pencil, but I use it as a sketch pencil to get the basic lines in before darkening with the Blackwing.

Warning, these pencils are addictive. Once you start writing or drawing with them, you won't want to stop.

title: Box came open and one was missing but otherwise ok
text:
They fit well enough if you really push them on the pencil, kind of dig the end in because are kind of tight. Otherwise they pop off. They erase about as well as any eraser of this type would. Nothing out of the ordinary here. Same as the one that comes built into your standard pencil.

I'm dinging it a star because the box came open, the erasers were spilled out all over the box, and one was missing (yes, I sat there and counted 143 erasers). I paired them with the Amazon branded pencil for a quick sketching pencil and that's good enough for my purposes. I would say I'd buy them again, but I think the odds are a bit slim that I'll ever run out.

title: Decent art pens
text:
They're fine point pens. They don't smear. They produce a clean line with no skipping and virtually no feathering.

The easel is a weird feature. You can't pull a pen out one-handed, even with it on the easel stand, because it's clicked in and the whole easel will come up, or at least hop around your desk some. It also doesn't close to fully cover the pens. So it's good for a small amount of reduced desk space use, but little ease.

You cannot use these to write on CDs/DVDs/etc -- the thing I use Sharpies for most often. It is too pale and smears right off. The line is too fine for use on dark paper or cardboard for labeling. They're marketed as art pens and art pens is what they are.

I'm dinging it a star because the color of the ink is too much lighter than the color on the cap. I know it's usually off, but not this much. I was hoping for a richer saturation of color.

title: Convenient and reliable
text: These are quite nice and the ink flows very well.  The color of the pen matches the color of the ink.  I put them to quite a bit of use, and the ink lasts a very long time, which for me is important in a pen.  They are sturdy enough that I have the red one clipped to my workout journal, so it sits in my gym bag, next to sneakers, jump rope, and all sort of stuff getting mistreated and dropped (too often with the sneakers on top) and it has shown no sign of damage yet.  I've had the clip pop off a few, so a nice sturdy pen is a good thing. Overall, I find these pleasant to write with and reliable.

title: Convenient, but no batteries
text:
The one thing that surprised me is that it is outlet only. You can't run it off batteries. That seems kind of last century, but then pencils are a bit last century.

I tried it with a host of art pencils from 8B to 5H and it was able to handle them all. The points came out clean and did not break in the process, which can be a problem with the very hard ones as they can run a bit brittle or the very soft ones as they are, well, very soft. This was able to deal with all of them.

The automatic shut off is a great feature. No pulling the pencil out to check if its done, just press it down until the sharpener stops. It's good to know I'm not the only person who wants an idiot proof pencil sharpener.

Beyond all that, it is useful. I take decent care of my car, but never manage to write down when I change the oil or when the last set of tires was put on, or when we replaced a flat that couldn't be fixed. For me ... this has some great details, that when I fill this book, I will create my own personal journal/notebook without all the stuff and fluff so I do not have to replace or update it every year.

title: very little to no ghosting
text:
UPDATE:
I had a chance to compare this 160 gsm journal to a Scribbles That Matter 160gsm journal and the Scribbles That Matter journal wins hands down. No ghosting at all or bleeding from all my favorite pens (aside from alcohol). I also now noticed the dots aren't all straight on THIS journal. I think it will be a problem once I start drawing boxes. So my take now is: This would be great if you are just into watercolor journaling, but for mixed media bujo-ing ... pass on this one and try another brand.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
160 gsm is about where you want to be if you are bullet journaling. I think I could only do better with a 180 gsm book I have my eye on. Right now I am using an 80 gsm journal and making do. The two journals are like night and day. I really haven't had a chance to do some major spreads in this journal because I am still in another journal but I had a chance to test tombows and a few other things on it. When I made the little swatches, I colored back and forth a few times. In theory it would have saturated the page good. When the page lays flat, there is no bleeding or ghosting at all. If you pick the page up and let a little light show through, you can see ghosting.

Like others have said ... this book lacks some details for the price ... numbered pages for one. A front index would be nice too. I think that is something people appreciate of don't. A journal index has been a game changer for me. What if I want to know when something special happened that I wrote about? Look at the index and find what page it is on. You can create all that yourself, but some journals take the work out of it. This one, for the price, does not.

I will update when I really start using all my pens in it. But the "usual" pens I use: tombows, faber castell pitts, and my favorite tombow hard tip black pen. They all work great. Oh and watercolors work pretty well without huge page curling.

Overall ... this is a great, thick paged book. For the price, I think there are better to be had. (and in updating this review I now really believe there are better to be had)

text:

If you want to use more than pencils and some pens and use the front and back of pages, you will want a higher GSM like 100 or 120. There are notebooks out there with a GSM of 160 just for reference.

Again, pens, like G2's (top) you won't see too much on the back side. A Pentel Fude touch shows a little more. Zebra Metallic brush pens don't bleed, but ghost. Artistro brush pens don't bleed but ghost. And alcohol markers ... there are very few papers that take those and this one, of course, didn't.

For the price, there is better quality out there. I was expecting more and I regret choosing these.

title: nice set, but falls short
text:
UPDATED REVIEW:
After really playing with this journal ... I assume the GSM is around 80. 100 would be pushing it. It is not listed. I got brave and started doing 2 page spreads. I mainly have to stick with colored pencils or a single wash of Tombow brush pens. Another items that mostly works is Zebra Mildliners. A single pass will not ghost too bad or bleed.

Still ... everything ghosts for the most part. Since I started using it, I figured I would finish using it and really get my feet wet with bullet journaling. My next journal in line is a 160gsm book. Which is what I would recommend. For the same price, or a little bit more, you can find yourself a high GSM (even 180!) bullet journal and really expand your use of mediums without ghosting and bleeding. This one works, but really is on the bottom end of journals out there.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Would make a great gift because it is an all in one and has so many goodies. However, this is not my favorite journal. This is mainly because I get bleed through on the pages. That, unfortunately is a dealbreaker and makes me go back to a known A5 bullet journal where I can utilize the front and back of pages. I like to color and doodle with markers in my journals along with my daily thoughts.

Other brands have numbered pages, this did not. The stencils were adequate but not fantastic. The pens were fine line and had ample colors but for lettering and writing. Personally ... I prefer a thicker pen.

The washi tape was the best part. Super cute patterns, peels up easily, sticks well, and stays stuck.

Overall ... for a young bullet journal-er, a newbie, or someone who wants to play around, this would be ok. It would be an all in one gift. For someone looking for more and to utilize all their pages ... this isn't the journal for you.

title: generous sticker pack!

title: quality phone system base
text:
I chose this phone because it is very similar to what I have used before when I worked in a law office, so there was a familiarity and a knowledge of the Motorola quality.

It is easy to set up and makes adding extra cordless phones easy. The digital receptionist is a little finicky. She says type 00 for the main mailbox and you do, only to have her ask again. So you do. You type 00. And then she asks again. So you do it again and finally it kicks you over to the right place.

Easy to record your own greetings and messages. Lots of options and ways to personalize this base system.

We have a small trucking company and I just needed a smaller phone system to direct calls here and there. I also needed an answering machine which this phone system has.

Overall ... this does the job. It hasn't failed us yet. It works as I expected it to work. It is not overly expensive, so a good value. Could recommend.

title: JUNK
text: Purchased one, would not advance the tape, and when it did, it would not stamp.  Amazon exchanged it.  The second one worked for a wee over 3 weeks and then it just stopped. title: works with a learning curve
text:
I purchased this because we volunteer in downtown Dallas and run across many languages in our work. I wanted an extra little tool to help me along.

The app was easy to install with the QR code. I could not find it alone in the App Store. Pairing with bluetooth was also easy. The item is small and easy to carry in your purse.

Setup and use could take some doing. The program itself took a learning curve and wasn't super simple to figure out how to use. There were a few spots in the app I could not back out of or hitting "done" would not back you out of it. Another spot, after typing in words, hitting "done" would not actually complete the task.

I mainly used this with German. I have an Uncle I regularly communicate with in Germany and he speaks little English and I speak terrible German. With some practice this was able to help that a little. Usually, we use google translate back and forth in emails. So have not tried out all the languages but so far, it works pretty well.

It is a little glitchy and learning how to use it will not be as easy as "plug and play" but overall this is a handy little device that I am happy to have.

title: good quality chair!
text:
I picked out this chair and my husband told me I wasn't going to like it. So then I was doubting myself. But ... I put it together and was quite impressed with the whole thing. Very few pieces, instructions were not too bad. Picture oriented, not word oriented instructions. Went together easily. Each piece was carefully wrapped in the package. The bar where you put your feet was covered with some grease ... not sure where it came from and it is a little a little difficult to get off, but not a deal breaker.

The metal this is made of is actually a heavy weighty metal. Does not feel cheap. It really exceeds my expectations. The chair now sits in our office in front of my computer. I am sitting in it now, one foot tucked under me, the other foot resting on the foot bar and the chair is quite comfy. The air lift is solid which I didn't know was a thing since I has been sitting in an old old office chair that seems to whoosh every time I say down.

Time will tell how the "leatherette" will hold up, but overall, I am pretty happy with this purchase.

title: thick, stays put ... mostly
text:

title: well made
text:

title: ... easy to set to up on Mac, wifi, & w/Apple phones
text:
We purchased this as a 'business expense". My husband is an owner operator and we need to scan many invoices, as well as print numerous items in a high quality fashion. This printer seemed to do everything we needed it to do, for the best value, with the least expensive toner cartridge replacements, and had the best range of Amazon reviews. I also liked the top scanner that scanned many multiple pages (like income taxes so one can fax them in a simple easy pdf file to the CPA.)

This machine has made my bookkeeping life easier.

We purchased this in mid February 2018 and have now had it about 3 months.

Some pro points to note:
- It was easy to set up on our iMac.
- It was easy to set up on our home wifi network
- it is easy to print from our Apple phones

... it also holds an ample amount of paper, prints crisp and clear in all colors. The toner cartridges all still appear full.

I think the only CON I can think of it is it pretty big. Some people may not like that. It is big because it takes large toner cartridges. It is a little over 17" tall with the top loading paper tray open. It is 16" wide and about 18" deep. This takes up some decent desk real estate so keep that it mind.

So far so good. I will update this as time goes on, but our first quarter with this machine has proven to be good.

title: good paper, and adequate for double sided printing

text:

title: Traveling Companion
text:
I myself do not own the Nespresso professional. However, I frequently find myself in a hotel that has a machine and so I took these with me.
Since hotel maid service no longer comes in to the room to replenish supplies every day since covid protocols, I use up the coffee pretty fast and find myself begging at the front desk, until I saw these!
Made in Italy, each one was full-bodied and delicious.
All three are very dark and rich, but the cremoso was exceptionally smoky. To be honest, I preferred the others, but since many people really enjoy that smokiness, no points taken off.
These are the easiest pods to tuck in your suitcase.

The only reason I have taken one star off, is that I carefully examined each pod before using them.
With most of them, I couldn't detect any coffee aroma, which means that they were sealed well for freshness. Unfortunately, some gave off a clear identifiable coffee fragrance, indicating they were not as well sealed. In addition, I found that those particular capsules were not as 'tight' and solid as the others, perhaps because of the introduction of air. I couldn't tell a taste difference, but since I'm using them shortly after they arrived, that's not surprising. For longer term storage, I question whether the ones that aren't completely sealed would taste as good.
Highly recommended as a break room or business coffee.

title: Nice for organization but flimsy
text: I am always on the lookout for ways to organize my you-know-what.  I saw these and liked the color and the whole crate look.  They are very nice looking in person but not as thick and sturdy as a real milk crate would be.  They come with plastic clip on labels with a marker.  I could not get the label to go into one of the holes.  I am hesitant to use tools to do so as I am not interested in using them for my needs.  I like them but they are on the pricey side.  UPDATE: I have used them in my camper for a couple of weeks and every time I slide them out to access the contents the sides disconnect and pop out of the rails. This has been extremely annoying.  I really wanted to like these but I had to remove 2 stars as they just do not hold up carrying any weight.

title: Helps me to stay warm while I work.
text: I get so cold working in the basement where my office is located.  I sometimes run a space heater buy ,y hands still get cold.  This product looked like it may help me stay warmer.  When I opened it I reverse rolled it to make it flat.  That worked pretty well.  I plugged it in at the lowest setting (green light lit) and it felt great to rest my hands on it.  I put it up to the highest setting and it felt even nicer although I think I will reserve that setting for the coldest days.  The lowest heat felt more comfortable.  It may even warm up the whole area in front of my face as I work, which would be nice.  You can set it up on a timer to play it safer.  I took a photo of the warnings, the timer and heat settings.  Just be sure and turn it off when not using it.  Otherwise, this is a great addition to my office in the colder weather.

title: Nice price for 3 dispensers
text: When I saw this 3-pack I thought "I need this."  The whole package is very inexpensive but then you get 3 dispensers and 3 rolls of tape.  They are very light.  I guess that is why they include the sticky bottom, should you decide to peel off the protective tape.  Without the sticky bottom you won't be able to rip off one piece of tape with one hand.  Small price to pay since I don't mind using 2 hands.

title: Really fun little bins and useful too
text: OK, for the price, just get these.  Worry about what you will do with them later.  They are that worth it.  You can stuff a heck of a lot in one of these little bins.  I have multiple pens, hand cream, pads of paper, scissors, measuring tape, dog trimmers, remote control and more just in one bin on my desk.  The others will go to my workshop tables.  Really for the price they are a steal.  So many ways to use them.  They are well constructed and if you don't want to use them they can be folded up and tucked away somewhere until you are ready.  They come in fun colors.  Oh my, just really fun to have and use.

title: Nice and sturdy drawers and easy to attach
text: I wasn't sure what to expect when I ordered this product.  I needed a drawer badly for my work bench so I could store small scissors, cutters, pencils, etc. to get more space on the table.  When it arrived I was surprised to see it was well made and sturdy.  I applied the glue pieces to both pieces and withing seconds I had 2 drawers.  I will wait overnight as suggested before putting anything in them.  I can open and close the drawers now no problem as they feel firmly attached.  I would recommend this product.

title: Crazy for These Towels
text:
Soft on skin, even delicate skin. Not for exfoliation on their own, but these are perfect with a squeeze of your exfoliating facial scrub. Part of the reason for that is because they are easy to rinse clean, and after exfoliating they are so soft on your face.
If you don't use any kind of scrub, because your skin is super delicate, these are really nice in that area. A little bit of cleanser goes a long way with these.
Sturdy enough to use a few times.

I'm crazy about the way I can just throw a couple into a bag and not have to use hotel or motel washcloths on my face. Each one is individually wrapped so you know that they are sanitary. Just add water.

title: Very nice portable paper cutter
text: Don't underestimate your need for a paper cutter if you do any crafts.  Cutting with a scissors is not very accurate and prone to errors.  This paper cutter would be worth it just for the straight cut given the price.  It is nice and heavy duty and doesn't seem like it will wear out quickly.  In addition to the straight line blade it has 3 more blade options: wavy line, dotted line and creasing blade.  I tried each of them on typical card stock and they each came out perfect.  You do have to press hard when sliding the blade and do it a few times.  See my photos for my results.

title: Comfortable but very thick
text: I got these because my elbows hurt after many hours in my computer chair.  These feel good and help raise my arm rests to a comfortable level.  Be warned they are thick and if you have long arms they may be too high for you.  I am short so they work out well.  They also attach well to the arm rests.

title: Does a good job with a small form factor
text: I have had laminators in the past but don't use them often enough to keep handy as they have a large footprint.  So I usually put them in storage and forget about them.  When I saw this SINCHI 9-inch Personal Laminating Machine I thought it looked small enough to tuck away in the office so I would be more likely to use it more often.  I was right.  It is very sleek and not very big.  It is easy to use, just turn it on and when the ready light goes on then put your paper inside the plastic sleeve and put it into the machine.  I did both small and larger paper and both worked great.  Then I took the machine and tucked it away.  Does a good job with a small form factor.

title: A nice verstatile label maker
text: I store a lot of small parts so I thought getting a label printer would be useful.  This one meets my needs for smaller labels.  The unit is easy to use.  It comes with one roll of tape stored inside which you have to unpackage and load properly in the printer before you start.  You download the app called "Print Master" from your respective app store, I have an iPhone.  You need to register when you get the app.  There are 2 types of labels: simple and creative.  I printed the simple one first which was easy.  Then I did the creative one where I selected a photo on my phone of my little dog and then added some text.  You can add photos, add borders, icons, lines, QR code, 1D code and time.  Both labels came out great.  The photo quality is not great, it is thermal.  but you get the idea and it's fun to see her face on the label.  The manual is very clear with excellent graphics.  The printer has a rechargeable battery, via USB, so once charged you can take it anywhere to use.  I was able to print while it was charging.  Overall I would recommend this printer as you get to create simple or more complex labels for a relatively small amount of money.

title: These rulers have many uses if you need metric
text: I got these rulers to help me draw perfect shapes when I need to.  It is nice that they also offer points of reference when you want things to overlap.  One is for Junior High and the other is for High School.  They are very similar to each other.  Both rulers are in metric so they have limited measuring uses unless you need to use metric.  I do electronics projects and many of those are in metric since most parts and kits are made in China.  The slide mechanisms on the rulers are a little rickety so one needs to be careful when doing exact measurements that the slide doesn't move.  I am not sure how long these will hold up amongst junior and senior high students.  The case on one came open on the side as the ruler's edge most likely opened it up.  For the money I guess they are worth a try given how many functions they serve.

title: Most impressive multi functional tape dispenser
text: In got this tape dispenser because I just bought a cricut machine and thought I could use this for holding my vinyl cutouts onto fabric.  This is the first time I ever used a tape dispenser like this so it took me a while to get my head around what it wants to do.  The instructions were not clear enough for me as I didn't get why I had to feed the tape under the wheel....a bit counterintuitive.  Once I got going and saw how it worked I felt better.  However, without the center section being fully loaded with tape rolls the one roll of tape I put on slid side to side.  I didn't have another wide tape roll but had a couple extra thin width rolls so I put them on next to my blue tape just to make it more stable.  The roll of tape I put on the outside operated like a normal tape dispenser EXCEPT the cutting blade is on an angle so I had to slide the tape the the part of the blade that sticks out the most.  It is pretty inexpensive unit given all it is trying to do so I should be impressed. It also comes with another size spindle for  tape with a smaller diameter.  I gave it 5 stars because it accomplishes everything it is supposed to and comes at a low price.

title: Retro Chic
text: These adorable cards are for people like me, that never seem to get the Christmas cards out to people. You can redeem yourself by sending New Year's cards!  Cute retro vibe with a bit of glitz.  Takes a regular postage stamp.

title: A real bargain for a nice rolling cart
text: I got this cart to put all the stuff I need for training on my inside bicycle.  It has a nice black unassuming color and doesn't stand out.  It was fairly easy to put together.  I took a phot of the instructions and another photo of where some of the not so obvious parts went.  I also included some detail photos so you could see what some of the connections look like.  Overall, the cart looks nice and rolls well and feels sturdy for my purpose.  For the money it is a real bargain for what you get.

title: Very easy to use and quick setup
text: This label printer was obtained in order to better manage the printing of my eBay labels.  It setup quickly and began printing labels right away.  If you use it for eBay be sure and tell eBay that the label is 5x7 or it will print the label very small.  Otherwise, it works great!

title: Must haves for multiple uses
text: I obtained these card protectors for not only my vaccination card but also to hold my kayak and raft stickers.  Since my inflatable boats tend to shed their stickers I got these to keep the stickers safe and also allow them to be tethered to the boat.  They are great for both purposes.

title: Great glue
text: This tape is very sticky and effective.  It is nice that it is refillable.  I still think it is a bit overpriced.  Easy to use.

title: Does the job but at a high price
text: I like that this thin double-sided adhesive can be used and not show through the paper.  It is a bit expensive for what it is.  I have seen where some people feel it needs more instructions but if you have worked in the business world I guess one picks up enough experience with this type of product to be able to work with it right out of the box.  I would recommend this product, especially if you can get a deal on it.

title: This is my Go To Printer!
text: I have used this printer for a few months now and I have to say it works very well.  I have printed from my desktop, laptop, tablet and phone.  I have multiple options for wi-fi Internet connections in my home and that sometimes gets me into trouble with this printer.  I have to remember that the device I want to print from is connected to the same Wi-Fi as my printer.  If I do that then I never get into trouble.  The only other thing that doesn't seem reliable is the app.  Sometimes the app says the printer isn't available but I can still print so I am not sure what the issue is there.  I also get multiple power outages living in the country and every time the printer comes back like a champ available for my next printing.

title: Can't Uncurl
text:
Does what it's supposed to do. It's translucent, protects your floor, and wheels go smoothly on it when you move your chair.
The problem is that after a long time of keeping weights on the edges, it's still curls up without them.

title: Good for Storage Boxes
text:
Good value for decent tape. Doesn't hold up well for shipping, however. I have to use more of this, for example instead of just one strip on the top of the box, I had to add one crosswise in order for it to be secure enough, and double tape.
If you just need it to close storage boxes, like seasonal items, these rolls are perfect.

title: Writes So Smoothly
text:
Very impressed with these slightly generic looking pens. They write smoothly, no skipping and no ink blobs.
Another thing that I noticed, you barely need to touch the paper in order for the pen to glide across it. So if you write with a light hand, or you write very fast, you won't have a problem with these.
Big upgrade from ballpoint pens.

title: Good Basic Folders
text:
You need a bunch of folders, and you don't want to break the bank. You don't need them to be super sturdy, you just need some basic folders for home or business.
Here they are.
If they get a lot of use, they're very quickly going to get edges like shown in the photo. That may or may not matter to you.
You can also look at it as a plus that they are not super thick. When you have a huge box of them, a thicker folder is going to weigh more.
Hopefully the photos show them in a way that will help you to make a decision about whether or not these particular folders are going to be what you need. They're easy to write on, good way to stay organized.

title: Very Cute Cards
text:
Very cute budget cards.
We all can relate to the challenges of getting through the past year, so the solidarity aspect of these cards lets someone know that you understand...AND that the two of you share a common experience.
Three yellow envelopes are slightly larger than each card.

title: Beautiful Card
text:
The great thing about this card is the way that it folds. That means it can stand up on its own and be a lovely decoration on any flat surface.
Since it is marked as 2021, it can be a keepsake for remembering the day for years to come, especially if your personal sentiment written inside is meaningful.

title: Beautiful pop-up card
text:
From the outside this is quite an unassuming card. A simple happy birthday on a white background. It's when you open it that the fireworks begin! It's a pop-up piece of cake with glitter sparkles and a glitter silver spoon next to it. The sentiment inside reads 'happy whole year, too!'
I can't imagine anyone not grinning ear to ear when they open this card. It's a great choice for just about anyone.

title: Great Markers, 'Storage Box' Needs Improvement
text:
These markers were listed as 10 sets of 15 markers, with a cardboard storage box. After opening the shipping box, there was another cardboard box inside filled with markers, as opposed to 10 separate sets. Naturally, it tipped over and markers were everywhere.
So keep in mind that these are a BULK set, not 10 sets. If they are to be distributed, in my case to participants making posters, you will need to sort them.
The above relates to the date of this review, please keep in mind that packaging might well be updated by the time you order.
That being said, the important thing is the markers themselves, and this review is focused ONLY on the performance and quality of the markers themselves.
They are quite nice, being the same quality as the familiar big brand. The tips are pointed for fine work, and you can use the sides for broad strokes or coloring larger areas.
To test how washable they are, I used a white cloth. The ink vanished after a rinse in water and dish detergent. How about on skin?
As you can see, the ink rinsed right off.
Perfect for kids.
Almost completely odor free to my very sensitive nose.
Minimal 'beading' on glossy paper or poster board, as the last photo shows. The enlargement of the grey marker on a white gloss cardboard shows how it beads, but it does not streak after drying. It's always best to use non gloss paper with these, but if you must use glossy, you can build the color if you let each coat dry completely before the next. Stick with non gloss for ease and a cleaner look.

Bottom line, you can have lots of creative fun without worry of stains.

title: SO Grateful I Found This!
text:
Yes, this is fantastic as part of your stretching routine. Using the weight of your own body, or not, there are all kinds of positions to use.
Haven't been on a plane since covid, but certainly will in the future.

But here is why I'm so grateful. My wife had a total knee replacement. I bought every possible piece of equipment you can imagine...the hospital said we were better equipped than THEY were, lol!
This simple device not only assists with critically important post op home PT, but she wouldn't be able (at this point) to get out of bed without it.
In our particular situation, we have a log bed frame, her left thigh is on it. Makes it doubly hard to get out of, despite the bed itself being an adjustable one.

Please, if you or a loved one is looking at a TKR, do consider this small investment. Rehab is painful, as anyone will tell you. Every little thing you can do to make it better is a lifesaver.
PS, getting our own ice flow and compression massage machines were also hugely helpful.
Best of health to you and yours.

title: Where have you been all my life?!
text:
[[VIDEOID:c296dca45d6d2620d8fdec0ffdb4d73e]] I've used a couple of stylus instruments in the past but they never felt comfortable in my hand. Usually they are too slim, and often the head wouldn't glide across the screen smoothly.

Pristine white.

Usually, if you want a monthly planner without the weekly planner in a small, slim size, your only option is the classic rectangular monthly planner.

The quality that Hallmark is known for.

Hallmark has long been the, well, hallmark...when it comes to greeting cards. This beautiful card is no exception.
Nice sentiment as well as artwork.
Having it conveniently delivered, is an added plus.

title: Cute and Handy

This cute little organizer keeps all of your coupons handy while shopping.

It's odd that the product has a pen loop, but does not include a pen.
If you have a purse that is large, and like a bottomless pit, the bright colors are easy to see.

title: And it started off so well...  UPDATE
text:
What a great idea, and perfect for our high ink use household.
By mail, I received an HP instant ink enrollment card. It looks like any ordinary gift card that can be purchased at most grocery stores. The value is $9.99.
With this program, you either purchase one of the enrollment cards, which by the way, make perfect gifts, or you can join the program online using your credit card.
After syncing your printer with the program, it automatically senses when you are low on ink and will send you more, right before you run out. You can select an option that best suits your printing needs.
Fabulous, right?
My HP Envy is one of the compatible printers, which of course I carefully checked to make sure that it would be.
I went to HP instant ink web page to sign up. The process couldn't have looked easier. The only glitch, which probably will be repaired before the next person makes a purchase, is that the cursor on my Galaxy tablet would go back with each letter or numeral entered on the online sign up form. So each and every time I entered a character, I would have to tap after the character in order to get the cursor positioned for the next character. What a waste of time.
Especially after what happened next.
My printer was being such a good boy. After pressing the online document button, it obediently printed out my congratulatory letter as well as further instructions.

Then I did MY part, dutifully entering the claim code as well as other codes.
Everything was fine, until it came to the shipping and billing information. No matter how I configured it, or how many times re-entered, it would not accept the prepaid key number. Also, I have a promo code provided by HP, and the online form had nowhere to use it.
Keep in mind the tedious process with the cursor issue.
Just to check, I did the whole process again, but this time using my credit card as opposed to the prepaid HP card. Not only did it joyfully take all of my information, but when I entered the credit card number it didn't have that cursor problem the way that it had with every other character entered. It still would not show a box where HP's promo code could be entered.

So, first thing Monday morning, I'll be contacting customer service.
Of course, I'll update this review right after my customer service experience, however, unless the fault is somehow with me, or they can assure me that it's a bug that has since been worked out, the review rating will stay the same.
I suspect that there will be a happy ending to this tale, however, enrollment with a compatible printer should not be this buggy.

UPDATE: after a lengthy conversation with customer service, it looks like I'm all set to go, and that within 7 to 10 days a new ink cartridge will be sent to me. According to the representative, the cartridge will not only be twice the size of an ordinary cartridge, it will also contain a chip that will inform HP if I'm no longer participating in the program. It will then turn off the ink. Don't think that just because you have a cartridge, you can print. You will print what you have agreed to pay for via your contract.
Your first enrollment month starts when you place the instant ink cartridge in your printer. It isn't when you first fill out your online enrollment.

That means that you aren't charged until you place the ink in, and if you have enrolled in the 300 page program, you can print up to 300 pages. After that, it will be a dollar for 25 pages. You don't get a new cartridge every month, you get a cartridge when you need it. The number of pages are monitored as well as ink usage. That makes this an economical option for many people.
Fortunately, the number of pages rolls over into the next month. If you only print 275 pages in a one-month period, the next two months you can print 325 pages. Another nice thing is that you can keep track of this online. It will show you the number of pages that you have left, as well as any rollover pages.

What I find puzzling, is that this process was so buggy. I asked the representative how long the instant ink program from HP has been in existence, and she said that it's been 4 years. It would seem to have been an easier process given that this program is not as new as I thought it was.
The representative was very nice and it only took 3 times before I wasn't disconnected prior to reaching a real person. That's actually pretty good given how these sorts of things usually work.

text:
This charming case can be used for pencils, pens, even smaller crochet hooks.
The really nice thing about this, is that you can roll it up and stick it in your backpack to do outdoor sketching. It's well-made and has a Bohemian rustic look.

The particular one that I'm reviewing has elephants on it, the symbol of good luck. The elastic holds your pencils just tight enough to keep them in place, however they are easily removed. It really is nicer than the photograph shows.

Product received at a discount or no cost, in order to test with the option to review.

title: Need for Speed
text:
One of the amazing things about this scanner is that it is lightning fast, yet has a small footprint.
That makes it a terrific addition to a home business or a consultant with limited space, as well as a small to mid-size office.
It comes with Document Capture Pro, which alows you to shuffle, add, and delete. Next you can save to a wide variety of formats such as jpeg, PDF, and BMP files.

If you have high volume needs, this scanner gets it done, and without wasting time.

text:

Not much will help with the sluggish process at the Division of Motor Vehicles, but having pre-paid and pre-printed shipping labels can cut through post office lines.
I like these because my usual shipping labels print the receipt on an adhesive label. These will print off the adhesive label, and a paper receipt without adhesive.

She is entering the wonderful, but sometimes hard to negotiate, world of adulthood.
May she always follow the right path of being the being the amazing girl/woman that she is.

title: Queen for a Day
text:

This cheeky card supplies both.

Soft green flocking and a 3D banner are on the front. Inside are the congratulations on the baby 'burrito', as well as plenty of room to write your own message.

title: Keeping Photos and More
text:
These smaller size pouches protect photos so well that they will be able to be passed down for generations without the worry of discoloration or any of the damage that can happen over time.
Easy to use, we had no issues with bubbles or feeding the pouches.

Nothing to get crazy excited about, just a set of decent file folders with oversized tabs and lines printed on the front.
Visability is further enhanced by the assorted colors. Between that and the tabs, these are good for those that might not see as well.

This gorgeous wristlet is for more than just your smartphone.

title: Your Appointments, Your Life
text:
[[VIDEOID:53f067d51beb263354dea6f1e50f6fdb]] So much more than just a planner, I hope the video shows exactly how lovely this product is.

But this would also make a nice diary or journal of sorts. A scrapbook of a year of your life, and how you lived it, each day.

Of course, it's also perfect if all you wish to do is keep appointments and obligations in order and close at hand.

The cover is sturdy, pages are a cut above super flimsy datebooks.

title: Instant Message Board
text:
This is a fun product, but don't expect it to have the same results as a regular chalkboard.
For example, in order to erase, a slightly damp cloth works best, and even then you may need to turn the cloth over to the clean side and wipe again.
Similar products have the same issues so that isn't a big deal.
As an impromptu message center, a square of this is perfect. There are cutting guide lines on the reverse side of the paper to make it easier.
Heavier than paper, it's a thin vinyl.

Product received to test with the option to review. No financial compensation is EVER accepted, and vendor may request that item be returned. Views and opinions are my own.

title: Days of Your Life
text:
Perfect for a small business or a large family, this wall calendar helps manage your time and prevent mix-ups and misunderstandings.

Holidays and other days of note are indicated, but there is still plenty of room in each day block for jotting in what is important to you. As with similar products, one side is vertical, the flip side is horizontal.
A marker is included, some people might prefer a tip that isn't as broad. The ink wipes off with a damp tissue or an alcohol pad.

title: Fashion for the Desk
text:
Smooth in the hand, hard on the staples.

title: Printer/Scanner Workhorse
text:
Set-Up:

I went to the Epson website and quickly found the appropriate software and drivers. It quickly recognized that I was on a Mac and which OS I was using and recommended the appropriate downloads. The downloads took a while, but this is expected with most printer set-ups. After following all the instructions, the printer was easily added. In addition to downloading the printer drivers, I also downloaded the scanner program.

Printing:
Printing from the computer worked great. I also tried to print from my mobile phone. I was worried that I would need to download an app, which I wasn't excited about doing, but I didn't! As long as you are on the same network, you are easily able to find the printer and print. I included a screen shot of the screen to print directly from my iPhone. I also played around with Epson Connect. You can create a custom e-mail address and any e-mails sent to that e-mail address get sent to you printer. It took a couple minutes to set up, but once it was set up, I also tried that and that also worked with no issues. I printed in both color and black and white. The quality is good, but I wouldn't be using this to print photos. It is adequate for printing of all types, but don't forget, this is not a laser printer.

Scanning:
This is where this printer really shines. I needed to scan some double sided documents. I didn't have to worry about watching over the printer while it scanned. The feeder worked perfect and sent the document to my computer in PDF format with both sides oriented in the correct direction. With my old printer/scanner, I always had to rotate the pages after the scan. It was quick and more importantly, easy.

Other Features:
It also provides a fax feature, but not sure whom uses faxes anymore. There are also two paper trays, which is really handy. You can have regular 8-1/2x11 inch in one tray and have a different size the alternate tray. May not be important for most users, but I thought it would be handy.

title: See through for me!
text:
Machines complex and simple are just better in see-thru acrylic. If I can see the workings and operation, it's 'better' by me. I bias toward clear acrylic stuff. I prefer to see the innards. Have you ever seen the operation of this simple mechanism before it's made clear? Perhaps a spark of invention might arise from seeing it? The world might beat a path to your door for a 'Better!" stapler.

Being my bias, clear cases reflect on the 'risk' that SEAKOS has taken by exposing their products innards to inspection. The universe of desk staplers are everyone, inexpensively made ... they are cheap no matter where they come from. Manufacturers shave a fraction of a mill of cost here and there and peddle it as "Improved!". And it is, from the manufacturer's standpoint.

Kudos to SEAKOS. These innards aren't "cheap" so much as suited for the purpose. The metal components flaunt that colorful flash of titanium vapor deposition. Does your not cheap 'brand-x' let you see what's inside? Of course not. Wanna bet that 'brand-x' is likely made side by side in the same Chinese factory? How many mass-market desk stapler production lines stamping, assembling, and encasing desk staplers would you imagine might exist? One can postulate.

Kidding aside. These are cool, and they work, and it's all I want out it ... that and flashy clear stapler and stuff. The kids like them better too, though I'm not taking surveys.

Enjoy.

The full fidelity color laser output on a standard stock paper is primo for marketing and proposal quality production. 800-page drawer capacity is an instant labor cost saving.

Note the size and weight to ensure or prepare your planned placement.

If you are used to setting up and using this class printer with ink or laser, there won't likely be a problem for you.

For gloss photo quality production, I prefer ink. Laser quality photo quality really does require the special laser gloss stock which I've not tried on this printer and likely won't ... deferring to inkjet.

Bottom line:
The Lexmark 2425 is the latest and greatest in small group laser printing. I love it so far. The transition to full laptop/desktop printer control has advanced and means no intermediate steps to the printer.

text:
This is a review for the MFC-J5945DW … NOT the MFC-J5930DW most everyone has reviewed here. I've seen this before when newer models come out and reviews have that two-tailed 1 star/5 star peaks. The MFC-J5945DW product is much better than 1 star territory.

So, most of the MFC-J5930DW review cons seem to have been addressed in MFC-J5945DW. This is the first Brother I've tried in a number of years since HP 8600-8700 came to dominate the market.

Adopting a new brand printer takes patience. The hardware appears similar. The proprietary software is different. Scanning, printing and faxing is working fine. Easy install.

Ink is less expensive. It's quiet. I'm doing standard 8.5x11 paper and nothing special.

All good so far. I'll keep you updated.

title: Excellent outdoor work marker
text:
Love the belt clip. Nice mark line.

I hope I can remember to put it back. The pencil/marker is surely the most "lost" item when I need it.

title: Sharpies the best, don't waste time on the rest
text:
The color palette is rich.

I judge permanent markers after 6 months of use. Sharpie color remains sharp. Wick stands up to general multi-user tip pressure, doesn't get mashed easily.

The real test is color coding convention booth boxes with contents for ease of show tear down and set-up.

Sharpie … 5 thumbs-up

title: Excellent Embossing
text: Deep, crisp embossing is the highlite. Everybody is superman for gosh sakes and need to be treated that way. As advertised.

title: Better than advertised. Very flexible to purpose.
text:
No shipping damage to report. It meets expectations. This is a heavy projects/conference table. The leg length adjustability is unique. The table will work for office and assembly platform use. It's really quite flexible in application. It's value for money.

If the packaging engineering is slip shod from the manufacturer I count that against the product but don't pin the blame on Amazon as the retailer. There is no doubt that the table is heavy enough to surprise the delivery workers into dropping. It's a 2 man carry. If it gets really hammered in shipment, it will be damaged.
