My five-year-old son cannot stay still. He's five! But every so often he wants to work on a nice craft project, do Play-Doh, or we would like him to sit and have a meal without his feet and booty wiggling all around. This is been a perfect fit for him, because it is just the right height to sit at his children's table, and the chair is surprisingly soft and comfortable. It looks like a hard and molded plastic, but it's actually soft and rubberized, so he doesn't slide off, and it just feels really surprisingly nice.

The downside is that it does not adjust at all. I would've loved if it adjusted from 14 inches to 16 inches or 14 inches to 18 inches. However, I knew going in that this was just a 14 inch stool and that we would have to be done with it after he outgrew it, so I really can't dock points for that. It does a great job of being what it is and we are very happy to have it. It's really solved the problem and allowed him to wiggle his booty while still staying put.

title: Exactly as expected!
text:
These are perfect little pencil boxes which I'm actually using in my office for storing stickers and other office errata. They are a great little stacking organizational tool and the colors are nice because I can see at a glance what I am looking for.

If at some point I want to transition to using them for the kids, they are definitely easy to open and yet do clasp shut well. I appreciate that as some brands have been so hard to open that I end up scattering the contents of the box when I open it. This is just a really well-made set of simple basic plastic pencil boxes without any dividers inside, and I'm really happy that it is exactly what I expected.

title: Another hit from Melissa and Doug
text:
We have a number of stamps sets from Melissa and Doug, and my kids really love playing with them. Since we are homeschoolers, we are always looking for ways of incorporating learning with art and other activities to keep people engaged in what we are learning. While my 3 1/2-year-old is too young to be building words with the letters, my 5 1/2-year-old finds it really fun to work with these stamps and try to stamp out names or short words to describe the pictures he's drawing.

I really like the divided stamper which lets both of my kids stamp different colors at the same time, which if you have two small kids of a similar age, you know they are always competing to be in exactly the same place at the same time.

These stamps work exactly as expected and I have nothing but love for this whole set. Lots of fun, great for education, and nicely presented.

title: Love these little sectioned pencil cases
text:
What cute little pencil cases! I used them to create some on the go art kits for taking to restaurants. I put some colored pencils, and eraser, and cut some little stickers to fit in there, and brought them with a clipboard and paper for the kids to use when we went out to eat. Worked a charm!

The clasp stays shut when you close it, but is easy for both me and the kids to get it open without spraying all the materials all over. Really happy with this simple basic pencil case with the cute little sections.

title: Great sturdy plastic tabbed dividers with folders
text:
These are perfect! I've used something similar from Avery and these seem identical. Nice generous tabs, supportive folders, made of plastic that seems sturdy.

This is perfect for document storage for my landscaping crew members.

title: Very happy with these for making family cookbooks
text:
These are great! I used them for binding a family cookbook of printed recipes from everyone. It's holding about twenty five pages with ease.

The presentation is crisp, and it's not hard to add pages as needed. They seem sturdy and nice.

title: Works great and adhesive excellent
text:
This was a perfect solution for attaching to the side of my monitor for my daily reminders. I just snap off the board and write on it, then pop it back in place.

The adhesive is better than expected. Install took a whopping to minutes including cleaning my monitor surface with alcohol.

title: Quality equivalent to Avery
text:
I've been buying smaller packs of these by Avery, to use with my landscaping business. These are of equivalent quality, sturdy and durable, and work perfectly for my needs to hold small sheaths of loose paper in a binder.

They are exactly as hoped. And a much better deal in bulk than buying individual packets from Avery.

title: Great for sitting with my chrome book
text:
I have a new chrome book and I was really excited to get to sit on the couch and do my work rather than be chained to my desktop. However, I quickly found that the shiny surface of my chrome book wanted to slip off my lap, and it wasn't angled in a way that was comfortable to look at. This laptop computer desk tray solved all of my problems, with a good surface for the grippy feet of my laptop to sit on, and a nice, lightweight cushioned beanbag bottom that sits on my lap very comfortably. There's a little curve in the front so that it doesn't cut into my tummy, and overall this makes my computing experience on the couch very comfortable. It's exactly what I hope for an expected.

It has less beanbag filling than other laptop desks that I have used in the past, but I actually prefer this because it makes it lighter weight and I have found the other ones a little heavier than I wanted.

title: Great for school reports or handing out small amounts of paperwork
text: Occasionally with new employees to my landscaping company, instead of giving them the full on binder, I will just give them some of the simple paperwork that they need, like their company handbook, instructions for basic work, etc., and one of these heavy-duty plastic folders. This is a great way of quickly getting some information into a protected folder where things will stay in order and not slip out. These are sturdy and thick and I haven't seen a broken one yet, despite a few months of use.

title: Love this line of Amazon basics office supplies
text:
I own a landscaping company and give out binders full of information, so that my crew can have not only their legal documents like a company handbook at hand, but also educational info as well.

These tabbed plastic dividers have a little pocket on them, so my crew can store loose paperwork in there until it gets filed, and the pockets can also act as a divider so that each section has its own holder for the loose paperwork. When they get something new for their safety section, they can pop it into the pocket divider until they actually put it into the ring portion of the binder.

These have nice wide tabs and are very sturdy.

title: Absolutely perfect for scheduling my landscaping crew
text:
I usually use Google calendars to do my scheduling, but recently Google calendars has done so many stupid updates that have made it incredibly hard to make small adjustments and drag-and-drop my calendar ideas around when I am working in the preliminary phases of scheduling.

Rather than look for a new software solution, I decided to do all of the preliminary scheduling on this cool little whiteboard. What a great excuse to get away from my computer. I picked up a set of rainbow dry erase markers and a little dry erase eraser, and for the last three months have been settling down on my cushy carpet and having a very pleasant few hours reviewing my notes and marking up my calendar, with each employee having their own color. This is lightweight enough that I can set it on my lap to work on the couch, have it on the floor, and pick it up and move all around. I haven't actually tried hanging it yet because I really appreciate using it while sitting. But the hardware for that looks fine.

Overall, my markers write very smoothly on this beautiful clean surface, and the calendar sections are just big enough for exactly what I need. I also appreciate the little line down the side that gives me a little bit of note taking area. This was thoughtfully designed and is an ideal size for me. I cannot imagine what would make it better.

title: Works exactly as expected!
text:
We wanted a simple calendar to be able to go over and visualize dates and the passage of time with our children, who are young, but homeschooled. These really fit the bill. We used magnets to attach it to our fridge since the fridge seemed extremely obvious that it is not a surface to draw on, as opposed to pinning it to a wall, and allow our children to mark off days with the dry erase crayons and dry erase markers that we have.

Special occasions such as birthdays, holidays, and friends visits are marked off, and it makes it easier to explain when something is coming up.

The calendars are thick and laminated, come rolled up, and unrolled perfectly for use. It is exactly as expected and I have no complaints.

title: Exactly as expected, nice poly folders with a little business card holder
text:
These are great for when I want to hand out some materials to clients or landscaping crew members. The poly material means that if the folder is sitting on a damp truck seat or gets carried in the rain from truck to home, the documents don't get damaged. They do not have holes punched in them, which is my preference for how I intended to use them. You could, of course, punch holes in them if that was what you needed.

My business card fit in the included business card holder on the interior, adding to the professional feel. I will use the brighter colored ones for my children's artwork.

title: Awesome magnetic dry erase board
text:
I so appreciate this magnetic dry erase board, which is perfect for making a vision board. I have some little superstrong magnets and they stick perfectly to this board, and I love that I can write down goals, and then stick some pictures next to my goals to inspire me and help me visualize what things will actually look like.

The size of 18 x 24 is just right for me. The edges of the frame came together nicely and didn't have any rough or jagged areas, and it was easy to hang on the wall.

Overall I encountered no unpleasant surprises when using this magnetic dry erase board. It's exactly what I wanted and needed, and is exactly as expected.

title: Exactly as expected
text:
This is a great set of tab dividers, with kind of a thick paperboard material and the usual plastic tabs as dividers. I can't really tell the difference in quality between this and the Avery ones that I had previously been purchasing. I use a lot of tab dividers and other things both in homeschooling my children, and in managing my landscaping company and organizing all of the safety, client, employee, and other documents I have to keep track of.

Overall there were no unpleasant surprises in this pack of six sets of eight tab dividers. And the tabs were substantial enough that they are easy to see when in the binder with lots of papers.

title: I love these so much
text:
I do a lot of scheduling work as the owner of a landscaping company with employees, and while for a long time I was just doing a drag-and-drop thing on Google calendars, every so often Google calendars likes to break their software and make everything more challenging for me. On a recent update, they started popping up a window that I had to click every time I moved a job from one date to another, and I finally had enough.

Enter this cool calendar whiteboard. I can stand where I have it mounted, make as many iterations of my calendar as I need to and easily adjust and erase, and when it's finally all done, I just record it into the software where I need it, and I'm good to go.

The little strip of cork board on the bottom works great and means that I can post little notes to myself as a reminder for when I'm going to be doing my calendar work.

This three pack is exceptionally cool because my family also has one to use, and I use the third one for doing scheduling iterations when I want to sit down, I just set it in my lap and it is a comfortable size to sit and work on it. I just slide it behind the bookshelf when I'm not using it.

I invested in a set of colored Expo markers that have little erasers on the top, and they have been working perfectly for all of the things I want to do on this board. The board wipes clean easily without a problem.

title: Sleek, shiny, as expected, but all the rubber bumpers are wanting to come off
text:
The one problem with this lovely metal document tray is that all of the rubber bumpers at the very bottom, seem loose, and one of them arrived already having fallen off. I'm not sure what type of glue one uses to replace the rubber bumper on extremely slick painted metal, but I guess I need to take a trip to the hardware store to figure that out.

Aside from the problem with the rubber bumpers, this is a very nicely made document tray that arrived well packaged so that it seemed very unlikely to be damaged in shipment. I like that it is a little bit wider than the standard document tray, because what I usually do is have little items off to the side, like plant tags, business cards, photographs – and then I have normal 8.5 x 11 documents taking up the majority of the tray. This is working well for my workflow to keep me somewhat more organized than usual. I have a real weakness for these types of tray, as I really love having everything organized in just the right spot.

title: Lovely set of assorted plastic clipboards.
text: My clipboards arrived looking exactly like the ones in the picture, same colors, same type of clips, everything. The plastic clipboards seem pretty much identical to every other plastic clipboard I've ever purchased, and they have the top that sticks out a little farther and is easy for children to clip and unclip because it has a little bit better leverage than the smaller, more form fitted clipboards. The bright colors are attractive and fun, and I've been using these both to hand out to my landscaping employees for use in the wet weather at work, as well as to my kids when they need something to color on and don't want to sit at the table. They've worked perfectly fine, and none of them has shattered or broken yet. Overall this is a really nice set of basic plastic clipboards and I'm delighted to see them offered from Amazon.

title: So much fun!
text:
We are a huge fan of this brands peel and stick stickers for the kids rooms in our house, and of their seasonal stickers for the living room, close to the holidays. I just love that we can decorate, redecorate, and involve the kids in making the holidays and every days feel special with the fun the core from this line.

Recently, my husband had been looking around for some kind of a solution to help our children understand days of the week, and the events in the months to come. We definitely needed a calendar, but a traditional calendar has to hang from a hole in the wall, and we kind of hate putting holes in the wall. We also hate having things that could potentially get ripped down, like a pushpin, and injure somebody. This was the perfect solution for us.

I had just purchased a really cute set of dry erase markers for use in my business, and so while this came with one functional dry erase marker, we were already set up to do something fun. We use the included black marker to mark out all of the days of the month. Then, we drew cute little pictures for our upcoming holidays, like grandpa's birthday, St. Patrick's Day, and other upcoming events. Then, we began marking off the days of the month as each new day arrived.

It's been a great learning tool for the days of the week and the flow of the month, and helpful to our children in understanding the passage of time. So far, everything we needed to wipe off has come off gracefully. Overall I think this is a really ingenious solution, and I'm delighted with it. I have used the notes and the blank white decals in my office for to do lists and out the door lists of things to remember. Great set for most households, homeschooling households, and businesses.

title: Great for landscaping
text:
I have a crew in my landscaping company, and everybody needs a clipboard to take notes and keep track of all of the details at every job. Everybody goes through clipboards frequently, because it seems that we have two options, paperboard ones which do not handle the weather very well, or plastic ones which shatter and fragment when dropped, which, let's face it, even the most careful individual will occasionally drop the clipboard.

These aluminum ones, by contrast, seem to have that longevity factor that the other ones were missing. It is very thin and has a slim form factor, yet it does the job, not bending through normal use in writing. I really like that it is rain proof and presumably will not rust over time. I'm hoping these will last the crew a longer time and I won't need to keep purchasing and throwing away cheaper clipboards.

title: Binder of champions
text:
Each of the members of my landscaping crew has a work binder that holds a lot of safety and legal information, information about best practices and processes, things for helping them learn, etc. These binders are the perfect size and shape for holding all of the information I like them to have on site with them.

I really liked the little tab that you can use to open the binder, it has a little bit of a plastic coating at the tip so that it is very smooth and comfortable to operate, and the binder, while being sturdy and not flying open for no reason, is easy to open when you actually try. The leverage mechanism works great.

The binder itself seems a sturdy build and I do not expect any problems. It looks very similar to the much more expensive one I purchased recently at a local store, only this came in a four pack for a very reasonable price.

title: Exactly what I expected out of a set of bookends
text:
These bookends shipped well and arrived with no scratching or shifting in the packaging. When I put them on my bookshelves and asked them to hold up my books, they did the job admirably well and there were no unpleasant surprises in the use of them.

They have the proportions I would expect, and the shiny black coating is nice that it does not stick to my books, I once had a cheap bookend with a painted coating that did stick, but these have a slick surface that does not look like it would have the same issue.

Overall, these are doing the job holding up my shelf of cookbooks and a shelf of children's books, and I'm very pleased with them. Nothing fancy, but exactly as expected.

title: Exactly as expected!
text:
I use this product in the creation of employee binders to keep company processes and information organized and clean. These tab dividers are exactly what I expected, with generously sized tabs which stick out from all of the papers much better than the ones that do not call themselves extrawide.

These are made of the standard paper that such things are generally made of, and I don't really see any difference between this and the Avery brand ones that I already owned. They seem reasonably sturdy and are exactly what I would expect from this product.

title: Works great, looks identical to the Avery ones I have, but packaging presentation not ideal
text:
So the actual product is fantastic and these look and feel identical to the Avery ones that I have been using for some years. Everything seems sturdy, made of thick materials, and reinforced well enough to be functional for some time.

The one problem that I have is that in a three pack, I would expect each pack to be somewhat distinct so that I could grab one binder's worth of A-Z tabs in just a moment without a lot of fussing. Unfortunately, these are packaged with all three a tabs set right next to each other, all 3B tabs set right next to each other, etc., so in order to grab what I need for a single binder, I need to sit down and manually pull out every single letter of the alphabet. This is not ideal for me as a busy business owner, and the thing that I plan to use them for only requires one tab of each letter of the alphabet for each binder. Perhaps some people will use three letter A's, 3 B's, 3 C's, etc. in a single binder and thus this is a helpful method of packaging, but for me that was just a time waster.

Overall, I would buy this brands tabs in a single pack but would not purchase a multipack again for this reason.

title: Beautiful and functional
text: Sometimes I have to carry around just a few sheets of varying types of paper in my role as the owner of a small landscaping company, and this cool little rainbow documents sorter or file folder is the perfect thing to do just that. I've put a few of the documents I need most often in the folder and stored it in my vehicle, and they have stayed safe and wrinkle free, and well organized, in this. The rainbow coloration with the black on the outside looks really cool and I find it very appealing.

title: Easiest installation for a printer ever, print quality is stellar for colored landscape designs
text:
While putting together the actual printer unit and getting it onto the stand was a little bit of a nailbiting enterprise, everything went together as expected and worked well. But the real surprise came when it was time to connect to my computer and begin actually printing things on to it. I wanted to use the Wi-Fi rather than a wired connection, because I wanted it in a front room of my office rather than right next to my computer. I was kind of worried given that my Wi-Fi router is across the garage and through a few walls, and my computer isn't even in the same room as it, but the installation went so ridiculously smoothly and it receives information just fine. I couldn't believe it! I just follow the instructions from the instruction manual online and everything set itself up, almost. This has never happened to me before, and printer installations are usually giant pain, so I've just got to give Epson mad props for doing such a good job on this.

The printing itself is stunning. I purchased some Epson paper and chose to go with the thicker standard paper rather than the regular, because I like to print out my landscape designs in full color with photos, little colored in shrubs, etc. and I want the presentation to be truly that. Though I'm used to going to the printshop and paying $15 a print for this, I was actually more impressed with the output of this Epson. Sometimes at my local printshop, I'll get little lines, or one or two colors will appear little bit dull. Right off the bat, the print quality on this was completely stunning, and I did not notice a single issue. With the Wi-Fi being so far away, it took about a minute and 1/2 for my document, which is full of color photos, to send to the printer, but as soon as it received all of the information it printed quickly and without a problem. It automatically defaults to cutting the paper itself, and it did a perfect job of this, crisply and cleanly cutting the paper exactly where it needed so that my design looked hundred percent perfect. I appreciate that it has a manual cut feature if I ever want to little bit of extra whitespace, but I'm mostly happy for it to do that job for me.

Overall, I could not be happier with the ease of set up, print quality, and overall build on this thing. I wish I'd gotten this 10 years ago!

title: Ridiculously cute and just perfect for family card giving
text: This set is absolutely perfect for my family. I have two small kids who will love the animal themed cards, and two family members that I want to give the cupcake and the I love you card two. All of the cards are beautifully embellished with different elements that make them a pleasure to examine and feel, and make it clear that you're giving a really thoughtfully made card. title: I didn't know I needed this until I found it. They are great!
text:
I am a landscaper and use vinyl flags on wire stakes to mark irrigation leaks, plants needing replacement, etc. Often our work is wet and dirty, so using a normal sharpie on wet and dirty flags simply does not work, the markers smear and refuse to adhere.

These markers by contrast work when the flags are damp, and I do not need to huddle in my truck with brand new flags and a dry pen, we can just mark in the field and reuse flags as is convenient.

These are fantastic and well worth the price.

title: So much fun! They really do erase
text:
I was so excited to get the test out these erasable highlighters, it felt like I was a little kid again. In contrast to the pilot friction line which has highlighters that are raised by the included "eraser" on the top which creates friction and heat on the paper to erase your inclines, these by contrast work by having a clear marker on the other side that acts as the eraser. I would have to guess this is a pH reaction? Whatever it is, it is super cool, and I have had fun making and erasing notes in my bullet journal and my kids also had fun making big scribble drawings and then erasing portions of them in fancy patterns.

These are super fun and make you feel like you are eight years old and a supersecret spy person.

title: Not that fancy, and a little heavy for normal white glue to hold on
text:

I was unimpressed with the cheap look, but my two and five year old had no complaints and enjoyed playing with them.

title: Simple crafts are great!
text:
My kids colored these up with glitter glue, stickers and more to make snowflakes for the holiday. I love simple craft products like this which allow us to be in charge of thinking up the ideas and implementing them.

My kids had a lovely time, the doilies seemed sturdy and nicely punched out, and I liked the variety of sizes.

title: Great peel and stick eyes for paper crafting
text:
These don't stick to odd materials or felt, but stuck great to paper. The little tabs on there meant that my two year old could even participate in giving things googly eyes and peel the backing off herself. She found this massively appealing.

Crayola always knows how to make things fun, and these eyes are no exception. While some of the colors and eyes made me cringe a bit (the yellow and red are valid but eeew to me), the kids loved them and had a blast.

title: Exactly as expected.
text: I have never purchased an unsatisfactory binder clip, and this was no exception. It works exactly right, had no issues with tension or the finish on it, and overall performs exactly as a small binder clip should.

title: Wish could choose color, but quality is stellar

It works great, is nicely designed, and seems very sturdy.

title: Great staple/ basic clipboard
text:
I give these out to my landscaping crews to keep their notes on. As the clipboards get dirty or start to fail every 6 months, I provide fresh ones.

These are the standard hardboard clipboard material - kind of shiny, but with a general feeling of texture to them. I am sure they should not remain damp if you want them to last. The clip is firm but not too firm to where it is hard to open.

These sturdy, quality folders are gorgeous. I LOVE the rainbow motif and the encouragement to create. I am using these for my landscape desigj work to stay organized on big projects, and two for my kids artwork (for the daily stuff on typing paper).

The finish is glossy, the stock is thick and not too bendy or cheap. Only complaint I have is that there is avery branding on the front of each folder, as well as the usual bar code and labels on the back. I'd prefer a clean front with no branding.

text:
I love correction tape. It is less necessary in the age of Frixion pens, but still, often I am filling out something official and need some wite-out, but don't want to deal with the smell, the mess, the clumps. This stuff is fast to apply, no mess, no fuss. It is as opaque as expected. I use two layers if needed, but usually one layer is fine if I didn't bold things.

This case is perfect for small offices. I've gone through two and after many months of storage, the rest of the pack is still functional and ready to roll.

title: Really great gift set!

title: It dissolves well, but doesn't stick, sharpies bleed on it, and doesn't look very white
text:
I have mixed feelings about these labels. On the one hand, they really do dissolve and I don't need to do anything in particular beyond just scrub them off with a sponge or put them through the dishwasher to have my food labels disappear.

On the other hand, they have a weird texture and don't look very sturdy, bright, or high-quality, my sharpie marker doesn't show up as well as usual on them and kind of bleeds out for an indistinct look, and they don't stick that well, so they often fly off of my frozen food container before I even get it in the freezer.

Overall I think I would buy them again, but I really hope that they continue honing this technology and come up with a label that sticks better and holds writing better.

I would definitely buy these again.

title: Absolutely love these effective dissolvable labels

These are great! Why didn't they come up with this sooner.

title: Work great and look professional
text: I have been sending out informational packets to landscaping clients for many years, either before I meet with them so that they know who we are and what we do, or after we have done some design work and I need to submit additional paperwork, documentation, etc. Having a big stack of these beautiful white peel and stick envelopes has been just the thing for streamlining the packaging of my marketing materials. We appreciate that the envelopes are not those ugly gold ones that seem ubiquitous at the office supply store, and I appreciate the sanitary peel and stick action. They look great, or thick enough to do the job and look nice, and they don't fly open in the mail. Very satisfied.

title: Lighting fast prints, minor lines in prints despite running maintenance on unit
text:
I've owned this printer for a whopping few hours thus far, so cannot speak to how the ink lasts. The lower cost of replacement ink (as opposed to my Canon laser printer) and the shorter warmup time were the two major selling points for his model. I got tired of waiting 5 minutes for a single print from my Canon, as it warmed up and spun itself.

For reference, the replacement ink is: DURABrite Ultra R02 Ink, and you buy black, yellow, magenta and cyan separately. At the time of writing the genuine ink cost at retail is cheaper than the off-brand cartridges I was buying for my Canon.

I had some hiccups with my driver installation and the printer initially just printed pages and pages of garbage whenever I plugged in the USB connection to my computer. An irritating support call ensued where the person (obviously Indian) didn't understand the problem and then persistently told me to call Microsoft because it was their problem, not Epson's. After getting used to the wonderful American tech support through Canon, this was a harsh comedown. I had to be extremely persistent, no joke, to get to talk with a tech support person who actually knew what she was doing, and she fixed my problem in 20 minutes and I was off to the races.

Unit has lightning fast printing. Seriously, it just spits stuff out. I adjusted it to operate in quiet mode and it was a little slower, more akin to a normal inkjet printer.

Only problem is that even on these early prints, I had some persistent (albeit very faint) lines in the photos that aren't going away with servicing the unit. I've run all the maintenance tests and activities from the settings window and I still have a line every inch or so. Kind of bummed to have a print quality issue like this right out the gate. Not the end of the world for me personally as I get anything truly important printed professionally, but for a printer in this price range, it doesn't seem right. From normal reading distance, the lines are not that perceptible, and overall the photos do appear vibrant. It's just if you really examine that the lines are definitely there on a variety of pictures I printed.

Overall, everything seems intuitive and easy to run so far. I've scanned, printed, copied, and inserted a memory stick and viewed photos on my computer to print from that. I like the very responsive touchscreen a LOT. This interface is a huge upgrade from my Canon, whose menu came out of the 80's and made that thick instruction manual a constant necessity.

I think the new ink is overall a successful innovation (thus far, on day 1, given the brightness of images and speed of printing) and the touchscreen interface is excellent, but given the print quality issues (faint lines that don't go away with maintenance) and offshore customer support I am not sure I'd pay an inflated price for this until they work out some of the bugs.

title: Quiet, competent, and free of all those little design flaws that make things a pain to use
text:
Sometimes, you don't know what you're missing in a product until you've tried one that is so far and away better but it seems laughable you struggled with your old one for so long. I own a small landscaping company with four employees, and have been starting to find it challenging to deal with the masses of paperwork that I unfortunately need to send to the recycling center each week. I had been using a junky little shredder that sat on top of a standard plastic waste basket, but because it was noisy and slow, I only used it for things that definitely, definitely needed it. It shredded things into little ribbons, which piled up and filled the basket quickly so it needed constant emptying. Of course, because it was such a pain and I only used it for the critically important things that absolutely must be shredded, I was left with a nagging sensation that it was only a matter of time before some personal information was stolen from the recycling center, because I was still putting hard to shred things like envelopes with credit card offers into the regular recycling bin without shredding.

So getting to try this incredibly sturdy, quiet, and highly functional crosscut shredder was amazing. The cross cuts don't pile up in a bulging mass the way the long skinny strips do, so I can appreciate its small size without noticing any real downside that it needs to be emptied more often, because it doesn't. And even though this unit is pretty heavy, if you lock the top on and use the handle, it's very easy to move and it is such a perfect shape that it fits underneath my desk and out of the way so I actually do use it daily. It's not nearly as noisy as my previous one, and I feel perfectly comfortable using it while my toddler's napping.

It shredded a few old DVDs that had delicate information on them, some old credit cards, as well as those ubiquitous credit card offers that I seem to get in the mail in spades, even though I never use them.

If I had known how much I was going to like this, I would've invested in it much sooner. It really takes a weight off my mind to know that all of the proprietary information as well as sensitive documents for my business are all being taken care of securely, and given how small and easy it is to use, it just tucks under my desk and gets used on a daily basis without feeling like it's a fuss. Quiet, clean, and competent. Not sure what more I can ask for in a basic business shredder.

title: ScanSnap vs Brother: One's better for home use, other better for a business network
text:
After owning a Fujitsu Scansnap S1500 for some years, and using it to digitize an entire file cabinet's worth of paperwork for my landscaping business so that I could make my home office more compact prior to having a baby, I was 100% sold on the idea of having a professional grade document scanner. I scan about 3 inches of stacked paper every month between the employee records, timesheets, landscape design notes, etc. I've also digitized a lot of my old family photos so that everybody in the family can have a copy of these special pictures to look at and save for future generations.

Given my digital office, I have a lot of experience with document scanners (I also have owned two portable ones, which both ended up being disappointing in comparison to my ScanSnap) and I was excited to test this brother brand against my Fujitsu scansnap.

First of all, I noticed that the action of my Fujitsu scansnap is so much easier than this Brother model. I open the scansnap, the software remembers my preferences, and all I have to do is load the paper and press one button. The Brother model on the other hand requires me to wait about 10 seconds for it to notice that I've opened the lid, then I have to press PC, file or photo, okay, and start. It then takes me back to the menu and makes me press two buttons prior to every scan. It also has a popup on my computer screen after every scan. Though it will continue scanning the next inserted document even if I ignore the popup, often I'm trying to multitask and type emails while it's scanning, and so it's deeply annoying to have this window keep popping up.

It's also noisier than my ScanSnap, by a long shot. It's OK in my home office, but in a cubicle office, this would get annoying quickly, while the scansnap is pretty unobtrusive.

I also didn't really like the flimsy, unresponsive touch screen. How hard is it to make a touchscreen that feels solid and actually noticed every time you push a button? If this is truly a technological challenge for a company like Brother, maybe they should have just had a few buttons on the front and ditched the touchscreen idea.

The Brother model also only holds 50 sheets instead of 100 with my scansnap. Not a big deal usually, but when scanning a large stack I appreciate not having to babysit the scanner to keep feeding more sheets in.

The scanning speed feels similar for simple text PDFs. For photos, they are of similar quality, with the ScanSnap ever so slightly better.

Here is where the Brother model shines: In an office setting where you are placing the scanner in a main room, away from everybody's computer, and you need people to be able to operate the machine and send a document to a USB thumb drive, an email server, to the web, to the network, or to FTP, the Brother model is able to do all of these things, while the Fujitsu scansnap can do none. This is obviously a model meant for a business setting.

Overall, if I were choosing a scanner for an office where multiple people will be using this via a network or in a setting where they are scanning but not in front of their own computer, the Brother wins hands down, because the Fujitsu scansnap just isn't set up to do any of these things. However, when scanning in a home office where the scanner is right next to your own desktop computer and you can set the default settings in the program and just enjoy fast, quiet, one click scanning, the Fujitsu scansnap beats the brother, both on function and on price.

title: IT WORKS!!!
text:
Love, LOVE, LOVE this!! This token board has been instrumental in getting my son to focus and work hard in school. The chart already has magnets on the back, so as soon as you take it out the box, it's ready to go up on your fridge! There also hooks for other surfaces. For set-up, you will have put the Velcro on the back of the stars, but that is it. What is great about Velcro is that you don't have to worry about them falling off or sliding around like magnets. Stickers need to be repositionable. So, Velcro really is the way to go. Using a dry erase marker, there's a spot for your child's name, the behavior you are working on and the reward for when that goal is accomplished. There are five spots on the caterpillar.

Just idea of how beneficial this has been He was young 5 in September so we decided to put him Pre-K instead of Kindergarten. While he attended Pre-School, all he wants to do is play; however, the Pre-K he goes to operates more like a play-based Kindergarten and Kindergarten next year will basically be 1st grade. So, he has academic structure at points within his day, but because he just wants to play, he was refusing to do his work and making negative choices. His teacher recommended an incentive at home to get him excited and focused. So, I found this, and after about a month, it's clicked and he's been on a roll. My son has a separate chart that his teacher fills out as they move throughout their day. I review it and if he has all green checks, he gets a star. If there was a problem, no star. After five stars, he has earned his reward. It took about 3 weeks for him to really understand the importance and significance of the chart, but now a month in, he has earned two rewards. I keep the rewards small like $5-$10 prizes. A bath toy or fun, smelly markers You can choose something else like a trip to the library or museum. Or a special dessert after dinner that night. Whatever works best for you and your family, but at the end of the day the most important thing is that IT WORKS!!!

text: Whether you're color coding, sending these to school with kids or sharing these with friends, you can't go wrong with these folders. My personal fave color is the aqua but I know I'll be using the others as well. The covers are a bit textured and might be the type to take a removable label easily. I usually just use a black marker on a folder unless I know it's not gonna be a permanent folder.

title: Very classy looking!
text: This is a great little paperclip holder or anything holder really. It's pretty enough to display in any room and might even make a cute little dish for wrapped candies. Great to keep and nice looking to give as a gift.

title: These are super cute and well made
text: This is a nice-sized package of lanyards you can use and switch out to match you or your kids' outfits or share with some coworkers. I got them to use at a craft show where they issue vendor badges. I got tired of trying to pin their badges to my sweater and not ruin it, so a lanyard (in my fave aqua color) from this set was the perfect solution! Great for vacation if you like to have your ID handy too.

title: Rolls smoothly and evenly
text: A nice amount of these because sometimes you buy two or three then end up doing a project and running out of adhesive. That probably won't happen with this nice-sized pack. The one I tried rolled nicely and laid out the adhesive smooth and even. Great for less mess with crafts or kids.

title: Very nice
text: I like that the end has a cap on it so tape isn't accidentally dispensed. Great for anything you need to turn into a sticky note! Or for scrapbooking or kids' crafts-no messy glue!

title: Very nice and a classy touch for my craft show table
text: These are so much better for payment notices etc. that I like to post on my craft bazaar table since it's got a little stand and takes up less room that way. The gold edging gives it a nice classy touch.

title: My favorite type of bag clip!
text: I just love this type of bag clip and have been using it from various places for years now. They're always pretty sturdy and hold the bags shut nice and tight. Sometimes it's just fun to color coordinate with the package you're closing. ;)

title: Love that the pen compartment's separate
text: This looked perfect for storing some of the papers I take to craft shows, and I like how the pen compartment's nice and generous as well as being separate. Usually my pens spill all over the rest of the inside of the clipboard  but it won't happen with this one. Can't wait to take it to my show in a couple weeks!

title: Using this outside the box of usual uses...
text: I sew a lot and found this was perfect to keep on my pressing board with all my tools I need to press while I sew. It even fits a small pair of scissors nicely. It's so much easier to rotate it instead of having to reach for a tool that's on the other side of the room.

title: The perfect count package for use at vendor and craft shows
text: I've always wanted to get some of these but never saw a smaller pack of four until now. Can't wait to use these at my first fall craft show in November! This type of holder makes for a super nice-looking sign and provides a good way to hold checkout information.

title: Super nice, great to keep all or share
text: These are really nice journals, basic smooth paper, nice colors and each comes in its own cello bag for easy sharing or gift giving. Just a note for teal fanatics like me: it's a touch darker than the picture but all monitors and phones look different and I'm still pleased with it.

title: Way nicer than the mouse pads from the 90s and early 20s
text: These are thinner but very sturdy and a good value. For my particular computer space, I like stacking two of them for the right height, but one works just as well. The colors are all nice-each pad's reversible if you get tired of the color on one side. My fave of the colors is the aqua.

title: It's nice and I like the tabs but...
text:
In this day and age (yeah I know, who keeps a paper list of passwords right?) the spaces provided for passwords should be tons longer! It has 3 spaces for passwords which is totally unnecessary, so out of needing more space for longer-required passwords, I just write right over top where it says 2 or 3.

The notes area is good for jotting down those answers to the annoying security questions. Those can't be stored in an online password keeper as far as I know, so this does have a tiny advantage over the cloud based keeper. It's also a good way to keep my passwords handy for my family in case they'd ever need them quickly. And it still beats having a notebook that gets dog-eared. With tabs, it's easy to find whatever site I might need to hunt for.

title: Great refills for the label printer I got
text: Very handy to have a whole roll of these if you want to print more than one label at a time. There's no waste like with using a printer--I was using whole sheets before and one side wouldn't get printed at all. More economical!

title: Professional looking labels
text: Great for using if you've got a small online business on Amazon or other places and doesn't take up much room. I was excited to add this to my own small biz.

title: Nice to have a book that was actually designed for passwords
text: I haven't kept a physical contact info book for a long time, but somehow I still like a physical book for passwords since you sometimes just need quick access to them. You get quite a few pages in the alpha dividers and some random blank pages at the end. There's a little pocket at the very end that I'll probably use to temporary house those little tiny scraps where I quickly write down a password. There's a couple ribbon bookmarks and an elastic to keep it open to a page you might use a lot and an elastic loop for a pen. Very nice little book!

title: Very nice pads, I like the narrow ruled kind!
text: Add in a fun light blue color and I have something functional and enjoyable to use for notes. The paper isn't the super smooth like school paper, (think more on the order of newsprint but nicer) but it's fine for notes. I'm not sure a Sharpie or gel pen wouldn't bleed through, but I like regular old black ink pens, so these work great for me!

title: Awesome concept
text: I've had those old type dry erase board erasers that once they get dirty, they just drag it around the board, but with this one, that'll be avoided. We don't cover our entire board with writing, so I think the amount of refills included might just last us fairly long. Very clean erasing!

title: Great legal pads
text: I like that they've got different colored spines so you can tell whose pad this is if you're in an office or just at home and assign family members a color. Very nice and smooth for writing.

title: Super nice file box
text: I love how sturdy this box is and the latch seems super secure too. I won't have to worry about it coming open while carrying it around. Nice to get a few little starter files and labels as well!

title: Absolutely love it!
text: Not only was it in my favorite color, but this cash box is just the right size for bills. I especially like the covering over the change part (it locks too) which helps keep it from spilling in case the box gets turned over accidentally. I can't wait to take this to the next craft show! Just a note of caution and it could only be this particular unit, but I found a fairly sharp spot inside the box which I'm going to need to use a metal file on so it doesn't cut or poke anyone who's helping me at the show.

title: Love the full backing of magnet
text: I love that these notepads are backed by a full magnet sheet on the back rather than just a small top magnet like some notepads. I have others that sag when hanging but these aren't about to do that. Very happy with this set! Would make a nice gift for someone too.

title: Lots of room for storage
text: Perfect for holding my Kindle and some notepads and pens as well as remotes. All my favorite stuff can live in one place now!

title: Love it!
text: I'm going to use it for my craft show pricing supplies or maybe eventually use it for sewing tools. Either way, it's an awesome product and super handy that it swivels.

title: Great cushion, very comfortable and supporting
text: I really like using this cushion on my home office chair. It's great for the lower back issues I get sometimes, but it also gives me a little more height that the chair itself won't do (it's up as high as it goes). The extra height should help with neck and shoulder pain by making me more the right level for working at the computer.

title: Get a set and share the extras
text: I love the colors these came in although I'm partial to the aqua-green one. The notebooks themselves are super nice, and I like the paper weight and thinner ruling.

title: Super cute!
text: I love list pads and these have magnets that aren't just a small strip on the back. The whole back is magnetic which makes them hang on the fridge so much nicer. The pages aren't trying to fall off the pad like other pads I've had. The dogs are just adorable. I'm partial to the dachshund one ;)

title: Very nice and like the choices
text: I liked that I was able to pick lined vs. dotted and whether I wanted a 3-pack or 10-pack. These definitely exceed expectations, and I also like that the paper's more the weight I like for writing.

title: Can't wait to try this on a road trip
text: This tray seems to be just what I was looking for in a nice road trip work area. I mainly read, but at least the tray makes for a nice little eating area for catching food on the fly or jotting down any notes. There seems to be ample room for storing anything an adult or a kid might need on a road trip.

title: Very nice and would make a great gift
text: I love a journal with normal lines that aren't dotted, so this was a no-brainer especially in my fave color. The lines are narrower too which I also prefer. The back pocket's a nice feature for hanging onto receipts you might need later. The elastic and ribbon are good for markig pages especially if someone's like me and writes kind of randomly! Would make a super nice gift!

title: They write really nice, erase nicely and don't smell
text: I like a good dry erase marker, and I was happy to find out these fit the bill. They even erased nicely after the message was up on my whiteboard for a few days. I've had some that refuse to erase, but these are great! There's no obnoxious marker smell either.

title: Greart for scrapbook projects or for sorting out your taxes or other papers
text: I never have enough room for papers at tax time, so these boxes are going to come in handy to separate out business, farm and personal papers and receipts. They'd be great for what they're actually intended for as well, but since I don't scrapbook, I thought I'd use them another way. Nice and sturdy.

title: Used these as reinforcement to close my Christmas cards
text: Sometimes the glue on card envelopes just doesn't cut it, so we used these fun Christmas stickers across the flap. About three did the trick. I also like them to cover up price tags that might be printed on a box I'm gifting.

title: Perfect midyear supply for your favorite teacher
text: Midyear is a perfect time for teachers to have a new stash of pencils on hand for kids who are always needing one. At least the teachers I know always do, and they did it out of the goodness of their hearts. Why not gift your elementary favorite teacher with a box of these this month?

title: Not just for pencils :)
text: This is a nice collection of these bags. If you do want to keep pens and pencils corralled they're great for that, but you can also store makeup or small electronics like your USB drives in them too. The mesh is easy to see through unlike some storage bags that are solid.

title: Nice size and sturdy
text: I really like these notebooks for carrying around in a purse or tote! Usually those softcover or spiral notebooks I'd haul around get all jumbled and messy at the bottom of your tote, but with the elastic helping keep the pages together and the fact that these are hardcover, I don't think I'll have that issue anymore. :)

title: Glaring mistakes in American History along with tons of typos, not a learning tool at all!
text: In our opinion, the only thing this calendar is good for is your basic calendar. Actually, my family's been having fun pointing out the errors. Seriously, even if someone made this using online sources, the least they could do was spell the names right! Teachers, this definitely isn't a learning tool for your kids! I was excited to get this because my husband and daughter are huge history fans, but when they caught something in the first couple of days, they paged on ahead and found yet more errors. Sorry, but this is not something I'd recommend, buy for someone or gift not at any price.

title: Very nice size sticker tags
text: FIrst of all I LOVE that they all say Merry Christmas because that's what I personally celebrate. The designs are cute, and the only drawback is the dark blue tag probably won't be usable because not even my black Sharpie shows up well on it. The other colors are fine.

title: Very nice and complete set for the small business owner
text: I use the fine taggers a lot with my doll clothes I sell at craft shows, so I was definitely happy to find this set. And it even came with some 'sale' tags along with lots of extra plastic barbs, 5 replacement needles and even more tags in a kraft brown color that'd be perfect for anyone selling pottery or rustic type items. I'm sure I'll be getting a lot of use out of this as craft shows are returning.

title: Just the perfect compact size but big enough for decent note taking or lists
text: This is a really nice set of notebooks that look like field journals (enough that I can gift another set of them to a nephew). I like the feel of the paper, and the pages are really generous for this size notebook. Easy to grab one of these quickly when you need some decent writing material.

title: A fun flowery notebook
text: I was so glad that the green I selected turned out to the be the aqua-green shade I love. And the embossed flower design on the cover just makes this notebook look like it'll be fun to use. The pages are smooth, and I'm pretty sure a gel pen could be used. The elastic band can either keep it shut or mark a page. The very back cover has an expanding pocket. I wouldn't stuff it full, but you could keep receipts, coupons or little flyers inside it.

title: Great for saving a wall paint job!
text: These are really nice and stick right onto the wall where your doorknob might be making some scratches in the wall paint or finish. I cleaned the wall before attaching so it'd be at its best sticking capacity.

title: Was glad to find my printer model listed on this
text: A drum unit is always a good thing to have around if you use your Brother printer a lot. When my first one went out, it just went out with the alert light coming on, so now I'm ready for when it needs another one.

title: This notebook is super versatile and elegant for gift giving as well
text: I like that you get the elastic and a couple of ribbons for page marking. When it said thick paper, I was worried it'd be too thick, but it's about what I've found in other notebooks like this. I think you could use a gel pen and not have it bleed through. The very back has a pocket that expands maybe half an inch. There're some sticker sheets inside there in case someone turns the notebook into a planner or budget keeper. Lots of uses, and the rose gold is so elegant, I'd be proud to give it as a gift.

title: Super nice and very attractive
text: Anyone would be happy to get a gift like this one. I personally like the elastic that lets me mark pages with it, and the bookmark is a nice feature too.

title: Very cute and portable
text: This is just the right size to take along on trips. Since it tucks easily in a bag, it shouldn't get lost easily. I like the various stickers that can be used too.

title: Kind of like the old pencils
text: These are shaped more like pencils were when I went to school eons ago. I don't particularly like the triangular shape, but since I don't use pencils, maybe others do like this shape. It just feels uncomfortable from what I remember. I was going to give these to my niece for her classroom. The kids will be excited over the different colors.

title: Nice sized assortment
text: Great for home use, keeping as incentives or for teachers to keep for those times when a kid doesn't have a pencil.

title: Perfect for home use or Sunday School/CCD classes
text: These are great little incentive stickers whether you teach your kids religion at home or if you're a teacher or religion class volunteer. Very nice assortment!

title: Super nice and attractive too
text: This is perfect for the home working office person who works in the same room as a TV and needs a little organization for TV remote along with pens and various office writing utensils. Best of both worlds in this nice-looking holder.

title: Works great and I love the length of the barbs
text: I love using one of these tools for pricing my craft show items, and the size barbs included are just the perfect length. I'm not sure I'll have much use for the dark color barbs at the moment, but they'd be nice for any dark colored fabric like jeans. The tool came in my favorite color which was just icing on the cake. Very nice product! I've gone through a few of these, so I'm hoping this one will last longer.

title: This is perfect for my return to being in craft fairs
text: This is just what I was needing to downsize a bit from my "stuff" that goes with me to craft shows. My current clipboard that holds things is bigger and kind of hard to lug around. I was so happy to find this nice streamline version (in my favorite color to boot!) that's big enough to hold what I need but small enough to discourage me from stuffing unneeded items inside it. A legal pad (the 8 1/2x11 kind) fits just perfect under the clip and inside for storage after the show, and a couple of pens will fit nicely inside. I'm looking forward to using this in November!

title: Lots of uses
text: Great for teachers of young kids as incentives or just a good way to mark your own home activity calendar and color code by stars. Reward yourself with a star in your planner for getting tasks done, lots of uses along with grading papers.

title: Flexible yet stable
text: Love the colors on each side and the idea that it's a little more flexible than the usual mouse mat. Yep I'm old school and still use a mouse with a laptop, so I'm glad there are even better mouse mats available now.

title: Great for personal or office use
text: It's the perfect size for a smaller family maybe 3 or less kids to all be able to add their activities. For office use (which this one will be doing) it'll be great to hang outside a meeting room and know at a glance when that room is booked and who it's booked for.

title: Perfect size and love the color
text: This color gives a nice little pop to my website orders when I send them. I like that the size is generous too. I don't think I'll need anything bigger than this. Very sturdy too.

title: Nice holding sticky notes
text: I was really pleased with how well these notes hold as far as the sticky on the back being good. Usually only the name brand was worth getting for me, but I do love having ruled notes to hang on different places as well as sticking to other paper. I like keeping a list of books currently downloaded on my Kindle, and these notes stick well to the back of a Kindle.

title: Convenient and easy to use
text: I love that these are just free standing pages. They can be used every day if you want, or you can use one for each project you have going. Very nicely arranged pages.

title: These are great!
text: We love this notepad. It's nice having it on the corner of the counter to work on grocery lists which is a big help for menu planning too. Or if the counter space is needed, it can hang on the fridge. It's great having both types of lists on one pad and handy.

title: Very pretty card
text: I loved this card when I got it to give. The little pictures on the front are raised up like someone would do if they'd handmade a card. A card that anyone would be proud to give a graduate!

title: Very gorgeous
text: A very classy and beautiful grad card that anyone would be proud to give. This company consistently supplies great products, and I always can rely on this brand to be top notch.

title: Nice generous size bottles!
text: Usually bottles of whiteboard cleaner come in such tiny sizes, they don't last very long. These are very nice sizes, and I especially liked the twin pack--one for home, one for the office or classroom.

title: Very nice and cute looking box
text: This is a nice little sturdy box, but as the listing pictures, if you're taking it to a vendor show, the bills will only fit in the bottom. It'll be nice though for transporting the extra cash home from the register when doing a two-day show though. Would also be ideal to keep items locked away and high on a shelf from inquisitive little hands.

title: Such a nice assortment, it makes me want to be in third grade again
text: This is a super nice kit to get that favorite third or second grade student all squared away for school this fall. Or you could split it apart and give it to various kids based on what they might need/want, your choice. Lots of very nice school supplies included.

title: Perfect for wearing or just keeping your card clean and unlost
text: I knew I'd misplace this card if I didn't have something to put it in, and these are just the thing. There's enough for me to share with the family as well. Want to wear it for your job? No problem, there are enough lanyards with clips for each card holder. I like that the top zips to protect the card inside from spills or jobs that have you getting wet from time to time. The plastic is very nice and sturdy, and the card just fits inside.

title: Perfect set whether for giving to your favorite teacher or student
text: This is an amazingly complete set of what kids this age are using in schools, at least around here. Perfect to leave as is to give to one favorite student or teacher, or use the separates to donate to school drives or even keep what you need. That's what I plan to do.

title: Attractive and very nice to write in
text: This journal makes writing a breeze and even though it's dotted instead of lines, it's still not a problem. It could be used for sketching out a room or space layout. I like that it has two marker ribbons too.

title: Very nice and handy to have a year's worth
text: This is a nice collection to keep on hand. Since we haven't been doing birthdays in person, it comes in handy to have a card to pop a gift card into for family members or good friends. I like that there's space to write your own message.

title: Gorgeous addition to any office (here it's our home office)
text: This is a functional yet attractive piece that has lots of storage for all your office needs. Goes together pretty easily, and I feel like it's sturdy for our needs. I love the rose gold color!

title: Classy looking and sturdy
text: This is a nice inbox/outbox or whatever you'd want to file in it type of tray. I really love the color, so not only is it useful but it's a touch of class for the home office (or away as your needs might dictate.)

title: Useful and pretty to look at too
text: An elegant addition to the office, this piece has lots of great storage in it too. I really think the gold looks so classy!

title: Dress up your home office or workplace away from home
text: A classy version of the "typical" pushpin, these will be great in the home or away office. Container they come in is sturdy enough to be "the" container--no need to re-home the pushpins. Very pretty!

title: Very happy with this!
text: Perfect size for our intended use--quick quotes or birthday greetings around the house or at the office. Would be ideal for photo ops (announcements for baby, engagement, etc.) and other short welcome greetings.

title: Very warm yet classy!
text: I love the soft-feeling cover on this notebook. The pages are normal paper weight type pages which I love for regular pen writing. I always like a book with an elastic band to mark where I am. There's also a ribbon for that and a small elastic loop for a pen. Once I find a pen that's perfect for a notebook, I like keeping it close at hand! Super pleased.

title: This is just the perfect size
text: The perfect size and weight, it was available in my favorite color, it bends just a little for easier toting around, and I love that the pages aren't too thick but thick enough to use a fine point gel pen on. There's a marker ribbon inside for anyone using this for journaling. Very pleased!

title: It's a nice concept
text: I loved the idea of being able to attach a marker and eraser holder to my whiteboard's frame, but the adhesive didn't quite hold it up there, and unfortunately my whiteboard isn't magnetic. I think instead we'll have to just use the hardware and attach it with the screw. The container itself is great and holds an eraser and a few markers as well. Very nice design and idea!

title: Best dry erase markers I've used
text: These markers are great! I especially was curious to see how the writing erased after being on my whiteboard for longer than just a day or two, and I found that after a week or more, it still erased beautifully and completely! The tip's just the right width, not too thick or skinny.

title: Generous size package dots are perfect size
text: Great little sticky dots for marking anything from items to be donated or sold to telling kids' property apart or other belongings when there's any possible confusion. My use will be marking items I've already gone through in my constant efforts to get more organized.

title: Great size and sturdy magnets
text: This is a nice sized list that can stick on the fridge or come down while you're making a list and menu. I like that the two are together, and it's perfect for ordering groceries online and seeing exactly what you need for a certain meal. Would make an awesome little "just because" gift for someone too.

title: Pretty and functional!
text: I loved how these looked on the screen, and they'r even nicer in person! The design is so pretty and goes perfectly with my doll clothes biz. When I get back to craft shows, these bags will be perfect for hiding surprise gifts that my mom shoppers get for their kids. Very classy looking too!

title: Great stickers, concise message, perfect!
text: These stickers are what I've hunted for a long time, and I'm so glad to find them. The message is clear, the sticker is just the right size, and I'm happy to finally have something to mark my fragile packages with.

title: Gorgeous folders, makes being organized a little more fun
text: I like this whole line of products and how they coordinate with each other. These folders are a little more sturdy feeling paper than the usual manila ones are. You get three nice designs and four folders in each. I was especially excited to see one design completely matches the zipper organizers I have from the brand.

title: Pack of four makes it easy to gift individual books to others or keep all or one
text: I loved the colorful paint-looking splashes on these books. They just make you smile looking at them. The paper is just enough heavier than regular notebook paper but not too heavy. I wouldn't call the lines college ruled exactly, but they're not super wide either for anyone wondering that. I like the double coils that seem to hold up better than single coils.

title: Great concept in a gel pen
text: I like a nice stick pen sometimes, and this product combines two of the best things: A good comfortable stick pen and gel ink inside that writes very nice and smooth.

title: These are so darn cute and perfect for stocking stuffers
text: I love that there's a nice variety of colors in this package, something for everyone. I can keep them in various spots in the house too where you just need a little something to write a note in. Great product!

title: Nice products and perfect for my needs
text: The folder size is just perfect and not too wide. Sometimes if box end folders are too wide, it's hard to keep enough things inside, but this appears to be a width that's perfect for my business needs. Plastic is sturdier than the cardboard box end folders I've had in the past too.

title: Very attractive and sturdy journal
text: This is a really nice journal for either personal use or gift giving. I always like the elastic to close it with or mark a place where I need to refer to. I found three place marking ribbons as opposed to the usual two. The paper is nice and thicker but not too thick to know if you've just got one page at a time. It should stand up to any gel pen use, and the pages are college ruled, my personal favorite kind.

title: Love this company's line of complementary and matching items
text: I just had to add another set of notebooks that happens to match some of my other items from this company. I prefer the college rule which these have, and with a set of three, I can keep a couple and share one.

title: One of my favorite notebook sets
text: These are great notebooks from the sturdy but not too thick paper to the elastic to hold it shut or keep the place you go to a lot. I absolutely love the aqua color.

title: Perfect for on-the-go note taking
text: When you can't really get to your phone easily, sometimes it's just easier to quickly write a note down then transfer to the phone later so it doesn't get lost. But in these nice sized notebooks, your notes should stay safe and well within your sight. I'm a visual person and I love that these are not too big but not too small. The paper inside has a place for the date, and I like the weight of it for any type pen or gel pen.

title: Nicely made and has just the right amount of goal-oriented lists and lots of to-do space
text: Perfect for using for yourself and attractive enough for gift giving, this planner has trackers for just about anything you could think of from personal goals like purpose and value to career-oriented things like where you are in your career and where you want to be. Use one or use them all. I love the overall design of the book. The months have tabs, and there's a really cool magnetic bookmark to slip over pages and keep your spot.

title: Love that these are full sheet labels
text: My old kind of labels had two large labels to a page, but there was a little space in between that sometimes didn't line up right. These labels are just perfect with no chance that the label won't line up right, love these!

title: Great mailers and attractive
text: My business color is aqua, so when I saw these, I knew I wanted them. I mail out small items and these are just perfect!

title: This is a much nicer mouse mat than the old kind!
text: This pad is so perfect and smooth for my wireless mouse to glide over effortlessly. I always hesitated using a mouse mat of any kind (yup just used a piece of paper to keep from marking up my work table) after I went to wireless mice (a LOT of years ago!) because the old mouse pads were thick and uneven. But this one blew me away at how nice and thin it was, so I even ordered another one for my work at home computer. I really love it!

title: Love this company's matching line of products!
text: I was excited to find this fun case after I got the document holder and some notebooks of this same brand. I love that the colors are all very compatible or match. If you have to store things or write, why not have fun with it.

title: Perfect size and love the designs
text: These designs are so happy and remind me of summer and the beach! It's the perfect size package to keep a couple and share a couple with a flamingo-loving friend.

title: Nice and handy with two colors
text: This is much handier than having to deal with two separate highlighters, and these are definitely the colors most used for highlighting. Very nice product.

title: Great little board for quick reminders
text: This is a nice little board to set up wherever you have your home office or decide to work for the day. You can keep it close, jot down messages that would otherwise get lost on those teeny pieces of paper or stickies. Being a visual person, it helps me to have my to-do right in my face.

title: Most items are really nice and would be great for any office
text: I love the zipper container that comes with all this cool stuff. I put the gel pens in it right away. The stapler seems to work well, although a heads-up to anyone getting this set, you need to supply your own staples. The scissors is compact but cuts nicely. The little binder clips being different colors is a fun touch. I'm not real sure what I'm going to do with all those erasers except maybe find some kids who use pencils and need them. The tape was a nice touch, but it's regular cellophane not the invisible kind, so I'm not real sure where to go with that. All in all the items are nice and everything someone just starting in an office or setting up a home office might need for their desk. The little holder works well for holding the stuff till you're ready for it.

title: Really nice super fine point gel pens write very smoothly
text: I like these pens a lot and how smooth and easily they write. This type of pen with the gel ink seems to work better on some papers than regular ink does. Not only that, they're cute and fun to use!

title: Very nice containers
text: I really like that these bins are made from plastic instead of the usual fabric that collapses easily. You do have to make sure when you're assembling it that you crease it well so it sits more squared away. I would definitely not mind having more of these around.

title: This is such a nice convenient item!

title: “The secret of your success is hidden in your daily routine“
text: Creating positive habits isn’t the easiest thing to do, but habit trackers like this one really help create a visual reminder and make it feel almost like a game. It’s like you’re getting points for every day that you do the things you need to do for your best life, whether that’s drinking a certain amount of cups of water, exercising, meditating, going to work, etc. This is a really helpful way to get started, and the habits don’t have to be giant things. I recommend starting small. If you’re planning on working out, don’t put one hour at the gym. Put something you can do at home and break it into smaller tasks, like 10 sit-ups on one line, 15 jumping jacks on another, 10 push-ups on another… Then next month you can increase it. This is the size of a standard piece of paper, so it’s not huge and doesn’t take up a lot of room. It comes ready to hang on a wall with a thumbtack, or you can carry it around like a notebook. The paper is a nice thick card stock, so if you’re using markers, you don’t have to worry about it leaking through. title: Easy to hang, great way to keep track for the month
text:
I’ve really gotten into checklists and ways to effectively establish habits and be productive the last few years. If you already use checklists but want to start a few new habits, a habit tracker like this one works beautifully. You quickly and easily fill in squares for every day you do one of the habits that you want to work on, and when you look back at it, you can easily track how well you did for that month and slowly improve. It’s great for motivation and as a reminder.
Suggestion for starting new habits: don’t add too many at once, and don’t set the bar too high. Make it easy to win, and incrementally add to the difficulty and quantity of habits once you’ve established easier and fewer ones. Example: if you want to start working out, you might start with a small routine with a few jumping jacks, sit ups, and hand weights, taking no more than 5-10 minutes per day. Once you’ve done that for a month, add a few more exercises and maybe some stretches.

I like the company mission to donate items, but at this price, I could probably just buy myself and someone else a notebook…or several. Plus, once you throw it out or if it breaks, you end up with glitter everywhere, which isn’t great for the environment. I won’t count that against this, since it’s kind of the whole point, but overall, it doesn’t seem worth it to me.

title: Nice alternative to drawing pencils
text: This is the first time I’ve seen this type of lead, I guess because I’ve been out of the artistic world for a little while. Having gotten back in recently with some new drawing pencils, it’s been fun experimenting with all the different options. These came in and I had to try them, and they’re great! Instead of having to worry about sharpening your pencil all the time or buying a new one, this allows you to buy a refillable mechanical pencil, some of which come with a little sharpener in the lid that you can remove to make a fine point, and you just refill the lead! Over a long period of time, if you draw a lot, this really saves on materials and expense. These lead refills worked great!
