title: Excellent eraser
text: This is an excellent eraser . Good price since you get 3 .

title: This paper is as good as the recommendation
text: I was told by several people that Rhodia is excellent paper for writing or drawing, and now I know that is true!

title: It gets the job done
text: This cart is easy to use and holds a lot...more than the storage bin that I used to haul around.  It's lightweight and kind of cheaply made but it does the trick.

title: Leaked all over upon 2nd (easy) use.
text: Disappointed. I expected better from the brand.

title: Quality as expected
text: Yep, they work just fine

title: NOT WATERPROOF....
text: NOT WATERPROOF.  I am an ‘ink and wash’ watercolor artist (hobbyist.).  When I use watercolor over the ink, it smears, even after allowing minimum 10 minutes for it to dry (which I shouldn’t have to do.)

title: Not especially easy to remove
text: I have to scrub really hard w/eraser to remove.  And sometimes, this scrubbing also removes some of the paint.

title: Alright
text: I have gone through two of these.  The first one jammed so bad I had to exchange it.  The second one has been working fine so far.  If you're on a tight budget this is a good buy.

title: Not great
text: Board is crooked and has scratches all over it.

title: Great journals for a doable daily journaling practice
text: I was given one of these little journals at a retreat and ordered some more for myself shortly after that. I love them! I’ve long wished to have a regular journaling practice. These make that feel doable. The pages are structured enough to get me started and asp have enough openness for whatever comes up. And it takes about a minute to journal. Totally doable!

title: Five Stars
text: In my pocket st work every day.

title: Love the tin
text: Love the tins and the collection of colors.  It's hard to get individual colored pencils unless you order from an art store.  This pencil set has some of the more unique colors that come in the larger sets.  I've ordered several of these because I use the colors so much.

title: Nice looking
text: Really like the presentation and option to keep this as a small rectangle or open to a line when in use.  However I'm not extremely confident about the hinges not breaking or the ability of the handle to carry the weight.

title: Looks cheap
text: Considered sending it back.  If I had bought it for a gift I would have.  Getting a this has been repackaged or sitting in storage forever vibe.  I have another of these bought as a single pen and it looked nicer.  But this was about half price on sale so hopefully the pens work.  They do seem cheap though - like they will break easy.  I have cheap fountain pens from Japan that are much more solidly built.

title: Super easy to refill
text: Very fine line, very easy to refill.  Took just a second.

title: Feels cheap and scratchy
text: I'm newer to fountain pens so I haven't used any expensive ones.  I love the Platinum Preppy but they can be hard to find.  I thought this would be a nice one to try out.  This is like the dollar store of fountain pens.  The plastic feels super cheap like it is going to break any time so it kind of makes the refill aspect not that attractive.  The nib also seems cheap and scratchy.  I compared it to the preppy and they are so different.  Just my opinion but the preppy is a joy to write with - nice feel and smooth.  This pen looks and feels odd, cheap and scratchy.  Extra star though for price and ease of refill.

title: Not a set as pictured
text: The picture when you scroll down shows a set in a plastic holder with the product name on it.  That is what I expected when I ordered it.  Instead the pens were in a ripped open unmarked Ziploc bag.  (Which resulted in half the pens scattered in the package).

title: Tape so bad it's getting a review
text:
This tape was the worst. If Scotch has a money back guarantee they're getting an email. I even think someone returned this because the package was opened. Stick with their magic tape if your using it for presents or anything you might want to look presentable.

First - and oh so annoyingly - the tape won't cut without a great deal of effort. People aren't kidding that you might just use scissors instead. Even more frustrating is this tape picks up EVERY mark - esp where you grap the tape to dispense it. I even tried plastic gloves and it STILL had blotchy marks where the tape touched the gloves. The tape is old timey looking, frustrating, annoying and something that will add extra minutes when your trying to hurry and wrap presents. It IS plenty sticky though and often to everything except where you want it to go.

title: Not if you really need to magnify
text:
It was cheap so I bought it hoping it would help with small print. This is more for those who don't actually need that help but just to make it easier. It is useless if you have vision issues. There is no light attached but I thought that was frivolous and wouldn't need it (not so). The print is larger but only slightly so I would still have to hold the paper a few inches away. I can already do that without a ruler getting in the way. I can't use handheld magnifier because the slight movement affects dizziness. I decided to buy a much more expensive desk lamp version.

If you can already read print without any issues this would probably work great. If you have vision problems then not so much or not at all.

title: Very nice but $$$
text:
I didn't buy the complete set because of the price but ordered individual pencils in 4H, HB, 4B and 9B. These are the "cadillac" of pencils as the saying goes. They are smooth and because of that blend exceptionally well using a small makeup brush (learned that from Kirsty Partridge Art). However that means they also smear exceptionally well - so prepare accordingly. The color is nice and these were able to be sharpened to a very fine point.

The set however is so expensive it doesn't seem practical to use these as everyday drawing pencils. I have Prismas, Derwent, Mars, Raffine, Tombow and Faber Castell. Overall the Prismas are my workhorses which I use the most. I notice enough deviation between grades too. And interestingly the Raffine are incredibly cheap (like $3 or $4 for a set) but a good pencil. The Derwent used to be a favorite but just too scratchy. None of the other ones are bad I just don't use them as much.

title: Still having issues with ink
text:
Comes with an ink cartridge (so I know it's the right one). However it still doesn't seem to flow and the tip still isn't saturated after a week. I liked that this was refillable but a copic brush pen (disposable) came ready to go and didn't leak either.

Edit- pen finally started working for me. Almost too much ink flow now! Very pretty pen too.

title: Smooth ink flow
text:
Smooth ink flow, nice color black ink, no smearing. Not sure how they will hold up but nice for the price. Looks better drawing than some art pens I bought.

Edit - doesn't last that long and when ink starts to skip it looks terrible (blotchy). I bought a bunch of them because I loved them so much but several have run out faster than I think they should.

title: Ok but not great
text: Trying out different waterproof pens.  I don't actually like the feel of microns so looking for a replacement.  These are ok but not great.  Two of the pens have good flow with nice lines (and just fine for lefties).  One of the set is not smooth and seems uneven and scratchy.  The tip doesn't look perfect so that may be the issue.  For $12 I don't think it's a great deal either.  So this isn't "the" pen.  On the plus side no smearing and ink dried right away.  Very dark ink too.

title: Impressive
text: Easy to use and quickly sharpens to a long sharp point with just a few turns.  You can attach this to a desk but you can use it freestanding.  The only thing that is slightly annoying is that you have to go through the whole process to insert each pencil.  So don't know if this will affect its long term use.

title: Meh
text:
Gave it away and am using a different one (Pusheen!). I love the art work on the cover but the planner was a big disappointment in that department. The art details were tiny and repeated for the whole month. So if it was a tiny bunny in the corner for Jan (can't remember exactly) then that was the same art work for all the pages. Boring esp considering the art wasn't that lavish.

Secondly for those with vision issues the weekly pages were not that clear or comfortable to look at. Fancy writing and same color lines and lettering makes nothing easy to read or stand out. So I highly recommend the Pusheen planner even though it is quite different from this. The layout (monthly and weekly), print size and colors are superb. I have issues with visual snow and contrast so even though I bought one as a gift I'm using it myself. And besides it's fun too.

title: Surprised
text: Surprised by the actual fine line.  Colors aren't too bad either.

title: Not thrilled like I thought I would be
text: I have the Mars Black and they are smoother but sometimes the black doesn't mesh with the lighter grades.  So I thought I would get around to giving these a try.  Several of the pencils in the set have been hard to sharpen.  Frustrating to have them keep breaking before you even get to use them.  I tried several different sharpeners and it made no difference.  Secondly a couple of the pencils actually smell unpleasant when sharpening them.  I love pencils and have lots of brands so this was kind of surprising the smell of the wood.  A couple of the pencils are scratchy too - easily digging lines into the paper.  (My Prismas don't do that even in the lightest grades).  However after adjusting for that they were ok drawing a picture.  Not fabulous however.

title: Very nice
text: Second mechanical pencil I've bought.  The first was a Pentel and it's ok but this Tombow is so much nicer.  It has a great feel to it and a nice tip.  The lead is smooth without being too slippery.  I use this for drawing.  It's been great for adding very fine detail and for lightly shading small areas.

title: Definitely not for graphite
text: I bought this at a retail store because of reviews on here.  I think this is about the worst sharpener I've owned as an adult.  It's too big for regular graphite and don't care for the fat tip it gave my colored pencil.  Now I have three of these - at least I was able to use a coupon.  I used to think it kind of silly the people who would use a knife to sharpen.  Not anymore after going through sharpeners.  Even if you find a good one it dulls so quickly.  And I hate the wastefulness of buying these and just throwing them away.

title: Probably best for those who color.
text:
I gave 5 stars because of the color range and price. I think these pencils would be best for those who would use them for coloring (I don't). I use colored pencils for original artwork and so need more durable ones to lay down lots of color. I also need pencils that can tolerate alot of layering and blending.

These pencils have an amazing amount of pigment though. And one of the best color selections that I've seen in any set I've ordered (Prismas, Derwent, Koh-I-Noor, Lyra). The colors are beautiful so I will find a use for these but they are just too soft for my drawings. Two of the pencils I tested drawing a flower went down quickly with needing to be sharpened. So I would go through these way too fast to rely on them solely.

As far as the feel of the pencils - they kind of remind me of Koh-I-Noor. Pretty colors but thicker lay down and averse to much layering. More pigment then Koh-I-Noor though.

These would also I think be a fantastic gift for someone new to or interested in CP. I avoided colored pencils for many years in artwork because I had been frustrated early on (like as a kid) due to hard/bland pencils. These would be great for a potential young artist.

title: Can't believe Staedler made these
text: I got these at a retail store on a clearance rack.  I love Staedler graphite pencils for drawing.  So I figured these would be ok for something.  Obviously not artist grade like my Prismas or Polychromos so I had low expectations.  These didn't even meet that.  No pigment and an unpleasant feel to use.

title: Nice assortment
text: Great colors for floral artists - especially if you only can afford small sets or as an add on to smaller prisma sets.  (Some of the colors are not in the smaller prisma sets).  The tin is nice looking too and at the current $8 (ish) price is cheaper than you can order them individually.

title: Ink stops flowing
text: I'm particular about pens and this one fails.  The pen itself feels ok (a little chunky).  The major failure is that the ink stops frequently often mid word so you have to rewrite over or start again on new paper.  You have to shake it to get it to keep working.  I got this product during a special but still not amused.  Another annoying factor is the way it retracts.  The button is on the side so you have to search for it rather than simply pressing the end.

title: Good enough for the price
text: I like the price but the eraser feels awkward to use.  I don't think it erases fabulously either but allright enough.  I prefer the Tombow eraser but that is for much finer work.  I was hoping this would be a nice middle ground between the finer Tombow and a rectangular eraser for art work.  The product doesn't quite fit that niche but it is ok.

title: Great instead of a pencil.
text: While these are considered "cheap" pens I really like them.  They don't leak or smear and the eraser actually works if you are careful with it.  If you keep trying to erase too much ink with the same part of the eraser it WILL smear.  I use these instead of regular pencils for doing crossword/word games.  While I wouldn't use these for important papers (like signatures), the ink doesn't erase very well after it sits for awhile.  The pens last  too.

title: Meh
text: They are ok I guess but honestly I don't use them.  I tried them a couple of times and they've been sitting in the case ever since.  I got these for presicion work but haven't been able to get excited about them.  They seem too hard actually especially when using them with regular prismas it easily indents the paper.  And the colors are limited so it hinders their usefulness.  I gave three stars because I don't think the pencils are flawed just not impressed with colors or application.

title: Eraser is great.
text: Not that impressed with the pencils (they are ok) but love the eraser.  The eraser can be bought separately along with refills.  This set is a nice price though.  Five stars for the eraser and three for the pencils.

title: Nice effect
text: These are the first oil colored pencils I've used so I can't compare them to any other oil based brands.  ( I have been using Prismas and Derwent wax based).  The Koh-I-Noor seem almost translucent so I like them for a background.  However I don't seem to find these very blendable so pretty much the color you see is what you get - unlike Prismas which layer very nicely.  I do not use solvents though to blend so that might make these work better.  The tips on these stay sharper much longer than a wax based pencil so that is nice too.

title: Just ok but watch out for the marker
text:
If you are at all sensitive to chemicals the marker is really strong! It has a very offensive chemical smell even after sitting on the paper. I eventually had to toss the drawing in a plastic bag and take it outside and I could still smell the marker in the room. And the marker was the main reason I bought the set.

If someone is brand new to CP art this might be nice especially for the price. The kneaded eraser is very tiny though and instead of a charcoal pencil a burnisher would have been better and more geared to colored pencil.

title: Not a great design
text: Definitely gives a very long point but the design makes it ackward.  The cover over the blades needs to be emptied after a couple of pencils and the shavings immediately obscure the pencil so you need to check the tip.  I use it with the cover open but it doesn't open all the way so it has some design issues.  The price is good though.

title: Quality control issues
text:
They get two stars because of the price. I am new to colored pencils but have been drawing and painting for years. These are very smooth however the pencils have issues. Every single one in the box of 24 is off center. They come presharpened with tiny little tips. As soon as you try to sharpen them to get a real tip it is a hassle. One pencil alone I had to stop and use sandpaper THREE times because splits and cracks were forming. I have used a number of graphite and charcoal pencil brands and own multiple sharpeners so I know how to deal with pencils. It seems impractical to have to fawn over each one to try and get a decent point.

I knew the bad reputation Prismas have and how artists are ditching them. Still the price was good so I thought it would be worth a try. If you know how difficult these are and enjoy spending hours sharpening then it might be a worthwhile purchase. At least they are cheap though so it could be an acceptable trade off for some.

I've quickly moved on to Derwent Soft colored drawing pencils. I prefer their muted tones. The Prismas ARE vibrant but the colors seem gaudy to me which is another minus.

title: Tin of Greetings
text: These Watercolor postcards are cut evenly with nice rounded edges. At 105lb weight they are flexible and will mail well in an envelope. The rough texture is uniform. The tin is hinged, light weight and has the picture as shown online. I am happy with this purchase and think it makes a nice gift.

title: See Paper
text: These durable Plastic Keepers have to be shaped by hand first. Once they are filled with Paper they stand up well. The price seemed high, just under $12. I'm glad I bought 3 of them and would get more.

title: Really nice stickers
text: Nice thick stickers with bright red color. Perfect for my Christmas card envelopes - thanks!

title: Chalk markers are bright and easy to clean off!
text: Love the brightness of the chalk markers on the black board. Easy to wipe off and wipes off clean! Very excited about decorating it for every season!

title: Five Stars
text: Smooth writing and great colors

title: Favorite pen of a Crazy Pen Lady
text: Lately I have been on the hunt for the perfect pen. I've tried many. I have used the Papermate Profile Elite ballpoint for several years, and these are still good pens. But I wanted to find a gel ink pen that came in many colors. I thought I had found it in the Uniball Signo, but I became annoyed with the scratching sound the fine tip makes, and it skipped too much for my taste.  This Pentel EnerGel RTX retractable marries the best features of ball point pens and gel ink. It writes smoothly with very little if any scratchiness.  It is a very smooth pen and allows me to write quickly (the Uniball Signo definitely slowed me down with the skipping and attempt to make it quieter). Highly recommend these pens!

title: Perfect size, high quality.
text: Beautiful notebook, exactly what I’m looking for. Love the high quality of the paper, and the cover.  Lays flat. I want more! Please make additional colors in this line.

title: Love these!
text: Love these! A friend bought me some and I bought more for myself. They remind me of an excellent trip to London. And they are perfect bookmarks.

title: Five Stars
text: These are very good quality. Will be purchasing again.

title: Five Stars
text: These are good quality. You should change the picture to match the actual size. Will purchase again.

title: Five Stars
text: These are great notebooks. High quality.

title: It's okay that it's small - you probably wouldn't want it any bigger
text:
I too was surprised at how small it was when it first arrived. However it is just big enough for what I need it for. Anything bigger would get in the way on my desk. In just a few days it has made a big difference in the comfort level of my wrist while I work.
I am going to order another as I run two computers at once and need a second for the other mouse.

title: Great for taking notes
text: I love these pens. I had bought a multipack before but my daughter stole them to use for taking notes in class. No probs, order another pack for myself. These Profile pens are my favorite pens. I use them for taking notes at work to help keep the different projects organized in my meeting notebook. Plus it's fun to use something rather than just old boring blue all the time.

title: Five Stars
text: Very good boxes and a great price.

title: These are my favorite type of pen
text: These are my favorite type of pen. I use them for work all day. It's fun to have the different colors just to liven my notes up a bit. The ink runs smooth and I greatly prefer these to gel pens.

title: Five Stars
text: Old standbys that still work great..

title: Great quality heavy duty card stock
text: I use this card stock for all my card bases. Very good quality. Would buy again.

title: Great little pen!
text: This pen was recommended by a fellow calligrapher so I thought I'd give it a try! I really like the fact that it has a lighter gray color in the other to add shadow to my letters if I want to! Adds a nice touch!

title: Truly Crappy Exterior
text:
These are terrific pencils--soft, highly pigmented, easy to blend, and come in a mouth-watering number of tones, hues, and shades. Prismacolors are supposed to be the standard by which all other pencils are measured. Given that, I was truly baffled by the pencil bodies, some of which sported ugly blue stains and deep scratches.

The exterior finish is what you might expect of cheap grade-school pencils. Rough, unfinished, inaccurate coloration, and unpleasant feel. This struck me especially after handling my Polychromos, Holbein, and Luminace pencils with their luscious laquered bodies that closely match the actual pencil color.

However, everyone needs a set of these creamy, dreamy pencils, regardless of the exterior...the pencils themselves are incredible.

title: This thing won't even punch two sheets of paper.
text: The title says it all. I couldn't get two sheets of 20# copy paper into the slot to punch it. And the holes are way too close to the edge. Returned it.

title: Beautiful, well-built, and compact.
text: This case is absolutely gorgeous. The drawers slide smoothly; the interior is well-padded; the exterior is handsome. There’s ample rooms for a pen collection, but the case is compact and doesn’t take up much room on my desk.

title: Okay, but too narrow for plastic pockets.
text: Meh. Not very interesting, and not wide enough for plastic pockets. It holds paper and seems reasonably well made. I won’t buy another one, because my pockets stick out, but if you don’t use them, it’s a reasonable choice for a small binder.

title: Fairly crumbless
text: I like this eraser better than most. The crumbs adhere to each other, making for a few larger, um, crumb bunnies that are easy to pick up and throw away. It erases very well and doesn't mar watercolor paper.

title: Bombproof circles
text: It's not the sturdiest desk tool I've ever seen, but it draws perfect circles. I haven't had any trouble with the inner ring--works very well.

title: Not good quality.
text: The outer layer split after three months and the inner sticky filling squished out.

title: Great little squishy thing
text: I have sensitive elbows...and ordered one of these to see if it helped at my desk. Short answer-yes. They are nicely squishy. They are also useful for raising up you hand when writing in thick journals.

title: Wonderul paper
text: Fantastic paper for fountain pens. Or any pens. The Seyes rule will help you improve your handwriting, too!

title: Wonderful ink
text: This is a gorgeous color--a rich, blue purple. The ink is well-behaved and doesn't bleed or feather. Private Reserve is getting hard to find--stock up while you can.

title: Ultimate Pinkness
text: Really, really, pink, but a lovely color--rich pink without the Hello Kitty in-your-face pinkness. This does stain pens, so be careful if you are using it in a white pen or a demonstrator.

title: Fountain pen love at a reasonable price
text:
These are quite nice--smooth paper, lies flat when opened. The cover color is bold and beautiful.

I tested a number of different pens, and there was no bleeding or feathering, even with my wettest pens. However, I tested a Derwent Inktense pencil, moistening the strokes with a slightly damp Q-tip. The paper actually peeled off in little crumbs. Don't choose this Apica variety if you are intending to do any water-based artwork. The Apica Premiums are a better bet for that type of medium.

title: A pleasure to use
text: This is a beautiful color--more green than brown, with wonderful shading. One of my favorite inks.

title: Over-hyped.
text: Meh. The paper isn't coated, so all my ultra-fine pens feather. My pens hate looking fat. The paper used for the Rhodia pads is much nicer--it's lighter weight, but coated and very pleasant to write on.

title: A terrific bargain...if you're Warren Buffet.
text: I bought a couple of dozen of these to hand out at the office as freebies. Everyone loved them. I was so pleased by their reaction that next year, I'll get a bunch of Montegrappa Chaos pens and give them away, too.

title: Small, but Mighty
text: Just...wow. I had been using a Staedler sharpener, which mutilated my colored pencils. This little guy made them beautiful again. Fantastic!

title: A wonderful journal!
text: The Stalogy's simple design makes it incredibly versatile. The faint ruling and tiny type for scheduling are unobtrusive, so you can ignore these features if you don't need them. The paper is either Tomoe River or a very close cousin--very thin, smooth, and fountain-pen friendly. The book fits perfectly in my elegant Hobonichi cover. The notebook comes from Japan, but the shipper was timely and pleasant to deal with. I'll be stocking up on these because they suit my needs perfectly.

title: Disappointed
text: I bought these on a recommendation for adding very dark shadows to pencil drawings. They are oddly scratchy...I was stunned. It would glide along the paper for a bit, then I'd hit a gritty bit and get an actual scratch in the paper. I threw the box away.

title: Okay, but not wonderful
text: Mmm. The covers are flexible. If you fill your notebooks full, as I do, the covers are just too flimsy to support the binder.

title: Astounding!
text:
I experimented with a variety of pencils, and this is unquestionably the best paper I've ever encountered short of super-expensive fine art paper. Pencil lines are sharp, dark, and crisp. But for those who like to sketch with a pencil, the feeling of the paper is indescribable. I can't recommend it highly enough.

Off to add a few more sketchbooks to my basket.

title: Wish the paper were heavier...
text: My extra-fine nibbed fountain pen isn't especially wet and my 0.5mm pencil lead isn't especially soft, but writing and drawing is visible on the back side of the paper. Also, the paper warps considerably. The paper texture is wonderful, though, and the dots are brilliant.

title: Pen Perfection
text: This pen is...so wonderful words fail me. The writing is smooth, the ink flow perfection, the mechanism classy, the appearance gorgeous. I want to buy another one. It's perfect for writing tiny kanji, for those taking Japanese.

title: Clear, Durable and Well Made!
text: These are very durable and well made.  I save patterns from my craft magazines and these will hold several pages comfortably.  I ran out of the first bunch I had so I reordered them, but these took quite a bit longer to arrive, around two months or so. I suppose they were a casualty in the shipping issues worldwide.  No matter, they arrived as shown in the first photo in a white envelope in my mailbox.  Major kudos to Amazon for trying to reduce the amount of its packaging.  The second picture shows how clear these actually are as I am holding up that Christmas paper BEHIND BOTH pieces of the pocket, not with it inside.  Awesome product and I would definitly purchase this again.  5* +++++++

title: This is my second purchase!
text: You cannot beat the price for these two cartridges.  They are long lasting, the black is dark and I truly can not tell a difference from the original dell cartridge....except for the price!

title: Totally worth the price!!!
text: I love these pencils!!!  There is a terrific range of colors and they blend fairly well.  But for the cost?  Nothing beats this deal!!! Totally worth the money!

title: Five Stars
text: These pens are amazing!!!!!

title: Five Stars
text: They are really great

title: One Star
text: Worthless could not use.

title: Just follow instructions when assembling
text: Very sturdy.  Not a lot of trouble to assemble

title: Perfect little printer
text: Hooked it up to work with my PC.  Easy installation.

title: Get a point
text: This sharpener really works as promised.  Best one I've ever used.

title: Canon can be depended upon

I did squeeze the cartridge a little before putting it together. I am so happy I stepped a bit out of my price range and bought this pen. It posts securely as well. title: Helps If You Struggle With Meal Planning...
text:
I'm not a good meal planner. At all. Ever. Until now.

I am a deal seeker and sometimes this can result with too much food in the house which means in order to dwindle it down, I HAVE to figure out a way to meal plan for a couple of months. I've tried a lot of different methods/products that are supposed to help and so far nothing has really worked for me. It was too detailed if that makes sense and too cluttered. I like plain and easy when it comes to things like this.

I can't remember how I found this meal planner on here because I wasn't looking for one at the time, but I did somehow stumble across it and the first thing that popped in my head was how easy and useful it looks. I do still have to purchase fresh food over the duration and this is PERFECT because you write what you need on the list and are able to tear it off to take it with you when you do your shopping.

The pocket under the paper sheets for coupons, notes, etc. could be useful. Even though I'm a huge couponer, I probably won't use it much because I don't coupon a whole lot of food. But, I can see how it would work great for anyone that does.

I seriously love the fact that it came with that small pencil and there is a clip at the bottom that will hold that pencil or any other pen/pencil of the same diameter. The pencil is standard diameter so a replacement would be no issue. It can get really annoying to have to repeatedly track down a pen or pencil to write something on the planner all the time. They solved that annoyance very easily.

The pad contains 30 sheets which I thought was kind of odd. For the price, I'm OK with it but since there's 52 weeks in a year I expected either 26 or 52. Maybe I'm just being weird about that but the number is just odd to me. It may be in the description and I overlooked it because I was too busy fangirling over the darn thing and buying it because I suspected it would work for me.

It's easy for me to scribble down what we will have for dinner every evening of that week, but if you go into too many details, you might have a space issue. When the week is over, you can just tear the page off and throw it away. I like that.

I will buy this one again that way I know I'll have another one to put up when this one is gone. So far this is the best meal planner that I have seen for me and it's not overpriced which is a serious plus. Plain and simple with no unnecessary or wasted space. Bravo! I love it.

text: Ordered these tri-fold brochures to do invites for a family reunion. About ready to send them back thinking it was a mistake in packaging when I caught a glimpse of a score mark on one sheet.  Rather skeptical, but ran the paper through the printer and then attempted to locate the fold score.  While I could not clearly 'see' the score, it was there, and the brochure paper did fold exactly where it should have.  I had some of this tri-fold before and the score marks were clearly visible, so this was an entirely different product.  It works great, however.  Once you get the hang of where the score line is, the brochures fold up clean and crisp.  Not one single piece crumpled or mis-folded.  Each sheet performed exactly as it should.  So long story short...this pre-scored tri-fold paper is excellent in overall performance.  Heavy enough to survive the post office treatment, produces clean folds and crisp clear printing.  Don't be fooled, the scores lines really are there!

title: I've gotten better quality graphing composition books from the dollar store
text: The paper in these is thin and the binding is poorly done.  The covers are nice and include some interesting references that students might find helpful.  I personally think they'd find a composition book with better quality paper and a tighter, more secure binding to be far more helpful though.  These books are absolutely not worth ten dollars for a pack of two.  I've gotten better quality graphing composition books from the dollar store ... for a dollar each ... and the paper wasn't so thin that everything you try to write with bleeds through to not only the back but often also the next page as well if not even the next two pages.  One thing I do like about them is that they can be very easily folded over and opened to lay flat because the binding is looser than you usually find in composition books.  If you intend to work only in pencil these would probably be okay, but if you plan to work in pen you'd be better off grabbing a sheet of loose leaf notebook paper and tucking it in underneath the page you are working on to help contain the bleed-through.  Also, the paper does not hold up well to erasing at all, so if you do use an eraser on it you need to be very careful or it will tear.  Very disappointed.  Not worth the cost at all.

title: Very light and comfortable to write with
text: One of the first things I noticed about these pencils is the fact that they are incredibly lightweight.  I'd liken the barrel size and length to a standard marker, which for me was ideal.  The barrel itself is completely hollow and the eraser on the end comes out easily enough that you could potentially stash some extra leads for a mechanical pencil or possibly even an extra ink cartridge for a pen inside this one.  As lightweight as this is it would be perfect for backpacking and I'm sure a backpacker could find a way to use that little storage space inside it for something.  It writes nicely, looks and feels like a normal pencil on paper.  Not one of the darker writing ones though.  More like one of those pencils with the weird not-wood barrels that always sharpen smoothly and cleanly.  For kids I'd say these are pretty close to perfect.  No frustration with the point breaking or becoming dull.  The erasers on the ends do work and they actually seem to work better than the little rectangular erasers that were also included.  Both my daughter and I were fine with that since we both had the same thought when we saw those little white rectangles.  'We're going to end up losing them anyway' was the thought.  Overall we are really happy with these and have already distributed them to different locations so one will always be handy when needed.

title: Love it
text: Assembly took a bit of time to get the pieces aligned and together, but once it was assembled the result was very solid and sturdy.  The pen holder section is of a good size, not so big that specific items could become lost in the crowd but still big enough to hold plenty of options.  The cork boards on both sides are where this product really shines.  They are real cork boards, nice and thick, not just a thin layer of corking on top of some sort of foam board.  The clip pins are amazingly useful for stuff you don't want to have to put a hole through and there are more than enough of them to use them exclusively if you want to since the cork boards themselves are so small.  They are the perfect size for a few small items and notes though, and the whole thing is both cute and functional.  For the asking price of about $15 I'd say it's worth the cost.  It really is a solid, well built little thing once you get it together.  Just take your time with the assembly and make sure things are lined up.  Pushing against a solid surface helps to apply the pressure evenly.

title: Very nice for eating or working in bed
text: When it comes to tables like this we actually haven't had much luck in finding that perfect balance between sturdy and lightweight, but this comes the closest for us so far.  We have a really nice solid wood one, but that thing is a beast when it comes to its weight and that makes it really difficult to move around.  This one is light enough to lift and move around easily even with things still on it.  That said, the surface on this is very slippy and there is no lip or anything to prevent stuff from sliding right off when you do.  May or may not be of use to note that our silicone baking mats are actually of a perfect size to lay on this and use as a grippy surface to prevent slipping.  Also noteable is the fact that it can be stored on the underneath of the table and held in place there by the legs when they are folded down to keep it handy and accessible but also out of the way.  Any sort of silicone mat would probably work for that and I have found that most silicone things like that can be cut to size if need be, so that would also make it perfect for messy little art and craft projects too.  It is an absolute dream when it comes to easy portability when empty though.  The handle is a really nice touch and makes it very easy to grab and go.  The little cup indent is basically pointless and we actually wish it wasn't there at all.  The same is true of the phone / tablet slot.  It's honestly just a waste of potentially useful surface area.  Remove those two things entirely and maybe throw in a silicone placemat instead and this very handy little table would be truly perfect.

title: Super cute and shockingly functional
text: I got this on an impulse because it just happened to match well with my Shiba mousepad and I thought it was adorable.  If nothing else I figured I might end up with a cute little 'mascot' for my desk.  I was very pleasantly surprised at just how comfortable this is to actually use as a wrist rest with my mousepad though.  It's the perfect height and angle to make using my mouse much more comfortable and it's been holding up really well to constant use.  Soft and squishy, not hard like a lot of these sort of things tend to be, and so far it isn't deforming at all either the way the gel type are prone to doing.  Not sure what it's made of, but it's actually perfect as long as you have a relatively small wrist.  Probably not ideal for anyone with really big hands, but I couldn't see someone like my husband using something like this anyway.  I love it though.

title: Works with modifications
text: If this was made of cheaper material it would have been lucky to get a three star rating out of me, but the fact of the matter is that once you get it all together and modify it just a bit it is actually a decently sturdy and very functional storage cart.  First of all, yes, you absolutely do need a mallet to get the bars together.  We found that we could get them started by sort of wiggling them back and forth while applying pressure and then bang them in by alternating sides with each hit.  A one pound mallet was plenty to get the job done, but we did have the two pounder at the ready just in case.  The cross bars on the back ended up getting taken back off and left off because they seemed to create problems with tension and getting the drawers into place and they really didn't seem to be necessary anyway.  Sliding the drawers into the grooves where they are supposed to be ended up causing us a lot of ffrustration with the drawers refusing to budge, so I just took them all out and slid them into place with the lips of the drawers resting on top of the groove slot instead of inside it.  That also allows us to access the drawers completely from either the front or the back and pull the entire drawers out when needed.  I really like having that full access from both sides of the cart.  For what it is I'd say it's reasonably sturdy.  It's way better than the plastic storage drawers on wheels that I was using before and the top of it is actually quite pretty.  The drawers are plenty large enough to hold a wide variety of different items and the wheels work about as well as you'd expect from a cart like this.  Just leaving off the cross bar and moving the drawers up to rest on top of the groove slot made a huge difference in how I felt about this.  As designed and following the assembly instructions to the letter it was most definitely frustrating and disappointing.  I am quite happy with it now that I've got it set up the way I want it though.  I'm thinking of adding a couple hanging pocket organizers on the sides for additional storage as well.

title: Very smooth rolling and quiet
text: Got these to replace the original plastic wheels that were broken to the point of falling apart on us.  First of all, the installation was practically effortless, which I loved.  It took more effort to flip the chair over than it did to change the wheels themselves.  The old ones pulled out easily and these replacements just popped right in with no struggle and no having to force the issue.  I just rotated the entire base to access each wheel one after the other until they were all replaced, then flipped the chair upright and pushed it to see how they worked.  Much better than the original wheels did even when the chair was brand new.  No scratching or scraping sounds against the floor at all either.  It rolls smoothly and quietly now, can be pushed or pulled easily with one hand while maintaining perfect control, which it could never do with the original wheels at all.  My husband said these are the sort of wheels that could win office chair races with a big smile on his face, so it's fairly safe to say he loves them as much as I do.  They're strong, sturdy, very well made.  I would absolutely get them again if we had another chair in need of them.

title: Large and beautiful, high quality calendar.

None of that overly glossy, thin paper that smudges and bleeds through here.  This is a high quality and truly gorgeous calendar with nice, big dates that are easy to see and wide boxes that are easy to fill with your own notations.  It has the cycles of the moon and all of the usual holidays fully accounted for, plus each month notes where the photograph was taken and includes a nice quote about nature. title: Perfect Planner!
text:
I’m always looking for ways to improve each aspect of my life and to also stay organized. I started researching “productivity planners” and after reviewing a bunch of options, I picked this Power Planner. I am SO happy with my purchase! The size of the planner is perfect, the cover looks professional yet simple, and the inside is the best part. There are pages for your goals, 6 pages for 6 months (undated), and then the majority of the pages are made for weekly planning. It’s organized so that you get to write your priorities for the week, make a weekly plan, and also address each aspect of your life: personal, family, work, social, etc. I did a couple bullet notes for each section. You also get a chance to review your last week! Anyway, I love how this planner looks, the way it’s organized, and that it takes in to account the many parts of our lives.

An awesome bonus is: at the end of the planner there is a note that offers you one free planner if you like and follow Power Planner on Facebook and then message them your order ID # and address!

Highly recommend this planner 😊.

title: Nice Daily Planner
text:
I really like that this is a daily planner. It is great for time blocking and listers. There is minimal note area, if you need to take daily notes. There is a small area for a daily gratitude, which is nice. The paper is about 28 to 32lbs, not heavy but not too light. The top has a place for the top 3 priorities for the day. The daily time is hourly from 5 am to 9 pm. I write small so I can plan half hourly with it, if needed. There is a nice quote everyday like "Do what you can, with what you've got, where you are." Theodore Roosevelt.

The only thing I can't figure out is the four squares at the top - Due, Dinner, Dollars, & Don't Forget. Did they just want things that start with "D"? I don't really get what you are supposed to do with it. I guess you can white out and put your meals? But why would you only track Dinner? Or one thing that is Due? Also Saturday and Sunday are on one page, so you get a daily plan and 3 things to do. But for me, I would prefer the To Do list rather than the hourly breakdown. I have less appointments on the weekends but usually a big to do list.

There are some things in the front about setting up goals, determining where you are, what is important and how you want to get there. Overall it is a nice planner if you like days over weeks.

title: Not "Pretty"
text:
So if you don't like "pretty" planners, this may be for you. It is very minimal - as in no page decorations. You will have to add any if you want them. The cover is the standard laminate. I really think the discs are getting thinner every year. Not really a problem for me because I replace them with metal discs or heavier plastic ones. But they will crack if you aren't careful. If you keep using Happy Planner, you really only need to buy one nice set of discs. Keep the cheap ones for storing your old planners and just switch out the nice ones each year.

Other than that, it is a pretty standard vertical Happy Planner. The paper is between 24 and 32lbs. The monthly tabs are heavier cardstock. The designs are mostly colorful but minimalist. They have positive quotes or sayings - i.e. "Seize the Day" or "Do Less With More Focus." Except for a few blue/grey/sage green tabs, the majority are based on a reddish orange/peach/yellow. I don't mind those shades, so it isn't a problem for me. But I do know some people really don't like orange and peach.

title: Nice quality
text:
I really like this planner. Though I will probably use it as a daily journal. I have been trying to get myself to write something everyday, but a full diary is just too big normally. The cover is a heavier soft cover and feels really nice. The pink is very pretty - which for someone who is not overly crazy about pink, is good. I believe it comes in other colors though. The paper is nice and thick and takes fountain pen well. The only thing that may have slightly ghosted was a highlighter when I overlapped the ink. But it was more wet paper than actual ghosting I think. As a planner, this is a nice horizontal one that you could potentially separate into appointments and to-dos easily. I like that it has extra pages for goals for the month or notes.

The additional notebook is also a nice addition with similar paper. I wish it was dot grid, but lined is good for notes or brain dumping. It also could be used as a purse sized to-do list.

title: If you like florals, the tabs are pretty
text:
This is a standard Dashboard Layout planner. I find these work well if you have a weekly to to list and a few daily items. There is not a lot of daily space on these.

It is a little different from the last year's one in that on the left side, It has only the Task listing replacing Errands and Calls/Emails. On the right side of the page, Important and Looking Ahead boxes replace Get it Done and Noted boxes. The box across the bottom third of the page says Notes instead of Focus On.

The day page is exactly the same. It is not overly decorated. The header on the day page changes color based on the month, but only that a little leaf design in the left corner of the dashboard page, there is no color or decoration. It would be easy to use stickers or washi to cover them if you don't like it. It does come with the cheap (aka thin and easily broken) plastic discs. I frankenplan, so I use metal discs in my actual planner and these disks will only be storage for not in use months.

Overall, I actually like the changes. I was feeling the need for more of a to do list for the week, rather than try to get things done on a specific day. I wish it came with the goal setting section on the hourly planner, I think it would work really well with this planner.

title: Mostly great set
text:
So, I am not the best at decorating. But I like to add color to my planners. For the most part, these are very usable for me. But what I like may not work for others. And what works for others may not work for me. This is the only problem I have with most sticker books. A lot of things that don't really work with my planning. I don't really want to knock them down because of that. They have a lot of stickers I see other planner people on YouTube use. And? My planning style changes regularly. So? I'm sure I will use them eventually.

One caveat to this bundle, the Sassy stickers have some colorful language in them. This doesn't bother me, but might offend others. I felt I needed to put that out there because it surprised me a bit. They aren't the usual "Let's Get It Done!" type of statements. More like "Maybe Tomorrow!"

title: Nice looking
text:
This is a really nice looking desk mat/mouse pad. I really like these because I don't have to worry about staying in the limited area of the pad. I also love the bright colors.

The mouse moves smoothly on it and is provides cushion for my keyboard and protects my desk.

title: Works well for planner stickers
text:
I'm going to put a caveat in that I haven't tried them with my cricut yet. It was easier just to use my cutter since the stickers I printed were mostly happy planner style boxes. Nice and straight. No problem for my trimmer. If the cricut rips them apart, I will edit my review.

I used my laser printer and was pretty happy with the results. Any issues I had were more a problem with the printer than the labels. The color doesn't always print as vibrant as I would like, but I have the same issue printing on plain paper, so not the labels fault.

title: Missing screws
text: So this thing looks really great but It wasn't until I took it all apart that I realized it was missing the screws and bolts packet needed to put it together.  Everything else is there.  My husband is a hobby woodworker, but it too busy with work and current projects to put it together for me right now.  It is not worth returning for me or I would. Plus the box got destroyed getting everything out.

title: Can be used with other scanning apps
text:
So my problem with something that scans to the "cloud" is what if it is sensitive information. How safe is the transferring? So I want it to work with my Adobe Acrobat or other scanning programs and save directly to my computer. This works great. I am very happy with how quick it works getting both sides of the paper. I can only upload pictures, so I rescanned with a different program and saved as a jpg.

For those interested, it shows up as a TWAIN scanner.

The actual program is very easy to download, install and use. You are just limited to online or emailing the results. This is great if you want your documents in DropBox, or your Google Drive (there are other options I don't normally use. You can also save it to Raven's Cloud drive for you, at least that is what it appears to be. I could be misunderstanding the whole thing. Just seems a little weird to me. However, I can see that saving articles you scan to Evernote or options like that. This is actually perfect for that.

Overall, I am really pleased with this scanner. Hopefully it continues to scan as smoothly.

title: So pretty
text: I really love these glass pens.  They are so pretty.  And the ink really lasts because of the way the spirals hold the ink.  It really writes smoothly.  I love the inks that came with it.  I haven't used the ink holder, I usually just open the bottle and dip.  The pen rest is really nice though.  Looks great on my desk.

title: I like it and I don't
text:
I like all the sections in this. I think the To Do and priority could be combined. Seems silly to have 3 To Do sections. A work/personal split would make more sense and then a ranking code. I like that it has a water tracker also. Not sure how usable the "greens" tracker is. The pad is nice and sturdy. Though this is something that sits on your desk unless you pull it out and punch it for your planner.

Now the negative. One sided paper, so kind of a waste to me. Also, if you use it daily? it gets pretty expensive. 50 pages doesn't even last 2 months. If you only need it once in a while on a busy day? It is great.

title: works well
text:
So I mostly got this to use with 7 mil laminating pouches because the 5 are not quite stiff enough for planner covers. Unfortunately, I'm having a problem getting reasonably priced 7 mil pouches. However, it works great on 5 mil pouches, which my normal laminator struggles with. The laminator is easy to use out of the box. One of the best things about it being so wide is that I no longer have to worry that I didn't get the pouch in perfectly straight. In this, it is amazing. The extra width is so great. No more crinkled edges and messed up lanimations. When you have to pay for each pouch and reprint pages, not messing up is a really big thing.

The paper trimmer and corner rounder are nice additions, though I have a number of them so they weren't really needed. I would recommend this, even if you never do 12+ inch laminated pieces.

title: Don't take ink well
text:
Other than ballpoint pen and maybe a G2, these don't take ink well. It is like writing on wax paper or plastic. My micron eventually dried but it formed drops as I was writing on it. My fountain pen ink didn't really dry. I guess I could have left it for a few minutes. I do however, think these will work great if you run them through a laser printer.

I love how they are transparent.

title: Love these Happy Planners
text:
Okay, I admit I frankenplan. For me, Happy Planners are a great starting point to frankenplan because the discbound system is so much easier to write in than the binder ones. I have slit the binder holes so that I can easily pull the pages out as I use them if the rings get in the way. But really, I just find the discs easier to work with. Plus, you can fold it back on itself like a notebook.

There are so many options in the Happy Planner, as well as printables for things that don't exist in the Happy Planner options. I really love the weight of the paper. It takes pretty much any pen, including highlighters and fountain pens. I usually keep the big planner on my desk. I do find it a little big to carry around, but as I mostly work from home, it really isn't a problem. This planner has some beautiful designs for the monthly tabs. They make them pretty plain now so you can decorate them how you want. The big HP has a lot of room for the daily tasks or decorating, if you have nothing to put in on a day.

title: I've become a fan of Happy Planners
text:
I think I might have planner peace with these. But I use them as part of my frankenplanner setup. I use a mix of happy planner and digital downloads and have been really happy. I love the discbound system. It is easy to pull out pages and replace. I love that I can flip it open like a notebook. Additionally, I love the pretty monthly dividers.

I generally use the dashboard setup for my non-regular to do's. Anything I have to do regularly goes into the vertical as a list. I have ADHD and find if I don't write it down, I won't remember to do it. Or really, I will remember briefly and immediately forget as I get distracted by something else.

The paper is a good weight without being too heavy. The discs are the plastic ones. I will usually switch for my metal ones. But then, my frankenplanner is usually only a month or two from each planner. So this planner will stay in the plastic rings.

title: Nice paper
text: I really like the feel of the paper in these.  They are really nice looking as well.  The covers are very classy.  I got the green color and it is just beautiful.  Perfect for my A5 travelers notebook.  They work really well with most pens I tried, including fountain pens and Micron pens.

title: worked
text: Okay, I'm going to say that I have used dry erase markers on laminated sheets before.  I don't think you need special laminating pouches.  These worked well for what they stated they will do.  I normally run them through the laminator  flip them and run them through again.  I find they stay laminated better when I do it that way.

title: Discs arrived cracked  Not as solid as prior years
text:
So it came all wrapped in airbags, but two of the plastic discs were cracked. I have ordered a number of these in past years and never had the discs crack. These seem to be much thinner than prior years. The cover seems a little thinner too, though it is close to last years.

The cover itself is very pretty. I love the designs on the cover - Pressed Floral Theme - and the majority of the monthly tabs have floral designs on them that are very pretty. Pages are about the same thickness as the current 2022 planner, as are the tabs. I really like the vertical planner over the dashboard or horizontal for my weekly schedule, so this is perfect. Fortunately, I usually frankenplan with some great metal discs I found here on Amazon, and I have some extra plastic discs to change out the broken ones. I'm just disappointed in the quality this year. I hope it is just supply chain shortages that caused this and not a permanent change to the product or I will start making my own planners.

title: Great highlighters
text:
So many colors. Some are a little dark, you definitely have to use a black pen underneath. But most are perfect with even colored pens, as long as they are a different color.

The only negative thing is that if your base pen is not waterproof, always highlight first or it will smear. I usually use Microns or something similar, which isn't a problem. But the other day, I tried highlighting over fountain pen and it wasn't so good. These definitely make my planner much more colorful, which I love.

title: great for replacing cutter blades
text: So technically I haven't had to use these yet, but I got them because the blades always seem to die at an inconvenient time.  So having a couple extra blades available is great.  They look like they will also fit into my memory keeper trimmer as well as my larger Zequan trimmer.  The current blade in the Zequan trimmer is actually lasting well.  But it is still nice to have the additional blades.

title: I only got one roll
text:
I only got one roll. Not sure if I was supposed to get 4.

It works okay. Standard double stick tape. Works great with paper. Not so great with other things like plastic.

title: Look good but not waterproof
text:
So I use these in my planner. I really love the color, mostly just brighten up my planner. They are fine tips which allows me to write small but still be readable. I don't really use the funky roller sides because I haven't got the time to find a ruler that will make them go straight. They tend to roll off in different directions than I want. They do work fairly well as far as printing the design.

My only negative is you can't highlight them without them smudging. So I usually put a highlight line first and write over it.

title: Worth it for the wood pen
text: I really love the wood pen!  I like the "feather" pen okay, but mine came with a somewhat damaged nib (doesn't match up at the point) and I keep forgetting to see if I can fix it with my jewelry pliers.  I like that it looks like a dip pen but works like a fountain pen.  The wood pen is great.  Has a nice feel and writes smoothly.

title: great daily diary
text: This is a daily planner/diary.  Not necessarily in the way a young girl might use a diary, but there are lines that allow you to write notes throughout the day about what is happening.  Or you can use it to list the To Do's for the day.  The paper is very nice and takes most pens without ghosting or bleeding.

title: Works great
text: I wanted to wait for a bit to make sure this was working before I wrote the review. This had been working great.  No problems when installing.  No error messages saying this is not Canon toner.  Print quality has been great and it is lasting much longer than the original toner cartridges.  Overall I would recommend this product.

title: Matches my desk pad
text: I have a pink swirly desk pad that this matches perfectly.  So when I saw this, I had to grab it for my pens and pencils.  It looks great on my desk.  It is not perfect.  Because of the marbled design, it doesn't match at the seam, but it is easy to hide, especially on a desk that sits against the wall.

title: Works great.  Just wish they fit in my Happy Planner
text:
The title says it all. Saw these were discbound and picked them up in the hopes of using them for planner checklists. Why waste paper when I can use a dry erase to check it off for the week or month, then erase it. But I didn't count well. The binder has one more disc and is about a half inch longer. Too much to make it work without cutting it, which is what I will probably end up doing.

I did check and dry erase pens work well and erase without a mess.

title: Can't figure out how to change the ring volume
text: Other than that, these phones are great.  Eventually, I will run out of blocked number spots, but it is working great so far.  Battery seems to last long, though I think they all do at first.  These replaced some old panasonic phones that we've had for maybe 10 years?  Not sure. A long time.  The batteries weren't lasting much more than a day and unfortunately, buying a new phone set is cheaper than replacing the batteries.  Easy set up.  There are probably things it does I haven't even looked at.  It does everything that my prior phone did that I use and keeps a charge. Perfect!

title: Says doesn't need tools
text:
My gas cylinder on my chair broke and it will no longer stay up. I have an non-adjustable standing desk, so sometimes I need it to be high, but then I need it to be regular height for my secondary desk.

It clips on easily. Then you tighten the bolt by hand. This is where the problem starts. I can't seem to tighten it enough that it doesn't allow the pipe to slide right through. Maybe if I were lighter? Like 100lbs? When I have time, I will see if my husband can take a wrench to it to fix it. Or I will just have to replace the gas cylinder, since the chair is in otherwise good condition.

title: I kind of like it
text:
Okay, I haven't quite figured out what I am going to use this for, but I really like the idea of it. I'm currently waiting on some more pen colors. It basically takes dry erase type pens and then you just rinse off the page or use the sponge eraser. A little water if needed.

I was thinking it would be great for brainstorming, to do lists, quick notes, and generally things you don't keep for long or consolidate elsewhere once you work it out. You can also take a picture of it if you want to keep it. I didn't pay attention as to whether there is an online organizer with it, but I don't normally like using those because if they quit business, you lose it all.

If you have used discbound planning systems or notebooks, this is easy to put together. And actually, I may move the pages to my discbound planner, just to keep it handy. It comes with 2 pen loops - one for the pen, one for the eraser/marker. I need to check the spacing to make sure it matches.

title: Don't stick on vertical surfaces
text: Well, that isn't entirely correct.  They stick, but don't stay stuck. The one I tested lasted for about 4 hours before it dropped.  The paper used is thin - this isn't a problem as long as you don't use sharpie type markers (there is some bleed through to the next layer with a sharpie).  Regular pens are not a problem.  I think these won't work for a Kaizen board, but it should work okay for notes in a book or quick to do lists that you are going to toss.  They don't leave any residue after you remove them.  I do like the colors.

title: Pockets stuck well.  Cards are okay
text:
I really like the pockets. They are great for adding a pocket on a notebook where you don't have one. It isn't a huge size but great for small things like stickers and cards. It goes on easy and sticks well.

They come with nice looking index cards. Like most index cards nowadays, they aren't real "cards" but more like a heavy paper. If you are old like me, you would remember the time when index cards were heavy. So, these look nice, but aren't what I consider index cards. And? I can't find anything better.

title: great for labeling cords
text:
I was redoing my computer set-up after changing out the hard drive and was tired of trying to figure out which cords plug in where. These were easy to use and attach solidly to my cables. I attached them as I removed the cables from the computer which made it so much easier to reattach when I put the computer back together.

They took ink easily. They are a little big, but it works for me. Overall, I would recommend if you are looking for cord tags.

title: No place to keep pen
text:
Overall, I like this daily planner. It has times from 6 am to 7 pm, with a blank hour after that you can use for any evening plans. The To Do list has room to write and there is a place for notes. I also like that there is a mini calendar for the month.

The months have room to note appointments and special days, but it is an A5/half letter size, so not a huge amount of space. There is a single note page for the month and a page with sections that you can use to write down goals for the month, monthly To Do's, or whatever. I guess a habit tracker could be put here somewhere, but otherwise, there isn't really a place for one. It is the only thing I really miss from not having a weekly section.

The paper is somewhat heavy and takes fountain pen well. I use a mix of my fountain pens and Micron pens and there is no noticeable bleed through and minimal ghosting. This gets down to my one problem. There is no pen loop. This planner doesn't fit in any of my planner holders which would provide a pen loop. I can clip the pen to the spiral, but have to unclip it to open the planner or it is in the way. I will probably end up trying one of those stick on pen holders, though my experience is that they only will hold small pens or they rip. None of my fountain pens fit in the stick on ones I've bought.

The planner seems pretty sturdy. I've been using it daily for a few weeks and the pages aren't coming out. The outside cover is heavy laminated paper and is very stiff. Overall, I would recommend it if this is the type of planner you like.

title: Measurement slightly off
text:
The problem I have with this type of cutter is that the measuring bars are never perfectly accurate. The arm pulls out and locks pretty well. I like how they have a case for the blades, though I think I would have preferred a second blade to a scoring blade. It also comes with a perforation blade. Not sure how useful that will be either.

The blade setup seems to be safe from accidentally cutting yourself. A good thing for me, as I am not always so good with these things. The other issue is the size. It will work chopping 8.5x11" paper in half (8.5x5.5") but not so good for most scrapbook paper. I guess if you get those 8x8" or smaller tablets. It has both metric and inches on the guide. It is a nice size for travel.

title: Nice tracker selection
text:
I'm kind of between 4 and 5 stars on this. These is a really nice selection of trackers for use in your planner or journal. They look good and still well. But I'm not sure for the price that it wouldn't be better just to get a stencil that will last forever (or almost forever) There is nothing fancy or colorful about these to make me want to keep getting them when I can get stencils for a similar price.

That said, if you don't want to deal with stencils, these are perfect.

title: Nice paper
text: I have no problem with the paper.  It worked well and prints fine.  My duplex printer would not work with it, so you have to manually print one side then the other.  I really liked that it had the holes punched so printing out planner pages were easy.

title: Works well
text: I like that I can print a bunch of small pictures from my phone and add them to my journal or memory keeping book.  But I can see this also being useful to keep pictures in place in a frame, especially where there are multiple photos in a frame.  Set it up once and it will never move.  The paper prints photos like any other photo paper.  The quality of your print will ultimately depend on your printer.

title: good addition to your planner line-up
text:
So this isn't really a planner. It is 12 monthly undated calendar pages with a goal page, month on 2 pages and a lined page so each month can stand on its own. There are stickers to use including the month, day numbers, flags, etc... and 4 dividers.

The rest is basically note paper. The paper is nice and seems to hold up well to fountain pens. My ink isn't overly wet and I do have a fine point pen. I would say the ghosting is so slight, as soon as you write on the next page, you won't see it.

I generally don't buy classic Happy Planner size. It is kind of an in between size. The Junior size fits in my purse and the full size (letter) gives a generous amount of room to write things down. But I think for a notebook, it is a great size.

title: Not sure it is any better than Franklin-Covey
text:
I used to use the Franklin-Covey planners. You put your to do's on your task list and then rank them A for must do's/priorities, B for would be good to get done, and C for do if you have time. This one is basically the same. But you do it at the beginning of the week for the week ahead. Then put them in the daily list split by personal/work. There's a space for daily brainstorming or notes and a daily reflection. There is no place for appointments or time tracking. So if your life requires more time related tracking/tasks, this isn't for you. This is also only for 3 months.

I think it is a great looking planner. I really like the quotes throughout and the daily productivity tip. The paper is nice to write on. There is also a free productivity class that you can access, if you want. I think if you have trouble prioritizing, this is a great system.

title: Mixed feelings on this
text:
Generally, it is not a good idea to write down your passwords. But there are so many of them and you are supposed to have different ones for every site. It is really too much to keep track of. You can pay for a password service or use Google's free one, but I always worry that if the initial account is compromised or you forget your password to it, you are basically screwed.

So a book like this makes sense as long as you have a safe place to keep it. It does look like a basic notebook and is unremarkable if you put it on a shelf with a lot of other similar notebooks. The paper is fine, I probably wouldn't use any wet pens as I think they would bleed through. But a ballpoint one should be fine. I like that it has an alphabetical index to help find the passwords easier. Overall, if you have difficulty remembering passwords, I'm not sure this is the best idea to use, as carrying it around defeats the purpose of having passwords. But as a backup? This is perfect

title: Nice binder day planner
text: This is a nice A5 size binder/daily planner.  The cover looks nice and I really like the elastic closure.  I just find the binder rings a little small for my usual planner pages.  It won't hold more than a couple months of daily pages.  I think if you have monthly and notes, it is perfect. But it comes with daily pages.  I do like the daily page setup though.  It has pretty much all the things I look for in a daily page.

title: Lots of choice
text: These are great if you have a bullet journal and don't want or can't draw them yourself.  They are most of the standard set-ups for habit trackers you see on Pinterest or Instagram, and are very easy to use.  Most of these would be for an A5 size bullet journal.  Though, you could probably resize them a bit.

title: Nice quality post cards
text: So, I collect postcards.  Usually I get them when I go places, but travel has been a little non-existent lately.  So I got these.  They are really great looking postcards of some really cool looking university buildings.

title: Great for organizing papers
text: I got these to organize my preprinted planner pages.  I like that there are different colors that allow me to organize by size and type.  Then I can find them when I need them.  They will take sizes up to 9 x 12 inches easily.  There is a slot for a card to label what is in the folder, though you can see through the cover easily.  The snap is easy to open and close.  Overall, I like them.

title: I love discbound planners
text:
Happy Planner is the standard for discbound planners and is letter size plus rings and cover overhang. They use really great paper of a good weight, with a colorful cover and monthly tab pages. I love the colors in this one and the horizontal weeks works well with my To Do list daily planning method. You can also use it as a morning/afternoon/evening time blocking planner.

The only thing I miss is a daily page, but since I don't use a daily page every day, as a discbound planner, it is so easy to add extra pages as needed. You just need a disc hole punch, which I really recommend getting if you are going to use a discbound planner system, whether Happy Planner or something else.

The only other complaint is that it is a little large to carry around. It is a perfect desk planner/organizer size. The classic size may be better if you are going to carry one around and stick with the Happy Planner method.

title: So far it's great
text:
I really love this put a pile in, press the button, and walk away shredder. You don't have to feed each individual item, which is great when you have a pile of papers to shred.

There are limitations to the auto-shred, such as cards and small pieces of paper. It has to be big enough to grab when in the tray. But if you are cleaning out a bunch of personal documents or a small office, this is great to have. I haven't tried shredding things that are stapled yet. Not sure how that will work with the feeder.

title: Works great
text:
I actually ended up using these with my laser jet printer and it worked really well. I use them in my planner to add some decoration. They work well and add color and a decorative touch without adding a lot of thickness to my planner. They take the print really well, almost better than paper. I am very happy with how they worked out.

As a note, they have a clingy effect. You may need to place sheets of paper between them if using to make overhead slides or you will spend a lot of time trying to separate them.

title: laminator works well
text:
This laminator works well and I've been happy with the results. The combo cutter seems like a great idea, but it is too small, measurement wise, to be really useful. You can use it to trim edges off the recently laminated parts. But if you want to take a few inches off a 8.5" by 11" piece of paper before laminating, you need to measure and mark elsewhere.

The inches/cm also don't quite line up with the blade either. But if you mark it, you can easily line it up and cut. The blade has stayed sharp, though I am expecting to have to change it soon, based on similar cutters. Not sure how standard it will be to replace.

I gave it 5 stars because it does do its main purpose - laminate - well, and because you can cut with it. The cutter gets a 3 stars though.

title: Works well as a magnetic bulletin board
text: I really got this as a magnetic bulletin board.  It works well.  I used sticky strips to attach it to my closet door, so I didn't use the mounting hardware.  The magnets stick great and it was perfect for my intended use.  It says it is dry erase, which it is, but it is not so easy to read anything written on it because it is metal and not white.

title: Works great as a desk/mouse pad
text: I like this because it covers most of the desk which means, 1) my mouse isn't limited to a certain area, and 2) it is easy to clean small messes.  Unfortunately, it won't protect against big messes.  It also stops me from scratching the top of my desk.  It lays nice and flat and looks good.

title: Too thin
text: The paper used to make this is a lot thinner than you would expect for tickets.  They do seem to rip well, which is a concern if the tickets are too thin.  Usually these are more cardstock like.  I think they will probably work okay for the usual short term things for which you use tickets.  I think for the price, you kind of get what your pay for.

title: Decorative
text: I get tired of boring planners. So I get stickers.  These worked great.  Go on easy and stay stuck.  There's lots of fun and useful stickers to brighten up your planner.

title: Good basic planner
text: There is nothing really fancy about this planner.  Has all the basics for a weekly planner including month at a glance and week on two pages.  The week on two pages has the 7 days with decent room for appointments, to dos and notes.  There is also a space for 3 priorities for the week.  There's space for basic information and contacts.  Though really, we all have our contacts in our phones.  The size is great for a backpack or purse.  And I really like the cover.

title: Stick well
text: These are great.  Do what they are supposed to do.  You can pull them up and put them on new page without a problem.  And I really love the colors.

title: Fits card slot
text:
These are nice cards with positive affirmations on them. There are supposed to be 60 different ones, but there a a couple duplicates - so four of each. They are nice sayings and fit into card slots in my planner. I like that you have extras to share or have in multiple places.

I gave it 5 stars because it is what it says it is. But sometimes these sayings are so overused to me and I actually find them a little de-motivating. But that is me. They are nicely made and colorful. If you like motivational quotes, they will be perfect for you.

title: Nice for  To do lists and appointments
text:
I like the set up of this planner. It is undated, so you can start anytime. It has months and weeks. There is a place for notes, one page of goal setting, important dates and favorite quotes.

The daily is to do's and schedule plus a small note area. Saturdays and Sundays are combined into a smaller space. This is made for someone with more to do during the week. I like that it is very basic and to the point. For most people, this is all they need. The cover is really pretty. It seems well made also.

I do not recommend this for fountain pen users. My pen bled through a bit, with definite ghosting. My Micron, however, was just fine. No ghosting or bleed. I'm assuming most ballpoints will be fine. Not sure about gel pens, as I don't have any to test.

title: Cute
text:
