This is a really fun planner. You get some intro pages/outro pages like book tracking, goal planning, habit trackers, etc.... things that you might put in your Bujo, but it is done for you. Frankly, it looks a little like my old Bujo when I took the time to make it pretty. Since making it pretty is a lot of work, getting this is much easier, yet still good. Months and weeks look like an artistic you drew them. There is variety in the weekly spreads, which is great. Plus it is undated, so you can start anytime, drop it and come back later if you want.

I think the only negative for me is no daily pages. But for this price, I can add a dot grid journal for when I need dailies.

title: Great for To Do's and Notes
text:
These are great for notes and lists. The tabs make it easy to find them in your planner. Or if you use them for taking notes in a book, you can tab the page and then write in the note. Great for students.

I'm currently using them to put my routines, to do lists, follow-up notes, etc... They stick well and pull up easy, then restick. There's a nice selection of colors as well, if you want to color code.

title: Different
text: So this is my first black-paged journal.  I need to find my metallic pens.  So far the only pen that works on it is my white gel pen.  Other than this, it is a great journal.  The paper is a nice weight and has gold edges.  It is really pretty.  I'm going to enjoy using this

title: Beautiful Leather Cover
text:
This is a beautiful leather cover. I didn't really pay attention to the notebook that came with it as I put my favorite A5 Tomoe River paper notebook in it. It fits perfectly. The stitching is perfect, and I love how the leather looks and smells. The closure is nice and allows for a little stretch.

The only negative I can see it the pen loop won't take a really thick pen, but does take most of my fountain pens. It also makes the cover a little lumpy if you have too thick of a pen in it. The loop location also makes it impossible to put a second notebook on the other side, if you wanted to. There is space for other things in the pockets.

title: Big footprint
text:
This was fairly easy to put together. The center poles, however, seems a little more wobbly than I like. I only put a 32" TV/monitor on it, though. I am not sure if a heavier TV would hold it down better or if it would make it more unstable. It is actually taking up too much floor space where it is, so I may put our old 42" TV on it and see if that works better.

I do like that it will hold a big TV, though I don't currently have a 70" one to put on it. It rolls pretty well on carpet, so I assume it will roll even better on hard floor. I use this TV as a second monitor and got the floor stand because when it is on the desk, it is too big/too close. Using the stand is great, but the wide legs made it difficult to situate them under the desk. I'm looking at some other options with either switching out the desk or getting a smaller stand. I think this would work well in the front of a room, like a classroom or meeting room, especially with a large TV screen.

title: Soft leather.  Nice cover
text:
This is a really nice A5 cover for your hobonichi, Stalogy, etc... The leather is soft and a little floppy. Putting a notebook in it does make it less floppy. If you put in a hard cover like a Leuchtturm, it will work great for giving it stability.

There's five card pockets in the back cover along with a side pocket. Four are at the top, perfect for credit cards or business cards. The fifth is at he bottom and, though card sized, will allow for a tall item to be placed in it. The front has an ID and a zip pocket, along with a side pocket. The side pockets are in addition to the pockets that hold the covers. There is also a large back pocket that should hold a letter size paper.

Overall, the stitching looks good, it comes with 2 bookmarks, and has a pen loop that will take a fatter pen, like my Kakuna.

title: Nicely made
text:
This is a nice looking cover for A6 size notebooks. I've put in my Stalogy and Zequenz A6 notebooks and both work well in it, though not together, as it won't stretch more than about 7/8" (about 2 cm) and still snap close.

I looks very well made. Smells like leather, without a funky smell. There are five card pockets in the front and a long pocket. The back has a corner pocket, a zipper pocket and another full pocket. There are 2 additional pockets - one front and one back - for holding the book covers. There is also a billfold type pocket that runs the back of the cover. There is a pen holder that fits a regular size pen, like my micron, but not a fat pen, like most of my fountain pens.

I think the only negative is the lining fabric is a little on the less expensive side. I have seen cheaper, but I have also seen better. I think the leather will outlast the lining. Though that might not be unusual to happen. For the price, this is a great deal.

title: Nice paper in an undated planner
text:
So this is a monthly/weekly planner. There are no daily pages. This planner starts out with goal planning, a place for a mind map, leisure activities list and a couple note pages. Then you get the 12 month sections. You get an undated month, planning page and end of month reflection page for each month. I think my only complaint is that the habit tracker on the month only has 3 items.

The rest of the planner is a week on two pages. I like that they have the days broken down by hours - 2 lines per hour - from 6 am to 9 pm. If you don't want to to track by hour, you can use it as a place to list your tasks for the day or break it up however you want. There are about 10 pages for notes at the end.

The pages, other the the first and last, lay pretty flat. There is a nice quote every week, and the paper is nice and heavy. My fountain pens don't ghost. Neither does my Micron. The paper is smooth and nice to write on. It is fairly lightweight and should fit inva standard woman's purse. Overall, as the cover says, this is a good weekly planner.

title: Inks aren't replaceable
text:
This is a very fat pen with 6 colors - black, red, orange, green, blue and purple. They tips don't come with the covers you find on some pens, so there is the potential some of the six will dry out before you get to it. they also don't appear to be replaceable like similar multi ink pens that I own.

That said, this pen writes nice and smoothly. I like the colors. And you get 6 pens of 6 colors for a great deal.

title: A little ghosting
text:
For the price, these are a great deal. You get 2 softcover journals with lined paper that has a place for a date and a memo number, which makes it easy to index if you are using it for notes or important events. I took a picture with the pen test and the ghosting wasn't bad. However, I wrote a journal entry and the ghosting is almost readable on the other side. I do use fountain pends. I think the ghosting may not be as bad with a ballpoint pen, but will likely be bad with a gel pen.

The ghosting is no worse than most of the notebooks I own, so it doesn't really bother me. The paper is nice and smooth and writes well. I didn't have any smearing with my pens. I was going to ding one star for the ghosting, but really, I don't think I have any journals in this price range that don't ghost.

title: Can't fit my Lamy's
text:
I really like these. They work well for my thinner pens but not my Lamy fountain pens, which means they also won't hole most highlighters. They easily hold my Microns.

They go on easily and stick well. The elastic just doesn't stretch enough for me. I can hook the clips on, so they still work for me.

title: perfect for a bujo
text: I think at 4"x 4", these are perfect for an A6, B6 or A5 bullet journal/planner.  Most are either a lot bigger.  These are easy to carry around.  I'm sure I will only regularly use about half of these. But, what I like, is not necessarily what others will like, so it is good to have variety. And maybe I should try some new spreads.  They are easy to use, though I usually washi tape them down so they don't move.

title: Great for smaller whiteboards
text: These work great for smaller print.  I love the colors and it erases well.  I have a smaller whiteboard that I use for my to do list that I have where I can easily see it.  The normal markers are hard to use to write smaller - at least for me.  These work great.

title: If it is what you need, it is great
text:
This is a really basic, somewhat thin, weekly planner. To me, it is perfect for a weekly to do list to carry around. It has all the basics you need. And, being undated, you can use it only when you need the basics. Or use it in conjunction with a separate daily planner.

Although I gave it 5 stars, I'm not sure it would work for me on a regular basis, as I like to have daily pages and more room, even though some days I don't have much going on. If I used it with another planner as a purse carry, I think it will be good. My regular planner is pretty big and I don't carry it out much.

title: Nice colors
text:
If you are tired of all those bright neon colors, these are great. I love the earth tones that go better with my planner than the usual ugly neon shades. They stick well and are great for color-coding.

The only cons are if your wires on your planner don't line up with the holes on the plastic backing. Only one of the planners I own seem to line up. They appear to be 3:1 binding size. I usually just put them in the front pocket anyway, because I switch planners regularly. The other con is that the dark colors may be too dark to read any pen ink on them, unless you have a white pen. I can't actually see my blue in on the really dark greens and browns. This isn't an issue for me because I mostly use them as quick find tabs. Most of them time, I don't write on them. I do have a white pen if I really need to use it.

title: Nice notebooks for your A5 TN
text:
Okay, so my favorite paper is Tomoe River paper, which is what I compare everything with. I actually think this compares well with TRP notebooks. It is not as thin, but it is still thin. It is not as smooth and feels like there is some cotton content in the paper. I tries with a few different pens and it barely ghosts (see pictures)

It writes very smooth and I like that there is enough pages to make it through at least one month, if not a few - depending upon how you use it. The booklets are sewn together well and, for me, the dot grid is the perfect size.

title: Nice pen
text:
I love fountain pens. This is generally a nice pen. It looks nice and writes well. I had some issues trying to get the ink into the converter that comes with the pen. I used a syringe that I bought to refill pens, which worked well. The only other negative is that he cap doesn't always post (stay on the pen when open) I can move it around and get it to stick on so I can write with it. It has some weight, so it isn't a lightweight pen. But I kind of like that.

It looks like it might fit a standard international refill, but I haven't tried it yet because I wanted to try my new ink with it.

title: Doesn't fit my 10" iPad
text: I got this more to store journaling supplies like pens, washi, and stickers.  So the fact it doesn't hold my iPad, is not a real problem.  I just don't like that it says it will fit, but it doesn't .  It holds a lot of stuff and looks good.  Overall, I like it and will use it.

title: The frame is metal. Baskets are heavy plastic
text: This is a beautiful cart.  the frame is strong and will take the weight.  The baskets, though plastic, a very solid.  It was fairly easy to put together with the provided tools.  It would have been easier if I borrowed my husbands drill/screwdriver to put the screws in.  I'm very happy with it and love the color.  It will brighten up my craft room.

title: Nice writing pen
text: Some of these inexpensive pens are scratchy, this one writes very smoothly.  It comes with a pump action refillable cartridge, which was very easy to fill once I realized you don't twist it to get it to fill.  Looks great.

title: Works well and looks nice
text: I normally use mouse pads, but sometimes they aren't quite big enough.  Maybe it is only me, but sometimes my mouse is a pain and I am constantly having to lift and move the mouse to the bottom of the pad because I ran out of room (my monitor is big)  I pretty much can't run out of room with this.  And it looks nice and neat on my desk.

title: Fits A2 paper but it is tight
text:
I have an A2 pad and tried to get it into this carrier so it would be protected. This bag collapses easily and is not really stiff, so it was a bit difficult getting it in as it is probably the biggest size of paper this will fit.

It is a nice carrier, lightweight and foldable, if empty, so you can take it with you easily. The handles are a good length. I can slide it over my shoulder and it sits under my arm, making it easier to carry. I'm planning on using it for large art paper which isn't quite A2 size.

title: Thinner than I would like, but good
text:
I got these to use as dividers in my planner(s). They will work, especially if put a piece of cardstock with them. I like the flexibility and can see them used for covers on things that won't get heavy use. I like that they are see through, so they will protect a cover page that is paper or cardstock without taking away from the page. They punched cleanly without a problem.

For the price, I think they are great.

title: Sturdy
text:
This seems like it will be a sturdy setup. It was easy to put together. Only negative is that once together, you don't really want to move it because it doesn't lock in place. The individual sections are solid and there is a knob and hole thing that is the way they connect. So on a flat surface, it isn't a problem. But you can't lift it by the top layer. You have to pick it up by the bottom.

It also comes with 8 feet - little rubber things that pop into the lock holes. So you can set up one set of 4 trays or 2 sets of 2 trays, which gives some variety.

Overall, it works for what I need.

title: A little messy
text:
I've been wanting a date stamp, so I thought I would try this. I see a lot of women using them in their planners and art journals to date the page. Getting the ink pad in the spot it goes in got ink on my hands. Then I realized the date that stamps is on the opposite side of what you see. Once the stamp has hit the ink, changing the date gets ink all over your hands. Now that I know to flip it to change the date first before I let it hit the pad and it should be okay.

It stamps well.

title: Gets you going
text:
These are good cards to get yourself going in your life, especially if you are feeling stagnant.

So I picked on - the front says "Do it with passion or not at all" The back says "Learn to say no! Today, say no to new projects and tasks that don't align with your goals and passions. If you find it super difficult or impossible, it is time to evaluate what's happening in your life." This is good in that it makes you think about what you are doing and whether it is time for a change in your life. Are you happy with what you are doing? Of course, not everything will line up with your passions - I will never be passionate about doing the dishes or vacuuming the floor, but maybe I'm a little passionate about living in a clean house? So you may be passionate about parts of your job, but not so much about some tasks. If you have to do them, evaluate how they fit in with the overall job.

Most of these things you can do yourself, others may need a second person, like call a friend.

Initially, I was so-so on the first few cards I pulled. This is not me. But, as I started going through them, more and more I could see doing these. I think it is something a lot of us women need - encouragement and a push in the right direction.

title: Great idea
text:
Part of a vision board is the pictures have to resonate with you. That said, these are really nice pictures that will work in a vision board in a general sense. Whether they will work on your vision board will vary with each person. There is a good selection of things people might have on their bucket list, such as travel to places, learn a second language, learn an instrument, learn to snowboard, etc... that should fit most peoples lists, as well as the usual "become a millionaire," "get in shape," "buy a house," etc... that are usually on most people's vision boards.

I have some flat sticker magnets that I may stick to the back of these so I can put them on my whiteboard. Otherwise, you can probably tape them inside a frame.

I did count them and found I had 99 original vision cards and 5 duplicate cards. I don't know if this is an error or planned. The cards are a heavy cardstock, like playing cards, with a shiny finish on the picture side and a papery finish on the other side. They seem like they will hold up pretty well.

title: Not Rose Gold
text:
This is kind of an ugly Rose-Silver. More of a beige-silver. Too much of a pain to return, and I will eventually get used to it. Just not what I wanted.

Otherwise, it is a great discbound book.

title: Didn't go together well
text:
The instructions to put it together are good, but one of the shelves that provides stability is not flat. Or the frame is not straight. Either way, I only have one shelf that clicks into place. It seems to be sturdy with only one shelf clicked into place, but I don't think I will put anything too heavy on it.

The organizer will hold a good amount of stuff, like letter size file folders and all the bits and pieces that collect on your desk, like pens, pencils, scissors, clips, post-its, etc.... The drawer will hold a good amount and moves in and out smoothly.

title: Smaller than I thought it would be
text:
I don't like to mark down for things that are my fault - i.e. not getting out a ruler and figuring out what the actual size will be when I get it. I have a bit of a difficulty estimating size.

That said, this is perfect for a small desk. The back section won't hold a file folder, but it will hold my 9.7" iPad or a A5 notebook. There's room for some post-its, clips, pens, etc... and it looks nice on my desk.

title: Works well
text: A great alternate to the more expensive tabs, plus you get plastic rulers to put in your planner/notebook.  They don't match up with standard planner binders, but work with the some spiral notebooks.  I just slide them into a pocket in my planner.

title: Love the closure
text: I've bought a few of these fake aged notebooks.  I think they look really great and I enjoy writing in them.  What I really loved about this one is the closure.  If you are just going to journal or draw in this, it is a perfect closure - always there and no long, hanging pieces of leather or cord.  Granted a snap isn't very "vintage" but I really prefer it or a TN type elastic closure to the long cords that aren't always attached.  The paper is nice and heavyweight.  No ghosting or anything.  Haven't tried watercolor on it yet, however, I can't see it would be a problem.  The paper reminds me of watercolor paper based on its thickness.

title: Pretty
text: These envelopes are beautiful.  They are perfect for giving the gift of money or whatever you want to place in the envelope.  There is plenty of space to write a note as well.

title: Very smooth writing
text:
I love how smoothly these write. I also like the colors as I love bright colors. The Lime green is a little more yellow than green to me. Lime is usually a little darker. But it is an okay color. The blue is great.

The one negative for me is they are a little thin for what I have become used to using. I've been using pens that are a lot fatter to ones that are slightly fatter and I've found the fatter pens are usually more comfortable for me if I have to write a lot. I can always put a grip on them if they aren't comfortable.

title: Nice looking notebooks
text: These are nice looking notebooks that come with their own pen holder.  They have a annual calendar for 2021,2022, and 2023 at the front.  The memo pages are very smooth to write on, however they do ghost a bit with my fountain pens and with the ballpoint pen that comes with them.  However, for me, it is not bad and will not bother me.  The covers are velvety feeling and flexible but not floppy.  They are professional looking enough to be good for work notes.

title: Very Nice Looking
text: This is a very nicely made notebook holder made from really nice feeling leather.  The leather isn't too stiff or too floppy.  There are places for 4 cards and a pocket, besides the pocket that holds the notebook.  You can easily get replacement fieldnotes notebooks here on Amazon when this one is full.  The pen holder won't take a fat pen, but it doesn't have to be really skinny.  And actually, the skinnier the better as far as folding flatter.

title: It works
text: This mousepad is double sided and seems well made.  It sits nice and flat, and the mouse seems to work well with it. I'm liking it better than the padded ones I usually get.  It doesn't seem to slide around much even though it doesn't have the non-skid bottom.

title: Has all the basics
text:
So if you are trying to get ahead with money, it is good to have a budget and track your spending. It starts out with a place to track annual expenses. I think you could fit semi-annual and quarterly expenses here as well.

Then there is each monthly section where you get a calendar to plan payments/income; followed by an income section; regular payments like rent/mortgage, car payments, etc...; then direct debits and bills of things may not be the same monthly; and savings. Then a a summary where you total all the required expenses, subtract from income, resulting in available funds. The rest is tracking daily spending.

The last two pages is a section to categorize what was spent so you can see where your money went. And a small monthly totals and available carry over. The last page is a place where you can summarize how your budget went.

Following is a pocket for receipts and bills. There are twelve months January through December but undated.

The size is perfect to carry in a purse, so you can track daily spending. Once you see where your money is going, it is easier to see where you can cutback and save to get ahead. I think the only negative is that, being small, the pocket will not fit most bills. Receipts should fit fine. It is a very nice looking book.

title: Nice Antique Looking Postcards
text: Not sure if anyone sends post cards anymore, but these are great if you like antique style cards these are great.  They would make good journaling cards as well.  Most of them are botanical pictures, but also old sheet music and ads. It is a nice selection and would work well in junk journals as well.

title: Nice journal
text:
This is really a nice journal. You will need some white gel pens for some of the pages that are black and dark blue, but other than that, the pictures definitely add to the charm of this book. A quick pen test with a fountain pen did not show any ghosting or bleed through. It was fairly smooth writing experience.

The pages are unlined, so they can be used for journaling or drawing. It is pretty tightly bound, so if you scrapbook or multimedia in it, you will end up with an alligator book (doesn't close) And, that may not matter to you.

It also came with some post-it type flags, a twelve centimeter plastic ruler and six cute shaped paperclips. I got a star, 2 dog bones, a plane, a cat and a heart.

title: Different
text:
I am a "planner girl" um, woman? So I love decorative things like paperclips to hold stuff in my planners. These are about the same length as standard large paperclips, so they are a perfect length. Not too short, not too long. They are about twice the width of a normal large paperclip. I think this will help them hold better. And they have that cute heart on the short side, which is the side that goes to the front normally.

A really nice addition to my planners.

title: Not A6
text:
Overall, this is a nice package of products for a personal sized binder. It will not fit in an A6 as it is too tall. However, it is the correct size for a personal sized binder.

The included paper takes fountain pen well. It is not smooth, but has a little roughness to it while writing. It also took my fineliners well. No ghosting. I like that it comes with additional items, including a page lifter, which are really nice to have. Other than the size being mismarked, this is a great starter set for a new planner/notebook or binder.

title: Funny
text: These are probably great to have right now, or may be they would have been great to have last year to cheer up a friend stuck at home.  I'm probably go to send these to my dad, as he lives in a senior apartment complex and they shut down a lot of the activities and he is stuck in his apartment alone most days.  These will at least let him get something fun in his mailbox.

title: If your planner is just to do lists this is perfect
text: Really the title says it all.  It is a daily planner of to do lists.  You could easily make it into a running to do lists as well.  The book is really pretty with nice paper and the perfect size for a purse.

title: great notebooks
text: These fit in my A6 TN perfectly.  I really like the paper and 48 pages is more than enough for a month plus note space if you make your own planners.  The box would last 4 years at least!  Otherwise, they are great for notes, drawing or whatever.  My fountain pens barely ghosted.  Though really, there wasn't really ghosting.  The paper feels great.

title: Cute florals
text: Okay, these are technically bookmarks, so they aren't supposed to hold more than one page.  I tried using them in my planner.  They only about 6 pages of copy paper before it gets not secure.  So if you think about it like  a paperclip ability to hold, it should be good.  I love the vintage-y floral pictures on them.  Very pretty.

title: Easy to use
text: I like this one because I can see where it is going to cut.  It cuts well and comes with extra blades.  If there is a con, I'm so-so on not having a full board to place the paper on.  It makes it a little more difficult to keep it straight.  But frankly, the fact that it folds down to a smaller size makes it worth not having a full board.

title: Lovely paper
text: I love paper, especially really nice paper that is smooth to write on.  This notebook is not only great looking, it provides  a wonderful writing experience.  It also takes fountain pen well.  I really felt the smoothness with my ballpoint pen. Almost no ghosting, just a shadow on one of my fountain pens, and no bleeding.  I'm not used to the size, but I'm sure I can easily make it work for me!

title: Probably won't hold a legal pad
text:
This is a really nice looking leather portfolio. The only real negative to me - and it really doesn't affect me personally, is that I can't see it working for a legal sized pad, unless it is one of those with nothing at the top. The portfolio measures not quite 14 inches in length, so a legal sized pad would only fit if it is the glued at the top type. And then it would be iffy as to if it is fully covered. I can fit a regular pad in it with no problem. Plus my 9.7" iPad Air fits in the pocket as well. There is a spot for a pen.

If you do have a pad and an iPad, there isn't much room left for papers though. Without the iPad, there is plenty of room and pockets for papers. There are also a couple of business card pockets that seem very secure. It is very professional looking and is a steal at $50.

title: Fun!
text:
This was so much fun to open. There's pads and sticky notes and stickers and paperclips - all with cats! If you are a cat loving stationery lover, these are a must have! I'm having a hard time not putting cat shaped flags all over my planner!

There's also a stencil with a number of cat shapes that can be used to line draw cats or fill in with stamp ink.

title: They work
text: Nothing fancy.  Two translucent plastic binders in an A5 size.  They each hold about 200 pages easily.  You get plain, lined, dot grid and grid paper with it, as well as stickers, dividers and zip pockets.  The paper is okay.  It ghosts a bit with most pens and had a little bleed through with my medium point fountain pen.  I didn't try any with bright colors and the fountain pen ink dried pretty quick.

title: bigger than I expected
text: I was thinking this would be about half the size it is.  It is very nice looking and holds a pen well.  I have some beautiful glass ink dipping pens that I'd like to display, but need care in their display.  I thought I would try this and it works well.  I just takes up a little more desk space than I was expecting it too. The pen that comes with it is very nice looking and writes very smooth.  I think this would make a great gift.

title: fun shapes
text: Okay, these are more for decoration than actual holding papers.  Most will hold papers together just fine.  But some are shaped in such a way, I'm not sure they will really hold much.  There is a great mix of animals and travel shapes.  The Eiffel Tower one is one of the ones I'm not sure will hold much more than 2 sheets together, but it sure is cute.  I'm using them in my planner to hold a quick note on a page and for decoration.

title: really nice book
text: This is a really nice hardback book with music staff paper.  The paper is a nice heavy weight and should hold up well to pencil and eraser, as well as pen. The pages are also perforated so you can remove them if you would like.  This is nice if you need to make copies.  I'm not sure how well this would work for orchestral writing, but it should work well for the normal bass/treble clef writing.  There's also a pocket at the back to hold loose papers, a nice ribbon marker and an elastic closure.  Overall, it feels and looks nice.

title: Works well
text: They are working well with my Amazon laminator.  I'm not sure how close to expect them to get to the edges - it could be the laminators fault if it doesn't get as close to the edge of the paper as I would like.  It laminates very clear with very few bubbles.  I made a bunch of planner dividers, both clear with dried flowers inside and covering cardstock, and am very happy with how they came out.  Looking forward to making more things with this.

title: Fun
text: I really like these.  They hold on well and are very decorative.  They are about the size of the large paperclip.  They are very colorful as well.  I get bored with the same boring paperclips, so I was happy to find these.

title: Bright!
text: If you are tired of boring manila folders, these are a great addition to your office.  They are very cheerful and bright colored.  I really love the patterns.  I also like that they are heavyweight.  Much heavier that the supposedly heavy manila folders I usually buy.

title: Smooth writing
text: I like these because they write smoothly while being a nice fine point.  The cap stays on the end when you put it there.  Overall a nice pen.

title: Damaged
text: Arrived open and damaged.  Trying to decide whether it's worth the headache of returning and getting something else.

title: Cute!
text: These are so much more fun than the usual post-its.

title: Nice notebooks
text: Overall, I really liked these.  They are a little narrower than my other A6 journals, but I like the paper and that they are dot grid.  Also, I like that they are hard cover and you get a pack of two. They have 192 pages each and three index pages.

title: Nice notebook
text:
I overall like this notebook. The cover feels nice, the paper is smooth and there are a good number of pages.

Pros:
Dot grid makes it easy to write the size you want while still having some direction plus you can use the dots for technical drawings or other art to line things up. A grid without the lines.
Lays pretty flat
256 numbered pages makes it easy to index
Box at the top gives a space for a page Title/Description
Size is good for notes
Option to join Thinkers group with training on how to think for free

Cons:
Ghosting with fountain and micron pens. bleed through with a brush pen
About an inch wider than my A5, so it won't fit in a cover - or at least covers I have. Fortunately, the cover it comes with seems like it will hold up fairly well.
There's supposed to be an app, but I can't access it on my iPad or Android phone

Overall, a very useful notebook aimed towards thinking out problems. But really, it would make a great bullet journal as well.

title: Nice erasable notebook
text:
This is a great little notebook. It doesn't have a lot of pages, but you are supposed to scan the pages and erase. I was able to easily erase with a damp towel using their pen. I think a Frixion would work as well.

The cover is really nice looking and has a pen holder in the front and a pocket. So far I haven't scanned anything from it.

title: Perfect
text: This is a perfect for bullet journaling.  The paper is lovely - minimal ghosting.  There's even a pen test page at the back.  It comes with index pages and all pages are numbered.  The paper is a nice weight and cream colored.  There's a pocket at the back and 2 bookmark ribbons.  The cover is really pretty also.  And there is an inspirational quote every 10 pages.

title: Great for crafters!
text: I have a lot of pens, paint brushes and tools for my various crafts.  This is great.  It holds a lot and the lazy Susan allows it to move freely, which makes it easy to find what you need.  It also looks great in my craft room.

title: Perfect!
text: This is the perfect size for a computer that sits on the ground to make it easy to pull it out from under a desk and slide it back in.  Perfect for  (1) if you need to get to the back of the computer regularly, and (2) to make it easy to clean out the dust that gets into the computer.  Where I live, the dust can get bad.  It is slightly adjustable, but most towers are about the same size.

title: daily journal
text: This is a daily journal to help with mindfulness.  There is a morning section where you take a moment to breathe and decide about your focus for the day.  There's a few questions you answer that are the same every day.  Then in the evening, you go back over how the mindfulness went for the day and a few other things.  The only problem I have, it there is a part about thinking about a positive memory.  The thing is, it is the same exercise every day.  I think it would be better if the daily evening mindfulness exercise changed daily.  Otherwise, it is a great way to get started on a mindfulness practice.

title: Nice, professional pen
text: This is a nice, professional-looking pen that writes very smoothly.  It comes in a nice looking case that would make a great gift.  Not sure what else there is to say.

title: Nice looking notebook
text:
I like this notebook. It has a soft leather cover with metal corners. The paper is heavy enough that there is no real ghosting or bleed-through. There are 5 signatures with 88 pages (44 sheets) in lightweight kraft paper covers. The paper is cream colored and blank. It should be good for drawing as well as writing and would make a nice travel journal.

The only somewhat negative is that the tie/closer is not attached. I tend to put it down and then forget where I put it.

If you've ever sewn your own signatures, I think the insides would be fairly easy to replace once the pages are full. You would just need to match the holes in the cover.

title: looks good
text:
So, to start, this was somewhat easy to put together - as long as you make sure the backs are all facing the same way. There are screw holes on one side of the flat ends. The first time I put it together, I found I messed up. Fortunately, it is easy to unscrew and start over.

Once together, it is pretty stable and will hold a lot of paper or magazines, while looking good.

title: great paper
text:
I like my A5 ring planner, but I also miss the dot grid of my bullet journal. This paper fits perfectly in my A5 planner and gives me the dot grid I need. The paper is a good quality and doesn't bleed through with a micron pen. There is some ghosting, though I think it will be okay when I write on the other side. There's a bit of a give and take as far as thin paper so your planner doesn't get too thick vs thicker paper with no bleed through but that means you have minimal pages due to the thickness. This paper is a happy medium I think.

The tabs are okay. They are heavy cardstock, but do not have the plastic reinforcement. So they bend really easily. They will not last long. I deducted a star for that.

title: smells
text:
This is a lovely hobonichi cover. The cover is well made and looks like real leather. The snap closure allows for the expansion of your hobonichi. I was also able to get my other A5 notebooks in it (not at the same time) except my XL Moleskin, which is a little too fat. But the usual 192 page bullet journal notebooks will fit without a problem. The leather is very soft and pliable.

I really love the 2 page markers than come with it. and the pen holder will fit my fat-ish fountain pen without a problem. There is only the one pen holder. There are a number of pockets to hold various items like stickers and ID. Overall, it is a very nice looking notebook cover.

The only negative, which is kind of big for me, is that it smells and is setting off my allergies. It is kind of a chemical smell. I will air it out and hope it gets better.

title: works well
text:
This is fun with the big peacock feather on the top. I've only used the main nib, though it comes with a bunch of calligraphy nibs. It writes smoothly and holds a decent amount of ink.

The only negative for me is the barrel part is a little short and my hand runs into the carved part that holds the feather. I don't think it will be comfortable for long writing sessions, but normally I don't use them very long.

title: Thin but fun
text:
Okay, these are just fun. Who doesn't want a big diamond on the tip of their pen. The pen writes smoothly and work well. They are a little thin and short, but it depends on your hand size. Perfect for small planners. They come with extra pen refills, however they are not your normal refills, so when they die, I'm not sure they are refillable.

These would also be great as gifts.

title: great colors
text:
I really like my fine tip colorful markers for journaling/planning. It is hart to find really fine tips with a lot of color choices. These are nice. I can use them in my dot grid planner and write within the grid. I like the case it comes it. They are all lined up in the holders and are in easy to remove trays.

The color selection is great. It comes with extra tips, though no directions on how to replace them. The caps are very tight, which is good to keep them from drying out. I think the price is great and I am looking forward to using them in my planner.

title: missing the slit
text: I think I must have got a damaged pen.  This pen is very pretty and totally unusable because the nib is missing the slit that allows the ink to flow.  Without the slit, no writing can be done.  So pretty pen that is totally useless.

title: Writes great!
text: This is a very smooth writing pen.  It has a nice weight and is not too thin, which my fingers like.  The opening action is a very smooth twist. It is very professional looking and would make a nice gift.  Not sure what else to say.

title: Pen is great, ink is a little messy
text:
The pen works great and is fun to work with. The swirly point holds the ink well, which makes it good for writing a paragraph before you need more ink. Okay, a short paragraph. Depends on how much you write.

The ink that comes with it is very pretty. Unfortunately, the plug they put in it so it won't dry out does not come out easily and there was more ink on my hands than on the pen tip. It took a few days to get rid of the remnants, but it eventually washes off. There is a little bit of a sparkly stuff in the ink - glitter? Not sure what it is. It does add something to the ink.

title: Good goal planning system
text:
This is a great planner for working on your goals. There is a whole section at the front where you set up your goals and break them down in to achievable steps. You then use this to plan for each monthly goal then daily tasks to get to the monthly goals that then achieve the annual goals. At the end of each month, you review where you are and adjust your goals as needed.

The weekly has daily by hours with a to do list at the bottom. I think the only thing I would like is more room for daily notes. Otherwise, it is a really great planner.

title: Work well/Look great
text: I was looking for some book ends to use on my shelves.  These look good and do the job.  Nothing too fancy.  They hold up the books and were a great price for the number you get.

title: Not very fine tip
text:
I love fountain pens, but I prefer the fine tip, probably because the way I write medium makes it unreadable. This is a very nice, professional looking pen. But in no way is this a fine tip

Like many of my fountain pens, it takes a while for the first cartridge of ink to really work. I did rinse out the nib before starting to get anything that might be blocking the ink, which helped a bit. I still have trouble getting it to start writing. Once it starts, it writes smoothly. Best of all, this might be one of the first pens that doesn't leak all over my hands. I hope it stays that way.

title: Nice looking notebook
text:
This is a great size to carry around. The leather looks nice and professional. I like how the pen "loop" keeps the pen inside the cover. The binder rings look like they will hold up to opening and closing. And the snaps keep everything closed.

The paper included is just brown kraft paper. Nothing great. I will probably change it out with something better. And? I can switch it out fairly easily because it has rings. There is a limit to what you can put in this and be able to close it. It will work great for notes, but if you want to add a bunch of pockets like places to hold receipts or cards, it may not close. So this is not one you can overfill. The 80 pages seem to be about maximum.

title: Good way to organize things
text:
I'm into planners and journals. So I have stickers and washi and pens and all sorts of other things that get lost easily. These are great for keeping track of all the bits and pieces. These are a little larger than I would normally like, but they are the perfect size for regular copy paper. So they can be used to sort papers too.

These could also be used for a lot of different hobbies. I do not think they are waterproof totally. The bag fabric is waterproof, but the zipper will not be as it is a normal zipper, which means holes between the locks and the heavy fabric the zipper teeth are attached to isn't waterproof. So I wouldn't drop it in water.

title: mouse pad is great
text:
I got this mostly for the mouse pad. I have carpal tunnel in my right hand and tend to hold my mouse incorrectly. This give the hand something to rest on that is raised and cushiony, yet firm enough to support. This keeps my hand in the correct position. The mouse works on it nicely. Mouse pad gets a 5 out of 5.

The keyboard rest doesn't work right with my keyboard. Don't know if it is the keyboard or the rest, but they don't line up right and ends up in the way. So I don't use it.

title: works great - don't have to shred so much
text:
I've been shredding everything lately, as with all the identity theft going on, it's just easier to shred than think if it actually needs to be shredded or not. This allows me to cover information easily rather than shred - I still shred things that definitely contain personal information. But all the junk mail for "refi your house!" "buy a new truck!" "magazine with stuff I'm not interested in" that shows up at my door just needs a quick run over the address with this and everything is gone. It covers well. Once in a while I do a second run over because it is still slightly readable. But mostly one roll over does it.

I also really love it for covering the information on address labels on my Amazon packages. Much easier than trying to remove the label before recycling.

title: Need to have your goals broken down
text:
This is a nice, portable journal to track your plans and progress for any projects you have. Every 15 days, you get a new set of plans and a discussion about how the prior 15 days went, the progress, what worked, and what didn't. This is dated, but not, in that there are no day of week or year, so it can be used at any time.

My problem with it is you need to have your plans in place. The set up is something like "I need to do x by date so that y can happen." This is not bad, but realistically, goals tend to be big and require a lot of little steps. This is for the little steps. If you have something else that will help you set up your goals and break them down into little steps, this will be useful. But this doesn't teach you how to do the initial goal setting and breaking down into steps. I currently look at this and feel a little at a loss for how to use it, as I need help with the goal setting and breaking down into small steps. Especially the second part.

title: Nice leather journal
text: This real leather journal is nice looking with a removable book inside.  It is pretty big, so will take something like a Stalogy or similar when you go to replace it.  I wouldn't use a hard cover book inside.  It was difficult to put in the hard cover notebook I had.  The notebook that comes with it is nice.  Lots of lined pages with a nice parchment look.  The strap to keep it closed works well.

title: Vintage-y
text: This is a nice leather traveler's notebook with pages that can be removed and changed out.  The pages are not  sewn together, so they aren't your normal notebooks that are found in a TN.  The paper reminds me of heavy handmade paper or heavy water-color paper. The color is a manila shade with darken edges.  I can see using this for a art journal or book of shadows.  It is too heavy for a planner or really a writing journal.  But it would be easy to change out the notebooks with something that is A5 size, though you may have to shorten it.  Or B6 with extra room.

title: Nice container
text:
So after getting this, I checked YouTube videos on these types of products. House fires get very hot, and these aren't airtight, so after looking at it, I was curious as to how "fireproof" it is. Somewhat. Basically, if you keep valuables in it, keep it near the front door so you can grab it in case of a fire, it should be fine, even if there is fire around it. It won't survive a full house burned to the ground fire.

It goes together easy and will fold flat for storage. There is plenty of room for a lot of documents, pictures, DVDs, etc... that will hold your important stuff. The straps make it easy to grab to take with you.

title: B6 refillable
text:
Okay, the lock is probably not going to really stop someone who wants to read your diary. But it will take them a little bit to get it open. It is a nice looking book The actual journal inside has nice paper, not too heavy or thin. The cover of the inside journal is pretty non-existent. So if you replace it after it is full, which can be done, I wouldn't put it somewhere where you see it because it is not finished. I was able to fit my B6 Stalogy in the cover, however, if you over-fill your journal, you may run into the problem of being unable to close the lock. I think a slightly thinner soft-cover B6 would be perfect.

There are pockets inside the covers, but you would have to be careful about how much you fill them as they will stop the lock from closing.

title: Fun!
text:
I really like these. They are bright and colorful and have lots of choices for my planner. I need color in my planner or I won't use it. The style is more grown up also. I really don't like all those stickers that look like they belong in a kid's book.

I think my only complaint is the same as with all planner sticker packs - I always end up with a bunch I never use and not enough of ones I do use. I don't know that there is an answer for this other than printing my own, which is a pain, because I'm sure others use the ones I don't and may not use the ones I do.

title: works if you get the right side
text: You do have to let it dry.  There is a print side and a not print side.  If you touch too soon it smears.  That said, it is great paper for photos.  Looks like those printed at the store.  Well, once you get your printer to get the colors right, but that is not the fault of the paper.  I've only used it on an inkjet printer.

title: Fun and cute
text: Okay, they don't do anything you can't do with the normal ugly paper clips.  But these looks great and work well.  They are not really huge, length-wise, which is actually nice.  They don't get in the way like some of the other bigger sized clips because they are not much longer than normal larger clip, just wider.  I use them in my planner to clip things in and as bookmarks.  I got the rose gold, though they are more rose copper to me. They go with other rose gold accessories I have.

title: Cool vintage-y notebook
text:
This is a great notebook for something fun like an art journal (where you don't need white background) or a Book of Shadows or maybe just a garden planning journal. The paper is like heavy watercolor paper or handmade paper in a manila color with brown inked edges. The paper feels uncoated and should take most mediums without a lot of ghosting or bleed through. Though there may be the normal bleeding that comes with uncoated paper and things like felt pens.

I also like that it is real leather and the key on the closure fits into the spot for it so it doesn't dangle.

title: Weekly review
text:
I would not call this a planner. This is more of a review of how your week went and where you think you are on your goals. Doing a weekly review on where your life is going is one of the things people who discuss meeting your goals recommend. If you don't have a process to do this in your planner, it is great to have something like this to get you started.

The one negative is they don't actually have a goal setting section. I would like a general goal section at the beginning of the book where at least you state the goals you are going to be reviewing at the end of every week. If you have a section in your planner with goals, you can use that and this will be a great accompaniment to your planner.

title: Can be A5 or Half Page
text:
Lightweight plastic cover discbound notebook. The cover is slightly larger than A5 - which is slightly shorter but slightly wider than half letter. The actual measurement is 8.75" x 6.25" - so either size would fit with a little room left over. The cover is a similar weight to the calendar discbound covers that I've bought from other companies. Though I do love the Monet print much better than the ugly calendar one I have.

The paper that comes with this is a nice weight, doesn't really ghost with a normal pen, and is reasonably smooth turning the pages on the discs. Overall, it is a nice notebook and can easily be refilled with A5 or half letter paper, if you have the punch.

title: Overall they are great
text:
There are so many of them in this set. Would be great for teachers who put together sets of pens and pencils or organizing smaller things. I think my eventual plan is to use them to store stickers and ephemera in a more organized way than the big box they are currently in.

However, I am using them as pen cases for my different sets of pens - i.e. one has highlighters, one has fine tip markers, etc... They come with a rope tag and I attach them to a carbineer clip to keep them together. They seem pretty strong, though I don't put anything pokey in them yet. I don't think they would last. They are not totally see-through because of the reinforcing web. But it is good enough to have an idea of what is inside. They are great for carrying craft supplies around.

title: 4.5 stars
text:
This is a very nice gift set for someone who likes calligraphy/pen and ink/ etc,,,

It comes with a stand for the pen, extra nibs, ink, and a journal. The stand was a little difficult to put together. There's a plastic nut that goes inside the pen cap/holder to hold it on. I finally got it to work by forcing a slot screwdriver into the plastic top (not too hard, just enough to hold it), put the cap on the screw, and used the screwdriver to tighten the nut. Once together, it works well. The cap is actually too big for the pen to fit snugly, but it works as a holder. I was a little disappointed in the feather color. It showed as a brighter green, this is more forest green/ green-black.

The notebook is leather like, but I'm not sure it is real leather. The inside is a soft velvety texture that you don't normally find on real leather. Other than that, it is a nice sized notebook to carry around. They actually overfilled the binder with paper, which is nice. Though I'd recommend removing some of the sheets to make writing easier. The paper is like a kraft paper, but nice weight and smooth. Testing the ink and pen gave a smooth writing experience. The trick is to get enough ink without too much. might be easier if using a ink dish rather than straight from the bottle like I did. Holding the pen at a normal writing angle, the ink flowed well with little spotting. I was very pleased with the results.

title: works well
text:
I have a standing desk and a barstool type chair I use. This works great as a foot rest. And if you flip it over, it lets you rock your feet and burns a bit of calories. It doesn't move (other than rocking) but is easy to flip with your feet.

It does say you can rest one foot on it at a time if you are standing, but I found this to be a little uncomfortable. It also won't take your weight (not that I really tried) if you want to to stand on it. It is hollow hard plastic.

title: great notebooks
text: So these are more small books with a narrow spine, rather than more of a traveler's notebook.  You still can use them in your TN, but also just as a notebook.  The paper is a nice weight and barely ghosts at all.  There's no bleed through.  I use Micron pens, but I think a ballpoint wouldn't ghost at all.

title: Great for what it is
text:
This is for use as a cash envelope system of budgeting. The binder is a personal size - slightly larger than A6 but not quite B6. It is a nice looking fake leather. The color I got - I think it was mint - looked more turquoise in the picture. It is definitely mint green. So the colors may not be representative, but the names are.

I don't really use cash at this point in my life, but I do like to track my spending. I plan on using the envelopes for receipts, as needed, and using the budget sheets to track my spending. Using this way would be great for a small business or if you travel for work and need to keep receipts like I do.

title: For a PU binder it is nice
text:
Okay, first thing, this is not A6, it is personal size. A6 is basically 4" x 6". The paper in this is 3.75" x 6.75" - actually closer to 6 7/8" which matches to what would be considered personal size in notebooks.

The binder is nice looking with one of my more favorite Van Gogh prints on it. The turquoise color is on the darker side. The rings close pretty well, but there are spaces that indicate they are already not closing perfectly. The card slots are a nice addition and there are two pen bands. Additionally, there is enough room between the paper and the closure to allow for one fat pen (i.e. Coleto) or two thinner pens (i.e. Micron). There is a little room to grow before the magnetic closure won't catch but not much.

The paper is very nice. A good weight that barely ghosts and only with the darkest pens. It is wide rule, so you may need a lot of pages if you were taking notes in it in a meeting, but the perfect size for quick notes/memos to self and to do lists.

title: Nice looking
text:
This is a nice, professional looking notebook. The cover looks like real leather, though you can tell it isn't when touching it. The paper inside is on the thinner side but doesn't seem to ghost much with regular ballpoint pen ink. My Micron's do ghost a bit more. Nothing that would be too noticeable if you are taking notes. The top of the page has a space for Memo# and Date as well as a day of the week check box and a weather icon - all good if you are tracking information like deliveries for the day.

Unfortunately, the way it is put together, when I tried to get it to sit flat, I seem to have cracked the signature a bit and it is starting to crack open in the back page. I'm not sure if it would last long in a business environment where people are not always careful how they use things. The front seems a little more stable and this could be fixed with a bit of tape.

title: Maybe not heavy duty
text: These are really pretty folders for sorting and organizing documents for projects.  They hold a decent amount of documents with tabs to organize them and a snap closure to keep them inside.  They seem pretty sturdy.  My concern is that a couple have little card holders that have already torn.  Now the part that holds the cover to the internal file structure seems pretty solid, it is similar to the way the card holders are attached.  I think if you don't overfill them, they will work great.  I don't really want to put too much pressure on them to see how much they take, but they aren't breaking under normal pressure.

title: Pretty
text: Well, other than the push-pins that are clear with a rose gold pin (doesn't really show much), these are really pretty and add a nice touch to my paperwork and my planner.  Though to me, they are more a bright copper than a rose gold, which is fine.  (comparing to my rose gold iPad)  I still enjoy the prettiness compared to the usual boring black and silver I normally used for paper and binder clips.

title: Works great
text: I've used these before at jobs where I did a lot of filing.  Been thinking of getting one for a while because they make filing papers so easy.  Though I guess if you properly keep up with your home filing, you don't really need it.  It is probably most useful if you have a business, but if you are like me and throw everything into a bin that you sort out at the end of the year for taxes and filing, it is great and doesn't take up a lot of room.  This one comes with alpha tabs, but it would be easy to cover them with categories if that would work better.

title: Nice
text: I really like Southworth paper, so I expected to like this journal.  There is no bleed through and very little ghosting - mostly only with the non-ballpoint pens.  I even watercolored a bit and it was not more than the highlighter.  I took a picture, but the picture shows no ghosting, so it wasn't really a good exhibit as I could see it with my eyes.  The paper takes watercolor without a problem.  Very nice feel - not too smooth, similar to their cotton based paper.

title: Nice
text: Makes circles easily for the most part.  I found if you aren't careful it will move when you adjust your hands to go all the way around in the circle, which kind of defeats the purpose.  But then if you hold it down too hard, you get a hole in your paper.  You also only can use the pencil lead with it.  Granted, mostly you want to use pencil, but sometimes, when crafting, I would like to make circles in colored pen or pencil.  It is easy to adjust.  And there are a lot of extra leads.  And a sharpener if you need it.

title: Beautiful
text: This is a beautiful leather cover that fits my Rocketbook notebook. It is a heavy leather with great looking stitching and a pen holder that fits the Frixion pen without a problem.  Makes the notebook look much more professional.

title: Little difficult to put together
text:
Once it is together, it seems pretty sturdy. I just had some problems getting the screw holes to match up. I do like how it folds flat if you take it apart.

As a note, this does not take legal or letter hanging files. The interior dimensions are about 12.5"x13.5" by 10" high. I will probably use it for storing my 12x12 scrapbook papers as it is a perfect size for them.

title: Nice looking
text:
This is a nice looking file storage box. It is made of fabric and cardboard, so it won't take the weight of a plastic or metal file box, but it is much more decorative looking and I won't worry about leaving it out/looking messy.

It was very easy to put together and came with some hanging folders and regular file folders - all in letter size. It will also take legal size hanging folders (not included) but, of course, not both at the same time. I do like the option. It can also be used for storage of non-office items like toys or craft supplies. Although there are handles on the side, I probably wouldn't use them much unless you have lightweight items inside. Having owned similar fabric cube storage containers, they do eventually break off if too much pressure is applied. However, carrying the box by the metal reinforced openings on the front/back works just fine.

title: Warm, but a little awkward
text: My hands are always cold, so I really want to like this.  It gets nice and warm and does warm my hands (and the mouse.)  There is a way to use it with a wired mouse, but frankly, it is awkward once your hand is warm.  I recommend using it with a wireless mouse instead.  When your hand gets warm, you can pull the mouse out and use it as normal much easier if it is wireless.  Otherwise, it is like working in a sheepskin pocket or you have to unplug the mouse, pull out the cord and plug back into the computer.  There is no issue with using the wireless mouse as far as the signal going through.  You do need a spare socket as it plugs in for energy. The mouse pad inside is a standard pad and works well.

title: really liking this.
text: It's like having a desk-sized mouse pad.  It has a smooth upper surface that allows for smooth movement of the mouse.  And the grip bottom makes it so it doesn't move.  It makes my desk look nice and calming.  I tend to not want to cover it with a lot of junk, so my desk stays cleaner.  Very happy with it.

title: Great selection
text: There is a great selection of various stickers for planning.  I'm having a lot of fun using them to set up next year's planner.  They are fairly  easy to peel off the backing and stick to my planner without a problem.  They have a page for each month, along with general stickers for various events and tasks/todo lists.  Bright colors, which I like. Some stickers may be too big for a monthly calendar - it depends on your planner's size as to whether these will all work well. for you.  I know there are some I will never use, but others I wish there were more of.  However, for others, those that I rarely use might be the ones they need more of.  So, overall, great selection

title: Water resistant
text:
These are great highlighters. You get a broad mix of colors that actually highlight rather than cover the writing underneath. Some that I've gotten in the past are so dark, you can't read what they are supposed to be highlighting. So far, even the darkest colors are sheer.

I'm sure they are great for color-coded studying, but I'm going to be using them for my planner/bullet journal. I did test them and they didn't run when watercolored over. Normally, I don't watercolor over highlighters, but I sometimes watercolor the back page, so it is good to know they won't run. I love having so much color choice. The only negative is that you can't really tell which are pointed tips and which are chisel tips until you open them. You can highlight with the pointed tips, but the chisels do a better job.

title: Good value
text: These are very solid binder rings and you get a lot for the money.  I use them in making crafty journals,  They are easy to open and close, yet stay solidly closed when they are supposed to.

title: Nice undated weekly planner
text:
It starts out with a how to use. Nothing too complicated. Then there is a place to set up 6 goals with action steps and a why. Goals with a "why" tend to work better if the why is important to you. Next is undated months. They have a place for your goal(s) for the month, top priorities, successes and wins, and lessons and insights. The blocks are a little small so you can't put too much in each day.

The week pages - also undated - had a spot for goals and top priorities for the week. The daily boxes have a decent amount of room for a planner of this size, plus the light gray dot lines can be used or are light enough to ignore if you need more space that day. My only issue is Saturday and Sunday are barely half the size of the weekdays. I usually need more room on the weekends as I clean and run errands more on weekends that during the week. There is also a big box for notes or whatever. You could put a habit tracker there if you want one. There is also a spot for a weekly gratitude and an uplifting quote.

In the back, there is a spot for Year in Review where there are spaces for "I accomplished", I Learned", Favorite moments, and Challenging moments. Then a Plan Ahead page where you can basically carry over goals that weren't finished.

Then there is a great little section for Morning/Evening Routines, Self Care Routines with suggestions, Self-Love Practices and a place to put Affirmations. Lastly there is a page for a vision board and Journaling Prompts with 30 dot grid pages.

The paper is very nice and smooth and is an off white shade, which I like because I find white paper to be a little glary when looking at it for a while. I did a pen test. The brush pen and highlighter did ghost, but most of the other pens, including a pigma micron and fountain pen were fine. It took watercolor and colored pencils without an issue. It has a nice elastic to hold it closed, an elastic pen loop and a cute charm. Overall, for its size - about an A5/half sheet, it is a good planner.

title: Great for packaging
text:
I sometimes sell handcrafted items on Etsy. These are perfect for sealing the tissue paper I use to wrap my products. It will look very professional. They are all slightly different but all are gold foil writing on a lovely pink background.

The box comes with a little slice opening on the side of the box that the roll of labels can come through. It was a little difficult to maneuver the roll edge through, and there was a label casualty in the process, but it will take me a while to go through 500 of these.

title: Nice notebooks
text:
If you are a TN person like me, you are always looking for good but inexpensive refills. for your notebook. These are a good deal. However, they are a little small for my A6 and are more of a pocket TN size. They fit perfectly in my pocket TN. Granted, I've found pocket and A6 can be interchangeable sometimes.

The kraft paper style covers are in a heavy cardstock and have a saying on the front. The paper is a nice thickness and feels very smooth. It actually feels like 2 pages thick of normal notebooks. For most of my pens, there was little to no ghosting and no see through. The brush pen did ghost a bit. There are 20 sheets that equates to 80 pages per book.

I think my only con, and it is a personal con, I prefer blank or dot grid to lines. But for the price, I was happy to find them.

title: Works well
text:
I used this to make planner stickers. It worked great. Went through my printer without a problem through the normal paper tray. Used an ink jet without any problem. No smudging or anything. Colors looked the same as normal paper.

If you are printing a full sheet sticker/label it is very easy to peel off. If you make a bunch of little stickers that you cut up, getting the sticker off the backing is a little more difficult, but not any worse than other stickers I've bought that don't have an edge to them. There's a short period of time if you mess up, you can still lift the sticker and reposition it, as long as you don't press down hard. Overall, I'm very happy with them.

title: Out of 4 only one works really well and now it is leaking everywhere
text:
Update: Just 2 days later and the good pen is now leaking everywhere. What a mess. I can't really recommend these at all.

So technically, I should say out of 3 because I didn't try the 4th yet. The first one wouldn't load ink well. It may improve, but after 15 minutes, I only got about 1/4 of the ink in the reservoir. The second loaded after about 5 minutes of fussing with it. But it leaks all over my hands when I write. It is clean on the page but my hands are a mess. The third also took a bit to load, but when it finally loaded, it filled all the way up and is writing beautifully. I only had 3 colors of ink to load, so I left the 4th one.

For the price, the one pen that works is great and gets a 5 star. The other 2 get about a one star, so I'm not sure how that works out.

title: Not A6
text:
This is a nice notebook. However, though it is A6 width, it is a pocket height and so is a little bit short for my A6 covers and sits weird.

Other than the fact it won't work in my covers, It is nice and sits flat.

title: Nice paper holder
text: This can be hung on the wall (if you have a place where sticking it out isn't a problem) or it can sit on your desk.  Nice clean lines look good on my desk.

title: Works
text:
I got this to catalog my library, because I have a lot of books. I tried a couple of library programs and it worked with all of them. I have a Windows 10 computer, if that matters. It read the scan code quickly and gave it to the program as written on the ISBN. I did not use it to set up codes. But I'm assuming it reads those fine if your program can interpret properly.

Now I just have to pick a program.

title: Solid and pretty
text: This is really pretty and very sturdy.  Looks great on the shelf and either organizes your magazines or papers or flip it around and hides the mess.

title: Nice mix
text: These are binder clips.  Not sure what else there is to say.  You get a great mix of sizes which I like better than buying a single size because you always need at least 2 different sizes and then there is a drawer full of clips that takes years to use up.

title: Great for planners
text: I have a modified bullet journal.  I really love using these to note the months and provides tabs to make it easy to go back to months

title: Great bulletin board
text: This is a really nice looking bulletin board.  Really large, but lightweight.  Mine was fine, but there is a note that if the frame gets bent in transport they will replace it.  They pack it well so it shouldn't be bent.

title: Works great
text: I actually cut these down into smaller tabs for my planner.  I really love the look of them. Like all post its, they stick well yet come up easy.

title: Nice leather TN
text:
This is a basic leather TN cover that comes with three very nice notebooks, an extra band and a plastic pouch/card holder. The leather is beautiful smooth reddish brown. And it comes with a nice cloth bag to keep it from getting scratched.

I think it will scratch somewhat easily if you throw it in a backpack or purse. I tried adding notebooks, but it would only maybe fit another, so if you like chunky TN's this is not the one for you. If you like slim and sleek TN's, this is perfect.

title: Pages don't stay in
text:
This is such a beautiful planner. I've gotten these Tools4Wisdom planners before. They come with these great planning tools, such as goal setting tools and mindmaps to figure out where you want to be. The paper is lovely.

There is a month at a glance, a week on two pages horizontally, and places to write notes. Each day has time in half hour increments from 5 am to 11 pm, plus a space for priorities (to do) and secondary to dos. Saturday and Sunday don't have the full day (7 am to 7pm) and no place for to do's. This is undated and you could start it at any time during the year.

My big negative on this book is that the pages are perforated and can be torn out, which might be nice. But they are already coming out. I've previously purchased the spiral bound versions and never had this problem. It is such a pretty cover with gold edged pages that having the pages come out is kind of ruining it.

title: Fun!
text: I like journal/scrapbooking and these are great for that.  There is plenty of space to write on the back if you want.  They are also fun little post cards with a vintage-y vibe.  Partially colored, partially sepia shaded like an old photograph.  Pictures include the Eiffel Tower, the Roman Coliseum, the Brooklyn Bridge(?), Central Park, the old pic of the guys building the Empire State building sitting along a beam, and an old 60's Volkswagen Van.

title: Perfect
text:
These are what I think of when I want classification folders. The folders are very heavy cardstock and aren't going to collapse when you put a lot of papers in it. Nice and solid.

The only thing I miss are the metal clasps that used to come with these. I haven't found them separately yet, and they really help keep the papers on the prongs. But maybe they aren't making them anymore.

title: Great stickers for your Bullet Journal
text:
I do a month at a glance, week at a glance and daily comments in my planner. It isn't really a bullet journal because I don't really follow the rules for that. But I draw everything out in my dot grid planner. So the tabs were perfect for locating the months and on the first of the daily sections for each month, I used a little month at a glance tab.

I like how easy they are to place. I also liked all the little stickers that come with this set. I am trying very hard to use them rather than hoard them, like I usually do.

title: Great little whiteboard
text:
So I got this to use in my craft room. I figure it was a good size to use to keep track of things. in a visible way. Also for planning projects. I came in a good size box with every thing you need to put it together. It went together fairly easy for me. I am fairly good at assembling things, so maybe not as easy of you are used to it? I did mess up on one side - realized I flipped the leg when the screw holes for the tray were wrong, but it was easy to fix. It is very sturdy once done, rolls around easily and is magnetic. Or at least magnets stick to it.

So far, it cleans well using dry erase markers.

title: Pretty
text:
I have various types of these magazine holders, some heavy duty and some not. These are not heavy duty. They are more for items that you won't be accessing a lot. However, I would say the price is consistent with the quality. My rating is based on the price and that they are not heavy duty holders, so I'm not expecting much. If you need something that will get a lot of use and isn't just for pretty storage, I wouldn't buy these.

On the plus side, they do look good on the shelf. They hold a good amount of magazines. They will not hold really large magazines, for example, Oprah's magazine barely fit. But if you are using them to hold notebooks or things like that, anything 11 by 8.5 inches should fit without a problem. I will probably store my old journals and planners in them.

title: nice desk calendar
text:
This is a nice and colorful monthly calendar meant to lay on your desk. I like these to take notes when working or on the phone, though sometimes things get piled on it. Who am I kidding, things always get piled on it. It is not my main calendar, but it is easier to write on it than on a hanging calendar.

You do have to rip the pages off when you are done, so if you want to keep them as records, you will need to find a way to do it. It is like a pad, but because the calendar paper is heavier than normal pad paper, it doesn't easily fold under. I ended up ripping the pages off. I will probably copy important information elsewhere.

title: concerned about the shank
text:
This is a great idea for keeping a spare key available, especially if you are needing to leave it for someone. It was easy to change the combination, so if you give it to someone for a specific reason, you can change the combination right after. And frankly, after locking myself out of the house when my car decided to lock on me with the keys inside (battery died in the key fob), I really am looking for a safe way to have a spare key outside somewhere.

My only concern is that the shank, which is covered in vinyl, seems like it may be easy for a bolt cutter to cut it. They would still have to force it open to get the key out. I'm not sure this is a good idea for a long term solution for a spare key.

title: Like the idea of this
text:
I really like the idea of this planner. And I may end up using it more for work. For a personal planner, I need more room for daily notes. This is really just a monthly/weekly planner. Plus it is large. Great for a desktop planner, not so great for something to throw in your bag. I like the initial planning pages. It helps you set your goals for the year.

Generally, it came down to size for me.

title: fun colors
text: Okay, they are post-its.  I don't know that they are stickier than the other post-its I've bought.  but the colors are great and if you are using them for organizing or a project, you will be able to easily see what you are organizing if you do it by color..  Great for visual people.  They do stick and come off, like your normal post-it notes.

title: Dressy but sturdy
text: These clip on to your clothes and have a pull out fishing line type cable that pulls out and goes back in very smoothly.  Great for ID's that you need to swipe to get in to a room.  Very pretty.  Two things that bother me a bit, the hook/clip back means you need a pocket or something to clip it onto, and because of the weight of the decorative "broach", if what you clip it onto is not heavy or reinforced, it may drag it down.  Otherwise it is great.  It didn't make the fabric flip when I put it on, just pulled it down.

title: great sheet protectors
text: Not sure what there is to say other than they are well made and don't look like they will fall apart in normal use and probably even heavy use.  Usually you put a paper you want to protect in it and all the pressure is on the holes section, which are heavy duty.  If you are putting stuff in and out of them, they will last well, but maybe not as long as if you just put it in there an leave it, if that makes sense.

title: Lightweight
text: Very lightweight folders.  Normally this type of folder will get a lot of use and needs to be heavyweight.  If it's not for heavy use, they are fine and you can save your money not buying the expensive heavyweight folders.  I like the bright colors better than the ugly colors the heavyweight folders come in.

title: Fat markers
text:
These chalk markers work okay. You have to hold in the tip to get the chalk flowing, which gets it all over your finger. Unless you wait until the tip is fully inked, it doesn't work well.

Once the tip is inked, it doesn't do thin lines well, so these are great for larger boards. Thi chisel tips do fat lines well. It stays on well and washes off with water. The color selection is good.

title: Great journal
text: Really nice looking journal with handmade paper.  I love these journals. They look and feel great and you just want to write something great in them.  The size is perfect for throwing in a purse or backpack.

title: Thin cardstock
