text: These are thin cardstock cards.  I really don't think they make heavy cardstock index cards anymore.  So really, for the price, these work.

title: Cute Christmas cards
text: Cute cards for Christmas.  Nice because they aren't over-sized so the take normal postage.

title: Pretty colors
text: It's a paper pad.  Pretty colors.  Nicely made.  Not much more to say.

title: Lightweight Folders
text: These are inexpensive lightweight file folders in a nice bright red.  But like all the current folders, they are very flimsy compared to the folders we used to get that lasted years.  These will be fine for filing papers away when you don't need to access them a lot.  I don't think they will hold up to heavy use.

title: Lightweight
text: These are basic lightweight file folders.  They don't seem to really make the old heavy duty type anymore.  I think they are best used for files that don't get a lot of heavy use as I have cardstock that is heavier.

title: Still heavy duty
text: I guess you could buy the stick on fasteners and make your own for less.  But these are made of much heavier cardstock that most manila folders.  I was actually expecting these to have dropped in quality based on the drop in quality of manila folders.  (they used to be much heavier weight)  But they are just as sturdy as the ones I bought 15 years ago.  They don't seem to come with the fastener holders anymore though, so you can't really fill them full and expect them to hold the paper.  But overall, I think they will work well for my office.

title: Scanner is fast, provided wrong cable
text:
Initial set up was an issue. Not because it was difficult to do. No, that was easy. The problem was they gave me a USB 2 cable to use. However, the connection is a USB 3 (b) connection. I don't have any spare cables. So now one of my hard drives is missing a cable.

Overall, this is a decent scanner though a little pricey. And, I haven't downloaded the program that comes with it because I can't figure out which will work better and they only allow you one of the two options. So I used the Adobe Acrobat that originally came with my Fujitsu. The first item I scanned - a technical magazine from a pile I've been trying to scan so I can get rid of the clutter. I did it in two batches even though, per the specs, I could have done it in one, as the total pages was 100 double sided or 50 pages. It worked pretty well. A couple of pages went through together, but it wasn't a large amount. And it definitely works better than the Epson scanner my work provides to me (which also only scans one side).

So Pros - it scans very fast to the point my computer program crashed. Well, that might be a con. But it is fast. The result is very clear and overall I am happy with it.

Cons are the lack of a proper cable and the issue with the provided programs not being very clear as to what they do. Or maybe I just don't speak scanner enough to understand what I want.

title: Nice ink
text: I really like the color of these ink cartridges. I got the brown and it is a light sepia color.  So far, they are working great.  The last set of Jinhao I got never quite work well.  I ended up throwing some away.  Now granted, for the price, they are still cheaper than the competition even if you toss half.  I'm using them in my Dryden pen and it is very smooth writing without any blotches during normal writing.  I will buy this again.

title: cute for what it is
text: okay, this is a cheap kids metal pencil box.  I got it to keep my paint pens in because the ziploc bag I was using was getting annoying.  And frankly, it looked bad.  This is cute and silly. But it does the job and fits a good amount of my taller pens.  The metal is heavier than I expected it to be and so far it seems to be holding up well.  Of course, I'm not a kid dragging it to school everyday.

title: Non-standard ink cartridge
text:
It is a very nice looking pen with a heavy weight but comfortable feel. However, that is about all the review I can give it at this time. It comes with a re-inker cartridge that broke before I could even fill it. (the plunger won't move) The description states it takes standard international cartridges but that they have to be .10 inches (2.6 mm) Okay. I have standard international ink cartridges from a lot of different manufacturers (Pilot, Waterman, Jinhao, etc...) that I have bought here on Amazon. None of them work. I can't find any that say they are that specific size. The pen is basically useless if it can't take a standard size cartridge. It is just a pretty paperweight. If I can find some cartridges that work, and I like how it writes, I will change my review. But right now, 2 stars is pushing it.

I received a free product in exchange for my honest review.

title: Decent planner
text:
Okay, I just started using this in July. It has a lot of cool planner tools at the beginning but really? I don't have any real 3 year goals at this time. Vision boards don't really work for me, or my house would be spotless by now and I would be skinny again. But I do like that it has a monthly calendar, a place for monthly notes after, a week at a glance, weekly to do lists and habit trackers. It is enough for a year. I would like more daily pages, though I guess it would be huge then.

I haven't quite found "planner peace" with this, but it is getting there. It is a little large to fit in my purse, but is a perfect size for a desk planner. I can't fit a lot in each day. Somedays it all fits in the rectangle day box, but others, my to do list is too long and there is little space for notes. I do love the color (turquoise) and the paper (does not bleed with fountain pen or watercolor (though the pages do crinkle when they dry)

title: Not what I was expecting
text: Some are great, some are just ugly.  I think I may like half of them.  I think I was expecting something more like the cover. Although a few might be similar,  most are okay and some are downright ugly to me.  I was planning on using them as journal cards in a botanical journal but they are too "artsy"? Sorry, blanking on what style to call it. Modern? Like navy blue flowers/shadows of flowers on white. I wanted "pretty"

title: Great ink
text: Love this ink!  It is very smooth and lasts well.  It looks like a nice sepia color if you're looking for a antique kind of ink.

title: Nice blank notebooks.
text: Nice blank paper ivory colored.  I made a grid out of black fine line felt pen that shows through enough to use as a guideline.  My Coleto ghosts a bit, as does my fountain pen. It is not enough to be a problem.  My brush pens bleed through, mostly the darker colors.  The paper has a very nice feel.  For the price, I would recommend it especially for TN’s.

title: Great pen
text:
So far, I am loving this pen. The tip is a little strange looking, but it works great. Nice flow even after hanging on the side of my notebook all night. My Pilot Metropolitan won't write unless I leave it point down in a container. So this makes me happy. The cap stays attached as you write, which has been a problem for me with other pens. And it has a nice weight to it.

The minus 1 start is because the pen itself is an enameled green, not a metallic like in the picture. I really loved the color in the picture. It actually is probably a minus half star, but they don't do half stars here.

title: Ink flow is bad
text:
Pretty pen but works worse than the cheap jihao ones I have. Although there is in in the tube, it is acting like it is dry. I had to rinse out the nib before it would work the first time, even after leaving it tip down in a holder for 2 days.

When it writes, it is really nice. I ordered more ink to see if maybe it was just this ink that came with the pen. I don't remember having this much problems trying to get fountain pens to work when I was a kid.

title: So pretty
text:
I really love this pen. Such a pretty print and 4 colors in one, though you have to buy the ink refills. I have the fine tipped pens in it, which I love.

I'd buy it again if I lost it. That might be the only reason I would need to.

title: Nice paper
text:
I love Tomoe River paper because though it is thin, it has no real bleed through. There is some shadowing. But best of all, if you like to watercolor your pages, it doesn't show through, and I have found less shadowing when writing over the watercolor background. The only con if you are a bullet journaler is that the pages aren't numbered. I don't really care, I just number as I have time.

Would buy again

title: It does work once you figure it out
text:
The instructions that come with this don't work. I followed them and came up with a mess. So then I experimented a bit and finally got it to work. It says it will make bigger envelopes, but I'm not sure how it will work because one of the things it does is score a line to fold, but the base for scoring is too small.

Despite all this, once I figured it out, it did make good envelopes. I recommend also getting a corner cutter. The rounded edges make a prettier envelope.

title: Pretty but not very useful
text: It would be a really pretty pen, but the feather ends up sideways and it kind of in the way when you hold the pen.  It does write well or at least the couple of tips I tried wrote well.

title: Good set of pens
text:
I got this set from Spot the Deal and received all 4 unlike prior shipments that were only one pen. I include this here only because there are multiple sellers with this same product and I am not sure how the reviews work for specific products/sellers or if they lump them together.

I like these pens generally. Getting used to how they work takes a bit of practice. Different angles change how they write. I think for most calligraphy uses, the 2.4 is perfect. The 1.5 is a little thin and the normal thicker down stroke is not very thick. The 3.8 sometimes turns into a black blob if you aren't careful, though it may work well for larger writing. That said, if you write really large or need to do something like a poster, the 6.0 will be perfect.

The biggest con on these pens is the cap. It screws on, which is good. However, once you remove it, there is no place to put it. The design of the barrel, though comfortable to write with, doesn't allow you to put the cap on the end. So it just hangs around loose. There is no clip on the cap to clip it anywhere and I can see me losing it at some point.

title: don't waste your money
text: Never worked properly.  The ink is there, but doesn't come out into the pen even leaving the pen nib down overnight after putting it in the pen.  Waste of money. I do like the Jinhao pens I have, but the ink is awful.

title: Great value
text:
As a journal, this is great. The paper is thick and there is no ghosting. However, if you are like me and like to put a wash of watercolor behind your writing, make sure you are pages ahead in your journal. I did a wash on an empty page that had writing on the prior page and it bled through badly. Additionally, the prior page was messed up. And this was with my waterproof micron pens. I do not have this problem in my Stalogy journal. The only time I've had an issue with watercolors and my Stalogy is when I use non-waterproof ink. And then it doesn't leak through from the prior page.

If you don't watercolor, however, this is a great journal for a great price. Fits in B6 travelers notebooks and makes a great bullet journal.

title: Hard to open
text: The idea of this is great.  But out of the 3 pens only one stays open without a lot of work.  You have to push back the tip cover and try to snap it into an open position to write.  You press a button to release to close it.  If you are using these because you have hand trouble, having to fight to get it to stay open does not help your hand pain.  Once you get it to stay open, the pen works well.

title: Great weight and texture
text: Great paper.  Nice weight and texture.  I use it to make my own travelers notebook inserts and planner pages  It prints well.

title: It is good.
text: The color is similar to a manila folder.  And the weight is pretty similar too.  Very smooth surface, which is not like my manila folders. Otherwise, it is basic cardstock.  I keep looking for some with more of a linen/cotton feel.  This reminds me more of cheap cards than of nice cards. But then, this wasn't expensive, so I guess you get what you pay for.  It will work for crafting.  And it should print very nicely in the printer.

title: Arrived damaged.
text: This paper on it's own is great.  It has a nice weight and is the right size. It has a nice smooth finish.  However, the package arrived open.  as in totally, falling apart, open in the box.  And since the cat treats also fell out of their packaging, it had some spots on it from the cat treats.  I find with Amazon, half of the paper I order comes in damaged. Since I am using it for crafting purposes and not for business where every sheet needs to be perfect, it is not worth sending it back.  But I might go elsewhere for paper if you need the whole ream, because this is not acceptable.

title: Doesn't stamp well easily
text:
I like the idea of this and maybe it just takes practice, but I haven't gotten a clean stamp out of it yet. Mostly I get the word and the year. If I press harder, I get more but I also get the edges.

This may not be a problem for the stamping experts, but it's not so good for newbies like me.

title: Perfect for what I wanted
text: I've bought a number of colored fine point pens for journaling. I love the fine points and colors but hate that they are so skinny making them hard to grip for any length of time. So these to the rescue. They fit perfectly and the make the grip more comfortable and are a great price.

title: Package damaged otherwise good for what it is
text:
So, based on prior reviews, it wasn't unexpected that the package arrived damaged. It wasn't damaged by shipping because nothing else in the box was damaged. So either the Amazon pickers damage it, or the packaging was damaged by the company sending to Amazon and they are doing the best they can with what they are being given. Either way, for the price, I get enough undamaged sheets to make it worth the price to keep it. I lost about 15 pages that were damaged on the corners. This is the minus 2 stars.

The paper is very smooth and heavier than standard copy paper. I tried a sharpie, a felt pen and a regular ballpoint pen. All dried quickly even though the felt pen looked a little wet still. None smeared. None of the ink could be seen through on the other side. I don't have ink in my cartridge pen or I would test it. This is the main reason for buying this paper. The last paper I bought was 20 lb and everything showed through. Even pencil. I'm using this for planner pages and I like using color pens to make seeing things easier. This should work.

It feels like it has a shiny coat on it and should print nice pictures. I will have to test it out later

title: Not as nice as 24 lb but acceptable for general use
text:
This is 20 lb paper, which is the same weight as cheap copy paper. However, the cotton content saves it from being awful. It will work for what I am planning on using it for. However, I really prefer their 24 lb product better. I just couldn't find it in the legal size when I bought this. It is not perfectly smooth like copy paper (because of the cotton content) but also not as textured as their linen type paper. It would be good for general business use.

Downgraded to 3 stars. Anything more than a ballpoint pen bleeds through. And truthfully, I can see the ghost of the ballpoint pen through this. Very disappointed.

title: Nice leather, good size
text:
So I bought this one and a passport size TN. I got the passport size first and have been trying it out. So this one is just waiting right now.

It is beautiful leather. I really like the feel of it. There are 3 notebooks inside. Based on my experience with the passport size, any more than 3 notebooks and maybe a folder or two will be too much. So if you like a chunky TN with lots of notebooks, this won't work. I really like the passport size because it fits in my purse easily. But the pages are a little small. So I may be moving to this TN soon. It is a good size for notes and journaling.

The only concern may be the size of the inserts which are 6.5 by 3.75 inches. This seems to be an odd size if you don;t make your own. Otherwise, I guess you can get the next size and cut them down.

title: Arrived damaged.
text: Paper package arrived damaged.  The shipping box was fine.  Nothing else in the box was damaged.  It was like the glue holding the package together just gave up the ghost.  It looks like all the paper is there and only a few sheets are actually damaged, so it is not worth returning,  However, I probably won't buy this again. The paper itself appears to be decent paper and the only reason I'm giving this 2 stars.

title: Very nice
text: I really love this book. The size is perfect for a purse. The leather has a nice feel. The embossing is beautiful. The color is a deep purple. It holds 3 small notebooks that are around 64 pages. It is the passport size for new notebooks.  It makes a nice little journal or to do list holder. It may be a little bit small for a day planner, but that depends on how small you write and how much you need to write/track.

title: Pretty but thin paper
text: The doors are very pretty. However, the paper is just too thin to hang. The holes have already ripped through for the cover and January. I'm using a binder clip now, which works.

title: Good ink
text:
I really like this ink. It took a bit of experimentation, practice and a few YouTube videos to figure out how to fill my pens. I think the problems I had was more with the pens than the ink. I definitely made a big mess the first couple times. I also bought some of those refill inks. The refill inks are so much easier and cleaner to load. BUT, I can't actually get the pens to write. This ink, however, wrote great right from the start. Even when all I could get in was a little bit. It is a nice green. Though sometimes is is almost black when I first start writing.

I just wish they had other colors.

title: Nice pen but the refillable ink cartridge won't fill
text:
So this is a nice looking pen. It writes very smoothly. I used Pelican ink on this one. I am kind of new to fancier fountain pens. I grew up with the classic cartridge style that tended to pool ink and just be messy. The point is fine or at least it is writing with a fine line with the Pelican ink.

The wood looks a little on the fake side. But what do I expect for this price.

The other negative which is what dropped my stars to three was that I couldn't get the plunger cartridge thing to fill. I followed the directions on YouTube that worked great on another pen by a different manufacturer. I could not get any of the Jinhao pens to work. It is funny, but they did get a little ink into them, but not enough to write a lot. Just enough to test the pen. I'll try again when the ink runs out and see if I can get it reseated. But I really pushed it in and it seems to be solidly in there. So it is something wrong with the actual plunger seal, since there isn't enough vacuum to suck up the ink.

title: Nice ink
text:
I'm having some issues and I can't tell if it is the pens (which are admittedly cheap). The plunger things don't seem to be sucking in any of the ink. But the ink that did get in writes smoothly and for the most part, doesn't show through the page. I have one planner that the ink shows through on. The only other issue, which may be pen related, is that the ink is very dark until you write and get "fresh" ink. So it doesn't look as purple as I would like.

The pen I put it in (a pretty Jinhao from China) has a fine point nub and the ink doesn't puddle and is really nice and smooth.

title: Decorative and heavy.  Great gift.
text:
I got this for my high school age son as a clever and decorative alternative to the standard Periodic Table. When we received it, the rist thing I noticed was the weight of the unit. I was actually bigger and more substantial than I had suspected, even thought the dimensions are plainly called out in the desctiption. While I had focused on the main dimensions of 8.2X5.5" length and height, I hadn't really given thought to the 1" thickness.

I already had a 6X4.5" version of this without a base and loved it, but while the overall dimensions of this unit may not seem like a lot more, trust me, it is huge compared to the smaller one. The addition of the lighted base makes a huge difference as well. Keep in mind, in we lit areas, it still looks as good or better without the light since the graphics are all in black.

This item makes a great display and is a great conversation starter. It looks great and surprisingly fits in most decor situations.

This includes 83 of the actual elements of the table including most of the gases. Obviously, the vast majority of radioactive elements are not included, but are represented with the typical Radioactive symbol. The base, while functional, is not overly decorative itself. Simple unfinished design, but the acrylic fits quite snugly and there's no chance of it just falling out. The light is powered by a 36" standard USB cable that is permanently attached to the base with an on/off switch in the center of the cord.

Overall, we are quite happy with this item. The price may seem a bit high to some, but I think considering all of the included elements as well as the sheer volume of the monolithic acrylic enclosure, it's not out of line at all.

title: Great Sub Ink Set
text: This ink set was one of the first I tried.  I had several I needed to try and review in a timely manner, but this was one of the first I decided to try.  Easy to load as it doesn't need a syringe, the print quality is great with bright vivid colors and the price is absolutely spot-on.  One of the great things about this ink, is that it currently is part of the subscribe and save, so you don't have to remember to order ink before you run out, just set your order frequency based on your usage and you are good to go.  As most people who work with sub inks, you know that the ink yields a ton of work and so you don't have to replace the ink as often as you do with inkjet, but one of the things you will also know is that it is important to grab inks that have less tendency to glob up and create havoc in your printer. It's not just the print quality you have to focus on, it's also how well the ink is made with pure ingredients that are non-toxic and safe to use.  This brand absolutely meets those standards and I had zero issues with clogging in the machine.  I would buy this brand again without hesitation and I hope this review is helpful!

title: A Deal Of The Day That Was Absolute Junk
text: These thing is an absolute joke.  I can't say that the price is bad, but when you feel like you have absolutely been ripped off, there is no value in that.  Right out of the box, you have to put the cutters in the slots yourself by tearing off the adhesive backing, simple enough, right?  Not so much.  They refused to stay stuck in there and the fit wasn't ideal to begin with.  I ended up using my hot glue gun because I truly wanted to give this thing a try and I really wanted it to work because the idea is great and I needed it to fit in my life to save me time and effort and I needed something like this so that it would be easier for my kids to use without the risk of cutting themselves on the original packaging cutter that comes with the aluminum or the plastic wrap.  So I was really optimistic and I really wanted this to work, and after hotgluing the strips so that they would actually stay put, I got our aluminum roll in there and a roll of the plastic cling wrap in there.  I tried the slider and it literally crumbled up my aluminum and absolutely would not cut it.  I checked to make sure there was an actual cutting blade under the blue plastic slider and there appears to be one there but it absolutely does not work.  The wood case itself is super cheap too.  I hate giving bad or negative reviews, it irritates me to have to do that, but getting a piece of junk irritates me even more, especially if it's a great idea and something that would give me some practical use that I would use all of the time.  It's just very disappointing to say the least.  I would suggest they go back to scratch and work out a way to have this be more sturdy, with the sliders pre-assembled into their slots for a better, more permanent fit and try again.  I hope this review is helpful to the company to maybe try again for a better product because the idea is fantastic and I hope the review helps people to steer clear of this one until they can improve on the design and functionality.

Also, it would be nice to have a pad I can haul around with me to the other chairs I have to sit in when working on other projects.  I seriously thought with the design of this cushion and the fact that it is made of gel, it would provide that comfort for prolonged sitting.  However, I am really disappointed in the fact that it is actually more discomforting than the chair itself.  I can't sit on it for more than 30-45 minutes without it bothering me and oddly, it makes my rear sweat, which it does not do when when I am just sitting in the chair itself.  You would think that the designed air flow it  has in it, this would not create this issue but, it does for me.  I have a rather "boney" rear-end, although I am not skinny, in any seating situation, whether it be on a bike on the floor or pretty much anywhere that isn't a couch or a bed, my tail bone does get bothered and painful which also leads to sciatica issues as well.  Hopefully I will be able to find a pad that works, so for personal experience only here, I can't confidently recommend this cushion.  It IS however, very durable.  One of our German/Aussie pups decided it would be a good idea to take off with it one day and use it as a chew toy, didn't work out too well for him.  There was no damage to the cushion or the covering, so there is something to be said for that. text:
Pretty sure one of the two signs I received was used. It had lots of scratches, and the protective plastic film had already been removed.

Specific concerns:
1) You MUST poke through your poster in order to get it to stay. You can't slide it in behind the cover.
2) This means the poster has to be perfectly straight. It is very challenging to attach.
3) The posters wrinkle behind the plastic. They are not weatherproof and do not create a seal around your poster.
4) Changing out posters is a pain. The plastic pieces that go through the poster break easily, and they did include a few extras, but I'm concerned that I'll have to replace those with every poster change.
5) They definitely need water or sand in order to stand up to wind. I saw reviews that said they were already heavy enough, put it my signs, and the wind knocked them down and scratched them.
6) The jumble sticker is impossible to remove, so it detracts from the poster message.
7) They're pretty tall, so my employees who are shorter struggle a bit to carry them easily.
8) When trying to open them, at least the first several times, it feels like you're going to break them. Thankfully, they don't break, but they're not super easy to pop open to stand up.

I had a family emergency and missed the deadline to return them, so I'm going to try to make them work until I can afford to buy something else.

title: Functional and Simple Planner
text:
Functional and simple customizable planner.

The planner is A5 size (8.3"Hx6"W) and comes with a nice faux leather cover. The cover is sturdy.

The planner is undated and meant to be filled in by the user. It starts with a contact page, then has a monthly spread followed by 5 weekly spreads. It then repeats. Theres a section on the month for notes and goals/improvements. The journal does start one Monday and end on Sunday which is preferable for me. On the weekly pages there is also a section for notes that has dots so you can even draw/doodle if you want. Theres icons for the weather on each day which I think is cute. There are goal and priority lists, work/personal to-do lists and habit/skill trackers. I like the separation between work and personal! There's also a section for journaling a little bit with "main win", "lessons learned" and "how to improve next week" There are also some blank bullet journaling pages in the back. It does come with stickers that have a month overview and tab . I ordered received this in November 2022 and the dates were from October 2022-March 2024 giving it a wide variety to start the journal with. However there isn't really a "spot" on the pages to put this and so you would have to cover up something on the page to use them. It also comes with a ribbon for page marking and a spot to hold a pen!

Overall I am pleased with this journal, it has good value for its money. I like that there are already some breakout boxes. I would love to be a person that could create her own BUJO but I just don't have the time. This will work perfectly for my for my everyday planner.

title: Variety Pack of Micron Pens
text:
Nice variety pack of "micron" pens. This pack provides a variety of sizes in the standard nib as well as few chisel tips and a brush tip pen. I do like the different variety of the sizes in the standard nib. I don't typically use chisel nibs. The brush tip pen was not a good quality - the brushes were separated and I was not able to use it like you should be able to with a brush pen.

The listing for the pens says "waterproof" but the pens themself say "water resistant". When testing the brush pen was certainly not waterproof but the smaller tips held up well to water. The pen is supposed to be archival as well, so will see how it lasts long term. The ink did dry quickly on paper and did not smear easily. They worked great in my art journal over acrylic paint and other inks.

Overall when comparing the standard nibs to the "Sakura Micron pens" I did not find a huge difference in quality and these are certainly cheaper. They have a decent amount of ink and we will see if they dry out quickly like the Sakura Micron pens have a tendency to do. I think these are a great addition to use in my art journal for a better price point!

title: Save Your Precious
text:
We have been laminating big time for well over a decade. It started out with a small laminator I got my wife when we needed to laminate for our school classrooms. We have been thru six or eight laminators since then. No matter what laminator you have though, the constant item that everyone needs is the lamination pouches. Numerous products out there. Fellowes is one of those quality sources.

Since we are both elementary school teachers, we need to laminate more things than the average person. We have come to understand the need for a 3mil, 5mil, and 7mil pouch. Most all laminators will handle the 3mil and 5mil sheets. We have one that does up to 7mil too.

Many things can be done on 3mil sheets, if the item is not heavily used. If you are going the have the student use the laminated item daily, then you should probably move up to the 5mil thickness. It will handle the wear and tear of use much better.

Fellowes always has quality products. I like the fact that you can buy 200 sheets at once. Most other companies only bundle 100 sheet packages. Since we really go through these sheets at a quick pace, this saves me the time to not have to order as often.

title: Works pretty well!
text: This is actually a pretty helpful little gadget! I often read during my lunch hour at work, so I will be eating with my right hand and trying to read with my left. This tool does help me to more easily grasp my book. I think it would be better if it was longer and clear (so you could see through to any covered up text), but I'm happy to have this. It would make a fun stocking stuffer for a reader!

title: Great pen with hard-to-find BOLD point!
text: I don't understand why so many people prefer fine ballpoint pens; I like a BOLD point, even bolder than "medium" width, which is usually 1 mm. These pens are available in the hard-to-find 1.4 mm size, which I love. They write cleanly and clearly, and they are comfortable to hold. Recommended for anyone who prefers a bolder point like I do!

title: Seems good at first, but ink doesn't last :(
text: I like a pen that writes with a strong, bold line. At first, I loved these, especially since they are capless (click-style) and have gel ink. However, I've found that the ink starts to give out with minimal usage. You can see from the photo I included that even though there is plenty of ink left in the pen cartridge, I can write more than one whole sentence before the ink starts to falter and give out completely! If I let the pen "rest" for awhile, it would start writing again, but the same problem would recur. Unfortunately I cannot recommend this product.

title: Hard to find refills
text: I use erasable pens for things like address books. These refills are hard to find, but they worked perfectly in my existing pens. I was glad to be able to reduce waste with this purchase.

title: So smooth - love these pens!
text: I am picky about pens. I *hate* a fine tip because I don't think they are very smooth. I decided to try this pen because of the thicker width, 1.2mm. The writing is SO smooth with this! I also believe this causes less hand fatigue when doing a lot of writing. Will definitely repurchase these.

title: Attractive and sturdy organizer
text:
I received this as a Christmas gift from my sister. I never felt the need for a planner this detailed before, but I recently stepping into a more administrative/supervisory role at work, and I was finding it difficult to keep track of everything.

What I like about this planner:
*The front cover is pretty, yet sturdy; both the front and back covers are plastic.
*There is a set of pockets on the inside behind the cover.
*There are both monthly and weekly views.
*In the weekly view, there is plenty of space for comments, notes, and whatever on the right-hand side.
*The wide spiral bound allows easy access and can hold a pen attached.

What could be better:
*It's too heavy, mainly due to the too many pages of notes in the back (50 total). I understand that they were trying to combine a planner and a notebook, but it doesn't really work. First, there is plenty of space on the weekly planning pages, so I almost never use the back. Second, when I do use the back, it is a pain to scroll between the current week and any additional notes I've taken. And third, the paper quality is very thick, which is a plus overall, but with the excess number of pages, it contributes to making this a bit heavy overall.
*It would be great if the weekly view had a small inset calendar featuring the upcoming month; this would make planning easier.

Overall I do really like this planner and would recommend it.

title: Nice quality mouse pad
text: Good mouse pad that is a bit larger, which is what I wanted. I would have liked it to be more "grippy" on the reverse, but overall, I am happy with it.

title: Very nice cards
text: I bought these to include as little notes in gifts, etc., and I am happy with them overall. These are the size of a standard business card and are of good quality, glossy on one side only. There appear to be 2 of each saying/message, and the ones pictured are what I received. I would recommend these.

title: Comfortable but difficult to position
text: Like many others, the pandemic led me to work from home. My home office setup did include an office chair, but not one that was very comfortable, and I was experiencing various aches and pains after sitting for long periods. I ordered both this cushion and other one, one with a dip in the center. I definitely prefer this cushion (I am sitting on it right now!). It is comfortable to sit on, and it does provide support. However, I find it difficult to position; it is constantly sliding around. Overall, I do find that having this cushion helps somewhat, but not as much as I had hoped.

title: Comfortable pen that generally writes well
text: I purchased these pens because I had a black BIC Velocity pen that I really liked.  Unfortunately, when I ordered the blue pens, I didn't realize that the black one I have is 1.6 mm with, and these blue pens are 1.0.  That was my mistake, as I prefer a thicker width, but I also honestly don't think that these pens write as smoothly.  Otherwise, they are generally comfortable to use.

title: Really cute mouse pad for a cheap price!
text: Like many, I am working remotely.  After purchasing a mouse for my laptop, I found that i needed a better surface, so I purchased this mouse pad.  I wanted something thin, and I loved the blue/green mandala pattern.  This is perfect!  It can be used vertically or horizontally - I do both.

title: Sturdy well made calendar
text: This calendar is just what I wanted.  I wanted lined blocks to use for appointments, which this has, along with moon phases.  I also wanted the a size that was small enough to use as a desk calendar.  This works on both counts.  I like that it has heavy quality paper and a sturdy cardboard backing.  The only thing that would have made it better (for me) would have been a clear plastic cover, but I just stick mine in a clear file folder.  Recommended as a simple, basic calendar.

title: Convenient and eco-friendly notebooks
text: These notebooks are the perfect size for recording my notes about yoga classes.  The recycled paper produces a smooth surface for ballpoint.  When I wrote on one side with a Sharpie, there was some bleed through, but I expect this of any standard paper.  I like the smaller (A5) size of these.  I think they would work to take notes for school, work, and as a journal, too.

title: Very cool idea but could be better quality
text:
This little set is intended for office decor. It could potentially make a nice gift for a secretary, co-worker, or supervisor, although I wish the quality had been better.

With this set, you receive a cardboard box designed to look like a frame. Behind the "frame," the box has space to hold the included 16 cards. The cards are double-sided, and they are printed to look like classic cross-stitch samplers but with pithy modern messages such as "meh," "whatever," and my personal favorite, "let me Google that for you." You can display any card that you choose, and the cards can easily be changed as often as you might like.

The cards themselves are a fairly substantial, thick, and coated to reduce dirt and wear; they seem like they would hold up well. The box is made out of similar material, but it feels much less substantial, with the front "frame" piece glued to the box. Also, although the box is designed to display the cards, it is not very stable in the portrait position and easily knocked over. The set is certainly nice for more information use/gift giving, but it could have been much better.

title: Pricey but pretty!
text: These tabs are so cute with the jewel-toned colors!  I like the clear section to write on.  They are thick, so very sturdy, and also seem very sticky.  I haven't yet tried reusing them over and over, but they seem like they would work for this.  The main down side to these tabs is that they are pretty pricey for what you get, so you may want to use sparingly.

title: Nice and smooth!
text: I can be picky about pens.  I generally prefer a thicker tip, 1mm or even more, but since I use red for more specialty writing, something a little finer is acceptable.  At .7mm, these are more in the medium-fine range.  I love that they are click style--no caps to lose!  They write smoothly and evenly, with no smudging, smearing, or transfer.  Definitely recommended!

title: Super cute quality card!
text: I have always loved the Hallmark "Shoebox" line, which offers amusing, whimsical graphics.  I order this card because I thought it would be perfect for my friend who 1) loves avocados and 2) fears aging (the sentiment inside says "being one day older only matters if you're an avocado").  The drawings are adorable, and the yellow envelope is a nice compliment.  Definitely recommended!

title: Good special use permanent marker
text:
I seem to have a collection of permanent markers that I use for various things. This one is specifically billed as being "multi-surface," or for use on such things as glass, wood, and mental. It is a bullet tip, which is correctly listed on the box, but the headline for the item description says "fine tip," which is incorrect.

I tried this marker on plastic and on wood. It wrote smoothly and evenly. It seemed to require a few seconds of drying time (less than 5), but after that, it was completely dry and smudge free. There is a bit more of strong odor as compared to other contemporary permanent markers. The one thing that could be better is this marker's performance on more traditional surfaces, such as paper and cardboard. On these materials, I thought that the marker dragged a bit. For specialty use, however, this a great product and I would recommend it.

title: Cute gimmicky bookmark
text: I was looking for a jokey gift to get my niece who likes piranhas, and this fit the bill.  There are three bookmarks that come on a flat sheet--you have to pop them out to use them.  They are cute and as pictured, but I would not that they are not a sturdy lamination like a driver's license; they are thin and rather flimsy.  Still, the bookmarks are cute with their unique design.

title: Convenient and compact little case, but can get bulky
text:
This thin wallet/case offers RFID blocking to prevent identity theft. I did not choose the wallet for this reason; rather, I wanted it to hold my work ID, which allows me to enter buildings. I was actually concerned that the RFID blocking might prevent me from keeping my ID in the case during building entry, but this has not been a problem.

The wallet comes with a strap for hanging around the neck, but I removed this and replaced with a key fob (it would have been nice if this had been included). This seems to be working well. Other than my ID, the only thing that I have added to this wallet is a total of 6 paper business cards. Unfortunately even this small amount has made the case a bit bulky, as you can see from the photos; I expect that this effect would be even more pronounced with credit cards or cash. But overall, I like this little wallet, and it works well enough for my purposes.

title: Cute design and high quality
text: I have purchased a number of these bookmarks from Peter Pauper Press.  They are very high quality, made of heavyweight cardstock and with the additional decor of beads/tassels.  This one is one of the funny ones but more serious/sentimental ones are available as well.  I purchased them for gifts and was able to find something for everyone!

title: A new version of the Sharpie in great colors
text:
I love my Sharpies! I use both the markers and the pens. These new "brush tip" Sharpies are described as pens, but I find them to be more of a cross between a pen and a marker. (See the product description for a comparison of different tip sizes.)

These are thin pens similar to the regular Sharpie pens. However, those pens have a fine point, where as these have the "brush" tip, more of a bullet-shaped tip. They can still be used for lettering--I think they would be perfect for creating labels for packages--but I won't use these like I would for a regular pen. I did try them on a thin piece of copy paper, and they didn't seem to bleed through, but I would still be a little wary. They could work for larger-scale (not detail) coloring projects.

Overall, another great product from Sharpie, with the best advantage of this pen being the unique variety of vibrant colors.

title: Attractive, high-quality card
text: This is a very high-quality card, made of thicker paper.  The envelope is also thick and foil-lined in gold for a nice effect.  The "Birthday Girl" lettering is raised, given the card a 3-D effect.  Overall, it is very attractive, and I plan to give it to my niece with a gift card later this month.  So why only 4 stars?  Honestly, even though the card is very nice, I would NOT pay full price for it; I just don't think that's a worthwhile expenditure for a disposable item such as this.

title: Good set of pencils for the price, although variety of colors could be better
text:
Like many adults, I have gotten into coloring as a form of relaxing; as a clinical psychologist, it's an activity I recommend to my clients as well. I have tried many different types of colored pencils, which are my preferred coloring implement. Overall, I found these to be very good, although not without a few down sides.

Here are the things I liked about these pencils:
*The pencils are pre-sharpened, allowing for immediate use.
*The pencils have flat sides (rather than being completely round), so they won't roll off your desk or table.
*The pencils are dual-sided, which is nice for travel (i.e., more colors with less pencils).
*The pencils generally perform well, with nice quality colors.

Here are the things I did not like as much:
*The colors are not labeled. Although each pencil is obviously a different color, the actual color name is not given, and it can be difficult to tell which color you are actually getting--is it the "red" or the "red brown"?
*The tips seem to wear down very quickly, even after coloring just small sections.
*The variety of colors could definitely be better. There are only two different blues (according to the product listing above, "Prussian Blue" and "Cerulean Blue"), and yet there are six shades of beige/brown!

If you are looking for an inexpensive, convenient set of colored pencils, this Paper Mate package is definitely a decent choice.

title: Comfortable, easy-to-use headset
text:
I have never used a telephone headset before, but I am in a position at work now where I am frequent doing telephone interviews and needing to use my computer at the same time. I was using the speaker option of my phone, but I felt like I was shouting, plus I was dealing with confidential information.

I decided on this headset because my work phone is a Cisco IP 7965. It was very simple to set up--there is a jack for the headset on the back of the phone, and I can keep it plugged in all the time. When I want to make a call using the headset, I push the "HEADSET" button that is on the front of my phone. Sound quality is generally good, but I took off one star because I have had some trouble hearing people on the other end, and there is no way to adjust this. Still, I am very happy with these headphones overall, so I would probably rate the about 4.5 stars.

title: So fun!
text: These "glitter" dividers are so much fun!  They just add a bit of interest.  I was a little worried that the "glitter" would be messy and flake off, but it's not like that at all--the glitter is embedded into the plastic coating of the divider, so no need to worry about it making a mess.  Plus, if you are not a glitter person, these dividers are reversible, with a more matte side opposite.  Like all of the newer divider products from Avery, they have large-size tabs; you can use the included tabs for labelling OR write on with a pen and erase later, no problem!  I definitely recommend these dividers, which are a bit of fun for both kids and adults alike.

title: Fun AND Functional!
text: What a neat idea--i.e., match the adult coloring trend to a useful product!  As a clinical psychologist, I often recommend coloring to my clients, and I've started to take the habit up for myself, although I never know what to do with my creations.  These folders solve that problem, as you can color the cute designs and still use the folders after.  The designs are fairly detailed, but not so intricate that they are frustrating to color.  As a bonus, they appear on BOTH sides of the folder.  There are 12 folders in all, with 3 of each of 4 designs:  1 circular shapes, 1 flowers, 1 plus the slogan "you are your only limit," and 1 graphical lines plus the slogan "give life meaning."  Overall, these are really cute, fun, and would make a great gift--definitely recommended!

title: Attractive, sturdy organizer that holds a lot
text: I was looking for a desk organizer that wouldn't take up a lot of space but would hold a lot.  This one does, plus it is attractive and sturdy.  My only complaint is that the tall compartments are actually a bit TOO tall--i.e., my pens don't reach out over the top, so I have to sort of reach into the organizer compartments to fish them out.  Luckily, this is a minor issue, and so overall, I would recommend this desk sorter.

title: Nice card for "girly" girls
text:
I have 9 nieces of varying ages, so that's what attracted me to this card. It sends a positive message about how girls "can do anything." It also includes one of the pink rubber bracelets that are so popular (although I'm not sure that the printed message, "Believe" is a good fit; perhaps "Believe in Yourself" would have been better).

I do wish that the card was a bit less gender stereotyped. I thought that one of my more "girly" nieces would like it, but not all of my nieces like pink! Also, although text ends by saying girls can be "even President," it starts with more stereotyped roles, mostly including performance and then going on to being a teacher. Where's astronaut, engineer, doctor? That's more along the lines of "anything" to me.

So, a quality card that's decent-looking, but could certainly be improved upon.

title: Nice brightly colored markers, but some usage issues
text:
NOTE: I received this chalk marker/calendar set free for review.

I recently moved to a new office, where I have several different white boards that I use for organization, publicity, and other purposes, so I was excited to try these markers. Also, my office has a chalkboard wall, so I was hopeful that these markers might work on my chalkboard as well even though I knew that there was a chance that the markers could stain chalkboard--which I find very odd since they are called "chalk" markers.

Unlike other white board markers, these markers are NOT ready to go when you receive them. They need to be "primed" by shaking them repeatedly and then pressing down on the tips until the ink starts to flow. This process took about a minute for each marker, which I found a bit annoying. I thought I would only have to do it once, but unfortunately, I found that for the most part, the markers would not work unless I shook AND pressed down on them every time I used them. Even so, I found that the writing tended to be uneven. (See attached photos; despite repeated attempts, I could not get the orange color to work, and I wound up throwing that maker away.)

On the plus side, the colors are nice and bright. Also, I did try them on my chalkboard, and they didn't stain (when removed with water; you can't just "wipe off" these markers), so that was good. However, another minus is that the marker tips are very easy to nick on the caps as you recap them, which means that although my markers are brand new, the tips are already looking ragged. (The set does come with two replacement tips.) The included wall calendar (it's 23" across, so much too large for a refrigerator) is a nice bonus, but you aren't likely to be able to use these markers to write much in the squares, which are just 3" x 2 1/2", so it's not very practical

All in all, this set is a really nice idea and I wanted to like it, but I found that it was just okay.

title: Attractive, easy-to-carry small notebook
text:
I've been collecting more blank journals lately. Although this is actually described as a "business notebook," I find it more akin to a journal, with the main difference being that it is quite thin. This does make it convenient for carrying around in a briefcase or other business bag. It is smaller than a regular notebook, yet I would say too large for most women's handbags (with the exception of larger oversized bags or totes).

This book has a very attractive, embossed floral deep rose-colored cover. It almost looks like leather; it's not, but it's quite sturdy. The pages inside are lined, with present date slashes on the top right corner of each page. The fact that this is not a spiral notebook means that it is smaller and easier to carry around, but it also means that the pages do not easily lie flat when you are writing on them. Also, the pages are not perforated, so the could not easily be torn out if one wanted to do so. Finally, this notebook includes only 48 double-sided sheets, so it's fairly pricey for the small size. Overall, however, it is a nice product.

title: Nice dry erase markers have added bonuses of being magnetic and including erasers
text:
My new office has several white boards (dry erase boards) for various programming and advertising purposes, so of which are magnetic. I always find it difficult pulling the dry erase markers in and out of the little clips attached to the white boards--half the time, the clip itself falls off, the board knocks down, etc. Having a marker that attaches to the boards magnetically makes things SO much easier.

The magnets on these are markers are fairly strong and work decently. I am not sure why they were made to be so narrow, however--I think that if they were wider, they would have worked even better. The markers themselves write well, although I think the idea of advertising them as having "3 widths" is somewhat overrated--yes, you can turn the marker to achieve different widths, but the line you will get is not nearly as distinct as what is pictured in the item description. Finally, I found that the eraser, which is just a small circle on the cap, worked better than I had expected, so this was a nice bonus.

So, overall, I like these dry erase markers, and I definitely would recommend them.

title: Very attractive little handmade travel journal!
text:
NOTE: I received a free sample of this journal for review.

I admit to having a bit of an obsession with journals, although the only time I actually DO any journaling is when I travel. Given that, however, I was eager to check out this travel journal by 7Felicity. When it arrived, I was surprised by its small size, but I shouldn't have been--it is described as a "pocket" journal, and that is in fact exactly what it is!

This adorable little journal offers a ton of options. It has an attractive leather cover with a self-fastener. Inside, there is a compass-like placeholder, a brass holder for keeping the pages down, two plastic inserts--one looks like it would hold mini photos, and the other has a zip top to catch mementos--and finally, four removable, refillable notebooks (actually, the fourth was included separate for me). I received one notebook with lined paper, one with craft-type brown paper, and two with ivory pages. They are secured with bungee-type cord, and there is an extra cord included. (I admit that when I removed two of the notebooks to rearrange them, I could not figure out how they were attached, as there was only two bungee cords but three notebooks; a short instructional sheet would have been helpful!)

This journal will certainly be an excellent little travel companion, and it would definitely make a wonderful gift as well. Highly recommended to anyone in search of a small, high-quality, attractive journal.

title: Love these!
text:
I have a tough time finding pens I like. Usually I prefer a thicker point, as I find that they write more smoothly. Sometimes I like a gel pen, although often, the barrel is too thick for my liking.

This Sharpie Pen is the ONLY fine point pen I have ever liked. It writes smoothly and perfectly every time--similar to a fine tip marker, except it doe snot run, bleed, or smear. Even on thin paper, I have never had these pens bleed over to the other side. The ink dries immediately, so there's no concern about the ink smudging.

Great for a wide variety of uses; highly recommended!

title: High quality journal with beautiful Curly Girl design
text:
I have been a long-time fan of Curly Girl, a line featuring beautiful original artwork combined with sayings for strong women. Some of the products can be a bit pricey, but when I needed a journal for my yoga teacher training program, I knew that I would treat myself to one from this line.

This is a gorgeous journal that is worth every penny! I love that it is spiral bound, and it has a substantial, quality cardboard cover featuring the Curly Girl design--this one is one of founder Leigh Standley's oldest ("She packed up her potential and all she had learned, grabbed a cute pair of shoes and headed out to change a few things"). The pages are lined and extra-thick--in fact, the ONLY downside I can find to this journal is that the pages are SO thick that sometimes they accidentally stick together. The journal is also a generous square size (7x7").

A final plus that sold me on this journal is that it is eco-friendly, made from recycled paper AND produced using wind power. I bought this for myself, but I would definitely consider purchasing another Curly Girl journal as a gift--highly recommended!

title: Heavyweight, attractive desk organizer
text:
NOTE: I received a free sample of this product for review.

The first thing I noticed upon receiving this desk organizer in the mail was how HEAVY the box it came in was! On the one hand, this organizer is significantly heavier and more sturdy than most comparable items, but on the other, because it is mesh, it is still quite easily maneuverable and certainly manageable despite the weight.

I brought this organizer to work with me me to use in my office, replacing another organizer that had only tray-type sections but no upright sections, which I thought I would be more useful. To me, the best thing about this organizer is that it is built UP--i.e., because the upright (vertical) slots are positioned OVER the horizontal ones (rather than next to them, as with many other products of this type), this organizer has a very small footprint and does not take up much desk space--this is crucial!

The only (small) complaint I have is that sometimes when I place things in the horizontal sections, they slide through the reverse side, as there is no back to the organizer; a small "lip" or something similar on the reverse might have been helpful. Overall, however, this is a high quality product, and I would recommend it.

title: Great for certain books
text: I have used this for both hardcover and paperback books. Books with 120 pages to 500 pages. No issues yet. The one thing I did notice is that if your book is a smaller book and has text that on the inside margins of the page is close to the spine, it won't work really well because the amount of weight/pressure needed would have to be pretty substantial. The designers had to pick a reasonable weight; the most 'bang for the buck'. There will be no one-size-fits-all for this unless you want something really heavy that will risk splitting or pulling pages from the spine. (Another reviewer listed a railroad spike. I wouldn't use that on small paperback books.)  So, for a small price, this is a good deal. When I use it, it is often when I am underlining various parts of text, so I have gotten in to a cadence of moving the weight around (sometimes more to the outside of a page to hold one side down, sometimes using it in a diagonal to read more before moving it. Also, sometimes I flip it upside down. Since it has a little grip, when I am reading something quicker, I find it moves easier while still holding the weight down. I like the black color since it doesn't distract my eye from reading. I'll be getting another one since my family member discovered it and likes it too.

title: Works as intended

However, this is not where these refills truly shine, as you can get comparable results from other competing brands. What has made these special for me is their resilience when exposed to air over time. Many parker pen designs (retractable tip versions) leave the tip of the pen constantly exposed to air, which in most cases tends to dry the ink out at the tip. This typically results in you having to scribble forcefully over some paper for a while until you can get past the dry ink. These, so far, resist that for weeks on end. title: lots of colors, all work well
text: This is a good value set of colorful markers. The variety is a plus. The pens themselves are super light--shockingly so actually, and comfortable to use even for extended time. The ink doesn't smudge or bleed through and you can layer one over the other.  The "fine" descriptions is correct, so you don't want to use them for large-scale coloring, more for sketching or fine detail. And the fine tips mean they're also good for text--not "superfine" but certainly sharp and precise enough to clearly write with. A good value.

title: good for speedy photo scans
text:
This is an excellent tool to add to your toolbox for saving old photos. It doesn't scan to the same quality as good photo scanners, and doesn't do slides or negatives, but if you have a lot of old photos and not everyone needs to be archive-quality, then this works great.

Pros: speed. If you want to have very low quality for saving/viewing digital copies, it will zip through a stack of dozens of photos very quickly. AS you scale up the dpi then it obviously slows down, but even the upper levels are surprisingly fast. I organized my photos into various categories of how good a quality I wanted, and then scanned accordingly. If I want top-notch quality I use my good flatbed photo scanner, if I want pretty good quality and something I can enlarge and edit, I used this one at a higher setting, and for those photos that are just "nice to have" and only had to be "good enough" to view on a screen, I used the second lowest setting

ability to handle photos: I noted some people had issues. I had no problems with artifacts in the photos themselves. As far as jams, I had only three out of hundreds of photo scans. All three were old photos. One was very thick, one was badly curved, and one had a rough, partly-torn back. All three went through fine individually with me just pressing a finger against it as it fed through. No major disasters, no major jams, not at all time-consuming

Ease of set-up: took a while for my Mac Airport to find it, several attempts, probably about ten minutes total. Once it connected though, it was smooth sailing. Instructions for usage are pretty simple and straightforward

Footprint: it takes up very little space which is nice.

I wouldn't use this as my sole scanner for old photos. But it's so much faster and so much more convenient to do stacks that I'm thrilled to have it for those "good enough" photos. Great scanners don't do you any good if you never use them because of how much time it would take.

title: writes as expected, erases better than expected
text: These serve well as basic pens. The ink flows pretty smoothly and generally evenly, though I notice that others have remarked about issues with that. I haven't found that using multiple test pens, but something to keep in mind. The color is a nice blue, vivid and bright. The pens are light and comfortable enough for long use. They're plastic so wouldn't say they "feel great" in the hand--I like a little bit of weight and solidity to my pens, but these are certainly good enough, just not my favorites or my preference.  The eraser works excellently, which hasn't often been my experience with erasable pens, making this a pleasant surprise.  So as writing instrument they're "good enough" and as erasable ones they're better than typical examples.

title: work well on dark items, Sharpie reputation and quality
text:
Really, you can't go wrong with Sharpies. At least, I haven't done so yet in several decades of using them to ID a whole bunch of things that regularly face the elements, like Frisbees, cleats, etc, amongst others. These seem to fall right into line. The one difference is the metallic coloring. The gold and silver both show up well on dark materials, so it's nice to have a better option as that was always a minor issue. The red is a basic Sharpie, less for dark backgrounds. And I'd call it more of a rust/maroon than a "red"

The points are typical Sharpie ones. In other words, they're fine for basic lettering on objects, etc. but not for fine lettering in small, constrained spaces. For those you want an ultra-fine (which I also recommend)

title: nice fine point, bit big
text: These pens have an excellent extra-fine point, which is certainly that--nice and thin and precise. Colors are sharp, vivid, and don't run, and the ink/pen glides smoothly and easily across the page.  The one complaint I have is that they are pretty bulky--thicker and a bit heavier than I prefer in a pen (more the thickness than the weight is the concern). So for me, they're not as comfortable as other good pens -- not enough to make me not use them, but I wouldn't purchase them again.  Fair to point out though that those with larger hands may not notice.

title: quick, effective, efficient
text: This is a nice sharpener that works quite well.  Seemed to charge quickly and I would imagine the charge lasts a while but can't tell yet.  As a sharpener it handles various types/sizes of pencils easily and brings them to a truly pointy--near dagger point--tip without any breakage or that annoying thing where it keeps grinding and grinding and you never see lead.  It's quick and quiet, and while not tiny has a relatively small footprint.  Recommended.

title: prints fast and clear, set up a bit of a pain
text:
Set-up
Came with image only instructions, which seemed minimalist past the point of customer service to me. I figured everything out, but a little bit of text wouldn't have hurt to make things go more smoothly and quickly.

I could not get the mobile app to work on either my iPhone or iPad in terms of setting it up. Once I switched to just using the keypad it was fine save for one issue (detailed below). Otherwise it went smoothly and connected easily and quickly to my home wifi.

That issue was an error message about the SMTP server. Eventually, going online, I found out it had to do with email and the fax and how to turn it off.

Size
It's bigger than even our biggest inkjet by a good margin. Twice as high as most of them, and 1 1/2 times our biggest. It can sit on a table, but I wouldn't put it on a desk I'm working at. I'd call it "manageable" size. We have it under a desk in a spare room so tucked out of sight. But if the desk was ever used, it'd be tough to find a place to put it where it wasn't at the least highly noticeable and at worst obtrusive. We might have cleared out some floor space in a closet I'm guessing. It certainly doesn't "blend in", but it's not massive or hulking.

Use
It was immediately recognized by all our sundry devices on the network--phones, laptops, tablets, desktops (all Apple products) and printed from all easily

Printing is super fast. I actually thought when the first sheet came out "Oh man, what went wrong" because it never crossed my mind it had actually printed a two-sided full-text document that quickly. We've had all inkjet in our house, so don't know if this is due to this particular machine or laser printers in general, but it certainly was a speed jump compared to our inkjet (which aren't ancient--the most recent is only a few months old)

Text was clear, dark, and precise

Good amount of paper

generally cheaper than inkjet based on design. We'll have to wait a while to update this on how long the the ink lasts in this particular device

Quiet

We'll use this as our "beast of burden" for text and major printing/copying (two teachers in the house) and reserve the inkjets for pictures/illustrations and for those times we're lazy and want to print just where we are sitting

So far we really like this save for the few blips on setting it up.

title: Small, easy set up, fast, Epson has been reliable for me over the years
text:
I've had good luck with Epson printers over many years now (we have several in the house and two in separate offices), and while I know some consider their ink pricey I've never noticed it being a major issue in comparison to other printers. This one, so far, continues Epson's quality, and if things change over usage time, I'll update.

Set-Up: Set up has always been a strength of Epson printers. From first ripping off of the tape on the shipping box to printing the first test pages was under 15 minutes. That includes unboxing, ensuring all the little blue tap has been removed from the printer itself, loading in the ink cartridges, letting the printer initialize them, and having it connect to our wi-fi network. About the only way it could have been easier if it had unboxed itself and walked up the stairs using its own mechanical legs.

It printed just fine one first tries via my MacBook Pro, my iPad, an iMac, and two iPhones (both on the network and direct). No problems at all. We're an Apple family obviously, so I can't speak to its ease of use with Windows. I did print of a USB though, again with no issues at all. And it scans to our laptop and desktop just fine (I haven't tested it on the iPad though I assume it won't be an issue there either)

The display is large, bright and clear and as always, easy to progress through to get to where you need to

The footprint is nicely small. We have it in a little cubby behind sliding doors under our bookshelf where it just has enough room to open the top high enough to install the ink. For so many features, and with an auto-feeder, the small size is greatly appreciated. The output tray automatically retracts and comes out, which makes it easier to keep in small spaces.

You can do some light editing just on the printer itself. Obviously using your device is going to be easier and more full-featured, and I doubt I'll get much use out of that, but I do think the rotate and resize options are pretty good basic ones to have available to someone without a computer.

Text quality is good, certainly on par with all the others. I'll update with photos later as that's a more involved process (not the printing but just getting good images to test with and good paper). It prints noticeably faster than my older Epsons, especially double-sided.

If you're planning on doing major printing/copying, you probably want to go up to the WorkForce (we have one that works great) just for durability and wear/tear. But otherwise this is a nice small home or small office usage printer that is unobtrusive, easy to set up, fast, and highly convenient thanks to its many ways of connecting to various devices, its features such as auto-feed and double-sided printing, and its ability to do some work even without a computer connected to it. I'll update photos and durability, but based on years of experience with more than a half-dozen Epsons, I imagine this is another winner

title: nice colors, moves easily, no splotching
text:
I’ve long been a fan of quality Pilot pens and these are just another example. They do exactly what you want a pen to do and don’t do the things you don’t want a pen to do. What more can you ask? A few specifics:

1) Colors are vibrant and distinctive (we get good multi-colored pens for grading purposes. These will work great)
2) The ink flows smoothly, steadily, and the pen moves smoothly on the page
3) There’s no smudging or splotching
4) The pens are quite comfortable in the hand
5) You get a lot of them
6) each nib is protected so it doesn’t dry out or get damaged in transport/packing (you remove the protection when you use each pen the first time)
7) The fine point is sharp enough for, well, fine work (for example, putting comments in between lines of text or in margin notes).

All around great pens!

title: conveniently sized, works as described, easy to use, quick, not too loud
text:
Right now it's a four only because I'm going to hold off giving it a five because it's always good to know about longevity. Otherwise:
Packaging: Came in a box that was easily opened and pretty much just the right size for what it contained. No real wasted space. All components were easy to remove and uncover/unwrap

"Assembly" I put this in air quotes because really, you can't call it assembly. The shredder comes in two pieces, the motor/blades inside the bin. You open the box, take the plastic off each component, put the motor/shredder on top, untwist the twisty tie holding the cord together, plug it in, and your good to go. From unboxing to shredding? About three minutes. Some of which was trying not to bang my head on my desk as I reached underneath and tried to find an empty outlet on my octopus.

Ease of use: There's a slot. Big paper goes in it. Machine goes whirr. Little paper falls like snow inside bin. I'm not sure how you could screw it up. Easy to use. (It does come with slim instructions if you need them)

Speed: shredded regular paper quickly, into small chunks that I'd feel secure about just tossing out.

Volume: I wouldn't call it "quiet", but it certainly isn't at an annoying or painful level of sound. It's about what one should/would expect for a machine that is chewing up a bunch of paper. It's noisy but not "loud" if that makes sense. It does go up a bit in volume, mostly in whiny volume, the more paper you add (i.e. shredding one sheet at a time versus six versus ten), but again, not horribly so. You could have a conversation over it without yelling, though it probably wouldn't be a pleasant conversation

Size: I love the size since it fit easily under the desk with enough space to lift the motor off (in other words, I don't have to slide it out to do so) and it's narrow enough to be unobtrusive, meaning I don't knee it or kick it as I'm working.

Durability: The motor/shredder component feels and looks hefty and durable, but really the only judge will be time. It certainly handled 10-sheet shredding as claimed, though as mentioned it will whine more noisily. The bin itself is light and easy to carry downstairs when full of paper.

Love the size, it's not overly noisy, very quick and convenient for its purpose. Like I said, the only reason I'm not giving it a five is because I can't judge its longevity yet. But so far very pleased with it.

title: Great product, nice colors, versatile

the markers themselves are thick. Not sure how comfortable they'd be for a small child, but for young teens or up they're fine in the hand. And if you're doing large poster-size writing, I think the larger markers actually are easier to use.

All in all, a great product for versatility, color, and I assume, quality/longevity

title: Solid, nice to look at, easy to put together
text:
This is a nice looking, easy to put together, and solidly built display. Specifics:

Packaging: Everything is nicely protected via styrofoam and plastic, with the wood pieces separated so as not rub against each other. Packaging was just the right size.

Assembly:

Total assembly time from opening the box to being done was 25 minutes

the only tool required is an allen wrench, which is included. Depending on how easily the screws go in, you might want a second allen wrench to keep the dowel steady as you tighten the other end (hard to hold onto the dowel tightly enough to keep it unmoving).

Assembly was easy and intuitive (i.e.--you could figure it out no problem even if they’d left out the instructions). Attach the bottom piece to one side piece. Insert the dowels into a recessed circle on the side piece, then use five screws to attach the dowels and side piece tightly (using the allen wrench to tighten the screws). Slide on the canvas. Align the other side piece with the dowels, use the remaining screws to attach. Finished.
Generally, it was very simple. More specifically:
1) Holes were all nicely aligned
2) 7 of the 10 screws went in easily with no problem at all. 3 of them got a bit harder at the 3/4 point and I found it difficult to tighten them because it was hard to get a good enough grip on the dowels to stop them from turning with the screw. I just used another allen wrench to “lock” the already screwed in side of the dowel and that worked fine. This was a minor issue--it wasn’t that the screws took a lot of effort to get in, just that as you turned it the dowel turned in your grip

Look. You can see the pics, but it looks quite nice. The feel is solid and sturdy, and the materials don’t feel cheap at all.Canvas is heavy and stitched well, so I can’t see it not holding up. The wood had no issues with splitting, chipping, etc. as I tightened even the tighter screws

Solid, nice to look at, easy to put together as the headline says

title: Not just another planner
text:
When I bought this I thought it was a planner with some extra space for lists, but I was pleasantly surprised when I received it. It helps you to look at the big picture of who you want to be and what you want to do with your life, and breaks that down into daily achievable steps to get you to your goal.

If you have something that you want to accomplish like lose wieght, start a business, write a novel, etc this book will definitely help break that monumental task into daily doable chores. At the end of the 90 days, I know I will know exactly what I accomplished because this tool is great for tracking your progress and holding you accountable.

The only things that would improve this tool for me are:
1) I would like a section in the front or the back where you can develop a central list of what you have accomplished over the 90 days.
2) The hourly planner needs to be longer. It goes from 5 am to 9:30pm. It needs to be from 4 am to midnight for the early risers and night owls.

I plan on buying one of these books per season. If you have a concrete goal that you are ready to finally achieve, this book will definitely help you check that box.
