text: I received the "classic" pack of American Greetings Premium Birthday Greeting Card Collection. You get eight beautiful cards - these are high quality and, while not as fancy as Papyrus, are reasonably impressive. I like them better than Hallmark Signature because they are subtle in their charms and not overdone. The only reason I may not use one or two is that the sayings inside each one are rather generic - they're made for almost anyone, so if you want something more personalized you'd have to go to Hallmark and get such a card. Otherwise these are great to have on hand.

title: Fun Card for Father's Day, with Some 3D Effects
text:
This is a two-dimensional card but it has raised printing for the dialogue balloons - "More Duct Tape, I Think it's Working" and "If Dad Had Been on Board". Glitter has been sprinkled on the waves and this makes the card sparkle in the light. Very nice touches for a card that pokes gentle fun at Dad for using duct tape on everything. Overall a fun card. Because of the humor, I really thought this was from the "Shoebox" line of Hallmark cards but it's actually "Fancy Schmancy" a new Hallmark card line that presumably has the irreverence of Shoebox with the bling of "Hallmark Signature."

The only thing that puzzled me was the price - there is no price on the back of the card, unlike other Hallmarks. This is good, because I always had to block out the price tag when I gave a Hallmark card to someone.

title: Great for Displays, Colorful and Eyecatching
text: Though aimed for children, these glitter, stick-on letters are great for any display. They are eye catching and the glitter doesn't rub off. Each letter is about four inches high and the pack includes numbers as well. My only critique is that I wish they included more duplicates of certain letters (like vowels) that you're likely to use repeatedly, since you have a limited supply. Overall I'm very pleased with it.

title: Great for Poster Displays
text: These are great for creating poster displays. The gold glitter is eyecatching while the black borders make the letters "pop out". The adhesive backing is a disadvantage only if you want to re-use the letters - once you've stuck these onto a posterboard, they're kind of hard to peel off. Otherwise these are great for displays.

title: Birthday Card with Nice Image of a Strong, Sassy Woman
text: This is a nice card for that sassy and wise girlfriend in your life. I chose to order this because it reminds your friend of what a strong woman she is and that age is just a number. The design is from the Mahogany line, usually associated with African Americans but actually applicable to people from all walks of life.

title: Teal and Silver Go Together Surprisingly Well in This well-Made Card
text:
Don't go by the photos - this much more impressive in person. The teal and silver color go together surprisingly well in this American Greetings Card. It's a little oversized in the way of pricier cards, which is great if you're making a statement, and of course one's anniversary is one of those times. The tiny cutouts within the two hearts give it a delicate, lace-like quality that would appeal to both sexes. The silver foil is shiny and eye-catching, and the sentiment is moving without being overstated.

Though I'm not a big fan of teal, the style and quality of this card won me over. The only other criticism I have is that, while appreciate the care that went into shipping this product (Amazon ships it in a larger bubble mailer), it can just as easily been packed with some cardboard in a tree-saving mailer.

title: Rich Hues of Green and Gold, Quality is Akin to Papyrus
text:
This is a high quality Xmas card that looks much better in person than online. I was surprised it was American Greetings - I associate this type of design with Papyrus (my favorite fancy card store). I also liked the addition of a plastic, 3D star on the top of the tree. The rich green and glossy gold hues mix together well. The sentiment inside is targeted toward friends rather than relatives, which is great if you want to get more personal. This is a good card to send if you want to impress your friends that you can afford high quality, well-made Xmas cards.

The only thing I didn't like was the excessive packaging - Amazon sent this in a huge, oversized padded envelope - for a card, I don't see why it couldn't have been simply packed with some cardboard and shipped inside a small cardboard mailer.

title: More Like an Oversized Binder with a Flap Rather Than a Real "Trapper Keeper"
text:
The design will please "Hello Kitty" fans but it's overpriced and I wouldn't call it a "Trapper Keeper". It's really more like your standard three-ring binder with two interior pockets and a snap clasp. When I think of a "trapper keeper", I think of a sturdy binder that's been laminated with a plastic cover, clearly defined tabs, and a Velcro snap.

Also, it's big - wider than your typical binder and will take up more space in a backpack. The flap feels flimsy though it does a good job of keeping papers in place. The problem is how it will hold up over time - it feels like it could tear at some point.

If I didn't know it was an official licensed product of "Hello Kitty," I would have sworn it was a knock-off. It's OK if you have low expectations, but it shouldn't have been called "trapper keeper" and the price is too high.

Once it goes into sleep (after ca. 1 minute) it becomes invisible on the network (status: offline) and it does not always wake up when materials are sent to print. I'd say it woke up about 20-30% of time and only on one PC, while other two would have documents piled up in queue with no printing - but the printer reported offline. I tried multiple things - USB or Ethernet to router, manual turning on, firmware tweaks (via Brother utility or web address) - NOTHING worked. The printer deep sleep (who invented it, by the way? Someone really challenged with voice of customer at Brother, apparently) makes it unusable when used as network printer. Ended up returning to Amazon.

For some reason I’ve always just attached a regular one with a magnet.
But I love that this one comes with a built in magnet.
The attached pencil is a nice touch, even though I prefer a pen - that’s an easy replacement!
The set is super sturdy on my fridge.
I don’t tend to look back on past months, so throwing away the previous month’s page isn’t an issue for me.
Having post its ready and available has been great.
The pages are thick enough that my marker doesn’t bleed through to the next month.

title: Easy to use
text:
These bin labels work great.
I like they look.
They slid over my fabric bags really well.
I have used some on plastic bins too.
They slide around on my acrylic bins more than I would like, but I’ve found I can just use chalk markers on them directly.
I’m really glad I bought them and they have helped keep my family more organized!

title: Organization!
text:
These bags are great and they have so many uses.
I can use them for travel, I love that they are semi transparent.
I can use them for vinyl pieces.
I have full sheets and I have scrap pieces.
I can store my HTV separate from my permanent.
They are easy to access and zip away.
I can label each bag.

title: Nice bag
text:
This is a really nice bag.
My only issue is that the zipper is a little loud/rough.
It seems cheaper than some of the other leather bags I’ve used.
The bag overall is great.

title: Great set of cards.
text:
These cards are really nice.
The messages are beautiful.
The cards are a little thinner than a Hallmark card from the Hallmark store, but not as thin as the ones at a drug store.

title: very unstable
text:
I got this to hold my Cricut Maker.
Sadly the top of the cart is a little too narrow for my machine.
The cart is very wobbly.
It does store a lot and the side attachments are nice.

title: Not cut the same.
text:
These card holders are really nice.
One thing I noticed with the card holders is that the card slot is not cut the same on each one.
One of them fits my cards and allows them to sort of angle back like I would expect.
The other one has the card slot a little smaller. The cards have to stand straight up.
I plan on using one for indoor events and the straight up one for outdoor events as my cards won’t be able to blow away if there is a strong wind!

title: Squeaky
text:
These markers are pretty noisy.
More noisy than the name brand markers.
But they work great!
They don’t smear.
They are well packaged.
They do have a scent while using, but it fades quickly.

title: Feels Weak
text:
These bookends are flimsy.
They are easy to bend when not holding books.
Once they are holding books, they do great.
I use these on top of a bookcase in my son’s room.
He has so many books we needed to start using the top of the book case for books also!
This does a good job at holding the books in place so they don’t fall down off the sides.

title: Not the most intuitive.
text:
I got this barcode scanner for personal use, not a business.
The gun works pretty good.
I did have some issues with the barcode numbers showing up correctly in Excel.
I was able to scan numbers into Word or Notepad or Forms without any issues.
The barcode scanner provides the number of the barcode and nothing else.
I love the small size of the scanner.
Some of the provided QR codes didn’t give the results I would have expected, but I was able to easily work around that.

title: Great for under 6’.
text:
This standing desk was easy to assemble. It included all the tools that were needed.
It took me about 20 minutes to assemble. The instructions are very clear.
The desk is easy to clean.
The desk is sturdy while using.
It’s a nice break from sitting down and working during my day.
I have enough room to work with my laptop, notebook and drink.
I’m 5’11”, I feel like this desk would be too short if I was any taller.
But it’s great for me.

title: Super cute!
text: This owl door stop was a perfect gift to my 12 year old niece that loves owls, but is starting to outgrow stuffed animals but still wants everything owls in her room. The wings are super soft and he is stable and holds the door open without tipping over or getting knocked over, does the job.

title: Cute!
text:
I’ve had other pop up cards that disconnect when opening.
This card doesn’t do that!
I did need to put push out the front of the tent when I first opened it.
A fun addition would to include stickers to add to the wooden post to have it say something specific to the sender/receiver.
The envelope is plain without and insert.

title: More like 11 Slots.
text:
This has 12 tabs.
11 of the tabs have a "private" blue pocket.
I wouldn't say this is for 13.
The way they get the 13 is by having the front and back area be for papers, but those areas are not private.
I use this for my girl scout troop.
I keep their health forms and permission slips in it for meetings and outings.
We have 11 girls in our troop so it works great.
Its important for me that their information isn't in a see thru area which is why the privacy blue area is so important to me.
I put each girl's name on a tab to keep it all separate and easy to find when/if needed.
I'm going buy a cricut and do some cool vinyl on it!

title: Smooth!
text:
I got this cart for hauling my materials - I'm a girl scout leader and we don't have a space where I can leave my materials every week, so I have to haul them back and forth between the meeting space and home.
This card is awesome!
I'm so glad I got it before the weather turned really cold as it saves me from having to make multiple trips to my car and the meeting space.
I can fit a TON of stuff in this cart.
Just last meeting we worked on tie dying shirts and I was able to get everything I needed into the cart!
Everything except the shirts - I could have if I hadn't pre washed them, they were all wet so I chose to use a tote to transport them instead of my cart!
I like this cart over the wagon style (that I've seen other leaders use) because I can easily lift the bags out (with stuff in them) and put them in my trunk.
Then I can fold down the cart and if I'm careful I can leave the stuff on the bottom of it and place it in my trunk as well!
With the wagon style everything has to get unloaded/reloaded each transfer.
I can even fit my kaper board on the side of the cart between the bags an the frame and it doesn't blow away!!!

title: LOVE
text:
Not only is this pen beautiful, its easy to hold.
The pen tip is AMAZING!
It writes super thin and smooth!
The ink container is very tight in the pen and doesn’t easily fall out.

title: Cuts a lot!
text:
This blade can cut cardboard!
It’s awesome!
I’ve been wanting one of these for 20 years and I’m not sure why it’s taken me so long to finally get one!
The only issue I have with this is that the guide is a flimsy plastic and isn’t as sturdy as I would like.
That being said, the first time I tried to move it, a plastic piece flew off of it. I’m not sure where it came from but maybe that is the reason it’s more flimsy than it should be or maybe that has nothing to do with the flimsy-ness.

title: Sleeves get little holes in them
text:
The sleeves get little holes in them if they are bent while loading and unloading or while using the rest of the sleeves, but not using all of them.
The sleeves are a lot thinner than I thought they would be.
Those little tears then become something that you can feel when the sleeves are then filled with their page(s).
The sleeves do not easily tear out of the cover, which is good, it has held up in that sense.
The pocket in the front is nice, it would almost be nice if there was another pocket in the rear or a small one for a business card somewhere.
The binder label is simple and holds on solid without looking rough around the edges after use.

title: Nice thick cover, binding is not weak
text:
The binding on this is solid, it doesn't bend like some other planners that I have had.
The cover is also nice and thick and makes it easy to use on the go without a hard surface to write on.
I like that this has a pocket in the back to insert loose papers.
I'm happy with this planner but think I'll get a bigger size for next year, but nothing wrong with this planner, I just think I'd like a little more room on the pages, but all the pages were perfect design function.

title: Perfect!
text:
I love how I can open the binding with just one hand and not have to do a top and bottom to open it.
It’s so easy to use!
I’m starting a Girl Scout troop this year and I need a binder but worry about germs.
This is the perfect binder for me!
It’s large and I can put sheets on the outside to identify it.
I’m so glad I don’t have to feel like I’m constantly needing to wipe down my binder!!!
This is a high quality binder that I would expect from Avery.

title: Hard to find a template
text:
I’m pretty impressed with this stickers.
I would’ve have thought that my a shiny sticker would have printed well on my but it does!
The labels don’t even smear when I’m pressing them onto the item after being printed.
My only issue with these label stickers is that I have a hard time finding a template that works properly.
I usually end up with 1/3 of the labels not printing properly.

title: slides easier then I thought it would
text: I have this on two-floor surfaces, a marble floor, and a linoleum floor. This two-pack was great because my marble floor is white and my linoleum floor is grey. The colors match really well.  The door stops work satisfactorily. They could be more aggressive in holding their spot. One spot is smooth and the other spot has lines on it. They slide with the wind and the door will sometimes be halfway shut from the wind and then finally hold its ground. I appreciate that my doors are no longer slamming shut from the wind when I have my windows open, but I also think the doorstops could do a better job and keep the door completely open.

title: perfect for a talent contest
text: My niece performed at an outdoor theatre for a talent contest and she didn't want her pages to flap. She used this with her pages slid inside and it was perfect. It was windy on stage because they had a large industrial fan blowing and this was able to keep the pages from flapping in the wind. It lied flat on the music sand and she was able to flip the pages easily and efficiantly as needed.

title: Nice thickness
text: These sheet protectors have a really nice thickness to them and they are easy to see through, easy to fill, and fit perfectly in a standard 3-ring binder. They are just as I expected, good quality sheet protectors and not disappointing at all.

title: Low odor and easy to clean
text:
These are good dry erase markers.
They are easy to erase and are don't transfer/accidentally erase too easily.
The color assortment was nice, and that is why we chose these. A lot of my daughter's favorite colors.
They are low odor, which is good, as some of them can be quite stinky upon opening and using.

title: Binding is lightweight metal, front cover is paper thin
text:
The wire binding arrived bent and had to be adjusted upon first use. I am not sure if I have gotten it in the right spot as it still doesn't open and close that smoothly.
The front cover is just a thin piece of paper so it doesn't have a nice solid book-like closing. Because of this, it is not something that you would want to take with you, it's more of a stay-on-the-counter type of planner.
I'm still trying to figure out exactly what I want in each section. I got this for a chore chart of sorts for my children. My goal was to put down what they needed to get done each week, what they need to do each day, etc.
I was writing this out on just a blank piece of paper and having it attached to a clipboard, but having something that could be found easier as it was its own thing seemed like the solution.
I like that the dates are not already on this planner so there is no wasted paper if I don't do a week, say during winter break.
I also like that I can include what activities are going on after school or if there are tests that week, I can include them on the page.
I wish the pages were also printed on the back as I feel like it is wasteful to only be printed on one side.
The paper thickness is satisfactory and not too thin, I was worried since the front cover was not thicker.
Overall, I like this weekly planner and I know that I could be using it for many different things, and might even find myself using some pages for meal planning, as I can see how it would work really good for that.

title: Doesn't tear up like my other one
text:
I had gotten a different pad early in the year and almost immediately it started tearing with my mouse.

This one has some scratches on it but nothing like the other one had at this point.
Plus I made the mistake of getting a white pad before and when I returned to the office, my coworker mentioned how disgusting it looked from just regular dirt, it was unwashable.
So I got a black one, problem solved.

Of course, I didn't love the branding on the pad so I used a sharpie marker to try to eliminate it, it covered it up slightly, but it's still visible, like a grey on the black.

title: Arrived looking Used and Damaged
text:
I received this in a flat box with broken styrofoam, dirty, and chipped top.
I was going to give this to my niece as a gift, but it looked so worn and dirty that I just gave it to her early.
This is not giftable.
Especially in the box that it arrives in. You would need to take it out of the box and put it in a different box, which especially makes it looked used.
I have several spots that were broken on it.
The cup holder falls out sometimes when you pick it up and hold it sideways.
Yes, it does the job, but not beautifully.

title: Locker organizer
text:
I got this for my daughter as a locker organizer for her dry erase markers and extra pencils.
The back is a FULL magnet!
It is a very stronghold, but not too much that you feel like you are going to break it when removing it from metal, it's perfect.
The center partition is removable and adjustable. It can split at 1/2, 1/4, and also at 3/4.
Not to mention it came in my daughter's favorite color.

title: Stores a TON
text:
This storage center holds so much stuff!!
It does take up quite a bit of space on a table but ends up saving space vs how much room other storage solutions would take up for the same amount of stuff!
I love that the handles on the triangle units are high enough that I can put a label on each one.
Even the center round unit comes out.
The base doesn’t turn like a lazy Susan, but that would be awesome if it did.
The base is right under 12” so if you had a 12” lazy Susan, it should fit nicely!

title: Stores a lot!
text:
For being a mini center this sure holds a lot!
My son uses this to store his legos.
He is able to keep different pieces that he’s working on and in the bigger compartment he can store his pieces when he’s in the middle of a project.

title: Handy!
text:
I really like having this binder around.
It keeps my papers secured without having to use a paper clip or staple.
The yellow is transparent but not super see through that everyone can see what you have inside!
It’s just enough for the user to know what’s inside.
The clasp is very tight and secure.

title: Space!
text:
This calendar is very helpful.
I like that it has lines in the date boxes.
It makes it easier to keep different events separate and easier to read.
It’s helpful that the calendar starts in July because the school year starts in August.
If I could change anything about this it would be that it ended in July instead of December the following year.
This would allow me to buy just these calendars every couple years and not have to transfer information from the previous calendar 1/2 a year early! (Or waist 1/2 a year of pages on the new one)

title: Generic and fun!
text:
These are nice cards.
They are generic enough that they can be used for many celebrations.
Bar/Bat Mitzvah, graduation, engagement, naming ceremony, etc.
The cards don’t have as heavy of card stock as the individual hallmark cards found in their store but they are still well made.

title: Great for kids!
text:
There is just enough lines for my kids to write a thank you note.
The lines are nice and tall for my kids tall lettering.
I think it’s super important for my kids to write thank you notes for the gifts they receive and having these easy to fill out cards make it a lot easier for them.
I think the way the paws hold the front for/from flap is really adorable.
I like how the paper is thick enough that my kids can use markers to fill out the card.

title: fits a crayon and pencils
text: This sharpener easily sharpens both crayons and pencils. They even fit our fatter crayons, not the fattest ones, but a normal size crayon is "loose" in the crayon slot.

title: Holds a lot of paper.
text:
These clips are cute!
They hold over 20 pages, easily!
My only issue with these clips is that some of them are not painted very well and the paint looks chipped.
My 6yo daughter is able to squeeze them but it’s a little hard for her to use them.

title: Felt under rainbow sequins
text:
This is a great birthday card!
All of the wording is printed in a pretty metallic yellow gold. Which matches the inside liner of the envelope.
The card is made of high quality cardstock.
The rainbow has a stiff blue felt as a back - it could technically be removed after delivery and used as a patch on a backpack if desired.
The yellow on the inside is so bright and cheerful - this card will certainly cheer up someone on their birthday!

title: Oh My - that envelope liner!!!
text:
That envelope liner is everything!
It’s glittery gold!!! It does rub off so be careful with not touching it too much! (Or your eye afterwards!)
I love so much about this card!
The glitter does transfer to the outside of the card a little - which just adds more wonderfulness!
The mint green envelope is adorable!
If I had to change anything about this it would be that the envelope was rectangular and not square so it didn’t require extra postage - I’ve seen other square cards have a rectangular envelope that was glued inside to fit a square card perfectly and then didn’t require extra postage.

title: Perfect graduation cards!
text:
I have twin nephews graduating from Kindergarten this year and 1 niece graduating next year - with more coming after that.
These cards are perfect!
They are not super heavy duty card stock like you would get with an individual Hallmark card, but they are still nice.
I really love the Woo Hoo! card!
The Congratulations and Congrats cards could be used for about anything - which is nice.
The Bravo and Woo Hoo cards are really for a job well done - not for say a wedding, baby or house announcement.
It’s nice having a variety of cards so that its easy to grab a card for each nephew and they are not the same. But I don’t have to spend half an hour looking through a whole collection of cards!
All of the cards have a cool metallic shiny gold foil on them on the front.
The silver/grey envelopes look nice - I like having envelopes that are not white!!

title: Love the yellow lined envelope!
text:
I got this card for my daughter’s kindergarten graduation!
I love the bright colors and the reflective silver foil!
The card is made of a nice weight cardstock and is high quality.

I love that my daughter can read the card herself without needing help!
She loves bright colors and this card is bright!

I appreciate that the envelope doesn’t say “Additional Postage Required” since I hand delivered this card.

If I had to change one thing about this card it would be the envelope - since it’s square it requires extra postage.
I’ve seen other envelopes that are rectangle and then are glued inside to fit a square card perfectly - these don’t require extra postage.

title: Super sharp point.
text:
This electric pencil sharpener does a good job at quickly sharpening pencils.
My only issue with this pencil sharpener is that once sharpened - the tip is very sharp.
When using the pencil for the first time after sharpening, the tip almost always breaks off.
It seems to eat a bunch of the pencil away.
I prefer pencil sharpeners that have a smaller area shaved with less visible lead.
I don’t have any jamming issues with the pencil sharpener.
There are very fine shavings after sharpening.

title: So great!
text:
This letter tray is great!
The width is just under 10”.
The depth is right around 12.5”.
The height is just under 5.25”.
There is no grippers on the top of the trays so the papers can slide easily.
The tray is big enough to hold a clip board - which I really like.
The white is white and the pink is like a fuchsia.
I got this for my daughter to put on her desk and it’s really nice.
My favorite part is that the trays stay put and don’t slide off of each other.
The pads on the bottom of the trays help to keep it from moving on the desk.

title: Easy to use, durable
text:
This luggage take is unique and quirky and easy to use.
I had to explain to my daughter the humor in the saying, but I really like it!
The color is nice and bright and easy to spot.
The ID card will not fall out because the strap needs to be removed in order for it to be inserted, which is a really great design. The plastic cover over the card is thick but clear and easily seen through.

title: Cute but not perfect.
text:
My wood card came a little damaged.
The top of the wood is missing a chunk and the front just has a little piece missing.
See attached photo.
The card is made with particle board, real nails and real string.
The card fits fairly good in the envelope provided - it closes around it and fully covers the corners.
The envelope seems like its made for a flat card - not a 3D card like this is.
The envelope is really cool - its got metallic gold on the outside and metallic silver in the inside.
Since the envelope is metallic it’s best to use a permanent marker not a gel marker for writing on it.
I like that the inside of the card has a solid gold metallic side thats on the back of the wood - this makes it nice for if you want to keep the wood for decoration.
The print on the inside is also metallic gold.
Love you, Love us - is a great expression.
This card is really nice for any time of year.
I think this card would be especially nice for a 5th anniversary as the theme is wood!!
It would also work for a 25th anniversary - silver or 50th anniversary - gold.
It’s recommended that you use an additional padded envelope for mailing this card.

title: Easy open/close!
text:
This card is beautiful!
It’s great for so many things - pregnancy, baby shower, birth of a baby, graduation, new job, new house, etc.
Since it’s a light pink it lends itself more to a female than a male gift.
I’ve had other 3D cards that don’t open/close as nicely as this card does.
The card folds pretty flat for being 3D.
The card is made of a very thick cardstock.
The pink strips on the front are beautiful and shiny.
The gold on the front and inside is metallic.
The envelope is lined with a really pretty shiny gold.
It says that additional postage may be required. Based off of the measurements and weight I didn’t need additional postage. If you add a gift card or something else to the envelope you will probably want to add an additional stamp.
This card separated from the 3D tab when I was opening it to write a message in it - I then had to figure out how to connect it again! Hopefully it didn’t come apart when my recipient opened it!!
For that reason I deducted a star.

title: Beautiful!
text:
The gold thread and print is metallic both on the front and inside of the card.
The card is made of a nice thick cardstock.
The envelope has a pretty metallic gold lining and is thicker than a standard envelope.
This card is great for your loved one any time of the year.
My husband was going to propose on a hot air balloon (couldn’t due to it being a windy day) so this card is really nice and meaningful for me to give to him.
If I could change anything about this it would be that the envelope wasn’t square.
I’ve seen other envelopes that are rectangular but have a square area in them.
The envelope doesn’t show that it requires additional postage but it will.

title: Perfect for my husband.
text:
This card is perfect for my husband.
We recently bought electric bikes and have had a great time this last year riding together.
This card is perfect for a loved one for any occasion.
It doesn’t need to be a holiday!
This card is super cute - the teal/blue color is metallic both outside and inside.
It says that additional postage may be required - I’m lucky enough to to be able to hand deliver.

title: Perfect for my sister in law’s birthday.
text:
My sister in law and I always make comments about what we want Alexa to do for us - put the kids to bed, pour me a glass of wine, etc! This card is perfect for her.
The card is made of a nice cardstock.
The teal color on the outside of the card is metallic.
If I had to change one thing it would be that the envelope that comes with the card would be yellow. The envelope is a basic blue color that doesn’t necessarily coordinate with the teal color on the card.

title: Perfect for my sister in law!
text:
My sister in law and I always make comments about what we want Alexa to do for us - put the kids to bed, pour me a glass of wine, etc! This card is perfect for her.
The inside just says “Cheers to you!” So its really great for any occasion thats worth celebrating!
Kid potty trained, went a week (or day) without yelling, etc.
The card is made of a nice cardstock.
The rose gold color on the card is metallic - both on the outside and inside of the card.
The envelope is lined with cute grey + signs. The envelope also has a nice texture to it.
If I had to change one thing it would be that the envelope that comes with the card would be rectangular - not square - as it requires additional postage.
I’ve seen envelopes in the past that are rectangular but are glued shut on one end to make it so it fits a square card nicely.

title: Well made.
text:
These photo pages are well made. The plastic used is durable but pliable.
They don’t alter the color of my photos at all.
There is about 1/4” gap above the vertical photos and a little over 3/4” gap on the horizontal photo.
It can be a little difficult to get the photos into the slots - this can be considered a good or bad thing.
It’s bad because it takes longer to load the photo book.
It’s good because the photos don’t slide out of the pages once loaded.
If I had to change one thing about these pages it would be that they provided a paper cut out for the empty odd space on the top right of each page. It would be nice to have a cut out cardstock to identify each page’s events, without having to do it myself of course!

title: Dirty and getting torn up
text:
Within a week of using this pad, it looks HORRIBLE.
It is all tore up and dirty.
I am the only one that uses it and I keep clean hands.
Maybe I shouldn't have gotten a white/light pink pad.
But the rough fabric. I don't know if my mouse is catching it or what, I didn't damage my mouse in any way, it's the way it came from the factory, so it's a big disappointment the way this pad looks. Maybe It's me, maybe it's not the pad.
It does hold it's position well on the desk. It is comfortable on my wrist. It just looks horrible now.

title: Lots of great colors!
text:
My 6yo and 3yo go through a lot of markers.
My 6yo is starting to really get into coloring in the lines.
These markers are great - the array of colors is really nice.
The markers are a good size - they fit will into my 3yo and 6yo’s hands.
I appreciate that the lids and the base have the color on them.
The box they come in can be used for storage but I have an ArtBin that I use to store the markers for the kids.
I’m very happy that these markers are not too tall for the ArtBin and the markers can stand up in the bin and the lid closes!
The lid of the markers can slide into the bottom of the marker. It has the top of the lid go into the bottom - so markers can be stacked end to end - which my kids think is pretty cool.

title: Perfect for beginning writers.
text:
These thank you cards are perfect for my kindergartner.
The lines have plenty of room above them for their sometimes oversides letters!
I love that these provide an easy way for them to get into writing thank you notes.
Perfect fill in the blank format.
The printing is really well done.
The paper is a nice cardstock.
The envelopes are bright and noticeable in the mail!
The backs are mostly blank besides the Hallmark logo and paper sourcing information - this leaves plenty of room for a custom drawing or a 4x6or 5x7 photo to be taped on.

title: Weak Magnet
text:
I was hoping to use these clips on the inside of my metal garage door to store my family’s masks.
The magnets on the clips is super weak. The clip holds about 2 kid masks and then it slides down off the door.
So now they are being used on the fridge to hold a few papers at a time.
These clips do work great for keeping bags closed.
Don’t buy these in hopes of hanging anything even slightly of weight.

title: Perfect for home schooling
text: I added these to the kid's bedrooms to help them create their homework stations. These are holding up well to their pushpin use and rearranging of papers. They hung easy, I didn't use the adhesive option, as I've gotten burned before with some adhesive stuff to the wall which caused me to have some major drywall repair. But a good little nail and a hammer did the trick here. The kids like the addition of these to their rooms and it gives them a place to display stuff without it being all over their walls with tic-tac and nails.

title: 35 pages!
text:
This stapler uses regular staples (not included).
I’m able to use this stapler to staple through (probably more than) 35 pages of lined writing paper.
This thing is awesome!
It’s easy to use and I can stand it up on the bottom of the plier handles so it takes up less room than a regular stapler.
I’m not sure why anyone would own a regular stapler when they could have this one instead.

title: basic paper folder
text:
These are a nice basic folder, but they don't feel cheap, but they also don't feel super high class.
They have the slits on the inside so that a business card can be placed in them.
They have a slight grey undertone to the white.
They are not a crispy white and will look like a different color from white paper inserted into it.
These are a great folder for a conference with a sticker on the outside with the company name and a business card and material on the inside.
Exactly what I thought they would be.

title: AMAZING!
text:
A tax preppers' dreams come true. Also, this could go through 3 layers of cardboard with no problem. Great for Halloween costumes!
This was very easy to use and it has the normal features of a stapler, except that it cannot be used opened up for corkboard displays.

title: Perfect eraser

title: Fun to have Alexa print & copy stuff!
text:
I was going to give this printer 3 stars - but then I figured it out - 4 hours later!!!!
So here’s my 5* review.
This printer took about 20 minutes to initially set up. I then chose to set up to a smartphone only - not through a computer.
I set up the printer using both WiFi and using Bluetooth.

I downloaded the Canon App to set up the printer.
When first opening the app - you are asked to approve location services. I didn’t approve. So I learned that I needed to turn it on in order to use the printer. When looking for the app in the settings I noticed that the app in under “Printer” not “Canon”.
After over 2 hours I was only able to get Bluetooth setup connected and not WiFi.
The things that ended up working to get Bluetooth connected:
In order to get my printer set up I ended up turning my airplane mode “on” for my phone.
That did the trick.
To get my phone to print using this printer with Bluetooth only I need to turn on “airplane mode”. The printer can’t be found otherwise.
It took another hour or so to get the WiFi figured out.
Here’s what finally worked - forget about setting up WiFi through the app - go straight to the printer.
From what I’ve experienced the printer can not connect to a 5G WiFi network.
I used my base WiFi network and manually typed in the password on the printer - it’s not convenient but it works!!!
Once WiFi was working I was also able to use AirPrint without an issue.

I was really looking forward to connecting the printer to my Alexa - once the printer was connected to WiFi I was able to open my Alexa app and download the Canon skill.
The process is a little confusing but the steps are laid out in the Canon skill in the Alexa app. As part of the process you need to enter a registration is which your printer actually has to print out.
From there I was able to easily printer coloring pages, origami pages with instructions and mini cards.
I even had Alexa run the copy function and it worked great!

I am able to leave my airplane mode off and use this printer as I would expect with the WiFi connected.

This printer comes with 5 ink cartridges - it’s nice that they can only replace the empty ones. But ink isn’t cheap - no matter which printer you have.
The paper tray doesn’t hold that much paper. So if you do a lot of printing you will need to reload the paper tray quite often.
The printer also comes with 3 5”x5” photo sheets.

Knowing what I know no - the setup process would probably take me less than an hour.
I really expected the app to work better - but thankfully the printer works as it should!

Plan to use short lengths or tolerated substantial waste.

title: Sharpen perfectly
text:
The Dixon No. 2 Standard pencils sharpen perfectly in the X--Acto 1041 and 1031 Boston style sharpeners.
I discovered that some cheaper pencils have off center leads and don't leave a sharp lead, but a sharp wood point. These Dixon pencils have a long lasting lead per sharpen.

title: Cautionary tale of off center pencil leads.
text:
I bought both the 1031 and the 1041, looking for a good sharpener. To my surprise both these are excellent copies of the Boston sharpener of yore. Both are sturdy and well built. For some years the Boston copies were shoddy with poor workmanship and materials. Not so these new X-Acto sharpeners.
Both sharpen the Dixon No. 2 Standard pencil perfectly.
But, I had some round pencils, just larger that the number 2, which fits the next size hole in the 1031. All of these round pencils sharpened off center. Upon close examination I discovered that the leads were off center. These were gimme advertizing pencils, so not the highest quality. Leaving me to wonder if all the problems with sharpeners and pencils over the years were off center leads in the pencils.

title: Cautionary tale, off center pencil leads.
text:
I also bought the X-Acto 1031 sharpener. Both the 1041 and the 1031 sharpens a Dixon #2 perfectly. Note that this sharpener only sharpens the Standard size pencils.
See my review of the 1031.
These are excellent copies of the Boston sharpeners of yore.
For sometime, copies of the Boston were very flimsy with shoddy internals. But the X-Acto have the quality and sturdiness of the Boston that I remember.

title: Not the best... probably not the worst?
text:
I think next time I’ll opt for a better box with a higher price tag, but these will do for now.

SHIPMENT
They arrived stacked and flat wrapped in a bunch of sticky clear wrap—like the type you use to cover food at home. There was one plastic strap around the whole bundle. I’d imagine the corners could get very dented depending on your carrier. If it would’ve been raining, I’m sure moisture would’ve gotten in rather quickly.

CARDBOARD
They are your standard brown corrugated cardboard; though, I’d say the paper and the larger spaces between the corrugated strips (inside the cardboard) are of poor quality. This makes it too easy to bend just about anywhere on the box—not just at the folding lines.

ASSEMBLY (OVERALL)
While putting together the boxes was simple to figure out, getting the boxes to fold properly was another matter. Like I said above, the poorer quality materials of the box make it all too easy to fold the box just about anywhere. This made for uneven folds. (See photo.) This could be remedied a bit by refolding but it just makes it a little harder and makes the final box look a little less professional.

ASSEMBLY ISSUE
Along with the weaker materials issue, it seems the few boxes I have tried to assemble are not staying together well. The notches where you tuck in the box flaps are not sticking to keep the side walls up/together.. I’ll probably need to use a little tape. Not ideal.

CONCLUSION
The price was low and the ratings were good, but these boxes are mediocre at best. If you’re looking for something better, more professional and sturdy for your business, you may need to skip this listing.

title: Pretty to look at, but not Pilot's best work
text:
I had my eye on this pen for almost 3 years before I finally bought it. I LOVE Pilot pens. Most of my favorite fountain pens are Pilots - they are usually so smooth and consistent, just a pleasurable writing instrument all around. I own around 30 fountain pens and a third of them are Pilots: Metropolitans, Preras, Vanishing Points, you name it.

But - this one has turned out to be my least favorite, unfortunately. I adore the way it looks, but functionally it's just not on par with other Pilots. My primary complain is that the collar containing the feed and nib comes unscrewed pretty frequently. It seems as though unscrewing the pen cap continually loosens the feed/nib unit. I have to rescrew the unit in at least twice a day with just regular use. Doesn't sound like a big deal and maybe for some people it won't be — but for me, when I have so many pens — and none of the others have this issue — it just feels like an unnecessary pain. And I don't think there's anything about this nib that makes it any better than my other Pilots. In fact, I prefer the feel of every other Pilot nib I own over this one, including the ones on the more affordable Metropolitans.

I don't completely regret buying it. I love the look of the black and yellow, and the pen isn't unusable. It's just not the best. If you're looking for a daily writer, or if this is going to be your only fountain pen, I wouldn't recommend it. But if you're a penhead with a collection and you just love the black and yellow look of this one, you could do worse. But you could also probably do better.

text:
This is a really nice pouch. I purchased it so I could have something to slip my A6 Hobonichi planner into when its in my backpack. My planner cover is expensive and I don't want it to get marked up, and this Delfonics pouch is a great solution. It looks really elegant and beautiful. It's made of polyurethane so it's easy to wipe down, but it looks and feels like soft, pebbled leather. The zipper on it is really nice - smooth and easy and straight.

The pouch is capable of holding a lot - my planner actually fits in the front snap pocket which leaves the larger, zippered portion available to fill with other accessories.

Highly recommend!

I used a long strip of this to hold a very lightweight plastic rack in my horse trailer (2 lb max), and it's already starting to droop on one side. I thought this would be a sturdier solution than command strips, but I'm not overly impressed.

EDIT: For how thick this stuff is, it does not hold up in a garage/trailer. I've replaced this stuff with heavy-duty command strips.

title: Black didn't work at all
text:
I first changed out the magenta cartridge. Worked fine. Then the cyan and yellow got low ink warning. I decided to change both those out along with the black even though I still had a small amount of black ink left since a lot of ink is used in the cleaning process. Once I changed them out, machine went through the motions. I tried to print something and the black would not print!

I did head cleanings, nozzle checks. Repeatedly. Did not work. I swapped the new black cartridge for my old one, and now it will not work.

I am worried that my printer is now ruined. I purchased GENUINE ink cartridges from Amazon. I'm very upset. I do NOT recommend this package of ink cartridges. For those who might think I don't know what I'm doing. I have five printers, two are Epson, and I have had Epson in the past. I've never experienced problems like this.

text: This is a cute set of stationery items, and they grow in the dark pretty well! The heart on the pen is flexible and vibrant, but it doesn't glow as well as the other items. The notebook pages have cute designs on each page. The slime has a STRONG smell... it's sort of a fruity smell that I don't like much, but my daughter loves it. The googly eyes can be removed from the slime and placed on other things. I'm not sure if they're supposed to come off, but that's what my daughter decided to do. lol! The slime isn't too mushy or slimy, it's more like a soft putty that sticks to itself well instead of a slime. I'm usually extra careful about slime because it can stick to clothes and be hard to get out, but this slime isn't like those kinds of slime.

text: First off, these pens are extremely cute and have a good grip. They also write fairly well, even though they write thin. The downsides are that some are defective and some are just plain. Like the ones that just have 1 leaf at the top - those seem incredibly pointless to me. With that said, the price isn't bad at all for the quantity you get. The price per pen is so low that it lessens the burn of opening the malfunctioning pens.

text: The cards are pretty and perfect for Fall, but you'll need to fold each and EVERY one yourself. I didn't realize that until they came in. The box is definitely sturdy enough to be used even after all the cards are gone, for things like jewelry or little toys. The only negative is a small one - the brand name is on basically every stationery piece.

No space is wasted on these either because the back is specifically designed for the kids to draw a picture to Santa! So cute!!

title: Awesome Planner With a Few Personal Issues
text:
This is going to be great, though I am a very right-brained person who didn't mind making/designing and filling out my own day planner, including adding the actual days of the month on the month calendar and the daily pages. Lots of room in the back notes section for putting in essential names, addresses, and email/website info. My only real issue is I actually hate the hinge/magnet closure and am pretty sure I will break it just with regular use. It's sturdy and well made but the latch is just awkward for me, especially when I'm writing on my lap. I might just remove it.

Just be careful to double check your dates when you fill this out! The days of the week on the overall monthly calendars start on a different day from most calendars (something I also wish was different).

title: Wish We Had These Back In The Day...
text: Could use better outer pockets but will hold a thinner textbook or composition book, etc in the open outside pocket.  This thing is built well and is easy to use.  I'm so relieved that this will probably last for at least 2 more years.  The double notebook style makes it easier for our student to break up her day into 1-3rd period and then 4-6th, and that seems to help the student stay organized, which is ESSENTIAL.  We added a zipper pouch (3-hole) in each half of the notebook and that helps keep pencils, calculator, whatever is needed for that part of the day ready without having to zip the side you're using closed, flip it over, and dig out what was stored on the other side.  This thing stays upright in the locker as well and travels well in the backpack between sporting events, etc.  The handle makes it work like a briefcase even, and that is something I wish we'd had when we were in high school.  I really appreciate the thick nylon and great quality zippers.

Not really practically priced or as thorough at erasing.

I would not trust them to keep a handgun or other dangerous items out of the hands of anybody.

Still, it will fit with maybe a little warping or laid against a sturdy piece of fiberboard or cardboard. Good for most documents, insurance papers, contact information sheets, and more than adequately sized for CD ROMS and thumbdrives full of family photos, etc. I hope we never have to worry about it working in a fire, but it doesn't have to try. This is a HEAVY box and not so easy to just jolt out of your house with. Not a safe but not lightweight. I have some hope it'll be waterproof or strong enough to withstand some falling debris in an earthquake. The handle appears to be hard core and though there are just keys to open it, you would need a locksmith to open it after a fire (most likely) anyway.

Highly suggest some of those silica packets to keep the things inside dry. I haven't seen or smelled moisture but it's just a good idea.

text:

What I might do with one of them is see if I can trim the tip for a finer line. Otherwise these are really really nice pens and a cheap way of getting that line variation and range of color with your inks. Not sure if it will work with shimmering inks, but general fountain pen inks are great.

title: Fantastic Quality Markers
text: Great little markers with a big ink capacity and line variation. I can make thin and thick lines real easily depending on the need. They may be a tad expensive, but I don't see needing any new markers anytime soon.

title: The hack to getting into Calligraphy
text:
I have been using brush pens, dip pens and fountain pens for around 6 years now and have to say these pens (I am particular to green cap size at 3.8MM) make calligraphy real easy. Especially if you are trying to write old english or gothic. They don't take a lot of time to learn besides lining the nib to the paper and maintaining a consistent 45 degree angle.

If you aren't good with pressure control, are heavy handed or want to break into calligraphy without much cost or hassle then these are great.

title: It feels better than my TWSBI 580 pen at times
text: I've used this pen for a couple years now and it is still going strong. No nib or feed issues even when I let heavy handed pencil users try it out. It feels better than my TWSBI 580 pen at times. I use waterman ink in mine so regular paper can be written on with little to no bleed or feathering.

title: Great pens! For beginners? Maybe?
text: Good nibs, although I don't think really needed the thickest one and kind of wish there were an even thinner one... but I like the 1.5mm best. The thing I like least is that you can't pop the pen cap on the end while you're writing; it's not designed for that, which seems weird to me. However, that's just a minor annoyance. The pens write well, and if you want to switch ink cartridge colors, it comes with a little squeezy bulb to push water through the nib for cleaning. Each pen also comes with a tiny rectangle of plastic that's meant to be a nib cleaner, but I foresee those getting lost.

title: My new favorite calligraphy pen!

I have all manner of calligraphy pens, these are the easiest that I've used , no spotting , no streaking , just  a continual smooth flow with sharp and crisp lines. The thin lines are very fine, I don't  get lines this fine and sharp unless I use my old speedball pens that I hand dip in ink but that doesn't give you a continually smooth flow like these pens do. title: Great Calligraphy ink
text: Higgins eternal ink is such an easy ink to use.  It goes on well, rarely feathers when using a moderate to good calligraphy paper and provides a nice black with good coverage.  It's not the deepest of deep blacks, but for practice it works well for me.  There's no weird smell.  I haven't seen any fading with lettering done several months ago.  There's never an issue with waiting long lentos of time for this to arrive.  I like that you can use it straight from the bottle without needing to dilute it.

title: Not the paper for Pointed Pen Calligraphy Practice
text: When I was looking for Pointed Pen Calligraphy practice paper, this paper kept coming up as one of the best.  My first ream of the paper seemed very good, I was satisfied with how it performed.  The ink didn't bleed and I was able to get good letter formation.  I used it for several months and found it to be very good practice paper.  The second ream of paper was a totally different story.  In fact I'm not using it for my calligraphy work at all, which is a real disappointment.  Each time I put my dip pen down on the paper the ink immediately begins to feather and bleed.  It's not usable at all as calligraphy practice paper.  I don't know what happened from the first ream to the second, but it's as if I'm suing two different papers, although I re-ordered the same exact paper and am using the exact same ink and other supplies.  This batch is useless for practice paper.  It  feels as if I've been ripped off.  This paper isn't inexpensive but I spent the extra after my first experience, where the paper acted so well.  I don't think  will try a third ream, but instead will go with Espon or Hammerhill, two other highly recommended papers for calligraphy.  I don't know what I'll do with all the extra paper I have that's not usable for my calligraphy practice.  Very, very disappointing.

title: Wonderful pens to start doing Calligraphy
text: These Pilot Parallel Pens are just so easy to use.  They come with a small instruction manual, as well as extra ink, and small piece of plastic to use to clean the tines of the nib, as well as a device to get the ink flowing (?).  I haven't had any issues with the ink flow, as long as I compress the cartridge and get a bit of a blob of ink out initially.  The pens are just so much fun.  My only complaint is wishing they had something between the 1st and 2nd sizes, that would make the set even more useable.  I haven't used the 6.0mm nib as that's extremely large, and more for use on posters and other large scale projects.  These pens are just fun to use!

title: Great colors for great pens!
text: I’ve just started using Pilot Parallel Prns and love what you can do with the pens especially once you move away from the black and red that come with each pen. It’s fun changing the color cartridge and getting an ombré effect as the ink changes color. The variety in the pack is good. The price for 12 cartridges is great. Depending on how much you use the pens each cartridge, with moderately heavy use each cartridge seems to last a good amount of time. I’m hoping to use the red and green to create my own Christmas cards.  The provided example was done with purple ink. The color is rich with a hint of brown. Right now I’m just experimenting with the various colors. I can’t say enough about the black which is quite deep. Depending on what type of paper you’re using (calligraphy paper is pretty much all you can use) will tell you how wet the ink will be. Lower quality paper will give you very wet ink that smears very easily

title: Off Label Use for Comic Boards-Fabric Organizing!
text: I use these Comic Book Boards for storing fabric yardage.  One board will hold one to three yards of fabric.  The fabric is folded in half and wound around the board and secured with a sturdy quilting pin.  Using these boards I have been able to organize all my fabric according to color and print, making it easily accessible.  Anything less than a yard goes in to a storage bin, also sorted by color.  My entire sewing room has a more organized look and feel to it now the fabric is under control.

title: Good print quality at a great price but only for about 3-4 weeks, now the ink is smudged and smearing.
text:
So far these inexpensive ink cartridges are giving me good print quality and seem to be lasting longer than HP branded cartridges. Even if they last less time than the branded ink it will still be worth it due to the price point difference. It is obvious that HP is making the majority of their money on their ink. Their printers are reasonably priced and work fairly well, but the ink is extremely expensive! I was constantly running out of black ink. I have an HP 7520 printer and frequently would run out of the photo black, despite the fact I never print photos. It was a chore to try and figure out which cartridge to buy (this printer has two black cartridges, one is regular sized and the other is much bigger, the issue is they aren't interchangeable and they would run out at different times and I would need to figure out which cartridge ran out). I'm happy I've tried OSIR and will continue to buy this ink as my printer had no difficulty recognizing the cartridges, they fit into the slots without difficulty, you can see how much ink is left in each cartridge (a huge difference from the branded cartridges), and the price can't be
beat. In the meantime, I plan on also investigating refillable cartridges although with these inexpensive OSIR cartridges I'm not sure if it's worth it. I do recycle the cartridges when they're empty.

I originally found these cartridges to be well worth money with good print quality. Unfortunately that was only until about 5 weeks of use. I mostly print in black and noticed that the print quality had degraded and was smearing and smudged, every time I printed. In fact, it's hard to read some of the printing. I cleaned the printer heads which didn't help at all. The quality of the color is also not very bright or true. I don't print that much but the printer is already notifying me I'm low on ink-this after purchasing the ink in early March. I'm changing my original 5 star rating to 3 stars (and could go down to 2 except they were inexpensive). What a disappointment to have this happen after thinking I had finally found ink that worked and was much less expensive than HP cartridges. I won't be buying this brand again.

title: Good Product for the Price
text: These seem to work just as well as the original HP cartridges, at a discounted price.  The color may be not quite as bright but as I'm not printing off photos it hasn't been an issue for me.  There's absolutely no difference in quality when printing in black or grayscale.  Next step is to start using refillable, remanufactured cartridges that are available (I think on Amazon, definitely in other places).  HP printers seem to use a LOT of ink, so any savings can mean a significant amount of money stays in your pocket.

title: Great small clips that securely hold your fabric
text: Love these mini clips by Clover.  I have two other sizes (regular and large), but find myself reaching for these small clips on a frequent basis.  The narrowness of the clip means it doesn't get in the way of the presser foot.  They hold just as well as the regular sized clips but are easier to use.  I love them and think they'll become my "go to" clip in the future.

title: Great Clips to use in place of Straight Pins!

These are just great little clips for holding your fabric together when you don't want to put a pin-hole in your fabric (if you are using say pleather, leather, cork etc). title: Wonderful way to keep fabric stash neat and tidy!

I followed a link from So Sew Easy and the first link brought me to the wrong product and the largest boards-they don't fit my Ikea shelving at all.  Finally after getting the proper size I started wrapping the material on the boards using a straight pin to hold the fabric in place and once finished, voila your fabric stash will look wonderfully neat.  If you have a big stash it can take a while to get through the job.  Great way to keep your fabric organized.

title: Great pens for sewing and creating easy to follow lines
text:
FriXioin pens have been getting a bad rap lately with some quilters saying the line drawn with the pen leaves a faint trace even after it's been ironed off. My local quilt store no longer carries them due to this. I personally haven't seen this happen and am very happy with my pens, especially now that there are different colors for when your first choice (usually black) doesn't show up. They are just so convenient, and if you draw on the wrong side of the fabric that will perhaps take care of the issue. The line is nice and fine, barely noticeable, but just enough so you can follow the line when sewing. Just be sure to cap them well, they do tend to dry out if they aren't capped.

title: This is everything I expected and more.
text:
First off, whether you end up loving or regretting this purchase highly depends on how you're going to use it, and coming into this with realistic expectations. To have an amazing Midori traveler's notebook experience, you have to put work into it. You're not going to have a beautifully cultured notebook with your daily thoughts and aspirations if you completely give up after a week.

And you can't expect to have a gorgeous Pinterest-worthy aesthetic MTN off the bat. The MTN is what you make it. It doesn't have to be perfect to be beautiful. But when you make it yours, it is perfect.

That said, this notebook is really gorgeous. The leather is even softer than I expected, and that was with absolutely everyone fawning over the leather. It is amazingly supple and soft, and smooth. The outside is soft, but the inside is even softer, as it is raw. The outside is smooth while the raw interior has a suede-like texture to it.

Note that your notebook will most likely arrive with a white powder-like coating over the outside of the leather. This is normal and a result of the natural tanning process of the leather. It is easily removed with gentle wiping. I, being lazy, used the cloth pouch the notebook came with to wipe it off. It came off easily with the dry cloth.

The smell is pretty strong. Some may find it to be a delectable leather scent, while others might find it chemical-y. I think it's somewhere in between, but it is not overly unpleasant or overwhelming. My sister couldn't get enough of the leather scent, so your personal experiences may vary. The scent will dissipate with age, however.

If you have been listing over this notebook, I recommend you purchase it. You can't beat Amazon's prices.

Remember that this notebook is what you make of it. Don't worry too much about making it "Pinterest-worthy" or whatever- just make it *yours!* That is the true beauty of the MTN. Embrace individuality and create your own version of perfection.

title: Superior version of the TWSBI pens, but with limited nib options.
text: This pen is everything that I wanted the TWSBI Eco to be. I love that pen, but let's face it, it does not look like a normal pen at first glance, and may even be called ugly. Upgrading to the nicer looking TWSBI 580 didn't help, because it came with the extra weight that many people associate with money, but my hand does not like weighty pens. I looked forever for a transparent piston pen until I came upon the Wing Sung 698. It is beautiful and sleek; it has great nibs as all Wing Sungs seem to; it even has a build element that TWSBI is lacking; it can take other standard nibs; it's lightweight and unfussy as a piston. It's everything I could dream of -- except that feed. I don't care that it's "cool" as a transparent feed; it's got a severe downward slope that makes it completely incompatible with nearly every nib out there that one would easily exchange among Jowo-compatible pens. Apparently it's supposed to take Pilot nibs, but really? What pen tinkerer, who Frankenpens cheap pens with upgraded nibs, buys a bunch of Pilot nibs to swap around with their pens? The only nib I could fit on this that I had on hand was the TWSBI 580 nib, but even that was a struggle. Maybe I would not be complaining about the unswappability of feed/nibs if Wing Sung came out with 1.1mm or larger stubs, but until then, I will only be looking for pens that can accept more standard Jowo stubs. It's a shame because this pen is perfect in every other way.

title: Not at all dry; beautiful and well behaved.
text: I bought this to tame my Pilot Parallel frankenpen that was a gusher, because everyone talks about how Pelikan 4001 inks are the driest inks out there. "Bone dry" they say. Well, I don't find this to be true at all -- this ink has good flow, is well behaved, and is a beautiful green with a hint of teal in it. Great value.

The stitching is quite intricate and decorative, so it's definitely got more time and effort put in than a few rawhide strings threaded in like some other leather journals. The paper is nice too, but it's got a few weird pages that feel like waxed paper, and ink just slides right off. I would love to see this quality leather on a refillable journal cover.

title: Beautiful leather, smart design, bad sizing
text:
This leather is very beautiful, and the design is extremely efficient - you can stick either a typical journal, or a vertical notepad onto it without having to buy two separate journal cover designs. The dimensions are generously sized, if you're looking at this two-dimensionally.

Unfortunately, since we live in a 3-dimentional world, this cover also needs depth, which it's sorely lacking. It can accommodate maybe a half inch notebook at best, but would prefer a thinner one. It can't come close to closing properly if I try to stick a regular A5 notebook in it. It's very very shallow and flat. If it were thick enough to hold a substantial notebook that doesn't get used up in a week, I'd be happy to run back to buy. For now, sadly I must return and continue my search for a cover that accommodates a grownup notebook.

title: Deep, saturated, wet ink.
text:
I'd been about to give up on using any blue on my very dry, extra fine nib pen. They'd all dry up into a faint wisp of a light blue, nothing close to the color they initially lay down. But then I tried the Sargasso Sea on a whim, not really ready to be impressed because it's yet another blue in a sea of blues.

I was wrong. This blue does not fade away after drying. It stays dark, vibrant, and beautifully similar to Tanzanite. My dry little ef nib now writes excellently, thanks to the wet properties of this ink. Who needs blue-black (what kind of color is a blue black anyway? dark blue? colored black?) when you have a dark, vibrant blue that isn't plain and boring, but has a delicious hint of indigo in it and best of all, writes nice and wet and stays vibrant with time? This unique-named ink from Diamine might end up becoming my go-to, everyday professional ink.

title: Beautiful little pen, almost perfect
text:
I was put off of the idea of pocket fountain pens after trying this company's newest chonk boi model, but decided to try the mini wancai just in case I'm so glad I did -- it's slim enough to fit in the hand, lightweight and perfectly balanced when posted, and sleek and elegant. It's really a joy to hold.

However, it's NOT a joy to write with. For such a great little instrument, the most important part - the actual writing part of it - is very hard and scratchy. I'm not asking for a flex nib by any means, but the ink flow is very dry and it feels like the nib is scratching the paper instead of writing on it. It's supposed to be a Fine nib, but my Extra Fine Chinese pen writes wetter than this. Ink is barely visible, and it's simply a very unpleasant experience to write with it. I do really love the idea and execution, but the nib is unusable. It's a shame because for such a tiny little pen with fragile looking body, it does cost quite a bit and I can't just keep buying new ones in hopes of hitting a good nib.

title: Good entry for fountain pens, but not ergonomic

While the nib is great to write with, Pilot undermined themselves here by putting it in such a cheap looking body that's hard to use. It's got curves in it but is still very thin and difficult to grip comfortably. The cartridge is so difficult to install that I near gave up after nearly a whole day of wrestling before it finally began to flow. I'm not even going to try a second cartridge, and since I didn't want to deal with wrestling this back and forth even with an eyedropper, I had to throw away the whole pen and give up on the idea. I'm just going to stick with something that's already pre-filled with converters, a piston, or vacuum.

It's very thick and therefore unwieldy; it's quite heavy, so difficult to balance. The transparency makes it look like glass, which can be pretty to look at, but combined with the weight, it makes one a bit nervous about dropping and shattering it. My hand just didn't know what to do with this because it's so heavy and chunky, and while it's a bit too short to use unposted, it's actually extremely imbalanced when it's posted, making it even harder to use due to the weight in the back. I think they did much better with the other small pocket pen they sell, but it is a very cute little pen and I will admire it from afar on other people's pockets.

title: Quick drying, long lasting, quite smooth.
text: This ink is almost as smooth as Parker Quink black, which can't be beat in my opinion in terms of smoothness. It's called "well-behaved" for a reason - it's very quick drying, and does not gush even in wet pens. It lays down a very thin line, and therefore the ink lasts a long time if you're looking to squeeze as much ink as you can for the buck. It's closer to a Tanzanite / indigo blue than a sky blue, which is a pleasant surprise. But as it dries, it will grow fainter. Despite its smoothness, I ended up looking for something else because this ink is thin and I wanted something a bit bolder.
